species.name: 5-gilled white mid-dorsal line hagfish
species.description: A female specimen (29.0 cm TL) was found with approximately 20 developing eggs, without terminal anchor filaments or hooks, and each egg measures approximately 4-7 mm in diameter and 10-12 mm in length (Ref. 122037).

species.name: Aapticheilichthys websteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a river less than 10 meters wide and less than 1 meter depth during dry season, warm water of over 80°F during the day, slightly acid water, pH just over 6, in primary forest (Ref. 78622). Non-annual reproduction with two weeks' water incubation of eggs and schooling in small groups of a few dozens of specimens of various ages and dominance; several individualos may have gone through a sex change (Ref. 78622).

species.name: Abactochromis labrosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky substrate (Ref. 6307).

species.name: Abadèche boulotte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Based on stomach radiographs, contents include crustaceans, gastropods, remains of polychaetes, and detritus (Ref. 80689).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche de Günther
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Adults feed on pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 27637).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche doigts
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche du cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rocky areas of the shelf and upper continental slope.  Juveniles found in shallow waters than adults (Ref. 36731).  Benthic and common species (Ref. 34024).  Feed on dragonets, mantis shrimps, hake, squid, and various fishes (Ref. 27121).  Spawning occurs from August to October.  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Utilized fresh and frozen; can be fried and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Abadèche mince
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species at bathyal and abyssal depth (Ref. 56809).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche noir
species.description: Common species found in rocky shelf and upper slope waters (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche rose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024). Found between depths of 22 m (Ref. 58489) and 1000 m (Ref. 33848). Feed mainly on crustaceans such as Munida and scampi and also on fish. Also caught above the bottom when feeding on hoki (Macruronus novaezelandiae) during the hoki spawning season. Available all year round. Juveniles are found in shallower shelf waters (Ref. 6390). Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205). Utilized fresh, frozen or smoked; can be fried and baked (Ref. 9988, 34024).

species.name: Abadèche rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species inhabiting rocky bottom in deep shelf and upper slope waters (Ref. 34024).   Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abadèche sans jambes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Feed on pelagic crustaceans like euphausiids, mysids and decapods (Ref. 27637).  Found on or above continental slope (Ref. 36731).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abalistes filamentosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abbottina binhi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abbottina lalinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abbottina liaoningensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abbottina obtusirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abe's angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over bottom that is  primarily composed of variably sized rubble, with temperature 20-21°C (Ref. 77035).

species.name: Abe's flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic surface waters (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Able de Heckel
species.description: Inhabits lowland riverine habitats especially oxbows and other water bodies only connected to rivers during floods.  Often encountered in ponds, steppe lakes and small water bodies not connected to rivers (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in large schools which are most numerous in autumn.  Found between weeds in shallow pools and creeks, shallow lakes, peat and clay excavations and canals.  It is exposed to the stormy flow of water (in spring, autumn and winter), but usually choose quite places like small bays, plots behind bottom stones extending out of water and concrete foundations of bridges.  In autumn, the schools of fish keep to the surface and rarely go to the pelagic zone.  Towards winter, the schools break up and the number of fish per unit of river square decreases rapidly (Ref. 27674); they spend the winter in deeper waters (Ref. 41592).  Feeds on phytoplankton and zooplankton and on flying insects (Ref. 27368).  Spawns among vegetation (Ref. 30578).  Aquarium keeping:  at least 10 individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm; not recommended for home aquariums (Ref. 51539).  Scales were utilized for production of Essence d'Orient, which was used for coating artificial pearls.  Locally threatened due to draining of wetlands.  Reaches up to about 9 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ablette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivore; remnants of insect larvae (Ref. 36901), weed, beetles and other insects (Ref. 42135) and fish (Ref. 36899) found in stomach. Juveniles predominantly insectivore, piscivore as adults (Ref. 85675).

species.name: Ablette de lacs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lower reaches of rives, coastal lakes, estuaries, and brackish areas of sea.  Occur close to surface and tolerate salinities up to 14 ppt.  Adults predominantly prey on planktonic crustaceans, terrestrial insects and small fish while larvae and young juveniles feed on zooplankton, algae and insect larvae.  Spawn in small rivers or streams with heavy current on gravel bottom.  Landlocked populations found in reservoirs spawn in reservoir tributaries (Ref. 59043).  Eastern populations migrate upstream for spawning (Ref. 13696).  Males assemble and wait at the spawning grounds for ripe females, which arrive later.  Deposit sticky eggs which adhere on pebbles or stones.  Embryonic development lasts 2-3 days, with larvae first staying among gravel for 8-11 days, then actively migrating to shallows and backwaters. Adults migrate back to sea, lakes or estuaries soon after spawning to forage.  Young juvenile undertake downriver migration in autumn of same year or next spring.  Due to dam constructions, almost all long-distance migrating populations lost as they were unable to reach spawning sites.  Survive in small water courses and as landlocked populations in some reservoirs.  Populations are expected to decline and to further decline due to expanding hydroelectric development and strong ecological impacts on Caspian sea  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ablé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open waters of lakes and medium to large rivers.  Forms large aggregations in backwaters and other still waters during winter.  Adults occur in shoals near the surface. Larvae live in littoral zone of rivers and lakes while juveniles leave shores and occupy a pelagic habitat, feeding on plankton, drifting insects or invertebrates fallen on the water surface (Ref. 59043).  Feeds mainly on plankton, including crustaceans (Ref. 30578) and  insects (Ref. 9696).  Spawns in shallow riffles or along stony shores of lakes, occasionally above submerged vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Excellent as bait for carnivorous fishes.  May be captured using the smallest hook and a fly as bait.  Its flesh is tasty (Ref. 30578).  Of little interest to commercial or sport fisheries in its native range because of its small size (Ref. 1739).  Scales were previously utilized in making Essence d"Orient, a coating for artificial pearls (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Aborichthys barapensis
species.description: The species was collected from the Barap Stream in shallow water (ca 10–30 cm depth) near Lazu Village in the southeastern part of Arunachal Pradesh, where the substrate comprises mostly of medium-sized boulders, and a mixture of pebbles, cobbles, small stones and large boulders somewhere of light to dark grayish colors. The water in the stream was cool, clear and moderately fowing due to considerable decrease in water volume in dry season. Riparian vegetaton found were grasses, shrubs and small to medium sized trees along the banks and larger trees uphill. Associated fish collected were Schizothorax richardsonii, Garra sp., Amblyceps sp. Psilorhynchus balitora, Devario aequipinnatus, and Exostoma labiatum (Ref. 128991).

species.name: Aborichthys cataracta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in waterfall habitat with a plunge pool (Ref. 95164).

species.name: Aborichthys elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Aborichthys garoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Aborichthys iphipaniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aborichthys kailashi
species.description: The type locality, Pange River, where the species was collected was characterized by the passage of the river between deep gorges flanked with thick vegetation; from relatively swift but clear and moderately deep (50-100 cm) water as the bottom of the river was clearly visible. The area has different types of substrate including gravels, cobbles and medium to large-sized boulders with thick layers of aquatic green algae and moss. The vegetation along the river bank is characteristic of tropical evergreen forest dominated by different types of bamboos and broad-leafed trees. Associated fish recorded from the collection site includes Schizothorax richardsonii, Creteuchiloglanis arunachalensis and Oreoglanis pangenensis (Ref. 128990).

species.name: Aborichthys kempi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Aborichthys palinensis
species.description: Collected from a small tributary of Palin River where the river bed is comprised of medium sized boulders, and mixture of pebbles, cobbles, sand and large boulders. The water was cool, clear and moderate to fast flowing and riparian vegetation were grasses, shrubs and small to medium sized trees along the banks and larger trees towards uphill. Collected with other species belonging to the following genera Oreoglanis, Pseudecheneis, Schizothorax, Exostoma, Garra, Neolissocheilus and Channa (Ref. 128992).

species.name: Aborichthys pangensis
species.description: The type locality, Pange River, where the species was collected was characterized by the passage of the river between deep gorges flanked with thick vegetation; from relatively swift but clear and moderately deep (50-100 cm) water as the bottom of the river was clearly visible. The area has different types of substrate including gravels, cobbles and medium to large-sized boulders with thick layers of aquatic green algae and moss. The vegetation along the river bank is characteristic of tropical evergreen forest dominated by different types of bamboos and broad-leafed trees. Associated fish recorded from the collection site includes Schizothorax richardsonii, Creteuchiloglanis arunachalensis and Oreoglanis pangenensis (Ref. 128990).

species.name: Aborichthys tikaderi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Aborichthys verticauda
species.description: Éspèce de poissons. Occurs in a stream with numerous rocks and large boulders.  Collected in areas where  there are cobbles and sand (Ref. 95164).

species.name: About
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in nutrient-rich, well vegetated lowland rivers, backwaters, oxbows, ponds and lakes.  Feeds mainly on plankton, terrestrial insects and plant material.  Breeds on roots or submerged plants. Can adapt to unfavorable environmental condition (Ref. 59043).  Colorless or pale yellow eggs are found attached to vegetation in shallow water (Ref. 41678).  Consumed fresh (Ref. 30578).  Threatened due to the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Abramites eques
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abrau sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools.  Feeds on crustaceans (juveniles feed on copepods, rotifer eggs and plants).  Breeds from May to October.  The eggs are pelagic, developing rapidly before sinking to the bottom.  Matures at 1 year, at 3.5 to 4.5 cm SL.

species.name: Abrolhos jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Abstract slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Abu mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly inhabit freshwaters, but often enters estuaries.  Form small schools.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abudefduf conformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplanktons, algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Abusseau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small pelagic fishes in coastal areas and estuaries.  Schooling, seasonal migrations in the Atlantic.  Feeds on carnivorous small crustaceans and fish larvae (Ref. 5980).  Reproduces in spring and summer (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Abyssal assfish
species.description: Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154) to bathyal and abyssal depths (Ref. 56809).    Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Specimens collected were 18 females, 5 of which (23.2-50.0 cm SL) are more or less ripe with eggs measuring up to 0.5 mm in diameter (Ref. 84269).

species.name: Abyssal cutthroat eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. On the continental slope (Ref. 57991).

species.name: Abyssal pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves and ledges in 107 m depth at the baseof a steep outer reef slope (Ref. 100512).

species.name: Abyssal rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Abyssal skate
species.description: Known only from three specimens, caught from abyssal depths 2320 - 2800 m (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Abyssal smooth-head
species.description: Abyssal, mostly found below 3,650 m; locally frequent, somewhat gregarious.  Feeds on engybenthic crustaceans, worms and sponges.

species.name: Abyssal snailfish
species.description: The holotype, a male, was found to carry developing eggs in its mouth (Ref. 6885).  Two females were ripe with large yolked eggs 6-7 mm in diameter, while the male of 33.0 cm SL had enlarged testes. Two smallest and immature females examined (18.0-18.5 cm SL) had small ovaries with many small white eggs ca. 1 mm in diameter (Ref. 91047).

species.name: Abyssal spiderfish
species.description: Solitary.  Occurs in waters with a temperature range of 4.5-0.4°C (Ref. 3590).  Uses its specialized fin rays (tripod) to elevate body into water column.  Specialized sensory pectoral fins are spread facing anteriorly, probably to detect prey.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans.  Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 6688).

species.name: Abyssoberyx levisquamosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is caught by bottom trawls (epibenthic sledge and semi-balloon otter trawl). The type series were collected at a single station where the terrain at these abyssal depths (4490-4640 m) is characterized by a complex topography of undulations, some hundreds of meters in height and where substratum is firm with very low megafaunal biomass. Lack of a rich benthic invertebrate fauna contrasts with the abundance and diversity of the fish fauna sampled. Also, this species occurred among 22 other species of Synaphobranchidae (1 species), Alepocephalidae (2), Ipnopidae (4), Bathysauridae (1), Ophidiidae (8), Aphyonidae (3) and Macrouridae (3). In overall abundance, it ranked fourth, equal to the ophidioid, Porogadus sp. (10 specimens), but less abundant than the ipnopids, Bathypterois longipes Günther, 1878 (24) and Bathymicrops regis Hjort & Koefoed, 1912 (28) and the ophidioid, Bathyonus laticeps (Günther, 1878) (51). Specimens (3) were examined internally, all females (15.2, 15.5, 16.8 cm SL), with ovaries in varying stages of yolk formation. Some 3-4 generations of oocytes were present in the ovaries. The ovaries of the 15.5 cm SL specimen were the most mature, with the most advanced generation (estimated at some thousands of ova) being c. 1 mm in diameter and containing a large oil globule. Also, intestinal contents of this specimen were chitinous remains, while that of the holotype bore a heavy infestation of cestode worms only (Ref. 75592).

Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms in bays (Ref. 43239). The life span of this species is one year:  fast growing before its reproductive period, with adults measuring within 30-40 cm and 100-400 g, it gets thinner towards the end of its life.  It feeds on shrimps, fish and crabs.  Female individuals carries about 60,000 eggs (ellipsoidal in shape, 1.97-1.42 mm average diameter) with some lobes of transparent membrane projecting from its end (Ref. 81825).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from reef slopes (Ref. 123364).

species.name: Acanthopoma annectens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attacks like a leech and produces wounds all over the fish which it attacks.  It spreads a bundle of opercular and inter-opercular spines into the wound and remains there, being very difficult to remove.  Invades the 'private parts' of wading or swimming animals but apparently exist in these passages only for a short while, as they quickly die from a lack of oxygen (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Acanthopsoides delphax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers with slow current and muddy to sandy substrate (Ref. 27732).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Acanthopsoides gracilentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in upper parts of river basins, with slow to fast waters, on gravel and pebbles (Ref. 27732).  Occurs over sandy bottoms in medium to large rivers.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Not fished commercially (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Acanthopsoides gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs sympatrically with Acantopsis. Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975). Feeds on the bottom on insects and algae (Ref. 12975).

species.name: Acanthopsoides hapalias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lower parts of river basins, with muddy to sandy bottom (Ref. 27732).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, particularly chironomid larvae, and some algae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Acanthopsoides molobrion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, lakes or swamps.  Feed on small animals in the bottom sediments.

species.name: Acanthopsoides namromensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acanthopsoides robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sand in forest and upland streams with moderate to fast current (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Acanthostracion guineense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the shelf (Ref. 11227).

species.name: Acanthure à pierreries
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles in shallow water (Ref. 9710).  Extremely territorial and solitary (Ref. 5503).

species.name: Acanthure à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in groups in coral-rich areas (Ref. 9710) or on rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573).  It small and numerous pharyngeal teeth suggest a diet that consists mainly of filamentous algae (Ref. 33204). Occasionally caught by traps and trawls (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Acanthurus reversus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 41630). Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Acantopsis dialuzona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers where they feed on small animals in the bottom sediments.  Occurs in swift, clear streams with sandy or gravelly bottom; also found in large rivers (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Acantopsis thiemmedhi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams and the upper reaches of rivers with sandy bottoms where clear running water is present (Ref. 48303).

species.name: Acapoeta tanganicae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It can be found in inshore rocky areas of Lake Tanganyika, and rapid sections of rivers; one of the most common species in the rivers (Ref. 4967). It feeds on aufwuchs (Ref. 28666).

species.name: Acara dauphin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Like all species of the genus, it is abundant in small, slow-flowing, shallow creeks with rocky-silty bottom. Occurs together with Guianacar owroewefi, Pyrrhulina filamentosa, Cyphocharax spilurus, Hemigrammus guyanensis and Heptapterus longior. Feeds on small crustaceans and insect larvae. Males are a little bigger and more colorful than females; they have elongated anal, dorsal and ventral fins, the latter exceeding the origin of the anal fins. The parents clean the flat stone where about 500 eggs will be spawned. Parents show a marked territorial behavior during this the spawning period (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Acara de l'Oelemari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).  Likely to occur in similar biotopes where other species of this genus are found (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Acara maroni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small creeks in the coastal zone, which have clear water and little current (Ref. 7020) and is rich in decaying wood (Ref. 35237).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  When faced with danger, this fearful species fix itself against a log adapting its color pattern to the substrate.  Parents take care of the spawned eggs, numbering about 400, which are laid down on a flat stone (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Acara vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the most colorful species of the genus, especially during its reproductive period.  Frequently occurs in zones with little current and over a substrate covered with vegetal debris (Ref. 27188).  Caught frequently but not abundantly in most varied biotopes- in small creeks and flooded zones with clear, shallow and slow flowing water.  Feeds primarily on insects, secondarily on fishes and plants.  Very territorial.  During reproduction, males attain a deeper coloration.  About 1,000 eggs are released during spawning.  Spawning takes place on stone or wood.  Parents take care of juveniles (Ref. 35237).  Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Acara à selle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers calm waters of inland creeks where it can be very abundant (Ref. 27188). May occur in back currents of cascades along with Ctenoloricaria fowleri, Leporinus despaxi, Hemiodopsis quadrimaculatus and Parodon guyanensis. Lingers over stony substrates along shallow banks (Ref. 35237). Spawns in a secret or hidden area. The males have harems. The male often joins in protecting the young if they are close to his cave or lair but it is mainly the females who care for the eggs and young (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Acara à selle (Guianacara owroewefi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251). Abundant, occurs in the zones of cascades along with Krobia itanyi, Corydoras guianensis, Characidium fasciadorsale and Cyphocharax spilurus, in quiet, shallow and sunny waters. Sympatric with G. oelemariensis in the Oelemari River, Suriname (Ref. 26372). Feeds on small invertebrates. Breeding may occur 3 to 4 times per year. Spawning takes place in anfractuosities of rocks so that guarding is easier for females which are generally smaller than males. Males defend the nest. Parental care in terms of food supply and protection lasts for 1 to 3 months (Ref. 35237).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, creeks, lakes and ponds in plains.  Also occurs in mouths of rivers draining into lagoons, in rocky shores of rivers and irrigation creeks, and in floodplain pools.  Deposits its eggs into host mussels (Ref. 78070).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acheloos roach
species.description: Adapted to still water (Ref. 96829).  Found in lakes. Larvae and juveniles live away from shore. Juveniles feed on invertebrates and plant material while individuals larger than 12 cm SL prey mainly on snails and mussels.  Spawns in shallow and sandy areas with vegetation.  Eggs are very adhesive, 1.0-1.4 mm in diameter (Ref. 59043).  The presence of spawners in February suggests that spawning season may commence at the end of January and extend possibly until March-April (Ref. 96829).

species.name: Acheron spring goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland water bodies (Ref. 26100); in clear, nearly stagnant, temperate, sometimes slightly brackish waters with abundant submerged vegetation and sand or mud bottom.  It lives up to 2 years. Spawns in February-March; juveniles free swimming while adults are benthic. Feeds on chironomid larvae and small crustaceans. Threatened for habitat are largely drained and filled with garbage (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Achigan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lakes, ponds, swamps, and backwaters and pools of creeks, and small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Usually found over mud or sand and common in impoundments (Ref. 5723).  They prefer quiet, clear water and over-grown banks.  Adults feed on fishes, crayfish and frogs; young feed on crustaceans, insects and small fishes.  Sometimes cannibalistic.  They don't feed during spawning; as well as when the water temperature is below 5°C and above 37°C (Ref. 30578).  Builds nest  at 25 mm-203 mm deep (Ref. 1998). An introduced species in Europe reported to avoid fast-flowing waters and to occur in estuaries with a salinity up to 13 ppt (Ref. 59043).  Popular game fish in North America.  Preyed upon by herons, bitterns, and kingfishers (Ref. 1998).  Excellent food fish (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Achigan à petite bouche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated lakes and ponds, as well as quiet pools of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on small fishes and other vertebrates (Ref. 1998), as well as fish eggs (Ref. 2058).  Adtults rarely form schools but occur in pairs or loose aggregations of three to four individuals; young individuals aggregate in fairly large schools (Ref. 120693). An introduced species in Europe which avoids swift waters and occurs in estuaries with a salinity up to 18.2 ppt  (Ref. 59043).  Reported in Europe to prey on a wide variety of invertebrates (Ref. 59043).  Considered undesirable catch (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Achigan à petite bouche (Micropterus dolomieu)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky areas of lakes and clear and gravel-bottom runs and flowing pools of  rivers (Ref. 86798).  Young feed on plankton and immature aquatic insects while adults take in crayfish, fishes, and aquatic and terrestrial insects (Refs. 1998, 10294, 44091). Is sometimes cannibalistic (Ref. 30578).  Preyed upon by fishes and turtles (Ref. 1998).  Builds nest, usually at three or four feet deep (Ref. 120821).  Excellent food fish (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Achiroides leucorhynchos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the bottom in flowing water and reportedly also in the brackish water of the lower courses of rivers.  Feeds primarily on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh, often in mixed catches (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Achiroides melanorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the bottom in flowing water and reportedly also in brackish water of the lower courses of rivers.  Feeds primarily on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Achirus novoae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Achirus zebrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Achondrostoma arcasii
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. A short-lived species which lives in lakes and mountain streams, including the middle reaches of rivers (Ref. 11240).  Also found in reservoirs in hilly areas.  Juveniles occur in shallow areas with slow current  and move to deeper and faster waters in late July.  Opportunistic feeder, but preying mainly on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Achondrostoma asturicense
species.description:
This species lives in rivers and lakes placed in the western of the Cantabrian mountains in 
oligotrophic waters shady with vegetation. Breeding occurs during summer and spring (Ref. 128766).

species.name: Achondrostoma garzonorum
species.description: This species is a typical inhabitant of rivers with clear water and from moderate to high water flow, in areas with granitic rocks in the riverbed (Ref. 128766).

species.name: Achondrostoma numantinum
species.description: This species lives in rivers and streams placed in the central plateau from Spain with heights over 800 m.a.s.l., in oligotrophic waters shady with vegetation. Breeding is reported to occur from April to the end of August. Known to mainly feed on detritus, plants and invertebrates (Ref. 128766).

species.name: Achondrostoma occidentale
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in small coastal streams that have a greatly reduced water flow in the dry summer period (Ref. 55625).  During dry summer time, fish become concentrated in a few pools seeking shelter in shady areas under the cover of vegetation (Ref. 55625).  Occur in lower stretches of rivers.  Threatened due to pollution, intensive agriculture and water abstraction.  Size reaches up to at least 9.5 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Achondrostoma oligolepis
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occur in coastal rivers and terminal segments of main rivers.  Adults are found commonly in lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Achondrostoma salmantinum
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in seasonal streams with clear waters, sandy bottoms and prefers slow flowing reaches with abundant aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 75032).

species.name: Aci spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acinocheirodon melanogramma
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Acipinar killifish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Acnodon oligacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The diameter of the eyes suggests a crepuscular activity for this species.  The inferior position of the mouth facilitates easy access to benthic plants like Podostemaceae and other fruits, seeds and flowers that fall into the water.  The juveniles live in small creeks with sandy substrate.  Between 5-10 cm, they migrate to large rivers where they form shoals along the river banks and sandy beaches of shallow waters.  Thereafter, they appear to lead a more solitary existence in the central beds of rivers (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Acnodon senai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aconcagua grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on copepods, pagurid and brachyurid crabs, and shrimp-like crustaceans.

species.name: Acoupa aile-courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters over sandy mud or soft mud bottoms (Ref. 3702).  Feeds mainly on small shrimps (Ref. 3702).  Important food fish.

species.name: Acoupa argenté
species.description: Occurs usually over sandy bottoms in inshore waters along beaches and in river mouths.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes.

species.name: Acoupa blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often in schools over rocky bottom and in kelp beds (Ref. 2850).  Also found in the surf zone (Ref. 2850).  Young in bays and along sandy beaches (Ref. 2850).  Feed on fishes, squids, and crayfish (Ref. 6885).  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Excellent food fish (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa blanc (Cynoscion leiarchus)
species.description: Found over mud and sand bottoms in river estuaries. Occurs up to 50 m but usually less than 25 m (Ref. 9626).  Marketed fresh and salted.

species.name: Acoupa bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lower estuarine regions (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on fishes, shrimps and cephalopods (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa cachème
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters and estuaries with high salinities (Ref. 9118).  Feed on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa cambucu
species.description: Usually found over sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters near river mouths (Ref. 3702).  Adults stay in deep waters during the day and swim to the surface at night (Ref. 35237).  Juveniles inhabit estuaries.  Marketed fresh; its flesh is of excellent quality (Ref. 3702).  Its swim bladder is being used to make glue (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Acoupa chasseur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud or sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters to about 60 m depth.  Juveniles abundant in estuaries and tidal mud flats.  Feeds on shrimps and fishes (Ref. 9626).  Important food fish.

species.name: Acoupa de sable
species.description: Occurs usually over sandy bottoms in shallow coastal waters, being relatively abundant in the surf zone.  During summer months the fish move to their nursery and feeding grounds in river estuaries.

species.name: Acoupa de Stolzman
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters, lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 9118).  Also found offshore (Ref. 11035).  Feeds mainly on small fishes and shrimps (Ref. 9118). Lower depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Acoupa doré
species.description: Usually found over mud and sandy bottoms in river estuaries and in marine areas from the coastline to about 30 m depth.  Marketed mostly fresh.

species.name: Acoupa du golfe
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 9118).  Juveniles found near river mouths (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa du pérou
species.description: Common species found in coastal waters (Ref. 9118).  Juveniles enter estuaries and shallow bays (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on shrimps and fishes (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa magdalène
species.description: Inhabits shallow inshore sandy areas (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on small fishes (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa mongolare
species.description: Found over sand or mud bottoms from the coastline to about 60 m depth (Ref. 3702); rarely in waters with a depth of less than 18 m (Ref. 9626).  Juveniles inhabit river estuaries (Ref. 3702).  Oviparous, with high fecundity (Ref. 54358).  Feed on fishes and crustaceans like crabs and shrimps (Ref. 35237).  Important food fish (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Acoupa nain
species.description: Occurs offshore (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa pintade
species.description: Inhabits river estuaries and shallow coastal marine waters over sand bottoms, often associated with seagrass beds.  Also occurs in salt marshes and tidal pools of high salinity.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes.  An important food and sport fish throughout its range.  Utilized fresh for steaming, broiling and baking (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Acoupa rayé
species.description: Maximum length assumed to be 1.5 * 40 = 60 cm TL (RF).

species.name: Acoupa rayée
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters and estuaries with high salinities (Ref. 9118).  Feed on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa reine
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters; juveniles entering estuaries, river mouths, and shallow bays (Ref. 9118).  Feed on shrimps, fishes and cephalopods (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa rivière
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies very diverse biotopes and carries out its biological cycle in freshwater as well as in brackish water (Ref. 27188). Juveniles feed on larvae of crustaceans (especially Macrobrachium), aquatic insects and copepods. Adults prey on fish. Captured during the rainy season (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Acoupa royal
species.description: Occurs usually in shallow coastal waters over sand and sandy mud bottoms.  Juveniles are euryhaline.  During summer the fish move to their nursery and feeding grounds in river estuaries.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes.  Oviparous, with high fecundity (Ref. 54406). The species leave estuaries during the fall when water temperatures decrease, but are also known to overwinter in these areas. It has been reported that the fish cease feeding and die when the water temperature reaches 7.9 deg C and 3.3 deg. C, respectively (Ref. 122657).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, pan-fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Acoupa tident
species.description: Mostly in brackish water swamps along the coasts; also entering freshwaters (Ref. 3702).  Feeds on fish, shrimps and sometimes plants (Ref. 35237).  Spawning takes place in the open sea.  Important food fish (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Acoupa toeroe
species.description: Forms schools (Ref. 35237).  Found over mud or sandy mud bottoms near mouths of rivers.  Juveniles are restricted to brackish and fresh waters.  Feeds on shrimps and fishes.  Important food fish (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Acoupa tonquiche
species.description: Found over mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 3702).  Marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Acoupa totoaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters; juveniles in river mouths and near rocky coasts (Ref. 9118).  Feed on fishes and shrimps (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa à grande gueule
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa à gueule jaune
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acoupa écailleuse
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters, along shores and in estuaries (Ref. 9118).  Feed on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Acourcie
species.description: Gregarious fish which swims near the surface (Ref. 30578).  Inhabits moderate to fast-flowing large streams to large rivers with rock or gravel bottom.  Adults aggregate in dense swarms in winter in the lower reaches of rivers or backwaters and often migrate to spawning streams in autumn and overwinter there.  Juveniles spend winter in cavities along the shores.  Early juveniles occur in very shallow shoreline habitats and when they grow, they leave the shores for faster-flowing waters.  Feeding larvae thrive along shores.  Prey on small invertebrates.  Spawns in fast-flowing water on shallow gravel beds, often in small tributaries (Ref. 59043).   Breeds in March and April (Ref. 30578).  Pale yellow eggs are found attached to gravel and stones in shallow, flowing water (Ref. 41678).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrochordonichthys falcifer

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, swiftly flowing forested streams with pH of 7 and sandy or rocky bottoms. Hides under submerged logs or rocks with some leaf litter in the swifter parts of the stream. A predatory fish, ambushing balitorid loaches of Nemacheilus and sisorid catfish of the genus Glyptothorax (Ref. 37794).

species.name: Acrochordonichthys strigosus

species.name: Acropoma argentistigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by trawl and landed in fish markets; apparently found on continental shelf and in nearby waters (Ref. 96184).

species.name: Acropoma hanedai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fairly deep water.  Caught by trawl net.  Food fish.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus beijiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food and ornamental fish keeping (Ref. 33326).

species.name: Acrossocheilus clivosius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Length type refers to body length.

species.name: Acrossocheilus macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus multistriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid streams with clean, highly oxygenated water, and a boulder/pebble/gravel substrate. Coexists with other fishes which include <i>Acrossocheilus parallens, <i>Opsariichthys bidens, and <i>Zacco platypus (Ref. 96674).

species.name: Acrossocheilus paradoxus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food and ornamental fish keeping (Ref. 5193).

species.name: Acrossocheilus parallens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food and ornamental fish keeping (Ref. 33326).

species.name: Acrossocheilus rendahli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food and ornamental fish keeping (Ref. 33326).

species.name: Acrossocheilus spinifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the bottom and in midwater of the  upper reaches of rivers and hill streams with fast-running and clear water and gravel substrate (Ref. 57453).  Preferably forms schools and feeds mainly on aquatic insects, benthic invertebrates and algae adhering to the surface of the gravel and plant detritus (Ref. 57453).  Reaches sexual maturity at approximately 10 cm SL and is a fractional spawner (Ref. 57453).  Used as a food fish but eggs are poisonous which can lead to diarrhea, nausea, vomiting and dizziness (Ref. 57453).

species.name: Acrossocheilus wenchowensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food and ornamental fish keeping (Ref. 33326).

species.name: Acrossocheilus wuyiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus xamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus yalyensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Acrossocheilus yunnanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes.

species.name: Acroteriobatus ocellatus
species.description: Rare species found offshore (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Probably caught by trawlers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Acute halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Herbivorous.

species.name: Acutenose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 41299).  Depth range from 80 m-150 m (Ref. 41299). Feeds on invertebrates and bony fish (Ref. 9908, Ref. 114953). Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 8.5-10.0 cm long and 5.5-6.4 cm wide (Ref. 41249 , 41253).

species.name: Acyrtus pauciradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters on hard-bottom habitats that consist of areas rich in calcareous and brown algae, corals and sponges (Ref. 54768).

species.name: Adamson's goby
species.description: Gut content of a 6-cm specimen had two isopods and one hermit crab (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Adamson's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Extremely common in lake shores; juveniles occur in the shallows close to shore, whereas adults form large schools over deep water adjacent to rocky cliffs.  Main food of the Foi people who live along the shores of Lake Kutubu (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Adana bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Adana chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift and warm flowing water, with bottom comprising of cobbles and pebbles. Lives in association with Capoeta turani, Oxynoemacheilus seyhanensis and Alburnus sp.

species.name: Adelaide's weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Estuarine (Ref. 75154). Found in seagrass beds, weedy reefs, often in silty areas to about 15 m.

species.name: Adelosebastes latens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Adelotremus leptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species' slender body is well-suited for using as shelter abandoned calcareous polychaete tube, especially if protective cover is scarce. The type locality is mostly sand, broken shells and rubble with occasional seagrass beds (Ref. 89959). This species was also found to occupy empty shells of scaphopod mollusc Dentalium (Ref. 117352).

species.name: Aden blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Aden sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in moderately steep reef that shelves southward, with high live coral cover of massive Porites, abundant foliose Montipora., and encrusting Echinopora (Ref. 106074).,

species.name: Aden torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Poorly known. Maturity size of males reported at 39 cm TL, still adolescent at 28 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Adolf's catfish
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Adonis shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow seagrass beds (Ref. 78636). Also seen in fine silt bottoms of coastal reefs, usually in turbid conditions in 2-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Adontosternarchus balaenops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Adontosternarchus clarkae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males considerably taller than females (Ref. 89705).

species.name: Adontosternarchus devenanzii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Adontosternarchus duartei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from white water in main river and close to beaches along the river margin (Ref. 91753).

species.name: Adontosternarchus nebulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to feed on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 78211).

species.name: Adontosternarchus sachsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Adorned dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live for 59 days at the most, with larvae spending three weeks in the open ocean and maturing within two weeks of settling on a reef, leaving the adults (which are 1 to 2 centimeters long) just three weeks to reproduce.  This strategy of 'live fast, die young' is perceived to be a response to intense predation.  Daily mortality rate,  from tag-recapture data, might be as high as 8% (Ref. 54199). Occur at depths less than 4 to between 17 and 21 m on sandy bottoms of lagoon reefs (Ref. 1602, 37816, 48637).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018. Spawning appears to be repeated on a regular cycle, semilunar or every 14 days (Ref. 116739).

species.name: Adrianichthys roseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is likely  to be pelagic (Ref. 54508).

species.name: Adriatic blunt-snouted clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aegean chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aelita icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Aeneus
species.description: Found mostly in quiet, shallow waters with soft bottoms (Ref. 26041), but also inhabits running waters (Ref. 11225).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Stays in schools of 20 to 30 individuals.  Because of its ability to breathe air intestinally, it takes air 1 to 45 times per hour (Ref. 35381).  Nocturnal (Ref. 35381).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Spawning occurs when the physical-chemical quality of the water changes with the onset of the rainy season (Ref. 35381).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Aequidens chimantanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The largest specimen collected was less than 15 cm long (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Aequidens diadema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In the Jenaro Herrera region, Peru, this species occurs in streams in aguajal-like conditions, clear water quebradas and black-water quebradites (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Aequidens epae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear-water streams with muddy, sandy or rocky bottoms (Ref. 26647).

species.name: Aequidens gerciliae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A clear-water species (Ref. 26647).

species.name: Aequidens mauesanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in black-water rivers (Ref. 26676).

species.name: Aequidens michaeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs and larvae are defended by both parents (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Aequidens paloemeuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to be rare and limited to its type locality because it has never been caught again since it was described (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Aequidens patricki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit streams.  Is rare in the aquarium trade but has been imported on occasion (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Aequidens plagiozonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aequidens potaroensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In fast-flowing 'blackwater' streams (Ref. 40602).  Both parents defend eggs and larvae (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Aequidens rondoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aequidens sapayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males defend the territory during breeding (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Aequidens superomaculatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aequidens tubicen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers small, fast running creeks and rapids.  Feeds on fish, insects and plant detritus.

species.name: Aequidens viridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In flood plains; used as food (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Aetheliparis taurocanis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aetomylaeus milvus
species.description: Found inshore (Ref. 9862).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Presumably utilized for human consumption in the western central Pacific (Ref. 9862).

species.name: Afele's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on algal mats of shallow exposed reefs.

species.name: Aflema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the marine environment, pelagic, along beaches and just off shore, down to about 25 m, also in lagoons and estuaries, penetrating into almost freshwater (Ref. 187, 188, 54448). A marine migrant (Ref. 117399). Rarely found below 35 m depth (Ref. 86940). It feeds on small planktonic animals, e.g. small fish and crustaceans; it doesn't seem to feed on plankton (Ref. 188, 3166, 47405).

species.name: Africa rivergoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits from fresh water to marine conditions in lowland rivers and bays (Ref. 34009).

species.name: African banded barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers well-oxygenated but vegetated waters such as floodplain river channels and permanent lagoons (Ref. 52193); shy, emerging in subdued light, most active in early morning and late afternoon (Ref. 7248, 52193). It feeds on  small organisms, often off plant surfaces (Ref. 52193), including worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020). Migrates during rainy season (Ref. 13337).

species.name: African basslet
species.description: Inhabits recesses of seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: African blackmouth croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African brown skate
species.description: Unknown depth range but probably inshore for at least some collected specimens were caught by gill-net (Ref. 110364).

species.name: African bullhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Concealed mostly among rocks during daytime.  Nocturnal habits prevail (Ref. 45232).  Feed on chironomid larvae, beetle larvae and small crustaceans with occasional ingestion of vegetable material (Ref. 6868).  Of no food value (Ref. 4967).  Mucus is poisonous to other fishes (Ref. 4537).

species.name: African butter catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lacustrine as well as fluviatile species, confined to lakes and moderate to large rivers (Ref. 43912).  Shoals in standing or slowly flowing open water with emergent or submerged vegetation.  Generally more active at night or in subdued light.  Feed from mid-water and surface waters on a wide variety of foods including fish, insects, shrimps, snails, plant seeds, and fruit.   Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).  Often important spawning migrations occur (Ref. 43912).  Breed during the rainy season and may be either a single or multiple spawner in different localities, laying eggs on vegetation.  May live up to 6-7 years (Ref. 7248).  Max total length 45.0mm (Ref. 43912).  Also caught with drawnets.  In general considered as a flavoured, first class eating fish (Ref. 43912).

species.name: African carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: African chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on ophiuroids (Ref. 27637).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: African coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African coris
species.description: A solitary species (Ref. 90102) found in areas of mixed coral, sand and rubble of exposed outer reef flats, lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602, 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on mollusks, crabs, and hermit crabs, and occasionally on tunicates and forams (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: African Creole wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African deep-water flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore areas on soft bottoms around rock outcrops, wharf pilings, weed beds, and others (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: African dwarf sawshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is a poorly known inhabitant of the upper continental slope in tropical waters found at depths of 286-500 m (Ref. 87357). Stomach contents include an unidentified organic material, partially digested shrimplike crustaceans, and small decapod shrimps; no fish or cephalopod remains were found (Ref. 87357). Larger individuals had small puncture marks and elongated parallel cuts on their backs and tails suggestive of combat injuries from the rostra of other sawsharks (Ref. 87357). Unknown litter size; it may be caught and discarded as bycatch by offshore shrimp trawlers and other deepwater fisheries operations off Mozambique (Ref. 87357).

species.name: African eel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow reefs, in areas with rock and rubble (Ref. 9710).

species.name: African frilled shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Riverine species with gregarious habits, confined to large as well as moderate and small water systems (Ref. 43912). Forms schools (Ref. 6868). Carnivorous with insectivorous preference; reproduction probably coincides mainly with flood periods (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Maximum total length recorded 148 mm (Ref. 43912, 81643).

species.name: African jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rainforest areas (Ref. 6801).  Maximum reported TL was 8.0 cm (Ref. 6801).

species.name: African longfin fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African pencil wrasse
species.description: Depth range (5-20 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: African perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African pike-characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on large insects and fish (Ref. 7020).

species.name: African pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper slope (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Probably taken by hake trawlers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: African redfinned barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in small rivers in forest zones (Ref. 2940). Maximum reported size: 12.5 cm SL (Ref. 81282, 81639).

species.name: African righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9792).

species.name: African sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Littoral species that inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 10797).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: African silver sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum SL reported is 17.2 cm (Ref. 57290).

species.name: African spotted scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably found over rocky bottoms (Ref. 4510).

species.name: African sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: African torpedo wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length and depth range (1-30 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: African whiptailed catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Phractura species are often associated with the vegetation of flowing waters (Ref. 57128).

species.name: Afronemacheilus abyssinicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the bottom of Lake Tana and in patches of macrophytes along the shore of the lake, and along the banks of the Blue Nile (Ref. 94278).

species.name: Afronemacheilus kaffa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sampled from riffles (Ref. 94278).

species.name: Agassiz' smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 96339). Rare and poorly known.

species.name: Agassiz's corydoras
species.description: Omnivorous.

species.name: Agassiz's dwarf cichlid
species.description: Poisson. Adults inhabit clear, black and white water.  Aquarium keeping:  several females for one male;  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).  Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Agassiz's glassfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit streams, ponds, swamps (Ref. 5259, 44894), rivers, creeks, reservoirs and drainage ditches (Ref. 44894); occurring in areas with plenty of weed cover at temperatures from 18°-27°C. Feed on small crustaceans. Spawn early in the morning: males display fins while chasing the female, swimming in a zigzag pattern. Demersal eggs are deposited and fertilized on vegetation with larvae hatching after 24 hours (Ref. 7311). Similar in appearance to A. agrammus and A. mulleri.

species.name: Agassiz's parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral, algal and rocky reefs and seagrass beds (Ref. 40827).  Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.

species.name: Ageneiogarra micropulvinus
species.description: Prefers streams with rapid current and stony substrate (Ref. 55924).  Feeds mainly on algae, occasionally on aquatic plants and larvae of aquatic insects (Ref. 55924).

species.name: Ageneiogarra nujiangensis
species.description: Found in shallow areas of river along the bank of the main course and tributaries (Ref. 81998). The river has slightly turbid black water and substrate consisted of large boulders, cobbles, gravel and sand (Ref. 81998).

species.name: Ageneiogarra theunensis
species.description: Inhabits fast flowing water (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Ageneiosus lineatus
species.description: This species is popular in aquarium trade (Ref. 124585).

species.name: Ageneiosus magoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ageneiosus militaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ageneiosus pardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ageneiosus polystictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ageneiosus ucayalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the quiet zones of swamps or the lower parts of stream.  Carnivorous.  Swims close to the bottom, feeding mainly on fish (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Ageneiosus uranophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ageneiosus vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agile chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in clear lagoon and seaward reefs, usually in loose aggregations near caves and ledges.  Abundant over branching corals and leeward coasts (Ref. 9710). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Agile klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and estuaries.

species.name: Agone atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at temperatures of 4.4 to -1.7 °C (Ref. 4700).  Benthic, possibly bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on pelagic and benthic crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 4700).

species.name: Agoniates anchovia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agoniates halecinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agonomalus jordani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agonomalus proboscidalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agonopsis asperoculis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Agrakhan shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Confined to semi-saline waters; non-anadromous, not entering fresh water.  Spawns in the eastern part at the north end of Caspian Sea, from mid-May to end of June, mostly when temperatures are 18-20°C, salinities 8-10 ppt and at depths of around 3 m.  The young move southward late in autumn, later than any other clupeids.

species.name: Aguarunichthys inpai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at depth of about 30 m using bottom trotline (Ref. 36506).

species.name: Aguarunichthys tocantinsensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in areas with strong currents, rocky bottom (Ref. 36506).

species.name: Aguarunichthys torosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aguglia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives close to the surface and has a migratory pattern similar to the mackerel (Ref. 35388). Feeds on small fishes, particularly clupeids and Engraulis (in the Black Sea). Leaps out of the water when hooked. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205). Utilized fresh and frozen; can be fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 130219.

species.name: Aguglia impériale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is the most common istiophorid in the central basin of the Mediterranean and completes its life cycle inside this sea as far as is known to date. Probably swims in the upper 200 m water layer, generally above or within the thermocline. Travels in pairs, possibly corresponding to a feeding behavior. Feeds on fishes. Probably more widespread in the Mediterranean Sea and may have been identified as T. albidus by anglers and fishermen.

species.name: Aguja skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Agulhas goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ahliesaurus berryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic to bathypelagic (Ref. 6602).  Sometimes taken at depths greater than 500 m (Ref. 6602).  Feeds on smaller plankton, mainly copepods.  Hermaphrodite, spawning probably occurs in the North Atlantic in a belt stretching across the ocean in subtropical latitudes.  Specimens approaching sexual maturity lose their teeth and gillrakers completely (Ref. 6689) suggesting semelparity (RF).

species.name: Ahliesaurus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic ; larvae at 0-600 m, adults at ca. 200-2000 m (Ref. 58302).  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 35934).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35934).

species.name: Ahlstrom's waryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic species (Ref. 6602).  Feeding adults are found on the continental slope in 400-500 m (Ref. 6602).

species.name: Aiakas kreffti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 5 specimens taken on the southern Argentine slopes (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Aiakas zinorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aifuf rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aigle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found inshore and shelf waters, close to bottom as well as in surface and mid-waters, pursuing shoals of clupeids and mugilids.  They congregate inshore to spawn during spring and summer.  Juveniles and sub-adults enter estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 3593).  Both adults and juveniles are migratory moving along shore or offshore-onshore in response to temperature change (Ref. 11025).  Feed on fishes and swimming crustaceans.

species.name: Aigle commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow lagoons (Ref. 3965), bays and estuaries; also offshore down to at least 95 m (Ref. 5578).  Often found in groups (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on benthic crustaceans, mollusks and fish.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Gestation period of 6-8 months, the females give birth to 3-7 young (Ref. 35388).  Caught by shore and ski-boat anglers, usually released after capture (Ref. 5578).  Flesh is highly esteemed (Ref. 3965).

species.name: Aigle de mer
species.description: Espèce de raie. Found in tropical to warm temperate coastal waters, but absent from islands of western Pacific.  Often forming large groups swimming near the surface and quite destructive of commercial oyster and clam beds.  Feeds on bottom-living mollusks, crustaceans and fishes.  Seldom marketed.  Ovoviviparous, gestation period up to one year with 2-6 embryos produced.

species.name: Aigle de mer commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays, estuaries, and near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951).  Usually solitary (Ref. 12951).  Feeds on clams, oysters, worms, and crabs (Ref. 12951).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Although the spine on the tail is capable of inflicting a painful wound, the poison is quickly neutralized by immersion of the injured area in hot water (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Aigle de mer du sud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  In coastal waters down to 130 m.

species.name: Aigle de mer espadon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little known coastal species, caught mainly over sandy bottoms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Aigle de mer léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in coastal habitats to at least 60 m depth (Ref. 114953). Swims close to the surface, occasionally leaping out of the water, or close to the bottom (Ref. 3175).  Frequently forming large schools during the non-breeding season (Ref. 7251).  Feeds on polychaetes, bivalves, gastropods, cepahlopods, shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Bears young in litters of 2-4 (Ref. 26938, 114953).

species.name: Aigle de mer rugueux
species.description: Benthic on soft bottoms in coastal waters.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Aigle de mer taureau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found frequently in coastal waters to 10 m depth, mainly in shallow estuaries.  Capable of traveling long distances, occasionally leaps out of the water.  Swims in midwater.  Cruises slowly over the bottom, rooting out bivalves with its beak and wings when feeding (Ref. 7251).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Aigle de mer técolette
species.description: Commonly found in sandy and muddy bays and sloughs, also on rocky bottom and in kelp beds (Ref. 2850).  Sometimes buries itself in sand (Ref. 2850).  Found singly or in schools (Ref. 12951).  Feeds on bivalves, snails, polychaetes, shrimps, and crabs (Ref. 9257).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Venomous spine on tail.  Not fished commercially, but shows up as by-catch species (Ref. 9257).

species.name: Aigle vachette
species.description: Espèce de raies. Found in coastal tropical and warm temperate waters, occasionally offshore.  Sometimes found in small groups (Ref. 5578).  Feed on bottom-living crustaceans and mollusks.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449), aplacental (Ref. 57025).  Prized angling fish, often released (Ref. 5578).  Flesh highly esteemed (Ref. 3965).

species.name: Aiglefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found more commonly from 80 to 200 m, over rock, sand, gravel or shells, usually at temperatures between 4° and 10°C.  Feed mainly on small bottom-living organisms including crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms, worms and fishes (sand lance, capelin, silver hake, American eels, herring and argentines) (Ref. 5951).  A batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Undertakes extensive migrations in the Barents Sea and Iceland.  Sold fresh, chilled as fillets, frozen, smoked and canned.  Also utilized for fish meal and animal feeds.  Can be steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Aiguillat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly the most abundant living shark (Ref. 247). A demersal, inshore and offshore dogfish of the continental and insular shelf and upper slopes (Ref. 247, 11230, 119696). Usually near the bottom, but also in midwater and at the surface (Ref. 26346); occurs mainly between 10-200 m depth (Ref. 247). Males and gravid females usually found shallower than non-gravid females. Tolerates brackish water, often found in enclosed bays and estuaries. Reported to enter freshwater (Ref. 11980) but cannot survive there for more than a few hours (Ref. 247). Highly migratory species, used to be observed in large foraging schools with up to thousands of individuals, usually segregated by size and /or sex, with schools of large gravid females preferentially targeted by fisheries. Their latitudinal (north-south) and depth-related (nearshore-offshore) movements appear to be correlated with their preferred temperature (Ref. 247). Tagging experiments showed that populations in the northern North Sea and northwest Scotland made winter migrations to off Norway and summer migrations to Scotland (Ref. 88880, 88881). Transoceanic migrations recorded, but rare (Ref. 88864). Longevity in the northern Atlantic is about 35-50 years (Ref. 88882), but most live only 20-24 years (Ref. 88187). Growth is slow. At sexual maturity, males are 60-70 cm long, females 75-90 cm (Ref. 35388). Gestation period is 2 years (Ref. 36731). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). Feeds on a diversity of prey, ranging from comb jellyfish, squid, mackarel and herring to a wide array of benthic fishes, shrimps, crabs and even sea cucumbers (Ref. 93252). The only species of horned sharks that can inflict toxins with its tail. Detects weak electric fields generated by potential prey (Ref. 10311). Utilized for human consumption, liver oil, vitamins, sand paper, leather, fertilizer, etc. (Ref. 247, 27436). Eaten fried, broiled, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Aiguillat coq
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves and upper slopes. Depth range from 16-440 m (Ref. 0247), and from 300-780m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Forms schools.  Off West Africa, water temperature and salinity where this species is often found ranges from 11-18°C and 36 ppt. (at 16 to 255 m depth), respectively.  Feeds on bony fishes, like denticids, mackerel and percichthyids, as well as crabs, lobsters, and octopi.  Ovoviviparous, with 3 to 4 young per litter.  Utilized fresh, dried salted and smoked for human consumption.

species.name: Aiguillat cubain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves and uppermost slopes.  Found in 60 to 380 m deep (Ref. 26938).  Found on or near the bottom in large, dense schools.  Probably feeds on bottom fishes and invertebrates.  Ovoviviparous, with about 10 young per litter.  A huge parasite (isopod) lives in its buccal cavity.  Seldom used for food, but taken in commercial catches for its liver which yields oil and vitamins. Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 55584.

species.name: Aiguillat cyrano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the insular slopes (Ref. 247).  Probably ovoviviparous, with 3 young per litter (Ref. 247).

species.name: Aiguillat du Pacifique
species.description: A demersal species found in coastal and oceanic waters; mainly epibenthopelagic which may be solitary or in groups (Ref.. 119696).  It  appears to prefer water temperatures between 7 and 15°C, and often makes longitudinal and depth migrations to follow this temperature preference (Ref. 48844). Reported taken at water temperatures of 0-12.7°C, with maximum catches at over 8° C. Juveniles are reported pelagic within the upper 25 m, settling to the bottom with maturity, mostly at 50-200 meters.  Opportunistic feeders, with no specific targeted prey, but fishes are the main prey of larger individuals; also consumes squids, octopi, medusae, ctenophores, crustaceans (e.g., shrimps, euphausiids, and amphipods), and polychaetes (Ref. 119696).  Edible but not appreciated. Its liver once served as a source of oil for mine lamps in the Nanaimo area (Ref. 6885).  Due to the high mercury content in large individuals, it is recommended that only those less than 60 cm are eaten (Ref. 11007). Males mature at 70-80 cm TL (median age is 18.5 years) and females at 80-100 cm TL (median age 35.5 years) (Ref. 85328).  In the high seas, this fish is taken as bycatch with salmon gillnet surveys from north of 40° to south of the Aleutian chain, over the Aleutian Basin and Bering Sea to about 60°N, along the chain and all across the Gulf of Alaska offshore; by bottom and pelagic trawls and gillnets northward from South Korea the Hawaiian Is., and southern California (Ref. 119696).

species.name: Aiguillat gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common deepwater dogfish of the outer continental shelves and upper slopes, commonest below 200 m (Ref. 247); usually benthic and epibenthic at depths from 50-1440 m with most records from 200-600 m (Compagno, pers. comm. 07/07).  Solitary (Ref. 26340).  Adults feed mainly on bony fishes such as hake, epigonids, lanternfish, herring, smelts, cods, rattails, squid and crustaceans (Ref. 247, IUCN workshop 07/07).  Males mature at about 105-118 cm TL (Ref. 94782).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Number of litter recorded, one in Mediterranean females, and possibly 1 or 2 for the species.  This species is fished in Eastern Atlantic by bottom trawls, long lines, fixed bottom nets, hook and line and pelagic trawls; caught and discarded, or utilised from by-catch fisheries (IUCN discussion 07/07).   Marketed smoked and dried salted for human consumption; also processed into fishmeal and a source of liver oil for squalene (Ref. 247). Maximum depth from Ref. 125614.

species.name: Aiguillat lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 6871, 75154).  Little is known of its biology; presumably ovoviviparous (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Aiguillat noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outermost continental shelves and upper slopes, mostly below 275 m (Ref. 247).  Epibenthic-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  At high latitudes, may move up to the surface especially during the winter (Ref. 247).  Bottom water temp.  Are from 3.5 to 4.5°C, but sometimes down to 1°C.  Segregation by sex and size as well as by movement into shallower water and by increase in school size is sometimes seen.  Feeds on crustaceans, cephalopods, jellyfish and small fishes.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with at least 14 pups in a litter (Ref. 247).  Has luminescent organs in skin.  May reach 107 cm.

species.name: Aiguillat peigne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known deepwater dogfish found on the continental and insular slopes. Incidentally caught in sablefish (Anoplopoma) traps but not utilized. Feeds chiefly on other fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 28023). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Aiguillat râpe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poorly known deepwater shark caught at a depth of 448 m (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Maximum total length at least 28 cm (adult male holotype).

species.name: Aiguillat togari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental and insular shelves and uppermost slopes, presumably on or near sandy-mud bottom (Ref. 31367, 11230).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Aiguillat à grosse tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aiguillat à nageoires blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known distinctive deepwater dogfish, biology almost totally unknown.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Aiguillat à nez court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelves and upper slopes, on or near the bottom (Ref. 31367); sublittoral below 130 m (Ref. 11230).
