species.description: Found in shoals and rocky reefs (Ref. 124208).

species.name: Anitápolis livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in upland rivers.  Viviparous (Ref. 45800).

species.name: Ankara barbell
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ankara nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anna's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore reefs (Ref. 7300). Also found among rubble and in crevices, solitary or in loose groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Annamia normani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits high gradient streams and rivers.  Typically found in shallow fast water over bedrock and cobble substrates (Ref. 12693).  Occurs in rapid-running mountain streams of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feed on small benthic animals, primarily insect larvae.  Not fished commercially (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Annamia thuathienensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Annandale loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, swift streams with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236). Also collected from slow-flowing streams and oxbows (Ref. 83671).

species.name: Annandale's guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily benthic (Ref. 114953). Occurs mainly in the marine environment, but also enters the lower reaches of rivers.   Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature by 68 cm TL; born at ca. 20 cm TL. Females produces litters up to 6 pups (Ref. 114953). Minimum depth range from Ref. 121775.

species.name: Annandale's skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anna’s sixgill sawshark
species.description: Probably occurs in deeper waters during the day but enters shallow water during the night.  The specimens were caught directly adjacent to a dropoff along the southern tip of Unguja Island where the water depth descends rapidly from ca.20 m to >200 m (Ref. 122027).

species.name: Annie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reefs and pools exposed at low tide.  A protogynous hermaphrodite.  Difficult to catch because of its small size.

species.name: Annular sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Anodus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anodus orinocensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anoli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms.

species.name: Anoli aile longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anoli bigarré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on sand or sand-rubble areas of lagoon and seaward reefs to over 20 m depth (Ref. 1602, 9710, 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 89972). Frequently buries in sand leaving only eyes and nostrils exposed (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Generally solitary (Ref. 1602). Sometimes in pairs or small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Anoli bigarré (Synodus variegatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep lagoon and seaward reefs to depths over 40 m (Ref. 9710); sometimes found on sandy bottoms concealing itself in the sand.  Prefers to rest on hard surfaces and frequently occurs in pairs (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on small fishes by seizing these from passing schools, also shrimps (Ref. 89972).  Caught with various types of artisanal gear; sold fresh or dried salted in markets.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Anoli brasil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf (Ref. 4472).

species.name: Anoli californien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Perch motionless on pectoral fins in a wide range of habitats; commonly found on sandy bottoms or sand patches around rocky reefs and boulder and gravel strewn slopes.  Active during the day.  May bury in sand with only the eyes and mouth protruding (Ref. 5227).  Feed on fishes (Ref. 9348).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35938).  Extended larval period (Ref. 35938).  Catches are either discarded or made into fish meal (Ref. 9348).

species.name: Anoli chilien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary.  Perches motionless on pectoral fins in a wide range of habitats.  Commonly occurs on sandy bottoms or sand patches around rocky reefs and boulder and gravel strewn slopes.  Is active at night, may bury in sand with only eyes and mouth protruding during the day (Ref. 5227).  Pounces on passing prey.

species.name: Anoli commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily found in shallow inshore waters (Ref. 4964).  Rests on hard surfaces rather than on sand (Ref. 9710).  Also occurs in reef areas, but ventures into open shelf water as deep as 90 m (Ref. 7251).  Caught with several types of artisanal gear.  Reportedly good to eat, but not utilized widely (Ref. 4964).

species.name: Anoli croix
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from coastal sand flats to deep off-shore (Ref. 48635).  Prefers deeper waters (Ref. 30573).  Sold fresh or dried salted in markets (Ref. 3520).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Anoli de sable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sandy bottom around boulders or in sandy corridors in patch reefs (Ref. 5521).  Uncommon near the shore.

species.name: Anoli grêle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and silty reefs (Ref. 58652).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Common in shallow lagoons, reef flats, and sheltered seaward reefs.  Feeds on fishes and ocacionally on crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Active at night (Ref. 5213).  Caught with artisanal gear. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Anoli iguane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 9348).

species.name: Anoli indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on current-prone (Ref. 48635) sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 11228), usually in depths of 20 m or more.  Usually buries itself in the sand (Ref. 48635).  Sold fresh and dried salted in markets.

species.name: Anoli liguise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A very common species found on soft bottom (Ref. 9348).

species.name: Anoli nuageux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in sand, mud, rock and eel-grass habitats (Ref. 58302).  Solitary on sand and silt bottoms (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 89972). Found primarily inshore, e.g. in mangroves and seagrass beds, also near streams and river mouths.  Piscivorous.  Caught with artisanal gear.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Anoli oreille noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy or mud bottoms (Ref. 11228).  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Anoli phare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs. Commonly found on sand or rubble near coral heads. Feeds on shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 89972). Frequently caught with S. variegatus and S. englemani, using artisanal gear and trawls. Sold fresh and dried salted in markets. Solitary,in pairs or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Anoli poignard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species found in shallow shelf waters.  Caught mainly with artisanal gear.  Sold fresh or dried salted in markets.

species.name: Anoli serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rest on or more often burrow into substrate, leaving eyes exposed (Ref. 4472).

species.name: Anoli tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 9348).

species.name: Anoli tumbil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 30573) and trawling grounds (Ref. 58652).  Adults feed on fishes, crustaceans, and squids (Ref. 30573).  Sold fresh.

species.name: Anoli à Capricorn
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas near reefs (Ref. 38189).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Anoli à deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs (Ref. 11228).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Generally solitary and typically rests on hard surfaces, occasionally with a head down position on a steep slope (Ref. 1602). Feeds on small fishes and shrimps (Ref. 89972). Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Anoli à grandes écailles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sublittoral zone above 100 m over sand or mud bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 11228, 11230). Feeds on fishes (anchovy and red mullet Mullus surmuletus), crustaceans, and other invertebrates (Ref. 5213). Spawns from April to May off Japan. Generally marketed frozen, sometimes fresh and as fish cakes ('kamaboko') in Japan (Ref. 4964). Minimum depth from Ref. 12260.

species.name: Anolis des plages
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on both shallow and deep sand flats among grass (Ref. 12342, 39154, 39155), inshore in saltwater creeks, rivers, bays, sounds (Ref. 39156), and deep channels within lagoons (Ref. 39155).  Probably more dense over mud than shell or calcareous bottom (Ref. 39157).  Also found in open ocean over continental shelf (Ref. 4639).  A solitary (Ref. 26340) voracious predator that lurks in shallow bays and shore waters; burrows in bottom sediments.  Juveniles are pelagic, and readily collected from open ocean, usually near land in vicinity of or in shallow water (Ref. 4639). Mostly piscivorous, also includes shrimps, crabs and cephalopodes (Ref. 93252). Oviparous, newly hatched larvae are found near the surface at depths from 27 to 46 m (Ref. 39159).  Salinity range 4.0-60.0 ppt (may include juveniles), more abundant above 10.0 ppt and 30.0 ppt (Ref. 39158, 39162, 39050).  Commonly caught by anglers but considered a nuisance.

species.name: Anomalochromis thomasi
species.description: Genre de poissons. Prefers shallow and muddy waters in savannah-like areas, with water temperatures approaching 30°C during the dry season; also found in waters bordering forested areas; when stressed or disturbed, the species will hide in the mud, sometimes up to 30 cm deep; biparental, open substratum spawner (Ref. 52307). Maximum recorded TL was 6.5 cm (Ref. 5599).

species.name: Anomalous lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, found between 800-2,000 m during the day and mainly below 1,000 m at night.  Small specimens in colder water to 330 m (Ref. 4479).  Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Anomolous goby
species.description: Found on silty sand, rubble, or seagrass (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Anoplagonus occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anostomoides atrianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anostomoides laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anostomoides passionis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky areas of the river with moderate to high current (Ref. 57460).  Feed on sponges (Ref. 57460).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anostomus longus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Anostomus ucayalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ansorge's fangtooth pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and streams (Ref. 188), also in lagoons (Ref. 2849, 81269).

species.name: Antalya bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools along the banks just under the water surface in clean, slow flowing water with very dense aquatic vegetation.

species.name: Antalya minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antalya rudd
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antalya trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in stream with cold and clear water, moderate current and gravel and pebble substrate (Ref. 99540).

species.name: Antarctic dark-mouth skate
species.description: Individuals collected deeper than 810 m indicate that the species possibly occurs in greater depths in the Pacific sector, but may also be the result of differing fishery efforts in the respective depths. Most specimens caught deeper than 810 m were adults but were also recorded from shallower depths elsewhere and juveniles in turn were also recorded deeper than 810 m and even below 1000 m (Ref. 123566).

species.name: Antarctic deepsea smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Some studies on feeding have shown that euphausiids comprised 46% by weight of the food consumed by this species.  Spawning probably occurs 3-4 times a year (Ref. 5002).

species.name: Antarctic spiny plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range: 0-5 m on rocky bottoms. Usually under rocks; rarely under algal fronds. A specialized feeder on amphipods, mainly Gondogeneia antarctica. Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041). Iteroparous and devotes a lot of time to parental care (Ref. 5191). Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 71843).

species.name: Antenna codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally oceanic.  Feed on zooplankton and phytoplankton, especially crustaceans (Ref. 6735).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 6735).

species.name: Antennablennius ceylonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Antennablennius sexfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antennablennius velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Antennaire des Sargasses
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the surface, usually associated with floating objects (Ref. 26340) or Sargassum. Found near shore and occasionally among floating seaweeds (Ref. 57225). Commonly blown into shore and bay waters during storms (Ref. 7251). Epipelagic (Ref. 58302). A solitary (Ref. 26340) and voracious predator (Ref. 5521). They feed on fishes and shrimps that seek refuge in the floating weeds (Ref. 48635). Oviparous. Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773, 48635). Solitary or loose groups among floating seaweed (Ref 90102).

species.name: Antennaire du Sénégal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 10959). Occurs in marine or brackish water (Ref. 57225).

species.name: Antennaire géant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), often on jetty (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on fish (Ref. 11889) and small shrimps (Ref. 89972).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773). Solitary and frequently among sponges in 1-50 m, usually less than 20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Antennaire tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sedentary (Ref. 68964). Inhabit intertidal zone to depths of at least 25 m on both lagoon and seaward reefs.  May be taken anywhere from the surface to approximately 176 m in the Indo-Pacific area, average depth of known captures at 19 m.  Those from Eastern Atlantic at deeper waters, between 44 and 293 m, average depth of 107 m.  In life, its esca resembles a tiny stout-bodied shrimp (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773). Voracious carnivore, attracting prey with front of their cavernous mouth by wriggling their baitshaped first dorsal spine (lure) (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Antennaire à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore banks and deeper shelf waters (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Antennarius pardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26999). Occurs in marine or brackish water (Ref. 97225).  Feeds on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Antennarius scaber
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antennatus flagellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a rock ledge on fine sandy slope (Ref. 13747).

species.name: Anthias asperilinguis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anthias bicolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large groups on outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).  Schooling species along upper parts of drop-offs and in outer reef lagoons.  Feeds at various depths to near surface in pursuit of zooplankton (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Anthias bicolore (Nemanthias bicolor)
species.description: Relatively uncommon inhabitant of lagoon patch reefs and outer reef slopes.  Found in deep coastal to outer reef slopes, in current prone areas (Ref. 48635).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  It occurs in small groups above coral outcrops or near crevices or ledges.

species.name: Anthias commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found above coral outcrops or patch reefs of clear lagoons, channels, or outer reef slopes.  Form large aggregations.  Feed on zooplankton (Ref. 6113).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Males are territorial and haremic (Ref. 9710).  Color patterns and size of sexual transition very slightly from one locality to the next.  Total length for females from Ref. 9137.

species.name: Anthias cyprinoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anthias de Pelicier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rests on the bottom with gravel and small round corals; usually in pairs.

species.name: Anthias flamme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes.  Occurs in aggregations, most frequently in clear waters of outer reef slopes and passes in depths ranging  from about 3 to 15 m (Ref. 54301).  Feeds mainly on zooplankton and  swims up to several meters above the bottom while feeding (Ref 54301). When threatened by passing divers or predators the anthias hastily retreat to the safety of rocky crevices.  It has a harem-type of social structure, with each male controlling a group of females.  When courting, the male color is greatly intensified and the bright red dorsal fin is fully erected (Ref. 54301).

species.name: Anthias helenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anthias menezesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anthias rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among coral outcrops, in aggregations (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Anthias splendide
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep reefs. Forms small groups near caves and ledges, steep dropoffs in 10-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Anthias à faux blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep coastal and inner reef drop-offs from 30 m downwards.  Rarely observed by divers because of its depth preference (Ref. 48635).  Collected with rotenone and quinaldine at depths of 14-65 m (Ref. 81822). Solitary at base of steep slopes among rubble or in crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Anthias à tache rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found on open substrate with low reef and remote bommies in depths over 20 m.  Juveniles maybe shallow in coastal reefs (Ref. 48635).  Form small, loose aggregations along current-swept drop-offs (Ref. 1602, 48635).

species.name: Antigonia aurorosea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia eos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between 19-600 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Antigonia hulleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia indica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the bottom; larvae pelagic (Ref. 9609).

species.name: Antigonia kenyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia ovalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia quiproqua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia saya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia socotrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia undulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antigonia xenolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antillean smooth-head
species.description: Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Antilles frillfin
species.description: Collected primarily from reef crests and from shallow tidepools on exposed beaches, where it typically co-occurs with B. mystacium and B. lacertus. A single specimen was collected from a sheltered rocky shoreline near an irrigation canal in Puerto Rico and associated with three species, B. geminatus, B. lacertus, and B. soporator. GenBank accession number for COI sequence of holotype: HM748393 (Ref. 85559).

species.name: Antimora bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope and upper rise (Ref. 6606).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426) and benthopelagic (Ref. 5951).  Deep waters to 3277 m (Ref. 58426).  May move offshore with age and spawn in the deep parts of its range.  Off the eastern coast of United States, it is speculated that the population use the area only as feeding grounds with spawning taking place to the north.  Feed on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9319).  Maximum weight of female from Ref. 128738.

species.name: Antimore violet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the lower regions of the continental slope between 800 m and 1, 800 m. It appears that sex segregation is also basic to this species, but whether or not the species migrates extensively or uses the North American west coast slopes only as feeding areas is not known (Ref. 1371). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9319). Taken frequently by deep slope water trawlers fishing for Microstomus pacificus and deepwater Sebastes species (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Antipodocottus megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antipodocottus mesembrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antler dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sand and mud habitats, and to a lesser degree, areas of coral rubble. May be encountered by divers in sandy patches among stands of coral or rocky reefs.  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous (Ref. 56078).

species.name: Antler toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antlered sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Anton's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit semi-open and silty substrates with remote outcrops of coral or debris (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Antonina toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Antrorse spined gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare deep water species (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Apache trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, cool mountain headwaters and creeks (generally above 2500 m elevation), and mountain lakes. A 95% (stream km) reduction in range has resulted due to hybridization with Oncorhynchus mykiss and competition from Salvelinus fontinalis and Salmo trutta.

species.name: Apagesoma australe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oviparous species caught at abyssal depths with remains of crustaceans in stomach and intestine. Presumably benthic or benthopelagic (Ref. 75736).

species.name: Apagesoma delosommatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family being oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Apagesoma edentatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Apparently a slow swimmer because of its poorly developed musculature.  Its large mouth opening and oral cavity may enable it to feed on a great size range of preys.  The enlarged and swollen anterior nostril may reflect increased reliance on olfaction in recognition of conspecifics or food sources (Ref. 40708).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family being oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Apalachee shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and silt-bottomed pools and runs of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers,  Usually occurs along undercut banks and debris (Ref. 86798).  Reported maximum length is 6.5 TL (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Apamean spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon agmatos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in backwaters or streams with little or no current and with substrate generally comprising of a mixture of sand and mud, frequently with abundant flocculent sediments and leaf litter (Ref. 79584).  Forms large schools (Ref. 79584). The extremely long intestinal tract, high gill-raker counts and the habitat preference of this species indicate a detritivorous diet (Ref. 79584).

species.name: Apareiodon argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon cavalcante
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon davisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon gransabana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams mostly less than 10 m width in rocky areas with moderate to strong current.  Schools of 20-40 individuals were found to swim in strong current near the substratum with a head-downward orientation.  In reaches with moderate current, these fish usually swam higher above the substratum, and with more horizontal body orientation.  Attains at least 9.2 cm SL.

species.name: Apareiodon hasemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon ibitiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and streams with rocky and sandy bottom, with water flow up to 40 cm/sec.  Forages during the day, grazing on algae and preying on bottom-dwelling invertebrates.  Uses its well developed pectoral fins to grip the substrate while grazing.  Engages in a succession of lunges at the algal growth on rocky bottom, the mobile pedicellate upper teeth likely favoring this grazing mode.  Particles thus caught are sorted out in the mouth and then either ingested or spat out.  Food is often visually located and picked up.  At night, fish congregates in the shallows and in fast-flowing water packs closely among the rocks.  Juveniles bear a plain silvery color pattern, gradually replaced by the barred pattern of the adults (Ref. 40391).

species.name: Apareiodon itapicuruensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon machrisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon orinocensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon piracicabae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon tigrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apareiodon vladii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphaniops furcatus
species.description: Inhabits rivers and springs that are often seasonal and characterized by shallow water and white layers of salt around and within the river. Often dominates on the riversides, where the water is shallow, warm and water flow is slow. Sympatric with Aphanius dispar (Ref. 96446).

species.name: Aphaniops ginaonis
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphaniops hormuzensis
species.description: Collected from the coastal rivers and streams between the Merhan and Minhab River drainages (Ref. 126233).

species.name: Aphaniops kruppi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphaniops sirhani
species.description: In shallow water among vegetation and stones, or over muddy grounds.  Its diet consists of insect larvae and crustaceans.  The breeding season lies in the spring (Ref. 13609).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphanius almiriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic adults inhabit fresh and brackish water springs with salinity of up to 23 ppt.  They are observed in shallow areas with slow current, among vegetation, as well as in the water column.  They are short-lived, form schools and fast swimmers.  Mature females are fractional spawners that breed in late spring - early summer, spawning 1-3 eggs a time (apparently the reproductive period may be prolonged until late summer) (Ref. 58344).

species.name: Aphanius chantrei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphanius d'Espagne
species.description: Inhabits lagoons, salt marshes, swamps, estuaries and freshwaters. Euryhaline, occurring in water bodies with salinities ranging from freshwater to 57 ppt (Ref. 59043). Occurs in lowland water with little current. Spawns from April to September. Is an egg-laying carnivorous fish which is used for mosquito control (Ref. 26100). This short-lived species is now threatened throughout its entire range because of habitat destruction and because of the introduction of Gambusia affinis (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish. Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphanius de Corse
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal lagoons and in hypersaline to shallow still to slow-flowing fresh water, especially at river mouths (Ref. 59043).  A short-lived species which inhabits ponds, ditches and swamps.  Feeds on invertebrates and plants.  Spawns from April to September (Ref. 26100).  Spawning takes place on the bottom and in submerged vegetation (Ref. 59043).
Threatened due to habitat destruction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphanius de Mer Rouge
species.description: Occurs in coastal zones, also found in oasis pools with hypersaline to fresh water (Ref. 3788).  Forms schools.  Chiefly a herbivorous species (Ref. 13530).  Spawn in areas where roots of hyacinth or other floating plants abound (Ref. 44327).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphanius desioi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sulfur-producing lakes, springs and their drainage canals (Ref. 3788).

species.name: Aphanius punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanius saharien
species.description: This species could be considered as critically endangered following IUCN criteria (Ref. 57144). Excessive ground water withdrawal for agricultural purposes, the drying of wetlands, and water pollution are, along with the introduced Gambusia, the major threats to the survival of this species (Ref. 57144).

species.name: Aphanope charbon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles mesopelagic (Ref. 6181).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Migrate to midwater at night and feed on crustaceans, cephalopods and fishes (mostly macrourids, morids and alepocephalids).  Mature at 80 to 85 cm.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6768). Data from study reveal mature individuals undertake horizontal migration to spawning and nursery grounds located off the Madeira and Canary islands (Ref. 108708).  Commercial catch up to 1000 t was caught off Madeira with a specialized commercial deep water longline (Ref. 6255).  Appear as bycatch in the trawl fishery west of the British Isles, along the Middle-Atlantic Ridge and at Corner Rise.  Important and fabled food fish in Madeira (Ref. 4537).  Some specimens reach 145 cm (Nuno Marques, Nomad@netmadeira.com, 12/09).

species.name: Aphanopus beckeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanopus capricornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanotorulus ammophilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanotorulus emarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives under the roots of trees and among rocks, and they issue from their hiding places to the sand-banks to feed at night.

species.name: Aphanotorulus horridus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanotorulus phrixosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphanotorulus rubrocauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in dark colored water river, with large boulders and rocky substrates (Ref. 129297).

species.name: Aphanotorulus unicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphareus bleuâtre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral and rocky reefs and in clear waters of lagoons (Ref. 9821).  Pelagic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Occur singly or in small groups.  Feed mainly on fishes, but also eat crustaceans.  Individuals with brilliant yellow on head may be nuptial males (Ref. 9821).  Often curious and approachable (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Aphips chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits piedmont and mountain streams with Mediterranean water regime, strong to moderate current, rock or gravel bottom.  Abundant along shores and may be restricted to very small pools during summer.  Feeds predominantly on terrestrial insects, benthic invertebrates and algae.  Breeds in shallow riffle habitats, with strong current and stone or pebble bottom, at 10-20 cm water depth.  Moves downstream in winter to deeper pools and to uppermost stretches of streams in summer (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Aphrodite anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mesophotic coral ecosystems of the island and observed while rebreather diving. A single observation at 260 m depth was taken from a submersible dive. It inhabits small crevices of complex rocky reefs. Ambient seawater temperature at the collecting depth (ca. 120 m) varied between 13 and 15 °C during the two-week observation period (Ref. 120716).

species.name: Aphyocharacidium bolivianum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharacidium melandetum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very rare.  Occurs in the headwaters of basins (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Aphyocharax agassizii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax colifax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax nattereri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax pusillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocharax yekwanae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in the lee side of islands and protected backwaters of the main river channel; sand with some rocks bottom.  Also collected near mouths of streams where it could be muddy and covered with terrestrial plant leaves.  Aquatic vegetation almost always absent; water clear to moderately turbid (Ref. 49521).

species.name: Aphyocheirodon hemigrammus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris amnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a stream section about 50 m long, composed of pools with a very low flow rate. At the time of collecting, the type locality is a pool about 5 m long and 3 m wide, no deeper than 0.5 m with moderately turbid water and surrounded by forest and with muddy bottom that has patches of gravel (Ref. 87785).

species.name: Aphyocypris arcus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris dorsohorizontalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris kikuchii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris kyphus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris normalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyocypris pulchrilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small, shallow, turbid,  canalized stream with low flow rate and aquatic plants covering almost half of the water (Ref. 93177).  The stream is  exposed to frequent local disturbance such as the presence of the ducks in the water. The sampling site is near a water treatment plant (Ref. 93177).

species.name: Aphyodite apiaka
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyodite grammica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyodite tupebas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyolebias boticarioi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyolebias claudiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyolebias manuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyolebias obliquus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a temporary swamp of seasonally flooded forest.

species.name: Aphyolebias rubrocaudatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyolebias schleseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyolebias wischmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion abacinum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swampy parts of quiet brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion ahli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, quiet parts of brook and flood pools in coastal rainforest (Ref. 47461, 80395). Usually in shallow water (Ref. 80395). Lives over mud substrate and among fallen leaves (Ref. 47461). Entomophagous (Ref. 51193). Not a seasonal killifish; difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion alpha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in clear creeks under forest cover, usually over a sandy soil, in the coastal plain (Ref. 80395).

species.name: Aphyosemion aurantiacum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives only in very small forest streams and water holes, often with a bottom consisting of roots and dead leaves, where it can be very abundant (Ref. 119374).

species.name: Aphyosemion barakoniense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives in a small river, if less than 1 m wide among roots or dead leaves in the middle of the river, or where the river is 2-3 m wide in small water holes of stagnant water close to the river, hidden among dead leaves and mud (Ref. 119374).

species.name: Aphyosemion bitteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a stream not wider than 60 cm and not deeper than 20 cm; no aquatic vegetation was present; only freshwater shrimps, tadpoles, and aquatic insects were present (Ref. 116793).

species.name: Aphyosemion bualanum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and swamps in the open and humid grassland savanna on the highlands (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion buytaerti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion callipteron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion campomaanense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in small streams and shallow pools in the rainforest; they stay close to the banks, avoiding the deepest and fastest water (Ref. 80559).

species.name: Aphyosemion castaneum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion celiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in wells, brooks, swamps and pools in the rainforest and secondary savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion chauchei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion citrineipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast flowing brooks and small streams in mountainous rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion cryptum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion cyanoflavum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from the type locality where it is found syntopic with Aphyosemion coeleste and A. mandoroense, where they occur in more or less similar microhabitats (Ref. 125647).

species.name: Aphyosemion decorsei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks found in the savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion deltaense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in raffia swamps and swampy parts of brooks in the humid coastal forest; annual species; 3 to 6 month incubation period for the eggs (Ref. 96625)

species.name: Aphyosemion ecucuense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion erythron
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion etsamense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species can be found in small rainforest creeks and rivers with slow flowing water (Ref. 56139).

species.name: Aphyosemion fellmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion ferranti
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Expérimenté:
Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion flammulatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives in very small forest streams, less than 1 metre wide, with sandy or rocky bottoms; it hides among roots or dead leaves (Ref. 119374).

species.name: Aphyosemion flavocyaneum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives in small, secondary rivers and small, forest streams, often with a sandy bottom, where it can be found along the riverbanks; it hides quickly in water plants or dead leaves (Ref. 119374).

species.name: Aphyosemion fulgens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small, mostly swampy brooks in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion georgiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small, mostly swampy brooks in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion grelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aphyosemion grelli was found in a stream no wider than 1 m with a depth less than 40 cm; with small unidentified Barbus species as the only other fish present (Ref. 94461).

species.name: Aphyosemion hera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aphyosemion jeanhuberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small and shallow permanent forest streams (Ref. 116455).

species.name: Aphyosemion joergenscheeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small streams in the highlands with fast or moderate flow (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aphyosemion kouamense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In small creeks.

species.name: Aphyosemion koungueense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality of this species is a small river in the forest, about 3 m wide and 0.4 m deep, and with muddy bottom on sand, covered with decomposing leaves (Ref. 76820).

species.name: Aphyosemion labarrei

species.name: Aphyosemion rubrogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found in 3 to 5 metre wide rivers with fast running water, and sandy bottoms with no aquatic vegetation; they were hidden in tree roots along the riverbanks, or under dead leaves at the mouth of small secondary brooks, but they were not found in the small brooks themselves (Ref. 119374).

species.name: Aphyosemion schioetzi

Not a seasonal killifish; difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139). Occurs near coast and not for inland; prefers clearer and more active water on fine substratum (Ref. 84174).

species.name: Aphyosemion striatum

species.name: Apistogramma angayuara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in association with rapids, with very fast running water; lots of aquatic plants (Podostemonaceae) which grow on the rocks.  During the dry season most of the rocks are exposed, and many pools are formed where the fishes are trapped and easily collected with rotenone.  Stomach analyses of five specimens (19-24 mm) from rapids showed that aquatic invertebrates were the most important food items consumed by this species; rhizopods were the dominant item, followed by sponges and cladocerans.  Both males and females dissected have well developed gonads (Ref. 56722).

species.name: Apistogramma arua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Remains close to the substrate, above the leaf litter, in calm shallow water (Ref. 28729).  Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Apistogramma atahualpa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Apistogramma barlowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to be restricted to forest streams, with a preference for fast-flowing, cooler, and crystal-clear, acid to neutral water (Ref. 75695).  A reddish morph of this species was collected in a small clearwater igarapé, about 1 meter wide and approximately 30 cm deep, with fine white sandy bottom, no submerged vegetation, rocks or pebbles, a pH of 4.8 at a temperature close to 29°C (Ref. 75695).

species.name: Apistogramma bitaeniata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Grows larger in aquaria, the largest being a male measuring 4.65 cm SL (Ref. 9088).  Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Apistogramma diplotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893). Attains a maximum length 2.92 cm SL (Ref. 98797).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length is 6.0 cm TL (Ref. 12225).  These fish practice harem breeding when the females outnumber the available males (Ref. 12251).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Apistogramma iniridae

Collected together with <i>Apistogramma  bitaeniata, <i>Bujurquina peregrinabunda, <i>Crenicichla sp., <i>Cichlasoma amazonarum, <i>Acestrocephalus sp., <i>Astyanax bimaculatus, <i>Characidium sp., <i>Knodus sp., <i>Leporinus sp. aff. friderici, <i>Moenkhausia margitae, <i>Moenkhausia oligolepsis, <i>Pyrrhulina semifasciata, <i>Corydoras fowleri, <i>Ituglanis sp., <i>Rhamdia sp., <i>Gymnotus sp., and <i>Sternopygus macrurus (Ref. 97388).

species.name: Apistogramma ortmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length is 7.5 cm TL (Ref. 12251).  Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Apistogramma similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apistogramma staecki

species.name: Apistogramma taeniata

species.name: Apistogramma trifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves (Ref. 1672).  Biparental care of eggs and larvae (Ref. 1672).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apistogramma velifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apistogramma wapisana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers smaller, muddy steams, influenced by whitewater with a thick layer of leaf liter and medium to comparatively high water temperatures (Ref. 57916).

Observed usually hiding among the leaf litter, which (apart from scarce driftwood) is the main substrate covering the sandy bottom (Ref. 104987).

species.name: Apistogrammoides pucallpaensis
