species.name: Aplodactylus punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is most abundant littoral species on the coast of central Chile, found in close association with the brown kelp Lessonia trabeculata. Juveniles found in tidepools to a maximum size of 15.7 cm TL and an estimated 3 years of age, adults occur subtidally. It is mainly herbivorous, feeding almost exclusively on brown, red and green algae, with a strong preference for green and red algae (digestion by acid hydrolysis). Its meat reported as an excellent pan-fish, with rich, white, sweet, and flaky meat (Ref. 86913).

species.name: Apocal
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apocryptes bato
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 1479). Burrows within tidal limits of river deltas from the east coast of India to Burma (Ref. 5218).

species.name: Apocryptodon punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in burrows made by the crustacean Alpheus at river mouths.

species.name: Apogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally forms schools; sometimes solitary. Inhabits muddy or rocky bottoms and caves (Ref. 4738). A sciaphilous species thriving in a number of shady/dark habitats and frequents marine caves, where it forms large schools (Ref. 118281). Feeds on small invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 4738). Observed to feed in the water column and just over the bottom, always at night; 93.4% of observed events occurring outside the caves, usually on rocky bottoms and Posidonia oceanica meadows, and to a lesser extent on pebbles (Ref. 118281). Oral brooding by males (Ref. 4738).

species.name: Apogon (Cheilodipterus artus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered bays and lagoon patch reefs from 5 to at least 20 m, forming small, loose aggregates in caves or just above branches of certain corals (Ref. 1602).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Apogon (Jaydia lineata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant on sandy and muddy bottoms from coastal inlets to deeper waters (Also Ref. 11230).  Breeding season is from July to September.  Males brood eggs in the mouth.  Made into fish paste (Ref. 559 and 637).

species.name: Apogon campbelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest mature male 2.59 cm SL and female 2.47 cm SL (Ref. 50837).

species.name: Apogon dammermani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon de Kaudern
species.description: Poisson. Common around the jetty, in silty sand bottoms with seagrass (Enhalus acoroides). Associated with Diadema setosum, the long-spined sea urchins. Individuals of 2 to 60 hover directly above the urchins, with the younger ones about 2-3 cm SL staying closer to the urchins. The fish retreat among the spines when threatened. Probably feed on small benthic and planktonic crustaceans at night. Male incubates the eggs until hatching; the large egg about 2.5 mm in diameter, with the young remaining within the mouth cavity for undetermined period after hatching (Ref. 9936, 48635). Newly hatched larvae have no planktonic period (Ref. 35886). Juveniles also use anemones for protection (Ref. 45560, 48635). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35417).

species.name: Apogon de platier
species.description: Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found in holes or ledges of outer reef flats in areas exposed to surge (Ref. 1602), to depths of about 10 m (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Apogon dianthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon doré
species.description: Inhabits holes in rocks or under ledges in shallow waters. Known to occur in mixed aggregates with Apogon apogonoides during summer and autumn, but form separate aggregates in winter and spring (Ref. 559 and 637). Forms aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Apogon erythrosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The smallest female with mature gonads was a 2.81 cm individual (Ref. 50837).

species.name: Apogon irisé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear water lagoon patch reefs and seaward reefs from the lower surge zone to a depth of 45 m (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Solitary (Ref. 93839). Feeds at night on small benthic and free-swimming crustaceans (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Apogon lativittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive species found in areas with rocky bottom along exposed shores (Ref. 41638).

species.name: Apogon latus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon marquesensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon photogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups. Found in lagoon patch reefs in 18-52 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Apogon rayé
species.description: Commonly found in clear-waters of seaward reefs; on reef crests and slopes, where usually shallow, and along deep drop-offs to 25 m (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on polychaetes and other small benthic invertebrates at night; cryptic under ledges or in holes by day (Ref. 1602). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Apogon rubellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon susanae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogon à bride fine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under ledges or among isolated coral heads in silty inner reef areas (Ref. 1602).  Solitary and rather rare (Ref. 559).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Often found at base of coral outcrops or under ledges (Ref 90102). Feeds on fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 89972).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Apogon à cinq lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of 40 m or more. Occurs singly or in small to large aggregations, taking shelter in dark crevices, branched coral, under ledges, and among the spines of Diadema setosum. Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Feeds on small crustaceans and gastropods, also on small fishes. Generally common (Ref. 9710). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35404).

species.name: Apogon à deux selles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs, in shallow silty areas, and in mangroves (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Apogon à grandes dents
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in outer reef slopes in 4-30 m depth; in caves and ledges of clear lagoon and seaward reefs from 0.5 to at least 40 m, generally hovering solitarily in midwater (Ref. 1602).  Adults usually in pairs or small groups comprising several pairs; juveniles solitary or small groups (Ref. 48635).  Feeds primarily on small fishes (Ref. 9710).  Sexual maturity reached at about 8 cm.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Apogon à nageoires noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300) and in deep offshore reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found among weeds (Ref. 1623).  Nocturnal species.  Feed at night on zooplankton (Ref. 43448). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35416). Mouthbrooders, the males incubate the eggs (Ref. 43448).

species.name: Apogon à nageoires rayées
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, in rocky and coralline areas.  In or near shelter by day (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on free-swimming crustaceans (Ref. 13550). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Apogon à points bleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The three known specimens taken from about 15 m (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Apogon à queue d'hirondelle
species.description: Forms large shoals among rocks or above corals of lagoon patch reefs (Ref. 1602). Often schools with R. gracilis (Ref. 37816). Spreads out at night, floating mid-water to catch plankton (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Apogon à rayures jaunes
species.description: Inhabits sheltered clear water areas of lagoon and seaward reefs from depths of 1 to at least 49 m.  Found in small or large aggregations under ledges, in holes, or even among long spines of sea urchins.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans and small invertebrates.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35404).

species.name: Apogon à stries oranges
species.description: Inhabits continental and insular shelves; on coral and rocky reefs in sheltered bays and lagoon, patch reefs, with muddy, sandy and silty bottoms or coral rubble, and mangroves (Ref. 54391); typically forming dense aggregations at the entrance of caves (Ref. 1602, 48635) and among branching corals (Ref. 2334).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Apogon à ventre doré
species.description: Inhabits rocky cliffs.  Also in sheltered coastal to outer reefs from shallow flats to over 50 m depth.  Usually in pairs, small aggregations, or occasionally schooling (Ref. 48635).  Occurrence is rather rare (Ref. 559). Feeds on zooplankons and invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides cantoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides cathetogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy-muddy bottoms around rocky reefs (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Apogonichthyoides euspilotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides gardineri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides heptastygma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides miniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthyoides niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitarily around boulders scattered on sandy and muddy bottoms in bays.  Breeding occurs from July to September.  Males brood eggs in the mouth (Ref. 559).

species.name: Apogonichthyoides regani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apogonichthys landoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apollo sharkminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from high gradient rivers with rocky, stony or gravel bottoms (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Apomatoceros alleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apostrophe goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Aposturisoma myriodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Appalachia darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble runs and riffles of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Apricaphanius baeticus
species.description: Inhabits lagoons, tidal canals and small, shallow coastal streams, with water fresh to hypersaline and with silt bottom. Omnivorous, feeding on zooplankton, small insects, vegetal matter and detritus. Freshwater populations are threatened due to the introduction of Gambusia holbrooki and Fundulus heteroclitus (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Apricot bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and rubble bottoms.

species.name: Aprion verdâtre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit open waters of deep lagoons, channels, or seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Found in benthopelagic waters (Ref. 58302).  Usually seen singly, but also in groups. They feed mainly on fishes, but also on shrimps, crabs, cephalopods and planktonic organisms (Ref. 30573, 48635).  Mainly marketed fresh but also dried and salted.  Excellent eating.  Large individuals may be ciguatoxic (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Apristurus albisoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sexual maturity attained between 40 and 50 cm TL (Ref. 36058). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Apristurus ampliceps
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Claspers of males are short and less than 2.0% TL in specimens  less than 52.7 cm TL, which is ranked as maturity stage 1 (immature); 73.3-76.5 cm TL have long but soft claspers (3.9-4.2% TL, maturity stage 2; greater than 78 cm TL have long, well developed and hardened
claspers (3.6-5.6% TL, maturity stage 3).  Immature males are less than 52.7 cm TL and for females 37.4 cm TL (maturity stage 1);  adolescent  in males of 73.3-76.5 cm TL and females of 57.8-65.6 cm TL are  (maturity stage 2); and adult in males with greater than 78 cm TL and females greater than 67.8 cm TL (maturity stage 3) (Ref. 76941).

species.name: Apristurus australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apristurus exsanguis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Apristurus fedorovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Apristurus internatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Apristurus pinguis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Apron ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on continental shelf. Produces 2-5 pups during each gestation (up to 12 reported from Argentina). Segregates by sex. Maturity size for males at 23-29 cm TL, females probably smaller (at least in Argentina); birth size at 8-9 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Apterichtus dunalailai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens caught using a benthic dredge.  One paratype with the tail missing is assumed to be approximately 33 cm TL by extrapolation  (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Apterichtus flavicaudus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Thrives in shallow coastal clean sand habitats near reefs (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Apterichtus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Apterichtus jeffwilliamsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured over a rippled sand bottom.  The largest female specimen (30.5 cm TL) was with ripened eggs, 0.7-0.9 mm in diameter (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Apterichtus keramanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apterichtus malabar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apterichtus monodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Apterichtus moseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater species, specimens were captured using dredge and trawl between 111-240 m depth but underwater photographs taken from the sandy bottom at Suruga Bay (Japan) suggest that it might occur as shallow as 15-25 m depth (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Apterichtus mysi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand with associated rock and coral reef bottoms; captured using ichthyocides and dredges.  The largest female specimen (30.1 cm TL) with eggs - 0.6-0.9 mm in diameter (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Apterichtus nariculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apterichtus orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy mud bottoms.

species.name: Apterichtus soyoae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apterichtus succinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus acidops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to length to the end of anal fin, LEA (Ref. 88927).

species.name: Apteronotus anu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift current habitats over substrates of rounded stones. It was observed that this species is a voracious nocturnal predator (Ref.  93867).

species.name: Apteronotus apurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus baniwa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapids habitat with rocky bottom (Ref. 93867).

species.name: Apteronotus bonapartii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus camposdapazi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus caudimaculosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus cuchillejo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams (Ref. 26543).  Feeds mainly on macro-invertebrates (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Apteronotus cuchillo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus ellisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus eschmeyeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow-flowing waters (Ref. 50571).

species.name: Apteronotus ferrarisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus galvisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits piedmont rivers with clear water, rocky bottom and strong current (Ref. 75033).  Has the ability to generate a continuous wave (tone) -type electric organ discharges (EOD) with a stable fundamental frequency of 700-957 (Ref. 75033).  Sexually mature males have more fundamental frequencies of the EOD than females, with no overlap between sexes (Ref. 75033).

species.name: Apteronotus jurubidae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus leptorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers fast flowing rivers (Ref. 26543).  Forms loosely associated groups in rocky habitats or river banks (Ref. 10605).  Nocturnal (Ref. 26543).  Each individual fish possesses a unique spatiotemporal pattern of electric organ discharge (EOD) potentials distributed over the body surface (Ref. 10595).  Chirps and EOD frequency modulations are important elements of courtship behavior and are sensitive to testosterone levels (Ref. 10011, 10883).  Seems to reach sexual maturity at 1 year of age, based on breeding experiments (Ref. 10011).  Tuberous electro receptors are differentiated and functional in  larvae at day 9; electric organ and electro receptors both present in the larvae at the time of first exogenous feeding (Ref. 10605).

species.name: Apteronotus lindalvae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus macrostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus magdalenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species can be distinguished by its pale coloration, marbled with patches of brown blotches.

species.name: Apteronotus magoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus mariae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus milesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus pemon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus rostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Apteronotus spurrellii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aqaba Cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sexual maturity reached at 6.5-7 cm.

species.name: Aqaba sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Aquavit hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Aquitanian pike
species.description: Espèce de poissons. E. aquitanicus should have similar ecological characteristics as E. lucius in terms of habitat, behavior, and predation, because no difference were mentioned about ecological traits between Aquitanian and the other French pike populations, except an earlier spawning in February instead of March-April. Its size can exceed 1000 mm TL (Dégrave, pers. comm.) A pike of 1370 mm was mentioned by Laporte in Lake Cazeau, right in the heart of the distribution area of E. aquitanicus. However, we cannot exclude early stockings of E. lucius. When there is cohabitation between the two species, the Aquitanian pike is able to hybridize with the northern pike (present study) (Ref. 97279)

species.name: Ara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 41299); also found near shore on rocky bottom (Ref. 11230).  Neither opercular spine nor anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Minimum depth from Ref. 41299.

species.name: Ara lunga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An epipelagic and mesopelagic, oceanic species, abundant in surface waters of 15.6° to 19.4°C; deeper swimming, large albacore are found in waters of 13.5° to 25.2°C; temperatures as low as 9.5°C may be tolerated for short periods (Ref. 168). Known to concentrate along thermal discontinuities (Ref. 168). Form mixed schools with skipjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis), yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares) and bluefin tuna (T. maccoyii), schools may be associated with floating objects, including sargassum weeds (Ref. 168). Feed on fishes, crustaceans and squids. Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). Sexual maturity reached at 90 cm (Ref. 36731). Highly appreciated and marketed fresh, smoked, deep frozen or canned. Eaten steamed, broiled, fried and microwaved (Ref. 9987). Also Ref. 1762, 1798, 1804. Angling: Largely caught offshore, where the waters are mild and blue. Albacore favor those areas where cooler water interfaces with warmer water. They are caught with live of dead baitfish such as mullet, sauries, squid, herring, anchovies, sardines, and other small fish. Albacore strike hard and make powerful runs (Ref. 84357).

species.name: Arab blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are known from shallow water with rocky bottom, sometimes in tide pools (Ref. 11441).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Arabian banded whipray
species.description: Known from the Persian Gulf which is mostly shallower than 40 m and with depths rarely exceeding 60 m; soft substrates, mostly sand and mud (Ref. 90168).

species.name: Arabian blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore species found on rocky bottoms.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Arabian blue-striped snapper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arabian chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults form aggregations on reefs to feed on zooplankton.  Take shelter in branching corals (Ref. 11411).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205)..

species.name: Arabian damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Arabian dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Takes refuge in burrows occupied by symbiotic alpheids and gobies of the genera Amblyeleotris and Cryptocentrus (https://www.oceandocs.org/handle/1834/10331?locale-attribute=ru)..

species.name: Arabian demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore reefs on soft bottoms around coral outcrops, rocks, debris, or wharf pilings (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Arabian eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from holotype record (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Arabian flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arabian flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No information available in habitat and biology (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Arabian gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A filter-feeder.  More data needed.

species.name: Arabian goby
species.description: Occurs in very shallow water, living in a burrow in sediment.  Probably associated with alpheid shrimp (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Arabian perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually on continental shelf and slope muddy bottoms and caught by bottom trawl (Ref. 114767).

species.name: Arabian sand diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton about half a meter above the sand substratum (Ref. 10682).

species.name: Arabian toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arabian yellowfin seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on echinoderms, worms, crustaceans and mollusks.  Mainly exploited by artisanal fisheries.  Sold fresh in markets (Ref. 3507).

species.name: Arabibarbus arabicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arabibarbus hadhrami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its habitat is characterized by high seasonal fluctuations in discharge; during the dry season, many sections of the wadis cease to flow and break up into series of isolated pools, connected by subterranean streams (Ref. 96964).

species.name: Arabic whipray
species.description: Immature male at 36.0 cm WD, while size at birth is probably slightly smaller than 17 cm WD (Ref. 110187).

species.name: Arafura catfish
species.description: Found in seas, estuaries and fresh waters (Ref. 32693).

species.name: Arafura perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arafura skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 114953). Length of one adolescent male 29.9 cm TL; males mature at 37.6-40.7 cm TL; smallest juvenile at 23.5 cm TL (Ref. 75645).

species.name: Araguaia toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Araiocypris batodes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a forest creek, apparently in the Ka Longo drainage (marks the border between Vietnam and China (known as Beilun He).  It is a small stream in the foothills.  The specimens were collected in a shallow bay (less than 40 cm deep), with slow water current and sandy bottom, adjacent to riffles (Ref. 75046).

species.name: Araiophos eastropas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Araiophos gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aral barbel
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in rivers, reservoirs, lakes and canals (Ref. 11145).  Occurs in the sea at depths of up to 25 m and in rivers in deep stretches with gravel or stone bottom.  In freshened parts of sea, preys mainly on benthic crustaceans. Does not feed while migrating upstream and starts to feed again at the spawning sites mainly on insects, juveniles of other fishes, rarely on algae, seeds and other plant material.  Spawns in fast-flowing water at areas with hard bottom and depths of 1-2 m (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Arapaima agassizii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arapaima leptosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arapaima mapae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arapaïma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often referred to as the largest freshwater fish.  Builds a nest of about 15 cm depth and 50 cm width in sandy bottoms.  Spawns in April and May and guards the eggs and the young.  Obligate air breather. The fish rises to the surface of the water and inspires air in a noisy, distinctive gulp, which is reported to carry for long distances (Ref. 50891). Migrates into higher floodplain habitats with rising water and moves back eventually to lacustrine habitats during low water level (Ref. 116898). Threatened due to over harvesting (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Arawana
species.description: Is an omnivore with a tendency to feed on fish at the surface.  The superior position of the mouth allows it to capture its prey while swimming from below.  Also jumps out of the water to feed on large insects (Coleoptera; Ref. 27548).  It is capable of adapting to environments with low oxygen levels (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Arbaletrier gris
species.description: Inhabit offshore coral reefs usually solitary or in pairs (Ref. 5503, 48637).  Common in surface waters around oceanic islands (Ref. 9318).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Shy species, usually retreating quickly into caves or large crevices of the reef (Ref. 48637).  Juveniles are pelagic, seen under floating objects (Ref. 9318).  Feed on tips of branching corals, algae, sponges, sea urchins, and mollusks (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Arbano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range reported at 0m-2500m (Ref. 125614).  A deepwater species of the outer continental and insular shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 6871, 75154), islands, seamounts and mid-ocean ridges (Ref. 125614).  Near bottom, occasionally pelagic, adults usually below 91 m (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles may be found close inshore (Ref. 6871), while nursery areas are in very shallow waters (Ref. 125614).  Found on the bottom by day, moving to the surface at night to feed, and where it may take longlines set for other species (Ref. 45445).  Depth distribution related to growth and temperature, with juveniles having most shallow records and from colder, poleward regions (Ref. 58302).  Generally occurs at a bottom temperature of 6 to 10°C (Ref. 125614).   Feeds on a wide range of marine organisms, including other sharks, rays, chimaeras, bony fish, squids, crabs, shrimps, carrion, and even seals (Ref. 26969).  Large sharks (at least 2m) take cetaceans and seals.  Viviparous, very large litters of 47-108 pups (Ref. 125614).  Give birth to almost 100 young (Ref. 35388).  Young and adults may be segregated, with the young using inshore nursery grounds. Possibly long-lived (Ref. 125614).  Is a eurytrophic predator that is capable of exploiting a wide range of prey species and habitats (Ref. 26969).  A vertical migrant, it may sit on the bottom  by day, and rise to the surface at night to feed (Ref. 247).  It occurs alone or in groups.  Adults are more sensitive to light than the juveniles and less seen in clear shallow waters, but more prevalent at night or areas with dense plankton blooms (Ref. 125614).  It is locally common in bycatch and target fisheries for food, fishmeal and oil, and in sports fisheries, but vulnerable to overfishing and requires careful management (Ref. 125614).  Marketed fresh, frozen, or dried salted (Ref. 247).  Not known to have attacked people without provocation (Ref. 247).

species.name: Arbiter Snailfish
species.description: All specimens examined were females, the largest, a ripe female of 15.3 cm SL (UW 150325).  The smallest female with yolked eggs was 13.6 cm SL  (UW 119827).  At least two sizes of eggs are present in ripe females:  yolked eggs 3.5-4.5 mm and white eggs 0.5-1.5 mm in diameter (Ref. 91047).

species.name: Arc en ciel jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand patches of lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 30 m (Ref. 1602); also on slopes to moderate depths along drop-offs (Ref. 48636).  Juveniles common at the bottom of surge channels (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey, including mollusks, crustaceans and sea urchins (9823).

species.name: Arcfin shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep coastal slopes, usually in depths over 20 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Arched sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a rocky tide pool with kelp beds (Ref. 45337).

species.name: Archolaemus blax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its elongated, laterally compressed body is completely covered with scales and is without a caudal fin (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Archolaemus ferreirai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality, Rio Mucajaí, is characterized by rapid flowing water and a 20 m high waterfall.  The species was encountered above these falls in an area with many rapids and no still backwaters (Ref. 93148).

species.name: Archolaemus janeae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in river with pronounced current that was faster towards the centre of the channel, with the substrate in the sampled areas formed by pebbly sand.  Also found in the main stream of shallow rapids and small waterfalls, always over a rocky bottom (Ref. 93148).

species.name: Archolaemus luciae
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift-flowing water habitats.  Also found in main stream of shallow rapids and
small waterfalls, always over a rocky bottom (Ref. 93418).

species.name: Archolaemus orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits portion of a river characterized by large rapids, a major waterfall and rocky and sandy substrates (Ref. 93148).

species.name: Archolaemus santosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids (Ref. 93148).

species.name: Arctic lumpsucker
species.description: Occurs on mud bottom (Ref. 4701).

species.name: Arengue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit harbors and shallow coastal areas (Ref. 9710). Pelagic (Ref. 27549). Form schools (but solitary individuals reported), probably not entering water of low salinity.  Feed by filtering plankton (copepods), but also take small fishes, crabs and shrimps.  Marketed fresh, frozen and salted; also used  in the fishmeal industry.  Occur in freshwater in St. Johns River, Florida (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Arenigobius bifrenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy coastal areas to upper estuaries, rocky reefs, in sea grass beds and mangroves (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Arfak rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams flowing through rainforest and agricultural (mainly oil palm) lands on a flat, alluvial plain.

species.name: Argente
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over all types of bottom, but mainly around coral reefs and on vegetated sandy areas.  In turbid as well as clear water (Ref. 9710).  They often form large aggregations, especially during the breeding season.  Feed at night on small fishes, bottom-living crabs, shrimps, worms, gastropods and cephalopods.  Good food fish, it is marketed fresh.

species.name: Argentin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relatively common on the continental shelf and upper slope, probably schools near the bottom.  Depth range from 50-500 m (Ref. 35388) and from 288-700 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on bottom-living polychaetes, mollusks and crustaceans, also on pelagic invertebrates and fishes.  Spawns from winter to spring in the Mediterranean and from March to July off the British coasts.  Its eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 4773).  They become sexually mature at a length of 12-13cm.  With a smell like cucumber (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Argentin (Trachipterus trachypterus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 2713), mesopelagic species.  Feeds on squid and midwater fishes (Ref. 6392).  Swims with head up (Ref. 36731).  Eggs and larvae are found frequently near the surface (Ref. 6392).

species.name: Argentina brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argentina du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the shelf edge and upper bathyal in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Maximum length of 25.5 cm TL from asymptotic length in Ref. 5952 (assumed to be TL).  Matures at 13 cm SL at 2 years old (Ref. 84005).

species.name: Argentina elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in offshore waters (Ref. 9258). Reported from depths between 69 m (Ref. 58489) and 600 m (Ref. 9258).  New maximum depth range from Ref. 89422.

species.name: Argentina euchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 3978).

species.name: Argentina kagoshimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the upper bathyal, 225-385 m on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Argentina stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argentinat antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The largest specimen studied, 20.75 cm SL had matured ovaries with developing eggs (Ref. 5123).

species.name: Argentine alice
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools near the bottom (Ref. 9270).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 9270).  Utilized as fishmeal (Ref. 9270).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Argentine de Bruce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.

species.name: Argentine du Pacifique nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic or mesopelagic (Ref. 265).  Frequently found in the stomachs of rockfishes (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with pelagic eggs and pelagic larvae (Ref. 265).

species.name: Argentine humphead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max.  length 20 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Argentine pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seasonal toothcarp living in waters that dry up during the dry season.  The adult fishes die but the eggs survive in the mud and hatch in the next rainy season.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Argentine skate
species.description: According to the capture localities of the type specimens, Dipturus argentinensis appears to have a restricted range distribution occurring in the central and southern Patagonian region on the southwest Atlantic. No recorded specimens have been reported northwards 45º S. The region where the type specimens of the Argentine skate were collected is dominated by sub-Antarctic cold-temperate waters with low salinity. These waters have a predominantly NNE flow and form the Patagonian Current (Brandhorst & Castello 1971). Range temperatures and salinities of the localities where the specimens were collected were 5.9-9.38ºC, and 33.24-33.64 ups, respectively. These physical characteristics agree with the Magellanic Biogeographic Province where the specimens have been captured (Ref. 79571).

species.name: Argentine striée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.

species.name: Argentine torpedo
species.description: Lives on the continental slope around 600 m in depth. Feeds primarily on fishes (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Maturity size of males at 62-67 cm TL; largest known specimens are females (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Argentine à petites dents
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, probably near the bottom.  Feeds on pelagic crustaceans.  Spawns from winter to spring in the Mediterranean (Ref. 4773).

species.name: Argentinian sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky and sandy bottoms in coastal waters (Ref. 53324). Oviparous with low batch fecundity (Ref. 53324). "We frequently catch P. semifasciata off the Rio de Janeiro coast. I have personally seen fish of 24 kg, with fish in the 12-18 kg range being fairly common (Capt. Eduardo Baumeier, pers. comm., 2001)." Ref. 27569 gave 10 kg as maximum weight.

species.name: Argentinian toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argentinolycus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the intertidal zone to about 40 m (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Argonectes longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently occurs in swift flowing waters, over a sandy bottom (Ref. 12225).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Argonectes robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Argopleura chocoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argopleura conventus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argopleura diquensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argopleura magdalenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Argus skate
species.description: Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slopes.  Bottom-dweller which feeds on invertebrates, mainly on crustaceans such as shrimps and prawns (Ref. 114953) and bony fish (Ref. 9908).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 30 cm TL, females at ca. 32 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Argus wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually in groups (Ref. 90102) in shallow coastal reefs and seagrass flats (Ref. 9710), also in algae-rocky reef flats and lagoons (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Argyripnus atlanticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pseudoceanic and benthopelagic species (Ref. 4462) found off oceanic islands and banks (Ref. 4739).  Feeds on unidentified crustaceans (Ref. 4739).  Spawning season unknown (Ref. 4739).

species.name: Argyripnus electronus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from seamounts (Ref. 31826).

species.name: Argyripnus pharos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species captured near the seafloor by bottom trawl (ref. 75774).

species.name: Argyrocottus zanderi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sea-well beds.

species.name: Argyropelecus olfersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mesopelagic with adults and juveniles at 200-800 m by day and 100 (sometimes shallower)-600 m by night, pre-metamorphic larvae at 100-300 m.  Adults and juveniles make short diel vertical migrations.  Dioecious, adult photophore complement acquired at about 16-17 mm SL (Ref. 4739).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Argyrosomus beccus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arhynchobatis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 26346). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Arinos cory
species.description: Most inhabits lotic environment in the rio Arinos and its tributaries. The rio Arinos is characterized by muddy-brown color and soft bottom of clay and sand.  Collected mostly in small forest streams of black or clear water, or in marginal ponds (Ref. 102660).

species.name: Ariomma brevimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesobenthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Considered rare but sometimes taken in large quantities by purse seine off Japan (Ref. 12862).

species.name: Ariomme brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters, usually on soft bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans (Ref. 3547).  Larvae and young are epipelagic, adults demersal or benthopelagic (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Ariomme grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs chiefly on the continental shelf, mostly on muddy bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Juveniles occur in surface waters.  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans.  Forms large schools (Ref. 36543).  Adults are demersal or bathypelagic (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Ariomme indienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small schools in areas with muddy substrates on the continental shelf and upper slope.  Feeds mainly on zooplankton.  Appears to be pelagic at night and demersal by day and may migrate seasonally.  Marketed fresh or dried-salted (Ref. 3300).

species.name: Ariomme pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults caught in shrimp grounds and deeper shelf areas, but occurrence is sporadic.  Juveniles inhabit offshore surface waters, especially around floating weeds.  Adults may be restricted to continental margins of the western Atlantic with juveniles found in the Caribbean expatriated from these populations (Ref. 51183).  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans.  An excellent food fish  (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Ariommid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariopsis canteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in costal marine and brackish waters; and sometimes entering freshwaters (Ref. 116660).

species.name: Ariosoma bauchotae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma kannani
species.description: This species is probably widespread in the east coast of India, but rare in catch (Ref. 130865).

species.name: Ariosoma majus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widespread in sandy areas.  A carnivore that feeds on fish and crabs (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Ariosoma meeki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma multivertebratum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma obud
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma ophidiophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma opistophthalmum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently a rare species. No biological data known (Ref. 57911).

species.name: Ariosoma sanzoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma sazonovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma selenops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma sereti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ariosoma shiroanago
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells on the shelf and shelf edge; usually on rough sand bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Ariosoma sokotranum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aristochromis christyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in places where rock and sand form an intermediate biotope.  Females which are solitary like males can enter the male's territory found among rocks, and spawn (Ref. 5595).  Feed on fish fry (Ref. 267).  When feeding, it turns on its side to place its large, laterally compressed jaws into rocky cracks where it captures small fish that are sheltering there (Ref. 6307).

species.name: Aristostomias grimaldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 27000).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Aristostomias lunifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4469).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Aristostomias polydactylus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Aristostomias xenostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius acutirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably of minor interest to fisheries.

species.name: Arius brunellii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius burmanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwaters and tidal rivers.

species.name: Arius cous
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius festinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius leptonotacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius macracanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius macronotacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly occurs in brackish waters (Ref. 58022).

species.name: Arius malabaricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius manillensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius nudidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arius uncinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arkansas darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs over mud in spring-fed vegetated headwaters and creeks.

species.name: Arkansas River shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing water over sand in creeks and small to large rivers.

species.name: Arkansas saddled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep, fast gravel and rubble riffles of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Armenian mountain cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Armitagei’s striped rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to shaded streams in the inland rain forests in southwest Sri Lanka (Ref. 123756).

species.name: Armored pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over muddy bottom.  Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch (Ref. 205).

species.name: Armored searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on the continental slope.

species.name: Armorhead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep records for this species is anomalous and must be regarded as questionable (Ref. 6793).

species.name: Armour croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Armour eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected off muddy bottoms (Ref. 92840); shallow depth (13.4 m) from Vietnam (Ref. 129446).

species.name: Armoured blenny
species.description: Occurs on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Armoured cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the shelf and shelf edge (Ref. 11230).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Armoured flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom (Ref. 75154) of the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Armoured gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater species.  Occurs on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563).  Bony scutes reduce commercial value (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Armoured sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Feeds mainly on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Armourhead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnaz's damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered fringing reefs, usually in bays at depths between about 3-20 m. They usually occur in small aggregations and is closely associated with branching formations of live coral, particularly Acropora spp. and the pocilloporid Seriatopora hystrix. This species hover a short distance above the substratum, presumably feeding on zooplankton (Ref. 84037). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Arno goby
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found only in freshwater, in shallow, well vegetated shores of small to medium-size streams with moderate flow (over pebble beds, Ref. 26100).  Spawns from the first time at 1 year; in May to June; females may repeat spawning during this season.  Adhesive eggs deposited between stones, shells and aquatic plants and males guard the eggs until hatching.  When spawning and defending the nest, males produce sounds (Ref. 59043).  Exhibits territoriality during breeding season.  Feeds on a wide variety of invertebrates.  A short-lived species which is threatened due to habitat destruction and pollution.  (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Arnoglosse de Kessler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper part of the continental shelf.  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates.  Breeding period between May and August (Ref. 4704).

species.name: Arnoglosse de Méditerranée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live on mixed or muddy bottoms.  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 4704).

species.name: Arnoglosse de Rüppell
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from 85-550 m (Ref. 04704) and from 288-897 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates.  Spawn during autumn in the Mediterranean.

species.name: Arnoglosse du cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud (Ref. 2683), sand and shell bottoms (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Arnoglosse imperial
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, mud, shell and corals (Ref. 27121).  Caught with bottom and pelagic trawls (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Arnoglosse tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper 100 m of the continental shelf.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 4704). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 52678 but has been caught in depths inferior to 10m (Ref. 57407).

species.name: Arnoglossus andrewsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus armstrongi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus boops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus coeruleosticta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus grohmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus kotthausi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus marisrubri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus micrommatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus multirastris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus nigrifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Arnoglossus sayaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus scapha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus septemventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnoglossus yamanakai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arnold's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary swamps and swampy parts of smaller brooks in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Aron's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral reefs.  Secretive (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Arothron carduus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arothron gillbanksii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arrose lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit continental slopes of all southern continents (Ref. 6545).  Adults found near the bottom; juveniles near the surface, usually in association with krill (Ref. 5194).  Feed mainly on salps (Ref. 27150).  Eggs float near the sea surface and larvae also inhabit surface waters (Ref. 6390).  There is no vertical migration during the day or night (Ref. 27150).

species.name: Arrose noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found close to the sea bed in deep water.  Form large shoals over rough ground near pinnacles and canyons.  Juveniles are pelagic and inhabit oceanic waters.  They tend to be dispersed over smooth grounds (Ref. 6390).  Feed mainly on salps and benthic crustaceans (Ref. 27150).  Eggs float near the sea surface and larvae also inhabit surface waters (Ref. 6390).  Based on trawl catch rates, there is no evidence of vertical migration during day or night (Ref. 27150).

species.name: Arrow blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 5521).  Drifts with bended tail to prey on small fish.  Retreats into holes or empty worm tubes.  Ignores divers (Ref. 9710).  Often seen with schools of  masked gobies (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Arrow bulleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In sheltered reefs in moderate depths, usually in caves or under coral plates (Ref. 48635); may also be found in rocky and open areas. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Arrow cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used in behavioral research (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Arrow darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on mayfly nymphs (heptageniids, baetids), blackfly and midge larvae, and lesser numbers of caddisfly, stonefly, and beetle larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Arrow dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on the bottom along coastlines and in estuaries and the lower courses of rivers.  Feed on worms, zooplankton, and phytoplankton.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Arrow goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand or mud bottom. Retreats into shrimp burrows when threatened and at low tide (Ref. 6885). Commonly in estuaries, lagoons and tidal sloughs. Reported to occur in freshwater. Adults feeds on diatoms, green algae, tintinnids, eggs and young of their hosts (Ref. 6885). Positions large food particles near crabs to be torn to smaller pieces (Ref. 6885). Preyed upon by Sebastes, staghorn sculpin, whitespot greenling, and terns (Ref. 6885). Unlike other gobies, it does not build a nest or care for its young (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Arrow stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits patches of sand around coral reefs, seagrass beds, boulders and pilings.  Avoids open beaches.

species.name: Arrow wriggler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs, probably on sand bottoms in 10-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Arrowhead shovelnose
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arrowhead soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in steep slopes of coral rich areas.  Usually hovers in mid water in caves (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 4326).  Secretive and solitary (Ref. 37816). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Easily missed and normally the yellow spot is noticed first (Ref. 48635).  Produces the skin toxin grammistin.

species.name: Arrowhead triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 106682.

species.name: Arrowtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, meso- (Ref. 6525) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Arrowtooth fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on characters common to the family, this species is oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Only record is of 2 specimens collected from 1919 by dynamite from Jolo Island, Philippines (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Arrowtooth grenadier
species.description: Feeds on shrimp-like crustacean and squid (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Arrowtooth lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Inhabits sandy bottoms close to rock or coral outcrops.  In New Zealand, frequently seen in pairs (Ref. 9818).

species.name: Arroyo chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms of flowing pools and runs of headwaters creeks and small to medium rivers.  Often found in intermittent streams (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Arroyo cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in fast moving water of the rocky upper river valleys.  Feeds on aufwuchs, from which it gets nourishment from algae and invertebrates.

species.name: Arrête-nef
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant remora in warm waters (Ref. 4389).  Occurs near as well as far from the coast (Ref. 5217).  Often found free-swimming in shallow inshore areas and around coral reefs (Ref. 26938).  Attaches temporarily to a variety of hosts including sharks, rays, large bony fishes or sea turtles, whales, dolphins and also to ships.  May follow divers (Ref. 9710); reported to attach itself to a diver's leg (Ref. 57809).  Feeds on small fishes, bits of its host's prey and host's parasites (Ref. 26938).  Juveniles occasionally act as reef station-based cleaners, where they service parrotfishes (Ref. 40095).  Sometimes used by natives to aid in fishing; a line is tied to the caudal peduncle of the remora and then is released; upon attaching to another fish, the remora and its host are hauled in by the fisher (Ref. 9682).

species.name: Arselet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in fresh waters, estuaries and coastal seas (Ref. 4119).  Anadromous, with numerous non-anadromous populations in brackish or pure freshwater, rarely in marine waters.  In the sea, confined to coastal waters.  In freshwater, adults prefer to live in small stream but may occur in a variety of habitats including lakes and large rivers (Ref. 59043).  Inhabit shallow vegetated areas, usually over mud or sand (Ref. 5723).  Form schools.  Young associated with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Juveniles move to the sea (anadromous populations) or to deeper, larger water bodies (freshwater populations) in July-August, forming large feeding schools (Ref. 59043).  Feed on worms, crustaceans, larvae and adult aquatic insects, drowned aerial insects, and small fishes; has also been reported to feed on their own fry and eggs (Ref. 1998).  Eggs are found in nests constructed from plant material (Ref. 41678).  Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).  Maximum length in freshwater is 8 cm while in saltwater is 11 cm (Ref. 35388).  Occasionally taken commercially in Scandinavia and processed into fishmeal and oil (Ref. 28219, 28964).  Commonly used as a laboratory animal (Ref. 1998).  A large bibliography is available at www.geocities.com/CapeCanaveral/Hall/1345/stickbibl.html.

species.name: Arsuz bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artedidraco glareobarbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artedidraco mirus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sublittoral and on continental shelf from 18-320 m, with maximum abundance at less than 200 m.  Main food consists of  mysids , with substantial amounts of errant polychaetes, gammaridean amphipods and some unidentified polychaetes; to a lesser extent, isopods (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Artedidraco orianae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sublittoral and continental shelf.  Feeds mainly on gammaridean amphipods, with substantial amounts of errant polychaetes.  Isopods were a minor food item.

species.name: Artedidraco shackletoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sublittoral and continental shelf.  Adults feed mainly on polychaetes and to a lesser extent, isopods (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Artediellina antilope
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artedielloides auriculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artediellus aporosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artediellus camchaticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length type refers to body length.

species.name: Artediellus dydymovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Artediellus fuscimentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Artediellus gomojunovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arthurs galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on rocky shores, particularly man-made rock piles at construction sites, and to a lesser extent among aquatic vegetation near these areas.  Also inhabits lacustrine environments near the shore among rocks or vegetation; occurs in pools of outlet streams (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on midge and caddisfly larvae, amphipods, other crustaceans and worms.

species.name: Aru gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits large rivers as well as small tributaries.  Prefers well-vegetated stream margins with soft mud bottom.  Feeds on insects, crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=10, 26°C water temperature, carnivore, egg layer, needs plant and rock cover, not easy for beginning aquarists (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Aru rainbowfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality on Trangan Island lies in a luxuriant rainforest on the downstream side of a spectacular 75 m-long limestone tunnel.  The stream has about 10-12 m width, 0.5-2.0 m depth and relatively clear and slow-flowing water with a rocky limestone bottom and abundant cover mainly in the form of submerged fallen tree limbs.  Another location on Kobroor Island where the species occurs is also lined by luxuriant forest and has 15-20 m width, 1-3 m depth, and clear and slow flowing water.  The margins of the channel are composed of abundant, partially submerged
terrestrial plants, which offered abundant shelter for small fishes (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Aruana toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Arulius barb
species.description: Inhabits large streams, rivers and lakes (Ref. 41236). Omnivorous, peaceful and schooling (Ref. 57467).

species.name: Arunachal barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asarcenchelys longimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ascension triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rockpools (4 m diameter) and among rocks covered in coralline algae at 2 m depth (Ref. 86997).

species.name: Aseraggodes andersoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes auroculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from steep sloping bottoms dominated by coral rubble (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes beauforti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes brevirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with rotenone from base of a drop-off and adjoining sand and rubble, with numerous caves at base and in reef (Ref. 57561).

species.name: Aseraggodes cheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes corymbus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes cyaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes cyclurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand at the entrance to a cave and on a steep rubble and sand slope (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes diringeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from clear water in a coral-reef environment; the deepest from sand beneath a ledge in 35 m depth (Ref. 57561).

species.name: Aseraggodes dubius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes filiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes heraldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer reef flats (Ref. 56490).

species.name: Aseraggodes holcomi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand near reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Aseraggodes jenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes kaianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore sand slopes and estuaries, occurs in small groups.  Often seen out during the day and sometimes crawling over reef (Ref. 48637).  Found in sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Aseraggodes kimurai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No information available re its type locality nor on method of capture (Ref. 75879).

species.name: Aseraggodes kobensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Aseraggodes kruppi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from sand in an isolated patch reef about 3 m in diameter, about 100 m from shore on the sheltered east side of a small island near the coast of Saudi Arabia and it was about 15 m from the steep outer-reef slope (Ref. 95111).

species.name: Aseraggodes lateralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rock and sand bottom of a protected bay and steep rocky slope with no sand (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes lenisquamis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand in bays (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes macronasus
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from sand or sand and rubble substrata near or within coral reefs.  It is typically hidden in sand by day, but active at night, may move from sand to rock or
coral, however, it quickly retires to sand if alarmed. Skin toxin present and may be used for repelling attacks (Ref. 95111).

species.name: Aseraggodes magnoculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a steep slope of a fringing reef, with coral rock, rubble and sand at base (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes martine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes microlepidotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Saleh Bay, Sumbawa I., Lesser Sunda Is., Indonesia, 8°19'S, 117°41'E, Siboga station, 312, 274 m (Ref. 9893).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Aseraggodes nigrocirratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
