species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes pelvicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes ramsaii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy bottom (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Aseraggodes sinusarabici
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes steinitzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aseraggodes texturatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Aseraggodes umbratilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ash Meadows killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly found in warm spring (Ref. 86798). Reported to attain a maximum length of 5.9 cm SL (Ref. 12193).

species.name: Ashy darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky pools with current in small to medium rivers, usually near vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Asian bumblebee catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and streams (Ref. 12693).  Found in the basin wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Feeds on aquatic insect larvae, including odonatans.  Adult females captured in February had well-developed ova.  Spawning takes place at the beginning of the rainy season, with the young appearing in fishing nets during August.  Market fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Asian butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky areas and coral reefs.  Often in pairs or groups (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Asian lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. FishBase common name coined by authors.

species.name: Asian pencil halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters estuaries and freshwater.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Asian redtail catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in most habitat types, but most frequent in large muddy rivers, with slow current and soft bottom (Ref. 27732).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Feeds on exogenous insects, aquatic insect larvae, shrimps, other crustaceans and fishes.  Moves into flooded forests to spawn and the young are usually first seen in August.  In Tonlé Sap (Cambodia),  maximum numbers are found as it returns to rivers in November and December.  A highly priced aquarium fish.  Usually marketed fresh (Ref. 12693). High in nutritive values especially omega-3 fatty acids (EPA, DHA) (Ref. 53337).

species.name: Asian swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams to lowland wetlands (Ref. 57235) often occurring in ephemeral waters (Ref. 44894).  Adults are found in medium to large rivers, flooded fields and stagnant waters including sluggish flowing canals (Ref. 12975, 12693), in streamlets and estuaries (Ref. 41236).  Benthic (Ref. 58302), burrowing in moist earth in dry season surviving for long periods without water (Ref 2686). Occasionally dug out in old taro fields, in Hawaii, long after the field has been drained; more frequently observed in stream clearing operations using heavy equipment to remove large amounts of silt and vegetation where the eels are hidden (Ref. 44091).  Nocturnal predators devouring fishes, worms, crustaceans, and other small aquatic animals (Ref. 44091); also feed on detritus.  Are protandrous hermaphrodites. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205). Marketed fresh and can be kept alive for long periods of time as long as the skin is kept moist (Ref. 12693).  Good flesh (Ref. 2686).  Important fisheries throughout Southeast Asia (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Askoldia variegata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asoka barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in relatively deep (1-2 m) fast-flowing water, in areas with gravel or sand substrates.  Juveniles (1-3cm TL) shoal together in schools of 30-100 individuals in very shallow water (5-25 cm), downstream.  Adults occupy deeper water (1-2m), upstream.  Usually occupies unshaded areas.  Fast swimmers and not easily identified from water surface.  Declining numbers due to intensive fishing by fish exporters.

species.name: Aspasma minima
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky shores with brown algae.

species.name: Aspasmichthys ciconiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and under boulders in the subtidal zone.

species.name: Aspasmodes briggsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspasmogaster occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspe
species.description: Occur in open water of large and medium-sized lowland rivers and large lakes (Ref. 59043). Adults inhabit lower reaches of rivers and estuaries (Ref. 30578). Prefer to stay near bridge pillars, near tributaries, under weirs, in deep currents and overgrown parts of river and in quiet bays of river bends (Ref. 9696). One of the rare cyprinids which is piscivore; also prey on small aquatic birds. Juveniles are gregarious predators while adults hunt in small groups or are solitary. Juveniles and adults feed mainly on fish, especially on Alburnus alburnus or Osmerus eperlanus (Ref. 59043). Migrate upstream in tributaries for spawning in April-June (Ref. 556, 30578). Spawn in fast-flowing water on gravel or submerged vegetation. Lake populations migrate to tributaries; semi-anadromous populations or individuals (Terek) forage mainly in estuaries and freshened parts of the sea, migrating to rivers only for spawning. Begins spawning migration in second half of October (Terek) and overwinters in the lower reaches of river. Hybridizes with Leuciscus idus. Threatened due to alteration of river morphology (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Aspidoras eurycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspidoras kiriri
species.description: Found in streams crossing the Atlantic Forest, at 244-303 meters above sea level, on rocky beds with sand and organic debris, from small and large pools below the rapids (Ref. 129224).

species.name: Aspidoras marianae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a slow-flowing stream with clear water and a sandy bottom with mud, leaf litter, submerged logs, and some aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 114781).

species.name: Aspidoras menezesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspidoras microgalaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspidoras spilotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspidoras taurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aspistor hardenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy, shallow coastal waters and tidal rivers (Ref. 40908).

species.name: Asprete
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing, cold and clear mountain streams.  Usually hidden under stones.  Active at night (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on larvae of rheophilic insects, mainly mayflies and stoneflies (Ref. 26173).  Territorial.  Spawns possibly in second half of May.  Deposits 120-150 eggs under stones (Ref. 59043). On the edge of extinction due to deforestation, construction of roads, extraction of stones and dam constructions (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Asprocottus intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asprocottus korjakovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asprocottus minor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asprocottus parmiferus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asprocottus platycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asprocottus pulcher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asquamiceps caeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Asquamiceps longmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Assamese snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs both in running and standing waters (Ref. 4833).  Found in ponds and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Assessor randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reef gullies.  Usually hovering at hole entrances.  Strikingly nervous.  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Assiculus punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300) and weed bed areas; usually in relatively silty waters at depths up to 30 m.  A secretive species usually found at highly eroded limestone reef and rocks (Ref. 37748).

species.name: Assiette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small shoals on rough, rock, gravel, or pebble bottoms.  Generally keeps far from the shore, near the bottom, mostly between 150 and 450 m in the northeastern Atlantic, and between 18 and 550 m in the northwestern Atlantic.  Occurs at a temperature range of 0°-10° C (Ref. 9988).  Solitary or in small groups.  Feeds on crustaceans and shellfishes, benthic fishes (flatfishes and gurnard) and even on starfishes.  Preyed upon by seals (Ref. 9988).  Sold fresh, frozen as fillets or dried salted.  Eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Assiette atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found near the bottom (Ref. 4233, 57392).  Occasionally enters lagoons and estuaries, especially during juvenile stage (Ref. 57392).  Juveniles occur in surface waters often near bays and river mouths (Ref. 4233).  Form schools (Ref. 4233, 57392).  Feed on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Astatotilapia burtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow streams, river mouths, shallow parts of lake near rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Astatotilapia desfontainii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astatotilapia flaviijosephi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in shallow water among stones and vegetation in lakes, ponds and streams (Ref. 13609).  Females feed mainly on chironomid larvae, oligochaetes and amphipods while the diet of larger males consists mainly of gastropods (Ref. 13609).  Breeds from April to July (Ref. 13609).  Maternal mouthbrooder and juveniles are released at 8-9 mm TL (Ref. 13609).

species.name: Astatotilapia stappersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Astatotilapia swynnertoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astatotilapia tchadensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Lake Boukou with emergent aquatic vegetation, mainly Cyperus laevigatus, Typha australis and Phragmites australis, covering approximately the two-thirds of the lake's surface; submerged macrophyte beds include Potamogeton (Ref. 112399).

species.name: Astatotilapia tweddlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swampy lakes and slow streams (Ref. 4967). The maximum length of 110 cm given by Eccles (1992) [Ref. 4967] is apparently a mistake, maybe for 11.0 cm.

species.name: Asterophysus batrachus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asterropteryx profunda
species.description: Occurs on gently sloping, sandy bottoms at about 65 m. In Lembeh Strait, habitat consisted of black volcanic sand exposed to considerable current, whereas in Lawadi,  the bottom was silty sand with little noticeable water movement. It was not previously noticed because of its small size and occurrence in relatively deep waters; more likely to be widely distributed in the East Indian region (Ref. 126739).

species.name: Asterropteryx striata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble bottoms in lagoons and sheltered coastal reefs.  Typically hovers a short distance above the bottom, apparently to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 31115). Solitary or in small group (Ref 90102).

species.name: Astourion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphihaline and anadromous fish (Ref. 51346, 51439), frequenting littoral zones (Ref. 2163, 51439, 51442). A long-lived and slow-growing species (Ref. 9988). It lives the major part of his life in sea but enters rivers for reproduction (Ref. 30578, 51442). Found on various substrates, from sand to rocks (Ref. 51346). At the sea, it occurs in coastal and estuarine zones. In freshwaters, it inhabits estuaries and large rivers (Ref. 59043). Juveniles found both in estuaries and in the sea (Ref. 2163), they slowly adapt to saltwater (Ref. 89103) and usually spend around 2-3 years in river estuaries before moving to the sea (Ref. 40152), some may migrate to the sea during their first summer (Ref. 59043). Usually solitary. Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, polychaete worms and small fish. Today most males only reach 100-150 cm length, females 130-215 cm (Ref. 59043, 89104). Utilized fresh and frozen, and also for caviar; eaten steamed, pan-fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988). A threatened species, mainly due to bycatch, poaching, habitat degradation (spawning grounds, nursery areas) and physical obstacles to migration (Ref. 26160).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection locality is around 1135 m above sea level, rio dos Couros in that point has moderate riparian vegetation and it is typically between 10 and 15 m wide, and 1.5 m deep. Although presenting some rapids, the water is clear, the substrate has stones, rocks, and some stretches with mud. Most of the specimens were collected on the stretch downstream from the waterfall, a few specimens on the stretch upstream of waterfall. Only 4 species were collected syntopically with A. courensis: Characidium stigmosum, C. aff. zebra, Gymnotocinclus anosteos and Trichomycterus sp. The stomach contents of five specimens consisted of Plecoptera, Trichoptera, Chironomidae (Diptera), authochthonous and allochthonous insects, and digested vegetal organic matter; these stomachs were partially full (Ref. 84461).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection locality is around 1135 m above sea level and the rio dos Couros in that point has moderate riparian vegetation, typically between 10 and 15 m wide, and 1.5 m deep.  Although with some rapids, the water is clear, the substrate composed of stones, rocks, and some stretches with mud.  A natural 10 m high waterfall named Cachoeira São Bento is located downriver and all topotypes were collected on the stretch downstream from the waterfall in a small stream draining directly into the river (about 100 m from the channel river).  This stream is about 0.8 m deep and 6 m wide, transparent water with moderate vegetation covering the channel (trees and shrubs), and bottom with small stones, submerged logs and roots.  No other fish species was collected with this species in the stream. The rio dos Couros has several waterfalls, some with about 100 m height (Cachoeira de São Vicente and Catarata dos Couros). Stomach contents of five specimens with fragments of allochthonous insect, fish scales, and vegetal organic matter (leaf parts) and the stomachs were not full (Ref. 84461).

Syntopic with Astyanax brachypterygium, ustraloheros sp., Cnesterodon brevirostratus, Eurycheilichthys sp., Jenynsia eirmostigma, Pareiorhaphis hystrix, Rhamdia sp., and Trichomycterus tropeiro (Ref. 94017).

species.description: Found in creeks with muddy, stony or sandy substrates, surrounded by grass and coffee plantations (Ref. 120347).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astyanax totae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in headwater stream with clear water, light to moderate water current and bottom consisting of stones, sand and moderate amount of vegetal debris (Ref. 56783).  Feeds most frequently on microcrustaceans (Cladocera and Copepoda), insect larvae (Chironomidae), adult insects and plant fragments (Ref. 56783).

species.name: Astyanax trierythropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astyanax utiariti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a large river which has several waterfalls, with crystalline water, segments with rapids, a well developed riparian vegetation and a substrate of stones, rocks and sand (Ref. 75035).  Occurs along the left bank of the river in semilentic stretches (Ref. 75035).

species.name: Astyanax validus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually captured upstream.  Appears to stay in groups, in creeks with alternating zones of rapidly flowing waters with sandy bottoms and calm waters with silty bottoms (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Astyanax varii
species.description: Found in lower basins with depths of 1.8 meters, bordered by aquatic vegetation and trees, with rocky, muddy or sandy substrates (Ref. 129191).

species.name: Astyanax varzeae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits headwater stream with clear water, light to moderate current and bottom consisting of stones, sand and moderate amount of vegetal debris (Ref. 72395).

species.name: Astyanax venezuelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astyanax vermilion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water streams, running over rocky, pebbles and sand bottom at low altitudes ranging from 188 to 258 m, with slow to moderate water current and less than 1 m deep (Ref. 81202).  Stomach contents of three specimens include filamentous algae, fragments of vascular plants and seeds, insects and other unidentified arthropods, and organic debris (Ref. 81202).

species.name: Astyanax villwocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Astyanax yariguies
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Asymbolus parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Asymbolus rubiginosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Asymmetrical deep-water clingfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in relatively cool water in an area with temporary upwelling along the northern coast of 
Papua New Guinea and in association with sunken logs; its specializations and especially the lateral asymmetry may be useful to be attached to these logs (Ref. 117884).

species.name: Asymmetrical goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits sandy or weed covered areas.  A good food fish.  Depth estimate based on its ecology.

species.name: Atacama grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atara nato - oneone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 9710) found in lagoon and seaward reefs.  Adults usually under coral heads or in caves, while juveniles are found in shallow lagoons.  Feeds on crustaceans and mollusks.  Generally marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Ataxolepis apus
species.description: All known specimens are males.

species.name: Ataxolepis henactis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum size Eschmeyer, pers. comm.

species.name: Ateleopus edentatus
species.description: Occur over sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 122089).

species.name: Ateleopus purpureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Ateleopus tanabensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherina lopeziana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in littoral inshore waters (Ref. 4499).

species.name: Atherinella beani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella chagresi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers of low to high current velocity, between 8 and 60 m elevation.  Swims in schools near the surface of the water.  An active fish that captures terrestrial and aquatic insects, but also eats filamentous algae and diatoms (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Atherinella colombiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella guija
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers (Ref. 6858).  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects as well as algae (Ref. 6858).

species.name: Atherinella jiloaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella meeki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella milleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the coast and in estuaries, may ascend rivers (Ref. 6858).  Feeds on crustaceans, terrestrial and aquatic insects, and diatoms (Ref. 6858).

species.name: Atherinella nocturna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella pallida
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella robbersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atherinella sardina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes (Ref. 6858).  Feeds on insects (Ref. 6858).

species.name: Atherinella venezuelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Athi elephant-snout fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Athi sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found mainly over sandy beaches (Ref. 30558). It might become important in dams (Ref. 4967). It is a shoaling fish (Ref. 30558). Little is known about its ecology, except that it is an insectivore (Ref. 30558). The juvenile distribution suggests that breeding perhaps occurs in shallow areas, especially flooded pools at river edges, some of which are seasonal (Ref. 30558).

species.name: Athérine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A very euryhaline species, where adults are frequently found in brackish waters and more sporadically in freshwater (Ref. 3788), preferring still or slow flowing waters in freshwater (Ref. 59043).  They are found in lower parts of rivers, estuaries, coastal lakes and sea; pelagic in lakes (Ref. 59043).  Adults occur in great schools.  They are carnivorous, feeding on small crustaceans, worms, mollusks (Ref. 5980) and fish larvae (Ref. 35388) in lakes and estuaries, and on benthos in rivers (Ref. 59043).  Can usually live 1 to 2 years, rarely up to 4 years.  Some populations undergo spawning migrations into estuaries.  Mature individuals are fractional spawners, larger individuals spawn for a longer period.  Eggs are demersal, with long hairy appendages attaching them to the substrate consisting of filamentous algae, often at depths of 2 to 6 m.  Larvae are pelagic often forming schools close to the shores (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Athérine argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms small schools in shallow bays and near coastal reefs (Ref. 9273).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36497).  Eggs are presumably attached to spawning substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 36497).

species.name: Athérine brillante
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Athérine brésilienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms, in brackish or hypersaline littoral lagoons and protected areas of the open sea.

species.name: Athérine charale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 9273).

species.name: Athérine chilienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools. Is mainly diurnal. Feeds primarily on the eggs of Engraulis ringens (Ref. 9120).

species.name: Athérine d'Argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal lagoons and near estuaries, usually in freshwater (Ref. 27363, 59043). Gregarious. Adults feed on zooplankton. Mature adults spawn for the first time at 1-2 years. Eggs are deposited among aquatic vegetation (Ref. 59043). Maximum length estimated from the fact that the congeneric Odontesthes incisa has a common length of 10 cm TL. This species is a cool water predator that has affected the abundance of other species native to the lakes (Ref. 1739). The fisheries has now flourished especially in lakes and reservoirs, in Peru, Argentina, southern Brazil and Chile.

species.name: Athérine de Barnes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons and along shorelines of outlying islands (Ref. 3302).  During daylight, schooling fish may be periodically seen to jump out of the water to avoid predators.  They are also easily attracted to light.  The fish are gravid at about 4-4.5 cm SL by July in the northern hemisphere.  Because of their large numbers, they are probably important as forage food for larger fishes (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Athérine de plage
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Athérine delta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy bottoms of coastal areas, estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 9273).  Adults feed on crustaceans, gastropods, and may take in sand (Ref. 9273).

species.name: Athérine des récifs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Caught with dip nets, with the help of artificial lights.  Occurs in large schools in shallow waters (Ref. 26938)

species.name: Athérine du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools along the coast and in estuaries, especially during spring (Ref. 3302).  Also found in coastal lakes (Ref. 7248).  Small individuals filter out small organisms such as phytoplankton and rotifers.  Above 3.5 cm TL, it feeds mostly on crustaceans especially amphipods taken from the water column as well as off the bottom.  Preyed upon by fishes and birds (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Athérine grasdeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore areas, including bays (Ref. 2850).  Form schools (Ref. 2850).  Demersal spawners in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).  Oviparous, with planktonic, primarily neustonic larvae (Ref. 36497).  Eggs are attached to one another by spawning substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 36497).  Sold fresh (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Athérine grognon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in bays, muddy and rocky areas and kelp beds, also in estuaries (Ref. 36497).  Form schools.  Adults feed on zooplankton (Ref. 9273), while juveniles feed on algae and kelp fly larvae (Ref. 4930).  Demersal spawner in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).  Oviparous, with planktonic, primarily neustonic larvae (Ref. 36497).  Eggs are attached to spawning substrate and to one another by adhesive filaments (Ref. 36497).

species.name: Athérine guatémaltéque
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in fresh and brackish waters, such as in rivers, estuaries, and coastal lagoons (Ref. 9273).

species.name: Athérine lacunaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy bottoms in lagoons or bays with brackish or hyper-saline waters (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Athérine landia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms small schools (Ref. 9273).

species.name: Athérine lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in estuaries and sometimes penetrates rivers (Ref. 9273).  Food consists mainly of terrestrial insects and fruit (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Athérine mexicaine
species.description: Found along sandy coasts (Ref. 9273).

species.name: Athérine museau piquant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Unlikely to be used for human consumption, possibly used as bait.

species.name: Athérine népente
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in surf zone and upper water column near shore along the open coast and in bays (Ref. 36497).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36497).

species.name: Athérine panaméenne
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Athérine samoan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in coastal waters and harbors within its range.  Important as food for larger commercial fishes (Ref. 9760).  Used as bait in the tuna fishery (Ref. 6822).

species.name: Athérine tropicale
species.description: Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 3302); broadly distributed throughout mangrove estuaries to the open coast (Ref. 93954). Occurs in schools along calm shorelines (Ref. 37816).  Important as forage food species to larger commercial fish and as bait fish (Ref. 3302).

species.name: Athérine tête-dure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms as well as in coral reefs (Ref. 5217).  Often in large schools (Ref. 5521).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Athérine têtue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in large schools along sandy shorelines and reef margins.  Reported to be mainly a nocturnal species which usually forms schools (from several hundred to more than 100 m long and 20 m wide) (Ref. 9760).  Feeds mostly at night when the school disperse.  Feeds on a variety of planktonic crustaceans.  Preyed upon by sharks, tunas, long toms, and amberjacks which swim alongside the school.  Among its other predators are crested terns, gannets, sea-gulls and herons.  Slow moving and not well regarded as bait.   Extremely important as forage fish for larger species (Ref. 3302).  Sold fresh, or salted and dried (Ref. 12484).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Athérine à dos bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations near reefs (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Athérine à nez râpeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually caught offshore in depths of less than 2 m.  Used as food for larger commercial species and possibly as bait.

species.name: Athérine écailleuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations in shallow bays and coastal reefs (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Atlantic barracudina
species.description: Oceanic species (Ref. 26340) occurring from the surface (young) to about 1,000 m depth (Ref. 4473).

species.name: Atlantic batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud or sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 26999).  Benthic adults are luminous (Ref. 40826).  Feeds chiefly on polychaetes; bottom-living amphipods, bivalve molluscs, brittle stars, starfishes and sea spiders (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Atlantic bigeye sixgill shark
species.description: Found on continental and insular slopes. Feeds mainly on bony fishes and cephalopods, sometimes on crustaceans  Viviparous, with 13 to 26 young in a litter. Size at birth measures to about 40-45 cm TL (Ref. 125614). It was reported that there is likely some stratification of the distribution by size, presumably with larger individuals present in deeper waters (mostly adult captured in the Bahamas at an average depth of 639.5 m) than the juveniles (< 350 m in Belize and northern Gulf of Mexico). Resource and habitat partitioning between juvenile and much larger adult bluntnose sixgill sharks has been suggested as predation avoidance (Ref. 117400).

species.name: Atlantic blackwing flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton. Eggs demersal. No importance to fisheries (Ref. 109257)..

species.name: Atlantic cornetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species (Ref. 27000).  Occurs over rocky bottoms in shallow inshore waters.  Feeds mainly on small fishes (Ref. 6554).

species.name: Atlantic fanfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives down to a depth of 400 m (Ref. 35388).  Seasonal migrant (Ref. 6697).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 94863.

species.name: Atlantic fangjaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Exhibit diel vertical migrations, juveniles and adults mainly at 300-600 by day and at 50-200 by night (Ref. 4463, 58302).  Feed on copepods and euphausiids (Ref. 4769).  Photophores developing in fishes over 12-20 mm SL (Ref. 4769).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35800).

species.name: Atlantic flashlightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep drop-offs (Ref. 7251).  Observed only on moonless nights (Ref. 9710).  Moves to deep water during the day and ascends to near top of drop-offs at night (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Atlantic footballfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwarf males of 4 cm length apparently do not become parasitically attached to females.

species.name: Atlantic knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantic pearlside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantic pelagic basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals 7.5 cm SL and longer mostly occur in the boreal areas, while those less than this the length occur in the tropical areas (Ref. 87004).  Maximum length reported in Ref. 87004:  11 cm TL.

species.name: Atlantic pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Width 19.6 cm (Ref. 13608).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atlantic Roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantic sabretooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 7300, 58302).  Feeds on fish and sepia by preferring the latter (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Atlantic sawtail cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 540 m (Ref. 26282).

species.name: Atlantic scombrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly caught by anglers at depths between 200-610 m.

species.name: Atlantic thornyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Atlantic triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantirivulus depressus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus guanabarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantirivulus haraldsiolii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus janeiroensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus jurubatibensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality near the lagoon, to Lagoa do Pires, is part of a series of lagoons close to the sea, isolated from river basins.  It is an open area of Restinga vegetation, the swamp dense with aquatic vegetation, clear and acidic (pH 5.28) water (Ref. 78703).

species.name: Atlantirivulus lazzarotoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atlantirivulus luelingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus maricensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in creek under a forest remnant and in small shallow stream, partially protected by a secondary forest remnant (Ref. 102354).

species.name: Atlantirivulus nudiventris
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus paranaguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow swamps and channels connected to small streams, within dense forest areas, in small river basins flowing into the Paranaguá bay.  The water of the sampling area is light yellow or tea-like colored and the habitat bottom is composed of litter (Ref. 102354).

species.name: Atlantirivulus ribeirensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow streams, 10 cm deep or less, within or close to dense forests of the Ribeira de Iguape river basin.  These streams are characterized by light yellow or tea-like colored water.  The bottom is composed of litter and sand.  This is the only fish encountered in these streams (Ref. 102354).

species.name: Atlantirivulus riograndensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is located in an open vegetation at the boarder of a forest and is a shallow pool, about 5-10 cm deep, with orangish hyaline water (Ref. 81223). A female-biased sex ratio (2.38 : 1, female : male) has been reported for this species (Ref. 92020).

species.name: Atlantirivulus santensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Atlantirivulus simplicis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwater swamps near a beach and a mangrove swamp, about 100 m from the sea (Ref. 55777).

species.name: Atlantirivulus unaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atoll butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep lagoons and seaward reefs. Occur singly or in pairs. Feed on algae and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 1602). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). May hybridize with C. xanthurus. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Atoll moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302, 75154) found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Atopochilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus chabanaudi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus christyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus mandevillei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus pachychilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopochilus vogti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small fast streams.  Of possible aquarium value (Ref. 4967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Atopocottus tribranchius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atopodontus adriaensi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atopomesus pachyodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atoyac chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atractodenchelys phrix
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atractodenchelys robinsorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrak crested loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrilinea macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrilinea macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrilinea roulei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in upper reaches of rivers, often in groups in search for food.  They feed on larvae of aquatic insects, diatoms and filiform algae (Ref. 45563). Utilized for food (Ref. 80318).

species.name: Atrobucca alcocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrobucca antonbruun
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrobucca bengalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrobucca geniae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrobucca trewavasae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrophacanthus japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Atrosalarias fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered, shallow reefs, hiding among live or dead coral branches (Ref. 1602).  From estuaries to outer reef lagoons (Ref. 48636), 2-12 m deep.  Solitary (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Attentive carplet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds, slow-flowing streams and canals (Ref. 41236).  Prefers still water with a mud substrate in the dry zone.  In aquarium, it feeds on phytoplankton (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Attenuated spider fish
species.description: Occurs on the continental slope, rise and abyss.  Extremely  eurybathic (250-5,150 m) and eurythermic (10-5°C) (Ref. 3590).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Attonitus bounites
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Attonitus ephimeros
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Attonitus irisae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aturiri’s pygmy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found perched individually on vertical surfaces at the back of crevices and overhangs. Collected with clove oil from exposed oceanic atoll with clear water, steep outer wall with small crevices and overhangs, coarse white coralline sand (38 m) and steep outer reef slope with white calcareous sand (40 m); the holotype from steep wall covered with coarse white Halimeda sand (60 m) (Ref. 102609).

species.name: Atypicthys latus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Atéléopode
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper continental slopes (Ref. 27121).  Benthic (Ref. 51024).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 6717).

species.name: Atéléopode de Loppe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper slopes (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on ophiuroids and fishes (Ref. 6717).

species.name: Auchenionchus crinitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenionchus microcirrhis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous; feeds on other fishes; juveniles favoring amphipods and shifts to diet of decapods as adults (Ref. 94105).

species.name: Auchenionchus variolosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles feed primarily on amphipods but shift to diet of decapods as adults (Ref. 94105).

species.name: Auchenipterichthys coracoideus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterichthys longimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterichthys punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the northernmost collecting site (altitude of about 150 m) along upper Rio Negro, the water was blackish, over rocky bottoms.  Stomach contents of four specimens indicate a diet consisting mainly of insect nymphs and adults (Ref. 26666).

species.name: Auchenipterichthys thoracatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus ambyiacus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus brachyurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus brevior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus britskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus demerarae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to inhabit the more upstream parts of rivers where it occupies the upper part of the water column.  Active at dusk, feeding mainly on insects and small crustaceans.  First sexual maturity occurs at a length of 16 cm.  Reproduction begins at the start of the rainy season.  Fertilization is internal, the female being capable of keeping the sperm in the epithelium of its genital tract.  Fecundity is approximately 15,000 eggs (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Auchenipterus fordicei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus menezesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenipterus nuchalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower courses of the larger rivers.  Free swimming species found near the surface.  Nocturnal, plus active during dusk and dawn.  Feeds on smaller fish.  The male is recognizable by his thick, ossified maxillary barbels and by the first few rays of the anal fin which are fused, supporting the urogenyla tube that runs along the anterior border to the tip of the rays (Ref. 6868).  This fish comprises the majority of the catches in the fish nets and is especially captured during the rainy season which is its reproductive period.  Occurs less frequently in flood zones, prefers eroded zones where it appears in large numbers (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Auchenipterus osteomystax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auchenoceros
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Over sandy and muddy bottoms in inshore waters to depths of 420 m.  Possibly an important forage fish for commercial species.  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Auchenoglanis biscutatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly occurs in running water, lakes and submerged vegetation in the Sudd, rare in fringing vegetation. Feeds on the bottom on mud, debris, insects, notably chironomid larvae and mollusks. Gravid fish are recorded throughout the year with a peak in the dry season (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Auchéniptère tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps.  Well-adapted to hypoxic environments, being able to survive for hours, emerged.  Adults feed on small fishes, arthropods, worms and sometimes on fruits (Ref. 35381).  The spiny structure of the pectoral fins enables the male to hold the females during mating (internal fertilization).  Sperm can be kept in the female's genital tract for several months, owing to a gelatinous emission from the seminal vesicle of the male.  At maturity, the size of the adhesive eggs (20% of the female's weight) is 3 mm.  Nine days after hatching, alevin size is 1.5 cm and they feed on microscopic worms or small insects.  At around 11 days, their negative phototropism pushes them to hide themselves under branches or rocks.  Its pink flesh is highly appreciated by the local population (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Aulixidens eugeniae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aulonocara aquilonium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas (Ref. 40898).  Territorial males defend a small patch of sand against conspecific males only (Ref. 40898).  Foraging females and non-territorial males form large schools (Ref. 40898).

species.name: Aulonocara auditor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small invertebrates that live in the sand (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Aulonocara brevinidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas (Ref. 40898).  Males territorial and defend a very shallow spawning pit (Ref. 40898).

species.name: Aulonocara brevirostre
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aulonocara chizumulu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Regularly found over pure rocky habitats, but forages over sand.  Feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Aulonocara Fort Maguire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Tends to hide in caves.  Feeds on small sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).  Aquarium keeping:  many females for one male; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Aulonocara gertrudae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas (Ref. 40898).

species.name: Aulonocara guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy areas.  Feed on small invertebrates which live in the sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Aulonocara koningsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intermediate zone between rocks and sand; feeds on sandy patches between rocks; males hold territories and excavate beneath rocks to construct their spawning burrow; females occur in small groups of 4 to 5 individuals (Ref. 55929).

species.name: Aulonocara rostratum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over open sand and feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).  Solitary specimens usually seen over soft and muddy bottoms.  Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 40898).

species.name: Aulonocara stonemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably found over a substrate consisting of mud or sand with a thick layer of sediment.  Feeds on benthic entomostracans, particularly ostracods and chydorid cladocerans (Ref. 267).

species.name: Aulonocara trematocephalum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably feeds on soft invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Aulonocranus dewindti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Semi-pelagic roamers and drifting plankton pickers which occur over sandy bottoms in schools of several hundred fish (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Aulopareia atripinnata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment needs clarification.

species.name: Aulopareia koumansi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aulopareia ocellata
species.description: Parachaeturichthys spp. inhabit deep water (Ref. 42915).

species.name: Aulopareia unicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auriglobus amabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds almost exclusively on large aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 2091).

species.name: Auriglobus modestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Feeds mainly on terrestrial insects, shrimps, seeds, and to a lesser extent on whole fish, fin rays or scales (Ref. 2091).

species.name: Auriglobus remotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Auriglobus silus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Aurin
species.description: Common species (Ref. 34024). Adults typically live as commensals in the gut of shallow-water holothurians, Holothuria tubulosa and Stichopus regalis (although some deep-water records exist, see Ref. 6347). Prejuveniles (tenuis larvae) probably inhabit the same host species while the vexillifer and egg-rafts are planktonic. The fish may partly protrude or entirely leave its host at night to feed on small fish and benthic invertebrates. Reproduction noted in July-September. (Ref. 4741).

species.name: Aurin (Chelon auratus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are neritic usually in schools, entering lagoons and lower estuaries (Ref. 7399); rarely entering freshwater (Ref. 3573, 59043).  Juveniles move to coastal lagoons and estuaries in winter and especially in spring (Ref. 59043).  They feed on small benthic organisms, detritus, and occasionally on insects and plankton (Ref. 2804).  Juveniles feed only on zooplankton (Ref. 59043). Reproduction takes place in the sea, from July to November.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Minimum size allowed for fishing is 20 cm.  The quality of the flesh is variable (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Aurin de Fowler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Inhabits pearl shells, rock oysters, and clams.  Feeds on crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 11228).  Reported to tend towards sexual pairing in the host (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Aurin ponctué
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Aurora anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky substrate deeper than 53 m; in a small group of one dominant male and several females.  The harems were on a protected slope with less current but were not on steep cliff, never swimming high above the substrate.  Each harem occupies an area about 20-25 m2, no fighting between males on the boundary of 2 harems.  Occasionally 2 or 3 males share boundaries.  While females swim close to the substrate, the males are more active and swim higher up in the water column.  Feeds on plankton about 1 m above the substrate.

species.name: Aurora goatfish
species.description: This species is most probably from shallow bottom reached by artisanal fisheries (Ref. 130857).

species.name: Aurora rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common offshore (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae and pelagic juveniles (Ref. 36715).  Trawled on soft bottom and when caught scales usually rub off, leaving white pockets bordered by red; also caught in sablefish traps (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Austellus barb
species.description: Inhabits the main river area and is found with cyprinids Dawkinsia filamentosa, D. lepida, Pethia punctata, Puntius mahecola, Devario malabaricus (Jerdon) and the cichlid Pseudetroplus maculatus (Ref. 127046).

species.name: Austral lightfish
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Australian anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly inshore:  chiefly in bays, inlets and estuaries, sometimes in low salinities.  Older individuals tend to move out to sea in winter and back in the spring.  Forms compact schools much preyed upon by larger fishes, common dolphins and birds.  Feeds on plankton.  Spawns in inlets, bays and also estuaries, probably throughout the year but mainly in late spring to early autumn and especially about November to February.  The eggs are ellipsoidal.  Utilized as fish paste.

species.name: Australian bandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep tidal channels in muddy burrows (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Australian barracuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in channels and other semi-protected areas.  Found in schools.  Feeds on various small fish (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Australian barred tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300).  A benthic carnivore which feeds on fish, mollusks, crustaceans (crabs, amphipods and stomatopods), and polychaetes.

species.name: Australian bartail flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 7300, 44894).  Inhabits lakes and small streams in upland and coastal plain areas, including brackish estuaries.  Prefers the cover provided by aquatic vegetation in rocky or gravel-bottomed pools.  Only female dwells upstream; male tends to stay in the lower, estuarine reaches of rivers.  Juvenile feeds on zooplankton; adult on insects, crustaceans and fishes.  Life cycle is catadromous: flood events between May and August trigger a downstream spawning migration to estuaries.  A plant thickets and sandbars are known sites for egg deposition (Ref. 44894).  A 63 cm LCF female was caught and released in Lake Samsonvale, SE Queensland with an estimated weight of more than 4.5 kg (Stephen T. Poole, pers.comm. elops1@yahoo.com, 03/09).

species.name: Australian blacktip shark
species.description: Found on the continental shelf from close inshore to about 150 m depth (Ref. 9997).  Found throughout the water column but usually near the sea bed during the day and near the surface at night (Ref. 6390).  Prefers teleost fishes but also feeds on cephalopods to a lesser degree.  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Forms large aggregations (Ref. 6871).  Utilized for its meat and fins (Ref. 6871).  The flesh has a relatively high mercury content (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Australian bluespotted maskray
species.description: A demersal fish found inshore to mid-continental ad insular shelves (Ref. 114953). Found over and adjacent to rocky and coral reefs from shallow water to at least 91 m depth (Ref. 116741).

species.name: Australian bonytongue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in still waters of streams and swamps where it is usually seen near the surface or close to shore among aquatic vegetation (Ref. 2847, 44894).  Solitary, territorial and spawn prior to the wet season when surface water temperatures approach 30°C (Ref. 44894).  Young feed primarily on microcrustaceans  (Ref. 2847).  Primarily a surface feeder, feeding on a variety of terrestrial and aquatic insects, small fishes, frogs, crustaceans, and some plant material (Ref. 44894).  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 56180).  Maximum weight reported in Ref. 5259 may be 12.27 kg  (W. Lau, pers. Comm. 07/05).  Important food fish (Ref. 58511) and a valuable aquarium fish (Ref. 83518).

species.name: Australian bull ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found off beaches and over sand flats in shallow water.  Also found offshore down to 85 m (Ref. 9862).  Feeds mainly on crabs and shellfish (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Australian butterfly ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species. Found on coastal to offshore on continental shelf in open sandy, muddy and silty habitat, including estuaries and intertidal zones. Mainly feeds on bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Maturity size 35-42 cm WD (males) and 44-46 cm WD (females); hatch size 22-25 cm DW. Produces litters of 1-6 pups (Ref. 114953). Caught by shrimp trawlers.

species.name: Australian combtooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Australian cownose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Biology little known (Ref. 9916).

species.name: Australian cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Australian damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and outer reef environments at One Tree Island, GBR in Australia.  Found solitarily or in small groups in open sandy or rubble areas with occasional coral outcrops.  Feed primarily on algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Australian darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Australian freshwater catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit slow moving streams, lakes and ponds with fringing vegetation.  They swim close to sand or gravel bottoms.  More abundant in lakes than in flowing water (Ref. 44894).  Usually solitary but juveniles sometimes form loose aggregations.  Mainly bottom-feeders (Ref. 44894).  Feed on insect larvae, prawns, crayfish, mollusks, and small fishes.  Breeding occurs between spring and mid-summer when water temperatures rise to between 20° and 24°C (Ref. 44894).  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Australian goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Subadults and adults of this species occur at relatively shallow depths of the upper shelf and usually around 20-30 m (Ref. 98481).  Adults feed mainly on shrimp (47%).

species.name: Australian grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit creeks and rivers, usually in cool, clear waters over gravel bottoms in sections alternating between pools and rapids.  Usually found in clear, moderate to fast-flowing water in the upper reaches of rivers (sometimes to altitudes above 1000 meters).  Often forming aggregations below barriers to upstream movement.  Timid species that forms fast-moving shoals (Ref. 44894).  Often form large schools especially prior to spawning.  Feed on small crustaceans, insects and their larvae and algae.  The intestinal tract is long, s specialization to assist in the breakdown of ingested plant material (Ref. 44894).  Spawn:  Feb.-May; 25,000-68,000 eggs which sink to bottom downstream of spawning site.  Hatching:  10-20 days; larvae, 6-7 mm TL, swept downstream to estuaries and the sea, return to freshwater after 6 months.

species.name: Australian gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found around dead coral outcrops, also in rubble areas in lagoons and on the outer edge of reefs (Ref. 510).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Australian grey smooth-hound
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian halosaur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species (Ref. 7300) occurring on the continental slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: Australian keel-head wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore species in rocky reef and on sandy bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Australian lungfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud, sand or gravel bottoms (Ref. 44894).  Sluggish species that prefers still or slow-flowing waters, usually in deep pools.  During period of drought, it can tolerate stagnant conditions by breathing air, surfacing 1-2 times per hour; however, it lacks the ability to survive dry spells by aestivation; it is a facultative air-breather that will die if forced to depend on air breathing (Ref. 36739, 44894).  The sound of the lungfish exhaling air at the surface prior to inhaling a fresh breath has been likened to that made by a small bellows.  Nocturnally active (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on frogs, tadpoles, fishes, shrimp, earthworms, snails, aquatic plants and native fruits fallen from trees overhanging the creeks (Ref. 36739, 44894).  It browses among the detritus, using its electroreceptors to pick up hidden mollusks, worms or crustaceans.  Protected by law.  Fossil records show that this species remained virtually unchanged for over 380 million years.  The Steinhart Aquarium in San Francisco had a specimen of 1 m length, 20 kg weight, and more than 65 years of age.  In 1933, an Australian lungfish was transported as a fully mature male (10 yrs. old at maturity) to the Shedd Aquarium, Chicago (C. Skonieczny, pers. comm. 11/08, e-mail: CSkonieczny@sheddaquarium.org). But this fish named Granddad, died in 2017 at the age of 95 (Ref 125841). By default, another individual which was brought to the California Academy of Sciences Aquarium in 1938 from Australia becomes the oldest at the age of 90 years. Biologists at the aquarium believe that Methuselah, as it is fondly called, is a female which measures 120 m and weighs 18,100 g (Ref. 125841).

species.name: Australian mado
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species, particularly common on coastal reefs in southern New South Wales (Ref. 9002).  Also commonly found under jetties in harbors and large estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Australian mottled moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  If provoked this species will make a lightning fast bite before retreating (Ref. 30464).

species.name: Australian no-line scorpionfish
species.description: Inhabits deep water habitats from depths of 228 to 990 m (Ref. 128947).

species.name: Australian pineapplefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves and under ledges of rocky, occasionally coral-reef habitats (Ref. 9710).  Also in muddy substrates (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Australian pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inner reefs and harbors, shallow rocky reefs in caves or under rocks (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Australian reticulate swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur often far up rivers, but also in estuaries and in Lakes Alexandrina and Albert near mouth of a river (Ref. 188).  Most commonly inhabit streams coursing through relatively dry eucalyptus-scrub or desert areas, preferring sluggish or quiet waters (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Also found in saline lakes (slightly less salty than sea water).  Tolerant of water temperatures between 9° and 38°C and pH 4.8-8.6.  Although these fish have a wide tolerance of temperature and pH, they are susceptible to oxygen depletion and are usually the first to perish when ephemeral habitats begin to dry up.  Common length is 15-20 cm (Ref. 44894).  Frequently noted in large shoals that feed on benthic algae; also feed on insects and small crustaceans.  Spawning may occur repeatedly in the north with a peak during the wet season; probably annual in the south (Ref. 5259, 44894).

species.name: Australian sailfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in seagrass areas, but also on rocky reefs to 20 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Australian short tailed hairtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams, backwaters, lakes, swamps and estuaries.  Occurs in brackish estuaries and inland salt lakes.  Most common in slow-flowing streams and still waters, shoaling near the surface or around the cover of aquatic plants and woody debris.  Forms large aggregations in open water (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on aquatic insects, microcrustaceans and algae.  Spawns throughout the Murray-Darling river system.  Breeds between July and March (mostly in spring) (Ref. 44894).  Spawning temperature is about 15 °C.  Newly hatched larvae measure 4.8 mm TL on the average.  Eggs are laid among aquatic vegetation and hatch in about 10 days.  Sexual maturity is attained by the end of the first year (Ref. 44894).  Eaten fresh or canned.

species.name: Australian snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Australian soldierbream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Australian spotted handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is recorded from depths of 18 m to at least 210 m, commonly at about 40-150 m depth, but may occur deeper; one specimen was taken by a trawler fishing in 123-277 m, but the depth of capture cannot be determined.  Newly hatched young and egg capsule diameter unknown; egg diameter 1.7-1.9 mm (Ref. 72490).

species.name: Australian spotted herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters (Ref. 188, 75154).

species.name: Australian sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters (in deep bays, Ref. 9563), appearing off Tasmanian shores in large schools (especially in August-November) and often entering estuaries (e.g. of Tamar and Derwent Rivers; said to ascend the former as far as Launceston in March).  More data needed.

species.name: Australian stargazer
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Australian stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in trawling grounds, generally on sand bottoms (Ref. 36661).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Australian striped velvetchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The habitat is likely to be dominated by a muddy rocky bottom (Ref. 76777).

species.name: Australian swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in backwaters of rivers, swamps, and stagnant ponds.  Inhabit soft bottom sediments in quiet, well-vegetated backwaters of brackish estuaries and nearby swamps.  Found in lower freshwater reaches of rivers.  Cryptic, nocturnally active species, which burrow in bottom sediments.  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).  The best chance of sighting this elusive fish is by spotlighting along thickly vegetated margins of suitable habitats at night.  They are capable of surviving short periods out of water.  A current taxonomic study of this family indicates this species probably should be placed in a new genus (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Australian tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Australian weasel shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A predominantly demersal species on continental and insular shelves from shallow, inshore bays down to 170 meters.  Sexual maturity of males reached at about 60 cm TL; females between 60 - 65 cm TL; with young are born at about 30 cm TL (Ref. 56150).

species.name: Australian whipray
species.description: Depth distribution is not well documented, but this species is primarily in shallow water from near the shore to at least 45 m depth (Ref. 110363). Enters estuaries and brackish water (Ref. 114953).  The largest specimen (140 cm WD) is a pregnant female with 2 embryos (30 cm WD) (data not year published); the smallest confirmed adult male is 112 cm WD (Ref. 110363); born at ca. 29 cm WD. Produces litters up to 4 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Australoheros acaroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It occurs in streams with moderate current and with sandy and clayey substratum.  During dry season, this species is found in deeper parts of the streams, usually shaded by vegetation.  It also inhabits marginal lagoons and flooded regions of great rivers.  Can tolerate moderately salt water in some lagoons and estuaries.  Diurnal, feeding preferentially on diptera larvae, macrophytes, cladocera, hirudinea and some aquatic ascaris (Ref. 85206).

species.name: Australoheros perdi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Lagoa Gambazinho, a small and elongated oligotrophic lake situated within Parque Estadual do Rio Doce (PERD) with maximum depth of 10.3 m without occurrence of thermal stratification. Adults feed on shrimp Macrobrachium jelskii, fish, aquatic and terrestrial insects, plant materials and other invertebrates. Immature individuals take zooplankton, mainly cladocerans as food. Smallest mature female and male measure 5.0 and 7.2 cm TL, respectively (Ref. 87295).

species.name: Auxide
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are principally caught in coastal waters and around islands (Ref. 9340).  Form schools.  Feed on small fishes, particularly anchovies, crustaceans (especially crab and stomatopod larvae) and squids.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769).  Because of their abundance, they are considered an important element of the food web, particularly as forage for other species of commercial interest.  Also caught with encircling nets and troll lines (Ref. 9340).  Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9340) and also dried or salted, smoked and canned (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Auxide (Auxis thazard)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are epipelagic in neritic and oceanic waters (Ref. 9340). They feed on small fish, squids, planktonic crustaceans (megalops), and stomatopod larvae (Ref. 5213). Because of their abundance, they are considered an important element of the food web, particularly as forage for other species of commercial interest. They are preyed upon by larger fishes, including other tunas (Ref. 9987). Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9340) and also utilized dried or salted, smoked and canned (Ref. 9987).

Degenerative changes in males and females suggest semelparity (Ref. 32364).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary or forms small groups on coral outcrops (Ref. 90102). Found in clear water, rich coral habitats on coastal to outer reef crests of slopes to about 15 m depth.  They live on rocks and corals on steep slopes. (Ref. 48636). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Axil spot wrasse

species.name: Axillary-spot cardinalfish

species.name: Ayarnangra estuarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from large tidal rivers in the lower Ayeyarwaddy [= Irrawaddy]; mud or clay bottoms and strong currents that reverse direction daily.  Collected with the use of large 'tiger mouth' nets that are reversed to fish in opposite directions when the tide changes.  Feeds on relatively large invertebrates such as prawns (Ref. 44046).

species.name: Ayu
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Typical amphidromous fish; appears in near shore from late autumn to spring (Ref. 11230).  Found in lakes and rivers, preferring clean river water and can be found the entire river long, from the head to the mouth (Ref. 12218).  Ascends the river during March when the temperature is around 10°C (Ref. 12218).  Adults spawn in the spring, in the lower reaches of rivers.  After spawning, some adults die while others return to the sea.  Larvae enter the sea immediately after hatching and remain there during winter, feeding on plankton.  In springtime, the young (5-7 cm TL) move upstream to the middle reaches of rivers to feed on algae.  Fish (about 6-9 cm) start schooling at the river mouth and are insectivores and eat algae
off small pebbles (Ref. 12218); this is assisted by small leaf-like teeth which are loosely attached to the jaw with two ligaments (Ref. 45181).  Those that are ready to spawn (about 20 cm TL) move downstream to the lower reaches of the river.  Spawning adults from the sea migrate upstream to the lower reaches as well.  Some fish spawn two or three years in succession, others only once (Ref. 9987 & 559).  River forms live usually only one year whereas lake forms can live two or three years (Ref. 12218).  Reaches maturity at 30-40 cm (Ref. 12218).  Highly esteemed food fish.  Marketed fresh and consumed fresh, fried and broiled (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Aze
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in cold, clear and fast-flowing water of small stream to medium-sized rivers as well as on gravel or rocky shores of cold lakes and in slightly brackish waters along eastern coast of Baltic coast (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates, mainly insects, crustaceans.  Pink to yellow eggs are found in clumps attached to undersides of large stones (Ref. 41678). Contrary to statements in older literature, eggs and larvae of fishes are not a common food item (Ref. 45167).

species.name: Aze (Cottus rondeleti)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small stream with clear, swift water and stone bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Aziz's toby

species.name: Azores dogfish

species.name: Azores rockling

species.name: Azov tadpole goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays in the biocoenosis of the estuarine silts (Ref. 2058).  Occurs in fresh and slightly brackish waters with salinity below 11 ppt , usually over mud bottom.  It lives about a year.  Females probably lay eggs in 2-3 portions within or under a molluscs shell and the adults die soon after spawning.  Feeds mainly on molluscs, crustaceans and chironomid larvae. (Ref.59043).

species.name: Aztec chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common Mexican fish.

species.name: Azuma perchlet
species.description: Uncommon deepwater fish.  Found over rock or sand bottoms (Refs. 559 and 9137).

species.name: Azure damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near sheltered shores at shallow depth. Inhabits rich live corals in pairs or groups of juveniles and subadults (Ref. 90102). Plankton comprise the dominant natural food (Ref. 7247). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Lacks pelagic larval stage; young remains with parents during early stages (similar to Acanthochromis polyacanthus) (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Azure demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and near shore reefs, usually among branching corals. Found in small aggregation, usually with Acropora corals (Ref. 48636). Feed on plankton about 0.3 to 0.5 m above substratum. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Azurina meridiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Azurio tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near shore in rock bottom (Ref. 11230).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Azygopterus corallinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Babbie tadpolefish
species.description: Collected by bottom trawl at depth 204 m with bottom temperature of -0.8°C and salinity 34.42 ppt, over brown silt and clay (Ref. 116680).

species.name: Babone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A voracious piscivore inhabiting coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs. Encountered most frequently in channels and outer shelf reefs. Migrate over short distances to spawn, forming large aggregations, maybe 1 or 2 per reef (Ref. 6390). Feeds mostly on fishes, and occasionally on crustaceans (Ref. 9710). The prey comprises a variety of large reef fishes, including groupers, and this diet of large fishes is responsible for the high concentrations of ciguatera toxins. Juveniles may mimic the pufferfish Canthigaster valentini. Usually wary (Ref. 9710). The young have a demersal existence in shallow water in reef habitats, especially around coral rubble (Ref. 27259). They feed on small fish and invertebrates such as crustaceans and squid (Ref. 27261). Eggs float just below the surface (Ref. 6390). The pelagic larvae are found in habitats similar to those of the adults (Ref. 27260). An excellent table fish (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Babone ponctuée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in shallow water (less than 10 m), however, Kyushin et al. (1977, Ref. 6894) reported specimens caught on a vertical longline at depths of 45 to 62 m. Solitary or in small groups. Often drifts well above the bottom (Ref. 9710). Feeds exclusively on fishes (parrotfishes, wrasses, holocentrids, acanthurids, a triggerfish, and a juvenile Sphyraena) (Ref. 6448). Also caught with trawls.

species.name: Babonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in protected coastal reef in mixed algae and coral habitat (Ref. 48635).  Common on inshore coastal reefs but absent in clear offshore reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles have a demersal existence in shallow water in reef habitats, especially around coral rubble (Ref. 27259).  Migrate over short distances to spawn, forming aggregations (Ref. 6390).  May move into shallow water to feed (Ref. 6390).  Eggs float just below the water surface (Ref. 6390).  Pelagic larvae are found in habitats similar to those of the adults (Ref. 27260).  Juveniles feed on small fish and invertebrates such as crustaceans and squid (Ref. 27261).  Commonly used for food.  Its flesh is delicate and well appreciated (Ref. 5503). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Babyface goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inner bays (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Bachneunauge
species.description: Espèce de lamproies. Adults are found in the lowland, piedmont and montane zone in clear, well oxygenated brooks (Ref. 59043). They live exclusively in freshwater; in middle and upper reaches of small streams and rivers, occasionally in lakes. Larvae lie buried in the substrate while adults live in the open water (Ref. 57699). Sexually mature adults have been observed burrowing in fine sand (Ref. 89241).
