species.name: Basilichthys archaeus
species.description: Above 2,000 m elevation.

species.name: Basilichthys semotilus
species.description: Occurs above 2000 m (Ref. 27834).

species.name: Basket hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in shallow sandy and vegetated areas located in sheltered bays.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Basketfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Basketweave cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species ranging from the shore to 110 m depth (Ref. 34024).  Usually found on sand bottom from 2.7-7 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Oviparous, with pelagic larvae (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bass Strait flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy habitat, commonly in estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Bassogigas gillii
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus elongatus
species.description: Specimens were caught on or near the bottom from upper slope to abyssal depths (Ref. 84269).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus levistomatus
species.description: Specimens were apparently caught on or near the bottom at abyssal depths (Ref. 84269).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus multispinis
species.description: Occurs on or near the bottom at continental slope depths (Ref. 84269).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  A female specimen caught was with 0.5 mm eggs (Ref. 84269).

species.name: Bassozetus nasus
species.description: Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus normalis
species.description: Almost exclusive inhabitant of the continental rise, but also caught from lower slope to abyssal depths (Ref. 84269).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus oncerocephalus
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus taenia
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).   Of the 7 female specimens caught, 1 with 0.6 mm eggs.  No identifiable stomach contents were found (Ref. 84269).

species.name: Bassozetus werneri
species.description: Known only from the holotype, a semi-ripe, female caught at continental slope depth.  Stomach and intestine remains indicate that the species feeds on or close to the bottom (remains of crustaceans: 7 amphipods (10 - 40 mm in length) and 1 isopod ca. 10 mm in length (Ref. 84269).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bassozetus zenkevitchi
species.description: Rare, deep pelagic species (Ref. 34024).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Of the 5 female specimens caught, 2 with 0.5 mm eggs.  No identifiable stomach contents were found.  Specimen collection used non-closing, pelagic fishing gear (bottom trawls) (Ref. 84269).   Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bastanago
species.description: A coastal species, which enters coastal lagoons, shallow bays and estuaries (Ref. 81259). Found over sandy and muddy bottoms, sometimes near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951). Feeds on bottom fishes, crustaceans and mollusks. Ovoviviparous, gestation period about 4 months and 4-7 young are produced. Wings marketed smoked, dried-salted, and also used for fishmeal and oil. Harmful to shellfish banks; dangerous to bathers and fishers due to its poisonous spine. Barbed poison spine is a modified denticle that can be 35cm long, shed occasionally and replaced (Ref. 35388). Maximum reported width about 150 cm (Ref. 81259).

species.name: Bastard seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among seaweed and near the base of red algae on shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 637).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bastard trumpeter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Bata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Batan longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Batangas groppo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Batanta mud goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mud-bottom habitat (Ref. 101679).

species.name: Batanta rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, moderately fast-flowing stream.

species.name: Batasio batasio
species.description: Found in streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Batasio fluviatilis
species.description: Occurs in rivers and streams with moderate to swift current and a predominantly rocky bottom; less often in slow-flowing streams with a muddy substrate.  Hides among stones or submerged vegetation during the day and comes out at night to feed (Ref. 44354).

species.name: Batasio macronotus
species.description: Found in lowland river with turbid water, mainly on sand substrate in lotic areas and sand/mud substrate with some submerged and emergent vegetation in lentic backwaters (Ref. 54041).

species.name: Batasio tengana
species.description: Occurs in rivers and canals (Ref. 1479).  Found in torrential streams (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Batasio travancoria
species.description: Occurs in hill streams and rivers at base of hills (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Batchwa vacha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, canals and tidal waters.  Feed on small fish and insects.  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).  An excellent food fish.

species.name: Bates' killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to the inland plateau (Ref. 47774) where it inhabits raffia swamps and swampy parts of shallow brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788, 47774).  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Bath's comb-tooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at depths of 3-25 m, solitary or in small groups around sponges and tunicates on coral outcrops (Ref. 90102) and in reef crests with large rounded corals (Ref. 8631, 48636), or encrusted sponges to about 10 m depth.  Females are commonly seen and seem to outnumber males (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bathophilus altipinnis
species.description: Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathophilus brevis
species.description: Meso- (Ref. 559) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathophilus cwyanorum
species.description: Most likely mesopelagic.

species.name: Bathophilus digitatus
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Bathophilus indicus
species.description: A mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Bathophilus irregularis
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468).

species.name: Bathophilus kingi
species.description: Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathophilus longipinnis
species.description: Meso- (Ref. 4468) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathophilus novicki
species.description: Most likely mesopelagic.

species.name: Bathophilus proximus
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathophilus schizochirus
species.description: Mesopelagic at ca. 265 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathophilus vaillanti
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468).

species.name: Bathybagrus graueri
species.description: Most common in sub-littoral area but extend to 150 m, with larger individuals at greater depths.  Inhabits muddy bottoms (Ref. 6868).  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 4967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Male parent guards the eggs (Ref. 45232).

species.name: Bathybagrus platycephalus
species.description: Inhabits lake Tanganyika at 20 to 110 m deep (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Bathybagrus sianenna
species.description: Present on the bottom of deep water to 150 m but most common in sub-littoral areas; very common in deep water (Ref. 4967). Specialized toward a life on the sandy bottoms (Ref. 6770). Upstream spawning migrations have been reported (Ref. 78218, 93972). Omnivore (Ref. 78218). Feeds on small fishes (usually Lamprologus spp.), ostracods, and larvae of dragonflies (Ref. 6868, 36901).

species.name: Bathybagrus stappersii
species.description: Most abundant at 80-120 m.  Common at south end of Lake Tanganyika.  Feeds on crabs, fish and carrion (Ref 4967).

species.name: Bathybagrus tetranema
species.description: Inhabit lakes 40 to 80 m deep but not deeper (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Bathybates fasciatus
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates ferox
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates graueri
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates hornii
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates leo
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates minor
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathybates vittatus
species.description: Forms schools.  Feeds mainly on clupeids (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Bathyblennius antholops
species.description: Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bathyclarias atribranchus
species.description: Inhabits lake bottom below 70 m.  Feeds on worms (Ref. 4967). Coloration of live fishes is unknown. Dark to blackish coloration of gill filaments and suprabranchial organ is characteristic of this species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias euryodon
species.description: Inhabits lakes (Ref. 4967). Piscivorous predator (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias filicibarbis
species.description: Has been caught at a depth of 55 m over a muddy bottom.  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5595). Indications that this species might perhaps normally be found in shallower regions (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias foveolatus
species.description: Occurs at a depth of 30 m and deeper, in rocky areas.  Feeds on rock-inhabiting species during the night (Ref. 5595). Prefers rocky substrates and feeds exclusively on fish (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias longibarbis
species.description: Occurs from the bottom to about 75 m (Ref 4967).  Commonly caught in deep regions.  A piscivore (Ref. 5595). Stronger tendency to liv ein open water than other clarids (Ref. 78218). Piscivore and often taken on lines (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias nyasensis
species.description: Occurs in open water and mainly filters zooplankton. Also feeds on small fishes and insect larvae (Ref. 5595). Forms groups when feeding on plankton and insect larvae (Ref. 5595). Sometimes feeds at the surface (Ref. 4967). It feeds on other fishes, but grain, insects (e.g. Corethra edulis) and small crustaceans have also been found in stomach contents (Ref. 78218). A female was caught at Nkhata Bay at between 20 and 50 m of depth (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias rotundifrons
species.description: Inhabit the lake bottom down to about 75 m.  (Ref 4967).  Sometimes caught at deep regions. A piscivore (Ref. 5595, 78218). Found in more than 40 m of depth over rocky substrates interspersed with areas of sand (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathyclarias worthingtoni
species.description: Prefers rocky habitats.  Feeds mainly on crabs, occasionally on fishes (Ref. 5595, 78218). Occurs down to a depth of at least 40 m, though juveniles are frequently found among rocks in very shallow water (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Bathycongrus aequoreus
species.description: Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bathydraco macrolepis
species.description: Found at depths ranging between 450-950 m and 1,750-2,100 m.  The discontinuity may be due to inadequate sampling.

species.name: Bathydraco scotiae
species.description: Depth range:  2,100-2,950 m.

species.name: Bathygadus dubiosus
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathygobius andrei
species.description: Occurs in both tidepools and sublittoral areas (Ref. 87607).

species.name: Bathygobius burtoni
species.description: Found in intertidal pools along rocky shores (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Bathygobius casamancus
species.description: Marine species, inhabiting the intertidal zone and entering brackish waters (Ref. 57403, 79590), occasionally found in lagoons (Ref. 4343). Found in intertidal rock pools and mudflats at high tide (Ref. 5299). Maximum reported total length 8.1 cm (Ref. 57403, 79590).

species.name: Bathygobius hongkongensis
species.description: Inhabits rocky shores (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Bathygobius lacertus
species.description: Exhibits diversity of habitat preference, from shallow warm pools formed in limestone on exposed beaches with moderate wave action, from sheltered intertidal pools on rock and pebble shorelines of bays or coves, on reef crests, and over silt and mud around mangrove roots (Ref. 85559).

species.name: Bathygobius ostreicola
species.description: Occurs in backwaters and estuaries.

species.name: Bathygobius petrophilus
species.description: Inhabits bottoms without rocks.

species.name: Bathylaco macrophthalmus
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathylaco nielseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagichthys kobylianskyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagichthys longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathylagichthys parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagichthys problematicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagus andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylagus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylutichthys taranetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathylychnops brachyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathylychnops chilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bathymaster derjugini
species.description: Inhabits rocky shore areas.

species.name: Bathymicrops brevianalis
species.description: Feeds on small crustaceans and squids.

species.name: Bathymicrops multispinis
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathymicrops regis
species.description: Depth range also reported at 4250 m-5700 m (Ref. 6688). Rare, probably solitary.  Feeds on small benthopelagic crustaceans (Ref. 6688).

species.name: Bathymyrus simus
species.description: Known from moderately deep water (Ref. 40794).

species.name: Bathyonus caudalis
species.description: Benthopelagic at bathyal and abyssal depths (Ref. 56809).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bathyonus laticeps
species.description: Locally abundant (Ref. 34024).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 34024.  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bathyonus pectoralis
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bathypelagic rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Mesopelagic and benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bathypterois insularum
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathypterois longicauda
species.description: Feeds on small crustaceans and squids (Ref. 5755).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathypterois oddi
species.description: Feeds on small crustaceans and squids (Ref. 5755).  Minimum depth from Ref. 90064.

species.name: Bathypterois quadrifilis
species.description: Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Fecundity of 4,500 eggs for one specimen.

species.name: Bathypterois viridensis
species.description: Found on continental slopes.  Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 3590).

species.name: Bathyraja papilionifera
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth between 940 and 1040 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bathyraja pseudoisotrachys
species.description: The paratype was collected from depth of 287 m (Ref. 6797).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bathysauropsis malayanus
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathysolea lagarderae
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathysphyraenops simplex
species.description: Family placement uncertain.  Mitsukurinidae follows Eschmeyer 1998 (Ref. 26282).

species.name: Bathytroctes breviceps
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathytroctes inspector
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathytroctes oligolepis
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathytroctes pappenheimi
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bathytyphlops sewelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary.  Bottom feeder.  Feeds on benthopelagic mysids and copepods.  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Fecundity per generation is ca 6,000 eggs (Ref. 6688).

species.name: Bathyuroconger parvibranchialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Batman loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by using tight-weave nets, in shallow, rocky, fast-flowing areas of the Sarim stream and the Han stream (Ref. 125633)..

species.name: Batrachus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sedentary species which occurs on soft sand or mud, often partly buried or concealed in rock crevices, solitary in shallow water.  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks and small fishes (Ref. 7405).  The female lays eggs which are large enough and which are turned over to the males who guard them (Ref. 5377). A species that is not venomous (Dr. Andread Kunznmann, Leibniz Centre for Tropical  Marine Research (ZMT), pers. communication 10/2021).

species.name: Batrochoglanis acanthochiroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 26543).  Carnivorous (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Batrochoglanis melanurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Batrochoglanis raninus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly occurs in creeks as well as in rivers (Ref. 27188).  Found in very shady and deep zones of rivers where the current is slow, the bottom is shady and the gravel is covered with plant debris.  During the day, it lies hidden under branches or rocks.  It goes stalk-hunting, swallowing prey within its range.  Starts feeding on micro-crustaceans and aquatic insect larvae, then shifts it diet to fishes of notable size (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Batrochoglanis transmontanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Batrochoglanis villosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Battalgil spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Batuna's damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in silty lagoons with large staghorn coral colonies, usually congregating in small groups (Ref. 48636).  Seen usually on <i>Acropora branching corals of sheltered lagoons and protected fringing reefs.  They are usually encountered alone or in pairs and hovers to about one meter or so above the coral substratum.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Nests on branches of dead corals (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Relatively common at all sites where it has been observed (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Baudroie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from shallow, inshore waters to 650 m depth.  Maximum depth range at 1013 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on nekton, mainly fishes (4712).

species.name: Baudroie (Lophius piscatorius)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy and muddy bottoms from the coast (below 20 m, Ref. 12382) down to depths of 1,000 m.  May also be found on rocky bottoms (Ref. 12382).  It lies half-buried in the sediment waiting for its prey.  It attracts prey by means of its fishing filament (Ref. 5377).  Feeds mainly on fishes, occasionally sea-birds.  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, sautéed, broiled, boiled, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  It is a well-studied species in Europe and is sold without the skin and the head under the name 'queue de Lotte' (Ref. 5377).  Does not adapt well in home aquariums due to its large size (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Baudroie africaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper slope waters.  Feeds mainly on fishes (Ref. 2742).

species.name: Baudroie bouche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 5213). Oviparous (Ref. 205), multiple spawner (Ref. 32832). Depth range in the East China Sea and the Yellow Sea is between 30 m-500 m (Ref. 11230)

species.name: Baudroie chinoise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230). A carnivore (Ref. 9137). Mainly feed on fish, euphausiids, sagittoids and shrimps (Ref. 53326). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).  Consumed as food, liver considered as delicacy in Japan (Ref. 47220).

species.name: Baudroie d'Amérique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelf, occurring deeper in southern parts of range (Ref 7251); tolerating a wide range of temperature (0-21°C) (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Baudroie diable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the deeper continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 27121).  Feeds mainly on bottom-living fishes (Ref. 27121, 27637) often on pilchard, round herring and horse mackerel (Ref. 36731).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 5213.

species.name: Baudroie fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic on the continental shelf and the upper regions of the continental slope (Ref. 9538).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 9538).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36490).  Eggs are presumably contained in floating gelatinous rafts (Ref. 36490).  Probably caught as a by-catch of trawl fishing (Ref. 9538).

species.name: Baudroie marache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope.  Feeds mainly on fishes (Ref. 5236).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Baudroie pêcheuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Feeds mainly on fishes (Ref. 3787).  Considered a good food fish; marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 3787).

species.name: Baudroie reticulée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental shelf waters.  A voracious carnivore.  (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Baudroie à queue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles and adults are benthic on the continental shelf and the upper regions of the continental slope (Ref. 9538).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36490).  Eggs are contained in floating gelatinous rafts (Ref. 36490).  Probably caught as a by-catch of trawl fishing (Ref. 9538).

species.name: Baudroie épineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the outer shelf and upper slope waters (7400).

species.name: Bavard
species.description: Inhabits streams with clear, cool, moderate to swift water, and stone substrate (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bavard (Cottus aturi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with clear, cool, moderate to swift water and stone substrate (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bavard (Cottus duranii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with clear, cool, moderate to swift water and stone substrate (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bavard (Cottus perifretum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in all kinds of streams and rivers including large main rivers, all kinds of shores with coarse gravel or large stones in flowing and stagnant water of rivers, harbors and backwaters (Ref. 55856).  Feeds on a wide variety of benthic invertebrates (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bavard (Cottus rhenanus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, cold streams with gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Baveuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are residents in intertidal areas with homing behavior (Ref. 32612). They are found between pebbles or at margins of steep, filamentous algae-covered rocks exposed to sunlight. They make underwater 'flight' over long distances. Feed almost exclusively on algae (Ref. 205), favoring the algae Ulva (Ref. 94105). Spawns from May to July. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Baveuse (Parablennius gattorugine)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Active mainly during dusk and dawn (Ref. 5204).  Adults live in rocky while young are found in shallow water in the seaweed zone.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Spawn in March - May.  Male guards the eggs from several females, until larvae about 1 month (Ref. 35388).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Baveuse (Salaria pavo)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the intertidal zone and shallow bottoms, on rocks or sand between pebbles and vegetation (Ref. 5981).  Often in brackish waters down to 5 ppt (Ref. 5981).  Inhabit crevices or piddock holes, males remain in cavities above water-level during low tide (Ref. 5981).  Feed on benthic invertebrates, mainly mollusks, also algae (Ref. 5981).  Also ingest large amounts of aquatic insects and pupae (Ref. 94105).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Mature males adopt a passive role during courtship, rarely court females, do not defend nest territory, but provide parental care to eggs.  Sneaker males assume a female-like behavior in order to approach the nests of nesting males and parasitically fertilize the eggs (Ref. 94113).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35421).

species.name: Baveuse (Salariopsis fluviatilis)
species.description: Adults occur in rivers and brooks (Ref. 4342), in relatively shallow water as well as in low altitude lakes (Ref. 30578), on stone bottom; in streams, deepest and fastest microhabitats are preferred and sometimes coastal lagoons with low salinity (Ref. 59043).  Reported from marine environment (Ref. 58342).  A territorial species that lives up to 5 years (Ref. 59043).   Adults feed on small benthic organisms, aquatic insects and pupae (Ref. 94105).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Females spawn for the first time at the end of the first year and spawning lasts up to 3 years but with most females dying at the end of the first spawning year.  One female spawns up to 1,200 eggs (usually 200-300) in a single layer under a large stone; spawns several egg portions during the season. On the other hand, the males clean, fan and defend the eggs until hatching.  Several females may spawn with one male, which may guard the eggs at different stages of development (Ref. 59043).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive; eggs hatch in about a week (Ref. 205, 59043).  Planktonic larvae until about 1.5 cm, are drifted to and remain in quiet pools or side arms of rivers (Ref. 59043). Populations are threatened due to pollution and water abstraction (Ref. 26100); most riverine populations affected by habitat alteration (especially siltation and alteration of stream morphology), and predation of exotic species.  Presence of habitat suitable for the pelagic 'larval' stage downstream of spawning sites is a limiting factor; lacustrine population are apparently safer (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bavispe sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bay blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal shallows (Ref. 11482).  Territorial (Ref. 37955).  They feed on small benthic invertebrates and algae (Ref. 37955).  Demersal spawners in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter.  Eggs are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56053).

species.name: Bay goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on mud bottom; from intertidal to 201 m depth.  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  Eggs are found attached to the walls of burrows (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Bay of Bengal hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coastal reefs and turbid lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bay pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in eelgrass of bays and estuaries, sometimes taken in shallow offshore waters (Ref. 5316).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 6885).  Females larger than males (R.C. de Graaf, pers. Comm., 2001; Ref. 93899).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bay snook
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and lower river valleys.  Prefers lower and middle reaches of rivers in the slower moving waters with soft substrate of sand and mud.  Feeds on fish.

species.name: Bayad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, swamps and rivers (Ref. 31256). Avoids salt water (Ref. 31439). Spends nearly the whole of the daylight hours in crevices of rocks and is therefor seldom seen (Ref. 51850). Lives and feeds on or near the bottom (Ref. 3034). Adults exclusively piscivorous (Ref. 31256). Preys on small fish, particularly Alestes spp. (Ref. 13851), or Chrysichthys auratus as in Lake Kainji (Ref. 3034), but also feeds on insects, crustaceans and molluscs (some debris and vegetable matter may also be ingested) (Ref. 28714). Efficiency of catching prey catfish is maximised by face to face attack, avoiding damage by dorsal and pectoral spines of the prey (Ref. 33614). There is some indication that the species comes to shallower water to breed (Ref. 43507). Spawning season extends from April to July (Ref. 51850). Parents build and guard the nest, which is like a flat disc with a central hole where the eggs are dropped; size of the nest and the central hole depend on the fish size (Ref. 51638). Males become up to 7 years old, females 8 years (Ref. 51644). Mean sizes and weight of males are less than those of females from the same age (Ref. 51644, 51645). An important food fish. Flesh is good eating and of economic importance (Ref. 36900), commonly sold as food (Ref. 43521). Reputed to reach 100,000 g.

species.name: Bayonetta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually in schools inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 3573); sometimes in lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 59043).  Juveniles around 2.0 cm SL move to coastal lagoons and estuaries in summer and autumn (Ref. 59043).  Adults are herbivorous feeding on algae and vegetal detritus while juveniles feed on zooplankton until about 3 cm SL, then on benthic organisms until 5 cm SL (Ref. 9987, 59043).  Reproduce in summer (Ref. 2804).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Utilized for roe, but also fresh, smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Bayou darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast, rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Generally feeds on aquatic insects as adults and on micro-crustaceans as juveniles (Ref. 26981).

species.name: Bayou killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays and brackish waters.  7.5 cm max TL (Ref. 7251).  Feeds on aquatic insects and isopods (Ref. 79012).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Bayou topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in swamps, sloughs, and vegetated backwaters and pools of streams.  7.8 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Beachrock mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs intertidally on marine shores, typically in beach-rock pools (near fresh water seepages), in brackish pools behind beach dunes, or in sandy mangrove lagoons along beaches or headlands (Ref. 43716, 44894).  Primarily a saltwater fish, but very occasionally found in almost entirely freshwater conditions (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Beachsalmon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently living inshore and migrating into brackish water as the specimens used in this study were collected from the lower reaches of rivers, estuaries or inner part of bays (Ref. 129587).

species.name: Beaded darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beady pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lower reaches of streams and rivers, also seagrass beds in estuaries and other shallow inshore habitats (Ref. 43081, 44894).  Occur in mangrove estuaries and tidal creeks (Ref. 44894).  Males exhibit parental care by incubating and guarding the eggs in their brood pouch (Ref. 43081).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Beagle cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Rare species and known from a single specimen (Ref. 34024).  Size at birth 2.33 cm TL (Ref. 34024). Maximum length of female from Ref. 10898. Depth range unkown, probably confined to shallow reefs among rock and coral crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Beaglichthys larsonae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaked sandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrowing in sand and benthic, sometimes pelagic at shallow depths (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bean's bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the largest and deepest-dwelling melamphid species.  Feeds mainly on pelagic prey.  Captured by bottom and midwater trawls (Ref. 26478).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bean-eyed snake moray
species.description:
Inhabits anchialine caves.  Hydrological measurements for water layers around traps in the caves revealed very low salinities (0.6-0.8 psu), which can be considered freshwaters. Although it is not known the exact water layer this species inhabits, it is highly possible that it lives in the
lower layer with saline water especially it was captured in the trap from the Whip Cave with another marine eel (unidentified Chlopsidae species) (Ref. 130726).

species.name: Bear Island charr
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A non-anadromous species which inhabits shallow lakes.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bear Lake sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms from near shore to deep (at least 53 m) water.

species.name: Bear Lake whitefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found near the bottom and rarely near shore.

species.name: Bearded catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapids where it lives in the rocky anfractuosities in the strong current zones.  The length of the male snout bristles might be related with the hierarchic level of the individual within the population.  Fished by harpoons or bows in the shallow zones (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Bearded clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal areas.

species.name: Bearded dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore reef areas (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Bearded Eel Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bearded eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud bottoms of mangroves (Ref. 2798), estuaries and rivers (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Bearded eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud-bottomed or sandy-mud bottom.

species.name: Bearded flathead goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit tidal creeks and river mouths, usually in brackish water, but occasionally penetrate fresh water (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Bearded ghoul
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on open sandy or silty substrates of lagoon and seaward reefs.  Often buries itself and easily overlooked.  Uses pectoral fins to startle predators and shows color during courtship (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 9710).  The venom of this fish can be deadly to man.  Its ability to camouflage itself by living half-buried presents a real danger. Solitary on sand and mud bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bearded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the water's edge on rubble bottoms (Ref. 7251).  Also found in coral reefs with clear water (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Bearded klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal weedy areas.

species.name: Bearded leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy weedy areas of coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Lives in open muddy substrates in estuaries as well as deep coastal bays.  Usually found lining up with ropes, seawhips and large stringy-type sponges.  Incredible mimic that may float over the open bottom like a mangrove-shoot, may stand on its head (Ref. 48637).  Enters mangroves (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Bearded puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 36453).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks and echinoderms (Ref. 36453).

species.name: Bearded rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bearded roguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy inshore waters of mangrove swamps and penetrates freshwater rivers (Ref. 1602).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 1602).  Possess venom glands at the base of some of the spines.

species.name: Bearded scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic to at least 30 m (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Bearded velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, in soft bottom.

species.name: Bearded warbonnet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft and rocky bottoms; usually near shore and shallower than 70 meters (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Bearded worm goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, estuaries (Ref. 4833) and rivers (Ref. 2847).  Mud-dweller presumed to occur in estuaries (Ref. 4343).  Capable of living out of the water for considerable time by taking air into the bronchial chambers (Ref. 4833).  Feeds on crustaceans and other invertebrates  and probably small fishes (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Beardie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A bottom dweller (Ref. 7300); in quiet, coastal bays and estuaries, usually silty habitat (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Beardless barb
species.description: Inhabits small streams, reservoirs, lakes (Ref. 4832), canals, ditches, and generally areas with slow moving or standing water (Ref. 12693).  Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975, 57235).  Stomach contents are composed of fish and insect remains (Ref. 56749). Typically found around surfaces, such as plant, leaves, branches and tree roots where it browses for small plankton and crustaceans.  Moves into flooded forests and non-forested floodplains.  Reported to breed late during high-water season from September to October as water levels peak and begin to decline (Ref. 12693).  Found in the basin-wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Common foodfish in markets (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Bearn beaked dace
species.description: Inhabits streams, sectors with current, clear, and cool water, in deep pool.  Reaches up to about 28 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Beate's coralbrotula
species.description: Maximum length of 14.9 cm TL. Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices, cryptic (Ref 90102). Maximum length for female 13.2 SL (Ref 57884).

species.name: Beau-clair du large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with rocky habitats and known from 80 to more than 100 m depth but probably also occurring in shallower water, especially as juveniles (Ref.5403).  From dive observations, juveniles and young individuals likely occur at 5-30 m depths (Ref. 94109).  Eggs are pelagic (0.75 mm), small and spherical.

species.name: Beauclair
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found in outer reef slopes and deep lagoon pinnacles from 8 to at least 80 m.  In small aggregations, sometimes schools in oceanic locations (Ref. 48635).  Also found under ledges or hovering next to coral heads during day (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fish, crustaceans, and other small invertebrates (Ref. 5213). Occasionally taken in moderate numbers in trawls and by hook-and-line (Ref. 68288). Generally marketed fresh, may be salted or dried (Ref. 5284).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Beauclaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A relatively uncommon inhabitant of rocky reefs and coral-rich areas.  Spine of preopercle venomous.  Usually seen solitary , but sometimes forms schools in deep water in oceanic locations (Ref. 48635). Found in seaward slopes in 5-90 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Beauclaire alalaua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur mostly at depths of 100 m or more and has been captured at night at relatively shallow depths (9-46 m).  More common around islands (records from the continental coasts are rare) (Ref. 9335).  Inhabit rocky bottoms but many specimens have been trawled from relatively open waters in Hawaii (Ref. 5403).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Gonads of specimens collected in Hawaii in November appear to be near spawning condition (Ref. 5403).

species.name: Beauclaire de Bloch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs, under ledges or in caves by day (Ref. 9710); often silty habitat (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).  Rarely trawled (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Beauclaire de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in lagoon and seaward reefs, primarily around islands.  Under or near ledges by day (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juvenile pelagic (Ref. 9335).  Nocturnal (Ref. 5213), feeding mainly on octopi, pelagic shrimp, stomatopods, crabs, small fish, and polychaetes.  Solitary (Ref. 5213).  During the day usually occurs singly or in small groups but at dusk it may gather in large numbers (Ref. 37816).  Known to produce sound.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3800).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Beauclaire de roche (Priacanthus arenatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral reefs and rocky bottoms (Ref. 3800).  Forms small aggregations near the bottom (Ref. 10786).  A nocturnal feeder (Ref. 5521), feeds mainly on small fishes, crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 3800).  Most of its prey are larvae.  Flesh considered excellent quality; marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Beauclaire du large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms between 5 (Ref. 5403) and 200 m depth, usually solitary and possibly territorial.

species.name: Beauclaire du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore and offshore reefs from less than 20 m to more than 400 m depths.  Apparently forms aggregations in open bottom areas and is very abundant in the South China Sea and Andaman Sea.  Marketed fresh, whole.  Sound production has been studied in this species. Also found under ledges or hovering next to coral heads during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Beauclaire longue aile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard bottoms to a depth of about 400 m and reported to be moderately common at depths of 165 to 260 m in association with rocky holes and ledges; preferably with rich invertebrate growth such as sponges and soft corals (Ref. 48635).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles pelagic (Ref. 9335, 9563).  Feed on pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 9335).  Probably spawns in the Caribbean from May to September. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Beauclaire pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral or rocky areas.  Sometimes forms aggregations.  Feeds on a wide variety of benthic animals.  Smaller fish are mostly found inshore.  Marketed mostly fresh, whole or dried-salted.

species.name: Beauclaire sémaphore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shy nocturnal fish that prefers the deeper water around islands.  It may be found with squirrelfishes and cardinalfishes but tends to range deeper than they do (76 m).  Known to occur at depths of less than 5 to over 100 m in rocky habitats (Ref. 5403).

species.name: Beaufort's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand or gravel-bottom creeks flowing through rainforest, usually within about 20 km from the sea (Ref. 2847).  Appears limited to small streams close to the coast in fresh and brackish waters (Ref. 34009).

species.name: Beaufort's mouth almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia cyclica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia fasciolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia huangguoshuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia kweichowensis
species.description: Poisson. Utilized for food (Ref. 33406).

species.name: Beaufortia leveretti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mountain streams with gravel bottom (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Beaufortia liui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia multiocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia niulanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia pingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia szechuanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia triocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaufortia zebroida
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beaugregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in seagrass beds, coral or rocky reefs and sandy areas.  Also found around mangrove shores and sponge beds; less common on flourishing coral reefs (Ref. 26938).  They remain within 50 cm from the substrate.  Adults feed on algae, polychaetes, amphipods, foraminiferans and gastropods while juveniles feed on harpacticoid copepods, nemerteans and polychaetes (Ref. 9626).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Caught incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Beautiful Dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beautiful hover goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal reefs and mangrove-lined inlets.  Hovers in schools among branching corals or mangroves to a depth of about 4 meters.

species.name: Beautiful pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with quinaldine in a cave in a steep reef slope  (Ref. 122369).

species.name: Beautiful shiner
species.description: Found in sandy and rocky pools of creeks (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Beautiful-cheek shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy reef slope at a depth of 26 m.  Associated with burrowing alpheid prawns (Ref. 26237).

species.name: Beau’s wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in groups in rubble areas near lagoons and seaward slopes (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Bec de canard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear vegetated lakes, quiet pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798). Usually solitary and highly territorial. Enters brackish water in the Baltic. Adults feed mainly on fishes, but at times feed heavily on frogs and crayfish (Ref. 27547). Cannibalism is common. In arctic lakes, it is sometimes the only species present in a given water body. In such cases, juveniles feed on invertebrates and terrestrial vertebrates; large individuals are mainly cannibals (Ref. 59043). Cannibalistic as juveniles (Ref. 30578). Feces of pike are avoided by other fish because they contain alarm pheromones. Deposits feces at specific locations, distant from its foraging area (Ref. 59043). Eggs and young are preyed upon by fishes, aquatic insect larvae, birds, and aquatic mammals (Ref. 1998). Does not generally undertake long migrations, but a few may move considerable distances (Ref. 27547). Oviparous (Ref. 205). This fish can be heavily infested with parasites, including the broad tapeworm which, if not killed by thorough cooking, can infect human; is used as an intermediate host by a cestode parasite which results to large losses in usable catches of lake whitefish (Coregonus clupeaformis) in some areas; also suffers from a trematode which causes unsightly cysts on the skin (Ref. 9988). Excellent food fish; utilized fresh and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, and baked (Ref. 9988). Valuable game fish (Ref. 5723). In spite of numerous attempts to culture this species, it was never entirely domesticated and does not accept artificial food (Ref. 30578). Locally impacted by habitat alterations (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bec de cane à museau long
species.description: Largest and the longest-snouted lethrinid (Ref. 37816).  Found in sandy coastal areas, lagoons, and reef slopes (Ref. 30573).  Juveniles are found in shallow sandy areas.  Often occurs in large schools.  Adults deep along coastal slopes and drop-offs, usually solitary (Ref. 48635).  Very active and swims fast (Ref. 90102).  Feeds mainly on fish, crustaceans, and cephalopods.  In Palau, it spawns throughout the year on the first few days of the lunar month along the edges of reefs.  Large individuals often ciguatoxic in New Caledonia and possibly elsewhere in Oceania (Ref. 9775). Caught mostly with handline and traps, occasionally by trawls and gill nets (Ref. 68703). Ref. 48635 reports maximum depth of occurrence.

species.name: Bec-de-cane
species.description: Adults inhabit coral reefs during daytime where they feed occasionally in sand and rubble areas between coral heads. At night, they move out over the sandy sea floor and forage actively. Usually occur in small schools. Juveniles live in shallow, inshore waters such as seagrass and mangrove areas, moving into deeper water as they age (Ref. 27260, 28202). Feed mainly on crustaceans, echinoderms, mollusks and fish, with crabs and sea urchins predominating. Much of the information reported for this species was based on misidentifications and referred to L. olivaceous (see Ref. 2295). Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9987). Caught primarily by handline. One of the favourite food and sport fishes around the Great Barrier Reef. A major food fish in New Caledonia. Occasionally implicated in cases of fish poisoning (ciguatoxin) (Ref. 68703).

species.name: Bec-de-cane (Lethrinus nebulosus)
species.description: Inhabit coral reefs, coralline lagoons, seagrass beds, mangrove swamps, flat sand bottoms, and coastal rock areas.  Adults solitary or in small schools; juveniles form large schools in shallow, sheltered sandy areas, also harbors where seagrasses, algae or sponge habitats are found at various depths.  Feed on echinoderms, mollusks and crustaceans, and to some extent on polychaetes and fish.  The reproductive nature of spangled emperors is uncertain, although they also may be protogynous hermaphrodites (Ref. 27260, 55367).  However, recent study classified juvenile hermaphroditism for this species wherein transition from ovary to testis occurs before ovarian maturation, hence, no true sex-reversal in the sense of protogynous hermaphroditism is observed (Ref. 107020).  May have a coppery or iodine taste or smell in the Indian Ocean (Ref. 2295, 11888).  It has been shown that this species can survive for long periods in salinities as low as 10 parts per thousand and therefore it is a potential estuarine aquaculture species (Ref. 2295).  Taken by handline, traps, trawls, seines, and gill nets. Marketed mostly fresh. Very important commercial and sport fish in some countries (Ref. 68703).

species.name: Bec-de-cane lippu
species.description: Occurs in deep lagoons and channels, outer reef slopes and adjacent soft bottom areas (Ref. 30573).  Solitary in or near ledges or caves by day (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on echinoderms, crustaceans, mollusks (Ref. 171), echinoids, crinoids and starfish (Ref. 37816).  May be ciguatoxic in some areas (Ref. 37816). Caught by handline, vertical longline, traps, and trawls. Marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 171, 68703).

species.name: Bec-de-cane à museau court
species.description:
Occurs in small groups over seagrass beds, sand and rubble areas of coral reefs, deep channels, and lagoons.  Usually found in shallow water to depths of 150 m.  Usually seen solitary but sometimes swims in small groups.  Juveniles in seagrass beds (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, fishes, and echinoderms. Caught mostly with handline, traps,
and trawl (Ref. 114226).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Bec-de-lièvre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Usually found in quiet water near boulders.  Males construct large circular or rectangular nests by piling pebbles carried in the mouth (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on insects and mollusks (Ref. 54729).

species.name: Bedotia albomarginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to inland, generally forested, highland habitats; not collected in deforested lower reaches of Mananara or Rienana Rivers; also found in swamps, small rivers and streams that are quite shallow and that are likely subject to periodic drying or very reduced flow (Ref. 56501).

species.name: Bedotia leucopteron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shaded streams between 100 m and 850 m above sea level flowing under degraded forest cover; occurrence not influenced by the composition of the riparian vegetation; pH values range from 6.0-7.0; water temperature is strongly influenced by altitude (17-26°C) (Ref. 76768).

species.name: Bedotia longianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bedotia madagascariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, well-shaded streams at altitudes up to 30 meters above sea level; prefers slow-flowing sections; observed in loose, size-graded associations up to several dozen of individuals; juveniles usually found in the shallows, adults frequent deeper waters (Ref. 76768).

species.name: Bedotia marojejy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bedotia masoala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bedotia tricolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bedrock shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually near emergent vegetation in bedrock pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  These areas are prone to intermittency and harbor relatively few other fishes.  This species appear to be extreme in its ability to tolerate stagnant conditions resulting from low water (Ref. 58354).  Feeds on midge larvae, chydorid cladocerans, water mites, copepods and small mayflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Beibu Bay seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belcher’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belize anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently entirely freshwater and presumably schooling.  More data needed.

species.name: Belize sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove areas (Ref. 75004).

species.name: Belize sponge goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with a hand net from a patch reef of mixed coral and sponge on sloping sand substratum at 5 m (Ref. 81169).

species.name: Belizean tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bell's flasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among dense algal beds of deep lagoons.

species.name: Bella goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with rubble, rock and sand bottoms of coastal reefs in 12-35 m. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Feeds on small invertebrates particularly copepods.

species.name: Bella shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand-rubble bottoms in 12-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bellator farrago
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belle carangue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in deep lagoon and seaward reefs where they feed by rooting for crustaceans and fossorial invertebrates in the sand but they also feed on small fishes (Ref. 9710, 90102).  Small juveniles live among the tentacles of jellyfish (Ref. 9710).  Adults form schools and are also noted for their behavior to closely swim around sharks and other large fishes, and also follow divers (Ref. 10361). Juveniles particularly display this piloting behavior  to gain protection from likely predators (Ref. 9710, 90102).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).  Juveniles are used in the aquarium trade.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Bellfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belligerent sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Strictly marine species (Ref. 82587).

species.name: Bellona flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms and feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Bellottia apoda
species.description: Depth range from 30-500 m (Ref. 6526) and from 460-569 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504). The food of Bellottia apoda appears to be a mixture of planktonic and benthic preys (Ref. 13359). Viviparous (Ref. 6526). Uncommon species (Ref. 34024), but it is not so rare as it seemed in the Adriatic Sea (Ref. 13359).

species.name: Bellottia armiger
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024). Viviparous (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Belly pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in the lower reaches of rivers and streams, and in estuarine habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205, 44894).  Occurs in mangrove estuaries and tidal creeks (Ref. 44894).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Male matures at 7.5-8.0 cm SL.

species.name: Bellybarred pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow coastal and estuarine waters, sometimes among mangroves.  Also found regularly in freshwater in the lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 4967, 44894) and tidal creeks (Ref. 44894).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males maybe brooding at about 9.8 SL.

species.name: Bellyspotted toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bellystriped blaasop
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belobranchus segura
species.description: Inhabits estuaries and lower parts of coastal streams, usually over rocky or gravel bottoms.  Feeds on small shrimps and fish.  Spawns in freshwater, its embryos drift downstream to the sea where they undergo a planktonic phase, before returning to the rivers to grow and reproduce (Ref. 91761).

species.name: Belodontichthys truncatus
species.description: Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975). Found from middle depths to the surface in deeper parts of large rivers. Feeds on smaller fish near the water surface. An excellent game fish which can be caught using hook and line. Presently large numbers are being taken near Stung Treng in Cambodia by explosives (Ref. 12693). Migrates upstream through the Khone Falls in June-July with other silurids and enters the flooded forest in July-October, where it feeds heavily on cyprinids of the genus Henicorhynchus (pa soi, identified as Cirrhinus spp.) (Ref. 38432). Marketed fresh or dried and salted (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Belone euxini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belonion apodion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Belonion dibranchodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Belonoglanis brieni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belonoglanis tenuis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belonophago hutsebouti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belonophago tinanti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Belted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in tide pools, shallow, rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Prefers deeper water habitats (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Belted cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky areas, often near drop-offs.  Solitary or in groups in caves or holes (Ref. 9710).  Often seen hovering in the spines of long-spined urchin.

species.name: Belted sandfish
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from water's edge to at least 18 m depth, often in silty water.  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Not a coral-reef species (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Belted shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotype was speared near a burrow in silty sand that appeared to have been made by an alpheid shrimp (although no shrimp was seen) (Ref. 118499).

species.name: Belted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Common in shallow water (maximum 22 m), over sand and lagal covered rocks; observed to take quick, seemingly indiscrimate bites of the substratum with sand emitted from its gills (Ref. 86689).  Feeds primarily on bivalves, polychaete worms, peanut worms, gastropods, various small crustaceans and foraminiferans (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Bembradium furici
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembradium roseum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep sea species (Ref. 559).  Benthic on sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bembras adenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught at a depth of 225 m.

species.name: Bembras japonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Inhabit sand or sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Bembrops cadenati
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembrops caudimacula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembrops curvatura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the shelf and shelf edge on rocky bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Bembrops macromma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female specimens collected in May have mature gonads (Ref. 13203).

species.name: Bembrops magnisquamis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembrops nelsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembrops nematopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bembrops quadrisella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ben-Tuvia’s deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benedetto's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually encountered solitarily or in small groups containing up to 4 individuals on sheltered reefs in the vicinity of Triton Bay at depths of about 5-20 m. It was often seen on algal-covered rocky surfaces, but on one occasion was found among the branches of an unidentified gorgonian sea fan.  The brood pouch is found immediately behind the anal fin and occupies the ventral surface of the first 10 tail rings (one pouch contained 34 ripe eggs with diameter ca 0.7 mm (Ref. 74959).

species.name: Bengal corvina
species.description: Found in coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Important food fish.

species.name: Bengal demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The island where it occurs has a coral community that extends from near shore to about 200 m offshore. There are large areas of sand ridges, rocky reefs with some mangrove formations, Pandanus vegetation, and scattered boulders/dead corals are the major characteristics of this locality (Ref. 123268).

species.name: Bengal eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit both fresh and brackish waters of rivers and swamps (Ref. 2847, 44894) or near the river mouth (Ref. 13533).  They occur mainly in thick vegetation of muddy, still water bodies, such as lagoons, swamps, canals and rice fields (Ref. 6028).  Live in soft bottom sediments in quiet, well vegetated backwaters of brackish estuaries and nearby swamps (Ref. 44894), usually in burrows.  Prefer estuarine or tidal areas, as efficient burrowers.  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh, usually not kept alive for long periods of time (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Bengal loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Bengal low-fin moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bengal sand diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 93824).

species.name: Bengal sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur singly or in small groups in inshore reef and lagoon environments.  Feed on algae, gastropods, and small crabs.  Highly territorial (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bengal spaghetti-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries.

species.name: Bengal thryssa
species.description: Presumably schooling and inshore.  More data needed.

species.name: Bengal tongue sole
species.description: Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms, often in shallow areas, including river estuaries and brackish waters.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Marketed mostly  fresh and frozen; also dried-salted (Ref. 9895).

species.name: Bengal whipray
species.description: Demersal on insular and continental shelves, and occasionally found in coastal embayments (Ref. 58048); primarily in shallow water from near the shore in estuaries to nearby fishing grounds in bays (Ref. 130662). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Caught in large quantities as by-catch of bottom trawl and trammel net fisheries. Utilized for its meat, but of limited value due to its very small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Bengal yellowfin seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bengala barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the middle and lower reaches of rivers and ponds (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Bengali
species.description: Occurs along cliffs and slightly deep water (Ref. 559, 48635), in coral reef crevices (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Forms small and large aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bengali (Pristiapogon fraenatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in relatively clear waters on reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 25 m.  Cryptic under ledges by day, singly or in small groups (Ref. 1602, 48635). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Minimum depth range reported taken from Ref. 11890. Frequent at base of coral heads or under ledges (Ref 90102).

species.name: Benitochromis batesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, larvophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260)with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns in caves (Ref. 52307, 81260). Both parents brood offspring (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Benitochromis conjunctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260)with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns on open substrates (Ref. 81260). Biparental, i.e. both parents brood offspring (Ref. 52307, 81260).

species.name: Benitochromis finleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns on open substrates; both parents brood offspring (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Benitochromis nigrodorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In coastal rivers and creeks (Ref. 42576). Pair-bonding, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns on open substrates; both parents brood offspring (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Benitochromis riomuniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns on open substrates; both parents brood offspring (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Benitochromis ufermanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) with delayed uptake (Ref. 81260). Spawns on open substrates (Ref. 81260). Both parents can brood offspring (Ref. 52307, 81260).

species.name: Bennett's stingray
species.description: This demersal species is found inshore and on continental shelf to at least 50 m depth.  It feeds on small bony fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 11889, 114953).  Max size may reach up to 85 cm WD (Ref. 47613).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Litters of only 1 pup (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Bennett’s perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by handnet from the ceiling of a cave at a depth of 63 m (Ref. 116682). Included in the aquarium trade (Japan and through Singapore (Ref. 123579).

species.name: Bensbach River Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bentartia cinerea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthenchelys cartieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of the genus Benthenchelys are pelagic (Ref. 39782).

species.name: Benthenchelys indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of the genus Benthenchelys are pelagic (Ref. 39782).

species.name: Benthenchelys pacificus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of the genus Benthenchelys are pelagic (Ref. 39782).

species.name: Benthobatis kreffti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep water species on the continental slope.  Feeds on worms, isopods and amphipods. The late-term embryos seem to gestate in a combined uterine/cloacal chamber. Produces up to 2 pups during each pregnancy. Maturity size of males at ca. 15 cm TL, females at 20 cm TL; birth size at ca. 10 cm TL. It is reported to be locally abundant as many individuals have been collected together in a single trawl (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Benthochromis horii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at depths from 60 to 126 m (Ref. 74417).

species.name: Benthochromis melanoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small crustacens as well as plankton (Ref. 7343). Mouthbrooder (Ref. 74417).

species.name: Benthochromis tricoti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small crustaceans as well as plankton (Ref. 7343). Mouthbrooder (Ref. 74417).

species.name: Benthocometes australiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthophiloides turcomanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 118284.

species.name: Benthophilus casachicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In estuaries and coastal zone of Caspian Sea.

species.name: Benthophilus ctenolepidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthophilus grimmi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns in March and April (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Benthophilus kessleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthophilus leptocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthophilus persicus
species.description: Inhabits brackish waters and is abundant on sandy bottoms in coastal areas (Ref. 126576).

species.name: Benthophilus ragimovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benthophilus svetovidovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Benttooth bristlemouth
species.description: Oceanic, deep-mesopelagic (Ref. 4769, 58302) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Usually vertically oriented during the day (Ref. 4769).  Nocturnal feeder (Ref. 9186) on copepods (Ref. 4769).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35800).

species.name: Berg redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found near vegetation except when the water is turbid.  It can tolerate extreme conditions and survive in various habitats from small streams to large impoundments.  Feeding habits varied in different seasons:  for small fish benthic feeding during spring and midwater feeding during summer; larger fish fed on corixid bugs during summer but switched to chironomid larvae and zooplankton in winter.  Capable of jumping when ascending rapids (Ref. 6465).

species.name: Bergiaria platana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bergiaria westermanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bering eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bering poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bermuda anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species occurring in coastal waters.  Apparently common (at least in August, but not in July).  Specimens with well developed eggs were taken in June, 1927, suggesting a summer spawning period.

species.name: Bermuda killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A euryhaline species found only in a limited number of small, isolated fresh water, brackish water, and marine ponds (Ref. 59051). Recent study confines the distribution of this species to seven small, anchialine ponds in Bermuda (Ref. 59049). Total estimated population is 15,200 individuals in Mangrove Lake which is the largest anchialine pond in Bermuda (Ref. 59049). Non-annual killifish (Ref. 27139). May form loose schools consisting of equally sized individuals (Ref. 59051). An omnivorous fish, feeding on filamentous green algae, plant material, mollusks, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 59156). The main predators include a variety of birds (mostly herons), and fishes (eastern mosquito fish Gambusia holbrooki, gray snapper Lutjanus griseus, and American eel, Anguilla rostrata). Additionally, it is believed that the introduced and invasive red-eared terrapin Trachemys scripta elegans is a significant predator in a limited number of ponds (Ref. 59051). Spawning period occurs from February to September in Mangrove Lake, with primary peaks in May and June for males and females, respectively (Ref. 59049).

species.name: Bermuda porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An important food fish.

species.name: Bermuda tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on coral rubble or sand bottom (Ref. 9952). Minimu depth from Ref. 009952.

species.name: Bernhard's elephant-snout fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bero elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bertella idiomorpha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also caught with plankton nets.

species.name: Bertelsen's lanternfish
species.description: High-oceanic, found between 200-300 m during the day and between 60-175 at night (Ref. 4479, 58302).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Berthold's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow parts of pools and small streams in the rain forest (Ref. 57261). Prefers clear, flowing water in coastal lowlands (Ref. 84174).

species.name: Beryx mollis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betadevario ramachandrani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a small, high-altitude stream with a cascade and riffle-pool habitat and with width of 2.27 m and at depth at most about 30 cm (Ref. 84468).

species.name: Betta albimarginata
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in forest streams with moderate current, in shallow water (5-10 cm deep) in plant roots and leaf litter along the shores.

species.name: Betta antoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta apollon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected in hill-streams strongly shaded by forest; mostly found in shallow water close to the shores between roots, plants or leaf litter.  Some specimens were also collected from the swift flowing area between boulders.  Water data from the type locality:   colourless, clear and with a pH of 6.2, an electric conductivity of 20-40 µS/cm and a  temperature of 24-26 °C (Ref. 78499).

species.name: Betta aurigans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta balunga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest streams with moderate current, very shallow water  among plant roots and submerged leaf litter along the banks.  Also occurs in slow flowing black water streams among submerged stream bank vegetation and submerged leaf litter (Ref. 56613).  An oral brooder (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta breviobesa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta brownorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit very shallow waters in peat swamp forests.

species.name: Betta burdigala
