species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in peat swamp along the road and in secondary forest.

species.name: Betta channoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest streams with brown, acidic waters, usually in shallow water among leaf litter or plant roots.

species.name: Betta chini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow (less than 0.5 m depth) peat swamps with substrate consisting mainly of detritus, leaves and peat (Ref. 12293).  An oral brooder (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta chloropharynx
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a secondary forest area in a pool among leaf litter.

species.name: Betta coccina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta compuncta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly slow flowing small streams in swampy areas of the heath forest, although it can also be found in faster flowing larger tributaries (Ref. 57022). Occurs in these habitats with very acidic waters due to the presence of subterranean and surface coal (Ref. 57022).

species.name: Betta cracens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater swamp forest (Ref. 56386).

species.name: Betta dennisyongi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland hillstream and acid water swamp habitats. Found in clear to brown-water habitats, from secondary forest to plantation and farmland environments. Syntopic with Osteochilus jeruk, Rasbora jacobsoni, Rasbora kluetensis (Cyprinidae); Nemacheilus tuberigum (Nemacheilidae); Mystus punctifer (Bagridae); and Ompok brevirictus, Kryptopterus piperatus (Siluridae) (Ref. 93059).

species.name: Betta dimidiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found very abundant in leaf litter in forest streams and swamp forest (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Betta edithae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally in the ornamental trade.

species.name: Betta enisae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest streams, usually among leaf litter along the shores in shallow water (Ref. 12804).

species.name: Betta falx
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically found among submerged bank vegetation, in near stagnant waters, with pH 4.7-6.8. Latin word falx means scythe, alluding to the continuous curved shape of the broad anal and caudal distal margins of a male in display. Caudal fin rounded.

species.name: Betta ferox
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality was described as a small river with current (0.4 m/s); ground formed by
gravel and in parts by sand. The fighting fishes were found at the banks, slower current , between roots and plants (Araceae).  Water data as described: pH 5.8-6.3, 30-52 µS/cm, 23.3-
24.2 °C.  Type specimens in February 2005 with pH 6.3, electric conductivity 51 µS/cm and water-temperature 25.5 °C (Ref. 78499).

species.name: Betta foerschi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rain forest creek.

species.name: Betta gladiator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is an aggressive and territorial species which inhabits heath forest with acidic water.  Single adults stay about one meter apart, usually together with a small number of juveniles. Individuals kept in captivity continuously fight and have to be kept separately, otherwise they would have killed each other (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta hendra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in peat swamps with depth of about 5 to 50 cm and with no water current.  The water was shaded by trees and bushes.  Collected among the aquatic and marsh plants. Forms bubble nest based on aquarium conditions (Ref. 93322).

species.name: Betta hipposideros
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in backwater peat swamps with substrate usually peat and leaf litter.  Large fish are found in the flowing sections of the blackwater streams and smaller ones appear to prefer pools and slower flowing waters.

species.name: Betta ibanorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in blackwater habitats, with water tinged orange in color due to leaching of tannins from dead plant matter and peat (Ref. 55025). Observed as paternal oral brooder with the typical egg-chase (Ref. 55025). Also Ref. 84801.

species.name: Betta ideii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta krataios
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta kuehnei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species were collected in shallow water, among aquatic plants (Cryptocoryn cordata) and leaf litter. It is a shaded, forested creek with clear water, colorless (pH 7,0, hardness 3 dGH, temperature about 25°C). Other labyrinth fishes collected with Betta kuehnei were Trichopsis vittata and Parosphromenus paludicola. A mouthbrooding species and its reproductive behavior similar to that of other species of the Betta pugnax group where males carry the eggs (usually between 40 to 80) in their mouth for about 12 days. The eggs measure 1.0 to 1.4 mm in diameter with the offspring leaving the mouth at size approximately 7 mm. No particular color pattern was observed during spawning (Ref. 82661).

species.name: Betta lehi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in peat swamp forests and acid water swamp forests.  Occurs in quiets parts of streams among overgrown submerged bank vegetation (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta livida
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a peat swamp forest (Ref. 84801), mostly in well shaded shallow waters (less than a meter deep) or along the vegetated banks of deeper streams.  Occurs usually in slow flowing water.  Preferred substrate appears to be leaf litter or submerged detritus.  Builds a bubble nest, with the male aggressively chasing the female to below the nest (Ref. 13213) .

species.name: Betta mahachaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Encountered in nipa palm (Nypa fruticans) swamps, especially in the water-holding phytotelma of the palm bract, which the pair use for bubble-nest building, courtship, and hatching of fry (Ref. 92085).

species.name: Betta mandor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta midas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A paratype series was collected from a blackwater river running through remnant and intact peat swamp forest, with pH  4.1(Ref. 81926).

species.name: Betta miniopinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shaded, acidic waters in a swamp forest, with leaf litter and soft mud substrate.

species.name: Betta nuluhon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fighting fish species is collected from a shallow, clear-water hill stream habitat, bordered by overhanging vegetation, situated at the edge of a dense forest canopy. The substrate was composed mainly of pebbles, sand and silt (Ref. 123126). Maximum size based on holotype specimen (Ref. 123126).

species.name: Betta obscura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta ocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit more slow flowing areas of the headwater habitats (Ref. 34011).  Found usually in ravines and isolated elevated pools.  An adult and several juveniles  are usually  encountered in submerged leaf litter. Adults may take cover under floating leaves and are excellent jumpers, which may explain their presence in isolated elevated pools (Ref. 56613).  Feed mainly on terrestrial insects and occasionally on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta omega
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is currently recorded only from the remnant black water swamps in Johor, Malaysia. Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 127779).

species.name: Betta pallida
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected in February 2005 in a slowly flowing creek which was only 20 to 50 cm deep; the water was clear and slightly tanned, bed covered densely with leaf litter; water
data pH 6.3, 82 µS/cm and 25.5°C.  From another creek, where the species was collected, pH 6.5, 69 µS/cm and 26.6 °C (Ref. 78499).

species.name: Betta pallifina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in headwater habitats (Ref 56613).  Probably a paternal oral-brooder (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta pardalotos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species collected from smaller feeder streams (Ref. 82268).

species.name: Betta patoti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta persephone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Betta pi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily found in well shaded peat forest blackwater swamps and creeks which drained out such swamps; the beds are usually covered with dense leaf litter and lots of roots and plants. The free water area is often small, with pH of about 6.0 (Ref. 78499); very soft and deep (up to 1.3 m ) substrate (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Betta pinguis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in forest streams with slow current and swamp forest, in shore vegetation and leaf litter (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Betta prima
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marshes and slow flowing streams (Ref. 43281).  Specimens were collected between overflowed plants; clear and colourless water; water data taken in Oct. 1999, 2:00 pm: pH 6.6, 180 µS/cm and 25.8 °C (Ref. 78499).

species.name: Betta pulchra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 84801). Occurs in blackwater habitats and commonly found only in the overgrown bank vegetation of the irrigation canals.  Paternal Mouth brooder (Ref. 13220).

species.name: Betta raja
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland swamp forests (Ref. 56386).

species.name: Betta renata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in black-waters draining out from peat swamp forests.  Also collected from a flooded peat swamp forest, among plant debris and logs in shallow tea-colored water, with a pH of 4.1 (Ref. 30225).

species.name: Betta rutilans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta schalleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest swamp, peat swamp and hill stream.

species.name: Betta siamorientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow freshwater marshes, grass fields, and paddy fields. Found at the water edge (with dense vegetation) of ponds, lagoons, ditches, canals, and others water ways. Occurs in still waters and uses water plants as shelter to set up safe territory for building the bubble-nest, courtship, and hatching of fry. Cohabits with Trichopsis vittata, Trichopsis schalleri, Trichopsis pumila, Trichopodus trichopterus, Anabas testudineus, Lepidocephalichthys hasselti, Pangio anguillaris , Macrognathus siamensis, and Monopterus albus (Ref. 93122).

species.name: Betta simorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Betta simplex
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits limestone streams and marshes (Ref. 58784).  The type locality was described as a pool of 10-15 m diameter, up to 10 m deep and the species was collected along the banks. Water data reported was 27 °C, pH 7.0, electric conductivity 530 µS/cm.   Examined specimens were collected in a comparatively fast flowing, clear-water creek and were found between plants (Ref. 78499).  Carnivorous, feeding on zooplankton and insects (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Betta spilotogena
species.description: Inhabits swamps as well as adjacent streams, usually in relatively shallow water about a meter or so in depth with dense vegetation growing along the banks and under shade.

species.name: Betta stigmosa
species.description: Found in hill streams (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Betta tomi
species.description: Inhabits well shaded shallow streams in very soft mud substrate with abundant leaf litter and detritus.

species.name: Betta tussyae
species.description: Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Betta uberis
species.description: Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 57022).

species.name: Betta waseri
species.description: Inhabits well shaded peat forest blackwater streams with dense leaf litter beds, mud substrates and dense growths of roots. Also Ref. 84801.

species.name: Betty's ocean sleeper
species.description: The 4 m2 clove oil station was deployed over a reef outcrop surrounded by sand at a depth of 11 m. Enclosed microhabitats included heavily sedimented reef matrix, live branching and massive corals, Halimeda, sand, and overhangs/crevices (Ref. 130190).

species.name: Bevecca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water between dense algal growth.  Feeds on bottom invertebrates.

species.name: Beyazsu chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift and clear flowing water over cobble and pebbles. Collected together with Capoeta umbla (Heckel, 1843), Barbus lacerta Heckel, 1843, Oxynoemacheilus sp., Alburnus mossulensis Heckel, 1843, Garra rufa (Heckel, 1843) and Alburnus caeruleus Heckel, 1843 (Ref. 94737).

species.name: Beysehir bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which occurs in lakes.  Is threatened due to the introduction of other species and overfishing (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Beysehir dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beysehir minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beysehir nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beysehir spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Beyşehir gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Beyşehir minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bezoule
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep waters. Disappeared in the 1960s (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Biajaca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In fast-flowing rivers as well as in lakes, preferably among plants.  Can be found in brackish river mouths.  Feeds on worms, other small fish, shrimps and water insects  (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Biara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently carnivorous, probably ichthyophagous.  Maximum length reported to reach 64 cm SL (Ref. 26147).

species.name: Bibarba parvoculus
species.description: This species is found in a karst cave at altitude of 232 m.  There exists an underground stream 30 m after entering the cave and about 12 m beneath the surface of the cave entrance. This fish occurs in pools with mud and cobblestone beds, 5-50 m2 area and 1-3 m depth.  This is syntopic with <i>Oreonectes microphthalmus Du et al. 2008, <i>Sinocyclocheilus brevis Lan & Chen 1992 and <i>Pterocryptis anomala (Herre, 1933) (Ref. 98800).

species.name: Bichique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift clear rainforest streams, where it feeds on algae (Ref. 26638).  Hatching and larval stages in the sea, post-larvae and adults in freshwater (Ref. 4343). Also Ref. 51243.

species.name: Bichique (Ophiocara porocephala)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in brackish estuaries, river mouths and freshwater creeks (Ref. 2847, 48637, 44894).  Found in the lower courses of rivers, often upstream from the tidal zone (Ref. 12693).  Young are usually found while wading in rocky creeks near the coast (Ref. 2847).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Bichique (Sicyopterus lagocephalus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fast-flowing sections of clear rainforest streams over rocky bottoms (Ref. 44894).  Hatching and larval stage occur at sea, postlarval stage to adult in freshwater (Ref. 4343, 79840).  Commercial in Reunion, where they are caught during the few days when they return from sea to enter the rivers (Doug Fenner, pers. comm., 2002, Ref. 79840).  Smallest gravid female reported 5.03 cm SL (Ref. 37578).

species.name: Bichique noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoons, estuaries and freshwater (Ref. 6028, 48637, 79840). They occur in the lower reaches of freshwater streams, usually on mud bottoms (Ref. 44894). Juveniles are found mainly among mangrove roots in the more saline areas of lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 6028, 79840). Carnivorous (Ref. 79840). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Bicolor basslet
species.description: Inhabits steep seaward slopes and walls (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Bicolor butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally encountered in shallower water in caves or at the bases of overhangs (Ref. 5288).  Also occurs on seamounts (Ref. 057925). Usually occur in pairs, which browse over the rocky substratum in search of benthic invertebrates.  Unknown to marine aquarium enthusiasts (Ref. 4858).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bicolor chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually seen singly or in small groups on coastal reefs, amongst mixed algae-coral reef or rocky reefs (Ref. 48636).  They are found on exposed seaward reefs; less abundant in lagoons and channels.  Feed on zooplankton.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Bicolor damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coral reefs and isolated patch reefs in deeper water.  Feed primarily on algae but also on polychaetes, hydroids, copepods and ascidians (Ref. 9626).  Aggressively territorial but only around a small area (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Bicolor false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare.  The sixteen individuals which have been collected were captured by dipnets at the surface under electric lights (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Bicolor minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bicolor scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bicolor slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bicolor spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bicolor toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bicolored foxface
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among hard corals at the faces of drop-offs at reef edges or in deep pools inside reef crests.  Juveniles form schools, adults occur in pairs.  Feeds on seaweeds (Ref. 9813).

species.name: Bicolour fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary in coastal, lagoon and seaward reefs from below the surge zone to 30 m depth (Ref. 9710, 90102). They feed on skin, scales, fins and mucus of other fish. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). A mimic of Meiacanthus atrodorsalis (Ref. 2334). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Bicoloured dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves in coral and rock reefs on reef slopes and dropoffs (Ref. 75154, 81967).

species.name: Bidenichthys beeblebroxi
species.description: Common species found in holes under rocks and boulders (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Bidenichthys slartibartfasti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species found in holes and crevices of rubble areas (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Bifid clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores.  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Big Bend gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated, spring-fed sloughs and ponds (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Big eye chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Big red cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Big red cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a generally turbid river with muddy banks, from a rocky stretch with an accelerated current (Ref. 78623).

species.name: Big roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Big tailed lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers, brooks, swamps and shallow parts of larger rivers and lakes (Ref. 47311).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Big-belly seahorse
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in large rock pools at low tide.  They remain motionless amidst seaweed.  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 30915) or attached to drifting seaweeds (Ref. 31838).  Feed on minute crustaceans (e.g. copepods and amphipods).  Nocturnal (Ref. 9003).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Seen in groups at night.  Also around jetties and other man-made objects; attached to sponges and colonial hydroids in deeper water (Ref. 30915).  Length measurements refer to height (= TL - head length).
This is the largest seahorse species in southeastern Australia, and has more dorsal fin rays and tail rings than any other seahorse (Ref. 31838).  Sold locally and internationally for the aquarium trade (Ref. 31838).  Dried and sold to the Oriental medicine trade as a tonic and aphrodisiac (Ref. 5316, 34026).

species.name: Big-eye mandarin fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Big-eye unicorn-cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic, inhabits the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Big-eyed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).

species.name: Big-eyed icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Big-head dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Big-head pennah croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.  Feeds on small invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 2113).

species.name: Big-head schizothoracin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and rivers with slight current and lives on other fishes and aquatic insects (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Big-headed deepsea herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Big-headed lanternbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by trawl and landed in fish markets; apparently found on continental shelf and in nearby waters (Ref. 96184).

species.name: Big-lip damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually among beds of branching corals in shallow lagoon reefs, singly or in small groups (Ref. 4966). Feed primarily on the polyps of Acropora corals. Diurnal species (Ref. 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Big-scale parma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Museum specimens indicate that this species is probably most abundant in non-coral reef coastal waters, although one specimen at the Australian Museum was taken at Great Island on the Great Barrier Reef, Australia.  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Big-scaled redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivore, feeding mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 41299).  Length type refers to body length and is assumed in TL.

species.name: Bigbarb dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Bigcheek snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7321).

species.name: Bigeye brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bigeye cabillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in outer reef slopes generally at depths below 30 m (Ref. 1602).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bigeye chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or silty sand substrates in areas of little or moderate current in larger creeks and small to medium rivers. Feeds on midge larvae, large mayfly and stonely nymphs (Stenonema, Ephemera, Isoperla) (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Bigeye cigarfish
species.description: Occurs from the border of the continental shelf to about 1,000 m depth (Ref. 13628).  Found near the surface at night (Ref. 9834).  Adults feed mainly on salps (Ref. 33689).

species.name: Bigeye clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024), inhabiting coral reefs (Ref. 13278). Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of shallow water (<10 m) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bigeye gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reefs (Ref. 7300) of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigeye jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep rocky runs and pools of small to medium rivers, usually among large rubble and boulders and rarely in riffles.

species.name: Bigeye lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Bigeye lates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles live in a specific inshore habitat until they reach 18 cm, thereafter they adopt a benthic habitat moving into deep water (Ref. 2216). Juveniles have been observed near or in affluent rivers (Ref. 36901). Top predator in depths below 100 m; exploits both fishes and invertebrates; migrate diurnally to surface to feed on pelagic clupeids; highly susceptible to intensive fishing (Ref. 2216).

species.name: Bigeye lightfish
species.description: Mesopelagic and bathypelagic species.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35839).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Bigeye mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found over vegetated sand grounds and over mud bottoms in mangrove areas (Ref. 3722).  May form aggregations.  Probably feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5217).  Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed; processed into fishmeal (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Bigeye notothen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-water species, generally inhabiting deep waters and less frequently in shallow waters.  Collected from flat bottom without big shelters, like rocky niches and seaweeds (Ref. 122792).

species.name: Bigeye numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs above sandy bottom near rocky reef areas. Females reaches maturity at 32 cm TL, males at ca. 24 cm TL; born at ca. 12 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Bigeye poacher
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Bigeye scabbard fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye sea perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Bigeye searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found mostly below 27 m depth.  Young are very common in bays and estuaries.

species.name: Bigeye searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic to benthopelagic in the northern parts of range, occurring from 300-1,000 m in the daytime, but as shallow as 100-120 m at night (Ref. 4461).

species.name: Bigeye shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing, usually clear and rocky, pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Often found near emergent vegetation along the stream margin (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on surface insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Bigeye silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 3.5-4.8 cm long and 2.5-3.0 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41298).

species.name: Bigeye snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, pebble, and rocky bottoms (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Bigeye squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species (Ref. 6868).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bigeye stardrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye stargazer
species.description: Occurs in surf beaches, usually in less than 3 m depth.  Burrows in soft sandy bottom, where it waits for prey, with only the eyes, nose and mouth protruding.

species.name: Bigeye sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky shore (Ref. 106074).

species.name: Bigeye triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigeye whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling along beaches and down to 22 m.  A single specimen was recorded from Coqueiros at the mouth of the Paraguaçu River, thus able to tolerate lowered salinities.  More data needed.

species.name: Bigfin eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Bigfin lanternfish
species.description: Epipelagic to mesopelagic, at surface at night (Ref. 31442).  Adults feed on small crustaceans (Ref. 11712).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Lipid content is 4.3 % in fresh body weight, while wax ester is present in trace amounts (Ref. 9197).  Preyed upon by fishes, cephalopods, birds and marine mammals.  Easily attracted to a light suspended above the water at night and many are captured in dipnets (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Bigfin mora
species.description: Trawled in shallow waters, less than 100 m depth (Ref. 121621).

species.name: Bigfin pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 6601, 58302).  Most adults are taken in hauls to depths exceeding 500 m, none in hauls to depths less than 250 m.  Larvae are taken year-round throughout its range, chiefly in hauls to depths less than 200 and apparently not in hauls restricted to the upper 100 m (Ref. 10755).  Adults are presumed to prey on other midwater fishes.  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 6691).

species.name: Bigfin shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy-muddy bottoms.  Observed associating with snapping shrimps (Ref. 37490). Also found in silty sand bottoms, often on slopes in 20-40 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bigfin snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms to 25 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Bigfoot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices in 0-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Bighead brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Two specimens known, one of which was collected from a depth of 22 m.

species.name: Bighead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in lowland wetlands and rivers (Ref. 57235). Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549). Occurs in shallow, open water and is capable of lying buried in mud for lengthy period if ponds and lakes evaporate during dry seasons (Ref. 9987). Can move out of the water using its extended fins (Ref. 9987). Found in medium to large-sized rivers, stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals and flooded fields of the Mekong (Ref. 12975). Spawns in small streams (Ref. 9987). Feeds on aquatic insects, young shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 6459). In Thailand, it was thought wrongly as female of Clarias batrachus (Ref 2686). Important foodfish and in pond cultures (Ref. 57235). Marketed live, fresh and frozen; consumed fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9987). Cultivated on a small scale but attempts to farm it are increasing (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Bighead catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bighead portholefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually associated with continental and island slopes (Ref. 4769).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Occurs at 100-300 m by day, 200-500 m by night (Ref. 4463).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4769).  Photophore development complete by about 27 mm SL (Ref. 4769).

species.name: Bighead pupfish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Bighead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly over stony bottom (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Bighead searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in bays.  Young occur in estuaries.

species.name: Bighead searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, but mostly bathypelagic to benthopelagic.

species.name: Bighead snailfish
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées.

species.name: Bighead viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of shallow water, usually in rocky crevices (Ref. 90102).  A 5.6 cm SL gravid female (USNM 394976) with 95 embryos, 0.41 cm TL in length, and approximately 50 orange eggs, 0.06 cm in diameter (Ref. 81230).

species.name: Bight redfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species (Ref. 7300) occurring on rocky reefs and muddy substrates of the continental shelf and upper slopes (Ref. 9563), singly or in pairs (Ref. 79654).

species.name: Bight skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over soft bottoms of the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Mainly feeds on small bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205); egg cases ca. 19 cm long (Ref. 114953). This species reaches maturity at ca. 13 years. Length of mature males at ca. 120 cm TL; young hatch at ca. 26 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Bight stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Biglip snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigmouth chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Bigmouth croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, estuaries and mouths of rivers.  Also caught with bottom trawls and handlines (Ref. 9772).  Marketed fresh as well as dried salted; swim bladder dried (Ref. 2113).

species.name: Bigmouth scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on rocky bottom or coral reefs, but also on sand and rubble bottom (Ref. 42181).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bigmouth sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Bigmouth sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and brackish waters near the shore (Ref. 4833).  Feeds on invertebrates and small fishes.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Bigmouth shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy and silty runs and pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Bigmouth shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seen hovering over holes. Associated with Alpheus djiboutensis. Found in sand and silt bottoms of sheltered reefs in 2-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bigmouth silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigmouth stardrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bignose fanskate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bignostril podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic, inhabits crevices in 15-45 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bigpored snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled at depths greater than 125 meters (Ref. 4241).

species.name: Bigscale bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling in caves and near rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Bigscale deepsea smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, perhaps with diel migration (Ref. 58302).  Usually caught singly, but also in small aggregations (Ref. 6345).  Feed on plankton (Ref. 6345).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bigscale flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigscale jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf; over silt bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigscale logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel and sand runs and pools of small to medium rivers, and also in impoundments.

species.name: Bigscale pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and lakes, apparently in both still and running water; seems to occur in rather acid waters (Ref. 188).

species.name: Bigscale ponyfish
species.description: Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigscale rubyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species occurring on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Bigscale scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore (Ref. 7300) and benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigscale squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Bigsnout whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigspined boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope, usually in depths greater than 300 m (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Bigspot barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from acidic swamps (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Bigspot minidartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty and sheltered reefs in a few meters depth.  Swims in small groups near corals (Ref. 48637). Also found in lagoon reefs in 2-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Bigspot rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found along rocky shores exposed to strong surge (Ref. 54980). Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bigtail skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 41299).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 13.0-14.6 cm long and 6.0-8.0 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: Bigtooth cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer exposed deep reefs and rocky outcroppings (Ref. 7251). Eggs are incubated orally by both parents (Ref. 240). This is the only species in the genus Apogon with mouthbrooding done by males and females (Ref. 85456).

species.name: Bigtooth flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef and soft bottom.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bigtooth pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found near land masses (Ref. 4388).

species.name: Bigtooth river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bihunichthys monopteroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dense water stream (pH approximately 3.5) with almost no current in leaf litter among dense grass growth (Ref. 26627).

species.name: Bikini Atoll moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in crevices of surge channels and rugged wave-swept reefs.

species.name: Bilabria gigantea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bilabria ornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters.

species.name: Biliton blenniella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in intertidal zones in large rock pools or coastal bays (Ref. 48636).  Found near-shore (Ref. 9962); common in tide pools (Ref. 559).  They feed on algae scraped from rubble or rock surfaces.  Sometimes numerous individuals can be seen clinging to rocks out of the water when the level drops on the low of the swell.  When disturbed in rock pools during low tide, they may jump out of the water to get to other rock pools or safer deeper water nearby (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bilobed ghost goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reef flats with algae and seagrass habitats (Ref. 48637). Common on blades of seagrasses (e.g. Enhalus) (Ref. 1602). Feeds on small crustaceans taken from the blades or water nearby (Ref. 37816). Depth range from 0-22 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Binoclard élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and offshore reefs (Ref., 90102). This species forms large groups in caves under ledges or beneath overhangs in reef (under Acropora plate corals) . Individuals forage at night, on zooplankton (mainly crustacean larvae and polychaetes (Ref. 43239, 90102, 107896).

species.name: Binocular fish
species.description: Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154).

species.name: Bintan damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in turbid coastal waters on rocky bottoms (Ref. 31117).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bintuni goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in turbid river channels and small tidal creeks on mud and sand bottoms.  Occurs occasionally in clear rainforest streams.

species.name: Biocellated righteye founder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A specimen was collected in the coral-reef lagoon of a fringing reef at a depth of less than 1 m (0-1 m), on coral gravel with scattered corals (Ref. 122002).

species.name: Biotoecus dicentrarchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality was a shallow laguna about 25 m wide, with transparent water, vegetation resembling needlegrass; water temperature 34°C; associated with another cichlid species, Crenicara filamentosum, the dominant species at the locality (Ref. 86446).

species.name: Biotoecus opercularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Birdi loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in clear mountain streams (Ref. 41236).  Benthic bottom feeder preferring lentic habitats (Ref. 33323).

species.name: Birdled jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits burrows in shallow coastal waters. Also found in sand/rubble bottoms in 2-17 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Birdsong's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184).  Max. length (Edward O. Murdy, pers. comm., 2000).

species.name: Biringo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater lakes and streams (Ref. 81467).  The females show breeding colors.  Caught for food in Japan.

species.name: Birthmark fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal pelagic species, to a lesser extent epipelagic to mesopelagic over the continental slope (Ref. 168). Schooling by size is well developed and initiates at approximately 3 cm (Ref. 168); may also form schools with Sarda chiliensis, Trachurus symmetricus and Sardinops sagax (Ref. 9340). Adults stay near the bottom during the day; go up to the open water at night, (Ref. 5377) where they feed on copepods and other crustaceans, fishes and squids (Ref. 168). They spawn in batches (Ref. 51846). Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). In Asian waters, they move to deeper water and remain inactive during the winter season (Ref. 4576). Commercially cultured in Japan. Marketed fresh, frozen, smoked, salted and occasionally canned (Ref. 9684). Eaten fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Bishop toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits calm zones of flowing waters, standing waters, marshes and other shallow areas (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Bismarck waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was trawled from a steep rocky slope with gorgonian corals (Ref. 118112).

species.name: Biting blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic or benthopelagic in or over coral (Ref. 58302). Common from the shallow waters to about 15 m. Taken with rotenone at 3-5 feet along rocky seashores where there was some sand bottom and where water circulation was good. Some specimens were collected from the stomachs of large fish (e.g. yellowfin tuna, Neothunnus macropterus) and from dolphins (Coryphaena hippurus) (Ref. 643). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bitschumbi lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swamps, shallows and shore regions of Lakes Edward and George; shore regions and papyrus swamps in northern part of Lake Victoria (Ref. 47311). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139). Development time of eggs in captivity is 14 days; sexual maturity reached at 6-7 months (Ref. 47311).

species.name: Bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs most abundantly in still or slow-flowing water with dense aquatic vegetation and sand-silt bottom as lowland ponds, canals, slow-flowing rivers, backwaters and oxbows, where mussels are present (Ref. 59043). Found among plants over sand and muddy bottoms in shallow waters. Remarkable for its habit of deposing its eggs in the cavity of bivalves (Unio). Feeds mainly on plants and to a lesser degree on worms, crustaceans, and insect larvae. Formerly used for pregnancy tests: females injected with urine from pregnant women protruded their ovipositors (Ref. 6258). Live span is exceptionally up to 5 years but most individuals do not survive the year of their first reproduction and population sizes fluctuate greatly over the years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bivalve pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024) inhabiting coastal waters. Found in the mantle cavity of pearl oysters (Pinctada spp.) and other large bivalves (Ref. 1602) as well as in holothurians (Ref. 7300). It feeds on crustaceans and polychaetes and is reported to tend towards sexual pairing in the host (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Bivibranchia bimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sandy and rocky bottoms.  Has a very protractile mouth which allows it to dig in the sand for organisms on which it feeds.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  The juveniles are often found in tributaries which may be very distant from the main river beds (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Bivibranchia fowleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bivibranchia notata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bivibranchia simulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The size of the eyes, which is relatively large in relation to body size, suggests a crepuscular activity (Ref. 12225).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bivibranchia velox
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Biwia springeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Biwia tama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Biwia yodoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Biwia zezera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bizet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults form large schools in coastal areas with sandy substrate.  They feed on fish, crustaceans, and cephalopods.  Are batch spawners (Ref. 51846).  Females lay 140,000 eggs, which hatch into 5mm long larvae (Ref. 35388).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).  Utilized fresh, smoked, canned and frozen; can be fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Divided into two stocks:  West stock and North Sea stock.  West stock spawns in a belt from the Biscay to Ireland in early spring, migrates north and eastwards to southern Norway and northern North Sea.  North Sea stock spawns in the southern North Sea in summer, migrates to central North Sea, Skagerrak and Kattegat.

species.name: Blaasop beauty
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blachea longicaudalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black Amur Bream
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Black angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 43239).  Found in small groups or solitarily.  Captured specimens few (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Black armoured searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken from the bottom with temperatures ranging from 7.3 to 10°C (Ref. 51211).

species.name: Black barnacle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black barracudina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Black bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Endemic in coastal areas, rivers and estuaries of Australia.  Most abundant in river mouths and estuaries (Ref. 28468, 28472).  Inhabit brackish waters of coastal rivers and lakes, occasionally penetrating fresh water (Ref. 44894).  Considered as the only true estuarine sparid in Australia.  Larvae and small juveniles are most abundant over seagrass beds in shallow estuarine waters (Ref. 28468, 28472).  Spawning period varies considerably between estuaries (Ref. 28468).  Remain upstream in sheltered waters to spawn and is not usually found in purely marine habitats (Ref. 44894).  Feed on shellfish, worms, crustaceans, small fish and algae.  Sold as whole, chilled products in domestic markets (Ref. 6390).  One of top angling species in southern Australia (Ref. 6390, 44894), as well as being a delicious table fish (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Black brotula (Stygnobrotula latebricola)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species inhabiting shallow rocky ledges and reefs (Ref. 7251), found deep within the reef during the day (Ref. 9710).  A live-bearing species (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Black buffalo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds and backwaters of small to large rivers.  Also lives in impoundments and lakes.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Feeds on Asiatic clam, algae, diatoms and crustaceans (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Black buntingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Black butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral rich to algae-covered rocky areas of lagoon and seaward reefs including estuarine areas.  Usually paired (Ref. 9710).  Omnivorous and feeds on algae, coral, and small benthic invertebrates.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Maintaining this species in captivity is difficult.

species.name: Black cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow well protected coastal bays, commonly found under jetties, hiding in dark areas (Ref. 48635); also in inshore rocky areas and among branching coral (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Black catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has oviducal fertilization.

species.name: Black cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 4774).

species.name: Black comb-tooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various coral reef habitats from estuaries to outer reef lagoons to about 20 m depth, but usually more common on shallow reef flat at the 6 m mark (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Cryptic usually on corals and sponges of isolated outcrops (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Black coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep slopes, subject to strong currents, with isolated outcrops of black corals (Ref. 48637).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Found in small groups.  Eggs are laid on a branch section after removing the polyps and guarded  by the male (Ref. 48637).  Associated with antipatharian corals at depths below 15 m (Ref. 2334).  Dart out to feed on small animals of the plankton (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Black coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in shallow water regions such as protected reef flats and reef crests. It is highly specialized and prefers fine-branched corals such as Acropora selago and small tabulate colonies of Acropora hyacinthus. Seldom occurs in other Acropora species, such as A. acuminata, A. samoensis, A. eurystoma and A. valida. Due to its black colouration it is sometimes difficult to detect within the dark interstices of narrow-branched Acropora colonies (Ref. 94082).

species.name: Black cow-tongue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore (including semi-enclosed sea areas) on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Black crinoid clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on a crinoid, Oxycomanthus bennetti (Müller, 1841), black colour phase with green tentacles (family Comasteridae). Exact locality and depth where the species was collected unknown (due to confusion of station data) but was probably collected in a pass leading out of the lagoon, with a depth between 5 and 20 m. (Ref. 98449).

species.name: Black damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow inshore reefs exposed to some wave action (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black dotted sand perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, usually on patches of rubble or pavement between corals.  Also found in habitats with rubble and rock (Ref. 48636) solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Black driftfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black drummer
species.description: Large schools form in the vicinity of rocky outcrops and in harbors under jetties.  Juveniles found in estuaries, mainly in seagrass areas.  Secretive during the day, among rocks and hiding in caves and ledges (Ref. 9002).  A popular angling fish in southern Queensland and New South Wales (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Black eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 2850).  May be used as bait (Ref. 27436).  Flesh considered firm and tasty but not esteemed (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Black fathead
species.description: An oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic species (Ref. 6891).  Feeds mainly on salps (Ref. 33689).  Potentially valuable food fish in warm temperate and tropical areas of the Indo-Pacific (Ref. 9811).  May be caught using a pelagic trawl (Ref. 33689).

species.name: Black fin moon tetra
species.description: This species was caught close to the bank of the river, at a depth of about 1 meter over sand and mud; banks covered with dense, undisturbed riparian vegetation consisting of large numbers of entangling lianas covering large trees which also bear many epiphytic orchids (Ref. 91757). Water temperature in the shallows where most specimens were collected was between 21.0-22.5°C and pH 7.6; water very turbid and current moderately rapid (Ref. 91757).

species.name: Black flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, generally at depth of less than 50 m.  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).  This species is poorly studied, fast growing and short lived (to at least 4 years) (Ref. 47621).

species.name: Black foxface
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers areas of staghorn or fire corals, or around rubble mounds composed of plate and staghorn corals.  Subadults and adults in pairs, juveniles probably form schools.  Feeds on seaweeds.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9813).

species.name: Black Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic and lotic freshwater (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Black garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on silty sand bottom (Ref. 33408) or muddy habitats (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in colonies (Ref 90102).

species.name: Black Garra
species.description: This species occurs in small rock pools, in shallow part of larger pools with almost stagnant water and in rather fast-flowing streamlets. It is most common over fine sand and muddy substrate with scattered boulders which provide the species some hiding places, and also over bare rock, gravel and among aquatic plants. Apparently, a substrate feeder as indicated by its inferior mouth and the large papillose mental disc. Stomach contents consist mainly on unicellular algae, filamentous algae, fragments of Rotatoria, Nematoda and crustaceans, as well as large amounts of inorganic matter like sand grains (Ref. 46647).

species.name: Black gill stardrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting shallow reefs (Ref. 9710). Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 26180). Often found near the bottom around soft and hard corals. Occasionally been seen spawning with the H. chlorurus (Ref. 26938)

species.name: Black Horabagrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality West Venpala of Manimala River has a width of 40- 50 m, depth <1 to 5 m, bank height of 1 m in summer season, sediments generally silty clay with occasional patches of sand, and moderately dense riparian vegetation. Syntopic with Catla catla, Cyprinus carpio communis, Labeo rohita, Labeo dussumeiri, Cirrhina mrigala, Puntius mahecola, P. amphibus, Pethia ticto, Haludaria fasciata, Drawkinsia filamentosa, Systomus subnasutus, Wallago attu, Heteropneusteus fossilis, Clarias dussumeiri and Ompok malabaricus (Ref. 94428).

species.name: Black jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, on rubble or soft bottoms.

species.name: Black lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An aberrant population was found in the deeper parts of lake Naivasha. May now be extinct in Kenya due to the introduction of Tilapia and Micropterus salmoides (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Black lancer catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large muddy rivers.  Feeds on crustaceans, other small benthic animals and on detritus of higher plants which are much more slowly digested and remains in the gut for longer periods of time.  Spawns at the beginning of the rainy season and utilizes the flooded riparian forests.  Juveniles begin to appear in August.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Black lantern fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at 100-1000 m at night, 640-900 m during day (Ref. 58302).  The two large specimens (19 and 21 cm SL) from near the Ogasawara Islands reported in Ref. 559 may represent another species (Ref. 36121).

species.name: Black legskate
species.description: Found on the slope (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsule measures 36.0 mm long and 19.0 mm wide (Ref. 41249).  Taken only by deep-trawling research vessels (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Black leopard wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Found in areas of mixed sand, rubble, and algae (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Black lined barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Tends to form small shoals.  More abundant in the larger, clear water, undisturbed, deep (>1m), heavily shaded streams.  Stays in the middle of the water column (Ref. 6468).  Feeds on filamentous algae, terrestrial insects and detritus (Ref. 6703).  No observations on breeding in captivity.  Maturity at 6.4 cm (Ref. 6468).  Does well at 29°C water temperature.  Exploited by the tropical fish export trade, larger specimens are eaten.

species.name: Black lip rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to form small schools (Ref. 26363).

species.name: Black madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits near vegetation in moderate to fast clear water over gravel and sand in permanent springs, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Black Margined Seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black margined-scale sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens of this species were collected together with A. caudobimaculatus and A. vaigiensis from Jia-le-shui, Kenting, southern Taiwan, and both do occur together in mid or near surface waters, forming feeding aggregations over shallow rocky reefs, thus implying that A. nigrimargo likely shares similar habitats with these two species (Ref. 123195).

species.name: Black midas cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black mirrorbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black morpho tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black mudfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit ephemeral areas that dry out over summer and autumn months, where they aestivate in damp areas or under tree roots and logs (Ref. 43717).

species.name: Black neon tetra
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plant matter.  In captivity, it swims in the middle and upper water layers of the tank; spawns in the open water and its eggs hatch in 24 to 30 hours (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Black perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults chiefly live in rocky areas near kelp, occasionally over sand bottom of coastal bays and around piers and pilings, and rarely in surf.  Occur from intertidal areas to 46 m depth, but usually at about 6.1 m.  Usually form small groups.  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black phantom tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small insects and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Black prickleback
species.description: Juveniles and adults inhabit intertidal areas down to 8 m depth (Ref. 2850);   Individuals to 2 cm in length have been taken from surface waters (Ref. 6885).  Found under rocks and in gravel areas (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Breathe air (Ref. 31184) and can stay out of water for 10-23 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).  Oviparous, eggs are laid in several clumps or masses which are guarded by the male (Ref. 58332).

species.name: Black prochilodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed to rock-bottomed pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Also found in impoundments (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adult feeds on small benthic invertebrates, especially microcrustacea and midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Black reef leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  Observed in pairs, secretly moving about in and out of holes among boulders (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Black ribbed snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Black River madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, swift, moderate to large high gradient streams.  Occurs in swift shallow riffles with gravel, cobble or large stone substrate, but can occasionally be found in shallower pools (Ref. 57745).

species.name: Black rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near rocky reefs in shallow water and in open water over deep banks (Ref. 2850).  Adults live both off and on bottom (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715).  Form schools (Ref. 2850).  Feed on fishes (Ref. 27302).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Young are important prey species for other fishes, marine mammals and birds.  Excellent food fish (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Black ruby barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, cool, shady streams in forested areas, on gravel or sand substrate.  Sometimes found in pools of quiet water in the margins of clear streams and rivers (Ref. 6471).  Bred in captivity.  Spawns in shallow water among marginal weeds.  Eggs (>100) hatch in 1-2 days; fry are free-swimming after 24 h (Ref. 6702).  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae and detritus (Ref. 6703).  Males brightly colored and with darker fins.  Popular aquarium fish.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Black scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs.  Feed on algae (Ref. 26966).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black scraper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commercially cultured in Japan.  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed.  Plankton feeder (Ref. 12114, 12115).

species.name: Black sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits springs and rocky riffles of headwaters and creeks.

species.name: Black Sea bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and migrates to upper reaches of tributaries to spawn.  Spawning takes place in riffle with heavy current on gravel bottom.  Forages in the lower section of rivers, close to the surface (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Black Sea salmon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. There are anadromous, lacustrine and resident forms. At the sea, it occurs along coasts at depths of up to 50 m.  Undertakes migration to hill streams.  Resident part of populations live in streams and uppermost reaches with fast current, cold clear water and stone or gravel bottom.  Spawns in upper reaches with fast current.  Spawns in October-January. Parrs live in rivers and streams for 2-4 years, then smoltify and migrate to sea or mature in freshwater. Spends 2-4 years in the sea. Parrs and resident adults feed on aquatic and terrestrial invertebrates. Anadromous and large lacustrine individuals prey mostly on fish and large crustaceans. Anadromous individuals feed while in rivers.  Damming hinders most returning adults to reach spawning sites (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Black sea shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-anadromous, entering limans and lower parts of river deltas, but only occasionally in freshwater.  They are more or less abundant in lower reaches of rivers and coastal lagoons.  A cold-loving species, tolerating 3 or 4°C.(Ref. 188).  At sea, pelagic in deep water and enters brackish lagoons to spawn.  Mature adults spawn first at 2 years and many individuals spawn for 2-4 seasons.  Eggs sink to bottom.  Spent individuals return to the sea to feed.  In autumn, they migrate to southern Black Sea to overwinter.  Juveniles migrate to the sea or estuaries during the first summer (Ref. 59043).  Adults feed mainly on small fishes (mainly sprats and anchovies) also on shrimps, gammarids and other large crustaceans (Ref. 188). In northern Black Sea, the decline in habitat quality in suitable estuarine ecosystems is expected to have an impact in the immediate future (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Black Sea shad (Alosa tanaica)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species migrates from sea to mouth and lower reaches of large rivers (at 1-2 years) and spawns in fresh or slightly brackish water, usually close to the shore, upper 2-4 m, in almost still water bodies as flood plains or lakes.  Many individuals spawn 2-4 seasons and spawners appear along the coast in late January to March, enter rivers when temperature reaches about 10°C in late April to May, and spawns at about 15°C or beyond in May to June.  Eggs are bathypelagic or sink to bottom.  Spent fish migrate to estuarine and coastal lagoons or to sea near river mouths to feed and in autumn, move to sea near river mouths to overwinter.  Juveniles migrate to sea or estuaries during first summer and remain there until maturity.  At sea, feeds on a wide variety of zooplankton (crustaceans), insect larvae and small fish.  Populations seem to have stabilized at moderate level after most have declined during the first decades of 20th century due to water pollution.  In northern Black Sea, immediate impact is foreseen due to the decline in habitat quality in suitable estuarine ecosystems.  On the other hand, the species is still abundant in Azov Sea basin (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Black Sea tadpole-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fresh and slightly brackish waters, preferring lower reaches of rivers, deltas, lakes and freshwater limans. In rivers, this is commonly abundant in main river bed.  Occurs usually on silty sand with mollusk shells (Ref. 58669). Longevity is about a year.  Spawns in May-August with females probably laying eggs in 2-3 portions inside or under mollusc shell and adults die soon after spawning.  Feeds mainly on chironomid larvae, amphipods and molluscs (Ref.59043). Invasive in the large tributaries of the Caspian and Black Sea (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Black Sea turbot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Trevor Meyer, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Black seacatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous on benthic invertebrates, primarily annelids (Ref. 4332).

species.name: Black serrivomerid eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Comes to 175 m depth during the night (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Black sharkminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, streams, canals and inundated floodplains.  Sometimes seen in impoundments, but not in great numbers.  Like other planktivorous and detritivorous carps, it begins spawning after the first thunderstorms of the coming rainy season.  It spawns upstream from shallow sandbars that line long river bends.  The eggs settle out in the shallow water and hatch just as water levels begin to rise following the initiation of seasonal rains.  The fry immediately move into inundated grasses along the bank and continue to follow the leading edge of the advancing water as floodwaters spread over the land.  Adults also migrate out into seasonally flooded areas where they feed on algae, periphyton, phytoplankton and detritus.  They return to rivers from October to December (Ref. 12693).  In Laos and Thailand, it migrates upstream at the onset of rainy season.  In Cambodia, it undertakes upstream migration between October and March and downstream migration from March to August (Ref. 37770).  A desirable food fish which is marketed fresh, dried and salted (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Black shinner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species usually found deeper than 500 m during the day (Ref. 2802).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 2802).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Black snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Black snake moray
species.description: Inhabits corals and crevices of shallow lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Black snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits medium to large rivers (Ref. 12975).  Occurs in shaded forest streams with sluggish, acidic water and submerged roots/leaf litter substrates.  Appears to be mainly nocturnal and  feeds on small animals (Ref. 85309).   Preys on fish (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Black sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in muddy bottoms of coastal rivers, estuaries and shallow inshore waters (Ref. 33839).  Flesh is of excellent quality (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Black splitfin
species.description: An experimental fish.

species.name: Black spot blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black spot piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has powerful dentition that can inflict serious bites (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Black surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in large groups in open areas near coral or rock (Ref. 9710).  Caught with nets (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 275.

species.name: Black tetra
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in the middle and upper water layers.  Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51150).

species.name: Black tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers quiet pools with marginal vegetation; it has been reported only from fresh water and low altitudes and latitudes, so that its salinity and temperature tolerances are probably narrower than those of O. mossambicus (Ref. 2).

species.name: Black triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock and coral reefs  (Ref. 90102), from the surface to 15 m, including intertidal pools (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Black warrior
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deeper waters (Ref. 35724).  Oviparous, with pelagic larvae (Ref. 35724).

species.name: Black wolf-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers and igarapés.  Occurs usually in pairs.  Exhibits diurnal as well as nocturnal habits and preys on various insects, larvae, small fishes, shrimps, worms and fruits (Ref. 81195).

species.name: Black-and-gold chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Two forms: long-tailed and black as adults occur in the Andaman Sea, ranging east to western Bali and north to Japan. Second form, probably valid as N. xanthurus occur in the rest of the West Pacific and the two overlap in range on Bali's north coast (Ref. 48636). Occur in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs. Usually solitary (Ref. 1602). Feed on algae, crustaceans, and pelagic tunicates and salps. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Black-and-Red Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found in surge channels or on vertical encrusted rock walls, in tidal pools on reef crests (Ref. 27223, 90102) and areas with some wave action and abundant algal growth (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Black-and-yellow rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit holes and crevices in rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Found in intertidal areas and to 37 m (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Black-axil chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear lagoons, passages, and seaward reef slopes, in thickets of live or dead coral. They occur in large aggregations feeding above staghorn Acropora corals (Ref. 9710). Stomach contents of individuals examined included mainly copepods, amphipods, and zoea.
