Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-back snake-blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty environments, commonly among rotting vegetation (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Black-banded demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and coastal areas (Ref. 9710).  Found in sandy or silty areas around outcrops of rubble on sand, mud, sponge or rocks.  Occur singly or in small groups.  Young often with anemones for protection (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Abandoned shells and waste bottles serve as nests (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-banded flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawl on coastal shelves at depths of 14-100 m (Ref. 9790). Also occurs on sand or rubble bottoms near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Black-banded pigmy boxfish
species.description: Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Black-belly barracudina
species.description: Collected by midwater trawl from surface to 532 meters, suggesting that it is a mesopelagic species that may have diurnal vertical migration. Stomach contents have myctophids or other pelagic fishes such as Bregmaceros spp. rather than sakura shrimps (Lucensosergia lucens) (Ref. 121637).

species.name: Black-belly dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found at less than 305 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Feed mainly on crustaceans and lanternfishes (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35900).

species.name: Black-breasted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Solitary or paired among corals and algae patches (Ref 90102).

species.name: Black-cheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black-ear javelin
species.description: Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Black-edged cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-edged fin sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black-faced reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimen was found in a small cave in the wall of seaward reef at a depth of 27-29 m, with the wall extending to a depth of 35 m (Ref. 111071).

species.name: Black-finned armoured-gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Black-finned flyingfish
species.description: Occurs in near-shore surface waters, juveniles spread to open sea with floating seaweed.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Black-finned gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves and insular areas (Ref. 9771) , trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).  Rare.

species.name: Black-flag tripodfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy flats in coastal areas.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Black-headed chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-jacket tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black-line shrimp-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in muddy coastal bays and estuaries (Ref. 48637). Also found in sheltered bays and lagoons in 2-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Black-margined goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Black-nostril false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small uncommon species which inhabits coral heads to depths of at least 14 m.

species.name: Black-spot croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Black-spot surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear seaward reef slopes, below 15 m, usually below 30 m (Ref. 9710).  Adults mainly on deep coastal reef slopes and outer reef walls (Ref. 48637).  Found singly or in pairs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on algal film on bare rocks (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles found in shallow protected reefs, usually between soft coral, in 0.2-3 m depth (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Black-spotted butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs, solitary or paired.  Home-ranging.  Feed at least partially on coral polyps (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-spotted goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal sand flats, usually silty bottom in a few meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Black-spotted gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, creeks, and brackish estuaries (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Black-spotted snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow estuarine (mangroves) to fresh water areas (rivers, streams)(Ref. 126575); adults also in the sea (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Black-spotted whipray
species.description: Demersal on soft bottoms on the continental shelf at depths of 10-140m (Ref.58048). Juveniles (20-22 cm WD) are free swimming.  Feeds on prawns, small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 9840).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Common by-catch of bottom trawl and beach seine fisheries in the Arafura Sea. Utilized for its meat, skin (high value) and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Black-striped pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves and crevices around coral reefs (Ref. 559).

species.name: Black-striped snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow areas buried in loose gravel and sand (Ref. 1602, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  It buries itself  with the aid of its pointed snout or its bony, sharp tail.

species.name: Black-tail sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit protected coastal areas often around docks or breakwaters (Ref. 7247).  Often found in loose aggregations or widely scattered individuals near or along shorelines (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Black-throated triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on rock surfaces and under ledges; common at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Black-tip sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow protected sandy areas of lagoon and seaward reefs.  Buries itself beneath the sand, exposing only its eye and tubular nostril.  Moves extremely fast when disturbed and is difficult  to detect when it resettles.  Apparently more active at night (Ref. 1602, 48637).

species.name: Black-tipped bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters in rocky reefs, ledges and caves during day (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Black-tipped garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species.

species.name: Black-velvet angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species that inhabits coastal reefs and drop-offs (Ref. 9710) that are exposed to strong tidal currents (Ref. 48636).  Juveniles on deep rubble slopes with rich invertebrate growth.  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Solitary or in pairs.  Frequently exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Black-vent damsel
species.description: Adults occur in lagoon reefs and generally prefers small patch reefs with sand or rubble substrates (Ref. 1602).  Feed on benthic algae which it aggressively guards against other herbivores (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles secretive in rubble (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Blackback barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, well-vegetated streams, floodplains and marshes (Ref. 52193). It feeds on small aquatic insects and algae (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer, laying eggs amongst vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193). Undertakes seasonal movements which might be correlated with spawning (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Blackback dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackbanded darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits headwaters to medium-sized rivers, usually over gravel or sand (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge, blackfly, mayfly, and caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Blackbanded gauvina
species.description: Found on muddy bottom, close to shore in turbid conditions.

species.name: Blackbanded limia
species.description: Inhabits streams, springs and lakes.

species.name: Blackbanded rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rainforest streams, lily lagoons and small streams.  Also occurs in larger streams, usually in backwaters or along the shoreline where there is minimal flow and grassy vegetation.  Often found in brackish coastal waters (Ref. 7020, 44894).  Temperature and pH ranges are 23°-28°C and 5.5-7, respectively (Ref. 44894).  Feeds mainly on aquatic and terrestrial insects and their larvae, and also filamentous green algae.  Usually co-occurs with other species of rainbows and blue-blue eyes.  A popular aquarium species which thrives in captivity.  Type species (first species to be described) of the family Melanotaeniidae (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Blackbanded seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blackbanded sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated lakes, ponds, quiet sand and mud-bottomed pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Blackbar blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shallows (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Blackbar coris
species.description: Found in exposed rocky shores.

species.name: Blackbar drum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackbar dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackbar filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow lagoons and seaward reefs to a depth of about 15 m; common in coral-rich areas.  Secretive species (Ref. 9710, 48637) among rocks, sponges or in crevices on the bases of large coral formations.  Adults usually form pairs but often only one is observed while the other one is hiding (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Blackbarred dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary. Inhabits silty coral reefs in 1-5 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Blackbarred limia
species.description: Occurs usually in large schools over a variety of bottom types.  Young hide in vegetation.

species.name: Blackbarred reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef crevices in 8-30 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blackbarred wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in groups, most commonly on outer reef areas, and also found in coastal reefs, lagoons and tide pools  (Ref. 57555, 90102).

species.name: Blackbelly Argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud and mud-shell bottoms (Ref. 37039).

species.name: Blackbelly blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in shallow water associated with coral (Ref. 51183) but may also be found in shallow, clear water with  limestone rubble (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Blackbelly cardinalfish
species.description: Found in inshore reef areas.  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Blackbelly cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackbelly dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in small groups near Acropora colonies where it hides when threatened. Feeds on plankton(Ref. 89963). Sometimes solitary, frequently in shady spots near corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Blackbelly eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty or sandy bottoms (Ref. 27436).  Moves into shallow water at night to feed on marine worms, crustaceans, small bivalves, and brittle stars (Ref. 6885, 27436).  Few live over 5 years (Ref. 6885).  If used live as bait, it attracts large rockfishes, greenlings or codfishes (Ref. 27436).  Flesh considered good but not esteemed (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Blackbelly limia
species.description: Found in streams.  Collected near the surface (Ref. 27228).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Blackbelly skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 38-40 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Blackbelly snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackbelly spoonbill eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackbelly tonguesole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Blackbelly triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit subtidal reef flats and protected lagoons, Ref. 48637.  Found mainly in rubble-algal habitat and usually in loose aggregations. Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102). Shy species, usually swimming away or when small, diving into holes (Ref. 48637).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Also taken by drive-in nets (Ref. 9770).

species.name: Blackbelly triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rock and coral reefs 5 m or shallower (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackbelt cardinalfish
species.description: On open substrate, schooling with large coral heads during the day.  Usually trawled inshore on soft bottom (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Blackbelt cichlid
species.description: Inhabits lakes and rivers but migrates to the extreme lower sections of the lower river valleys where current is slow.  Prefers muddy and sandy bottoms and lives among submerged trees and logs for protection.  Thrives well in shady bank areas of rivers.  Able to tolerate brackish and marine conditions.  Feeds on benthic detritus consisting of vegetable matter, both aquatic and terrestrial plants, seeds and fruits.

species.name: Blackbelted cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms dense aggregations above or among the branches of Porites cylindrica and other branching corals (e.g. Acropora Ref. 54391) of sheltered lagoons and inshore bays (Ref. 1602); over sandy bottom at depths of 1-40 meters (Ref. 54391). Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Blackblotch blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs and rocky reefs (Ref. 529).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackblotch swallowtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-water species.

species.name: Blackbodied leg skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum width at least 38 cm. Seldom caught. Utilization for human consumption limited (Ref. 9905).  Found in soft, sandy bottoms; by-catch of trawls and usually discarded because of its small size (Ishihara, pers.comm. 07/07). Males reaches maturity at ca. 53 cm TL (Ref. 114953)

species.name: Blackbrow bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Blackburn's herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters (Ref. 188, 75154).

species.name: Blackburns's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, but also in small lagoons and in Lake Maracaibo, Venezuela.  More specimens and data needed.

species.name: Blackcap basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) found on nearly vertical cliffs and drop-offs beyond outer reefs. Often upside-down. Retreats into recesses when alarmed (Ref. 9710). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420). Most common in water more than 30 m deep. Gradually replaces G. loreto at depths of 15-30 m (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Blackcheek blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Blackchin blacksmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Undergoes daily vertical migrations, rising into the epipelagic zone during the night.  Feeds mainly on zooplankton (Ref. 9875, 33698).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604).

species.name: Blackchin dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackchin tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species can tolerate high salinity (Ref. 5723).  It occurs abundantly in mangrove areas and ventures in to both fresh, like lower reaches of streams (Ref. 5723) and salt waters in native and non-native ranges (Ref. 46816, 53405).  In West Africa, this species is confined to brackish lagoons and estuaries, and is abundant in the mangrove zone (Ref. 2).  Forms schools; is mainly nocturnal with intermittent daytime feeding.  Feeds on aufwuchs and detritus (Ref. 2), as well as on bivalves and zooplankton (Ref. 28587).  Feeding behaviour: picking up and swallowing "bites" (no gill rakers) (Ref. 55661).

species.name: Blackdwarf shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabitsf sand bottoms in 8.2-10.7 m depth and partners with an alpheid-shrimp which remains unidentified (deposited specimen CAS 244344). Adults mature at 2.34 cm SL or less (Ref. 118501).

species.name: Blackear angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with coral or rock bottoms and numerous crevices (Ref. 4858).  Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Forms harems of 3-7 individuals.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Blackear bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Synchronously hermaphroditic.

species.name: Blackear cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackear wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Commonly found in clear seagrass beds; uncommon on reefs or muddy bays (Ref. 9710).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Blackedge cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302, 75154) found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species found in the deep shelf and upper slope (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 34024.

species.name: Blackedge greeneye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope.

species.name: Blackedge moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in seagrass beds and banks from 10-19 m depth.  Rarely found in bays; absent from coral reefs.

species.name: Blackedge pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Blackedge tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackedge triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit patch reefs surrounded by white sand bottom (Ref. 5521).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackedge whipray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters and estuaries.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Blackedged angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in current-swept outer reef slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 4859).  Feeds on plankton.  Forms harems of 2-5 individuals.  Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Blackest whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Blackeye goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually in sandy areas near rocks.  Occurs from intertidal areas to 106 m depth.  Retreats to rocks or holes when approached.  Young are found usually offshore among plankton.  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 34256).  Forms permanent harem groups composed of a single male  and several smaller females (Ref. 55367).  Eggs are guarded by the male (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Blackfin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky tide pools, eroded limestone slopes and basins, and algae-covered rocks surrounded by sand (Ref. 5521).  Also found in areas with coral (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Blackfin cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in clear Thalassia testudinum beds where it often inhabits empty snail shells (Ref. 9626). Caught at night or in the early hours of the morning (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Blackfin cisco
species.description: Formerly found in deep waters (90-160 m) of Lakes Michigan and Huron, and in 2-100 m in Lake Nipigon. Belongs to C. artedi complex.

species.name: Blackfin coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives exclusively among the branches of the coral Pocillopora damicornis, sometimes as deep as 20 m.

species.name: Blackfin coralfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefer algae covered and mud bottoms areas of estuaries and coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Usually occur in pairs.  Feed on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackfin damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usual habitat consists of passages and outer reef slopes in about 1.5-12 m, adjacent to vertical walls or in the shadows of overhanging cliffs and ledges (Ref. 114927).

species.name: Blackfin darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Blackfin dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfin eel goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along muddy bottoms of coastal rivers, estuaries, bays and lakes.  Feeds on small crustaceans and other invertebrates.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Blackfin fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs over rocky bottoms.

species.name: Blackfin flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfin flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats.

species.name: Blackfin gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers the current along steep banks and seeks food in the stony crevices.

species.name: Blackfin glass blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to mainly perch on live coral surfaces and terminal phase males in holes, also typically within live coral heads. It has been reported to be widely distributed down to 20 m in Cayman Islands (Ref. 125603).

species.name: Blackfin goodea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfin grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfin gulper shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Diet poorly known, but stomachs examined contained fishes and cephalopods. Caught by demersal fisheries operating in deepwater areas. Utilized for its meat, fins (low value) and liver oil (very high value)(Ref.58048).

species.name: Blackfin hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602), on slopes or along upper part of drop-offs (Ref. 48636).  Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled, invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 9823).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackfin hookear sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the bottom; also in the water column over bottom depths to 3,730 m (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Blackfin pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Bottom spawner, 2-4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Blackfin poacher
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Blackfin pupfish
species.description: Feeds on detritus (Ref. 94405).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Blackfin pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 26340).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Blackfin rat tail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blackfin roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shallow depth from Ref. 95664.

species.name: Blackfin sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky reef, gravel and rubble bottom on Wanganella Bank, western Norfolk Ridge, Tasman Sea, south to the North Island of New Zealand, from North Taranaki Bight, north to the Three Kings Islands and south-east to the Bay of Plenty and Colville Ridge, in depths of 56 to 280 m. Apparently relatively common where suitable habitat exists, with 14 specimens collected by trawl in depths of 56–280 m. The species has also been observed and photographed off the North Island of New Zealand by divers using rebreather apparatus in depths of 55-71 m in the Poor Knights Islands Marine Reserve, at locations known locally as Ngaroimata Point, Northern Arch, Serpent Rock and Landing Bay Pinnacle. A large individual was identified from an underwater photograph taken by Kendall Clements in 2010 at 'The Archways', Burgess Island, Mokohinau Group, outer Hauraki Gulf, at a depth of 16-20 m which  is the shallowest confirmed record for the species (Ref. 116625).

species.name: Blackfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Blackfin seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow rocky areas (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Blackfin silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfin slatey
species.description: Juveniles in estuaries and silty reefs on open substrates with remote outcrops or reef or debris.  Adults on deep reefs along walls with large caves.  Often in small aggregations in depths of 30 m or more (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Blackfin soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known about this shy and secretive species.  It lies motionless, often on its side, hidden in dark recesses on rocky reefs and along walls during the day.  Actively hunts at night, preying on small fish (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Blackfin spiderfish
species.description: Common on mid and lower continental slope.  Rests on the bottom with the use of elongated, stiffened outer pelvic and lower caudal fin rays (tripod).  Sensory pectoral fins are thrown forward in front of its head, facing the current.  Feeds on benthopelagic plankton.  Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 6688).  Spawning is seasonal with peak during fall in the Bahamas (Ref. 3590).

species.name: Blackfin stonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 68964) species occurring over muddy substrate (Ref. 11441), It has dorsal spines with venom glands (Ref. 11441) which can cause extremely painful and potentially fatal wounds (Ref. 13710).

species.name: Blackfin sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small rivers.  Hides in bedrock crevices, near boulders or under shoreline brush (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae, microcrustacea and occasional larger insect larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Blackfin sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Blackfin tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally forms schools; is mainly diurnal; juveniles feed on mayfly larvae and various terrestrial insects among a diet in which animal items formed a high proportion (Ref. 2). Adults feed predominantly on phytoplankton (Ref. 2, 52307). Congregates in small groups (under 10 individuals) in open water regions and at a maximum depth of about 5 m (Ref. 52307). Lacks marked sexual dichromatism when sexually active (Ref. 81260). Ovophilic, maternal mouth brooder (Ref. 52307) that forms temporary pair bonds (Ref. 81260) prior to spawning, but none after (Ref. 52307). Ventures to regions near the edges of the lake for spawning, where the male constructs craters in the sand; males infrequently incubate the eggs (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Blackfin triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on rock surfaces and under ledges; common at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 6211).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackfinned clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfinned snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackfinned toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackflap blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral rocks, some on sandy bottom in water about 5 m deep or on irregular rocky bottom with sparse live coral and no sand (Ref. 630). Also in shallow protected reefs with rich coral and algae growth, usually found at depths less than about 10 m; occasionally deeper.  Usually seen solitary (Ref. 48636).  One specimen taken from 20 m in the Comoro Island.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackflash ribbonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 7300).  Enters estuaries (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 27637); fishes, squids, urochordatans, and nematodes (Anisakidae) were found in the stomach of specimens caught off the coasts of Santa Catarina and Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil (Ref. 56498).

species.name: Blackfoot firefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in sheltered coastal bays and fine sand or muddy habitats.  May partly bury itself in the substrate during the day and is easily overlooked.  When disturbed, the brightly colored pectoral fins probably serves to startle predators.  The large fins serve primarily to corner prey when hunting (Ref. 48635).  Trawled on soft bottom in coastal waters (Ref. 4313), to 300 m depth (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Blackfringe Bigeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackgill rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom in deep water, but young in shallower areas (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Blackgullet cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits both rivers and lakes with softer substrate.

species.name: Blackgut conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackhead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit small patch reefs surrounded by fine white sand (Ref. 5521). It is usually found on live corals or gorgonians, often photographed nestled in the grooves of brain corals, with the TP males occupying holes in live corals or sponges; depth range extends to 20 m at least (Ref. 125603).

species.name: Blackhead shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand bottoms in 20-62 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blackhead strainer snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackish skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackish stingray
species.description: A poorly known species; attains at least 32 cm DW, mature at this size (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Blacklancer catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits main rivers over muddy substrate, in deep waters with swift current (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on insects and small fishes (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Blacklash scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from one specimen.

species.name: Blackline barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackline cucumberfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackline fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults swim above the bottom (Ref. 9710). Juveniles observed to mingle with apogonid fishes among Diadema spines as a means of protection against predators like Pterois (Ref. 79545). Adults feed on zooplankton (Ref. 9710). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackline myleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was reported to inhabit slow-flowing habitats such as backwaters and lake, feedng mainly on aquatic and terrestrial plants. Collection localities include clearwater rivers chemically characterized by a low concentration of suspended sediments, dissolved minerals and humic compounds and also from extremely acidic oligotrophic blackwaters. The type locality is also a blackwater system that has its headwaters in the Purus-Madeira interfluvium and like other blackwater rivers, is of low sediment load and low pH. These blackwater environments are reported to be inhospitable to certain species of fish (Ref. 123127).

species.name: Blackline rasbora
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in swamps (Ref. 57235), ponds, streams and drains (Ref. 13061), usually in slow flowing, often somewhat turbid water (Ref. 27732).  Found from midwater level to surface in nearly all ponds, ditches, canals and reservoir margins of 2 m depth or less (Ref. 12693).  Inhabits medium to large rivers, flooded fields and brooks of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on zooplankton, insects (Ref. 12693), worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Very popular aquarium fish (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Blackline snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove habitats, in shallow tidal areas and possibly be sympatric with Pseudogobius poicilosoma (often) and P. fulvicaudus (less often; five sites detected in Singapore and one in Brunei). A small species, with a gravid female at 1.7 cm SL, while males are with obvious genital papillae at 1.55 cm SL (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Blackline tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Blacklined filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive species found in lagoon and protected seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637), often in silty conditions. Solitary (Ref. 90102). Sometimes seen deep inside branching corals (Ref. 48637).  Has been from deeper water by trawls.

species.name: Blacklined zipper loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blacklip damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blacklipped pike cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackmargin brotula
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky habitats.  A 72 mm SL female collected was found to contain eggs 0.5 mm in
diameter and a 75 mm female with eggs 0.8 mm in diameter (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Blackmargin dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore reefs; also tide pools and lagoons (Ref. 1602). Solitary or in pairs in crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Blackmargin maori wrasse
species.description: Collected in protected waters of lagoons or harbors on mixed sand and coral-reef habitats (Ref. 56651).

species.name: Blackmargin pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Blackmargin rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in tidepools (Ref. 54980). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackmargined damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in outer reef slopes of coral reefs, usually around rocky outcrops in sandy areas.  Also along deep walls with caves to 50 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Feed on zooplankton and algae.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Blackmast
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, flowing streams, as well as in still water.  Found in well-vegetated stream and lake margins.  Forms moderate-sized shoals, swimming just below the surface (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects and their larvae, small crustaceans, snails and some algae.  Although attractive, they are delicate and usually difficult to maintain in captivity (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Blackmouth bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep shelf and slope waters (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Blackmouth eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackmouth lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackmouth pyrrhulina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackmouth rat tail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blackmouth shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in backwaters and quiet pools of creeks and small rivers.  Usually found over mud near vegetation.

species.name: Blacknape large-eye bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species apparently lives on the coral sandy bottom in the vicinity of coral reefs (Ref. 107926).

species.name: Blacknose dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices 10-30 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blacknose sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blacknose silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blacknose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackpored eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackpotted paedomorphic goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow fringing reef lagoon at night (Ref. 116797)..

species.name: Blackray damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackring waryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young epipelagic to mesopelagic; adults benthopelagic on slopes in about 500 m (6602).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Blacksaddle herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  Uncommon.

species.name: Blacksaddle triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blacksaddle wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackside dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools of headwaters and creeks.  Usually found along undercut banks, near large rocks or among detritus (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on attached algal growth and aquatic insect immatures (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Blackside darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit pools of creeks and small to medium rivers, usually with moderate current and gravel or sand bottoms (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on dipterans such as midge and blackfly larvae; mayfly nymphs are second of importance, followed by caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Blackskin catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in lowland wetlands, bogs and peats (Ref. 57235).  Found in swamps with slightly acidic water (Ref. 43281).  Occur in standing water habitats .  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Blacksmith
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur near bottom over or near rocks, especially over steep banks, and also in kelp beds.  Young school in open ocean.  They retire to rocky holes at night (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Good eating.

species.name: Blackspine dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackspot allotoca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in very clear water with muddy or boggy bottoms (Ref. 26130).  Species used in research (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Blackspot angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dead coral and rubble reefs in clear lagoons and exposed seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Extremely cryptic; never seen by divers except  poison stations.  Feeds on algae.  Never exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Blackspot bandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults pair and feed in loose groups; juveniles gather in small groups on deep sand slopes, usually in current-prone areas (Ref. 48635).  Occurs in mud bottoms 15-100 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Commonest member of the Japanese cepolid fishes.  Caught by trawl net from sandy or muddy bottoms. Used mainly for fish cake.  (Ref. 559 and 637).  Minimum depth of 15 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Blackspot barb
species.description: Occurs in clear streams, lakes and ponds (Ref. 41236).  Inhabits lowland rivers and also estuaries, reservoirs and marshes (Ref. 55036).

species.name: Blackspot butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oceanic waters and well offshore (Ref. 43132).  Biology unknown; maximum size unknown, probably reaching 20 cm FL (Ref. 43132)

species.name: Blackspot cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered coastal reefs, often in silty areas. Forms small aggregagations, usually among branching Acropora corals (unlike Archamia biguttata which prefers caves and ledges) (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blackspot cleaner wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of seaward and clear lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).  Occur solitarily or in pairs.  Creates 'cleaning ' stations to which fishes come to have crustacean ectoparasites and mucus removed.

species.name: Blackspot climbing perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in dense marginal vegetation of rivers, lakes, lagoons and channels of swamps and floodplains (Ref. 52193). It feeds on insects and other small organisms (Ref. 52193). Males build a bubble nest on the water surface under which spawning takes place; the eggs float and are stowed in the nest, to be guarded by the male (Ref. 52193). Its shallow water habitat make it susceptible to aerial spraying of insecticides (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Blackspot coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups in live corals of lagoons and sheltered coastal reefs at 1-15 m deep (Ref. 90102).  In Papua New Guinea, various individuals were seen swimming around large coral heads on reef slopes and would not rest on the corals like those seen in Indonesia.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  It seems that the Indonesian and Philippines form may represent a new species (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Blackspot damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore reefs.  They are found in small groups around coral outcrops (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Blackspot gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom (Ref. 75154) of the continental shelf, inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blackspot hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rubble bottoms of steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 75973).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blackspot mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuarine areas (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Blackspot minigoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently inhabits over open sand or up in the water column. Collected using rotenone over Halimeda or Caulerpa or Zostera beds (Ref. 76968).

species.name: Blackspot porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently encountered in bay areas.

species.name: Blackspot razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154). Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blackspot shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers, usually in shallow water (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on dipterans, ephemeropterans, tricopterans, coleopterans, and odonats (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Blackspot shrimpgoby
species.description: Found in silty sandy substrate with small boulders or large rubble pieces in 3-10 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Blackspot skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the bottom of the outer shelf and upper slope (Ref. 5578).  Probably caught by trawlers (Ref. 5578).Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 57 cm TL, females at ca. 64 cm TL (Ref. 114953)

species.name: Blackspot sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, shallow lagoon and seaward reefs, quite common along the reef margin.  Feeds on benthic and planktonic crustaceans, other small invertebrates, and fishes at night.  By day, it forms aggregations in caves.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Blackspot tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit flat sandy or weedy areas near lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Solitary.  Feed mainly on hard-shelled prey including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins.  Marketed mostly fresh.  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Blackspot waspfish
species.description: Little is known of the species' biology, taken in trawls (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Blackspotted flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Blackspotted grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Blackspotted gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300).  Captured at depths from 60 - 556 meters, usually less than 250 meters (Ref. 54394).

species.name: Blackspotted hawkfish
species.description: A rocky shore species.

species.name: Blackspotted livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in small flowing and standing waters with dense vegetation.

species.name: Blackspotted nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in temporary pools in floodplains, rice fields, swamps, ditches and small streams (Ref. 3788). Found in water-filled depressions in floodplains of rivers; with vegetation often near edges, usually grasses; occasionally grasses cover the entire pool; if aquatic vegetation is present, it may comprise of Nymphea, Ottelia, Lagarosiphon, and Utricularia species; annual species; eggs deposited in substrate where they survive dry season; hatching at onset of wet season; rapid growth of fry; sexual maturity may be attained in six weeks; may be associated with other annual or non-annual fish species (Ref. 83514). Bottom spawner; 4 months incubation; difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Blackspotted rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackspotted snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mixed patches of sand and turtle grass (Ref. 5521).  Rare (Ref. 9710).  Has been observed buried in the sand with only the head showing (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Blackspotted snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackspotted toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing waters that are only rarely deeper than 30 cm and connected to standing marshy area; over muddy bottoms (Ref. 26130, 36880).  Lives between 35 and 600 m elevation at temperatures of 23-30°C.  Swims in small groups near the surface of turbid waters, on the shoreline or among the undergrowth.  Feeds on unicellular algae, diatoms, ooze and sometimes insect larvae (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Blackspotted topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits near surface of quiet to flowing water, usually near margins of clear, sandy to gravelly headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  9.7 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on terrestrial arthropods, aquatic insects, small crustaceans, and diatoms (Ref. 10294).  Spawning occurs over gravel (Ref. 79012).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Blackspotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal reef flats and outer lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Usually in areas with mixed sand, rubble, and coral (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on gastropods, other hard-shelled prey (Ref. 9823), and foraminiferans (Ref. 37816).  Rarely marketed.

species.name: Blackstreaked blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackstripe barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. deserti (dorsal spot not covering tip of fin) (Ref. 2940).

species.name: Blackstripe basslet
species.description: Lives in tolerable depths with rocky places (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Blackstripe clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology not known (Ref. 37955).  Maximum length not reaching 3 cm (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Blackstripe coris
species.description: Common around small coral heads in silty sand-rubble areas.  Generally found at depths of more than 20 m (Ref. 33411).  Occurs in small groups on sandy or muddy substrates along reef margins or on soft bottom.  Enters shallow estuaries as well (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Blackstripe dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species; collected from tide pools, around boulders, and rock and coral reefs. May sometimes take refuge among spines of large Diadema sea urchins (Ref. 12720). In Socotra Archipelago, it inhabits equally frequently mixed communities of macroalgae and hard corals and sparse hard coral communities on rock platform, including the south and west coast, as well as hard coral communities including those dominated by Acropora, Porites, Galaxea, and encrusting and massive Agariciidae, Pectiniidae, and Mussidae (Ref. 88695).

species.name: Blackstripe livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackstripe lizardfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This species is found on sandy bottoms and sometimes seen with only the snout and eyes
protruding above the substrate. Like other synodontids, it is a 'lie-and-wait' predator, it relies on its camouflage, hiding under the sand to wait for approaching small fishes (Ref. 114926).

species.name: Blackstripe minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackstripe pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackstripe topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet surface water, usually near margins of creeks and small rivers, ponds, and lakes (Ref 5723, 10294).  7.4 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Feeds primarily on terrestrial arthropods, emergent stages of aquatic insects, benthic larvae, and midwater insects (Ref. 10294).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Blackstriped combtooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blackstriped dwarf galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in slow-running, tea-colored streams usually in sandy areas. Also found in swamps, small ponds and roadside ditches. Also lives in the vegetated shallows of some freshwater lakes. Water is typically acidic (pH 4.5-6.5) and darkly tannin-stained. An inhabitant of temporary waters, capable of aestivating in damp bottom sediments over summer. Spawning habits similar to G. munda. Most individuals perish after their first spawning (Ref. 44894). Feed on small insects, larvae of aquatic insects and micro-crustaceans. Breeding is associated with winter rains. Males take on a bright color pattern at the start of the breeding season (Ref. 33842).

species.name: Blacktail chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit seaward reefs, particularly coral-rich outer reef crests (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blacktail dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from tidal pools and rock and coral reefs, common in high surge areas (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Blacktail goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons or bays, in passes, or on outer reef slopes; over hard substrate as well as patches of rubble or sand, usually at the base of the reef.  Adults are usually in pairs and share burrow which is often under a piece of rubble or slab of coral rock.  Adults feed on current-borne zooplankton as high as 3 m above the burrow; tend to remain together while feeding, separated by not more than 1-2 m.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884, 48637).  Juveniles occur in large groups, as many as 500.  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Blacktail humbug
species.description: Schooling species, adults inhabit sheltered lagoons, harbors and inlets. Also in somewhat open substrates with outcrops of Acropora corals (Ref. 48636). Often associated with small coral heads. Feed on a variety of plankton, including larval shrimps and crabs, algae, ostracods, amphipods, pelagic tunicates, copepods, and fish eggs. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Blacktail moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore banks.

species.name: Blacktail pikeconger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blacktail redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits sandy and rocky pools, runs and riffles of small to medium rivers.  Also found in impoundments (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on detritus, diatoms, and a wide variety of small invertebrates such as microcrustacea, rotifers, caddisfly larvae, and phantom midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Blacktail shiner
species.description: Usually found in sandy pools and runs of small to medium rivers.  Also occurs in creeks and rocky pools and runs (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Adult feeds on surface insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Blacktail snailfish
species.description: Found on mud bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Possibly the most commonly captured liparid below 200 m; captured frequently by fishers (Ref. 26773).  Known to feed on polychaete worms, small crustaceans, tiny clams and other invertebrates (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Blacktail threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow waters, mainly on the reef flat or crest.  They are found on shady vertical rock walls with some current and relatively high oxygen level (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blacktail triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on seaward and lagoon reefs, usually less than 5 m (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Blacktail wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic over coral and rocks (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Blackthroat cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic omnivore.  Breeds in April to August (Ref. 38279).

species.name: Blackthroat cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blackthroat goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty sand bottoms and seagrass areas (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Blackthroat seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on large crustaceans and mollusks.  Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 637).

species.name: Blackthroat Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on intertidal and subtidal areas, specifically on reef's surface, usually in weedy areas, on algal-covered rocks , or on rubble.  They prefer silty habitat of upper regions, commonly on pylons, estuaries and harbors (Ref. 9002).  They feed mainly on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 2334).    Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blacktip cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays under ledge overhangs and other shaded areas on rocky reefs and slopes during the day.  Feeds in the open at night (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Blacktip jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Blacktip morwong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef and rocky reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blacktip poacher
species.description: Inhabits soft bottoms.  Larvae pelagic (Ref. 6885).  Feeds almost exclusively on crustaceans, mainly mysids.  Preyed upon by flatfishes, hake, and lancetfish (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Blacktip sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms next to reefs in 7-31 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blacktip shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand- and gravel-bottomed pools, sometimes runs, of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Blacktip skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on upper continental slope (Ref. 114953). Lengths of juvenile males ranged between 23.3-34.3 cm TL, smallest juvenile 20.4 cm TL (Ref. 75649). Males reached maturity at ca. 63 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Blacktip tripodfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy flats of coastal waters.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Blacktongue rat tail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Blackvent cardinalfish
species.description: Occurs in aggregations in caves in vertical walls (Ref. 37816). Also found in steep outer reef slopes in 15-50 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Blackvent filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One juvenile taken between 73-200 m.

species.name: Blackwing hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly at the surface on insects, but also takes crustaceans.  Aquarium specimens reach 3.5 cm TL (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Blackwing searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Blageon
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit middle reaches of streams and rivers with clear water, moderately swift current and gravel bottom.  Occurs in groups.  They feed on invertebrates and algae.  Breeding occurs in fast-flowing water on gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Used as bait.  Not so well fished although the flesh is excellent (Ref. 30578).  Locally threatened (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Blanche argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms of bays and shallow inshore areas, often along sand beaches (Ref. 2850).  Enters freshwater (Ref. 7251).  Juveniles are encountered in lagoons of mangroves.  Omnivorous (Ref. 9303).  Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed; processed into fish meal and used as live bait in the snapper fishery (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Blanche armée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults often in clear coastal waters up to about 50 m depth; juveniles often in estuaries or lagoons influenced by fresh water (Ref. 41108); they prefer shallow waters over sandy bottoms, from coral reefs to brackish waters (Ref. 30573).  Fry about 10 cm in length enter the estuaries and stay until they reach maturity (Ref. 34363).  Occur singly or in groups (Ref. 9710).  Feed on small bottom invertebrates (Ref. 3409).  In the Gilberts, the species forms spawning aggregations for a few days around the new moon (Ref. 37816).  Sold fresh in markets; processed into fishmeal.  Also taken with stake-nets (Ref. 3409).

species.name: Blanche brésilienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water, over soft bottoms.

species.name: Blanche cabuche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, especially in mangrove-lined creeks and lagoons, but also found on vegetated sand grounds in typical marine areas.  Young more widespread than adults.  Feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates.  Consumed fresh.

species.name: Blanche cendré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters in open sandy and surf areas, seagrass beds, near reefs, and mangrove channels (Ref. 7251).  Enters brackish water, sometimes even fresh water  (Ref. 3722).  May occur in small aggregations (Ref. 3722).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates such as worms, clams, crustaceans (Ref. 3722); also feeds on insects (Ref. 9303).  Often seen feeding in sand patches among reefs by thrusting its mouth into the sediment and expelling sand from the gill openings (Ref. 13442).  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed; also processed into fishmeal (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Blanche commune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the coast, saltwater lagoons, and estuaries (Ref. 5213).  Also in sand bottoms in sheltered waters near reefs (Ref. 90102).   Occurs singly or in groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on small organisms living on sandy bottoms.  Utilized as fish meal and duck food.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Blanche drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species entering estuaries, lower courses of coastal rivers, and lagoons (Ref. 4323, 7352, 57394). Found over sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 3722, 57394). Feeds on fish, shrimps, mollusks, zooplankton and detritus (Ref. 28587); including other benthic crustaceans and polychaetes. Forages at daytime in small groups, hovering close to the bottom and either picks off prey on the substrate or digs into it sifting the mouthed sediment through its opercular openings. Its conspicuous black tip on dorsal fin is mimicked by juvenile guianan snooks, Centropomus mexicanus, an example of aggressive mimicry (Ref. 43465). Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Blanche drapeau du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms of coastal waters.  Juveniles are commonly found in estuarine regions, mangroves, tidal streams and rivers far from the coast.  Adults occur in deeper waters.  Forms schools (Ref. 37955).  Omnivore (Ref. 37955), feeds on vegetable matter, micro-invertebrates and detritus (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Blanche espagnole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, being especially abundant over mud bottoms in mangrove-lined lagoons or creeks; larger individuals may also occur on vegetated sand grounds in marine areas.  Enters fresh water in limestone regions (Ref. 7251).  May occur in aggregations (Ref. 3722).  Probably feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3722).  Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Blanche fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are coastal inhabitants found on soft bottoms (Ref. 44894), over sandy substrate (Ref. 12693).  Juveniles are found in brackish mangrove estuaries, sometimes enter fresh water (Ref. 2847, 44894), lakes (Ref. 4323), tidal creeks (Ref. 44894) and lower freshwater reaches of rivers (Ref. 12915).  Feed on small crustaceans, polychaetes and forams on sand or muddy-sand bottoms (Ref. 12915), worms and insect larvae (Ref. 12693).   Length at first reproduction was reported to be around 12 cm SL,  for a population in a South African estuary (D. Woodland, pers.comm. 07/13).  Salted or made into fish sauce.

species.name: Blanche gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms of coastal waters, especially abundant in brackish waters (Ref. 9303).  Feeds on crabs and shrimps (Ref. 37955). Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Blanche gros yaya
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in mangrove-lined lagoons; also found over shallow mud and sand grounds in marine areas.  Juveniles common in hypersaline lagoons and in brackish water (Ref. 5217).  Probably feeds on small benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh but not highly esteemed.  Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.

species.name: Blanche malacapa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons, preferring areas with sandy bottoms (Ref. 9303, 37955).  Forms schools (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, algae and small fishes (Ref. 9303).

species.name: Blanche naine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons.  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, algae and occasionally small fish (Ref. 9303).

species.name: Blanche palometée
species.description: There is not much knowledge of the biology of this species, aside from being found in coastal areas, but are very rare in coastal lagoons. It is commonly found in the discarded fauna of shrimp trawls (Ref. 95681).

species.name: Blanche rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and common in brackish waters (Ref. 36880), mostly over mud bottoms in mangrove-lined creeks and lagoons (Ref. 3722); often entering a considerable distance into  freshwaters (Ref. 36880).  Feeds on aquatic insects, crustaceans, micro-bivalves and detritus (Ref. 36880).  Marketed fresh; processed into fishmeal  (Ref. 3722).

species.name: Blanche selles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in tidal areas of estuaries and very shallow coastal waters.  Feeds on small animals living on mud-sand bottoms.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3409).

species.name: Blanche à nageoire courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons (Ref. 9303); on muddy or sandy bottoms to depths of 30 m and penetrates freshwater habitats in Mexico and Central America (Ref. 94655).

species.name: Blanche à nageoires jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in coastal waters.  Juveniles inhabit lagoons of mangrove areas and tidal streams; adults are found over soft bottoms of deeper waters.  May enter brackish waters (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and fishes. Its flesh is considered of good quality (Ref. 9303). Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Blanche à pagaies
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters.  Forms large schools.  Probably feeds on small benthic animals.  Used for fish meal and duck food.

species.name: Blanche à taches sombres
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft substrates of coastal waters.  Juveniles are encountered in coastal lagoons and estuaries.  Forms schools.  Omnivore.

species.name: Blanche élégante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers coralline areas (Ref. 30573).  Migrates to specific sandy areas near outer reef edge to spawn in late afternoons during full moon.  Feeds on small benthic organisms living on sandy bottoms (Ref. 3409, 48635).  In Palau, migrates to specific sandy spots near the outer reef edge to spawn in late afternoons around full moon (Ref. 37816).  Forms schools.  Feeds on small invertebrates found in the sand.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12915).

species.name: Blanchet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide variety of habitats, mainly in lowland areas. Most abundant in nutrient-rich lakes and large to medium sized rivers and backwaters. Also recorded from small lowland streams and from brackish coastal lagoons. In fast-flowing rivers, confined to stretches where backwaters or shelters allow for overwintering. Larvae and juveniles live in wide variety of littoral habitats. Preys predominantly on benthic invertebrates, zooplankton, plant material and detritus. May shift from littoral to pelagic habitats and between benthic food and zooplankton when abundance of a specific food item is high or for avoidance of predation and/or competition. Breeds among dense submerged vegetation in backwaters or lakes, flooded meadows or in shallow, fast-flowing river habitats on plant or gravel bottom. Undertakes short spawning migrations. Stays in backwaters or in deep parts of lakes to overwinter. Produces fertile hybrids with Abramis brama (Ref. 59043). Pale yellow eggs are found attached to vegetation and tree roots (Ref. 41678). There is only little commercial fishing for this species, but valued for recreational fishing. Utilized fresh and dried or salted; can be pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Blanquette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shelf and slope waters (Ref. 4426).  Found on sand and rock-sand bottom (Ref. 6808).  A bottom-predator of bony fishes, other elasmobranchs, fish offal, crabs, shrimps, mysids, octopi, and cuttlefish (Ref. 5578).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 4426.  Maximum length for female is 202 cm (Ref. 41333).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 12.5-18.3 cm long and 10.0-13.9 cm wide (Ref. 41250).  About 55-156 eggs are produced per individual annually (Ref. 41250).

species.name: Blaufelchen
species.description: Lacustrine, pelagic, usually at 0-40 m during summer. Feeds on plankton and insects; preys on juvenile Perca fluviatilis in summer. Spawns at surface over deep water, off-shore. Spawns for the first time at 2-3 years and in first half of December, when temperature falls below 7˚C. Males aggregate at surface and females ready to spawn come from deeper water to join these aggregations. Eggs sink to bottom and hatch in March. Larvae swim to surface and start to feed after 8 days (Ref. 59043). Also Ref. 13813, 47057.

species.name: Blazed cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bleeding shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs, riffles and deep, flowing pools of clear, fast creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably nest spawners like congeners.

species.name: Bleeker's blacktip sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters.

species.name: Bleeker's catfish
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters and estuaries.  Diet unknown (Ref. 38478).

species.name: Bleeker's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered inshore reefs and deep coastal reef slopes, usually in 20 m or more.  They occur singly or in pairs, usually seen close to the substrate near their burrow (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Bleeker's flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bleeker's lionfish
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230). Also seen in areas of cool upwelling on fine sand and mud bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bleeker's viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tidepools (Ref. 76869). Cryptic in shallow water (usually <5 m) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bleeker's whipray
species.description: Enters estuaries (Ref. 4832).  Found mainly on muddy bottoms to at least 40 m depth.  Most likely to feed on small crustaceans (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Bleeker’s deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bleher's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bleheratherina pierucciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Blemished razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits locality with extensive open sand with gradual sloping bottom at 10-25 m.  Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed.  Occurs in loose groups  (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Blennechis à dorsale élevée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in shallow protected lagoons and reef flats with algal and seagrass clumps. Juveniles often in floating Sargassum weeds and maybe dispersed over great distances (Ref. 48636). They swim with the tail oriented vertically. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Empty mollusk shells are used for nesting. Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Captured at the surface using a hand net (Ref. 26165).

species.name: Blennie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 5377).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blennie (Cirripectes stigmaticus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or forms small groups in the upper edge of seaward reef slopes, less than 10 m, but may be found up to 20 m deep (Ref. 90102). Adults inhabit coastal reef flats with rich coral and algae habitats (Ref. 48636); also on rocky and coralline structures (Ref. 529); among Acropora and Pocillopora corals of surf-swept algal ridge. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Blennie (Plagiotremus rhinorhynchos)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear, coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). They hide in deserted worm tubes or other small holes when alarmed (Ref. 1602, 48636), bite divers occassionally (Ref. 90102). They feed on the skin, mucus and sometimes scales of other fishes by quick attacks. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Juveniles mimic the cleaner wrasse Labroides dimidiatus (Ref. 9710). According to Ref. 53299 they are facultative mimics that change their color: at cleaning stations they mimic the cleaner wrasse and attack unsuspecting customers; elsewhere they adopt an alternative color and striping pattern to conceal themselves among fish shoals from which they can strike at passing fish.

species.name: Blennie atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are restricted to shallow waters and dwell among rocks and coral reefs (Ref. 5298), where there is considerable wave action (Ref. 26938).
