In the area of the type locality, it feeds on small aquatic invertebrates and spawns during the rainy season, approximately December to April. In the lower río Ucayali of the type locality region, it occurs sympatrically and syntopically with Brachyhypopomus beebei, B. benjamini, B. brevirostris, B. sullivani, and B. walteri (Ref. 116763).

species.name: Brachyhypopomus walteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in floating meadow habitats, composed mostly of the grass Paspalum repens, Poaceae. Occurs mainly in white water, but also in areas near the confluence of black water rivers with the Amazonas/Solimões ranging from low to medium conductivity. Syntopic with the species of Eigenmannia, Gymnotus, the apteronotid Parapteronotus hasemani and the electric eel Electrophorus electricus in the floating meadow habitats (Ref. 94132).

species.name: Brachyistius aletes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brachymystax savinovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Bogdan Dresler, pers. comm., 2000).

species.name: Brachymystax tumensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyopsis segaliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 56527).

species.name: Brachypetersius altus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachypetersius cadwaladeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachypetersius gabonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: most similar to Brachypetersius huloti from the Congo River basin, from which it differs in the extension of the lateral band onto the median caudal fin rays, presence of a humeral spot and fewer scales (4.5-5.5 vs 6.5) in transverse series between lateral line and dorsal fin origin (Ref. 80290).

species.name: Brachypetersius huloti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachypetersius notospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum size 70 mm SL (Ref. 80290).

species.name: Brachypetersius pseudonummifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyplatystoma capapretum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected below 200 m asl in the Amazon mainstream and largest white and black water triburtaries; trawled 10s to 100s m off shore, on mud and sand substrates (Ref. 55106).

species.name: Brachyrhamdia heteropleura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyrhamdia imitator
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyrhamdia marthae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyrhamdia meesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyrhamdia rambarrani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brachyrhamdia thayeria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers small streams not prone to flooding and is associated with marginal vegetation or along sandy beaches in shallow streams (ca. 1 m depth), with sandy or silt bottom substrate (Ref. 94149).

species.name: Brachysomophis atlanticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand and mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Brachysomophis longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Brachysomophis porphyreus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed nearly fully buried within a muddy bottom at a depth of 20 m (Ref. 42180).

species.name: Brackish damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitarily or in small groups in lagoons, harbors, coastal reefs and outer reef slopes, frequently among branching alcyonarians.  Also found in mangrove creeks (sometimes in freshwater), brackish lagoons and shallow reefs exposed to freshwater runoff; found well upstream in pure freshwater (Ref. 48636).  Feed primarily on benthic algae.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Brackishwater frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Unusual among antennariids in often occupying brackish or even totally freshwater habitats.  Most specimens were taken at 10 m depth or less.  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).

species.name: Bradbury’s triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brahm’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brainbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Brame
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit a wide variety of lakes and large to medium sized rivers.  Most abundant in backwaters, lower parts of slow-flowing rivers, brackish estuaries and warm and shallow lakes (Ref. 59043).  Adults occur usually in still and slow-running waters where they travel in large shoals (Ref. 9696).  Larvae and juveniles live in still water bodies, feeding on plankton. One to two years old juveniles move from backwaters to river to feed. In the absence of opportunity to leave backwaters, juveniles may adapt but have a slower growth and attain maturity at a smaller size.  They also drift to brackishwater estuaries to forage when water level of flooded areas drops in lower reaches of large rivers. Foraging juveniles in brackish waters stay in lower parts of rivers to overwinter in freshwater (Ref. 59043).  Feed on insects, particularly chironomids, small crustaceans, mollusks and plants.  Larger specimens may feed on small fish.  Juveniles feed on zooplankton (Ref. 30578).  Able to shift to particle feeding or even filter feeding at high zooplankton abundance.  Usually spawn in backwaters, floodplains or lakes shores with dense vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Can survive out of the water for extended periods (Ref. 9988).  The flesh is bony, insipid and soft (Ref. 30578).  Marketed fresh or frozen.  Eaten steamed, broiled, fried and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Branched ray flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare.  Minimum depth at 121 m and feeds on bottom-living animals (Ref. 9797).

species.name: Branchiostegus albus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy areas (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Branchiostegus argentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Branchiostegus auratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy areas (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Branchiostegus gloerfelti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Branchiostegus ilocanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from Herre's original description.

species.name: Branchiostegus saitoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits burrows as do other tilefishes (Ref. 89848).

species.name: Branchiostegus vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brandade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widely distributed in a variety of habitats, from the shoreline down to the continental shelf. Juveniles prefer shallow (less than 10-30 m depth) sublittoral waters with complex habitats, such as seagrass beds, areas with gravel, rocks, or boulder, which provide protection from predators (Refs. 89383, 89384). Adults are usually found in deeper, colder waters. During the day, form schools and swim about 30-80 m above the bottom, dispersing at night to feed (Ref. 1371, 89385). Omnivorous; feed at dawn or dusk on invertebrates and fish, including young cod. (Ref. 1371). Migrate between spawning, feeding and overwintering areas, mostly within the boundaries of the respective stocks. Migrations >200 km are rare occurrences (Refs. 89386, 89387). Marketed fresh, dried or salted, smoked and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Branded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Bras-de-rêve menton-uni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep-sea species (Ref. 12204).  Males parasitic on the females (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Brassy cardinalfish
species.description: Benthic species which inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brauer's dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468, 75154).

species.name: Braun's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow areas of reef and weed (Ref. 31790).

species.name: Brauner's tadpole-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in deeper, standing areas of fresh and brackish waters.  Feed  on chironomid larvae, small crustaceans, and gastropods (Ref. 4696).  Eggs are large and pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).  Very rarely observed and lives only one year.  Spawns in July to August with possibly only a small batch of about 20-30 eggs (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bravo clinid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide range of habitats, from boulder strewn slopes and reefs to ledges and undercuts along wall faces (Ref. 5227).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Males are territorial.  During the spawning season, the males often engage in aggressive activity with other males of the same species (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Bravo's bearded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among live and dead corals on sand, in tide pools and on shallow reefs to as deep as 5 m (Ref. 1602). Cryptic (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Brazhnikov's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazil blenny
species.description: Found either solitary or in small groups of up to 10 individuals; in small holes or associated with sea-urchins and sponges on the rocky reefs (Ref. 94079).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Brazil long nose cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazilian basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over coral and rocky bottoms, on the mainland coast and on coastal as well as oceanic islands. May be solitary or in groups of up to 4 individuals in small caves and under ledges, often swimming upside down, oriented to the ceiling. Feeds by picking at planktonic organisms in the water column; observed occasionally cleaning other fishes, including the pomacentrid Chromis multilineata and the haemulid Haemulon plumieri (Ref. 27309).

species.name: Brazilian blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallo reefs (Ref. 123106), on sandy bottoms and Thalassia testudinum beds (Ref. 13628). Feeds mainly on crustaceans but also on gastropods and worms (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Brazilian bocachico
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazilian croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An important foodfish.

species.name: Brazilian cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazilian damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow, coral or rocky bottoms and sometimes near the shore in areas with little visibility (Ref. 9626). Juveniles were collected from tide pools and on rocky Lithothamnion reefs; adults found up to 15 m depth (Ref. 40395). A diurnal species, adults feed on benthic algae, polychaetes and harpacticoid copepods (Ref. 9626); also consume hydroids and sponges and has been observed to feed on Abudefduf saxatilis eggs at night (Ref. 9626). 16:21 SL/TL (Ref. 9626). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding; eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate; males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brazilian dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used in the aquarium trade under the name Opistognathus leitoso. The population is declining fast in some areas of the Brazilian coast (mainly off the States of Espirito Santo and Bahia) due to commercial exploration of the calcareous algae banks. This species hovers over its burrow feeding on plankton and dives headfirst in to the burrow when threatened. Found usually over sandy bottom close to reefs, but also common over sand patches as small as 10 cm in diameter, enclosed by rocky areas or in calcareous algae (Lithothamnion sp.) banks (Ref. 84213). Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.

species.name: Brazilian dusky jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is common in coastal regions, in depths associated with gravel-sand bottoms, near coral reefs and rocky areas. Feeds mainly on small benthic organisms near the bottom (e.g., small shrimps, crabs, and isopods) (Ref. 129348).

species.name: Brazilian filetail catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably a demersal-benthic dwelling shark. The stomach (8.5 cm in length) of the paratype was almost empty, except for one fish eye lens, but an analysis of the intestine (9.0 cm) revealed small pieces of teleostean musculature and a fin spine, a crustacean appendage (pleopod or pereopod), a well-digested 5.0 cm long polychaete body piece, and five dark 22 mm long chaetae, possibly from this same annelid specimen. Reproductive mode oviparous, with just one functional ovary, the right, with four follicles (between 5 and 17 mm diameter), a well-developed nidamental gland, 18 mm (right) and 15 mm (left) in width and fully developed oviducts. Two completely formed slender vase-like dark brown (after fixation) egg cases, one in each oviduct, and both measuring 73 mm in length and 24 mm in width, narrowing at about 1/4 of its length from the anterior border. The surface seems to be smooth in macro view, but with numerous delicate longitudinal ridges and lateral keel along the entire both sides. Both small lateral keel-associated respiratory fissures not reaching to the borders, the anterior measuring 8 mm and the posterior 6 mm in length. Anterior border slightly convex, measuring 1.81 cm in width, pointed in each corner. Posterior margin very small, not measured, with two horn tendrils 3 mm in length in each tip and very small fringed fibrous hair-like filaments between the horns (Ref. 125615).

species.name: Brazilian flamefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Inhabits rock pools but also found to depths of at least 50 m.  Hides in holes and crevices during the day (Ref. 13121).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 40849).

species.name: Brazilian glass blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth range documented from Santa Catarina, South Brazil (S.Floeter, pers.comm. 04/10).

species.name: Brazilian guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from the coast line to the continental edge.  Females mature at ca. 90 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Feeds on crustaceans, cephalopods, polychaetes and small fishes.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Produces litters of 4-12 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Brazilian large-eyed stingray
species.description: Apparently associated with coral or sandstone reefs of the northeastern Brazilian continental shelf. Two female specimens were collected from the stomach of Rachycentron canadum (Ref. 36974). Juveniles also occurred in sandy beaches and estuaries. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Brazilian luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The young are pelagic, near the coast (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Brazilian sand stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from shallow reefs; inhabits the margins of sand flats in small caves and below reef walls at depths of 1 to 6 meters; these areas are deposits of coarse gravel largely composed of f fragments of mollusc shells, crustaceans, corals, calcareous algae and sea urchin skeletons and spines. Found buried in the gravel, with just the eyes and the dorsal finlet exposed; it appears to 'swim' in the gravel; solitary or in groups. Associates with other sand-dwelling fishes such as Dactyloscopus tridigitatus, D. crossotus, Gillellus greyae, and toadfish Thallasophynne punctata; also an unidentified shrimp and juveniles of crabs (Callinectes sp.).

species.name: Brazilian skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 1200 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brazilian slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazilian soft skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brazilian stardrum
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This species is rather common in inshore waters, from the surf zone to estuaries along the
northeastern Brazilian coast. Occurs near beaches with accumulations of detached macrophytes, mostly between September and February, feeding on amphipods and other crustaceans (Ref. 125562).

species.name: Brazilian wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits organic and rocky reefs (Ref. 48669).  Large individuals at depths of 10 m or more; juveniles in areas as shallow as tide pools (Ref. 48669).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 40849).

species.name: Bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over muddy bottoms in shallow as well as in deep waters and feeds mainly on snails, preferably of the genera Melanoides and Lanistes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Breast toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Breast-spot blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the intertidal areas and shallow coastal reefs (Ref. 8631, 48636).  They inhabit rubble and algae reefs (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Bregmaceros arabicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic (Ref. 46075).

species.name: Bregmaceros cayorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bregmaceros lanceolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. On the continental shelf.

species.name: Bregmaceros neonectabanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bregmaceros pescadorus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bregmacère de l'océan Indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. If taxonomy is correct, both onshore in brackish water and oceanic.  According to larval survey, occurrence in the tropics is wide (Ref. 9902, 45075).  Feed on planktonic crustaceans.  Also caught with bagnets (Ref. 2872).

species.name: Breitensteinia cessator
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Breitensteinia hypselurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Breitensteinia insignis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sexually dimorphic (Ref. 45707).

species.name: Brephostoma carpenteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Breton africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 2683, 81286, 81657) where reproduction takes place, marshes and lower courses of rivers, sometimes ascending over long distances into freshwater (Ref. 81286, 81657). Also lives in the sea, mainly in shallow bays and harbour areas (Ref. 81286). Sometimes found in shoals composed of several hundred individuals (Ref. 81657). Feeds on fish, shrimps, zooplankton (Ref. 28587, 81657) and various small invertebrates (Ref. 81657). Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406). Maximum reported standard length 200 mm (Ref. 81657).

species.name: Brevibora cheeya
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is in a coastal heath forest where the habitat consists mainly of Melaleuca (Myrtaceae) stands on sandy and peaty substrate; waters are tannin stained, slow flowing, and acidic (pH 4.5, measurement done in February 2009) (Ref. 65950).

species.name: Brevibora exilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in black water habitats of Sebangau and Kahayan basins.  Occurs syntopically with <i>Brevibora cheeya in the Rungan system, a major branch of the Kahayan basin (Ref. 95539).

species.name: Brevimyrus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distribution area is mainly continental and it is rarely found in the lower courses of basins (Ref. 81274). Inhabits fringing vegetation in the Sudd and migrates onto the floodplain to spawn (Ref. 28714). Bottom feeding insectivore (Ref. 28714). It possesses electro receptors over the entire head, the dorsal and ventral regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located (Ref. 10011). Also sensitive to sound frequencies (Ref. 10831).

species.name: Briarium pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens taken at the surface with nightlight and dipnet. May also be found on shallow mudflats with sparse seagrasses. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Found in association with Briareum soft corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Brichard's lampeye
species.description: Occurs in weedy parts of small rivers, brooks and swamps in river drainages (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Brick goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been collected from lagoons and drop-offs (Ref. 1602). Also found in reef crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Brick seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brick soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and seaward slopes to depths of more than 52 m where it is found  in groups in caves and under ledges (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on polychaetes, also on crab megalops, hermit crab larvae, and larvae of alpheid shrimps (Ref. 12419).  Forms large schools in oceanic locations (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Bridge duckbill eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Bridle cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common in seagrass beds, but occurs from water's edge to 75 m depth.  Commonly trawled on shallow shrimp grounds.

species.name: Bridle pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bridled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Etnier & Starnes (1991) considered the conservation status of Percina kusha to be endangered, like two other Percina species endemic to the upper Coosa River system, P. antesella and P. jenkinsi. In a review of conservation status of fishes in Georgia, Freeman (1999) assigned a status of rare (a species in need of protection because of its scarcity) to populations in Georgia. Warren et al. (2000) and Freeman et al. (2005) both regarded P. kusha as vulnerable (any taxon that may become endangered or threatened by relatively minor disturbance to its habitat). Based on the authors' sampling and snorkeling observations, P. kusha appears to be a species that naturally occurs in low abundance, at least when compared to sympatric congeners such as P. nigrofasciata and P. palmaris. We do not know, however, what the actual range of the species was prior to European colonization. Its association with slow-flowing habitats suggests P. kusha could have occurred throughout the Conasauga and Etowah rivers, and possibly in the geographically intermediate Coosawattee River, below the gorge now impounded by Carters Dam and Reservoir. Considering its very limited distribution in portions of two small rivers and threats to its habitat from municipal and industrial development and forestry and agriculture activities the authors consider P. kusha to be endangered (Ref. 58738).

species.name: Bridled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear white sandy areas near deep reefs and grassy and rocky areas. Burrows in the sand and the male guards the eggs (Ref. 5521). The Bridled goby, which has X-shaped marks and spots, occurs in both clear and more murky inshore waters, while the paler, very similar Sand goby, Coryphopterus tortugae [= Coryphopterus glaucofraenum], occurs over white sand (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Bridled leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily found in estuaries, schooling over seagrass beds and in Sargassum seaweed areas (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Bridled seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coastal waters, mainly around reefs; also enter estuaries and bays (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Bridled tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef and rock reef (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brienomyrus adustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brienomyrus brachyistius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: Brienomyrus longianalis. Occurs in most coastal basins in West Africa (Ref. 2703). Within this species complex, four distinct waveforms of electric organ discharge (EOD) were noted in the Gabon (Ivindo River) populations, probably pointing to separate species (Ref. 10460). Exhibits sexual dimorphism in its EOD waveform and duration (Ref. 10011; 10764 ). EOD has a constant waveform and variable sequence of pulse intervals (SPI) (Ref. 55567).

species.name: Brienomyrus longianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: related to Brienomyrus brachyistius, distinguished by longer anal fin in Brienomyrus longianalis and by lower peduncle height SL ratio. May be limited to the delta and the lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 3203).

species.name: Briggs' pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Preferred habitat is uncertain. Some specimens have been dredged, others have been taken among loose seaweed and floating dead Zostera sp. Over fine sand bottom. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may be brooding at 12.3 cm SL.

species.name: Briggsia hastingsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bright goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bright lanternfish
species.description:
Oceanic, mesopelagic (Ref. 4479, 75154).  Nyctoepipelagic at the surface (Ref. 4479). 
Reach sexual maturity at 7,4 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Brightbelly sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in the littoral zone at depths up to 30 m. Probably spawns in the littoral zone and its larvae and fry are transported to river estuaries in tides (Ref. 26949).

species.name: Brightchin dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Brighteye damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found exclusively in the surge zone of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). They always remain close to the shelter of small holes or sea urchin furrows in bare rock (Ref. 1602).  Feed on benthic algae and small invertebrates.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Brighteye darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky riffles of creeks and small rivers, and near debris in sand and gravel runs (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on midge and blackfly larvae and mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Brightspot skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brilliant lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brilliant pearlside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Brilliant rasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits forest streams (Ref. 13061).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Brindled madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits riffles, pools below riffles and runs over gravel and sand mixed with sticks and leaves in creeks and small rivers. Also found in lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294). Feeds on dipteran larvae (midges and blackflies), mayflies (Potamanthus and Stenonema), and hydropsychid caddisflies (Cheumatopsyche) (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Brinkmannella elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bristle-tail file-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef, weed, and rubble areas on shallow coral reefs (Ref. 43248, 48637),  commonly found in seagrasses (Ref. 58881). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Major food items include amphipods, polychaetes and molluscs (Ref. 58881).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bristlemouth
species.description: Oceanic (Ref. 4769).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154) and bathypelagic (Ref. 5951).  Does not exhibit diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4769).  Lipid content is 5.3 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 54.0 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).

species.name: Bristlemouth catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bristly grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Close to T. villosus.

species.name: Britski's catfish
species.description: Diurnal.

species.name: Britski’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brittanichthys axelrodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brittanichthys myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Broad clingfish
species.description: Inhabits intertidal to subtidal reefs in rocky weed areas (Ref. 9002).  Secretive, found under rocks (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Broad flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays, lagoons and shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Broad sandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually buried in the upper parts of wave-formed sand in clear sand estuaries and coastal bays (Ref. 9002).  Occurs in shallow waters and to at least 130 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Broad striped rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Broad-barred citharine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marginal vegetation of large rivers, in flowing water; picks small insects and other invertebrates from plant surfaces; pot sufficiently common for aquarium trade (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Broad-barred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among branches of Acropora corals; a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Solitary or in pairs, also found in reef crests and lagoons to 15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Broad-head croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Broad-snouted catfish
species.description: Omnivorous, feeding on terrestrial arthropods, aquatic insects, plants, mollusks, prawns and fishes (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Broadband barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in marshy habitats (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Broadband flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawl over sand or coral rubble bottom at 15 to 110 m; also taken by SCUBA off coral or rocky slopes (Ref. 9790). Occurs near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Broadbanded cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits coastal reefs, in sandy or weedy areas (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal.  Juveniles often occur with sea anemones (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Broadbanded thornyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in places with the steepest downthrow and sharp bends of sea bottom often in the places of the slope surrounded by large depths (the steep bottom relief causes vertical turbulent currents that provide the accumulation of food items) (Ref. 26289).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are extruded in floating gelatinous masses (Ref. 52092).

species.name: Broadbanded velvetchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Most specimens were collected by bottom trawl in depths less than 100 m and smaller individuals (about 10.0 cm SL) by set nets at 20-50 m (Ref. 76777).

species.name: Broadbodied toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Broadbrow flounder
species.description: Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Broadfin lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442). Adults feed on Sagitta, young fishes, copepods, and euphausiids (Ref. 6885). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442). Lipid content is 14.2 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 58% in total lipids (Ref. 9197).

species.name: Broadfin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 26773).

species.name: Broadfoot leg skate
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth of about 458 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Broadgilled hagfish
species.description: Espèce de myxines d'océanie. Occurs on soft bottoms of the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Able to form locally abundant populations and is often associated with inshore reefs (Ref. 85052).

species.name: Broadhead anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably coastal, pelagic and schooling (Ref. 189, 75154).  Adults are not yet known, only juveniles to a length to 4.2 cm SL.  More specimens and data needed.

species.name: Broadhead cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from 425-500 m depth (Ref. 26282).

species.name: Broadhead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky rapids of large rivers (Ref. 7248, 78218).  Known to feed on fish (Ref. 7248). Adults feed on fish while juveniles probably feed on small invertebrates (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Broadhead clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky shores.

species.name: Broadmouth cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 913 m (Ref. 26282). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Broadnose skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Broadnose wedgefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently confined mainly to brackish coastal and estuarine habitats in shallow water (Ref. 84284). Diet unknown, but presumably similar to other wedgefishes (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Broadnose worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tidal creeks or protected and semi-protected bays, never from the surf zone (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Broadsaddle cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral and rocky areas with little sand.

species.name: Broadsnout lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Broadspotted molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm, calm and vegetated waters.

species.name: Broadstripe goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coral-dwelling goby (Ref. 51183).  Found in groups near coral heads (Ref. 9710).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35408).

species.name: Broadstripe shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clay, sand and bedrock pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  Usually found  among vegetation and debris (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Broadstripe silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters; schools to feed on plankton and small nekton (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Broadstripe topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs at the surface near shoreline vegetation in quiet pools and backwaters of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Broadstriped barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams and the larger river systems with or without aquatic weeds (Ref. 13337); prefers slow-flowing streams with vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193). It forms shoals and undertakes seasonal movements up tributaries and onto floodplains (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Broadtail mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, fast flowing water over rocks and pebbles (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Brochet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, penetrating into freshwater; usually prefers very low brackish water or freshwater.  Found over soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on small fishes (Engraulidae, Clupeidae, etc.) and crustaceans (mainly shrimps) (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Brochet africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species seems to prefer upper river courses or small rivers where Hydrocynus species are absent or scarce (Ref. 81278).

species.name: Brochet d'Amérique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in lakes, swamps, and backwaters, and sluggish pools of streams.  Usually occur among vegetation in clear water (Ref. 86798).  Also found in brush piles, overhanging brush or rocks and boulders in areas lacking vegetation.  Rarely occur in rivers (Ref. 4639).  In winter, they are found associated with dead leaf litter (Ref. 39089).  Juveniles are found in flood pools and rivulets among exposed roots, twigs, leaves, and grass in 7.6-10.2 cm of water (Ref. 39088).  Larvae are sometimes found in very shallow water in roadside ditches, also in dead leaf litter (Ref. 39089).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brochet de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, penetrating into freshwater; usually at depths less than 20 m (Ref. 3713).  Feed on fishes (Gobiidae, Gerreidae, Engraulidae) and crustaceans (shrimps and crabs) (Ref. 35237).  Mature individuals congregate at mouths of passes and rivers during the spawning season, May through September (Ref. 3713).  Seasonal movements into freshwater occur but poorly understood (Ref. 3713).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5712).  Valued game fish and an excellent food fish (Ref. 26938).  The world record for hook and line is a 53-lb., 10 ounce fish caught at Parismina Ranch, Costa Rica (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Brochet de mer (Lates calcarifer)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, in clear to turbid water (Ref. 5259, 44894).  A diadromous fish, inhabiting rivers before returning to the estuaries to spawn.  A protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32209).  Larvae and young juveniles live in brackish temporary swamps associated with estuaries, and older juveniles inhabit the upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 6390, 44894).  Have preference for cover on undercut banks, submerged logs and overhanging vegetation (Ref. 44894).  Feed on fishes and crustaceans.  They reach 1500-3000 g in one year in ponds under optimum conditions (Ref. 11046, 44894).  Juveniles also eat insects (Ref. 44894).  Sold fresh and frozen; consumed steamed, pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9987).  A very popular and sought-after fish of very considerable economic importance (Ref. 9799).  Presently used for aquaculture in Thailand, Indonesia and Australia (Ref. 9799).  Australia's most important commercial fish and one of the most popular angling species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Brochet de mer (Merluccius merluccius)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 128002.  Found usually between 70 and 370 m depth.  Adults live close to the bottom during day-time, but move off-bottom at night.  Adults feed mainly on fish (small hakes, anchovies, pilchard, herrings, cod fishes, sardines and gadoid species) and squids.  The young feed on crustaceans (especially euphausiids and amphipods).  Are batch spawners (Ref. 51846).  Almost entirely marketed fresh, whole or filleted, to specialized restaurants or retail markets (Ref. 58452).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted and frozen; can be steamed, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Stocks seem to be over-fished (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Brochet de mer (Psammoperca waigiensis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky or coral reefs, frequently in weedy areas, usually in holes and crevices by day.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Forages on fishes and crustaceans at night (Ref. 9710).  Mainly marketed fresh.  In Hong Kong sold live in fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Brochet de mer (Sphyraena sphyraena)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and offshore waters (Ref. 2683).  Feeds mostly on fish, less often on cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 11101).

species.name: Brochet du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish of no commercial or angling importance (Ref. 41072).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brochet maillé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in vegetated lakes, swamps, and backwaters and quiet pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 26373).  Also found in deep, cold water with little or no vegetation (Ref. 39109, 39108).  Adults migrate to deeper water during winter (Ref. 39110, 39097, 39111) undertaking shoreward spawning migrations soon after spring ice disappears (Ref. 39109).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Juveniles tend to lie motionless near shore or burrow themselves in mud beneath debris (Ref. 39112).  Larvae hide among vegetation (Ref. 39113).  Oviparous, with pelagic eggs.

species.name: Brochiloricaria chauliodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brochiloricaria macrodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brochiraja aenigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from a single specimen; no information on mature males or juveniles (Ref. 58023).

species.name: Brochiraja albilabiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Male paratypes were found to be immature at 50.7 cm TL, no information re juveniles (Ref. 58023).

species.name: Brochiraja heuresa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brochiraja leviveneta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Male paratype mature at 43.2 cm TL (Ref. 58023).

species.name: Brochiraja microspinifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Male paratype mature at 27 cm TL; no information on juveniles (Ref. 58023).

species.name: Brochiraja vittacauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brock's bristle-mouth fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brock's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lagoon and seaward reefs, at moderate depths (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Solitary and cryptic among corals and weeds (Ref 90102).

species.name: Brokenbar blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only around islands (Ref. 51183).

species.name: Brokenbar dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brokenbar Grouper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is landed in trawling and longline fisheries at 28-93 m and this appears in commercial hauls and not common in fish markets in Hong Kong (Ref. 122001).

species.name: Brokenfin sandburrower
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small demersal species found in bays and coastal waters (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Brokenhband cleaner goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in crevices and deep recesses in the rocks. Like other Elacatinus, this species is a cleaner; it picks parasites from other fishes. In areas of the reef where there is a floor of sand that is protected by an overhanging ledge, reef whitetip sharks may be observed lying about like a stack of cord wood. It is in these areas that this goby lives and it can clean the reef whitetips (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Brokenline lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 5572) at 0-200 m at night, 200-1000 m during day (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Brond-snout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes including reservoirs in Iraq.  Prefers stone grounds and still waters in river and lakes in Turkey.  Feeds on insect larvae, and eggs and fry of fishes as well as diatoms and algae (Ref. 109283).

species.name: Bronze cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in Thalassia testudium beds (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Bronze catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, from estuaries onto the continental shelf.  Found mostly on mudflats; males incubate eggs in its mouth (Ref. 68964). Mainly opportunistic and carnivorous; feeding on sea urchins, crustaceans, fish, prawns, loose scales, and detritus (Ref. 38478).  Has a sharp and venomous dorsal and pectoral spines that can inflict extremely painful injuries(Ref. 68964). An important food fish (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Bronze darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift riffles over gravel and rubble in small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294). Feeds on blackfly larvae and pupae, and hydropsychid (Cheumatopsyche) caddis larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Bronze featherback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear streams and enters brackish waters (Ref. 4832).  Adults inhabit standing and sluggish waters of lakes, floodplains, canals and ponds (Ref. 12693).  Undertake localized lateral migrations from the Mekong River to floodplains during the flood season and back to the mainstream or other permanent water bodies during the dry season (Ref. 37770).  Common in tanks throughout the greater parts of India.  Feed on insects, fish (Ref. 12693), crustaceans and some young roots of aquatic plants (Ref. 6459).  Active during twilight and night.  Colonize and breed seasonally during rainy days and migrates back to permanent waters in dry season (Ref. 12693).  Breeding takes place in stagnant or running waters in the rainy season.  Eggs are laid in small clumps on submerged vegetation.  A female measuring 21-25 cm usually lays 1,200-3,000 eggs.  The fish is relished both in fresh and dried state.  Soup made from it is reported to be given to people with measles (Ref. 7431).  Of high economic importance as food fish in South and Southeast Asia to Borneo and Sumatra and taken by all types of small-scale fishing gears (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Bronze sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A nocturnal species that form aggregations in caves by day and feeds on zooplankton at night (Ref. 2334).  The smallest gravid female found was 8.61 cm SL and the largest 14.94 cm SL.  These  were found among collections made in October through March, although specimens from the early dates carried immature eggs.  The smallest specimens, 3.03-3.18 mm SL from the Kermadecs, were collected in June, suggesting that juveniles settle early in the year. Over its entire range, collections are known from September to June (Ref. 88976).

species.name: Bronze whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bronze-lined rabbitfish.
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in schools, usually in coral and sandstone reefs and also seagrass beds; juveniles reportedly live in large estuaries such as Negombo Lagoon (5 km x 3 km).  Apparently, estuaries are an important habitat for juveniles and sub-adults, with older fish moving to coral reefs.  Feeds by scraping algae from rock and coral substrates and browsing on seaweeds and sea grasses.  It supplements its diet with small items of animal tissue. A report on analysis of gut contents of specimens (2 - 27 cm SL), collected by trap and seine, from lagoons and coastal areas of Sri Lanka contain diatoms, green, blue-green, red and brown algae and a seagrass.  It appeared that this species have a preference for feeding during the night when percentages of gut fullness between day and night catches were compared.  It appeared to be nocturnal because it was mostly seen to be inactive during the day (Ref. 95994).

species.name: Bronzespotted rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Bronzestriped grunt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore species found over rock-sand bottoms.  Usually in schools.

species.name: Brook Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and creeks (Ref. 27671).

species.name: Broom filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear coastal to outer reefs, usually in rich coral areas with rubble patches or gutters (Ref. 48637). Feeds on coral polyps (Ref. 89972). Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Less approachable than most filefishes (Ref. 9710).  Usually seeks coverage in large corals when approached (Ref. 48637).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Broomfin dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 559, 75154).

species.name: Brosmodorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon to locally abundant cryptic species found in areas with dense algal growth (Ref. 34024).  Sometimes in rock pools (Ref. 9003).

species.name: Brossé améthyste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, found to depths of at least 1,524 m.  Migrate in the water column at depths of 150-250 m during the day and to about 50 m at night (Ref. 57912, 107678).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951); abundant near continental shelf-slope breaks and seamounts, rare in the open ocean (Ref. 107678).  A cyclic selective feeder of copepods and euphausiids (Ref. 4739).  They become sexually mature when 1 year old.  Spawning takes place in March - September, producing 200-500 eggs, floating on the surface (Ref. 35388).  Lipid content is 5.5 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 15.3 % in total lipids (Ref. 8966).

species.name: Brossé réunionnanais
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brotula flaviviridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brotule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Adults benthopelagic (Ref. 34024) down to 650 m, but most often on the continental shelf (Ref. 3686), on sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Juveniles common in reefs (Ref. 34024).  Smaller silvery specimens taken far out at sea in the epipelagic (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotule barbe-de-boue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic on shelf and upper slope (Ref. 34024).  Larvae found in the epipelagic far offshore (Ref. 34024).  Found in shallow lagoon and seaward reefs and occurs at depths of at least 220 m.  Adults (30-90 cm) move to depths of 100-650 m (Ref. 58472).  A nocturnal species, rarely seen for it lives in caves and crevices during the day and periodically emerges from cover at night to feed on crustaceans, mainly crabs, and fishes.  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Utilized fresh and eaten steamed, pan-fried and baked (Ref. 9987).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Brotule barbiche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Found on soft bottom (Ref. 7251).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotule de banc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species ranging from coastal bays to 75 m depth (Ref. 34024).  Inhabit soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Flesh is appreciated (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Brotule liserée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotule noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on soft bottoms, between 429 and 732 m in depth, while juveniles are encountered at shallower depths (Ref. 9329).  Prejuveniles mesopelagic (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae and extended pelagic juvenile stage (Ref. 36413).  Oval pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotule sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Found on the continental shelf, on soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Consumed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Brotule tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Found on the continental shelf, on soft bottom (Ref. 5217).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotulotaenia brevicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brotulotaenia nielseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Broussonnet's mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species with no data available.  Oviparous, eggs could be pelagic and non-adhesive like other members of this family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brown bleheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a swamp with silty bottom and lush aquatic vegetation> Lays floating eggs, with the mail guarding the nest (Ref. 120631).

species.name: Brown brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat not known; no ripe females were observed (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Brown chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The depth range of occurrence of this species seems to follow the 1000 m depth contour around New Zealand, but may be an artifact of sampling.  Size range for juvenile females 27.7-75.9 cm TL (18.2-37.6 body length) and males 41.0-83.5 cm TL (16.7-52.2 cm BDL); for adult females 85.5-103.5 cm TL (51.9-59.9 cm BDL) and males 74.0-97.5 cm TL (48.7-57.0 cm BDL) (Ref. 107024).

species.name: Brown codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the outer edge of the shelf (Ref. 4495).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Brown coral blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among branches of live and dead corals of sheltered shallow reefs (Ref. 2334).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Brown coscarob
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brown damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Brown darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy runs, especially near vegetation, of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Brown demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sporadic distribution (Ref. 48636).  Adults inhabit soft bottoms of lagoons and inshore reefs around coral outcrops, rocks, debris, and others (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Brown dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among corals of subtidal lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Also found in crevices and ledges. Usually found in association with branching corals (e.g. Acropora and Pocillopora). Sometimes enters the aquarium fish trade (Ref. 37748). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Brown drombus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic, littoral, often in mangroves and rivers (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Brown grenadier cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brown guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore on sandy-mud bottoms (Ref. 11230, 30573).  Reported to occur offshore (Ref. 58784). Feeds on small benthic animals.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature at ca. 55 cm TL. Produces litters of 1-14 pups (Ref. 114953).  The best edible fish in the family, served in raw slices or hard boiled with seasonings (Ref. 637).  Dried fins used for shark-fin soup (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Brown hagfish
species.description: Attains over 50 cm TL (Ref. 559).

species.name: Brown Irish lord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal areas and down to at least 130 or 780 m depth (Ref. 5515).  Usually found in subtidal areas of exposed coasts (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Brown lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water.  Males mature at 55 cm.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brown leaf catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brown lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on bottom-living animals.

species.name: Brown madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-gravel riffles and runs among debris, rocks and undercut banks of springs, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Brown numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 9912).  Biology little known (Ref. 9912).

species.name: Brown pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Brown puller
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs, occurring in small to large aggregations (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brown pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brown rat clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from dense mats of macroalgae attached to rocky substrate in water up to 1 meter depth. A female specimen (1.42 cm SL) contained ca. 20 mature eggs (ca. 10 within each ovary) of ca. 0.3-0.@ mm diameter. The largest eggs in each ovary exhibited a dark orange cap that may represent an 'attachment apparatus' at the animal pole as described from the eggs of three species of European gobiesocid (Ref. 120657).

species.name: Brown ribbed snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brown rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A sedentary rockfish found in shallow water and bays (Ref. 2850), among sheltering weed-covered rocks or around pilings (Ref. 27436).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae and pelagic juveniles (Ref. 36715).  Fin spines are sharp and mildly venomous and can cause annoying wounds (Ref. 27436).  Small live specimens make excellent bait for large lingcod (Ref. 27436).  Flesh is firm and tasty, but rarely found in markets (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Brown slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brown snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brown spotted moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among corals and rubble of seaward reefs.  Very secretive (Ref. 9710, 75154).  Benthic at 1-22 m (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Brown spotted snake moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 30874, 75154), among rubble with algae and invertebrate cover (Ref. 48635, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Brown stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the outer continental shelf (Ref. 6871, 75154).  Size at birth about 10 cm (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Brown stingray
species.description: Demersal or benthic on insular and continental shelves (Ref.58048, 58302); on on upper slopes to 800 m (Ref. 114953). Found on sand or mud bottoms, sometimes near coral reefs (Ref. 12951). Feeds on crabs, prawns and small bony fishes (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature at ca. 100 cm WD, and females ca. 110 cm WD; pups born at ca. 35 cm WD; but these data measurements needs confirmation (Ref. 114953). Caught often by demersal tangle net and longline fisheries operating in shelf waters.Utilized for its meat, cartilage and thorny tail (58048).

species.name: Brown topknot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found among large brown algae (Carpophyllum and Cystophora). They feed on weed dwelling crustaceans and small fish (Ref. 9003). Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240). Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Brown-banded butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep rocky reefs, generally between 120-190 m in the tropics (Ref. 9710), in the East Indies usually found below 110 m (Ref. 90102).  Found in shallow, muddy open substrates with outcrops of reef or debris in sub-tropical waters (Ref. 48636).  Often in aggregations (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brown-banded cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Rarely in markets (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Brown-banded pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 5.0-5.5 cm SL (Ref. 5316). Also found in lagoons and seaward reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Brown-red coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on reef flats, crests and upper reef slopes in less exposed areas; and prefers Acropora selago, but also occurs in a number of other, narrowly branched Acropora species such as A. acuminata and A. hyacinthus (Ref. 94082).

species.name: Brown-spotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand-weed areas close to shore.  Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Brownband shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs in moderately sloped areas (about 20 degrees) with mixed substratum (mud, sand, and gravel). Of the five individuals observed, three are solitary and a mixed sex pair (male holotype and female paratype) shared the same burrow. It is associated with an unidentified alpheid shrimp (Ref. 116711).

species.name: Brownbanded dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from less than 5 to between 8 and 24 m. Solitary, rests on bottom. Inhabits exposed coastal reefs and outer slopes (Ref 90102).

species.name: Brownboy goby
species.description: Inhabits rock pools of intertidal zone, rocky shores and mangrove habitat (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Browncheek blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in shallow, rocky areas (Ref. 37955).  Inhabits empty worm and mollusk tubes on rocky reefs (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 11482), benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 37955).  Spawns in the spring (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Browneye skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.6-6.0 cm long and 3.0 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).

species.name: Brownfields wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected seagrass beds (Ref. 33839) and rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brownish sculpin
species.description: inhabits muddy bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Brownmargin flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf off western and northern Australia (Ref. 9790).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Brownsnout spookfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 6686).  Taken regularly at depths shallower than 458 m, with scientific deep-sea fishing gear.  Feed mainly on small crustaceans, particularly copepods (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35626) and eggs (Ref. 6686).  Paedomorphic (Ref. 35626).

species.name: Brownspot largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also caught with drawnets. The habitat preferences are strongly influenced by the presence or absence of the tigerfish Hydrocynus forskahlii: if the tigerfish is absent, S. thumbergi is found in open waters and sometimes in fast-flowing rocky habitats; in areas where the tigerfish occurs, S. thumbergi is relegated to lagoons, backwaters and marshy shallow areas. Feeds on small fish, insects and snails (Ref. 6465).

species.name: Brownspotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Browntail snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bruening's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the rainforest and forested savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Brunei dartfish
species.description: Form loose aggregations of 10-50 individuals, observed hovering 50-100 cm above the substrate on a very gradual but strongly current-swept sand and rubble slope in 28-31 m depth. Collection reef with visibility invariably quite low (5-8 m maximum) and where there was frequently a minor thermocline at the 20-25 m depth range, with the fish exposed to moderately cooler temperatures down to 27°C. When approached too closely, individuals would dive into burrows in the sand, sometimes individually but also multiple individuals entering the same burrow (Ref. 105381).

species.name: Brush-tail toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in clear estuaries in shallow depths over sand, sometimes in small aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Brushtail pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in moderate to shallow depths (Ref. 205).  Inhabit seagrass (Ref. 75154).  Largest known pipefish, may well reach 65 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 20-21 cm SL.

species.name: Bruun's cutthroat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryan's sand dart
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of this family burrow in shallow marine to estuarine areas with fine coral sand or muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 48316).  Of no commercial interest but may be taken incidentally (Ref. 48316).

species.name: Bryaninops annella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from its commensal sea fan, Annella mollis (Ref. 94797).

species.name: Bryaninops dianneae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryaninops discus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryaninops earlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on sea pen in seagrass bed (Ref. 94797).

species.name: Bryaninops spongicolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryaninops tectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by hand from the gorgonian Ellisella quadrilineata (Ref. 94797).

species.name: Bryaninops translucens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commensal with an unidentified, horizontally elongate, cylindrical sponge (Ref. 94797).

species.name: Brycinus abeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus bartoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus batesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on the surface; feeds on insects and leaves (Ref. 51193).

species.name: Brycinus bimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and inshore areas of lakes; sand, filamentous algae, vegetal debris, Povilla, insect remnants have been found in the stomach of this species; juveniles feed on cladocerans and small insects (Ref. 41580).

species.name: Brycinus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. macrocephalus

species.name: Brycinus carmesinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology unknown.

species.name: Brycinus carolinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. imberi, with red fins no black longitudinal stripe; B. nigricauda, with colored caudal fin margin.

species.name: Brycinus derhami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus epuluensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus fwaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among aquatic plants around the edges of Lake Fwa (Ref. 39244).

species.name: Brycinus humilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus leuciscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. nurse, B. longipinnis and B. luteus.

species.name: Brycinus luteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus nigricauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus opisthotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus peringueyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus poptae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus rhodopleura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Brycinus schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus taeniurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus tessmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycinus tholloni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon alburnus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon amazonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Important food fish.

species.name: Brycon argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon atrocaudatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reported to reach 40 cm TL (Ref. 9585).

species.name: Brycon behreae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and rivers of moderate to high current velocity in 10-640 meters elevation.  Swims upstream in search of  small tributaries in which to breed; lays eggs in excavated nest in the sandy bottom of creeks.  Omnivorous, feeds on fruit, flowers, seeds, insects, annelids, crustaceans, and small fishes (Ref. 36880).  Popular fish among sport anglers (Lopez-Pinto, pers. comm.).  Maximum length reported to reach 40 cm TL (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Brycon bicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon cephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon chagrensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon coquenani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon costaricensis
species.description: This species is found in lakes, but also abundant in fast-flowing rivers and streams.  It occurs at elevation from 0-600 m in lakes, rivers and creeks, and tolerates temperate ranging from 21-34°C (Ref. 95069).

species.name: Brycon coxeyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon dentex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon devillei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon falcatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Is an omnivorous species.  Little is known of its biology (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Brycon ferox
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon fowleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon gouldingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fruits and insects (Ref. 55407).

species.name: Brycon henni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 16.93 cm TL specimen (girth 28 cm) caught from Quebrada la Compania, Columbia weighed 1.125 kg (G. Kelley, IGFA application for all-tackle records, pers. comm., 10/2002).

species.name: Brycon hilarii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon labiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Brycon medemi

The stomach contents of three specimens include adults and larvae of different species of Diptera (12.5%, 4.0 mm3), Diptera: Simulidae (12.5%, 3.0 mm3), Diptera: Chironomidae (12.5%, 3.0 mm3), Diptera: Dixidae (12.5%, 2.0 mm3), Trichoptera: Leptoceridae (12.5%, 14.0 mm3), Ephemeroptera: Baetidae (25%, 5.0 mm3), Hymenoptera: Vespidae (12.5%, 2.0 mm3).

Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and creeks in lentic habitats over detritus and decomposing vegetal material with low transparency, neutral pH, high dissolved oxygen, high conductivity and total solids, and low turbidity and hardness.  These water parameters indicate a highly disturbed environment that
affects the survival of this species and those that share its habitat (Ref. 104976).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams or rivers with gravel bottom, low depth, clear rapidly flowing water  and scarce submerged vegetation (Ref. 55778).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small river with sandy and rocky bottoms in areas of low current flow.

The water is tea-colored with transparency usually moderate to high, pH usually around neutral (6.07-7.06), and high oxygen concentration (5.7 mg/l- 7.1 mg/l) as well as oxygen saturation (50.5% - 90.5%). Occurs sympatrically with Bryconamericus alpha, Bryconamericus cismontanus and Bryconamericus loisae (Ref. 86277).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks and brooks of moderate to high current velocity in between 60 to 940 m elevation.  Feeds on seeds and other vegetable matter and insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Bryconamericus thomasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryconamericus turiuba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Ribeirão Santa Barbara, the type locality, which has two distinct reaches: a lentic pool which is 23-49 m wide, 1.5 m deep, with a water velocity of 0.4 m/s, over a gravel bottom and some smaller areas with sand or mud; and a rapid located further upstream, which is 6.2-13.5 m wide, 0.5 m deep, with a greater water velocity of 1.1 m/s and a rocky bottom. Both stretches have margins with altered riparian forest or herbaceous vegetation (Ref. 54761).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a river with clear water (Ref. 49957).

species.name: Bryconops collettei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in habitats with moderate to fast moving waters over rocky and sandy bottoms; in both acidic, black waters, as well as in clear, but slightly acidic waters.  In the Caura, it was found in rapids covered by vascular plants (Podostemonacae), as well as in small springs with sandy bottoms.  Found in the upper part of the water column in the main channel, usually in schools with other characid species.  Observed food items include several groups of terrestrial insects (Ref. 56366).

species.name: Bryconops cyrtogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand and rocks, in areas with fast current intersecting with cascades (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Bryconops disruptus

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryconops imitator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large river habitats in swift current and in rapids among dense stands of the rooted vascular Podostemonaceae, as wells as in small streams with current.  Also inhabits small streams, rapids, bays and backwaters over sand, gravel and rocky bottoms (Ref. 47228).

species.name: Bryconops inpai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryconops magoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a morichal with fast moving waters over sandy bottoms; often in water from mid-depth to the surface, at the center of the main channel, where it schools with other characid species.  Feeds at the surface and attracted to allotochtonus material that falls into the water; also on several groups of terrestrial insects (Ref. 56366).

species.name: Bryconops melanurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Does not appear to prefer a particular biotope.  Lives in groups and feeds on insects.  Its need for space makes it difficult to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Bryconops munduruku
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Igarapé Açu presents clear water running over sandy beds; its headwaters are located within the limits of the Tapajós National Forest and are densely covered by marginal vegetation (Ref. 104128).

species.name: Bryconops piracolina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryconops tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stream and lotic shallow areas (depth up to 1.5 m) with riparian vegetation composed by trees and shrubs. The stream is characterized by transparent water and sandy, stony, and rocky bottom. Occurs syntopically with Eigenmannia trilineata, Hoplerythrinus unitaeniatus, Astyanax cf. goyacensis, Knodus cf. breviceps, Knodus sp., and Ancistrus sp. (Ref. 109891).

species.name: Bryconops transitoria
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryconops vibex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bryozoan goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.
