Closely associated with a bryozoan, which is provisionally identified as a member of the genus Triphyllozoon; the color pattern of the fish effectively blends with the coloration of the host invertebrate, and the fish effectively maintains a burrow within the folded recesses of the bryozoan colony; the depth range of collections and observations was about 15-30 m, usually on black volcanic-sand slopes, with the inconspicuous bryozoan colonies (roughly spherical-shaped with a diameter ranging from 3-7 cm) often attached to small pieces of coral rubble or volcanic rock (Ref. 107790).

species.name: Bryx randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bryx veleronis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males may be mature at 4.5 cm SL.  Planktivore (Ref. 28023).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Brème
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms and feeds mainly on small fishes and squids.  They are abundant near oceanic islands (Ref. 9626).  Small individuals are taken as by-catch in trawl fisheries (Ref. 5217).  Marketed mostly fresh, sometimes frozen.  Flesh of good quality.

species.name: Brème bordelière
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious and frequents stagnant waters of lakes and reservoirs, rivers and canals with calm waters. Occurs in a wide variety of shallow, warm lowland lakes and slow-flowing lower reaches of large rivers and canals. Frequently very abundant on bottom of large sandy rivers. Larvae live in still water bodies. Mainly nocturnal. Feeds on benthic invertebrates. Spawns along shores on submerged vegetations, roots or even on shallow gravel bottom (Ref. 59043). Reproduction takes place in May to July. Exhibits polyandry (Ref. 6114). Regularly hybridizes with Vimba vimba (Ref. 59043). Of little interest to game fishers and consumers (Ref. 30578). Unpopular with commercial fishers due to its small size and competition with more desired species.

species.name: Brème de la mer Noire
species.description: Inhabits brackish estuaries, large to medium rivers and some large subalpine lakes.  Sedentary populations inhabit even in small rivers or barbel zone.  Feeds mainly on small molluscs and insect larvae.  Breeds in riffles in shallow, fast-flowing streams and rivers on gravel.  Semi-anadromous populations forage in freshened parts of sea and migrate for long distances to spawn.  Lacustrine populations move to fast-flowing tributaries.  Spent adults return to foraging habitats (Ref. 59043).  Threatened from its range due to water obstruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Brème de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and epipelagic species, also found to 1,000 m depth (Ref. 27121).  Occasionally comes close to shore (Ref. 9563).  Seasonal migrant occurring in small schools, movements apparently temperature-related.  Opportunistic feeder on small fishes, cephalopods, amphipods, and euphausiids.  Sold fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Brème de mer (Rhabdosargus sarba)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 30573, 44894), usually entering estuaries (Ref. 44894).  Abundant in shallow water and often caught at the surf-line or in rock pools (Ref. 9987).  Larger, solitary fish sometimes enter brackish mangrove areas (Ref. 9987).  Juveniles in estuaries move into deeper water with growth (Ref. 4335).  Often in schools (Ref. 9710).  Feed on benthic invertebrates, mainly mollusks (Ref. 5213) and aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 26055).  Popular angling species commonly captured with hook and line (Ref. 44894).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Brème de Pékin
species.description: Feeds on higher aquatic plants.  Its flesh is tasty but very bony.  One of the most important commercial fishes of China (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Brème à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand and rubble areas near coral reefs.  Solitary fish are often encountered, but large adults usually form aggregations of up to about 50 individuals (Ref. 9710).  Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal feeders (Ref. 9710).  Feed mainly on gastropods, ophiuroids, and echinoids.  Pagurids and brachyuran crabs, polychaetes, tunicates, and holothurians are consumed in lesser quantities. Caught mainly with gillnets, traps, spears, and handlines (Ref. 2295).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9775).  Ciguatoxic in Marshall Is. (Ref. 171).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Bréme noire à longues nageoires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along the shelf edge (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Brême de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over seagrass beds and rocky and sandy bottoms to about 300 m (Ref. 3688).  Gregarious, sometimes in large schools (Ref. 3688).  Omnivorous, feeding on seaweeds and small invertebrates, especially crustaceans (Ref. 3688).  Protogynic hermaphrodites (Ref. 4781).  An important food fish.

species.name: Buan goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty inner tidal flats near mangroves and among seagrasses, usually hovering a little above the bottom (Ref. 34765).  Feeds on small invertebrates and organic matter (Ref. 34765).

species.name: Bubble-head snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male (5.30 and 6.20 cm) specimens appear to be mature, while the female (9.40 cm) was mature with ovaries containing numerous mature and immature, spherical, pale-colored, opaque, yolked oocytes, ranging in diameter from 0.20-2.12 mm; from gross observation, there appear to be fewer than 100 eggs in each ovary.  Specimens were collected with a 60 cm bongo net, epibenthic sled and bottom trawl (Ref. 82595).

species.name: Bubblefin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow weedy areas of rocky shorelines with little coral growth (Ref. 9710).  Found in groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Bubu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and large rivers (Ref. 4967). Has never been observed in large quantities in forested areas (Ref. 57126). Occurs in shallow water with muddy bottom. Bottom feeder, omnivore, feeds on plankton, seeds, detritus (Ref. 13868), mollusks (Ref. 13868, 28714), mud, debris (Ref. 28714), insect larvae (Ref. 6868, 28714), worms and small Crustacea (Ref. 6868). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Nested eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 47642). Furthermore, the male plays host to eggs and young of Dinotopterus cunningtoni which takes advantage of the already prepared nest and feed on the host brood (Ref. 49546). An example of interspecific brood care.

species.name: Buccochromis atritaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups over open sand and preys on small sand-dwelling haplochromines (Ref. 5595).  Hunts in pairs or in large groups (Ref. 3817).

species.name: Buccochromis heterotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been observed in different habitats but always near rocks.  A piscivore which regularly hunts in packs (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Buccochromis oculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reportedly caught at a depth of 18 m near Rifu Point, in an area consisting of sandy and swampy shores (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Buccochromis rhoadesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy bottoms in shallow, sheltered bays.  Also occurs over sandy areas off beaches.  Juveniles inhabit very shallow sandy shores.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Buccochromis spectabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water near sandy shores (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Bucktooth tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Buenos Aires tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plants.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  In captivity, spawning occurs among plants and eggs hatch usually in 20 to 24 hours.  One of the hardiest tropical fishes for the home aquarium (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  eats plants; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Buffalo darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Buffalo sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in inshore rocky and sandy areas (Ref. 2850).  Feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 2850) but also shrimps, crabs, amphipods, mussels, and small fishes (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Buffalo à petite bouche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools, backwaters and main channels of small to large rivers.  Also occurs in lakes and impoundments.  Feeds on shellfish and algae, by grinding with the bony plates in its throat (Ref. 9988).  Appears to be a good candidate for aquaculture.  Marketed fresh and eaten pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Buffon's river-garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at the surface levels in coastal waters, estuaries and rivers.  Feeds on terrestrial insects.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Bufoceratias microcephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bufoceratias shaoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males and larvae unknown (Ref. 51070).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bufoceratias thele
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males and larvae unknown (Ref. 51070). Specimens caught in bottom trawls (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Bufoceratias wedli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic and bathypelagic near or on continental shelf (Ref. 6939).  Males and larvae unknown (Ref. 51070), probably dwarfed, non-parasitic (Ref. 6939).  Minimum depth from Ref. 6613.

species.name: Bugeye dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reef slopes amongst algae boulder habitat to about 20 m depth (Ref. 48635); also inhabits inshore reefs (Ref. 7300). Cryptic and seen with the use of collecting chemicals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Bujurquina apoparuana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit streams with clear, tea-colored water (Ref. 9088)..

species.name: Bujurquina beniensis
species.description: This species inhabits streams and whitewater riverbanks (Ref. 128932).

species.name: Bujurquina cordemadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams with clear, tinted water (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina eurhinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bujurquina hophrys
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit brooks (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina huallagae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers with swift, clear water and with sand, rubble, gravel and mud bottoms (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina labiosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit slow flowing or pool-like portions of rivers (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina mabelae
species.description: This species inhabits streams and riverbanks, with white and clear water. Also found in lagoons of fluvial and tectonic origin (Ref. 128932).

species.name: Bujurquina mariae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bujurquina megalospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bujurquina moriorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit forest streams with near colorless, clear to slightly turbid water with moderate to swift current varying with rains (Ref. 9088).  Both parents guard eggs and larvae (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Bujurquina oenolaemus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on snails (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Bujurquina omagua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small rainforest streams, with shallow water (<1 m except in deeper pools) but deep mud and accumulated debris, blackish water , with weak or moderate water current (Ref. 128854).

species.name: Bujurquina ortegai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bujurquina pardus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a whitewater habitat of Rio Danta with a substrate of sand and silt, a relatively fast current, little aquatic vegetation and primary forest on the riverbanks.  Collected with 4 m seines from the middle of the current at a depth of 1.2 m (Ref. 96081).

species.name: Bujurquina peregrinabunda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with very little clear and slow running water, coming down a slope with primary forest (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina robusta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit slow flowing or pool-like portions of the river.  Apparently territorial (Ref. 9088).  Both parents guard eggs and larvae (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Bujurquina syspilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit forest clear-water streams running down slopes, with much reduced flow, and abundant forest litter (Ref. 9088).  Eggs are deposited on leaves and guarded by both parents; larvae are taken into the mouth (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Bujurquina tambopatae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit brooks with bottom substrate consisting of sand, mud and sparse gravel (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Bujurquina zamorensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Bukoba lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow parts of papyrus swamps of Lake Victoria; also found in river mouths, rice fields and ditches connected to lakes (Ref. 3788, 47311). Sexual maturity is reached at an age of about 6 months (Ref. 47311). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Bulatmai barbel
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occur in the sea, mostly close to shores and forages also in estuaries.  This species is semi-anadromous and non-anadromous, rarely landlocked in reservoirs.  Adults and juveniles feed on invertebrates, algae, detritus, plant material, and small fishes, while larvae prey on zooplankton and small benthic invertebrates.  Spawn in lowland streams and rivers on sand-gravel bottom, usually in strong current.  Undertake migration to uppermost tributaries of rivers.  Non-anadromous populations begin to migrate during late summer-autumn and spawn following spring, but some enter rivers in early spring and spawn same year.  Migration by non-anadromous populations takes place just before spawning to upper stretches of tributaries or spawn in lakes and reservoirs on sand to mud bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bulb-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bulbless dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 7300, 75154) at ca. 800 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Bulbonaricus brucei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type material was collected amongst the coral Galaxea clavus. Males may be mature at 4.35 cm SL. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bulbous rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bulgarian minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams with clear,  well oxygenated water, over gravel to stone bottom. Maximum size reaches up to at least 6.7 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bulgarian spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species.  Adults occur in highland and lowland water courses with little current, in springs and associated wetlands and in lakes (Ref. 26100), with sand or silt bottom (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bulgarian stone loach
species.description: Inhabits flowing water with gravel to stone bottoms, usually in riffles and rapids.  Spawns in June (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Bull chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Bull goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bull klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at bottom of tidal and subtidal zones (Ref. 5496).

species.name: Bull pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters, usually from 18-127 m depth.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bull sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bulldog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with dipnets in the Kafue floodplain, Zambia.  Prefers well-vegetated, muddy bottomed marginal habitats of rivers and floodplains.  A shoaling species which moves inshore after dark.  Migrates within rivers.  Recorded to move up tributaries in shoals during flood season (Ref. 13337).  Feeds on invertebrates, especially midge and mayfly larvae and pupae taken from the bottom and off plant stems.  Breeds during the rainy season in shallow vegetated localities; females carry up to 6,000 eggs (Ref. 7248).  Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head and on the ventral and dorsal regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located  (Ref. 10011).

species.name: Bulldog eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mud-dweller, occurs inshore and in estuarine areas (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Bulldog goodeid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bulldog lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35839).

species.name: Bullhead minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet pools and runs over sand, silt, or gravel, in small to large rivers.  Most common in medium-sized rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on insect immatures (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Bullhead scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bullhead triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal areas (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bullish conger
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Bullneck seahorse
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Trawled from fine sand or hard bottom, possibly in association with gorgonian coral (Ref. 205).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Bullockia maldonadoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bullrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in freshwater streams and brackish shore areas.  Inhabit still or gently flowing freshwater streams over rock, mud or gravel, a bottom-dwelling fish.  Usually found near aquatic vegetation or woody debris.  During rainy periods, may migrate downstream into estuaries, but they normally frequent fresh water.  Relatively sedentary species, spending majority of their time stationary on the bottom or among weeds waiting for prey.  Breed in fresh water, as juveniles have been collected from the upper reaches of rivers, including impoundments.  Both adults and juveniles have venomous dorsal, anal and pelvic spines and therefore should not be handled (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Bulls-eye cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected coastal bays and estuaries in sponge and soft-coral areas (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Bullseye jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms (Ref. 11482), in about 20 m depth (Ref. 27115).  Feeds on benthic and planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Bullseye pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bullseye wriggler
species.description: A benthic, inshore species, on the sandy fringe of coral reefs (Ref. 75154). Also found in rubble in lagoons and sheltered waters in 9-24 m (Ref 90102) and crevices close to the base of fringing reefs in the depth range of 1.5-16 m (Ref. 115539).

species.name: Bulmer's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rainforest tributaries with boulder, gravel or sand bottoms in hilly terrain between about 35 to 1070 m elevation.

species.name: Bulolo rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in fast flowing water of rapids or below waterfalls.

species.name: Bumblebee cory
species.description: Found in sandy shallow waters with little current.

species.name: Bumblebee fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Bumblebee goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bumphead sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is presumed to prefer warmer water temperatures than Mola mola (in Sanriku coast of Japan, this species occur at sea surface temperatures of 16.8-25.6°C, average 19.9°C (vs. 11.5-25.6°C, average 17.7°C when Mola mola appeared in the area). The maximum recorded weight of 2,300 kg applies to a 272 cm TL female caught off the coast of Kamogawa, Japan by a set net (Ref. 117083).

species.name: Bumpy lumpsucker
species.description: Found on stony bottoms (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Bunagaya goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bundoon blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults swim above the bottom.  They feed on zooplankton.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Bunjako barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters or sandy banks (Ref. 36900) and marginal water-lily swamps (Ref. 104790). During the biannual floods specimens are found some distance up lakeside streams; this migration may be connected with breeding (Ref. 104790).

species.name: Bunocephalus aleuropsis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shaded waters with sand, clay and bedrock areas below riffles.  Stomach contents include insect and plant debris (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Bunocephalus aloikae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus chamaizelus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus colombianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus doriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clearwater streams with sandy to muddy bottom, up to 2.5 m deep, with water flow up to 50 cm/sec.  Supposedly an air-breather that hides amidst plant debris on the bottom during the day.  Feeds mainly on chironomid larvae and oligochaetes, besides larvae of several aquatic insects (Ref. 39865).

species.name: Bunocephalus erondinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus hartti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus larai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bunocephalus minerim
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Burchell's redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and deeper flowing stretches of larger tributary streams and mainstreams.  Feeds on detritus and small organisms, usually taken from the bottom.  Breeds in summer.  Fry and juveniles form large shoals, adults occur in small groups.  Due to the development of towns, agriculture and industry, the habitat of the species has been destroyed.  Populations have also been eliminated by introduced predatory fishes (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Burdur spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and their sources in Lake Burdur Endorheic Basin (Ref. 94468).

species.name: Burgess' butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in drop-offs where gorgonians and black corals are abundant.  Usually in depths over 40 m, but in some localities much shallower (Ref. 48636); usually in depths less than 40 m in East Indian region, solitarily or in pairs (Ref 90102).  Reported to have been collected from a depth of 380 feet (= 115.8 m) in Palau (J.C. Delbeek, CAS, pers.comm. 10/2017) . Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  They do well in the aquarium and are exported from the Philippines (Ref. 37816).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Burma hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species, but probably tolerating some salinity in estuaries, thus similar to S. phasa. More data needed.

species.name: Burmese bat catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on insect larvae and benthic organisms (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Burmese carplet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Burmese geel goby
species.description: Found in ponds.

species.name: Burmese gobyeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river mouths and estuaries.

species.name: Burmese kingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Burmese loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams with moderate current and pebble to stone bottom (Ref. 43281).  Found in clear, swift streams and lakes with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Burmese mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Burmese river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, pools and lakes.  More data needed.

species.name: Burmese River ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, reaching at least 650 km up the Irrawaddy, perhaps more.  More data needed.

species.name: Burmese river shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the middle and upper reaches of rivers.  More data needed.

species.name: Burmese snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length recorded is 19.4 cm SL (Ref. 116754).

species.name: Burmese spineless eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lowland wetlands in dense vegetation (Ref. 57235).  Occur on the bottom of shallow standing waters.  Most common on grassy floodplains, often in water only a few centimeters deep (Ref. 12693).  Possibly consists of multiple species (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Burmese stone loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In fast-flowing mountain creeks on rocky bottom; feeds on algae (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Burmese stream catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Burmese trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shady areas and muddy bottoms in deep hill streams.  Adults usually collected in clear water with moderate to swift currents, juveniles in quiet pools further downstream (Ref. 27732).  Found in medium to large-sized rivers, flooded fields and rapid-running mountain streams (Ref. 12975).  Diet consists of insects and small fishes.  (Ref. 12693).  One of the most delicious fish in Nepal (Ref. 9496).  Rarely seen in markets.

species.name: Burnt tail fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Buroca toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in currents of all velocities, but is more frequently found in brooks, creeks and rivers of low to moderate velocity.  Lives from sea level to 940 m elevation and swims near rock, gravel or sand substrata.  Feeds on diatoms, flocculent detritus and ooze (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Burrhead chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel riffles and runs of small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Burrhead shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, sandy pools and runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Burrough's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and coastal reefs, usually on open rubble patches.  They occur singly or in small groups.  Feed primarily  on benthic algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Burrow splitfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in back-reef rubble habitat. Collected from a sand and rubble (ca. 0.5-10.0 cm in diameter) substrate, 45-90 m from the gradual reef drop-off. Found in or near yellowhead jawfish (Opistognathus aurifrons) burrows. Although not a common species, this species is regularly seen from April to November, which is when jawfish are abundant (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Burrowing goby
species.description: Lives in burrows excavated in clean sand, often in association with the sandprawn Callianassa kraussi (Ref. 52193). Restricted to sandy, quiet water areas and is unable to form burrows where the substrate is disturbed by water movements, is muddy or consists of sand with a particle diameter > 0.5 mm (Ref. 28077). Food consists of slow moving benthic organisms like chironomid larvae, gastropods, bivalves and amphipods (Ref. 28077). Breeds throughout summer, males are territorial (Ref. 52193). On exposed shores, they occur deeper than 3.5 m (Ref. 28077, 2798). Occasionally intertidal.

species.name: Burt’s damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Buru cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near river mouths and estuaries (Ref. 54391), on shallow inner reefs and mangroves (Ref. 37816), over soft or hard bottoms (Ref. 54391). Forms aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Buru glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in brackish mangrove estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847, 37816).  Probably feed on small insects, crustaceans and other invertebrates.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Busakhin's beardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Bushymouth catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  feeds on plants and roots; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Bussing's mudbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth and method of collection unknown (Ref. 55786).

species.name: Bussing's stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.

species.name: Butis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is reported to occur in many coastal streams in brackish to freshwaters and estuaries over substrates of mud, sandy mud or leaf litter and is often observed clinging upside down under dead wood, eyes facing downwards. An ambush hunter, feeding mainly on small fish and crustaceans (shrimps (Atyidae), prawns (Palaemonidae)) (Ref. 130228). .Usually found in brackish mangrove areas and in creeks and rivers, sometimes well upstream (Ref. 2847), 48637).

species.name: Butis gymnopomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Butis humeralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Butis à épaulette noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish mangrove estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams, usually on mud bottoms (Ref. 44894).  Usually found in lagoons and estuaries, particularly where there is vegetation (Ref. 6028, 79840).  Occurs frequently in mangrove swamps (Ref. 2847, 79840).  Occasionally ascends rivers (Ref. 6028).  Feeds mainly on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 6028, 79840).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Butler's frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154). Solitary and usually found among weeds and rubble (Ref 90102).

species.name: Buton glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Butter catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in quiet, shallow (0.5-1.5 m), often muddy water, in sandy streams, rivers and tanks (Ref. 6028).  Also occur in canals, beels and inundated fields (Ref. 1479).  Feed on vegetable matter and fish (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Butter sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow water on soft, silty bottom.  Moves into shallow water in summer and to deeper water in winter (Ref. 6885).  Spawning adults exhibit north-south migrations (Ref. 6885).  Feeds on chaetopod marine worms, young herring, shrimps, and sand dollars (Ref. 6885).  A tasty food fish, sometimes marketed (Ref. 2850).  Also used for mink food (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore waters where rocks and brown algae are abundant. Browses on algae and feeds mainly on brown algae Carpophyllum (Ref. 26966), Lessonia spp., and Macrocystis spp. (Ref. 116706).

species.name: Butterfly barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Butterfly flying-gurnard
species.description: Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Butterfly goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic and littoral, entering estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 4343).  Usually seen in pairs, hovering a short distance above the substratum.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  t builds its burrow in sand or silty sand by moving out mouthfuls of sediment (Ref. 11441).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Butterfly gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal marine waters, over on the continental shelf (Ref. 33616).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Butterfly perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found over rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Forms large aggregates in deeper water where it feeds mostly in the lower part of the water column.  Usually occurs in areas which are exposed to continual strong tidal water movement (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Butterfly scorpionfish
species.description: Inhabits the rocky littoral and sublittoral zones of northern Taiwan (Ref. 39597).  Found on sandy mud or gravel bottom (Ref. 559).

species.name: Butterfly sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Butterfly shrimpgoby
species.description: A single specimen collected from a sandy-mud bottom at a depth of 45 m in a protected bay.  Observed to be usually at 40-50 m depths (area with pebbles); the young at depths of 8 m to about 30 m, but apparently on rare occasions;  the species symbiotically associates with alpheid shrimp (species name uncertain) (Ref. 55718).

species.name: Butterfly splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Raised commercially in Florida, U.S.A.

species.name: Butterfly whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty coastal bays to deep muddy habitats offshore.  Swims on open substrate adjacent to reefs, usually in small aggregations.  Often with large bottom feeders such as stingrays to catch disturbed prey (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles found close to reefs.  Feeds on small crustaceans.  Also taken by bamboo stake trap in Thailand.  Used also in fish balls, fried and as duck food.  Not much appreciated for food, and low priced.

species.name: Byblis Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bynoe goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in protected bays and harbors; often on silty habitat or fine white sand just below the intertidal zone.  Make burrows under solid objects; hovering close to the substrate.  Adults usually in pairs (Ref. 12723).

species.name: Bythaelurus incanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bythites gerdae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Bythites islandicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 51024).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Viviparous (Ref. 4758).

species.name: Bâtarde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found inshore in schools, frequently entering brackish lagoons and freshwater (Ref. 30578).  They migrate occasionally tending to move northward in summer-time as temperatures rise.  Females are larger than males (Ref. 59043).  Adults feed mainly on benthic diatoms, epiphytic algae, small invertebrates and detritus (Ref. 2804), juveniles only feed on zooplankton (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Reproduction occurs in the sea during winter (Ref. 30578).  Eggs and larvae pelagic.  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4645).

species.name: Bècune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore (Ref. 11230).  Feeds on fishes.

species.name: Bècune (Sphyraena pinguis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore on mud, sandy mud or rock bottoms (Ref. 11230, 48637).  Usually forms large schools (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on fishes.

species.name: Bécasse de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and epipelagic species usually found above the thermocline.  Most densely distributed in waters close to coasts and islands (Ref. 9688).  Most likely schools by size.  Undergoes spawning migrations in the Pacific.  Feeds mainly on fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods. Caught mainly with longlines, set nets, and sometimes by trolling and harpooning from boats (Ref. 43). Utilized fresh, smoked and frozen; also used for sashimi and sushi; eaten broiled and baked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Bécasse de mer (Macroramphosus scolopax)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between the seabed and midwater on the lower continental shelf, over sand. Juveniles found in oceanic surface waters (Ref. 2683); adults normally live close to the bottom (normally in 50-350 m depth (Ref. 47377)). Gregarious. Juveniles feed mainly on pelagic invertebrates, mainly copepods, while adults feed on bottom invertebrates (Ref. 6732). Seems to be sympatric with Macroramphosus gracilis (Lowe, 1839) all around the world (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Bécasse de mer tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bécune aiguille
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Bécune argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually near shore or near the surface (Ref. 2850).  Often in small schools (Ref. 2850).  Young enter bays (Ref. 2850).  Feed mainly on other fishes (Ref. 2850).  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Migrate south from the California coast during autumn, but may remain in front of the Mexican coast throughout the year (Ref. 9345).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted and frozen; eaten broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Considered as potentially dangerous due to its large, sharp teeth and aggressive disposition, though there are no reports of attacks (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Bécune chandelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters.  Found in rocky or coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  More abundant over muddy bottoms.  Juveniles are encountered in seagrass beds (Ref. 9626).  Often occurs in large schools, sometimes near the surface (Ref. 9626).  Marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Bécune chevronnée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near prominent current-swept lagoons or seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Also in bays and inner turbid lagoons (Ref. 9768).  Nocturnally active, but occurring in relatively large schools during the day (Ref. 9768).  Sold fresh or processed into fish cakes (Ref. 27550).

species.name: Bécune de Forster
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnally active, but occurring in large schools above lagoon patch reefs and along outer reef slopes during the day (Ref. 9768, 48637).  Feeds mainly on fishes, but also on penaeid shrimps and squids.  Sold fresh, frozen or dried salted.  Reports of ciguatera poisoning need confirmation.

species.name: Bécune guachanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow and generally turbid coastal water over muddy bottoms, often around river estuaries.  Schooling species (Ref. 6949).  Occasionally enters estuaries and brackish waters (Ref. 57401). Feeds on mainly on fishes belonging to the Engraulidae, Clupeidae, Lutjanidae and Synodontidae families and also on squid from the Loliginidae family (Ref. 9626).  Maximum reported size: 71cm (Ref. 57401). Marketed fresh and salted.

species.name: Bécune mexicaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fairly common species (Ref. 9345) found in the continental shelf (Ref. 11035).  Important food fish (Ref. 9345).

species.name: Bécune pélican
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in temperate waters (Ref. 9345).  Seen in groups of 3-20 from the surface to about 24 m (Ref. 5590).  Feeds mainly on fish .  Large individuals may slash prey into pieces before swallowing them.  The front of each jaw is toothless and there is a series of large triangular teeth along each side of both jaws (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Bécune à bouche jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its habits are probably similar to those of the phylogenetically closely related Sphyraena sphyraena (Ref. 6949). Feeds on cephalopods, crustaceans and fishes. Caught in trammel nets and beach seines (Ref. 11101).

species.name: Bécune à ligne jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 122826.

species.name: Béluga
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des esturgeons. Pelagic at the sea, following its prey. Undertakes upriver migration to spawn. Juveniles occur in shallow riverine habitats during their first summer. Spawns in the main course of large and deep rivers with strong current and on stone or gravel bottom (Ref. 59043). Feeds mostly on sea fishes (Black Sea whiting, anchovies, flatfishes, gobies, fry of bottom-living fishes), also crustaceans, mollusks, mysids and amphipods. Fisheries are based almost entirely on the value of the caviar, but meat also is sold fresh, smoked and frozen; eaten broiled, boiled, fried and baked (Ref. 9988). Bester, a hybrid of female Huso huso and male sterlet Acipenser ruthenus, has been successfully cultivated for its high quality eggs (Ref. 9988). The largest sturgeon and largest European freshwater fish. In Guinness Book of Records as the most expensive fish (Ref. 6472). Threatened due to overfishing for meat at the sea and for caviar in estuaries. These threats will soon cause global extinction of the natural populations. Survival can only depend on stocking (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Béryx
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ca. 500 m on mud or sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230). Occurs on the continental slope; adults demersal, young pelagic (Ref. 9563). Feeds on crustaceans, small fishes and cephalopods (Ref. 3321). A 35 cm SL specimen was found in the stomach of Latimeria (Ref. 58472). Young have heavy spines on the head (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Béryx (Beryx splendens)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the outer shelf (180 m) and slope to at least 1,300 m depth, probably moving further from the bottom at night; often found over seamounts (Ref. 9833) and underwater ridges (Ref. 33648).  Juveniles pelagic (Ref. 9072).  Feed mainly on fish, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 33648).  Oviparous, spawn in batches (Ref. 30291).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 30291).  Marketed frozen and eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Béryx australien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on rocky reefs and muddy substrates of the continental shelf and upper slope, forming dense schools close to the bottom at dawn and dusk and dispersing throughout the water column at night to feed (Ref. 9563).  Juveniles also aggregate in schools (Ref. 33987) and are found in estuaries and shallow costal waters (Ref. 9833).  Feed on small fish, crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 27111).

species.name: Bœuf
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The shoulder spines can inflict, painful stings.  Usually found buried in the sand or mud.  Equipped with an acoustic apparatus that generates both acoustic and electric pulses.  Electric discharge activity shows two temporal patterns:  1) reflexive discharges of short duration (milliseconds), elicited by mechanical stimulation, and 2) those of much longer duration (several seconds) observed only during the summer spawning period (Ref. 10011).  Low-frequency spontaneous discharge activity (5-10 Hz), with a sexual dimorphism in discharge amplitude is also said to exist.  This species suggestively represents a transitional form in the evolution of electric organs in fishes (Ref. 10577).  Oviparous, eggs, larvae and juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 6763).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 9987).

species.name: C-O sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on flat bottoms and rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Young are common in shallow water during the summer but adults frequently in deeper water (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Caban podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cabezon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, sandy and muddy bottoms as well as kelp beds (Ref. 4925).  Adults and juveniles feed on crustaceans, fishes and mollusks (Ref. 6885).  Commonly captured by sport fishers (from shore, boats or piers) and by scuba divers (Ref. 2850).  Flesh is good eating but eggs are poisonous and will make humans violently ill (Ref. 13513).

species.name: Cabillaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 1371).  Enters rivers and may go considerable distances upstream, but usually remaining within regions of tidal influence (Ref. 1371, 27547).  Adults exhibit seasonal movements:  inshore during winter for purposes of spawning and offshore during summer for feeding (Ref. 1371).  Juveniles and adults are opportunistic epibenthic feeders; juveniles feed on fish and small benthic crustaceans (Ref. 1371).  Taxonomic problems to be solved.

species.name: Cabilllaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal habitats during summer and winter (Ref. 1371).  Cryopelagic or epontic, from surface down to 1383 m (Ref. 58426).  In the Beaufort Sea, it may also be found in brackish lagoons and in almost fresh water in river mouths (Ref. 1371).  Although associated with the occurrence of ice (White Sea), it is present in ice-free near-shore waters (Alaska) (Ref. 1371).  Onshore-offshore movements are associated with spawning and movements of the ice (Ref. 27547).  Feeds mostly on epibenthic mysids, also amphipods, copepods and fishes (Ref. 1371).  Also caught with mid-water trawls (Ref. 1371).  Utilized as fishmeal and source of oil (Ref. 1371).  Euryhaline and eurythermic.

species.name: Cabillus atripelvicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cabillus caudimacula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand near reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Cabillus nigromarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cabillus nigrostigmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sandy bottom, in shallow water in open sandy areas. It is active at night and partly borrowes quickly in the sand when alarmed, like dragonets, by shaking the body and digging using large pectoral fins with their thickened membranes (Ref. 94146).

species.name: Cabillus pexus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected amongst a pile of dead-coral rubble in coral reefs (Ref. 94253).

species.name: Cable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters.

species.name: Cable's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms adjacent to rocky reefs.  Common in tide pools and near-shore areas (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Cabocolo tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected above and below a waterfall along the Rio Mucajaí.  The river in that region was characterized by steep banks and with dense forest along the shore; large amounts of aquatic plans of the family Podostemonacease were present in the area, the water acidic (pH 5.8) and well oxygenated (91% saturation) (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Cabot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal waters (Ref. 2850, 44894, 57400), often entering estuaries and rivers (Ref. 2847, 3573, 11230, 44894, 57400), sometimes far-up-river, lagoons and hypersaline environments (Ref. 57400).  They are usually in schools over sand or mud bottom (Ref. 2850), between 0 and 10 m, occurring equally in tropical, subtropical and temperate waters (Project MUGIL).  They are mainly diurnal, feeding on detritus, micro-algae and benthic organisms (Ref. 56548, 74902, 74760).  Juveniles feed on zooplankton until about 3.0 cm SL (Ref. 59043).  Reproduction takes place at sea, at various times of the year depending on the location (Ref. 74907, Amour).  Adults form schools and migrate offshore to spawn and developing larvae migrate back inshore (Ref. 81659). There is absence of an obligatory freshwater phase in the life cycle (Ref. 74752).   Females spawn 0.8 to 2.6 million eggs which develop at sea (Ref. 74912, Chen & Su 1986).  Sexually mature at 3 to 4 years (Ref. 74902).  Maximum length reported as 120 cm SL (Ref. 7399, 57400, 81659) remains to be confirmed (Project MUGIL).  Maximum weight reported as 12 kg (Ref. 56527) seems too high for the area and remains to be confirmed (Project MUGIL).  Widely cultivated in freshwater and brackish ponds (Ref. 2847, Jackson 1984, Liao 1981).  Marketed fresh, dried, salted, and frozen; roe sold fresh or smoked (Ref. 9321); also used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Cabot aux yeux verts
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only in deep water in the vicinity of coral reefs.  Biology unknown.  It is an excellent food fish.

species.name: Cabot cafre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably occurs in rocky reefs.  Its apparent rarity may be due to its preference for relatively deep water.

species.name: Cabot de fond
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters from 80-370 m on slopes of islands, sea mounts or continental shelves. Feeds on benthic fishes and large invertebrates (Ref. 89707). Considered rare in Tahiti but quite common in atolls (Ref. 4821). The species is easily confused with E. poecilonotus, E. radiatus, or E. tuamotuensis, three closely related deep-water groupers. Known to be ciguatoxic at Mauritius. Uncommon in local markets (probably due to it deep-water habitat).

species.name: Cabot gueule rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal reefs and lagoons, often on silty habitat (Ref. 48635), in or near caves and holes in the reef. They feed mainly on small fishes (including Pempheris sp.), also on stomatopods (Pseudosquilla sp.) (Ref. 6448); and crustaceans (Ref. 37816). Preliminary data indicate that mature individuals spawn at any time of the year and mature (females?) at about 35 cm SL (Ref. 6448). Small juveniles mimic Centropyge vrolikii (Ref. 8631), and C. nox until they outgrow their model in size (Ref. 48635). Taken as part of the live reef food fish trade centered in China and In Hong Kong and are occasionally found in markets (Ref. 89707). They are caught with hook-and-line, spear, and probably in traps (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Cabot mara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline.  Adults are often found in mangrove areas (Ref. 9962).  They inhabit sheltered rocky shorelines and mangroves (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cabot noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cabot noir (Epinephelus marginatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer rocky bottoms (Ref. 5222), are solitary and territorial (Ref. 12382).  Juveniles are found closer to shore (Ref. 48605) in rocky tidal pools (Ref. 48609).  Enters brackish environments (Ref. 57293).  Mainly feed on crabs and octopi; larger individuals feed on a greater proportion of fishes, the majority of which are reef-associated species (Ref. 6842).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Mature individuals form spawning aggregations (Ref. 55367).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 171).  Readily caught by anglers (Ref. 5222).  Not adapted well in an aquarium (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Cabot nègre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear to turbid water in shallow as well as deep water (Ref. 4787). Juveniles are found in inshore coral reefs (Ref. 5222). They feed in water to more than 100 m depth (Ref. 27275). It has been suggested that juveniles mimic the herbivorous damselfish Neopomacentrus sindensis, presumably to get closer to their unsuspecting prey (Ref. 5222, 9710). Feed on small fishes and crabs. Probably spawn during restricted periods and form aggregations when doing so (Ref. 27352). Eggs and early larvae are probably pelagic (Ref. 6390). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cabot rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cabot sale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sedentary reef-associated species (Ref. 89707). Occurs on coral reefs, areas with rocky substrata, algal flats and seagrass beds.  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 30573).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Forms spawning aggregations (Ref. 55367). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cabot sale (Epinephelus longispinis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral reefs or rocky areas and occasionally on sandy bottom.  Feed mainly on crustaceans, especially crabs and stomatopods, rarely on small fishes, squids, and pelecypod flesh.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cachama
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually solitary.  Adults stay in flooded forests during first 5 months of flooding and consume but fruits and grains.  Young and juveniles live in black waters of flood plains until their sexual maturity.  Feeds on zooplankton, insects, snails and decaying plants (Ref. 32894).  Used in aquaculture because it can live in mineral poor waters and is very resistant to diseases.  Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Cacique antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, primarily amphipods.

species.name: Cacique hérisson
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms (Ref. 27121).  Periodically sheds the outer keratinous layer of its skin (Ref. 27121).  Flesh edible but rarely eaten (Ref. 6626).

species.name: Cacique lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms (Ref. 9602).  Flesh edible, but not utilized commercially (Ref. 9602).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 6626.

species.name: Caddo madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles, pools and shoals near shorelines of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Cadenat's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs and deeper offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Caduchon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms along the shoreline (Ref. 5213) to depths of 200 m (Ref. 5755).  Nocturnal, found buried in sand or mud during the day (Ref. 5755).  Feeds on benthic and burrowing invertebrates (Ref. 5755).  Pelagic young preyed upon by seabirds or found ashore during bad weather (Ref. 3975).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3411).

species.name: Caecieleotris morrisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave inhabitant.  The cave entrance at the type locality lies at about 6.1 m deep beneath a rocky bluff along the shoreline of the lake. Immediately within the cave, the depth drops to about 27.4 m before rising to a depth close to 12.2 m where it then levels off.  Flowstone (sheet-like mineral deposits typically consisting of calcite) was observed in the cave (Ref. 109339).

species.name: Caecocypris basimi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted fish.

species.name: Caecogobius cryptophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave-restricted species (Ref. 27297).

species.name: Caecula kuro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Caelatoglanis zonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Caenotropus labyrinthicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on autochthonous invertebrates, sponges, and detritus.  Maximum length based on largest examined specimen.

species.name: Caenotropus mestomorgmatos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Black-water species, in streams, rivers, and tributaries.

species.name: Caenotropus schizodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Caesio azuror
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in schools in deep lagoons and along seaward reefs in coastal areas (Ref. 9710), mixing with other species of fusiliers (Ref. 48636). Juveniles are used as tuna bait fish. They are oviparous, with small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Caesio rose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs (Ref. 58652), sometimes forming schools with other Pterocaesio species. Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations. Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402). Also caught mostly by drive-in nets. Important tuna baitfish.

species.name: Caesio tricolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs.  Juveniles occasionally appear in large numbers in shallow lagoons and on reef flats (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Also caught by drive-in nets.  Tuna baitfish.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Caesio à ceinture d'or
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs.  Found in schools.  Feeds on zooplankton in large midwater aggregations. Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Also caught by drive-in nets.  Valuable tuna baitfish.

species.name: Caesio à croissant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal areas, mainly on or near coral reefs (Ref. 30573). They are more common along steep seaward reefs than in lagoons (Ref. 9710). They form large aggregations in midwater on upper edge of steep slopes and around patch reefs, often with other fusiliers (Ref. 90102). They feed on zooplankton. Are oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: Caesio à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found primarily around coral reefs, with a preference for coralline lagoons. They feed on zooplankton in large midwater groups and form schools with other caesionids. Mature adults migrate to select areas around the reef to spawn near the surface in the entrances of deep channels during outgoing tides on a lunar cycle. They are oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402). Are caught with drive-in nets.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Caesio à ventre rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often in silty areas with low visibility at 1-30 m depth (Ref. 90102).  Inhabits coastal areas, usually over rocky and coral reefs.  Forms schools in midwater and feeds on zooplankton.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Taken primarily by handline in Sri Lanka; caught mostly by fish traps in western Thailand and Malaysia; caught in trawls in the Gulf of Thailand; caught by a variety of methods including drive-in nets, fish traps and gill nets in Indonesia, the Philippines and Papua New Guinea.  The most ancestral living caesionid species.

species.name: Caesiura pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reefs; within crevices and caves of mostly dead coral rock and sandy rubble bottom (Ref. 9710, 57688). Solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Caffrogobius caffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic, littoral, intertidal in rock pools (Ref. 4343).  Also found in brackish waters (Ref. 11344).

species.name: Caffrogobius dubius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water.

species.name: Cagna armée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in benthic over soft bottoms of coastal waters.  Also caught with trammel nets.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Cagna cabinza
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Over rocky and sandy bottoms.  Maximum size assumed to be the same as for the family.  Feeds on small crustaceans such as isopods and amphipods but also on polychaetes and algae.

species.name: Cagna gros yeux
species.description: Forms schools over sandy shallow bottoms (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Cagna jopaton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. During the day, it occurs in large schools that slowly move to the boarders of reefs (Ref. 9114).  At nightfall, they move offshore and divide into smaller schools to feed (Ref. 9114).  Feeds on mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Cagna rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along sandy shores and over shallow muddy bottoms (Ref. 3798).  Adults feed at night on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Cagna œil jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably caught with trawl nets and marketed fresh.  Additional information not available.

species.name: Cagnassun de paise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found usually near the bottom, at times also in surface waters; pelagic and migratory in large schools.  They feed on other fishes especially sardines, anchovies, etc. and small crustaceans (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Cagnole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and well offshore (Ref. 5578), over continental and insular shelves (Ref. 244).  Coastal, pelagic, and semi-oceanic, but often bottom associated at 1-139 m (Ref. 58302).  Migrates northward in summer; young often in large aggregations of hundreds of individuals (Ref. 13562).  Prefers to feed on small sharks, skates and stingrays, but also preys on bony fishes, shrimps, crabs, barnacles and cephalopods (Ref. 244).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Regarded as being dangerous to people, though only few can be tentatively attributed to this species due to its occurrence in temperate waters (Ref. 244).  Reported to cause poisoning (Ref. 4690).  Caught occasionally by shark and tuna longline fisheries (Ref.58048). Meat utilized fresh, dried-salted, and possibly smoked for human consumption; liver oil for vitamins, fins for soup, hide for leather, and carcasses for fishmeal (Ref. 244).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).  Become sexually mature when 250 to 300 cm long.  The female gives birth to 30 - 40 young (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Cahaba shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flowing pools, usually over sand or gravel, less often near rocky riffles.

species.name: Cahabón toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cahita sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Caiapobrycon tucurui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cailleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal waters, usually along the shoreline (Ref. 9710) and over clear coral reefs (Ref. 5217). May form large schools in beaches, mainly over Thalassia beds (Ref. 5217). Often in polluted areas (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Cairns rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rainforest creeks usually in hilly terrain with alternating sections of rapids and rocky pools varying in depth from several centimeters to one to three meters.  Bottom composed of boulders, cobbles and gravel with minimal plant growth.  In spite of the limited distribution its future seems secure as long as the rainforest habitat of the Bellenden Ker Range is protected.  Much of this area lies within a national park (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Cairnsichthys bitaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Calabazas shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Calambe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and coastal reefs, in areas with mixed sand, rubble, and coral (Ref. 9710).  Occasionally in grassy areas.  Feed mainly on benthic  invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Calamopteryx jeb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species, found in rocky areas and reefs (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Calandre antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Regarded as the only truly pelagic fish in Antarctic waters (Ref. 6390).  Larvae and postlarvae occur between 0 to 135 m; juveniles 50 to 400 and adults below 400 m (Ref. 5179).  Postlarvae feed mainly on eggs and larvae of copepods; juveniles mainly on copepods, but take also eggs and larvae of euphausiids, polychaetes and chaetognaths (Ref. 5179).  Larger items are ingested with increase in size (Ref. 5179).  Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 28916).

species.name: Calandre fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton.  The storage of lipids in cells of adipose tissue as well as the reduced calcification of the skeleton provide buoyancy to this species.

species.name: Caledonian weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cali toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Calicagère blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, over turtle grass, sand or rocky bottom and around coral reefs (Ref. 3725). Young commonly found among floating Sargassum seaweeds (Ref. 3725). Feeds on plants, mainly on benthic algae, as well as on small crabs and mollusks (Ref. 6547, 44187). Also feeds on spinner dolphins’ feces and vomits at Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, southeast Atlantic. The offal feeding may be regarded as a simple behavioral shift from plankton feeding to drifting offal picking (Ref. 48727). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3725).

species.name: Calicagère bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in aggregations over hard, algal coated bottoms of exposed, surf-swept outer reef flats, lagoon and seaward reefs, to a depth of at least 24 m (Ref. 30573).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles associated with floating material (Ref. 58302).  Mainly herbivorous, feeding on seaweed and associated invertebrates (Ref. 30573).  Appear to be more commonly involved in hallucinogenic fish poisoning than most other related species (Ref. 4690).  Caught with other types of artisanal gear.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Calicagère bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612).  Can leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Also found near or over rocks and in kelp beds up to about 30 m depth.  Feed mainly on seaweed, occasionally takes invertebrates.  Form dense schools in spring in kelp beds.  Pelagic spawner (Ref. 56049).  Breathe air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Considered an important game fish and may incidentally be caught in commercial fishing activities (Ref. 9310).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9310).

species.name: Calicagère de Cortez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes seen in schools of K. analogus, also known to school and graze with Prionurus laticlavius. Stays close to shore in shallow waters. Feeds mainly on attached algae, occasionally ingests plankton and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Calicagère demi-lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often occur in rocky areas and in kelp beds.  Found from inshore areas to 40 m depth.  Feed on seaweed and small invertebrates.  Pelagic spawner (Ref. 56049).  Also caught with harpoons.  The flesh is of excellent quality and is marketed fresh (Ref. 9310).

species.name: Calicagère grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aggregate over hard, algal coated bottoms of exposed surf-swept outer reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 24 m. Found in exposed areas around rocky reefs (Ref. 559); adults usually close to the shore and the coastline, while juveniles are associated with flotsam and can be encountered in the open ocean close to the surface (Ref. 95491). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Usually in groups (Ref. 90102). Young (up to 5 cm) found among floating seaweed; feeding on small crustaceans (Ref. 559). Adults are carnivorous during summer and autumn but feed on Endarachne binghamiae during winter (Ref. 559). Good food fish (Ref. 559). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Calicagère jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, especially over rocky bottoms in coral reef areas; also among floating Sargassum weeds (Ref. 3725).  Feeds on algae including much Sargassum (Ref. 5521).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3725).

species.name: Calicagère mignonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow inshore areas to 8 m depth (Ref. 9310); coastal rocky reefs and reef flats with algal growth (Ref. 95491). Exclusively herbivorous (Ref. 95491). Encountered frequently in schools near Abudefduf troschelii. Pelagic spawner (Ref. 56049). Also caught with harpoons (Ref. 9310).

species.name: Calicagère oeil bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms big schools in shallow rocky areas that are rich in algae.  Feeds on algae and small invertebrates.

species.name: Calicagère saléma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs both as solitary individuals and in schools together with K. elegans and K. vaigiensis and are found close to the surface (< 25 m) on rocky shores, the open ocean and reefs on isolated islands (Ref. 95491). Also swim rapidly in small, somewhat polarized groups or schools in open water over deep reefs, along walls and drop-offs (Ref. 5227) or usually seen near floating logs far out to sea (Ref. 11482). This species differs from its congeners in having an omnivorous diet that includes zooplankton (Ref. 95491). Not common.

species.name: Calico rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on or near soft bottom (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae and pelagic juveniles (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Calico sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal rocky areas, most often in middle intertidal zone (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Calico surfperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur usually in sand beaches in surf (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: California clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal and shallow subtidal areas (Ref. 36496).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36496).  Eggs are attached under rocks and cobble and guarded by a parent (Ref. 36496).

species.name: California flashlightfish
species.description: Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: California headlightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Feed at night or in the morning (Ref. 9199), on euphausiids, copepods, and amphipods (Ref. 11712).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Lipid content is 15.8 % in fresh body weight while wax ester is present in trace amounts (Ref. 9197).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 28981.

species.name: California killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in bays and salt marshes near shore, may enter freshwater (Ref. 36572).  Often used in laboratories for environmental studies.  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Oviparous, with micro-nektonic larvae (Ref. 36572).  Single demersal eggs are attached to spawning substrate via small weakly adhesive filaments (Ref. 36572).

species.name: California roach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: California slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near or on bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feed on small crustaceans.  Regarded as inferior food because of its soft, fleshy texture (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with mesopelagic and bathypelagic larvae (Ref. 35724).

species.name: California smoothtongue
species.description: Abundant in midwater from near surface to 690 m (Ref. 2850).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604).

species.name: California worm blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits weedy areas along rocky shores.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Californian salema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among rocks and high up in kelp beds (Ref. 2850).  Usually in schools (Ref. 2850).  Primarily nocturnal feeders but occasionally forage during the day.  Although the species is a good foodfish, it is of limited interest due to its small size.

species.name: Callanthias japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy gravel or rock bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Callanthias parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 325 m (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Callanthias platei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callanthias splendens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callechelys bitaeniata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callechelys galapagensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callechelys leucoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand in shallow water from near shore to the beach.  The burrows may be uncovered by low tide (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Callechelys maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callechelys randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over sand at 35 m depth.

species.name: Calliclinus geniguttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on amphipods as juveniles and shifts to diet of decapods as adults (Ref. 94105).

species.name: Calliclinus nudiventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Callionyme bélène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms in shallow coastal waters.  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans.  Oviparous, eggs and larvae are pelagic.

species.name: Callionymus kanakorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms with few rubble or coralline gravel and sand (Ref. 78107).

species.name: Callochromis macrops
species.description: Adults occur over sand bottoms near rocks where they feed.  Form schools (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Callochromis melanostigma
species.description: Occurs over sand bottoms near rocks where they feed on invertebrates.  Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Callochromis pleurospilus
species.description: Occurs over sand bottoms near rocks where they feed on invertebrates.  Forms schools.  Bury themselves in the sand to evade predators (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Callogobius albipunctatus
species.description: Found under deeply accumulated coral rubble in 6 to 15 m depth (Ref. 124175).

species.name: Callogobius dori
species.description: Specimens collected from the base of coral patches on silty sand of a closed lagoon at depths of  5-7 m, with one collection reaching 21-27 m (Ref. 116311).

species.name: Callogobius dorsomaculatus
species.description: Found under deeply accumulated coral rubble in 6 to 15 m depth (Ref. 124175).

species.name: Callogobius snelliusi
species.description: Inhabits rocky shores and coral reefs in 3-15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Callogobius tanegasimae
species.description: Inhabits estuaries.  Associated with snapping shrimps.

species.name: Callopanchax monroviae
species.description: Occurs in swamps, swampy parts of brooks and pools in the humid coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  9 cm TL (7372).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Callopanchax sidibeorum
species.description: Habitat of type locality is depression with small water bodies, ditches and connected pools in a secondary forest adjacent to small creek; seems to prefer shaded areas (Ref. 84062). This species is an annual species with eggs with prolonged development of 2-9 month (Ref. 84062).

species.name: Callopanchax toddi
species.description: Occurs in shallow brooks and temporary swamps.  9 cm TL (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Calloplesiops argus
species.description: Secretive species (Ref. 27115).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Calypso tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear to slightly turbid standing water at low elevations and along the edges of swamps (Ref. 11225).  Occurs frequently in brackish waters (Ref. 11225).  Maximum length of aquarium specimen 4.0 TL (Ref. 12468).

species.name: Cambeva pascuali
species.description: Found in small stream with clear water and moderate water flow. Collected under rocks and aquatic vegetation in a muddy bottom bordered by riparian vegetation (Ref. 116172).

species.name: Cambeva ytororo
species.description: The species is collected from the waterfall areas of Tabay stream, Paraña River basin, Misiones, Argintina (Ref. 118111).

species.name: Cameroon goby
species.description: Sublittoral, collected at about 1 m on vertical rock face (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Cameroon killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, swampy parts of shallow brooks and small streams under dark forest cover on the inland plains rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cameroon lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rainforest brooks and swamps on the inland plains (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Caml grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Camotillo
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
