species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, rock-, mud-bottomed or detritus-bottomed pools and backwaters of lowland creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge, isopods, amphipods, mayfly and caddis larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Chat-fou du nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mixed sand and rock riffles and runs with debris in small to large, often swift rivers.  Forages at night, feeding largely on aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 55397).

species.name: Chat-fou liséré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of clear, fast creeks and small to medium rivers. Seek cover during the day and actively forage at night (Ref. 93252).

species.name: Chat-rochier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore and offshore shark found on the continental shelf over rough, even rocky or coralline ground, and algal-covered bottoms. Found at depths of 1 or 2 m to at least 125 m. Feed on bottom-living invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans and on demersal fishes (e.g. sharks, S. canicula). Oviparous (Ref. 50449). Utilized fresh and dried salted for human consumption, and processed into fishmeal. May attain 170 cm (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Chatham deep-water triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in shallow waters (12-80 m) then migrate into deeper waters as they mature (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Chaudhuria fusipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaudhuria ritvae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chauffet Acapulco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  Territorial herbivore, feed on farmed turf-algae within their territories  (Ref. 57615).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet ayanque
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs, below the surf zone (Ref. 9334).  Feed mainly on low-profile, attached algae (Ref. 28023).  Defend both feeding and reproductive territories by driving off other fishes and divers who come too close (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet beau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet Clarion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet de Baldwin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet de Cortez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet de Limbaugh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  They feed mainly on plankton (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet de nuit
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs exposed to wave action (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky coasts (Ref. 9334).  Feed on benthic algae and invertebrates (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet des îles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Adults are territorial and aggressive, vigorously driving off other fishes and certain invertebrates from their feeding and reproductive territories.  They graze on algae and invertebrates including tubeworms, small crustaceans, and the tentacles of anemones (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet Garibaldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottom in clear water, often near crevices and small caves, occasionally in kelp.  Adults defend a home territory.  Feed mainly on attached invertebrates.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Chauffet jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs exposed to wave action and currents.  Primarily herbivorous but occasionally takes a baited hook (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are deposited in crevices among the rocks in areas of strong current, usually in the lee of the current (Ref. 28023).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet main jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in current-swept seaward reefs; occasionally found around lagoon patch reefs.  Form aggregations that feed on zooplankton (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 9710. Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Chauffet queue blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 9334).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet queue blanche du sud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  Somewhat territorial, they chase away small intruders (Ref. 5227).  Omnivorous, they graze on algae and nibbles at small crustaceans and the tentacles of anemones (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauffet tono
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9334).  Usually in large aggregations.  These diurnal feeders feed on plankton at the surface or mid-water;  also graze on benthic invertebrates and algae on the reef.  Breed during early summer in the Gulf and continues throughout the summer until fall.  This fish is a warm-water, stenothermal species.  Juveniles of second year class have been observed cleaning schools of striped mullet, halfbeaks and needlefish (Ref. 5592).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chauliocheilos saxatilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a very small stream, about 1 m wide, up to 30 cm deep, with a bottom consisting of gravel, pebbles, sand and clay,  and besides trees and shrubs, with its margins composed of many specimens of <i>Hedychium sp. (Zingiberaceae).  This species was collected mostly in the bottom but also associated with vegetation at the margins.  Other fishes found in the same stream include <i>Astyanax fasciatus, <i>Rhamdia cf. quelen, <i>Rhamdiopsis sp., <i>Trichomycterus jequitinhonhae and <i>Trichomycterus sp.  Based on four specimens ranging from 4.10-4.75 cm SL, food items in the stomach were mainly fine particulate organic matter and periphyton (unicellular algae, diatoms, zooplankton and microcrustaceans) (Ref. 98819).

species.name: Chauliode de sloane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep oceanic waters to more than 1,000 m depth; may migrate to near-surface waters at night (Ref. 4759).  Up to depth of 1800 m (Ref. 47377).  Depth range 473-1192 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Meso- and bathypelagic from near the surface to 2800 m (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous (Ref. 5951).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4759); mainly on myctophids (Ref. 5951).  Lipid content is 2.4 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 7.2 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Chauliodus barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type specimen was taken from a depth between 2,071- 2,198 m (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Chauliodus dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chauliodus minimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected offshore in the Atlantic (Ref. 3981).

species.name: Chauliodus pammelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chauliodus schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 3588).

species.name: Chauliodus vasnetzovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunacops coloratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunacops roseus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunax abei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral to upper bathyal zone (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Chaunax apus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunax breviradius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunax flammeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunax latipunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chaunax umbrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  A poorly known species which is apparently represented only by a few  specimens collected from the Hawaiian Islands and the Emperor Seamount (Ref. 94130).

species.name: Chaves' lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic, found at 600-800 m during the day, mainly at 40-175 m during the night, but locally nyctoepipelagic at the surface (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Cheat minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and pools of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Checked goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, vegetated littoral habitats in floodplain pans, lakes and estuaries (Ref. 7248, 52193). It feeds on small crustaceans and insect larvae (Ref. 7248, 52193). Spawns in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Checked swallowtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary males were often seen in and near the coelacanth caves in 180-270 m.  Occurs in 70-300 m (Ref. 58472).

species.name: Checkerboard cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In forest creeks and sandy river shores, often near fallen leaves or among plants.  Young are all females; at about 8 months of age one female changes into a dominant male (Ref. 42575).

species.name: Checkered barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In creeks, rivers and lakes.  Feeds on worms, small crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Checkered blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and coral reefs, often inside tube sponges (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Checkered dottyback
species.description: Collected on reef slopes and reef surge channels (Ref. 81967). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Checkered goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rock and sand bottom (Ref. 11441).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Checkered madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and backwaters of clear small to medium rivers with moderate to high gradients.

species.name: Checkered pupfish
species.description: An egg laying omnivorous fish which prefers rocky-gravelly substratum with vegetation.  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=12, 28°C water temperature (Ref. 6398).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cheek-streaked goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on clear sandy bottoms with fast tidal currents.  Retreats in burrows made possibly by sea cucumbers or polychaetes (Ref. 30347).

species.name: Cheekbar wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet weedy bottoms.

species.name: Cheekscaled frill-goby
species.description: Benthic in rocks and coral of shallow waters (Ref. 58302). Also occurs in rocky pools of intertidal reef flats and exposed rocky shores in 0-2 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Cheekspot blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from a tide pool.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cheekspot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mudflats and shallow bays.  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  Males guard the eggs which are found attached to the walls of burrows (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Cheekspot wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common around patches of rubble or mixed rubble and coral along steep drop-offs (Ref. 1602) at 10-56 m depth (Ref. 90102). Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Cheekveil longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow water, often in less than 5 m depth on coral reef flats (Ref. 27772).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chefoo thryssa
species.description: Presumably marine, pelagic and schooling, but more data needed based on correct identifications.

species.name: Cheilinus abudjubbe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cheilodipterus nigrotaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently a Batesian mimic of the saber-toothed blenny Meiacanthus grammistes. Observed to swim in open water in a similar fashion as this blenny by using its tail to swim rather than the pectoral fins; but if approached, it quickly swims to the cover of reefs (Ref. 48635). Sexually mature between 6 to 6.5 cm. Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cheilodipterus octovittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheilodipterus pygmaios
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest female with mature gonad and large eggs measured about 3 cm.

species.name: Cheilodipterus subulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef lagoons.  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Cheilopogon doederleinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Cheilopogon japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheilopogon melanocercus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic, inhabiting surface waters.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and other planktonic animals.

species.name: Cheilopogon olgae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheilopogon pitcairnensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic surface waters.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Cheilopogon ventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheilotrema fasciatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirocerus abuelo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirocerus eques
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirocerus goeldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon australe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon galusdae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon ibicuhiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon jaguaribensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon kiliani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon luelingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon ortegai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon parahybae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodon pisciculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheirodontops geayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chela cachius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds, ditches and rivers in plains and submontane regions (Ref. 41236).  Breeds freely in ponds, tanks and small streams.  Utilized also as larvicidal fish (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Chela khujairokensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chela macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelaethiops congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelaethiops elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelaethiops minutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelidonichthys ischyrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelmon commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species found singly and in pairs along rocky shores and coral reefs; also in estuaries and silty inner reefs (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Territorial species (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Forms pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chelmon à très long bec
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A generally uncommon species that inhabits seaward reefs to depths greater than 60 m (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on whole organisms such as small crustaceans.  Usually seen in pairs.  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Forms pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Sometimes dark brown instead of yellow (Ref. 48636).  In the East Indian region this species is replaced by <i>F. wanai at Cenderawasih Bay (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Chelon caeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chelonodon bengalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chen's worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs over soft bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Adults apparently have a pelagic lifestyle (caught with many mesopelagic species in Taiwan) (Ref. 96531).

species.name: Chendol keelini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shady forest streams with clear water near the banks among the tree roots and leaf litter.

species.name: Chendol lubricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits black water streams under forest cover with quite swift current.

species.name: Chenille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 26346), large, sluggish, deepwater shark found on continental and insular shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Sometimes found in shallow water (Ref. 247).  Feeds on smaller sharks, bony fishes, and crabs (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 15-26 young in a litter (26346).  Never recorded as attacking people.  Sometimes hooked by shore anglers (Ref. 5578).  Processed into fishmeal.  May be used in traditional medicine in southern Africa (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Chereshnev’s horsefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cherokee darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cherry darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bedrock pools and rocky riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Cherry dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat information not available but probably frequents coral crevices and overhangs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cherry perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cherry seabream
species.description: This species is more likely to inhabit the somewhat shallower coastal waters around its area of occurrence than other Polysteganus which have been trawled deeper than 200 m (Ref. 106993).

species.name: Cherry snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest female with yolked eggs measured 10.5. cm SL; smallest male with enlarged, swollen testes 7.45 cm SL (Ref. 57077).

species.name: Cherryfin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and gravel-bottomed pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cherskii's char
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes (Ref. 26334, 593).

species.name: Cherskii's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cherskii's thicklip gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cherubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Normally occurs in rubble areas.  Feeds on various types of algae.  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Retreats into holes when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35408).

species.name: Chesapeake logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chessa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors large rivers, shoaling over both rock and sand; omnivorous, preferring algae and plant matter to snails, shrimps, and small fish; breeds in summer during the rainy period, moving upstream to suitable spawning sites (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Chessboard blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in crevices and on rubble to depths of at least 40 m (Ref. 13121).

species.name: Chessboard catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chessboard cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Chesterfield bigeye dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Chestnut eyelash-blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in wave-swept algal ridge (Porolithon ridge) of outer reef flats.  Usually found on rocky and coralline substrates at depths less than 10 m.  Usually seen in small loose groups spread over sections of reef (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Have  been collected as deep as 30 m in the Red Sea, 32 m at Rowley Shoals off Western Australia (Ref. 529).

species.name: Chestnut moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocky bottoms (Ref. 26340).  Also found in and around coral reefs.

species.name: Chestspot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chetia brevicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in quiet backwater (Ref. 52267).

species.name: Chetia mola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cheval de bois
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer clear water areas on coral reefs; juveniles have been taken from reef flats and in tide pools, adults found in deeper waters. Solitary and common in lightly fished areas (Ref. 37816). Adults from Oceania almost exclusively feed on fishes (holocentrids, mullid, and pomacentrid); and occasionally, crustaceans (Ref. 89707). Present in the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874. Occasionally ciguatoxic (Ref. 37816). Reports of sizes in excess of 80 cm total length for E. tauvina are probably based on misidentifications of E. coioides, E. malabaricus, and E. lanceolatus; these species grow much bigger than E. tauvina (Ref. 5222, Heemstra pers. comm. 09/04). .

species.name: Cheval de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass and algal beds (Ref. 52034). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cheval de mer (Hippocampus hippocampus)
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dense, complex habitats as well as patchy, relatively open and sparse habitats of coastal areas. Found on soft bottoms amongst rocks and algae (Ref. 6733), on sparsely vegetated areas, and in coastal lagoons with strong oceanic influences (Refs. 52034, 89230). Mimics the green or yellow coloration of plants allowing it to hide among the vegetation. This ability likely plays a role in seahorse feeding strategy and in predator avoidance (Ref. 52034). Makes limited daily movements within very restricted home ranges (0.7-18.1 m2) (Refs. 52034, 89256). May over-winter in deeper water. (Ref. 53712). Adult dispersal over large distances is probably caused by strong wave action during storms or when it anchors itself to floating debris (Ref. 52034).
Is thought to live for 3-5 years (Ref. 52034). Because of its short generation time and multiple breeding cycles during each spawning season, resilience is thought to be high. However, in tropical areas where seagrass beds are regularly exploited for other species of seahorses for the aquarium trade, traditional medicine, etc., populations have been quickly eradicated (Ref. 89253). Feeds on small prey and organic debris. Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35416).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Cheval du bois
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary adults inhabit coral rich areas and clear waters on lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref 90102). They feed mainly on fishes and probably on crustaceans. The distinctive blue and gold striped juveniles are mimics of the wrasse Halichoeres purpurescens (Ref. 39231) or dark damsels in surge zones (Ref. 48635). This allows the species to approach their preys. Often seen in markets but not plentiful enough to be of commercial importance. Caught with hook-and-line, spear, and probably in traps (Ref. 39231). Sold in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cheval marin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly referred to as Hippocampus ramulosus. Occurs mostly in shallow inshore waters including littoral lagoons (Ref. 9937) among algae and eel grass (Zostera or Posidonia), or among rocks and in gravel bottoms (Ref. 52034). Juveniles were observed to recruit to vegetated habitats at 8.8- 10.4 cm length (Ref. 79902). Adults (from 12.5 cm length) appear to maintain very restricted home ranges (19.9 ± 12.4 m2) over multiple years making limited daily movements. (Ref. 79902). May move to deeper waters during winter (Ref. 53712). Like other seahorse species, adult dispersals over large distances is probably caused by strong wave action and currents during storms or when it anchors itself to floating debris (Ref. 52034). Is thought to live for 4-7 years (Ref. 79902). Because of its early age at maturity, rapid growth rate, short generation time and multiple breeding cycles during each spawning season, resilience is thought to be high (Ref. 88171). However, in tropical areas where seagrass beds are regularly exploited for other species of seahorses for the aquarium trade, traditional medicine, etc., populations have been quickly eradicated (Ref. 89253). Can be maintained in an aquarium environment if trained to feed on dead animals (Ref. 88171). Length type OT refers to height (= TL - head length), Ref. 30915.

species.name: Cheval marin (Hippocampus spinosissimus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf, on muddy, sandy bottoms, rubbles and in coral reefs (Ref. 75154); in a sponge or seagrass habitat, often attached to hard and soft coral species (Ref. 128284).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Maximum length is based on a straight-line length measurement from upper surface (ignoring spines) of first trunk ring, to tip of tail; female 13.8 cm (Ref. 42735). Less desirable for traditional Chinese medicine, but use may increase with the rise in patent medicines. Taken in trawls (Ref. 42735).

species.name: Chevalier au nez pointu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on shrimps and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevalier au nez retroussé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on shrimps and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevalier bigle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow areas but not common in brackish waters with low salinity (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevalier blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud-bottomed to rock-bottomed pools and runs of small to large rivers.  Occasionally found in lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on immature midges, mayflies and caddisflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Chevalier cocodia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water but not common in estuaries with low salinities (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevalier cuivré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky pools, backwaters and swift runs of medium to large rivers.

species.name: Chevalier de Point Tuza
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water (Ref. 9118) (Also Ref. 55763).  Feeds mainly on shrimps and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevalier de rivière
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and swift runs of small to large rivers.  Also occurs in impoundments (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Locally common but disappearing from northern and western parts of range (Ref. 5723).  Adult feeds on small bivalve mollusks (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Chevalier jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy to rocky pools and runs of medium to large rivers, and also in lakes.  Spawning occurs along edges and midstream areas of riffles, on pebble, cobble, and gravel substrates (Ref. 49090).

species.name: Chevalier rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools, runs and riffles in small to large rivers.  Also occur in lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on benthic insect larvae; juveniles consume microcrustacea and midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Chevalier tacheté
species.description: Found usually in shallow coastal waters over sandy mud bottoms.  Feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling organisms.

species.name: Chevalier vermiculé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and muddy bottoms of shallow waters (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Chevron tang
species.description: An uncommon species that inhabits seaward rocky or coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles found in relatively deep coral rich areas (Ref. 42056).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on film algae (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Chi wriggler
species.description: A benthic, inshore species found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Chiangmai stream goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on insect larvae, small fishes and shrimps (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Chiapaheros grammodes
species.description: Inhabits lower river to middle river valleys as well as lake.  Prefers moderate flowing streams and large rivers with strong currents which are clear, clean and high in oxygen content.  Can be found over rocks, sand, silt, or mud.  Occurs in most all the habitats available within its small territorial boundaries.

species.name: Chiapas catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep river channels and pools with rocks and strong eddy currents. sometimes taken in stream mouths; collected in both high and low water seasons, and generally during the night.  Food include fishes, crabs, prawns, and large and tough seeds (Ref. 54757).

species.name: Chiapas cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits faster flowing water of the middle and upper reaches of rivers.  Maximum length 14 cm SL (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Chiapas killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Chiapas swordtail
species.description: Found in fast flowing river.

species.name: Chiasmodon asper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the mesopelagic to bathypelagic zones; where juveniles are known from 180-450 m, while adults are found at greater depths, 5154-5691 m (mean 5423 m) (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chiasmodon braueri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the mesopelagic to bathypelagic zones (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chiasmodon harteli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the mesopelagic to bathypelagic zones (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chiasmodon microcephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the meso- to bathypelagic zones (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chiasmodon pluriradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the meso- to bathypelagic zones, with adults more frequently collected below 900 m (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chiasmodon subniger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the mesopelagic to bathypelagic zones (Ref. 82429).

species.name: Chickasaw darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams (Ref. 52025).

species.name: Chicken grunt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cultured and released for fishery in Japan.  The species prefers relative warm water, high salinity, and rocky shores.  The species does seasonal offshore-inshore migrations in limited areas (Ref. 34104).

species.name: Chien corail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common but little-known inshore shark found on coral reefs and though to inhabit crevices and holes on reefs (Ref. 11146).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught occasionally by various fisheries operating over coral reefs and probably adversely affected by dynamite fishing (Ref.58048). Utilized fresh and dried-salted for food or processed for fishmeal and oil (Ref. 244).

species.name: Chien de mer
species.description: A common littoral shark found inshore from the surf zone and in shallow bays to at least 191 m on the outer continental shelves (Ref. 13568).  Often on or near the bottom but also occurs in midwater or at the surface (Ref. 247).  Only shark known to gulp and store air in its stomach to maintain neutral buoyancy while swimming (Ref. 13568).  Found singly or in small to large schools (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bony fishes, small sharks, rays, squids, crabs, and lobsters (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous, embryos feeding on yolk sac and other ova produced by the mother as well as other siblings in the womb (uterine cannibalism) (Ref. 50449).  Usually gives birth to 2 pups after a 9-12 months gestation period (Ref.58048). A migratory species in parts of its range, particularly in its northern and southern extremities where pronounced poleward migration occur in the summer and equatorial movements in autumn and winter (Ref. 247).  Usually inoffensive and not aggressive when not provoked (Ref. 247) but has known to bite swimmers and be aggressive towards divers with speared fish (Ref. 6586).  Utilized for fresh, frozen, smoked and dried for human consumption (Ref. 247); also for fishmeal, liver oil, fins, and hides for leather (Ref. 13568).  Flesh highly appreciated in Japan (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Chien de mer (Heptranchias perlo)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental and insular shelves and upper slopes in depths of 100 to 400 (Ref. 13573, 11230), also inshore and down to 1,000 m (Ref. 6871, 11230).  Feeds on small  sharks and rays, small bony fish, shrimps, crabs, lobsters, squid, and cuttlefish (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 9-12 young born per litter (Ref. 247).  Very active and aggressive when captured and quick to bite but too small to be very dangerous to people (Ref. 247).  Liver utilized as a source of oil.  Maximum length may reach 214 cm, but this is uncertain.

species.name: Chien de mer (Mustelus mustelus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves and uppermost slopes, from the intertidal region to at least 350 m depth (Ref. 244). Collected to depth of 624 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Sometimes in midwater but prefers to swim near the bottom (Ref. 244).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, but also cephalopods and bony fishes (Ref. 244).  Viviparous, with a yolk-sac placenta (Ref. 244).  Taken by shore and ski-boat anglers (Ref. 5578).  Utilized for human consumption, oil, and fishmeal (Ref. 244).  Sexual maturity is reached at a length of 70-80 cm (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Chien de mer (Rhizoprionodon terraenovae)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches at least 103 cm TL (Ref. 244).  Abundant in the continental shelves, from the intertidal to deeper waters.  Often occurs close to the surf zone off sandy beaches, and also enclosed bays, sounds, and harbors, in estuaries and river mouths.  Feeds on small bony fishes, shrimps, crabs, segmented worms and mollusks (gastropod feet).  Viviparous, with 1 to 7 young in a litter (Ref.  27549).  Size at birth about 29 to 37 cm.  Utilized for human consumption. Minimum depth from Ref. 055195.

species.name: Chien de mer gris et roux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental and insular shelves and upper slopes, ranging from shallow inshore waters and the intertidal to 200 m, occasionally down to 579 m (Ref. 244). Occasionally found in freshwater. It is doubtful that this species can live in fresh water for an extended period of time (Ref. 244). Active swimmer and bottom feeder (Ref. 27549). Swims in packs or schools (Ref. 27549). Feeds on large crustaceans, mainly crabs, but also heavily on lobsters (Homarus) (Ref. 244). Probably non-territorial. Off the Atlantic coast of the USA, this species is migratory (Ref. 244). Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with 4 to 20 young in a litter. Longevity given as 7 years (Ref. 775) but appears too low. Utilized fresh, dried-salted, and smoked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Chien de mer roux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, especially abundant off river mouths on muddy bottoms.  Salinity:  35-36 ppt.  Oxygen:  3-4 ppm.  Feeds on small bottom and littoral organisms like crustaceans, bony fishes, octopi and sponges.  Viviparous (Ref. 50449), with 7 young in a litter (Ref. 244).  Dental sexual dimorphism is manifested by males having greatly enlarged anterior teeth.  Utilized fresh, smoked or dried salted for human consumption, skin for leather.

species.name: Chien espagnol
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outermost shelf and upper slope.  Feeds mainly on small bony fish, including lanternfish, hakes, grenadiers, rockfish and lightfish, also squid and crustaceans.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Tolerates bottom with low oxygen levels (Ref. 5578).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 244).

species.name: Chien gecko
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known, but very common shark, found in deep water near the bottom (Ref. 11146).  Maximum length of at least 40 cm TL, probably reaching 50 cm (Ref. 11146).

species.name: Chien islandais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slopes.

species.name: Chien lime
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known bottom-dwelling shark found on the continental shelves (Ref. 11146).  Possibly at depths greater than 90 m (Ref. 244).

species.name: Chien marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known inshore catshark found on sandy and rocky bottom (Ref. 11146).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Hatching length around 10 cm (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Chien nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known bottom-dwelling shark found on continental slopes (Ref. 244).  One of the smallest sharks (Ref. 244).

species.name: Chien planeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with possibly a single egg laid per oviduct.

species.name: Chien poivré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly oviparous (Ref. 244).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Chien priape
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chien tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf, from close inshore to offshore.  Oviparous (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Chien tasmanien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widespread on the continental shelf and slope edge (Ref. 244).  Oviparous, with a single egg-case to each oviduct at a time (Ref. 244).

species.name: Chien à queue rude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental and insular slopes.  Feeds on deepwater shrimps.  There is partial segregation by depth.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Chien à taches noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal habitats and offshore reefs (Ref. 6871).  Nocturnal (Ref. 6871).  Probably oviparous (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Chien égoine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known but common Australian catshark found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, presumably on or near the bottom (Ref. 11146, 75154).  Feeds mainly on fish, crustaceans, and cephalopods (Ref. 6871).  Appears to aggregate by sex (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Chien étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chignahuapan silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chihuahua chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing pools of creeks and small rivers, usually near brush or other cover (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Chihuahua darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only darter to occur naturally in the Pacific drainage.

species.name: Chihuahua mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chihuahua shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy, rocky pools and runs of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Chilatherina alleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilatherina pricei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in the main channel of Reifafeif River, over rocks or boulders.  Forms midwater aggregations to feed on algae and small invertebrates, mainly insects (Ref. 26386).

species.name: Chilean eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Chilean grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is nowhere found in great abundance.

species.name: Chilean roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilean round stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilean sandpaperfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilean worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in shallow waters, on sand and debris between rocks and crevices (Ref. 89357, 104540).

species.name: Chilka lake's snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilo trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilobrycon deuterodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilochromis duponti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds primarily on aquatic vegetation (mostly algae) but also minor quantities of small insects; typical substratum spawner; aggressive species in captivity (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Chiloconger philippinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chilodus fritillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons over soft bottom with abundant debris and sand overlying a solid clay bottom.

species.name: Chilodus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chiloglanis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Maximum total length reported is 5.5 cm (Ref. 3202).

species.name: Chiloglanis angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis asymetricaudalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs rocky or sandy-rocky substrates of rivers with rapidly flowing waters; feeds on algae which grow on rocks in the river and cascades; is probably also an insectivore since some specimens which were examined showed the presence of insect larvae in their stomachs (Ref. 27627). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis batesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Maximum total length 47 mm (Ref. 3202).

species.name: Chiloglanis benuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis camarabounyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in large numbers in a medium stream with large areas of exposed bedrock (Ref. 116018).

species.name: Chiloglanis carnatus
species.description: TThe species was collected from Mukwadzi River, a perennial river that originates from wetlands (dambos) on the eastern side of the Great Dyke. This river flows in a north-western direction cutting through the Great Dyke before it joins the Manyame River. The substratum at the sites was composed of bedrock, cobbles and gravel, and the riparian vegetation was mainly Syzygium Gaertner, 1788 and Phragmites Adanson, 1763. It co-occurred with native fish species that include Labeo cylindricus Peters, 1852, Opsaridium zambezense (Peters, 1852), Enteromius trimaculatus (Peters, 1852), Tilapia sparrmanii Smith, 1840, Clarias gariepinus (Burchell, 1822), and Labeobarbus marequensis (Smith, 1841) as well as the non-native species Serranochromis jallae (Boulenger, 1896) and Micropterus salmoides (Lacepède, 1802) (Ref. 130906).

species.name: Chiloglanis carnosus

species.name: Chiloglanis longibarbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a medium-sized river with moderate canopy coverage; the substrate mostly sand, except for two rocky runs created by a bridge structure (Ref. 116018).

species.name: Chiloglanis lufirae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis lukugae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores of lake and rapid stony stretches of streams (Ref. 4967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chiloglanis microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis modjensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found where the Rio Mongo was shallow, substrate mostly sand and gravel, and there was little flow (Ref. 120898).

species.name: Chiloglanis niger

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Maximum size 6.2cm TL (Ref. 3202).

species.name: Chiloglanis orthodontus

species.name: Chiloglanis pezoldi

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis polypogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis productus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an affluent of Lake Tanganyika, a clear, fast-flowing stream with boulders, gravel and sand as substrate (Ref. 57468).

species.name: Chiloglanis reticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast-flowing streams (Ref. 27627). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis sardinhai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis voltae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chiloglanis waterloti

species.name: Chilomycterus spinosus

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).
