species.name: Chrysiptera albata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sand and rubble bottoms of steep outer slopes.  Numerous individuals in loose aggregations observed in gullies that dissected the steep slope.  Invariably sighted to stay close to the bottom, quickly retreating into holes among the rubble when approached closely,  The largest individual that was observed was estimated to be about 35 cm SL (Ref. 53986).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980).

species.name: Chrysiptera chrysocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A moderately territorial species mostly found between 0.5-10 m depths in relatively protected areas; either inside the lagoon or within galleys on the exposed outside edge of the reef (Ref. 79841).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chrysobrycon eliasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chrysobrycon hesperus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chrysobrycon myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chrysobrycon yoliae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a white-water drainage characterized by average width of 3 m and depth between 0.3 and 1.6 m (very narrow shore), beige water color, rather clear and showing at least 20 cm of transparency and riverine vegetation.  Collected from shallow areas with vegetation, rfiles or rapids along 250 m (Ref. 96866).

species.name: Chu's croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters.  A schooling, seasonal, migratory species living off sea-bed.  Feeds mainly on invertebrates.

species.name: Chuanchia labiosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits river valleys and plateau lakes at an altitude from 3,000 to 4,300 meters above sea level.  Favors slow current and surface level of clear and cold main streams (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Chub shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sand and gravel runs of small to large rivers.  Tolerates turbidity (Ref. 5723).  Invertivore and piscivore (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Chubby clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal waters (Ref. 4489).

species.name: Chubby livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chubby pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species (Ref. 35929).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35929).

species.name: Chubbyhead barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers cooler waters (Ref. 52193), occurring in small groups and shoals, in various habitats from small streams to large rivers and lakes (Ref. 52193). Frequently associates with cover or shelter such as fallen logs, brushwood or marginal vegetation (Ref. 52193). It feeds on insects, zooplankton, seeds, green algae and diatoms.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Breeds during summer when rivers are swollen after rain and lays adhesive eggs amongst vegetation.  Is preyed upon by larger fishes and birds (Ref. 7248 & 5214).

species.name: Chubsucker minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chucky madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chukot char
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Chumbe sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Churchill
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow and muddy waters, sheltered bays, in lagoons, and swampy areas; prefers quiet parts of rivers where there is abundant vegetation (Ref. 13337). Forms shoals (Ref. 13337) within quiet reaches of rivers and floodplains, and with other species with identical electric organ discharge (EOD) waveforms (Ref. 10460). Feeds  on insects, found on river bed or in marginal vegetation (Ref. 12526), on insect larvae and other invertebrates at night (Ref. 5595). Known to undergo upriver migration (Ref. 13337, 10608) which may well be correlated with breeding (Ref. 13337). Breeds during the rainy season, possibly moving upstream to suitable sites (Ref. 10608). An unconfirmed report claims the males are territorial and build a nest (Ref. 7248). Caught in nets for food (5214). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Châtillon
species.description: Espèce de lamproies. In fresh waters, in rivers, brooks, and lakes. Anadromous, but some populations are permanent freshwater residents (e.g. Lough Neagh, Northern Ireland (UK); Loch Lomond, Scotland (UK); lakes Ladoga and Onega, Russian Federation) (Ref. 89241). Amphihaline species (Ref. 51442). Metamorphosis takes place at a length of about 13 cm and they migrate to the sea (Ref. 51442). Most river lampreys live 4-7 years and reach 30-35 cm length (Ref. 88187). Females grow larger than males (Ref. 58137). Adults spend 1-2 years at sea, often along the coast or in estuaries (Ref. 59043). They live on hard bottoms or attached to larger fish like cod and herring (Ref. 88174). Adults are parasitic, feeding on fishes by sucking their blood and afterwards consuming the flesh (Ref. 1998). Adults predatory on marine fishes from the end of July to October. Trematodes and cestodes have been found in the intestine of prespawning adults at sea. (Ref. 89241). In autumn, adults commonly undergo reproductive migration from the sea to shallow middle or upper reaches of rivers and streams with strong currents (1.0-2.0 m/s in British rivers) and gravel bottoms (Ref. 51442, 59043, 88171). Spawning migration upriver (Vistula and Neman rivers) begins near the end of September in the Baltic Sea Basin. In tributaries to the Gulf of Finland (Narva, Neva, and Luga rivers), upstream spawning migrations occur twice yearly; once in summer-fall and once in spring. In the upper Rhine River, the spawning season is February to April; in England (UK) from April to May; and in the lower Neva River, Russian Federation, from early June to early July (Ref. 89241). During reproductive migration and reproduction, adults do not feed but instead utilize their lipid reserves (Ref. 30578) and are known to undergo a considerable shortening of up to 27 per cent (Ref. 83507). Fecundity is highly variable and ranges from 650 to 42,500 eggs/female; 10,000-16,000 eggs/female in Lake Ladoga. Communal spawning in the same redd by L. fluviatilis and L. planeri has been reported in the River Tywi Basin, Wales (UK), in April, at a water temperature of 11 °C. Both species participated in constructing a redd about 23 cm in diameter and 5-8 cm deep, consisting of pebbles, gravel and coarse sand (Ref. 89241). Spawning takes place in pre-excavated pits in river beds, its depth between 50-100 cm; after spawning the adults die (Ref. 51442). The blind ammocoetes are filter feeders of detritus and microorganisms; they live mostly buried in sand, silt or clay sediments for up to 4.5 years, often at the edges of rivers and streams where currents are slow (Ref. 51442, 59043, 88184, 88185). Sometimes they are found in substrates with submerged vegetation and plant debris (Ref. 12285). Ammocoetes may tolerate low oxygen levels but when burrows reach near anoxic levels, the larvae need to emerge from the substrate in order to survive (Ref. 88184). Fisheries exist in England (UK), Finland, France, and the Russian Federation. In the 19th century, up to 450,000 adults yearly were used by the English fishing fleet as bait in the fisheries for Gadus morhua and Psetta maxima. In Finland, the catch in 1983 was 2.3-2.4 million individuals (about 100 t) for a value of $800,000 US. There are reports of intoxication through eating this species (Halstead 1967). The mucus and serum are poisonous and the flesh must be thoroughly washed and all the blood removed before consumption (Ref. 5504). Cooking method involves de-sliming, removal of heads and branchial regions, the rest of the body covered in sunflower flour, and cooked in sunflower oil (Ref.89241). Utilized fresh and smoked; eaten fried (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Chèvre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in soft bottom areas of the continental shelf and upper slope.  They feed on both benthic and pelagic organisms (crustaceans, fishes, cephalopods, and echinoderms) (Ref. 4570). The reproductive mode is a zygoparous form of oviparity, intermediate between oviparity and viviparity (Ref. 36265, 79712).  Larvae and juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 4570).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).  Sold fresh (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Chèvre (Sebastes norvegicus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found off the coast from 100-1000 m; juveniles found in fjords, bays and inshore waters.  Normally trawled in deep water (Ref. 9988).  Benthic (Ref. 5951).  Feed mostly on euphausiids in summer; herrings in autumn and winter; capelins, herrings, euphausiids and ctenophores in spring.  Gregarious throughout life.  A slow growing species (Ref. 9988).  Ovoviviparous, gonads of male and female do not mature at the same time.  The spermatozoa are kept in the ovary of the female after copulation until such time that the eggs ripen paving the way for fertilization (Ref. 74488). Copulation takes place in late summer or early autumn (Ref. 35388, 34817); in winter females give birth to 50,000-350,000 pelagic larvae of 8 mm length (Ref. 35388).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Chèvre de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 27000).  Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms of estuaries (Ref. 2683).  Feeds mainly on benthic and planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 3612).

species.name: Chèvre de mer noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy or muddy bottoms in coastal waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Chétodon citron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow exposed reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs; in relatively open areas with scattered corals and occasionally at depth of 36 m (Ref. 205). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). May be solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Usually in pairs. Juveniles often in small aggregations and commonly mix with other similar sized juveniles, especially C. kleinii. Feed on small worms, small benthic invertebrates, coral polyps, and filamentous algae. Oviparous. Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Chétodon de Bennett
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in lagoon and seaward reefs in areas with rich coral growth (Ref. 1602). Juveniles may be found in shallow Acropora thickets (Ref. 1602). Adults occur in pairs (Ref. 1602, 48636). Omnivorous. Feed on coral polyps (Ref. 37816). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). This species is extremely difficult to maintain in an aquarium and is very rarely imported.

species.name: Chétodon de klein
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in deeper lagoons and channels, and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Depth 2-61 m, usually below 10 m (Ref. 90102). Occur singly or in pairs (Ref. 37816). Common, omnivorous individuals that feed mainly on soft coral polyps (mainly on Sarcophyton tracheliophorum and Litophyton viridis), algae and zooplankton. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon de Meyer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coral rich areas of clear lagoon and seaward reefs, and feed exclusively on coral polyps (Ref. 9710).  Juvenile usually solitary among branching corals, adults usually paired and home-ranging (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon faucille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the reef edge and upper slope. Usually in current-prone habitats; juveniles secretive in corals (Ref. 48636). Generally seen in pairs or in small aggregations (Ref. 4858). Feed mainly on invertebrates (Ref. 6113). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). Indian Ocean species counterpart of sibling Chaetodon ulietensis which is found in western and central Pacific (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Chétodon moucheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Occur in pairs or small groups (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Feed on polychaetes, coral polyps, and algae (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in small groups in reef flats, clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on soft and hard corals, also on polychaetes, small crustaceans, and filamentous algae.  In Indonesia, usually seen at moderate depths, usually swimming in small groups.  Adults are mainly in depth 20-60 m (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in lagoon and seaward reefs, usually in pairs in coral rich areas (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed mainly on coral polyps and anemones, but also on small invertebrates and algae (Ref. 1602).  Largest species in the genus (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à chevrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Closely associated with Acropora corals, particularly the staghorn variety. Territorial and in pairs (Ref. 9710). Juveniles solitary among coral branches (Ref. 48636). Feed mainly on coral polyps and therefore does not adjust easily to aquarium conditions. Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à collier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coral reefs in pairs or several aggregations.  Juveniles in estuaries (Ref. 48636).    Commonly exported to Europe and America, but quite difficult to acclimate to aquarium conditions.  Feed on coral polyps.  Usually found on reef edge and upper slope (Ref. 6113).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à croissant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species that is usually in pairs or small groups in shallow reef flats of lagoon and seaward reefs to depths of over 30 m.  Juvenile occurs among rocks of inner reef flats and in tide pools (Ref. 205).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Adult feeds mainly on nudibranchs, tubeworm tentacles, and other benthic invertebrates, also feeds on algae and coral polyps.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Forms pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à damiers
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer reef habitats.  Adults usually occurs in pairs (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed mainly on polyps of Acropora corals in lagoons and outer reefs. Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). Clean parasites from other fishes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Chétodon à dos noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary or in pairs in coral-rich areas of reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs to a depth of over 15 m.  Juveniles inshore.  In pairs or traveling in small groups (Ref. 48636).  Feed on octocorallian and scleractinian coral polyps.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Easy to maintain in the aquarium.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Chétodon à mitre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not much is known of this deep-dwelling butterfly, but recent observations indicate that it can form small groups of up to 5 individuals and inhabits steep outer reef drop-offs in rubble areas or among growths of black coral and sea fans.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à nageoires rouge orange
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coral-rich lagoons and semi-protected seaward reefs. Territorial and aggressive to other Chaetodon. Small juveniles secretive in corals (Ref. 48636). Swim in pairs. Feed exclusively on coral polyps, particularly of the Pocillopora type (Ref. 5503, 48636). Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Chétodon à tete jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hybrids with C. ephippium known. Usually solitary (Ref. 48636), but may form loose shoals of 5-6 individuals and usually found around isolated coral heads. Territorial and aggressive to other chaetodonts; omnivorous (Ref. 5503). Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cicerelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shell-gravel and coarse sand bottoms (Ref. 6450).  Minimum depth from Ref. 122877.

species.name: Cicerelle (Gymnammodytes semisquamatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically offshore over shell-gravel, also inshore where shell-gravel beaches occur.  Feed on plankton.  Summer batch spawner (Ref. 4674).  By-catch in sand eel fisheries (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Cicerello du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, mainly on sandy bottoms (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Cichla intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often captured near submerged rocks or woody structure in the primary river channel within or near swift current.  Diurnal piscivore.  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 27531).

species.name: Cichla jariina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla kelberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla melaniae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from Balneário do Pedral were in shallow water, pH 6.5, less than 1 dGH, and temperature 30- 32°C, in strong current among lava rocks (Ref. 57716).

species.name: Cichla mirianae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla monoculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected were from flood prone areas, but in the Amazon the biotopes are more varied.  This fish forays along the shore where small fishes may be concentrated.  Juveniles feed on shrimps, while adults are almost exclusively piscivore.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Males are sexually mature after one year while females mature after two years.  During reproduction which is not markedly seasonal, large males develop a frontal hump and become territorial (Ref. 35237).  Maximum length 80 cm TL (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Cichla nigromaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla orinocensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).  Is usually captured in shallow near-shore areas of lagoons and slow moving reaches of the river channel.  Feeds mainly on small characiform fish (Ref. 26329, 27531).

species.name: Cichla pinima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla piquiti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla pleiozona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla thyrorus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichla vazzoleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma araguaiense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma bartoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs sympatrically with C. labridens. Inhabits rivers and lagoons. Feeds on other smaller fishes, aquatic insects, algae and other invertebrates. Omnivore, egg layer, needs plant and rock cover, not easy to raise in tanks (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Cichlasoma boliviense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow clayey portion of the shore and from shallow pools with muddy water.

species.name: Cichlasoma dimerus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma geddesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma orientale
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma orinocense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma paranaense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma portalegrense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma pusillum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlasoma sanctifranciscense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Cichlasoma zarskei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cichlid
species.description: Less rheophilic and a more active swimmer than Steatocranus species (Ref. 52307). Maximum TL was recorded at 13.4 cm (Ref. 5696).

species.name: Cichlidé du Texas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and runs of small to large rivers; prefers warm water and vegetation.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Cichlidé nain de Gosse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length is 7.0 cm TL (Ref. 12251).  Males are generally larger than females (60 cm vs. 40 cm) and have more filamentous fins and deeper coloration during reproduction (Ref. 12251).  Females take care of the spawned eggs and the juveniles (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Cichlidé ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been caught, sporadically, in lentic environment such as zones of flooded grounds, as well as estuaries where the tidal current is notable, along the banks with thick riverine vegetation.  Omnivorous but mainly frugivorous (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Cichlidé à bande
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidés. Adults inhabit flowing water from small creeks and streams to the shallows of large and fast flowing rivers (Ref. 7335).  Prefer rocky habitats and finds sanctuary in the various cracks and crevices provided by this type of environment (Ref. 7335), or among roots and debris (Ref. 44091).  They occur in warm pools of springs and their effluents (Ref. 7020).  Feed on worms, crustaceans, insects, fish and plant matter (Refs. 7020; 44091).  Also used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537).  Approximately 100-150 eggs are deposited and are vigorously guarded and cared for by both male and female (Ref. 44091).  A popular aquarium fish which requires high temperature to maintain itself in an environment, e.g. artificially heated waters of power stations.  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Cichlidé à deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal swamps and flooded grounds (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Cichlidé à deux taches (Cichlasoma bimaculatum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in canals and swamps (Ref. 7020).  Tolerates low oxygen.  Feeds on crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Males are bigger than females which become mature at 7 to 9 cm (20-25 g).  Spawning occurs at the start of the rainy season.  About 700 eggs are spawned on open substrate and are cared for by the parents.  Max length 35 cm TL (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Cichlidé à deux taches (Rubricatochromis bimaculatus)
species.description: Occurs in mud-bottomed and sand-bottomed canals (Ref. 5723); some distance inland from the coast, associated with areas of intact or recently disturbed forest cover.  Considered the true 'jewel fish' of aquarists, this species is also used as an experimental animal by physiologists and ethologists (Ref. 5644).  Attains a maximum of 12 cm in captivity.  Aquarium keeping:  aggressive; in pairs; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Cichlidé à grands yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a small creek, quite sunny, with amber-colored water, slow current, muddy substrate and approximately 1 m in depth. Solitary. Feeds on shrimps, insect larvae of Odonata, Coleoptera and Hemiptera, as well as on fishes like cyprinodonts, characids. Males are bigger than females. Reproduction occurs during the rainy season. Found together with Pterophyllum scalare, Heros efasciatus, Hypselecara temporalis, and Mesonauta guyanae (Ref. 35237). Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Cichlidé à tête d'or
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and stagnant waters of forest creeks where it finds shelter in very shallow zones along the banks with little sunlight.  Females are almost two times smaller than males (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Cichlidé à œil d'or
species.description: Espèce de poissons tropical. Frequently occurs in flooded savannas of the coastal zone (Ref. 27188).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Quite popular among aquarists who breed it without difficulty.  Males are larger and more colorful, possessing more distinctly more elongated unpaired fins (Ref. 35237).  Aquarium keeping:  several females for one male; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Cichlidé émeraude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In slow flowing, turbid waters (Ref. 40602).  Maximum length 30 cm TL (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Cihanbeyli gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ciliata tchangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ciliate cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water to depth of about 5 meters (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Cilida toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cinder cloudy catshark
species.description: The size of males ranged from 29.4-41.6 cm TL (n = 6) and females from 30.1-38.6 cm TL (n = 22); size at first maturity is not precisely defined, but males had well-developed claspers at 34.6 cm TL and females had egg cases at 34.2 cm TL. Reproduction is by single oviparity, one egg case for each oviduct. The egg cases are amber in color, with tendrils and surface irregularities that resemble wrinkles. Maximum case length without tendrils (ML) was 44.6–56.25 mm, and maximum case width was 19.45–22.5 mm (33.4–42.1 %ML) (n = 7). Stomachs contents have small crustaceans, small bony fishes, and polychaets (Ref. 125694),

species.name: Cinnamon Killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks under forest cover on soils of the basement complex and volcanic soils.  6 cm TL  (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cinnamon skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cinta Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species typically occurs on brightly illuminated surfaces of either living Colpophyllia natans or algae encrusted covered coral remnants in shallow waters (3-8 m depth). Most specimens were observed not to move before an extremely close approach and once disturbed, individuals would move rapidly a short distance (less than 50 cm) across the substrate, before returning again to a stationary position. After repeated disturbances, these individuals would retreat into the cover of small holes, crevices or the underside of eroded corals. No feeding, cleaning and reproductive behaviors were observed (Ref. 58341).

species.name: Circle-cheek wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in coastal, very shallow and usually algae-rocky coastal reefs (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Circled dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on seaward reefs of Guam and Tinian, to a depth of 8 m (Ref. 1602).  Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms 2-35 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Circular cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species seldom observed by divers, but are collected with ichthyocides, dredges and sleds. Its collection data suggests that it frequents 10-40 m depth zone, in association with beds of a calcareous algae, Halimeda or calcareous rubble, sometimes mixed with the pocilloporid coral Seriatopora hystrix (Ref. 77037).

species.name: Circular seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Circular stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore areas as well as offshore reefs, on rocky bottoms or in areas with kelp.

species.name: Circumspect goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish waters of tidal creeks and river mouths, usually among mangroves.  Penetrates the lower reaches of freshwater streams within about 10 kilometers of the sea.  Rests on mud, sand or gravel bottoms (Ref. 44894).  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Circé à branchies longues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually near coasts (Ref. 12204).  Oviparous, with large mesopelagic larvae (Ref. 35760).

species.name: Cirrhilabrus katoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observations at Kashiwa-jima Island and in adjacent waters showed the species to form aggregations comprising one or two males and several females, pairs, or solitary to several females. In some cases, single male appeared to maintain harems of several females. This species often forms aggregations with Cirrhilabrus cyanopleura, C. lunatus, C. rubrimarginatus and C. temminckii, over rocky substrata (Ref. 36346).

species.name: Cirrhilabrus lunatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at depths ranging from 32 to 45 m on dead coral and rubble substratum.

species.name: Cirrhilabrus rubrisquamis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhilabrus ryukyuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhilabrus sanguineus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena cheilopogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena chinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena oliveri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena playfairii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic but sometimes seen swimming at surface (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Cirrhimuraena tapeinoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhimuraena yuanding
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhinus inornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhinus jullieni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits midwater to bottom depths of rivers, occurring in the main stem and on the floodplains, including freshwater areas that undergo tidal fluctuation.  Feeds on algae, detritus and occasionally benthic invertebrates.  Often marketed fresh and used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cirrhinus mrigala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549)..

species.name: Cirrhinus rubirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers.

species.name: Cirrhitichthys bleekeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhitichthys randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhitops hubbardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water carnivore occurring around rocky and coral reefs.

species.name: Cirrhitops mascarenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirrhitus albopunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirricaecula johnsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens collected from the surge-washed sand patch at Rongerik Atoll (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Cirricaecula macdowelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cirripectes jenningsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coral reefs (Ref. 529).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cirripectes kuwamurai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a moderately exposed rocky reef about 3 m deep  (Ref. 635).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cirripectes polyzona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in algal ridge and ridge crests between surge channels of exposed seaward reefs to a depth of about 3 m (Ref. 205, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on algae and associated minute invertebrates like forams, ostracods, and gastropods. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cirripectes randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on coral patches in surge channels of rocky reefs with light surf, 0-8 m deep (Ref. 529).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ciscaucasian spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on gravel substrate along steep banks of rivulets and streams 3-10 m wide and less than 1 m deep in foothills and plains, sometimes in channels (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cisco
species.description: Occurs in near-shore coastal waters, open water of lakes and small to large rivers, and often in current in rivers. Belongs to C. clupeaformis complex (Ref. 5723). Anadromous (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Cisco arctique
species.description: Occurs in brackish waters (20-22 ppt) of coastal lagoons and mouths of rivers and bays (Ref. 4779). Mostly in larger lowland rivers (Ref. 59043). Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426). Feeds on small crustaceans, insects, small fishes (Ref. 28219, 28857), worms and clams (Ref. 58426). At sea, feeds on larger crustaceans and small fish (Ref. 59043).  No feeding occurs during the upstream migration (Ref. 4779).  Lives 10 -12 years, rarely up to 20 (Ref. 59043). Enters rivers in shoals to spawn (Ref. 4779). Spends 6-8 years at sea before maturing and returning to rivers in June - July, to spawn in September - October of same year. A second run in autumn; those fishes remain a year in rivers before spawning. Moves far upstream, sometimes our to 1500 km. Spawns in shallow tributaries with some current in well oxygenated water over gravel bottom. Individual females do not spawn every year; spawns only 2-3 times during entire life. After spawning adults return directly to sea. Embryonic development lasts up to 7 months. Alevins migrate downstream in May - June (Ref. 59043). Collected by fyke nets (Ref. 4526). An important commercial species, but catches and abundance markedly reduced in last years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cisco de Béring
species.description: Found near river mouths and brackish lagoons (Ref. 5723).  Makes extensive migrations related to spawning (Ref. 27547).  Feeds on invertebrates and cottids (Ref. 27547).  Apparently does not feed during its spawning runs (Ref. 27547). Some populations anadromous (Ref. 96339).

species.name: Cisco de lac
species.description: Inhabits open waters of lakes and large rivers, and also coastal waters of Hudson Bay (Ref. 9988, 86798).  Nerito-pelagic species that feeds on plankton and large crustaceans (Ref. 58426).  Utilized fresh, smoked, and frozen; can be steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Cisco sardinelle
species.description: Adults occur in coastal waters, estuaries, large lakes and rivers (Ref. 5723).  Lake-dwelling populations appear to be non-migratory, while those found in streams or brackish water move considerable distances to reach or leave spawning sites (Ref. 27547).  Semi-anadromous populations forage in estuaries, lower courses of rivers, backwaters and lakes (Ref. 59043). Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feed on planktonic crustaceans and insects (Ref. 1998); also plant material (Ref. 27547) and fishes (Ref. 58426).  Do not usually feed during its spawning run (Ref. 28219, 28860, 28861).  Migratory forms are observed to live longer than fresh water forms (Ref. 1998).  Spawn in deep pools on sand and gravel (Ref. 59043).  Flesh is said to be tasty (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Cisco à mâchoires égales
species.description: Usually found in deep water of large lakes. Belongs to C. artedi complex. Formerly commercial important, but now extinct.

species.name: Cisque
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in various inshore habitats:  sand or mud bottoms, reefs, estuaries and harbors (Ref. 9800).  Found near coral and rock reefs at temperatures ranging from 26° to 29°C.  Feeds on invertebrates and benthic fishes (Ref. 5213).  Generally marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Cithare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit soft bottoms from the coastline to about 300 m depth, but rarely caught at depths greater than 200 m (Ref. 9537).  They feed on small fish and crustaceans (Ref. 231).

species.name: Citharichthys amblybregmatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Citharichthys gnathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Citharichthys minutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Citharichthys surinamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Citharichthys valdezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Citharidium ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 69.7 cm (Ref. 7095).

species.name: Citharinops distichodoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Monospecific, distinguished from other genus of family by the body form which is more elongated than 2 other genus: Citharidium and Citharinus (Ref. 2938).

species.name: Citharinus congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Citharinus eburneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: Citharinus citharus.

species.name: Citharinus gibbosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and river mouths (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Citharinus latus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in open water and vegetation beds of lakes and flowing water; ingests mud containing benthic and sedimented algae; spawns in the perennial wetland at high water (in the Sudd in South Sudan) (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Citharinus macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Citharoides orbitalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Citico Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Citrine goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms (mixed mud, shell and leaf litter) (Ref. 93147).

species.name: Citron mudgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected using rotenone in a sheltered bay on a mainly flat mud bottom in 30 m depth. Seldom collected due to its small size and predilection for seldom-dived, mud-bottom habitat. It is likely to live in the burrows of larger mud-dwelling fishes such as jawfish or Oxymetopon ribbongobies (for P. aithiops found at the type locality also shelters in the burrows of Oxymetopon compressus) (Ref. 118649).

species.name: Citron perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Citron pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Claea dabryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Claire's fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with strong current (Ref. 41654).  FishBase common name agreed by authors.

species.name: Clanwilliam catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among rocks and cobbles and under banks in clear, flowing streams.  Feeds on insects, especially the larvae of caddis and mayflies, and other small invertebrates taken from the bottom (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Clanwilliam redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers large, deep pools in clear streams. Feeds mainly on insects from the surface waters. Breeds in summer, males congregating in a nuptial school over vertical rock surfaces in flowing water. Closely related to the Twee River redfin Barbus erubescens (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Clanwilliam sandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the mainstream and larger tributaries, favors pools and deep runs of the river.  Feeds on algae, detritus and small invertebrates by grazing off rocks as well as grubbing in soft sediments.  In the clear water of the Olifants this species is frequently observed as silvery flashes as it rolls and twists when feeding.  Migrates upstream in masses during spring and summer for breeding (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Clanwilliam yellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors deep pools and runs of large tributaries and mainstreams as well as impounded waters.  Omnivorous, feeding on algae and aquatic invertebrates such as insects, snails, and crabs.  Large specimens also take frogs and small fish.  Breeds in summer, migrating upstream to spawn over gravel beds.

species.name: Claqueur dix-barbes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic fish occurring mainly in brackish water.  Found on soft bottoms of shallow turbid water near river mouths.  The species has a peculiar mode of egg incubation wherein the female banjo catfish carries the eggs firmly attached to the underside of the body.  This seems to be an adaptation to facilitate the oxygenation of the eggs in muddy environments.  Reproduction takes place in March and June (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Claqueur sept-barbes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic fish which lives on sandy-muddy littoral waters, estuaries and flooded zones of rivers.  Reproduction takes place in April and June (Ref. 35381).  The species has a peculiar mode of egg incubation wherein the female banjo catfish carries the eggs firmly attached to the underside of the body.  This seems to be an adaptation to facilitate the oxygenation of the eggs in muddy environments (Ref. 35381).  It is captured in coastal traps of stakes driven into the tidal mud (Chinese fish traps) (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Clarence Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shelter of rocks and boulders in lacustrine habitats, also found in swamps and streams draining in and out of lakes (Ref. 44894).  Adults occur in the rocky margin of Clarence Lagoon, its outlet stream and several tributaries that flow into the lake.  Adults feed on benthic crustaceans while juveniles feed partly on planktonic crustaceans, and insects and their larvae (Ref. 30189, 44894).  Very secretive species, darts for cover under boulders if disturbed.  The entire life cycle (may live for up to four years) takes place in fresh water.  Adults move into inlet streams to spawn in spring.  The demersal eggs take about 2 months to hatch.  Fry reside in open surface waters of the lake (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Clarence river cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pristine sections of clear, flowing, rocky streams strewn with logs and other woody debris.  Life history and general biology are similar to that of the Murray cod; however, it has a slightly slower growth rate.  Spawns in spring when water temperatures exceed 16°C (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Clariallabes attemsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apart from the original description nothing is known about this species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes brevibarbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In no way predatory, but consumes any material available, including detritus. Decayed plant remains, remains of terrestrial insects, insect larvae and other small invertebrates have been found in the stomach (Ref. 41580, 78218). Found among dead leaves in the forest streams of the inundation zones (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes centralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles have been found in the inundation zone of forest streams and pools and appear to be omnivores. Sand, decayed plant materials and decomposed insects were found in juvenile stomachs (Ref. 41580, 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes heterocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known about the biology of this species, but it is probably similar to that of the other slender Clariallabes species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariallabes longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Remains of decayed plants and insects have been found in the stomach of a female specimen from central Congo (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes manyangae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Clariallabes manyangae has been found in rapids (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes melas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams. Stomach content analysis revealed a quantity of decayed plant material as well as insect larvae (Ref. 415802, 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes mutsindoziensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 26960, 78218).  Voracious species, feeds on insects and insect larvae (Coleoptera and other unidentified larvae) (Ref. 26960). Insects and insect larvae have been found in stomach (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clariallabes pietschmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariallabes simeonsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariallabes teugelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariallabes uelensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariallabes variabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among leaf litter in shallow streams, as well as along the bank of watercourses. Stomach content analysis revealed a quantity of sand, decayed plant remains, crustaceans, insect larvae, and the remains of terrestrial insects (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias abbreviatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias agboyiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found more abundant in forest floodplain ponds, grassland floodplain ponds and marshes than in rivers (Ref. 31579). Maximum reported size 235 mm TL for West Africa (Ref. 57129) and Lower Guinea (Ref. 81644).

species.name: Clarias albopunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species' biology is unknown (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias anfractus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias batu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwater sections of torrent streams, in clear, cool, fast flowing water over a substrate of sand, rocks and large granite boulders.  Largely carnivorous, subsisting on small fish, crustaceans and insects.  Seems to be nocturnal, emerging into the open at night. Also Ref. 84801.

species.name: Clarias buettikoferi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known about the biology of this catfish (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias camerunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Data on the diet of C. walkeri (=C. camerunensis) showed larvae of mayflies, chironomids, and caddis insects to be the main food of small and middle-sized specimens (Ref. 248). Stomach content analysis showed presence of practically everything edible from plant remains, insects and their larvae to fish remains (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias cataractus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast-flowing streams (Ref. 43641).  Found in hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Clarias dhonti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias dumerilii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias dussumieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ditches (Ref. 4833); prefers lower reaches of streams, rivers and canal with muddy bottom; commonly found in ponds, swamps and paddy fields (Ref. 44149).  Predatory, feeds on small fishes and insects (Ref. 44149).

species.name: Clarias ebriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons and coastal rivers (Ref. 248).  Feeds on insects, mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 41457).

species.name: Clarias engelseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known about the biology of this catfish (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias gracilentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias hilli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias insolitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias jaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ecology, food and breeding: unknown (Ref. 248).

species.name: Clarias kapuasensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swampy areas bordering the mainstream of the Kapuas River and its tributaries (Ref. 49847).

species.name: Clarias lamottei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is situated in a savannah area, in a swamp which completely dries up every year (Ref. 248).

species.name: Clarias leiacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias longior
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Practically nothing is known about the biology of this species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias maclareni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lacustrine species living in deeper as well as in shallow waters (Ref. 248, 78218).  Larger specimens feed mainly on fish, especially Cichlidae; small specimens feed on insect larvae, Chironomids-Odonata (Ref. 248, 78218).

species.name: Clarias macromystax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No information is available on the biology of the species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias magur
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias microspilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias nebulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias nigricans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias nigromarmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known about the ecology and reproduction of this species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias olivaceus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias pachynema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known on the biology and reproduction of this species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias planiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias platycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to equatorial forest and galley forest rivers (Ref. 248). Inhabits smaller rivers, ditches and inundation zones (Ref. 78218). Feeds on fish (Ref. 248, 78218).

species.name: Clarias pseudoleiacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamps in coastal forest areas (Ref. 49847).

species.name: Clarias pseudonieuhofii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias salae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in river systems which arise in mountainous areas and are entirely within the rain forest (Ref. 248). Very little is known about the biology, but on basis of its distribution the species appears to be restricted to the rain forest (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Clarias serniosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias submarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The biology of this species is in the main unknown (Ref. 78218). Maximum size reported is 159mm TL (Ref. 81644).

species.name: Clarias sulcatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarias teijsmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small forest streams in the primary forest in slow-moving or still water and were extremely cryptic.

species.name: Clariger chionomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded only from shallow subtidal zone, 0.5 to 1.5 m deep under stones.

species.name: Clariger cosmurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky tide pools.

species.name: Clariger exilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Clariger papillosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravelly tide pools.

species.name: Clariger sirahamaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clariger taiwanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tidal pools with gravel on the rocky substratum of northern coast of Taiwan. Occurs with other marine gobies, mostly with other species of Bathygobius, as well as Eviota, Gobiopsis, and Luciogobius species, as well as Priolepis semidoliata (Ref. 90262).

species.name: Clarion clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clarion snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters (to 20 m) among rocks and sand (Ref. 40867).

species.name: Clarisse africain
species.description: Inhabits exposed outer reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs, in areas of mixed sand, coral and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles occur in small tide pools, exposed reef flats with algae-rubble.  Generally solitary (Ref. 5213).  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey, including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 5374).  Turns over rocks to prey on hiding invertebrates (Ref. 11441).  Young look very different (Ref. 1623).

species.name: Clarisse clown
species.description: Occurs in the vicinity of sand or rubble patches of exposed outer reef flats, lagoon reefs, and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602), often in semi-exposed surge zones (Ref. 48636).  Adults solitary.  Juveniles common in shallow tide pools (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled invertebrates including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 9823).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Randall (1999, Ref. 33411) question identity of specimens exceeding 70 cm.

species.name: Clarke's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal rock pools.  Larger adult size in cooler water and shallow estuaries under jetties (Ref. 9002).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Clarotes bidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Claudia's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near reefs on sand-rubble bottoms at 1-10 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Claudia's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary usually on outer slopes of reefs 1-35 m deep.  Formerly identified as <i>H. ornatissimus<i> which is restricted to Hawaiian Islands and Johnston Island (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Clavelade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shelf and upper slope waters. Reported depth ranges varies, from 10-300 m (Ref. 4426,  82319, 88187), and from 300-577 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504); most common in coastal waters between 10-60 m depth (Ref. 58137). Tolerates low salinities (Ref. 88171). Found on mud, sand and gravel bottoms, rarely on rougher bottoms (Ref. 6808, 58137). Nocturnal species. Feeds on all kinds of bottom animals, preferably crustaceans (Ref. 3167) and fishes (Ref. 114953). Undertakes migrations with mean distances of 54-117 km per month; shows a clear annual migration cycle (Ref. 89017, 89018), moves from deeper offshore waters (10-30 m) in autumn and winter to shallower areas (<10 m) in spring (Ref. 82319). Young are non-migratory, inhabiting inshore nursery grounds (Ref. 89019, 89020, 89022); in the Bay of Douarnenez (France) they are found to remain in shallow waters for at least 2 years (Ref. 89023). Maturity age 7-8 years (Ref. 114953). Oviparous. Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205). Detects weak electric fields generated by other organisms (prey detection and predator avoidance) but may also generate its own weak electric fields (Ref. 10311, 88171). Utilized fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Clavière
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the littoral zone, in rocky areas and seagrass beds. Act as "cleaners". Feed on worms, small amphipods, copepods, bryozoans and hydrozoans (Ref. 4742). Males keep watch over Cystoseria-covered spawning territory though no nesting is done (Ref. 4742). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clavière (Symphodus cinereus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in littoral areas, in eel-grass beds, sometimes on soft bottoms (1-20 m), often in lagoons and estuaries with plenty of vegetation and detritus (Ref. 4742).  Often in aggregation (Ref. 4742).  Feed on shrimps, amphipods, isopods, small gastropods and bivalves (Ref. 4742).  Females spawn in a nest built and guarded by the male (Ref. 4742).  Males grow faster than females (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clea's threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cleaner goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on live coral.  Removes ectoparasites from other fishes.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35408).

species.name: Clear chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and silt-bottomed pools, often near riffles, in creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Clear Creek gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated springs.

species.name: Clear fin-base flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from a depth of 296 m.  Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Clear Lake splittail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shoreline (as young) and open water of Clear Lake.  Formerly spawned in tributaries of lake (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Clear wriggler
species.description: A benthic, inshore species, found in intertidal and coral reef areas, over sandy bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Clear-finned dragonfin tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clearfin livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on amphipods (Ref. 50313).

species.name: Clearfin squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly around oceanic islands (Ref. 9710). It is an uncommon inhabitant of reef flats, lagoon and semi-sheltered seaward reefs to depths over 20 m. Occurs with N. sammara in coral-rich areas with large staghorn Acropora corals. Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 11889).

species.name: Clearhead icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cleft-lipped goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast-flowing streams with cobble and boulder bottoms (Ref. 2847).  Occurs at least as far as 50-60 km upstream from the sea (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Cleftbelly trevally
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in shallow coastal waters where they often swim near the surface.  They feed mainly on shrimps, copepods, decapod crustaceans and small fish.

species.name: Clementina toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clepticus brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.

species.name: Clic
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in open waters but also near the coast (Ref. 9293, 11230).  Form schools.  Feed on almost all  forms of fish and zooplankton; also takes crustaceans and squid (Ref. 2850).  Sexual maturity is reached in 4-5 months (3 for captive fish) (Ref. 11441).  Spawn in the open sea and probably approximate to the coast when water temperature rises (Ref. 9293).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6755).  Attracting devices such as floating bundles of bamboo reeds or cork planks are used to concentrate dolphin fish before the nets are set.  Marketed frozen (Ref. 9987) and fresh and is of high value (Ref. 9293). Caught by trolling and on tuna longlines; also occasionally with drift nets (Ref. 9846).

species.name: Cling goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coloured, large floppy or fan sponges, usually in depths greater than 10 meters. Found on the underside of the sponges (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Clinging goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 6371).  Found in a fast-flowing creek in hilly terrain about 15 km from the sea (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Clinie donzelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clinus arborescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clinus exasperatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clinus musaicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clinus ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clinus superciliosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal and subtidal areas (Ref. 5496).

species.name: Clipper barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: belongs to ablabes group, distinguished from other West African Barbus by the dorsal fin spot. B. deserti (spot fully covering dorsal tip) (Ref. 2940). Maximum SL observed is 65 mm (Ref. 2940, 81282).

species.name: Clipperton angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cloister blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs with oysters, and often found in estuaries (Ref. 90102).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Closefin pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Cloudy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in shallow protected waters (Ref. 1602).  Benthic on silty sand or mud (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Clown barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in forest streams of the foothills zones, usually in clear, slow to fast flowing waters, preferring quieter areas along the shores; commonly found  in shallow waters (less than 5-15 cm) such as puddles in the forest (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Clown de l'Île Maurice
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoons and outer reefs. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Heteractis aurora, Heteractis magnifica, Stichodactyla mertensii, Macrodactyla doreensis, Stichodactyla haddoni, and Stichodactyla mertensii (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Clown featherback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing waters of large and medium-sized rivers (Ref. 12693).  Within the Mekong mainstream, it occurs in pools (Ref. 37770).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  A predator on surface-feeding fishes, crustaceans and insects, with a crepuscular or nocturnal activity pattern.  Moves into inundated forest during the high water period from June to October.  Individuals from the Great Lake are shipped to markets in Thailand (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Clown goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mangrove streams with very fine silt-mud substrate (Ref. 92840) with salinity ranging from 0.0 to 36.6 ppt (Ref. 97140).

species.name: Clown knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit freshwater rivers, lakes, beels, nullahs in the plains (Ref. 41236), reservoirs, canals and ponds (Ref. 1479).  Feed on aquatic insects, mollusks, shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 1479).  Females lay eggs usually on stake or stump of wood, males fan them with tail, keep them aerated and silt-free, guard them against small catfish and other predators; complete give-away to fishermen; females not observed at egg posts; moderately important food fish (Ref. 2686).  Spawn once a year during May to August (Ref. 6459).

species.name: Clown loach
species.description: Poisson. Adults are found mostly at the bottom of main river channels, often hiding under rocks, woods, or in mud cavities (Ref. 92922).  Juveniles are often found in the floodplains (Ref. 92922). Adults feed on worms, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  aggressive; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 150 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Clown panaque
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clown rasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Clown wedgefish
species.description: A poorly known benthic species with restricted distribution, probably coastal.  Males mature at ca. 71 cm TL, born at ca. 14 cm TL. Embryos with yolk sacs at 20.9-23.6 TL; juvenile male at 39.5 cm TL, adolescent at 64.2 cm TL and adult at size greater than 70.5 cm TL; immature females at 41.5 and 60.9 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Clown wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant on reef tops and in shallow rocky areas. Found to depths of at least 25 m (Ref. 26938). Also found in Sargassum beds (Ref. 9626). Solitary and wary and can be difficult to approach (Ref. 26938). The tricolored pattern of the initial phase is similar to that of the juveniles of the yellowmouth grouper, Mycteroperca interstitialis, an aggressive mimic (Ref. 43465). A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367). Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Club cory
species.description: Occurs in creeks with sandy to sandy-muddy substrate, medium or little sun, 0.5 to 2 m depth. Rarely caught. The mature male's pectoral spine is uniformly very thick along its whole length and is provided with fine needles (Ref. 35381). Sympatric with C. amapaensis.

species.name: Club-barbel sheatfish
species.description: Inhabits mainstream river.  Carnivorous, feeding on insects and benthic fauna (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Clubhead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found exclusively in empty barnacle shells on rocky reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Oviparous (Ref. 56066).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56066).

species.name: Clupea manulensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clupeacharax anchoveoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to reach around 8.0 cm SL (Ref. 81048).

species.name: Clupeocharax schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clupeonelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Essentially a brackish water species but tolerating salinities up to 34 ppt and with semi-anadromous and purely freshwater forms in rivers and lakes.  Forms schools.  Migratory between winter or autumn feeding and summer spawning grounds.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 188); crustaceans such as copepods and cladocerans (Ref. 59043).  Breeds in early summer in the Sea of Azov with a peak in May, and from about May in the lower reaches of rivers (e.g. Dneiper and Dneister) (Ref. 188). Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Clupisoma bastari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers in upland areas (Ref. 41236).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma longianale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma montanum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rapid rivers and streams (Ref. 41236).  Live in hill streams (Ref. 4833).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma naziri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma nujiangense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rivers with silty and slow to medium flowing water over mixed substratum ranging from sand to boulders (Ref. 56056).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma prateri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma roosae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Clupisoma sinense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).  Sold fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Clupisoma yunnanense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clypeobarbus bomokandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clypeobarbus hypsolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. pleuropholis from Chad and Congo basins (Ref. 2940). Maximum TL was recorded at 4.2 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Clypeobarbus matthesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 7.9 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Clypeobarbus pleuropholis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. hypsolepis (Ref. 2940).

species.name: Clypeobarbus pseudognathodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Clypeobarbus schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cnesterodon brevirostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coad's riffle minnow
species.description: During the time of the collection of the type specimens, the upstream portion of Namroud River at the type locality had clear water, with medium to fast water flow. The stream had a width of about 3 m and a maximum depth of up to 1 m, with grassy shores, submergent plants. The stream bed consisted of gravel and mud.  Found syntopic with <i>Barbus sp., <i>Capoeta aculeata (Valenciennes, 1844), <i>Capoeta buhsei Kessler, 1877, <i>Carassius auratus (Linnaeus, 1758), <i>Carassius gibelio (Bloch, 1782), <i>Squalius cf. orientalis (Nordmann, 1840), <i>Paracobitis malapterura (Valenciennes, 1846), and <i>Oncorhynchus mykiss (Walbaum, 1792).

species.name: Coal darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coal grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lentic and lotic freshwater (Ref. 7300). They inhabit clear, rapid streams (sometimes very small creeks) flowing over sand and mud; also in rocky pools. Prefer the upper reaches of coastal drainages. Water temperatures are always above 15°C. Feed on crustaceans (especially prawns) and small fishes. Spawning in the wild has been recorded in November and probably continues through to early autumn (March). Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205). Sexual maturity is reached at a size of about 13 centimeters. Juvenile coal grunter is attractive and popular in the aquarium hobby. Closely related and nearly identical in appearance to H. raymondi from south-western Papua New Guinea (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Coalskin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Coast cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coastal darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coastal shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand in pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers, spring effluents and lakes.

species.name: Coastal stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coates' catfish
species.description: Found in rivers only.  Occurs at temperatures ranging from 26 to 32°C.  Mainly diurnal.  Feeds mainly on fine and coarse detritus, other plant material (particularly seeds and small pieces of bark), and especially prawns.  Also preys on aquatic insects and nymphs, fishes, worms and leeches (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Coates' goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in main river channels and smaller tributaries in both open plain and rainforest habitats to elevations of at least 125 m.

species.name: Coatzacoalcos gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobalt chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Adults inhabit offshore reefs on relatively level bottoms, often covered with coralline algae rhodoliths (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in a variety of habitats, over mud, sand and gravel bottoms; over coral reefs, off rocky shores (Ref. 10948) and in mangrove sloughs; inshore around pilings and buoys, and offshore around drifting and stationary objects; occasionally in estuaries (Ref. 9739).  Form small groups and may pursue small pelagic inshore (Ref. 48635).  Feed on crabs, fishes, and squids (Ref. 5213, 10948, 13442).  Form spawning aggregations during  the warm months in the western Atlantic; eggs and larvae planktonic (Ref. 12459). Caught in small quantities due to its solitary behavior (Ref. 9626). Caught mainly with handlines, and by trolling pelagically offshore over the continental shelf (Ref. 10948). Good food fish; marketed fresh (Ref. 5284), smoked, and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Also caught for sport (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Cobitis albicoloris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis amphilekta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis arachthosensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in burrows mostly in sandy to silty substrate in still to moderately flowing waters during the day. May sometimes inhabit gravel bottom and vegetation (Ref. 59043). Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205). Threatened due to small distribution range, habitat alterations and risk of hybridisation with C. hellenica (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis arenae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis bilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, rivers, brooks and irrigation channels with still or moderately flowing water on sand, gravel or mud bottom, often with vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Females mature at 2 years of age (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis biwae
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Commercially cultured in Japan (Ref. 559).

species.name: Cobitis brachysoma
species.description: This species occurs in Suijian River, Zengjiang River, and Nalongjiang River, Guangdong, China (Ref. 129344).

species.name: Cobitis brevipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis crassicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis dalmatina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lakes and streams with sand or mud bottom (Ref. 59043).  Females reach up to about 6 cm SL  and 5 cm SL in males (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Population is categorized as threatened (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis dolichorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis dorademiri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in moderate to fast-flowing stretches of shallow rivers, on sandy banks and shores, sometimes on rock bottom with submerged vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Population not threatened as most are stable and occurs only as a few restricted populations (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis elongatoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in flowing or still waters from small brooks to large rivers, springs, lakes and oxbows on sand, silt or mud bottom (Ref. 59043). Usually found together with hybridogenous, sperm-parasitic lineages, which have originated by hybridisation with C. taenia and C. tanaitica. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205). Spawning period occurs from April to July in aquatic vegetation (Ref. 59043). Distinguished from C. vardarensis and C. pontica only by chromosome characters. They cannot be distinguished in the field. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis faridpaki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis fasciola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length for female taken from Ref. 118058.

species.name: Cobitis fimbriata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis gladkovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis guttata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis hankugensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis hellenica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species. Adults inhabit marshlands, rivers, springs and associated wetlands (Ref. 26100), in still to moderately flowing water on sand to silt bottom (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis herzegoviniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis illyrica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in still waters of lakes on mud bottom (Ref. 59043). Congeners are oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis jadovaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis kaibarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cobitis keyvani

species.name: Cobitis linea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens from Pulwar River were caught on muddy bottom (mud 5-6 cm thick, below which is a stony bottom) with aquatic vegetation (Juncus, Cyperus, Typha). One specimen was caught in flowing water near the foot of a muddy bank at Kul River, near Darab (Ref. 33850). Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis longitaeniatus
