species.name: Cobitis maroccana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which occurs in highland and lowland water courses with little current.  Is threatened due to pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100). Max. length (Juan Antonio Delgado Saez, pers. Comm. 1997).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis matsubarae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sandy bottoms of the middle to lower river reaches (Ref. 41299).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis melanoleuca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found from small lowland streams to large rivers with gentle current, and lakes mostly with dense vegetation on sand-silt to sand-gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis meridionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lakes and highland water courses, with sand or mud bottom and underwater vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Feed on invertebrates.  Spawn in April and May (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Threatened due to water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Cobitis narentana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lake and river shores on sand bottom (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).  Are batch spawners (Ref. 59043). Population is threatened by the construction of Neretva dam and competition from introduced species (Ref. 59043).

Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).  Population is threatened due to very restricted area of occurrence (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cobitis tanaitica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large coastal lakes and lower part of rivers on silt bottom, as well as smaller streams with sand bottoms (Ref. 59043).  Adults migrate to larger water bodies in autumn for overwintering (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis taurica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with still to moderately flowing clear water, on sand to silt bottom or in dense vegetation (Ref. 59043).   Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).  Population is threatened due to a concentrated distribution in a very limited stretch of stream which might dry up in summer (Ref. 59043).  Females grow up to a maximum length of 9.1 SL (Ref. 78640).

species.name: Cobitis tetralineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cobitis trichonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species.  Adults occur in lakes and  lowland water courses with little current.  Spawn from April to June (Ref. 13696).  A multiple spawner (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).  Is threatened due to water abstraction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Cobitis vettonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep, large stream with clear water, and sand to rock bottom (Ref. 59043). Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205). Spawns in April-June. Mainly distinguished by mtDNA characters and difficult to distinguish from C. paludica in the field (Ref. 59043). Population is threatened due to very restricted area of occurrence, agricultural water pollution, drought and introduced predators (Ref. 59043).

Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).  Population is threatened due to very restricted area of occurrence, habitat alteration and land-use changes (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cocco's lantern fish
species.description: High-oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066), found between 300-800 m during the day and between 25-100 m (juveniles 14-22 mm) and 200-300 (adults 50-56 mm) at night (Ref. 4479).  Size stratification with depth both day and night (Ref. 4775).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Reach sexual maturity between 40 and 45 cm (Ref. 47377).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Coccorella atrata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cocher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be seen in a variety of habitats ranging from rich coral reefs (Ref. 58652) to weedy and rubble covered areas (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Maybe found singly, in pairs, and in aggregations that roam over large distances in search of food.  Feed mainly by tearing pieces from polychaetes, sea anemones, coral polyps, and algae (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cocher (Heniochus monoceros)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in lagoon and seaward reefs with rich coral growth.  Juveniles solitary; adults are often paired and occasionally found hovering side by side under tabular corals (Ref. 1602).  Feed on bottom living animals (Ref. 6113), e.g. invertebrates associated with algal zones (Ref. 5503).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Cocher blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit turbid inner lagoons, reef flats, and clear seaward rocky and coral reefs  (Ref. 1602, 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Generally encountered in small groups of 2 or 3 individuals (Ref. 9267).  Adults occur singly, in pairs and occasionally are seen in large schools (Ref. 48637).  Feed on small encrusting animals (Ref. 6113).  Size of metamorphosis from postlarva to juvenile is 7.5 cm (Ref. 9267).  The long pelagic larval stage is the reason for the wide distribution and strong colouration that shows no geographical variation (Ref. 48637).  Popular aquarium fish but rarely survives in tanks (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cocher grégaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur primarily along outer reef slopes, in current channels.  Juveniles in aggregations around isolated patch reefs, adults in large schools well above the bottom (Ref. 9710).  In Indonesia, adults most common in depth 40-50 m, reported to 200 m (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on plankton.  Juveniles may act as cleaners (Ref. 9710); also observed in adults (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.description: Poisson. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Cockatoo dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky bottom, near sand and rubble (Ref. 12718) and apparently has  preference for deeper habitats (15-30 m), at lower reef slopes and bases (Ref. 88695).

species.name: Cockatoo Handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cockatoo righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 3132, 48637).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9792).  Flicks the long dorsal filaments on the front of the head when alarmed, looking just like the sticky threads that are produced by a holothurian when handled (ref. 48637).

species.name: Cockatoo waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, subtidal areas with sand rubble and weed (Ref. 9710).  A strongly compressed fish that can be seen rocking back and forth on the bottom in response to surge.  Easily caught with small hand nets.  Nocturnal (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cockerel wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various habitats from shallow algae reefs to deep offshore on soft bottom with sponges and hydroid colonies (Ref. 9002).  Mostly small, secretive species, usually hiding among dense weeds (Ref. 9002).  It rarely leaves its cover except to move quickly between hydrozoan colonies, but not before having a good look around first to make sure its safe (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Cocktail wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among algae patches of coral or rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Also found in weedy bottoms (Ref. 30573).  Cryptic and with excellent camouflage, making it difficult to detect (Ref. 90102).  Males territorial (Ref. 9710).  Edible but not tasty (Ref. 559).  Female length is from Ref. 9137.

species.name: Cocky gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on coastal waters, in the continental shelf area (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Coco coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cocoa damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs.  They feed mainly on benthic algae but also on sponges, ascidians and anemones while juveniles feed on invertebrates like harpacticoid copepods and nemerteans (Ref. 9626).  Often solitary (Ref. 9626).  Juveniles are aggressively territorial (Ref. 9626).  Aggressive when breeding (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Cocos barnacle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small benthic reef fish which is common in shallow water, but also occurs to depths of at least 31 meters (Ref. 81029).  Oviparous (Ref. 56066).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56066).

species.name: Cocos frill-goby
species.description: Lives among rubble, in sand pockets, or on reef rock and is abundant on silty intertidal reef flats (Ref. 9360, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Gut analysis composed of  polychaetes, isopods, amphipods, and brachyurans (Ref. 9360, 48637).

species.name: Cocos Island flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on pale sandy substrates in clearwater coastal bays to outer reef lagoons and sandy gutters on reef flats.  Often crawls over low stony reef (Ref. 48637).  The membranous structure at the tip of the first dorsal fin resembles a small fish or crustacean (possibly a small hippolytid shrimp), authors called the ray the illicium and the structure at the tip as the esca.  The  illicium waves the esca back and forth near mouth to attract prey.  Shows sexual dimorphism in width of the interorbital origin, wider in males than females.  Most frequently collected by divers.

species.name: Cocos triplefin

Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cocos-Keeling angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This rare species is a secretive dweller of crevices and clefts in caves of outer reef drop-offs (Ref. 1602).  Natural diet unknown; forms harems of 3-7 individuals.  Almost never exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cocosoda kakinette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy bottoms in brackish river mouths.  Probably prefers large rivers and slightly brackish waters (Ref. 11225, 27188).  Occurs in very thick schools over muddy bottoms.  Omnivorous, with a tendency towards detritivorous feeding.  Searches for food in the zones of the village waste waters.  During reproduction, towards the month of December, the ventral fins and the mandible turn pink.  At this time, the weight of the male and female's mature gonads account for  10% and 25%, respectively, of the body weight (Ref. 35381).  Marketed fresh.

Feeds mostly on crustaceans and other planktonic organisms; often attracted to lights at night (Ref. 2797).

species.name: Coelacanthe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known as the living fossil. Inhabits steep rocky shores, sheltering in caves during the day (Ref. 38425), with as much as 14 individuals in a single cave (Ref. 38426). Foraging singly over open substrate at night (Ref. 38426), it drifts passively with the current or swims slowly with its paired fins and its second dorsal and anal fins (Ref. 38427). May travel as much as 8 km at night searching for food and retreats to the nearest cave before dawn (Ref. 38426). Preys on fishes and squid (Ref. 26162). Beryx, Polymixia, Symphysanodon, apogonids, a skate, an eel and a swell shark have been known to be eaten (Ref. 11228). Its main enemies are likely to be large sharks (Ref. 26162). Ovoviviparous, with as much as 5-29 young (Ref. 11228, 37171). Gestation period estimated at 3 years, which would be the longest known in vertebrates (Ref. 30865). A small relative gill area (Ref. 38428) restricts coelacanths to a life 'in the slow lane', drift-feeding at night in cold waters and resting in slightly warmer caves for food consumption during day time (Ref. 38429). Recently, Prof Hans Fricke and associates have succeeded in observing and filming Latimeria in their natural habitat. Using a two-man submersible, Fricke found several coelacanths in depths of 120-400 m on the barren lava slopes off Grand Comoro. Coelacanths have distinctive white markings, and this allowed recognition of individuals and tracking of their movements. During the day, Latimeria retreat to caves, with as many as 13 fish crowded together in a single cave. Several individuals occupy overlapping home ranges, and Fricke never saw any aggressive encounters between coelacanths. By resting in caves (were there are no strong currents) the coelacanths save energy and avoid encounters with large predators (deep-water sharks). After sunset, the coelacanths leave their caves and drift slowly across the substrate, presumably looking for food, within 1-3 meters of the bottom. On these nightly hunting forays, the coelacanth may travel as much as 8 km; and before dawn they shelter in the nearest cave. While searching for prey, or moving from one cave to another, Latimeria appears to move in slow motion, either drifting passively with the current and using its flexible pectoral and pelvic fins to adjust its position, or slowly swimming by a synchronous sculling movement of the second dorsal and anal fins. In slow forward swimming, the left pectoral and right pelvic fins move forward, while the right pectoral and left pelvic fins are pulled backward. This tandem movement of alternate paired fins resembles the movement of the forelimbs and hindlimbs of a tetrapod walking on land. Latimeria does not use its lobed fins for walking on the bottom, and even when they are resting in caves they usually do not touch the substrate. Like most slow moving fishes, the coelacanth can make a sudden lunge or fast start by means of a quick flip of its massive caudal fin. During its nightly foraging swims, Latimeria was often seen to perform head-stands, in which it rotates its body into a vertical position, with its head near the bottom and its caudal fin curved perpendicular to its body. It then held this position for two or three minutes at a time. This curious behavior may be used when it is scanning the bottom with its putative electoreceptive rostral organ, or it may be a reaction to the bright lights of Prof. Fricke's submersible (Ref. 38228).

species.name: Coelorinchus nazcaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on pelagic food items including shrimps (Gennadas, Sergestes, Plesionika), the mysid Paralophogaster glaber, the copepod Pleuromamma, squid, and fish (Chauliodus sp., Lampanyctus sp., and Myctophidae gen., sp. (Ref. 9949).

species.name: Coelorinchus notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coelorinchus nox

species.name: Coelorinchus obscuratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently a deepwater species and have a very low abundance as it was taken only in small numbers (Ref. 80968).

species.name: Coelorinchus osipullus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus platorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27121.

species.name: Coelorinchus pseudoparallelus

species.name: Coelorinchus sexradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus sheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 54421).

species.name: Coelorinchus simorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus sparsilepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus spilonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One specimen with a large squid beak in its stomach (Ref. 9949).

species.name: Coelorinchus spinifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coelorinchus thompsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus tokiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus trachycarus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Coelorinchus triocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coelorinchus trunovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus vityazae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus weberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelorinchus yurii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coelotilapia joka
species.description: Mainly feeds on plants, preferring algae; pair-bonding, open substrate spawner with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coffre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit inshore on coastal muddy or sandy habitats in still bays, and commonly found in harbours and estuaries.  Small juveniles on protected shallow mudflats (Ref. 48637).  Found in weedy areas near rocks or reefs.  Juveniles often near river mouths and in brackish water.  Adults are solitary, juveniles often form small groups (Ref. 1602).  Large adults are shy (Ref. 48637).  Feed on benthic invertebrates by blowing away the sand (Ref. 1602).  Readily dried and used to make ornaments (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Coffre (Rhynchostracion nasus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found around rocky and sandy substrates (Ref. 1602). Solitary, also found in sheltered bays exposed to heavy silt and mud bottoms of coastal trawling grounds (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Coffre (Tetrosomus concatenatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters muddy bays or estuaries; usually with large remote sponges (Ref. 48637). Solitary. Also found in seagrass and weed bottoms of coastal reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Coffre baguette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral reefs (Ref. 12204).  Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on a wide variety of small bottom invertebrates such as mollusks, crustaceans, worms, sessile tunicates and sponges exposed by a jet of water ejected through the mouth (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh locally (Ref. 3696).  Toxins released when excited kill other fishes (Ref. 5521).  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Coffre bossu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep coastal slopes and sheltered muddy substrates, usually in deep water offshore, but occasionally shallow near seagrass beds with silty rubble substrates (Ref. 48637).  Usually occurs in sandy bottoms in coastal waters. Solitary (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Generally considered as trash fish; not consumed.  Its flesh and organs are poisonous (IUCN, http://www.iucnredlist.org/details/154933/0) however,

species.name: Coffre nid d'abeille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocks, rubble and sand (Ref. 5288), mainly around islands (Ref. 11227).

species.name: Coffre polygone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear water around coral reefs.  Feeds on sponges, alcyonarians, tunicates, and shrimp.  Uncommon and wary (Ref. 9710).  Consumed fresh, generally roasted (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Coffre taureau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water down to about 80 m, mainly in seagrass beds (Ref. 3696).  Feeds on sessile invertebrates such as tunicates, gorgonians and anemones, as well as on slow-moving crustaceans, sponges (Ref. 3696), hermit crabs and marine plants (Ref. 13442).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Considered an excellent food fish; marketed fresh (Ref. 3696).

species.name: Coffre zinga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear water around coral reefs.  Sometimes under ledges and near small holes (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on a variety of small bottom invertebrates such as mollusks, crustaceans, starfishes, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, sessile tunicates, sea grasses (Ref. 3696), algae, crabs and brittle stars (Ref. 13442).  Toxins released when excited kills other fishes (Ref. 5521).  Probably marketed fresh locally (Ref. 3696).

species.name: Coffre à cornes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds, coral rubble areas, and offshore reefs  down to about 50 m.  Feeds on a wide variety of small benthic invertebrates such as mollusks, crustaceans, worms and sessile tunicates, as well as some sea grasses (Ref. 3696).  Highly esteemed food fish in the Caribbean (Ref. 3696).

species.name: Coffre à taches blanches
species.description: Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reefs from the lower surge zone to at least 30 meters (Ref. 37816, 48637).  Juveniles among rocky boulders, often with long spined urchins, and adults on reef crests and slopes.  Males swim about more openly than females that are often in close vicinity to the males (Ref. 48637).  Solitary.  Feeds on didemnid tunicates, polychaetes, sponges, mollusks, copepods, and algae (Ref. 37816).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cohana delagoa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 30573). Feeds mainly on crustaceans, cephalopods (Loligo), small fishes and polychaetes.

species.name: Cohana doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy or sandy bottoms.  Young fish generally occur in shallower water between 18 and 33 m.  Feeds on crustaceans, fish and cephalopods.  One of the most important commercial fish in the East China Sea and northern South China Sea.  May be made into fish balls (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Cohana japonaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very abundant in coastal waters, found on mud or sand bottoms, usually in schools.  Feeds mainly on small fishes, crustaceans, mollusks (mainly cephalopods), polychaetes and echinoderms.  Marketed mainly fresh, but also frozen, steamed, dried-salted, dry-smoked, fermented or made into fish balls and fish meal.

species.name: Cohana tolu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or mud bottoms and feeds on fish, crustaceans, mollusks and polychaetes.  Usually in small groups; flighty during the day (Ref. 48635).  Trawled in commercial quantities in the Straits of Malacca and off the Terengganu coast, South China Sea.

species.name: Cohana élégante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand bottoms near rocks (Ref. 30573).  Swims in groups and feeds on benthic organisms.

species.name: Cohen's mudbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cohen's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Coitor croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters, estuaries and rivers (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Colares stingray
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Colas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, mostly around coral reefs.  Usually seen well above the bottom, frequently in aggregations.  They feed on a combination of plankton and benthic animals including fishes, crustaceans, worms, gastropods and cephalopods, mainly at night (Ref. 9987).  Young individuals are usually found over weed beds.  They feed primarily on plankton (Ref. 9710).  Spawning occurs throughout the year, with peaks at different times in different areas (Ref. 26938).  Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Colas bagnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573) of the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  They feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs, cephalopods, miscellaneous benthic invertebrates and pelagic organisms, including urochordates.

species.name: Colas de La Réunion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Colas dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sharptooth snappers are found in tropical and sub-tropical deep waters.  They are found in schools and live in areas of hard, rocky and uneven sea floor (Ref. 27354).  They feed on benthic invertebrates and fishes.

species.name: Colas drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky bottoms; off Guam, caught most abundantly from 180 to 270 m (Ref. 55).  They feed on fishes and salps.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 55).

species.name: Colas enchanteur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 54833). Probably feeds on zooplankton. Reported to be frequently consumed by the lutjanid Pristipomoides at Pathfinder Reef, Mariana Archipelago (Ref. 54833).

species.name: Colas fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573); off Guam, caught most abundantly between 180 and 270 m (Ref. 9821).  At night, they migrate vertically to the upper part of its habitat to feed (Ref. 11888).  They feed on small fishes, shrimps, crabs, amphipods, ascidians and salps.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 55). Caught mainly with bottom longlines and deep handlines, marketed main fresh and a good quality food fish (Ref. 9821).

species.name: Colas gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are most commonly found in deeper waters of the shelf near the edge of the continental slope.  They feed on small fishes and larger planktonic animals.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Colas lavande
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573); off Guam, caught most abundantly from about 180 to 270 m (Ref. 9821).  They feed mainly on fishes, shrimps, crabs, polychaetes, cephalopods and urochordates.  Marketed mostly fresh.  Caught mainly with bottom longlines and deep handlines.

species.name: Colas oeil doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms; off Guam, caught most abundantly between 180-270 m (Ref. 9821).  They feed primarily on benthic fishes and to a lesser extent on crustaceans, squids, and pelagic tunicates.  Marketed mainly fresh.

species.name: Colas vorace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-water species.  Feeds mainly on small fishes.  A good food fish, it is marketed fresh, rarely frozen.

species.name: Colas à bande dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gold band snappers are deepwater fish inhabiting tropical and sub-tropical waters.  They are schooling fish and live in areas of hard, rocky and uneven sea floor and steep off islands (Ref. 27354).  They feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs, lobsters, stomatopods, squids, gastropods and urochordates.  Marketed fresh.  An excellent food fish. Maximum depth from Ref. 082366.

species.name: Colas écailleuse
species.description: Genre de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Colas élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Although the habitat is poorly known, most specimens have been trawled from relatively deep water at the upper edge of the continental shelf.  Reported to occur on soft or semi-hard bottoms (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Colchic nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Coldwater darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit vegetated springs and spring runs (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on amphipods, midge larvae, isopods and copepods (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Cole's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Coleman's pygmy seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Found in sand bottoms with sparse Zostera and Halophilia in 4-12 m (Ref 90102). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Colin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters but also down to 200 m depth, in areas with hard bottoms. Juveniles are pelagic, spending 2-3 years near the coast including rocky areas, kelp beds, sandy shores and estuaries (Ref. 1371, 58137, 89343, 89362). Juveniles may form schools with saithe (Pollachius virens) (Ref. 88187), and have also been found solitary and defending their feeding territory (Refs. 42174, 89363). Larger individuals move to the open sea and are often found around rocky areas at 40-100 m depth (Ref. 1371). Also observed around shipwrecks and oil platforms (Ref. 88187). Adults occur singly or in small dispersed shoals but is known to form dense shoals on spawning grounds (Ref. 89364). Suggested to undertake spawning migrations (Ref. 88171). Caught as bycatch in cod and saithe fisheries. Flesh is dry but of good flavor (Ref. 35388). Classified as a "hearing generalist" (89365); has also been found to produce sound. Juveniles have been reported to make repeated short grunts during competitive feeding and aggressive encounters (89366).

species.name: Colin (Pollachius virens)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An active, gregarious fish occurring inshore and offshore waters.  Usually enters coastal waters in spring and returns to deeper waters in winter (Ref. 9988).  Smaller fish in inshore waters feed on small crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, euphausiids) and small fish, while larger fish prey predominantly upon fishes.  Spawn in batches (Ref. 51846).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked, canned and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Colin's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and inshore coral reefs, frequently associated with Pavona coral (Ref. 7247). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Colin's fairygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward sand slopes (Ref. 37816).  Found over pebbles (Ref. 43239).  Hovers above the substrate (Ref. 44093).  May occur in small groups (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Colin's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vertical wall with small caves, overhangs and crevices, hard corals (<>iAcropora, Montipora), hydroids, and sea fans (Ref. 109919).

species.name: Colistium guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, generally at depth of less than 50 m.  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).

species.name: Colistium nudipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, generally at depth of less than 50 m.  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).  Utilized fresh or frozen for broiling, frying and baking (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Collared dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species; occurs at the edge of the reef adjacent to sand. Also found in sandy fringe of coral reefs, common around low rock outcrops in 30-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Collared eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) occurring in and around coral reefs.  Sometimes lives in tubular sponges, and suggested that this is its primary habitat (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Collared large-eye bream
species.description: Poisson. Generally solitary over sand or rubble areas adjacent to reefs .  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Sometimes has a distasteful iodine flavor; however, untainted fish are good to eat.

species.name: Collared seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably pelagic (Ref. 42735).  Maximum length is based on a straight-line length measurement from upper surface (ignoring spines) of first trunk ring, to tip of tail (Ref. 42735).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Collette's basslet
species.description: Specimens collected from coral reefs at depths of less than 6 to 33.5 m (Ref. 6180).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Collette's coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoons and silty coastal reefs at 1-10 m deep, and found solitary or in small groups on coral outcrops (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Collette's herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species occurring in coastal waters.

species.name: Collette's viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic and solitary inhabitant of reef crevices to about 5-10 m  (Ref 90102).

species.name: Collichthys lucidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries and down to 90 m depth (Ref. 11230); with sanddy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Collichthys niveatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone above 80 m (Ref. 11230); in sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Coloconger cadenati
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coloconger canina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coloconger eximia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment needs verification.

species.name: Coloconger japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coloconger meadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coloconger saldanhai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Colombian blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Colombian dwarf numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species on inner continental shelf. Unknown life history. Smallest known specimen at 10 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Colombian goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Colombine annelée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral reefs and rocky substrates to depths of at least 30 m (Ref. 9823) on offshore reef slopes (Ref. 90102).  Juveniles generally solitary (Ref. 9710).  Feeds primarily on small fishes, also on crustaceans (Ref. 2334).

species.name: Colombine pastel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit seaward reefs, in areas of mixed sand, rubble and coral (Ref. 9710) to at least 30 m depth (Ref. 9823).  Juveniles seen in groups near the bottom while adults found high above the bottom (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles and females usually in small groups.  Males solitary and territorial, patrolling large sections of reefs (Ref. 48636).  Feed mainly on fishes (about 50%, Ref. 5503) and crustaceans (shrimps) and to a lesser extent on brittlestars and polychaetes (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth taken from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Colombo damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit silty coral or rubble reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Colomesus tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Colon goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs, tide pools, limestone caves, algae-covered rocks and isolated patch reefs surrounded by white sand (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Colonial cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Colored snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coloured righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare.  Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Colurodontis paxmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Comanche Springs pupfish
species.description: Occurs in springs, spring-fed canals and ditches, usually over mud in current (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139)

species.name: Comb flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Comb goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft mud bottoms, river mouths areas near mangrove forests; omnivore feeding on benthic invertebrates like crustaceans (Ref. 92840). Burrows in mud or shingle areas in inshore and estuarine waters (Ref. 4343, 11230).

species.name: Comb rockling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools.

species.name: Comb wrasse
species.description: Inhabits fairly deep sandy bottoms around rocky reefs.

species.name: Comb-gilled catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs primarily on the floodplain and in permanent lakes, occasionally encountered in river channels, but in low numbers.  Feeds on small crustaceans, aquatic insect larvae and nymphs, terrestrial insects, plants, detritus, gastropods, leeches and worms (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Comb-spined catfish
species.description: Found in rivers.  Feeds on aquatic and terrestrial insects and their larvae, prawns and detritus.

species.name: Combattant
species.description: Occur in standing waters of floodplains, canals, rice paddies (Ref. 12693) and medium to large rivers (Ref. 12975).  Feed on zooplankton, mosquito and other insect larvae (Ref. 12693).  Air breather and bubble nest builder.  Used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537).  Males will fight each other.  The many colorful varieties are popular aquarium fish, however, the holding of the males in very small containers should be discouraged (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping: sexes should be kept separate unless for mating, and that only one female should be brought into the breeding tank measuring about 20-30 L (http://www.kampffischnet.de).

species.name: Combed snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest female with yolked eggs measured 16.2 cm SL; smallest male with enlarged, swollen testes 12.4 cm SL (Ref. 57077).

species.name: Combside hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Comely shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in runs and flowing pools over sand, gravel or rubble, of creeks and medium to large rivers.

species.name: Comet dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from consolidated coral growth rising 2 m off sand and silt bottom, in 9-15 m depth; also from turbid waters on fine-sand and coral-rubble bottom (Ref. 127576).

species.name: Comet snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Comical blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs from below the surge zone to at least 30 m, where they typically rest between corals, sides of crevices or shallow caves.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Commafin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuarine, intertidal and inshore waters; usually on mud (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Commander skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).

species.name: Commerson’s anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Commet dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand-rubble bottoms with isolated small coral patches in 12-18 m depth (Ref 90102).

species.name: Common bully
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in various habitats such as small hypertrophic lakes, large oligotrophic lakes and lower reaches of rivers.  Amphidromous (Ref. 11115).  Feeds on a wide variety of benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Common dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi- and mesopelagic, with most caught in nets fishing above 160 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Common false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widely distributed species occurs on seaward reefs.

species.name: Common frog flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly on sandy bottoms in shallow coastal waters (relatively dominant over P. cornutus in Tokyo and Ise Bays, and the Seto Inland, Ariake and Yatsushiro Seas. Probably have some tolerance for reduced salinity forit is reported to be occasionally occurring in river estuaries in China and Korea and brackish waters in Japan (Ref. 126213).

species.name: Common fusegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Inhabits tidal reef flats and shallow lagoons, on sand or rubble patches (Ref. 48637). Feeds on organic matter and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Common gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally demersal on the continental shelf  (Ref. 9563).  Found on rocky reefs in coastal waters (Ref. 33616); particularly sponge areas in sandy patches (Ref. 54394).  Adults have a curved lateral line near the dorsal-fin base and long, venomous dorsal-fin spines (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Common hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling and occurring mostly in coastal waters, but also entering estuaries (Ref. 11230) (e.g. the Hooghly and Godavari in India) and penetrating at least 20 km up the Godavari, tolerating salinities as low as 8.7 ppt.  Feeds on prawn, copepods, crustacean larvae, mollusks and fishes.  Fairly common (Ref. 189).

species.name: Common labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively still waters and occurs in deep pools in larger rivers and in most low-country reservoirs.  Feeds mainly on algae.  Breeding in rivers is highly influenced by monsoon rains (Ref. 43628).

species.name: Common mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184) that spends most of its time out of the water; able to meet its oxygen requirements as long as it stays wet.  Typically resting on mud, rocks, or mangrove roots with their tails dipped in the water. Active at low tide and hunt in the intertidal zone for invertebrates; feeds on worms, crustaceans, and insects as well as polychaetes living on or near surface (Ref. 92840)

species.name: Common Natron tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at a temperature range of 30-32°C (Ref. 2). It feeds actively in the early morning; mainly on algae as well as copepods and dipterous larvae (Ref. 2). A maternal mouthbrooder: males excavate pits in the substrate in shallow water (Ref. 2, 118638). The species is occasionally caught as a food fish in its natural range; although it attains a small size, its tolerance of hostile environments may make it suitable for culture in high salinity environments; potential as an aquarium fish (Ref. 118638). Classed as endangered, due to its restricted distribution (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Common river galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers.  Spawning occurs from July to September (Ref. 58147).

species.name: Common roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported from between depths of 70 m (Ref. 9872) and 327 m (Ref. 58489).

species.name: Common seadragon
species.description: Genre de poissons. Recorded from the intertidal zone to a depth of 50 m (Ref. 9563).  Frequently among seaweeds and coral reefs (Ref. 9137).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Common shore-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal and up to 10 m depth (Ref. 9002); found under rocks (Ref. 9002) and, reef and weed areas (Ref. 33839, 56640).

species.name: Common silver belly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries, harbors, to fairly deep water along the shores (Ref. 30392); strongly affected by freshwater; and reported to congregate in schools (Ref. 58476).

species.name: Common spiny loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually in quiet, flowing waters with a sandy substrate.  Feeds mainly on detritus, but also algae (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Common stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Common stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy beaches and reefs but also well offshore.  May venture well upstream in estuaries (Ref. 6871).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, bony fishes, and other stingarees (Ref. 12951).

species.name: Common stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The name 'stinkfish' refers to the acid smell of the slime covering the body; the slime tastes bitter and may be toxic; only some birds of prey take this species (Ref. 557).

species.name: Common triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are most common in shallow water (0-5m), although recorded from depths of 30 m (Ref. 84085).  They are commonly found in intertidal rock pools, particularly those with adequate rocky or algal shelter.  They feed mainly on amphipods, isopods, and polychaetes (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Common warehou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit continental shelf and slope waters (Ref. 6390).  Reported from depths between 22 m (Ref. 58489) and 400m (Ref. 30458).  They are schooling species, usually aggregating close to the sea bed (Ref. 26498) although there is some evidence that they move into the middle water column at night (Ref. 30459).  Juveniles recorded offshore to a depth of 100 m and sometimes entering estuaries, often in association with jellyfish (Ref. 9563) and schooling close to the surface.  Feed mainly on salps but also takes euphausiids, krill, crabs and small squid (Ref. 9072).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Common weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. inhabits rocky reefs, on sand with sparse algae growth or weeds (Ref. 9002).  Often under rocks (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Communard
species.description: Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102).  Occurs over shallow sandy and seagrass beds, in mangrove swamps, lagoons, channels and outer reef slopes.  May enter rivers.  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  A protracted spawning peak from July to December is recorded in New Caledonia.  Smaller and more numerous females than males have been confirmed in Australian populations.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Communard (Lutjanus russellii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit offshore coral reefs and also inshore rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 30573), at moderate depths, usually over 20 m, and is more common in about 50 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles frequent mangrove estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 30573, 48635).   They  feed on benthic invertebrates and  fish (Ref. 5213).  Sold in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).  A common market fish throughout its range; also a component of artisanal fisheries. Caught with handlines, traps, and bottom trawls and marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9821).

species.name: Comoro cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.  Type specimen taken from a depth of 400 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Compressed ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore pelagic (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Compressed toby
species.description: Inhabits sandy areas of shallow lagoons and channels (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Also found in silty bays or harbors around wharf pilings.  Adults usually in pairs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Compsaraia compsa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Compsaraia iara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in white waters at depths ranging from 2- 30 meters.  Feeds exclusively on dipteran (Ceratopogonidae) larvae mixed with very fine sand, suggesting a benthic foraging behavior (Ref. 115978).

species.name: Compsura gorgonae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Compsura heterura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Compère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays, estuaries and protected coastal waters.  Sold as `sea squab' in northern part of range.  Feeds primarily on shellfish, occasionally on finfish.  Reportedly non-toxic.

species.name: Compère bonite
species.description: Hides in shaded, protected recesses in rocky reefs, boulder strewn slopes and along walls (Ref. 5227). Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Compère collier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in all inshore habitats where there is adequate cover, such as seagrass beds and reef flats.  Feeds on mollusks, crustaceans and echinoderms (Ref. 36453).  Generally common (Ref. 9710).  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Compère corotuche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in bays, tidal creeks and protected coastal waters, especially on seagrass beds, and in brackish water.  Rare or absent on coral reefs.  Does not form schools, but may form huge aggregates.  Hides in the sand when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on bivalves, gastropods, foraminiferans and several other benthic invertebrates specially crustaceans, which it crushes with its powerful teeth (Ref. 35237).  To ward off predators, it inflates itself like a balloon.  Highly toxic; used to poison cats and dogs (Ref. 2861).

species.name: Compère de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Compère Diane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom (Ref. 9349).  Juveniles inhabit estuaries (Ref. 9349).  Makes a loud grating noise (Ref. 3157).

species.name: Compère foutre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays, estuaries and protected coastal waters.  Feeds primarily on shellfish, also on some finfish (Ref. 3821).

species.name: Compère lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore and near-shore areas, over sand or mud bottoms.  Usually found alone or in small, loose aggregates.  Adults are pelagic, but near continental margins; young are commonly found on coastal and offshore banks (Ref. 7251).  Feeds on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).  Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.  Its flesh is very delicate; nevertheless, in certain region like the Pacific and the Indian Ocean, it is toxic (particularly the skin and the viscera) (Ref. 5377).  Poisonous, should not be eaten (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Compère lièvre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily an oceanic (Ref. 2850, 2683), pelagic species but may enter estuaries (Ref. 4919).  Feeds on crustaceans and squids (Ref. 10001).  Suspected responsible for fatal poisoning (Ref. 4919).  Should not be eaten (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Compère luisant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom of shallow coastal areas (Ref. 9349).

species.name: Compère marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms.

species.name: Compère pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral-rich areas of clear lagoon and seaward reefs, Ref. 48637.  Prefers oceanic localities (Ref. 48637). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on tips of branching corals and to a lesser extent on sponges, mollusks, bryozoans, tunicates, forams, algae, and detritus.

species.name: Compère pygmée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom (Ref. 9349).

species.name: Compère péruvien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom of shallow waters (Ref. 9349).

species.name: Compère rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore (incl.  semi-enclosed sea areas), and in estuaries (Ref. 11230).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Compère taché
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species found on soft bottom (Ref. 9349).  Carnivorous.

species.name: Compère vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms generally with vegetation such as Thalassia testudinum. Prefers turbid water (Ref. 9710). Feeds on marine invertebrates (Ref. 36453). Locally consumed but its visceral organs may be toxic.

species.name: Compère à bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in groups of 2 or 3 individuals but never in schools (Ref. 35237).  Inhabits shallow inshore waters usually on soft bottoms.  Frequently found in freshwater (Ref. 13608).  When threatened, it becomes inflated like a balloon, in order to ward off predators.  Carnivorous, feeding mainly on mollusks which crushes with its powerful teeth (Ref. 35237).  Of negligible commercial importance and usually not marketed (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Compère à nez long
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly caught in bays, estuaries and shallow coastal areas (Ref. 9349).

species.name: Compère à points blancs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow coastal waters, also in estuaries (Ref. 2683), bays and lagoons, as well as in offshore trawling stations.  Feeds on crabs, echinoids and mollusks (Ref. 10001).  Occurs over hard substrate (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Compère à taches blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit outer reef slopes to depths of at least 50 m, inner reef flats and lagoons.  Juveniles common in weedy areas of estuaries (Ref. 4919).  Also found in coastal bays and estuaries, usually near rocky reef or on sand-stretches between reefs with low algae-rubble reef to about 20 meters depth, or in shallow with sparse seagrass growth (Ref. 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Usually solitary and territorial on sandy to rubble areas.  Feed on fleshy, calcareous, or coralline algae, detritus, mollusks, tunicates, sponges, corals, zoanthid anemones, crabs, tube worms and echinoderms (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Compère à tête étroite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers just above the substrate in mixed areas of sand, gravel and boulder.  Buries in the sand at night (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Compère émoussé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy, muddy and rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Young are pelagic (Ref. 7251).  Feed mainly on squid.  In southeast Brazil captured between 50 and 145 m (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Comète coussut
species.description: Adults occur in mid-water or near the bottom; also near the surface (Ref. 5217).  They feed on smaller planktonic invertebrates, primarily copepods.  Maximum depth recorded from Ref. 57551. Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Comète fine
species.description: A predominately pelagic schooling species (Ref. 9283, 48635, 58302).  Occasionally seen in small groups along reef slopes adjacent to deep water in pursuit of zooplankton (Ref. 48635).  Adults feed mainly on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Comète indienne
species.description: Adults dwell from middle to benthic (Ref. 11230), forming large schools in deep water, but occasionally inshore in sheltered bays in small to large groups (Ref. 48635). The most common Decapterus in coastal waters and on open banks of the Indian Ocean. They feed mainly on smaller planktonic invertebrates. Generally marketed fresh, may be dried or salted. Also sold frozen and canned (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Comète japonaise
species.description: Adults are found in the sublittoral zone and may enter semi-enclosed sea areas (Ref. 11230).  In Guam, it is encountered in large numbers around fish aggregating devices, buoys anchored offshore to attract pelagic game fishes.

species.name: Comète maouane
species.description: Adults are found in deep waters.  They feed on small planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 5213).  Occasionally seen in small groups along reef slopes at moderate depths.  Mainly known from trawls and shows red tail after capture (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Comète mexicaine
species.description: Adults are pelagic (Ref. 58302), in oceanic and inshore waters (Ref. 9563) forming schools (Ref. 9283).  They feed mainly on planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Comète ruban
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found inshore and in coastal waters throughout its range.  Feed mainly on planktonic crustaceans and larval fishes.  Marketed fresh and dried salted.

species.name: Comète à grandes nageoires
species.description: Adults are found near reefs, and in caves and crevices along drop-offs (Ref. 8631). A nocturnal species that hides under ledges and in holes by day (Ref. 9710). They possess a false eye which is actually the dorsal fin ocellus confuses predators because it poses an inverted image of a fish.  When alarmed, this fish will poke it's head into a hole and expose its tail end which mimics the head of the moray eel (Ref. 9710).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35426).  Reported to be living in a marine aquarium for 8 years and 6 months (Danilo Ronchi, Italy, pers.comm. 2014 February).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Coméphore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer deep waters but females and occasionally males may be found on the surface. Depth of distribution in January and February is 150-250 m; 100-120 m in March and April. Adults feed mainly on the amphipod Macrohectopus branickii. Mature individuals spawn in July to October. Fat content of the body is about 25%. The dead fish does not sink but float up to the surface and freeze into ice. In spring, they are cast ashore by the waves (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Conasauga logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and flowing pools of Conasauga River, a small, fast flowing river (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Concave goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in both large turbid lowland rivers and relatively steep gradient tributaries in mountainous terrain (Ref. 2847).  Occurs in clear, flowing streams over gravel or rock bottoms (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Feeds mainly on insects and crustaceans (Ref. 5259, 44894).

species.name: Concertina fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, on sand or mud bottoms, reefs, estuaries and harbors.  Maximum depth for this species is less than 50 m.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5213).  Breeds close inshore during spring (Ref. 5324).  Flesh edible, but not esteemed (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Conchfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers clear insular waters of oceanic islands (Ref. 9626). Has a commensal relationship with the conch shell Lobatus gigas (where it is found in the mantle cavity) and with the bivalve Atrina rigida (Ref. 9626). Emerges at night from the conch shell to feed on small crustaceans. Males brood the eggs in their mouths. (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Conchos chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conchos darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conchos pupfish
species.description: Occurs in sloughs, backwaters, and margins of small to medium rivers (avoiding hot springs).  5 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Concombre
species.description: Inhabits marine waters, estuaries and large lakes (Ref. 59043).  A midwater species, rarely far from shore, primarily anadromous in the west and lacustrine in the east; shoaling at least during spawning season (Ref. 4545).  The essential part of its life is spend in the estuarine zone, with just short incursions in the littoral zone (Ref. 51442).  The migratory form is grouping together in the estuarine zone for reproduction (Ref. 51442).  Enters the rivers for spawning on sandy or gravely bottoms (Ref. 13696).  Spawns in tributaries of lakes or along shallow shores of lakes and rivers on sand, gravel, stones and plant material, preferably in fast-flowing water (Ref. 59043).  Reproduction takes place between February and May, depending on the water-temperature (Ref. 51442).  Produces 8,000-50,000 yellow eggs with a diameter of 0.6-0.9 mm which adhere to the bottom (Ref. 13696, Ref. 51442).  Eggs hatch in 3-5 weeks and the larvae descend to the estuarine zone (Ref. 13696, Ref. 51442).  Feeds on shrimps and small crustaceans; larger individuals feed on small fish (Ref. 30578, Ref. 51442).  Utilized as foodfish, smoked, as bait and fish oil (Ref. 35388).  Smells like cucumber (Ref. 37032, 51442).  Locally threatened due to pollution and barriers to migration (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Conde's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Relatively common on sloping rubble bottoms (Ref. 31120).

species.name: Conesnout grenadier
species.description: Feeds primarily on fish (including Bregmaceros) and squid, but polychaetes and Pagurids crabs have also been found in the stomach (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Confused podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs around rocky areas.

species.name: Conger erebennus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conger jordani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conger macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conger monganius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conger oligoporus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in crevices of hard substrata (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Conger philippinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congiopodus kieneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congo barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congo ctenopoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congo killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only known from brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Congo squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congo tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small insects, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51150).

species.name: Congocharax olbrechtsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congochromis dimidiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from larger rivers and lakes (Ref. 72415). Pair-bonding, biparental, cave-spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Congochromis pugnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congochromis robustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congochromis sabinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from small rainforest streams (Ref. 72415). Monogamous, biparental, cave spawning, substrate spawner (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Congochromis squamiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in larger rivers and lakes (Ref. 72415).

species.name: Congoglanis alula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically found in fastest flowing portions of rivers and always associated with large rocks; appears to congregate underneath rocks near where water breaks over the rocks during the day, and will move out onto the tops of rocks at night (Ref. 88958).

species.name: Congoglanis howesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the rapids of the Luachimo River (Ref. 92838).

species.name: Congoglanis inga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species has been collected from "a long channel with moderate current, numerous pools and a predominantly rocky bottom" (Ref. 42510, 88958).

species.name: Congoglanis sagitta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Congoglanis sagitta is typically found in the fastest flowing portions of rivers and are always associated with large rocks; they appear to congregate underneath rocks near where water breaks over the rocks during the day, and will move out onto the tops of rocks at night (Ref. 88958).

species.name: Congolapia bilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swampy forested zones (Ref. 52307) in grass-bank as well as forest-bank habitats, during the dry as well as the wet season (Ref. 92878). Pair-bonding, open substratum spawner with both parents guarding their fry (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Congolapia crassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Congolapia crassa is found in grass-bank as well as forest-bank habitats, and this during the dry as well as wet season (Ref. 92878).

species.name: Congolapia louna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in fast flowing water over a sandy bottom (Ref. 92878).

species.name: Congolli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and estuaries.  Inhabits slow-flowing water around log snags, under over-hanging banks or among leaf litter (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Adult fish migrate downstream to spawn in weedy estuaries from late April to August (Ref. 5259).  Feeds on insects, crustaceans, mollusks, worms and fishes (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Often buries itself in the substrate to ambush passing prey.  A highly efficient osmo-regulator, able to withstand direct transfer from salt to fresh water without any indication of stress.  Good eating, but too small to be considered a prime angling target (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Congre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in rocky places.  A carnivore that feeds on fish and crabs (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Congre (Paraconger notialis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottom (Ref. 26999).  Burrows into the substratum tail-first, with only the head exposed (Ref. 3597).

species.name: Congre argentin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 27363).  Feeds on fishes, shrimps, crabs and mollusks.

species.name: Congre aux anneaux blancs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms big colonies on sandy areas near reefs (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on zooplankton suspended in the water column (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Congre bec-fin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy or sandy bottoms of the continental slope.  Adults feed on benthic invertebrates and probably small fishes.

species.name: Congre crin
species.description: A deep-water species living on the continental slope (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Congre d' Evermann
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Congre de Californie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congre de Gilbert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand flats, often in protected bays and coves.  Can bury and move about beneath sand.  Often bury during the day and forage in the open at night (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Congre de plage
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic waters of the continental shelf; not observed around oceanic islands (Ref. 5217).  Found on muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Congre de sable argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal sandy and muddy bottoms (also Ref. 11230).

species.name: Congre de sable à barres sombres
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A colorful congrid that lives beneath the sand of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Congre de Trewawas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims close to the bottom in zigzag movements.  Caught by traps and trammel nets (Ref. 7446).

species.name: Congre dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly around islands.  Benthic (Ref. 26340) on hard, rocky or coral bottoms (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Congre denté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Congre des Baléares
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the shelf, littoral, burrowing in galleries on sandy mud bottoms.  Carnivorous.  (Ref. 6521).

species.name: Congre du Pacifique nord-ouest
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on coasts of Japan, in sandy-muddy bottoms (also Ref. 11230); most relished among the congrids.  Captured and cultured for fishery in Japan.

species.name: Congre du talus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congre gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore, on soft sandy mud (Ref. 305730 and in coastal areas with sandy bottoms (Ref. 5213).  Benthopelagic or benthic at 622-704 m (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on small benthic crustaceans (Ref. 9603).

species.name: Congre gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 26340) found in rocky areas or coral reefs (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on fishes.  Marketed fresh and salted.

species.name: Congre jardinier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottom, living in colonies (Ref. 26938).  Feed on plankton and detritus (Ref. 26938).  They retreat into burrow when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Probably spawn during warm season (Ref. 6521).  Larval life spans 6-8 months (Ref. 6521).

species.name: Congre jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters (Ref. 10713).  May occur in crevices of steep drop-offs in as little as 25 m (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Congre jaune (Rhynchoconger flavus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26340).  Found on soft bottoms.

species.name: Congre noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats, clear shallow lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans during both day and night (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Congre oiro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary species common on reef flats and seagrass beds of shallow lagoons but ranges to depths of 80 m on outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602).  Also found in estuaries (Ref. 5213). Feeds on fish and crustaceans at night, assuming a pattern of broad dark grey bars (Ref. 11441).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Congre ponctué
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congre pâle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms big colonies on sandy bottom near reefs (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on zooplankton suspended in the water column (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Congre tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits crevices (Ref. 5503). Minimum depth based of 20m (Ref. 81209).

species.name: Congre tacheté (Gymnothorax nudivomer)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in oceanic locations (Ref. 48635). Adults are found inhabiting inner and outer reef slopes (Ref. 30404).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Mucus is toxic (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Congre à grand nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congre à grosses lèvres
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are secretive and bottom-dwelling and prefer soft substrata where they can burrow with their tails (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, with planktonic leptocephali (Ref. 35590).

species.name: Congre à queue courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Congre à queue rigide
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A soft bottom inhabitant.  Reported to burrow into loose sand, and appears to be fairly resistant to chemical preparations used for collecting fish (Ref. 2850).  Bottom feeding predators devour conger eels when encountered in the open (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Congre à tache noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the shelf on sandy areas of rocky sublittoral zone.  Burrows in the sediment during the day and swims actively at night in search of prey (Ref. 6521).

species.name: Congre á museau aigu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from shallow inshore waters to depths of 477 m and up to 260 m in the Gulf of Maine (Ref. 7135).  Benthic (Ref. 5951).  Nocturnal predators  (Ref. 93252). Feeds mainly on fishes, but also on shrimps and small shellfish.  Commonly caught by anglers along piers, docks and jetties in middle Atlantic states.

species.name: Congre-brochet féroce
species.description: Found on the shelf on sand and muddy bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Larger individuals caught mainly in 75-100 m depth (Ref. 26999).  Carnivorous.

species.name: Congre-brochet à dents de sabre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the littoral zone to the upper bathy-benthic region (Ref. 9942, 11230).  Inhabits soft bottoms (Ref. 11230), also found in estuaries.  Sometimes enters freshwater environment (Ref. 9987).  Feeds on small bottom fishes and crustaceans.  Captured and cultured for fishery in Japan.  Marketed mainly fresh (Ref. 7238).  Also used as bait for shark fishing (Ref. 2872).  Also caught by bag (dol) nets.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Congrhynchus talabonoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congriperle arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species ranging from the shore to 86 m depth (Ref. 34024).  Found in rubble bottoms (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs benthically, from 210-307 m in the Gulf of California and 73-293 m on the outer coast (Ref. 91765).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle auriculaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024) found in mangrove areas, on muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle cornu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024) found on muddy bottom (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024) inhabiting sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9329).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Biology little known (Ref. 9329).

species.name: Congriperle strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found from near shore to 75 m depth (Ref. 34024).  Inhabit bottoms with fine sand, mud, rubble or marine plants, at moderate depths (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Frequently caught by  shrimp trawlers (Ref. 9329).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Congriperle tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Adults inhabit soft bottoms, from shallow waters to moderate depths (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle à grande tête
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Adults inhabit sandy bottoms of the continental shelf, up to a depth of 91 m (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Congriperle à nageoire tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024) inhabiting soft bottom (Ref. 9329).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Little is known of this species (Ref. 9329).

species.name: Congriscus maldivensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Congriscus marquesaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Congriscus megastoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conguito sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conidens samoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conocara bertelseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conocara paxtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conorhynchos conirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Conspicuous angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally inhabits deep coral reef areas.  Juveniles as shallow as 1 m on lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Forms pairs.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Constellationfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic, with marked stratification of size with depth (Ref. 4739). Generally non-migrant or only short diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4739). A selective daytime feeder on copepods (mainly Pleuromamma and ostracods, Conchoecia) (Ref. 4739). Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: CONSTITUTION
