species.description: Espèce de poissons. Off Venezuela, Caribbean Sea, 11°40'N, 62°33'W, 585-622 m.

species.name: Conta catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky streams at the bases of hills.

species.name: Conta pectinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from shallow (10-30 cm) and moderately clear water with pebbles, cobbles of variable colours and sand particles, at an altitude of 127m. Associated species: Aborichthys elongatus, Acanthocobitis botia, Amblyceps mangois, Barilius barna, B. bendelisis, Balitora brucei, Botia rostrata, Chanda nama, Crossocheilus latius, Garra annandalei, G. gotyla, Neolissochilus hexagonolepis, Pseudolaguvia shawi, Psilorhynchus balitora, Puntius ticto, Schistura savona and Tor tor (Ref. 89475).

species.name: Contusus brevicaudus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually observed in estuaries to about 20 m (Ref. 9002).  Nocturnal (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Convex sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies different habitats, where 3 individuals were taken from 3 different areas a coral reef, a rock wall in a small boat harbor, or from a large surge channel which is fully exposed to the open sea (Ref. 97766).

species.name: Convict blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow lagoon and coastal reefs (Ref. 9710, 48635). Forms schools that are often found under ledges or around coral heads (Ref. 9710). Swim in tight formation to look like a single large body (Ref. 48635). Juveniles resemble the venomous striped catfish Plotosus lineatus. Adults live secretively in reefs and have a barred or spotted color pattern (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Convict goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Convict julie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Likes to live in the open and ventures quite a lot over sand in the shallows (Ref. 6770).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Convict snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A burrowing species of inshore, soft bottom areas (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Convict zebra sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms; feeds on bottom living invertebrates (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Coné bande
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs; also along rocky shores (Ref. 5222).  A shy and secretive species (Ref. 5222). Feeds on fishes and crustaceans; reaches at least 25 years; recently confirmed as a protogynous hermaphrodite, spawning peaks in July and August in the Gulf of California (Ref. 089707).

species.name: Coné dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on semi-hard bottom.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Coné essaim
species.description: Poisson. Inhabits Thalassia beds and coral reefs. In the Gulf of Mexico, they are found on rocky reef ledge in depths greater than 27 m. Solitary (Ref. 26340) and secretive, they usually stay near hiding places during the day. Prefer to remain within a small area of the home range of about 2,120 square m especially during the day (Ref. 56524). Nocturnal predators, adults feed mainly on fishes, with preference on Chromis multilineata, while juveniles feed on shrimps. Due to its small size, this is not a particularly sought-after species. Easily approached and fed by divers (Ref. 9710). Protogynous (Ref. 26938). Between 1995 and 2000, at least 10 specimens have been traded as aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Coné grand œil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over hard bottoms.

species.name: Coné langue rugueuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found on outer continental shelf reefs.  They primarily feed on zooplankton while common in the diet of larger predators like snappers and groupers (Ref. 96848).

species.name: Coné ouatalibi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer coral reefs and clear water.  In the Gulf of Mexico, they are found in clear deep reefs (at least 45 m).  At Bermuda and the West Indies, they are common in shallow water, but they usually hide in caves or under ledges during the day.  The species is protogynous with females maturing at 16 cm TL and transforming to males at about 20 cm.  Males are territorial.  Feed mainly on small fishes and crustaceans.  May follow morays and snake eels to feed on flushed preys.  Wary, but approachable (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Cook Islands Flashlightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Cook's cardinalfish
species.description: Found close to ledges of rocky areas or coral reefs during the day (Ref. 559).  Subtidal zone to depths of about 10 m (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cook's rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cooke's sandburrower
species.description: Found in sand along shores exposed to wave action or in the spur and groove zone. Feeds on chironomid insects (56%), amphipods Amphilocus menehune, Cymadusa hawaiiensis, Grammaropsis atlantica, and unidentified gastropod (Ref. 86689).

species.name: Cook’s swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coolie loach
species.description: Poisson. Lives in hill streams to lowland forest canals and peats (Ref. 57235).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Well known in aquarium trades as "Kuhli's loach" (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Cooman's grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and in estuaries, but the extent of its movements into the sea and up rivers is not known.  Rare in museum collections but this may not reflect its actual abundance.

species.name: Cooper creek catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in larger, more permanent waterholes with an earth and clay substrate (Ref. 27663, 44894).  Significant flow occurs only after severe rainfall events, water is typically very turbid.  Very aggressive towards other fishes, particularly in captivity.  Feeds on gastropods and crustaceans.  Has the largest egg size (3-4 mm) and lowest fecundity (about 1000 eggs per spawning) per unit length of any plotosid catfish in Australia (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Cooper’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coosa chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, moderately large flowing streams with a sand, gravel, or fine rubble bottom above the Fall Line in the Cahaba, Coosa and Tallapoosa river systems (Ref. 116539).

species.name: Coosa darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on midge and blackfly larvae, supplemented with cladocera, copepods, mayfly nymphs, and caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Coosa shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, gravel-bottomed pools and runs, but common in spring-fed streams (Ref. 5723).  Also inhabits small creeks and rivers (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Copadichromis atripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sand/rock interface; territorial males construct bowers on sand slopes near rocky areas with distances between bowers approximately 2-7m; females gather in large schools, sometimes numbering more than a hundred individuals; foraging schools are about 2-3m off the bottom and feed on plankton in the water column and on benthic invertebrates; mouthbrooding females are found close to the bottom (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis azureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sand/rock interface; territorial males defend their bower with a bowl in front of a spawning cave that spans about half a circle or less, about 19-33cm in diameter; females gather in small groups or are solitary, and feed from the plankton and benthic invertebrates near the bottom (Ref. 57549). Aquarium trade names: 'Haplochromis chrysonotus mbenji', 'Haplochromis chrysonotus maleri' (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Copadichromis chizumuluensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males build bowers at the sand-rock interface at depths of 12-20m; females form small groups; feeds on plankton in the water column and on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis chrysonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore waters and feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 267).  Mouthbrooder (Ref. 94785).

species.name: Copadichromis cyaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only found over sediment-free rocks in clear water (Ref. 5595).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 267).

species.name: Copadichromis cyanocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores; territorial males defend bowers at depths of 15-22m; females occur in small groups and normally stay within a meter from the bottom (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis diplostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Territorial males construct bowers at the sand-rock interface at depths of 12-18m; females and immature males form small groups and feed on plankton in the water column and on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis flavimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly caught on sandy beaches, and feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Copadichromis geertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Copadichromis ilesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with rocks (Ref. 54524).  Males build their spawning sites at depths of approximately 25 meters or deeper; females, in particular mouth brooding females, can be found in shallower water, but they rarely venture into regions shallower than 10 meters (Ref. 47113).

species.name: Copadichromis insularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand/rock interface and over sandy patches around the islands, between 13 and 18m; territorial males build spawning bowl from beneath flat rocks; spawning occurs underneath the rock; females and non-territorial males occur in small groups (up to 10 individuals) and feed on plankton in the water column 1-3 m above the bottom (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis jacksoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in sheltered bays with deep water and forms schools in the open water of the bay, and feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Copadichromis likomae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 267).  Forms schools (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Copadichromis melas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sand/rock interface along the lake shore; territorial males build their bowers at depths of 10-15m; females commonly occur solitarily or in small groups of 3-4 individuals; both males and females feed on plankton near the bottom and on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis mloto
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools (Ref. 2788).

species.name: Copadichromis nkatae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs around rocks and over sandy beaches and feeds mainly on zooplankton, but also takes phytoplankton (Ref. 267).

species.name: Copadichromis parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Territorial males are found at depths of 11-23 m and build bowers by excavating sand from beneath rocks; females and non-territorial males feed in the open water column 1-3 m above the bottom and on benthic invertebrates; mouth-brooding females occur solitarily and stay close to the substrate (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis pleurostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Copadichromis trewavasae
species.description: Inhabits the sand/rock interface (Ref. 47113, 57549) where sand and rocks are found in almost equal proportions (Ref. 47113). Territorial males construct a bower next to a rock, under which spawning takes place; females normally occur in small groups rarely numbering more than 10 individuals and remain close to the bottom (Ref. 57549). Mouthbrooding females remain closer to the bottom than foraging females and sometimes form small groups (Ref. 47113). Both males and females feed on plankton in the water column near the bottom and on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copadichromis verduyni
species.description: Lives in the sand/rock interface; among congeners, this species defends the least-visible spawning sites; most males defend spawning sites at depths of 9-15m; females and non-territorial males feed from the plankton in the water colmun 1-3m off the bottom and on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Copella carsevennensis
species.description: Lives in groups at the surface of small creeks with clear waters. Also found in ponds where it is found together with Rivulus (Ref. 27188). Feeds on Ephemeroptera larvae and ants. The spawned eggs are deposited on submerged leaves and are guarded by the males (Ref. 12225). During incubation, the male oxygenates the eggs (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Copella metae
species.description: Found in weedy river bays.

species.name: Cophecheilus brevibarbatus
species.description: Type specimens were collected in a large 10 m depth pool by gill net; water flow out from a hole at the bottom of the pool; the artificial pool have been built 1995; water of the pool had pH 7.7, water temperature 28.9 °C and dissolved oxygen 13.4 mg·1-1 at 20 cm under surface; and 23.2 °C and 7.4 mg·l-1, respectively, at 2 m depth (Ref. 103410).

species.name: Copionodon elysium
species.description: Collected from a stream with slow-flowing water running over rocky bottom or boulders, with rifﬂes and shallow pools 10-30 cm deep and 1-3 m wide (Ref. 118359).

species.name: Copper rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Particularly abundant in shallow, protected bays and inlets, among rocks and kelp beds; also found around pilings and jetties or under floats (Ref. 27436).  Juveniles found in loose aggregations in shallow weedy bays, around wharfs, or among floating drift associated with summer tidelines (Ref. 27436).  Mainly a benthic feeder, may also take pelagic fishes (Ref. 27436).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Flesh is tasty, firm and flaky (Ref. 27436).  Sold mainly as fresh fillets or live in Chinese restaurants and fish markets; excellent for fish chips or for pan frying as fillets (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Copper tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coppercheek darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, fast rocky riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on hydropsychid caddis larvae, midge larvae, mayfly nymphs, blackfly larvae, and a wide variety of additional aquatic insect immatures plus a few snails (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Coppernose barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Copperstripe barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, well-vegetated water in backwaters, floodplains and river margins (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Copperstripe rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Copperstriped cardinalfish
species.description: Forms aggregations. Found in coastal reefs, sometimes in silty areas, in 15-35 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Coptodon bakossiorum
species.description: Clearly prefers plant material, but also accepts detritus, sponges and phytoplankton (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding (Ref. 52307), open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260). Prefers to spawn in pits or shallow cavities in submerged wood; clusters of eggs fairly small in size, containing about 30 eggs; female usually guards the eggs while the male defends the territory (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon bemini
species.description: Smaller specimens primarily found between sunken pieces of trees near lake shore, while larger specimens are found at greater depth - between 3 and 8 m; feeds mainly on plants and small quantities of diatoms and insects (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260). Biparental species that constructs a nest at a depth between 1 and 5 m, usually on a muddy bottom; pit relatively large and normally surrounded by some smaller satellite pits; when threatened, females will often seek refuge in these pits while males tend to swim away to open water (Ref. 52307). Maximum size recorded is 8.7 cm TL (Ref. 5163).

species.name: Coptodon bythobates
species.description: Prefers to live at depths greater than 8 m; seems to have adapted to greater depths and reduced dissolved oxygen levels; feeds mainly upon vegetative materials (higher plants and algae (Ref. 52307). Probably a pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon cameronensis
species.description: Substrate brooder (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Coptodon camerunensis
species.description: Probably pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon coffea
species.description: Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon congica
species.description: Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon dageti
species.description: Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon deckerti
species.description: Pair-bonding, open substrate brooder/spawner with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307, 81260). It breeds in shallow water above 2 m water depth, where pairs excavate shallow pits often close to stones, branches or similar structures (Ref. 85854). Coptodon cf. deckerti observed to primarily feed upon zooplankton, copepods and small amounts of insect larvae; juveniles were observed nibbling on fins of Sarotherodon species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon discolor
species.description: Mainly herbivorous, but also takes small amounts of crustaceans and insects (Ref. 52307). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307, 55659). Eggs are laid and incubated in nests (Ref. 55659).

species.name: Coptodon ejagham
species.description: Pairs breed exclusively in the shallow inshore region above 2 m; pairs excavate large nest-pits under large branches or logs (Ref. 85854). Non-breeding Coptodon ejagham are moving solitarily and are and appear to permanently scan their environment for prey while swimming permanently without a hast, and rarely being motionless (Ref. 85854). Observations suggest that this species are predators of small fish, mostly juvenile cichlids (Ref. 85854).

species.name: Coptodon flavus
species.description: Feeds primarily on phytoplankton, but also accepts higher plants and sponges (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307). Prefers to spawn at depths of 1-2 m; eggs are normally deposited on sunken pieces of wood; occasionally, colonies consisting of about 10 pairs have been found, with pairs separated from each other by about 30 cm; pairs defending juveniles collectively have been observed, which might be an indication of cooperative broodcare (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon fusiforme
species.description: Deepwater specimens primarily feed on planktonic organisms in the open water column; inshore specimens pick on small particles from substrate and feed on allochtonous matter from water surface (Ref. 85854). The 'little-black' form breeds in all depth zones; the 'large-black' form breeds preferentially in log-holes of dead wood in the shallow region above 1 m (Ref. 85854).

species.name: Coptodon gutturosus
species.description: Prefers sponges, but small amounts of diatoms, plants (mostly algae) and detritus have also been found in their stomachs (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder/spawner (Ref. 52307, 81260) with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307). Usually spawns in shallow waters, building colonies of up to 6 pairs separated by about 30 cm; eggs are hidden between leaves and pieces of wood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon imbrifernus
species.description: Prefers a herbivorous diet, especially phytoplankton which might be taken from the water column and not from the substrate; primarily found near the lake shore, forming stable pairs and preferring to spawn on sunken wood or on stones (Ref. 52307). Substrate brooder (Ref. 81260). Both parents guard their brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon konkourensis
species.description: The very slender body in combination with a rounded head shape and slightly retrognathous jaws suggests that it is a benthic-rheophilic species, modified for life in rapids (Ref. 90097).

species.name: Coptodon kottae
species.description: Diet primarily consists of plants and small particles like detritus and aufwuchs; pair-bonding; prefers to spawn in obscured places, like crevices in sunken wood; both parents diligently guard eggs and fry (Ref. 52307). Substrate brooder (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Coptodon louka
species.description: Seems to prefer brackish regions and coastal lagoons; probably has a high tolerance for elevated salinity levels; herbivorous; pair-bonding, open substrate spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon margaritacea
species.description: Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon nigrans
species.description: This species breeds exclusively in excavated caves below 5 m depth (Ref. 85854).

species.name: Coptodon nyongana
species.description: Substrate brooder (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Coptodon rheophila
species.description: Rheophilic species (Ref. 53405). Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon snyderae
species.description: Feeds primarily on vegetative matter (preferably algae), but also takes detritus, insects, diatoms and small amounts of sponges (Ref. 52307). A dwarf species, with females reaching sexual maturity at 25 mm SL, making this the smallest tilapiine known (Ref. 26738, 52307). The number of eggs produced is accordingly small, with 10-20 eggs usually deposited, preferably in shallow water on various substrates; large colonies composed of many pairs have been observed (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substratum brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood and fry (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon spongotroktis
species.description: Feeds mainly on freshwater sponges, but also filamentous algae, phytoplankton and small amounts of insects (Ref. 52307). Substrate brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260). Probably pair-bonding, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon thysi
species.description: Feeds primarily upon plants (especially algae), diatoms and insects (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307)substrate brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260), with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptodon walteri
species.description: Mainly herbivorous, but also takes small amounts of insects; pair-bonding, biparental, open substrate spawner that builds large, deep pits on the river bottom (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Coptostomabarbus bellcrossi
species.description: Maximum recorded total length is 3.4 cm (Ref. 93834).

species.name: Coquette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the  algal zone of rocky shores (Ref. 35388).  Usually solitary or in pairs with young.  Females lay about 1,000 eggs in a nest of algae; the nest is guarded by the male (Ref. 35388).  Feed mainly on crustaceans but also fishes and mollusks (Ref. 4742) and worms (Ref. 35388).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Coradion à bandes orange
species.description: Found in coastal to outer reef drop-offs with rich invertebrate growth to 60 m depth; may also occur in areas with sparse coral growth.  Feed on sponges (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Coradion à grandes nageoires
species.description: A poorly known species (Ref. 4855).  Found in inshore reefs in mixed algae and coral habitats and coastal drop-offs (Ref. 48636). Uncommon (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Coral blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pockets of coral rubble on reefs or in tide pools.

species.name: Coral demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and inshore coral reefs, usually in areas where silting is prevalent.  Aggregates over coral outcrops to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Coral scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small patch reefs (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Coral sea gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Coral sea jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs inshore; inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Coral Sea perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coral sea stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coral siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered waters of lagoons and coastal inlets. Often seen in groups of approximately 30-40 individuals, hovering over pocilloporid coral Seriatopora hystrix (Ref. 11890).

species.name: Coral toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in or near rocky caves from 10-15 m depth.  Feeds on small fishes, snails and polychaete worms (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Coral worm eel
species.description: A shallow water species occurring from rock tide pools or coral reefs to 60 m depth (Ref. 104540).

species.name: Coralline sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky areas, intertidal and to 21 m depth.

species.name: Coralline-red flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Coralliozetus springeri
species.description: Inhabits empty worm and mollusk tubes on rocky reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Corazon's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs singly or in pairs, above sheltered low-lying reefs. It is unknown whether or not it is more widespread for previous surveys of Malagasy and western Indian Ocean reefs did not report the occurrence of this species (Ref. 120617).

species.name: Corb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters mainly on rocky and sandy bottoms, often entering estuaries and more active at night.  Also inhabits caves and reefs (Ref. 9987).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4780).  SCUBA diving observations suggest this to be a very calm fish with remarkable buoyancy control and an ability to move without much apparent effort (Ref. 9505).  Marketed fresh and frozen; in Turkey, otoliths are ground to a powder and used as remedy for urinary tract infections (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Corbine longnez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Corcyrogobius lubbocki
species.description: Occurs over rocky bottom or caves (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Cordonnier blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters and generally in schools of 50 to several hundred individuals; prefers protected areas.  Feeds by grazing on algae.

species.name: Cordonnier bossu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults solitary in coastal water near the bottom to at least 50 m and strong swimmers (Ref. 7079, 57392).  Juveniles usually pelagic and drifting, sometimes occurring in brackish water (Ref. 4225, 57392).  Feed on squid and other fishes (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Cordylancistrus nephelion
species.description: Inhabits rivers with transparent waters, moderate to strong flow and bottom generally consisting of stone, gravel and sand (Ref. 56900).

species.name: Cordylancistrus perijae
species.description: Collected from mountain rivers associated to humid tropical areas.  From transparent waters, with strong to moderate current with river beds formed by rocks, small stones and sand, scarce or absent aquatic vegetation (Ref. 40935).

species.name: Cordylancistrus pijao
species.description: Occurs in quebrada Aguas Blancas which has a gravel and sand bottom, and in the area of its mouth in the Cuide Blanco River, mainly with moderate-sized rocks that allow the formation of small backwaters; average temperature is 18° C, with a slightly basic pH (8.1) and moderate conductivity (192.8 µS). The area is characterized by the presence grazing zones and small coffee farms. The original forests have been felled, and zones at different stages of secondary succession are found. At the stream’s mouth, are some large trees (common name caracolí) and some shrubs (Ref. 117343).

species.name: Coregonus albellus
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep water. Spawns in September, at 30-100 m depth. Spawns for the first time at about 120 mm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus alpinus
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep water. Feeds on benthic invertebrates, especially chironomids. Spawns in August - December, at 40-150 m deep, mainly near torrent deltas (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus arenicolus
species.description: Lacustrine, near flat shores, or near bottom, sometimes on steep slopes. Inhabits and spawns in shallow coastal areas (Ref. 13696). Feeds on benthic invertebrates (especially mussels and snails). Spawns in shallow water along shores (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus atterensis
species.description: Pelagic, usually at depths of 10-30 m.  Feeds on zooplankton and small amounts of benthic invertebrates.  Spawns in open water close to surface, above depths of 20-40 m (Attersee) or at 2-3 m and close to shore (Mondsee). Spawns for the first time at 4 (Attersee) or 3 years (Mondsee). Spawns in early February - mid March (Attersee), late December - mid January (Mondsee).  Individual fishes usually spawn 2-3 seasons. Eggs sink to bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus austriacus
species.description: Feeds on deep-water zooplankton.  Spawns at depths of 80-120 m (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus baerii
species.description: Adults occur in deeper places while alevins and juveniles mostly found along eastern shore.  Feeds on benthic organisms such as crustaceans, insect larvae and mollusks. Used to migrate to River Volkhov up to its uppermost reaches for spawning, now blocked by a dam. Migrates to eastern coast before spawning, starting in May - June. Spawns in October - early November. In Volkhov, used to spawn high upstream, in riffles. Information about spawning in lake is sparse, but continued presence confirms lacustrine reproduction. Spawning is now assumed to occur in Volkhov estuary, probably also in lower River Svir  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus baicalensis
species.description: Spawning takes place in December and January in the lake (Ref. 593).

species.name: Coregonus bavaricus
species.description: Spawns on bottom at depths of 40-50 m, usually between mid June - mid July (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus confusus
species.description: Lacustrine, deep waters. Spawns in December to January in Lake Morat on sand or mud at 35-40 m. depth, in Lake Bienne on slopes, at 2-20 m. depth (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus danneri
species.description: Recorded from 40-60 m, up to surface in summer. Spawns close to shore. Spawns for the first time at 2 years from mid October - early March (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus duplex
species.description: Inhabits close to bottom of lakes.  Feeds on snails, worms and insects.  Spawns in late November in very shallow water, over stones close to surf zone (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus fatioi
species.description: Lacustrine, in midwater. Spawns in December, along shores at 0-30 m depth. In both Lakes Thun and Brientz, there are forms (?) of this species spawning as deep as 70 m, some with a deeper body. They were reportedly more distinct earlier and had more distinct spawning seasons. The original pattern might have been blurred by hybridization with introduced species (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus fontanae
species.description: Found in lakes, inhabiting deep water layers of 20-60 m. Undertakes migration above 20 m at night (Ref. 59043). Most abundant below 20 m depth (Ref. 52872). Syntopic with Coregonus albula in Lake Stechlin (Ref. 52872). Feeds mainly on Cladocera and Copepoda (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus gutturosus
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep water. Feeds on benthic invertebrates (especially mussels and snails). Spawns in 10-60 m. depth. After spawning migrates to deeper places, at depths of up to about 140 m. Migrates to 50-60 m in March - April (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus heglingus
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep waters. Feeds on plankton in midwater and on benthic invertebrates (snails, chironomids). Spawns near shores at depths of 20-80 m. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus hoferi
species.description: Feeds on zooplankton and small insects. Spawns in shallow water 1-5 m deep, on gravel or rock bottom, mid November - early January, usually in first week of December (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus holsatus
species.description: Attains a maximum size of up to about 47 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus kiletz
species.description: Found in lakes at all depths.  Preys on zooplankton and small benthos during juvenile stage and switches to fish diet  at 17-20 cm SL.  Life span ranges from 7-9 years, with exceptional records up to 19 years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus ladogae
species.description: Occurs in lakes. Adults prey on fish, mostly Osmerus eperlanus, while juveniles feed on zoonplankton. Reaches sexual maturity at 2 years, 30 g for males, and 60-70 g for females. Hybridizes with other Coregonus species (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus lucinensis
species.description: A lacustrine species reported to inhabit deep water layers (20-58 m) and move to shallow waters to spawn (Ref. 59043). A small deep-water species with large eyes (Ref. 13696). Spawns April-July, usually May-June. Feeds mainly on chironomids and Mysis relicta (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus lutokka
species.description: Prefers stone and gravel bottom. Feeds on benthos (insect larvae, molluscs and crustaceans), in summer usually moves to upper water layers to feed on zooplankton, especially Cladocera  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus maxillaris
species.description: Lacustrine, in deeper waters. Feeds on benthic invertebrates, especially gammarids, molluscs and insect larvae. Spawns on gravel to stone bottom, at 1-10 m depth (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus migratorius
species.description: Important food fish in the Lake Baikal.

species.name: Coregonus nilssoni
species.description: Lacustrine, pelagic. Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus nobilis
species.description: Lacustrine, pelagic. Feeds on crustaceans and at 5-30 m depth. In July to September, moves to depths of 80-200 m to spawn (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus pallasii
species.description: Lacustrine. Often enters rivers to spawn. Spawns in October - November, on gravel to stone bottom, near shores. Feeds on zooplankton and insects from surface. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus renke
species.description: Pelagic in surface layers. Feeds  mainly on zooplankton, rarely on benthic invertebrates. May consume large amounts of small fish in summer. Usually spawns above gravel or rocks on bottom or along shores. Spawns for the first time at 3 years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus trybomi
species.description: A lacustrine species which inhabits deep water (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus vandesius
species.description: A lacustrine species which occurs in open water. Gregarious, forming shoals. Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Entomostraca), supplemented by small insects. Spawns on gravel or stone shores (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus vessicus
species.description: A lacustrine species. Attains first sexual maturity at 2 years, males may spawn for the first time in their first year (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coregonus zuerichensis
species.description: Lacustrine, in midwater. Feeds on plankton. Spawns at depths of 12-100 m.

species.name: Coregonus zugensis
species.description: Lacustrine, pelagic feeder. Feeds on zooplankton and insect nymphs. Spawns at depths 20-80 m, along littoral slope (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Coreius septentrionalis
species.description: Found in lower and middle levels of water bodies with sluggish current in sandy and rocky substratum.  Usually found in shoals.  Hides beneath deep water rocks or in ponds in winter and migrates upstream in spring for breeding purposes (Ref. 45563).  Also known as "Yellow River pigeon fish" because of its economic value.  Large-bodied, rich in fat and delicious in taste, this fish is highly valued by local residents (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Corematodus shiranus
species.description: Found in the same habitat as its prey, Oreochromis, but can also be found over open sandy floors and sometimes near rocks or in the open water (Ref. 5595). Diet consists of scales from the caudal fins of shoaling species of Oreochromis (Ref. 267).

species.name: Corematodus taeniatus
species.description: Often seen with other sand-dwelling cichlids. Although it prefers shallow water, it may penetrate deeper layers as well. Feeds on small scales of fins and peduncle of haplochromines (Maravichromis sp.) (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Coreoleuciscus aeruginos
species.description: Usually occurs in rapids of streams (Ref. 100736).

species.name: Coreoperca kawamebari
species.description: Prefers clear, slow currents of the middle reaches of rivers.  Feeds on aquatic insects and small fishes.  Lays eggs on water plants in May and June.  Eggs and fry are guarded by the male.

species.name: Corfu dwarf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in freshwater spring and small brook flowing towards nearby lagoons; also in associated wetlands. No biological data available (Ref. 59043).   Is threatened due to water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Corfu toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species.  Adults inhabit swamps, lowland water courses with little current, lagoons, springs and associated wetlands (Ref. 26100).  Can tolerate salinity of up to 4 ppt in the wild and 46 ppt under laboratory conditions, but prefer freshwater.  They feed mainly on insects, especially chironomids (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to the introduction of other species and water abstraction (Ref. 26100).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Coris ballieui
species.description: Adults are benthopelagic over sand, rubble, and rocky areas (Ref. 9710, 58302).

species.name: Coris centralis
species.description: Relatively common in sand and low-profile patch reefs.  Courting males raise the black anterior part of their dorsal fin (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Coris hewetti
species.description: Found on rubble bottom or substrates with a mixture of sand and rock.  Feeds on small benthis invertebrates (Ref. 89972). During courtship, the male roam over a wide area; erect its dorsal fin, compress and expand the caudal fin, and changes its color (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Coris marquesensis
species.description: Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Corne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit mid-waters along steep outer lagoon and seaward reef drop-offs.  Also found along rocky shores (Ref. 30573, 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Usually in small groups but form large schools in oceanic locations or on reefs subject to strong currents (Ref. 48637).  Juveniles and subadults feed on benthic algae; adults feed on zooplankton.  Pair spawning has been observed.  Caught with nets (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Corne (Naso unicornis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit channels, moats, lagoon and seaward reefs with strong surge (Ref. 48637). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Typically occurring in small groups. Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102). Juveniles in shallow protected bays and harbours (Ref. 48637). Mainly diurnal, feed on coarse leafy brown algae like Sargassum. Pair-spawning has been observed. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cornelia's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cornette fluteau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur at depths greater than 30 m, along continental and insular margins (Ref. 36710), over rocky substrates (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 37955).  Marketed fresh, salted or dried and smoked but more frequently processed into fishmeal (Ref. 9301).

species.name: Cornette rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230); inhabits coastal areas over soft bottoms, usually at depths greater than 10 m (Ref. 30573).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on small fishes and shrimps (Ref. 3401).  Maximum length reported is 200 cm TL (Ref. 26999), however, no specimen over 100 cm is known to J.E. Randall (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Cornette à taches bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef habitats to a depth of at least 128 m, except in heavy surge areas.  Also found in sandy bottoms adjacent to reef areas (Ref. 36710), either solitary or in schools (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on small fishes, shrimps (Ref. 36327, 36710) and squids (Ref. 37816).  Probably marketed fresh, salted or dried or smoked but more often reduced to fish meal (Ref. 9301).

species.name: Cornette à taches bleues (Fistularia tabacaria)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) occurs over grass flats and reefs, and on hard and rocky bottoms (Ref. 5377).  Feeds on fishes, small crustaceans (Ref. 6557) or invertebrates.

species.name: Cornish jack
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles occur in marginal habitats, adults prefer deep quiet water between boulders and below overhangs, away from strong currents; also occurs beneath Salvinia mats and in river estuaries in Lake Kariba; juveniles prey on invertebrates, mainly shrimps and insect larvae (Ref. 7248, 52193). Adults/larger individuals are piscivorous (Ref. 28714), feeding on small cichlids, minnows and labeos (Ref. Ref. 7248, 52193). May live for 8 years or more; breeds in summer during the rainy season; mature females carry 25000 or more eggs (Ref. 7248, 52193). A fractional spawner (Ref. 10606, 10605). Affinities: M. breviceps.

species.name: Cornish sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky, seaweed covered shores, particularly among small boulders. Most common in the intertidal zone amongst the algae Himanthalia and Laminaria (Ref. 4489).

species.name: Coroatá
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coromandel ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, apparently entering estuaries.  More data needed, based on better identifications than in the past.

species.name: Coromandel whipray
species.description: Found in inshore coastal waters (Ref. 30573). Typically found in estuarine habitats, but also reported from the Great Lake. The single record from the Great Lake may in fact refer to Dasyatis laosensis. Young and adults feed on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 124). Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates (Ref. 68964). May grow to a maximum of 140 cm disc length in the sea (Ref. 43081). Juveniles may be present in mangroves (Ref. 43081). Examined adult males 17.1 cm DW (32.0 cm TL) - 20.5 cm DW (39.8 cm TL); females 13.8 cm DW (25.6 cm TL) - 20.4 cm DW (39.6 cm TL); early juveniles (USNM 222564, immature male 12.0 cm DW and female 8.8 cm DW) have lost umbilical scars. Reported maximum disc width 30.0 cm (Ref. 11312) was found excessive (Ref. 130662).

species.name: Corona rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not very well known.

species.name: Corroncho
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Corrugated darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Corrugated pipefish
species.description: Found on coral reefs of inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Live openly on muddy or silty substrates (Ref. 48635).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Males carry the eggs in their brood pouches (Ref. 205).

species.name: Corsula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cortez barnacle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cortez bonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cortez brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over sand, weed, and coral or rocky bottom; including tide pools.  A 55 mm SL female (USNM 322029) specimen contained about 150 eggs about 0.5 mm in diameter and 19 embryos, 6-8 mm TL, with two rows of 9-11 small pigment spots along dorsal and anal fin bases (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Cortez clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal (Ref. 31184), found around large boulders and vertical outcrops.  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Cortez hake
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Cortez pikeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cortez triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in the intertidal zone.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 11482).   Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Coruh trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear and moderately swift flowing water, with a substrate of sand and pebbles.  Prefers to inhabit middle stretches of the main branches of rivers and streams, sometime the lower stretches.  Also occurs in very short coastal streams (less than 5 km) and usually has not been encountered in intermediate size streams (5-35 km).  Moves to the sea or the lower stretches of streams and rivers after spawning, where it stays until about April-May, when temperatures of the water start to rise.  Possibly does not go far into the sea, but may stay in river mouths or at sea close to river mouths during winter.  Spawns in October-November.  Migrates upstreams in small groups of more than 10 individuals and probably comes back after breeding (Ref. 85599).

species.name: Corumba cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered primarily by the female parent (Ref. 47893).

species.name: Corumbataia britskii
species.description: Found in deforested areas in moderate to fast current streams and in association with aquatic macrophytes or in the submerged portion of marginal vegetation.  Feeds on filamentous blue-green algae, chlorophytes, diatoms and periderm (Ref. 57842).

species.name: Corumbataia liliai
species.description: Inhabits small stream, with low-flowing water. Found associated with marginal vegetation (Ref. 118639).

species.name: Corumbataia lucianoi
species.description: This species Inhabits large and fast-flowing water rivers. Found associated with marginal vegetation (Ref. 118639).

species.name: Corvina honnibe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commercially cultured in Japan.  Widespread in sandy and muddy places (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Corydoras brittoi
species.description: Found in small clear water stream (2-3 m wide and 0.5-2 m depth), with preserved riparian vegetation, swift water current, and bottom composed mainly of sand and dead leaves (Ref. 128862).

species.name: Corydoras froehlichi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Corydoras hephaestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on substrate with sand and dead leaves (Ref. 111516).

species.name: Corydoras nain
species.description: So far, only about ten specimens have been collected of this rare species.  Two were from a creek with moderate current, 0.5 to 3 m wide, shallow (20-50 cm depth) with sandy to sandy-muddy bottom and not so brightly illuminated (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Corydoras pavanelliae
species.description: Found in small clear water stream (2-3 m wide and 0.5-2 m depth), with preserved riparian vegetation, swift water current, and bottom composed mainly of sand and dead leaves (Ref. 128862).

species.name: Corydoras zawadzkii
species.description: Found in small stream (2-3 m wide and 0.5-1.8 m depth), with clear water, preserved riparian vegetation, and swift water current.  Bottom substrate composed mainly by sand and dead leaves (Ref. 110223).

species.name: Corymbophanes andersoni
species.description: In the main channel over gravel and cobble (Ref. 37093).

species.name: Corymbophanes kaiei
species.description: Found among cobble and submerged logs in sun-lit areas of swift riffles.

species.name: Coryogalops bretti
species.description: Small marine gobies living predominantly in calm water of estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 92840). Collected from an estuary.

species.name: Coryogalops guttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from shallow waters of a large inner lagoon, from the base of an isolated small coral patch (Ref. 97667).

species.name: Coryogalops nanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species were collected on a patch of rubble-sand bottom in less than one meter to 3 meters deep; found among shells sparsely covering the patch.  More material and data are needed to check the relationship of this species to shells and their use as shelters (Ref. 116571).

species.name: Coryogalops pseudomonospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected at the base of a small isolated coral patch at depth of 7-8 m in a large shallow-water lagoon which is characterized by mixture of isolated coral reefs and broad flats covered with coral patches and sand.  This species was collected at the island where reef flat ends by fringing reef with depth at base about 2-3 m, followed by moderate sandy slope that has scattered small coral patches down to 12-15 m (Ref. 97667).

species.name: Coryogalops tessellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from protected waters; sand to gravel substrate, with some rock, algae, or seagrass (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Coryphaenoides affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides alateralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides asper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides asprellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides camurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides castaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides dubius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides filamentosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides gypsochilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides hextii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides hoskynii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides lecointei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental rise area.

species.name: Coryphaenoides longicirrhus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides macrolophus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides marshalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides oreinos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on seamounts and guyots of the eastern Pacific (Ref. 11650).

species.name: Coryphaenoides orthogrammus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Coryphaenoides paramarshalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides semiscaber
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides sibogae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides spinulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A recent reference acknowledging the validity of this species is needed.

species.name: Coryphaenoides tydemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides woodmasoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphaenoides yaquinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Coryphopterus curasub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and rubble on a sloping area (Ref. 103699).

species.name: Coryphopterus venezuelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand or mud-sand bottoms.

species.name: Corythoichthys conspicillatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Corythoichthys insularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sexually mature at 8.2 cm SL (Ref. 5316).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Corégon de lac
species.description: Inhabits large lakes and large rivers and enters brackish water (Ref. 86798). Primarily a lake dweller (Ref. 27547).  Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Appears to be rather sedentary, at least in the Great Lakes (Ref. 27547).  Movement in large lakes generally consists of 4 stages:  movement from deep to shallow water in the spring; movement back to deep water in the summer as the shoal water warms; migration to shallow-water spawning areas in the fall and early winter; and post-spawning movement back to deeper water (Ref. 27547).  Forms separate populations in large lakes (Ref. 27547).  Adults feed mainly on aquatic insect larvae, mollusks and amphipods (Ref. 1091, 3849); also other fishes and fish eggs, including their own (Ref. 1998).  Extensive hatchery programs for the propagation have been carried out on the Great Lakes and other areas for years (Ref. 3746, 3849).  Valued for its meat as well as for its roe, which is made into an excellent caviar; utilized fresh, smoked, and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Corégone
species.description: Gregarious lacustrine forms (Ref. 2163) and anadromous estuarine forms, rarely in full saltwater.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans, or larger benthic crustaceans in brackish water.  Movement in water column as a function of zooplankton repartition (Ref. 2163). Spawns in gravel, near shore, in shallow water, in December (Ref. 59043).  Likely to benefit from environmental regulations in France passed on 8/12/88 (Ref. 2163).

species.name: Corégone blanc
species.description: Lacustrine and marine in open water. At sea, forages close to coast (Ref. 59043).  Forms pelagic schools in deeper lakes (Ref. 4779).  Spawns along shores, at 3-10 m depth, rarely to 22 m depth or just below surface. Spawns deeper in clear lakes and closer to surface in lakes with humic waters (Ref. 59043). Spawns on shallow sand or gravel substrate.  Anadromous in the Baltic.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 4779).

species.name: Corégone tschir
species.description: Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Lowland river and lakes (Ref. 59043) but most frequently in streams (Ref. 5723).  Lacustrine and estuarine anadromous forms exist (Ref. 593).  Alevins and juveniles feed on zooplankton, adults on benthos, mainly chironomid larvae and molluscs (Ref. 1998, 59043). Males reproduce for the first time in 4-8 years, females at 5-9. Adults start upstream migration in late July - August and reach spawning sites by October - November and spawn in stretches with swift current and sand-pebble bottom, often under ice. Spawning lasts 5-7 days and fish leave spawning site soon after, migrating downstream to overwinter in deeper places of lower stretches of rivers together with older juveniles. In spring, alevins drift from spawning sites downstream with flood-water and forage in floodplain lakes and oxbows where they remain until end of summer before moving to river or reaching maturity (if lakes are large enough and do not dry out). Widely used for aquaculture in eastern Europe (Ref. 59043). Flesh is highly esteemed (Ref. 1998). Sold fresh, dried, or smoked (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Cosmocampus coccineus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common among red algae and coral.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 7.8 cm SL.

species.name: Cosmocampus heraldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky reefs and sand bottoms.  Males may mature at 7 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cosmocampus retropinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit oceanic and coastal waters.  Known only from pelagic sub-adults taken in stramin nets or midwater trawls (Ref. 4509).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cosmochilus cardinalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits river with moderate water current and predominantly muddy bottom.

species.name: Cosmochilus falcifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers.

species.name: Cosmochilus harmandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from midwater to bottom depths in the middle and lower Mekong.  Inhabits clear waters of the main channels during the dry season and moves to floodplains and riparian forests during the rainy season.  Relatively common in the upland river habitat of the middle Mekong until water levels begin to rise.  Dietary habits still unknown, but the subterminal mouth and papillate lips indicate that it probably roots around for food in fine-grained sediments (Ref. 12693).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).

species.name: Cosmochilus nanlaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cotte blême
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6696).

species.name: Cotte polaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on polychaetes, mysids, amphipods and pycnogonids.  Spawns probably from June to July, ovarian eggs large and few (up to 220) (Ref. 6696).  Female lays 200 eggs with a length of 4.5-5 mm (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Cotte subantarctique
species.description: Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Cottiusculus gonez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs on sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 83439).

species.name: Cottiusculus nihonkaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs on sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 83439).

species.name: Cottiusculus schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottoclinus canops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottocomephorus alexandrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on mesoplankton, young Cottocomephorus and benthic amphipods (Ref. 51998). Lives deeper than 10-400 m during feeding (Ref. 51998).

species.name: Cottoperca trigloides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottunculus spinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottunculus tubulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by bottom trawl (Ref. 58914).

species.name: Cottus altaicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus bendirei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus chattahoochee
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams with gravel or cobble substrate (Ref. 72414).

species.name: Cottus cyclophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus dzungaricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus gratzianowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. During summer, this species is found in a relatively cool small river with moderate to rapid current, gravel and cobble bottom, and not very dense submerged aquatic vegetation (Ref. 101366).

species.name: Cottus hangiongensis
species.description: Adults occur in the middle and lower reaches of rivers.  Larvae inhabit coastal waters. Usually found in clear and cold water streams with sandy and gravelly bottom (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Cottus kanawhae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus kolymensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus koreanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus koshewnikowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits medium-sized rivers to small streams, and lake shores (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cottus kuznetzovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus metae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams to medium-sized rivers.  Attains first sexual maturity at 2-4 years.  Spawns in March-April (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cottus microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams to medium-sized rivers.   Feeds on a wide variety of benthic invertebrates.  Females spawn once a year (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cottus nozawae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits middle and upper reaches of rivers.  MtDNA studies revealed three distinct phylogenetic groups (Hokkaido Island, Northern Tohoku District and Yamagata Prefecture) of the species.  This also provides the basic information for the conservation of the species populations in the Tohoku District which have been designated as endangered local populations (Ref. 43190).

species.name: Cottus reinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus sabaudicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus schitsuumsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common to abundant in cool to cold tributaries with cobble and gravel bottoms. Sympatric with Oncorhynchus clarkii and Salvelinus confluentus throughout its distribution, with Cottus rhotheus in Idaho, and withCottus cognatu in Montana (Ref. 94998).

species.name: Cottus szanaga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cottus tallapoosae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clean gravel or rocky bottomed streams with moderate to swift current.  Frequently found in streams 3-15 m wide and at depths of 0.5-0.7 m (Ref. 72414).  Feeds on anything alive which fits into its mouth (Ref. 72414).

species.name: Cottus transsilvaniae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from a cold and fast-flowing stream (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cotylope à nageoires rouges
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Couette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools, backwaters and main channels of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 10294).  Also occurs in lakes.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Feeds on bottom ooze and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 10294), including insects, mollusks and crustaceans, along with plant detritus and sand (Ref. 93252).

species.name: Coupe-fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in oceanic and coastal waters (Ref. 26340).  They are most common along surf beaches and rock headlands in clean, high energy waters, although adults can also be found in estuaries and into brackish water (Ref. 6492).  Small fish may be found in shallow coastal waters at least 2 m depth (Ref. 9563), in schools pursuing and attacking small fishes (Ref. 9626).  Adults are in loose groups, often attacking shoals of mullets or other fishes and destroying numbers apparently far in excess of feeding requirements (Ref. 9860).  Feed on other fish (Ref. 5377), crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 47377).  Associated with sharks and billfishes (Ref. 26340).  Voracious and aggressive  (Ref. 9626), reported to bite when handled.  Migrate to warmer water during winter and to cooler water in summer (Ref. 9987).  Popular game fish (Ref. 6638).  Good food fish; marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9860), but also dried or salted (Ref. 5284), and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Courbine aile tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow muddy coastal waters.  Marketed fresh and dried salted.

species.name: Courbine barbiche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Courbine barbue
species.description: Found over hard and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9118). Feeds on zooplankton, euphausiids and other small crustaceans (Ref. 9118). Often caught with Merluccius gayi (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Courbine blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms (Ref. 9118).  Feed on polychaetes, small shrimps, crabs and mollusks (Ref. 9118). Oviparous, multiple pelagic spawner (Ref. 51256).

species.name: Courbine blonde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Regarded as a prime table fish in South America.

species.name: Courbine caroune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters, enters estuaries and mangrove swamps (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Courbine carutte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.  Sold fresh and dried-salted in markets.

species.name: Courbine chinoise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Feeds on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 30573).  Marketed fresh, dried salted.

species.name: Courbine de Belanger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and estuaries.  Feeds on invertebrates, particularly benthic worms.  Marketed fresh and dried salted.

species.name: Courbine de fond
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud bottoms between 70-140 m around islands and between 250 and 600 m on the continental slope (Ref. 3702).  Feeds mainly on shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Courbine de l'Angola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand and rock bottoms in slope and shelf waters, in temperatures which are below the thermocline.  Feeds on swimming crustaceans and small fishes.  Spawns from August to November in waters at 15°-16°C (Ref. 3593).

species.name: Courbine dentue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries, and rivers.  In India, matures at the size of 14 to 16 cm TL; attains an average size of 15.8 cm TL, 20.6 cm TL, and 24 cm TL, at the end of 1 year, 1.5 years and 2 years, respectively.  Juveniles prefer crustaceans and as they grow , show piscivorous tendency (Ref. 9772).  Marketed fresh and dried salted (Ref. 3490).

species.name: Courbine dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).  Feeds on small crustaceans.  Marketed fresh as well as dried salted (Ref. 3490).

species.name: Courbine du Sud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lower reaches of rivers, estuaries, rocky reefs, ocean beaches and on the continental shelf down to 150 m (Ref. 9772).  Caught near the bottom and in mid-water.  Feed mainly at night or in turbid waters (Ref. 27121), preying on cuttlefish (Ref. 27121), fishes, crabs, prawns, and worms (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Courbine fuseau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters.  Feeds on benthic worms and crustaceans.  Marketed fresh and also dried salted.

species.name: Courbine grenadine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms.  Catch is primarily from exploratory fisheries (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Courbine grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters.  Feeds on small crustaceans, benthic worms and small fishes.  Marketed fresh and dried salted (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Courbine kathala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Courbine lugubre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal throughout its range.  Sold fresh, also dried salted in markets.

species.name: Courbine maroto
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters, usually over sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 3702).  Feeds mainly on shrimps (Ref. 3702).  Important food fish.

species.name: Courbine noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters down to a depth of 200 m or deeper (Ref. 9772), on seaweed beds and gravel (Ref. 11230).  Important food fish.

species.name: Courbine pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters over muddy bottoms, off the sea-bed.  Ascend tidal rivers and estuaries (Ref. 9772).  Feed mainly on crustaceans and small fishes.  Also caught with bottom trawls (Ref. 9772).  Sold fresh and dried salted (swim bladder) in markets.  An important food fish.  Minimum depth range based on occurrence (Ref. 118911).

species.name: Courbine pélin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mid-water, over mud and sand bottoms in coastal waters.  One of the most abundant sciaenids in shallower waters (Ref. 3593).  Feeds on fish, cephalopods, shrimps, and annelids (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Courbine ragane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries; young and juveniles occur in mangrove swamps (Ref. 9772).  Also caught with bottom trawls, and handlines (Ref. 9772).  Sold fresh and dried salted in markets.

species.name: Courbine reine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur inshore, often over sandy bottoms.  Common in bays and tidal sloughs, around pilings.  Moves to deeper water at night (Ref. 9118).  Form schools.  Feed on small shrimps, marine worms and fishes (Ref. 9118).  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Courbine soldat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).  Juveniles occur in brackish estuaries and often ascend the lower reaches of large, turbid rivers (Ref. 2847).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Encountered in medium to large-sized rivers both in the lower and middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.  Marketed fresh as well as dried salted.

species.name: Courbine tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.  An important foodfish.  Sold fresh and dried salted in markets.

species.name: Courbine tachetée (Roncador stearnsii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in sandy shores and bays, mostly in shallow surf zones, but also to 15 m depth.  Often found near rocks and entrances to bays.  Usually form small groups, but aggregate for spawning.  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Feed on invertebrates, such as marine worms, clams, crabs and small crustaceans.

species.name: Courbine tiyeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy muddy bottoms in coastal waters and in estuaries.  Juveniles restricted to brackish waters (Ref. 9626).  Feeds mainly on shrimps.  Marketed mostly fresh and salted, an important foodfish.  One of the most highly priced species in Trinidad.

species.name: Courbine à bouche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep shelf and upper slopes over mud, sand and rock bottoms.  Also moves in midwater, in equatorial regions below the thermocline (Ref. 3593).

species.name: Courbine à grande nageoire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters.  Feeds on benthic worms and small crustaceans.  Sold fresh and dried salted in markets.

species.name: Courbine à petit œil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the surf zone of coastal waters, in estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Occasionally found in markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Cowcod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the bottom at moderate depths, to 366 m (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715), over fine sand and clay, whereas adults (>44 cm TL) inhabit rocky areas at 90-300 m (Ref. 49962).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Cowley’s torpedo ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is mostly found along the outer continental shelf and upper slope near the bottom, but also well off it and at bottom depths of 110-457 m (Ref. 100734). Females mature by at least 100.5 cm total length and males at about 58.2 cm total length (Ref. 100734); born before 19 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Neonates reported to have been collected during pelagic plankton tows on the edge of the outer continental shelf southwest of Cape Town (Ref. 100734). The limited capture of this electric ray in bottom trawls is suspected to be not indicative of its abundance in the area, but rather by its ability to move well off the bottom while foraging for fish and other large prey; diet consists mainly of large bottom and pelagic bony fishes and small sharks (Ref. 100734).

species.name: Cox's gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Populations appear more abundant in southern rivers, in flowing areas, including rapids (Ref. 2906, 44894).  Adults are not found in lower reaches but individuals range upstream into areas of altitudes up to 700 m (Ref. 2906).  Rarely found near to the sea (Ref. 44894).  Individuals have been observed climbing dam walls using their pectorals, out of direct water flow (Ref. 2906).  Adults feed on aquatic insects and mosquitofish. Juveniles generally found closer to the sea.  During upstream migration these fish are capable of climbing waterfalls and steep dams.  The female lays eggs on rocky surfaces and the male guards and fans the nest until hatching several days later (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Cozumel toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crampton’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles captured along the margins of main river channels in várzea; adults captured in the main channels of the sampled rivers (de Santana, pers. observ.).

species.name: Cran's bully
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cranoglanis bouderius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river bottom with clear water flows.  Lives on shrimps and small fishes.  Fish delicious and main edible of the Zhujiang River valley (Ref. 45563).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
