species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des scorpaenidae. Most widespread stonefish (Ref. 4313).  Found on sandy or rubble areas of reef flats and shallow lagoons and in small pools during low tide well camouflaged among the substrate and sometimes even covered with algae (Ref. 5213, 5503).  Solitary species (Ref. 37816).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans.  The dorsal fin has 2 grooves serving as seringes of venom; their stings are excruciatingly painful and can occasionally be fatal.  A serum exists which is effective if applied immediately after the infliction.  World's most venomous fish (Ref. 37816).  Uncommon in markets.  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).  Also Ref. 57406.

species.name: Crapaud angolais
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud barbu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coral reefs in inshore waters.

species.name: Crapaud cheval
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud de Boulenger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal zones (Ref. 9277).

species.name: Crapaud de Dow
species.description: Occurs in shallow waters (Ref. 9277).

species.name: Crapaud de Greene
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters up to depths of 27 m (Ref. 9277).

species.name: Crapaud de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows into sand and sand-mud bottoms with salinities of 32-35 ppt, sometimes as low as 16-30 ppt (Ref. 4698).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small benthic amphipods and polychaetes (Ref. 4698).

species.name: Crapaud de mer (Hemitripterus americanus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky or hard bottom and is a voracious eater.  Food includes crustaceans, mollusks, sea urchins, fishes such as herring, sand lance and silver hake, and any bottom invertebrates that are available.  When taken out of the water the belly becomes inflated so that when returned to the water they are unable to submerge.  Adults attach their eggs near the base of a sponge to use as a spawning bed (Ref. 34819, 41075).

species.name: Crapaud de Rossignol
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 3572).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 3572).  Marketed mainly fresh (Ref. 3572).

species.name: Crapaud de Schmitt
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Crapaud de Walker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud de Walter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in bays (Ref. 9277).

species.name: Crapaud du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes enters fresh water (Ref. 9277).

species.name: Crapaud enchainé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud or sand bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Most common on rather shallow offshore banks, such as commercial shrimp grounds; less common inshore.

species.name: Crapaud funèbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from the intertidal zone to a depth of 224 m (Ref. 9277).  Maximum depth range from Ref. 119198.

species.name: Crapaud goulu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits littoral (subtidal) waters; usually found on sandy or rock bottom; large fish may be found in waters less than 1 m of depth hiding in crevices or caves (Ref. 3273).  Feeds mostly on molluscs and crustaceans.  Reported to be moderately abundant and regularly consumed by fishermen (Ref. 50841).  Eggs are deposited on the shells of mollusks and on stones.  One of the very few marine fishes that guards fry and juveniles.  It is caught in traps and special types of hooks (garrapinos) (Ref. 50841).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Crapaud guinéen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Crapaud guyanais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in brackish water (Ref. 5217).  Found on sandy-muddy bottoms in shallow warm water.  Not so active, lingers over the substrate disguised.  Feeds on small gastropod mollusks, crustaceans like crabs (Calappidae, Portunidae, Xanthidae, etc.), shrimps (Penaeidae, Palaemonidae, Alphaeidae, etc.) and fishes.  Females are mature at around 20 cm length, males at 25 cm.  Spawns 400 to 500 eggs, with a size of 4 to 5 mm (Ref. 35237).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: crapaud huître
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Largely inhabits inshore water on rocky bottoms and reefs, jetties and wrecks.  Frequently occurs among litter and tolerates polluted water.  Becoming important as an experimental fish because of its size and hardiness.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35422).

species.name: Crapaud lagunaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow muddy bottoms.  Abundant in mangrove-lined lagoons.  Feeds mainly on small gastropod mollusks and crustaceans.  Marketed fresh, but the flesh is of low quality.

species.name: Crapaud marguerite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore, soft bottom habitats and migrate into shallow reef areas to spawn in late spring and early summer.  Mainly nocturnal.  Stays buried in the sand or other soft substrate during the day.  Rises up the water column at night to feed (Ref. 28023).  Neither opercular nor dorsal glands is venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Crapaud mimétique
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud petit oeil
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crapaud pipa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers muddy bottoms (Ref. 68964). Caught by handlines and bottom trawls.  Sold mostly fresh in markets.

species.name: Crapaud poilu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in littoral and coastal waters.  Enter estuaries (Ref. 4482).  Feed on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Crapaud réticulé
species.description: Inhabits shallow waters (Ref. 9277).  Both opercular and dorsal glands are venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Crapaud tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sandy bottoms of reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Partially buried in mud or sand.  Wounds from the venomous spines have caused severe pain and illness that persisted as long as one week (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Crapaud à nageoire tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky areas and soft bottom, common in bays.  Ranges from the intertidal zone to 126 m depth (Ref. 9277).  Usually rests on or buries itself in bottom.  Can create a humming or grunting sound.  More active during night time.

species.name: Crapaud à nageoire unie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from intertidal areas (where they may remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds, Ref. 31184) to deeper water over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 4925).  Adults make vertical migrations at night (Ref. 6885).  Feed on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous with eggs and larvae attached to nest wall (Ref. 36489).  Nest is guarded by male (Ref. 36489).  Important prey item for seals and sea lions (Ref. 2850).  Adults breathe air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Possess photophores which are arranged on the underside of the head in a 'U' fashion.

species.name: Crapet arlequin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found frequently in lakes, ponds, reservoirs and sluggish streams (Ref. 5723, 10294); occur primarily in reservoirs in Hawaii; preferably live in deep weed beds (Ref. 5723).  Active mainly during dusk and dawn.  They feed upon snails, small crayfish, insects, worms and small minnows (Ref. 5723).  Young feed on crustaceans, insects and worms (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Crapet calicot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sand-bottomed and mud-bottomed pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers, and lakes and ponds.  Often found in turbid water (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adult feeds on forage fishes such as shad (Ref. 10294).  Younger crappie consumes small invertebrates, including microcrustaceans and small insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Crapet de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in rocky areas in shallow water of lakes, and the lower, warm reaches of streams (Ref. 1998).  Inhabits vegetated and brushy stream margins, pools of creeks and small to medium rivers, and rocky and vegetated margins of lakes (Ref. 86798).  Commonly found in clear, silt-free rocky streams (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on small crustaceans, insects and fish (Ref. 30578).  An introduced species in Europe which avoids swift waters and occurs in a wide variety of slow-flowing to stagnant waters such as large rivers, lakes, ponds, canals and backwaters (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Crapet à longues oreilles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nearly always found in shallow water, preferring habitats with dense vegetation in small lakes, ponds and slow moving rivers and streams.  Feed on small aquatic invertebrates, insects, and occasionally small fishes.  (Ref. 4543, 10294).

species.name: Crapet à oreilles rouges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds, swamps, lakes; and vegetated pools, usually with mud or sand bottoms, of small to medium rivers.  Also occurs in warm, clear and quiet waters rich in vegetation and snags.  Has a preference for mollusks as food thus has potential for the control of snail vectors of schistosomiasis (Ref. 1739, 10294).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

Collected in a large river with high, turbid monsoon flow and with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).

species.name: Crenicichla gillmorlisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens composed of an adult and 2 young were collected from a small stream with brownish very turbid water, with moderate current, about 4 m wide and 1-1.5 m deep. The bottom substrate was composed of rocks and stones. Fishes were encountered along overhanging banks. Associated species included Gymnogeophagus setequedas Reis, Malabarba & Pavanelli (Cichlidae) and Bryconamericus stramineus Eigenmann (Characidae), Astyanax sp. (Characidae), Hypostomus dlouhyi Weber, Hypoptopoma sp. (Loricariidae), Hoplias sp. (Erythrinidae), Leporinus lacustris Amaral Campos (Anostomidae), Steindachnerina brevipinnis (Eigenmann & Eigenmann) (Curimatidae), Eigenmannia virescens (Valenciennes) (Sternopygidae), Crenicichla lepidota (Cichlidae), and Pyrrhulina australis Eigenmann & Kennedy (Lebiasinidae). A juvenile was also captured in a small stream, more than 1.5 m deep with running, dark and turbid water and bottom consisted of sand, in open landscape with low trees and grass. Associated species with this juvenile were Characidium sp. (Crenuchidae) and Bryconamericus stramineus (Characidae), Astyanax sp., Cheirodon sp., Hemigrammus sp., Mimagoniates microlepis (Steindachner) (Characidae), Corydoras diphyes Axenrot & Kullander (Callichthyidae), Bunocephalus sp. (Aspredinidae), Gymnogeophagus setequedas (Cichlidae), Hypoptopoma sp., (Loricariidae), and Phallotorynus victoriae Oliveros (Poeciliidae) (Ref. 93325).

species.name: Crenicichla jupiaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla jurubi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla labrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla lacustris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla lenticulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla lucenai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla lucius
species.description: Known from streams and in black waters.

species.name: Crenicichla maculata
species.description: Feeds on bivalves, gastropods, fish and coleopteran larvae (Ref. 57632).

species.name: Crenicichla mandelburgeri
species.description: Collected with electrofishing from rapids in a large stream, 5-10 m wide, to 1 m deep; water turbid and brownish; rocks came from road building; slope of rapids was about 10°. Associated fauna include Crenicichla lepidota (Cichlidae), Ancistrus sp. and Rineloricaria sp. (Loricariidae), Bryconamericus sp. (Characidae), Heptapterus mustelinus and Rhamdia quelen(Heptapteridae). All other collection sites were small, shallow brown-water streams up to about 3 m wide; varying velocity and transparency; bottom of sand and stones; and, generally absent vegetation, mostly sampled in unfavorable high water conditions in the month of February. Associated species here were generally typical forest stream species such as species of Astyanax and Bryconamericus, H. mustelinus, Rineloricaria sp., Rhamdia quelen, Oligosarcus paranensis (Characidae), Apareiodon sp., C. lepidota, and Gymnogeophagus cf. caaguazuensis (Cichlidae) (Ref. 80386).

species.name: Crenicichla missioneira
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla mucuryna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla multispinosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies the same biotope as C. ternetzi. C. ternetzi lives in the rocky zones of rapids where it finds shelter against back currents. Stays in shallow waters with bright sunlight (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Crenicichla nickeriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla niederleinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla notophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla pellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla percna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla phaiospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla ploegi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla prenda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla proteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, quiet waters associated with abundant aquatic and shoreline vegetation (Ref. 9088).

species.name: Crenicichla punctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae.

species.name: Crenicichla pydanielae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla regani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla reticulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla rosemariae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large, clear pool with large rooted macrophytes.  Large specimens observed near the bottom of pool.

species.name: Crenicichla santosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla scottii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla sedentaria
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla semicincta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from lakes, streams and swamps.

species.name: Crenicichla semifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds.

species.name: Crenicichla sipaliwini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male holotype was about 12.7 cm long without the tail (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Crenicichla stocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla strigata
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae.

species.name: Crenicichla sveni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla taikyra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stony environment with Secchi disk 212 mm, water temperature 25.1°C, pH 7.14, conductivity 51.4 μS cm-1, dissolved oxygen 99.7% saturation, and alkalinity 9.0 mg l-1.. Stomach contents of two specimens contained snails (Potamolithus sp. and Limnoperna fortunei) and remains of fishes (Ref. 94256).

species.name: Crenicichla tapii
species.description: Relatively common only in the main channel of the Iguazú River, where they can be observed in schools on the flat-rock substrate from the walkways over the river grazing on periphyton. Always encountered in direct association with flat slab-like exposed rocky bottoms with epiphyte growths, never above gravel or soft sediment-covered bottoms.  Grazes on periphyton  (Ref. 104794).

species.name: Crenicichla tendybaguassu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla ternetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic species living in the zones of rapids where it finds shelter against back currents. The water is shallow with bright illumination. In the same biotope, Lasiancistrus longispinis, L. brevispinis, Ctenoloricaria fowleri, Bryconops cyrtogaster and Astyanax leopoldi (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Crenicichla tesay
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla tigrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae.

species.name: Crenicichla tingui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 57632).

species.name: Crenicichla tuca
species.description: All specimens, except two, were collected in the main channel of the Iguazú River, where they occurred as single individuals among the rocks from the walkways over the river ramming their heads and thick lips against the rock surfaces (Ref. 104794).

species.name: Crenicichla urosema
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crenicichla ypo
species.description: Recorded both before and after the Urugua-í hydroelectrical dam was built in 1989. Presently inhabits also directly in the reservoir. Occurs in a moderately fast flowing river with tributaries of an average depth of 1 m outside of the dam influence and with bottom consisting of mud, sand with gravel and/or bedrock. Sympatric with Crenicichla yaha(Ref. 85167).

species.name: Crenulate-lipped rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found along semi-exposed rocky shorelines (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Crenulated silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters around islands.  Biology unknown.  May be foraged by larger commercial species.  Dried for pet food.

species.name: Creole damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and inshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Creole darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel riffles, current-swept vegetation and debris in creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Creole perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Creole topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit pools and areas along banks of swift, clear, cool, well-oxygenated highland streams.  A midwater swimmer, never found at the surface and seldom on the bottom, over hard substrates composed of smooth rocks, gravel, or sand.  Feeds on algae, aquatic plants and insect larvae.

species.name: Crescent betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in stagnant pools and ditches in clear to brown water (Ref. 56613).  Found also in lowland swamps and paddy field.  Bubble nest builder species (Ref. 57235).  Eggs shrink to the bottom and were then collected by one or both parents and were embedded among the foam bubbles in the nest (Ref. 41595).

species.name: Crescent dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rubble bottom by clove oil at 13.5 m depth (Ref. 113376).

species.name: Crescent gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crescent goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with demersal eggs (Ref. 56079).  Cryptic, benthic and found on sandy bottoms near rocks or corals (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Crescent gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently in intertidal areas, in tide pools or under rocks protected by seaweeds (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Probably feeds on small crustaceans and marine worms (Ref. 28499).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Crescent shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy pools and runs of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably nest spawners like congeners.

species.name: Crescent sweetlips
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs, near rocky and coral areas (Ref. 9710).  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Crescent-tail hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species has been photographed at depths of 25-50 m, with adults occurring in groups along ledges on steep dropoffs at depths greater than 20 m, and juveniles observed at about 50 m (Ref. 75973).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crescent-wing pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crested bandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crested bellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Crested blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Crested flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 9824).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Crested goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit tidal creeks, mangroves and other quiet, fresh to fully saline coastal waters (Ref. 7251) with salinity ranging from 0.0 to 39.3 ppt (Ref. 97140).  Opportunistic feeder, ingests diverse crustaceans, molluscs and barnacles, greatest part of their food comprises algae (Ref. 92840)

species.name: Crested morwong
species.description: Occurs in inshore and offshore rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9563, 9710).

species.name: Crested oystergoby
species.description: Found in estuaries and harbors, very shallow oyster zones, usually under rocks or nearby on mud (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Crested pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 26340).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crested scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Crested sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore (Ref. 2850); often well above the bottom (Ref. 48798).

species.name: Crested spiny plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in the littoral zone, under rocks, but may occur to depths of 40-50 m (Ref. 5191).  Accorded full species recognition because of the presence of tubular cephalic pores and a single knob bearing a tentacle above each eye, thus setting it apart from the other species (Ref. 5191).  Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041).

species.name: Crested threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the intertidal zone and on vertical rock surfaces and jetty pylons (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cresthead flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Creteuchiloglanis arunachalensis
species.description: Inhabits various substrata such as gravel, cobbles or medium to large boulders, and green algae on substratum, in low to moderately deep (40-80 cm) running water.  Habitat is characterized by  cool, clear and moderate to swift running water.  River bank is composed of bamboo and other trees, without aquatic vegetation.  running water moderate to swift, cool and clear (Ref. 96853).

species.name: Crevice kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore rocky areas in algae, usually on exposed coast.

species.name: Cribroheros altifrons
species.description: Inhabits rocky and sandy stream usually with moderate to fast flowing water and between 20-400 meters elevation.  Feeds upon aufwuchs and invertebrates as well as various aquatic insects.

species.name: Cribroheros bussingi
species.description: Recorded from streams and large rivers and collected between 40 and 150 m elevation.  Prefers sand or mud bottoms where it extracts aquatic insects, seeds and detritus (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Cribroheros diquis
species.description: Inhabits creeks and rivers, in backwaters or even waters of moderate current velocity between 16 and 700 m elevation.  Lives over rocky, sand or gravel bottoms.  Eats insects, seed and fruit (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Cribroheros rhytisma
species.description: Prefers moderate to fast flowing rivers between 40 and 60 m elevation.  Feeds on aquatic insects and detritus (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Cribroheros rostratus
species.description: A floodplain fish found between 0 and 200 m elevation.  Inhabits lakes and rivers of low to high current velocity.  Feeds on aquatic insects in large part with abundant  detritus and sediments (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Cricamola toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in shallow and marshy river tributaries (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Crimean barbel
species.description: Occurs from mountain streams with strong current to brackish estuaries, preferring river stretches at 100-600 m above sea level.  Spawns on gravel or rock bottom.  Feeds mainly on zoobenthos. Threatened due pollution and water abstraction.  Water abstraction is expected to increase in all streams of Crimea (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Crimson cleaner fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sand patches adjacent to reef areas in shallow waters.  The species is a facultative cleaner symbiont, removing parasites and damaged scales and skin from other fishes; also feeds on small crustaceans from the bottom and from seaweed fronds.

species.name: Crimson sea bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crimson triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in environments very similar to E. obscurus. They also commonly occur in isolated reefs far from coasts wherein other Enneapterygius spp. could not be found (Ref. 88983). Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240). Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Crimsonband wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common coastal reef fish collected from 15 m but may occur much deeper than this (Ref. 26203).

species.name: Crimsonspotted rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, creeks, drains, ponds, dune lakes and reservoirs.  Usually occurs in still or slow-flowing conditions near the surface or around vegetation, log snags, or other debris.  Occurs in both sandy coastal habitats and forested areas farther inland.  Water conditions vary from very soft and acidic (coastal) to relatively alkaline (inland).  The pH and temperature ranges are 5.4-7.8 and 16°-28°C, respectively (Ref. 44894).  Omnivore (Ref. 75154).  A popular aquarium fish which readily breeds in captivity.  Life span in the wild is probably 3-4 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Crimsontip longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found under stone or corals in flood basins and lagoons (Ref. 9137).  They are common but very secretive and usually found when turning rubble pieces in pools (Ref. 48635). They  venture out in the open at night to feed on small crustaceans, fishes and gastropods (Ref. 37816).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Crinoid clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in protected coastal reefs from shallow reef flats to about 20 m depth along slopes and walls (Ref. 48635). Found among arms of crinoids (Ref. 2334, 559) as a commensal particularly with Comanthus bennetti (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Crisscross prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from intertidal rocky areas to 21 m depth.  Stomachs examined contained mostly invertebrates; mostly crustaceans (mysids, amphipods, and shrimps) and mollusks (Ref. 4930).

species.name: Cristatogobius aurimaculatus
species.description: Found in brackish water (Ref. 43239).  Specimens have been collected in inlets of river mouths where water depth is 10-50 cm at the lowest tide (Ref. 37940).

species.name: Cristatogobius lophius
species.description: Found in brackish waters (Ref. 43239). Occurs in river mouths and bays, on muddy bottoms (Ref. 37940). Found in burrows dug by Alpheus shrimp and other invertebrates (Ref. 37940).

species.name: Cristatogobius nonatoae
species.description: Found in brackish waters (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Cristivomer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow and deep waters of northern lakes and streams and is restricted to relatively deep lakes in the southern part of its range (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Rarely found in brackish water (Ref. 11980).  A solitary wanderer, the extent of their movements apparently limited by the size of the lake and individual (Ref. 27547).  Although lake trout generally feed on a variety of organisms such as freshwater sponges, crustaceans, insects, fishes (with a preference for ciscoes), and small mammals, some populations feed on plankton throughout their lives (Ref. 27547).  Such plankton-feeding lake trout grow more slowly, mature earlier and at smaller size, die sooner and attain smaller maximum size than do their fish-eating counterparts (Ref. 30351).  Lake trout are highly susceptible to pollution, especially from insecticides (Ref. 14019, 27547).  Utilized as a food fish, its flesh is usually of a yellow or creamy color but may be anything from white to orange (Ref. 27547).  Often caught by fishers (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Croaking gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in shallow sluggish or standing-water habitats with a lot of vegetation.  Common throughout the middle and lower Mekong (Ref. 12693).  Found in flooded fields in the middle Mekong (Ref 12975).  Feed on zooplankton, crustaceans and insect larvae.  Eggs sink to the bottom and were then collected by one or both parents and were embedded among the foam bubbles in the nest (Ref. 41595).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Usually not fished commercially, occasionally sold as part of mixed catches in markets and regularly seen in the aquarium fish trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Croaking tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit small to moderate-sized streams or rivers (Ref. 30267).

species.name: Croatian pijor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lowland water bodies, with little current, and in springs and associated wetlands (Ref. 26100). Inhabits streams and sources with clear (often cold) water. Occurs in subterranean waters during winter or droughts. Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and introduction of Alburnus arborella, Squalius cephalus and Lepomis gibbosus (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Crochet arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, mud or hard bottoms (Ref. 4698).  Benthic; feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Crochet butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit seaward reefs in areas with rich coral growth.  Usually solitary, but also a schooling species that is often on the move, usually in areas prone to strong currents.  Usually deep in Indonesia and adults are rarely found in less than 40 m depth.  Mainly found in sponge zones and deep water occurrence is habitat related, not cold water as sometimes suggested.  This species will travel in open water and cleans large pelagic fishes (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crocodile catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit large rivers (Ref. 12693).  Usually associated with rapids (Ref. 43281).  Feed on fishes.  Sold fresh, although the value of its meat is limited because it spoils rapidly and can cause illness (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Crocodile de Georgie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed mainly on krill and fish.  Synchronous spawner (Ref. 50743).

species.name: Crocodile snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in shallow lagoon sand, rock and broken coral substrates at depths of 0-2 m (Ref. 42180). Benthic (Ref. 58302), occurs in sandy bottoms from intertidal to over 12 m.; remains buried in sand with only the eyes protruding where it waits to ambush fish (Ref. 9710) and octopuses (Ref. 275). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Crocodile-tooth pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 1479).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crocro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found primarily on sponge and coral bottoms.  Feeds mainly on invertebrates (Ref. 9739).

species.name: Crocro (Haemulon album)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds, sand flats, coral reefs, and wrecks (Ref. 9710).  Found in pairs or larger schools (Ref. 3798).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3798).  Has been observed to nose into the sand to eat such subsurface invertebrates as peanut worms and heart urchins (Ref. 13442).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Crocro (Pomadasys incisus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottom (Ref. 2683, 57395) and sand (Ref. 57395).  Enters estuaries and lagoons at sexual maturation (Ref. 57395).  Feeds on bottom and near-bottom invertebrates (Ref. 5535).

species.name: Crocro à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 7356).  Inhabits inshore water, frequenting rocky coast and beaches to depths of 20 m (Ref. 9675).

species.name: Croissant
species.description: Usually seen in clear-water areas at depths below 15 m, and prefers islands and offshore reefs rather than continental shores.  Feeds mainly on fishes, and on crabs, shrimps and stomatopods.  It is highly appreciated for the quality of its flesh.  It may not be sold in Mauritius because of cases of ciguatera poisoning (Ref. 11888).  In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). This common and important food fish is caught with handlines, spear, and traps (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Croissant queue blanc
species.description:
A generally uncommon species that inhabits seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles inshore on algae and soft coral reefs, usually swimming well above the substrate, looking much like a basslet (Ref. 48635).  Solitary (Ref 90102) or found in small groups (Ref. 11888).  Feeds on fishes. Of little interest to fisheries, because of its small size and rarity, but flesh is excellent.
Caught with handline, traps, and spear (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Cromeria occidentalis
species.description: Maximum TL was recorded at 4.1 cm (Ref. 3566).  Occurs on several substrates from fine mud to rough gravel and plant material; almost never buries into the substrate (Ref. 57474).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 57474, 91322) and phytoplankton (Ref. 91322).  Reproduction likely takes place during the rainy season (August to September) (Ref. 57474) at high water levels in floodplains, brooks or rice fields (Ref. 91276, 91322).

species.name: Croncron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic fish occurring on sandy-muddy bottoms of brackish waters (Ref. 35381) and coastal rivers (Ref. 36695).  Found on soft bottoms of shallow turbid water near river mouths.  The species has a peculiar mode of egg incubation wherein the female banjo catfish carries the eggs firmly attached to the underside of the body.  This seems to be an adaptation to facilitate the oxygenation of the eggs in muddy environments.  Reproduction probably occurs during the earlier part of the year (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Croncron rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in brackish water.  Found on soft bottoms of shallow turbid water near river mouths.  Reported to migrate from estuary into freshwater, but actual spawning apparently takes place in brackish water (Ref. 6868).  The species has a peculiar mode of egg incubation wherein the female banjo catfish carries the eggs firmly attached to the underside of the body.  This seems to be an adaptation to facilitate the oxygenation of the eggs in muddy environments.  Reproduction probably occurs during the earlier part of the year (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Cross' damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow gutters of rocky areas or coral reefs of protected bays and lagoons.  Solitary and shy (Ref. 9710).  Often swimming near the surface (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Crossed-fork back golden-line fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Troglobite (Ref. 86777).

species.name: Crosseyed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Crosshatch bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crossie aile jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found mainly in estuaries but also enter freshwater to an elevation of 50 m.  Diet consists primarily of fish, crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Crossie argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Can possibly reach 117 cm TL (Ref. 9284).

species.name: Crossie armée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crossie chucumite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, penetrating into freshwater; usually prefers very low brackish water or freshwater.  Occasionally in hypersaline lagoons (Ref. 5217).  Found over shallow soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on fish and crustaceans.  Its flesh is well appreciated (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Crossie constantin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, penetrating into freshwater; usually prefers very low brackish water or freshwater (Ref. 3713).  Feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 36880). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3713).

species.name: Crossie mexicaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mouths of rivers and the littoral zone; spawns on banks; feeds on small fish and crustaceans (Ref. 35237). Juveniles bear conspicuous black tip on the dorsal fin and often join foraging groups of similarly sized and looking flagfin mojarras, Eucinostomus melanopterus. The snooks mingle with the mojarras and prey on fishes and shrimps attracted to the digging activity of the mojarras. The resemblance to a fish harmless to shrimps and small fishes allows the snook to approach this otherwise wary prey, an example of aggressive mimicry (Ref. 43465).

species.name: Crossie mexicaine (Centropomus poeyi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, penetrating into freshwater.  Spawning occurs in fresh or low brackish water.  Feeds on fish and crustaceans.

species.name: Crossie serran
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crossie à nageoire noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit bays and estuaries (Ref. 37955).  Also found in high altitudes of at least 250 m elevation and a distance of some 20 km from the coast.  They also occur in coastal waters, but is more abundant in estuaries of any size.  Enter freshwaters mostly in large rivers and feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Crossie épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults enter mangrove areas and lagoons.  Also occur in estuaries (Ref. 11035) and fresh water (Ref. 4537), as well as rustic ponds (Ref. 85798).

species.name: Crossocheilus atrilimes
species.description: Usually associated with clear, relatively fast waters with gravel or boulders (Ref. 43281). Crossocheilus atrilimes and C. oblongus sometimes occur in syntopy, but C. oblongus is collected in swift water, in rapids and torrents, whereas C. atrilimes is found in somewhat quieter habitats (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Crossocheilus burmanicus
species.description: Found in the middle and lower layers of swift, mountainous streams and rivers (Ref. 83502).  Feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 83502).

species.name: Crossocheilus cobitis
species.description: Occurs usually in large rivers with turbid water, often found under floating houses, logs, boats (Ref.  43281).  Found at bottom depths of rivers.  Probably moves into the floodplains during high water periods and may spawn there.  Feeds on algae, periphyton, phytoplankton and some zooplankton.  Used for prahoc or nuoc mam (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Crossocheilus diplochilus
species.description: Apparently prefers lakes and main river banks, and does not ascend cold-water tributaries.  Primarily a lotic species feeding from epilithic growth.

species.name: Crossocheilus elegans
species.description: Occurs in hill-stream habitats, usually near or in the riffle zone in fast flowing waters over a rocky bottom (Ref. 87793).

species.name: Crossocheilus periyarensis
species.description: Inhabits fast flowing streams with rocky bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Crossocheilus pseudobagroides
species.description: Occurs in lowland streams (Ref. 81211).

species.name: Crossocheilus reticulatus
species.description: Usually found in clear, relatively fast waters with gravel and boulder (Ref. 27732).  Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Moves out onto the floodplain during high water where it feeds on algae, periphyton, phytoplankton and some zooplankton.  Used to make prahoc in Tonlé Sap, Cambodia.  Occasionally imported in the aquarium trade. (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Crossostomus chilensis
species.description: Inhabits the littoral zone to the upper slope (Ref. 11954)

species.name: Crossostomus fasciatus
species.description: Feeds on polychaetes (Ref. 33379).

species.name: Crossroads goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs in 10-30 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Crossthroat sawpalate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Croupia roche du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 9312).

species.name: Crown darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Breeding individuals found beneath rocks and undercurrent banks in mid-April (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Crown lanternfish
species.description: High-oceanic and mesopelagic species occurring in the upper 100 m at night (Ref.4066).

species.name: Crown Scaly Stream Loach
species.description: Found in upland areas on the bottoms of cool, clear, flowing streams with pools and forest canopy. Collected between 721-1,155 m above sea level in steep streams in Huay Nampan and tributaries of the Nan River basin. At the time of sampling during the start of the hot-dry season, Huay Nampan was about 2-4 m wide and 0.2-0.5 m deep; water volume might be higher during the rainy season. Encountered only in shaded areas and was absent from light-exposed open areas and lowlands. Substrate was composed mainly of stones, bedrock, and some sand and gravel in small pools. The upper stream bank was covered by large native trees with more than 90% canopy cover and at the time of sampling, the water was clear, and the temperature was 18.4°C (air temperature 22.5°C), conductivity 2.6 S/ m, and pH 6.5. Collected together with Schistura menanensis (Nemacheilidae) and Oreoglanis suraswadii (Sisoridae). Gut content analysis indicated that this species feeds mainly on aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 102608).

species.name: Crown spotty blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are reported to occur on rocky slope area and small individuals are known to occur around sea urchins.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  They lay eggs in a nest, using holes made by invertebrates on massive corals. The well-developed eggs are taken into the mouth and squeezed by the males and the newly hatched larvae swim out of its mouth.  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Spawning season extends from the middle of May to the beginning of October in Kinko Bay, Japan (Ref. 76746).

species.name: Crown sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently occurs in underwater caves or crevasses in coral reef areas during the day, but found in open water at night (Ref.92923).

species.name: Crown-of-thorns cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found in lagoons, among the spines of Acanthaster planci, in groups of up to 31 (Ref. 1602) from depths of 7 m or more (Ref. 37816). Minimum depth taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Crowned seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Sargassum belts near shore. Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Length type OT refers to height (= TL - head length). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crozet scad
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cruciglanis pacifici
species.description: Inhabits undisturbed clear and shallow rivers in strong current and on gravel to small stone substrates (riffles or runs). Associated with Gobiesox sp., Chaetostoma marginatum, Cordilancistrus daguae, Astroblepus trifasciatus, Trichomycterus taenia; as well as shrimps (Atya). Stomach contents of 5 specimens caught in the Aguaclara River, revealed immature aquatic insects belonging to Trichoptera, Diptera, Ephemeroptera and Odonata, and terrestrial insects of the orders Hymenoptera and Coleoptera (Ref. 57850).

species.name: Cruriraja hulleyi
species.description: Reported to be a moderately common species of the outer shelf and upper continental slope, 39-545 m deep, but most common between 200 and 500 depth.  Larger individuals tend to occur on the west coast of southern Africa, while those on the south coast are slightly smaller.  The egg case was described to be small, vase-like, measuring less than 50 mm long excluding horns, surface coarsely striated, and with very narrow lateral keels, <1% of maximum egg case width; its posterior horns are approximately 45% longer than the anterior horns, tapering to thin tips, curving inwards and with fine attachment fibers; the anterior horns are hook-shaped, with acute tips (Ref. 85323).

species.name: Crying cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crying Izak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cryprinodonte de Valence
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species. Adults are found in swamps, lagoons, springs and associated wetlands and other water bodies with little current and plenty of vegetation (Ref. 30578). They feed mainly on crustaceans and insect larvae (Ref. 59043). Threatened due to habitat destruction, water abstraction, pollution (Ref. 26100) and competition with the introduced Gambusia holbrooki (Ref. 59043). The first toothcarp in the German aquarium trade. Not a seasonal killifish. Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cryptarius daugueti
species.description: Inhabits large rivers (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cryptarius truncatus
species.description: Occurs in estuaries, lower courses of rivers (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cryptic anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300) but has been recorded to a depth of 130 m (Ref. 9563).  Adults found with sponges or ascidians (Ref. 48635).  Oviparous.  Eggs are attached to each other by a single, flattened, acellular filament and are brooded in a hollow behind the left pectoral fin (Ref. 6773). Mimics sponges with its spots that resembles pores of sponges (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cryptic bearded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms, usually in surge channels or on exposed outer edge of reefs in 1-15 m (Ref. 90102). Burrows in sand adjacent to coral or rock (Ref. 2798).

species.name: Cryptic cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually found solitary or in pairs at about 10-40 meters. It also displays a cryptic behavior, at least during daylight hours, sheltering between rocks and rubble. It has not been observed free swimming, but only when flushed from its lair with the use of clove-oil or rotenone. Specimens collected were living in a rubble field in sheltered waters at the base of a small islet or were found under rock slabs on a submerged patch reef (several km from shore) with abundant sponges and gorgonians and minimal hard corals. Some specimens were also collected from a flat sand and shell bottom with abundant Gonipora, some Fungia and considerable macroalgae (Ref. 83499).

species.name: Cryptic carp gudgeon
species.description: Maximum size based on type specimen (Ref. 128732).

species.name: Cryptic hagfish
species.description: This species is more commonly found deeper than 500 m. Its biology is largely unknown because it has been misidentified as the common hagfish E. cirrhatus; its stable carbon and nitrogen isotope signature indicated that this species feeds at a high trophic level, 3 levels above primary producers (Ref. 115309).

species.name: Cryptic Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottoms in 15-25 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Cryptic triplefin
species.description: Adults inhabit rock pools and in surge zones, especially in exposed areas.  Usually on steep slopes or sides of boulders encrusted with invertebrates and algae (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cryptic wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A secretive species occurring on coral reefs where it hides among soft corals and benthic algae.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Rarely found in the aquarium trade (Ref. 2334).  Population from Western Indian Ocean and Red Sea may be different species from fishes from the Pacific; genetic studies are needed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Cryptocentrus polyophthalmus
species.description: Inhabits coastal mud slopes in a depth range of 10 to 30 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Crystal cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Crystal darter
species.description: Occurs in clean sand and gravel runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Crystal tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typical of quiet waters in creeks and shorelines of larger rivers where there is low to moderate current.  Found in slightly brackish waters at sea level and in waters up to 610 m elevation, though generally more abundant below 200 m.  Food consists of fish scales, including those of other characins, cichlid and others, and aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Crystallichthys mirabilis
species.description: A recent reference confirming the validity of this species is needed.

species.name: Crystallodytes enderburyensis
species.description: This species inhabits coarse sand or fine gravel in exposed tidepools and the spur and groove habitat (Ref. 54980).

species.name: Crènilabre paon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near rocks mainly in eel-grass beds, sometimes in salty lagoons.  Often gregarious.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Nest of seaweed built and kept by male with one or more females spawning.  Feed on sea urchins, ophiuroids, bivalves, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 4742).  Rate of growth is slow (Ref. 4742).  Undergoes sex reversal (Ref. 4742).

species.name: Crénilabre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found mainly in eel-grass beds.  Often in pairs.  Males nest-makers.  Feed mainly on mollusks, gastropods, bivalves, tubicolous worms, chitons, sea urchins and bryozoans (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crénilabre (Symphodus melops)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This schooling, territorial fish occurs in the littoral zone, near rocks and eel-grass beds, also in lagoons.  In summer ripe females show short ovipositor.  Seaweed nest built by male among rocks or in crevices.  Sex reversal sometimes observed.  Feed on mollusks, hydroids, bryozoans, worms and various crustaceans (Ref. 4742).  Males grow faster than females (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crénilabre de Baillon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the littoral zone in seagrass beds and around rocks (Ref. 5292).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crénilabre de Doderlein
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit eel-grass beds (Ref. 4742).  Feed on bryozoans, worms, small mollusks, and amphipods (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crénilabre ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near rocks and eel-grass beds. A nest of seaweed (Cystoseria) built and kept by male. Feed on bryozoans, hydroids, tubicolous, worms, shrimps, amphipods and mollusks. Males grow faster than females (Ref. 4742). Undergoes sex reversal (Ref. 4742). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Crénilabre à cinq taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near rocks, mainly in eel-grass beds (Ref. 4742).  Mainly solitary (Ref. 4742).  Nest of seaweed built by male (Ref. 4742).  Feed on mollusks, bivalves, gastropods, shrimps, sea-urchins and hydroids (Ref. 4742).  Males grow faster than females (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cteniloricaria maculata
species.description: Lives in creeks and rapids where the vegetation is poor, the water is clear and well-oxygenated and shallow (less than 1 m), with sandy to rocky substrate. Found together with Characidium fasciadorsale, Imparfinis minutus, Corydoras guianensis and specially Harttia surinamensis (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Ctenochaetus flavicauda
species.description: Inhabits coral reefs from the shallow waters to depths of at least 30 m (Ref. 42056).

species.name: Ctenocheirodon pristis
species.description: Occurs in clear water over a sand and gravel bottom with a slow current and no vegetation (Ref. 91049).

species.name: Ctenochromis scatebra
species.description: This species has been observed feeding upon epilithic and epiphytic algae in Chemka Springs, as well as sifting soft sediment, and pecking on skin of swimmers; it is therefore most likely an omnivorous generalist (Ref. 127080).

species.name: Ctenogobiops tongaensis
species.description: Collected from silty sand and rubble substrate (Ref. 50606).

species.name: Ctenogobius chusanensis
species.description: Collected from a puddle in a mudbank exposed at low tide, on an islet across the tidal stream (Ref. 29060).

species.name: Ctenogobius lepturus
species.description: Inshore marine species; may also be found in brackish waters of lagoons (Ref. 7390, 57403, 79590).

species.name: Ctenopharynx intermedius
species.description: Found in sediment-rich areas (Ref. 5595) of the rocky habitat (Ref. 5595, 55925), the intermediate habitat, over sand, and in the open water (Ref. 5595).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Ctenopharynx nitidus
species.description: Occurs in shallower part of the sandy shores but also found at levels below 30m (Ref. 5595), and frequents muddy/soft bottoms (Ref. 5595, 55925), but also found over rocky habitat (Ref. 55925).  Feeds mainly on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 267).  Scoops up large amounts of silty sediment from the sand; commonly observed in small groups of about 5 individuals, but also forages in large schools (Ref. 55925).

species.name: Ctenopharynx pictus
species.description: Inhabits rocky areas with a deposit of fine sediment (Ref. 267, 55925), but also found on soft-bottom habitats (Ref. 55925).  Feeds on small invertebrates, mainly benthic copepods (Ref. 267, 55925) obtained by sucking up the fine sediment and passing it over the gill-rakers (Ref. 267).

species.name: Ctenopoma maculatum
species.description: Maximum TL reported 20.0 cm (Ref. 6803).

species.name: Ctenopoma petherici
species.description: Inhabits marginal vegetation, swamps, and floodplains.  Browses on plant tissues with ostracods, dipteran larvae, beetles, mollusks and debris (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Ctenotrypauchen chinensis
species.description: This species was collected at depths of 62-65 in the Arafura Sea and 50-70 m from the Samar Sea; possible that this species may be confined to deeper waters than most other members of this subfamily (Ref. 78624).

species.name: Cténolabre
species.description: On rocky, weed-covered shores (1-50 m); larger specimens deeper than young.  Feed on bryozoans, crustaceans and gastropods (Ref. 3397).  Spawning takes place in summer when the male defends a territory (Ref. 35388).  Used in salmon culture as cleaner fish (Helmut Tethmeyer, pers. comm.).

species.name: Cuatro Cienegas pupfish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cuatrocienegas gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cuatrocienegas killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cuban cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species inhabiting shallow water caves, sinkholes ad crevices (Ref. 34024). Feeds on cirolanid isopods. Viviparous. Sometimes found together with L. dentata and L. teresinarum (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Cuban gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater ponds, lakes and streams.  Prefers stagnant or slow-flowing streams, although may occur in mountain streams at elevation up to 600 m.  Usually found in schools close to the shore.  Carnivorous surface feeder.

species.name: Cuban killifish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cuban leg skate
species.description: Solitary (Ref. 26340).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cuban legskate
species.description: Deep water species (Ref. 6902).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cuban limia
species.description: Inhabits streams, lakes, estuaries, coastal lagoons and mangrove swamps.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Often found in the company of sailfin molly and mosquitofish (Ref. 4409).

species.name: Cuban longfin herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters.

species.name: Cuban pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 26340).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cuban topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers stagnant water in ponds, lakes and streams.  Found in midwater and on the bottom, seldom at the surface, over soft bottoms, frequently with abundant aquatic vegetation.  Feeds on aquatic vegetation, algae, detritus and insect larvae.

species.name: Cubango kneria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among rocks in flowing water; feeds off diatoms and other algae and detritus scraped from rock surfaces (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Cuchia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults known to hibernate in mud during cold season (Ref. 6351).  Feed mainly on small fishes, tadpoles and aquatic insects (Ref. 6351).  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cuckoo Catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among rocks in lakes (Ref 4967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cucumber fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate, generally demersal species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563; 7300). Inhabits sandy to muddy bottoms (Ref. 41636).

species.name: Cucumberfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Migrates into estuaries and lower reaches of rivers during spring.

species.name: Cuffum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters, bays, estuaries, mangrove-lined lagoons, and rivers (Ref. 3789, 27188). Often found in river mouths and bays, entering fresh water (Ref. 27227). Lower depth limit at 40m (Ref. 118621). Large schools may frequent particular spots for years (Ref. 9710). Feed on fishes like sardines, anchovies, Mugilidae, Centropomus, Cichlidae (mainly those forming schools) and crabs (Ref. 3789, 27188). The swim bladder, attached to the esophagus, can be filled directly with air and permits the fish to live in oxygen-poor waters. Has high fecundity, a 203 cm female is estimated to produce over 12 million eggs (Ref. 10863). Spawn in waters which can be temporarily isolated from the open sea (Ref. 27188). Transparent leptocephalus larvae migrate into estuaries (Ref. 57533). Famous for its spectacular leaps when hooked. Marketed fresh or salted (Ref. 3789). Large scales are used in ornamental work and in preparation of artificial pearls (Ref. 3789). Used to be cultured commercially in Colombia (Ref. 7306). Highly appreciated by sport fishers. The flesh is also highly appreciated despite its being bony (Ref. 27188). The world record for hook and line is 283 lbs. from Lake Maricaibo, Venezuela (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Cui-ui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep water.  Spawns only around margin of Pyramid Lake in Nevada, USA but formerly made spectacular spawning runs up Truckee River in Nevada, USA.  Populations were subject to intensive fishing in the 19th and early 20th century; habitats have been greatly altered by water development projects; species is now endangered (Ref. 47054).

species.name: Cuisinier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral-rich areas of lagoon pinnacles, channels, and outer reef slopes.  Solitary (Ref. 37816), a secretive species, usually hiding in caves and crevices in the reefs.  One of the smallest species of groupers known.  Omnivorous with diet composed of fishes and crustaceans; relatively low egg production per individual (Ref. 089707).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Cuisinier (Cephalopholis urodeta)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear, shallow waters of outer reef areas, in lagoons, back-reef areas, and on the reef-top.  As solitary individuals (Ref. 90102), they prefer healthy coral reef in shallow areas, and are therefore greatly affected by reef degradation (Ref. 89707). They feed on small fishes (68%) and crustaceans. Because of its small size, the darkfin hind is not of much interest as a food fish (except perhaps to subsistence fisheries), but it does well in an aquarium and may find a market as an aquarium fish. They are caught with hook-and-line, gill nets, and in traps (Ref. 39231).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Culion silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology is unknown.  Probably preyed upon by commercial fish species as food.

species.name: Culter alburnus
species.description: Inhabits rivers (Ref. 1441, 26334), floodplain lakes which are overgrown with aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 41072).

species.name: Culter recurviceps
species.description: Utilized for food (Ref. 44394).

species.name: Cumberland darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cumberland darter (Etheostoma susanae)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cumberland plateau darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Cumberland snubnose darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in small to medium streams in gravel riffle areas (Ref. 6466).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Cunene barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cunene dwarf happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307). Mouth-brooding females (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Cunene happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovophilic, agamous, maternal moutbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Cunene kneria
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cunene labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers flowing water in rocky habitats (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Cunning silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cunningham's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Cunningtonia longiventralis
species.description: Gregarious, drifting plankton picker in coastal waters.  Occurs off rocky slopes but build its crater nest on sand (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Cuphead skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Reportedly taken as bycatch in deeper water benthic trawl and longline teleost target fisheries as well as in target longline skate fishing from off Mar del Plata, Argentina (Ref. 104534).

species.name: Curate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs primarily on coral reefs.  Secretive and usually solitary, under ledges or near small caves (Ref. 7251).  Often seen during the day around the bases of corals (Ref. 26938).  Feeds at night on crabs, shrimps, and polychaetes.  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Curator brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Curator sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Curaçao jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on a sand bed (Ref. 114925).

species.name: Curculionichthys insperatus
species.description: Inhabits streams, with banks covered by vegetation partially submerged into the water (Ref. 53011).

species.name: Curculionichthys karipuna
species.description: Inhabits two small, shallow, fast-flowing streams (rio Cassiporé and rio Jari) bordered with marginal vegetation. Sections of the stream of rio Cassiporé have large rocks and the vegetation has suffered high anthropic influence causing intense penetration of light. The stream of the rio Jari has 1-meter deep water in which C. karipuna lives associated to aquatic roots stuck on the border (Ref. 112322).

species.name: Curculionichthys luteofrenatus
species.description: Found in flat areas in creeks of headwaters of the Rio Tapajós in places of shallow clear waters with low current and sandy substrate, where the marginal vegetation is represented mainly by grass in deforested areas (Ref. 75061).

species.name: Curculionichthys monolechis
species.description:
This species was collected in rivers and small- to medium-sized rainforest creeks in areas of rocky rapids and sandbanks. The extinction risk of this species is estimated to be low despite  incomplete knowledge of its populational trends and geographic distribution. The species is known from at least 16 localities in the Saramacca River of Suriname and the Marowijne
(¼Maroni) in Suriname and French Guiana, with an estimated Extension of Occurrence (EOO) of 56,513 km2, based on the minimum convex polygon around known localities.  It seems to be abundant and despite logging and gold mining being widespread in the area, no specific threats were identified in the region, which is largely forested. Thus, for these reasons, this species is tentatively categorized as Least Concern (LC) according to the IUCN categories and criteria
(IUCN Standards and Petitions Subcommittee, 2019) (Ref. 130866).

species.name: Curculionichthys scaius
species.description: This species was collected in a third order creek with clear water, bottom formed mainly by sand and leaf litter, wirh an average width of 2.5 m and depth of 0.3 m; collected when water temperature was 23.6 Celsius and dissolved oxygen 1.88 PPM. The creek edges were covered by gallery forest, but portions have been deforested and pastures are now reaching to the river margin (Ref. 119375).

species.name: Curimata cerasina
species.description: Inhabits rivers, ponds and other highly turbid still waters, usually over muddy bottoms (Ref. 34109).

species.name: Curimata cyprinoides
species.description: Inhabits swamps and feeds on organic debris, benthic organisms and periphyton.  Has filaments on its palette which play a gustatory role and also functions in mucus secretion which facilitates ingestion of food.  Appears to undergo mass migration during reproduction (Ref. 12225).  During reproduction, it is then easily captured with nets along the banks where the dense vegetation is flooded (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Curimata inornata
species.description: Feeds on detritus (Ref. 12371).

species.name: Curimata vittata
species.description: Feeds on detritus (Ref. 12371).

species.name: Curimatella immaculata
species.description: Inhabits still waters along the margins of lagoons.  Feeds on a variety of algae and fungi.

species.name: Curimatopsis cryptica
species.description: Lives mainly in swamps.  Forms schools near the surface.  Males appear rare, they represent less than 10% of captured specimens (Ref. 12225).  Males are smaller than females (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Curious wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and rubble slopes (Ref. 48637, 58302) or mud bottoms and take refuge in burrows (Ref. 2334).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Solitary or paired.  Feed primarily on benthic and pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Curipe Toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Curlfin sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on soft bottom (Ref. 2850).  Feed on brittle stars and nudibranchs (Ref. 27436).  Minimal interest to anglers, usually an incidental catch (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Curmuca barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, usually in deep pools and shady parts in the hilly regions.  Lives and breeds in hilly terrain but comes down to tidal reaches for feeding.  Spawns in small streams with sandy and weedy bottoms.  Feeds mainly on algae and occasionally on insect larvae.

species.name: Current darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Curtain-nose worm eel
species.description: Inhabits tide pools or around coral reefs (Ref. 106110).

species.name: Curumim tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Curve-bar cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits a karstic warm spring, Media Luna, which exists because of a tectonic ridge forming a hill southwest (SW) of El Jabalí. This spring formerly emptied into Rio Viejo, which has been blocked and diverted for agricultural purposes. It is sympatric with H. bartoni and H. cf carpintis which was translocated into the Media Luna system (Ref. 94458). Aquarium conditions: pH=7, H=3, 25°C water temperature, omnivore, egg layer, needs plant and rock cover, not easy to raise in captivity.

species.name: Curved sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits holes and crevices in eroded limestone shoreline (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Curvedspine scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Cut-face pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves in drop-offs (Ref. 10685).

species.name: Cutribbon wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal to outer reef crests.  In Japan, it is found in areas of mixed sand, rock and coral (Ref. 9710).  Occurs in small groups to about 20 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Feeds by sorting small animals from mouthfuls of sand and detritus.

species.name: Cuyo coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary in reef crevices to 33 m, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Cyan hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs all around Chinyamwezi near small rocks (Ref. 5595). It feeds on algae from the biocover on rocks as well as on plankton from the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Cyanocharax uruguayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cyanogaster noctivaga
species.description: Specimens were caught with a seine pulled at approximately 1.5 m depth. The type locality is a beach on a rocky poorly vegetated plateau, where the water was dark black with slow current. Individuals were collected at night, approximately between 20:00 and 24:00, during the dry season (October). Stomach contents of cleared and stained specimens were mainly remnants of insect larvae (Ref. 93233).

species.name: Cyathochromis obliquidens
species.description: Found in shallow water and always in the presence of plants (e.g. Vallisneria sp.).  Males are territorial and prefer rocks but some are found nesting among the weeds.  Females are mainly seen foraging in the weed beds.  Grazes mainly on loose algae from plant leaves (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys armatus
species.description: Occurs at midwater to bottom levels in rivers and streams.  Individuals are sometimes found in reservoirs but occur more frequently in flowing water.  Inhabits rivers during the dry season and migrates to floodplains to spawn during the rainy season.  Reproduction takes place relatively late in the high-water season during September and October.  Feeds on zooplankton, small crustaceans, chironomids, and other insect larvae.  Fish measuring 15-20 cm are marketed fresh and small ones are used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys enoplos
species.description: Occurs at midwater to bottom levels of rivers (Ref. 12693).  Feeds mainly on bivalves, roots of plants, zooplankton and green algae (Ref. 6459).  Young are known to feed on zooplankton while adults prey also on insect larvae, crustaceans and fish (12693).  Lives in rivers and spawns during the rainy season, probably on the floodplains or inundated riparian forests.  Returns to the rivers from October to December.  Does not occur in impoundments (Ref. 12693).  A strongly migratory species which lives in the mainstream and larger tributaries of the Mekong (Ref. 9497).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  In the Mekong, it undertakes an upstream migration from Phnom Penh to Khone Falls from November to February, and a downstream migration from May to August.  This migration continues down to the Mekong delta area in Viet Nam, where it continues until the peak of floods in October-November.  These two migrations mainly constitute juveniles and sub-adults, although adults of  90 cm are reported very near the Khone Falls.  Above the Khone Falls, upstream migrations occur from April to September which are dominated by adult fishes and probably these are spawning migrations because of the presence of mature fishes bearing eggs (Ref. 37770).  These upstream migrations above the Khone Falls are reported to be triggered by the first rainfall at the end of the dry season, rising of water levels and higher turbidity (Ref. 37770).  A desirable food fish, marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys furcatus
species.description: Inhabits large rivers and probably migrates into flooded riparian forests and smaller streams during the rainy season.  Does not occur in impoundments.  Little is known about the biology of this species.  Occasionally seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys heteronema
species.description: Inhabits rivers over muddy substrate as well as forest streams (Ref. 56749).  Occur near the bottom of large rivers.  Typically found in the middle Mekong during the dry season and moves into flooded forest during high water periods. Little is known about its biology.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693, 57235).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys janthochir
species.description: Inhabits areas with black water where it feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys lagleri
species.description: Found in lowland floodplains.  Most likely used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Cyclocheilichthys schoppeae
species.description: Inhabits streams, medium and large rivers with clear, slowly moving to relatively fast flowing water, with gravel and muddy substrate.  Feeds on shrimps, worms, insect larvae and detritus (Ref. 57971).

species.name: Cyclopharynx fwae
species.description: Mainly feeds on algae and diatoms; ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Cyclopharynx schwetzi
species.description: Mainly feeds on algae and diatoms; ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Cyclopteropsis bergi
species.description: Maximum depth reported at 200m (Ref. 56557).

species.name: Cyclothone de Brauer
species.description: Oceanic, precise depth range dependent upon developmental stage, latitude, season (Ref. 4769).  Generally horizontally oriented (Ref. 4769).  Feeds on small zooplankton, mostly copepods (Ref. 5162).  Sexually dimorphic with large females and small males (Ref. 9503).  Sex ratio vary with size groups but is about 1:1 around spawning. Length-frequency histograms are bimodal; has a two-year life cycle (Ref. 82363).

species.name: Cyclothone livida
species.description: A pseudoceanic, deep mesopelagic to bathypelagic species (Ref. 4769).  Does not exhibit vertical migrations (Ref. 4463).

species.name: Cyclothone pygmaea
species.description: Precise depth range dependent upon developmental stage and season.  Presumed dioecious, spawns during spring to autumn (Ref. 4769).

species.name: Cyclothone à petites dents
species.description: An oceanic, deep mesopelagic to bathypelagic species (Ref. 4769).  Precise depth range dependent upon developmental stage, latitude, season (Ref. 4769).
