Doest not exhibit diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4769). A non-seasonal breeder with no recognizable age-cohorts (Ref. 82363).  Feeds mainly on copepods (Ref. 4769).

species.name: Cylindrical lantern shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Cylindrical sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered bays, harbors and lagoons, but mainly clear water habitats (Ref. 48636).  Occurs on sand, rubble, seagrass, or weedy bottoms near shallow reefs (Ref. 42740, 48636).  Common in seagrass beds (Ref. 9710).  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Cynodon gibbus
species.description: Apparently carnivorous, probably ichthyophagous.

species.name: Cynodon meionactis
species.description: Predatory species.

species.name: Cynodonichthys birkhahni
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys boehlkei
species.description: Questionably non annual breeder (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys brunneus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys chucunaque
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys elegans
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys frommi
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys fuscolineatus
species.description: Mainly in waters of moderate to high current velocity between 525 and 695 m elevation, also abundant in a pool with much vegetation and little current.  More abundant in waters of greater current velocity.  Always swims near a grass or undergrowth refuge over muddy or sand bottoms.  Eats aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys glaucus
species.description: Recorded in brooks and creeks between 540 and 680 m elevation, tolerates low temperatures and currents of low to moderate velocity.  Eats terrestrial and aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys hildebrandi
species.description: Recorded between 10 and 1220 m elevation in swamps, creeks or brooks and most abundant in waters of little current.  Eats insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys isthmensis
species.description: Inhabits swamps and ditches and slow moving waters of brooks and creeks between sea level and 1500 m elevation.  Feeds on insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys kuelpmanni
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys leucurus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys monikae
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys montium
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys pacificus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys rubripunctatus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys siegfriedi
species.description: Inhabits waters of lower elevation between 20N and 80 m.  Found in puddles, swamps and brooks of low to moderate velocity.  Eats insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys uroflammeus
species.description: Inhabit puddles, swamps and brooks of low to moderate velocity.  Recorded between 750 and 1100 m elevation.  Feed on insects (Ref. 36880).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynodonichthys weberi
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynoglossus robustus
species.description: Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Cynoglossus sealarki
species.description: Recorded from a depth of 225 m (Ref. 5297).

species.name: Cynoglossus sibogae
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters, on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 27550).  Feeds on benthic animals, especially crustaceans (Ref. 27550).

species.name: Cynolebias akroa
species.description: Known only from the type locality, in temporary pools of about 1.3 m deep. Commonly found co-existing with other annual fish species of the genus Hypsolebias. Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 127992).

species.name: Cynolebias brillant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is very difficult, experimented, to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias de Constance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium conditions preferred:  pH=7, H=10, 22°C, with rocks, plants and driftwood.  Egg laying peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).  Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias gilbertoi
species.description: In temporary ponds.  Known only from the type locality (Ref. 27234).  Bottom spawner, ? months incubation.

species.name: Cynolebias griseus
species.description: Bottom spawner, 4 months.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias leptocephalus
species.description: Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias marbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Collected in clear water shallow pools (about 30 cm deep) in forest; no aquatic vegetation (Ref. 50094).

species.name: Cynolebias microphthalmus
species.description: Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner,10 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias obscurus
species.description: Occurs in vestigial small pools, measuring about 3 m wide and extending close and parallel to the road for about 1 km. The whole area around the pool is composed of plantation, without any vestige of the original habitat.  Sympatric with <i>Hypsolebias macaubensis (Ref. 97357).

species.name: Cynolebias opalescent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium conditions preferred:  pH=6.8, H=7, 25°C, with rocks, plants and driftwood.  Carnivorous, egg laying and peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).  Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias oticus
species.description: Occurs in temporary pools of the Verde river drainage, near the village of Pindaí.  The region has been highly deforested in recent years, resulting to the extinction of some seasonal killifishes (<i>Cynolebias gilbertoi, <i>C. leptocephalus, <i>Hypsolebias fulminantis) previously inhabiting the area. <i>C. oticus<i> can still be easily found in the area even under such condition (Ref. 97357).

species.name: Cynolebias parietalis
species.description: Inhabits temporary pools in the floodplains (Ref. 97357).

species.name: Cynolebias parnaibensis
species.description: The type locality of this species is inserted in the Caatinga domain, a semi-arid phytogeographic formation, typical of northeastern Brazil; the lagoon is within the Canindé River drainage, which is part of the Parnaíba River basin. It was about 60 m long, 15 m wide, maximum depth 1 m, average depth 50 cm; water is turbid, light brown, and the bottom was sandy-muddy; emerging aquatic vegetation in moderate amount, scattered over the lagoon surface, while large amount of submerged vegetation was found, the predominant species of the family Hydrocharitaceae. Margins of the pond were in part densely covered by bushes and low vegetation (Ref. 84460).

species.name: Cynolebias perforatus
species.description: Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias porosus
species.description: Inhabits river floodplain (Ref. 97357).  Bottom spawner, 5-7 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynolebias rectiventer
species.description: Found in two adjacent and shallow temporary lagoons of about 1.0 m deep with an area of about 5 km2, within a small farm for cattle breeding, and with sparse aquatic vegetation.  Collected close to the lagoon bottom (Ref. 97357).

species.name: Cynopoecilus melanotaenia
species.description: Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cynopoecilus notabilis
species.description: Found only in a temporary pool characterized by clear water over a muddy bottom covered by large amount of litter within a dense fragment of wetland forest connected and adjacent to a swamp where the only known two specimens of <i>Listrura depinnai were collected (Ref. 98301).

species.name: Cynopotamus essequibensis
species.description: Is a predator whose main food is not known.  Appears to prefer an environment with fast current over rocky bottom which is typical of the rapids.  Frequently found in the upstream areas of rivers (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Cynotilapia afra
species.description: Found common in the upper part of the rocky biotope which is usually sediment-free (Ref. 5595). Males which are territorial mainly feed from the biocover on the rocks close to their homestead while others which are more gregarious feed on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Cynotilapia axelrodi
species.description: Occurs in the more rocky areas of this biotope.  Feeds mainly on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Cynotilapia zebroides
species.description: Found in all rocky habitats of Lake Malawi (Ref. 88848).

species.name: Cyphocharax aspilos
species.description: Inhabits swamps and rivers (Ref. 26543).  Feeds exclusively on detritus (Ref. 26543).  Hardly ever consumed (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Cyphocharax biocellatus
species.description: The type locality of the holotype is a side channel of  Litani River that isolated a small, elongate, forested island.  The channel dominantly consists of shallow cataracts over a bedrock substrate strewn with boulders in the upper portions and a small, shallow (less than 2 m deep) backwater over a sand substrate in the downstream portion.  The channel margins  are composed of shallow pockets of slackwater habitat, often with submerged vegetation and shaded by overhanging bank vegetation extending into the water.  Found in shallow (0.50 m deep) tributary to the  main river in an area with relatively rapid water flow (around 1m/s) and principally sandy substrate with some rocky bars and large pieces of dead wood (Ref. 90234).

species.name: Cyphocharax gilbert
species.description: Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Cyphocharax gillii
species.description: The species was reported to swim near the bottom to feed, substrate containing food are scooped and ingested.  Stomach content with diatoms, desmids, and epiphytic filamentous algae.  Apparently territorial, guarding areas with submerged grassy plants with algal cover, defending with chases, nips, strikes, and mouth fighting.  May form schools of up to 30 individuals.  Also reported to occur in small streams or places of weak currents in adjoining swampy areas.  Captured along banks of rivers (Ref. 11334).

species.name: Cyphocharax helleri
species.description: Usually occurs over sand or mud, in areas with slow moving current.  Feeds on detritus (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Cyphocharax laticlavius
species.description: Inhabits shallow, slow-moving blackwater streams with sandy bottoms (Ref. 30552).

species.name: Cyphocharax magdalenae
species.description: Inhabits rivers or creeks of moderate current between 20 and 10 m elevation.  Abundant in shallow waters over sand or mud bottoms where it feeds on detritus, diatoms and algae (Ref. 36880).  Found in swamps or marshes and rivers (Ref. 26543).  Feeds exclusively on detritus (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Cyphocharax multilineatus
species.description: In flooded areas.

species.name: Cyphocharax muyrakytan
species.description: Collected in floodplain tributaries (Ref. 119424).

species.name: Cyphocharax naegelii
species.description: This species is engaged in large-scale seasonal migrations in the Rio Mogi Guassu (= Mogi-Guaçu), a tributary of the upper Rio Paraná.  Forty to 50-day old juveniles were reported to be zooplanktivores and the larger individuals were detrivores (Ref. 11334).

species.name: Cyphocharax nigripinnis
species.description: Occurs in both island lakes and woody shore margins in acidic black-waters of the Rio Negro basin (Ref. 11334).

species.name: Cyphocharax pantostictos
species.description: Specimens were collected in acidic blackwaters among grass and submerged vegetation (Ref. 11334).

species.name: Cyphocharax pinnilepis
species.description: Found in small rivers with relatively slow currents and somewhat turbid water and also in shallow areas of a reservoir along the Rio Gongogi. These areas have muddy substrates to some degree (Ref. 85320).

species.name: Cyphocharax platanus
species.description: Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Cyphocharax punctatus
species.description: Occurs in extensive shoals over sand or mud,  in tributaries of rivers or in inundated areas of creeks with little current (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Cyphocharax sanctigabrielis
species.description:
The type locality is a shallow (30-50 cm), slow-flowing stream over fine and sand substrate
within a well-preserved forested setting with the stream borders lined with grasses and rushes (Ref. 96871).

species.name: Cyphocharax spilurus
species.description: Occurs in the rapids, in creeks with sandy or rocky bottoms.  Feeds on detritus (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Cyphocottus megalops
species.description: Occurs mainly at a depth of 100 m where the bottom is silty (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Cyphomyrus cubangoensis
species.description: Adult specimens prefer larger river channels with soft bottom; small specimens also found in rocky environment; shoaling species (Ref. 119538).

species.name: Cyphomyrus lufirae
species.description: Found in river sections with moderate current, he depth of the water was variable, between 50 cm and 10 m (Ref. 122874). This species is highly appreciated by the local inhabitants of the Lufira River due to the high fat content of its meat; they prefer to eat it smoked (Ref. 122874).

species.name: Cyphomyrus psittacus
species.description: Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head, on the ventral region (except abdominal area) and the dorsal region of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located  (Ref. 10011). Found in large rivers. Edible fish (Ref. 11970).

species.name: Cyphotilapia gibberosa
species.description: Type specimen was caught at a depth of 34 m (Ref. 52029). Cyphotilapia species are known to occur in big schools in the 30 to 40 meter layer or even deeper (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Cypress darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in standing or slow-flowing water, usually in vegetation over mud (Ref. 5723); found in streams, swamps and oxbow lakes (Ref. 10294).  Feed on midge larvae and microcrustaceans, with isopods, amphipods, and mayfly nymphs important seasonally (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Cypress minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over mud and near detritus in swamps, oxbows, and backwater and pools of sluggish streams (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably open substratum spawners like congeners.

species.name: Cyprichromis coloratus
species.description: Occurs exclusively over rocky substratum, 1-5 m above the bottom from 5 m to at least 35 m depth; most abundant at ca. 15 m depth; females and sub-adult males forms mixed-species schools; adult males each maintain territories above adjacent large rocks or boulders; feed almost exclusively on cyploploid copepodids; mouthbrooding females (Ref. 57033).

species.name: Cyprichromis leptosoma
species.description: Gregarious, adults occur off rocky slopes.  'Headstanders', often remain still with the head low.  Drifting zooplankton feeders, but also feed on shellfish (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Cyprichromis microlepidotus
species.description: Gregarious, occurs off a rocky slope; drifting plankton feeder but also feeds on shellfish; occurs in quiet waters (Ref. 6770). Pelagic species, occuring in deep water; copepods have been found in stomach of one specimen (Ref. 53528). Maternal mouthbrooder and typical lek-breeder (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Cyprichromis pavo
species.description: Found rocky habitats in in-shore waters at a depth of usually 20 to 50 meters; copepods and algae were found in stomach (Ref. 103657).

species.name: Cyprichromis zonatus
species.description: Found 1-5 m above rocky bottoms; forms schools consisting of females and sub-adult males (often joining other schools of related species); mature males keeping a territory above a large rock or boulder in areas 15-25 m depth; mouthbrooder (Ref. 46826).

species.name: Cyprin lippu tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A gregarious species which inhabits near shore lakes and slow-flowing stretches and backwaters of streams and rivers (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on fish, invertebrates (Ref. 26100), insect larvae and periphyton (Ref. 59043).  Spawns over gravel beds or among vegetation at temperatures above 12°C (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Cyprin-sucet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a wide range of habitats, from rocky pools and riffles of headwaters to large lakes.  Usually occurs in small, clear, cool creeks and small to medium rivers.  May be found at a depth greater than 45 m (Ref. 1998).  Moves to shallower water near sunrise and sunset to feed.  Fry (1.2 cm in length) feed on plankton and other small invertebrates; bottom feeding commences upon reaching a length of 1.6-1.8 cm.  Preyed upon by birds, fishes, lamprey, and mammals (Ref. 1998).  Flesh is white, flaky, and sweet (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Cyprinion acinaces
species.description: It is locally consumed (Ref. 129076).

species.name: Cyprinion microphthalmum
species.description: Found in montane and submontane regions (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Cyprinion milesi
species.description: Found in montane and submontane regions.

species.name: Cyprinion watsoni
species.description: Lives in montane and submontane regions (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Cyprinodon brontotheroides
species.description: Inhabits six hypersaline lakes (Crescent Pond, Osprey Lake, Oyster Lake, Little Lake, Wild Dilly Pond and Moon Rock Pond). Sympatric with Cyprinodon variegatus in all six lakes and with C. desquamator in four of the six lakes (except Wild Dilly Pond and Moon Rock Pond). Feeds on gastropods and ostracods. Spawning occurs in spring and summer seasons, but may be more more common in the spring. Breeding territories are guared by males (Ref. 94405).

species.name: Cyprinodon dearborni
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cyprinodon desquamator
species.description: Inhabits six hypersaline lakes (Crescent Pond, Osprey Lake, Oyster Lake, Little Lake, Mermaid Pond and Great Lake). Sympatric with Cyprinodon variegatus in all six lakes and with C. brontotheroides in four of the six lakes (except Great Lake and Mermaid Pond). These lakes are shallow, rarely exceeding 3 m depth, and densities of Cyprinodon are greatest in mats of macroalgae (Batophora, Acetabularia and Cladophora) and wigeongrass (Ruppia maritima) along the littoral margins of each lake. Feeds on scales of other fishes. Spawning occurs in spring and summer seasons, but it seems to be more common in the summer. Breeding territories are guarded by males (Ref. 94405).

species.name: Cyprinodon higuey
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cyprinodon nichollsi
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cyprinodon riverendi
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Cyprinodon suavium
species.description: Carnivorous, feeding on snails (Pyrgophorus coronatus), ostracodes and bivalves (Ref. 55026).

species.name: Cyprinus acutidorsalis
species.description: Occurs in river mouth (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Cyprinus barbatus
species.description: Adults live in lake (Ref. 26563).  Previously important in fisheries (Ref. 45623). Length type refers to body length (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Cyprinus ilishaestomus
species.description: Adults dwell mainly in deep water with aquatic plants.  Feed mainly on shrimps, small fishes and some aquatic plants (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Cyprinus longipectoralis
species.description: Inhabits lake (Ref. 26563).  Length type refers to body length (Ref. 26563).  Stays in the open water area of the lake.  Feeds mainly on zoobenthos, insect larva and plants.  Spawning period from March to April.  Local people call it "Chun-Yu" (spring fish), as it spawns early (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Cyprinus longzhouensis
species.description: Utilized for food (Ref. 33508).

species.name: Cyprinus megalophthalmus
species.description: Lives in the upper and middle layers of the lake along the shore and in winter it stays in deep places of water.  Feeds on plankton, small fishes, shrimps and algae.  Spawns in May and June mainly at the bottom sides of rocks in shallow clear water (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Cyprinus multitaeniatus
species.description: Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 9671).

species.name: Cyprinus rubrofuscus
species.description: Found in freshwater, but tolerant to slightly brackish water (Ref. 82587).

species.name: Cyprinus yilongensis
species.description: Adults mostly live in the deep parts of the lake without waterweeds.  Feed mainly on plankton.  Spawning period is in April and May (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Cyprinus yunnanensis
species.description: Adults live in shallow water with aquatic plants and usually seeks food in the middle and lower layers of water bodies.  Feed mainly on small fishes and shrimps.  Viscid eggs are spawned on aquatic plants in April and May (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Cypselurus hiraii
species.description: Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Czekanowski's minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, backwaters (Ref. 59043) and rivers (Ref. 1441).  A mature male measures 7.0 cm TL (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Cépole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottom (Ref. 26999).  Lives in vertical burrows but may be found swimming in midwater.  Occurs singly or in groups.  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans and chaetognaths (Ref. 5984).

species.name: Céteau
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Inhabits mainly sandy or sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on a wide range of small bottom-living organisms, mainly crustaceans, polychaete worms, bivalve mollusks, etc. (Ref. 4710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27121.

species.name: Céteau ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, occasionally up to 150 m depth (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Córdoba livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Córrego toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Cœur saignant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and plants (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: D'Arros pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef flats at depths of less than 3 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dabra goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dacodraco hunteri
species.description: Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 41551).

species.name: Dadio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and pools.  Adult females can grow up to 3 cm (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Dadyanos insignis
species.description: Inhabits the intertidal zone, where it spawns, to the inner shelf.  It may occur deeper than 40 m (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Daector gerringi
species.description: May have potential of entering estuarine habitats.

species.name: Dagmar’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dagsit
species.description: Occurs on continental and insular shelves and oceanic waters adjacent to them (Ref. 244).  Common on coral reefs, often in deeper areas near drop-offs to the open sea, in atoll passes, and in shallow lagoons adjacent to areas of strong currents (Ref. 244).  Coastal-pelagic near the bottom, near drop-offs at 1-275 m (Ref. 58302).  Forms daytime schools or aggregations in favored areas (Ref. 244).  Although active during the day, it is more active nocturnally (Ref. 244).  Viviparous, with 1-6 pups (Ref. 37816).  Feeds on reef fishes, squids, octopi, crabs, lobsters and shrimps (Ref. 244, 5578).  Tends to be aggressive under baited conditions (Ref. 6871) and readily enters into a frenzy feeding pattern, at which time it may become quite dangerous.  Repeatedly incriminated in human attacks.  Utilized for human consumption, fishmeal, and other shark products.  Minimum depth from Ref. 6871.  Maximum length of female taken from Ref. 5213.

species.name: Dahl's frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in the continental shelf and inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Dainty dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky tide pools and along the shore.

species.name: Dalaman spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dalhousie catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the bottom of warm, artesian, spring-fed pools and their outlet streams.  Tolerates salinity to 10 p.p.t. and temperatures between 16° and 44°C, but usually remains in water between 30° and 38°C.  Fish active at night.  Stomach contents consist of hydrobiid snails, conchostracans, hard parts of unidentified insects or caddisfly larval cases (Ref. 27663, 44894), microcrustaceans, fishes (hardyheads) and some plant material.  The smallest member of the family; females become sexually mature at length of only 5.2 centimeters (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Dalhousie goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water at the edges of warm, spring-fed pools and outflow swamps. It has a broad temperature tolerance (21.6°-43°C), but usually does not venture into water above 36°C. Diurnally active, omnivorous species which feeds on filamentous algae. Also cannibalistic, with adults feeding on young fish. Breeding biology is probably similar to C. eremius, a species formerly considered to be conspecific (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Dalhousie hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm water artesian springs and their outlet streams (Ref. 2906, 44894).  Tolerates temperatures ranging from 20°-39°C, but has been recorded briefly entering water of 41.8°C to feed.  A diurnally-active species which has one of the highest recorded voluntary temperature tolerances of any fish species in the world (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on gastropods, aquatic plants (Ref. 2906), green filamentous algae, detritus and small invertebrates which are taken from the bottom (Ref. 44894).  Dimorphic:  bigger females with concave head and flat belly, long cylindrical sac-like ovary on left side of fish while the yellow-white testis lies on the right side.  Appears to suffer thermal stress above 38°C but can tolerate low oxygen levels (Ref. 7276).

species.name: Dalhousie mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits artesian springs and associated swampy areas over a wide range of temperatures (13°-36°C). At one spring it was found in temperatures ranging from 21.6°-35.6°C, although it was most abundant in the cooler, downstream sections. Feeds on filamentous green algae, snails and fishes. Co-occurs with 5 other species at Dalhousie springs including Neosilurus gloveri (Plotosidae), Craterocephalus dalhousiensis and C. gloveri (Atherinidae), Leiopotherapon unicolor (Terapontidae) and Chlamydogobius gloveri (Gobiidae) (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Dali
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in seagrass areas, rocky reefs, and adjacent soft bottoms (Ref. 12951). Avoids temperatures above 20°C (Ref. 10011). Nocturnal, usually burying itself during the day with only the eyes and spiracle jutting out (Ref. 12382). Feeds on small benthic fishes Trachurus, Mugil, Mullus, Dicentrarchus, Spondyliosoma, Boops, Labrus, Dascyllus, Pomacentrus) and crustaceans (Ref. 10011). Females outlive males; viviparous, neonates measuring 10-14 cm at birth (Ref. 10426). Produces 2-32 pups in a litter after a 10-month gestation (Ref. 12951, Ref. 114953). Males reaches maturity at ca. 30 cm TL, females at ca. 40 cm TL; born at 10-14 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Electrocytes start developing when the embryo weighs about 1 g; electric organs functional before birth and newborns can use their electric organ discharge (EOD) in capturing prey (Ref. 10428). Can produce electric discharges of up to 200 volts; EOD frequency up to 600 Hz. Jumps on fast-moving prey, paralyzing it with its EOD (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Dallia
species.description: Usually found in heavily vegetated swamps and ponds; occasionally in medium to large rivers and lakes with abundant vegetation (Ref. 5723).  Migrations appear to be limited to inshore or upstream movements to spawning grounds in the spring and (presumably) reverse migrations to deeper water in the fall (Ref. 27547).  Oviparous, batch spawner (Ref. 205).  Known for their tolerance to cold water:  survives exposures to -20°C for up to 40 minutes, and can survive for a few days after complete freezing of parts of the body, even the head (Ref. 28673, 28674).  Uses its esophagus as auxiliary breathing organ (Ref. 27797).

species.name: Dalmatian barbelgudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit streams with swift water, still waters and lakes and enter subterranean waters during winter or dry seasons.  Larvae and juveniles live on the bottom and are solitary. Omnivorous.  Spawn in shallow areas of rivers and lakes. Attain up to about 20 cm SL.  Threatened due to small range, water abstraction and pollution.  The sharp decline of its population during 20th century had been caused by habitat loss and pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Dalmatian moray eel
species.description: Collecting depth and environment of the present specimens are unclear, but the holotype is strongly considered to be from the muddy bottom of less than 100 m depth because it was collected with Gymnothorax mccoskeri, Ophichthus cephalozona, Muraenesox cinereus, and some apogonid and leiognathid fishes that generally collected from shallow coastal water (Ref. 114785).

species.name: Dalophis boulengeri
species.description: Mainly nocturnal.  During the day, this fish lies buried in the sediment with the head out.

species.name: Dalophis cephalopeltis
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud in shallow water near estuaries and in rivers (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Dalophis multidentatus
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Dalophis obtusirostris
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud in shallow water near estuaries (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Dampierian threadtail Anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by benthic sled and beam trawls (Ref. 127477).

species.name: Dana lanternfish
species.description: Found in the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Mesopelagic species.

species.name: Dana pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 6601, 75154).  Adults have usually been taken in hauls at depths between 300 to 800 m; most larvae in hauls to depths between 0 to 200 m.  Most records in all areas are from localities near continental or insular land masses.  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 10755).

species.name: Dana viperfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 3588).  May migrate to near-surface waters at night (Ref. 4759).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4759).

species.name: Danakilia dinicolai
species.description: Found in Lake Abaeded, a small oval depression in a volcanic crater; lake surface is about 30 m below sea level; sand from dunes along the eastern and southern rim is frequently blown into the lake; the lake is fed by many hot springs at surface level and underwater (Ref. 85754). The lakeshore is almost completely encircled by reeds, Phragmites australis, and stands of tamarisk, Tamarix aphylla, but is free of vegetation in the proximity of hot springs (Ref. 85754). Diet primarily consisting of algae grazed from the surface of plants and rocks; however, it is likely that this species is an opportunistic feeder, as individuals were caught on lines baited with grasshoppers (Ref. 85754). Large males guard pits over sand (Ref. 85754).

species.name: Danaphryne nigrifilis
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Dancer shrimp goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coastal to outer reef habitats, around reef patches on sandy bottoms with rubble; in coral-reef moats and lagoons, outer-reef slopes, or under drop offs (Ref. 48637, 90832). Also reported in areas with patches of fine carbonate sand on subtidal reef flats and seaward reefs and uses the burrow of Alpheus rubromaculatus for refuge. It was observed to constantly wave its large, spotted, fan-like pectoral fins as it hovers close above the entrance to its burrow (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Danford’s killifish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Daniel's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in turbid channels of main rivers and also in swampy lagoons and backwaters (Ref. 2847). Also found in river deltas and mangrove areas (Ref. 38478). Feeds almost exclusively on Macrobrachium and Caridina prawns (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Danilevskii's dace
species.description: Prefers to live in main course of rivers with clear water, moderate to slow current, sand or sand-clay bottom.  Commonly stays on bottom at 0.3-3 m deep.  Avoids turbid and still waters. Occurs in small groups of individuals of similar size. Feeds mainly on insects and their larvae, molluscs, also on other benthic invertebrates and algae.  Breeds in stretches with heavy current and stone bottom.  Eggs are sticky and slightly transparent.  Larvae which don't possess adhesive glands lie passively on bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Danio absconditus
species.description: Occurs in headwaters of small coastal streams (Ref. 106271).

species.name: Danio aesculapii
species.description: The type locality is a small stream flowing out of the forest into cultivations, at most 3 m wide and about 30 cm deep.  This small stream is characterized by clear water and only slight current, bottom comprising pebbles rock, and gravel, and by the absence of aquatic vegetation.  Also occurs in a stagnant pool with leaf litter and sandy bottom and in small forest streams with rocky bottom (Ref. 81818).

species.name: Danio annulosus
species.description: Found at the foot of a waterfall draining into the Kaptai Lake, a reservoir formed by the damming of the Karnafuli River, completed in 1962. During the wet season, the fall has a height of about 100 m and falls directly into the lake. At the time of collection, the lake level was low: the waterfall had almost ceased and only some dripple moistened the rock. Water was retained in a small pool at the foot of the fall, at most about 40 cm deep, holding some pieces of rock but devoid of vegetation. Specimens were collected using seine from the deeper shadowed area of the pool along with numerous specimens of shrimp, snails, and a small species of <i>Garra. The pool drained to the lake by a small stream, only about 1 cm deep. The following species were caught in the lake at the mouth of the stream using seine:  <i>Esomus danrica (Hamilton), <i>Rasbora daniconius (Hamilton) (Cyprinidae), <i>Dermogenys burmanica Mukerji (Zenarchopteridae), <i>Aplocheilus panchax (Hamilton) (Aplocheilidae), and <i>Trichogaster lalius (Hamilton) (Osphronemidae), which are considered ubiquitous species in Bangladeshi freshwaters (Ref. 104133).

species.name: Danio catenatus
species.description: The type locality is a small clear water forest stream with bottom of pebbles, rock, and gravel. Associated with 21 fish species which include <i>Danio aesculapii and <i>Devario xyrops (Ref. 101154).

species.name: Danio choprae
species.description: Lives in streams and wells.

species.name: Danio concatenatus
species.description: Occurs in a small coastal stream (Ref. 101154).

species.name: Danio dangila
species.description: Lives in mountain streams.  Reaches to about 15 cm (Ref. 4832); reported to attain up to 8.3 cm SL (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Danio feegradei
species.description: Found in small coastal streams (Ref. 106271).

species.name: Danio flagrans
species.description: The type locality was a very small stream, about 50 cm wide, almost dry and with no other fish present.  Also found in a small stream, about 2 m wide and less than 1 m deep, with fast flowing cold water, no aquatic vegetation, lots of boulders and wood in the stream, substrate composed of sand and gravel. Another collection site was a stream up to 4 m wide and 2 m deep, with clear cool water, faster flowing parts but also deeper pools with slower water and no aquatic vegetation (Ref. 93124).

species.name: Danio htamanthinus
species.description: This species was collected from the type locality which was a small, shallow stream with clear water, margined by low vegetation, coming out of the forest and crossing a dirt road under a bridge. Associated species found were Paracanthocobitis cf. rubidipinnis, Channa gachua, Pethia meingangbii and P. thelys; and undetermined species of Badis, Dario, Danio and Esomus. The second locality near Htamanthi was a flooded cleared area with stagnant clear water over grasses and a small trickle of stream feeding it and associated species found were the following: Danio cf. quagga, Puntius chola, Pethia meingangbii, Rasbora ornata and undetermined species of Amblyceps and Dario. A female individual as small as 1.66 cm SL was found to have ripening ova (a second female 1.79 cm SL has the same large ovary with ripening ova) (Ref. 119087).

species.name: Danio kyathit
species.description: Sexually mature females were collected from a small stream with clear, brownish and fast running water with deep bamboo forest on both banks, more than 80% shaded, with mud and small stones on the bottom (Ref. 33084).

species.name: Danio roseus
species.description: Inhabits small streams with relatively cold, running water under forest cover, associated with springs and waterfalls (Ref. 37789).  Occurs usually in springs and small creeks, but also found in the Mekong main river (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Danionella dracula
species.description: Inhabits small stream (Ref. 81221).

species.name: Danionella translucida
species.description: One of the smallest freshwater fishes.

species.name: Danube barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fast to moderate-flowing premontane and montane streams and small rivers with gravel bottom.  Found most abundantly in rapids and riffles during the day.  Spawn in riffles. Attain up to about 17.5 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Danube delta dwarf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Vasile Oţel, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Danube delta gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters of large rivers on sand bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Danube ruffe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open sandy and muddy bottom in backwaters and large rivers with moderate current. Undertake migration from river mainstreams to backwaters to spawn.  Nocturnal, feeding on small invertebrates (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Danube streber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in main course of small to large rives and in stretches with strong current.  Found on stone bottom.  Active at night, feeding on aquatic invertebrates.  Spawning occurs on gravel bottom in March-May (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Danubian brook lamprey
species.description: Espèce de lamproies. Adults inhabit clear, well-oxygenated brooks in piedmont and mountain zones.  They are non-parasitic and remain in freshwater.  Ammocoetes live in detritus-rich sands or clay sediments.  Ammocoete stage lasts 3.5-4.5 years.  Ammocoetes feed on detritus and micro-organisms.  They metamorphose in July - September and spawn in March - May.  Males dig shallow nests in habitats with moderate currents (Ref. 59043).  Males and females die after spawning.

species.name: Danubian longbarbel gudgeon
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit riffles of small, fast-flowing rivers and bottom of large rivers with water velocities of 0.7 m/s and more, stone bottom, in submontane zone.  Young individuals prefer areas with slow current and shallow shoreline on sand bottom.  Adults are nocturnal and solitary while juveniles are diurnal.  Spawning occurs in shallow areas with very high current of about 1 m/s (Ref. 59043).  Adults feed on insects and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 556). Are sensitive to pollution and damming; locally threatened, especially in western and southern Danube drainage; extirpated in the upper Danube (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Dapple coris
species.description: Occurs often on sand and rubble substrata in coral reef areas (Ref. 33411).  Benthic predator (Ref. 33482).

species.name: Dapple-bellied softnose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in deep water (Ref. 8630).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.5-11.1 cm long and 7.2-7.5 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: Dappled catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dappled reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky outcrops in areas with silt or mud bottoms in 15-20 m (Ref. 90102). Specimens taken from a muddy substrate.

species.name: Dard arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fast gravel and rubble riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feed on midge larvae, hydropsychid and hydroptilid caddisfly larvae, mayfly nymphs, and fish eggs (Ref. 10294).  Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 36980).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Dard barré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in small to medium upland streams (Ref. 10294).  Adults feed on midge, blackfly, and caddisfly larvae, mayfly nymphs, isopods, and amphipods (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Dard de sable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs of small to medium rivers, usually in 60 cm or deeper water.  Locally common but rapidly decreasing in abundance due to siltation and deterioration of water quality (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Dard à ventre jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit vegetated lakes, pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Dard-perche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common over gravel and sand in medium-sized rivers but can be found almost anywhere from small, fast-flowing rock-bottomed streams to vegetated lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on larvae of midges, mayflies, caddisflies (especially hydropsychids), riffle beetles, stoneflies, limpets, and fish eggs (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Darekh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters rivers for spawning in spring (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Dargo Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Recorded from a small (0.5-1.3 m average width, 0.05-0.40 m average depth), cool, clear, alpine creek, flowing through a grassy plain, consisting predominantly of riffles and pools, and with very little shading except that provided by grasses. During winter this catchment is often covered by snow for varying periods of time. Substrate consisted mainly of bedrock with some loose boulders, with smaller amounts of pebble, gravel, sand and clay and overlain in backwaters by silt. Instream cover provided by rock and by bank and vegetation (alpine grasses) overhang, and pools averaged 0.5 m in depth. Recorded at densities of 4.2-6.4 fish/m2 and is the only native fish species so far recorded from within its range and the only species of Galaxias found within its current restricted range. Historically have been found with Galaxias olidus, which is present nearby. Galaxias brevipinnis, Galaxias maculatus and Galaxias truttaceus are found farther downstream in the Dargo River system and their ranges may also have historically overlapped with this species. Alien trout have substantially altered distributional patterns in the last 150 years and fragmented and reduced the distributional range of galaxiids and their populations (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Dario dario
species.description: Collected from a stream (in November, dry season) which varied in width between 2-5 m and in depth 30-70 cm; the water is crystal clear and around 26°C; dense vegetation of aquatic plants (e.g. Limnophila, Hygrophila, Vallisneria, Ottelia, and Rotala species); bottom cover was sand and fine gravel (Ref. 46238).

species.name: Dario dayingensis
species.description: Collected from a small stream, wider than 2 m, about 30 cm deep, with relatively fast current, running through an open cultured area.  Bottom composed of substrate rock, sand, leaf litter and mud (Ref. 46238).

species.name: Dario huli
species.description: Occurs in a small, clearwater stream, up to 5 m wide and 2 m deep, with sandy bottom and larger rocks and boulders.  Collected from among vegetation hanging down into the water along the edges of the stream.  Found associated with the following fish species:  <i>Devario malabaricus, <i>Rasbora dandia, <i>Danio rerio, <i>Lepidocephalichthys thermalis, <i>Acanthocobitis cf. mooreh, <i>Pterocryptis wynaadensis, <i>Mastacembelus cf. armatus, <i>Channa cf. gachua, and <i>Pseudosphromenus cupanus (Ref. 98908).

species.name: Dario kajal
species.description: This species is collected from a small, shallow pool with stagnant to slow-flowing water; at the time of collection, the pool was turbid and had no aquatic vegetation (Ref. 94460).

species.name: Dario urops
species.description: Found in a small clear water stream, up to 10 m wide and 2 m deep, with a bottom formed of a mixture of sand and mud and larger boulders. Occurs mostly from among bundles of tree roots hanging into the water along the edges of the stream and from thicker layers of leaf litter that had accumulated in low current depressions of the stream (Ref. 90259).

species.name: Dark banded rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which inhabits upper slopes (Ref. 26363).

species.name: Dark blind ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species on continental slope. Probably suction feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates based on its oral morphology. Biology little known. Maturity size uncertain, probably close to 18 cm TL in males (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Dark brown snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Maximum length  based on a juvenile specimen (Ref. 42734).

species.name: Dark chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes.

species.name: Dark coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices between about 2-10 m depth, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Dark cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154) and uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous (Ref. 6555).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dark damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dark deepwater snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is captured by trawl over sand and muddy bottom between 36-1350 and observed from submersibles to be most abundant between 250-350 m, with only the heads exposed over sandy substrates or resting on the sediment with their bodies in S-shaped curves (Ref. 86730).  Mature females collected 48-62.8 cm TL (Ref. 40865).

species.name: Dark dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often in rocky crevices (Ref. 9137); coral reefs on reef slopes (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Dark dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a surge channel cut well back into the shore.  Most of the other collections were taken from rocky and coral areas in waters less than 10 m (Ref. 96083).

species.name: Dark fin cusk eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Smaller specimens are found in deeper waters (Ref. 9942).  Feeds on crustaceans and gastropods (Ref. 68964). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dark freckled catshark
species.description: Recorded specimens are mostly demersal, about 400-500 m deep, and associated with coral formations, where it possibly lays its egg-cases. Stomach contents consist of small invertebrates (cephalopods), small bony fishes, and one hagfish (Class Myxini) egg-case which was found in the stomach of an adult specimen. The size at first maturity is not well defined, but 45.0 cm TL males and 47.0 cm TL females are adults.  Reproduction is by oviparity, with at least two amber colored egg capsules (one for each uterus) which are smooth, lacking longitudinal grooves and measuring about 15.2 cm long and 5.8 cm wide (Ref. 101269).

species.name: Dark ghost shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 26346).  Feeds on crustaceans, shellfish, worms and small fish (Ref. 26346).  Maximum length 87 cm without tail filament (Ref. 26346), assumed to have 96 cm TL.  Marketed as fillets (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Dark mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Dark mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found around the tidal estuaries and intertidal zone at or near the boundary between freshwater and brackish water areas of small insular streams with gravel bottoms and boulders. It is usually seen perched on large boulders, and nimbly skates on the surface of the boulders when disturbed (Ref. 128872).

species.name: Dark sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dark smiling whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Dark snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally restricted to relatively narrow regions, characterized by humid rainforest climate (Ref. 43157).

species.name: Dark stonebasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors the shallow mud bottom waters near fringing vegetation such as papyrus and Vossia (Ref. 9606). Feeds on aquatic insects, mainly chironomid larvae (Ref. 12526), on Caridina and caenid larvae (Ref. 9606), but also on algae and plankton (Ref. 36900). A male to female ratio of 1:10.5 has been noted for this species; it breeds continuously throughout the year with obvious peaks during the rains (Ref. 10608). Anadromous (Ref. 10608). Migrates up the rivers to spawn in temporary pools and streams (Ref. 4903, 10608). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dark throat worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dark toad plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dark toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dark-barred goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In shallow to deep coastal muddy substrates.  Swims in small to large aggregations and mixes with other similar species (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Dark-belly skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dark-fin chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral rich areas of outer reef passes and slopes.  They occur singly or in small groups near the bottom (Ref. 7247).  Diurnal species (Ref. 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dark-finned sand goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand or sand and leaf litter bottoms; where collections are found in the latter, this species was collected with several specimens of Ptereleotris carinata and M. erectus. Presumed to be a burrowing species (Ref. 91780).

species.name: Dark-finned stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft bottoms of lower continental shelf (Ref. 128009).

species.name: Dark-finned velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Dark-margin Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dark-shouldered snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy to sandy inshore areas and occasionally forages in the open at night (Ref. 637).  Burrowing species (Ref. 75154).  Caught rarely with gill net from the muddy shallow bottoms of Ryukyu Islands (Ref. 637). Nocturnally active (Ref 90102).

species.name: Dark-spot tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit flat sandy or weedy areas (Ref. 3131).  Found solitary in rubble, silt or sand bottoms (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  A good food fish.

species.name: Dark-spotted moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Darkbar flyingfish
species.description: Found in near-shore surface waters, never spread to open sea.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Darkblotch goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with leaf, shell and organic debris (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Darkblotched rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-water species found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Darkedged splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darkfin jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Founf on bottoms with gravel and sand or on silt and sand bottoms, near coral reefs and rocky areas (Ref. 129348). Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Darkfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darkfinned numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore continental waters (Ref. 9912).  Biology little known (Ref. 9912). Size usually smaller to 35 cm TL. Males reaches maturity smaller than 28 cm TL; born at ca. 13 cm TL (Ref. 114953).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Darkgill snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Darklip snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Darkmargin grouper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darksaddle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darkspotted catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diurnal.

species.name: Darkspotted scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species.  Inhabits deeper reefs. Solitary and cryptic, also found in seaward reefs, mainly at oceanic islands (Ref 90102).

species.name: Darktail cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary and secretive, found in patch or fringing reefs near shore, often in silty conditions (Ref 90102).

species.name: Darktail parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal to outer reef crests and along drop-offs, usually in small groups (Ref. 48636); occurs at depths greater than 20 m (Ref. 40928).

species.name: Darktip cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Darling river hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing, clear waters of small creeks and streams; usually in the shallows or at the surface, often among aquatic vegetation (Ref. 44894). Found in rivers (Ref. 26703). Solitary or in small aggregations of 10-15 fish. Spawning possibly occurs in late to mid summer as indicated by the capture of sub-adults in September. The upper Hunter river (New South Wales) has yielded specimens of a similar hardyhead which are tentatively identified as C. amniculus but could prove to be a separate undescribed species. Formerly mis-identified as C. eyresii (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Darom's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Dart sand-diving lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from 100 m on sand, possibly from finer shell hash deposits. This collection also yielded high diversity of other organisms, including a large amount of sponges, as well as rubble while the second area of collection included gorgonians and shell hash (Ref.117888)

species.name: Dart stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sand dweller.

species.name: Darter characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lentic environment (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Darter characine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Darter goby
species.description: Euryhaline species, ranging from brackish water (almost entering fresh water) to hypersaline littoral lagoons (Ref. 13628), with a salinity range of 0.0 to 25.9 ppt (Ref. 97140).  Found in quiet waters of bays and estuaries, in grassy and muddy areas.

species.name: Darter sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species.

species.name: Dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sand-dweller (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Daruma stinger
species.description: Found in inshore reefs (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Darwin jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow reefs, in sand or rubble areas.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Darwin Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darwin's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Darwin's sanddab
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only found on Isla Isabela which has distinctive oceanographic conditions.  The island is directly over the Galápagos hotspot, recently has an active volcano, exceptionally dry, and has extensive local upwelling of colder deep water which occurs seasonally in the area.  The unusual combination of colder water and particularly light erosion sedimentation due to low precipitation and rocky shores create a distinctive habitat.  The Tagus Cove itself is a breached tuff cone and is characterized by coarse black sands (Ref. 93094).

species.name: Dascyllus auripinnis
species.description: Adults are found around atolls (Ref. 39312).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Dash goby
species.description: Inhabits open bottoms composed of sand and fine silt (Ref. 5521).  Observed to share a burrow with shrimps.

species.name: Dash-dot barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dashed catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river with sandy and rocky bottom and little amount of riparian and submerged vegetation (Ref. 57143).

species.name: Dashed knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dashed livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from headwaters of rivers.  Viviparous (Ref. 45800).

species.name: Dashed toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a river with dense vegetation. Occurs along with Xiphophorus signum.

species.name: Dashed-line blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or groups (Ref. 90102) near-shore rocky areas, including tide pools and at depths usually less than 1 meter (Ref. 9962).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Dashtail barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in riverine and floodplain habitats, frequently in association with the striped robber (Brycinus lateralis). Feeds on insects and small organisms. Used as bait for tigerfish (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Dasyatis hypostigma
species.description: Usually found in sandy bottoms. Mobile invertebrate feeder, feed primarily on benthic mobile invertebrates, such as mollusks, crustaceans, and worms associated with hard or nearby unconsolidated substrate (Ref. 103985).

species.name: Dasyloricaria filamentosa
species.description: Feeds on algae (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Datnioides campbelli
species.description: Occurs in brackish river mouths, coastal lagoons and rivers above tidal influence.

species.name: Datnioides polota
species.description: Lives in brackish water at the mouths of large rivers and coastal lagoons, as well as in freshwater lakes and rivers above tidal influence (Ref. 10425).  Feeds on fishes, prawns, crabs and some insect larvae.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Daubanet bélier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear reef areas over soft or semi-hard bottoms. Juveniles are encountered in seagrass (Thalassia) beds (Ref. 9626). Marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Daubenet bouton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottoms.  Sometimes taken in trawls and hook and line; good food fish (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Daubenet campèche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters.  An important food fish.

species.name: Daubenet cendre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sea grass beds from near shore to at least 22 m.  Small individuals have been known to form small aggregations.  Feeds primarily on invertebrates.  Marketed mostly fresh and frozen (Ref. 9739).

species.name: Daubenet du Golfe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly on sedimentary bottoms from 10 and 100 m depth.

species.name: Daubenet grostache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand or sandy-mud bottom.  Marketed mostly fresh, the flesh is of good quality (Ref. 3815).

species.name: Daubenet loto
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are frequently found in coral areas, while the young prefer vegetated (e.g. Thalassia), sandy bottoms. Feeds mainly on mollusks, worms, brittle stars, hermit crabs, crabs and sea urchins. Easily approached (Ref. 9710). Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Daubenet marotille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas to about 69 m depth but usually from 3-18 m.  The young occur in very shallow water on reef flats and in sandy bays over mixed sand and rock bottoms (Ref. 5592).  Probably feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9344).  Only caught incidentally with trawls (Ref. 9344).

species.name: Daubenet plume
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults often seen over rocky areas or reefs, but also on flat bottoms to about 85 m depth, while the young inhabit shallower waters (Ref. 3815).  Feeds on crabs, mollusks, worms, brittle stars and hermit crabs (Ref. 3815).  This is the most common species of the genus in the Antilles (Ref. 3815).  Important food fish (Ref. 3815).

species.name: Daubenet trembleur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters. Found on vegetated sand bottoms and more frequently on coral bottoms. Occasionally found at depths at least 180m (Ref. 09710) and 200 m. (Ref. 26938). Large adults are usually solitary. Feeds mainly on sea urchins, (including Diadema, Ref. 13442), crabs and mollusks. Excellent food fish (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Daurade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass beds and sandy bottoms as well as in the surf zone commonly to depths of about 30 m, but adults may occur to 150 m depth.  A sedentary fish, either solitary or in small aggregations.  In spring, they often occur in brackish water coastal lagoons and estuaries.  Mainly carnivorous, accessorily herbivorous (Ref. 3688).  Feed on shellfish, including mussels and oysters.  One of the most important fishes in saline and hypersaline aquaculture.  Utilized fresh and eaten steamed, pan-fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Daurade grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms.  Feeds on zoobenthos and zooplankton (Ref. 5535).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 5535.

species.name: Daurade rose
species.description: Live in small groups though large individuals may be solitary.  Inhabit inshore waters, close to the bottom on various substrates (specially rocky) to 150 m.  Adults feed on fish, crustaceans and cephalopods while the young feed on plankton (Ref. 4781).  Important food fish.

species.name: Daurade rose (Pagrus caeruleostictus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in hard bottoms (rocks and rubble), the older individuals in the deeper part of the range, the young in inshore areas.  Feed mainly on bivalves and also on crustaceans and fish.  Sexual maturity at 2 years old.  Spawning migration occurs parallel to the coast with intermittent spawning between spring and autumn over soft bottoms in shallow waters (Ref. 3688).

species.name: Daurade à gros yeux
species.description: Inhabit rocky or sandy bottoms; individuals descending to greater depths with growth.  The stocks migrate seasonally between the coast and deeper waters in accordance with local hydrographic conditions and their life cycle.  Feed mainly on fish and crustaceans; the young on plankton (Ref. 3688).  Gonochorists (Ref. 4781).

species.name: Davao pughead pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Planktonic fish taken within upper 200 m over depths of 610 to 7,120 m, whereas metamorphosed demersal examples are from coral habitats in 1.8 to 8 m. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Apparently associates with live corals, including Galaxea fascicularis (Ref 90102).

species.name: David’s Angel Shark
species.description: Currently known from depths between 100-151m (Ref. 110242).

species.name: Dawkinsia assimilis
species.description: Occurs in a variety of habitats such slow-flowing areas close to the banks with muddy substrate, clear-water, rock substrate areas and relatively fast-flowing waters (Ref. 55036).

species.name: Dawkinsia chalakkudiensis
species.description: Inhabits upper reaches of rivers with overgrowing plants (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Dawkinsia exclamatio
species.description: Occurs in clear-water, rock and pebble substrate areas (Ref. 55036).  Inhabits both slow-flowing pools and relatively fast-flowing areas (Ref. 55036).

species.name: Dawn tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dawn threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sand and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9785).

species.name: Dawn’s shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is currently known only from the type locality, where the habitat consists of a gently sloping bottom with clean white sand and was well-removed (more than 100 m) from reef habitat, in an area exposed to periodic strong currents. An estimated 20 individuals were observed in an area approximately 30 sq.m and were seen mainly in pairs, occasionally solitary, although invariably associated with an unidentified snapping shrimp of the genus Alpheus that share the burrows (a symbiotic relationship found in all Vanderhorstia species (Ref. 123061).

species.name: Day's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in turbid rivers with densely vegetated margins.  Feeds mainly on aquatic insect larvae.

species.name: Day's glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwaters and estuarine lakes (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Day's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in burrows on mud or silty sand bottoms.

species.name: Day's mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, tanks, rivers, canals and beels.  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).  Caught with other fishes from fishing operations.

species.name: Day's pellona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and perhaps, like P. ditchela, entering estuaries.

species.name: Day's round herring
species.description: Found in rivers, estuaries (Ref. 188) and coastal waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Day's sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Day's thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably a schooling and found inshore.  More data needed.

species.name: Day-night pygmy goby
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Most specimens  of this 'twilight zone' species are reported from the 70 m depth range (though
have been collected as shallow as 45-55 m in the Lembeh Strait).  The species do not appear to school or aggregate as with many congeners, but rather are found individually in small caves and crevices, frequently quite deep into the interstices of the reef and only visible using a strong underwater flashlight.  Specimens collected were found exclusively on deep reefs sheltered from wave exposure but nonetheless exposed to currents, and although there was frequently significant silt build-up present in the caves in which they sheltered, water visibility was always good because of the significant water flow over the reefs (Ref. 96671).

species.name: De Buen's coris
species.description: Occurs in areas of mixed sand and rocky substratum; juveniles found in tide pools, but may occur in deeper waters. Stomach and gut contents have gastropods (mainly Strombus maculatus), pelecypods (with mytilid and Lima), ophiuroids (Ophiocoma), hermit crabs (Pagurus pascuensis), crabs (with Trapezia), and echinoids; with mollusks as the major prey items (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Deacon rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Decapterus akaadsi
species.description: Adults are found along shelf edge (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Deccan barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Deccan mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is mesopelagic, potadromous. Inhabits cool, fast flowing, rocky streams and rivers.  Occurs in mountain lakes (Ref. 41236).  Moves to upper reaches of small streams to spawn (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on plants, insects, shrimps and mollusks.  Can be cultured in ponds and lakes.  Regarded to be of medicinal value.  Known to grow over a meter and 45 kg in weight but have not been recorded in recent times (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Deccan white carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and tanks (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Deceitful velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, in soft bottom.

species.name: Deceiver fangbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimics the species Meiacanthus lineatus.

species.name: Decorated dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoons and bays to well offshore, usually on fine sand substrata not ordinarily disturbed by surge (Ref.  33412).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Decorated glidergoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas.

species.name: Decorated goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species that inhabits areas of coralline sand of clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Found singly.  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Decorated ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Diet depend on size; small fish (<6.9 cm) eat small crustaceans including copepods, whereas larger fish (>7.0 cm) have a generalized diet of amphipods, polychaetes and detritus (Ref. 31455).

species.name: Decorated splitfin goby
species.description: Known from deep reefs. Collected from sandy habitats with scattered rocks and calcareous rubble. This species perch on open sand and retreat into crevices when disturbed (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Decorated warbonnet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually among seaweed on rocky bottoms (Ref. 2850); in reef crevices, usually among algae (Ref. 51666).  Occurs in subtidal areas to 91 m depth (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Decorus decorus
species.description: Adults inhabit gravel bottom in mountain streams (Ref. 80318). Utilized for food (Ref. 80318).

species.name: Deep blue Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults appear to prefer depths more that 115 m, staying close to the substratum, sand and rubble slope with boulders and rock outcroppings. They take refuge in small caves and holes. Juveniles and some subadults were observed around limestone talus. Adults were usually solitary or in pairs, while subadults and juveniles were seen in small groups. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Other Chromis associated with this species include C. brevirostris, C. degruyi and C. earina (Ref. 59379).

species.name: Deep bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer reef drop-offs in caves at moderate depths to about 40 m (Ref. 48636).  Occurs in groups under ledges in caves.

species.name: Deep hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing streams or still, isolated pools in either clear or turbid conditions.  Can tolerate marine conditions and temperatures well above 30° C.  Can live in water where salinity levels twice that of sea water.  An extremely hardy species capable of surviving hypersaline conditions and a wide temperature range.  Its tolerance to salinity is much higher than that of most other fishes.  The omnivorous diet includes small invertebrates and plant material (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Deep reef whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is seldom collected and occurs relatively deep (below 60 m) outer reef habitat. It was invariably observed at the base of 60-70 m reef drop-offs, swimming in small schools of 2-10 individuals and 1-2 m above the steeply-sloping sand, rubble and sea-fan substrate (Ref. 123129)

species.name: Deep velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottomed inshore areas.

species.name: Deep water ateleopid fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth range from Ref. 122680.

species.name: Deep water pike smelt
species.description: Meso- or perhaps benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Deep-blackfin butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Areas of collection vary from sheltered rocky outcroppings which are heavily covered by fine sediment to areas exposed to strong currents. Ambient seawater temperature varied between 19 and 21°C during dives conducted in April-May over several years. Azooxanthellate gorgonians, black corals, and solitary stony corals were the most abundant benthic invertebrates in this area (Ref. 116443).

species.name: Deep-bodied mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Marine species that enters estuaries and coastal lagoons in Madagascar (Ref. 4323).  Forms schools on sandy bottoms (Ref. 12915, 48635).  Small juveniles feed on zooplankton, larger fish feed on small polychaetes, bivalves, crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 3409).  In Palau, spawners migrate from mangroves and sand flats to the outer reef edge around the full moon (Ref. 1602).  Marketed fresh or made into fishballs (Ref. 12915).

species.name: Deep-bodied pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in algal beds in coastal or estuarine areas.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Deep-body righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Deep-dwelling moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 250 m (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Deep-reef klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over gravel (Ref. 28111).

species.name: Deep-reef pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Deep-sea lizardfish
