species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a typical blackwater habitat with clear, acidic and very soft tea-colored water, with total and temporary hardness <1°  dH (Ref. 76847).  Encountered along the bank of small rivulet in zones of extremely shallow water, approximately between 10 and 50 cm depth, where this species occurs either in a layer of dead leaves covering the bottom of the bank side or among the submerged terrestrial vegetation (Ref. 76847).

species.name: Dicrossus maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Rare in the aquarium trade (Ref. 122510.

species.name: Dicrossus warzeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exclusively clear-water rivers.  Juveniles measuring about 2.0 cm SL occur in small brooks with sandy bottoms and patches of leaf litter.  Observed searching the bottom substrate for small invertebrates and detritus by picking up and turning the leaves.  Collected only in very soft water (no detectable hardness) with high acidity, pH value mostly less than 4 (Ref. 85095).

species.name: Dictyosoma burgeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal to subtidal rocky bottoms (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Dictyosoma rubrimaculatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal zones of rocky reefs (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Didogobius lanceolatus
species.description: Like other members of the subfamily Gobiinae, this species has a cryptobenthic lifestyle, living at least temporarily sheltered in soft sediment burrows. Its discovery was accidental after being collected with (silty) mud The sediment sample contained agglutinated worm tubes and shells of Atrina chautardi. Live associated fauna comprised a second unidentified fish species and beyond abundant polychaetes, gastropods, bivalves, amphipods and shrimps. A potential burrow-dwelling lifestyle might provide shelter against predators on this relatively flat seafloor lacking any hard substrates (Ref. 130223).

species.name: Didymothallus criniceps
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Some of the female specimens were observed to have 9-18 eggs in the body cavity, 2 females (of 44 mm SL) were opened and found to contain orange-coloured eggs, 1.4-1.7
mm in diameter; no reported specimens have embryos inside.  This observation apparently indicate that this species is oviparous rather than viviparous, which is an assumed diagnostic character for all Bythitoidei. However, this first indication will need to be confirmed by in-life observation (Ref. 76869).

species.name: Didymothallus nudigena
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Didymothallus pruvosti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is associated with crevices of silty coralline rock and the presence of live corals is not essential (Ref. 76869).

species.name: Dieidolycus adocetus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dieidolycus gosztonyii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Dieidolycus leptodermatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dienbienia namnuaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dikume
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Mainly feeds on mosquito larvae; possesses elevated levels of hemoglobin in its blood as an adaptation to reduced oxygen levels at great water depth; possibly an ovophilic
mouth brooder that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Dillie grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer to inhabit fast flowing portions of creeks and rivers, although often found in deep, slow flowing pools.  Juveniles stay mostly in riffle habitat.  Occurs in clear waters over rocky substrates, often where algae are in abundance.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae that are scraped off rocks with its specially modified teeth (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Dimidiochromis kiwinge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually encountered near rocks (Ref. 267, 55954), but also often forms schools offshore (Ref. 267). A common predator in surface water near the shore (Ref. 267). Feeds on small fishes; the small Utaka and lake sardine, Engraulicypris sardella, are among the favorite items (Ref. 5595). Hunts in pairs or in large groups (Ref. 3817).

species.name: Diminutive dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coral and rocky reefs at depths from 3-41 m; very abundant at Nuku Hiva, where nearly 250 individuals were captured in a single collection between 3-6 m depth (Ref. 94084).

species.name: Diminutive worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dinah's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble bottoms, taking refuge in dead shells, empty bottles and tunicates (Ref. 90102). Hovers a short distance above the substrate (Ref. 45340).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 45340).

species.name: Dinnawah snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill-streams, in deep run backwaters.  Mainly carnivorous.  Breeds in the upper reaches of river and travels down after breeding.  Known as a delicious table fish in Nepal (Ref. 40948).

species.name: Dinotopterus cunningtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More common in rocky areas; wide depth range from about 10 m to at least 130 m (Ref. 4967). Found in the littoral zone at an average depth of 10 m, above all over rocky substrates (Ref. 36901). Larger specimens feed exclusively on fishes; exhibits cuckoo behaviour (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Diodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found in reefs and over soft  bottoms to depths of 100 m, but may occur deeper in the tropics (Ref. 30573).  Often found washed up on beaches.  Known to brace themselves against the substrate to sleep at night (Ref. 4930).  Appear to be active during the day.  Juveniles often with floating weeds (Ref. 48637).  Solitary.  Juveniles pelagic in oceanic surface waters (Ref. 30573).  Feed on hard-shelled invertebrates.  Not usually marketed.

species.name: Diodon (Diodon liturosus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef edges and slopes (Ref. 6113, 48637).  Hides in caves and ledges during the day and forages at night (Ref. 9680).  Also found below plate-corals during the day and often deep, ranging to at least 40 meters depth.  Juveniles occur in lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 48637).   Solitary.  Feeds on crustaceans and mollusks.  Not usually marketed (Ref. 9680).

species.name: Diodon porc-épic
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 50 m.  Commonly seen in caves and holes in shallow reefs (Ref. 26938, 48637).  Juveniles to about 20 cm are pelagic.  Adults benthic (Ref. 30573).  Solitary and nocturnal that feed on hard shelled invertebrates like sea urchins, gastropods, and hermit crabs (Ref. 9680).  Generally common (Ref. 9710).  Not normally used as food (Ref. 3717).  Reached a life-span of 10 years and a length of 69 cm in the McGinty Aquarium (E. Dashiell, pers. comm 2004), suggesting a preliminary K=0.12.

species.name: Diogenes lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442) at 0-100 m at night, 600-650 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Diogenichthys panurgus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.

species.name: Diphasic goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits isolated patch reefs surrounded by white sand (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma alcockii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 900 m (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma brachysoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Locally abundant (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma brunneum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 685 m (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma japonicum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 559).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma jordani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024), known from only two specimens (Ref. 6610).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma raniceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplacanthopoma riversandersoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 1,640 m (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diplecogaster ctenocrypta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplecogaster euxinica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplecogaster pectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on hard bottom on the outer shelf; taken with the alga Hildenbrandtia (Ref. 4489).

species.name: Diplecogaster umutturali
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from three discrete localities along the Turkish Levant coast; Akıncı Burnu (Iskenderun Bay), Kaş and Fethiye Bay. The type locality (Akıncı Burnu) is a broad cove, a pebble beach of ca. 1000 m long. Smooth pebbles with various dimensions (1x1 cm to 15x10 cm) extend from the high water mark to one meter of depth, as a large band throughout the coast. The deeper parts of the shore (>1 m) with dense rocky substrates encircled by fine sand. Large rocks were covered with two dominant algae, Jania rubens and Cystoseira spp., together with chthamalid barnacles. The holotype was collected from under a greyish flattened stone at a depth of 0.3 m, salinity at 39.2 ppt, bottom water temperature 28.5°C and dissolved oxygen 4.75 mg/l while the paratypes were observed and collected on coarse shell grits around the Posidonia oceanica (Ref. 117931).

species.name: Diplocheilichthys jentinkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing waters (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Diplocheilichthys pleurotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplodus ascensionis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed among rocks, usually at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 86997).

species.name: Diplodus levantinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from shallow water to 50 m depth, usually on sand bottom near rocks; while juveniles are found above sandy substrate near rocks at depths of 0.2-2 m (Ref. 110175).

species.name: Diplodus striatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplomystes camposensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplomystes incognitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplomystes nahuelbutaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplophos australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplophos orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Diplophos pacificus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Diplotaxodon aeneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found near rocky reefs (Ref. 55949).

species.name: Diplotaxodon altus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in offshore, deep-water environments; found at depths between 40-70 m and, although rare, in trawls between 110-130 m (Ref. 127500).

species.name: Diplotaxodon apogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep-water species, usually found close to the bottom on shelf areas; zooplankton feeder (Ref. 55949).

species.name: Diplotaxodon argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in open water at mostly deep levels, where it can form enormous shoals (Ref. 5595). It is a piscivore that mainly feeds on lake sardine, Engraulicypris sardella (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Diplotaxodon dentatus
species.description: Based on the exposed teeth in the oral jaws and the unicuspid teeth of the pharyngeal jaws, it is suggested that Diplotaxodon dentatus is a piscivore (Ref. 123828).

species.name: Diplotaxodon ecclesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in open water at mostly deep levels but infrequently taken by trawl nets. Feeds mainly on the lake sardine, Engraulicypris sardella (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Diplotaxodon greenwoodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef and shelf zones; feeds on small cichlids (Ref. 55949)

species.name: Diplotaxodon limnothrissa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore and offshore, on reefs and over the shelf; abundant over the anoxic zone; female mouthbrooder (Ref. 55949).  Zooplanktivorous; probably the most abundant species in Lake Malawi (Ref. 94786).

species.name: Diplotaxodon longimaxilla
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found offshore; common in trawl nets from depths below 80 m near Domira Bay (Ref. 127500).

species.name: Diplotaxodon macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant near the bottom over shelf habitats (Ref. 55949).  Apparently a plankton feeder that preys on insect larvae, crustaceans, and diatoms (Ref. 30390).

species.name: Dipturus chinensis
species.description: Commonly found on inner continental shelf. Biology poorly known (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Dipturus flavirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Diptychus sewerzowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dipulus norfolkanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon secretive species found in shallow waters (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Diretmoides veriginae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dirette aile longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic.  Young near the surface while aged adults often descend below 1,000 m depth (Ref. 2683).  Largest adults may be benthopelagic (Ref. 9851).  Plankton-eaters like the other members of the family (Ref. 6744).  Breed all year round (Ref. 6744).  Minimum depth range taken from Ref. 27000.

species.name: Dirette argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found from near surface to about 250 m to more than 1,000 m (Ref. 6536).  Largest adults may be benthopelagic (Ref. 9851).  Adults are plankton-eaters like the other members of the family (Ref. 6744).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36622).

species.name: Dirette de Parin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles found near the surface; adults mesopelagic below 500 m (Ref. 27121).  May occur at depths greater than 2,000 m (Ref. 6536).  Feed on small crustaceans and planktonic organisms (Ref. 27121).  Breed all year round (Ref. 6744).  Minimum depth range taken from Ref. 27000.

species.name: Diri
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf over soft bottom (Ref. 7300); associated with coral
reefs or rocky bottoms and other inshore environments of tropical seas (Ref. 97263).  Nothing has been published on its biology.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Dirty bandit cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Disalvo's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the highest pools of the intertidal and some  in the splash zone above high tide, at pools no deeper than 10 cm (probably with extraordinary tolerance to extremes of temperature and salinity (Ref. 82648).

species.name: Discherodontus ashmeadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to be associated with streams and rivers with clear water, moderate to fast current and a gravel to stony bottom (Ref. 27732).  Found near the bottom in pools of small to medium-sized rivers.  Typically occurs near decaying plant debris where it feeds on insects and other invertebrates.  Possibly moves out into flooded forests during high-water periods.  Apparently found in localized populations and encountered sporadically (Ref. 12693).  Reported as a nocturnal species by villagers in Ban Pakphanang (Laos), where all specimens were obtained at night (Ref. 27732).  Rare in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Discherodontus halei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discherodontus parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discocheilus multilepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discocheilus wui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio antethoracalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit fast-flowing water of limpid streams with cobble substrate.  Reported by local people to feed mainly on algae and occasionally on aquatic plants and larvae of aquatic insects (Ref. 75176).

species.name: Discogobio bismargaritus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential waters of mountain areas, clinging to the substratum using its mouth sucking disc (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio brachyphysallidos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential waters of mountain areas, clinging to the substratum using its mouth sucking disc (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio caobangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio dienbieni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential waters of mountain areas, clinging to the substratum using its mouth sucking disc (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential waters of mountain areas, clinging to the substratum using its mouth sucking disc (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio longibarbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio macrophysallidos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits torrential water of mountain area, clinging to the substrata on bottom by its sucking disc of mouth (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio microstoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio multilineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio pacboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discogobio poneventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit fast-flowing water of limpid streams with cobble substrate.  Reported by local people to feed mainly on algae and occasionally on aquatic plants and larvae of aquatic insects (Ref. 75176).

species.name: Discogobio propeanalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit fast-flowing water of limpid streams with cobble substrate in the water body.  Reported by local people to feed mainly on algae and aquatic plants (Ref. 75176).

species.name: Discogobio tetrabarbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit torrential water of mountain area, clinging to the substrata on bottom by its sucking disc of mouth (Ref. 38450).

species.name: Discogobio yunnanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit torrential water of mountain area, clinging to the substrata on bottom by the sucking disc of mouth (Ref. 38450).  Local people claim that this fish feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 75176).

species.name: Discolabeo wuluoheensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Discordipinna filamentosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the deepwater trawling of up to 82 m.  Observed through scuba diving and current trawl specimen record, that the species seems to live in 30 to 82 m depth water with substratum of coral-reef hard debris (Ref. 90871).

species.name: Discotrema zonatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Single specimen collected from the base of a soft coral (Ref. 75094)

species.name: Discus commun
species.description: Poisson. In deep, rocky areas in crevices and among roots.  Normally in schools, but territorial during breeding season.  Feeds on insect larvae, insects, and planktonic invertebrates.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; keep pairs in small tanks for breeding;  minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Discus de Heckel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter.  Maximum length 20 cm TL  (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Discus ray
species.description: Common in shallow areas and near banks (Ref. 27749).  Reproductive biology in upper Orinoco basin provided by Lasso et al. (1997a), where females appear to bear only two young per gestation.  Larger individuals may attain 25 kg in weight.  Food includes insects, crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 36687).

species.name: Discus tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, insects, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Disk tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has powerful dentition that can cause serious bites.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Disque du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore areas with sandy bottoms or coral reefs, forming small schools (Ref. 9299).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 37955).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 2850.

species.name: Disque panaméen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal over coral reefs and rocky bottoms of shallow waters (Ref. 9299).  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 9299).  Maximum TL of at least 30 cm (Ref. 9299).

species.name: Disque portugais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in shallow coastal waters, from mangroves and sandy beaches to wrecks and harbors.  Juveniles (black phase) are common in estuaries and often found in very shallow water swimming at an angle resembling dead leaves or as infertile red mangrove pods and other debris.  Adults often occur in very large schools of up to 500 individuals (Ref. 9710).  Feed on benthic invertebrates like crustaceans, mollusks, annelids, cnidarians as well as on plankton (Ref. 35237).  Good food fish (Ref. 5521); marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).  Often circles divers (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth from Ref. 9710.  In southeastern Brazil found between 23 and 45 m (Ref. 47377).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35425).

species.name: Distant clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distant goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs.

species.name: Distichodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus altus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus antonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The fry and juveniles of Distichodus antonii live in aquatic prairies and in plant fringes; adults feed in Echinochloa patches and live at the edge of streams along islands and even on the bottom in the middle of the stream (Ref. 96324). The species is a phytophagous species; stomachs almost always contain plant fragments, with easily recognizable twigs and leaves of Echinochloa, which comprises the largest part of their diet (Ref. 96324). It has two annual periods of reproduction and spawning and egg deposition have to take place at the border of the stream, just before the flood. Maximum reported total length is 550 mm (Ref. 1878), although it is stated it can reach a size of more than 800 mm (Ref. 7094, 96324). Maximum weight was recorded at nearly 10 kg (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Distichodus atroventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus brevipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 70 cm (Ref. 7094).  Prefers flowing water.  Feeds on vegetation and periphyton (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Distichodus decemmaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus hypostomatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus ingae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus kasaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus kolleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 21.5 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Distichodus langi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus nefasch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Albert found in the shallow inshore waters, especially in the region of deltas; also in rivers (Ref. 4903). Macro-herbivore, feeds on submerged water plants (Ref. 4903, 28714), Eichornia roots and periphyton (Ref. 28714), but also molluscs and small Crustacea (Ref. 4903). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Distichodus noboli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distichodus petersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 44.5 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Distichodus polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. There seems to be a preference by small specimens of Distichodus polli for stretches with a swift current (Ref. 122090).

species.name: Distichodus rufigiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Distichodus teugelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riparian or flooded forest; in shallow as well as deep areas; in acidic waters due to humic acids (Ref. 78699).

species.name: Distocyclus conirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs in floodplain and main river channels at depths of 3.8-28.3 m (Ref. 96854).

species.name: Distocyclus guchereauae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Distoechodon tumirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Ditrema jordani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky shores among Sargassum (Ref. 76763). Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ditrema temminckii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in sandy bottoms and rocky areas (Ref. 76763); also in areas with Sargassum (Ref. 559). Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ditrema viride
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow Zostera marina beds (Ref. 559, 43239). Viviparous, number of embryos about 30. Young born from April through July (Ref. 43239). Female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ditropichthys storeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles (less than 3.5 cm) were captured in shallower depth range (650-877 m).  Larger specimens appear to dwell deeper (Ref. 9791).

species.name: Divandu albimarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the middle and lower parts of the river basins; collection sites are in regions with primary or secondary forests. The water is clear with transparency of more than 100 cm, acidity approximately neutral (pH 7-7.5) with low conductivity (50 µS) and temperatures 21-22°C. The species lives syntopically with Chromidotilapia mamonekenei, which is more abundant than D. albimarginatus (Ref. 45129). Feeds on small particles (both animal- and plantbased), detritus and aufwuchs (Ref. 52307). Polygamous, ovophilic, female mouthbrooder (Ref. 81260). Possibly larvophilic (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Dividedspot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Divine dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coral, crevices and under ledges (Ref. 58302).  In the spur-and-groove habitat in Kaneohe Bay, Oʻahu, Hawai‘i, it feeds mainly on harpacticoid copepods, tanaids, and amphipods, as well as a large variety of other small invertebrates (Ref. 107299).

species.name: Dixie chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand- and gravel-bottomed pools of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Dnieper chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lowland rivers, lower reaches of montane rivers, limans, lakes, deltas, backwaters with moderate to no current.  They prefer to stay in warm water with temperatures up to 30-32° C, on sand, sand-mud or mud bottom, and in shallow places with slow current along banks, in backwaters, in small lakes and similar calm-water sites. Can tolerate slightly brackish water and low oxygen concentrations.  Feed predominantly on insects and their larvae, but also takes plankton, benthic invertebrates and algae.  Form spawning groups of up to 150 individuals.  They do not undertake migration but move to deeper places in winter.  Sharp decline of some populations is due to drainage of flood-plains and channelization of river beds (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Docimodus evelynae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in rocky areas but also lives in intermediate zone (Ref. 5595).  Juveniles feed mainly on aufwuchs and plankton, but specimens up to 5 cm SL clean, scrape fungi from other species (Ref. 267), while adults feed on skin of catfish (Bagrus meridionalis) and scales of larger fishes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Docimodus johnstoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits over sandy and muddy bottoms and feeds on fins of clariid catfishes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Docked snailfish
species.description: Benthic species of cool northern seas, living on mud, gravelly or rocky bottoms. Minimum depth reported at 58 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Dodekablennos fraseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools (Ref. 33390).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Doederlein's cardinalfish
species.description: Commonly occurs in rocky areas near shore and abundant on ledges.  Solitary but pair off during breeding.  Mouth brooding is done by the male.  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Dog-toothed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon reefs to depths of at least 12 m. Usually in small groups among staghorn corals (Ref. 48635). Often collected with C. quinquelineatus, but tends to prefer deeper areas (Ref. 37816). Feeds on small fishes. Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Dogface witch eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small deep-sea crustaceans (Ref. 28023).  Caught well offshore in pelagic waters to depths of several hundred meters (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Dogface witch-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit scattering layers to depths of several thousand feet.  Known to eat small, deep-sea crustaceans.  Also captured mostly in bottom trawls (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous (Ref. 35597).  Planktonic leptocephali (Ref. 35597).

species.name: Dogtooth lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic at 0-200 m at night, 425-1500 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Depth range is between 300 to 600m during the day, and from 25 to 300 at night (Ref. 54154).   Reported to feed on crustaceans (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Dogtooth pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 75154) and rare species (Ref. 34024).  Probably a free-living species of the outer shelf and upper continental slope.

species.name: Dogtooth rivulus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Easy to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Dolichallabes microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly nocturnal. Conceal themselves by day among rocks of the shore zone or roots and branches of trees at the edges of lakes and rivers. Omnivores feeding primarily on small aquatic organisms and their larvae (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Dolichamphilius brieni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichamphilius longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus atratoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus carnegiei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus cobrensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus fuesslii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus pediculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichancistrus setosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx anascopa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx binocularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx minuscula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx pseudolongipes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx rostrata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx trunovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichopteryx vityazi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolichosudis fuliginosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from below 600 m.  All species of this family are supposed to be hermaphrodites.

species.name: Dollar sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and mud-bottomed, usually brushy, pools of creeks and small to medium rivers; and also swamps (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae and microcrustaceans (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Dollfus' stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dollfus' stargrazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolloidraco longedorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sublittoral and continental shelf.  Adults feed mainly on errant polychaetes; also in the gut content were gammarid amphipods, isopods, sedentary polychaetes and unidentified polychaetes (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Dolly varden
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep runs and pools of creeks and small to large rivers; also in lakes and the sea (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Lives in very clean mountain streams (Ref. 12218).  Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Typically anadromous, but many populations are landlocked.  Anadromous fish may spend 2-3 years at sea, evidently near shore, migrate upstream usually in fall, and spawn during spring (Ref. 86798).  Young remain in streams for 3-4 years and feed on insects, leeches, snails, and salmon eggs (Ref. 1998) before entering brackish and salt water to feed on insects, fishes, and other invertebrates.  Utilized fresh and eaten fried, broiled, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Dolopichthys allector
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolopichthys danae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Dolopichthys dinema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic.

species.name: Dolopichthys jubatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Dolopichthys karsteni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dolopichthys longicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 10524) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Dolphin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Domingue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit exposed seaward reefs with sand patches (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dominican gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 205). Introduced to billabongs and streams in the vicinity of Alice Springs during the 1940s and 1950s for the purpose of mosquito control. Some researchers place it in the genus Limia (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Domino skate
species.description: Probably a benthic species, found more widespread on deep insular slopes of Coral Sea (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Don gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide variety of habitats in rivers and streams.  Size reaches up to about 10 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Don tadpole-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers fresh and brackish waters, mostly on river mouths (abundant), lower reaches of rivers and reservoirs and does not enter the sea (Ref. 58669, 59043).  Lives on silty sand with mollusc shells; feeding mostly on molluscs and crustaceans.  Life span about a year; spawns in May to August; females probably lay eggs in 2-3 portions inside or under a mollusc shell; and adults die soon after spawning (Ref. 59043). Invasive in the large tributaries of the Caspian and Black Sea (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Don whitefin gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottom of moderately flowing lowland rivers, preferring sand bottom.  Nocturnal. Feeds on insect larvae and other large benthic invertebrates.  Locally threatened due to pollution and river engineering.  Populations most likely decline due to construction of large reservoirs in Don in 20th century (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Doncelle striée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow waters, especially where brown algae exists (Ref. 9311).  Diet consists of crustaceans, sea urchins, mollusks, and brittle stars.  It loses its blue-green coloration, turns dull brown in captivity.

species.name: Donets ruffe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flowing waters and lakes with clear water.  Also inhabits rapids during summer.  Occurs over sand and gravel bottom but prefers hard compact sand.  Usually crepuscular but feeds also during daytime. Preys predominantly on benthic invertebrates (crustaceans, insect larvae, molluscs), rarely on fish.  Forms small schools. In September, starts forming large schools and moves to deeper places and remains inactive until ice melts.  Does not undertake long distance migrations.  Spawns in small schools river stretches with heavy current and sand or gravel bottom (Ref.59043).

species.name: Dongnai mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dongu snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mountain rivers, streams and lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Donzelle arc en ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found on shallow patch or seaward reefs down to 55 m (Ref. 9710); juveniles and subadults in shallower (1 to 5 m) coral reefs (Ref. 3726).  Feeds on mollusks, sea urchins, crustaceans, and brittle stars (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3726).

species.name: Donzelle arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow lagoons or bays; usually over sand, rubble, or seagrass bottom (Ref. 41878), rather than on coral reefs.  May be found in groups (Ref. 90102).  Usually solitary and aggressive towards members of its own species.  Feeds on small crustaceans by picking them off the sandy bottom (Ref. 5503).

species.name: Donzelle arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Donzelle blissée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly encountered in rocky reefs and sandy areas adjacent  to reefs.  Feeds on mollusks, crabs, brittle stars and sea urchins.  Not utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Donzelle caméléon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 5227).Inhabits shallow waters, over rocky or coral reefs separated by sandy areas (Ref. 9311).  Feeds on small invertebrates found in the sand (Ref. 9311).  Large specimens in the Gulf of California are known to feed on small blennioid fishes (Ref. 28023).  Buries itself in the sand when disturbed and at night to sleep (Ref. 9311).  Marketed fresh in local markets (Ref. 9311).

species.name: Donzelle créole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reef slopes; occasionally on shallow patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found in large midwater aggregations feeding on plankton (Ref. 9710), small jellyfishes, pteropods, pelagic tunicates and various invertebrate larvae (Ref. 13442).  Form leks during breeding (Ref. 55367).  Also caught with beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Donzelle de Malpelo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over coarse sand and gravel bottoms.  Does not form schools (Ref. 9311).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Donzelle de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found close to rocks near patches of sand and in tide pools.  Dart into sand when disturbed and sleep at night buried in sand with head protruding.  Feed on gastropods, small crustaceans and has been observed to pick ectoparasites from other fishes (Ref. 9311).  Each individual functions first as female but changes to a male at length of about 30 cm.  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Donzelle de Socorro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fairly abundant over rock and coarse sand substrates.  Forms schools of various sizes that move approximately 1 m above the bottom.  Too small to be marketed commercially.

species.name: Donzelle des mangroves
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently found over sand and mud bottoms of  mangroves and estuaries but occasionally found over rocky bottoms of the marine coast.  Not utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Donzelle dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reefs (Ref. 9311).

species.name: Donzelle jaune et blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the reef edge, in sand and rubble areas (Ref. 9710, 48636) usually in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Donzelle lame
species.description: Inhabits clear shallow areas with sandy bottoms, usually in the vicinity of seagrass beds and corals (Ref. 2683).  Feeds mainly on mollusks; also crabs and shrimps (Ref. 3726).  A protogynous hermaphrodite; sexual dimorphism apparent in head shape and length of pelvic fin (Ref. 5292).  Builds nests with coral debris.  Dives head first into the sand when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3726).

species.name: Donzelle mannequin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on shallow coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found solitary or in small loose groups in mixed coral and rubble areas of lagoons and outer slopes 2-30 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Donzelle noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally encountered around islands, over rocky bottoms (Ref. 9311).

species.name: Donzelle rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Found on the deeper parts of the continental shelf (Ref. 6555).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Donzelle tamarin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow weedy areas of rocky shorelines, not where there is rich coral growth (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Donzelle vierge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and gravel bottoms near coral reefs.  Adults are solitary but juveniles form aggregations, sometimes with other species of wrasses.  Feeds on mollusks, brittle stars, sea urchins and crabs.  Hides under the sand to sleep and to seek shelter, in cases of danger.

species.name: Donzelle à nageoires jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found in the shallows and to 150 m depth (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Donzelle à nageoires noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref.  122785.

species.name: Donzelle à tache noire
species.description: Lives over sandy bottoms with gravel and isolated reefs.  Often caught in the open sea as a by-catch of trawlers fishing for prawns and shrimps.  Each individual functions first as a female but  later changes to a male (Ref. 47122).

species.name: Dorada
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used to be cultured commercially in Peru (Ref. 7306).

species.name: Dorade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 9702). Also occur in estuaries (Ref. 9563). Juveniles mainly inhabit inlets, bays and other shallow, sheltered marine waters, often over mud and seagrass (Ref. 6390). Small fish measuring less than 30 cm TL are common inshore around reef areas often in groups of around 30 individuals. Larger fish are shy and are less frequently seen (Ref. 26966). Adults often live near reefs, but are also found over mud and sand substrates (Ref. 6390). They are relatively sedentary. However, tagging studies have shown them capable of substantial migrations (Ref. 28591). Crustaceans (crabs, shrimps, etc) form the basis of the diet, but marine worms, starfish, sea urchins, shellfish and fish are also important (Ref. 28591). Not commercially cultured at present but considered as a prime aquaculture candidate (Ref. 28590). Maximum estimated age for SW Pacific is 54 years with validated longevity on the order of 40 years based on minimum age from bomb radiocarbon dating (Ref. 92924; Allen Andrews, pers.comm. 01/13). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus cirrusspiralis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Dorade australe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky substrates of oceanic waters.  Enters estuaries where it lives among the weeds.  Feeds on algae and small crustaceans (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Dorade de palétuvier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and semi-protected seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  They prefer sheltered areas with deep holes or  large boulders (Ref. 37816).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Solitary or in loose aggregations (Ref. 90102).  Juveniles sometimes found in shallow mangrove swamps and the lower parts of freshwater streams.  Adults feed at night on fishes, shrimps, crabs, holothurians and cephalopods (Ref. 30573). Commonly seen in markets, usually fresh. Caught with handlines, traps, and gill nets. This fish sometimes causes ciguatera poisoning, particularly in the Pacific portion of its range (Ref. 9821).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Dorade grise
species.description: Found in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 2263).  Feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling invertebrates.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 171), smoked and dried salted (Ref. 2295).  Abundant during the winter months (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Dorade japonaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from 10 to 50 m depths, often on rough grounds, but also on softer bottoms.  Also inhabits reefs (Ref. 9988).  Adults migrate into shallower parts of their depth range to spawn in late spring and summer; juveniles occur mainly in the shallower areas.  It is a popular food fish throughout its range.  It is high-priced in Japan and used in various occasions such as wedding and festival.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, including echinoderms, worms, mollusks and crustaceans; also on fishes.  Marketed live, fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, pan-fried, broiled, boiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Cultivated in cages (Ref. 9988).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Dorade marbré
species.description: Found on the shelf, over sandy and muddy bottoms as well as seagrass-beds and estuaries.  Gregarious, sometimes forming sizeable schools.  Feeds on worms, mollusks and small crustaceans.  Protandric hermaphrodite (Ref. 3688).  Flesh excellent (Ref. 3198); sold fresh and dried.

species.name: Dorado
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Carnivorous (Ref. 79585).  Feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 13614).

species.name: Doraops zuloagai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, preferring muddy bottom of  backwaters (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on insects, worms, small crabs and snails (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Doras carinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Can emit sounds by moving its pectoral spines.  Every basic unit of sound emitted lasts for 60-70 millisecond, with a frequency of 60-90 Hertz corresponding to the reply frequency of the muscles utilized (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Doras higuchii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doras micropoeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doras phlyzakion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doras zuanoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doras à écusson dorsaux
species.description: Feeds on fruits when the forests are flooded and on the blades of macrophytes.  Acts as seed dispersal agent (Ref. 6868).  Reproduction occurs once a year and juveniles are often seen in large numbers in the estuary of the Amazon, in the region of Mario (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Dormeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit marshes, muddy ponds and channels with a salinity range of 0 to 21 ppt (Ref. 7251), up to 38.4 ppt in some cases (Ref. 97140).  Mostly found in fresh water but also in brackish mangrove areas. They ascend upstream but remain in the lower reaches.  Sexually mature after one year.  Gonads develop during the dry season.  Average size at maturity is 5.1 cm for males, 4.5 cm for females.  Omnivorous, adults feed mainly on plants, sediments and invertebrates.  They undergo coloration change during reproduction, carrying out a complex nuptial parade.  Adults guard the nest.  Egg is 0.3 mm, incubation time is 11 to 16 hours at 27°C (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Dormeur (Gobiomorus dormitor)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in fresh water, often well inland.  Found over sand streams, usually in current near cover (Ref. 86798). Inhabits larger free flowing clear water streams (Ref. 11225).  They lie mostly on the bottom in slower moving part of streams, sometimes on logs or large stones and on leaf debris or gravel (Ref. 11225).  A carnivorous and benthic fish that relies on its sluggish behavior and cryptic coloration (Ref. 36880). Feeds on all greater invertebrates and regularly also fish (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Dormeur (Guavina guavina)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy bottoms, generally in brackish waters of estuaries but also occurs in fresh water and hyper-saline environments.

species.name: Dormitator cubanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dormitator lebretonis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish water estuaries, creeks, lagoons and mangrove areas; occasionally enters freshwater (Ref. 7391, 57413, 81660).  Known to be tolerant of wide range of salinity.  Used as bio-control agents, e.g., use in control of mosquito larva (Ref. 42628). Endemic to West African coastline from Senegal to the Cunene River in Namibia (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Dormitator lophocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dorothea's wriggler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from two specimens taken from Bikini and the Great Barrier Reef (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Dorothy's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were trawled off bottoms of mud, fine sand, rock, and clay (Ref. 57076).

species.name: Dorsal-spot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from rocky reefs (Ref. 9484).

species.name: Dorsalspot shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The alpheid Alpheus cf rapacida is the symbiotic snapping shrimp that shares the burrows with this species in both Papua New Guinea and Majuro (Ref. 78591). Found in estuaries, lagoons and sheltered reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Doryichthys boaja
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Largest freshwater pipefish.  Found in rivers and streams (Ref. 5316).  Feeds on small crustaceans, worms and insects.  Of little food value.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryichthys contiguus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in river stretches with slow current, among grasses, roots or shore vegetation (Ref. 43281).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryichthys deokhatoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually associated with river stretches with slow current, among grasses, roots or shore vegetation (Ref. 27732).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 13.6 cm SL.

species.name: Doryichthys heterosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May attain longer than maximum length.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryichthys martensii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to feed on mosquito larvae.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). May brood at 10.4 SL.

species.name: Doryrhamphus abbreviatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in reefs and tide pools at depths of about 9 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryrhamphus aurolineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in caves, on rocky substrate.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryrhamphus malus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to depths of ca. 6 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doryrhamphus melanopleura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doryrhamphus paulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 2.4 cm SL.

species.name: Doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, pools, backwaters, and runs of medium to large rivers.  Frequently found in clear water, usually near brush (Ref. 86798). Prefers large, shallow lakes with high turbidity (Ref. 9988, 10294).  Rarely found in brackish waters (Ref. 1998).  Feeds at night, mainly on insects and fishes (prefers yellow perch and freshwater drum but will take any fish available) but feeds on crayfish, snails, frogs, mudpuppies, and small mammals when fish and insects are scarce (Ref. 1998).  Although not widely farmed commercially for consumption, large numbers are hatched and raised for stocking lakes for game fishing (Ref. 9988).  Utilized fresh or frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Doré (Zeus faber)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas close to the sea bed (Ref. 6390).  Generally solitary.  Feeds mainly on schooling bony fishes, occasionally on cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 27121).   Reproduction takes place at the end of winter and at the start of spring in the northeastern Atlantic, earlier in the Mediterranean.  Eggs are pelagic, maturity reached at 4 years (Ref. 36731).  Sold fresh (Ref. 9563) and frozen (Ref. 9988).  Can be steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  The flesh is excellent but is utilized little in West Africa (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Doré noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs, sandy and muddy pools and backwaters of small to large rivers (Ref. 86798). Less frequent in lake and impoundments (Ref. 86798).  Larvae feed on cladocerans, copepods, and midge larvae, while juveniles consume fishes (Ref. 10294).  Spawn between March and June (Ref. 10999) in pairs or small aggregations (Ref. 11003).

species.name: Dotted butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 9710) found in coral rich areas of clear water lagoon and semi-protected seaward reefs.  Usually in pairs or small groups, more wary than most species.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Dotted cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 637) and near rocky areas (Ref. 559).

species.name: Dotted catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal and crepuscular; preys on insect larvae, crustaceans, and small fishes (Ref. 6868). Maximum reported total length 24.5cm (Ref. 3236).

species.name: Dotted coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are closely related to Ecsenius yaeyamaensis and look most similar to E. stictus from the Great Barrier Reef (Ref. 48636). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Minimum depth of 5 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Dotted dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered reefs in 1-20 m (Ref 90102). Occupies a limited range of substrates: dead reef, dead reef with silty sand, silt, and also fine sand (Ref. 116739).

species.name: Dotted flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dotted sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stomach contents include a half-digested polychaete about 45 mm by 5 mm, along with copepods, crustacean larvae, and small fishes (Ref. 107896).

species.name: Dotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over coral or rubble of shallow protected reefs, occasionally in exposed areas (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Dottedline snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dotterel filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The drop-off at the type locality starts at 8 m, the substratum leading to this consists of coral rubble, a typical habitat for species of Cirrhilabrus . Apparently, the two small angelfishes sought by the collectors at this area are Centropyge bicolor and Paracentropyge multifaciata (Ref. 82647). Also found in crevices and overhangs on steep outer reef slopes (Ref 90102).

species.name: Dottybelly dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Water temperatures of two photograph sites were 18°C and 21°C , suggesting that this species is tolerant of relatively low temperatures (Ref. 118103).

species.name: Double whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on clear coastal reef slopes (Ref. 48635).  A solitary species (Ref. 9710) but may be found also in groups (Ref. 90102).  Excellent eye-sight (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans, ophiuroids and sipunculid worms.

species.name: Double-fin cheek-hook goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy-mud or silt bottoms with dead-coral rubble at depths of 15-35 m (Ref. 84001).

species.name: Double-spot tonguesole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Double-striped dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rich coral reefs (Ref. 8631) and coastal reef slopes (Ref. 37816). Also found in crevices and caves on steep slopes (Ref 90102). A possible mimic of Pholidichthys leucotaenia (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Doubleband stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds.

species.name: Doublebar cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doublebar chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer reef slopes and deep lagoons (Ref. 9710).  They form small to moderate aggregations on reef crests with moderate currents (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doublebar goby
species.description: Found on protected reefs or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Doubleheader
species.description: Inhabits shallow rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710); in shallow waters, generally in less than 20 m; usually in small groups with a large male dominating; with the young being collected in tide pools (Ref. 33411).  Feeds mainly on gastropods and pelecypods; also on crabs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Doubleline clingfish
species.description: Lives on the crinoidsLamprometra klunzingeri and Capillaster multiradiata and feeds on the pinnulae of its hosts (Ref. 33548). Often swims about openly when feeding or simply moving about where there are a lot of crinoids (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Doublesash butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found among weeds in estuaries (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Doublespot acara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from lotic black to clear water:  in Rio Uatumá, this species was collected from marginal pools in rapids after the Balbina dam was closed and the river level dropped  considerably below normal low water Ievel; Río Preto da Eva site was a relatively slow flowing small forest stream, while the Igarape Tarumázinho site was a swift flowing forest stream.  Although collections indicate swamps and lakes, this species has been collected mostly in running water.  Reported food items of specimens from Río Negro were chiefly fish and detritus (Ref. 86501).  Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).  Maximum  length 20.0 cm TL (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Doublespot grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on open sand or muddy bottoms with small reef or debris outcrops (Ref. 48636).  Mainly known from trawls in depths over 35 m (Ref. 48636).  Found near reefs in open mud bottoms at depths of 20-50 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Doublespot perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs in lagoons and exposed areas (Ref. 8944).  Deep-dwelling fishes.  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 37816). Solitary in crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Doublestripe goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat sand bottoms.

species.name: Doublethread grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured together with the commercial red shrimp (Pleoticus robustus).

species.name: Doubletooth soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered coastal and offshore reefs, usually in turbid areas of bays and lagoons, in 3-40 m (Ref 90102). A nocturnal fish hiding in caves or beneath ledges by day, feeding on plankton such as crab larvae at night.  Found in loose aggregations in caves, sometimes with other soldierfish (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Doublewhip threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or mud bottoms.

species.name: Doule à queue rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doule à queue rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily a freshwater species; extent of penetration into brackish and marine environments uncertain (Ref. 41640).  Has been found in moderately deep (1.5-3 m), rocky, unshaded, flowing water areas of mid-hill rivers (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Doumea angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumea chappuisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumea gracila
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumea reidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality of Doumea reidi is a cool, briskly flowing, upland stream less than 4 m wide and less than 1.5 m maximum depth; substratum was reported to consist of large, granitic boulders interspersed among deposits of coarse sand, mud, and leaf litter (Ref. 85844).

species.name: Doumea sanaga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumea skeltoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumea stilicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in a 'blackwater' rainforest system with low pH waters, its mean pH 6.2 (Ref. 85844).

species.name: Doumea thysi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Doumé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dourmillouse
species.description: Espèce de raies. Found on soft bottoms, usually inshore but occasionally deeper.  Feeds on small fishes and also benthic invertebrates.  Ovoviviparous, with 3-21 in a litter (Ref. 12951, Ref. 114953).  Size at birth 9 cm (Ref. 12951).  Capable of inflicting a severe shock of up to 200 volts.

species.name: Doux-rêve ouvre-boîte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Also mesopelagic.  Males dwarfed, non-parasitic (Ref. 10524).  Feeds on fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Dow's mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters, including estuaries; usually over sand or mud bottoms.

species.name: Downing's shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty sand-rubble bottom, in association with snapping shrimps Alpheus bellulus Miya & Miyake and A. ochrostriatus Miya (Ref. 11441). Inhabits coastal, open sandy substrates in 10-20 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Downy blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky and rubble shores with algal mats, reefs and seagrass beds.  Found in holes and crevices or amongst coral formations (Ref. 13628).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Doydixodon laevifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Draa trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits small and shallow streams with clear and cold waters (Ref. 107622). The habitat of this species suffers catastrophic seasonal floods that influence dramatically the demography of the population; the continuous deforestation of the Atlas Mountains and the disappearance of the riparian vegetation, increase the adverse effect of the overflows over the small Atlas rivers; overfishing is also a problem for a small population ; therefore this species should be included in the IUCN category of endangered (Ref. 107622).

species.name: Drab emperor
species.description: Found on or near reefs (Ref. 50562).   Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Drab flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Drab longfin gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Drab moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively turbid areas of sheltered lagoon reefs (Ref. 1602, 37816). Including mangroves in 1-20 m (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Drab reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from mud bottoms.

species.name: Drab snake moray
species.description: Found in reefs and crevices of shallow lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 37816, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Drachmann's lanternfish
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Draco waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on sandy bottoms, often in bays.

species.name: Draconectes narinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dracula shrimp-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open sand and rubble zones adjacent to reefs (Ref. 30404). Occurs in pairs and hovers above the burrow entrance. Lives symbiotically with Alpheus randalli (Ref. 9360).

species.name: Dragon abyssal
species.description: Genre de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).  Pronounced sexual dimorphism:  females are black, with well developed canine teeth, barbel and pelvic fins with six stripes.  Males are dark-brown, have no teeth on maxilla and neither barbel nor pelvic fins (Ref. 47377).  Apparently, females live below 500 m during the day and perform vertical migration at night to shallower depths; males always in deep water, ca 1,000-2,000 m (Ref. 5169).

species.name: Dragon fin cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dragon gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dragon poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky gravel and muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Dragon-boa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep oceanic waters to more than 1,000 m depth, may migrate to near-surface waters at night (Ref. 4783).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4783).

species.name: Dragon-boa (Stomias ferox)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species that lives deeper than 500 m during daylight and migrates to the upper 200 m at night.  Observed by submersibles to position themselves horizontally in the water column with pelvic and pectoral fins spread wide, with barbel pointing forward.  A predatory fish presumed to lie-and-wait and capable of quick bursts of speed (Ref. 86779). Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4783).  Oviparous.

species.name: Dragon-saumon de Richardson
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, usually living deeper than 500 m during the day.  Smaller individuals migrate to the surface at night.  Possibly feeding on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 58426).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dragon-saumon à grands yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species usually found deeper than 500 m during the day (Ref. 2802).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 2802).

species.name: Dragon-saumon élancé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic (Ref. 2802) and mesopelagic-bathypelagic species (Ref. 4465).  Usually found deeper than 500 m during the day (Ref. 2802).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 2802).

species.name: Dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal protected reefs on rubble or algal covered rocks (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth of 5 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Dragonet de Shango
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters (Ref. 6941).

species.name: Dragonet lyre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand and muddy bottoms from sublittoral to 200 m (Ref. 6444) and to 400 m or more (Ref. 9900).  Feeds on small invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans.  Territorial, males aggressive with each other.  Complex courtship behavior consists of 4 phases:  courtship, pairing, ascending, releasing eggs and milt.  Pelagic eggs and larvae (Ref. 5968).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Neither opercular spine gland nor anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Dragonfin tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimens reach 8.0 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Dragonnet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dragonnet de Haifa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy substrate of the coastal area down to a depth of about 100 m (Ref. 5213).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 4405. Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, mainly crustaceans and worms (Ref. 5968).  Minimum depth of 2 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Dragonnet de sable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy bottoms (Ref. 5213).  Feeds on benthic crustaceans, worms and snails (Ref. 9608).

species.name: Dragonnet fascié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy bottoms.  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans (Ref. 5968).

species.name: Dragonnet lyre du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in deep water (Ref. 4405).  Preyed upon by kingklip and other commercial species, as well as fur seals (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Dragonnet phaeton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from 80-650 m (Ref. 06941) and from 302-848 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Found on sand or mud bottoms.  Territorial, males aggressive to each other.  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates, mainly worms, snails and crustaceans.  Eggs and larvae pelagic (Ref. 5968).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 26999.

species.name: Dragonnet réticulé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters, even intertidally, on sandy shores (Ref. 6444).

species.name: Dragonnet tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sandy bottoms.  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates mainly worms, snails and crustaceans.  Eggs and larvae pelagic (Ref. 5968).

species.name: Dragonnet élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters with sandy bottoms, occasionally found at a depth of 100 m.  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans (Ref. 5968).

species.name: Dragonu joue de feu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species.

species.name: Drague à godet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  It has been suggested that this species does not undergo substantial diel vertical migration and remains below 500 m (Ref. 78501).  Feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Drain mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, relatively still, brackish to freshwater creek habitats (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Driftwood catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Drin brook lamprey
species.description: A non-parasitic species (Ref. 58030).  Adults inhabit piedmont and montane zones in clear, well oxygenated brooks.  Ammocoetes live in detritus-rich sands or clay sediments (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Drombus kranjiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of the genus Drombus are found in shallow reefs and estuaries (Ref. 42915).

species.name: Drombus palackyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Drop Knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Drop-shaped tadpolefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by a bottom trawl at 206 m depth, where bottom water temperature was - 0.6 to - 0.7°C and salinity at 33.31-34.33 ppt (Ref. 116680).

species.name: Dryanin's char
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Drysdale grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit larger streams rather than small tributaries, forming schools in rock pools and over sand bottoms (Ref. 2906, 5259, 44894). They retreat to crevices when threatened (Ref. 44894). Feed on filamentous algae by grazing on rocks. (Ref. 2906, 5259, 44894). Sometimes form mixed shoals with S. trigonicus. Breed during the late dry or early wet season (October to December) (Ref. 44894). Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205). Aquarium conditions: pH=7.5, H=12, 26°C, egg layer, peaceful community fish, plant and rock cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Drysdale gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits clear, freshwater pools of slow-flowing streams over rock and sand bottoms (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Drysdale hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky pools in clear, flowing streams.  Occurs in still or flowing water of sandy river channels and rocky pools (Ref. 44894).  Feeds chiefly on insects and their aquatic larvae and crustaceans, but some algae is also consumed.

species.name: Dryzone butter catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dubois' Panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in the shallow and weedy parts of brooks, small streams and swamps in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Duck-billed eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154) and shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Duck-billed golden-line fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species (Ref. 27297).  Encountered in two caves at about 30 m from their entrance at 1.5 m depth.  Feeds on plant and insects (Ref. 86777).

species.name: Duckbill catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools.  Is mainly nocturnal.  Feeds primarily on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 9084).

species.name: Duckbill conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duckbill flagfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duckbill flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found below 100 m to at least 400 m (Ref. 13628); enters shelf waters (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Duckbill grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duckbill oceanic eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans.

species.name: Duckbill pugolovka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with a Sigsbee trawl at a depth of 294 m over white silt, on 22 April 1904 by the expedition of N.M. Knipovich (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Duckbilled buntingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duckbilled catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large turbid rivers. Feeds mainly on Macrobrachium and Caridina prawns.

species.name: Duckbilled clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duhamel’s catshark
species.description: Occurs along the continental shelves, a benthic dweller (Ref. 120402).

species.name: Dumbéa river pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers to elevations of at least 8 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at about 10 cm SL.

species.name: Dumeril's lanternfish
species.description: High-oceanic and mesopelagic populations are found between 225-750 m during the day (maximum abundance at 450-500 m) and is nyctoepipelagic at surface down to 125 m at night (Ref. 4479).  Pseudoceanic and pelagic populations are found in the upper 50 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Feeding is acyclic in northwest Africa (Ref. 9198).

species.name: Duncker's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand, rubble, or reef habitats to a depth of at least 14 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also found in coastal algal-rubble slopes in 5-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Duncker's river garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A tropical estuarine species (Ref. 10943).  Found at surface levels in estuaries.  Its habitat may be confined to brackish water.  Feeds on terrestrial insects.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Dundocharax bidentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 2.4 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Dungu sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species (Ref. 188).

species.name: Dunker's pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 205, 75154) and continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Duopalatinus emarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Duopalatinus peruanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dupouyichthys sapito
