species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river banks with vegetation (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Durango shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Durban goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwater and estuaries (Ref. 2798, 4343).

species.name: Durban sweeper
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in exposed rocky shores and often in small groups that shelter in caves or beneath ledges by day from depths as little as 1-2 m to at least 15 m. It has been observed to venture out of shelter at night to feed on planktonic invertebrates and larval fishes. It was also reported to have an extensive spawning season, judging from seeing shoals of juveniles through
most of the year. The gonads of adults were noted to be nearly always mature regardless of the time of year. It was also observed to swim slowly, when not stressed, propelling itself mainly by characteristic ‘sweeps’ of the pectoral fins (hence the common name sweeper). Smallest fully mature female specimen, 11.6 cm SL (Ref. 97766).

species.name: Durban tonguesole
species.description: Enters brackish waters (Ref. 6805).  Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Duringlanis perugiae
species.description: Inhabits large rivers where the water is swift, preferring littoral zones adjacent to the shoreline over hard, sandy bottoms devoid of vegetation.  Feeds on insects, mostly ants, beetles, and mayflies (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Dusky betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mouth brooder (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Dusky blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms with rocks or boulders (Ref. 5521), seagrass beds, and patch reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Dusky brotulid
species.description: Rare species, known from a single male specimen (Ref. 34024). Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices to at least 20 m depth, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Dusky cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral, gravel, or shell bottoms (Ref. 9626).  Found near open basket stars at night (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Dusky crawler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal outcrops with somewhat sheltered sandy bays (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Dusky cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Adults occur in shallow coastal waters, usually in turtle grass beds (Ref. 7251).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dusky damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky shores exposed to wave action.  Often in tide pools.  Feed primarily on algae and detritus.  Territorial and pugnacious.  Generally common (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Dusky darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit fast gravel runs, sometimes riffles, of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Often found near brush (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Young are found in shallower gravel riffles (Ref. 7043). Juveniles feed on midge and blackfly larvae; adults consume caddisfly and mayfly larvae (Ref. 10294).  Males are larger and darker in color during breeding (Ref. 69400).

species.name: Dusky fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sighted in a habitat characterised by a steep slope beginning in relatively deep water; about 10 individuals, including the holotype, were observed at 40 m, on a flat to gently sloping rubble bottom along the upper edge of a vertical drop-off (Ref. 75880).

species.name: Dusky finless skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare, restricted to deep waters (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dusky flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally inhabit shallow bays and inlets and can be found in estuaries as far as tidal limits (Ref. 27246); they often invade freshwater. They occur over mud, silt gravel, sand and seagrass (mainly Zostera species) beds from intertidal areas to depths of 10 m in Queensland and to 30 m in southern New South Wales. Eggs and larvae are dispersed along the coast by tidal and current movements (Ref. 27112). Small juveniles less than 12 cm TL first appear in coastal bays 1-2 months after spawning. They mainly inhabit shallow mangrove and mud flats and seagrass beds (Ref. 27246, 27245). They are usually solitary but may form loose aggregations (Ref. 2165, 27247). Feed on small fish, crabs, prawns, small crustaceans. octopus, squid and polychaete worms. They have spines on the outer edges of their head which can inflict nasty cuts during handling (pers. comm., Bernard Moss, 2001).

species.name: Dusky frillgoby
species.description: Inhabits shallow rocky areas, often in pools of the intertidal zone (Ref. 2798).  Occurs mostly in coastal areas.  Also found in estuaries, tidal zones and often ascending into freshwater streams; smaller species live between branches of corals where they exploit several crustacean groups. Feeds on crustaceans, fish and algae (Ref. 92840). Sometimes seen as fresh catches at markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Dusky goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Dusky jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock and sand bottoms or the eroding edges of weed beds.  Egg mass incubated in mouth of males (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Dusky kob
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries, the surf zone and further offshore. In southern Angola, it is caught mainly in depths of 20-40 m. Becomes more abundant in Argyrosomus catches going northwards, indicating its preference for warmer waters. Fish up to 13,000 g were found to be immature. Adults are rarely found in Namibia but are said to be abundant in southern Angola, where the lack of permanent estuaries there suggests that this habitat type does not play an important role in the life history of this species (Ref. 11025).

species.name: Dusky lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066), found between 550-850 m during the day; between 60-850 m at night with maximum abundance between 100-150 m (Ref. 4479).  Size stratification with depth during the day (Ref. 4066).

species.name: Dusky leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in weedy areas, usually in harbors (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Dusky millions fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamps and drains of Perth metropolitan area, Western Australia (Ref. 44894).  Omnivorous.

species.name: Dusky morwong
species.description: Found in seagrass beds and near rocky outcrops (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on polychaetes, isopods, amphipods and brown algae.  Flesh of smaller fish is excellent eating, but its quality deteriorates with age (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Dusky mountain goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast-flowing streams over gravel or rocky bottoms.

species.name: Dusky panaque
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusky pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in seagrass beds along coasts.  Northern populations move offshore during colder months (Ref. 26938).  Found mostly at 5 m or less (Ref. 126547). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Feeds mostly on small grass shrimp and other small crustaceans (Ref. 93252).

species.name: Dusky rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably inhabits areas not suitable for sampling with a bottom trawl (Ref. 26363).

species.name: Dusky rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found hovering in loose organized groups just above rocky reefs and along shorelines, or may rest singly upon rocky substrate (Ref. 27436).  Feed by picking and seizing food items that are either drifting or suspended in the water column (Ref. 27302).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Sold as fresh or frozen fillets; eaten as fish cakes (Ref. 27436).  Captured by the nearshore jig fishery and has been reported to comprise up to 25% of the catch in the 'black rockfish' jig fishery of the northern Gulf of Alaska (citation in Ref. 53613).

species.name: Dusky sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore (Ref. 2850).  Most common near drop-offs (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Dusky shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and runs over sand and mud, usually in clear or tannin-stained creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Dusky skate
species.description: A demersal species found on upper continental slope. Males reaches maturity at ca. 32-35 cm TL, smallest juvenile 8cm TL. Discarded bycatch of local trawl fisheries (Ref. 114953)

species.name: Dusky snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusky snout catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by bottom trawls and midwater trawls. Maturity size for females at 48.1 cm TL and are immature at 43.0 cm TL, males at 45.2 cm and immature at 38.0 cm TL (Ref. 102637).

species.name: Dusky sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusky splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusky squirrelfish
species.description: Inhabits inshore reefs and tide pools.  Hides in small recesses.  Common, but rarely seen (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 26938).   Intertidal observations were also reported (Ref. 49162).

species.name: Dusky sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fish is common on coral reefs (Ref. 6645); forming aggregations in caves or crevices or under overhangs (Ref. 48636) by day, but a few may at times be seen in the open, close to the shelter of reefs. This species is also observed forming small groups with Myripristis murdjan at 0.5-1 m below the surface. At night, it is known to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 94773). Spawning occur during April to June, and is year-round in Okinawa I. (Koeda et al., in press - in Ref. 95675). Spawning occurred after sunset with individuals larger than 11 cm SL joining the spawning group (Ref. 95675). Flesh is edible (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Dusky tongue sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusky tripletooth goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits both brackish and freshwater and may spend its whole life in freshwater.  Caught for food.

species.name: Dusky velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Inhabits sandy or mud bottoms in shallow waters (Ref. 559 and 637).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Dusky-hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was recorded up rivers at 90, 150 and 210 km from the sea, but it is not known if these are permanent freshwater populations or migrants from the sea.  At least small numbers enter artisanal river and lake fisheries (Ref. 9822).  Found in large rivers far upstream from the estuary (Ref. 12693).  Feeds mainly on insect larvae and small fishes.  Used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Dusky-pink skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.6-12.0 cm long and 7.54-7.8 cm wide (Ref. 41253, 41249, 41250, 41298).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).

species.name: Dusky-purple skate
species.description: Deep-sea species (Ref. 8630).  Small individuals feed on crabs and annelids, while larger ones prey on fish and cephalopods (Ref. 27640).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.9-11.3 cm long and 6.5-6.7 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: Dusky-tailed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and fringing coral and rocky reefs with sand or rubble bottom in relatively clear water.  Usually in aggregations, among branching corals, sometimes with its congeners (Ref. 36661, 48635, 54391).

species.name: Duskybanded sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Duskyfin glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in main rivers and lakes (Ref. 56749).  Occurs in sluggish rivers and floodplains.  Grows to a fairly large size and is probably the most common species of this family, seen in the markets.  Feeds on insects, crustaceans, and small fish (Ref. 12693).  Used as feeds for caged fishes (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Duskyshoulder trevally
species.description: Adults inhabit coastal waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Duskystripe shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, runs and deep riffles of clear, fast creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably nest spawners like congeners.

species.name: Duskytail chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep outer reef slopes.  Feed on zooplankton above the bottom (Ref. 10375).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Duskytail darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dusted dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf Altai osman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Dwarf atom goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mainly oceanic drop-offs between 20 to 30 m (Ref. 38635). Also found in lagoons and outer reefs in 5-35 m (Ref. 90102). One of the smallest (=shortest) vertebrate of the world, with mature females reaching only 8-10 mm SL; scaleless (Ref. 9360).

species.name: Dwarf barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf black stingray
species.description: This demersal species lives offshore on continental shelf, probably occasionally shallower; caught incidentally in trawl and net fisheries; llfe history unknown (Ref. 114953). Maximum length for females of similar form, possibly up to 49.8 cm WD (Ref. 76959).

species.name: Dwarf blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Dwarf botia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers and flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Found in small muddy lakes and other standing water habitats.  Active by day and often schools in some distance above the bottom (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Not fished commercially, but highly regarded as aquarium fish (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Dwarf bumblebee catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been found only in peat swamps with very acidic (pH 3.5-4.5) and tannin-stained water (Ref. 40801).  Occurs in well shaded forest streams with fast-flowing water and dense growth of submerged vegetation (Ref. 85309).  A gregarious species which feeds on small aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Dwarf cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf cigarfish
species.description: Feeds mainly on salps (Ref. 33689).  Caught by midwater trawl (Ref. 28222).

species.name: Dwarf citharine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, quiet, well-vegetated habitats; common on floodplains and in the Okavango Delta; feeds by picking periphyton and tiny invertebrates from the stems and leaves of water plants; breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Attractive and peaceful in aquariums (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Dwarf corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among plants.  Forms small schools (Ref. 26041).  Found in ponds (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Dwarf danio
species.description: Lives in rivers.

species.name: Dwarf deep-water sculpin
species.description: inhabits muddy bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Dwarf dory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dwarf dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and coral reefs.

species.name: Dwarf False Catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawling over sand bottoms from about 5 to 53 m (Ref. 9790).

species.name: Dwarf freshwater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly near patches of reef and rock.  Relatively uncommon (Ref. 9710).  Smallest frogfish in the western Atlantic (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Dwarf Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawning occurs from September to December (Ref. 33843).

species.name: Dwarf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs or isolated coral head habitats (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Dwarf gulper shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known deepwater dogfish found on the upper continental slopes to at least 450 m (Ref. 31367).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Probably taken in bottom trawls (Ref. 31367). Caught by demersal longline fisheries operating in deepwater areas. Utilised for its meat, fins (low value) and liver oil (very high value) (Ref.58048).

species.name: Dwarf gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf inanga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf Lake Turkana robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic species, usually occurring with A. ferox, widespread throughout the open waters of Lake Turkana; situated in midwater scattering layer during daylight hours; disperses through surface waters after dark; feeds chiefly on zooplankton with occasional small insects; spawns within the lake; matures at exceptionally small size for an Alestes (Ref. 53378).

species.name: Dwarf lantern shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dwarf lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Dwarf mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Dwarf marbled catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in creeks with little current; living on the bottom covered with decomposing leaves (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Dwarf medaka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water swamps (Ref. 43281).  Non-annual breeder (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Dwarf molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small, bottom-living fishes usually inhabiting moderately deep water (up to 500 m) on outer shelf and continental slope waters (Ref. 26271).

species.name: Dwarf moon tetra
species.description: Found in the main river channel of Ngoko River, usually in or close to riparian vegetation over a substrate of fine particles and organic material (Ref. 110423).

species.name: Dwarf noodlefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in the main stream of middle Mekong.  Usually taken  incidentally in haul seines and trap catches.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Dwarf panaque
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered fresh and brackish water tanks, small streams and rivulets overgrown with vegetation (Ref. 41236).  Valuable for mosquito control (Ref. 6028).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Dwarf perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky inshore areas and in depths up to 9.1 m, often among seaweeds.  Feed on algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dwarf pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Dwarf pygmy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is one of the smallest freshwater fishes:  males are mature at 9 mm, females at 15 mm.  The species used to frequent shady river banks in the Malabon River, Rizal Province, Luzon, Philippines; however, the type locality has been reclaimed and the remaining waters in the area are heavily polluted; the species is considered extinct in the Philippines (Rainer Froese, pers. comm., 2004).  It has been apparently imported into Germany in 1958;  a color photo of the fish was taken in an aquarium (Ref. 2060).  Found in brackish waters and mangrove areas of Indonesia (M. Kottelat, pers. comm.).

species.name: Dwarf rainbowfish
species.description: Poisson. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Dwarf rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet forest streams with slow-flowing acidic water (Ref. 85309).  Feeds on worms and small crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  One of the world's smallest cyprinid species.

species.name: dwarf sanjika
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift-flowing streams in rocky reaches over clean sand (Ref. 52193).; prefers clear, fast flowing waters (Ref. 26673). It feeds on insects and other invertebrates in the drift (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Dwarf sawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal in shallow coastal inshore habitats in mangrove swamps and embayments (Ref. 114953),  intertidal species found in estuaries and on tidal mudflats (Ref. 9859).  Ascends brackish areas of rivers (Ref. 9859).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Pupping thought to occur during the tropical wet season (November to March in Australia (Ref. 114953). Biology little known (Ref. 9859). Males mature at approximately 260 cm TL, females possibly slightly larger; born at 65 cm TL (Ref. 114953).  Flesh may be good to eat (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Dwarf scissortail rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near the surface in shallow marshes, swamps and inundated fields (Ref. 12693).  Inhabits swamps with clear water (Ref. 43281).  Usually found in shallow layers of open water above beds of fine-leaved aquatic macrophytes and submerged grasses (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on zooplankton and some insects.  Probably too small to be marketed.  Rarely seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693)

species.name: Dwarf scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154) and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Dwarf sculpins
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A single male specimen is known (Ref. 2058); found over sand and stone in coastal waters (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Dwarf seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shallow grass flats, especially in association with Zostera and other seagrass; periodically found in floating vegetation. Diurnal, males more site faithful than females. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Specimens lose their skin filaments in aquaria (Ref. 30915). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Dwarf shore-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reefs in pale brownish weeds and seagrasses, from the intertidal to a few meters depth (Ref. 9002, 56640).

species.name: Dwarf slippery goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf snakehead
species.description:
Occurs mostly in lotic waters such as streams and rivers, also in lentic habitats such as pools and ditches in the lowlands. This species is usually associated with submerged roots, leaf debris and marginal vegetation during daytime, with adults solitary or occurring as pairs. At night, individuals can be more easily observed in open waters. It occurs even in highly modified habitats such as concretized drains and canals in urban areas. Highest elevation recorded for this species was ca. 700 m asl at Lunugala, but it has also been reported it from Diyatalawa, ca 
1200 m asl. Reported from southern peninsular India from east-fowing drainages (Ref. 124133).

species.name: Dwarf sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottoms including reef flats and tide pools in 0-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Dwarf spinyhead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in burrows made by invertebrates (usually those of sipunculids) in dead corals in shallow water (<5 m) (Ref. 51564).

species.name: Dwarf squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 37816).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Secretive (Ref. 37816). Cryptic, never seen during day, remain close to reef shelter at night (Ref 90102).

species.name: Dwarf stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered bays, shallow inshore and probably ranging to deep offshore in mud-sand habitats (Ref. 559, 48635).  Buries itself during the day in the substrate and is rarely observed, except when found by accident or at night (Ref. 48635).  Usually covered with hydroids (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Dwarf stonebasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dense vegetation along margins of rivers and floodplain lagoons (Ref. 7248, 52193). Often found in lagoons and backwaters in shallow water just underneath the surface vegetation (Ref. 13337). It feeds on aquatic insect larvae including a large component of Chironomidae (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Dwarf sturgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare and endangered species; smallest sturgeon; sensitive to chemicals in  the water  Ref. 35930).

species.name: Dwarf threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 3810) of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Rarely seen in markets (Ref. 3810).

species.name: Dwarf whipray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dwarf whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Dwarf wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow beds of turtle grass (Thalassia). Common but seldom noticed (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Dwarf wrymouth
species.description: Apparently lives partly buried in mud bottoms (Ref. 2850, 4925).

species.name: Dwarf-red rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably occur deeper than 183 m.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Dysalotus alcocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species.  Adults have been taken mostly in depths exceeding 1,000 m.

species.name: Dysalotus oligoscolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic.  Apparently all adults have been taken in hauls to depths exceeding 1,500 m (Ref. 6944)

species.name: Dysomma fuscoventralis
species.description: Larvae do not seem to live in shallow water.

species.name: Dysomma opisthoproctus
species.description: Maximum depth reported based on a single specimen (Ref. 31561).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dysommina proboscideus
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Dysommina rugosa
species.description: On the continental slope (Ref. 57911).

species.name: Dérivant
species.description: Oceanic, epipelagic or mesopelagic in warm and temperate waters.  Feeds mainly on salps (Ref. 33689).

species.name: Dérivant des physalies
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore in warm waters. Juveniles pelagic in coastal and offshore waters down to at least 30 m, but adults possibly demersal in deep water (Ref. 9563). Occur in association with floating Portuguese man-of-war, Physalia, feeding on its tentacles and gonads and may drift with it into shore waters with proper wind conditions (Ref. 4777). Probably also feed on other soft-bodied jellyfish as well as on zooplankton (Ref.4777).

species.name: Dérivant gélatineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species (Ref. 6891).  Associated with jellyfish (Ref. 7251) and floating weed patches (Ref. 6891).  Large adults may be benthic on continental slopes (Ref. 6891).  Feeds on zooplankton and small pelagic fishes (Ref. 4777).

species.name: D’Arros sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eakin’s plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eared blacksmelt
species.description: Oviparous.  With planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604). Adults generally within mesopelagic depths (Ref. 96339).

species.name: Eared conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Earle's soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed in caves and under ledges (Ref. 49349). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Earle's splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in large zooplankton feeding aggregations along steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 37816). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Postlarvae are caught with midwater trawl. Apparently preyed upon by Pristipomoides filamentosus (Ref. 8524). This species has been collected at Kwajalein Atoll at depths of 46-55 m (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Earspot longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral heads, on reefs or in rocky areas, to depths of 15 m, but often in shallower water (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Earspot snakeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with seagrass, reef and weed (Ref. 33839).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Earth eater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: East African red finned barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary and permanent streams as well as in marginal water-lily swamps in Lake Victoria basin (Ref. 104790). Found in pools near papyrus vegetation (Ref. 9606) and in smaller bodies of water or near the margins of rivers between the vegetation in the Lake Rukwa drainage (Ref. 27292). Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 4903). Spawns in temporary streams when flooded during rainy season (Ref. 104790) and spawns all year round with maximum at beginning of rainy season (Ref. 27292).

species.name: East African skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: East China leg skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: East Coast barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, well-vegetated streams and pans (Ref. 52193). It feeds on small aquatic organisms (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer, possibly migrating to spawning sites (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: East coast flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on bottom-living animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: East Gippsland Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish not able to undertake diadromous migrations. It occurs from small to moderately large (in average 1.5-6.0 m width and 0.15-0.40 m depth), well-shaded and cool, clear to slightly tannin-stained streams, flowing through densely forested catchments, consisting of pools, glides and riffles, with smaller amounts of rapids and backwater areas. The substrate consisted predominantly of bedrock with boulder and cobble, with smaller amounts of gravel and coarse sand, and relatively large areas of silt deposits. Instream cover provided mainly by rock, vegetation overhang and timber debris, with smaller areas of aquatic vegetation, and pools averaged 0.6-0.8 m in depth. Recorded at a density of 0.10-0.28 fish/m2 and collected with the native species Anguilla australis (Shortfinned eel), Galaxias brevipinnis (Broadfinned Galaxias), Euastacus bidawalus (East Gippsland spiny crayfish), Euastacus kershawi (Gippsland spiny crayfish) and Paratya australiensis (Common freshwater shrimp). The predatory alien species Salmo trutta is present farther downstream in the Goolengook River system. Apparently spawning period is during winter to spring, but may be variable. Individuals collected in late February 2002 (late summer) were at an early stage of gonad development but in late May 1992 (end of autumn) were at an advanced stage, with males running ripe and female gonads well developed and generally in a ripe stage. The majority of fish recorded in late May were > 5.4 cm LCF (length to caudal fork), with the smallest sexually developing individual 5.48 cm LCF. Confusingly, there were three individuals also collected in late May were juveniles (3.7, 3.95 and 4.14 cm LCF), considered of 0+ age, possibly indicating a late spawning with a possible November-December hatching. One individual was found to be infected with a short, thin, white worm, coiled and pointed at both ends, from amongst fat deposits around stomach in the body cavity (Ref. 98815).

species.name: East Indian lipsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal, found in rocky shorelines (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: East indian soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims in small aggregations in current prone channels, at moderate depths (Ref. 48635). Poorly known species on outer reef slopes in 3-50 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: East Indies siltgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: East Siberian grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: East-Australian stripey
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles and young  adults are often seen in rock pools and rocky shores to 5 meters. Adults are more commonly seen near rocky reefs, but are also common in harbours, embankments, and under piers, where they occur in large groups (Ref. 123714).

species.name: East-Pacific ventbrotula
species.description: The holotype, a male with spindle-formed, unripe testes, does not contain any identifiable stomach contents while the paratype was eviscerated only leaving the strangely formed kidneys which may be an adaptation to the special conditions near the vents. The capture of the two specimens using baited trap indicates a necrophagous diet; specimens grazing on the bottom. The poorly developed teeth and the presence of 10-11 long gill rakers on the anterior arch indicate that it preys upon rather small food-items. The thick skin could be an adaptation to endure the high temperatures in the hydrothermal vent area. The same condition is found in another vent-fish Thermichthys hollisi. The presence of a male without an intromittant organ shows that it is oviparous. The vent site Oasis is composed of active black smokers covered with the tubeworm polychaete Alvinellaspp., large patches of mussels, clams and stalked cirripeds. A milky fluid diffuses from crevices and collapsed lava lakes, with clouds of swimming amphipods. The two specimens were collected next to such a hole surrounded by the mytilid mussel Bathymodiolus thermophilus Kenk & Wilson, 1985, the clam Calyptogena magnifica Boss & Turner, 1980, the stalked barnacle Neolepas cf. zevinae Newman, 1979, actinostolid sea-anemones (Chondrophellia-like), the bythograeid crab Bythograea thermydron Williams, 1980, the galatheid crab Munidopsis sp. And a recently described nematocarcinid shrimp, Nematocarcinus burukowskyi Komai & Segonzac, 2005. Other fish occur in this environment such as the synaphobranchid Ilyophis saldanhai Karmovskaya & Parin, 1999, the bythitid Thermichthys hollisi (Cohen et al., 1990) and an unidentified hagfish. Additional specimens were observed at other sites (Yaquina, Hobbs, and Gromit), between 2585 and 2840 m , at places with sometimes 10 or more individuals swimming in the shimmering vent fluids with temperatures between 2 and 7°C (Ref. 57890). Eggs may be oval and pelagic which may float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastcoast lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brackish water and mangrove swamps, pools and lagoons from the Tana river delta (Kenya) and probably the Rufigi river delta in Tanzania (Ref. 3788).  Successfully kept in the aquarium and even bred, albeit extremely difficult to keep (Ref. 31267).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Easter damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ubiquitous at Easter Island. Juveniles occur in surge pools, and both adults and juveniles found in coral and rocky reefs. They occur solitarily or in aggregations of about 10 to 30 individuals, frequently near the coral Porites (Ref. 7247). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Easter filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Easter island moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Aegean bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Angel Shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Atlantic cleaner clingfish
species.description: This species has been collected and observed at 10-38 m depth, mainly on hard substrate.  It acts as a facultative cleaner of larger fishes (e.g. <i>Gymnothorax afer; in the Canary Islands, cleaning a muraenid and a serranid) (Ref. 106378).

species.name: Eastern Australian banjofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Australian legskate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Australian longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern banded catshark
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from a variety of environmental substrates ranging from sandy to course rubble at depths of capture from 10.6 to 74 m, with most records shallower than 50 m.   Maximum size in total length for males 19.0- 47.0 cm and for females 17.8-48.4 cm TL. The average mass of adult males was 92.5% of the adult females, with considerable overlap between large males and small females. Mass of adult males 182.5-286.0 g (n=5, mean = 203.8, sd = 43.6); adult females 150-386.3 g (n=4, mean = 220.3, sd =111.2); while there was a considerable overlap in the mass of juveniles and adults for both males and females.  
Smallest sexually mature female 35.4 cm TL with size at first maturity being possibly lower; while the smallest sexually mature male recorded was 34.5 cm TL.  Reproduction is expected to be oviparous, although no egg casings were recorded from the sample specimens.  This species feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates and small teleost species.  Stomach content of 4 specimens included penaeid prawns, brachyuran crabs, cephalopods (Order Teuthida) and teleost species from the families Gobiidae and Platycephalidae (Ref. 75152).

species.name: Eastern barhead damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered outer reef often associated with branching coral in about 15-45 m (Ref. 90102). Close relative of N. thoracotaeniatus (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Eastern blue devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic species which occur inshore (Ref. 7300).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern blue groper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal rocky areas at depths to about 40 m (Ref. 26878).  Protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Max. length for female species (Bernard Yau, pers. Comm., 2000).

species.name: Eastern bluespot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow-water estuarine, in estuaries of rivers, streams and mangroves, typically much more coastal in distribution than the frequently inland P. olorum (likely in part relating to the topography of higher gradient streams along the Great Dividing Range habitat of south-eastern Australia, compared to the lower relief in south-western Australia). Co-occurs with P. aquilonius and P. jeffi at its northern distribution range (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Eastern bottlenose mormyrid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves and muddy areas, also hides among weeds (Ref. 13337). Favours quiet deep water with a soft muddy bottom (Ref. 52193). Forms shoals (Ref. 13337, 52193). Feeds on weeds (Ref. 5595) and insects but may also feed on small fishes (Ref. 5595, 52193) and fish eggs (Ref. 52193), blood worms (Ref. 13337), small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 13337, 52193). Active mainly at night; breeds during the rainy season, moving upstream in rivers after flood spates have receded (Ref. 52193). Migrations appears to occur at irregular interval as this fish is not a powerful swimmer and would not be able to cope with very high water current (Ref. 13337). Females carry 10,000-70,000 eggs; can give a mild shock when caught (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Eastern Cape redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species refers clear rocky pools; fry and juveniles occur in large schoals, adults in small groups (Ref. 7248). Once common and widely distributed, but Pseudobarbus afer suffered severe decline in distribution and abundance, mainly due to the invasion by alien predators and competitors, deterioration of water quality and loss of critical habitat (Ref. 114782). Omnivorous, feeding mainly from the bottom on algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 7248). Breeds in summer, spawning in riffles above pools (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Eastern Carpathian golden loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy streams with clean water and moderate to fast current, in sand burrows, rarely in gravel (Ref. 59043).  Spawning occurs in spring where eggs are laid in batches (Ref. 59043).  Eggs measuring 0.9-1.1 mm are scattered over sand, gravel or other substrate.  Larvae at 3.0-3.4 mm TL start to feed after 6 days.  These larvae lack external gill filaments but are characterized by a bump on forehead (Ref. 59043).  Population is gradually getting threatened because of very limited distribution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Eastern cleaner-clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually on kelp, on which they deposit their eggs, which are guarded by the male, although the female is often present as well (Ref. 9002).  Often on ascidians or sponges in deep water, probably depositing eggs on algae nearby (Ref. 9002).  Often observed cleaning  boxfishes, porcupine fishes and morwongs (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Eastern clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive, occurring under rocks, often behind sea urchins.

species.name: Eastern creek chubsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel-bottomed pools of clear headwaters, creeks and small rivers, often near vegetation.  Occasionally found in lakes (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on microcrustacea, aquatic insects and some algae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Eastern crested loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern dwarf false catshark
species.description: Specimens were taken as bycatch in deep-sea longline fishery for gulper sharks (Centrophorus spp.) (Ref. 119154).

species.name: Eastern dwarf galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently found among vegetation along the edge of still or slow-running waters like swamps, drainage ditches and backwaters of creeks. Adults live in both ephemeral and permanent habitats. A short-lived fish, reaching maturity in the first year of life and perishing shortly after spawning. Fish occupying ephemeral water possibly aestivate or shelter in crayfish burrows when surface water evaporates during summer (Ref. 44894). Probably an annual species. Spawn from July to October. Like its southwestern relative G. munda, this species is also a multiple spawner (Ref. 44894). Females deposit a few eggs per day on leaf litter. Eggs hatch after 10-17 days at 16°-21°C. Scanty information on diet: captive specimens eat small invertebrates and filamentous algae.

species.name: Eastern eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern fortescue
species.description: Found in seagrass beds in estuaries (extremely common during reproductive season in the austral Spring) and coastal bays, and sponge gardens on inshore reefs.  Venomous dorsal spines often inflict a painful sting to fishers (Ref. 34095, 39597).  Of no commercial importance but often entrapped in fishing gears such as trawls and can be dangerous to fishermen who attempt to remove these (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Eastern frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf.  Also found in inshore waters (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Eastern gobbleguts
species.description: Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Eastern happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated areas in shallow water, but also found in rivers and streams around the lake.  Feeds on invertebrates, algae, plants, small fishes and plankton (Ref. 5595). Ovophilic, agamous (Ref. 52307) maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 6307, 52307).

species.name: Eastern headspot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. rotenone

species.name: Eastern highfin spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Honduras molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern hulafish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern jumping blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal and subtidal areas on exposed rocks covered with algae (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Eastern keelback mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit inlet waters and estuaries of rivers.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Used as food fish in Japan.

species.name: Eastern longfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern longnose spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern looseskin skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep pools among vegetation and log debris.

species.name: Eastern mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in standing to slow-flowing water, mostly in vegetated ponds and lakes, backwaters and quiet pools of steams (Ref. 5723), typically seen shoaling at the edges (Ref. 44894).  They also frequent brackish water (Ref. 5723).  Adults feed on small terrestrial insects usually in the drift and amongst aquatic plants, actively selecting very small prey (Ref. 6154).  Also observed to take in mosquito larvae (Ref. 41168).  Introduced worldwide.  Introductions to Europe have seriously threatened many endemic species (Ref. 59043).  It is now widely accepted that their effect has been minimal and even may have exacerbated the problem due to their voracious appetite for natural invertebrate predators of mosquito larvae (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Eastern numbfish
species.description: Maturity size reaches ca. 26 cm TL; born at ca. 8 cm TL. Biology little known (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Eastern Pacific black chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Pacific bonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern Pacific roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern pomfred
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools are found in coastal bays, protected island coves, deeper part of large estuaries close to the sea entrance, and along rocky drop-offs with kelp (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Eastern Queen scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collection data of specimens of blackish form indicates a coral reef habitat, usually at depths less than 20 m, and specimens of yellowish form were collected from deeper sandy bottom areas below 30 m depth (Ref. 121601).

species.name: Eastern rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and lakes, often forming large schools at the surface.  Temperatures in their environments range from 20 to 29 °C and pH from 5.3 to 8.5 and the water varies from clear to turbid (Ref. 7298).

species.name: Eastern red scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocks, crevices and caverns at all depths.  Occasionally found in large rock pools in the lower littoral zone.  Is nocturnally active and feeds mainly on small mobile benthic animals.  Stalks its prey and swallows it whole (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Eastern sand catlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flowing water with a sandy substrate; they do not adapt to dams and do not occur in Lake Kariba (Ref. 94654). They partly bury themselves in the sand, leaving only the head exposed, and snap at particles of food, such as minute aquatic animals (Ref. 94654).

species.name: Eastern sea garfish
species.description: Found in sheltered bays, clear coastal waters and sometimes in estuaries (Ref. 27012). Generally herbivorous. Feed mainly on seagrasses and algal filaments (Ref. 26551, 27013). Eastern sea garfish also consume a high proportion of crustaceans (Ref. 27013). A schooling fish, found generally near the surface at night and close to the sea floor over seagrass beds during the day (Ref. 6390). They are being preyed upon by mulloway (Argyrosomus hololepidotus) and tailor (Pomatomus saltatrix), as well as coastal water birds. No studies have been reported on the spawning of this species (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Eastern shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de raies. Found on soft bottoms off beaches, lower parts of estuaries and offshore (Ref. 9909).  Feeds on bottom crustaceans, mollusks, and fishes (Ref. 9909).  Males mature at 60-68 cm TL, females at 54-66 cm TL; birth size at 13-15 TL. Produces 4-18 pups after 3-5 month gestation, usually around November and December (Ref. 114953). Caught in nets (Ref. 9909).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9909).

species.name: Eastern shovelnose stingaree
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and coastal waters from close inshore near beaches to depths of at least
120 m (Ref. 76956).

species.name: Eastern smooth boxfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Eastern spiny gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs and estuaries; also offshore (Ref. 12723).  Found on rubble and sand (Ref. 12723).

species.name: Eastern striped grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore.  Omnivorous species (Ref. 7300).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern tadpole coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eastern talma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Usually in pairs.  Feed on algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 4859).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern triangular butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs. Feeds exclusively on the polyps of the tubular Acropora corals. Swims in pairs and are territorial. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eastern tubenose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a variety of slow-flowing or still waters; usually associated with dense vegetation or coarse rocks.  Spawns for the first time at 1-2 years, and usually only for 1 to 2 seasons, April-August with females spawning more than once during a season.  Males guard the eggs which are deposited in cavities; larvae and juvenile are benthic.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  It is invasive in Volga where reportedly, the spreading was due to canalization of main river and reservoirs or slow-flowing waters created by hydroelectric plants (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Eastern wirrah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Eastern yellow blindfish
species.description: A common, secretive species of inshore reefs (Ref. 34024). Lives on rocky shores, often buried in sand, mud or silt below stones or other hard substrate. Specimens in collections often had medium to coarse grained quartz sand trapped in the gill opening (a sand-bottom adaptation and might explain why it is so rarely caught together with D. hoesei, even though both species live in the same general area of south-eastern Australia Depths down to 5 m. A female specimen (AMS I.16469-016, 62 mm SL ) was found to contain two pale unpigmented embryos, 6-7 mm SL. Maximum length for female taken from Ref. 57886.

species.name: Ebeling's fangjaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, primarily at about 125-300 m depth at night and 520-700 m during the day (Ref. 35800).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35800).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Eber bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eber gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ebinania costaecanariae
species.description: Occurs on the upper slope (Ref. 11228).  Feeds on crabs, shrimps, benthic copepods and polychaetes (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Ebinania gyrinoides
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Ebinania malacocephala
species.description: Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Ebony eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ebony gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the surge zone of inshore boulder areas (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ebony snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 128 m (Ref. 50550).

species.name: Echelus pachyrhynchus
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Echinomacrurus mollis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bathypelagic to benthopelagic (Ref. 37108).

species.name: Echinomacrurus occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length given is taken from E. mollis (Ref. 557).

species.name: Echiodon atopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Echiodon coheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Echiodon neotes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare and questionably pelagic species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Echiodon pegasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Echiodon pukaki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Type specimen taken from 857-860 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Eclectochromis lobochilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eclectochromis ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ecsenius fijiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius isos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).
