species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius niue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral reefs (Ref. 50537).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius pardus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius portenoyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from the ocean side of reef crest with rock and dead coral and some live coral (Ref. 5296).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ecsenius tessera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ectodus descampsii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious; found over coarse sand bottoms.  Feeds on microorganisms, diatoms and algae (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Ectrepopterus uruguayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams and semi-lentic and lotic shallow areas (up to 1.2 m deep) with moderate submerged vegetation and riparian vegetation composed by trees and shrubs. Streams are characterized by transparent water and bottom with mud, some stretches with sand or gravel (Ref. 89798).

species.name: Ecuador banjo catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ecuador skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal species with unknown depth distribution but presumably inhabits outer continental shelf and/or upper slope (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Length of specimen (39 cm TL) was based on a young male observed to have developed state of thorn patches on pectoral fins, and presumambly approaching maturity (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Ecureuil rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surge-swept tunnels and crevices of the reef margin and reef front.  Rarely occurs below 30 m, but has been observed at depths of 101 to 183 m in the Hawaiian Islands (Ref. 1602); majority of specimens collected in less than 3 m, often in tide pools (Ref. 27370).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  It disperses at night over sand flats and open reef bottom to feed on small crustaceans, crustacean larvae, and polychaete worms.  Spine of preopercle venomous.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Edea killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Edentoliparis terraenovae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Notable for its purely pelagic mode of life (Ref. 30823).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Edgbaston goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, very shallow, clay-bottomed pools, vegetated with emergent grass tussocks. The pools are fed by artesian mound springs. Diurnal fluctuations in water temperature can be as great as 21°C. Tolerates temperatures between 3° and 39°C. Co-occurs with the Red-finned blue-eye Scaturiginichthys vermeilipinnis another endangered species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Edmondson's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Specimens have been taken from a tide pool, shallow reefs and beaches.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 9.4 cm SL.

species.name: Edmund's spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly caught by demersal longline fisheries operating in deepwater; utilized for its meat, fins and liver oil which is of high value (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Eel catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers forest streams and swamps, where it lurks among the roots of trees and may even capture its prey on land. Also found in rapids (Ref. 78218). Channallabes apus is an omnivore (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Eel cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eel pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Presumably free-living (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Eel slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Eel snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in very specific habitat, primarily in still estuaries where living seagrasses are based on decaying ones (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Eel worm goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries (Ref. 4833), shallow coastal waters and rivers (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Eelgrass blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rubble areas covered by mats of algae and sponges or in beds of finger coral.  Generally found in less than 10 m depth (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Eendracht Land silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters. Schools with A. lacunosus, A. ogilbyi, Craterocephalus mugiloides, and Hypoatherina temminckii, in the coasts of northern Australia.

species.name: Egg-mimic darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults concentrate in headwaters and creeks in quiet to gently flowing pools (Ref. 33867).

species.name: Eggcarrying buntingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The eggs are carried between the pelvic fins with each egg attached to the body by 10-20 filaments (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Egglestone's bumblebee goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Egglestonichthys melanoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Egglestonichthys patriciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Egglestonichthys rubidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from mud-bottom habitat (Ref. 123361).

species.name: Egglestonichthys ulbubunitj
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected by a 2-meter beam trawl or small dredge over (and occasionally
in) very soft to firm mud (sometimes with broken shell and plant detritus such as drifts of leaves), at depths of 1-16 m. Water quality varied with the tide, from 25.8-28.4°C and 28.0-30.3 ppt‰ salinity. Reported to co-occur with estuarine fishes such as small polynemids, juvenile sciaenids,
engraulids and cynoglossids in this soft-substrate habitat (Ref. 95099).

species.name: Eggleston’s lightning goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ego zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a drop-off with small caves and ledges.  Occur in groups of 10 to at least 20, hovering in the water column near small holes and crevices where they could retreat into in case of danger.  May be feeding on zooplankton with short darting movements.

species.name: Egorgé petit-oeil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope and abyssal plain.  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans, and squid (Ref. 31334).

species.name: Egorgé à oeil bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Egyptian mouth-brooder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and ponds (Ref. 4967).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects (Ref. 7020), algae, vegetable fragments and small fish (Ref. 28714). Ovophilic, agamous maternal mouthbrooder; no pair-bonding takes place (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Egyptian seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Egyptian sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to be preyed upon by the groupers Cephalopholis hemistiktos and C. miniata in the Red Sea (Ref. 107896).

species.name: Eichler’s Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rubble habitats in low rocky outcrops or with low coral heads.  Also photographed at 5 m  depth in an open area with sand and some isolated corals and rocks (Ref. 89094). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Eidinemacheilus proudlovei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from an ephemeral spring close to the village of Kanishok (Ref. 115525).

species.name: Eigenmann's toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia besouro
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia goajira
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia humboldtii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia limbata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia meeki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia trilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eigenmannia vicentespelaea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave-restricted species (Ref. 27299).

species.name: Eight-lined wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits among rubble or live corals of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602), usually in caves and crevices with rich invertebrate growth to at least 40 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans, but also takes small mollusks, echinoids (sea urchins) (Ref. 1602), fish eggs, and crab larvae (Ref. 37816).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Eightband butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swim in pairs in coral rich areas of sheltered lagoon and inshore reefs; juveniles seen in groups among Acropora corals. Feed exclusively on coral polyps. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eightbar reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Eightbarbel gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Eightbarbel loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Eightspine cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Secretive among boulders or under debris (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal species. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Eightspot dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 42832).  Feeds on crustaceans, worms, and snails (Ref. 42832).  Utilized as fish meal; sometimes marketed fresh (Ref. 42832).

species.name: Eilat sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from 42-50 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Eirmotus furvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is the only member of the genus Eirmotus which occurs in the black waters of peat swamp forest. Encountered only in deep inside the forested area in a less disturbed portion (Ref. 78741).

species.name: Eirmotus insignis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in small streams with slow flowing water, backwaters, among overhanging roots along shores, and occasionally in swampy areas among dense vegetation (Ref. 78741).  Generally inhabits quite murky and slightly acidic water, with bottom usually muddy or covered with leaf litter (Ref. 78741).

species.name: Eirmotus isthmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and large permanent water bodies in the floodplain. Caught in water column together with Hyalobagrus flavus (Bagridae), Pseudeutropius brachypopterus, P. moolenburghae (Schilbeidae) and Gymnochanda filamentosa (Ambassidae) (Ref. 78741).

species.name: Eirmotus octozona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ejagham killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ekemblemaria lira
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eknomoliparis chirichignoae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: El Dorado anchovy
species.description: This species is bundantly caught by trawl and marketed fresh in northern Vietnam and caught by set net as bycatch in south-western Taiwan (Ref. 130210).

species.name: Elachocharax geryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elachocharax junki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elachocharax mitopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elachocharax pulcher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elassodiscus obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elassodiscus tremebundus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elat electric ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on outer continental shelf. Presumably feeds on soft bottom invertebrates such as polychaetes and crustaceans. Males reaches maturity at ca. 15 cm TL. Material rare; specimens from Gulf of Aden and Red Sea slightly differ (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Electric Blue Hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits several habitats where rocks are found; usually found in caves and cracks of the biotope; feeds on small fishes, mainly small mbuna that live among the rocks (Ref. 5595).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Electric blue kande
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas (Ref. 40899).  Feeds on small cichlids, possibly small invertebrates as well (Ref. 40899).  Breeding males protect an area of about 2 meters in diameter with a nest located at its center (Ref. 40899).

species.name: Electric shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits relatively steep outer reef slope with fish occupying burrows on black volcanic sand/ rubble substrates. About 20 individuals were observed in an area that occupied about 600 sq.m. Solitary individuals encountered were invariably associated with an unidentified snapping shrimp of the genus Alpheus that share the burrows, a symbiotic relationship found in all Vanderhorstia species (Ref. 122681).

species.name: Electrophorus varii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Electrophorus voltai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elegant coris
species.description: Common in shallow sand and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on bivalves, gastropods, crabs, sea urchins, heart urchins, hermit crabs, shrimps, polychaetes, amphipods, isopods, chitons and foraminiferans (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Elegant killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks, swamps parts of small streams, swamps, pools and border regions of lakes;  5 cm TL (Ref. 3788, 47461). Not a seasonal killifish; difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Elegant madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of clear creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Elegant molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift headwater streams.

species.name: Elegant pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elegant pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef areas and tide pools.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Elegant wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are primarily found in lagoons (Ref. 9710).  Also in coastal reef areas.  Feed on a variety of invertebrates.  Females in groups of up to 80 or more, males territorial (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eleotris andamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris annobonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris balia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris bosetoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy to clear rivers with sandy to gravel bottom between 5 and 15 m in altitude. A carnivorous species that feeds on crustaceans and fishes, as seen with X-ray and stomach contents (M.I.M.). Sympatric with E. fusca and E. acanthopoma (Ref. 118063).

species.name: Eleotris brachyurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris daganensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish environments and freshwaters of coastal rivers (Ref. 57413). Maximum reported standard length 97 mm (Ref. 81660).

species.name: Eleotris diamsoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris douniasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris décoré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often occurs on deep outer coastal to outer reef drops-offs subject to moderate to strong currents (Refs. 48637, 95112). Found over hard, open bottoms at the bases of reefs and over sand and rubble patches (Refs. 1602, 95112). Often in pairs (Refs. 1602, 95112).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Feeds on zooplankton, especially copepods and crustacean larvae.  Darts into a hole when alarmed (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Eleotris fasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris klunzingerii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris macrocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit brackish estuaries and medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 2847, 12975, 48637, 44894); also in submerged bank vegetation of freshwater streams (Ref. 41184), marshes and rice fields (Ref. 54520). Usually found on mud bottoms (Ref. 44894); sometimes penetrating into freshwaters (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Eleotris oxycephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris pellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is supposed to be mainly amphidromous (Ref. 123271). Maximum size up to 64 mm standard length (Ref. 123271). Epibenthic in fresh and brackish waters (Ref. 6802); it lives in the lower part of rivers, in muddy to clear rivers with sandy to gravel bottom between 5 to 10 m in altitude (Ref. 123271). It is carnivorous (Ref. 123271).

species.name: Eleotris sahanaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris senegalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in freshwaters and brackish environments along the coast (Ref. 6802). Maximum reported standard length 165 mm (Ref. 81660).

species.name: Eleotris soaresi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris sumatraensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris taché d'orange
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas of clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Occurs in pairs and use burrows as refuge.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  The burrow is shallow, only a few cm, and made under large pieces of rubble.  May be found on dark volcanic sand such as those in the Philippines, Indonesia, and the northern Mariana Is.  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Eleotris tecta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and creeks of little to high current velocity between the sea and 75 m elevation.  Carnivorous (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Eleotris tubularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris valadei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is supposed to be amphidromous (Ref. 123271). It is found in the lower part of the river, near the estuary; it lives in muddy to clear rivers with sandy to gravel bottom between 0 to 5 meters in altitude (Ref. 123271). It is carnivorous (Ref. 123271).

species.name: Eleotris vittata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal rivers, lagoons, creeks, estuaries (Ref. 6802, 57413, 81660) and mangrove areas (Ref. 6802, 57413). Maximum reported total length 265 mm (Ref. 6802).

species.name: Eleotris vomerodentata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris woworae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eleotris à bande noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rubble or sandy areas of seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Burrows occasionally.

species.name: Eleotris épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit brackish estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams, usually on mud bottoms (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Elephant ear gourami
species.description: Occurs in pools of large rivers and in flooded forests during the rainy season.  Feeds mainly on plant matter including fruits, leaves, and flowers, with some insects and crustaceans.  Known to reproduce in non-flowing waters near the river shore during lowest water levels (Ref. 12693).  Undertakes lateral migrations from the Mekong mainstream into floodplain areas during the flood season and returns to the Mekong River or other permanent water bodies during the dry season (Ref. 37770).  These movements are triggered when water levels change (Ref. 37770).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Elephant Fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies floodplain pools in Sudd. Feeds on mud, vegetable debris and small invertebrates (Ref. 28714). Affinities: only to P. adspersus, morphologically similar; distinguished through scales on caudal peduncle, dorsal and anal fin rays and body coloration. Generates electric organ discharge (EOD) of short duration (0.08 ms) that seems to correlate with aggregative behavior of the species (Ref. 10460; 10601). During the breeding season, males build nests and while patrolling their territory sporadically emit EODs at a mean rate of 18 Hz. Participating females, on the other hand, discharge at a fairly regular rate (8-11 Hz) and this has been shown to play a role in sex recognition during courtship and spawning. Male and female EOD waveforms also differ in the amplitude ratio of the first and third phase (Ref. 10764). Also produce natural sounds ('grunts', 'moans', 'growl', etc.) at different phases of courtship, nesting and territorial defense (Ref. 10832). A fractional spawner; females able to spawn up to 26 times in the course of one reproductive cycle, laying about 125 eggs per spawning episode. Larval electric organ situated in the deep lateral musculature; that of adults in the caudal peduncle (Ref. 10605).

species.name: Elephant snout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head and on the ventral and dorsal regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located  (Ref. 10011).  A fractional spawner (Ref. 10605; 10606).

species.name: Elephant-snout fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary, nocturnal species (Ref. 28714). In Lake Victoria in both coastal and offshore waters (Ref. 4903). May spawn in the main lake, perhaps in deep water over rocks (Ref. 52083). In Lake Kyoga in open water rather than weedy areas (Ref. 55624). Bottom feeder; small fishes eat lithophilic insects; adults almost exclusively insectivorous; chironomids dominate in the diet (Ref. 12526). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Elizabeth reef jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs inshore; inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Elizabeth springs goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits marshy, vegetated shallow pools (1-10 centimeters in depth) fed by mound springs.  Captive breeding populations have been established to ensure its survival (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Ellipse spot toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elliptical sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles were collected from a tide pools at low tide (Ref. 106074).

species.name: Ellopostoma megalomycter
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits bottom of swift-flowing water.  Feed on small invertebrates, algae and detritus from the bottom.

species.name: Elokhin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. inhabits stony bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Elongate blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elongate bulleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens trawled over presumably relatively open bottom.

species.name: Elongate bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling near rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Elongate coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446).

species.name: Elongate dory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elongate dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and seaward reefs in 5-60 m, solitary in caves or around rock outcrops (Ref 90102).

species.name: Elongate flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Elongate glass-perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in standing and running waters; clear streams, canals, beels, ponds, and inundated paddy fields.  Abundant during rainy season (Ref. 1479).  This species could effectively be used in the control of guinea worms and also for malarial control.  These small, bony, fleshy fishes are sold in heaps along with other small fishes in the market.  Popular for aquarium purposes (Ref. 44325).

species.name: Elongate glassfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater streams that frequently have moderate to high turbidity levels (Ref. 5259).  Found among vegetation at the margin of creeks and rivers (Ref. 44894).  Not much information on natural history, however, Ref. 7276 reports that it is a carnivore (confirmed by Ref. 6398) and Ref. 2906 reports that it breeds in small ponds or aquaria.

species.name: Elongate goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on shallow sandy bottoms (Ref. 123711).

species.name: Elongate hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  A schooling species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Elongate hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elongate mbuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallow rocky biotope in sediment-free areas.  Common around small rocks (Ref. 5595). It feeds by combing loose algae from the biocover (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Elongate nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and temporary pools in the floodplains (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2-4 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Elongate paedomorphic goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by a light trap in a shallow fringing reef lagoon at night (Ref. 116152).

species.name: Elongate sand klipfish
species.description: Found in sandy areas, from the intertidal down to 10 m depth (Ref. 42968).

species.name: Elongate siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal, silty habitat on reefs amongst branching corals or with long-spined urchins, in depths to at least 15 m (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Elongate smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 51327.

species.name: Elongate tigerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms shoals; an open water predator often found near the water surface; feeds on fishes, preferring long bodied fish as they are easier to swallow and also takes insects, grass and snails; cannibalistic; preyed upon by fish eagle Haliaeetus vocifer; breeding migrations have been reported up several tributaries of Lake Kariba during the rains (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Elongate toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms large schools among mangroves in estuaries and brackish river mouths; also abundant in salt pans (Ref. 11482).  Often in turbid, shallow surface waters.  Ingests ooze and detritus (Ref. 36880).  A truly viviparous fish (Ref. 45952).

species.name: Elongate unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal to outer reef slopes subject to strong currents. Sometimes in large schools (Ref. 48637).  Generally uncommon species found in steep outer reef drop-offs (Ref. 9710).  Usually found in waters deeper than 6 m. Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 90102). Solitary or in groups (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Elongated Kerala Mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Elongated Turkana robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fringing vegetation of rivers and lakes, feeding on zooplankton, beetles and other insects (Ref. 28714). Often reported in West Africa under name of M. acutidens. Affinities: most similar to M. acutidens, from which it differs in the presence of conical, monocuspid (vs multicuspid) inner dentary teeth, inner premaxillary and outer dentary with fewer cusps, and a slightly more slender body (Ref. 80290).

species.name: Elongated whiptail catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in watercourses with slow to medium flow, clear to brown water, sandy or muddy bottom (Ref. 75788).

species.name: Eltanin handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This deepwater handfish is known only from the mid continental shelf, and possibly the upper continental slope, off Tasmania (Ref. 82446).

species.name: elusive cardinalfish
species.description: Found on deep rocky or coral reef areas (Ref. 125387).

species.name: Elusive signal blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty mollusk tubes on sand-rubble bottoms.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Eléotris cyprin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors shallow vegetated margins of freshwater streams entering estuaries.  Feeds on mosquito and other insect larvae.  Threatened by coastal development and destruction of habitat through farming, industrial and urban activities (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Eléotris serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in fresh water, estuaries and inshore (Ref. 86252).  Found in a variety of habitats including rivers, swamps, coastal streams and floodplains over mud bottoms, often among dense aquatic vegetation or the cover of undercut banks. They feed mainly on aquatic insects and nymphs, but also takes lesser amount of algae, other aquatic plants and small crustaceans. Pelagic larval stage is found in marine water, but adults are always found in freshwater (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Emanuela’s boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ember tetra
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Emblem goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand or mud broken-shell bottoms of beach areas (Ref. 11482, 91780).

species.name: Emblemaria australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rubble and sand bottoms (Ref. 47837).

species.name: Emblemaria hudsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Emblemaria vitta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Emerald catfish
species.description: Inhabits sluggish waters with dense vegetation.  Occurs in shallow muddy waters.  Feeds on insect larvae, worms and small crustaceans (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Emerald clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spend the entire cycle in beds of turtle grass, Thalassia (Ref. 51567) usually attached to the underside of the blades of the seagrass (Ref. 7251). Feed on small crustaceans: Isopoda, Amphipoda, Harpacticoida, and Ostracoda (Ref. 5521). Multiple spawner (Ref. 51567).

species.name: Emerald coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found exclusively among branches of Seriatopora hystrix coral (Ref. 2334); usually in pairs. Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Emerald darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, sometimes riffles, of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds primarily on midge larvae and pupae, also eats caddisfly and mayfly immatures and microcrustaceans (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Emerald dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, often including  tide pools of exposed seaward reefs (Ref. 37816, 116739), usually in high-tide splash zones and at shallow depths (Ref. 107299).

species.name: Emerald goby
species.description: Adults inhabit shallow, muddy bottoms of the continental shelf, often in turbid waters.  Usually found among algae. A euryhaline species (Ref. 13628), with salinity ranging from 0.0 to 42.9 ppt (Ref. 97140).  Also Ref. 7251.

species.name: Emerald green tetra
species.description: Collection areas are impoundments of tributaries of the rio Mutum formed by the road building, where the water is transparent, with maximum widths ranging 50-60 m and depth 0.3-2 m. The substrate is formed by sand, silt, and organic matter, with the presence of submerged aquatic macrophytes and large amounts of filamentous algae. The only other species collected syntopically was Hoplerythrinus unitaeniatus (Spix & Agassiz, 1829), which is probably a predator of the H. comodoro. The streams that form the lagoons are small, 2-4 m wide and 0.5-2 m deep, with clear rapid waters and a bottom composed of sand and leaf litter. Local vegetation is composed of secondary forest. The other known locality lies at the rio Mutum itself, downstream to the other two and here the new species occurs syntopically with Hyphessobrycon hexastichos and Hasemania nambiquara. The diet was mainly composed of resources autochthonous (91.6% of the volume of food items), mainly vegetable fragments (57.7%) and aquatic insects (32.7%). The vegetable fragments were composed of aquatic macrophyte structures and the aquatic insects were fragments of adults, larvae, and pupae of Diptera and larvae of Trichoptera, and Odonata). Specimens analyzed were collected in a region under moderate anthropogenic pressure, which may influence the diet of fish species. Further, damming streams to road building changes the taxonomic and functional of fish assemblages and limits the longitudinal dispersion. The transformation from lotic to lentic environments, with an increase in the width of the canopy-opening channel, creates pelagic and benthic areas that allow the proliferation of macrophytes and algae. Biological data taken from regions impacted by human action has high scientific value, but in the case of this species, it is crucial that the data also be available from less impacted environments (Ref. 128640).

species.name: Emerald sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy to marl bottoms in full-salinity coastal waters and mangrove areas.

species.name: Emery's gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Emery's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Emily’s shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection area is exposed to periodic strong currents and cool upwelled water with sea temperatures of 23-25°C at the time of collection in August 2019 . The specimens were observed on gradually sloping, sand-rubble bottoms, in pairs or solitary, in shared burrows with the brightly colored alpheid shrimp Alpheus randalli (Ref. 121269).

species.name: Emissole blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore bottom-dwelling shark found on the continental shelves.  Feeds primarily on shrimps and probably other crustaceans.  Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with 4 young in a litter.  Size at birth, 21 to 23 cm.

species.name: Emissole brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on the continental shelves from the intertidal region to at least 200 m depth.  They  feed on crabs, ghost shrimps, mantis shrimps, isopods, squids, polychaete worms, tunicates and small bony fishes.  Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with 3 to 5 young in a litter.  Size at birth between 19 and 21 cm.  Readily kept in captivity.  Utilized for human consumption.  Marketed fresh, smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Emissole d'Arabie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 244).  Sometimes seen on coral reefs (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small bottom fishes, mollusks, and crustaceans (Ref. 244). In the Gulf of Aqaba on cephalopods, decapods and terrestrial food items while off Al-Ghardaqar near the entrance of the Gulf of Suez,  prawns, small crabs and small fish were found in the specimens (Ref. 124465).  Viviparous (Ref. 244).  Caught by shore anglers (Ref. 5578).  Readily lives in captivity (Ref. 244).  Utilized as a foodfish (Ref. 244).

species.name: Emissole etoilée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intertidal zone, on mud and sand bottom, down to a depth of at least 360 m (Ref. 13563).  May also be found in semi-enclosed sea areas (Ref. 11230).  Feeds mainly on bottom invertebrates, also bony fishes (Ref. 244).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught regularly by demersal longliners operating both inshore and in deep-water (Ref.58048). Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 244).

species.name: Emissole fine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore and offshore shark found on the continental and insular shelves (Ref. 244).  Ovoviviparous, with 7 young in a litter.  Size at birth about 30 cm.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole gatuso
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Feeds on crabs and probably other crustaceans, and presumably small fishes.  Ovoviviparous (aplacental) with 2 to 7 pups per litter.  Size at birth 26 cm.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole gommée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore and offshore shark found from intertidal waters (Ref. 13563) to a depth of 350 m.  Feeds on crustaceans, marine worms and small fishes (Ref. 13563), also cephalopods.  Forms schools by sex and size .  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Newborn and juvenile gummy sharks are found in many areas across southern Australia, but no well-defined nursery areas have been identified.  These sharks  are capable of long migrations, females traveling longer distances than males (Ref. 6390).  Utilized fresh for human consumption (Ref. 6871).  Maximum length data for female species is taken from Ref. 6390.

species.name: Emissole grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore and offshore shark found on the continental shelves, and entering shallow muddy bays. Feeds mostly on crabs, including cancrids and grapsids, ghost shrimp, innkeeper (echiuroid) worms (Urechis), and small fish (herring and midshipmen, Porichthys). Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with 2 to 5 young in a litter. Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole grivelée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the insular shelves, often close inshore (Ref. 244).  Feeds on crustaceans, especially crabs (Ref. 244).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Makes seasonal inshore-offshore movements (Ref. 244).  Makes extensive coastal migrations, with one tagged female moving at least 1160 km (Ref. 54100).  Forms schools separated by size and sex (Ref. 244).  Utilized fresh for human consumption (Ref. 244).

species.name: Emissole mamon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves, close inshore to well offshore.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole moustachue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, commonly on rock bottom, seaweed and kelp beds.  Feeds on octopi, squid, bony fishes and lobsters.  Peanut worms and seagrass are also included in their diet (Ref. 6390).  Ovoviviparous, with 5-24 in a litter (Ref. 6871).  Young are 20-25 cm long at birth (Ref. 13840, 244).  Marketed fresh for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole palombe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and upper slope from the intertidal region to deeper waters over sand and gravel bottoms (Ref. 244).  Feeds on crustaceans, octopi, bony fish, and fish offal (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Catch usually discarded but may be utilized in a local fishery that processes sharks into jerky (Ref. 244).

species.name: Emissole piruche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An offshore bottom-dwelling shark found on the continental shelf.  Prefers rocky bottom around islands.  Feeds on crabs, mantis shrimp, and small bony fishes.  Viviparous, with 5 to 10 young per litter.  Size at birth about 25 cm.

species.name: Emissole rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Newbies are found on beaches of between 1 and 5 m depth, juveniles occupy  inshore waters at between 15 and 50 m, and adults are found down to 50 and on upper slopes of up to 250 m in depth (Ref. 56500).  Presumably feeds on crustaceans and other benthic invertebrates.  Ovoviviparous, embryos feed solely on yolk (Ref. 50449).  Size at birth at or below about 39 cm.  Utilized fresh-frozen and dried salted for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole tiyeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf on muddy, sandy and calcareous bottoms.  Also occurs in shallow brackish water.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and occasionally on bony fishes, squids, and coelenterates.  Viviparous (with yolk-sac placenta), with 1 to 7 young per litter.  Catches consisting of mainly adults of one sex suggest at least partial sexual segregation.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Emissole veuve
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves, on muddy or sandy bottoms to about 80 m depth.  Feeds on crabs and shrimps, and also bony fishes.  Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with 7 to 14 young in a litter.  Size at birth 30 cm.

species.name: Emma's basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimen was caught in the same haul with the following species : Roa jayakari, Heniochus acuminatus, Pristigenys refulgens, Wattsia mossambica as well as several other reef-associated fish species (Ref. 118516).

species.name: Emma's short-tail conger
species.description: Reaches maturity at ca. 22 cm TL (Ref. 123550).

species.name: Emmelichthys cyanescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Emmelichthys elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Emmelichthys marisrubri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Empereur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic and oceanic species, usually found above the thermocline. Generally inhabit cooler water than either black (Makaira indica) or blue marlin (M. mazara) (Ref. 43). Most dominant and widely distributed of all billfishes. Their abundance increases with distance from the continental shelf (Ref. 6390). Usually seen close to shore only where deep drop-offs occur (Ref. 6390). Mostly solitary, but form small schools by size during the spawning season (Ref. 9987). They are usually dispersed at considerably wide distances. Feed on fishes, crustaceans and squids. Also caught with the harpoon. The flesh is the best among billfishes for sashimi and sushi. Marketed mostly frozen, sometimes fresh (Ref. 43); also smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987). Also Ref. 9137, 9574.

species.name: Empereur (Makaira mazara)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic and oceanic species mostly confined to the waters on the warmer side of the 24°C surface isotherm and known to effect seasonal north-south migrations.  Not usually seen close to land masses or islands, unless there is a deep drop-off of the shelf.  Remain mostly within the upper 37 m.  Believed to form small-scale schools of at most 10 individuals.  Larger fish tend to swim solitarily (Ref. 43) but smaller ones form schools of about 10 individuals (Ref. 9987).  Feed on squids, tuna-like fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 9308).  Also caught with troll lines (Ref. 9308).  The flesh is of good quality and is marketed frozen and prepared as sashimi and sausages in Japan (Ref. 9308); also utilized fresh (Ref. 9987).  Also Ref. 9692.

species.name: Empereur bariadiva
species.description: Inhabits the outer edge of the continental shelf.  Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates and small fishes.  Caught mainly with bottom longlines and bottom trawls (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Empereur de Futuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift clear streams with rocky bottom; collected at an altitude of 147 m.  Observed to swim in open water and are not always on the bottom of the river.  Although feeding habits have not been studied, a few examined specimens apparently feed on aquatic insects and crustaceans (Atyidae) (ref. 75883).

species.name: Empereur gueule de vin
species.description: Solitarily inhabits sand, rubble, and weed areas near corals (Ref. 90102) in deep reefs.  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Gonads in spawning state have been observed in October.  This species is not well represented in museums due to the relatively large capture size for most specimens (Ref. 2295).  Also caught with handlines (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Empereur gueule longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, usually in schools near the bottom.  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans, polychaetes and algae (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Empereur honteux
species.description: Found over sand and rubble areas of outer reef slopes (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, fish, echinoderms and mollusks (Ref. 30573).  In New Caledonia, spawning peaks are observed in December and a fairly high percentage of gonads in advanced stages of maturity occurs between October and February  (Ref. 9775). Caught mostly by handline, trap, and trawl. Marketed mostly fresh. An excellent food fish (Ref. 114226).

species.name: Empereur hypselopterus
species.description: Occurs over coral reefs and adjacent sandy areas.  May be solitary or in small groups.  Feeds on echinoderms, mollusks, crustaceans, and small fish.  Caught mostly by handlines and traps. Marketed fresh. Also caught with handlines (Ref. 9775, 687103).

species.name: Empereur maillé
species.description: Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102).  Inhabits shallow seagrass beds, reef flats, lagoons, and sandy areas near coral reefs.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and small fish.  Also caught with beach seines and handlines and is marketed fresh (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Empereur orné
species.description: Inhabits sandy and soft bottoms and seagrass beds in inshore bays, lagoons and areas adjacent to reefs.  Usually in small groups (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms, polychaetes and small fishes.  Juveniles commonly visit the tidal reef flats to feed when the water is high (Ref. 48635). Caught by trap, handline, shore seine, trawl, and handline. Minor importance in fisheries where it occurs (Ref. 68703).

species.name: Empereur strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  May be solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102). Sometimes forms aggregations of about a hundred or more individuals.  Feeds at night on benthic invertebrates like crabs and gastropods, occasionally on small fish.  Usually marketed fresh.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Emperor cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed over sand in the vicinity of rocks, possibly for breeding purposes only.  Feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Emperor reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Emperor seamount lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Adults form dense aggregations at daytime in upper mesopelagic waters and disperses at night on the surface (Ref. 102274).

species.name: Empire gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lower reaches of rivers (also found further upstream) in flowing or still water (Ref. 44894) among aquatic vegetation or branches of submerged trees.  Juveniles often occur in swiftly flowing water or brackish estuaries.  Tolerant of salinity levels equal to sea water, temperatures up to 35°C and pH 5.0-9.1 (Ref. 44894).  Feed on micro-crustaceans, mosquito larvae and algae.  Spawning occurs during the warmer months, when males establish breeding territories and display their dazzling colours to attract a mate.  The eggs adhere to rocks, sand or weeds and are guarded and fanned by the male until hatching, which occurs in 10-14 hours (Ref. 44894).  Smallest vertebrate eggs with max 0.32 mm length.  Hatching larvae are about 1mm long.

species.name: Encheliophis chardewalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotype was found in the coelomic cavity of the holothuroid Actinopyga mauritania caught at a depth of 1 m in a lagoon (Ref. 51068).

species.name: Encheliophis sagamianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 34024) deep-water species (Ref. 559).  Holothurian commensal (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Encheloclarias baculum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Encheloclarias curtisoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a stream about 3 m wide and half a meter deep in a peat swamp forest.  The stream has a soft and peaty substrate, covered with large pieces of wood and submerged branches.

species.name: Encheloclarias kelioides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shaded blackwaters in coastal peat swamps about 20 m from the sea, among submerged shore vegetation and branches at a depth between 0.5 and 1.5 m.

species.name: Encheloclarias prolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from peat swamp forests (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Encheloclarias tapeinopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Encheloclarias velatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enchelybrotula gomoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Enchelybrotula paucidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Enchelycore nycturanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on largest immature specimen (Ref. 50539).

species.name: Enchelyurus brunneolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic in dead coral (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Enchelyurus petersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Endeavour skate
species.description: Occurs mainly on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, recorded up to 500 m. Diet mainly based on crustaceans; juveniles feed on amphipods and carid shrimps while adults feed on prawns and bony fishes (Ref. 114953).  Lengths of adolescent males unknown, but largest juvenile male was 23.4 cm TL, adult males 31.5-32.1 cm TL, with smallest juvenile 17.0 cm TL (Ref. 75648). Females mature at ca. 31 cm TL; young hatch at 10-11 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Endlers guppy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Endorheic chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Endormi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental and insular shelves, from the intertidal down to at least 70 m (Ref. 247).  Occurs on or near the bottom in lagoons or along the outer edges of coral and rocky reefs, sandy areas near reefs and off sandy beaches (Ref. 247, 43278).  Primarily nocturnal, but may be active during the day (Ref. 247).  Prefers crevices and caves on reefs but may be found hiding in more exposed areas (Ref. 247).  Forms resting aggregations, and often seen piled across or on top of one another (Ref. 247).  Feeds on a wide variety of bottom invertebrates, small fishes (Ref. 247), including cephalopods, crustaceans and sea urchins (Ref. 37816), corals (Ref. 68964).  Docile and known to allow itself to be touched, but a few non-fatal attacks have been recorded (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 43278).  4 or more young are born per litter (Ref. 37816).  Survives in captivity (Ref. 247).  Marketed fresh and dried-salted; fins dried for the oriental sharkfin trade; liver processed for vitamins and oil; offal processed for fishmeal; hide potentially valuable for leather (Ref. 247).

species.name: Endormi (Pseudoginglymostoma brevicaudatum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known inshore bottom shark of the continental and insular shelves.  Well adapted to lie amongst coral reefs due to its tough skin (Ref. 391); depth data not available (Ref. 43278).  Breeding and feeding habits are unknown.  Presumably oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Survives for many hours out of water (Ref. 391).

species.name: Englert's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Engraulicypris bredoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Engraulicypris gariepinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This shoaling fish favours open, shallow water, normally occurring in slack pools and particularly below riffles; populations found in the lower Orange and Fish Rivers are limited by the Augrabies and Fish River Falls; they are restricted to turbid waters, which provide protection from visual predators (Ref. 116496). They are thought to feed mainly on small autochthonous invertebrates, e.g. planktonic crustaceans or insects, and are caught in large numbers where they occur (Ref. 116496).

species.name: Engraulicypris howesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species appear to favour turbid, rocky, river regions where they can gather in pockets of recirculating currents (Ref. 116496). They feed on drifting invertebrate larvae and adults and plankton (Ref. 116496).

species.name: Enneacampus ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal rivers and streams (Ref. 4127, 81680), and swamps (Ref. 57226, 81680).  Seems confined to fresh water habitats and breeds in fresh water (Ref. 81680). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). Feeds (mainly) on copepods (Ref. 81680). Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Dawson (1981) reported 17-36 postlarvae in the brood pouch of males of 75.5-82.5 mm SL; a larger male (MRAC 143259: 136.4 mm SL) caught in December 1964, in a swampy area about 200 m from the coast of Bioko Island (formerly Fernando Poo), has its brood pouch filled with several hundred postlarvae (Ref. 81680).

species.name: Enneanectes smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This crypto-benthic (caves and crevices) species is commonly found from the surface to depths of at least 55 m around rock (Ref. 58184).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240). species.name: Enneapterygius senoui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in 3-6 m, but are not observed in tidal pools or deeper than 11 m.  Adults are usually found in areas with strong regular surges generated by wave swells, but not in areas with strong unidirectional currents or breaking waves. Individuals often inhabited inclined, usually near vertical, flat surfaces of large rocks, being found near the substrate.  Spawning in Hachijo-jima Island was observed early morning until 8:00 am, from the end of March to July (Ref. 78435).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.description:

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. anniae (massive head, long and wider, dorsal shorter, smaller spots); B. tiekoroi (longer head, shorter dorsal, smaller spots, colored fins); B. traorei = sympatric with B. trispilos, (3.5 scales below lateral line, shorter barbels) (Ref. 2940).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enteromius validus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is omnivorous and opportunistic (Ref. 106731). Gut contents contained disarticulated insect remains, woody debris, seeds, macerated grasses and terrestrial arthropod remains of spiders and ants (Ref. 106731). Specimens collected in June, July, and August showed no sign of maturation of ovaries or testes; most large individuals collected in March had enlarged testes or ovaries filled with numerous small, round eggs suggesting that peak breeding occurs at that time (Ref. 106731).

species.name: Enteromius vanderysti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enteromius vandewallei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enteromius walkeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: distinguished from other Barbus species by 4 spots on sides (Ref. 2940).

species.name: Enteromius walshae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small, forested streams where water levels remain low throughout most of the rainy season (Ref. 119360). It feeds principally on detritus and organic debris; guts contain detritus, sand grains, some chironomid larval head cases and other fragmented, unidentifiable insect remains (Ref. 119360).

species.name: Enteromius wellmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enteromius yardiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow shoreline habitats of the main channel of Awash River, deep stretches of side channels, stagnant water bodies of the adjacent floodplain, and in the shoreline of the lakes (Ref. 121538). A preference for structured habitats with aquatic plants, woody debris, dense river bank vegetation and fine substrate, sand and finer fractions, was noted; a pronounced difference between wet and dry season is characteristic for the area Ref. 121538). Water is usually turbid and water temperature ranged from 26.1°C to 31.9°C (Ref. 121538). Gut contents contained unidentifiable fine organic detritus and remains of planktonic crustaceans but also nematodes, remains of terrestrial arthropods, diatoms, larger plant material, seeds, and wood debris, and some non-organic material (Ref. 121538).

species.name: Enteromius yeiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Enteromius zalbiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: B. niokoloensis; B. punctitaeniatus (Ref. 2940).

species.name: Entomacrodus lemuria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomacrodus lighti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on exposed rocky coasts in the intertidal zone to 3 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomacrodus longicirrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomacrodus randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomacrodus solus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only known specimens are from a single collection from Ras Mohammed at the southern end of the Gulf of Aqaba. They were collected from a rocky shore at the north end of a mangrove channel from a depth of 0.2 m (Ref. 84157).  According to traits of the family where this species belongs, adult individuals are oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomacrodus vomerinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rock pools and sheltered areas in the intertidal (Ref. 13121).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Entomocorus benjamini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Entomocorus melaphareus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known about diet or feeding habits of this species (Ref. 57707).

species.name: Entomocorus radiosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens  were collected from a creek and in wide open environments, as river channels and bays of the upper Rio Paraguay basin in the periodically flooded areas known as the Pantanal.  Known to be a zooplanktivore which also eats insects.  Stomach contents predominantly has microcrustaceans (cladocerans, copepods and ostracods); insects (ephemeropterans, coleopterans and hemipterans); and/or small amounts of water mites, rotifers, fish scales, bryozoans, unidentified eggs, detritus, and sand (Ref. 57707).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epalzeorhynchos munense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed among boulders and rocks (Ref. 27732).  Known from midwater to bottom levels of streams and rivers.  During the flood season, it moves into inundated forests and returns to the river as water levels recede.  Feeds on phytoplankton and zooplankton.  Used to make prahoc along the Tonlé Sap, Cambodia.  Probably used in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693)

species.name: Epapterus blohmi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a variety of habitats where there is poor visibility and the water is still or slow-flowing.  Feeds on filamentous algae and other plant material during the dry season (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Epapterus dispilurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the lower part of larger rivers (Ref. 6868).  Nocturnal, plus active during dusk and dawn.  Feeds on smaller fish.

species.name: Epaulette goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eperlan arc-en-ciel
species.description: Inhabits brackish water of estuaries, lagoons, coastal shallows and bays, and fresh water in lowland and piedmont rivers (Ref. 59043).  A schooling species that inhabits lakes or inshore coastal waters (Ref. 1998).  Pelagic at the sea where it occurs at 4-8 m depth (Ref. 59043).  In the spring, it leaves the sea or the lake and ascends freshwater streams to spawn.  Some remain in fresh water throughout their lives (Ref. 1998); those that enter the sea stay within 8 to 10 km of the shore and probably do not stray far along the coast from the estuary (Ref. 28996). Spawns in rapids, in clear water, over stone-gravel bottom and at depth of 0.2-0.5 m (Ref. 59043).  Possibly found up to 425 m depth (Ref. 6793).  Young-of-the-year feed mostly on copepods and cladocerans, also rotifers, eggs and algae; adults feed on small crustaceans, fishes and shellfish, also squid, worms, and various insects (Ref. 27547).  Feeding virtually ceases during spawning (Ref. 27547).  Females grow faster, get bigger and live longer than males (Ref. 27547).  Highly esteemed as a food fish ever since white men came to North America (Ref. 27547).  Flesh is firm and tasty (Ref. 27547).

species.name: Eperlan du large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and upper slope over mud and clay bottom.  Catch data indicate a schooling habit.  Feeds mainly on bottom-living invertebrates.  Also known to feed on pelagic crustaceans like euphausiids, decapods and mysids (Ref. 27637).  A hermaphroditic species.  Marketed fresh and sometimes made into fishmeal (Ref. 6688). Young are pelagic, living near the surface, the adults are demersal, living between 50 and 1000 m depth (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Eperlan du large de l'Atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water of the continental shelf (Ref. 3166).

species.name: Ephesus goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits marshlands, lakes and lowland rivers with little current.  Is threatened due to habitat destruction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Epigonus angustifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  No length type given but assumed to be SL.

species.name: Epigonus atherinoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Inhabits tops of seamounts (Ref. 559).  Aggregations hovered over sand patches near steep, irregular cliffs (Ref. 7460).

species.name: Epigonus chilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epigonus constanciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs chiefly on the upper portion of the continental slope.  Depth range from 200-600 m (Ref. 07321, 74332) and from 351-742 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504, 74332).  A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Adults are strongly associated with the substrate (Ref. 4738).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Minimum depth range from Ref. 122680.

species.name: Epigonus glossodontus

species.name: Epigonus heracleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).

species.name: Epigonus trunovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epigonus waltersensis

species.name: Epinephelus clippertonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Insular, reed-associated species inhabiting depths to at least 30 m (Ref. 089707).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
