species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: epinochette a queue lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow still water with dense vegetation.  Feed predominantly on zooplankton, small crustaceans and benthic insects.  Spawn for the first time at 1 year of age.  Spawning takes place in April-June (Ref. 59043).  Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).

species.name: Epinochette marichaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams, tributaries, and ponds. May also have a tolerance of salinity like the other species of Pungitius. In the Garonne drainage, it has a very restrictive habitat with low elevation and short distance from the source. Monogamy observed, also nest building, but monogamy needs to be verified because ordinarily, the ninespined-sticklebacks are polygamous. It can hybridize with the two other species where they are in sympatry: with P. pungitius in the Vienne basin and P. laevis in the coastal Atlantic Basins (Ref. 125067).

species.name: Epiplatys ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epiplatys atratus
species.description: Epiplatys atratus is found in small, rather fast flowing rivers containing acid water with temperatures ranging from 24.3-30.3°C (Ref. 94049).

species.name: Epiplatys barmoiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swampy areas and small rivers on the coastal plains (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys biafranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small brooks and swamps (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys bifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, small brooks and rivulets in the savanna, weedy parts of rivers and swamps in coastal areas (Ref. 3788).  5.0 cm max SL (Ref. 7372).  Browses on algae and higher plant material, terrestrial and aquatic insects, notably culicid larvae and pupae and small beetles (Ref. 28714).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys cashneri
species.description: Found over a range of substrates (sand, gravel, bedrock, silt and clay) and most common in small headwater streams four meters or less in width; presence of woody debris, leaf litter and instream vegetation varied among sites (Ref. 123813).

species.name: Epiplatys chevalieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. E. chevalieri chevalieri occurs in small rivers, creeks and swamps in the rainforest and forested savannah, while E. chevalieri nigricans is most probably restricted to forested areas and is not expected to inhabit the adjacent savannah (Ref. 47774). Not a seasonal killifish. Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys coccinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139)

species.name: Epiplatys esekanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks between the inland plateau and coastal lowland (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys etzeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys fasciolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal rivers, brooks and swampy areas in forested savanna and under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys grahami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swamps and swampy parts of small streams in the coastal forest (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish. It is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys guineensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys hildegardae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. 10 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys huberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. 6.5 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys infrafasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epiplatys josianae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. 7 cm SL (Ref. 7372) and 8.7 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Occurs in small rivers and brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys longiventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and swampy parts of small streams in the savanna (Ref. 3788).  5 cm max SL (Ref. 7372).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys mesogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs between border vegetation in streams, brooks and small rivers under gallery forest cover (Ref. 3788, 47774).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys multifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams, small rivers and brooks under forest cover (Ref. 47774).  7 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys neumanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks and other small bodies of water under rainforest cover (Ref. 47774). Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys njalaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers and brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  6 cm max SL (Ref. 7372).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys olbrechtsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, small streams and rivers (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys phoeniceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small rivers under forest cover (Ref. 47774).  6.5 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys roloffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks, swamps and small streams (Ref. 3788).  7 cm max SL (Ref. 7372).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys ruhkopfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys sangmelinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, brooks and small streams under forest cover (Ref. 47774).  7 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys singa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small river, brooks and swamps in the coastal rainforest and forested savannah (Ref. 47774).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Maximum length presumed to be TL.

species.name: Epiplatys spilargyreius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swampy areas, small brooks and small streams and other bodies of quiet water in the savannah (Ref. 47774).  6 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Browses on algae and higher plant material, terrestrial and aquatic insects, notably culicid larvae and pupae and small beetles.  Males are smaller than females (Ref. 28714).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Epiplatys togolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Epiplatys à 6 rayons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in calm and weedy parts of rivers, lakes, swamps and brooks.  10 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and fish (Ref. 7020).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Epiros minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in springs, streams, ponds, usually in shallow, quiet water with dense vegetation (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Episemion krystallinoron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast flowing rivers of 4-5 m wide and 0.80-1 m deep; sandy bottoms and no aquatic vegetation; found amongst overhanging terrestrial vegetation (Ref. 57728).

species.name: Eptatretus aceroi
species.description: Collected from an area with clams and mussels of the families Solemyidae, Vesicomydae, Lucinidae, and Thyasiridae, along with empty tubes of vestimentiferan polychaetes of the family Siboglinidae which are typical chemosymbiotic metazoans observed at methane seep sites. Also the geological characteristics of the area, such as accretionary prisms that favor cold seep formation, suggest the tolerance of this species to this habitat. (Ref. 103732).

species.name: Eptatretus alastairi
species.description: Iteroparous (Ref. 94918).

species.name: Eptatretus ancon
species.description: Iteroparous (Ref. 94918).

species.name: Eptatretus astrolabium
species.description: The observation re the 'silty mud bottom’ were the specimen was taken, was inferred from sediment in traps retrieved.  The female holotype with several small, rounded eggs, ca. 2 mm diameter; all eggs in the mesentery, which is attached to the body wall (Ref. 85154).  Iteroparous (Ref. 94918).

species.name: Eptatretus chinensis
species.description: Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Eptatretus fudgei
species.description: From collection data, the bottom was covered by coral and sand (Ref. 128403).

species.name: Eptatretus laurahubbsae
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Eptatretus luzonicus
species.description: The holotype was collected from the type locality over green muddy bottom at bottom temperature of 6.8°C, surface water temperature 28.3°C (Anonymous, 1910).   Additional specimens from the Verde Island Passage were collected at 578 and 710 m, sediment type ranged from mud to sand (Ref. 95645).

species.name: Eptatretus menezesi
species.description: This species lives on the continental slope.  It is a scavenger caught together with dead fish.

species.name: Eptatretus multidens
species.description: Minimum depth given from Ref. 52140.

species.name: Eptatretus nelsoni
species.description: A dwarf species; males develop testes at about 20 cm and a 22.4 cm female had elongated eggs; a 26.8 cm specimen had eggs 2.4 cm long; and a 24.4 cm specimen had 11 eggs about 1.5 cm long with polar caps already forming (Ref. 51420).

species.name: Eptatretus strahani
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Equille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Territorial; found in  inshore waters, especially sandy bays and beaches, including the inter-tidal zone and estuaries; rarely offshore.  Alternate between lying buried in the sandy substrate and swimming in schools in the water mass.  Adults feed on zooplankton and some large diatoms (Ref. 3397).  They hibernate in winter buried in sand at depths of 20-50 cm (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Equulites laterofenestra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Equulites rivulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore (Ref. 11230).  Searches for prey using a protruding pipette-like mouth or by sieving potential food through their gill rakers (Ref. 26569).

species.name: Erdmann's fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at depths of 3-15 m (Ref. 87904), but at Cenderawasih Bay they may be found at about 65 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Erdmann's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species was found along the coasts of the islands, a combination of mangrove, rocky shore, and an occasional sand beach; the inshore habitat of the islands consists of low-diversity, fringing coral reef exposed to turbidity and siltation, underwater visibility often less than 3 m where the tidal current can be very strong (Ref. 85096).

species.name: Erdmann’s Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs around low coral outcrops (Ref 90102). Maximum depth from Ref. 087199.

species.name: Erdmann’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erdmann’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs, often outer slopes on isolated rock or coral outcrops in 12-66 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Erect goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal areas on sand, mud and broken-shell bottoms (Ref. 91780).

species.name: Eremo skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.6-13.2 cm long and 7.6-8.6 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).

species.name: Eremophilus mutisii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An excellent food fish which was introduced to the Ubate, Chiquinquirá and Tundama valleys.  The only species of food fish which have been able to survive competition from introduced trout and carp species into the region.

species.name: Erethistes nareshi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams (Ref. 101395).

species.name: Erethistes pusillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in hill streams (Ref. 4833).  Found in muddy parts of rivers overgrown with vegetation (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Erethistoides ascita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pebble and cobble riffles with moderate depth of about 20 cm (Ref. 55978).

species.name: Erethistoides cavatura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow (approximately 10-20 cm) gravel and pebble riffles of streams and rivers with predominantly sandy bottoms, in moderate to fast current (Ref. 55978).  Found in clear to turbid waters (Ref. 55978).

species.name: Erethistoides infuscatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a large, moderately deep, fast-flowing river with sandy/muddy bottom (Ref. 57691).

species.name: Erethistoides longispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erethistoides luteolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erethistoides montana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streamlets with swift current (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Erethistoides pipri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streamlets with swift current (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Erethistoides senkhiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected at low depth (15-35 cm) in moderately clear water as well as in turbid running water over pebbles, cobbles, concrete of variable colors and sand particles using a 3 m diameter cast net with 8 mm meshes (Ref. 79562).

species.name: Erethistoides sicula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erethistoides vesculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eretmichthys pinnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).   Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eretmobrycon bayano
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eretmobrycon festae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eretmodus marksmithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow (1-2 m deep), well-oxygenated, clear water of the surge zone; bottom composed of small stones varying from 10-40 cm in diameter; feeds on biocover which is scraped from rocks; small invertebrates (crustaceans, mites, insects, insect larvae) are eaten as well; biparental mouthbrooder (Ref. 92306).

species.name: Eretmophorus kleinenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Perhaps the early stage of a known species of Moridae, or else neotenic (Ref. 4774).

species.name: Ereunias grallator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in about 500 m depth (Ref. 559).

species.name: Ereğli minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in marshes and lakes (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Ericandersonia sagamia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erisphex philippinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erisphex pottii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters on sand or mud bottoms.  Processed into animal feeds and fertilizers (Ref. 637).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Erisphex simplex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ernstichthys anduzei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ernstichthys intonsus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ernstichthys megistus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ernstichthys taquari
species.description: Collected in a white water river, with moderate water flow, over rock and sand. Its habitat is not the deep bottom of a large river, but rather a small river accessible by hand-seining. Aquatic macrophytes were present in some sites and riparian forest was well preserved; all specimens were collected in a shaded sector covered with dense vegetation and large rocks on the bottom (Ref. 124573).

species.name: Erotelis clarki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erotelis shropshirei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erromyzon compactus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Collected during rainy season from swift flowing, turbid water over large boulders (Ref. 54043).

species.name: Erromyzon kalotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water at depths of 0.1-0.5 m among boulders and cobbles mixed with sand on the river bed. In Dishui River, other fishes found together with this species include cyprinids (Opsariichthys bidens, Acrossocheilus parallens), balitorids (Pseudogastromyzon fangi, Vanmanenia pingchowensis, Yaoshania pachychilus, Schistura fasciolata) and sisorids (Glyptothorax fokiensis, Pterocryptis anomala). In Liuding River, this species occurs together with Zacco platypus, Puntius semifasciolatus, Pseudorasbora parva, Carassius auratus, Oreonectes platycephalus, Traccatichthys pulcher, Cobitis sinensis and Tachysurus adiposalis (Ref. 93072).

species.name: Erromyzon sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erromyzon yangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erythrinus erythrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in creeks and marshy zones where it can survive in water with low oxygen levels due to some anatomical modification of its swim bladder which serves as a respiratory appendage.  It stays on the bottom as well as at the surface among floating vegetation (Ref. 27188).  Feeds on small fishes and insects (Ref. 12225).  Known among aquarists since 1910, its culture is reputedly difficult and its reproduction in captivity has not been reported to date (Ref. 27188).  Reported to reach around 25 cm SL (Ref. 81048).

species.name: Erythrinus kessleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erythrocharax altipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erythrocles acarina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erythrocles microceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Erythrocles taeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Erythrops goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on certain branching coral forms of fire coral (Millepora spp.) and on other massive corals ones (e.g. like Porites cylindrica, P. lutea) in shallow lagoons at depths of 1 to 10 m.

species.name: Escherich's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal swamps and swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Eschmeyer nexus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Escolier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at continental slopes, around oceanic islands and submarine rises (Ref. 6181).  Meso-benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Migrate to midwater at night (Ref. 6181).  Feed on fish, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 6181).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6766).

species.name: Escolier (Thyrsites atun)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit continental shelves or around islands. Feed on pelagic crustaceans (Euphausia, Nyctiphanes), cephalopods and fishes (Ref. 6181) like anchovy and pilchard (Ref. 36731). Form schools near the bottom or midwater; sometimes even at the surface at night (Ref. 6181). Prefers temperature between 13° and 18°C (Ref. 36731). Marketed fresh, smoked, canned and frozen; eaten fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988). Good for fish and chips or smoking; also made into fillet or fish cake in Japan (Ref. 6181). Commonly called as Baracoutta and because it is a fast predator, several English vessels were named after it. In the UK during WW II, this canned fish was commonly eaten that many older people have an aversion to it (D. Parkyn, pers. comm. 05/2022).

species.name: Escolier aile longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.  Found on the continental shelf and underwater sea rises (Ref. 10817).  Rather rare.

species.name: Escolier américain
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Escolier antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults and subadults epipelagic to mesopelagic, or mesobenthopelagic at shelves and slopes from surface to 830 m (temp.  0° to 4°C).  Larvae and juveniles, probably mesopelagic to bathypelagic, down to 2,830 m depth (Ref. 5084).  Feeds on krill, squid and fishes (predominantly myctophids).  Larval and juvenile specimens mostly obtained between southern land masses and the Antarctic continent.

species.name: Escolier barracuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on squid and fish.  Matures at about 25 cm.

species.name: Escolier bengalais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Matures at about 10 cm standard length.  A squid was found in the stomach of one specimen (Ref. 9784).

species.name: Escolier blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesobenthopelagic (Ref. 47377).  Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 6181).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 6181) and euphausiids (Ref. 47377).  Since 1980, no catches have been reported, except for 21 t caught in 1990 by Argentina (Ref. 6181).  Good for smoked fish and fish and chips (Ref. 6181).

species.name: Escolier bécune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are probably benthopelagic from 400 to 470 m while juveniles are pelagic from 270 to 400 m depth.

species.name: Escolier dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesobenthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Matures at about 25 cm standard length (Ref. 6181).

species.name: Escolier gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesobenthopelagic, down to depths of 400 m or more, often at the surface at night around Okinawa, Japan (Ref. 6181).  The largest populations are probably on the slope of seamounts or ridges (Ref. 6181).  Feeds on a variety of mesopelagic fish, squid and crustaceans (Ref. 6181).

species.name: Escolier long nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults, benthopelagic to mesopelagic, dwell on the continental slope or underwater rises, migrating  to midwater at night (Ref. 6181).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 6766).  Larvae and juveniles, epipelagic to mesopelagic, are rather common in oceanic ichthyoplankton and are only found in the tropics (Ref. 6181).  Feed on squid, fish and crustaceans (Ref. 6181).  Consumed as food (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Escolier maître
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, probably mesobenthopelagic.  Consumed as food (Ref. 4537).  Reported to have been taken from 200-350 m in Jamaica (J. Tame pers. Comm. 08/16).

species.name: Escolier noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly over the continental slope, down to 200 m and more (Ref. 6181).  Migrates  upward at night (Ref. 6181).  Feeds on squid, crustaceans and a wide variety of fishes (Ref. 6181).  Flesh oily and may have purgative properties (Ref. 9784).  Sometimes caught by tuna long-liners (Ref. 26938).  Marketed frozen and as fish cakes in Japan (Ref. 9302).

species.name: Escolier oriental
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 30573).  Matures at about 15 cm SL.

species.name: Escolier rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, migrating upward at night to 100 to 200 m (Ref. 6181).  Probably forming schools during daytime (Ref. 6181).  Feed on crustaceans and small fish (Ref. 6181).  Females mature at  about 16 cm (Ref. 36731).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6766).

species.name: Escolier reptile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 47377), migrating to the surface at night (Ref. 6181).  Feeds on myctophids and other small fishes, squid and crustaceans (Ref. 6181).  Matures at 15 cm SL (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Escolier royal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods (Ref. 5213, 9784).  Utilized as a food fish food (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Escolier royal (Rexea solandri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in schools on continental shelf and slope.  They are normally caught close to the sea bed but probably move into midwater at times (Ref. 28786).  Juveniles are pelagic, adults also occur near the surface off Tasmania and New Zealand.  Dense schools of pre-spawners migrate along the continental slope at about 400 m during winter (Ref. 9563).  Feed on fish, squid and crustaceans.  The flesh is of good edible quality and especially tasty when smoked.  In Australia, the eastern gemfish stock has been subjected to a prolonged period of poor recruitment which started in 1989 (Ref. 28843, 28786).  This event resulted in a very significant decline in the gemfish resource.  In Australia, efforts are now being channeled towards the recovery of the fishery.

species.name: Escolier serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Strictly oceanic and usually solitary (Ref. 6181).  Adults migrate to the surface at night while larvae and juveniles are found near the surface during the day (Ref. 6181).  Feed on fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 9302).  Males mature at 43 cm SL, females at 50 cm (Ref. 36731).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6766).  Sold frozen, as sausages or fish cake (Ref. 9302).  Not eaten raw, but cooked in any way, also dried (Ref. 7364).

species.name: Escolier tonga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably mesopelagic or mesobenthopelagic (Ref. 6181).

species.name: Escolier à longues ailes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably schooling, migrates to midwater at night. Feeds on fishes (myctophids, Maurolicus, eels, macrourids, carangids, emmelichthyids, etc.), prawn and squid; large prey items are swallowed in parts (Ref. 6202). Matures at about 25 cm standard length. No special fishery but appears as a bycatch of deep-water prawn trawl fishery in New South Wales, Australia.

species.name: Escolier élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper continental slope (Ref. 6181).  Juveniles probably pelagic (probably mesopelagic) (Ref. 6181).  Specimens 35 to 40 cm SL had ripe gonads (Ref. 6181).

species.name: Esei lake char
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Esmaeilius darabensis
species.description: Occurs in low numbers. Threatened mainly by drought and introductions of exotic species, particularly Gambusia holbrooki and Amatitlania nigrofasciata (Ref. 95579).

species.name: Esmaeilius isfahanensis
species.description: Collected from the lower reaches of the Zayanadeh River, 50 m width and 0.5 m depth, where water temperature is 27°C, pH 6.7, brackish water, conductivity 10.9 mS, dissolved solids 5450 ppm, dissolved oxygen 12.3 mg/L; current is slow and no cover (Ref. 57741).

species.name: Esmaeilius sophiae
species.description: Mainly herbivorous (Ref. 13530).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Esomus ahli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pools and ditches.

species.name: Esomus altus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Esomus caudiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Esomus malabaricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Esomus manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams in plains.

species.name: Esomus metallicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and swamps (Ref. 57235).  Usually associated with standing or slow-flowing, shallow waters (Ref. 27732).  Abundant in flooded rice-paddies, canals and ditches.  Avoids large rivers and only moves from temporarily inundated habitats if necessitated by seasonal habitat disappearance .  Moves into seasonally inundated areas as soon as they are flooded.  Feeds on zooplankton, terrestrial insects and aquatic insect larvae.  Occasionally sold fresh and used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693, 57235).

species.name: Esomus thermoicos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds and ditches and can tolerate very muddy water during droughts (Ref. 4832).  More common in muddy pools than in flowing water.  Feeds on insect larvae, small worms and crustaceans.  Spawns semi-adhesive eggs usually on floating or marginal vegetation.

species.name: Esox cisalpinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Espadon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in the upper layers of warm water above the thermocline, but also capable of descending to rather deep water.  Often migrate into near-shore waters.  Occasionally form schools or smaller groups of 3 to 30 individuals, but often occur in loose aggregations over a wide area.  Feed mainly on small pelagic fishes but also takes bottom-dwelling organisms.  Females grow larger (Ref. 4770).  Utilized fresh, canned and frozen; eaten steamed (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Espadon (Kajikia albida)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually above the thermocline.  Its distribution varies seasonally, reaching higher latitudes in both the northern and southern hemispheres only during the respective warm seasons.  Usually found in deep (over 100 m) blue water with surface temperatures over 22°C and salinities of 35 to 37  ppt.  Currents of 0.5 to 2 knots occur over much of its habitat.  Feeds on fishes and squids.  Females grow larger (Ref. 4770).  Flesh is of excellent quality.  Marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Espadon (Makaira nigricans)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic species.  Water color affects its occurrence, at least in the northern Gulf of Mexico, where the fish show preference for blue water.  Rarely gathers in schools and usually found as scattered single individuals.  Feeds mainly on fishes but also preys on octopods and squids.  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 43).  Feeding takes place during daytime.  Maturity reached at about 80 cm in males and 50 cm in females (Ref. 36731).  Females grow larger (Ref. 4770). Recent study indicates maximum age close to 20 years using a series of deductions in the ¹⁴C dating method (Ref. 120707).

species.name: Espadon (Xiphias gladius)
species.description: Oceanic but sometimes found in coastal waters (Ref. 9354).  Generally above the thermocline  (Ref. 9354), preferring temperatures of 18°C to 22°C (Ref. 9987).  Larvae are frequently encountered at temperatures above 24 °C (Ref. 9702).  Migrate toward temperate or cold waters in the summer and back to warm waters in the fall.  Adults are opportunistic feeders, known to forage for their food from the surface to the bottom over a wide depth range (Ref. 9702).  Feed mainly on fishes (Atlantic mackerel, barracudinas, silver hake, redfish, herring and lanternfishes (Ref. 5951); also on crustaceans and squids (Ref. 9354).  They use their sword to kill their prey (Ref. 9354).  Large individuals may accumulate large percentages of mercury in its flesh (Ref. 9354).  Are batch spawners (Ref. 51846).  Spawning takes place in Atlantic during spring in southern Sargasso Sea.  Migrate to cooler waters to feed (Ref. 4689).  Females grow fastest.  Determination of age is difficult since the otoliths are very small and scales are missing in adults.  Year rings have been successfully counted on cross sections of the fin rays (Ref. 35388).  Pelagic eggs measure 1.6-1.8mm and the newly hatched larvae is 4 mm long.  Sword is well developed at a length of 10mm and young live pelagically in the upper water layers where they quickly develop into very voracious predators (Ref. 35388).  Mt DNA restriction analysis reveal that genetic differentiation occurs between populations inhabiting the Mediterranean Sea and the tropical Atlantic ocean, indicating little genetic exchange occurring between the two (Ref. 12784).  Good food fish, marketed fresh or frozen, and can be made into sashimi, teriyaki or fillets (Ref. 9354).

species.name: Estrella goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Water temperature of collection sites Estrella Falls was cool even during the hottest dry season (water temperature was 26.5°C, 13 May, 2016), while water in the Malatgao River was warmer (estimated to be nearly 30°C) (Ref. 125663).

species.name: Estuarine glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams, usually within about 10 km of the sea.  Found in coastal areas (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Estuarine hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly carnivorous.  Frequently caught in estuaries and enclosed coastal lakes.  Preyed on by larger, juvenile of commercial species occurring in estuarine nursery habitats.

species.name: Estuarine perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Estuarine sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large to medium-sized rivers, lagoons and small drainages.  Typically inhabits freshwaters, but may also occur in marine waters (Ref. 75004).

species.name: Estuarine stonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs and estuaries (Ref. 9710).  Makes a shallow depression by scooping up sand or mud with its pectoral fins until it is piled up around the sides of its body.  Lies motionless on sandy bottom areas.  Comes out at night and often moves on top of reefs (Ref. 48635).  In Guinness Book of Records as most venomous fish (Ref. 6472). Solitary in coral rubble and rocks, extremely difficult to detect (Ref 90102).

species.name: Estuarine thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed marine, pelagic, coastal, but also estuarine, thus tolerating lowered salinities.  More data needed.

species.name: Estuarine triplefin
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in estuaries and lower reaches of rivers and streams (Ref. 13227) where
there is cover from rocks and submerged trees (Ref. 84085).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Estuary cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mangrove-lined shores and estuaries.

species.name: Estuary clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from shallow bay (0-29 m) and estuarine areas along the coast of New Zealand. Usually it is asscoiated with mixed shell-bryozoan rubble benthic communities. Some speciments have also been collected in association with Zostra and mangroves. At the type locality, it is found predominantly in association with spent shells of bivalves over a substrate of fine sand and silt at depths below the low tide mark (0-3 m) (Ref. 116173).

species.name: Estuary croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Estuary filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy substrates in estuaries and usually found near algae rubble reef (Ref. 48637). Also found in sand bottoms of trawling grounds in 10-50 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Estuary glassfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish mangrove estuaries, tidal creeks and lower reaches of freshwater streams.  Aggregations are common among mangrove roots, log snags and aquatic vegetation (Ref. 44894).  Occurs in lotic and lentic freshwater as well as in mangrove areas (Ref. 7300), forming schools (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Estuary goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and brackish mangrove creeks.  Also recorded from rivers (Ref. 45915).

species.name: Estuary perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An estuary-dependent catadromous fish inhabiting the tidal reaches of rivers, lakes and coastal lagoons where it is found (Ref. 7300, 123463); with salinities less than 1-2 ppt (Ref. 5259). Popular angling species that tends to swim near the bottom in deeper water.  Feeds on small fishes, molluscs, worms, shrimps and other crustaceans.  During winter (July and August) they move to the mouth of estuaries to breed (Ref. 44894).  Individuals are long lived, reaching to more than 40 years (Ref. 123463). Oviparous, egg is pelagic (Ref. 5259) and hatches in 2-3 days.  Male reaches maturity at a length of about 22 centimeters; female at about 28 centimeters (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Estuary sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Estuary sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and the lower sections of freshwater streams, usually within 1-2 km of the sea (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Estuary stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Estuary stingray
species.description: Found in mangrove swamps and estuaries (Ref. 9840).  Feeds on shellfish (Ref. 6871), worms, crabs and other crustaceans (Ref. 114953).  Size could possibly reach 160 cm DW (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Maturity size ca. 41 cm WD (males) and 63 cm WD (females); hatch size ca. 11 cm WD (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Esturgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the sea close to shores and estuaries and in deep stretches of large rivers over muddy substrate. Are usually solitary.  Juveniles live in shallow riverine habitats (Ref. 59043). Feed on mollusks, amphipods and chironomid larvae.  Spawning takes place in strong-current habitats in main course of large and deep rivers on stone or gravel bottom (Ref. 59043) from end of April to June (end of May in Rioni River, Black Sea) (Ref. 3193).

species.name: Esturgeon blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spends most of its time in the sea, usually close to shore (Ref. 27547).  Enters estuaries of large rivers and moves far inland to spawn (Ref. 5723).  Individuals larger than 48.3 cm feed mainly on fishes; smaller ones feed mainly on chironomids, but also takes small crustaceans, other insects and mollusks (Ref. 1998).  Feeding ceases just before spawning (Ref. 1998).  Excellent food fish that is sold fresh, smoked or frozen (Ref. 9988).  Eggs marketed as caviar (Ref. 1998).  In the past, the airbladder was made into isinglass (Ref. 27547).

species.name: Esturgeon de l'Adriatique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the sea close to shore and estuaries, not entering pure marine waters.  In freshwater, it inhabits large deep rivers (Ref.  59043).  A long-lived species which is found mainly over sand and mud.  Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates and small fishes.  Reproduction takes place from May to July.  Is threatened by habitat destruction, pollution and overfishing (Ref. 26100).  The flesh is used for food (Ref. 6866) and eggs used for caviar production (Ref. 128183).

species.name: Esturgeon de Sibérie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep and shallow parts of rivers, with moderate to swift current usually at depths of 1 to 8 m (Ref. 57765).  Adults live essentially in freshwater although some fish frequently occur in estuaries.  Males are sexually mature between 9 and 29 years; females between 9 and 34 years (Ref. 57765).  Spawn in main river channel over stone-gravel or gravel-sand bottom and with strong current (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Esturgeon de Sibérie (Acipenser ruthenus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A fluvial fish which inhabits rivers and their tributaries (Ref. 9696).  Occurs in large rivers, usually in the current and in deep water.  Moves to flooded areas to feed (Ref.  59043).  Chiefly potamodromous (Ref. 58897).  Like other sturgeons, it aggregates in bottom holes in winter and exhibits little activity.  In spring, when ice breaks, it rises from the bottom holes and moves upstream for spawning (Ref. 593).  Spawns in habitats with strong-current on gravel, rarely on gravel-sand bottom or in flooded sites.  Juveniles stay in riverine habitats during their first summer.  Classified as endangered species.  Anadromous populations are now extirpated; local populations are still surviving in most parts of range (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Esturgeon du Danube
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anadromous and freshwater populations exist.  At the sea, it occurs in shallow coastal and estuarine zones.  In freshwaters, it inhabits deep parts of large rivers with moderate to swift current (Ref. 59043).  Found mainly near the shore over sand and mud.  Usually solitary, but swarms when hibernating or during spawning migrations.  Occasionally forms schools (Ref. 3241).  Feeds on benthic molluscs, crustaceans and small fishes.  Spawns on stone or gravel bottom in large and deep rivers with strong current, 1-1.5 m/s (Ref. 59043).  Mainly propagated through artificial reproduction.

species.name: Esturgeon du Yang Tsé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Esturgeon noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anadromous species. Occurs solitarily or in small groups; inhabits shallow waters of continental shelves. At the sea, it occurs in coastal and estuarine areas on soft bottom (Ref. 59043) down to a depth of 50 m (Ref. 89115). Adults are highly migratory while at sea (Ref. 57533) and make long migrations along the coast (Ref. 59043). Feeds on benthhic invertebrates such as mollusks, crustaceans and aquitic insects from the sediments (Ref. 93252). They forage mainly in brackish waters (Ref. 59043). Ascend large rivers to spawn (Ref. 59043). Juveniles may remain in fresh or brackish water until 2-5 years of age or 76-91.5 cm long (Ref. 4639, 59043). Today most individuals do not exceed 250 cm length. Tagging studies have shown that this species may move distances up to 1,450 km (Ref. 89119). Used smoked and fresh (Ref. 37032). Near threatened globally, but extirpated in Europe due to massive overfishing, damming, river regulation and pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Esturgeon perse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anadromous.  Inhabits coastal and estuarine zones at the sea.  Breeds in strong-current habitats in main course of large and deep rivers on stone or gavel bottom.  Juvenile stay in riverine habitats during their first summer (Ref. 59043).  Adults migrating to breed take the path of short, fast flowing mountain rivers (Ref. 33773). Maximum reported length for female is 176.1 cm TL(Ref. 58888).

species.name: Esturgeon vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries, lower reaches of large rivers, and in salt or brackish water off river mouths (Ref. 5723).  Probably spawns in fresh water (Ref. 27547).  May cover considerable distances in the ocean (Ref. 27547).  Edible but with a disagreeable taste and unpleasant odor (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Esturgeon à museau court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit river mouths, lakes, estuaries, and bays; occasionally enters the open sea. Feeds mostly at night over soft substrates; juveniles feed primarily on benthic crustaceans and insects, adults prey on benthic crustaceans, insects and mollusks (Ref. 93252). Maximum known age is 67 years for females and 30 years for males.  Flesh of good quality; eggs are suitable for caviar (Ref. 3192).

species.name: Esturgeon étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the sea, it occurs in coastal and estuarine zones and forages on the bottom mostly on clayey sand and intensively in the middle and upper water layers (Ref.  59043).  Found mainly near shore over sand and mud, stays at the bottom during the day and rises to the surface to feed at night.  Feeds mainly on fish, also mollusks, crustaceans and worms (Ref. 3193).  Spawns in strong-current habitats in main course of large and deep rivers, on stone or gravel bottom.  Spawning also takes place on flooded river banks and if gravel bottom is not available, on sand or sandy clay.  Juveniles stay in shallow riverine habitats during first summer (Ref. 59043).  One of the three most important species for caviar; also utilized fresh and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Overfishing at the sea for meat and caviar will soon cause extinction of the natural populations and their survival can only depend on stocking (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ethmalose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ethmalosa fimbriata is found in fairly shallow coastal waters, lagoons and estuaries, and sometimes also in lower courses of coastal rivers, even more than 300 km up rivers (Ref. 187, 188, 81269, 81631). It feeds principally on phytoplankton, chiefly diatoms, filtered by the very fine gillraker sieve (Ref. 187, 188, 3166). It breeds throughout the year in waters of salinities 3.5-38 ppt, but with peaks in at least some areas; spawns in the sea, in estuaries and in rivers (Ref. 188). The largest fisheries are in Senegal, Sierra Leone, Ivory Coast, Nigeria and Cameroon, mainly in the dry season (Ref. 188).

species.name: Etia nguti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles were collected with beach seine in the shallow inshore zone in a water depth of few centimeters, adults in deeper water; juveniles prefer shallow water riffles with medium current, while adults congregate around submerged tree branches and rocky outcrops (Ref. 49597).  Mainly feeds on detritus, occasionally on insects and plants (Ref. 52307). Delayed uptake, ovophilic (Ref. 81260), larvophilic (Ref. 52307) mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307), spawning in couples over open substrate (Ref. 49597). Female (rarely the male) incubates the fry (Ref. 49597, 52307).

species.name: Etincelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, found between 225-750 m during the day and between 90-375 m (juveniles) and 450-550 m (adults) at night.  Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Widespread distribution in all oceans, limited by 10° and 15°C isotherms at 200 m and by a productivity greater than 50g Carbon per square meter per year.  Sexually mature from about 5.9 cm.  Spawn mainly during summer to autumn in the Mediterranean (Ref. 4775).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Eugnathogobius kabilia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A euryhaline species (Ref. 12041).  Occurs in estuaries, primarily in slow flowing canals and smaller bodies of water.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates, including mosquito larvae and entomostracans (Ref. 12693).  The following aquarium observations describe its captive behavior and breeding:  strictly benthic and quite secretive; males constructed nests under flat stones, shoveling sand with their large mouths while pieces of gravel (up to 12 mm diameter) are carried one by one; males display to each other with mouths wide open and may push against each other jaw to jaw, if observed may often switch to locking jaws (as if biting); about 1,000 eggs per batch (1.5 x 0.5 mm) and hatched after 44-95 hours at 25°C; larvae 2.4 mm long and floated up near the water surface until yolk absorbed after 124 hours, these then moved down into the water column (Ref. 80545).  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693); rarely collected (Ref. 80545).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eusurculus pistillum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sublittoral area, with rocks, mud, corals and brown algae.  It appears to be most common in reef environments, often on outer reefs, and avoid inshore and back reef areas (Ref. 76869).

species.name: Eutaeniichthys gilli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools of estuaries under stones.

species.name: Eutelichthys leptochirus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also pelagic.  Apparently occurring peripherally at bathyal depths around the western basin of the Mediterranean (Ref. 4702).

species.name: Eutropiichthys britzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eutropiichthys burmannicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eutropiichthys cetosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a clear, slow and moderate flowing river with a depth of 1-4 m (Ref. 96851).

species.name: Eutropiichthys goongwaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rivers and canals.  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eutropiichthys murius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers, streams and canals (Ref. 1479).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eutropiichthys salweenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evelyn's cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains a length of almost 5 cm.

species.name: Everglades pygmy sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, heavily vegetated sloughs and small sluggish streams, usually over mud. Feeds on worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020). Oviparous, eggs are deposited in aquatic vegetation, preferably on strands of Ceratophyllum sp. when available (Ref. 58020).

species.name: Evermann's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep recesses of caves in the outer reef slope (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Swims upside-down on ceilings (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Evermann's lantern fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic; nyctoepipelagic at the surface (Ref. 9192).  Neustonic at 1-125 m at night, 600-1150 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Feed at night in the western equatorial Pacific (Ref. 9192).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 31442).  Lipid content is 3.1 % in fresh body weight and  wax ester is10 % in total lipids (Ref. 9197).

species.name: Evermann's snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom, inshore (Ref. 75154); in shallow sand and mud bottom (Ref. 123091).

species.name: Evermannella ahlstromi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small, mesopelagic species of the open ocean (Ref. 36017).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36017).

species.name: Evermannella megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evermannia erici
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evermannia panamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evermannichthys bicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate sponge dwellers. Live deep within canals of the sponges, near the openings to the incurrent canals. Sponges provide species with protection from predators and an available food source in many invertebrates. Eggs found within sponge or small plankton brought through incurrent pores (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Evermannichthys spongicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Always lives in large loggerhead sponges and other similar sponges (Ref. 7251).  Live deep within canals of the sponges, near the openings to the incurrent canals. Sponges provide species with protection from predators and an available food source in many invertebrates. Eggs found within sponge or small plankton brought through incurrent pores (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Evia barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams on gravel bottom, with flow usually interrupted in summer when only a few pools may remain.  During dry years, streams dry completely and this species survives only in a few pools (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in water bodies on low-lying plains, with little current.  Is threatened by water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).  Attains up to about 18 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Evileye blaasop
species.description: Common in tide pools, estuaries, and in the sea to depths of 400 m.  Very poisonous, not touched by fishes and sea birds.  Hands should be washed after handling this fish.

species.name: Evoxymetopon moricheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evrotas minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in springs and spring-fed creeks and in the mainstream of Evrotas and upper main Alphios.  Occurs in shallow areas, with slow or no current, close to the shore, among overhanging roots and dense vegetation.  Feeds on variety of plants, insects and microcrustaceans.  Attains maturity in the second year of life and spawns between mid-March and June (Ref. 52474).

species.name: Evynnis ehrenbergii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Evynnis mononematos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ewa blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic and benthopelagic in or over coral (Ref. 58302).  They hover generally above the reef waiting for unwary prey.  They feed on fishes. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Difficult to rear in aquaria because they cannot easily be induced to accept ordinary fish food (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Ewaso Nyiro barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ewaso Nyiro labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ewens pygmy perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing streams and ponds in clear water, most common in creeks between ponds (Ref. 5259). Occurs in small, swiftly flowing, well-vegetated creeks in clear, cool water (14°-16°C), over gravel or cobbles. Often found around accumulated flood debris and log snags Feeds on aquatic insects and benthic microcrustaceans. Breeds from spring to early summer. First discovered in the early 1980s. Co-occurs with N. australis at Ewen ponds, but generally prefers faster flowing streams rather than ponds (Ref. 44894). Aquarium conditions: pH=7.2, H=8, 22°C water temperature, carnivore, egg layer, peaceful community fish requiring rock and plant cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Exallodontus aguanai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exastilithoxus fimbriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exastilithoxus hoedemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exclamation point dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mixed volcanic and coral sand, broken shells, and rubble substrate, with low relief and no algal cover (rarely on pure sand) (Ref. 11666).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Exechodontes daidaleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known along the continental shelf; inhabits hard bottom areas under the Florida Current and on muddy bottoms with isolated hard substrate in the northern Gulf (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Exile cusk eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Exile snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Exocet
species.description: Found on sand, mud or over rocks in sandy areas, exploring the bottom with the free part of the pectoral fins (Ref. 6544).  Feeds primarily on benthic crustaceans, especially crabs, clams and small fishes.  Neither anterolateral glandural groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Exocet africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surface waters of the open ocean, capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 3395). Planktivore (Ref. 97629).

species.name: Exocet aile courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in neritic surface waters (Ref. 9839), rare in the open ocean (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding above the surface (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Exocet aile jaune
species.description: Inhabits neritic surface waters, rare in the open ocean (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 3395).

species.name: Exocet aile noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits oceanic surface waters.  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for considerable distances above the surface (Ref. 3720).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 109257).  Eggs with bunch of filaments opposed by a single filament on opposite pole (Ref. 6523).  Reported to have no importance to fisheries (Ref. 109257).  Depth assumed from ecology data.

species.name: Exocet atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in surface waters near the coast (Ref. 5217).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 3613).

species.name: Exocet bandé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in oceanic waters.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances over the surface.

species.name: Exocet barbu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in oceanic and neritic waters (Ref. 9839).  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet bouledogue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in surface waters, both near and far from the coast (Ref. 5217).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet bécune
species.description: Epipelagic in coastal and oceanic waters.  Often near oceanic islands.  May leap out of the water and glide over considerable distances above the surface.  Also caught using dipnet and light method (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Exocet bécune (Fodiator acutus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic, oceanic and epipelagic species (Ref. 27000) at surface (Ref. 96339).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet californien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are epipelagic and neritic.  Capable of leaping and gliding out of the water for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet casque
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surface neritic waters.  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons sautant hors de l'eau. Adults occur in surface waters, both near and far from the coast (Ref. 5217).  Form schools.  Capable of leaping out of the  water and gliding for long distances above the surface.  Feed mostly on crustaceans and other planktonic animals.  Preyed upon by swordfish, tunas and many other larger pelagic fishes (Ref. 9987).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36606).

species.name: Exocet coromandel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit surface waters of both neritic and oceanic areas (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet de Bennett
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in near-shore waters.  Tends to occur near land or islands in cooler waters.  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fishes.  Eggs with filaments over entire surface (Ref. 6523).

species.name: Exocet de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oceanic or near-shore surface waters.  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet de Hubbs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Known only from caverns in coral reefs and rocky shores (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Exocet de I'île de Pâques
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic surface waters.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish.

species.name: Exocet de Sutton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oceanic and neritic surface waters (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding above the surface (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on planktonic organisms and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Exocet hirondelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in surface waters both near and far from the coast (Ref. 5217).  Forms schools.  Capable of leaping out and gliding for long distances above the water.  Seasonal variation in abundance was noted in the eastern Caribbean countries, a phenomenon that may be due to post-spawning mortality (Ref. 6838).  The most important commercial fish species of the eastern Caribbean (Ref. 6504).  Considered a good food fish; marketed fresh.

species.name: Exocet holandais
species.description: Inhabits near shore surface waters.  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet jibeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in surface waters and capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 3613).

species.name: Exocet marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in coastal and oceanic waters.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Exocet matelot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oceanic surface waters.  Leaps out of the water and glides for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet miroir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oceanic surface waters (Ref. 9839).  Caught in surface waters over the depths 80-10,400 meters, usually 2000 to 6000 m (mean 4423 m) (Ref. 93339).  Spawns throughout the year in warm waters (Ref. 6523).

species.name: Exocet méditerranéen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic, coastal species which can fly over long distances.  It is thought that this behavior is a means to escape danger.  This flying fish is not commercially exploited although it is very good to eat  (Ref. 5377).  Spawns during summer in Italian waters.  Eggs with filaments over the entire surface (Ref. 6523).

species.name: Exocet omé
species.description: Epipelagic in coastal waters.  Capable of leaping and gliding considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet papillon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in coastal waters.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet pharaon
species.description: Found in surface waters of both neritic and oceanic areas (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Exocet planeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in neritic and oceanic waters (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding  for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in the surface of oceanic waters, occasionally near the coast (Ref. 5217).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for long distances above the surface (Ref. 3720).

species.name: Exocet tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in surface waters of the open ocean (Ref. 30573).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for considerable distances above the surface (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Exocet tringa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic and neritic in coastal waters (Ref. 36606).  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances from the surface.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36606).  Eggs are presumably attached to one another or floating objects via filaments (Ref. 36606).

species.name: Exocet voilier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 9300), rare in the open ocean (Ref. 9839).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding for considerable distances above the surface.  3-4 individuals aggregate during breeding (Ref. 47825).  Carnivorous (Ref. 9137).  Not important as food fish, but occasionally taken by fisheries.

species.name: Exocet voilier africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in near-shore surface waters, never spread to open sea (Ref. 9839).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding above the surface (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Exocet à dos tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in near-shore waters, never spread to open sea.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface (Ref. 9300).

species.name: Exocet à grandes écailles
species.description: Occurs in near-shore surface waters, never spread to open sea.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).  Capable of leaping out of the water and gliding above the surface (Ref. 30573).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Exocet à pointe blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in oceanic waters.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocet à tache blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic in oceanic waters.  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.

species.name: Exocoetus peruvianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exostoma berdmorei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exostoma effrenum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exostoma sawmteai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exostoma stuarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exostoma tenuicaudatum
species.description: Occurs in a steeply sloping mountain drainage with fast flowing water, debouching into the Siang River (Brahmaputra River basin), about 3 km from Bomdo village on the main road to Tuting, Upper Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh. Substrates are mostly composed of large, dark-brown boulders and with pebbles, cobbles, concrete fragments of various colors and minute gravels in certain places. The banks have mosses, shrubs, small trees, with larger trees further uphill. The gravel bed was more or less clean, with only a little algal slime over the substratum. Other fish species collected at the type locality are Neolissochilus hexagonolepis, Pseudecheneis sulcata, Garra magnidiscus and Schistura sp. (Ref. 105469).

species.name: Exostoma vinciguerrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exotic snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Exquisite pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a drop-off wall with a few small caves, coralline algae, antipatherians and numerous hard corals (Ref. 57544). Inhabits reef walls and rubble in 10-60 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Exquisite rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep gradient streams with numerous cascades and normally crystal clear water. Tends to congregate in pools at the base of small waterfalls where flow is rapid but is also found in quieter sections of streams and lakes. Prefers areas fully exposed to sunlight. Found in small, clear, swift-flowing streams, occasionally seen above high waterfalls. Also occurs in a lacustrine environment at the base of Edith Falls (Northern Territory) (Ref. 44894). Feeds mainly on aquatic and terrestrial insects and their larvae, also on green algae. Sympatric with M. splendida australis. A good aquarium fish, typical of most rainbowfishes in this respect. Should probably be provided with more space and additional aeration than is usually recommended for fish of this size due to its fast swimming habits and affinity for well-oxygenated waters at the base of waterfalls and rapids (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Exquisite sand-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal bays and sandy estuaries sometimes in seagrass (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Exuma goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Exyrias volcanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eye-bar goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in loose groups in sand (Ref. 90102). Inhabits shallow coastal bays and estuaries on silty sandy substrates with sparse algae-reef or seagrasses (Ref. 48637).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on organic matter and small invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Eye-spot blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in clear coastal to outer reef habitats to about 20 m depth (Ref. 48636), perched on live corals in sheltered reefs (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Eyebar goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species that occurs in sheltered sandy areas from reef flats to seaward reefs; over sandy bottoms near pieces of rubble, rock, or coral (live or dead) (Ref. 9710, 48637, 92171). Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Feeds on algae, detritus and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Eyebar spiny goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon reefs (Ref. 37816).  Found on sandy and muddy bottoms of coral rubble (Ref. 43239). Depth range 1-30 (Ref 90102).

species.name: Eyebrow bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 4241).  Trawled at depths greater than 500 m (Ref. 4241).

species.name: Eyebrow goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries, enters rivers, lagoons (Ref. 4967) and  lake (Ref. 13446).

species.name: Eyebrow scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known on basis of only two specimens collected with beach seine in shallow water at Cammahala Bay, Luzon, Philippines (Ref 90102).

species.name: Eyebrow wedgefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poorly known benthic species that occurs in shallow water on the continental shelf. Presumably feeds on bottom-dwelling fishes and crustaceans. Males sexually mature at 103 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Eyebrowed large-eye bream.
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on coral-sand bottom and collected using handlines; in lagoons and large pools.  Stomach contents include broken bivalve shells and scraps of urchin shell (Ref. 107926).

species.name: Eyed sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Flesh excellent to taste.

species.name: Eyelash handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eyeless golden-line fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species. The Karst limestone cave is located 1,638 m above sea level (Ref. 127045). Adults have a naked body and are blind, either eyeless or with small eye dots (Ref. 127045).

species.name: Eyeline coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  The male takes care of eggs deposited on a coral branch (Ref. 32163).  Has the ability to change sex in both directions to favor reproductive success (Ref. 32163).

species.name: Eyeshade sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eyespot coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deepest capture of a specimen collected from a trawl station covered 20-850 m depth interval (Ref. 94130).

species.name: Eyespot gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small muddy streams.

species.name: Eyespot grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on copepods, polychaetes, small fish (including juveniles of Bregmaceros), and other bottom invertebrates.

species.name: Eyespot pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aggressive against conspecifics.  Not a brackish water species.  Feeds on snails and other benthic organisms.

species.name: Eyespot rasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Eyespot skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Eyestripe clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eyilikler gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eyipantla silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Eyre's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is collected over low-relief reef of dead coral and coral rock rubble (Ref. 107299).

species.name: Eğirdir minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes.

species.name: Facciolella castlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen collected at 230 m depth.

species.name: Facciolella karrerae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably inhabiting holes found on soft sea-bottom.

species.name: Facciolella saurencheloides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Floating or actively swimming larvae seem to live in the upper pelagic region.  In the Red Sea, metamorphosing or post metamorphosed stages seem to descend vertically down to the deep-sea bottom.

species.name: Face-stripe pygmy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes in 10-52 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fahal sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Faintbanded whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Faintsaddled snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Faintstripe filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud or sand bottoms of trawling grounds (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fairy cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Northern populations occur in pure rocky habitats and in places with large boulders, while southern populations are found in intermediate habitats and males occupy small caves (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Fakfak damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Falcate chameleon catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainstreams (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on crustaceans and benthic organisms (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Falcon red banner blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with dead colonies of Colpophyllia brain corals, and less than one meter deep at Los Roques. Occur in groups (Ref. 125603).

species.name: False anchovy codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False Argus skate
species.description: Inhabits outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 114953). Lengths of adolescent males varied from 32.5-37.5 cm TL, with smallest juvenile at 21.9 cm TL (Ref. 75648).

species.name: False baelama anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its habitat and biology is probably similar to T. baelama, but not separated from it in previous records.

species.name: False Bandit Dottyback
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Specimens of this species were collected in 22 m depth at the bottom of a current-
swept channel with strong coastal influences (it has relatively low visibility and otherwise silty conditions).   Individuals were associated with low rocky outcrops covered with sea fans (Ref. 89094).

species.name: False Bay klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False black body moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The 73.6 cm TL female was gravid and distended with 1.0-1.2 millimeter eggs (Ref. 106142).

species.name: False black lancer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large muddy rivers.  Feeds on small fishes, benthic invertebrates and large amounts of plant detritus.  Spawns at the beginning of the rainy season and utilizes the flooded forests along the river edge.  Juveniles appear in August.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: False black tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False brown moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs in 1-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: False cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Viviparous (Ref. 10800).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: False dory
species.description: Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: False duckbill whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: False firemouth cichlid
species.description: Found in rivers and lakes.  Inhabits lower and middle sections of rivers in slower moving waters.  Prefers a soft substrate of sand, mud and small stones (Ref. 7335).

species.name: False graceful whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False Indian anchovy
