species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably coastal, pelagic and schooling, but more material and data needed. Egg presumed to be oval with a knob (as in S. indicus).

species.name: False jewel killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and swamps in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish. Bottom spawner, 1 month incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: False kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, on rock bottom (Ref. 11230).  Commercially cultured in Japan.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: False kinglip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: False lance codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: False lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: False leopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and sheltered seaward reefs, in areas with mixed sand, rubble, and coral to at least 30 m.  Occurs singly or in small groups (Ref. 9710).

species.name: False macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Principally active during the day.

species.name: False midnight dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected around corals and Millepora and usually enters the cavities of 'blue tubular sponges' (Ref. 81967). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: False moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic  and solitary species (Ref. 26340) occurring in and around coral reefs and rocky shores.  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: False oblique hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).  Life history stages apparently stratified vertically, depth of occurrence increasing with age.  No marked vertical migration (Ref. 5168).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: False osman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).  Young and small adults occur in shallow streams and pools while large adults inhabit the main river (Ref. 4832).

species.name: False papillose blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False peacock skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal species on upper continental slope. Smallest mature male reaches 32 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: False rummynose tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: False saddled snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only known sample was collected in less than 10 cm water.

species.name: False scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300); on rocky reefs and rubble bottoms in shallow coastal waters.  Feeds on small fishes, shrimps, and crabs during the day.  Occasionally enters the aquarium trade (Ref. 37107). Also found in brackish estuaries and silty coastal reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: False senator wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reef-algal habitats, more common in the shallow surge zone (to 5 m depth) (Ref. 26203).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: False silver whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: False singlespot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: False spotted catfish
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: False sunny dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently a relatively deep-reef inhabitant primarily associated with small caves in the vertical slopes of the drop-offs. Collected by rotenone or clove oil from outer reef, vertical wall of drop-off with small caves, broad sandy ledge at 30 m, some gorgonians, sea fans, sponges, various hard corals, Acropora, Pocillopora, Halimeda (Ref. 122127).

species.name: False Tasmanian blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: False yellowjacket cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and rivers but prefers the moderate to fast flowing waters of the lower and middle river valley sections.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 12251),  aquatic and terrestrial insects (Ref. 7335).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: False-comet dwarfgoby
species.description: This species apparently prefers outer reef slopes exposed to clear oceanic water and is  frequently observed resting individually on coralline algae outcrops or live plate corals (Ref. 126577).

species.name: False-eye sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs with some wave action (Ref. 9710) while juveniles are usually found in shallow water zones in lagoons and flat bottom areas.  Feed on algae and sometimes on crustaceans and small invertebrates.  Solitary or in loose aggregations (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: False-spined catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and flowing streams, swimming close to rocky or sandy substrate (Ref. 44894).  Widespread in rivers and creeks of the Kimberley region and prefer habitat of variable-sized rocky pools, usually with slow to relatively swift-flowing water (Ref. 27663).

species.name: Fan shrimp-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open sand and rubble areas adjacent to reefs (Ref. 30404, 48637). Lives with the snapping shrimp Alpheus randalli (Ref. 30404).

species.name: Fan-bellied leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and on coastal and offshore reefs (Ref. 9563); also on weed bottoms and on trawling grounds.  Found on muddy or silty substrates (Ref. 48637).  Is an omnivore which feeds mainly on seagrass, algae, gammarid amphipods and caridean shrimps as well as on bryozoans, hydroids, ascidians, copepods, caprellid amphipods and tanaidaceans (Ref. 13426).

species.name: Fanfin angler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathy- and mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).  Males parasitic on the females (Ref. 559).

species.name: Fanfin skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Fanfin smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Fanfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore in warm mesopelagic waters (Ref. 6697).

species.name: Fanfre jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larvae epipelagic (Ref. 34024).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fanfre noir
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found around rock jetties and on rocky bottoms in shallow water.  Marketed fresh and eaten fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Fanfre noir (Grammonus ater)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky areas (Ref. 4758).  Probably a deep dweller that migrates to coastal areas in August (Ref. 12382).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Nocturnal, hides in caves during the day (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Fang's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef caves and crevices in 5-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fanged seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fangfangia spinicleithralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fangtooth dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468, 75154).

species.name: Fangtooth perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Fanning pyrrhulina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fantail filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef areas (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic over rock, rubble and sand; juveniles epi- and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on algae, small benthic invertebrates, and corals (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Farcimen goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Farlowella altocorpus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella amazonum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella colombiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella curtirostra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in running, but not torrent, waters (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Farlowella gianetii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Farlowella hahni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella hasemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella henriquei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella isbruckeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella jauruensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella knerii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella mariaelenae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella martini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella mitoupibo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a clear water stream with slow to moderate current over a sandy substrate with round stones, gravel and leaf litter.  The largest specimen was a male measuring 20.96 cm in standard length (Ref. 128477).

species.name: Farlowella nattereri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella odontotumulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella oxyrryncha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella paraguayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella platorynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella schreitmuelleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella taphorni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella venezuelensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella vittata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Farlowella wuyjugu
species.description: Known from small, forest creek (Ref. 128687).

species.name: Farlowella yarigui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among wood sticks and partially-submerged vegetation using a bottom net.  Encountered  only in such microhabitat despite collection efforts throughout the main channel of the río Topón.  Occurs together with <i>Astyanax caucanus, <i>A. magdalenae, <i>A. filiferus, <i>Roeboides dayi, <i>Sturisoma cf. panamense, <i>Chaetostoma sp., <i>Lasiancistrus caucanus, <i>Creagrutus cf. guanes and <i>Hemibrycon sp. (Ref. 94974).

species.name: Farnis’ goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens were collected from a fish market, hence no natural habitat information is available (Ref. 116177).

species.name: Fartail coraldgudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a sheltered, silty reef situated close to shore in 5-12 m depth (Ref. 84036).  Inhabits crevices and caves (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fat greenling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky coastal areas; often gather around artificial reefs.  Breeds from October to December.  The egg masses are attached to small rocks, guarded by the male (Ref. 559 and 637).  Commercially cultured in Japan.

species.name: Fat spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fat-headed cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slopes (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Fathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fatlips minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble runs and riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294, 86798).

species.name: Fatspine spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at the lower continental shelf and upper continental slope (Ref. 58437).

species.name: Fatty sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fausse bourse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 25 meters (Ref. 5503). Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 9710). Adults usually in pairs, but sometimes seen in small aggregations (Ref. 48637). Mimic the poisonous puffer, Canthigaster valentini which it greatly resembles. Feed on eggs, gastropods and grazes the substrate (Ref. 5503, 48637).

species.name: Fausse carangue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over sandy and muddy bottoms in coastal waters and river mouths (Ref. 35237).  Juveniles often found in estuaries (9626).  Spawning generally occurs in summer.  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 35237).  Good food fish, consumed fresh (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Fausse daurade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools over hard as well as sandy bottoms, especially in the upper 100 m.  Omnivorous with a predominantly carnivorous diet (including crustaceans, cephalopods, small fish, amphioxus and worms).  Protogynic hermaphrodite (Ref. 3688).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Fausse limande de banc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between the shore and 100 m depth, on sand or mud bottoms rich in organic matter.  Feed mainly on shrimps (Penaeidae), amphipods, crustacean larvae and annelids.  The whole life cycle develops on the continental shelf.  During reproduction in May and September, adults gather in shallow waters of the estuaries and along the coast.  Sexual activity takes place during the rainy season which corresponds to quite a large influx of organic matter, thereby ensuring food for the breeding fish.  Sexual dimorphism affects the interorbital width and pectoral fin length of the hidden side.  Juveniles remain planktonic for a long time with a high growth rate of >5% per day (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Fausse limande du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over sand and gravel substrates to depths of 339 m; larvae collected over depths less than 1,000 m (Ref. 37594).  Feed on mollusks, polychaete worms, crustaceans, brittle stars, and fishes (Ref. 6885).  A tasty food fish; in some years commercial catch in Canada reaches 3,000 t (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Fausse limande du Pacifique (Paraplagusia bilineata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud and sand bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 30573).  Enters shallow estuarine waters (Ref. 4833) and tidal rivers (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Fausse limande paté
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fausse limande sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predator which lives on the bottom where it hides partially or almost completely in the sand in order to disguise itself in the environment.  Feeds on small fish and invertebrates.  Exhibits sexual dimorphism (Ref. 35237).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Fausse morue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky or mud-sand bottom; juveniles have been taken in coastal lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 5222, 57293).  In the west African waters, diet comprise of fishes (58%), stomatopods (21%), crabs (10%), and cephalopods (10%).  It is a protogynous hermaphrodite.  The seasonal migration of the species off the coast of Senegal is influenced by the seasonal upwelling off Senegal and Mauritania.  Utilized fresh and smoked (Ref. 9987).  Highly esteemed in the market of West Africa (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Faux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal over continental and insular shelves and epipelagic far from land (Ref. 30573, 43278, 58302).  Oceanic although most abundant near land, pelagic at 1-366 m (Ref. 58302).  Young often close inshore and in shallow bays (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on schooling fishes (including mackerels, bluefishes, clupeids, needlefishes, lancetfishes and lanternfishes), squid, octopi, pelagic crustaceans, and rarely seabirds (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous, embryos feeding on yolk sac and other ova produced by the mother (Ref. 43278, 50449).  Uses its long caudal fin to bunch up and stun prey (Ref. 2850).  Spatial and depth segregation by sex in northwestern Indian Ocean populations (Ref. 247).  A few attacks on boats are doubtfully attributed to this species, but it is otherwise apparently harmless to humans, though the size of adults of this species command respect (Ref. 247).  May cause damage to fishing gear (Ref. 6885).  Valued for its meat, liver, hide, and fins; utilized fresh, dried-salted, smoked, and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Faux anchois du Panama
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The habitat and biology is probably similar to A. panamensis. In the Gulf of Nicoya, Costa Rica, A. mundeola was noted to occur only in the northern part where salinities are generally lower.

species.name: Faux demi-bec
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters.  A tropical species found within the 24°C isotherm.  Placement in Exocoetidae follows Ref. 13705.

species.name: Faux fletán du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feed on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 6885).  Not marketed as human food (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Faux flétan du Japon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Faux nettoyeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in lagoons, subtidal reef flats and outer reef slopes (where it occurs to depths of over 20 m). Often in pairs in empty worm tubes or narrow holes. They mimic the cleaner wrasse Labroides dimidiatus and nip fins, skin and scales of other fishes (Ref. 9710). They even copy the motion of the cleaner wrasse that may induce other fish to come close, then target their scales or mucus for a feed, biting and quickly retreating to the corals before the victim realizes that it was tricked; experienced fish recognize imposters and often give it a chase (Ref. 48636). Diet is supplemented with benthic invertebrates and zooplankton (Ref. 94105). Also feed on tubeworms and demersal fish eggs. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Faux poisson-pierre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear-water outer reef slopes and channels from depths of 1 to at least 35 m, in areas with mixed rock and coral substrates.  Venomous spines. Solitary on coral and rocky bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Faux St.-Pierre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently encountered in coastal waters (Ref. 27000).  Occurs near the bottom or in midwater, over muddy substrates (Ref. 5377).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951).  Found in small schools (Ref. 4968).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 5213) and squids (Ref. 5951).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 27363.

species.name: Faux-capitaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sandy (Ref. 2683) and muddy bottoms in shallow waters (Ref. 4340), frequently in brackish habitats (Ref. 4340, 57402) and estuaries, but not in freshwaters (Ref. 57402).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5377).  Sold fresh, dried salted or smoked (Ref. 36127).

species.name: Faux-trigle armé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported at 530 m (Ref. 58426). In the Barents Sea usually between 100 to 200 m at temperatures of 1°-3°C and salinities not less than 34 ppt; in the White Sea in somewhat shallower waters at temperatures between 6-12°C and salinities of 23-29 ppt.  Prefers sandy bottoms (Ref. 7297).  Benthic to epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on polychaetes and crustaceans (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Faux-trigle aux grands yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported at 1270 m (Ref. 58426).  Commonly occurs between 200 and 600 m on silty or muddy bottoms at temperatures ranging from -0.1°C to -1.8°C and salinities ranging from 34.8 to 34.9 ppt. (Ref. 7297).  Benthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Faux-trigle bardé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud bottoms with some rocks (Ref. 4698).  Maximum depth reported at 930 m (58426).  Benthic to epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small crustaceans, usually amphipods and mysids, rarely polychaetes and fishes (Ref. 4698).

species.name: Favonigobius aliciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and in the freshwater tidal zone of rivers.  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans and insects.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Favonigobius opalescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Feather blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit oyster reefs and rocky shores.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Feather goby
species.description: Collected from coral reefs (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Feather-barbelled squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Synodontis manni was only found in the main river of the Lower Tana drainage. According to local fishermen it is most abundant in deeper waters of the river where it lives near large logs and stranded trees (Ref. 39831). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Featherduster blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Featherfin cichlid
species.description: Adults are gregarious, drifting plankton picker which occur off rocky slopes (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Featherfin squeaker
species.description: Poisson. Maximum TL was recorded at 22.2 cm, max. SL at 22.2 cm (Ref. 57223).  Occurs over a muddy bottom but may also be found over rocks.  Feeds mainly on insect larvae but will also take algae (Ref. 6868).  This is also an upside-down species (Ref. 4537).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Feeler fish
species.description: Found on the continental slope on soft mud bottoms; deep-sea bottom photographs have shown triple trails made by 'walking' on their pelvic fins and lower tail fin lobe (Ref. 30464).  Feeds on small crustaceans and squids (Ref. 5755).

species.name: Fenerbahce devosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fenestratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores and adjacent sandy areas.  Characteristic of areas where the rocks are covered with a sediment layer.  Feeds by blowing sediment off the rocks and picking at food items remaining (Ref. 267).

species.name: Fernandez whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Ferocious coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ferraris' goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Inhabits shallow, well protected bays and estuaries.  On sand or mud along algae-reef margins (Ref. 48637).  Specimen collected from a patch reef, 2-3 m in depth.

species.name: Ferrarissoaresia ferrarisi
species.description: The type locality is a small headwater stream with width of 1-1.5 m, depth of 0.3-1.0 m, moderate current and bottom composed of sand-silt and pebbles in some stretches. Collected near submerged logs, and caught by overturning a log with the hand-net positioned immediately below. Occurs syntopically with Knodus cf. savannensis (Characidae), two species of Phenacorhamdia (Heptapteridae), and Melanorivulus cf. zygonectes (Rivulidae) (Ref. 114786).

species.name: Ferrarissoaresia meridionalis
species.description: Found in 1st and 2nd order streams, with 1.22 to 3.16 m in width and 0.17 to 0.72 m in depth, characterized by clear water and slow current that varies from 0.15 to 0.36 cm/s, over sand bottom with litter, and riparian surrounding vegetation. Collected under trunks and principally inset somewhat compressed submerged litter banks. Nocturnal. Feeds on small fish (Moenkhausia phaeonota, Characidae), shrimps, aquatic insect larvae and nymphs, fragments of terrestrial arthropods (ants, spiders), seeds and particulate organic matter. Syntopic with Astyanax sp., Bryconops spp., Knodus heteresthes, Moenkhausia spp., Erythrinus erythrinus, Hoplerythrinus unitaeniatus, Rivulus kayabi, Gymnotus aff. carapo, Gymnorhamphichthys petiti, Eigenmannia aff. trilineata, Aequidens sp., Crenicichla inpa, Tatia strigata, Tatia neivai, Helogenes marmoratus, Cetopsis sandrae, small unidentified cetopsid, Hisonotus spp., Cetopsorhamdia sp., Imparfinis aff. stictonotus, Phenacorhamdia somnians, Rhamdia quellen, Ituglanis aff. amazonicus, and Synbranchus sp. (Ref. 94696).

species.name: Festa toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small to large bodies of flowing waters, as well as springs, brooks and ponds.  Prefers water with dense vegetation.

species.name: Festive lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic, found between 475-1,000 m during the day and between 40-325 m at night (Ref. 4479).  Some small juveniles may be non-migratory (Ref. 4775).

species.name: Festive ribbonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults probably bathypelagic, young from 10-200 m (Ref. 6533).  Feed on copepods (Ref. 6714).  Observed hovering vertically (Ref. 6619).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36689).

species.name: Festive snailfish
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées.

species.name: Festucalex armillatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Festucalex erythraeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Reported to have been dredged in 80.5 m (Ref. 4281).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  It is exported as an aquarium species from Hawaii.

species.name: Festucalex prolixus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Planktonic specimens were taken in the upper 0 to 167 m over depths of 1280 to 4825 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Festucalex rufus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in exposed coral reef slopes and generally encountered solitarily or in pairs at depths of about 10-25 m. It exhibits highly effective camouflage with regards to its shape and colour, closely matching an unidentified, short tubular sponge among which this fish is invariably found (Ref. 116662).

species.name: Feuille de canne à sucre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters over corals and rocky substrates (Ref. 5213, 48635).  Usually hides beneath ledges and small caves during the day (Ref. 4326, 48635).  Small juveniles have only two white stripes, dividing with growth into numerous lines.  The lines break-up into dashes and spots when adult (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 4821).  Has toxin-producing glands in the dermis (Ref. 4326) which is extremely bitter to the taste (Ref. 11441).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Feux-de-position
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along the coastal zone and prefers water bodies with little current.  Lives in groups.  Feeds on worms, small insects, crustaceans and plants (Ref. 7020).  The males are generally very much smaller and more svelte than the females.  It is a very prolific species and its reproduction can easily be carried out in the aquarium (Ref. 12225).  With an incubation temperature of 26°C, hatching of the eggs occurs within 48 to 60 hours (Ref. 27188).  Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Few-pored wriggler
species.description: Found in sandy areas (Ref. 115539).

species.name: Few-ray hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Few-rayed pipefish
species.description: Known from a single specimen collected from a reef slope with algae-covered coralline rock-rubble (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Few-spotted toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits currents of all velocities, with a preference for waters of moderate to strong current, between 20 and 940 m elevation.  Recorded from brooks, streams and shorelines of moderate sized rivers.  Found in small aggregations on rocky or sandy bottoms.  Browses on ooze and detritus (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Few-vertebrae moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky shores by longline and rotenone (Ref. 79875).

species.name: Fewpored gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits backwaters of rivers and small creeks, swamps, and lily lagoons, usually among thick aquatic vegetation over soft mud bottoms.

species.name: Fiatole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over continental shelves (Ref. 6561).  Young are often found associated with pelagic medusae (Ref. 6561).  Form large shoals (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on small fishes and zooplankton, also medusae (Ref. 6561).

species.name: Fiatole antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 5205) oceanic species.

species.name: Fieraster atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species.  Free-living, fairly deep.  Assumed to feed on small invertebrates and fish (Ref. 34024).  Feed on small bottom animals (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Fieraster denté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Adults are benthic, juveniles are free-swimming (Ref. 6491). Depth range reported in Ref. 57178 taken from Ref. 040919.

species.name: Fierce pike smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to bathypelagic (Ref. 35950) and mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae, primarily in upper 250 m (Ref. 35950).

species.name: Fiery dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fiery lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic, mesopelagic fish with some size stratification with respect to depth:  small specimens (<2.3 cm SL) were taken in nets as shallow as 60 m, while specimens >4.0 cm SL have only been taken in trawls fished to 490 m and deeper.  During daytime minimal catch data indicate that the species is not found in the upper 500 m, but at night, small specimens (< ca. 2.5 cm SL) may migrate into the upper 120 m.  Mature and expended females (Stages V and VI) have been caught in January and April, suggesting late summer spawning period (Ref. 96467).

species.name: Fiery redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favours cobble riffle areas in the lower gradient reaches of tributary streams, with juveniles preferring the stream edge and adults preferring pools with slightly slower current speeds (Ref. 94787).  Inhabits pools and riffles of clear flowing rocky bottomed streams; feeds on detritus and small bottom-living insects; breeds in summer; males are territorial (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Fieryblack shiner
species.description: Inhabits rocky runs and pools near riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Fiji anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fiji sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters.  Euryhaline (Ref. 12743).  Used as bait in the tuna fishery.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Fiji threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms close to reefs.

species.name: Fijian silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relatively common in both high island and atoll lagoons (Ref. 1602).  They are not found in the rougher waters over reefs and are attracted to light at night in lagoons (Ref. 9760).  Used as bait in the tuna fishery (Ref. 6822).

species.name: Fijian zebra dwarfgoby
species.description: Most samples were collected from habitats with rock and green algae, also from a lagoonal habitat with mixed sand, coral rubble, macroalgae and scattered live coral. Collected from the intertidal to a maximum depth of 5 m. Collected by hand net and clove oil and rotenone (Rer. 126577).

species.name: Filambase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in lagoons while adults inhabit clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs up to depths of at least 30 m (Ref. 9710). They ‘sleep’ in caves and often in shipwrecks at night (Ref. 48636). They are usually in small groups feeding on benthic algae, live corals (Ref. 9710) and shellfishes (Ref. 58784). They sometimes ram their head against corals to facilitate feeding (Ref. 9710). The largest and wariest of the parrotfishes. Assessments showed their vulnerability to overfishing (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Filament blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Joyce Burek, pers. comm., 2004).

species.name: Filament cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Filament cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Filament cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Filament-finned prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pairs and live symbiotically with Alpheus randalli. The pair hover above the burrow's entrance on dark sandy bottoms. Inhabits deep coastal slopes and sand flats, usually in depth over 10 meters (Ref. 48637). Also found in sand-rubble bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Filamented pygmy sand-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected around an isolated, relatively large coral patch on flat, clean and fine sandy bottom at a depth of 15 m; the area is typical for other sandy-bottom dwellers (e.g., Fusigobius inframaculatus, Limnichthys nitidus). Similar to its congener G. arenicola, as observed, this species did not display symbiotic association with any other organisms. Found to be widespread in Indonesia, and often found on light coloured sand or rubble to about 15 m depth (Ref. 75132).

species.name: Filamented rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathybenthic (Ref. 36385).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Filamenteux de fond
species.description: Found on continental slope and rise between temperatures of 12°C to 4°C (Ref. 3590).  Usually solitary; probably forms occasional aggregates.  Feeds on mysids and benthopelagic copepods. Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 6688)

species.name: Filamentous anthiine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Filamentous blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species can tolerate a wider range of environmental conditions than others of this genus.  Adults usually are found on coral or rocky reefs to 20 m deep (Ref. 529).  Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Filamentous flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Filamentous perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Filamentous rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Holotype collected in 1171-1159 m (Ref. 12965).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Filamentous scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty inshore reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Filamentous shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fine silt bottoms of coastal reefs in 6-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Filamentous wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This group may consist of several different species and genetic studies are required (Ref. 90102).  Found in rubble areas in passages and outer reef slopes.  Also occurs in lagoons.  Feeds on zooplankton and other benthic invertebrates.  Occurs in small to large groups of mix sexes but females outnumber males greatly.  Some geographical variations of nuptial males that are influenced by the presence of similar species.  Males readily display to each other or to females to spawn by flashing their colors and 'racing' past with erected fins.  Hybridizes with several other species, and are most colorful where other similar species occur in the same area (Ref. 48636).  At 15 cm SL, this could well be the largest species of the genus so far (CB).

species.name: Filesnout grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Filespine chulín
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typical in highland brooks and in rivers or creeks of moderate to high current velocity, found between 35 and 1350 m elevation.  Lives on sand and stone bottoms where it feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 36880) and in caves (Ref. 27297).

species.name: Filetail fanskate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fimbriate gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits rivers, creeks, swamps, lakes and ponds.  Usually shelters among log debris or undercut banks (Ref. 44894).  Occurs in headwaters, often in hilly or mountainous terrain.  Found on both rock and mud bottoms.

species.name: Fin-joined goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic, benthic and found on sandy bottoms near rocks or corals (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Fine flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottom area of the continental shelf (Ref. 11035).

species.name: Fine Patterned Puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fine-scaled dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300), in crevices near drop-offs (Ref. 8631, 48635). Also found in caves (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fine-spined skate
species.description: This species inhabits perhaps the deepest waters and prefer low temperature, high oxygen environments compared to its congeners. Little is known about the diet of this species, except noted to consume deep-water shrimps. Based on materials examined, size at maturity for males is at least 64-75 cm TL and 60-70 cm TL for females; with reported size at birth to be about 17 cm TL.  Egg cases are small (7.9-8.1 cm TL), dark golden brown in colour, coarsely striated with irregular rasp-like denticles, making it rough to the touch. Horns at the corners with the anterior ones robust at base, but flatten towards tips and the tips curve dorsally and back towards the egg case (Ref. 126515).

species.name: Finelined surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  A good food fish (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Finescale menhaden
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling in inshore waters, including bays (possibly euryhaline).  Feeds on plankton.  No data on breeding (Ref. 188).  Spawns during winter and possibly during early spring (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Finescale razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the lower reaches of rivers, ponds, beels, ditches and canals (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Finescale razorfish
species.description: A solitary species (Ref. 90102) common over sandy areas of reef flats and shallow sandy lagoons to a depth of at least 6 m.  Also found in estuaries. Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Usually in current zones such as tidal channels.  Juveniles often with small outcrops of rubble and algae or around the edges of sparse seagrasses (Ref. 48636).  The species is capable of diving into sand when threatened.

species.name: Finescale sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers and creeks of low to moderate current velocity.  A benthic piscivore (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Finescale splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a quiet pool of clear to murky water at a depth of up to 1.2 m and with bottom consisting of sand, silt, rocks and boulders.

species.name: Finescale tigerfish
species.description: Inhabits freshwater rivers, lakes and reservoirs, frequenting areas with a lot of submerged branches, such as flooded forests (Ref. 12693).  Adult fish feed on small shrimps, fish fry and small fishes while young individuals take zooplankton  (Ref. 6459).  Also feeds on crabs, worms and insect larvae (Ref. 12693) and plants (Ref. 56749).  Esteemed food fish which is marketed fresh and often seen in aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Finespotted jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans, and other invertebrates.  Nocturnal.  Cleans and excavates its burrow, like keeping its home clean and tidy.

species.name: Finespotted plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on isopods, gammaridean amphipods, octopods, polychaetes and mysids.

species.name: Fingered dragonet
species.description: Lives on sand-weed bottoms (Ref. 559).  Inhabits protected sand and mud flats and slopes at depths of 1 to 55 m (Ref. 37816); also include estuaries and deep water (Ref. 48636).  May be seen  solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Finke goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among detritus in shallow pools with rock, sand or gravel bottoms. Recently separated from C. eremius on the basis of electrophoretic and morphological evidence. The life history and general biology of these species are similar (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Finke river hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open water or around aquatic vegetation in permanent waterholes. Tolerance to temperature and salinity is broad. An omnivore which probably spawns during warmer months. Mis-identified as C. eyresii (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Finless eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in the sand on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Finless sleeper ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 9913); primarily inshore on soft substrates (Ref. 114953). Probably feeds on small benthic invertebrates. Females reported to produce 4 pups a litter (Ref. 114953). Biology little known (Ref. 9913). Maturity size of males reaches at 8-10 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Finspot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The smallest gravid female 1.74 cm SL (Ref. 5293). Found in coral reef, benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Finspot gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Finspot wrasse
species.description: Found in shallow waters with dense coral growth on coral rubble and sand, also in weedy areas.

species.name: Fiolenti's smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fire clownfish
species.description: Poisson. Adults inhabit lagoon and outer reef environments. Feed predominantly on planktonic copepods and algae. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Entacmaea quadricolor (usually), Heteractis crispa (occasionally), and Heteractis magnifica (rarely) (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35404, 35413, 35420).

species.name: Fire eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A large lowland floodplain species occurring in slow moving rivers and inundated plains.  Feeds on benthic insect larvae, worms and some plant material (Ref. 12693).  Caught by dry pumping bodies of standing water.  Marketed fresh and often seen in the aquarium trade.  Has apparently become rare in recent years (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Fire-eye cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations, sometimes among staghorn corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fire-eyed loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, forested streams and backwaters.  Feed on small invertebrates, algae and detritus from the bottom.

species.name: Fire-tail devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shelter of coral or rock of shallow reefs (Ref. 9710), with moderate surge or currents, in spread-out groups of mixed sexes.  Also in tidal pools, reef flats and reef slopes, often in relatively silty areas at depths ranging to 20 m (Ref. 81967).  Moves about activity through the gutters and passages (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 559).  Frequently seen in the aquarium fish trade, and has been bred in captivity (Ref. 35416, 37748).

species.name: Fire-tailed Pseudocrenilabrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at open beaches (Ref. 114630).

species.name: Firebelly darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel-bottomed pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Firebelly grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over steep slopes of islands.

species.name: Firefly lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.  Nyctoepipelagic at the surface (Ref. 4066).  Neustonic at 0-150 m at night, 500-700 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Firehead tetra
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Firemouth cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae. Prefers lower and middle sections of rivers in slow moving waters (Ref. 7335).  Lives in mud-bottomed and sand-bottomed canals and rocky ponds (Ref. 5723).  Stays close to the shoreline vegetation for protection (Ref. 44091).  Omnivorous, but feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 6466).  Used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Firetailed gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams, ponds, swamps and drains, usually among aquatic weeds.  Juveniles feed on zooplankton while adults on insects, larvae and small crustaceans.  Breeds between October and January in response to rising water temperatures.  Male colouration intensifies at this time.  Eggs are laid underneath rock ledges, logs or leaves and are guarded and fanned by the male parent until hatching, 3-5 days later (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Firewood catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly nocturnal.  Feeds primarily on nekton (Ref. 9110).

species.name: Fischer's Victoria squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams and rivers and in lakes, where it prefers shore regions (Ref. 78218). More common in rivers than in lakes (Ref. 12526). Common in marginal vegetation of Kagera River (Ref. 4903). Replaces S. victoriae in shallow waters of Lake Victoria (Ref. 4903), prefers areas less than 20 m deep (Ref. 34290). Feeds on insects (Povilla and chironomid larvae) and molluscs (Ref. 12526). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Rarely grows to lengths greater than 15 cm SL (Ref. 34290).

species.name: Fishelson's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fisher's seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to Height (= from tip of coronet to the tip of straightened tail).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fishgod blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Fishnet pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices and caves in 2-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fison's lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Fissi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The young of the species are more carnivorous than the adults; the latter feed predominantly on phytoplankton (Ref. 2). Lacks marked sexual dichromatism when sexually active; forms temporary pair bonds (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Fistulose cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Post-larvae were collected from the branches of Pocillopora damicornis at a depth of 18 m in Apra Harbor, Guam.

species.name: Five-eyed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters on mud and sand bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9774).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 4896).  Marketed fresh and salt-dried (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Five-lined coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in groups among branches of Acropora coral (Ref. 9710, 48637); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Feeds on small invertebrates and zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). Monogamous (Ref. 52884). The male takes care of eggs deposited on a coral branch (Ref. 32163). Has the ability to change sex in both directions to favor reproductive success (Ref. 32163).

species.name: Five-rayed sanddab
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fiveband barb
species.description: In calm waters in the low land (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Fiveband barbelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms adjacent to reefs in 0-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fivebar grouper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fish is part of a large, deep-water drop line fishery, which focuses its efforts on banks and promontories of shelf habitat in depths of up to 350 m (Ref. 111063).

species.name: Fivelined threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms.

species.name: Fivespine fairygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered, silty reefs in 25-35 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Fivespot flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud and sand bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9774, 11230).  Feeds on small benthic crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 9774).  Marketed fresh and salt-dried (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Fivestripe wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear outer lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710) and exposed seaward reefs. Abundant in shallow exposed areas with surge channels (Ref. 9710, 48636), with gutters, large Acropora plates and algae bottom (Ref. 48636). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Males are often in small loose numbers, swimming over reef sections where small groups of females stay close to the bottom. Juveniles secretive in shallow gutters (Ref. 48636). Feed mainly on benthic crustaceans (crabs, shrimps), small fishes, gastropod mollusks, and sea urchins.

species.name: Flabby sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Flabby whalefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flabellicauda akiko
species.description: Found on sponge on a rubble bottom in 70 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Flag acara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max.  length 10 cm TL (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Flag cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae. Reported to reach around 10 cm SL (Ref. 81048).  Tapajos (NRM) specimens were taken from a sandy shore at Aveiro and a small creek at Santarem, close to vegetation and with mud and sand bottom; Vila Bela da Santfssima Trinidade (NRM) specimens were seined in the shadow of the ferry, in shallow water with much aquatic vegetation; while from Madre de Dios, one sample was seined from a pool in a stream with clear, slightly tinted water and no vegetation; another, mixed sample came from a small stream and nearby cattle pool (Ref. 86444).

species.name: Flag rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky areas. Reported to reach 64 cm, but specimens over 51 cm may have been the redbanded rockfish, Sebastes babcocki. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Flag serrano
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flag tailed panda cory
species.description: Although quite abundant, it has not been found anywhere else except upstream of the first rapids. Sympatric with C. condiscipulus (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Flag tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Flag-in cardinal-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Normally found in sandy to muddy bottoms. Has luminous organs on the thorax and abdomen which contain luciferin obtained from Cypridina plankton. Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Flag-tailed glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, flowing creeks, usually within 20 kilometers of the sea (Ref. 44894).  Commonly found in brackish waters and river mouths.  Occurs near mangroves, stagnant and running freshwater (Ref. 7300) and coastal areas (Ref. 45255).  This species has a marine larval stage, judging from its broad distribution.  One of the best viewing areas is at the Freshwater creek picnic ground in Cairns, where individuals frequently aggregate along the vegetated stream margin (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Flagfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary species.

species.name: Flagfin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Photographed on live and dead coral substrate (Ref. 125603).

species.name: Flagfin cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species which occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Flagfin prawn goby
species.description: Occurs in silty coastal bays (Ref. 9710).  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4343) and freshwater tidal zone habitats (Ref. 12693).  Found on muddy bottom at the base of the reef at Toguan Bay, Guam.  Uses the burrow of a mottled brown alpheid prawn with two or more short white saddles or spots.  Lives coastal sand and mud habitats from shallow estuaries to moderate depths on slopes (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Flagfin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing pools and runs of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers.  Occurs usually over sand and near vegetation (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Flagfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In vegetated sloughs, ponds, lakes, and sluggish streams; enters brackish water.  6.5 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  In Guinness Book of Records as the fish with the fewest eggs (20 eggs are spawned over a period of several days) (Ref. 6472).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Flagtail dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710). Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Usually away from reefs at moderate depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Flagtail shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with Alpheus randalli, the red-banded alpheid shrimp, on coastal sand flats, slopes and in deep lagoons at depths of about 3-30 m. Inhabits coastal sand slopes in 6-30 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Flagtail swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flagtail triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Flagtail wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, exposed tide pools and shallow rock and coral reef areas (Ref. 28023).  Spawns upon reaching 3.4 cm SL (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous (Ref. 56086).

species.name: Flame cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in caves and under ledges. Solitary and seldom seen, hides under crevices during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Flame chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in springs and spring-fed streams, usually over gravel (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on midge larvae supplemented with isopods, oligochaetes, hemipterans, and snails (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Flame hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common along surge-swept reef fronts and submarine terraces to a depth of about 11 m. Usually seen hiding among branches of live corals (Stylophora mordax, Pocillopora elegans, P. eydouxi, or P. verrucosa). Retreats deep into the coral when approached (Ref. 9710). Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, monogamous (Ref. 52884). Highly priced aquarium fish, requires well-oxygenated water and fades in captivity (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Flame humpback scorpionsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flame lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flame perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species (Ref. 93435).

species.name: Flame pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flame wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, in aggregations above at base of drop-offs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on zooplankton 1-2 m above the bottom (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Flameback angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common among isolated patches of staghorn coral Acropora cervicornis. Feeds mainly on algae and sponges (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Flamefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found along sea walls and pilings, in harbors, and coral reefs.  A nocturnal species, it remains hidden in cracks and crevices during the day (Ref. 9626).  Reaches depths of more than 100 m (Ref. 9626).  Males with eggs have been spotted in Bahamas in June and July (Ref. 26938).  Most common cardinalfish in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Flametail tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flaming blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow seaward reefs, from the intertidal zone to 25 m depth (Ref. 9710, 529).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Flaming flagfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently prefers hard to cobble substrate habitats (Ref. 94775).

species.name: Flannelmouth sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky pools, runs and riffles of medium to large rivers.  Less often found in creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Flap-gilled dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy and muddy bottoms in the sea, but also enters mouths of rivers and may live even in freshwater .

species.name: Flapnose conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flappy snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 58302) and burrowing species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Flapscale blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Flarenostril clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flasher scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare inhabitant of mixed sand and rubble areas of reef flats and shallow lagoons. Feeds on fishes (Ref. 89972). Usually buries itself in the substrate when in sand or sits amongst rubble where it has good camouflage (Ref. 48635).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Flat bullhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mud-bottomed, sand-bottomed, or rock-bottomed pools of small to large rivers.  Also found in lakes, impoundments and ponds (Ref. 54507, 10294).  Feeds on aquatic insects, small fishes, and snails (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Flat catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow mudflats and river mouths; also in muddy coastal waters (Ref. 40908).

species.name: Flat-backed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in estuaries with mangroves and soft silt bottoms.  Can tolerate fresh water, but is basically a marine species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Flat-headed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools and river mouths.  Is frequently encountered in places where small brooks fall into the sea and may occasionally be found in purely fresh water.  During low tide it stays under stones on the dry bottom (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Flat-headed loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits near the bottom of clear, fast-flowing streams.  Feeds on benthic organisms and detritus (Ref. 5258).

species.name: Flat-tail mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools in shallows, bogs and lower estuaries, and more saline lagoons.  Often seen jumping at the surface (Ref. 9812).  Fish younger than one year can be found in freshwaters, but not when older (Ref. 9812).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawn in the sea.  Feed on minute benthic organisms, including small crustaceans and filamentous algae.  Marketed fresh and filleted (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Flatbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology unknown.

species.name: Flatface seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow algae or weedy reef areas from the intertidal to about 20 m depth (Ref. 42735).  Maximum length is based on a straight-line length measurement from upper surface (ignoring spines) of first trunk ring, to tip of tail (Ref. 42735).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken in 366-395 m.

species.name: Flathead cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a cave.

species.name: Flathead dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flathead galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stream margins over rock or sand bottoms, sometimes among aquatic vegetation.  Still or gently flowing water on the margins of lakes, billabongs and streams.  Usually swims in midwater over rock or sand bottoms, also in the vicinity of aquatic plants.  Shoal forming (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on a wide range of aquatic insects and crustaceans.  Spawning has been recorded between August and September (Ref. 44894).  Each spawning female releases 3,000-7,000 eggs which are slightly adhesive and settle to the bottom.  Hatching in nine days at 9-14°C; newly hatched fry are 6-7 mm long.

species.name: Flathead goby
species.description: Found in shallow rocky reefs, including estuaries (Ref. 9002).  Very secretive, under rocks or in narrow ledges (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Flathead gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in still and flowing waters; often abundant in dams and lakes, usually among weeds or over mud bottoms.  Occurs in reservoirs and brackish estuaries, less common in gently flowing streams (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on crustaceans, insects, other fishes and tadpoles (Ref. 44894).  In breeding season (mainly spring to summer), males darken and display more vibrant fin markings.  Females lay a clutch of eggs on a hard surface such as a rock or piece of wood.  The male cares for the nest, chasing away intruders and fanning the eggs with his pectoral fins.  Hatching occurs after 4-6 days (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Flathead porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An important food fish.

species.name: Flathead pygmy-stargazer
species.description: Inhabits turbulent sandy beach zones (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Flathead searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky slopes (Ref. 51211).

species.name: Flathead sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flathead slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found in the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Flathead trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly based on introduced S. trutta (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Flatjaw minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flatnose catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeding on a wide variety of foods, including such things as fish fry and eggs, crustaceans, insect larvae, and plant material (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Flatnose xenocongrid eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302). Can be found in reef crevices and under rocks in 7-200m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Flatscale triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flatwhiskered catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools.  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9084).  Known from a temperatures ranging from 24-29 °C, pH range of 5-9, and an alkalinity range of 42-142 (Ref. 9110).

species.name: Flavescent peacock
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Some individuals of a population are very shy and hide permanently in caves whereas others form large schools over sand.  Feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Flecked pikeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected with a semi-balloon trawl from a coarse-rubble bottom (Ref. 13293).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Fleckfin dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rock and coral reef habitats, including surge channels, reef slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 50540). Cryptic and seldom seen (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fleet klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock pools; agile and difficult to capture (Ref. 5496).

species.name: Fleshy-lipped spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on scales of fishes.

species.name: Fleshyfin dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Fleshylip buffalo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fleshysnout catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in turbid inshore waters, estuaries, embayments, and brackish water lagoons (Ref. 38478).  Feeds mainly from the bottom (Ref. 26909).  An excellent food fish.

species.name: Flet
species.description: A coastal species not found far offshore (Ref. 27547).  Occurs at shallow depths on mud bottoms, often in brackish water (Ref. 4705) and frequently entering freshwaters (Ref. 59043).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small fishes and bottom invertebrates (Ref. 4705).  Moves closer inshore in the evenings, especially on a rising tide (Ref. 27547).  Appears to move offshore in the fall and inshore in the spring (Ref. 27547).

species.name: Flet (Platichthys flesus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Migratory fish, which is most of the year found in estuaries (Ref. 51442).  Adults occur on mud and sand bottom in shallow water, at sea and brackish; often entering freshwaters (Ref. 59043).  During winter, adults retreat to deeper, warmer waters, where they spawn in spring (Ref. 30193).  The growing larvae are moving to the coast (Ref. 51442).  Larvae and early juveniles use selective tidal transport to migrate upstream rivers (Ref. 57575) using a range of triggers such as salinity, prey density and water temperature (Ref. 57573, 57574).  Juveniles live in shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 57574), which are also the summer feeding grounds for the adults (Ref. 30193).  Juveniles of less than a year old feed on plankton and larvae of insects, juveniles of more than a year and adults feed on benthic fauna (Ref. 51442), including small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 30193).  Nocturnal and burrowing (Ref. 30193).  Marketed fresh and frozen; can be steamed, fried, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Worms and mollusks are excellent baits for line fishing (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Flet étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, often in very shallow water and in estuaries during the summer; moving into deeper water in the winter (Ref. 27547).  However, they may occur in deep water throughout the year (Ref. 27547).  Does not venture into water of high salinities (Ref. 28899).  Young and adults move up rivers, as much as 120 km (Ref. 27547).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on crustaceans, worms, small mollusks, brittle stars, and small fishes (Ref. 6885).  Important game fish (Ref. 2850).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Fleurin trois yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral heads of lagoon and seaward reefs; common in shallow caves or under ledges and can lie flat against vertical rock surfaces (Ref. 1602, 48637).  Found in rubble slopes in sand or fine-rubble patches (Ref. 9792).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Comes out at dusk and hunts on low reef.  It has low profile and crawls along like a flatworm, but activity waves its black pectoral fin as it goes (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9792).

species.name: Flier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in swamps, vegetated lakes, ponds, sloughs and backwaters and pools of creeks and small rivers, usually over mud (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Invertivore: feed mainly on Hemiptera and Corixidae (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Flier cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly shallow waters or swampy areas of lakes and rivers.  Often found in many eutrophic oxbow lakes, ponds, roadside ditches and remnant pools of floodplains with thick vegetation.  Prefers warm temperature and thrives in stagnant waters.  An open water substrate spawner which lays eggs in extreme shallows.  Fry feed on parents' dermal mucus for first few days (Ref. 7335).  Feeds on detritus and insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Flinders ranges mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky streams flowing through steep-sided valleys.  May also be found on mud bottom lowland creeks if the specimen from the Bulloo River, Queensland  is identified to be this species.  Spawning occurs at temperatures over 20°C.  Females lay between 200 and 800 eggs, usually on the underside of a hard object.  The male guards the eggs until hatching, which takes about 7 days.  Fry are approximately 5 millimeters long and there is no parental care after hatching.  A poorly known species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Floral banded wobbegong
species.description: Collected from the inner continental shelf off southwestern Australia (Ref. 74934).

species.name: Florenciella lugubris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flores mud moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over dark, silty sand (Ref. 83560). Found in mud bottoms of coastal bays in 3-35 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Florida blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in clumps of oysters on mangrove roots and sea walls.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Florida hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Florida round herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurring inshore.  Forms schools.  Feeds on plankton.  Probably grows to 5 or 6 cm SL.

species.name: Florida sand darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Florida torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore to 10 m depth in coral-reef habitats (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Smallest specimens at ca. 15 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Floros goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly on sandy bottoms (Ref. 123119).

species.name: Flotte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species in shelf and slope waters, mainly within the 200 m range along the continental shelf, but down to 600 m along continental slopes and seamounts (Ref. 127222). Feeds on all kinds of bottom invertebrates and fish, including other skates (Ref. 114953). Oviparous, with long embryonic development. Males reach maturity at ca. 115 cm TL, females at 123 cm TL; birth size at ca. 21 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Biology may be unclear due to past taxonomic confusion Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Mate in spring and the egg capsules are laid during the summer.  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.6-24.5 cm long and 5.0-14.5  cm wide (Ref. 41250).  About 40 eggs per individual are laid annually (Ref. 41250).  Flesh is marketed fresh or smoked (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Flower cardinalfish
species.description: Common in shallow coastal reefs with moderate currents (Ref. 48636).  Also in tidal channels of estuaries (Ref. 48636).  Adults usually in small schools comprising pairs (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Fluffy sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612) found in shallow rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Commonly found in tide pools, often in algae (Ref. 2850).  Can leave tide pools when aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Fluvial shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in main channels, usually with current, of small to large rivers.  Often found over sand or gravel.

species.name: Fluviphylax gouldingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected close to the deadwood in a shallow, slow flowing, high transparency black-water stream, about 30-50 cm deep with dense vegetation. In the small stream they were found in small shoals of about 3-5 individuals swimming near the surface, while in the Lago Tiburiari this species formed larger shoals of about 20 individuals. Found sympatrically was the miniature scoloplacid, Scoloplax dolicholophia (Ref. 123788),

species.name: Fluviphylax obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on autochthonous micro-algae and detritus in a swamp (Urubaxi, Brazil) and on allochthonous invertebrates and detritus in an island lake (Buiú-Açu, Brazil).

species.name: Fluviphylax palikur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Among dense vegetation (Cabomba, Eichornia, Nymphaea) in shallow depths of about 30 cm. Also at the surface during hot periods of the day, where they move around with their pectoral fins only and maintain a bent posture of the posterior body that allows them to dart for cover if they are attacked (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Fluviphylax pygmaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fluviphylax simplex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fluviphylax wallacei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In the Igarapé Mauaú, this species was collected in a shallow area, about 30-70 cm deep, in a slow flowing high transparency black-water stream, with sandy beaches and leaf litter areas on the bottom near stream margin. It was found forming shoals of about 15-20 individuals that were swimming near the surface. This species was found sympatrically with the Hyporhamphus brederi (Ref. 123788).

species.name: Fluviphylax zonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open areas with shallow muddy shores.

species.name: Fluvitrygon kittipongi
species.description: Occurs in the mainstream of the Maekhlong River, in an area above the limit of tidal influence.  Prefers sandy or sandy-muddy bottom (Ref. 59378).

species.name: Fly River garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries, lowland rivers and tributaries, sometimes penetrating well inland.  Favors warm (25°-30°C), shallow water in areas with dense aquatic plant growth.  A shoal-forming species which swims near the surface.  Mainly herbivorous but insects are also consumed (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Fly river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, but no indication whether it descends to estuaries.  A filter-feeder.  More data needed.

species.name: Fly River rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in small rainforest creeks (Ref.2847).  An omnivorous egg layer and a peaceful community fish which prefers the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.1, H=8, 27°C water temperature, vegetative cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Fly river thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits turbid channels of large rivers, also lakes and swampy backwaters (Ref. 2847).  The very high number of gillrakers suggests filter-feeding habit (Ref. 189).  Feeds on plankton including calanoid copepods (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Fly-specked hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, small streams, lakes, ponds, reservoirs and warm springs.

species.name: Flying barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in ponds, weedy ditches (Ref. 4832) and irrigation canals (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Flying fox
