species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly collected from the lower surface of floating objects such as boats and floating houses (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  solitary species, adults territorial; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flèche
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Flèche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes, also inhabits lagoons and bays.  Usually in pairs as adults and in small aggregations as juveniles, Ref. 48637.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Feeds on zooplankton while hovering 1 to 2 m above the bottom.  Swims away from danger rather than retreat to its burrow.

species.name: Flétan
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Adults are benthic but occasionally pelagic (Ref. 4705).  Feed mainly on other fishes (cod, haddock, pogge, sand-eels, herring, capelin), but also takes cephalopods, large crustaceans and other bottom-living animals.  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Growth rate varies according to density, competition and availability of food.  Slow growth rate and late onset of sexual maturity, halibut populations can be seriously affected by overfishing (Ref. 35388). Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked and frozen; can be steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Also Ref. 58426.

species.name: Flétan (Psettodes belcheri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Unlike other flatfish, this species has a broad body; width is half the length (Ref. 4883).  This demersal fish is not always in close contact with the bottom, it can chase its prey by swimming (Ref. 5377).  Feeds on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Flétan du Groenland
species.description: Une espèce de poissons plats de la famille des pleuronectidae.. Often caught pelagically (Ref. 4705). Adults prefer bottom temperatures of -0.5°C to 6.0°C (Ref. 5951).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feed on crustaceans, fishes (Ref. 4705, 6885), eelpouts, capelin, redfishes, deep sea prawns and other bottom invertebrates (Ref. 35388).  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Utilized dried or salted and frozen; can be steamed and fried (Ref. 9988). Size of the Greenland halibut collected from 400-599 m deep in eastern Bering Sea, ranged from 9 to 99 cm FL with a mean of 56 cm (Ref. 55110).

species.name: Flétan du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Found on various types of bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Young are found near shore, moving out to deeper waters as they grow older (Ref. 6885).  Older individuals typically move from deeper water along the edge of the continental shelf where they spend the winter, to shallow coastal water (27-274 m) for the summer (Ref. 28499).  Feed on fishes, crabs, clams, squids, and other invertebrates (Ref. 6885).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Flûte rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit tide pools, lagoons, and outer reef slopes.  Found in caves and crevices.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35416). Solitary, pairs or in small aggregations in caves or under ledges (Ref 90102).

species.name: Foa leisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons, bays and near mouths of small tidal streams; one specimen was collected in a pen shell, Atrina pectinta. Specimens were collected with rotenone without identifying cryptic associations/locations during the day (Ref. 93673).

species.name: Foa madagascariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Foa nivosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in Halimeda beds in 15-27 meters and in one collection, it included species of Padina, Caulerpa, and Dictyota (Ref. 93673).

species.name: Foa winterbottomi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Foa yamba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky wall with silt and mud, probably also in other tidal estuaries (Ref. 97601).

species.name: Fodiator rostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic and neritic, usually at surface in  warm coastal waters (Ref. 33606).  May leap out of the water and glide for considerable distances above the surface.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36606).  Eggs are attached to floating objects via long filaments (Ref. 36606).

species.name: Fody dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coral reefs (Ref. 57771).

species.name: Foerschichthys nigeriensis
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139). It forms schools near the water surface and is usually found in clear water, in small rivers, brooks and swamps in the primary and secondary rainforest of the coastal plains (Ref. 57261).

species.name: Foetorepus australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Foetorepus garthi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Foetorepus kamoharai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf edges (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Foetorepus talarae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Folded ghostgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commensal with large staghorn corals in 3-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Folded viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on volcanic rock boulders and sandy channels, shallow coral reef (Ref. 81230). Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of shallow water (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Folifer brevifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Folifer yunnanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fonchiiichthys rupestris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fonchiiichthys uracanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and creeks of moderate velocity between 20 and 160 m elevation, living fixed to branches or stones where they scrape off algae and its attached microbiota.  Feeds mainly on detritus and some aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Fonchiiloricaria nanodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rheophilic species that has been collected in swift current, over rocky substrata of stones, shingle, gravel and sand of the main stream of Río Huallaga and its tributaries. The type localities are located at 600 to 700 m above sea level, between the eastern slopes of the Andean Cordillera and the western slopes of the Cordillera Azul. In this region, the Río Huallaga is shallow ((30-250 cm) during the dry season, but may rise to 4 m after heavy rains or during the rainy season. Huallaga River is a white water river ranging from 50-90 m width in the main channel during low water level and with dense vegetation growing along its banks. The pH, at various sites along the river where type specimens were collected, ranged from 7.3-7.6 with conductivity from 250-432 μS cm−1. The Río Monzón, next to the bridge located 7 km upstream of Tingo Maria (MUSM 38338 and MHNG 2710.048 were collected), is a clear water river with 50 cm of visibility and with sandy areas and pebbles along the shore. Rheophilic fauna collected together with some of the specimen were Chaetostoma, Hypostomus, Lamontichthys, Spatuloricaria, Ancistrus, Farlowella, Pimelodella, Centromochlus, Parodon, Hemibrycon, Knodus and Eigenmannia (Ref. 87853).

species.name: Fondule barré
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des fundulidae. Inhabits shallow, quiet margins of lakes, ponds and sluggish streams, usually over sand or mud and often near vegetation.  Enters brackish water.  Forms schools a few inches below surface of water (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Euryhaline and salinity-tolerant (Ref. 5951).  Feeds on small crustaceans, mollusks and worms (Ref. 93252). Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Footballer demoiselle
species.description: Adults inhabit lagoon and inshore weed and sand flats (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Footballeur à diagonales
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on offshore reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Fork-tailed threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms; also in sheltered estuaries (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and small fishes.  Principal catch in the Taiwanese pair-trawl fishery off the coast of northwestern Australia.  Good food fish (Ref. 171).

species.name: Forked bar blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Forked jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mouthbrooders.  Eggs which are clumped together in a sticky ball get incubated inside the parent's mouth (Ref. 40511). Found in sand/rubble areas in 25-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Forktail blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102) in lagoon and seaward reefs below the surge zone to 30 m depth (Ref. 9710). A common species, often seen along slopes and drop-offs, adults sometimes in small groups (Ref. 48636). Feed on zooplankton and also on small benthic invertebrates. Inoffensive, but immune from predation (Ref. 9710). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimicked by Ecsenius bicolor and Plagiotremus laudanus (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Forktail dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves or around silt-covered rocks.

species.name: Forktail large-eye bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or low-relief rocky bottoms (Ref. 11228).  Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9775). May be solitary or in small groups, on flat offshore trawling grounds, occasionally near shallow coral reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Forktail lates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles live in a specific inshore habitat until they reach 18 cm, thereafter it lives in the superficial pelagic zone; exclusively pelagic predator, feeding on clupeids and to a lesser extent on Luciolates; highly susceptible to intensive fishing (Ref. 2216). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Juveniles often found near river mouths, but not in the rivers (Ref. 36901). Also caught using handlines (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Forktail pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes, often upside-down in caves, in 15-50 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Forktail rainbowfish
species.description: Poisson. Inhabits rainforest streams with thick vegetative cover (Ref. 2847).  An omnivorous egg layer and peaceful community fish which prefers the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.6, H=14, 25°C water temperature (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Forktongue goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Forlon gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams, small rivers and especially adjacent shallow marshes and pools.

species.name: Formosa dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosa grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosa swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A medium-sized species that matures at size less than 65 cm TL (Ref. 94801).

species.name: Formosania chenyiyui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania davidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania fascicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania fasciolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania galericula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania lacustris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid flowing streams.  Feeds on periphytic algae on rock surfaces.

species.name: Formosania paucisquama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Formosania stigmata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams (Ref. 26563). Length type refers to body length (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Formosania tinkhami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Fortescus grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky pools and slow-flowing sections of streams.  Also found congregating at the base of small waterfalls (Ref. 44894).  Feed partly on small prawns and juvenile fishes (Ref. 5259, 44894), but is basically an omnivore. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).   Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=8, 25°C water temperature, live food, egg layer, peaceful community fish, requires rock and plant cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Fossorochromis rostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs frequently over sand in shallow areas off sandy beaches and feeds on invertebrates like insect larvae and small crustaceans (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Fouille-roche gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit pools and margins of riffles of small to medium rivers over sand or gravel bottoms, and also shores of lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on midge larvae, with mayfly and young of caddisfly (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Fountain darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in vegetated springs, pools and runs of effluent rivers (Ref. 5723).  Feed primarily on cladocerans, copepods, amphipods, and aquatic insects (Ref. 54633).  Spawn throughout the year (Ref. 75081) at 33-day interval (Ref. 31966).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Four hooked mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide range of habitats such as ponds, drainage ditches, lakes, wetlands, brackish lagoons, large rivers and swiftly flowing spring-fed streams (Ref. 91760).

species.name: Four twin-spot flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water (10 m) on mud and sand bottoms of coastal zones (Ref. 9774) to a depth of 150 m (Ref. 9494).  Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9774).  Caught mainly with prawn trawls (Ref. 9774).  Marketed fresh and considered a good food fish.

species.name: Four-armed frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and inshore areas over soft bottoms (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Four-bar porcupinefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Continental shelves to 100 m (Ref. 9680). Also found on sand-rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102). Adults benthic, juveniles pelagic (Ref. 30573).  Presumably feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 9680).  Not usually marketed (Ref. 9680).  Not a common species (Ref. 9680).

species.name: Four-eye pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives under corals in embayments, which are sometimes covered by siltation. Also found in caves and crevices of sheltered reefs (Ref. 90102). It often positions itself upside-down on the roof of the recess (Ref. 58123).

species.name: Four-eyed sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore waters, sometimes entering fresh water (Ref. 9671).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Four-eyes perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Four-fin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Four-fingered lipsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocks in the surf line constantly washed by sprays or breakers.  Attains less than 12 cm TL.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Four-lined wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A secretive species that inhabits seaward reefs, among live coral or rubble (Ref. 1602). Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Often observed hiding around the base of small heads of live coral, especially Pocillopora meandrina. Stomach contents of specimens taken from Oahu and Johnston I. consisted of demersal eggs, copepods, amphipods, alpheid shrimp, crab megalops, larval shrimp and gastropod. However, it is likely that the copepods and larval food items are from demersal plankton because this species is never seen more than a few centimeters off the bottom (Ref. 33410).

species.name: Four-spined glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Four-spined leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf  (Ref. 9563).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Four-spotted pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in small groups in small caves in the reef wall of fringing reefs in seaward reefs and bays (Ref. 104898).

species.name: Four-stripe goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fourband leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found on muddy substrates with outcrops of algal reef, or among broad-leaved seagrasses. Young with floating Sargassum rafts and in shallow estuaries (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Foureye rockskipper
species.description: Intertidal, actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 31184), also, crabs; with acute vision to detect prey in the air  (Ref. 94105).  Breathes air (Ref. 31184) and can remain out of water for 1.5-4 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).

species.name: Fourhorn poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rocky sand, gravel, or pebble bottoms.  Frequently covered by featherlike polyps (small hydroid animals) (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Fourline blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs 2-11 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Found in shallow areas.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fourline hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fourline tonguesole
species.description: Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Fourline wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fringing reefs, among coral heads and in areas with dense coral growth (Ref. 9710).  Adults feed on coral polyps while juveniles act as cleaners of other fishes.

species.name: Fourpored blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fourspine cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sand-dweller. Feeds on mollusks, insect larvae, and fish. N. tetracanthus is not a typical crusher of mollusk shells but it is able to suck the mollusk out of its shell (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Fourspine leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in running freshwater (Ref. 6801).  Maximum TL recorded was 4.8cm (Ref. 6801).

species.name: Fourspine scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs in 0-12 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fourspine sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the middle reaches of rivers during the summer; migrates downstream in autumn (Ref. 559).  River bed consists of cobbles, boulders and gravel in riffles and sand and gravel in pools (Ref. 56353).  Feed on fishes (Ref. 559).  Juveniles migrate from the spawning ground in the sea to the middle reaches of rivers to grow (Ref. 56353).

species.name: Fourspot butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found almost exclusively on exposed seaward reefs (Ref. 205). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feed mainly on polyps of Pocillopora. Solitary or in pairs. Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fourspot triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at depths of 8 m and shallower, in surge channels and exposed rocky and coralline boulders (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fourspotted barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fourspotted toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from two creeks with slow current and from a small stagnant puddle at 40 m elevation; at temperatures between 26-34°C.  Swims in small aggregations among vegetation or in shallow waters.  Feeds on diatoms, desmids and detritus (Ref. 36880).  Observed to occur in  10 to 50 cm deep (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Fourteen-gill hagfish
species.description: TBK: demerspelag.

species.name: Fowler's cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fowler's rockskipper
species.description: Adults are found in tide pools and rocky shores to a depth of over 9 m.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fowler's snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens caught from a tidepool during the night, from 92 m depth and at 155 m (Ref. 86689).

species.name: Fowler's surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary and wary species found in clear seaward reefs and drop-offs (Ref. 9710, 48637). Often grazes algae from surface of sponges (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Fowleria amblyuroptera
species.description: Found in coastal reef slopes and bays, on macro-algae rubble substrates, from shallow waters  to 20 m depth (Ref. 126002).

species.name: Fowleria flammea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered lagoon waters with scattered coral outcrops (Ref. 11890). Solitary and cryptic, seldom seen during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fowlerichthys scriptissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs of coastal areas (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Foxfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 75154).  Found in oceanic reefs in 10-40 m, usually in caves (Ref. 9002).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fragile cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered lagoons and bays, above branching corals and among reef crevices.  Forms large schools, often with other species (Ref. 1602, 2334, 37816).  Nocturnal (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Fragile lantern fish
species.description:
Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oceanic species found at 520-600 m by day and at 15-125 m by night (Ref. 4479).
Specimens reach sexual maturity at a length of 7,3 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Frail cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in corals and coral debris of ledges (Ref. 10632), also in clear coastal reefs with mixed algae (Ref. 48635).  Comes out at night only, usually seen drifting above sand patches (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Frail gourami
species.description: Found in rivers and lakes with overgrown vegetation (Ref. 41236), streams (Ref. 4833), ponds and beels (Ref. 1479).  Larvivorous.

species.name: Frailscale goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Francis' goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Franciscodoras marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Frans' cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits steep drop-offs; usually seen in caves or under ledges during the day in 13-40 m depth (Ref. 11893). Forms groups in crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fransmadam
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in the vicinity of scattered and flat reefs from 5 to 30 m depth.  Found in shoals.  Feeds on small crabs, worms, red bait and small pieces of seaweeds.  Good food fish but spoils rapidly.  A good bait for larger game fish.

species.name: Franz's cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fraser's goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottom areas near edge of low profile reefs, usually solitary, occasionally in loose pairs (Ref. 82839).

species.name: Frash
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits eutrophic lakes, lowland and piedmont rivers. Most abundant in estuaries of large rivers, brackish lakes with salinities up to 10-12 ppt and reservoirs. In general, its abundance increases with increased eutrophication (Ref. 59043). Reported to prefer still or slow-flowing water with soft bottom and without vegetation (Ref. 59043) and deep water with deposits of sand and gravel (Ref. 9696). Can tolerate some degradation of the environment (Ref. 30578). Can co-exist in deep lakes with Perca fluviatilis. Both species partly occur at different depths with Gymnocephalus cernua being more abundant in deeper layers (Ref. 59043). The membranous external walls of the head canals of this species provide high directional sensitivity; can feed at night in the dark using the lateral line system; feeds on zooplankton, chironomids, oligochaetes and amphipods (Ref. 10999). Pelagic in coastal lakes and tidal estuaries, preying on zooplankton and fish. Spawns on a variety of substrates at depths of about 3 m or less (Ref. 59043). White to yellow eggs in sticky strands are found on rocks and weed in shallow water (Ref. 41678). Used as bait for pike (Ref. 6258). Females live up to 10 year while males up to 7 years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Frecked dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a cave at 13.5 m depth (Ref. 118500).

species.name: Frecklebelly darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Frecklebelly madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky riffles and runs of medium to large rivers.  Often found near vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on hydropsychid caddisfly larvae, ephemerellid mayfly nymphs, and blackfly and midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Freckled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Herbivorous, with short chisel-like teeth used to scrape algae and detritus from surfaces (Ref. 94105).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Freckled cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on shallow rocky and coral bottoms (Ref. 9626), in empty conch shells, rubble, or empty containers. Abundant where Acropora palmata abound (Ref. 9626). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Presence of buccal pouch for brooding eggs (Ref. 39366).

species.name: Freckled cichlid
species.description: Inhabits cooler, fast flowing water of high mineral content.  Feed on aufwuchs and invertebrates.

species.name: Freckled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast, deep rocky riffles of small to medium rivers.  Giant of the darters.

species.name: Freckled driftfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the open ocean (Ref. 26340). Found under floating weeds or debris. Adults were found under large weed-rafts at a depth of about 20 meters, using the shade as cover. They also form schools (Ref. 48637). Associated with Sargassum (Ref. 26340) and jellyfish (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Freckled frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Freckled garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Poorly known species found on sand in 10-24 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Freckled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Inhabits estuaries and lagoons, on shallow sand-rubble substrates at few meters depths (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Freckled hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear flowing streams over rocky bottoms.  Occurs in still or flowing streams over sandy, muddy or rocky bottoms.  Collections have also been made from small isolated brackish pools on the tidal flats, in turbid water.  A solitary specimen of a similar species, which may prove to be new to science, was recently collected near Rum Jungle (Northern Territory) (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Freckled madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-gravel riffles and runs near debris and among tree roots along undercut banks in creeks to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on aquatic insect immatures dominated by mayflies, caddisflies, midges, and blackflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Freckled pike-conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 37039.

species.name: Freckled rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Freckled sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Freckled skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Freckled soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting sandy bottom strewn with rocks (Ref. 5521).  Rarely observed on reefs (Ref. 13442).  Like other soapfishes, it has special skin glands that produce an irritating, mildly toxic slime (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Freckled splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Freckled stargazer
species.description: Adults mostly found on deeper part of shelf from 180 to 440 m.  Young enter much shallower water.

species.name: Freckled tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Found over muddy bottoms (Ref. 5213).  Considered poisonous by local fishers in the Red Sea and thus are generally discarded (Ref. 9880).

species.name: Freckled tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A species rarely collected; captured on soft mud substrates.  Little is known about its biology (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Freckled wriggler
species.description: Found on sand and rubble with small patches of mostly dead coral or at the base of a drop-off.

species.name: Freckleface podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coral (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874. Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Freckleface reef-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in crevices of shallow reefs, as well as drop-offs (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Frecklefin eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams in lowland and upland areas (Ref. 56749) and peats (Ref. 57235).  Found in shaded forest streams with acidic water and dense growth of submerged vegetation and leaf litter beds (Ref. 85309).  Tends to hide among vegetation (Ref. 85309).  Often occurs in clear water over rocky bottom in flowing streams.  Feeds on bottom-dwelling insect larvae, worms (Ref. 12693) and crustaceans (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Frecklefin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on clear, shallow bottoms with coral formations, principally in oceanic, insular areas (Ref. 13628). Occupies burrows created by the chiton (Choneplax lata) burrows in red coralline algae at shallow depths, usually less than 1 meter (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Freemanichthys thompsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Freeman’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on various types of aquatic larvae and annelids (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Freespine flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over gravel bottom of the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Freetail brotula
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024), inhabiting rocky tide pools (Ref. 6610).

species.name: French butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit steep offshore rocky reefs (Ref. 47838).  Feed on sponges, filamentous algae and small crustaceans (Ref. 9626).  Rarely seen except from submersibles below 100 m (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fresh water puffer fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers and lakes (Ref. 2829).  Also occurs in estuaries (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Freshwater cobbler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in slow-flowing streams, ponds and reservoirs.  Occurs in isolated pools in riverbeds and some freshwater lakes, swimming close to rocky, gravelly or sandy bottoms.  Underwater cavities in river banks and root mounds of sedge tussocks may be utilized for shelter.  Tolerant of brackish conditions (Ref. 44894).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Freshwater croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Freshwater demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mangroves, estuaries, lower reaches of freshwater streams, and harbors with freshwater discharge.  Also found in pure fresh water, but always within a few kilometers of the sea (Ref. 2847).  They occur in brackish waters of coastal embayments and mangrove estuaries (Ref. 44894).  Spawning may take place in both brackish and fresh waters (Ref. 2847).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Freshwater garfish
species.description: Adults occur primarily in rivers (Ref. 4833); also in ponds, canals, beels, and inundated fields (Ref. 1479).  Often found in slow-flowing pools in rivers with a rock or sand substrate (Ref. 6028).  They inhabit large and medium-sized rivers with adults occurring in areas that lack floating vegetation (Ref. 12693).  A solitary species that swims in midwater, usually against the current, and is capable of bursts of speed, especially when in pursuit of its prey.  Observed to feed exclusively on crustaceans in the wild; but take live fish only when in an aquarium (Ref. 6028).  Also feeds on small fishes and insects (Ref. 12693).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).  This fish is capable of nipping the fingers or killing a person by leaping at them at great speed (Ref. 6028; Kullander (pers. comm., 2001), however, suggests that the "killing a person" statement may be exaggerated).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Freshwater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and estuaries, including quiet swift water (Ref. 4967, 79840).  Sometimes abundant in lagoons (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Freshwater gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit brackish or freshwater at salinities ranging from 3 to 31.5 ppt., found in bays, estuaries, and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Freshwater gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in floodplain lakes.

species.name: Freshwater herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It occurs in clear, moderately fast-flowing streams, as well as in quiet backwaters, estuaries, and in the sea ( Ref. 5259, 44894).  Also found in sluggish lowland rivers (Ref. 44894).   A schooling species and appears diadromous.  A fast swimming, shoal-forming species.  Nothing much is known of its biology, although it may have a catadromous life cycle.  Downstream migration to estuaries, presumably for spawning, has been reported in winter months (July-August).  Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and insects (Ref. 44894).  Breeds in estuaries in July to August.  Taken in nets during the spawning season; will also take bait.

species.name: Freshwater mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Freshwater minnow
species.description: Adults are common in streams and rivers with rapid water flow, but not deep or stagnant waters.  Feed on zooplankton, small crustaceans, macroscopic algae, small fish and detritus.

species.name: Freshwater mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in freshwater to estuarine conditions. Adults breed at sea, throughout the year; juveniles move into estuaries and enter rivers usually in late winter or early spring (Ref. 52193). Females remain in freshwater for 7 years, males for 4 years (Ref. 52193). Return to estuaries before maturing sexually prior to spawning (Ref. 52193). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Feed on benthic algae and small invertebrates over muddy bottom (Ref. 6465).  Decline in population from obstruction, by dams and weirs, of free passage into rivers.

species.name: Freshwater pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It occurs in coastal rivers and streams (Ref. 4127) where it can be found in quiet water amongst vegetation (Ref. 30558, 52193) or in the vicinity of logs at river edges (Ref. 30558). It is ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). During mating the female passes eggs to the male and the eggs become fertilized as they pass into the pouch of the male (Ref. 30558). The male brood the eggs and larvae in an abdominal pouch (Ref. 7248, Ref. 30558). After about three weeks the pouch opens and the male gives birth to fully formed young (Ref. 30558). The young begin to feed soon and may take refuge in the male pouch if necessary (Ref. 30558). It probably feeds on minute invertebrate organisms such as crustaceans and insects (Ref. 30558, 52193).

species.name: Freshwater sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes. This is the only species of Sardinella that is apparently found only, or even mainly, in freshwater. Presumably schooling. Also caught using ring nets (Ref. 5520). Mainly caught by gill net, beach seine, ring net and motorized push net (Refs.81494, 80728, 5520). Eaten fresh or dried (Ref. 5517). Is threatened by overfishing (Ref. 6308).

species.name: Freshwater sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and brackish water.  Prefers still water and occurs both in shallow sandy areas and deeper rock pools.  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and aquatic insects.

species.name: Freshwater tongue sole
species.description: Inhabits main river channels and tributaries on soft mud or fine sand bottoms (Ref. 2847).  Occurs in brackish estuaries and freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Freshwater tyulka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pelagic zone of large freshwater lakes and reservoirs.  Preys on crustaceans such as copepods and cladocerans.  Spawns in open water (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Freshwater whipray
species.description: This benthic species is found mainly in rivers, estuaries and low salinity coastal environments.  It feeds mainly on small fishes and prawns, which it actively pursues, even beaching itself to trap prey (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Fria toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Frillfin goby
species.description: A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612). Lives benthically over sandy and muddy substrates (Ref. 79590). Mainly found in pools (Ref. 4343). Abundant in rocky tide pools and along water's edge (Ref. 7251) in lagoons, creeks, estuaries (Ref. 5299, 57403, 79590) and (mangrove) swamps (Ref. 57403, 79590). Occasionally found in fresh waters (Ref. 57403, 79590), with salinity range of 0.0-38.8 ppt (Ref. 97140). Maximum standard length reported 113 mm (= 145 mm TL)(Ref. 79590).

species.name: Frillgill conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on soft bottom of the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154) and shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Fringe-eyed flathead
species.description: Inhabits shallow rocky coastal areas frequently associated with seaweed beds and mangroves, most commonly at depths of less than 5 m (Ref. 9790).  Also found on sand bottoms (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Fringe-lipped worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottoms in vicinity of coral reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fringe-nose worm-eel
species.description: This species was collected by fishery otter trawl in the same haul with many macrourids, ophidiids, deep-sea shrimps and other demersal fishes that would suggest a benthic habit (Ref. 106137).

species.name: Fringe-scale round herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually inshore schooling fishes (Ref. 188).  Occurs in midwater in bays, inlets and coastal waters (Ref. 9563).  Also often found around shallow offshore reefs (Ref. 33617).

species.name: Fringechin dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from silty sand and rubble in  27 m depth in the lagoon (Ref. 75638).

species.name: Fringed blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral reefs.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Fringed cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fringed darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on aquatic insect immatures, including midge and caddisfly larvae and mayfly nymphs, and crustaceans, such as isopods, amphipods, and small crayfishes (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Fringed pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fringed sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 6885).  Occurs on soft bottom.

species.name: Fringed stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Fringed-lipped peninsula carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers above tidal reaches and culture ponds (Ref. 41236).  Mainly herbivorous, feeding on diatoms, blue-green and green algae, higher aquatic plants, insects and detritus (Ref. 4832).  Spawning occurs during the southwest monsoon in the Western Ghats (Ref. 44177).

species.name: Fringefin trevally
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, sometimes in estuaries or river mouths (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Fringelip blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow protected reefs, usually in intertidal areas (Ref. 9710).  Often seen in tidepools (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fringelip dwarf flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in shallow water of the surge zone (Ref. 58302). Females mature as small as 2.7 cm (Ref. 89467).

species.name: Fringelip flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble areas of  lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  The species buries itself in the sand for camouflage.  Feeds on crabs and prawns, also on fishes. Also found in sandy fringe of coral reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Fringelip rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats exposed to waves and intertidal shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Fringelip snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms of inshore waters.  Burrowing species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Friture
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 2683).  Semipelagic, remains near the bottom during the day and moves up to the open water at night (Ref. 5377, 57395).  Occasionally enters lagoons and estuaries at start of sexual maturation (Ref. 57395).  Occurs over sandy and muddy bottoms.  Feeds on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 5535).

species.name: Friture rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on littoral mud and sand bottoms to about 60 m depth (Ref. 57394).  Often enters estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 7375) during reproduction (Ref. 57394).  Feeds on fish, shrimps, mollusks, plankton and detritus (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Frog shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by crab pot and bottom longline (Ref. 50224).

species.name: Froghead eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Frogmouth sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Frontilabrus caeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimen was reared from May 3, 1985 to July 22, 1986 in an aquarium at the Musée de Zoologie de l'Université de la Ville de Nancy.

species.name: Frosted snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the seagrass areas, commonly amongst blackened dead Amphibolus seagrass leaves in collective areas in Western Port (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Frostfin cardinalfish
species.description: Adults form small schools in estuaries and sheltered bays with soft-bottom habitat to depths of 25 m (Ref. 48635). Usually seen among sponges, crinoids, or Diadema urchins in weedy areas. Eggs are incubated orally (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fryer's false moray
species.description: Benthic within rock crevices (Ref. 58302).  A specimen was collected from 0-1.5 m depth (Ref. 7490).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Frère Jacques
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from shallow coral reefs to offshore deeper waters (Ref. 3724).  A nocturnal species aggregating around coral reefs and deeper rocky reefs (Ref. 3724).  Feeds mainly on planktonic organisms (Ref. 3724).  Occasionally found swimming upside down (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh but not popular as a food fish (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Fuelleborn's labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on the bottom (Ref. 4967). Mud and vegetable debris found in stomach; caught near shores and in open water (Ref. 98757). Seems to feed mainly on aufwuchs and plants, but probably takes small animals such as insects as well; nothing is known about the breeding habits (Ref. 27292). May ascend rivers to spawn (Ref. 4967) but this has not been reported (Ref. 27292).

species.name: Fuelleborn's mouthbrooder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fuelleborn's squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swampy areas of lakes (Ref. 4967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Fuentesi's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on mollusks, benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Fuerte silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fugitive blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fuller's cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear water streams; the substrate with fine white sand, gravel, sunken roots and wood as well as leaf litter. It occurs only in the open water bodies (Ref. 124435).

species.name: Fundulopanchax avichang
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in  small temporary pools of the river Ecucu drainage systems (Ref. 44365).

species.name: Fundulopanchax gresensi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulopanchax intermittens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulopanchax kamdemi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. According to Kamdem Toham (1992) the species generally lives in the shallow swampy pools at the edge of small creeks under forest cover. These pools, up to 35 cm in depth, are partly covered with a layer of fallen leaves under which the fishes in the pools take cover (Ref. 58752).

species.name: Fundulopanchax mirabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small streams in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax moensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulopanchax ndianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and swampy parts of brooks in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Bottom spawner, 1 month incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax oeseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax powelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulopanchax puerzli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and shallow, swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish. Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax robertsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax rubrolabialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools, raphia swamps and swampy parts of slow flowing brooks in the swampy rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, X months incubation.  Very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax scheeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small streams in the coastal rainforest and forested savanna, mainly in waters on tertiary sedimentary soil (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax spoorenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Bottom spawner, 5 months incubation.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulopanchax traudeae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulopanchax walkeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, pools, brooks and small streams in the coastal rainforest and forested savanna (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Fundulus philpisteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fundulus saguanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Furcina osimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs.

species.name: Furcodontichthys novaesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Furneaux scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on reef areas (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Furrowed soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Furry coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which inhabits muddy bottoms of the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Furry whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Feeds on crustaceans and molluscs (Ref. 44075).

species.name: Fuscotaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widespread but uncommon (Ref. 55922).  Usually solitary in shallow, vegetated areas and in the intermediate sand-rock habitat (Ref. 5595, 55922).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Fushun gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Fusiform sculpin
species.description: inhabits muddy bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Fusilier capricorne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas, primarily around coral reefs at a depth of about 20 m.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Rare species (Ref. 6639).

species.name: Fusilier de Marr
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs (Ref. 58652) and appears to prefer clear waters of oceanic islands or reefs far from large land masses.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Also caught by drive-in nets.  Used as tuna baitfish.

species.name: Fusilier de Randall
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs in school.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Easily recognized from a distance by the bright yellow marking (Ref. 48636).  Also caught by drive-in nets.

species.name: Fusilier de Suez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas, primarily on coral reefs.  Forms large midwater aggregations and feeds on zooplankton.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: Fusilier marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily a near-shore pelagic species (Ref. 30573), but swims mainly in open water away from reefs (Ref. 48636).  Forms dense aggregations (Ref. 90102).  Mixed with other planktivores and is easily overlooked.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 30573).  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Caught at night using lights and dip nets (Ref. 30573).  Important tuna bait fish in some countries (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Fusilier strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas, primarily around coral reefs.  Forms aggregations in midwater and feeds on zooplankton.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: Fusilier à bande large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal, lagoon, and seaward areas around coral reefs (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Maximum length observed in the field estimated at about 20-25 cm TL (Ref. 74965).

species.name: Fusilier à bandes variées
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep lagoons and seaward reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Forms schools with other caesionids.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Juveniles used as tuna bait fish.

species.name: Fusilier à deux bandes jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal areas, primarily around coral reefs (Ref. 402), turning bright red (Ref. 48636).  Feed on zooplankton in midwater aggregations (Ref. 402).  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: Fusilier à dos jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep lagoons and along seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), primarily around coral reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton in large midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: Fusilier à trois bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges widely around coral reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).

species.name: fusilier à une bande
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear coastal to outer reef slopes or drop-offs (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater aggregations.  Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402).  Caught mainly by drive-in-nets.

species.name: Fusilier élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas around coral reefs (Ref. 30573). Feeds on zooplankton in large midwater aggregations. Forms schools with members of the genus Pterocaesio. Oviparous, with numerous, small pelagic eggs (Ref. 402). Often mistaken for juveniles and easily overlooked because of small size (Ref. 48636). Also caught with drive-in nets. Utilized as tuna bait fish (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Futuna deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Féra
species.description: Lacustrine, in moderate depth. Feeds on insects in summer. Moves to deeper water in winter. Spawns in February in deep water over aquatic vegetation. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Férit
species.description: Lacustrine, in deep waters. Spawns on sand or mud at 35-40 m depth in January (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gabon clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the type locality at 1-2 m depth, where it was moderately common on and below shallow rocks covered with algae. Several members of the family Gobiidae are the most common other species in this habitat, including undescribed species (Ref. 119349).

species.name: Gabon jewelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small, mostly swampy brooks in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Gabon killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and brooks in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Gabriel's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the upper slope, over hard bottom (Ref. 4495, 4774).  Depth range from 150-700 m (Ref. 01371) and from 368-748 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Possibly a spring spawner with pelagic larvae (Ref. 4774).

species.name: Gadella brocca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella dancoheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella edelmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters (Ref. 26165).

species.name: Gadella filifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella molokaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in crevices of rocky habitats (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Gadella norops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the outer shelf to mid-slope depths.

species.name: Gadella obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella svetovidovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadella thysthlon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadicule argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large schools over mud, muddy sand, gravel and rock bottoms.  Feeds on small crustaceans and maybe worms.  Preyed upon by other valuable fish (Ref. 1371).  Spawns in the winter in the western Mediterranean and in the spring farther north (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gadicule argentée (Gadiculus thori)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Over muddy bottoms.  Spawns in spring.  Important prey for several commercial fish.

species.name: Gadomurène de Patagonie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells on the continental and insular shelves and slopes.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Gadomurène marbrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells on continental and insular shelves and slopes.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Gadomurène microcéphale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells on the continental shelf and slope.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Gadomurène petit oeil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells in continental and insular shelves and slopes.  Feeds on zooplankton. Synchronous spawner (Ref. 50743).

species.name: Gadomus capensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus colletti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus denticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus dispar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus filamentosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gadomus magnifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus melanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gadomus multifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagata dolichonema
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagata itchkeea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagata melanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagata pakistanica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagata sexualis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Gagata youssoufi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gagora catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries and tidal rivers.  Ascends rivers beyond tidal reach (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Gaidropsarus mauli
species.description: Found in hydrothermal vents (Ref. 129620).

species.name: Gal oya blue laubuka
species.description: Occurs mainly from the headwaters of the Gal basin in the Kotagama and Nilgala areas (194-294 m asl), with a single specimen collected from the headwaters of Hepola stream in Bibile, which drains to the Mahaweli River. Observed in streams and rivers, usually in groups of 5-10 individuals, close to the banks and occupying the upper level of the water column. Cyprinids commonly encountered with this species were Rasbora dandia, R. cf. microcephalus, Devario malabaricus, Dawkinsia singhala, Puntius bimaculatus, and P. dorsalis

species.name: Gal oya striped rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is a common fish found in both lotic and lentic habitats, usually in groups of more than 10 individuals. Occurs close to the bank, occupying the upper levels of the water column. Associated species frequently encountered with this species include R. dandia, Devario malabaricus, Dawkinsia singhala, Puntius bimaculatus, Puntius dorsalis and Laubuka species (Ref. 123756).

species.name: Galactacma scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rubble areas of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Galame rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs, usually in areas with mixed coral, sand, and rubble (Ref. 9710). Young common on silty reefs, usually along edges with algae-rubble and sand (Ref. 48636). Juveniles are secretive. Individuals often solitary and mainly on sand and rubble substrata near coral reefs, but more common in protected than exposed areas, generally at depths less than 20 m. (Ref. 117607). Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled invertebrates, including mollusks, crustaceans and sea urchins (Ref. 5374).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Caught on hook-and-line with some frequency, this species is marketed in small numbers. Occasionally seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 9823).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Galapagos barnacle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in empty barnacle shells.  Often perches in the opening with only the head protruding.  Seldom seen in the open.  Darts out to nab bits of floating food (Ref. 5227).  Oviparous (Ref. 56066).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56066).

species.name: Galapagos blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, weed-covered reefs (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Galapagos blue-banded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Tiny, bold and aggressive fish (Ref. 28023) which lives in small recesses of rocky reefs, slopes and walls (Ref. 5227).  Feeds on various small crustaceans (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Galapagos clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in small recesses on rocky reefs, slopes and walls, clinging to rocky substrates (Ref. 5227) in the surge zones (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Galapagos cuskeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Inhabits rocky crevices; cave species (Ref. 27297).

species.name: Galapagos damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently this species prefers open water near drop-offs, although individuals are found in a variety of inshore habitats to depths of 30 meters. It is not a common species and resident aggregations have strong preferences for specific sites. Feeds mainly on plankton in the water column, usually in heterotypic aggregations with Chromis atrilobata. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Prior to the 1982-83 El Niño, a small aggregation frequented the shallow water just west of Pinnacle Rock at Bartolomé. But despite intensive observations during the decade after this event, no records of this species were made (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Galapagos garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clean sand.  Found in large colonies.  Feeds on plankton.

species.name: Galapagos grey skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Galapagos gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in sand-rubble bottoms near rocky reef areas.

species.name: Galapagos jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms.  Feeds on benthic and planktonic invertebrates.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Galapagos mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools over sandy bottoms.  Fees mainly on detritus and algae, but also on insects, fish eggs, and plankton.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Galapagos porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand-rubble bottoms adjacent to reefs (Ref. 11482).  Its strong molariform teeth are well adapted for crushing crabs, clams, and snails (Ref. 28023).  An important food fish.

species.name: Galapagos razorfish
species.description: Inhabits open sand slopes; adults usually share this habitat with Heteroconger klausewitzi.

species.name: Galapagos snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in sand flats and rocky areas mixed with boulders, gravel rubble and sand.  Can bury and move beneath sand or gravel rubble (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Galapagos triplefin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in rocky reefs, boulder strewn slopes and walls (Ref. 5227).  Males occupy territories of less than 50 cm diameter, on vertical or overhanging rock faces, from November through February.  Females leave the territory after spawning, but the male continues to court and to spawn with other females in his territory while guarding the previously spawned egg masses from predators like wrasses and gobies (Ref. 28023).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Galathea assfish
species.description:
A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Of the 22 examined specimens 16 are
males, including a 55.5 crn SL specimen with spent testes. One of the six females measuring  23.2 cm SL had fully ripe ovaries with eggs of about 0.5 mm in diameter. These were caught on or near the bottom mostly at slope depths but also extending into the abyss. Identifiable contents from the digestive tract found in six specimens include scales and vertebrae from fish, dorsal felt from polychaetes and remains of crustaceans (Ref. 84269).

species.name: Galathea cuskeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The previous maximum depth reported was 8730 m, supposedy the deepest fish caught. However there was a mistake in the logbook of the station, the correct depht is now 7965 m, the third deepes fish 9as of Novemeber 2023 (Ref. 130003).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family being oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Galathea gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits marine waters, but enters (and presumably breeding in) freshwater (Ref. 4832).  A filter-feeder.  More data needed.

species.name: Galathea sand dart
species.description: Members of this family burrow in shallow marine to estuarine areas with fine coral sand or muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 48316).  Of no commercial interest but may be taken incidentally (Ref. 48316).

species.name: Galathea sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Maximum depth reported at 594 m (Ref. 58018). Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Galaxias anomalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams.  Preys on invertebrates (Ref. 27776).

species.name: Galaxias cobitinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias depressiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams.  Preys on invertebrates (Ref. 27776).

species.name: Galaxias eldoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias globiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias gollumoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias macronasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected mainly from small gravelly riffles in small streams. This fish appears to be cryptic (Ref. 75601).

species.name: Galaxias neocaledonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias platei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxias pullus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galaxy rasbora
species.description: Inhabits small and shallow ponds, at most 30 cm deep and maintained by seepage or springs. The water is clear unless roiled with water temperatures of 22-24°C in January 2007. The ponds have luxuriant submerged aquatic vegetation mainly one or two species of Elodea or Anacharis (Hydrocharitaceae). Present terrestrial vegetation is open grassland. Three other species were collected in the ponds, a Microrasbora similar to M. rubescens; a small species of Yunnanilus; and a piscivorous snakehead, Channa harbourtbutleri (Ref. 57973).

species.name: Gale's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rubble bottom of inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Male may be brooding at 3.65 cm SL.

species.name: Galeichthys troworum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. inhabits the relatively warm, shallow coastal waters of the east coast of South Africa, and is not known to enter estuaries.  Reported to likely to utilize both rocky reef and soft substratum environments and is probably inactive by day, remaining in caves and other forms of refuge offered by reefs. Reported to feed on small fish and crabs and preyed on by a large variety of sharks. Gut contents in several prepared specimens (for osteological study) contained substantial amounts of crustaceans (prawn and crab) as well as small fish. Two females (43.5 and 45.0 cm SL) had more than 50 ripe eggs in each ovary, measuring up to approximately 1.7 cm in diameter.   Reported to at least to 57 cm (questionably in TL) and 58 cm FL, from a survey of shore anglers (Ref. 85159).

species.name: Galeocharax gulo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galeocharax humeralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galeocharax knerii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galeus antillensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galeus corriganae
species.description: Size vary with 3 juveniles at 20.3-27.1 cm TL, 4 adolescent males at 28.2-37.2 cm TL and a single female 27.8 cm TL (Ref. 116735).

species.name: Galibi tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galjoen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters and rivers.  Feeds on mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).  Flesh of excellent quality (Ref. 6082).

species.name: Galjoin franc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reefs, rocky and sandy areas.  Feeds on mollusks, crustaceans, and other invertebrates (Ref. 5213).  Abundant in winter, breeding occurs in deeper water.  Becoming scarce because of overfishing (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Galzin podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Galápagos batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms and believed to be predatory, feeding on small invertebrates.  Common below 10 m and seem to be incautious, unlike other batfishes which are limited in their range due to many predators.

species.name: Galápagos four-eyed blenny
species.description: Intertidal, actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).  With acute vision to detect prey in the air (Ref. 94105).  Treks on land as far as 30 m from the sea which it can remarkably carry on due to its physical adaptive modifications like, laterally flattened corneas to avoid myopia and thickening and filament enlargement of the gills for respiration out of water.  Feeds on insects and shore crabs.

species.name: Galápagos sheephead wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in both shallow and deep waters.  Its strong dentition makes it an opportunistic predator, even of hard-shelled benthos as shown by its stomach contents of coarse calcareous remains and detritus (Ref. 11295).

species.name: Gambusie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant in lower reaches of streams (Ref. 44091).  Adults inhabit standing to slow-flowing water; most common in vegetated ponds and lakes, backwaters and quiet pools of streams.  Found frequently in brackish water (Ref. 5258).  Pelagic and surface predatory fish (Ref. 94816).  Feed on zooplankton, small insects and detritus (Ref. 5258, 10294).  Used as live food for carnivorous aquarium fishes.  Viviparous (Ref. 5258, 30578).  Effective in mosquito control and widely introduced, but found to compete with indigenous fish and to upset the ecological balance (Ref. 6351).

species.name: Gamtoos redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pseudobarbus swartzi inhabits perennial mountain streams with clear or peat stained water as well as cobble, pebbles and boulders (Ref. 114782). Remnant populations of the species are under severe threat from multiple human impacts including habitat degradation, complete water abstraction and potential invasion by alien fish predators and competitors that are now dominant in mainstream sections of the rivers (Ref. 114782).

species.name: Ganges river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and pools.  More data needed.

species.name: Ganges river sprat
species.description: Occurs in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4832).  Also found in coastal areas of Bay of Bengal (Ref. 45255).  Depth estimate based on ecology.

species.name: Ganges stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Also found in shallow bays and estuaries in the Bay of Bengal.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Gangetic ailia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found in large rivers and connected waters.  They inhabit surface to mid-waters.  Occur in shoals (Ref. 4833).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gangetic gagata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Gangetic hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species, but also found in estuaries and presumably tolerating some salinity.  Adults feed mainly on mysids and small prawns (reduced feeding during breeding), juveniles mainly on copepods.  Possibly breeds throughout the year, with peaks in October and November (Hooghly at Barrackpore) or March-May (Ganges at Allahabad).  Its large size makes it an attractive foodfish.

species.name: Gangetic koi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, ponds, ditches and paddy fields.  Able to live out of water for protracted period.

species.name: Gangetic latia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit streams and rivers (Ref. 1479).  Found over gravel and stony bottom of mountain streams (Ref. 51717). Observation reports this species in a variety of microhabitats in a headwater stream in the Ganges River basin, with stronger preference for pools. Spawning in a Himalayan population reported to occur from July to September, possibly triggered by high turbidity and stream velocities from seasonal rains. Food consists of macrophytes, algae, and diatoms (Ref. 127037).

species.name: Gangetic leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur frequently in ditches and inundated fields.  Common in summer months when it is collected from dried-up beds of tanks, beels, bheries and others.  Found most commonly in standing or sluggish waters of lakes, reservoirs or canals (Ref. 12693).  Feed on aquatic insects and fishes (Ref. 12693).  A high-prized fish and sold fresh.

species.name: Gangetic loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hill streams (Ref. 4832) and mainstream rivers (Ref. 58784).  A carnivorous species which feeds on insect larvae and benthic organisms (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Gangetic mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tidal rivers and lakes; also beels, canals, ditches, ponds, and inundated fields.  Its pectoral spine can cause painful wounds (Ref. 4833).
