Found in the basin-wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gangetic scissortail rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gangetic sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Gangfisch
species.description: Lacustrine, midwater along shores. Feeds on insects and plankton (Ref. 59043). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are buried in unguarded nests (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gaoligong mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gaouta-roussa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are pelagic occurring near shore, entering lagoons and lower reaches of rivers in schools; often in polluted waters (Ref. 51442, 59043) between temperatures 8-24°C.  Juveniles colonize the littoral zone and estuaries (Ref. 51442).  Adults feed on epiphytic algae, detritus and small benthic or planktonic organisms, pelagic eggs and larvae while juveniles feed on zooplankton until about 3.0 cm SL, then on benthic animals and plants (Ref. 59043).  Spawning takes place at sea near the coast between September and February (Ref. 30578, 51442).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Adults undergo migrations (Ref. 51442).

species.name: Gaper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in great shoals.  Moves to the surface at night.  Minimum depth range from Ref. 121941.

species.name: Garcette petit-oeil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Garcette sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diurnal migration. Feeds mainly on copepods, appendicularians, euphausiids, pteropods, chaetognaths and cephalopods (Ref. 45488).

species.name: Garcette-goitre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Sometimes caught in large aggregations.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6345).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 5951).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 117245.

species.name: Garde-boue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit ephemeral areas that dry out over summer and autumn months, where they aestivate in damp areas or under tree roots and logs (Ref. 43717).  Spawn all throughout the year (Ref. 33843).

species.name: Garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in colony, on sloping sand bottom (Ref. 33408).

species.name: Gardner's butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep reefs below 25 m, rarely as shallow as 15 m (Ref. 9710).  Found in East Indian region at 2-40 m (Ref. 90102).  Paired or in groups (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gardon galant
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits deep waters of large, subalpine lakes and large to medium sized rivers.  Occurs in small groups.  Feeds in invertebrates, algae and detritus.  Moves to shallow parts of rivers to spawn (Ref. 59043). Threatened due to overfishing and construction of weirs, which block access to spawning sites (Ref. 59043) and the introduction of two alien species (European roach, <i>Rutilus rutilus and  European nase, <i>Chondrostoma nasus) (Ref. 96829).  Sexual maturity is attained at age 3+ or 4+ in males and 5+ in females at about 28-33 cm SL. Spawning occurs in April and May (Ref. 96829).  Reaches a maximum size of about 45 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gargantuan blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in the surge zone of rocky and coral reefs less than 6 m deep (Ref. 529, 9710, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Gargare la lumière à pectorales courtes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A meso- to bathypelagic (Ref. 85782).  One record at 4,631m deep (Ref. 78616).

species.name: Gargare noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic to bathypelagic species (Ref. 6944, 28429).  Specimens larger than 4.5 cm are more frequently collected between 730 and 1900 m with shallowest record being 150 m, the deepest 3900 m (mean 1390 m).  Juveniles are found in shallower water, from 0 to 1,050 m (mean 542 m), with the smallest specimens (>10.0 mm) collected nearest to the surface (Ref. 82429).  Feed on  whole fish, often of individuals longer than themselves (Ref. 9686).  Most specimens were taken at depths greater than 750 m (Ref. 6649).

species.name: Gargoyle cusk
species.description: A benthopelagic species at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gargoyle fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally demersal on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Garlanded rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal, found in rocky shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Garman's lanternfish
species.description: Meso- and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Pseudoceanic, at 325-750 m by day and nyctoepipelagic at surface to 125 m at night (with maximum abundance at 100 m) (Ref. 4479). Lipid content is 8.7 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 1.7 in total lipids (Ref. 9193). Often appears with sergestid shrimp Sergia spp., marine hatchetfishes Argyropelecus spp. and Polyipnus spp. (Ref 39633). Specimens reach sexual maturity at a length of 4 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Garmot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal marine waters and brackish estuaries (Ref. 3791); also found in hyper-saline lagoons and may enter freshwater (Ref. 5217).  Never far from the sea (Ref. 3791).  Form sizeable schools (Ref. 3791).  Appear to undergo trophic migrations along the coasts (Ref. 35237).  Feed on organic detritus and filamentous algae (Ref. 9626).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawn several million eggs (Ref. 35237) at sea (Ref. 3791).  Also caught with beach nets (Ref. 5217).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 5217).  The roe is marketed salt-pickled  and dried and considered a delicacy (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Garnet lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559).

species.name: Garnet minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Garnet sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Garnet tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plants.  In captivity, spawning takes place among plants and eggs usually hatch in 20 to 24 hours (Ref. 7020).  Maximum length reported to reach 4.5 cm TL (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Garo spineless eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Garpique alligator
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des lepisosteidae. Adults inhabit sluggish pools and backwaters of large rivers, swamps, bayous, and lakes.  Rarely enter brackish and marine waters (Ref. 5723).  Feed on blue crabs, turtles, waterfowl or other birds and small mammals (Ref. 10294).  Giant of the gars (Ref. 5723).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Garpique cubain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and lakes. Adults feed on other freshwater fishes and even birds. Young are preyed on by introduced Micropterus salmoides. The flesh is edible; but the eggs are poisonous to eat.

species.name: Garpique longnez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in sluggish pools, backwaters and oxbows of medium to large rivers, and lakes (Ref. 10294).  Usually found near vegetation.  Occasionally found in brackish waters.  Spawning occur in freshwater and possibly slightly brackish water (Ref. 4639).  Migrate up rivers during the spawning season (Ref. 4639).  Eggs and larvae are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 4639).  Voracious predator, feeding on various fishes and crustaceans.  The roe is poisonous.

species.name: Garpique tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in quiet, clear pools and backwaters of lowland creeks, small to large rivers, oxbow lakes, swamps and sloughs.  Occasionally enter brackish waters.  A voracious predator feeding on various kinds of fishes and crustaceans.

species.name: Garra nepalensis

Other fishes collected include Schizothorax richardsonii (Gray), Barilius bendelisis (Hamilton), Naziritor cheilynoides (McClelland) and Tor tor (Hamilton). The following physico-chemical parameters were taken in the sampling site on 11 April 2014: air temperature 20ºC, water temperature 23ºC, pH 7.2, dissolved oxygen 7.9 mg/l, conductivity 021 μs, and total dissolved solids 163 ppm in 2 pm at noon (Ref. 118052).

species.description: Inhabits medium to large dark to grayish brown boulders along the river banks with heavy sand deposits. The river with cool and clear, fast to moderate running water, the bed consists of flat boulders, pebbles, cobbles covered by slime algae, and somewhere heavy sand deposits. The river banks and uphill with small to large trees and shrubs. Associated species collected at the type locality includes Garra kalpangi, Tor putitora, Neolissochilus hexagonolepis, Barilius bendelisis, Schizothorax richardsonii, Chagunius chagunio, Aborichthys cataracta, Psilorhynchus balitora, and Schistura sp. (Ref. 119513).

species.name: Garra rezai
species.description: Found in April 2016 in a spring in Boein-e-Olia (Iran), which was about 2-3 meters wide, the outflowing stream had a low velocity and the bed was covered by gravel. When the place was revisited in June 2021, the species could not be found anymore in the spring, but specimens were collected from the stream Boein-e-Sofla (which is fed by the spring). At the type locality (Boein-e-Olia spring and Boein-e-Sofla stream), the species was not found, but G. rufa is widespread in the Lesser Zab drainage, including the Chooman River drainage. In Turkey, all three sampling sites were shallow, with clear and swiftly flowing water and cobbles and pebbles substrate. Among the three sampling sites, Çıratan was visited several times during different seasons and this species is abundant in its Turkish distribution area. This stream hosts several regionally endemic species, such as Turcinoemacheilus kosswigi. Paracobitis zabgawraensis, Glyptothorax daemon, and G. kurdistanicus (Ref. 124212). In Çıratan, two adult individuals of G. rufa were found, one half-grown individual in the stream Büyük, both were syntopic with G. rezai (Ref. 128981).

The river banks consist of shrubs, small trees, and larger trees somewhere, with the river water clear and cool. Associated fish collected in the type locality belongs to genus Bangana, Labeo, Barilius, Devario and Chagunius (Ref. 110172).

species.name: Gaterin rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inner and outer reef lagoons, usually in caves along steep slopes.  Juveniles in shallow lagoons or protected shallow reefs (Ref. 48635).  During the day, occurs under coral ledges of channel and outer reef slopes (Ref. 37816). Solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Gaterin rayé (Plectorhinchus plagiodesmus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal, generally turbid reefs (Ref. 9710).  Adults in coral crevices with protruding lips looking like orange sponge.  Frequently in pairs (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Gaterin à bandes diagonales
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep inner to outer reef habitats (Ref. 48635).  Occurs singly or in aggregations along coral slopes of clear lagoon and seaward reefs.  Juveniles solitary on shallow protected reefs (Ref. 48635).  Generally nocturnal, feeding on benthic invertebrates in open sand flats and seagrass beds at night and conspicuously rests during the day (Ref. 9710, 90102).  At Palau, it aggregates to spawn around new moon (Ref. 37816). Taken by handline and spear. Marketed fresh, a small quantity is salted (Ref. 47695).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Gaurochromis obtusidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over shallow water with a soft mud bottom. A few specimens have been caught over sand (Ref. 4983). Feeds mainly on insects (esp. larval Diptera) and mollusks ( particularly the bivalve Corbicula, although some gastropods like Melanoides are also eaten (Ref. 558).

The stomach contents of one specimen taken from the Rio Asisa include adult dipterans, including one whole individual of Sciaridae and large wing fragment of a Ceratopogonidae.  Matures at 1.5-2.2 cm SL.

The well-developed penis and reported presence of numerous spermatophores in histologically examined testes indicate internal fertilization. Eggs are found up 1 mm in diameter, but embryos were not observed (Ref. 105129). Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Geminate dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef slopes and coralline blocks.  Collected by ichthyocide, the female from a shallow slope of a fringing reef with coral patches, 5-12 m, at the seaward side of the island, the male at about 12 m from the opposite side, with a steep slope down to 30-40 m (Ref. 94740).

species.name: Gendarme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Herring schools move between spawning and wintering grounds in coastal areas and feeding grounds in open water by following migration patterns learned from earlier year classes (Ref. 88171). Juveniles (up to 2 years) shoal close inshore, while adults are found more offshore (Ref. 6683). Adults spend the day in deeper water, but rise to shallower water at night (Ref. 89562). Light is an important factor in controlling their vertical distribution. A facultative zooplanktivorous filter-feeder, i.e., it can switch to filter-feeding if the food density and particle size are appropriate (Ref. 28664).  Feed mainly on copepods finding food by visual sense.  Herring schools often attract predators such as fish, birds, and marine mammals (Ref. 89563). Schooling, silvery sides, excellent hearing (capable of detecting frequencies between 30-4,000 Hz , Refs. 89391, 89564, 89566), and very fast escape response act as anti-predator devices (Ref. 28664).  The most important races in the East Atlantic are the winter-spawning Norwegian and Icelandic herring, the autumn spawning Icelandic and North Sea herring and the Baltic Sea herring. Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked, canned and frozen; can be fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

Unlike the Tatia which lives mostly in estuaries, G. leopardum appears to live mainly in the upstream portion of rivers (Ref. 35381).

Adults feed mainly on pelagic crustaceans: Euphausia superba, Hyperiella antarctica, Euphausia crystallorophias and other amphipods (Ref. 5192). Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 41551).

Found in tidepools and rocky shores, solitary or  in small groups (Ref. 90102).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ghost candiru
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is rheophilic.  Dwells on patches of loose sand where water flow forms ephemeral sand ripples.  Diurnal and mostly visually oriented, forages on aquatic immature benthic insects (dipterans and coleopterans).  Moves along the ripple grooves while scanning the bottom back and forth, alternating between adjacent grooves.  Feeding activity peaks at late morning and afternoon.  When disturbed buries in the sand, and at night remains buried.  Seasonal reproduction indicated by mature females caught in the wet months (Ref. 52491).

species.name: Ghost cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in reef flats and shallow lagoons, but hiding by day within Acropora thickets and other corals, as well as in holes and crevices and emerging at night to forage on free-swimming invertebrates (Ref. 1602). Also found in sheltered seaward slopes in 1-20 m (Ref 90102). Feeds on small fishes and benthic invertebrates (e.g. shrimps - alpheids and penaieds; isopods, copepods, crab larvae, polychaete worms); relatively close to cover, within about 1-2 m (Ref. 11890).

species.name: Ghost Catfish

species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Inhabit exposed sandy shorelines in only a foot or two of water, and also the bare sand bottom adjacent to patch reefs (Ref. 5521).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ghost flathead

species.name: Ghost goby

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deeper slope waters (Ref. 4426).  Feed on cephalopods, mysids and small bony fishes (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ghost velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble areas of seaward reefs (Ref. 34765).  Minimum depth from Ref. 49352. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ghostly grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Ghostly scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Giant barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in large rivers and seasonally in canals and floodplains (Ref. 12693).  Adults prefer big pools in the Mekong at least part of the year while juveniles are mostly seen in swamps and small tributaries, from where they are sometimes collected and stocked in ponds (Ref. 37770).  The young can acclimatize to live in ponds, canals and swamps.  A migratory species (Ref. 37772).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Young individuals occur in October in the lower Mekong basin (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on algae, phytoplankton and fruits of inundated terrestrial plants (Ref. 12693) and detritus (Ref. 58784).  Its numbers have declined seriously.  Individual fishes rarely survive to reach reproductive maturity.  Its catch should be strictly regulated by size.  A very desirable food fish, sometimes eaten fresh or pickled (Ref. 12693). Maximum length of 300 cm needs confirmation.  Threatened due to over harvesting and habitat loss (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Giant betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a murky stream, up to 1.2 m deep and pH 7.5. The stream water was sluggish and drained from cultivated area upstream (Ref. 81926).  Seen only in local markets.  Mouth brooder (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Giant boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  Feeds mainly on benthic organisms (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Giant bully
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal seas.

species.name: Giant cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits near-shore surface waters.  Firm flesh is highly valued (Ref. 4967).  Largest African cichlid (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Giant clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rock pools, larger individuals found in subtidal area. Usually attached to seaweeds (Cystophora, Macrocystis and Lessonia), sometimes on rocks and boulder in areas with dense seaweed. Remains motionless when the pool is disturbed.

species.name: Giant danio
species.description: Adults inhabit hill streams up to an elevation of 300 m (Ref. 4832).  Found in shaded, mid-hill clear waters with pebble or gravel substrates (Ref. 11966).  They occur in schools at the surface in small high-gradient upland streams (Ref. 12693).  They feed mainly on exogenous insects (Ref. 12693) and also on worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Not seen in markets, but popular in aquarium trade (Ref. 12693, 44325).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Giant featherback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainstreams and forest streams (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on fishes, probably has a crepuscular or nocturnal activity pattern (Ref. 12693).  Other food of this species includes insects and small vertebrates (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Giant freshwater whipray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in estuaries and large rivers (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693) and fishes (Ref. 32457).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught occasionally by demersal gillnet and longline fisheries operating in riverine and estuarine areas. Utilized for its meat and possibly its cartilage (Ref.58048). Marketed fresh, with large individuals being sold in cut pieces by the kilogram (Ref. 12693).  Size reaches to about 500 cm TL.  Threatened due to over harvesting and pollution (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Giant glassfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in relatively large rivers characterized by high turbidity .  Feeds primarily on small fishes, prawns (Ref. 5259, 44894) and crustaceans.  Breeds in the dry season (June-July) (Ref. 44894).  Is the largest member of the family (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Giant grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young apparently bathypelagic to some degree but become bathydemersal at a size of 50-60 cm (Ref. 1371).  Adults feed mainly on cephalopods, fish and shrimps; other food items include ctenophores, echinoderms, worms, crabs, and amphipods (Ref. 1371).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Giant gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits rivers, creeks and billabongs, usually in quiet o slowly flowing water among vegetation, around log debris or undercut banks.  A nocturnal carnivore, feeds on fishes, crustaceans, and aquatic insects (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Giant hagfish
species.description: Largest known hagfish.

species.name: Giant Haplochromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms with swards of Vallisneria.  Feeds by scraping epiphytic algae from the leaves, grasping a leaf in its mouth and working along it (Ref. 267).

species.name: Giant hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimens reach 9.0 cm TL (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; may jump out of the aquarium; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Giant jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms.  Feeds on benthic and planktonic invertebrates.  Often caught by trawlers and anglers.

species.name: Giant kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal and to 40 m (Ref. 96339). Found among rocks with large seaweeds, often in kelp.  Young occur in schools while adults are solitary.  Feeds on small crustaceans, mollusks and small fishes.  Female attaches eggs to seaweeds, male guards them.

species.name: Giant killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Giant kokopu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Giant lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Giant leptocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Giant mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sea, estuaries, and lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 4833).  Commonly found on muddy shores in estuaries and in the tidal zone of rivers (Ref. 12693).  Lives in burrows in the mud and emerges on sunny days at low tide.  Moves quickly across the mud, but can be caught with entangling nets strung above the ground or with cast-nets tossed onto the exposed mud (Ref. 12693).  An amphibious air-breather that actively shuttles back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184). Gulps air at the surface of its burrow and then transports the air to the bottom of the burrow in order to aerate its eggs; preys upon fiddler crabs, insects and worms (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Giant pangasius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers.  Juveniles are found in larger tributaries (Ref. 58784). Both young and adults feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 12693).  Larger individuals have been known to feed on carcasses of fowl or dog (which are commonly used for bait) (Ref. 7432).  A migratory species (Ref. 37772).  Spawns just before the rainy season and the young of the year reach a length of about 10 cm by mid-June (Ref. 12693).  Fishery used to be accompanied by rites and ceremonies of a religious nature (Ref 2686).  Important food fish and is often referred to in textbooks and popular press or news media (Ref. 4537).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Threatened due to over harvesting, habitat loss and pollution (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Giant prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty inshore bottoms, deep coastal mud slopes and also occurs in estuaries in muddy channels (Ref. 48637).  Also found in sand bottoms of lagoons and sheltered reefs in 5-30 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Giant pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes in caves and crevices in 57-73 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Giant redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reproduction is unknown, but spawning possibly occurs around November-December, based on the observation that males had large tubercles; juveniles and sub-adults probably feed by picking prey or algae from rock; adults have more predatory lifestyle and are possibly water column feeders (Ref. 93872).

species.name: Giant river-catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, canals, beels, ditches, inundated fields and other freshwater areas.  Adults fight well and provide good sport.  Carnivore.  Breeding occurs before the commencement of monsoons.  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same genus (Ref. 205).

species.name: Giant salmon carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainstreams of middle reaches in deep rocky rapids. Juveniles occur in tributaries (Ref. 58784). A large fast-swimming predator, feeding on fish of the middle and the upper water levels. Although most common along the Thai-Lao border at the mouth of the Mun River, its numbers have drastically decreased in recent years. This is perhaps due to dam construction or excessive gill netting, to which active pursuit predators, like this species, are particularly vulnerable (Ref. 12693). Undertakes upstream migration at the same time as Probarbus sp. in December-February (Ref. 37770) which may be related to spawning activity (Ref. 9497). Attains over 30 kg (Ref. 9497).

species.name: Giant sand stargazer
species.description: Sand dweller on protected beaches and near-shore sites in less than 5 m.

species.name: Giant sawbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Giant sharkminnow
species.description: Occurs from midwater to bottom depth in large and medium sized rivers.  Does not persist in impoundments.  Occurs regularly in fisheries of the middle and lower Mekong.  Used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Giant shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and offshore, from the intertidal to offshore continental and insular shelves (Ref. 9909).  Adults are found offshore waters while young individuals are found inshore on sand flats, around atolls, and in mangrove swamps (Ref. 6871).  Feeds on shellfish, mainly on prawns and crabs (Ref. 9909, Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Maturity size at 150-180 cm TL; born at 38-40 cm TL (Ref. 114953).  Reported to live and breed permanently in fresh water (Ref. 6871).  Probably the major commercial guitarfish in the Western Central Pacific (Ref. 9909). Caught regularly by demersal tangle net fisheries operating throughout the area. Utilized for its meat, fins (both very high value), skin and cartilage (Ref.58048). Reported to attain a maximum length of 4 m (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Giant skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms of upper continental and insular slopes (Ref. 41299, Ref. 114953).  Feed on invertebrates and bony fishes (Ref. 9908, Ref. 114953).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 22.0-23.5 cm long and 14.0-14.5 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253). A male holotype reaches maturity at 135 cm TL, females at 115 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Giant stumptail stingray
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Giant sweetlips
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along outer reef slopes.  Adults usually solitary but may occur in pairs.  Juveniles in shallow turbid coastal areas (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Giant tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This deep-water tonguefish species is known only from the continental shelf and upper continental slope off northeastern and eastern Taiwan; from 471-640 m by research vessels.  Polychaetes, small crustaceans and some unidentified detritus were found in the digestive systems of fishes examined. Little else is known regarding the biology of this species (Ref. 82423).

species.name: Giant trahira
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An important food fish.

species.name: Giant triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gibara cave brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gibberfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Kasidoron, once given family status as Kasidoridae, is the larva of this species (Ref. 6993). Adults found at depths of 320 - 1,100 meters and larvae at 0 - 50 meters (Ref. 51655). Feeds on amphipods and copepods (Ref. 37039).

species.name: Gibberichthys latifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, bathy-, and benthopelagic species, mostly occurring over continental and island slopes.  Distinctive kasidoron larval and pre-juvenile stage in epipelagic waters.  Zooplankton pickers, with small crustaceans in stomachs of both pre-juveniles and adults.  Rare deep-sea fishes.

species.name: Gibbs' pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also seen in open sand and rubble areas (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gigantactis balushkini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males and larvae unknown (Ref. 43997).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gigantactis elsmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis gargantua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis gibbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 10761).

species.name: Gigantactis golovani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10761).

species.name: Gigantactis gracilicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis herwigi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis ios
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 3 specimens, the biggest of which is an adolescent female measuring 5.7 cm SL (Ref. 41361).

species.name: Gigantactis kreffti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gigantactis longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype collected in an open midwater trawl (Ref. 41361).  Maximum length based on an immature female (Ref. 41361).

species.name: Gigantactis longicirra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10761).

species.name: Gigantactis macronema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appear to be active predators which feed on midwater fishes, including Cyclothone acclinidens, Triphoturus mexicanus and Bathylagus stilbius; cephalopods like Vampyroteuthis; and various invertebrates like amphipods, natant decapod crustaceans and coelenterates (Ref. 4525). Maximum length for female from Ref. 41361.

species.name: Gigantactis meadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis microdontis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 8 specimens (Ref. 41361).

species.name: Gigantactis microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gigantactis perlatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Male unknown.

species.name: Gigantactis savagei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 6 specimens (Ref. 41361).

species.name: Gigantactis vanhoeffeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarely caught (Ref. 559).

species.name: Gigantactis watermani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Giganthias immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by handline from fairly deep water over rocky bottom.  Food fish.

species.name: Gigantura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Gila chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and undercut  banks of creeks and small rivers, usually near woody debris.  Also found in marshes.  Maximum length is presumably about 38 cm TL  (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Gila topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly occurred from Frisco Hot Spring, New Mexico, to near the mouth of the Gila River:  it was perhaps more widespread in spring-fed creeks and marshes of southern Arizona between 900 and 1500 m above sea level.  Inhabits vegetated springs and margins, pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Usually found in shallow, warm water.

species.name: Gila trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear and cool mountain creeks (above 2000 m elevation).  May bite when handled (Bob, pers. comm., 2006).

species.name: Gilbert & Cramer's bristle-mouth fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Gilbert's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In large aggregations among branching corals in sheltered lagoons and bays (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Gilbert's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit slow flowing, often turbid waters over mud or gravel bottoms.  Feed primarily on algae (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Small mouth equipped with rows of flattened teeth is suited fro scraping algae off rocks, wood and bottom litter (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7, H=8, 26°C water temperature, egg layer, peaceful community fish requiring rock and plant cover (Ref. 6398).  Not much is known of the biology (Ref. 2906).

species.name: Gilbert's halosaurid fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the middle and lower slope primarily above the 4°C isotherm.  Hovers within a few meters of substrate, parallel to it or inclined at varying angles (Ref. 6727).  Feeds on polychaetes, pelecypods, amphipods and other benthic prey (Ref. 6727).

species.name: Gilbert's Irish Lord
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gilbert's large lantern fish
species.description: Pseudoceanic, epibenthic species (Ref. 4479, 4775, 51024).  Bentho- and mesopelagic in nearshore areas at 0-550 m at night, 500-686 m during day (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Gilbertidia dolganovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gilbertidia pustulosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gilbertolus alatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gilbertolus atratoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gilbertolus maracaiboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamps or marshes of the lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Gilchrist's round herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the sea, but found mostly in estuaries; also found in landlocked brackish and freshwater lagoons (Ref. 93596), also rivers and lakes (Ref. 188). Maximum size 10 cm (Ref. 4967). Entire life cycle is completed in the estuary (Ref. 32693). Breeds throughout the year with a peak in spring and early summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Maturity may be attained within the first or second year and an age of up to 5 or 6 years is recorded (Ref. 7248, 52193). Feeds chiefly on zooplankton by filtering or selecting individual organisms from the water column (Ref. 7248, 52193). It can tolerate salinities under 4 ppt and of up to 52.6 ppt (Ref. 32693). Utilized fresh or dried and salted (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Gilchrist's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One known specimen.

species.name: Gilded catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens measuring 130 cm and weighing 50 kg are not rare. In the Amazon, this fish is found quite upstream, in the main bed of the big tributaries with muddy bottom (Ref. 35381). Mainly piscivorous, hunts at night, sometimes going into flood prone areas of rivers. Some migrations in pursuit of migrating Triportheus and Anodus have been reported. Sexually mature upon reaching 10 kg weight. The nursery ground is at the river mouths (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Gilded goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Forms schools in coastal waters.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 13710).

species.name: Gilded tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gill's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gill's molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in waters of all current velocities, but are more abundant in slack waters.  Very large individuals (up to 105 cm) are found in brackish water, while smaller individuals occur in brooks to an elevation of 1220 m.  Inhabit swamps, brooks and in shallow waters of large rivers, generally found near the substratum browsing on detritus, ooze and filamentous algae, reproduces throughout the year, but with a peak in juvenile abundance in August (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Gill's sand lance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms, occasionally near shallow rocky reefs.

species.name: Gillbar barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gilled lungfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swamps and flood plains (Ref. 43033).  Lungfishes survive for months under the dried mud of floodplains (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Gillellus inescatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gillellus jacksoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gillichthys detrusus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at low tide in deep channels produced by the 10 meter tidal amplitude in the Colorado River estuary.  Bottom with fine, silty sediments and turbid conditions are prevalent (Ref. 90849).

species.name: Gillspot cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rubble bottoms in 17-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gilt darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Ginglymostoma unami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ginsburg's tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy substrate.  Size at sexual maturity of females around 5 cm SL (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Giraffe-spotted snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girardinichthys ireneae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girdled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rubble-sand or soft bottom habitat (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Girdled pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rubble bottom.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  In New South Wales, Australia, males may be brooding at 9.9 cm SL.

species.name: Girdled scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Girdled wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs, above coral, rubble or algae.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Girella albostriata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Large herbivorous fishes (Duhart & Ramírez 1998) with a juvenile phase in tide pools.

species.name: Girella fasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girella feliciana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girella freminvillii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually seen in aggregations while grazing over shallow reefs (Ref. 11482).  May also mix with schools of other species (Ref. 5227).The fine mat of comb-like, bicuspid and tricuspid teeth are used to scrape algae from rocks and corals (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Girella leonina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 36349).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Girella mezina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Girella simplex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girella stuebeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girella zonata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 7373).

species.name: Girelle
species.description: Occurs in the littoral zone, near rocks and eelgrass beds.  Usually found between 1-60 m, but old males stay in deeper water.  Found in deeper waters during winter.  Sometimes solitary, among rocks, often with numerous specimens in its immediate vicinity.  Buries itself in sand at night or when frightened.  Feeds on small gastropods, sea urchins, shrimps, worms, isopods and amphipods.  Sexually mature when 1 year old.  Protogynous species; females change sex to become males; specimen above 18 cm length are all males (Ref. 35388).  Pelagic eggs (Ref. 4742).

species.name: Girelle arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs, along the upper edges of coral-rich areas (Ref. 9710, 58534).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  May be solitary or found in small group (Ref. 90102). Juveniles are encountered in exposed outer reef flats (Ref. 1602).  Feed on a wide variety of small invertebrates as well as fish eggs.

species.name: Girelle crépuscule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 5227) found in reefs subjected to surges (Ref. 9311).  Moves over great distances to feed on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 9311).

species.name: Girelle de Cortez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms small aggregations over reefs.  Feeds on suspended plankton and small hard-shelled invertebrates.  Not utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Girelle de Noël
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102) in shallow exposed reef flats, usually with rock-base and mixed coral and algae (Ref. 48636, 58302).  Also occurs in surge-swept reef flats, reef margins, and clear rocky shorelines, but may venture to deeper waters up to 10 m (Ref. 3921).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on crustaceans (especially crabs), mollusks, and ophiuroids (brittle stars) (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Girelle diamant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and sheltered seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Occurs singly or in pairs; females often found in small groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on invertebrates by picking items from the substratum.  Burrows in the sand at the sign of danger (Ref. 5503).

species.name: Girelle guêpe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups (Ref. 90102) in exposed crests of seaward and lagoon reefs, usually rock-based. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115. Replaced by T. nigrofascatum in Papua New Guinea (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Girelle hublot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found almost exclusively in the surge zone of outer reef flats, reef margins, and rocky coastlines, down to a depth of about 10 m (Ref. 5213).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Occur in groups of females that are spread out over large reef sections and dominated by few males.  Males grow much larger than females (Ref. 48636).  Feed on small invertebrates (crabs, sea urchins, brittlestars, mollusks), small fishes, echinoids, ophiuroids and polychaetes (Ref. 37816).  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).

species.name: Girelle nébuleuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in groups (Ref. 90102) on reef flats, reef margins, and rocky shores (Ref. 9710).  Mainly in inshore weedy areas but has been collected as deep as 40 m (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Girelle paon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found singly or in small groups consisting of one male and a few females (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on small invertebrates, especially crustaceans and mollusks.

species.name: Girelle paon (Thalassoma lunare)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102)  in the upper portions of lagoon and coastal reefs, and in protected seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Enters estuaries (Ref. 48636).  Usually found on upper portions of ledges and heads (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on small benthic invertebrates and fish eggs (Ref. 9823).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Girelle paon (Thalassoma pavo)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters near rocks and eel-grass beds.  Usually solitary, sometimes in small groups.  Feeds on small mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 4742).  Protogynous hermaphrodite, with distinct sexual dichromatism (Ref. 5292).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4742).

species.name: Girelle paon de Hardwicke
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow lagoon and seaward reefs, slopes and along drop-offs to moderate depths.  Occurs in small, loose groups (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic and planktonic crustaceans, small fishes, and foraminiferans.

species.name: Girelle pommelée
species.description: Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs to over 15 m (Ref. 9710) and nearby sand-rubble bottoms at 2-30 m, solitarily or in small groups (Ref. 90102).  Food consist of small crabs and gastropods.

species.name: Girelle reine
species.description: Adults found in weed, rock and coral areas; juveniles in shallow tide pools (Ref. 30573).  Generally solitary (Ref. 5213).  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey, including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 5374).  Young very different (Ref. 1623).

species.name: Girelle trois points
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy areas of deep lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), usually along deep drop-offs with large caves, rich with invertebrate growth in depths over 20 m.  Occurs in small groups of females, usually a male swimming nearby (Ref. 48636).  May be found solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Girelle à bande jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girelle à oeil rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in seaward reefs, over rubble with some rock and coral (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Girelle à petits cailloux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky bottoms or reefs rich in algae.

species.name: Girelle à tache caudale
species.description: Found usually in sandy or algal-rich areas near reefs or in seagrass beds.  Feeds on amphipods, tanaids, pelecypods, brachyuran crabs, gastropods and polychaetes (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Girelle à épaule jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Girelle émeraude
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Giti damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered fringing reefs, usually in bays at depths between about 3 to 20 m.  They occur in small aggregations; closely associated with branching formations of live coral, particularly Acropora spp. and the pocilloporid Seriatopora hystrix.  The fish hovers a short distance above the substratum, presumably feeding on zooplankton (Ref. 74966).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gjellerup's mouth almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gladiator goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools of sandy intertidal areas of lagoons, bays, and river mouths.  Also lives in sheltered sandy bays and estuaries among rubble and in lagoons along edges of coral patches. Usually found in small loose groups (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Gladioglanis anacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flooded forest on the border of the lake, in a shallow (up to 0.5 m) marginal area on a deep mat of leaf litter as substrate.  Also collected on leaf litter along the shore of the lake (Ref. 79081).

species.name: Gladioglanis conquistador
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gladioglanis machadoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, heavily forested black-water streams with large leaf-litter deposits.  Feeds on small invertebrates.

species.name: Gladius sea chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length of individuals observed from the wild may be in excess of 52 cm SL (Ref. 92523).

species.name: Gladys' cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glanapteryx anguilla
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glanapteryx niobium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glanidium botocudo
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lotic sections of rivers and also lakes.  Active at night.  Feeds on allochthonous resources, such as beetles, and autochthonous aquatic invertebrates, such as insect larvae
and gastropods based on gut contents of 8.2 cm SL specimen (Ref. 93811).

species.name: Glanidium catharinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glaphyropoma spinosum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glaridoglanis andersonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glass blenny
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide range of substrates, where photographs show this species mostly on live coral 
surfaces of all morphologies, but also common on sponges, gorgonians, and dead hard bottoms; with  TP males occupying holes in live corals, dead corals, and sponges (Ref. 125603). Inhabits globose coral heads of <i>Montastrea sp.<i> and sea fans (Ref. 51514).

species.name: Glass bloodfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glass blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits narrow, clear creeks flowing through rainforest in generally flat terrain.

species.name: Glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers with turbid waters (Ref. 27732).  Reported to prefer fast flowing water and usually occurs along the shores (Ref. 56749).  Enters flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Found in lowland streams to peat adjacent in large school up to 100 fish (Ref. 57235).  Diurnal.  Feeds mostly on pelagic hemipterans and some small fishes (Ref. 12693), also on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  The clearest body of world's fish (Ref. 57235).  Used to make prahoc or fish sauce and regularly seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  at least 10 individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539, 57235).

species.name: Glass fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rivers and lowland wetlands including peat canals (Ref. 57235). Found in medium to large-sized rivers and is a common resident of seasonally flooded forest. Leaves the flooded forest in November as the water levels begin to decline substantially. Seems to be more tolerant of high amounts of suspended solids than P. maculicauda or P. williaminae and are more common in habitats disturbed by farming activities. Feeds on zooplankton, insects (Ref. 12693) and fish (Ref. 56749). Normally sold in markets held side by side in a piece of split bamboo. Good for Tieo pa ka tao and extensively used for making padek (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Glass goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools near large coral columns and heads (Ref. 7251).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Glass headstander
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lentic environment (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Glass knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to be gregarious, timid and nocturnal (Ref. 27188).  Prefers deep still waters (Ref. 75964).  Found in ponds (Ref. 11229) and creeks with a substrate rich in plant debris (Ref. 12225).  This gymnotiform fish can be found in colder waters of 18°C (Ref. 10011).  Electric organ discharge (EOD) frequency cues have been experimentally shown to play a role in species and sex recognition in this species (Ref. 10598).  Playback of a conspecific male's electric courtship display elicited spawning in ripe females.  Diel rhythmic change in EOD may be manifested by the increase in EOD amplitude at night among dominant breeding males as they compete with other conspecifics (Ref. 10599).  A fractional spawner; fecundity reported at 905 eggs (Ref. 10605).  Males reportedly reach 45 cm TL, females to 20 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Glass schilbid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious schooling species confined to larger lakes and rivers (Ref. 43912). Benthic species, occurs in deep water (Ref. 13851).  Feeds mainly on small planktonic and benthic insects and crustaceans (Ref. 13851, 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Rarely exceeds 15 cm TL (Ref. 43912). Usually smoked or sun-dried, after which they are very tasty and may fetch high prices; sometimes ground into fish flour or fish meal and stored for long periods in sealed containers as an insurance against famine (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Glass tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A gregarious species which prefers the counter current zones of small creeks.  Omnivorous.  It is very prolific and reproduction in the aquarium is very easy to carry out (Ref. 12225).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Glass-barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, canals, beels and ponds (Ref. 1479).  Occurs in backwaters of flowing rivers over sandy substrate (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Glassgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in quiet coastal estuaries, enters fresh water, usually in small to large schools (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Glasshead barreleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic.  Does not exhibit diurnal vertical migration (Ref. 6686).

species.name: Glasshead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common at depths less than 500 m (Ref. 1371).  Feeds predominantly on pelagic copepods, to a lesser extent on euphausiids and gammarian amphipods, and to a minor extent on shrimps, ostracods, cumaceans, other small crustaceans, and small fish (Ref. 1371).  Due to its small size, it is not of significant interest to fisheries (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Glassy Bombay duck
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and estuaries.

species.name: Glassy cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear seaward reefs (Ref. 37816).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary; inhabits deep caves and crevices during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Glassy darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Glassy sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow sandy parts of bays and estuaries, perhaps tolerating lowered salinities.

species.name: Glassy sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear water with coral bottom.  Form aggregations in dark crevices and caves (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal (Ref. 9626).  Its name probably refers to the juveniles, which are so transparent that the backbone can be seen in the living fish (Ref. 26938).  Feeds on zooplankton, particularly the larval stages of invertebrates (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Glauert's anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate (Ref. 7300) and benthic (Ref. 75154) species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300) but has been recorded from the continental shelf in depths greater than 145 m (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Glittering pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats to a depth of over 17 m.  Easily recognized by color but secretive and not often seen (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also seen in coral reefs in 1-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Globe fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers (Ref. 2829), open water, weed beds and vegetated fringes; feeds on mollusks (Ref. 28714). Ventral pocket communicates gill chamber with oesophagus, allowing fish to inflate its body like a ball (Ref. 57417).

species.name: Globehead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small fishes and planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 6187).

species.name: Globosehead rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Globular snailfish
species.description: The sediment from the Agassiz trawl was a mixture of sand, pebbles and stones, and numerous large fragments of dead and living glass sponges. Invertebrates found were dominated by at least 5 species of isopods and caprellids attached to colonies of hydroids (5 - 6 species), some benthopelagic shrimps (2 - 3 species), and a few gastropods and ophiurids (Ref. 123108).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossanodon macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is collected from mud-bottom habitat in 300 m depth from the Arabian Sea, off the southwestern coast of India.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Glossanodon polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand, mud and rock bottom.  Changes in color pattern with age (Ref. 37473).

species.name: Glossogobius ankaranensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave-restricted species.

species.name: Glossogobius bellendenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Kroon and Johnson (2006) document Queensland records of this species. Although the species currently is restricted in its distribution, it may have been mistaken for juveniles of other species because of the small size of the species. Consequently it is likely to be more widely distributed in Australia (Ref. 80299).

species.name: Glossogobius clitellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius gnomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits small stream, with width of about 2-4 and depth of up to 2 m, near the coast, slowly flowing through closed-canopy rainforest.  The stream has very clear water with rocks, sand, mud, and tree debris on the bottom.  In Aru Islands, specimens were recorded from a moderately fast flowing stream, with substrate comprising of white sand, leaf litter and fallen trunk (Ref. 116998).

species.name: Glossogobius illimis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius mahalonensis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the shoreline of the Lake Mahalona. Found in a moderately steep inshore habitat
characterised by mangroves over gravel substrate in the shallows, turning to predominantly rocks alternating with sand and mud in about two meters depth. The habitat was also composed of submerged dead wood, especially in less than two meters depth. Occupies shallows up to about 2 meters depth, but not present in depths between 2 and 12 m, the maximum depth visited by diving at sampling site. Occurs sympatrically with other fish species which include <i>Telmatherina celebensis, <i>Paratherina striata, <i>P. wolterecki, <i>Oryzias marmoratus, <i>Mugilogobius latifrons, <i>M. rexi, <i>Glossogobius intermedius and <i>G. matanensis (Ref. 99936).

species.name: Glossogobius matanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius multipapillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glossogobius munroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from freshwater from about 1 km above tidal influence to 400 km inland (Ref. 90210).

species.name: Glossogobius muscorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally occurs in rainforest creeks at elevations below 50 m (Ref. 80299).

species.name: Glossogobius nanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Material from Australia was found in clear streams with considerable fine gravel on the bottom in  elevations of a few meters to about 100 m (Ref. 116998).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glover's anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Glovers hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm water (>20°C) of spring-fed pools. Upper temperature tolerance is probably not as high as C. dalhousiensis. Omnivorous. Only co-occurs with C. dalhousiensis in one spring (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Glowlight rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glowtail pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 8 cm SL.

species.name: Glutin assfish
species.description: Benthopelagic at bathyal and abyssal depths (Ref. 56809); found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Glyptophidium argenteum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Glyptophidium macropus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Glyptophidium oceanium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax annandalei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or rocky bottoms of springs (Ref. 12045).  Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Glyptothorax chimtuipuiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax dikrongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift, moderate and turbid running water consisting of various substrate such as gravel, cobbles or large boulders, sand and green algae on substratum, in low to moderately deep (30-50 cm) running water (Ref. 86401).

species.name: Glyptothorax dorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Glyptothorax exodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, clear streams with a substrate consisting of gravel, cobble or large rocks (Ref. 2091).

species.name: Glyptothorax famelicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax filicatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax fokiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Glyptothorax forabilis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in a stretch of the Xe Katam with high gradient and very fast water on boulders and rocks (type locality) and in the Houay Makchang-Gnai in a degraded stretch with relatively slow
current over riffles and pools, also in a stretch with fast current on large stones, in a coffee plantation (Ref. 117341).

species.name: Glyptothorax fucatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in foot-hill streams (Ref. 43281).  Occurs under rocks and logs in fairly strong currents in medium and large-sized rivers.  Feeds on aquatic insect larvae.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Glyptothorax garhwali
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax giudikyensis
species.description: This species was found is a small hill stream draining moderately dense forest. Inhabits relatively swift but clear and shallow (50-100 cm) water where the bottom of the river is visible.There are different types of substrates in the area, including medium to large-sized boulders, gravels, and cobbles with thick layers of aquatic green algae and mosses. Vegetation along the stream bank is characteristic of tropical evergreen forest dominated by different types of bamboos, orchids, banana plants and different types of trees. Associated fish recorded from the type locality includes species of Channa, Garra, Neolissochilus, Puntius and Schistura (Ref. 130785).

species.name: Glyptothorax gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pool and run areas of mountain streams (Ref. 12045).  Collected in a large river with high, turbid monsoon flow and with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax housei

species.name: Glyptothorax indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in fast-flowing streams.  Prefers backwater of quiet eddies (Ref. 12045).  Collected in a large river with high, turbid monsoon flow and with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).

species.name: Glyptothorax interspinalum
species.description: Adults inhabit fast-flowing water, rapids (Ref. 43281).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in foot-hill streams (Ref. 27732).  Occurs over coarse substrates in medium-sized upland rivers (Ref. 12693).  Found in running waters of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Feeds on aquatic insect larvae.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Glyptothorax lanceatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches up to at least 17 cm in total length (Ref. 89835).

species.name: Glyptothorax laosensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit flowing waters of small and medium-sized streams.  Found over coarse substrates and in small upland streams with alternating pools, waterfalls and rapids.  Feed on aquatic insect larvae.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Glyptothorax lonah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Glyptothorax longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax maceriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, shallow, moderately flowing streams with a predominantly sandy bottom. Lives in association with Garra spp. (Cyprinidae), Balitora cf. brucei (Balitoridae), Botia cf. almorhae (Botiidae), Lepidocephalichthys sp. (Cobitidae), Schistura spp. (Nemacheilidae), Amblyceps laticeps (Amblycipitidae), Glyptothorax botius (Sisoridae), G. telchitta (Sisoridae), and Channa sp. (Channidae) (Ref. 91243).

species.name: Glyptothorax macromaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually associated with fast flowing streams and headwaters (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Glyptothorax madraspatanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Glyptothorax major
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in upland and montane brooks as well as small streams (Ref. 12693).  Found in running waters of lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Feeds mainly on aquatic insect larvae.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Glyptothorax malabarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from submerged crevices formed by large boulders in an upland stream (210 m a.s.l.), which is about 6 m wide and 0.5-1.5 m deep, flowing through a forest patch on the western slopes of the Western Ghats in Kerala. The streambed in this area is composed of pebble and sand in which are embedded large boulders. Collection was done in February, a relatively dry month, and the stream was in a depleted phase with clear- but not fast flowing-water. Riparian forest vegetation in the vicinity of the stream provided ample shade. Associated fishes from the collection site included Barilius bakeri Day, Garra mullya (Sykes) (Cyprinidae); Bhavania australis (Jerdon) and Schistura denisoni denisoni (Day) (Balitoridae), from the pebble-bottomed area of the stream (Ref. 84486).

species.name: Glyptothorax manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Glyptothorax mibangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a fast flowing hill stream with a substrate consisted of boulders, cobble, pebbles and sand.  The stream substrate is dominated by cobbles (Ref. 102623).

species.name: Glyptothorax poonaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236). Gut content of three specimens suggested that the fish feeds on benthic macroinvertebrates such as freshwater prawns, maxillopod crustacean (Branchiura), and Odonata nymph. Collected gravid females suggests that this species probably breeds during June to August (which is the monsoon season) and according to the local fishermen, found only during Jthese months in the Markal area. Important threats to this species include alteration of hydrological regimes because of damming, increasing pollution, deforestation leading to siltation, and introduced fish species (Ref. 87891),

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in streams and creeks with stone to rock bottom, in fast current. (Ref. 117341).

species.name: Gnatholepis caudimaculata

This species has been shown to exhibit red fluorescence on the dorsal half of the eye, assumed to be part of a 'private communication system' as the fluorescence occurs in features that are used for intra-specific signals, especially the eyes (Ref. 92171).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens have been collected from shallow habitats, tide pools or 'brackish pools', at depths of 0-5 m, from sand and mangrove areas (Ref. 92171).
