species.name: Gnomefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found in deep rocky areas; young found in shallow water.  The diet consists of fishes, crustaceans and squids.  Spawns from October to March.

species.name: Gnomus tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits channel with clear water (Ref. 56955); visibility of approximately 2 m and the pH ranging from 6.6-7.6 (Ref. 84053).  Feeds on insects such as chironomids, ephemeropterans and trichopterans (Ref. 56955).

species.name: Goalpara loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in shallow slow moving streams with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Goan catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers in plains and submontane regions (Ref. 41236).  Common in rivers and wetlands.  Piscivorous feeding on other small fishes (Ref. 44149).

species.name: Goatee blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goatee velvetfish
species.description: Collected and observed usually in broad shallow pools within degenerating low-relief reef, with dead coral heads, overhangs and crevices, with scattered shell and coral rubble, often among thick stands of brown macroalgae, Padina and Sargassum species (Ref. 89851).

species.name: Goateed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobbleguts
species.description: Inhabit inshore reefs and estuaries (Ref. 9710).  Occur in groups in weedy areas (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Goberge de l'Alaska
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The adults usually live near to the sea floor, but sometimes they also appear near the surface (Ref. 1371).  They perform diurnal vertical migrations (Ref. 1371).  They mainly feed on krill (Ref. 39882) but they also eat fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 6885).  The adults which are spawning are often solely captured for their roe (may have been the case in the first years of the fishery in the U.S., but hasn't been true for some time. In 1994, the North Pacific Fishery Management Council/NOAA enacted an amendment to the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska Fishery Management Plans effectively banning the practice of stripping roe and discarding the carcasses, R. Rogness, pers.comm. April 2022).  The meat is used to produce surimi (this is an imitation of shellfish meat) (Ref. 28499).  They are traded as fresh fish, boneless flesh, in frozen blocks or as surimi.  The fish is cooked in the microwave, steamed or fried in butter (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Gobi de tas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal areas, estuaries, lagoons and coastal rivers.  Common in mangroves (Ref. 4343, 44894).  Occasionally penetrates the lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Gobi milet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly recorded from mangroves and estuaries, but also found in coastal freshwater streams (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Gobi tase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit creeks, rivers and brackish estuaries (Ref. 2847, 44894).  Found in tidal streams (Ref. 4343, 44894).  Sometimes seen upstream a short distance from the tidal zone.  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Gobie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives with the alphaeid shrimp, Alpheus randalli, in burrows on coral reefs, with coarse sandy bottoms. Occurs in clear coastal to outer reefs on sand and rubble flats in depths of 20-35 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Gobie (Amblyeleotris wheeleri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently the most common shallow-water species of the genus found in coral reef areas, but may occur at depths greater than 30 m. Usually found in rubble areas near or within coral reefs and in symbiotic association with alpheid shrimps, most often with Alpheus ochrostriatus. Found in coastal sand slopes and deep lagoons, shallow to 40 meters depth range (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Gobie (Eleotris pisonis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on shallow, muddy or sandy bottoms (Ref. 13628).  They appear to prefer estuarine freshwater tributaries, occurring in waters with a salinity range of 0 to 19 ppt (Ref. 7251), or up to 36.6 in some cases (Ref. 97140).  Feed on dipteran larvae and pupae (especially the juveniles); crustaceans like crabs and shrimps; and small fishes.  The diet changes with sexual maturity and season.  Gonadal development takes place during the dry season.  Average size at maturity is 5.7 mm for males and 4.3 mm for females (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Gobie (Glossogobius giuris)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in freshwater and estuaries, but also enter the sea (Ref. 4833). Also occur in canals, ditches and ponds (Ref.  12693). Found in clear to turbid streams with rock, gravel or sand bottoms (Ref. 2847). Encountered in medium to large-sized rivers of the lower Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feed on small insects, crustaceans and small fish.  Grow to a much larger size in brackish water than in fresh water.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Cannibalism is relatively common for this species (Ref. 48660).

species.name: Gobie (Sicydium brevifile)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larvae ascend rivers, adults in freshwater (Ref. 4343). Amphidromous endemics living as adults in clearwater streams of the volcanic islands in the Gulf of Guinea and of Mount Cameroon streams in Western Cameroon (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie a quatre taches
species.description: Epibenthic over sand or muddy sand (Ref. 5299). Meiofauna feeder (Ref. 92840). Up to depth of 90 m (Ref. 5299) but collected up to depth of 333 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Minimum depth from Ref. 104982.

species.name: Gobie akahachihaze
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs, over hard bottoms as well as over sand and rubble.  Typical along reef-crests in depths of 1-6 m, but has also been collected from depths of 24 m.  Usually seen in pairs, hovering near their burrow.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884,  48637).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, fishes, and fish eggs by sifting mouthfuls of sand.

species.name: Gobie blanc
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore, on sand near rock crevices, weed-covered stones, and grottoes (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie cavernicole
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore; in a grotto (Ref. 4696, 51024). Prefers caves abd other dark habitats (Ref. 92840). Benthic (Ref. 51024).

species.name: Gobie cavernicole de Steinitz
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore, in submarine grottoes (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie chauve
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually offshore, 5-330 m on sand, mud, shell debris, gravel and corallines.  Feeds on young fish (Ref. 92840). Eggs found in mollusk shells, guarded by male (Ref. 42425).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie colonien
species.description: Inshore, including sea-grass meadows; to about 120 m depth.

species.name: Gobie commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters estuaries, salt marshes and pools (Ref. 4343); usually on sand or mud (Ref. 59043).  Lives in sea as well as brackish waters and migrates into limnetic sections of rivers (Ref. 92840). Also rock pools where it feeds mainly on epibenthic meiofauna like harpacticoids and small amphipods (Ref. 92840); small crustaceans, worms, chironomid larvae and mites (Ref. 4696).  Its burrowing habit allows it to survive low water levels and to avoid predators (Ref. 30508).  Spawns after first winter, at sea, in February - September, depending on latitude; individual females spawn several times during a season.  Adhesive eggs (0.9 x 0.7 mm) are deposited under or between stones, shells and aquatic plants and males guard the eggs until hatching.  Juveniles enter freshwater habitats in late summer to forage (Ref. 59043).  The male defends and aerates the eggs for about 9 days.

species.name: Gobie comorien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and river systems (Ref. 92840); lives in poolson the bottom amongst cover such as cobbles or vegetation (Ref. 52193). It feeds on bottom-living insects and small invertebrates (Ref. 52193). Breeds in early summer; eggs are oval (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Gobie coureur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish- and fresh-water habitats with low salinity (< 2 ppt); lagoons and lakes; large rivers to small, fast-flowing streams; on sand or mud bottom; mainly in well vegetated or high-complexity habitats. Abundant in backwaters and still channels  (Ref. 59043).  Longevity is 4-5 years; spawns for the first time at 2 years; spawning season in April to June, occasionally until mid-August; females may repeat spawning during a season; usually spawns for a single season.  Males guard eggs until hatching; with adhesive eggs deposited on stones, shells and aquatic plants (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on crustaceans (esp.  Corophiid amphipods), aquatic insects (mostly chironomid larvae), polychaetes, also small fish and mollusks (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie cristal
species.description: Benthic and free swimming (Ref. 92840). This occasionally territorial species occurs in coastal waters, over shell, sand, or mud bottoms; males bottom-living during breeding season.  Feed on zooplankton (Ref. 5204).  Spawning takes place when 1 year old.  Adults die afterwards.  Eggs are laid in the empty tube-worms and are guarded by the male (Ref. 35388).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie crécerelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie de Bath
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found on sand and gravel in 7 m (Ref. 4696, 92840), muddy sand bottom in 10 m and rock sand ecotone in 14 m; meiofauna feeder; live together with G.geniporus, prefers benthic prey as well as fish and suprabenthic like harticoids and ostracods. (Ref. 92840). Max. length (Robert A. Patzner, pers. comm., 1999).

species.name: Gobie de Bellotti
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore and in lagoons, among seagrass (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie de Brito
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small crevices in vertical rock outcrops; also collected from a tide pool (Ref. 41100). Also found from intertidal and shallow subtidal to depths up to 65 m (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie de Canestrini
species.description: Found in inshore habitats, lagoons, lakes and large to medium-size rivers; on sand or mud bottom.  Spawns after first winter in March-July; individual females spawn several times during a season.  Adhesive eggs deposited under or between stones, shells and aquatic plants and males guard the eggs until hatching. Feeds on a wide variety of benthic invertebrates (worms, amphipods, Ref.4696) (Ref.59043).

species.name: Gobie de Couch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore and intertidal, under stones on sheltered muddy sand.  Feeds on polychaetes, algae, crustaceans, bivalves.

species.name: Gobie de De Buen
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Juveniles reported to occur at 35 m.  Not much is known on reproduction and food of the species (Ref. 4696).  Inhabit sandy areas in the Kvarner area (Croatia), in places scarcely covered with cobbles (6-20 cm) and boulders (>20 cm).  Average sand particle size coarse (0.7-0.8 mm), and medium (0.2-0.4).  Sediments are mostly coarse biogenous fragments (calcite skeleton remains) mixed with finer lithogenous material (Ref. 45055).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie de feu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper portions of outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Hovers above the bottom, facing the current to feed on zooplankton, copepods, and crustacean larvae.  Several individuals may share the same hole (especially juveniles).  Has a habit of flicking its pennant-like first dorsal fin back and forth (Ref. 1602, 48637).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Gobie de Guam
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Adults occur from lowland streams and rivers to relatively swift streams at elevations of 1000 m.  They often burrow into the substrate with only the eyes showing; feed on filamentous algae, worms, crustaceans, various insects and insects larvae, and suspended food particles; has been long favored as food by the early Hawaiians (Ref. 44091).  Larvae develop and metamorphose in the marine zooplankton and as juveniles, about 161 days old,  recruit to freshwater streams, where they undergo rapid growth and morphological changes necessary for upstream migration to the adult habitat (Ref. 51037).

species.name: Gobie de Kner
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Gobie de lagune
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. A short-lived species (less than 2 years) which inhabits shallow, well vegetated habitats - streams, lakes, estuaries, lagoons, lower reaches of rivers, springs and brooks.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Spawns after first winter in April-August.; females may spawn every 10-15 days during the season.  Males defend eggs in cavities under stones, plant material or shells; may overturn and clean suitable shells for spawning and these are then covered with substrate.  Postlarvae are pelagic (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobie de Lesueur
species.description: Found inshore (Ref. 4696). Up to depth of 230 m (Ref. 04696) but from 322-337 in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).

species.name: Gobie de Lozano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters.  Spawn when 1 year old.  Eggs are laid under empty bivalve shells (Ref. 35388).  Feed on small crustaceans (mysids, amphipods, copepods), nematodes.

species.name: Gobie de Madère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal pools (brackish waters?) (Ref. 4343).

species.name: gobie de Marquet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie de Meggitt
species.description: Inhabits rocky pools of intertidal zone and rocky shores (Ref. 90102). Specimens collected from tide pools of exposed coasts (Ref. 11441). Feeds on planktonic crustaceans, polychaetes and algae (Ref. 36558).

species.name: Gobie de Port-Saïd
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters, near holes and crevices, on sand and mud flats, with algae, and on stony areas in salinities ranging from 30-50 ppt (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie de Rainford
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms of turbid coastal reefs (Ref. 1602) to depths pf 20m (Ref. 48637).  Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Does not appear  to use a burrow and seen in areas with coral growth (Ref. 1602).

species.name: gobie de Randall
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie de Roule
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore in the Mediterranean but found in deeper waters off Portugal (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie de Salamansa
species.description: Known only by 2 specimens at the date of the description.

species.name: Gobie de Sanzo
species.description: Occurs offshore on muddy sand or mud (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobie de Steven
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore on muddy sand and coarser deposits (Ref. 4696, 51024).  Benthic (Ref. 51024).

species.name: Gobie de Tortonese
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits lagoons, brackish to slightly hypersaline, in shallows on sand near seagrass prairie.  Feeds on small crustaceans and gastropods.

species.name: Gobie de Yaté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from freshwater streams mostly under tidal influence.  Stream bottom consists mostly of shifting sand.  Known to dive head first into sand when threatened (Ref. 48272).

species.name: Gobie des Baléares
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs offshore over coralline grounds (Ref. 4345).

species.name: Gobie doré
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in deeper inshore waters; over rocky substrates with algae and gorgonians (Ref. 4696).  Abundant populations on coasts with steep bedrock.  A shy species and difficult to collect due to long flight distances and hiding in deep clefts (Ref. 87880). Macrobenthos feeder on hard substrates ingest also shelled organisms like molluscs and echinoderms (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal estuaries, lakes (Ref. 48637), and entering lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894). Also found in quiet mangrove estuarine habitats (Ref. 84480). Also Ref. 43716.

species.name: Gobie du Caucase
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabit fresh to hyper-saline waters (to 55 ppt) of lakes, estuaries and lagoons, in shallow areas with much weed. Feed on small crustaceans and chironomid larvae (Ref.12215); larvae of the mussel Dreissena polymorpha (Ref. 59043). Lives less than 2 years. Spawns after first winter. Eggs are attached to the roof of a cavity under stones, plant material or shells and are defended by male. Postlarvae are pelagic. (Ref.59043).

species.name: Gobie du désert
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in pools and streams associated with artesian springs and bores (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Lives in shaded areas around plants or rocks (Ref. 44894).  Found in harsh environment characterized by rapid fluctuations in temperature and salinity (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Field observations and laboratory experimentation indicate that it can withstand wide ranges of temperature (5°-41°C), salinity (0-60 p.p.t.), pH (6.8-11.0) and very low dissolved oxygen level (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, crustaceans, filamentous algae and detritus (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Gobie fascié
species.description: Found offshore in the shelf and upper slope areas (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobie fluviatile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore habitats, estuaries and brackish- and fresh-water lagoons and lakes; large to medium sized rivers and streams; on sand or mud bottom.  It is one of the most abundant fish in lowland rivers.  This species lives up to 5 years; spawns for the first time at 2 years; spawning season in April to July, locally until September, when temperature is above 13°C; females may repeat spawning during a season.  Males with body completely black with yellow fin margins during the spawning season; these excavate nests under any kind of hard substrate and guard eggs until hatching; with adhesive eggs deposited on stones, shells and aquatic plants.  Feeds on a variety of invertebrates, especially molluscs (Ref.59043).

species.name: Gobie galonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected, silty lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 48637).  Occurs in pairs, over its burrow beneath rock or rubble; usually hovers a short distance above the bottom.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Gut contents of a 6.5 cm SL specimen contains mainly fine, unbranched, filamentous algae and harpacticoid copepods, also polychaetes, tanaids, decapod shrimps, amphipods, and nematodes (may have been parasitic).

species.name: Gobie grêle zébré
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit intertidal to offshore areas, probably within interstices of coralline nodules (Ref. 4696).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie hector
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered bays and inner reefs on fine rubble shaded by large living corals (Ref. 48637).  Occurs solitarily, hovering a short distance above sandy bottoms of reef bases.  Stomach contents of one specimen comprise of filamentous algae, harpacticoid copepods, ostracods, amphipods, and nematodes (Ref. 9360).

species.name: Gobie kokou
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie lote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, inshore, brackish water, estuaries and lagoons, on mud and eel-grass meadows.  Commercial in the Black Sea and in Sivash (Ref. 2058).  Occasionally recorded in freshwater, but there are no documented records of actual occurrence in European freshwaters (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobie marbré
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found inshore, over sand.  Enters brackish and hyper-saline waters.  Feeds on small crustaceans and chironomid larvae (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Gobie moucheté
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. This species occurs on all kinds of rocky substrata: gravel, cobbles, boulders and bedrock, but on sand only when it is mixed with the hard substratum, thus, never on pure sand. The substratum was bare or covered with short thallus algae and no other biocover in the habitat were recorded (Ref. 110727).

species.name: Gobie mulet noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie méconnu
species.description: Collected from just below the water surface (north Adriatic Sea) down to 12 m in depth (Israel). The depth range in Israel (4-12 m) was deeper compared with other areas (Adriatic 0-5 m, France 1.5-6 m, Crete 2-9 m). It occurs on all kinds of substrata: sand, gravel, cobbles, boulders and bedrock, but mostly on different combinations of mixed substratum which can be bare or covered to varying degrees by short thallus algae, Caulerpa prolifera and Cystoseira spp., or sea grasses Posidonia oceanica and Cymodocea nodosa (Ref. 110727).

species.name: Gobie nabot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly on coarse grounds, especially coralline deposits. Occur in caves and other dark habitats (Ref. 92840). Feeds on small crustaceans (decapods, amphipods), polychaetes and bivalves (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie nageur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Suprabenthic (Ref. 92840). Found inshore in groups around over-grown structures and among Laminaria or Zostera beds. Adults feed on small crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, mysids) and chaetognaths (Ref. 4696). Eggs are about 1 mm long, pear-shaped, and adhere to seagrass or weeds; hatch in 10 days (Ref. 4696). Pelagic larvae hatch at 2.5 mm length (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gobie nageur de Ferrer
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs inshore over sand (Ref. 4345). Benthic and free swimming (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie nain de Ben-Tuvia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore, on muddy sand substrate; probably a burrower (Ref. 4345).

species.name: Gobie nain de Dollfus
species.description: Found on sand with rocky outcrops (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobie nain de Guillet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on coarse ground, including coralline deposits (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie nain de Pruvot
species.description: Occurs offshore, on coralline and other coarse grounds (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobie nain des Canaries
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits at rock outcroppings with large expanses of sand between (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie nain des Canaries (Vanneaugobius canariensis)
species.description: Found under loose stones on sandy ground (Ref. 5299).  At the Cape Verdes localities, the species was collected in 11-16 m on mixed substrata of sand, stones, calcareous algae and rock (Ref. 39517).

species.name: Gobie nain à barres brunes
species.description: Found in small submerged caves, sometimes associated with Corcyrogobius liechtensteini (Ref. 10711). Can occur in remarkable abundance within suitable habitats, medium and large-sized caves, with fine sediment bottom (Ref. 44207). Also found in rocky shores in deep caves in water depths from 5-56 m, usually resting directly in front of its hole and in small cavities near sea grass (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie nain à grosse tête
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in inshore shallows and lagoons, among and under stones (Ref. 4696).  Benthic (Ref. 51024).

species.name: Gobie nain à taches blanches
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. A rare cryptobenthic gobiid species of the Mediterranean, that spends the day hidden to become active during the night. It swimming movements are slow, and when disturbed, swims approximately 20 cm above the bottom. It lives on a bottom substrate of pebbles or on sand among Posidonia oceanica or Caulerpa racemosa (Ref. 92840, 130809).

species.name: Gobie noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries, lagoons and inshore waters over sand or mud, in seagrass or on algae (Ref. 4696).  Occasionally recorded in freshwater, but there are no documented records of actual occurrence in European freshwaters (Ref. 59043).  Feed on crustaceans (larger amphipods, isopods, shrimps, mysids, small crabs), bivalves, gastropods, polychaetes, chironomid larvae, sometimes small fish (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie nonnat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic and free swimming (Ref. 92840). A neotenic, pelagic species inhabiting inshore and estuarine waters, over sand, mud and eel-grass (Ref. 4343).  Adults feed on zooplankton, especially copepods, cirripede larvae and mysids (Ref. 4343).  They spawn in summer in empty bivalve shells (Ref. 35388).  Probably migrate to deeper water to spawn during summer (Ref. 57814).  Adults die after breeding (Ref. 4696) which does not qualify as a manifestation of semelparity but abbreviate iteroparity according to a recent study (Ref. 81039).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie norvégien
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found offshore on mud and coarse shell deposits (Ref. 4696). Can hybridize with Pomatoschistus lozanoi (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gobie nu de la Caspienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lower reaches of rivers, deltas and estuaries; over muddy sand with shells (Ref. 4696).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696). Feeds on benthic invertebrates, rotifers and algae (Ref.59043).

species.name: Gobie ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on fine gravel bottoms from estuaries to fresh water of rivers.

species.name: Gobie paganel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly marine, but may enter freshwater. Adults occur inshore in intertidal waters, under stones and in pools on sheltered rocky shores with much weed cover. Macrobenthos feeder on hard substrates (Ref. 92840), they feed on crustaceans (larger amphipods, isopods, small crabs) and polychaetes; juveniles eat harpacticoid copepods, amphipods, polychaetes and mites (Ref. 4696). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Fusiform shaped eggs are found in patches of several thousand on undersurface of stones, shells, polychaete tubes or Ciona mantles (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie peint
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and sand; young may occur in shore pools.  Feeds on crustaceans (copepods and amphipods) (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie pâle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef areas deeper than 6 m.

species.name: Gobie pélagique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found offshore but was also recorded from shore pools (Ref. 5299).  Found in shoals (Ref. 27121).  Juveniles epipelagic, adults migrate to deeper waters, and large adults are only recorded from demersal trawls (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on phytoplankton and preyed upon by fishes, penguins, Cape cormorants, and fur seals (Ref. 27121).  Although targeted by purse seines, it may also be caught incidentally in trawls (Ref. 27121).  Prefer cooler waters of 11° to 15°C (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Gobie quagga
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Suprabenthic plankton feeder (Ref. 92840). Max. length (Francesco Costa, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Gobie rayé
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs offshore on coralline grounds. Aufwuchs feeder (Ref. 92840), feeds on harpacticoids and other crustaceans (including plankton), polychaetes, algae and poriferans.  Rarely captured (Ref. 4696).

species.name: gobie rayé (Stenogobius genivittatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4343) and enters brackish and fresh water along the upper tidal zone of rivers (Ref. 12693).  Larvae spend time in the marine zooplankton and as juveniles, about 135 days old,  recruit to  freshwater streams where they undergo rapid growth and morphological changes neceassary for upstream migration to the adult habitat (Ref. 51037).   Marketed fresh in mixed catches (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Gobie zèbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This schooling species inhabits exposed seaward reefs in relatively shallow water, over hard bottoms.  Usually many individuals occupy the same refuge.  Found to be subjected to strong currents, where in small to large aggregations (Ref. 48637). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Gobie zébré
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in lagoons and intertidal pools, under stones, among algae and seagrass (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie à bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Adults inhabit coastal reefs and lagoons on sand and rubble margins of algal reefs and sometimes near seagrass beds (Ref. 48637).  Feed by sifting mouthfuls of sand and expelling it through the gills, to capture small invertebrates, organic matter, and large quantities of algae.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884). Spawning is synchronous with semilunar periods (Ref. 84980).  Eggs are deposited in burrows which are tended by the male parent (Ref. 55919, 84980). Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Gobie à bouche rouge
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found inshore, on rocks, sand and sea-grass meadows (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobie à deux ocelles
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults occur in sandy to silty bottoms of lagoons and coastal bays near coral, rubble or leaf litter shelter. Solitary or in pairs that share sandy burrows (Ref. 90102). Feed on small interstitial invertebrates by sifting mouthfuls of sand.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884, 48637).

species.name: Gobie à grandes écailles
species.description: Cryptobenthic, burrowing in muddy sand or mud; often associated with a decapod crustacean Nephrops norvegicus (Ref. 5299). Feed on polychaetes, small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 4696). Eggs are deposited in burrows (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gobie à grandes écailles (Thorogobius macrolepis)
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults probably occur inshore (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie à grosse tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the intertidal zones, among rocks, weeds and pools where the water is usually brackish (Ref. 4343, 5299). Occasionally recorded in freshwater, but there are no documented records of actual occurrence in European freshwaters (Ref. 59043). Macrobenthos feeder on hard substrates (Ref. 92840), feeds on green algae (Enteromorpha), crustaceans (amphipods, crabs), polychaetes, and insects (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie à grosse tête (Ponticola kessleri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in freshwater and brackish water with very low salinity (< 2 ppt); in lower rivers and lagoons, lakes, large rivers, harbours on rocky or well-vegetated bottom (reed thickets) in still waters as well as rapids.  Initial spawning at 2 years, in March to May, where adhesive eggs are deposited on stones, shells and aquatic plants; while males guard the eggs until hatching.  (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on crustaceans (mysids, corophiid amphipods) and small fish (gobies) (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie à joues poreuses
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occur inshore, on sand or mud near seagrass (Ref. 4696).  Breeding males are dusky (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobie à longue queue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in shallow water, on sand and among weeds (Ref. 4696). Live less than 2 years. Feed on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 59043). Spawn after first winter. Females may spawn several times during a season. Males defend eggs in cavities under stones, plant material or molluscs shells (Ref. 59043) like underside of lamellibranch valves (Cardium, Monodonta, Unio, etc.) (Ref. 4696). Eggs hatch at 3.0-3.8 mm (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobie à museau plat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to brackish water habitats, endemic to Black and Caspian Seas. (Ref. 92840). Occurs inshore, among boulders, rocks, stones and Cystoseira (Ref. 4696) but is also known to live over gravelly bottoms offshore, away from inlets (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Gobie à narine tubulaire
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Pure inhabitant of brackish waters (Ref. 92840). Occur in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4696).  Based on morphological and molecular data, this species does not enter pure freshwater and inhabits brackish waters in Sevastopol, Crimea (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobie à quatre bandes
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults occur in shallow inshore waters, under stones or between weed tufts.  Also found in mid-tide pools.  Feed on small decapods and amphipod crustaceans (Ref. 4696).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: gobie à queue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie à six taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty or sandy areas of lagoons and bays (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Usually in pairs and lives in a burrow under rocks.  Commonly seen in aggregations over large areas in lagoons of atolls.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Gobie à tache noire
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Prefer shallow, brackish waters but also occur in fresh waters (Ref. 36771); in lagoons and lakes, large rivers, harbors, on sand or rock bottom; mostly found on well vegetated or rock bottom (Ref. 59043).  Can tolerate a temperature range of 0 to 30°C, but mainly thrive in warm 
temperate waters; able to tolerate low oxygen content waters for several days (Ref. 36771).  Oviparous, with demersal eggs (Ref. 36771).  Longevity up to 4 years.  Males reproduce for the first time at 3-4 years, females at 2-3 years. Spawning season in April to September; females may repeat spawning during a season, every 18-20 days; body of males entirely black during this season.  Adhesive eggs deposited on stones, shells and aquatic plants; males guard eggs until hatching and usually die after spawning season.  Egg clutches are supposed to be occasionally transported attached to the hull of ships, facilitating introduction to other areas.  Feeds on a wide variety of invertebrates and small fish, mostly on molluscs (Ref. 59043). Due to its large size, it has a major commercial value in some areas, especially in Azov Sea. It is usually salted, dried and consumed with beer (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie à taches oranges
species.description: Espèce de poissons marins. Gobius kolombatovici is a bottom-dwelling and secretive species, observed at depths of 15-38 m. It was found to inhabit localities with a combination of soft sediment and rock. Common fish in the same habitat are epibenthic Gobius vittatus, Parablennius rouxi, Thorogobius macrolepis and hyper-benthic Coris julis, Chromis chromis and Serranus hepatus (Ref. 37044).

species.name: Gobie à tête de crapaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore, estuaries, brackish- and fresh-water lagoons on sand or rock bottom.  Rarely occurs in pure freshwater (Ref. 59043).  Found on sand, shell, and rocks near cliffs; at 20-60 m in summer, sometimes as deep as 100 m.  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 4696).  Approaches the sea coasts for spawning in spring (Ref. 2058). Due to large their large size, have certain commercial value in some areas and are popular for sport fishers (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Gobie à tête de grenouille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4343), mud bottoms of estuaries and protected bays (Ref. 37816).  Found on open flat bottom and large adults mostly seen at about 30 meters depth.  Dives head first into the mud for safety (Ref. 48637).   Hides in a burrow, but can dive into mud to escape predators (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Gobie à tête jaune
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits rocky substrates, coralline grounds and also in the area of Posidonia oceanica meadows in water depth from 3-36 m; macrofauna feeder from hard substrates which also feed on suprabenthic organisms (Ref. 92840).

species.name: gobie écailleux
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobie égyptien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore shallows, on sand.  Feed on harpacticoid copepods and nematodes; also oligochaetes, gastropods and other meiobenthos. Life span probably does not go beyond 2 years (Ref. 44579).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Gobie-corail nain
species.description: Possibly occurs in offshore coralline grounds (Ref. 4696).  Reported to settle on cave walls (Ref. 10711).

species.name: Gobie-léopard
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Cryptobenthic, found inshore, in or near crevices in vertical rock faces, rarely in deep lower tide-pools, to a depth of 40 m, usually between 6 to 12 m.  Feed on crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, decapods), polychaetes, gastropods, algae (Ref. 4696).  Spawns up to 12,000 eggs (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gobie-têtard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal lagoons and lowland rivers in  freshwater and brackish water with salinity below 12 ppt.  Adults occur in muddy reaches of rivers; in brackish water, more than 3 m deep (Ref. 4696, 59043).  This species spawns after first winter, May-June and females die shortly after spawning while with males, some weeks after.  Feeds on mollusks, crustaceans, insect larvae and small fishes (Ref. 4696, 59043).  Eggs are pear-shaped (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Gobies des Célèbes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in clear streams, usually close to the sea (Ref. 5259).  They occur mainly in fresh water, but larvae in marine environment (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Gobiesox crassicorpus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox daedaleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox fulvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox juradoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not syntopic with Sicyases brevirostris (Guichenot, 1848) in Juan Fernández Is. (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Gobiesox milleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox multitentaculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiesox pinniger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal, may remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Tolerates extreme changes in temperature and salinity (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Gobiesox potamius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and creeks from the sea to 140 m elevation, more abundant in currents but also found in slow moving waters.  Feeds on crustaceans, aquatic insects and fish scales (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Gobiesox stenocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio acutipinnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio artvinicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with swift and warm flowing water, and cobbled and pebbled bottoms (Ref. 115536).

species.name: Gobio bulgaricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stretches of streams and rivers with moderate flow, usually on sand bottom (Ref. 59043).  Size reaches up to about 9 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio caucasicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio coriparoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio delyamurei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately flowing and stagnant section of  a medium-sized stream (Ref. 56890). Water in the lower part of the stream is extracted in large quantities for irrigation and the stream is almost dry in summer (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio huanghensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio kizilirmakensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio kubanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide variety of habitats from montane rivers to small lowland streams with gravel or sand bottom.  Size reaches up to about 9 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio lingyuanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio lozanoi
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in streams and rivers with clear water, gravel or sandy bottoms (Ref. 57030).  Also inhabits slow moving lowland waters with gravel, sandy and clay bottoms (Ref. 57030) and streams in foot hills with moderate current and with sand or gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio meridionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio obtusirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes with sand bottom.  Breeds in shallow water, over stones, sand or plant material (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio occitaniae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams in hilly area with moderate current, over sand bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gobio rivuloides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to prefer sandy bottom in shallow slow current (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Gobio sibiricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio tchangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobio volgensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia abbreviata

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia cheni

species.name: Gobiobotia filifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia guilingensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel bottom (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Gobiobotia homalopteroidea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia jiangxiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia kolleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia lii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in turbid, slow-running water with mixed substrates including sand and gravel. In Lake Dongting in Hunan, it was collected in lotic habitats or estuaries of effluents. Associated with Misgurnus anguillicaudatus, Opsariichthys bidens, and Parabotia fasciata (Ref. 126141).

species.name: Gobiobotia longibarba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Gobiobotia macrocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia meridionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia naktongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia nicholsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia paucirastella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiobotia tungi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Gobiobotia yuanjiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiocichla ethelwynnae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic, found near river banks, primarly in small caves and cracks in stones, in flowing water with high turbulence and water speed (Ref. 52307). Found only in rocky habitats with little or no sand or gravel (Ref. 53766). Presumably feeds upon plants and other organisms which grow attached to the rocky substrate (Ref. 53766). Forages on algae using specialised, abrupt movements of the head (Ref. 52307). Probably a cave-spawner that practices pair-bonding, albeit weakly (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Gobiocichla wonderi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307), occurs in swift waters (Ref. 7378, 53405) and rapids (Ref. 2756, 3012). Feeds mainly on algue attached to rocks (Ref. 2756, 53781). Probably a cave spawner that practices pair-bonding, albeit weakly (Ref. 52307). From aquarium observations: no assistance from male exhibited during guarding or cleaning of eggs and larvae; juveniles swim freely at about 3 weeks post-spawning and are guarded by both parents for about 1 month; male is not as strongly involved during brood care
as female (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Gobiocypris rarus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in paddy fields, ditches, ponds, and rivulets.  Feeds on tiny aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Gobiodon aoyagii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed in protected bays and reef edges and slopes of Japan, in the interstices among branches of corals of the genus Acropora. In Papua New Guinea and the Great Barrier Reef, it is reported to almost totally be confined to Acropora tenuis (Ref. 94251).

species.name: Gobiodon atrangulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among Acropora spp. Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Gobiodon erythrospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is observed to be found among branches of table-like corals, usually Acropora nasuta, also A. valida, A. millepora (the coarse branched form) and sometimes A. tenuis (Ref. 94251).

species.name: Gobiodon fulvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446).

species.name: Gobiodon micropus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among the branches of Acropora (Ref. 2334); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Monogamous (Ref. 52884). The male takes care of eggs deposited on a coral branch (Ref. 32163). Has the ability to change sex in both directions to favor reproductive success (Ref. 32163).

species.name: Gobiodon multilineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among Acropora spp. Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Gobiodon winterbottomi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef slopes where individuals only live as commensals on the plate-shaped coral, Echinopora lamellosa (Ref. 91086)..

species.name: Gobioides africanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in muddy inshore marine habitats (Ref. 79590, 92840), over sandy bottom and in estuaries (Ref. 92840). Perhaps also found in brackish waters (Ref. 79590).

species.name: Gobioides grahamae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy areas, under stones (Ref. 27974).

species.name: Gobioides sagitta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4343) in brackish waters (Ref. 57403), i.e., estuaries and occasionally lagoons; sometimes ascends rivers, but rarely moves beyond the intertidal zone (Ref. 57403, 79590). Maximum size: perhaps reaching 500 mm total length (Ref. 57403, 79590).

species.name: Gobiomorphus alpinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobionellus liolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tidepools, over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 55435).

species.name: Gobionellus munizi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobionotothen barsukovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopsis exigua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopsis liolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic inhabitant of sand-rubble bottom next to reefs in 3-20 m (Ref, 90102).

species.name: Gobiopsis namnas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All type specimens were captured by a beam trawl at the depth of 101 m; no substratum data of the habitat were available. Found with many other fish specimens, e.g., the champsodontid Champsodon snyderi and the gobiid Amblychaeturichthys sciistius (Ref. 84002).

species.name: Gobiopsis uranophilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopterus birtwistlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopterus brachypterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of the genus Gobiopterus are found in fresh and brackish waters (Ref. 42915).

species.name: Gobiopterus chuno
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Occurs in slow flowing water and swamps, often in backwaters (Ref. 43281).  Found in fresh and brackish water in the lower courses of rivers.  Feeds mainly on zooplankton.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Gobiopterus macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopterus panayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiopterus smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiosoma hildebrandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiosoma homochroma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobiosoma schultzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobitrichinotus arnoulti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobius ateriformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from tide pool to 11m, on sand, stones and rock substrata (Ref. 39517).

species.name: Gobius bontii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Marine epibenthic littoral species, entering estuaries and even freshwater (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Gobius hypselosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobius koseirensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobius leucomelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobius rubropunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobius scorteccii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gobius senegambiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore on sand (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gobius tetrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found most commonly on mixed coralline algae, but also on open sand and rock substrata, often with Gnatholepis thompsoni (Ref. 39517).

species.name: Gobius tropicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This doubtful species requires taxonomic clarification.

species.name: Goblinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Goby flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters shelf waters.

species.name: Goby killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in very small pools, shallows in swamps and shallow swampy parts of brooks in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Godavari thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An estuarine species, but there is no indication if this signifies a marine or riverine fish.

species.name: Goeldiella eques
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goeldi’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In an aquarium environment, this species demonstrated increased activity levels at night, and only sporadic foraging activities in the course of the day (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Goemon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and sheltered seaward reefs (Ref. 9710); also found in bays (Ref. 9768).  Often schools on coastal reefs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Gogangra laevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gogangra viridescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Goggle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in the surge zone of seaward reefs (Ref. 9360).

species.name: Goggles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Gogo arcuatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gogo arcuatus is found in pools surrounded by large, exposed boulders from a clear, shallow, forested stretch of the river, where the substrate is very rocky and the current swift (Ref. 56142).

species.name: Gogo atratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over an open sand/cobble bottom interspersed with scattered rocky ourcroppings at a depth of less than 1 m; the water is clear, with the bottom consisting of either sand or rock/cobble; the bottom is lightly overlain with leaf litter in quieter stretches of the river (Ref. 75790).

species.name: Gogo brevibarbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gogo ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a clear, clean, and well oxygenated river with a substrate composed of sand and gravel, with large scattered boulders (Ref. 56142).

species.name: Golani’s lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Saurida golanii has the deepest known distribution of any species of Saurida in the Indo-West Pacific. Its occurrence in depths of 200-500 m is similar to other more typically shallow water species in the Gulf of Aqaba that have also been captured in deep water (Baranes and Golani 1993). This phenomenon is probably a consequence of the unusual deep convective mixing of warmer surface waters to depths of 600 m or more, that occurs in the Gulf of Aqaba (Wolf-Vecht et al. 1992), resulting in an almost constant temperature throughout the water column (Reiss & Hottinger, 1984) that extends the distribution of many species of shallow water origin into much deeper water (Baranes & Golani 1993).

species.name: Gold brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in soft mud bottoms at shallow depths (0.7-6 m) of quiet lagoons, backwaters and saline parts of estuaries (Ref. 7251, 55786).  Reported to give birth to very few, about 15 mm long juveniles in each clutch; one female found to have four 5-8 mm long embryos and has a 3.2 mm bivalve in the intestine (Ref. 55786).  Probably common where it occurs (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Gold sheen silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gold-bar sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Like other sand divers, it occurs on sand slopes with strong currents at times (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 26146.

species.name: Gold-birdled sandsmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottoms 9Ref. 11230).

species.name: Gold-browed dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered habitats with rich coral growth to about 30 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Observed in western New Guinea in habitats of silty dead coral reef, near the base of steep slopes 13-29 m depths; these reefs are characterised by numerous small caverns/overhangs and fish were usually seen adjacent to vertical surfaces. They appear to occupy territories or home ranges of about 2 sq. m and are often encountered solitarily, sometimes in loosely associated pairs (Ref. 74963).

species.name: Gold-colored angle fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species.

species.name: Gold-lined dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from reefs and reef slopes (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Gold-marked shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sloping silty sand bottoms in 20-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gold-rim Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was observed at Yap (Caroline Islands), in a group of about a dozen individuals living among large (about 1-2 m) rock boulders just above the upper edge of a precipitous drop-off.  A juvenile of approximately 4 cm SL was observed at a depth of 120 m, below the site where the type specimens were collected. Its color pattern was consistent with that of the adults (Ref. 59379).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gold-ring Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Exclusively found in reefs subject to strong currents and frequent cold-water upwellings;  associated with coral overhangs or large rubble pieces on hard bottom substrates.  When approached, individuals retreat under the rubble or overhang (Ref. 89054).

species.name: Gold-specked prawn-goby
species.description: Occurs on fine sand and silt bottoms of subtidal reef flats and lagoons to a depth over 20 m.  Uses burrows of alpheid shrimps for refuge.  Inhabits coastal sand slopes to about 15 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Gold-specs jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males of this species are strongly territorial and frequently engage in jaw locking combat, apparently to evict rivals or confiscate their burrows (Ref. 81517). Found in sand/rubble bottoms near reefs in about 5-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gold-spotted dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently prefer harsh, monsoon and upwelling impacted habitats in the south and west of Socotra Island. It was also collected from a macroalgae dominated biotope with large sponges and very sparse encrusting hard coral on rock platform with gravelly sand; in sparse hard coral and filter feeder community on rock outcrops; and additional visual records were made in from a Porites dominated community on rock platform (Ref. 88695).

species.name: Gold-streaked prawn-goby
species.description: Found on sandy lagoon bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Inhabits coastal sand slopes in rubble patches on reef crests, usually on dark substrates to about 20 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Goldback damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs, also in sheltered clear water reefs in moderate depths (Ref. 48636).  Feed on planktonic crustaceans, fish eggs, algae, and small invertebrates.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Goldbelly damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults mainly inhabit inner reef slopes with mixed rubble, coral and algae.  They aggregate close to the bottom (Ref. 37816), usually in small groups (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Goldbelly topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds, lakes and lowland streams (2-150, usually less than 30, m elevation).  Prefers stagnant water over muddy substrate with abundant aquatic vegetation.  Feeds on diatoms, algae, leaves of aquatic plants, detritus and insect larvae.

species.name: Goldbreast splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among coral and sponge of seaward reef slopes (Ref. 37816).  Cryptic, seldom seen by divers.  Feeds on flake food and brine shrimp (Ref. 37816).  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Golden barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in rivers and standing water over silt and mud (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on small crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Golden barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly reaches twice the maximum size reported and a weight of more than 5 kg; predominantly piscivorous, larger specimens feeding exclusively on fish; in Lake Mweru omnivorous with a piscivorous and sarcophagous tendency; probably reproduces during the rainy season (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Golden butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal and inner reefs; juveniles among branching corals. Solitary or paired (Ref. 9710). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). Hybridizes with Chaetodon rainfordi (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Golden cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Golden carp gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools amongst dense clumps of submerged water weeds and dead branches (Ref. 2906, 44894).  Presumably the species has a high tolerance to increased salinity levels and water temperatures, which typically occur in the habitat during drought periods (Ref. 44894).  Males with slightly pronounced hump on forehead (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Golden charr
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes.  Feeds on zooplankton in summer and on benthic invertebrates for the rest of the year.  Spawns over gravel and stones in shallow water, along stone shore line (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Golden cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Rarely in markets (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Golden darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on walls, in shallow reef areas (Ref. 85755). Minimum depth at 5 m (B. Victor, pers. omm. 10/18).

species.name: Golden Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky areas and vegetated margins of lakes and streams (Ref. 5259), primarily in lakes preferring still or gently flowing waters (Ref. 51290, 44894).  Adults prefer the shelter provided by complex habitats such as rocky lake shores and also in-lake macrophytes beds and marsh habitats (Ref. 51290).  Juveniles occur in the water column until 4-5 months of age (40 mm in length) and then move inshore seeking shelter and larger prey items (Ref. 51290).  Shoaling in open water when young (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 5259, 44894) and mollusks with cannibalism of eggs and juvenile fish being common (Ref. 51290, 44894).  Breeds in early spring among rocks in the shallows (Ref. 44894). Most fish live for 3-4 years with some reaching over 6 years of age (Ref. 51290).

species.name: Golden gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slowly flowing and standing waters rich in vegetation and with shallow areas.

species.name: Golden gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Golden hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Previously known from deep reefs but has since been found in shallow water (1-8 m).  Territorial on reef tops (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Golden julie
species.description: Poisson. Rock-dwelling.  Usually solitary; territorial.  Feeds on microorganisms.  Breeding in captivity has led to changes in its colors and behaviors.  Since there have been few new importations,  this dwarf species has generally been available only in a somewhat degenerate form and does not always show its true colors (Ref. 6770).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Golden killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small fast flowing mountain brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Golden lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neustonic (Ref. 58302).  High-oceanic and mesopelagic.  Found from the surface to 300 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Golden livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing waters.

species.name: Golden mbuna
species.description: Poisson. Found in rocky habitats.  Feeds from the biocover by nibbling and picking on the algae (Ref. 5595).  Aquarium keeping:  aggressive towards conspecifics; many females for one male; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Golden mola hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow vegetated habitat.  Feeds on invertebrates and probably insect larvae that are mostly found on 'dead' edge near rocks and close to the roots of weeds (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Golden Nile catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In those parts where Chrysichthys maurus and Chrysichthys auratus overlap (from Liberia to Ghana, to the east of the Volta), C. auratus does not enter rivers, but remains in estuaries and lagoons, where both species are sympatric; in the coastal region, C. auratus has been reported as C. filamentosus (Ref. 57126). Found in lakes and coastal rivers (Ref. 3236) and appears to tolerate a certain amount of salt (Ref. 78218). Occurs usually over soft, slightly muddy substrates or substrates with heavy layers of leafy detritus in deep, relatively quiet waters (Ref. 6868). Feeds on mollusks and small crustaceans (Branchiopods, Copepods, Ostracoda) which it digs from the substrate (Ref. 27935), and also on insects (Ref. 28714) and fish (Ref. 28714, 78218).

species.name: Golden otocinclus
species.description: Mainly nocturnal.  Feeds on algae (Ref. 6868).  Aquarium keeping:  feeds on plants and roots; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Golden perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Golden perch live throughout the river systems, from the clear, fast flowing upper reaches to the turbid, slow flowing lower reaches and associated billabongs and backwaters. They favor deep pools with plenty of cover from fallen timber, rocky ledges or undercut banks (Ref. 27439, 44894). Prefer warm, slow-moving, turbid sections of streams. Also occur in flooded lakes, backwaters and impoundments. Tolerant of temperatures between 4° and 35°C and high salinity levels (up to 35 p.p.t.). Solitary species (Ref. 44894). Their diet is dominated by yabbies (Cherax destructor), and a variety of fish species (Ref. 27439). Juveniles disperse throughout the floodplain to find food and cover (Ref. 27440). They feed on abundant zooplankton on recently inundated floodplains (Ref. 6390, 44894). Adults feed on fishes, mollusks and crayfish (Ref. 44894). Spawn from early spring to late autumn. Golden perch is Australia's most migratory freshwater fish species (Ref. 6390). Spawn in flooded backwaters near the surface at night after heavy spring and summer rains. Usually a long upstream spawning migration is undertaken (movements of 2000 kilometers by tagged fish have been documented). Eggs float near the surface and hatch in 24-36 hours. Males mature after 2-3 years (20-30 centimeters), females after 4 years (40 centimeters) (Ref. 44894). They are being reared by private and government hatcheries in Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland (Ref. 27552) and the fry and fingerlings produced from these hatcheries are stocked in public waters and farm dams (Ref. 26869).

species.name: Golden pheasant panchax
species.description: Occurs in pools, swamps and swampy parts of brooks in the rainforest and humid forested savanna.  9 cm TL  (Ref. 3788).  Parents die during dry season and eggs left in the mud hatch only when the waters return at the start of the next rainy season.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Golden pike-characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden pomfret
species.description: Pelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Golden ponyfish
species.description: Inhabits offshore coastal waters (Ref. 47581).  Probably treated as by-catch by trawlers (Ref. 47581).

species.name: Golden redbait
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Golden redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mud-bottomed to rock-bottomed pools, runs and riffles of creeks and small to large rivers.  Occasionally found in lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on immature mayflies, caddisflies and midges (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Golden roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Golden sand-eater
species.description: Inhabits shallow waters with muddy bottoms in sheltered bays.  Feeds on small invertebrates, and also on zooplankton and occasionally diatoms (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Golden scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal lagoons, large intertidal pools or estuaries; also in silty reefs or amongst large coral rubble (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Golden silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 12.4-15.0 cm long and 8.7-9.0 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).  Reported to feed primarily on amphipods, decapods, fishes, euphausids, and squid on Yamato Bank in the Sea of Japan.  Maximum length reported 116 cm TL (Ref, 89865).

species.name: Golden skiffia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An experimental fish. Pinnate diatoms (largely benthic), filamentous algae indicate that this species grazes rocks and plant surfaces along or near the bottom (Ref. 29410).

species.name: Golden spadefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur mostly in large schools along drop-offs, including outer reefs; singly in coastal waters.  Juveniles are on deep slopes among tall coral formation (Ref. 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Golden spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur mainly in the upper and middle reaches of rivers (Ref. 31729).

species.name: Golden Systomus
species.description: The type locality, the river bed of Keezhvaipur of Manimala River, is generally occupied by sand and gravel, with bed rocks and black clays occasionally present. This stretch of the river has a width of 40-120 m, depth of the water column in summer season ranges from 0.5 to 7 m and bank height varies from 4 to 7 m with respect to general water level. It is covered by more or less dense riparian vegetation; the flora includes Dendrocalamus strictus, Ochreinauclea missionis, Acacia caesia, Bambusa bambos, B. vulgaris, Hydnocarpus pentandra and others and with Colocasia esculenta, Cynodon dactylon and Nymphaea forming the majority of the stream vegetation. Some fishes co-occurring with this species in this region are: Anguilla bengalensis, A. bicolor, Salmostoma boopis, Barilius bakeri, Rasbora dandia, Osteobrama bakeri, Puntius mahecola, Pethia punctatus, Dawkinsia filamentosa, Gonoproktopterus kurali, Catla catla, Labeo ariza, L. dussumieri, Garra mullya, Horabagrus brachysoma, Mystus oculatus, M. gulio, Wallago attu, Xenentodon cancila, Ambassis commersoni, A. gymnocephalus, Pseudambassis ranga, Pristolepis malabarica, Etroplus maculatus, E. suratensis, and Glossogobius giuris (Ref. 104747).

species.name: Golden tank goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers in clear to turbid water, usually over sand or gravel bottoms (Ref. 5259) and mud (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on aquatic insect larvae and prawns (Ref. 5259, 44894) and small fishes (Ref.  12693).  Larvae occur in the marine environment (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Golden topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in swamps, sloughs, vegetated pools, and backwaters of sluggish creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feed primarily on insects (Ref. 10294).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Golden weedfish
species.description: Occurs in rock pools and subtidal area down to 30 m (Ref. 9003).  Inhabits kelp beds, sometimes with loose weeds on sand; also in coastal bays.  Feeds on weed dwelling crustaceans and small fish (Ref. 9003).  Viviparous (Ref. 94108).

species.name: Golden-line barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Golden-margined hap
species.description: Common at 10 m depth and prefers the area where non-breeding individuals congregate into schools over the sandy part of the biotope.  Feeds on phytoplankton or takes its food from the somewhat muddy layer on the substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Golden-nosed lantern fish
species.description: Meso- (Ref. 58302, 75154) and benthopelagic in nearshore areas at 0-190 m at night, 418-960 m during day (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Goldencrown tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goldeneye shovelnose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is mostly collected at depths shallower than 150 m.  Male individuals mature at 46 cm TL, immature at 37.6 cm TL (Ref. 58070).

species.name: Goldeneye snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest female with yolked eggs measured 9.1 cm SL; smallest male with enlarged, swollen testes 7.67 cm SL. Eggs were collected from the octocoral Primnoa sp. from Seguam Pass, with eggs of another liparid (Ref. 57077).

species.name: Goldface toby
species.description: Occurs in deep reefs, most probably over hard bottom (Ref. 43205).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Goldfin tinfoil barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in midwater to bottom depths in large and medium-sized rivers.  Found in large rivers in the dry season and moves to medium-sized rivers in the wet season.  Usually found over coarse substrate.  Has not persisted in any impoundments.  Its gut is usually full of  fine matter with occasional insect exoskeleton.  Breeds at the end of the rainy season, as the water levels fall, young of the year 2 cm length appear in February to March.  Marketed fresh and also seen in the aquarium trade (Ref.12693).

species.name: Goldfinned barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Goldie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally caught by trawlers in 50 to 200 m (Ref. 11228).

species.name: Goldie barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools in clear, rocky streams often streams with emergent marginal vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193). Spawning is likely to begin in summer, from October to November (Ref. 122070); breeding pairs lay eggs in vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Goldie river mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rapid-flowing streams in hilly or mountainous terrain (Ref. 2847).  Adults may ascend rivers, reported to 350 m above sea level.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Goldie River rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamps, backwaters, tributary streams and large rivers.

species.name: Goldline blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits limestone rock, rubble and coral reef areas.  Usually near sea urchins (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on amphipods and copepods (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Goldline darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky runs of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Goldlined coris
species.description: A shallow-water species inhabiting rubble and sandy bottoms with algal cover (Ref. 2334).  Often encountered in small groups (Ref. 33411).

species.name: Goldman's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas with both living coral and coral rubble, and from both moderately clear and turbid water (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Goldsash fusilier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species schools with Caesio variliniata and both have been observed together in large shoals in northern KwaZulu-Natal. Prolific spawning in the Park Rynie area, KwaZulu-Natal (30°20’ S, 30°45’ E) is apparent due to abundance of eggs of this species from plankton collections (Ref. 94071).

species.name: Goldspot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open sand, rock, and rubble areas. Often occurs with the bridled goby, Coryphopterus glaucofraenum. Feeds on organisms and organic material by taking sand into its mouth and expelling it through the gill openings, filtering out its food in the process (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Goldspot sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs in 5-25 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Goldspotted angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Encountered in channels and outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602), and drop offs at depths of 10-65 m.  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Solitary, pairs or in small groups.  Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Goldspotted eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common near islands and in rocky or coral areas (Ref. 7251).  May move beneath the sand (Ref. 9710).  Found in seagrass bed sand areas with sand and coral rubble (Ref. 26938).  Feeds mainly on crabs (Ref. 32).  Forages at night for prey.

species.name: Goldspotted killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in marine, on tidal flats and creeks, but enters brackish water (Ref. 7251).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Goldspotted snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goldspotted tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Goldstripe characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goldstripe darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clay and sand-bottomed runs and pools of vegetated, spring-fed headwaters and creeks (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae, dipteran pupae, caddisfly larvae, dytiscid beetle larvae, and small crayfish (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Goldstripe rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goldstripe wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open sand and rubble areas of seaward reefs, to depths greater than 34 m (Ref. 9710).  Usually in small groups of females with single males patrolling the area (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Goldtail demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral-rich areas of sheltered lagoon and inshore coral reefs (Ref. 9710). They occur in small groups on Acropora patches (Ref. 48636). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Goliath hagfish
species.description: Adult female holotype had dozens of small eggs, 45 X 14 mm, in the mesentery, which was attached to the body wall.  The eggs did not have terminal anchor filaments and hooks (Ref. 57440).

species.name: Gollum snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a paddy field (Ref. 120401).

species.name: Gomez' shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in sheltered water at depths ranging between 8-15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Gomon's tuskfish
