species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be a synonym of C. margaritiferus (Ref. 90102). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Usually in groups in rubble bottoms 30-82 m deep (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gomon’s frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gomon’s gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gon's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal, mangrove zones and thought to enter rivers, but also found with shipwrecks in deeper water laying on muddy substrates (Ref. 48635); also on reefs, over sandy and muddy bottoms in silty conditions (Ref. 54391) Forms aggregations that hover above rocky outcrops (Ref 90102). Feeds on fish eggs and larvae, shrimps, and pelagic polychaetes (Ref. 31551).

species.name: Gonelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters (seashore, tide pools), but descends (especially in winter) to 100 m or more.  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on small crustaceans, polychaetes, mollusks and fish eggs.  The eggs are laid on the sea bed in a large clump, which is closely guarded until hatched (Ref. 9900).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Spawning occur in November - January .  Female lays 80-200 eggs in a large ball under a stone or in an empty bivalve shell (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Gongota loach
species.description: Inhabits streams and rivers (Ref. 1479).  Occurs in shallow slow-moving streams with sandy, muddy or gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Gonichthys venetus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goniistius quadricornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fairly deep water.

species.name: Goniistius rubrolabiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154), in rocky reef areas (Ref. 120445).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Gonorynchus abbreviatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone, 50-100 m on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Gonorynchus forsteri
species.description: Inhabits coastal sandy habitats , bays and estuaries where they remain buried during the day.  Also found in deeper water 160-678 m.  Juvenile, subadult and adult occur in shallow coastal areas; adults also inhabit deep shelf and slope areas and isolated offshore plateaus, and are capable of moving between the two  (Ref. 48492).  With the first New Caledonian record based on one ripe female and one spent male, captured at 960-1233 m depth, over 700 nautical miles from the nearest known populations, it is hypothesized that adult sandfish migrates along oceanic ridges to spawn in southern New Caledonian waters (Ref. 48492).

species.name: Gonorynchus greyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic fishes in shallow estuaries and outer shelf; juveniles are pelagic in open ocean.  They bury themselves head first when disturbed (Ref. 33838).  White flesh is firm and of good flavor.

species.name: Gonostoma denudatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Exhibits diel vertical migrations, juveniles and adults in 400-700 m by day and 100-200 m by night (Ref. 4769).  Photophores developing in fishes over 18-35 mm SL (Ref. 4769).

species.name: Gonostome a grandes dents
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Occur between 100-200 m and 500-800 m at night and 25-600 m and 1,250-1,500 m during the day (Ref. 4463).  Feed on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4769).  Photophores develop in fishes over 6-22 mm SL (Ref. 4769).  Protandric hermaphrodite, oviparous with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35800). Minimum depth from Ref. 4463.

species.name: Gonostome étincelé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  There is marked stratification of size with depth and no diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4769).  Initial photophore develops at about 1.1 cm SL (Ref. 4769).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Gon’s sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goobala whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Goodlad's stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds, generally on sand bottoms.

species.name: Goonch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goosefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Goosehead scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow clear waters from shore to 75 m depth.

species.name: Gopher rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit holes or crevices in rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Territorial (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Goram dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal bays and estuaries (Ref. 48636), over  sand, mud, or dead coral rubble of lagoons and outer reef slopes.  Feeds mainly on small benthic invertebrates.  Usually buried in substrate.  Occurs in small groups (Ref. 48636).  May also be solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Gordiichthys combibus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow water, over a gray sand beach (Ref. 43688).

species.name: Gordiichthys randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water, over sand and algal beds (Ref. 43688).

species.name: Goret bossu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Goret bronze
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 9114).  Juveniles are common in littoral pools (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Goret bélier
species.description: Found on sand and gravel bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 26282).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Goret corocoro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, over sand, rock or mud bottoms (Ref. 13608). Juveniles found near the shore, associated with Thalassia beds (Ref. 9626). Also found in brackish water (Ref. 3798). Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, polychaete worms, fishes, and other invertebrates (Ref. 9626). Well appreciated as a food fish; marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Goret cubain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, over sand and mud bottoms.  Forms schools.  Mainly nocturnal and non-burrowing.  Feeds on crustaceans and smaller fishes.  Undergoes seasonal migration as well as local nocturnal-diurnal foraging migrations (Ref. 25).

species.name: Goret olive
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 5213).  Plentiful in tidal estuaries (Ref. 2135).  Stomach contents of specimens collected from Iraq composed mainly of mollusks, sponges and tunicates (Ref. 97537). Large shoals of juveniles occur around shallow water reefs where they consume shrimps and other small invertebrates, being themselves eaten by larger fish; larger specimens are found in deeper water where they spawn throughout the year.  Used extensively for bait, flesh rather insipid (Ref. 2799).

species.name: Goret zapate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 9114).  Important food fish (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Goret à six bandes
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters and frequents sandy areas near rocks.  Flesh good but undergoes rapid softening (Ref. 2799).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3412).  Depth range based on occurrence; to be replaced with a better reference.

species.name: Goret à trois bandes
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Gorette allongée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy or muddy bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Gorette bacoco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools above rocky, boulder strewn reefs, slopes, and hard substrate with good water movement (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Gorette blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in dense aggregations during the day on patch reefs, around coral formations, or on sandy bottoms (Ref. 9710). Juveniles common in Thalassia testudinum beds (Ref. 5217). Feeds on crustaceans, small mollusks, and small fishes. Frequently exhibits a territorial 'kissing' display in which two contenders push each other on the lips with their mouths wide open (Ref. 9710). Marketed fresh. Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Gorette brillante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal seas, on sandy or muddy bottoms.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Gorette caco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear reefs (Ref. 9710).  Forms dense schools (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on crustaceans and sea urchins (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette casse-burgot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal reefs during the day but disperses at night  in search for food.  Often feed by digging in sand (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Gorette catalinète
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh or reduced to fishmeal (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Gorette catire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups over coral and rocky reefs and drop-offs (Ref. 9710). Juveniles are abundant in Thalassia beds (Ref. 5217). Feeds on crustaceans, bivalves, and occasionally on small fishes. Marketed fresh.

species.name: Gorette charbonnier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear rocky or coral reefs (Ref. 5217) and mangroves (Ref. 26340).  Often forming schools (Ref. 3798).  Nocturnal feeder on crabs, gastropods, starfish and annelid worms (Ref. 5521).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette chere-chere
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and rubble bottoms; occasionally on coral reefs and rocky areas (Ref. 3798).  Rarely in clear oceanic insular areas (Ref. 5217).  Often found in schools (Ref. 3798).  Juveniles encountered near the shore, over sandy bottoms near seagrass beds (Ref. 9626).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow neritic areas, over shallow mud to sand-mud bottoms; less common in areas with clear water and coral reef habitats (Ref. 5217).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large schools on rocky and coral reefs, often under ledges or close to elkhorn coral (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles abundant in near-shore seagrass beds (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette marchand
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal reefs, the young on seagrass beds, adults in schools in relatively open areas (Ref. 9710).  Rare at oceanic islands (Ref. 9710).  Feeds at night on mollusks and small fishes (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette mèche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear inshore and offshore reefs (Ref. 9710) and adjacent grass beds, often in schools (Ref. 3798).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along exposed outer or deeper reefs.  Found on semi-hard substrates (Ref. 5217).  Maximum depth down to 210 m was recorded from individuals observed by submersibles (Ref. 27283). Feeds mainly on plankton (Ref. 5217); small crustaceans (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Gorette ronco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal seas on sandy or muddy bottoms (Ref. 11482).  Found in estuaries (Ref. 9114).  Feeds on polychaetes, copepods and amphipods (Ref. 50313).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Gorette ruí
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally in protected areas such as bays or inlets; rarely in insular areas with clear oceanic water and coral reefs (Ref. 5217).  Juveniles encountered near the shore.  Feeds on small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 3798).  Taken incidentally and not considered commercially important (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coastal waters.  Forms schools over rocky and sandy bottoms.  Feeds at night.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Gorette tibouche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed rocky areas and coral reefs. Often near elkhorn and staghorn corals (Ref. 9710). Commonly found in schools. Juveniles are encountered in Thalassia beds (Ref. 9626). Adults are observed in coral reefs during the day but enters open waters at night to feed on mainly on plankton (Ref. 9626), but also on small crustaceans and mollusks. Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette tomtate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Inhabits seagrass beds, sand flats, and patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Forms schools (Ref. 5521).  Feeds on small crustaceans, mollusks, other benthic invertebrates, plankton, and algae (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Gorette à queue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in schools around coastal reefs during the day, dispersing over sandy bottoms at night (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Gorgasia cotroneii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gorgasia inferomaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gorgasia japonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sand flats adjacent to reef, usually at moderate depth below bases of drop-offs or steep slopes to feed on plankton drifting over (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Gorgasia sillneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gorgasia taiwanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Identified by shape of the snout (Ref. 47567).

species.name: Gorgasia thamani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gorgeous barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gorgeous goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs.

species.name: Gorgeous swallowtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in moderately deep waters, on rocky substrata on steep slopes (Ref. 120660). Piscivore (Ref. 97629).

species.name: Gorgona guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Living individuals reported to be in sandy and rocky environments near coral-reefs at 18-24 m depth of the Colombian coast (Ref. 101827).  In contrast the type specimen was taken from a depth of 70 m (Ref. 26282).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature at ca. 71 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Gorogobius nigricinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal rocks and pools.  Also found ,on rocks, sand and girders in the sublittoral zone as well as in areas of heavy wave surge perhaps facultative on echinoderms (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Gorogobius stevcici
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Types were collected between 15 and 25 m depth, but otherwise observed at entrances of small caves between 20 and 40 m depth.  Small individuals (about 4 cm SL) were seen at Rolas Island in 20 m depth hovering upside down; individuals of approximately twice this size were reported in small caves between 35 to 40 m depth at Diogo Vaz (Ref. 75175).

species.name: Gorongoza kneria
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gossamer blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in mangrove swamps and river estuaries, but more often in freshwater lakes (Ref. 4404, 58302). Benthic (Ref. 58302). The size and shape of the mouth, the presence of large canine teeth suggest that this fish is probably a predator on small aquatic animals (Ref. 44091). Oviparous; eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Gosztonyia antarctica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Goto's herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools in coastal waters and appears to enter estuaries, if not to ascend some way up to rivers.

species.name: Gouanie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters (Ref. 10954). It reaches highest abundances in pebble and boulder beaches of less than 0.5 m depth (24 individuals/m2 in Messina), but reported to be found down to 2 m of water depth. It was also observed to occur with Lepadogaster lepadogaster and that males build and guard nests under boulders during spawning season (Ref. 123696),

species.name: Gougeon à gorge épineuse
species.description: Occurs in estuaries and coastal streams, usually over rocky or gravel bottoms.

species.name: Goujon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in nearly all types of riverine and lacustrine habitats with sand bottom.  Found in small mountain streams, large lowland rivers and large lakes (Ref. 59043). Inhabits fast flowing rivers with sand or gravel bottom but may also occur in still waters.  Forms schools.  Feeds on insect larvae, mollusks, and crustaceans.  Normally active during the day but if they are disturbed, in particular, by predators, they can defer their activity to periods when light intensity is weak.  Capable of emitting squeaking sounds.  These vocalizations, which is a means by which fish communicate with each other, vary with the degree of activity and the temperature and are independent of the season of reproduction (Ref. 30578).  Breeds in shallow water over stones, sand or plant material.  Eggs are released above substrate and drift with current, sinking to bottom and sticking to substrate. Larvae and juveniles occur on the bottom and prefer detritus-rich sandy habitats and low current (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gourami
species.description: Inhabits swamps, lakes and rivers (Ref. 9987), among vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Found in medium to large rivers and stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals (Ref. 12975).  Omnivorous.  Feeds on both plants and animals such as some aquatic weeds, fish, frogs, earthworms and sometimes dead animals (Ref. 6459).  Can breathe moist air, so can be kept alive for long periods out of water, making it possible to distribute it in areas lacking a cold chain (Ref. 9987).  Was reported from miocene deposits in Central Sumatra (Ref. 7426).  Utilized fresh and eaten steamed, pan-fried and baked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Gourami bleu
species.description: Espèce de poisson. Lives in lowland wetlands (Ref. 57235).  Found in marshes, swamps and canals (Ref. 43281).  Inhabits shallow sluggish or standing-water with a lot of aquatic vegetation.  Occurs in seasonally flooded forests throughout the middle and lower Mekong (Ref. 12693).  Undertakes lateral migrations from the Mekong mainstream, or other permanent water bodies, to  flooded areas during the flood season and returns to the permanent water bodies at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Feeds on zooplankton, crustaceans and insect larvae.  Processed into salted, dried fish in Java (Ref. 4929).  Also marketed fresh and commonly seen in the aquarium fish trade (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Gourami embrasseur
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in lakes and rivers (Ref. 56749).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Prefers slow-moving water with thick vegetation.  Feeds on a variety of plants and animals, including green algae and zooplankton (Ref. 6459) as well as aquatic insects near the water surface (Ref. 12693).  Utilized fresh for steaming, pan-frying, broiling and baking (Ref. 9987); also processed as dried or salted fish; ripe ovaries are collected and separately eaten (Ref. 56749). Large quantities of small fish are exported for aquarium use in Japan, Europe, North America, Australia and other parts of the world (Ref. 9987).  Very popular with aquarists due to its habit of sucking its lips and kissing other fishes, plants and other objects (Ref. 4833).  Aquarium keeping:  not recommended for home aquariums; minimum aquarium size 150 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Gourami miel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools, ditches, inundated fields, ponds and beels (Ref. 1479).  Occurs in rivers and lakes with vegetation (Ref. 41236).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Gourami nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow moving streams, rivulets and lakes with plenty of vegetation (Ref. 41236).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Gourami peau de serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sluggish or standing-water habitats with a lot of aquatic vegetation.  Occurs in flooded forests of the lower Mekong and gradually moves back to rivers and Great Lake as floodwaters recede (Ref. 12693, 57235).  Generally feeds on aquatic plants.  Can breathe air directly, as well as absorb oxygen from water through its gills (Ref. 9987).  The flesh is of good quality; may be grilled or used for fish soup.  In Thailand there is a trade of dried pla salid for the benefit of people in areas where it is not caught (Ref 2686).  Cultured both for food and for export as aquarium fish (Ref. 9987).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Highly economic species; both by capture and culture includes in the peat areas (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Gourami à grosses lèvres
species.description: Found in rivers.  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Graceful dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Graceful mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather that actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Graceful pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Benthic (Ref. 58302, 75154). Lives in starfish (Culcita discoidea) and sea cucumbers (Holothuria scabra and H. argus). In the latter reported by Trott (1970) to form male - female pairs and to parasite host. Parasitic, feeding on gonads and respiratory tree of its host. Usually associated with Bohadschia argus (Ref 90102).

species.name: Graceful pimelodella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly active at dusk.  In captivity, it feeds on worms and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Graceful priapella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Graceful threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on mud or sand bottoms.  Appears in small quantities in local markets.

species.name: Graceful whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Graceful-tailed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Found in caves and among corals of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Secretive, feeds on zooplankton well above bottom at night (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gracilis wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Found in coastal bays, estuaries, and on sand near reefs (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Graery threadfin seabass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mangrove areas as well as shallow inlets and bays (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Graham's conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Graham's gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock pools and subtidal areas down to 50 m.  Found in areas of sand or mud, associated with rocks, shells, or other partially buried objects.

species.name: Graham's stonebasher
species.description: In Lake Victoria in shallow, coastal waters particularly where bottom is sandy (Ref. 4903). In Lake Kyoga it frequents areas overgrown by water lilies (Ref. 49805). Feeds on chironomid larvae, and to lesser extent on Trichoptera, Gastropoda (Ref. 12526). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Males grow to larger size than females; breeds twice a year, during the rainy seasons; migrates up the river to spawn (Ref. 10608).

species.name: Graham's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Grahamina capito
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on sheltered coastal reefs and rock and shell substrata in bays and harbors;  from intertidal pools to at least 12m (Ref. 84085). They feed on small benthic organisms.  Prey is stalked and swallowed whole (Ref. 26966).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Grahamina gymnota
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky shores and occasionally in exposed rocky pools (Ref. 13227).  Also common on wharf piles among encrusting invertebrates. Depth to at least 7 m (Ref. 84085).

species.name: Graham’s skate
species.description: A demersal species most commonly found on continental slope. Biology poorly known (Ref. 114953). No observed adolescent males, but with undeveloped claspers at 46.8 cm TL; adult males from 54.5- 62.2 cm TL, and smallest confirmed juvenile 18.3 cm TL (Ref. 75648).

species.name: Grain de café
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This small species exhibits a calm behavior.  It was introduced in Germany in 1962 for the aquarium trade (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Grallenia arenicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found to be solitary on sandy bottom, around boulders or rocky reefs (Ref. 75132).

species.name: Grallenia dimorpha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sandy substrate (Ref. 116128).

species.name: Grammatonotus ambiortus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatonotus lanceolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatonotus laysanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatonotus macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatonotus surugaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatostomias circularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatostomias dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Grammatostomias flagellibarba
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatostomias ovatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grammatotria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults in aggregation roam over sandy bottoms.  Probably carnivorous, feed on mollusks and diatoms (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Grammonus longhursti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, found on soft bottom (Ref. 34024).  Viviparous (Ref. 6526).

species.name: Grammonus minutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depending on the changes in the current system in the Bay of Nha Trang and adjoining areas, juveniles and adolescents of deep-water fishes occur in the collection area at these shallow depths. According to T.T. Hieu, Institute of Oceanography, Nha Trang (personal communication, 2009), there are a number of deep canyons cutting into the outer shelf, which explains the capture of many relatively deep-living species. It is thus possible that G. minutus may live deeper than indicated by the actual trawling depths (Ref. 84063).

species.name: Grammonus nagaredai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. From caves off O'ahu and Hawai'i (Ref. 79569).

species.name: Grammonus robustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found on soft bottom (Ref. 34024).  Ref. 9942 gives maximum depth to be 1,260 m.

species.name: Grammonus thielei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed in limestone caves and sinkholes which are probably connected at depths between 2 and 30 meters; often in lightless chambers without current, few are found at the entrance of caves where they hide beneath rock ledges.  No reaction to torchlight was shown and escape distance was only about 2 centimeters; mostly were seen motionless, with only a slight movement of the fins maintaining the fishes' position (Ref. 56143).

species.name: Grammonus waikiki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coral reefs (Ref. 58302).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Grammonus yunokawai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from one female specimen with ovaries containing eggs up to about 0.5 mm in diameter and apparently with no embryos. It was caught by hand in the back of the cave in absolute darkness. The head and lateral line pore systems are well developed, also the sensory papillae on the head and body, indicating adaptation to the lightless environment Also observed and caught were a shrimp Parhippolyte misticia and the fishes Pseudamia hayashiiand Apogon evermanni (Ref. 75999).

species.name: Grammoplites knappi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grand Cayman limia
species.description: Inhabits brackish water in mangrove coastal lagoons and fresh water in limestone depressions.

species.name: Grand forte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow reefs and rocky bottoms. Usually solitary and territorial. Feed mainly on crabs (Calapa and Mithrax) and other crustaceans (alpheid shrimps and scyllarid lobsters), fishes (labrids and haemulids), and octopus. Some undergo sexual inversion at 28 cm TL; most fish larger than 40 cm are males. Important in terms of numbers caught and total weight of landings in the Caribbean. Easily approached by divers (Ref. 9710). Hermaphrodite species. Excellent food fish (Ref. 26938). Readily caught on hook and line and easily speared (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Grand gonostome
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Postlarvae and juveniles occur near the surface at night.  In southern Atlantic and southeastern Pacific, adults are usually found at depths between 100-2,000 m (Ref. 3991).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Grand gueule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs. Usually solitary (Ref. 29). Difficult to approach (Ref. 9710). Juveniles often seen in rockpools (Ref. 86997). Feeds mainly on crabs (67%) and fishes (20%). In the Ascension I., feeds on juvenile Melichthys niger and young sea turtles. Its flesh is of good quality. Marketed fresh. Angling: Like other grouper, rock hind are caught by fishing at the right depth over an irregular bottom (Ref. 84357).

species.name: Grand gueule (Epinephelus malabaricus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species found in a variety of habitats: coral and rocky reefs, tide pools, estuaries, mangrove swamps and sandy or mud bottom from shore to depths of 150 m. Solitary (Ref 90102). Juveniles found near shore and in estuaries; sex reversal probable; catch statistics poor being previously confused with E. andersoni (Ref. 4332). Feed primarily on fishes and crustaceans, and occasionally on cephalopods (Ref. 9710). Present in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). Widely used in mariculture mainly in the Far East (Ref. 43448).

species.name: Grand moro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Grand pêcheur abyssal
species.description: Majority of collected materials taken by trawls that reaches maximum depth of greater than 650m (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Grand requin blanc
species.description: Primarily a coastal and offshore inhabitant of continental and insular shelves, but may also occur off oceanic islands far from land (Ref. 247, 43278, 58302).  Often close inshore to the surf line and even penetrates shallow bays (Ref. 247).  Maximum depth of 700 fathoms (or 1280 m) reported by Bigelow & Schroeder, 1948 is erroneous (Francis et al., 2012 in Ref. 106604).  Pelagic, capable of migration across oceanic regions (Ref. 58302).  Usually solitary or in pairs but can be found in feeding aggregations of 10 or more; does not form schools (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bony fishes, sharks, rays, seals, dolphins and porpoises, sea birds, carrion, squid, octopi and crabs (Ref. 5578) and whales (Ref. 32140).  Ovoviviparous, embryos feeding on yolk sac and other ova produced by the mother (Ref. 43278, 50449).  Number of young born per litter, 7 (Ref. 31395) to 14 (Ref. 26346).  Reported by some experts to attack humans which they mistake for their normal prey (Ref. 47).  Most attacks occur in estuaries.  Caught by big-game anglers and line boats for its jaws (Ref. 5578).  Reported to cause poisoning (Ref. 4690).  Flesh is utilized fresh, dried-salted, and smoked for human consumption, the skin for leather, liver for oil, carcass for fishmeal, fins for shark-fin soup, and teeth and jaws for decorations (Ref. 13574). Maximum total length is leading to much speculation and some measurements are found to be doubtful. Possibly to 6.4 m or more in length (Ref. 43278), considered the world's largest predator with a broad prey spectrum.  The record of 10.98 m is incorrect (Ref. 13574). Maximum total length for male from Ref. 91029. Sometimes considered the most dangerous shark in the world (Ref. 26938).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Grand requin marteau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal-pelagic, semi-oceanic shark, found close inshore and well offshore, over the continental shelves, island terraces, and in passes and lagoons (Ref. 244, 58302).  Often bottom and reef associated at 1-80 m (Ref. 58302).  Prefers to feed on stingrays and other batoids, groupers and sea catfishes, but also preys on other small bony fishes, crabs, squid, other sharks, rays, and lobsters (Ref. 244, 13562, 1602).  A viviparous species, with 13-42 of about 56 to 70 cm young in a litter (Ref. 26938, 1602).  Potentially dangerous to people (Ref. 13562) but only few, if any, of the attacks on people can be definitely attributed to it because of the apparent difficulty of distinguishing large hammerhead species involved in attacks (Ref. 244).  Caught occasionally by target shark longline, demersal tangle net and tuna gillnet fisheries (Ref.58048). Meat utilized for human consumption (fresh, fresh-frozen, dried-salted, and smoked), liver oil for vitamins, fins for soup, hides for leather, and carcasses for fishmeal (Ref. 244).  Its large fins, including the tail, sail-like first dorsal fin, are prized in the Oriental sharkfin trade (Ref. 47737).

species.name: Grand savon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting shallow water on bottoms with eroded limestone or mixed sand and rocks, as well as around reefs.  Often found lying motionless against rocks (Ref. 13121).  Secretes copious mucus which makes its surface slimy and when disturbed the slime turns into a soapy foam.  The mucus has been shown to contain a toxic protein (Ref. 3632).  Nocturnal, frequently seen around the bases of coral colonies and near mouths of caves (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Grand tambour
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually over sand and sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters, especially in areas with large river runoffs.  Juveniles often enter estuaries.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, mollusks and fishes.

species.name: Grand-gousier pelican
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to abyssopelagic (Ref. 58302) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Adults feed mainly on crustaceans, but also take fishes, cephalopods, and other invertebrates (Ref. 2850, 11041).  Oviparous, planktonic eggs hatch into planktonic leptocephalus larvae (Ref. 6719, 35600).  Degenerative changes in males and females suggest semelparity (Ref. 35600).

species.name: Grande allache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal, pelagic species, but tolerant of low salinities (Ref. 188, 5286, 27000, 86940); sometimes in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 188, 2683). It forms schools, preferring waters of 24°C, at surface or at bottom down to 50m, strongly migratory (Ref. 188, 5286). It feeds on a variety of small planktonic invertebrates, also fish larvae and phytoplankton (Ref. 188, 27165). It breeds only once in the year, during the warm season between July and September, in coastal waters; juveniles and adults show clear north-south migrations in the Gabon-Congo-Angola sector and the Sierra Leone-Mauritania sector of the Atlantic Ocean, each area having nurseries; these movements are correlated with the seasonal upwelling (Ref. 188). It is of considerable importance off West African coasts, but combined with Sardinella aurita in most statistics, partly because both species are often caught together (Ref. 188).

species.name: Grande argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426). Prefer depths of 182.8-255.9 m, temperature 7-10°C and mean salinity 34 ppt (Ref. 5951). Probably form schools close to the bottom. Feeds on planktonic invertebrates including euphausiids, amphipods (arrow worms, krill and Thermisto (Ref. 5951)), chaetognaths, squids and ctenophores, also small fishes. Spawns from April to July (Ref. 4773). Growth is slow. Eggs and young are pelagic at depths of 400-500m. Used fresh or in fish meal production (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Grande gueule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found from near shore to farther than 750 m.  Feed mainly on fishes and occasionally on algae.

species.name: Grande gueule à voile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Food includes cephalopods and fish (Ref. 11892).

species.name: Grande Lanternule longue-gueule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066).  Found within the upper 200 m in the region of Antarctic Polar Front, but inhabits deeper northwards at night.

species.name: Grande lycode
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at a temperature range of -0.4° to 5.6 °C (Ref. 117245).  Optimal temperatures appear to range between 2.6° and 3.5°C.  Inhabits soft bottom areas (Ref. 13532).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds almost exclusively on ophiuroids (Ref. 13532).

species.name: Grande Mancopsette
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grande raie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur from water's edge to 430 m depth; absent from shoal waters in south during warm months (Ref. 7251).  Found in salinities that range from 35 along the continental edge to 31.5 inshore along the open coast and as low as 21-24 (Ref. 6902).  Live on all kinds of bottom (Ref. 205).  Benthic (Ref. 5951).  Feed on bivalve mollusks, squids, rock crabs, lobsters, shrimps, worms and fishes.  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited during summer (with 6-month development) in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205, Ref. 114953).  Egg capsules are 7.1-13.2 cm long and 4.6-7.4 cm wide (Ref. 41250). Males reaches maturity at ca. 100 cm TL, females at 96-105 cm TL; hatch size at 18-19 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Little use is made of the small quantities that are caught.  In some cases, they are made into fish meal.

species.name: Grande raie guitare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and in shallow estuaries (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on crabs, lobsters, bivalves, small fishes (Ref. 5578) and squids (Ref. 37816).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Takes crayfish and pilchard bait.  Meat and fins sought after in Asian markets (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Grande rascasse rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sedentary species which occurs in rocky areas (Ref. 4510).  Feeds on fishes, shrimps and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Grande verrue tigre
species.description: Found in coastal waters (Ref. 30573).  Adults feed on fishes, prawns and other invertebrates (Ref. 5213, 9772).  Generally marketed fresh, may be dried or salted (Ref. 5284).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Grande vive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. On sandy, muddy or gravelly bottoms, from a few meters to about 150 m.  Rest on the bottom, often buried with eyes and tip of first dorsal fin exposed (Ref. 9988).  At night they swim around freely, even pelagically (Ref. 35388).  Feed on small invertebrates and fishes; chiefly nocturnal.  Oviparous, eggs and larval stages pelagic (Ref. 4675).  There are dark markings along the scales; the anterior dorsal fin is black and contains venomous spines.  Utilized fresh and frozen; can be pan-fried, broiled, boiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Spawning takes place in June and August, pelagic eggs are 1 mm (Ref. 35388).  Also Ref. 57406.

species.name: Grande écaille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, but enters lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 4832) [actual freshwater records remain to be confirmed].  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Young and adults feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).  Probably spawn at sea, but the transparent larvae migrate to inshore areas and are often found in brackish water (Ref. 7050).  Are voracious carnivores that take fish, squid and shrimp bait (Ref. 3968).  Edible, but not tasty and full of bones (Ref. 3968).  A total length of 126 cm for this species has  been reported from Knysna, South Africa (G. Bernardt, pers. comm., e-mail:  gerard@smallstreams.com) .

species.name: Grande-gueule antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed mostly on fish and krill.  Synchronous spawner (Ref. 50743).  Larvae have a long pelagic phase (Ref. 71843).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Grande-gueule ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found most commonly at depths from 200-400 m.  Adults feed mainly on fishes and krill.  Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 71843).

species.name: Grande-gueule épineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallower waters of the continental shelf, especially on banks less than 250 m deep in areas where local upwelling increase food supply (Ref. 6390).  Postlarvae and pelagic juveniles are also found in the upper 100 m (Ref. 5200).  Food consists of fishes and krill.  Spawn in winter (Ref. 6390).  Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 28915).  Prey to penguins and seals (Ref. 6390).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 5200).

species.name: Grandperrin’s giant sawbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Granular pugolovka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers brackish and slightly saline zones in deltas and estuaries; in summer inhabits shallow coastal waters (0.5-20 m) and shallow deltas; in winter, moves to deeper areas (up to 60-70 m).  Spawns after first winter. Feeds mostly on molluscs and crustaceans (Ref.59043).

species.name: Granulated catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal predator. Occurs in small groups. Feeds mainly on the fruits of Astrocaryum javary (Ref. 9084).

species.name: Grape-eye seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near drop-offs and among rock out-croppings over sand and rock, in depths greater than 10 meters.  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Grapevine dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 3984, 75154).

species.name: Grass emperor
species.description: Juveniles found in seagrass beds and mangrove swamps.  Adults found over coral reefs.  Often in schools (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes.  Considered a good food fish.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Grass klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among weeds; mainly in tide pools.  Though not of great angling importance, it provides good sport for young anglers (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Grass rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found commonly on rocky bottom in tide pools and near shore, also in kelp and eelgrass beds.  Occur up to 46 m depth but usually at less than 15 m.  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Most important rockfish to rocky shore and jetty fishermen.  Good eating.

species.name: Grass-eater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Marco-herbivores, feed on submerged plants, Eichornia roots and periphyton (Ref. 28714). Maximum length 62.5 cm SL (Ref. 2936, 81638, 86396).

species.name: Grasseichthys gabonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Open water species, not burrying in sand; forms schools; spawns during the raining season, during which it may be very abundant, forming aggregations in open water areas in the swamps; females of 20-24mm carry about 40 round, ripe eggs of about 0.4mm diameter; males mature at a size of about 18mm total length (Ref. 91379).

species.name: Graus nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very popular among sport line fishers and spear fishers (Luiz Antonio Pereira, pers. comm., 2002).

species.name: Graveldiver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas, tide pools and off beaches (Ref. 2850).  Burrows in loose gravel and sand or among broken shells on the bottom (Ref. 2850).  May not utilize the intertidal zone for reproductive and recruitment purposes (Ref. 56899).

species.name: Gravelier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel riffles and runs of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Gravenche
species.description: Lacustrine. Found in deeper parts of the lake. Spawns in shallow water, on gravel, near shore in December. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Gray bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits marginal swamps and freshwater lagoons (Ref. 3066) and it appears to favor sheltered inshore habitats (Ref. 3034); it inhabits the muddy regions at the sides of rivers and swampy waters, where it lies quiet or glides about with snake-like movements (Ref. 49805). During the hottest hours of the day, it comes to the surface just on the outer edge of the vegetation, and it goes back to the bottom when disturbed (Ref. 45962). It feeds on insects, crustaceans, mollusks, frogs and fishes (Ref. 4903, Ref. 28714). Polypterus senegalus senegalus is mainly insectivorous (Ref. 367). Longevity of Polypterus senegalus in captivity can be 34 years and more (Ref. 48954). Larval fish 1.1-3.8 cm SL were found in papyrus root mat and juveniles up to 10 cm SL retaining external gills were found in fringing water hyacinth. Feeds mainly on fishes (Ref. 9695), insects, crustaceans, mollusks, frogs as well as on plant fragments and seeds.

species.name: Gray corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gray flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually deeper than 40 m.

species.name: Gray loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Usually found in water with slow currents, river coves and lakes.  Prefers dense weeds or quiet water (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Gray parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840. Occurs in oceanic islands, dwelling in coral, algal and rocky reefs and on algal beds (Ref. 40827). An herbivore (Ref. 33499), cleaned by Elacatinus figaro observed off the coast of São Paulo, southeastern Brazil (Ref. 40102) and by Pomacanthus paru observed at the reefs of the Abrolhos Archipelago, off eastern Brazil (Ref. 40094).

species.name: Gray redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and deep runs and pools of small to medium rivers (Ref. 52299).  Feeds on aquatic insects, mollusks, amphipods, ostracods, algae, plant seeds and fish (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Gray rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep waters.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Gray starsnout
species.description: Inhabits rocky areas (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Gray unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over coral and rock (Ref. 58302).  Occurs singly or in aggregations along clear seaward and outer lagoon reefs and channels (Ref. 37816). Feeds in midwater on zooplankton (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Gray's grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and estuaries, presumably with a biology similar to that of other members of the genus.  Feed on zooplankton, small insects, crustaceans, and fish (Ref. 5258).

species.name: Gray's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in muddy habitats, often covered with silt and extremely well-camouflaged (Ref. 48635).  Planktonic specimens taken in the upper 0 to 100 m over depths to at least 2980 m while the demersal fish have been taken in SCUBA and trawl collections from 9 to 91.4 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Males exhibit parental care by incubating and guarding the eggs in their brood pouch (Ref. 43081).

species.name: Gray's stone loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential hill streams.  Prefers backwater and quiet eddies (Ref. 12045).

species.name: Graytail skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Great Barrier Reef blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed mainly on a diet of coral polyps and mucous (Ref. 94105).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Great blue spotted mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather that actively shuttles back and forth between tide pools and air (Ref. 31184).  Creeps around and browses on mud flats at low tide; stays in a burrow in the mud at high tide. Herbivores that graze on diatoms on the mud surface during low tide (Ref. 92840). Caught for food.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Great freshwater stingray
species.description: Reported stomach contents in this species include fishes, insects and insect larvae, mollusks, and crustaceans, with predominance of insect larvae. Ontogenetic dietary shifts occur in species of this genus. Sexual maturity for males at about 58.0 cm TL (37.5 cm DL, 35.6 cm DW, MZUSP 120369, claspers almost fully calcified). Specimens greater than 100 cm in TL can easily weigh 20 kg. Great disparity in the largest sizes achieved by males and females (Ref. 115938).

species.name: Great Lake Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in rocky shores, among aquatic vegetation, inundated terrestrial scrub and debris.  Cryptic.  They are benthic, preferring rocky lake margins in shallow water, but also occur to at least 10 meters depth.  Found in swampy areas bordering lakes during floods.  Remain close to available cover (rocks, wood, plants).  Behave like a gudgeon, remaining motionless on the bottom most of the time and darting after prey with rapid bursts.  They adopt the typical gudgeon posture of supporting itself with the pectoral fins (Ref. 44894).  Feed on a variety of insects, microcrustaceans, worms, galaxiid eggs and algae.  Spawn in spring; sexual maturity is reached after one year, maximum life span is two years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Great sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the intertidal area and to 244 m  depth, on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 4925).  Often caught near shore (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Great seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep water species, associated with corals (Ref. 52034).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Great snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in sluggish or standing water in canals, lakes, and swamps (Ref.  12693).  Inhabit waters with submerged aquatic vegetation (Ref. 12693).  Usually found only in deep pools in rivers and occasionally in lakes.  They enter flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Carnivorous and subsist on fish, frogs, snakes, insects, earthworms and tadpoles (Ref. 1479).  There are reports of this species taking water birds, snakes, and rodents.  Males are territorial.  May bite when caught (Elliot Bligh, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Greatbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology unknown.

species.name: Greater jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of clear small to medium rivers.

species.name: Greater scissortail
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits forest creeks, usually over sandy substrate (Ref. 56749).  Occurs near the surface of streams.  Not a common species, with apparently localized populations.  Feeds mainly on exogenous insects.  Rarely seen in markets, but common in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Greater sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Green blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, weed-covered rocky areas.  Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Green carplet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits still or slow-moving water, frequenting swamps, rice fields and similar still waters. Found in weedy ponds of coastal plains (Ref. 4832). Common in less saline mangrove swamps and in less polluted canals. Often encountered together with Aplocheilus. Feeds on insects.

species.name: Green clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sheltered seagrass beds (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Green damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in quiet waters with rocky bottoms in inshore and offshore reefs; juveniles sometimes found in surge pools (Ref. 205).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Adults form school.  Feed on a variety of algae and zooplankton.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Used as food by the Hawaiians (Ref. 7364).

species.name: Green dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary. Found in fringing coral reefs in 1-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Green dwarf tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Green goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove streams with very fine silt-mud substrate (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Green goodea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Green guapote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the lower river valley sections.

species.name: Green icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A piscivorous species; stomach contents contain fish (Ref. 80896).  Females mature at about 30-32 cm TL or 26-28 cm SL.  Caught by bottom trawls in an area of barren of benthic fauna (Ref. 80896).

species.name: Green labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a few localized, rocky, fast-flowing mountain streams.  Has not been recorded from unshaded, silty or turbid waters (Ref. 11966).  Moves fast through the water, staying close to the bottom.  Juveniles have been observed picking algae off submerged rocks.  Feeds on algae.  Occurs sympatrically with (and possibly mistaken for) <i>Puntius<i> sp. 'martenstyn' throughout the known range.  May be greatly endangered by the damming of Mahawel River.  Too rare and difficult to capture for food.

species.name: Green neon tetra
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Green panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stationary and sheltered waters of rivers (Ref. 4833).  Found under the surface in still waters, mainly coastal and often brackish, especially where there is surface vegetation or cover, such as mangrove swamps and rice fields.  Swims slowly or stays stationary, often in small groups.  Feeds on insects, larvae and fish fry.  Valuable for mosquito control (Ref. 6028).  Not a seasonal killifish.

species.name: Green pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur usually in slow-moving rivers, estuaries and the upper reaches of backwaters.  Prefers shady, marginal areas.  Feed on mollusks, crustaceans and other invertebrates as well as vascular plants and detritus.  Occasionally feed on fish scales and fins (Ref. 12693).  The muscular tissue and viscera are extremely toxic.  Common in the aquarium trade, but adults are known to be pugnacious and aggressive with its tankmates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Green puller
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Green rat clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in subtidal fields of macroalgae (Ref. 120657).

species.name: Green razorfish
species.description: Most common in shallow, sandy areas in and around seagrass beds.  Prefers clear waters (Ref. 9626).  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Green rivulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in upland streams (Ref. 4537).  Abundant in rivers and lakes with clear and abundant vegetation (Ref. 13498).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Green sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit quiet pools and backwaters of sluggish streams, lakes and ponds.  Often near vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Juveniles feed on immature insects and microcrustaceans (Ref. 10294).  Nest spawners (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Green sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Green terror
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In small and larger coastal streams (Ref. 6329).  Females care for the eggs and larvae while males defend the territory (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Green trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits Isli Lake, situated on a high plateau, 2270 meters above sea level; it is a large and deep, ±2 km of diameter and 92 m deep, oligotrophic lake (Ref. 107622). The spawning of this species takes place at the end of October and November in the sandy beaches of the lake (Ref. 107622). The habitat of this species is threatened due to eutrophication, related to intensive overpasture; overfishing is also a problem due to the low protection of the lake; no juveniles have been observed in the last years and several malformations in fins and skull were observed; therefore this species should be included in the IUCN category of endangered (Ref. 107622).

species.name: Green wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reefs and lagoons (Ref. 8631), often on sand-rubble substrates with large staghorn coral colonies.  Occurs in small loose groups of females (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Green-striped coral bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant on shallow inshore reefs and adjacent sand or mud bottoms.  Feeds on small fishes and benthic invertebrates.  Unimportant as a food fish.  No major fishery exists.

species.name: Greenback flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on silty sand substrates from estuaries and inshore waters down to 100 m depth.  Juveniles occasionally entering rivers.

species.name: Greenback stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the outer continental shelf (Ref. 6871, 75154).

species.name: Greenband goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal estuaries and muddy slopes adjacent to algal reef to about 30 meters depth (Ref. 48637). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Found in mud or fine silty sand bottoms, usually in the  vicinity of its burrow.

species.name: Greenband wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep reefs (Ref. 9710).  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Greenbanded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pitted limestone faces and tide pools in surf areas in clear waters.  Usually found among spines of rock-boring sea urchins (Ref. 26938).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Greenbeak parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral, algal and rocky reefs and on algal beds (Ref. 40827).

species.name: Greenblotch parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep rocky and coral reefs with steep walls (Ref. 9710).  Generally seen in seagrass beds or on reefs with thick algal cover (Ref. 13442).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Greenblotched rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rough bottom (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Greenbottle pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in flowing waters of rivers and streams.  May also be found in flooded forests and plains during the river's high water levels.  Feeds on fish scales and fins.  Seen in markets as part of mixed catches.

species.name: Greenbreast darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit fast rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 33799); also found in medium to large streams (Ref. 10294).  Adults occur in the deepest portions of riffles with moderately strong current.  Prey mainly on insects (midge and other dipteran larvae, mayfly nymphs, and smaller quantities of water mites and caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294)).  Feed by pecking small prey from the surface of rocks (Ref. 33799).

species.name: Greenbubble dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble and algal-covered dead reef near shore in 0-5 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Greene's triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is relatively abundant within its depth range, on coral rubble and holes adjacent to deeper drop-offs (below a thermocline) at several localities of the coasts of Kiritimati (Christmas Island). It has always been observed near the reef substratum, where it would seek shelter when approached (Ref. 94129).

species.name: Greeneye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous.

species.name: Greeneye spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Greenface aulonocara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly encountered at around 12 m depth.  Feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Greenface sandsifter
species.description: Found usually in shallow water over open sand.  Feeds mainly on insect larvae (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Greenfin darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits very fast, rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Greenfin horse-faced filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Greenfin shiner
species.description: Inhabits rocky and sandy pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Greenfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max depth: at least 50m (Ref. 86997).  Littoral, near rocks and seagrass (Ref. 5292).  Juveniles have been observed cleaning many other fish species (Ref. 98447).

species.name: Greenhead dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was ollected in 55-62 m and observed to at least 70 m depth. It is found on deep reef slopes with gentle incline but exposed to strong currents and generally found in association with small gorgonian sea fans or low-growing barrel sponges (Ref. 118104).

species.name: Greenhead shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky flowing pools of clear headwaters, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Greenhead wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty lagoons and coastal reefs in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Greenland dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Greenland manefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported (Ref. 27121).  From catches of mature females and juveniles, spawning apparently occurs on the periphery of subtropical waters (in the Sargasso Sea, in the zone of the Gulf Stream and off the Azores) (Ref. 95096).

species.name: Greenside darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers, and shores of large lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Juveniles feed on midge larvae and microcrustaceans; adults consume midge larvae, blackfly larvae, and other immature aquatic insects, primarily mayflies and caddisflies (Ref. 10294).  Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 36980).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Greensnout parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of outer lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Usually solitary (Ref. 9710).  Females usually in small groups with a male nearby; they may mix with females of similar species (Ref. 48636).  An uncommon fish patchily distributed through much of its range.

species.name: Greenspot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and the freshwater tidal zone of rivers.  Occurs in the Mekong delta and may be found as far upstream as the tidal zone in Cambodia.  Not seen in markets  (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Greenspotted flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Greenspotted rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on soft bottom (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Greenstreaked eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Greenstripe barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in ponds, streams and lakes in plains (Ref. 41236).  Often found in rice fields.  Enters brackish water.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae and blue-green algae (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Greenstripe pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Greenstriped rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inhabitant of both inshore and offshore areas (Ref. 2850, 6885).  Found on rocky as well as soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Only the largest individuals are filleted for human consumption, smaller ones are processed into fishmeal or used as animal feed (Ref. 27436).  The flesh has a delicious flavor and appealing texture (Ref. 27436).  Rarely caught by sports anglers, but an excellent bait for large lingcod (Ref. 27436).  Rare appearances in public aquariums (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Greenthroat darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in gravel and rubble riffles, especially spring-fed and vegetated riffles, of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Greenway's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit moderately to swiftly flowing streams in clear or turbid water over mixed sand and rocky bottoms (Ref. 44894). Not much known on the biology of this species, although a single collection of 100 specimens taken in 1969 indicate that they occur in fast flowing rapids; the water being green-colored with visibility reduced to 30 cm (Ref. 5259). Adults occasionally exhibit the 'blubber lip' condition seen in members of the closely related genus Hephaestus. Omnivorous, feed on algae and small invertebrates. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205). When freshly captured, a distinctive pattern of broad vertical bars is displayed on sides which is an indication of stress (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Greenway's toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing waters.

species.name: Greenwood's happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers still or slow-flowing water and dense vegetation; feeds primarily on insects, small snails and other invertebrates and occasionally small fish (Ref. 7248, 52307). Agamous, ovophilic (Ref. 52307) female mouthbrooder, breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52307).

species.name: Greenwoodochromis abeelei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sand-dweller; rarely seen (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Greenwoodochromis bellcrossi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rather deep, open waters (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Greenwoodochromis christyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rather deep, open waters (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Greenwoodochromis staneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sand-dweller (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Gregori's labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic, in deep waters down to 2740 (Ref. 58426).  Adults are commonly found in about 300-500 m depth.  Temperature preferences appear to range from about 1-4°C, although bottom temperatures below 0°C have been recorded at capture depths.  Amphipods predominate in the diet, although polychaetes and various natant crustaceans are also important.  Also feed on bivalves, isopods, echinoderms (notably ophiuroids), and ctenophores (Ref. 1371).  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).

species.name: Grenadier abyssal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-slope upper continental rise species, common in deep waters of most oceans (Ref. 1371).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on a variety of benthic invertebrates (especially crustaceans and holothuroids) when young, switching to primarily mesopelagic and bathypelagic fish, and sea urchins and cephalopods as adults (Ref. 1371).  Sex ratio was 2.6:1 male to female (n = 449) in the Rockall Tough, N.E. Atlantic (Ref. 40742).

species.name: Grenadier barbu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slopes (Ref. 1371).  Utilized mainly for fishmeal and oil (Ref. 1371).  In the past, fishers in the North Atlantic were reported to have used the luminescent excretion from the ventral light organ to enhance baits used for cod fishing (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Grenadier bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appear to live usually on or near the bottom, but may occasionally move up into mid-waters.  Large adult fish generally occur deeper than 400 m, while juveniles may be found in shallower water (Ref. 9072), more commonly found in large estuaries and bays, and may even enter freshwaters (Ref. 1371).  Juvenile specimens and especially adults belonging to the American subspecies, have been caught from the coastal zone to 110 m (Ref. 58452). Form schools.  Feed primarily on lantern fishes.  In New Zealand, it feeds in midwater on small fish, crustaceans and squid.  Oviparous, spawn 1 million eggs on the average which are released all at one time (Ref. 6390).  Utilized fresh and frozen; can be steamed, fried, cooked in microwave and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Grenadier bleuté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at the continental rise at depths from 2,525-3,931 m.  Biology is unknown.

species.name: Grenadier californien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Food items are generally forcibly regurgitated by the fish's expunging gas bladder as it is hauled from the depths, but fish remains have been caught inside the mouth of a few individuals.  Considered opportunistic feeders and will eat whatever animal food they encounter in the natural habitat as long as it is of appropriate size (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Grenadier can
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are bathypelagic (Ref. 9315).  Feeds mainly on copepods and other small crustaceans, but not exclusively  bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 9315).

species.name: Grenadier carmine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found in the continental slope (Ref. 9315).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Grenadier cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 9563) to more than 1,000 m (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Grenadier de Baird
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, reported as deep as 2295m  (Ref. 58426).  Taken much shallower in areas with cold surface waters.  Feeds primarily on euphausiids, amphipods, and polychaetes, although a 200 mm individual had many copepods in its stomach (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Grenadier de Berry
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso-, bathy- and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Maximum TL of at least 39.2 cm.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Grenadier de Günther
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (annelids, isopods and mysids) (Ref. 6187).

species.name: Grenadier de Marini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently occurs below 350 m depth in winter.  Feeds on benthic crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 54164).

species.name: Grenadier de Myers
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype caught at a depth of 457 m.

species.name: Grenadier de Parin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic species that probably feeds on pelagic invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9315).  Caught only with midwater nets, far from the bottom (Ref. 9315).

species.name: Grenadier de Patagonie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling species which are concentrated on the outer part of the continental shelf (Ref. 1371).  Feeds mainly on fish (herring, anchovies, lantern fishes), also on mysids, cephalopods, euphausiids and amphipods (Ref. 1371).  Migrates southward in spring and summer and northward in winter (Ref. 1371).  Utilized fresh, frozen and for fishmeal (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Grenadier de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic to bathypelagic in about 400 and 1200 m depth.  Minimum depth from Ref. 1371.  Form large schools at 600 to 900 m depth (Ref. 9988).  Feed on a variety of fish and invertebrates, but primarily on pelagic crustaceans such as shrimps, amphipods and cumaceans; cephalopods and lantern fishes constitute a lesser portion of the diet.  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846). This species is currently facing overexploitation in the North Atlantic.  Utilized frozen and for fishmeal; can be fried and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Grenadier denté
species.description: Feeds on fish, copepods and other small invertebrates (Ref. 5097).

species.name: Grenadier du Cap
species.description: Probably inhabiting very rough bottom or mid-waters.

species.name: Grenadier fragile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL of at least 20 cm.

species.name: Grenadier grand œil
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  This species is being imported and sold to the United States by the Argentines under the name grenadero (Ref. 5171).

species.name: Grenadier largenez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 9315).  Feeds mainly on copepods and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9315).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Grenadier lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic as well as pelagic animals like mysids, amphipods, small shrimps, copepods, isopods, ostracods and polychaete worms (Ref. 6187).

species.name: Grenadier lisse (Nezumia liolepis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught as a by-catch of trawlers fishing for Dover sole but of no commercial value (Ref. 9315).  Problems with taxonomy.  Shallowest depth record from Ref. 37930.

species.name: Grenadier pichirat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier péruvien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common grenadier in the Eastern central Pacific but occurs in very deep waters that  it is not regularly taken by trawlers (Ref. 9315).  Maximum TL of at least 30 cm (Ref. 9315).

species.name: Grenadier scie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm to temperate waters on the continental slope (Ref. 2683).  Feeds on pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Grenadier smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on soft bottoms (Ref. 51024).

species.name: Grenadier spatule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stomach contents reveal the ingestion of shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9315).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Grenadier voyou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-slope species of the tropical eastern Pacific (Ref. 9315).  Polychaetes and benthic crustaceans are encountered in its stomach contents (Ref. 9315).  Fairly common but of no commercial value (Ref. 9315).

species.name: Grenadier à barbe courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 6187) and worms (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Grenadier à barbillon court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on polychaete worms, copepods, amphipods, isopods and mysids (Ref. 6187).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Grenadier à grande tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier à long nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found commonly in about 200-500 m.  Feeds on a variety of benthic organisms, such as polychaetes, gastropods, cephalopods, numerous crustacean groups (copepods, gammarians, isopods, cumaceans, Natantia) and fish.  Minimum depth range taken from Ref. 1371.

species.name: Grenadier à lunettes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier à museau étroit
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grenadier à nez court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope, between 605 and 1000 m in depth.

species.name: Grenadier à queue mince
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL of more than 30 cm (Ref. 9315).

species.name: Grenadier à tête carénée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental rise to abyssal depths of 2,470-5,070 m (Ref. 5171).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Grenadier-scie
