species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic-pelagic (Ref. 58426); also benthopelagic (Ref.5951).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).  Max. length (Andrey Dolgov, pers. comm., 2003).

species.name: Grenouille de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coastal waters at shallow depths, generally from 10-20 m, more seldom from 75-100 m, on rocky bottom with seaweeds.  Solitary and secretive, undertakes only limited local movements.  Spawns from May to September at 50-70 m depth near the shore throughout its entire range.  Feeds on sea stars, crustaceans, worms, mollusks and small fish (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Grenouille ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky areas, including the intertidal zone.  Found on sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9269).  Young individuals feed heavily on crustaceans but as they grow bigger, they consume more and more fish, sometimes catching and eating fishes their own size (Ref. 4930).

species.name: Grenouille saignante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on small recesses in rocky reefs and especially along walls.  They blend almost perfectly with the background and appear like encrusting sponges (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Grenouille à queue barrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small recesses on rocky reefs and especially along walls.  They blend almost perfectly with the background, they often take the markings of tube-worm snails or appear to be encrusting sponges (Ref. 5227).  Demersal.  Found between the surface to 15 m in depth; rarely until 38 m.

species.name: Grenouille écarlate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tide pools as well as lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602); secretive among rocks and sponges (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 89972). Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773). Found among reef crevices or among rubble in 1-75 m, but usually less than 10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Grey brotula
species.description: A rare species found in rocky areas (Ref. 34024).  Reported to occur in rock pools (Ref. 9003).  Possibly nocturnal (Ref. 9003).

species.name: Grey chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit deep offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Grey cutthroat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slope (Ref. 50610, 75154), over rocky substrata (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Grey demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur among rubble or consolidated reef rock of exposed intertidal reef flats and sandy beaches, subject to mild surge.  Also near freshwater run-offs (Ref. 48636).  They occur in small groups.  Feed mainly on benthic algae.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Grey goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in backwaters.

species.name: Grey grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grey knifefish
species.description: A plankton-picking species completely lacking teeth, they live in surface layers, rarely leaving the upper few meters of water, swimming rapidly and continuously (Ref. 30464).

species.name: Grey mirrorbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grey pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grey skate
species.description: Occurs mainly on the upper continental slope, but also known to be found at 155-1050 m depths (Ref. 114953).  Adolescent males varied from 64.9 - 72.1 cm TL; smallest juvenile 13.4 cm TL. Egg cases described are about 9.3 - 10.7 cm long with a maximum width of about 5.1 - 5.7 cm (Ref. 75648).

species.name: Grey's deepsea smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually caught in small aggregations, at 600-900 m in the daytime and 25-500 m at night (Ref. 6345).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 6345).

species.name: Grey-banded loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits fast flowing forest streams with acidic water and sand-gravel substrate (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Grey-bearded pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef caves and crevices in 1-14 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Greyback damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky substrates, frequently close to shore and often in gullies just below the surge zone at depths of about 1-6 m.  Generally solitary or in small, loose groups (Ref. 103843).

species.name: Greycheek basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154) of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Greyhead wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral-rich lagoon and inner channel reefs to at least 15 m depth (Ref. 34765); in mixed coral and algae habitats (Ref. 48636).  May be found solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Greytail angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very close to Chaetodontoplus mesoleucus (Bloch, 1787) with different colors on pelvic, dorsal and caudal fins. The two species coexist in several islands of Indonesia (Ref. 82330). These islands include Lesser Sunda Islands. Molucca Islands, Halmahera, and Bird's Nest Peninsula of West Papua (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Grideye fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abyssobenthic on the lower slope and rise. Largest eggs ca 0.8 mm; fecundity is low with ca 85-300 eggs per clutch. Eyes are particularly modified into flat lenseless plaques as in Ipnops murrayi.

species.name: Griffin's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Griffis angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer reef slopes and steep drop-offs.  Solitary or in pairs or small groups; uncommon to rare (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Griffiths' pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs to about 30 meters depth, usually hovers near caves (Ref. 48637). Forms small to large mid-water aggregations, often upside down on ceilings of caves (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Griffiths' razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms and dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Grifin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over a wide range of habitats like seagrass beds and outer reef slopes (Ref. 5213), also on mud bottoms. Solitary (Ref. 90102). Feed on small fishes and crustaceans (mainly stomatopods and crabs). Sexual transition from female to male occurs between 35-45 cm, but not all females change sex. Mature individuals form spawning aggregations (Ref. 55367). E. chlorostigma is closely related and very similar to E. polylepis and E. gabriellae which seem to replace it in the northwestern Indian Ocean. Solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Grijalva gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grijalva studfish
species.description: Inhabits slow as well as rapid flowing waters. Occurs with two other genera of livebearers, Poecilia and Xiphophorus, depending upon locality.

species.name: Grisette
species.description: Poisson. Generally inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs and are typically found in dead or silty areas (Ref. 9710).  Also found around coral reefs and in tide pools.  Growth is very slow.  Feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 37816).  Artificial spawning was accomplished in the work of Tang et al. 1979 (Ref. 6568) where buoyant eggs measured 0.80-0.83 mm in diameter with a single oil droplet.  Larvae died 7 days after hatching.  Juveniles are commonly caught for the aquarium trade while adults are utilized as food fish (Ref. 9710).  Sold in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Grisette (Epinephelus maculatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in shallow coral rubble, adults in isolated coral heads of lagoon and seaward reefs to depths of 82 m.  Feeds mainly on sand-dwelling fishes and crustaceans, sometimes on octopuses.  In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).  May be ciguatoxic in certain areas (Ref. 37816). Solitary, often seen on open sand and base of reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Grive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in littoral zone, near rocks and eel-grass beds (Ref. 3666).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Grogneur rayé
species.description: Found mainly around fringing reefs.

species.name: Grondeur argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 30573, 48635).  Enters freshwaters (4867).  Marketed fresh, may be salted (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Grondeur coche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the littoral zone of coastal waters (Ref. 9114).  Penetrates estuaries (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114). Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Grondeur coq
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 5213).  Plentiful in tidal estuaries (Ref. 2135).  Not eaten around the Island of Mozambique because the natives believe it is responsible for leprosy.  Others consider the flesh causes boils.  Excellent food fish.

species.name: Grondeur crocro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and creeks of low to high current velocity (Ref. 36880).  Found along sandy shores and over mud bottoms in shallow water, quite common in brackish mangrove-lined lagoons.  Often ascends rivers more than 100 miles from the sea.  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Grondeur de sable
species.description: Found on sandy bottoms near the coast (Ref. 9114).  Penetrates estuaries (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Grondeur gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, over sandy or rocky bottoms.  Also found in water with low salinity (Ref. 9626).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Marketed fresh.  Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.

species.name: Grondeur gueule pourpre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic-pelagic species of coastal waters which may enter rivers (Ref. 55763).  Apparently confined to fresh waters, ascending rivers with moderate currents (Ref. 9114).  More abundant near the outlets of rivers and creeks, but not in brackish or marine waters.  Reaches at least 640 m elevation and inhabits currents of low to moderate velocity.  Feed on crustaceans and fish (Ref. 36880).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Grondeur javelot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit turbid inshore waters with sandy to muddy bottoms to a depth of 75 m.  Enter estuaries, may tolerate water with low salinity.  Often associated with inshore wrecks (Ref. 4332).  Feed on crustaceans and fish (Ref. 5213, 48635).  Spawners form shoals near river mouths during the winter.  Good food fish (Ref. 2799). Taken by handline, set net, trap, and spear. Marketed fresh, a small quantity is salted or smoked (Ref. 47695).

species.name: Grondeur moucheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, estuaries, and tidal fissures; can tolerate freshwater.  It can jet a stream of water into the mud to expose crustaceans, worms and small bivalves which it feeds on (Ref. 11441); including fish (Ref. 5213).  Tasty food fish (Ref. 2799).  Maximum depth range from Ref. 122702.

species.name: Grondeur panaméen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sandy bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Grondeur rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters from the shoreline to about 50 m on sand or rocky bottom.  Feeds on crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 5535).

species.name: Grondeur selle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters over sand near reefs.  Feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 5213).  Edible but spoils easily.

species.name: Grondeur à grande éspine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species that has been collected in estuaries; may enter fresh water (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Grondeur à joues bleues
species.description: Found in coastal waters and trawling grounds.  Caught with bottom trawls, bottom longlines, handlines, gillnets and traps.

species.name: Grondeur à nageoires jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from littoral to 100 m, over sand and rocks (Ref. 6946).

species.name: Grondin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally  forms schools.  Found over sand and gravel, crag, and rocks in the continental shelf (Ref. 2723).  Feeds on benthic crustaceans, other invertebrates and bottom-dwelling fishes (Ref.4697).

species.name: Grondin (Chelidonichthys lucerna)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at temperatures ranging from 8.0-24.0 °C (Ref. 4944).  Inhabits sand, muddy sand or gravel bottoms.  Up to depth of 318 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on fish, crustaceans and mollusks.  Has three isolated rays on the pectoral fin which function as legs on which the fish rests and also help in locating food on the soft bottom (Ref. 9988).  Marketed fresh or frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, microwaved or baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Grondin (Lepidotrigla cadmani)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays in relatively deep water; very abundant on the continental plateau (Ref. 5377).  Found over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 26999).

species.name: Grondin aile bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from estuaries to edge of continental shelves over sand and sandy shell seabed (Ref. 9258).  Reported to be often found in rivers (Ref. 4316).  Juveniles may occur in bays (Ref. 33616).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Dorsal spine reported to be venomous (Ref. 9771).  Neither anterolateral glandular grooves nor  venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Current information in the table (dangerous fish) do not match; needs verification.  Excellent food fish (Ref. 9771).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Grondin aile tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A tropical to warm temperate species (Ref. 9771).  Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Excellent food fish (Ref. 3542).

species.name: Grondin aile-courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters, mostly from 73-180 m depth.  Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.

species.name: Grondin armure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental and insular shelves on sandy or muddy bottoms.

species.name: Grondin belugan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand or sandy-mud bottom (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Grondin brossé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin camard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocks and sand, from the coast down to a depth of about 150 m.  (Ref. 5213).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 12382).  Minimum depth from Ref. 12382.

species.name: Grondin carolin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy bottom.  Feeds on shrimps, crabs, other crustaceans, squid, bivalves and small fishes.  Produces loud, drumming sound by vibrating its swim bladder (Ref. 9988).  Used both for food and fish meal; other uses include bait for lobster traps and flatfish, handlines, pet food and fertilizer.  Utilized fresh and frozen; also used for caviar ;  can be broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Grondin chevrette
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin cornu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably caught with trawls (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Grondin costa-ricien
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin d'Oman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Grondin de Bean
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Grondin de Carole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 26999.

species.name: Grondin de lagune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Grondin du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and muddy bottoms in coastal areas.  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 4316) and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).  Excellent food fish (Ref. 4316).

species.name: Grondin du Gabon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble bottoms from the shoreline to about 200 m depth (Ref. 3699).

species.name: Grondin encre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species with a wide depth range (Ref. 9771).  Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Grondin fil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Grondin galinette
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on sandy grounds, sometimes on rocky bottoms, and also on mud between coastline to 140 m depth.  Up to depth of 340 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on crustaceans, mostly shrimps and shore crabs; fishes, mostly gobies, flatfish, young herring and sand eels.  Makes croaking sounds (Ref. 9987).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten fried and baked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Grondin lyre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on shrimps and crabs (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Grondin mauricien
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin mineur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water to 150 m depth (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Grondin morrude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on the continental shelf in 77 m; inhabits soft bottoms and fallen rocks (Ref. 4697).  Minimum depth range from Ref. 121790.

species.name: Grondin nez blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms, may bury in sand during the day.  "Walks" about on spines of ventral fins (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Grondin nez double
species.description: Inhabits soft bottoms.

species.name: Grondin pirelon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin pointu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on the continental shelf; juveniles enter bays and estuaries (Ref. 9563); benthic (Ref. 75154).  Specimens less than 12.5 cm SL are found at depths less than 55 m (Ref. 91768).

species.name: Grondin poule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or muddy bottoms of the continental and insular shelves.  Occasionally occurs over reefs.  Feeds on shrimps, crabs, other crustaceans and fishes.  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Grondin rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin taureau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on sand or mud  on continental shelves; found at depths down to 115 m.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and mollusks.  Of little economic importance, bycatch of bottom trawls.  Flesh is firm and delicious (Ref. 13710).

species.name: Grondin vachette
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grondin volant
species.description: Inhabit coastal waters with sandy substrates (Ref. 1602, 48635); a shallow-living species, benthic in adults; only species found in oceanic islands (Ref. 27821).  Solitary, well-camouflaged and slow-moving (Ref. 37816, 48635).  Feed on crustaceans, clams, and small fish.  May be caught using ring nets (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Grondin volant (Prionotus evolans)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly on sand bottom from inshore estuaries to about 180 m depth.  Found occasionally over reefs.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes.  Used both for food and fish meal; other uses include for bait, pet food and fertilizer.

species.name: Grondin volant cocarde
species.description: Found in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Rarely observed due to mud-preferred habitats (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Not fished commercially but taken incidentally throughout its range.  Usually caught near shore.  Marketed fresh occasionally (Ref. 3392).

species.name: Grondin épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental and insular shelves on sandy or muddy bottoms.

species.name: Grooved razor-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy floors of shallow inlet waters.  Usually in large schools among branching corals, seawhip gardens and black coral bushes to about 15 m depth.  Small juveniles in surface waters and sometimes in small groups along beach edges in quiet bays and settle with crinoids or urchins (Ref. 48635).  Usually processed into fishmeal (Ref. 2858).

species.name: Gros barbudo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on semi-hard and soft bottoms on the continental shelf and slope.  Marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Gros poutassou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over the continental slope and shelf to more than 1000 m, but more common at 300-400 m.  Feeds mostly on small crustaceans but large individuals also prey on small fish and cephalopods.  Makes daily vertical migrations:  surface waters at night and near the bottom during the day.  Sold fresh and frozen, and also processed as oil and fishmeal (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Gros prêtre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic fish, inhabiting near edge of continental shelf to shallow coastal waters, often of low salinity and high turbidity (Ref. 30199, 48637); also found in drop-offs, and shallow or gently sloping reef and lagoon waters (Ref. 1602, 48637).  Feed primarily on small fishes like anchovies, clupeids, carangids, also squids and penaeoid shrimps.  Usually hunts solitary and often swim in shallow water along coastal slopes (Ref. 48637). Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). Caught mainly with drift gill nets, bamboo stake traps, midwater trawls, and by trolling. Marketed mainly fresh; also dried-salted; commonly made into fish balls (Ref. 9684), frozen, smoked, and canned (Ref. 9987). A lipid-soluble toxin, similar to ciguatoxin has been found in the flesh of specimens caught on the east coast of Queensland, Australia. Known to undertake lengthy long-shore migrations, but permanent resident populations also seem to exist.

species.name: Gross's stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds, generally on sand bottoms.

species.name: Grosse poule de mer
species.description: Basically solitary rather than a schooling fish.  They exhibit a homing instinct (Ref. 9737).  Adults inhabit rocky bottoms but may occur among floating seaweed.  They migrate considerable distances in an annual cycle between deeper waters in winter and shallower waters in summer (Ref. 26141).  Maximum depth reported at 868 m (Ref. 58426).  Epibenthic-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Juveniles are found among algal clumps in bays and fjords moving offshore as they mature (Ref. 96431).  During the spawning season the males become reddish in color on the underside, whereas females turn blue-green.  Adults feed on ctenophores, medusas, small crustaceans, polychaetes, jelly fish and  small fishes.  Valued for their eggs, which make an inexpensive caviar (Ref. 9988).  Eaten in Nordic countries, marketed fresh or smoked.  Male flesh is most demanded and roe is sold fresh (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Grotto sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in cave streams as well as their resurgences, primarily over gravel, cobble, or bedrock bottom (Ref. 92978).

species.name: Grub fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Grundulus bogotensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 49958).

species.name: Grundulus cochae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 49958).

species.name: Grundulus quitoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Grunt sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal areas and to 165 m depth, in tide pools and rocky areas but also sand bottoms (Ref. 2850). Frequently observed taking shelter in empty shells, including those of the giant barnacle, Balanus nubilis, and discarded bottles and cans (Ref. 48784). Young feed on zooplankton and invertebrate and fish larvae; adults feed also feed on crustaceans (Ref. 28499). May use its pectoral fins to crawl over rocks and seaweed (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Grunting toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bottom areas mainly in the coastal waters.  Euryhaline (Ref. 12041).  Found in the sea and estuarine areas (Ref. 4833).  Occurs in estuaries over muddy bottoms (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Grusinian scraper
species.description: Inhabits clear and slow-flowing water with a stone and pebble substrate (Ref. 57083).

species.name: Gruvel’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guadalupe bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel riffles, runs and flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Guadalupe blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guadalupe cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky crevices and caves at depths to 18 m or more during the day, but moves off the bottom and out into open areas at night.  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4930).

species.name: Guadalupe clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guadalupe darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky runs of small to medium rivers, often near brush (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Guadalupe roundnose minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, sometimes runs, of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers.  Usually occurs  among filamentous algae (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Guam barred butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guam damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in exposed seaward reefs, on relatively barren gently sloping terraces with scattered low-profile corals.  Feed on zooplankton found 1 to 2 meters above the substrate (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Guam scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rock crevices in reef flats, shallow lagoons, and channels.  Feeds mainly at night on small shrimps, crabs, and polychaetes.  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Guama guppy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guapore corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guapote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes but also thrives in various lower and middle river valleys.  This species is an avid cavern digger.  Piscivorous, though also eats crustaceans and insects in smaller numbers (Ref. 36880).  Made into fillets or eaten baked.

species.name: Guaramiranga cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools.

species.name: Guarana cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guardian damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shelter shores.  Inhabits rich branching coral areas of <i>Porites cylindirca and <i>Echinopora horrida (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Has no pelagic larval stage but young remains with parents during early life (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Guardian darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults concentrate in headwaters and creeks in quiet to gently flowing pools, often near brush over sand or in gravel riffles (Ref. 33867).

species.name: Guatemalan headstander
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guavina micropus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guayas cichlid
species.description: In various biotopes, from small to medium-sized rivers.  Occasionally found in fish markets.  Feeds on benthic organisms such as small shrimps (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Guaymas goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gubal goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The fish is caught by trawling most  probably on sandy or muddy bottom (Ref. 121834).

species.name: Guenther's mouthbrooder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Substrate spawning, ovophilic, pair bonding, male mouthbrooding species (Ref. 81260). Both parents take care of the young after hatching (Ref. 47115).

species.name: Guentherus katoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guercif barbel
species.description: Found in large rivers, mainly in mid-stream, usually in riffle areas (Ref. 107618). It is a rare species that has been found in few places (Ref. 107618).

species.name: Guetteur à nageoire noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found between 500-800 m depth while the oceanic young stages between 70-200 m (Ref. 6689).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  The young feeds mainly on copepods while the large ones on euphausiids, hyperiids and mesopelagic fishes.  Adults undertake far-ranging feeding migrations (outside the spawning season) to the slope areas of Europe, North America and West Africa.  Spawning probably occurs in midwater far offshore, with a concentration in the Sargasso Sea (Ref. 6689).

species.name: Gueze's butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep reefs (Ref. 4858).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Guianacara cuyunii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guianacara dacrya
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually found associated with clear water streams with moderate current; also in seasonally flooded lagoons with no current in the Rupununi savannas.  The substrate is usually sandy with nearby large rocks; large numbers of juveniles were observed in river sections formed by mixtures of pebbles and small rocks over sandy bottom, frequently with some leaf litter.  Water parameters where it was collected showed a temperature range of 24.8-28.5ºC, with relatively high dissolved oxygen levels (5.3-6.56 mg/L) and very low conductivity (27.1-34.5µS) at localities in the Rupununi and Pirara (Ireng) drainages (Ref. 86674).

species.name: Guianacara sphenozona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guianacara stergiosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately shallow, clear-black, acid waters with slow to moderate currents on rocky bottoms (Ref. 57436).

species.name: Guianan cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guigarra cailaoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guinea oreo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Perhaps a midwater species, occasionally deeper.

species.name: Guinea swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Guinean angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common off Ghana where it is generally found among rocks.

species.name: Guinean bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guinean damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocks and rubble on inshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Guinean killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and small streams in the savanna (Ref. 3788).  7 cm SL (Ref. 7372). Not a seasonal killifish; difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Guinée du Sénégal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal pelagic species, occurring inshore and some way up the tidal rivers to the edge of the shelf (Ref. 4445).  Feeds on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Guinée machète du pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in schools in shallow inshore areas.  Penetrate lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 9297).  Feed on fish and penaeids (Ref. 50313).  Spawning probably occur in the open sea and the transparent larvae migrate towards coastal areas (Ref. 9297).  Struggle vigorously when caught on hooks and lines (Ref. 9297).  Low commercial value due its numerous spines (Ref. 9297).

species.name: Guinée saumon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal fish, commonly entering lagoon, bays, and estuaries (including fishponds) (Ref. 2847, 58302), particularly around mangroves (Ref. 44894).  Sometimes enters freshwater streams, but does not penetrate very far inland (Ref. 2847).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Younger fish often penetrate the lower freshwater reaches of rivers (Ref. 44894).  An active swimmer, commonly traveling in schools in open water.  Feeds on various fishes and crustaceans.  Little detailed knowledge exists of its biology.  Has a leptocephalus larva.  Spawning takes place offshore and young larvae are found in the open sea, moving close to shore as they develop.  Juveniles commonly found in salt marshes, canals, and tidal streams.  Marketed fresh or frozen; in some places ground up as fish meal.  A good sport fish on light tackle, striking a variety of artificial lures as well as live shrimp or baitfish.  No separate statistics available.  (Ref. 10983).

species.name: Guitare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms, from the intertidal zone to about 100 m.  Sometimes near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951).  Slow swimming over bottom or partially buried.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, mainly crustaceans and small fishes. Males mature at ca. 56 cm TL, females at ca. 64 cm TL; born at ca. 25 cm TL (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous, one or two litters per year with 4-10 embryos.

species.name: Guitarrita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229) and forest creeks rich in plant debris (Ref. 35381).  Benthic fish which feeds on a wide range of food, including organic debris from the bottom.  Spawns eggs on sandy substrate, in groups.  Unlike the other species of Aspredinidae, the female does not carry her eggs (4,000 to 5,000 per spawning) in bags (cotylophores).  It swims with undulating motion of its body and tail, rhythmically ejecting water from its opercles, thus resulting in a forward propulsion (Ref. 35381).  Aquarium keeping:  needs fine gravel or sand; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Guite de Patagonie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gulaphallus bikolanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Gulaphallus eximius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain streams (Ref. 12768).  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Gulaphallus falcifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Gulaphallus mirabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Gulaphallus panayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal brackish to marine localities.  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Gular cardinalfish
species.description: Known only from the type specimens trawled from silt or sand bottoms at depths between 30 to 40 meters (Ref. 11904). Also found in flat bottoms in 33-290 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Gulare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, pools and swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the humid coastal rainforest.  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Gulf blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Almost exclusively benthic.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Gulf brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Found in rocky crevices (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Gulf butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic fish forming large loose schools across the continental shelf over sand/mud bottoms; depth range from 2 to 275 m at least, but most abundant at 155 to 225 m; found near the bottom during the day and migrating into the water column at night.  Juveniles often found under floating weeds and with jellyfish. Adults feed on jellyfish, small fish, crustaceans, and worms; the juveniles are plankton and jellyfish feeders. Mature within 1 year and rarely lives past 2; spawning takes place at discrete intervals twice a year slightly offshore. Highly esteemed for food, marketed fresh and frozen; caught mainly with otter trawls (Ref. 53006).

species.name: Gulf chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large, moderately clear to turbid rivers and lowermost parts of their major tributaries in the Pearl, Pascagoula, and Lake Pontchartrain drainages of Mississippi and Louisiana (Ref. 116539).

species.name: Gulf damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually identified as P. jerdoni (Day, 1873), a junior synonym (Ref. 48636). Adults are found mainly along continental margins rather than truly oceanic areas. Inhabits flat sandy or rubble bottoms around patch reefs of lagoons and trawling grounds (Ref. 7247). Adults often seen in small groups out in the open on sandy substrate, swimming well-above the bottom and unlike other damselfishes rely on speed to get away from predators rather than diving into the shelter or reefs or burrow. Juveniles often shallow estuaries, but adults mainly in deeper water offshore at depths of 20+ m and have been reported to 80 m depth (Ref. 48636). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Gulf darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow rocky riffles, current-swept vegetation in headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae, with isopods and immature blackflies, mayflies, hydroptilid and hydropsychid caddisflies, and dragonflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Gulf filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by otter trawling to depths of 35 m and also by beach seine and chemical ichthyocides at shallow waters; on rock and sandy bottoms (Ref. 33065).

species.name: Gulf flashlightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A specimen taken from a steep sandy slope with profuse black coral growth.

species.name: Gulf gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing waters (such as rivers, streams and the adjacent areas), as well as standing waters.  Prefers the deeper water of 1 m or more.

species.name: Gulf gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic. Filter feeders (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Gulf herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters. Coastal pelagic (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Gulf killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers grassy bays, canals and nearby fresh water, avoiding tidal flats.  Also found in marginal fresh waters.  18 cm max TL (Ref. 7251).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Feeds on small crustaceans and other invertebrates (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Gulf logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gulf of Carpenteria anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed coastal, pelagic and schooling.  Probably tolerates lowered salinities, judging from the type locality and its occurrence in bays and inlets.  Apparently not abundant.  More material needed.

species.name: Gulf of Mexico barred searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Gulf of Mexico fringed sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gulf of Mexico ocellated flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays, lagoons and shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Gulf pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in bays and estuaries.  Usually found amongst vegetation (Ref. 26938).  Enters fresh water.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gulf signal blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty mollusk tubes on sand-rubble bottoms.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Males are somewhat territorial (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Gulf silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gulf skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep water species (Ref. 6902).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Gulf smoothhound
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Gulf Stream flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deeper water.  Rarely found in shallow water.

species.name: Gulf surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and inshore grassy and rocky areas.  Forms schools.  Mainly herbivorous. Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Gulf toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in seagrass beds and rocky cuts in coastal bays and lagoons, and in shallows along open coast.  In western coast of Florida, adults spawn in February and March (Ref. 26938).  Nesting males produce grunt calls called the boatwhistle as advertisement of competition among males and to attract females (Ref. 45338).  Neither opercular nor dorsal gland is venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Gumbo darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found invariably along the bank, sometimes under cuts, where there were exposed roots with accumulated vegetational debris, and sand to mixed sand and gravel substrate with very little silt.  Forms spawning aggregations and spawns in vegetation along the drop-off area close to shore.

species.name: Gunn's leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reefs, primarily deepwater outcrops (Ref. 9002).  Juveniles are common in estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Gunnari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed mainly on krill and mysids.  Spawn in autumn and winter (Ref. 50743).  Synchronous spawner (Ref. 50743).  Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 71843).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Gunnellichthys copleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gunnellichthys grandoculis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gunnellichthys irideus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guntea loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flowing or even clear standing waters.

species.name: Gunther's baril
species.description: Found in clear gravelly streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Gunther's lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to live in deeper water (Ref. 44036).

species.name: Guppy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm springs and their effluents, weedy ditches and canals (Ref. 5723).  Found in various habitats, ranging from highly turbid water in ponds, canals and ditches at low elevations to pristine mountain streams at high elevations (Ref. 11225).  Occurs in wide variety of habitats with low predation pressure, usually in very small streams and densely vegetated lakes and springs (Ref. 59043).  Has a wide salinity range but requires fairly warm temperatures (23-24 °C) and quiet vegetated water for survival (Ref. 7248, 44894, 79840).  Feeds on zooplankton, small insects and detritus.  One of the most popular aquarium fishes with many standardized varieties.  Used in genetics research.  Female reaches 5 cm SL (Ref. 2847).  Males mature at 2 months and females at 3 months of age (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).  A very popular and widely available species in the aquarium trade.  In Australia, wild populations were established prior to the 1970s, undoubtedly the result of thoughtless aquarists discarding unwanted pets (Ref. 44894).  Maximum length for female taken from Ref. 43281.

species.name: Guttigadus latifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental slopes (Ref. 31160).

species.name: Guttigadus nudicephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guttigadus nudirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guttigadus squamirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Guyana leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear and turbid water, often brackish water (Ref. 11225).  Feeds on worms, insects and fish (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Guyanan croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries but mainly in streams where it may be found very high beyond major waterfalls.  Preys on fish.  Little is known about its biology but it may form small schools (Ref. 35237).  An important foodfish.

species.name: Guyanancistrus brevispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons-chats. The most ubiquitous, frequently occurring and abundant species of this genus. Occurs in all kinds of streams where the substrate is rocky and the water is flowing (Ref. 35381). Found in great numbers in zones of plunging waters (Ref. 27188). May be found together with Lithoxus in little forest creeks as well as in rapids (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Guyanancistrus brownsbergensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons-chats. The type locality in the upper Kumbu Creek at Kumbu Falls (430 m asl) is a small mountain stream with 2.5-3.7 m width, 28-50 cm water depth,  with cool (23.1-23.2°C) water, high dissolved oxygen content of 93-96% saturation and  7.08-7.72 mg/L, a pH of 7.0-7.5, conductivity 30.8-31.6 μS/cm,  a current strength of 0.29-0.56 m/s taken on 12 July 2014, bottom substrate consisting of sand, gravel, pebbles, boulders and bedrock, and mostly clear water.  The creek is sheltered by overhanging vegetation, leaf litter and some woody debris (Ref. 116863).

species.name: Guyanancistrus megastictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons-chats.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a broad (30-40 meters wide), clear, flowing stream with a rocky bottom.  Temperature ranges between 15° and 25°C and pH from 5.0 to 6.0.  During the day it shelters in the cover of undercut banks, boulders, log snags and submerged root masses, darting into crevices if threatened.  Nocturnally active, feeding on insects and their larvae, crustaceans, fishes and plant matter.  Sexual maturity is reached at a length of about five centimeters.  One of the most recently discovered Australian freshwater fish species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Gymnarque du Nil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate air-breathing (Ref. 118411, 126274). Inhabits marginal vegetation and swamps constructing a flask-shaped nest in vegetation during the floods, which it is reputed to defend with vigour (Ref. 28714). Following flooding of the Gambia River banks, large elliptical floating nests are build in densely vegetated swamps at depths of about 1-1.5 m, in which about 1000 ‘amber-like’ eggs are laid; larvae hatch after 5 days (Ref. 10609). Feeds on crustaceans, insects and fish (Ref. 28714). No pelvic, anal or caudal fins (Ref. 28714). Possesses an electric organ that extends along almost the entire trunk to the tip of the tail (Ref. 10840). Also equipped with ampullary receptors and two types of tuberous receptors for electroreception (Ref. 10841). Showed increased electric organ discharge (EOD) rate by 50-60 Hz between 21 and 31°C (Ref. 10837).

species.name: Gymnogeophagus caaguazuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers habitats that are bare sandy bottoms among rocky areas in small rivulets which may have a strong current during the rainy season. During the dry season and period of low water, this species is found in pools and ponds with more or less stagnant water. In February, water data collected at the type locality has pH 7.9; electrical conductivity 240 μS/cm; temperature 24.2 °C. Associated fish fauna included Phalloceros caudimaculatus (Poeciliidae), Rineloricaria sp. (Loricariidae) and two small characid species. This species displays a variety of parental care and mating systems ranging from mouthbrooding and polygyny to substrate spawning and monogamy. In the aquarium, breeding was observed and the species was azuensis found to be a delayed (larvophile) maternal mouthbrooder, where like several of its congeners, it starts reproduction like a substrate spawner, i. e. the parents initially spawn on a stone, but just prior to the hatching of the larvae the female picks up the eggs and then orally broods the larvae and young. Courting males, in from of ripe females, display a conspicuous quivering movement of their mouths caused by opening and closing the mouth with extremely high frequency and this peculiar behaviour during courtship seems to be a synapomorphy of the mouthbrooding species, as it has been observed only within this species complex (Ref. 78439).

species.name: Gymnogeophagus jaryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with sandy and rocky bottom and abundant marginal vegetation. The climate where it is found, on the mountain ridge in Aristóbulo del Valle, is classified as warm and temperate. In this area there is a significant rainfall throughout the year (average per year is 1,678 mm), and even in August with the lowest precipitation, it still has a considerable amount of rain (111 mm). The lowest precipitation occur from July to September, the driest period and lowest water levels from December to February due to the marked seasonal change in temperature, and peaks in precipitation occur from May and October. The annual average temperature is 19.1°C, with 23.9ºC monthly average temperature in January and 14.3ºC in June. Water level in the stream can have important changes: water turbidity is variable among the year with peaks of turbidity after rains and increases in water visibility the rest of the year. Specimens are frequently collected in the rocky areas or associated with marsh and marginal vegetation. The holotype was collected together with the female paratype under the marginal vegetation and with fry on November 2016 (Ref. 119666).

species.name: Gymnogeophagus terrapurpura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in a large variety of habitats including shallow lakes, floodplain lakes, rivers, and streams, mainly associated with cobble, sandy or muddy substrates. It is an omnivore, feeding on zooplankton, macroinvertebrates, and periphyton (to a lesser extent). Feeding activity reduces greatly during autumn and winter when water temperature decreases (behavior reported in a low-impacted lowland stream in Florida Department and in a eutrophic shallow lake of Montevideo). It has been observed to brood on the substrate and exhibits substantial parental care, including aggressive territorial behavior in both males and females during the reproductive season which is from November to January (Ref. 123556).

species.name: Gymnote rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aggressive (Ref. 27188). Inhabits turbid slow moving or standing waters (Ref. 11225). Found also in shallow edges of streams (Ref. 75964). Can survive when ditches, canals and small ponds dry out. (Ref. 11225). Feeds mainly at night on worms, insects (e.g. odonate larvae), shrimps, fish (preferably small characids, e.g. Ctenobrycon and Curimata) and plant matter (Ref. 7020; 10011). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Mouth brooding by males is observed in this species (Ref. 55570). Males provide parental care in nests excavated for eggs and larvae (Ref. 55570). Uses its long anal fin for locomotion. Can distinguish between a `friendly neighbor' and a potentially `threatening stranger' based on electric organ discharge (EOD) waveform alone (Ref. 10011). Relationship between EOD pattern and agonistic behavior in this species has been demonstrated (Refs. 10531, 10532, 10533). Shows auditory abilities, responding best to a frequency of 1000 Hz, with an upper limit above 5000 Hz (Ref. 10831). Also responds to vibratory stimuli (water waves: 125-250 Hz) with transient increase in EOD rate (Ref. 10834). 'Prefers' temperatures of 24-25°C (Ref. 10836).

Undertakes aerial respiration by gulping atmospheric air into the hypervascularized posterior chamber of the gas bladder (Ref. 55508). Observed to survive out of water for many hours on a moist substrate (Ref. 55508).  Feeds mainly on chironomid larvae, insect nymphs and allochthonous invertebrates that fall from the forest canopy (Ref. 55508).

Adults both breed and forage in the meadows and are never encountered in other floodplain habitats such as flooded forests.  Both juveniles and adults feed on small aquatic animals, especially chironomid larvae (Ref. 41292).

In the whitewater floodplain, juveniles are encountered in patches of floating macrophytes along lakes margins and along the edge of canos (drainage channels from lakes to the main river channels) and paranás (channels connected at both ends to the main river channel that transport whitewater through the floodplain).  Floating macrophytes form extensive floating meadows.  Undertakes aerial respiration by gulping atmospheric air into the hypervascularized posterior chamber of the gas bladder.  Feeds primarily on chironomid larvae, small insect nymphs and small crustaceans (Ref. 55508).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rooted grasses and floating macrophytes in small creeks and along the banks of larger backwater rivers (Ref. 54472). Occurs syntopically with Gymnotus inaequilabiatus and G. sylvius (Ref. 54472).

species.name: Gymnotus pantherinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus paraguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus pedanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus stenoleucus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus sylvius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus tigre
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gymnotus ucamara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from static, vegetation-choked shallow water (Ref. 49730).  Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 49730).

species.name: Gymnotus varzea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in root mats of floating meadows in floodplains (Ref. 55508).  Gulps atmospheric air into the hypervascularized posterior chamber of its gas bladder (Ref. 55508).  Feeds on small aquatic invertebrates such as chironomid larvae, insect nymphs and microcrustaceans (Ref. 55508).

species.name: Gymnoxenisthmus tigrellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a narrow reef flat, the sandy slope with patches of corals and a rocky wall of about 3 m with small caves and shelters, and the slope began at depths of 8-10 m.  The holotype was captured on sand at the base of coral at a depth of 8 meters (Ref. 94949).

species.name: Gymnura afuerae
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Gymnura crooki
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Better reference needed.

species.name: Gymnura lessae
species.description: This demersal species lives along the coast on sandy and muddy bottoms. Reported stomach contents include fishes, crustaceans, molluscs and other invertebrates.  This species is matrotophic viviparous (lipid histotrophy). Young are reported to be produced from late May through July and into August, and probably even later in the season.  Pregnancy is reported to occur during the summer months (Ref. 116399).

species.name: Gyre codlet
species.description: There is little information available relating to its vertical distribution, but it is probably upper mesopelagic with maximum tow depths 80 m, 270 m, and 320 m (Ref. 130813).

species.name: Gyre flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly restricted to cores of central oceanic gyres (Ref. 35505).

species.name: Gyrinomimus andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at depths ranging from the surface up to 1,360 m.  At the collection site in the Lazarev Sea, specimens were caught from 1,370-1,400 m.  Biology unknown.

species.name: Gyrinomimus bruuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Gyrinomimus myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 37039.

species.name: Gérys killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools, swamps, brooks and small streams in the forested coastal savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Göksü spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Günther's boafish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Some individuals may migrate to the surface at night (Ref. 27000).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 27000.  Feed mainly on myctophids (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Günther's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in backwaters.  Marketed live.  Contributes to a local fishery during rainy season (October to February).

species.name: Günther's flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-mud bottoms; sometimes found on sand-and-broken shell bottoms (Ref. 9824).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Günther's karanteen
species.description: Apparently feeds on algae (based on unique teeth formation) (Ref. 94712).

species.name: Günther's pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Günther's sabre-gills
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Günther's waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Günther's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and coral reefs generally in shallow water (Ref. 9823).  Feeds primarily on small benthic crustaceans.

species.name: Günther’s deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Günther’s lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic (Ref. 4066).  Found between 425-750 m during the day and between 40-125 m at night (maximum abundance in the upper 50 m) (Ref. 4479).  Feeding is acyclic in northwest Africa (Ref. 9198).  Reach sexual maturity at 4.7 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Hache d'argent diaphane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and non-vertical migrant (Ref. 4739).  Mesopelagic at 275-1200 m (Ref. 58302).  Commonly found in 500-800 m both day and night (Ref. 4054).  Possibly a cyclic feeder of copepods, ostracods, euphausiids, amphipods, fishes and other taxa (Ref. 4739).  Adult photophore complement acquired at 11-13 mm SL (Ref. 4739).  Lipid content 1.4 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 4.2 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).

species.name: Hache d'argent à épines
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species concentrated at 300-600 m by day and 100-300 by night (Refs. 4462, 4739).  A selective dusk-time feeder mainly on conchoecid ostracods, to lesser extent on copepods, decapod larvae, fish larvae, etc (Ref. 4739).  Adult photophore developing at about 15 mm SL (Ref. 4739).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Hachette marbrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in groups.  Feeds on crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  The females have an abdomen which is larger than those of the males.  The eggs fall on the bottom or on vegetation and these hatch after 36 hours incubation at 25°C (Ref. 12225).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; may jump out of the aquarium; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Hadropareia middendorffii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal and shallow subtidal zones (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Hadropareia semisquamata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal and shallow subtidal zones (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Hadropogonichthys lindbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haemomaster venezuelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haemulon atlanticus
species.description: It is found in estuarine, coastal waters, and coral reefs, in sandy and rubby substrates up to a depth of 30 meters.  The largest specimen observed was 22.4 cm, standard length (Ref. 122368).

species.name: Haemulon schrankii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haemulon squamipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically occurs in reefs, at depths of 2-30 m where it forms large schools during the day.  Smaller schools, with less then 100 individuals, mostly juveniles, are seen on shallow reefs (2-6 m).  At night the schools disperse to feed (Ref. 37051).

species.name: Hagedorn’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality of this species in Quebrada Pachija, was described as an open-gallery, high flow stream with a flow of 0.748 m/s, a mean stream depth of 0.397 ± 0.059 m, and a mean stream width of 19.1 ± 1.0 m.   It was also observed t in the fastest flowing water sampled; where most adult specimens were captured from a single rocky rapids. These collections
also yielded numerous fry and small juveniles from within floating debris along the fast-flowing
edges of the Río Manu, however, identification of these samples still to be confirmed (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Hagen's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate to fast-flowing streams with cobble and boulder bottoms.

species.name: Hainan darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hainania serrata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hair-finned filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over reefs and sand bottom.  Feeds on small invertebrates.

species.name: Hairfin dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble of lagoon reefs (Ref. 37816).  Also occurs in various reef habitats to about 15 meters depth (Ref. 48637). Occurs in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hairfin smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hairfinned leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits weedy and sandy areas of coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found on open muddy substrates from shallow estuaries to deep offshore.  Males elongate with age (Ref. 48637).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Hairhead sculpin
species.description: Found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Hairtail blenny
species.description: Adults occur on open soft-bottom and mud habitats from shallow bays to deep water.  They are found in tube-like burrows in sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Very rarely encountered but more usually seen at night (Ref. 90102).  Nocturnal feeders.  Stomach of two specimens trawled in 50-54 m off western India contain crustaceans (including copepods), polychaete remains, forams, fish scales, and some sand and mud (Ref. 11441). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Have eel-like bodies but are rarely seen swimming away from their burrow (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Hairy blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diurnal, bottom-dwelling species which occur in rocky and rubble shores with algal mats, reefs and seagrass beds.  Generally at depths of a few cm (Ref. 13628).  Usually seen resting in holes or crevices, and when disturbed quickly move to another crevice.  This species is the largest of the labrisomids in the Caribbean region (Ref. 26938).  Feed mainly on crustaceans and gastropods (Ref. 13628), brittle stars, sea urchins, fishes and polychaete worms (Ref. 13442).  Oviparous, spawn in territories and exhibit paternal care of eggs (Ref. 55747).  Larvae are pelagic which eventually settle down at the bottom as juveniles (Ref. 42064).

species.name: Hairy bleny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit tide pools, surge channels, and outer slopes upper edge, near surface 0-5 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hairy pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lower reaches of rivers, estuaries or other protected inshore habitats (Ref. 5316). Found mostly in algal or Zostera beds (Ref. 5316), rarely at depths of more than a few meters (Ref. 31838). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hairy puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in rocky habitats including rapids of the Mekong mainstream and its larger tributaries (Ref. 27661).

species.name: Hairy scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 40 m (Ref. 1602).  Benthic in coral reefs (Ref. 58302).  Venomous spines (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Hairy seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hairyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic (Ref. 51024).  Only known specimen was caught near the surface.  Feeds on copepods (Ref. 6713).

species.name: Hairytail fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species, forming small aggregations in well protected narrow bays or inlets. Usually in sponge habitats (Ref. 48636). Adults may be found solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimics the young of Pentapodus trivittata (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref.7401.

species.name: Haiti coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haitian cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and streams. Largely found solitarily or in pairs, rarely in groups of 6-8, often in association with poeciliids and the mugilid Agonostomus monticola. Occurs with introduced cichlids at numerous localities. Adults swim in open water, taking refuge in small crevices under debris or in rocks when pursued. Young fish are frequently found in aquatic vegetation. Feeds on algae, other aquatic plants and turret shells.

species.name: Hakeling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Halaphritis platycephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives deep inside caves or under ledges in semi-exposed habitats in the near shore where light levels are low.  Adapted to creeping around the bottom in cramped confines.  In captivity, it crawls over the substrate rather than swim.  Feeds on shrimps and other small crustaceans in captivity (Ref. 43123).

species.name: Halavi ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species often found in very shallow water near the coast and offshore on the continental shelf (Ref. 9909, Ref.114953). Feed on small mollusks and bony fishes (Ref. 12951).   Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Produces up to 10 pups a litter, mainly from May to October (in the Red Sea region) (Ref. 114953). Size at least 171 cm TL. Males matures at ca. 83 cm TL, birth size at ca. 29 cm TL (Ref.114953). Utilized where it occurs but information lacking (Ref. 9909).

species.name: Hale's drombus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Half fringelip mullet
species.description: Found in coastal waters and ascending rivers into freshwater, penetrating far upstream from river mouth.  Found in turbid channels and over gravel-bottoms.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Food-fish.

species.name: Half naked goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species occirs in estuarine, intertidal and shallow coastal areas and frequently found associated with epilithic organisms (2 centimeters or more in size) found at depths ranging from tidepools to 13 meters. Some specimens from Lagoa da Conceição (state of Santa Catarina) were collected while snorkeling along the granitic shores in 1.5 to 2 meters of water in an area where the non-native tunicate Styela plicata (Lesueur 1823) are found and this solitary ascidian forms extensive aggregations in bands about 1 meter below the lower limit of the intertidal zone. Other species collected in the area included: gobiid Bathygobius soporator (Valenciennes 1837), the native blenny Hypleurochilus fissicornis (Quoy & Gaimard 1824), the invasive blenny Omobranchus punctatus (Valenciennes 1836), and the gobiesocid Gobiesox barbatulus Starks 1913. In Mar Chiquita lagoon (Buenos Aires Province, Argentina) this species has been recorded in high numbers associated with the reefs built by the invasive tubeworm Ficopomatus enigmaticus (Fauvel 1923; also known as Mercierella enigmatica) (Cervigón & Bastida, 1971). Nearby in Mar del Plata, this species inhabits the encrusting community in both the harbor and the mesolittoral zone of Cabo Corrientes; where in the latter community, composed of the mussels Brachidontes rodriguezii (d'Orbigny 1842) and Mytilus edulis platensis d'Orbigny 1842, this species is rare. In Uruguay, it was observed in tidepools 20 and 50 cm deep with clear water and sandy bottoms (A. Carvalho-Filho, pers. comm., 17 May 2013); other fish species in the pools included: H. fissicornis, juveniles of Mugil curema Valenciennes 1836 and adults of Jenynsia multidentata (Jenyns 1842). In São Paulo, both this species and Barbulifer enigmaticuswere collected within the same tidepools (J.L. Figueiredo, pers. comm., 20 September 2010). In northern Argentina and southern Brazil, this species has been collected at 8-13 meters. Also this species uses the empty shells of the cultured mussel Perna perna (Linnaeus 1758) for spawning and is an intermediary host of Bucephalus margaritae (Ozaki & Ishibashi 1934), a trematode worm parasitic on the mussel, in Santa Catarina (Ref. 104557).

species.name: Half-and-half chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit passages and outer reef slopes, solitarily or in small groups. They are sometimes seen in mixed aggregations with the closely related species C. margaritifer (Ref. 7247). Feeds on planktons (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Half-banded pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found amongst eelgrass (Zostera sp.). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Smallest examined brooding male is 13.95 cm SL.

species.name: Half-banded stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 11482).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 11482.

species.name: Half-barred cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep coastal reefs (Ref. 8631).  Form small schools with outcrops on reef on sand to depths of 20 m (Ref. 48635); or among rocks or corals of shallow sheltered lagoons (Ref. 7300); often in seagrass beds (Ref. 37816).  A nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Half-barred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in caves and crevices of seaward reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Half-lined cardinal
species.description: May enter semi-enclosed sea areas; forms schools over rocky bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Breeding pairs are found from July to September in Japan.  Mouth brooding is done by the male (Ref. 240).

species.name: Half-moon barred butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Half-moon blotch snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Half-naked hatchetfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 4739) and mesopelagic, mainly at 250-650 m (Ref. 4054).  Depth range from 100-700 m (Ref. 4462) and from 460-1082 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Adults make marked vertical migrations (Ref. 4739).  Found singly or in small groups (Ref. 4739).  An opportunistic feeder at dusk on calanoid copepods, small fishes, etc (Ref. 4739).  Sexual dimorphism with regard to body size (Ref. 5168), the males being slightly smaller than the females (Ref. 8966).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35838).
Occurs between 200 and 700 m depth during the day, concentrated between 350 and 550 m, and between 100 and 650 m at night, preferring a depth between 150 and 380 m Ref. 47377).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Half-scaled sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clean sand areas in the vicinity of rocky reefs (Ref. 9002).  Buries deep in sand (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Halfband snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf and inshore waters, over soft bottom.  Burrowing species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Halfbanded angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep coral reef areas (Ref. 4759).  Also found in rocky reefs. May be found in groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Halfbanded pike cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max length 40 cm TL (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Halfbanded pyrrhulina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Halfbanded rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common offshore water on flat bottom (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Halfbanded seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal and estuarine rocky reefs (Ref. 9002).  Common in sponge areas, sometimes in loose aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Halfbarred wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at 250 m by handline from Easter Island.

species.name: Halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More coastal than O. m. micropterus and frequently found near islands.

species.name: Halfbelt wriggler
species.description: A benthic, inshore species found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Halfblack Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in various reef habitats (Ref. 48636) especially in reef flats and tidepools (Ref. 90102) and in surf-swept reef margins.  Also found in intertidal areas and is usually associated with coralline rock and coral reef lagoons (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Halfblind goby
species.description: Adults hide among rocks and kelp holdfasts.  Young are often in schools in kelp canopy.  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Halfbridled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in upper estuaries, in seagrass beds, and mangroves (Ref. 9002); inhabits burrows (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Halfline hemiodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Halfline leporinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Halfmoon picassofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species that lives in outer reef areas. Feeds on fishes, benthic invertebrates, algae and organic matter (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Halfnaked jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Halfscaled jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits burrows.

species.name: Halicampus marquesensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and rubble bottoms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 7 cm SL.

species.name: Halichoeres bleekeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halichoeres dimidiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually observed solitary; juveniles relatively common in shallow waters (3 - 20 meters) while adults are in deeper waters (30 - 60 meters) (Ref. 52607).

species.name: Halichoeres iridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep seaward reefs, in sand and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Halichoeres kallochroma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rubble-algae reef flats and in seagrass habitats. Very similar to H. leucurus and at some stage was thought to be the same (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Halichoeres leptotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halichoeres melas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary, ranges over a wide area, stopping briefly every 2 to 3 meters to pick food from the reef substrate.

species.name: Halichoeres orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halichoeres penrosei
