species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in coral and rocky reef tops to depths of 30 meters and often solitary or in pairs (Ref. 52607).  Photo of individual from Brazil (Toque-Toque Beach, municipality of São Sebastião, state of São Paulo), 10.5 cm TL in length (T. Vaske, Jr. pers.comm. 2011).

species.name: Halichoeres rubrovirens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known about the ecology for this species, however, juveniles seem to mimic and usually swim together with schools of Thalassoma noronhanum which they resemble in color. Specimens were observed over high rugosity rocky bottoms with calcareous algae at depths (Ref. 83981).

species.name: Halichoeres sazimai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840. This species was observed foraging solitary on sand bottoms immediately adjacent to the lower end of rocky reefs. Harems that are composed of a few (5-10) individuals are not common but occasionally seen. This fish sometimes venture over the reefs, but generally never shallower than 20 m depth depending on water temperature (they seem to be associated with temperatures lower than 18°C). It also forages mostly on mobile invertebrates on soft and hard substratum, being more commonly observed foraging on sand bottoms and this behavior makes it a potential nuclear species in following associations, as it has been observed in other species of Halichoeres (Ref. 80967).

species.name: Halichoeres signifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often seen at the interface of low rocky reef and sand, foraging either over either reef or sand.  Occurs mainly in small groups of one male and approximately 10 females; with the male observed swimming rapidly and making frequent courtship displays.

species.name: Halichoeres socialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coral reefs over coral, sand, rubble or seagrass substrata (Ref. 46844).  Forms tight coherent schools when chased (Ref. 80499). Feeds on zooplankton and forms evasive, compact schools when threatened (Ref. 46844).

species.name: Halichoeres tenuispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit exposed rocky reefs. Feed on amphipods and other benthic crustaceans (Ref. 128523).

species.name: Halichoeres zulu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species with paucity of specimens, this is partly due to its misidentification as Halichoeres nebulosus, its usual shallow-water habitat off exposed rocky shores where it is difficult to collect and its being very elusive. Found on rocky bottom or sand with scattered patches of reef at depths of 0.5-1.5 meters. A male individual was photographed from a pool (about 5 m long, 2 m wide and 1.2 m deep) almost close to the sea at low tide (Ref. 83900).

species.name: Halicmetus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halicmetus odysseus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halicmetus ruber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Halidesmus polytretus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutaea nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutaea retifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Halieutichthys caribbaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutichthys intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis bathyoreos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 1,500 m (Ref. 33390).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Halieutopsis galatea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Halieutopsis ingerorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis margaretae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by otter trawl and shrimp trawl or trap (Ref. 58309).

species.name: Halieutopsis nudiventer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis simula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Halieutopsis stellifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis tumifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halieutopsis vermicularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halimeda ghostpipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reef of inshore waters. Benthic species (Ref. 75154). Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch (Ref. 205). Often among Halimeda or coralline algae, whhich it greatly resembles (Ref 90102).

species.name: Halimochirurgus alcocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halimuraena hexagonata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halimuraena lepopareia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water among weed, rock, and coral.

species.name: Halimuraenoides isostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halloween Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Percina crypta inhabits relatively swiftly flowing areas over bedrock or a mixture of coarse (boulder to gravel) bed sediments (Hill 1996; Marcinek 2003). The species is frequently associated with the aquatic macrophyte Podostemum ceratophyllum (Marcinek 2003). All of our observations of P. crypta have been in shoal habitats, which contrasts markedly with the broader range of stream habitats (pools, runs and riffles) occupied by the co-occurring congener P. nigrofasciata (Ref. 79864).

species.name: Halosaur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Feeds on copepods (Ref. 4448).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 4448.

species.name: Halosaurus attenuatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the lower slope and continental rise, at  2°-3°C (Ref. 4448).

species.name: Halosaurus carinicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halosaurus guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bathyal depths.  Feeds on small crustaceans, annelids, mollusks and echinoderms (Ref. 4448).

species.name: Halosaurus ovenii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The shallowest-occurring halosaur in the Atlantic.  May form aggregations.  Feeds on polychaetes, sipunculids, crustaceans and fish.

species.name: Halosaurus radiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halosaurus ridgwayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom feeders; mainly on crustaceans and other small invertebrates.  Males with markedly enlarged olfactory organs at maturity.  Leptocephalus larvae pelagic.  Taken occasionally in deep bottom trawls (Ref. 12887).

species.name: Halosaurus sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Halstead's sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups near reefs in sand-rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Halstead's toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand just beyond turbulent zone off surf beaches (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Haludaria afasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haludaria kannikattiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haludaria melanampyx
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Hameçon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms, mostly in brackish waters with bottom temperatures mostly near to or below 0°C and salinities of 10-15 ppt (Ref. 4698).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small bottom invertebrates (Ref. 4698).

species.name: Hamilton's barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It prefers quiet waters, like pans and large pools (Ref. 52193). It feeds on insects (Ref. 52193). Used as bait for tigerfish (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Hamlet à lèvres bleues
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in reef areas, with  its foraging behaviour suggesting that like the other hamlets, it is a mesopredator. In Bocas del Toro and Guna Yala (Panama), it has been observed at depths
ranging from 2 to 12 m.

species.name: Hampala ampalong
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hampala barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in clear rivers or streams with running water and sandy to muddy bottoms (Ref. 4832).  Found in most water bodies, except small creeks, torrents, and shallow swamps (Ref. 27732, 57235).  A migratory species (Ref. 37772).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Abundant in the Mekong and in the Nam Ngum Reservoir.  Found in the basin-wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Largest individual believed to be in a pool below the Chendoroh Dam in Perah, Malaysia.  A predatory fish:  adults mainly piscivorous in Zoo Negara Lake, Malaysia, but  in Saguling Reservoir, West Java, 74 % of the diet  consists of  aquatic insects.  Breeds throughout the rainy season (Ref. 12693).  Good fish though bony.  May be made into `Lap pa'.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Commonly seen in markets; economic important foodfish (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Hampala bimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hampala dispar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slowly moving or standing water habitats (Ref. 12693).  Encountered also in rapid-running mountain streams of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Common in impoundments, with small individuals frequenting areas of dense vegetation.  Feeds mainly on prawns, crabs, and shrimps, along with some insect larvae and some fish as well.  Breeds at the start of the rainy season and the young are found in seasonally flooded habitats in June.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Hampala lopezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hampala sabana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from rivers and streams (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Hampala salweenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hancock's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty worm and tube mollusk tubes on rocky reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Handlirsch’s minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes.  Is threatened due to pollution and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Handsome snailfish
species.description: The sediment from the Agassiz trawl was a mixture of sand, pebbles and stones, and numerous large fragments of dead and living glass sponges. Invertebrates found were dominated by at least 5 species of isopods and caprellids attached to colonies of hydroids (5 - 6 species), some benthopelagic shrimps (2 - 3 species), and a few gastropods and ophiurids (Ref. 123108).

species.name: Hannelore's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hansen's lanternfish
species.description: Oceanic and mesopelagic; occurs at between 608-728 m during the day and between 57-110 m at night.

species.name: Haploblepharus kistnasamyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis acidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered, shallow areas near submerged plant stands, over mud and hard substrate (Ref. 4983).  Major content of the guts which were examined consisted of macerated phanerogam tissue and varying amounts of epiphytic diatoms.  Some specimens contained a flocculent, grey-green mass thought to be bottom debris, principally blue-green algae.  Also fish, insect eggs, tissue mass and fragments of Ephemeroptera and other insects were found (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis adolphifrederici
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Entomophagous despite its massive enlarged pharyngeal jaw apparatus with molariform dentition (Ref. 13338).

species.name: Haplochromis aelocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with firm substrate (sand and rock) (Ref. 4983).  Gut contents showed that this species preys on a variety of invertebrate animals and possibly even small fish.  Predominant food organisms were insects (esp.  dipterous larvae but also Ephemeroptera & Trichoptera larvae).  The non-insect food were fish, oligochaete worms, prawns, plant tissue, ostracods, and fragments of lamellibranchs & gastropod shells (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis aeneocolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common near papyrus shores (Ref. 4983).  Apparently it never occurs offshore.  Seems to be a detritus feeder since plant fragments and insect larvae are predominant elements of the gut (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis akika
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis albertianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis altigenis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered gulfs and bays and relatively undisturbed offshore places, over hard and soft substrates (Ref. 4983).  The gut content of the specimens which were examined consisted mainly of finely macerated fish remains, identifiable as cichlids (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis ampullarostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis angustifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore, over both mud and sand (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on planktonic and benthic animals, of which, respectively, chaoborid and chironomid larvae are the dominant food organisms (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis annectidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in the vicinity of or amongst marginal vegetation, only rarely over exposed sandy beaches away from rooted plants (Ref. 4983).  Does not enter deeply into the marginal swamps and is rarely recorded at the swamp ends of inlets.  A common gut content is a barely recognizable mush of plant debris, both algal & phanerogamic, with blue-green algae predominating.  Also Diptera larvae, plant epidermis, diatoms & filamentous green algae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis antleter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found in sub-littoral areas of the Mwanza Gulf mainly over mud bottoms; the depth range is 2-11 m (Ref. 85523). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, this species fed mainly on detritus, but also included phytoplankton, mainly Aulacoseira, and occasionally insect larvae and zooplankton in its diet (Ref. 85523). Based on the egg dummies on the anal fin of males and the egg size in ripe females, it is a female mouth brooder (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis apogonoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively sheltered areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis aquila
species.description: Found in inshore areas over muddy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis arcanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from two localities only; over mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis argens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Haplochromis argens is a pelagic species from the littoral and sub-littoral zone (Ref. 92860). At night the species is virtually restricted to the two upper metres of the water column; by day, the highest densities were found at two to three metres from the surface, but individuals of this species were also caught with bottom trawls over sand and mud bottoms, and in gill nets and traps near rocks (Ref. 92860). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, the diet of H. argens comprised mainly zooplankton during the day; Chaoborus larvae were important at night (Ref. 92860). The current diet is unknown, but all the studied resurgent species in the Mwanza Gulf changed their diet (Ref. 92860). Haplochromis argens is a female mouth brooder (Ref. 92860). Spawning sites are located at depths less than 9 metres (Ref. 35300).

species.name: Haplochromis argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered localities with a mud bottom. Some specimens were collected from more exposed areas with a hard substrate. Juveniles have been collected from exposed beaches (Ref. 4983). The gut content of the specimens which were examined consisted of insect remains (terrestrial insects & Ephemeroptera larvae) and fish remains of Engraulicypris argenteus (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis artaxerxes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type (only specimen known) was caught near a fringing stand of swamp grass (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis astatodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives mainly in shallow waters with vegetation (Ref. 13338).

species.name: Haplochromis aureus
species.description: Abundant in the upper water layers of deepwater regions (Ref. 128938). It feeds on chaoborids and winged ants; most probably an insectivorous species that catches aquatic and terrestrial insects from the water surface (Ref. 128938).

species.name: Haplochromis avium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis azureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in rocky substrates. Inhabits moderately steep and steeply sloping large boulder stones. Feeds on plankton. Females and sexually inactive males form foraging shoals, often mixed with P. nyererei.

species.name: Haplochromis barbarae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, exposed sandy beaches, over a hard substrate situated a short distance off-shore near the water lily zone fringing a papyrus swamp (Ref. 4983).  The gut of the specimens which were examined contained recently fertilized cichlid ova (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis bareli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis bartoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas near dense plant stands, either sheltered or exposed, with hard or soft bottoms. Possibly most abundant some distance off-shore (between 200-300 m) (Ref. 4983). Feeds on fish: Cichlidae (Haplochromis) and Cyprinidae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis bayoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in waters with a hard substrate (sand and shingle).  Also occurs in exposed sandy beaches and fairly exposed bays (Ref. 4983).  Gut content of the specimens which were examined consisted entirely of finely macerated fish remains identifiable as small Cyprinids (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis beadlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore regions of the main lake and the lake ward inlets to the marginal swamps (Ref. 4983); over sand, sand with mud-detritus overlay and deep mud.  Feeds on insect larvae (Chironomid & Trichoptera) as well as on plant epidermis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis boops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep water near islands and over mud bottoms (Ref. 4983). Feeds on fish (Haplochromis) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis borleyi redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocky areas.  Mostly found near very large boulders, but in shallow water large schools congregate at rocky islets on the sand.  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Haplochromis brownae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or shingle beaches which are relatively or completely exposed to wave action (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis bullatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis bwathondii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sub-littoral areas of the Mwanza Gulf, over mud bottoms; it is a mainly pelagic species (Ref. 85523). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, this species fed mainly on Cyanophyta, both during day and night; Aulacoseira and occasionally other small diatoms such as Nitzschia were also consumed, as well as adult insects and insect pupae from the water surface (Ref. 85523). This species is a female mouth brooder that spawns the whole year (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis cassius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open, yet relatively sheltered areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis cavifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relatively common a few hundred meters off-shore over hard substrates.  Few specimens caught over mud (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis chilotes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered sublittoral and littoral zones with a hard substrate. Few specimens caught over mud (Ref. 4983). Feeds mainly on the larvae of the mayfly Povilla adusta; also on Trichoptera and Diptera larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis chlorochrous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open waters with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983). Gut content of the specimens which were examined consisted of crustacean fragments, probably Caridina sp. (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis chromogynos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably confined to the littoral zone, over a firm substrate (Ref. 4983).  Gut contents of the specimens which were examined consisted mainly of Trichoptera larvae and sand-grain cases, but a few larval chironomids and baetids were also identified (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis chrysogynaion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis cinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All six specimens were collected from a trawl haul made over both hard and soft substrates (Ref. 4983).  The stomach and intestine of the one specimen which was examined were filled with blue-green algae, diatoms and other algaceous material (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis cinereus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over a sandy bottom on both protected and exposed shores (Ref. 4983).  The stomach and intestinal contents of the specimens which were examined consisted of sand grains, bottom detritus (including fragments of plant epidermis) and some larvae of dipterous insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis cnester
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rather exposed area with a soft mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis concilians
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gut short, diet mainly molluscivorous (Ref. 126074).

species.name: Haplochromis coprologus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Before the ecological changes, this species occurred in the sub-littoral areas of the Mwanza Gulf, mainly over mud bottoms; juveniles occured in sheltered bays (Ref. 85523). It fed mainly on detritus during daytime; other important food items comprised the diatom Aulacoseira and copepods (Ref. 85523). This species is a female mouth brooder; like most other detritivorous species, it is a seasonal spawner; sexually active males were abundant from March till October, brooding females were abundant from March till September (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis crassilabris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis crebridens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis crocopeplus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open water over mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis cronus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with an exposed beach, a sandy littoral of a sheltered gulf, a mud-bottom sublittoral of a sheltered bay, and near a reed bed (Ref. 4983). Feeds on fish larvae identifiable as Haplochromis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis cryptodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow beaches (Ref. 4983).  The stomach of one specimen which was examined contained recently fertilized cichlid ova, while numerous small fish vertebrae were found in the posterior intestine (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis cryptogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in relatively exposed areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on the pupae of chironomid flies (which occur in dense aggregates), and apparently feeds away from the bottom (Ref. 6708).

species.name: Haplochromis curvidens
species.description: Found over muddy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis cyaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to rocky substrates; lives and feeds exclusively on the surface of rocky substrates, usually exposed to wave action; never observed or collected in crevices, and rarely in sheltered embayment; feeds predominantly on Chironomid larvae that live among algal filaments on the surface of rocks; polygynous female mouth brooder with maternal parental care (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Haplochromis decticostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively exposed areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983). The gut content of the specimens which were examined consisted of remains of the crustacean Caridina and fish fragments (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis dentex
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered bays with mud substrates, exposed sandy beaches, open off-shore waters with rock and shingle bottoms, and a fairly exposed bay with a hard substrate. Depth range extends to at least 7.5 m (Ref. 4983). Feeds on small Haplochromis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis dichrourus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in both sheltered and exposed places (including beaches), over sand and shingle substrates (Ref. 4983). Gut contents of the specimens which were examined consisted of fish remains (Haplochromis and other cichlids) and fragments of larval insects (Ref. 558 and 6708).

species.name: Haplochromis diplotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis dolichorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in open off-shore waters and in a relatively shallow bay. All localities had a mud substrate (Ref. 4983). Fishes from greater depths feed on small crustaceans, especially Caridina sp. and to a lesser degree, on Diptera pupa. Fishes from shallower locality fed on Diptera pupa with considerable quantities of mud ingested (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis dolorosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis eduardianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, over both mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 5690).

species.name: Haplochromis eduardii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore regions especially near papyrus shores where the bottom is sandy (Ref. 4983).  Feeds mostly on chironomid larvae, although emergent aquatic Diptera are also eaten when available (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis empodisma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with organic mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Is a bottom feeder which feeds mainly on the larval stages of dipterous insects together with diatoms derived from the bottom mud.  Remains of mollusks and fragments of bivalves and gastropods were found in the stomach and intestines of specimens which were examined (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis engystoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis erutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diet mainly mollucivorous (Ref. 126074).

species.name: Haplochromis erythrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits off-shore areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  The stomach and intestine of specimens which were examined consisted of blue-green algae, diatoms and smaller quantities of green algae; in some fishes a few fragments of crustaceans and insect larvae were found (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis erythromaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Present in shallow waters along vegetated shoreline; also in small affluents of Lakes Bulera and Ruhondo (Ref. 26716).

species.name: Haplochromis estor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered bays and gulfs with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis eutaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on shrimps (Ref. 31624).

species.name: Haplochromis exspectatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In shallow waters; thought to feed on juvenile fish (Ref. 52362).

species.name: Haplochromis falcatus
species.description: Found over sandy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis fischeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy substrate, interspersed with patches of shelter which can be rocks or vegetation; especially common over exposed sandy beaches; feeds on gastropods, insect larvae, diatoms and copepoda (Ref. 79882).

species.name: Haplochromis flavipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed sandy beaches; sheltered bays and gulfs with a soft mud bottom; rocky shelves running out from exposed islands (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis flavus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to rocky substrates.  Microhabitats of this species range from very gentle to moderately steep slopes.  Feeds on chironomid larvae, filamentous Chlorophyta, diatoms and macrophytes.

species.name: Haplochromis fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis fusiformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in off-shore areas with a mud substrate (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis gigliolii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis gilberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught over a mud bottom at the type locality only (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on cyprinid fish and chironomid pupae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis glaucus
species.description: Found over sandy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis goldschmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught over mud bottoms at depths of 4-10 meters (Ref. 92860). Stomach and intestines of five examined specimens caught by day contained mainly zooplankton and some insects (Ref. 92860). Based on the egg dummies on the anal fin of males,  this species is probably a female mouth brooder (Ref. 92860).

species.name: Haplochromis gowersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open beaches; off-shore islands; sheltered bays and gulfs; over soft and hard bottoms (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis gracilifur
species.description: This species has a paedophagous diet (Ref. 127594).

species.name: Haplochromis gracilior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis granti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually collected from exposed sandy beaches and exposed shorelines with a hard substrate, few from sheltered bays with organic mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).  Specimens which were examined contained soft parts of gastropods in the stomach (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis graueri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis greenwoodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in rocky shores.  Inhabits mainly steeply sloping large boulder shores but is also found on gently sloping shores if the boulder size is large enough to provide interstices.  Adults forage in shoals, mixed with other species.  Omnivorous, feeding on  algae, Bryozoans, insect larvae, plankton, prawns and juvenile fishes (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Haplochromis guiarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis harpakteridion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis heusinkveldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed and sheltered areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis hiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis howesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on crabs (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis humilior
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Victoria, confined to shallow water over sandy beaches in both sheltered and exposed areas (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained bottom debris (sand grains, plant fragments, diatom frustules and blue-green algae) together with remains of both larval and pupal insects (esp.  Diptera & Trichoptera less frequently Ephemeroptera); also mollusks (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis humilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis insidiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis iris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with bottoms of organic mud (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis ishmaeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore regions with a soft mud bottom. Few specimens caught over sand and shingle bottoms (Ref. 4983). The stomach and intestinal contents of specimens which were examined indicate that w/in a size range of 8.4-13.5 cm SL, H. ishmaeli feeds almost exclusively on mollusks, with accidental ingestion of insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis kamiranzovu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis katonga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Katonga River, which is choked with vegetation and hardly recognizable as a river, with no directly visible current (Ref. 85068).

species.name: Haplochromis katunzii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found in sub-littoral areas of the Mwanza Gulf, mainly over mud bottoms; the depth range is 2-15 m (Ref. 85523). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, this species fed mainly on detritus, but also included phytoplankton, insect larvae and copepods in its diet (Ref. 85523). Based on the egg dummies on the anal fin it is supposed to be a female mouth brooder (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis kimondo
species.description: Found over sandy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis kujunjui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis labiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diet insectivorous (Ref. 126507).

species.name: Haplochromis labriformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis lacrimosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  The stomach and intestinal contents of the specimens which were examined consisted of fine sand grains, bottom detritus (incl.  fragments of plant epidermis and diatom frustules), some Cladocera, and insect larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis laparogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively exposed waters with sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on Diptera larva and pupae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis latifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis latifrons
species.description: Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis limax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in places which are suitable for the growth of aufwuchs.  It is never found far from the shore line but the substrata over which it occurs are varied (Ref. 4983).  Aufwuchs, its associated micro-fauna and macerated phanerogam tissue are the commonest types of ingested matter recorded from the gut.  Feeds by scraping food items from the lake bottom (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis lividus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallow littoral zone, especially near emergent and submerged vegetation, less frequent in the water lily zone and at margins of papyrus swamps, commonly encountered over rock foundations of piers (Ref. 4983). The diatoms Melosira and Rhopalodia comprised the predominating digested stomach contents. Plant epidermis, filamentous green algae and fragmentary animal remains were also recorded (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis loati
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies the hyacinth fringe in Sudd lakes and moves into submerged vegetation during the flood. Omnivorous, consumes algae, vegetable fragments, zooplankton, Caridina and insects. Males are twice as numerous as females (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Haplochromis lobatus
species.description: Diet insectivorous (Ref. 126507).

species.name: Haplochromis longirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy beaches, exposed or within a sheltered gulf (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on both insects (particularly pupal stages) and small fishes (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis luluae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Agamous, ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Haplochromis macconneli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is confined to water more than 20 m deep and is probably most abundant in deeper water (i.e. at depths of 50-70 m) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis macrognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered gulfs with a hard or mud substrate, and exposed sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy region (Ref. 4983). Feeds on sub-imaginal Ephemeroptera. Isoptera and colonial blue-green algae were also found in a few specimens. The occurrence of sub-imaginal or adult insects and planktonic blue-green algae, together with the absence of bottom debris suggests that H. macrops feeds at the surface or in mid-water (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis macropsoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas close to papyrus fringes of islands or more exposed areas offshore of islands over mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on dipteran larvae and pupae.  The absence of phytoplankton or sand grains in the stomach of the specimens which were examined suggest that the fish were feeding away from the bottom (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis maculipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered gulfs and bays where the substrate is either soft mud or sand and shingle.  A few specimens were from exposed beaches and from deeper water (10.5-12 m) near off-shore islands (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fishes and insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis mahagiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis maisomei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis malacophagus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis mandibularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 5 close inshore localities with a sand bottom, sheltered (4) or partly exposed (1) (Ref. 4983). Feeds on fish (Haplochromis) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis martini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on exposed shores and in sheltered bays, over both sand and mud but probably not close inshore (Ref. 4983).  Feeds mainly on fish, also on Diptera larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis maxillaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the littoral and sublittoral zones.  Most are caught over sand or shingle, few over mud substrate (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on cichlid embryo or larvae.  The smallest specimen which was examined proved exceptional in that the stomach was filled with Copepoda and blue-green algae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered bays with a mud substrate or a substrate of interposed sand and mud patches (Ref. 4983).  The predominant ingested material in the specimens which were examined consisted of macerated dipterous (?chironomid) larvae, together with small quantities of bottom mud (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis melanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype collected from an area with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  The stomach of the specimen which was examined was packed with early embryos of a cichlid fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis melanopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis melichrous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively exposed areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983). The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained small quantities of mud and fragments of crustaceans (probably Caridina sp.); other fragments were tentatively identified as remains of Dipteran pupae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis mentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in offshore areas, mostly in shallow waters (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis mento
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits littoral areas with a sand or sand and rock substrate.  Most localities are exposed but one is a sheltered gulf (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of a small number of specimens which were examined contained remains of cyprinid and cichlid fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis michaeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens caught less than 200 m from the shore over mud substrate in a sheltered gulf or bay, or in the lee of a large island (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of 7 specimens which were examined contained unidentifiable fish remains (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis microchrysomelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis microdon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the littoral zones over both firm and soft substrates (Ref. 4983). Since the dentition and jaw structure of H. microdon so closely resemble those of H. parvidens, the feeding habits of the two species may well be similar (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis molossus
species.description: This species has a paedophagous diet (Ref. 127594).

species.name: Haplochromis multiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis mylergates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively exposed areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983). The specimens which were examined contained fragments of the gastropod, Melanoides tuberculata,in their stomachs and intestines (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis mylodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the shoreline over mud and mud-sand substrates (Ref. 4983). Feeds mainly on gastropods, particularly Melanoides tuberculata. Chironomid larvae are also eaten (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis nanoserranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow off-shore waters with a muddy sand substrate (Ref. 4983).  One of the specimens examined contained a small cichlid in its intestines while others contained fragments of larval insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis nigrescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis nigricans
species.description: Inhabits rocky and shallow areas of the littoral zone (Ref. 4983). In the lake H. nigricans has been observed to graze on algae from rock surfaces (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly found in open offshore waters, sometimes found close to the shore in sandy areas (Ref. 4983). As suggested by its long and coiled intestines, H. nigripinnis is a vegetarian. It feeds mainly on suspended phytoplankton. Like most Haplochromis species, it is an opportunistic feeder (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis nigroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis niloticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis nuchisquamulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed littoral zones (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained fragments of plant tissue and numerous epiphytic algae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis nyanzae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively sheltered or exposed areas over hard bottoms (sand or shingle) (Ref. 4983). The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained remains of fish identifiable as Haplochromis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis obesus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the littoral and sublittoral areas.  Most specimens were caught over a hard substrate (sand, shingle and rock), few over mud (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish embryos or larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis obliquidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallow littoral zone, particularly in the vicinity of emergent vegetation (Ref. 4983). Less commonly found in the water lily zone, over exposed sandy beaches and at the margin of papyrus swamps. Has often been collected and seen around rock foundations of piers. Feeds mainly on diatoms (Melosira, Surirella, Gomphonema, Rhopalodia, Navicula, and Cyclotella) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis occultidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis oligacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis olivaceus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis omnicaeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores.  Usually solitary.  Feeds mainly on filamentous Chlorophyta and Cyanophyta where it inhabits gentle slopes and on Cyanophyta and diatoms on steep slopes.

species.name: Haplochromis oregosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore areas over both sand and mud substrates (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis orthostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis pachycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens but one were caught over soft bottoms some distance off-shore but close to islands (Ref. 4983). The specimens which were examined contained macerated fish remains in their stomachs. Fragments of Haplochromis species, other cichlids and cyprinids were identified in the samples (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis pallidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from one locality only (an exposed, shallow and sandy beach) (Ref. 4983).  The specimens which were examined contained moderately large quantities of bottom debris (sand grains, diatom frustules, and fragments of plant tissue) together with fragmentary insect larvae (? Diptera) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis paludinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and swampy areas (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Haplochromis pancitrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sub-littoral waters of the northern part of the Mwanza Gulf over mud bottoms; occasionally it was caught over mud bottoms, in shallower areas more southward in the Gulf (Ref. 85523). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, this species fed on phytoplankton, mainly Cyanophyta; the diet further included Chaoborus larvae, copepods and occasionally detritus (Ref. 85523). Based on the egg dummies on the anal fin and the egg size in ripe females, this species is a female mouth brooder (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis pappenheimi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in upper water levels in offshore regions (Ref. 4983); abundant in and near sublittoral regions and present in deepwater regions (Ref. 128938). It feeds on zooplankton, particularly copepods and cladocerans (Ref. 558, 128938) and larvae, pupae and emerging adults of chaoborids (Ref. 128938).

species.name: Haplochromis paradoxus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis paraguiarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on exposed wave-washed beaches where the substrate is of sand, rock, or shingle.  A few records were from more sheltered areas (Ref. 4983).  Most of the specimens which were examined contained either macerated plant tissue or a mixture of plant tissue and insect fragments (Ephemeroptera larvae) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis paraplagiostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught over a mud bottom (known from only one locality) (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis pardus
species.description: Found in inshore areas (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis paropius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in off-shore areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  The specimens which were examined contained large quantities of blue-green algae and diatoms and smaller amounts of other plant material.  Fragmentary remains of Diptera larvae were found in some specimens (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis parorthostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on exposed areas over hard bottoms (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis parvidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the littoral and sublittoral zones.  May occur commonly over a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on cichlid embryos or larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis paucidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis pelagicus
species.description: Abundant in upper water layers of deepwater regions of Lake Edward, occasionally found in upper water layers of sublittoral areas of lakes Edward and George and Kazinga Channel (Ref. 128938). It feeds on copepods and chaoborid larvae, pupae and emerging adults (Ref. 128938).

species.name: Haplochromis pellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the relatively exposed sandy beaches near dense stands of submerged and emergent plants (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained an unidentifiable sludge, insect remains, Ephemeroptera pupae and Diptera larvae, and post-larval fish (fragmentary but identifiable as cichlids) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis percoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water over exposed or partly exposed sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  Is nowhere common but seems to be widely distributed around the lakeshore.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558)

species.name: Haplochromis perrieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis pharyngalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The stomachs of a small number of specimens which were examined contained both larval and emergent insects (Ref. 558). Specimens from Lake George insectivorous, those from Lake Edward both insectivorous and molluscivorous (Ref. 128436).

species.name: Haplochromis pharyngomylus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with a hard bottom (sand, shingle or, less frequently, rock).  Often found amongst stands of aquatic plants (Ref. 4983).  At a size range of 7.5-11.5 cm SL, this species feeds mainly or even exclusively on mollusks.  Both bivalves and gastropods are eaten in approximately equal proportions (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis phytophagus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallow littoral zone where the bottom is sandy and near fairly dense strands of rooted aquatic plants (Ref. 4983).  The stomach and intestinal contents of the specimens contained fragments of phanerogam leaf tissue which filled the entire alimentary canal.  Large numbers of epiphytic diatoms and colonial blue-green algae were also found (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis piceatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a relatively sheltered gulf with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Bottom mud and Diptera pupae (probably Chironomidae) were identified in specimens which were examined for gut content (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis pitmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis placodon pointed head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow (Ref. 5709, 55954) inshore waters (Ref. 5709).  Frequently seen in vegetated areas; feeds on insect larvae and crustaceans that it locates in the soft substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Haplochromis placodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis plagiodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water over a exposed sandy beach (Ref. 4983).  Remains of Diptera and Ephemeroptera larvae (together with many fine sand grains) were found in the intestines of the two specimens which were examined (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis plagiostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered and relatively shallow areas with either soft (mud) or hard (sand or shingle) substrate (Ref. 4983). The few specimens which were examined were found to be piscivorous, the prey being predominantly Haplochromis and less often, small Cyprinidae (probably Engraulis argenteus) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis planus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis plutonius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over a mud bottom in exposed water (known from only one locality) (Ref. 4983). The relatively long and much coiled intestine of H. plutonius suggests that a certain amount of plant material may be part of the normal diet (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common within its distributional range; prefers shallow, slow-flowing zones near riverbanks; likely feeds on detritus, algae, small insects or crustaceans; agamous, ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Haplochromis prodromus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the littoral zones, particularly where the substrate is hard (sand or shingle), less frequently over mud (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on mollusks and insects (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis prognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in both sheltered and exposed localities where the substrate is hard (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish, insects and plants (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis pseudopellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sheltered bays and fairly exposed off-shore and deep areas.  Caught over mud bottoms (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis ptistes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the type locality; an exposed area with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on mollusks (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Haplochromis pyrrhocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over mud bottoms in exposed areas (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis pyrrhopteryx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis quads
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at the sand/rock interface (Ref. 57549). Found at an average depth of 15 m (Ref. 5595). Feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595, 57549) and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 57549). Territorial males build a bowl-shaped bower beneath and/or adjacent to a rock, 18-42cm in diameter and a 4-7 cm high rim; females occur in schools numbering up to 50 individuals, remaining within 2m above the bottom (Ref. 57549).

species.name: Haplochromis quasimodo
species.description: Found in offshore, benthic areas in shallow and deep waters (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis relictidens
species.description: This species has a paedophagous diet (Ref. 127594).

species.name: Haplochromis retrodens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the littoral and sub-littoral zone, especially where the substrate is hard and usually where there is submerged vegetation (Ref. 5648).  Feeds mainly on mollusks (particularly Lamellibranchiata).  Insects (esp.  Ephemeroptera, Trichoptera and Chironomidae together with crustaceans and Hydracarina) were ingested less frequently (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis rex
species.description: Found over sandy substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis riponianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in exposed and sheltered littoral areas with a sand or rock substrate (Ref. 4983).  Is mainly insectivorous.  Trichoptera and Ephemeroptera larvae were in the stomachs of the fish which were examined.  Bivalves and gastropods were also found in the samples (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis rubescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis rubripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Confined to rocky substrates.  Commonly found in the water column above rocky substrates.  Occurs at depths between 1 (rarely) and at least 8 m.  On moderately steep slopes, they usually stay several meters offshore, while they occur immediately inshore on steep slopes in the southern Mwanza Gulf, Lake Victoria.  Feeds on zooplankton and insect larvae.  The distribution of individuals in gill nets indicates that this species often forages in small shoals (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Haplochromis rudolfianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is confined to the shallow and protected inshore areas of the lake although there is a population inhabiting a crater lake on Central Island (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis rufocaudalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters of most rocky areas.  Females, non-territorial males and subadults forage in shoals of sized-matched individuals.  Feeds predominantly on epilithic algae (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Haplochromis rufus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is restricted to rocky substrates.  Inhabits inshore, on gentle, as well as on steep slopes.  Feeds on insect larvae and snails (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Haplochromis sauvagei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the littoral zone where the bottom is hard; especially common over exposed sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  Feeds mainly on gastropods, bottom deposits, which include insect larvae, copepods and diatoms, and Insecta (chiefly larval boring may-flies, Povilla adusta) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis saxicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits various areas (exposed beaches, dense plant stands near rocky shores) with hard substrates of sand, rocks or shingle (Ref. 4983).  Feeds mainly on insect larvae (Diptera, probably chironomids); also snails and ostracods (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis scheffersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis schubotzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in offshore areas over both sand and mud (Ref. 4983). May inhabit exposed or relatively protected localities. An examination of the gut contents of a few specimens suggests that H. schubotzi is insectivorous but the extent of its dependence on this food source needs confirmation (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis schubotziellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in muddy bays and near papyrus fringed shorelines, but rarely encountered in open waters (Ref. 4983).  The presence of plant and other organic debris, together with dipteran larvae in the stomach suggests bottom feeding, possibly insectivorous habits (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis serranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered bays and gulfs where the bottom is of soft organic mud. All localities were less than 500 m from the shore (Ref. 4983). Feeds on fish, predominantly Haplochromis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis serridens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis simba
species.description: Found in inshore areas over hard substrates (Ref. 126312). Based on its morphology, most probably a piscivorous species (Ref. 126312).

species.name: Haplochromis simotes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis simpsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore over a variety of substrates, amongst emergent vegetation, over exposed sandy beaches and some distance offshore over a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Is an omnivorous bottom feeder which preys chiefly on insect larvae (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis smithii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis snoeksi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic species (Ref. 97348), found on a substrate of sand with pebbles and mud (Ref. 85558).

species.name: Haplochromis spekii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over hard (mostly) and soft substrates, in sheltered and less often, exposed areas (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis sphex
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in waters up to a depth of 10 m both over sand and mud (Ref. 85523). It fed mainly on phytoplankton (Cyanophyta and Aulacoseira) and occasionally on copepods (Ref. 85523). This species is a female mouth brooder (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis squamipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in offshore benthic areas in mostly shallow and deep waters over muddy substrates (Ref. 4983, 126312). With a piscivorous diet (Ref. 558, 126312); insects contribute substantially to the diet of small Haplochromis squamipinnis (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis squamulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from a wide variety of habitats; sheltered and exposed, littoral and offshore.  Mostly found over hard substrate (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis sulphureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in exposed areas with a soft mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  The specimens which were examined contained remains of dipteran pupae and some fragments of unidentifiable crustaceans (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis sunset
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Encountered usually in shallow water in vegetated  and sandy areas.  Swims in midwater.  Feeds on small fish (such as juvenile Utaka) and invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Haplochromis tanaos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from relatively sheltered areas with a sandy substrate in Lake Victoria (Ref. 47153).

species.name: Haplochromis taurinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently confined to inshore areas of the lake where it has been taken off the papyrus fringe and also over sandy beaches in sheltered areas (Ref. 558, 4983). It has a paedophagous diet (Ref. 127594).

species.name: Haplochromis teegelaari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in relatively sheltered areas with a mud substrate (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on bivalves (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis teunisrasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rather exposed areas with a soft mud bottom (Ref. 4983).

species.name: Haplochromis theliodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exposed, shallow and sandy beaches (Ref. 4983). The stomach contents of the specimens which were examined indicate that H. theliodon is a bottom feeder. Its diet includes small fishes (cichlids), gastropods, lamellibranchs and insect larvae. Large quantities of bottom debris were also ingested (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis thereuterion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Haplochromis thereuterion occurs in the upper layers of the water column in Lake Victoria (Ref. 47153).

species.name: Haplochromis thuragnathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in exposed water with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983). Two specimens which were examined for gut content had small fragments of small Haplochromis species in the stomach and intestines (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis torpedo stripe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been observed over sand.  Preys on small fish, mainly cichlids, and on invertebrates collected from the sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Haplochromis tridens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs some distance offshore over a soft bottom, in deep water (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs of the specimens which were examined contained mainly undigested blue-green algae and empty diatom frustules.  Crustacean fragments and unidentifiable insect remains were also found (Ref. 558).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Haplochromis tyrianthinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in open water with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Fragmentary crustacean remains  were found in the stomachs of the specimens which were examined (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis ushindi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes (Ref. 55928).

species.name: Haplochromis vanheusdeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Haplochromis vanheusdeni is a benthic-rheophilic fish, mostly found among stones over sand and debris in smaller streams or larger rivers (Ref. 97348). Underwater observations suggest a mixed diet of sand-and-debris dwelling organisms and drifting food particles (Ref. 98348). Large males and brood-caring females defend small territories, sometimes centred around a whole under stones; it is a maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 97348).

species.name: Haplochromis vanoijeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species, caught mainly in the deeper parts, more than 10 m depth, in the Mwanza Gulf, over mud bottoms; occasionally caught over mud in shallower areas (Ref. 85523). Before the ecological changes in Lake Victoria, this species fed mainly on detritus; occasionally remains of shrimps and insects were found (Ref. 85523). This species is a female mouth brooder (Ref. 85523).

species.name: Haplochromis velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found both close inshore and some distance out, over muddy and sandy bottoms in bays, and over clear sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  Is an omnivorous bottom feeder which preys mainly on insect larvae (esp.  chironomids and trichopterans) (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis venator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More abundant in offshore, open areas than in other regions.  Possibly pelagic over mud bottoms in the middle of the lake (Ref. 4983).  Is predominantly piscivorous although insects (esp.  adult Ephemeroptera) are also eaten (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis vicarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis victoriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sandy littoral zone (type specimen only) (Ref. 5672).

species.name: Haplochromis victorianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered areas with a mud bottom (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on small fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis vonlinnei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Piscivore, feeding on small haplochromine cichlids (Ref. 74923).

species.name: Haplochromis worthingtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haplochromis xenognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in littoral zones where the substrate is hard, most known specimens from exposed sandy beaches (Ref. 4983).  The stomachs which were examined contained soft parts of gastropods, insects ( chironomid and ephemerid larvae), bottom detritus (sand grains and plant tissue), and unidentifiable sludge (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis xenostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered or relatively undisturbed areas where the bottom is soft mud, sand or shingle (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 558).

species.name: Haplochromis yellow black line
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most frequently seen over sand but may also occur in the intermediate sand-rock habitat (Ref. 5595).  Usually collected from trawl hauls in shallower stations.  Feeds on small fish, gastropods, and lamellibranch mollusks (Ref. 267).

species.name: Haplotaxodon microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults roam the open waters of the lake, solitary or in pairs (Ref. 86760).  Occasionally found schooling in coastal waters along rocky coasts.  Feed on zooplankton (Ref. 6770).  Biparental mouthbrooding of the young (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Haplotaxodon trifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Happy
species.description: Found over sandy bottom  but frequently stays in midwater.  A specialized predator which steals brood from females by ramming the head from below.  Stomach contents revealed only eggs, larvae and fry (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Haptenchelys texis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Haptoclinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hara filamentosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast flowing river with depth nowhere more than 80 cm and with bottom mainly consisting of stones and sand with numerous empty gastropod shells (Ref. 37833).

species.name: Hara hara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow-moving rivers and streams.

species.name: Hara horai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Hara jerdoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow-moving hill streams with sandy bottom (Ref. 4833), rivers and beels (Ref. 1479).  A very sluggish fish.

species.name: Hara koladynensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hara longissima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hara mesembrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hara minuscula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hara spinulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harasti’s pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits semi-exposed bay entrances and ocean embayments in which the underwater terrain is characterised by sandy areas interspersed with boulders and hard flat reefs. Individuals and pairs of this species were observed in close association with a species of finger sponge appearing to a member of the family Callyspongiidae and several different species of red algae appearing to be of the family Gracilariaceae in the genera Crassiphycus and Gracilaria. It was not seen associating with any of the other numerous species of small to large sponges or tunicates present on the sessile-rich boulders nor within the canopy kelp Ecklonia radiata. It has also been observed on occasion active individuals swimming from one clump of red algae to another or feeding actively just outside the red algae. Feeding behaviour appears to be similar to other congeners, with individuals darting out from the cover of their alga to capture food such as small copepods and shrimp. (Ref. 123272).

species.name: Hard-drinking atomgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hard-palate catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers lakes, but also occurs in the main river channels. Enters floodplains occasionally. Occurs at temperatures ranging from 26 to 32°C. Mainly diurnal. Feeds on large crustaceans such as Macrobrachium, large insects and nymphs, fishes (usually Ophieleotris aporos), leeches, earthworms, plants and detritus.

species.name: Hardenberg's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal pelagic (Ref. 68964). A schooling species occurring in coastal waters. More data needed based on correct identifications. The record from the Godavari estuary implies tolerance of lowered salinities, but the identity of the material is uncertain (perhaps S. waitei). Appears to be fairly common throughout its range. Used as bait in the tuna fishery in the South Pacific, although rather fragile.

species.name: Hardenburg's burrfish
species.description: Found over soft bottoms to depths of 100 m, usually trawled.  Presumably solitary and feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates.  Not usually marketed.

species.name: Hardhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep, rock- and sand-bottomed pools of small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Hardhead halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in bays and waterways, especially around seagrass beds.

species.name: Hardhead snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently occurs over coarse bottom with hard patches, over-grown with sponges; with bottom temperature of 4.2°C (Ref. 57785).

species.name: Hardwicke's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Harelip cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species inhabiting shallow coastal waters (Ref. 34024).  Found on sandy bottom near reefs (Ref. 51183).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Harelip sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hareng
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sardinella rouxi is found in inshore waters and along beaches, forming schools (Ref. 188).

species.name: Hareng (Sardinops sagax)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic (Ref. 11230).  A coastal species that forms large schools (Ref. 188).  Occur at temperatures ranging from 16° to 23°C in summer and from 10° to 18°C in winter.  Feed mainly on planktonic crustaceans.  Young fish feed on zooplankton such as copepod and adults on phytoplankton (Ref. 39882).  Oviparous, with pelagic eggs, and pelagic larvae (Ref. 265).  Possibly can live up to 25 years (Ref. 265).  In the California region, pilchards make northward migrations early in summer and travel back south again in autumn.  With each year of life, the migration becomes farther (Ref. 6885).  Marketed fresh, frozen or canned.  Utilized mainly for fish meal; but also eaten fried and broiled (Ref. 9988).  Main source of landing:  NE Pacific:  Mexico (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Hareng araucian
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools at or near the surface in coastal waters.  Feeds on plankton, especially diatoms (filter-feeding).  Breeds mainly from June to November, from a length of about 10 cm.  Eggs and larvae are planktonic (Ref. 52017).  Mainly used for fishmeal.

species.name: Hareng de La Réunion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species occurring in coastal waters.  Caught with artisanal fishing gear (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Hareng du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 11230).  A coastal and schooling species (Ref. 188).  Landlocked populations exist.  Mature adults migrate inshore, entering estuaries to breed.  During the summer of their first year, young  form schools in shallow bays, inlets and channels that appear at the surface; these schools disappear in the fall and remain in deep water for the next 2-3 years (Ref. 6885, 27547).  Young feed mainly on crustaceans, but also take decapod and mollusk larvae; adults prey mainly on large crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 6885, 27547).  Because it does not undertake extensive coastal migrations, the mixing of local populations is relatively rare (Ref. 27547).  In the eastern Pacific, the fish is mainly caught for roe markets in Asia (Ref. 9988).  There is a fishery for eggs laid on kelp, which when salted, is called kazunoko-kombu, and is considered a delicacy in Japan (Ref. 27547).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked, canned, and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled, and baked (Ref. 9988).  Possibly to 475 m depth (Ref. 6793).

species.name: Hareng gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually an inshore schooling species, inhabiting relatively clear waters of coastal, lagoon, and seaward reefs (Ref. 11230).  Relative fecundity is 1596 eggs per unit body weight (Ref. 4383).  Caught with beach seines, purse seines, ringnets and dipnets.  Marketed fresh or dried-salted (Ref. 5213).  Used as bait in the tuna fishery.

species.name: Hareng rond
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic (Ref. 68964). Usually an inshore schooling species, inhabiting relatively clear coastal waters, lagoons, and along reef margins.  Feeds near surface on plankton.  Found in large schools (Ref. 9710).  Pelagic (Ref. 58302).  Marketed fresh or dried-salted (Ref. 5213) and used as tuna baitfish.

species.name: Hareng tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters (Ref. 188). Marketed fresh, dried and dried salted or made into fish balls.

species.name: Hareng à bande bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults form schools near mangroves, shallow coastal bays and lagoons during the day and moves further offshore into deeper water by night (Ref. 188, 48635); at depths of 0-13m (Ref. 58302, 82332). Known in mills around in large schools under wharves or along sandy beaches in protected bays (Ref. 26367). Pelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on zooplankton, mainly at night, chiefly copepods in juvenile stages, but larger prey as adults (chaetognaths, polychaetes, shrimps and small fishes) (Ref. 188). Breeds during its first year and probably survives only a few months after maturity (Ref. 188). Marketed fresh and dried salted (Ref. 188).  Usually parceled in leaves and baked in a motu oven. Do not recover quite as quickly as other species of baitfish after heavy fishing (Ref. 26367).

species.name: Harengule jagane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, over mud sand bottoms and frequently near brackish or hyper-saline estuaries (Ref. 5217).  Forms schools.  Marketed fresh or canned.

species.name: Harengule piquitinga
species.description: A coastal-pelagic species that forms dense schools in beaches, lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 9291).  Tolerates brackish and fresh waters (Ref. 9291).  Feeds on plankton, especially on small crustaceans and fish larvae (Ref. 9291).  Processed into oil and fishmeal (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Harengule piquitinge
species.description: Occurs inshore, over muddy bottoms and in brackish or hyper-saline littoral lagoons (Ref. 5217).  Forms schools.

species.name: Harengule écailleux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, tolerating low salinities.  Can tolerate a broad range of salinity levels (Ref. 26938).  Forms schools, small individuals often along sandy beaches.  Its flesh has an unpleasant odor.  Utilized as fishmeal (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Harengule écailleux (Harengula thrissina)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  Form dense schools along shores and estuarine areas with salinities slightly lower than that of saltwater (Ref. 9291).  Feed on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9291).
