Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35601).  Utilized as bait (at least in Mexico and Costa Rica) (Ref. 9291).

species.name: Harlequin bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common in areas with rock or scattered coral.  Solitary or in pairs.  Feeds mainly upon crustaceans (Ref. 5521).  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  The most common member of the genus (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Harlequin darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs of small to medium rivers, usually near debris (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge, blackfly, and caddisfly larvae, and mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Harlequin fish
species.description: Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on various small fish (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Harlequin ghost pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually settle along reef edges in current-prone areas (Ref. 48635).  Uncommon species found solitary or paired, among branches of gorgonians, floating weeds, or crinoids (Ref. 9710).  They feed mostly on mysids but also target small benthic shrimps (Ref. 48635).  Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch (Ref. 205).

species.name: Harlequin goldie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harlequin jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow protected coastal bays (Ref. 48637).  Rare species.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Harlequin prawn-goby
species.description: Found on open sand bottoms of clear water reefs (Ref. 9710).  Lives in association with alpheid shrimps.

species.name: Harlequin rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams (Ref. 13061).  Found in primary peat swamps in larger than 100 fish (Ref. 57235).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Eggs spawned at the underside of broad leaves and similar structures (Ref. 38434).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).  Previously known as "Rasbora" but revised as separated genus by Kottelat & Witte (1999) (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Harlequin rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Too small to be of high commercial value (Ref. 27437).

species.name: Harlequin sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species found in shallow estuaries and protected coastal bays to depths of about 25 m (Ref. 48636).  Inhabit sand bottoms solitarily (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 48636.

species.name: Harlequin sandsmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harlequin sharkminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harlequin smiler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over sand bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).  Eggs which are clumped together in a sticky egg ball inside the parent's mouth are sometimes released in a burrow during brief feeding periods (Ref. 40511).

species.name: Harlequin tuskfish
species.description: Poisson. Adults inhabit seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feed on mollusks, crustaceans, various worms, and echinoderms.  Solitary and territorial species (Ref. 9710).   Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Harlequin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A sequentially protogynous hermaphrodite.  In the Galapagos, the colorful appearance may be due to selective pressures and their increased feeding and decreased reproductive activities may serve to avoid extraordinary predation (Ref. 9227).  Adults forage on a wide range of invertebrates and algae (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Harlot pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected specimens came from patch reefs and coral slopes with diverse coral cover, except for the 3 specimens collected from a steep (45°) wall of large boulders with little algal or coral growth (Ref. 59340).

species.name: Harpadon erythraeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Harpadon microchir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harpadon mortenseni
species.description: Espèce de poisson.

species.name: Harpadon nudus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harpadon squamosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harpagifer andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harpagifer macquariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harpagifer marionensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041).

species.name: Harpagifer nybelini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Harris's flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken over sand and mud bottoms by trawling at depths from 8-64 m.  Young and juveniles frequently found in Darwin Harbor  (Ref. 9790).

species.name: Harrowed sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sand bottoms (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Hart's rivulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at the foot of waterfalls, in swamps, streams and ponds (Ref. 11225).  Eaten in its native range and exported for the ornamental trade (Ref. 4537).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Has been observed to hunt insects from overhanging vegetation by jumping out of the water; has also been observed to travel on land and feed on insects in wet weather (Ref. 43279).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hartel's dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported maximum depth at 1258 m (Ref. 120413).

species.name: Harttia absaberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality, ribeirão São Mateus,  is a small creek with sand bottom, clear water and about 1.0-2.0 m wide and 0.5 m deep. Also collected from rio Passa Cinco, a relatively large river about 5.0-10.0 m wide and 1.0-2.0 m deep, with fast flowing clear water  with sand in the bottom and stretches with rocks (Ref. 94714).

species.name: Harttia carvalhoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia depressa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia dissidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia duriventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia fluminensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequents main channel over rocky and sandy bottom in fast flowing waters (Ref. 90209).

species.name: Harttia fowleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known about this species except that it was taken from the rapids along with Metaloricaria paucidens (Ref. 35381). Its morphology is intermediate to that of Cteniloricaria maculata and Harttia surinamensis. The appearance of its abdominal plaque is retarded and its caudal fin's shape is similar to that of the other two species. As far as the body shape is concerned, it appears to be closer to H. surinamensis than to C. maculata, thus justifying its move to genus Harttia (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Harttia garavelloi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia guianensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia kronei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with rocky and sandy bottom; in shallow and deeper (up to 0.7 m) areas with water flow up to 70 cm per second.  Forages at night, although occasional diurnal activity is also recorded.  Grazes on microscopic algae, mostly diatoms and green algae growing on rugged and light-colored rocks, and submersed vegetation.  Chironomid and simuliid larvae, as well as tiny crustaceans, are recorded in its diet.  Before grazing on a patch with dense sediment, the fish makes wiggling head-down movements, which raise sediment and blown away by the water current.  When scraping algae off the substrate, the fish makes vigorous mouth movements and jerky movements, probably related to its mouth making alternate grazing and attaching to the substrate.  Density may reach about 0.1 fish per square meter both in shaded and sunned stream stretches (Ref. 26630).

species.name: Harttia leiopleura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia longipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia loricariformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia merevari
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia novalimensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia panara
species.description: Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 117418).

species.name: Harttia punctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the upper and middle courses of the rio Tocantins (Ref. 39753).

species.name: Harttia rhombocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia rondoni
species.description: Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 117418),

species.name: Harttia surinamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very abundant in zones of swiftly flowing plunging waters (Ref. 27188).  The adult male of this species has very well developed odontodes on the front edge of its pectoral fins (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Harttia torrenticola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia trombetensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia tuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia uatumensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttia villasboas
species.description: Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 117418).

species.name: Harttiella crassicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Was discovered in a little forest creek, with some cascades and with sandy and rocky bottom.  The males have odontodes developed on their pectoral fins (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Harttiella intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttiella janmoli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttiella longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain areas. Sympatric with Guyanancistrus aff. brevispinis, Krobia itanyi, Rhamdia quelen, Ancistrus cf. leucostictus, Lithoxus planquettei, Characidium fasciadorsale, Melanocharacidium cf. dispilomma, and Rineloricaria aff. stewarti in the Trinité Mountains (Ref. 90209).

species.name: Harttiella lucifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sympatric with Rivulus igneus and Ituglanis sp.

species.name: Harttiella parva
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Harttiella pilosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was encountered immediately upstream of a 30 m high waterfall and was collected downstream of the waterfall.  The area of the river where this species was found was 10 m wide with shallow clear water and a bottom substrate consisting of gravel, pebbles, boulders, bed rock and sand mainly constituted of iron hydroxide (Ref. 90209).

species.name: Hartzfeld's cardinalfish
species.description: Benthic and nocturnal species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Found in small groups among debris or corals of sheltered reef flats and shallow lagoons (Ref. 1602); also among massing long-spined urchins (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Hartzfeld's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, prefers open expanses of sand or mixed sand, rubble, and pavement usually below 11 m.  Occurs in loose groups of one male and numerous smaller females and juveniles.  Small groups of females and males moving over large areas by themselves, regularly checking females (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Haseman's toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hasemania crenuchoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hasemania hanseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hasemania kalunga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the margins of semilentic stretches of a shallow, clear water river, greatest depth of 1.20 m, width of 1.5 to 10 m, with sand and leaves on the bottom, with moderate submerged vegetation (mainly Poaceae and Cyperaceae) and a little riparian vegetation (shrubs).  Feeds largely on Formicidae, followed by Diptera, Chlorophyta, unidentified vegetal organic matter, and insects fragments in lesser amount (Ref. 83954).

species.name: Hasemania maxillaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hasemania nambiquara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along the margins of semilentic stretches of a shallow, clear water river, with sand and leaves on the bottom and a moderate amount of riparian vegetation (Ref. 75743).

species.name: Hasemania piatan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on larvae and adults of Trichoptera, adult of Diptera, fragments of unidentified arthropods, large amount of filamentous algae, and organic debris (Ref. 83965).

species.name: Hasemania uberaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from its type locality in the headwaters of the rio Uberaba. These headwaters are marshlands with abundant Cyperaceae, Poaceae and algae, crystalline water and muddy bottom. Collected together with a new genus and new species of Crenuchidae, the most abundant species (under analysis), Hyphessobrycon uaiso and Rivulus sp. Feeds on angiosperms, Chironomidae larvae (Diptera) and Trichopterans (Ref. 104909).

species.name: Hassar affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hassar gabiru
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Like its congeners, this species was usually collected in swift water over sand beaches at night. It has been considered that specimens of Hassar orestis(=Hassar gabiru) collected at the Volta Grande rapids have preference for benthic invertebrates and detritus (Ref. 87857).

species.name: Hassar orestis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hassar wilderi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hasselt's goby
species.description: Found in tide pools and lagoons.  Also occur in rubble, intertidal to a few meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Hasselt’s rainbow sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hatai's ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hatcheria macraei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4739).  No indication of diel migration (Ref. 4739).  Adult complement of photophores acquired at about 1.4 cm SL (Ref. 4739).

species.name: Hawaiian anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found around coral outcrops and escarpments (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Rare in less than 15 m.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Hawaiian bigeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs.  Found under ledges during the day (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Spawning may occur by December or soon after.  Sound production has been studied in this species (Ref. 5403).

species.name: Hawaiian bigeye dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian blackhead triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic in dead coral, rubble, or rock (Ref. 58302) and other habitats exposed to moderate surge (Ref. 54619).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hawaiian butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in the vicinity of steep slopes, solitary or in pairs and occasionally in small aggregations (Ref. 4858).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on a variety of planktonic and benthic organisms (Ref. 4858).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  High-priced aquarium export (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Hawaiian chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Collected from depths of 6 to 46 m.  Sexual maturity at about 12.7 cm.  Spawning period occur from February through May.  Diet consists mainly of calanoid and cyclopoid copepods, but tunicates, mysids, euphausiids, crustacean larvae, larval polychaetes, siphonophores, and fish eggs are also taken (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hawaiian chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic in shallow water, in the surge zone near coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian cleaner wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in most coral reef habitats except in the surge zone (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Obligate cleaner (Ref. 9710), picks parasitic crustaceans from other fishes.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Swims with a dancing-flitting motion.  It spends the night resting in a balloon-like mucous cocoon.

species.name: Hawaiian dascyllus
species.description: Adults are found in very shallow, protected water, over coral and rocky bottoms. Young often sheltering among the branches of Pocillopora; occasionally commensal with the anemone Marcanthia cookei (Ref. 9710). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Peak spawning from May to August. Age-at-maturity estimated at one year. Feed on zooplankton, benthic invertebrates, and algae (Ref. 9710). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35412).

species.name: Hawaiian deep anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over hard substrates with holes (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian flagtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length at maturity about 18 cm.  Taken with hook and line using bread or shrimp for bait (Ref. 44091).  A native Hawaiian fish found in both marine and freshwater habitats.  Feeds on fishes, invertebrates, and insects.  Sr/Ca profiles from otoliths of juvenile and adult fish from fresh and salt water indicated that use of stream habitats by this species is facultative (Ref. 51353).

species.name: Hawaiian garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, burrowing in sand (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Hawaiian gold-barred butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over rocks (Ref. 58302).Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hawaiian grenadier
species.description: Not normally taken by commercial fishers because of the absence of a deep-water trawl fishery where it occurs (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Hawaiian halosaurid fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between 530-2321 m, associated with islands and continental slopes (Ref. 58302).  Found at bathyal to abyssal depths.  Feeds on amphipods, mysids, copepods and polychaetes.  Sexually dimorphic, maturing males have enlarged nostrils, anterior nostrils are black and tubular.  Females outnumber males 4:1 in western North Atlantic.

species.name: Hawaiian Islands silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swim in small schools during the day close to the shoreline, disperse at night spreading over the reef.  Nocturnal feeders of plankton, mostly crustaceans and forams.  Preyed upon by larger species.

species.name: Hawaiian lionfish
species.description: Found under ledges in turbid lagoons and clear seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Collected in depths from near shore to about 50 meters (Ref. 10482).  Benthic in crevices and caves during day, or sometimes benthopelagic at night, at 1-134 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian longfin anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian morwong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species found in seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on a wide variety of small invertebrate animals such as crabs, shrimps and other crustaceans, polychaete worms, mollusks, heart urchins and foraminiferans (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Hawaiian mustache conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian orbicular velvetfish
species.description: Benthic and inquiline in the branches of Pocillopora meandrina (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian ruby cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water and observed to be active only at night, near the bottom, and never far from its shelter (Ref. 27665).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian sea-moth fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately deep water (Ref. 1418).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Larvae and juveniles are often collected in neuston and plankton nets, and midwater trawls (Ref. 1418).

species.name: Hawaiian softhead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hawaiian spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and rock, with soft corals at 275-515 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawaiian spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poisson.

species.name: Hawaiian squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs below the surge zone, common near caves and ledges (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans.

species.name: Hawaiian surf sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rough surf and waves around rocky headlands and reefs.  Nothing is known of the biology of this species (Ref. 9769).

species.name: Hawaiian turkeyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Generally hidden beneath ledges or caves during the day; a nocturnal feeder on crustaceans (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Hawaiian whitespotted toby
species.description: Commonly found on lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic over coral, rock, rubble, and sand at 1-89 m (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on sponges, algae, detritus, tunicates, polychaetes, bryozoans, sea urchins, brittle stars, crabs, peanut worms, shrimps, zoanthids, fishes, amphipods and foraminiferans (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Hawaiian wonder dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clean sand off beaches, burying just under the surface of the sand with the eyes exposed (Ref. 33412).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hawkfish anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near coral reefs (Ref. 7300).  Also occurs in small groups near caves, ledges and drop-offs (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Also a solitary species, sometimes in loose aggregations (Ref. 48635).  Secretive, swims upside-down (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Hawknose grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hayashi's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs; hides in small caves and under ledges. Solitary and usually seen at night (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hazar bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hazeus ammophilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-bottom habitats (Ref. 125639).

species.name: Hazeus maculipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hazeus profusus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-bottom habitats (Ref. 125639).

species.name: Head and tailspotted coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Solitary or in groups. Also found in sheltered lagoons and coastal reefs in 3-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Head-and-tail-light fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Head-spot moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Headband conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental shelf (Ref. 48635, 75154).  Generally known from trawl over muddy substrates (Ref. 48635).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Headlight angler
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Headlight fish
species.description: High-oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4066), found between 501-700 m during the day and between 40-175 m during the night, exhibiting size stratification with depth (Ref. 4479).  Probably spawns in deep water during spring (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Headspot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocks of corals reefs in the infralittoral zone (Ref. 559, 48637). Solitary or in groups, resting at bottom (Ref 90102). Spawning appears to be repeated on a regular cycle, semilunar or every 14 days (Ref. 116739).

species.name: Headstripe longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300) at depths of 12 m or less in dead coral, reef flats, and on coral heads, habitats with somewhat less wave energy (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Headwater catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky riffles, runs and pools of clear creeks and small rivers and also springs.  Greatly resembles a small channel catfish, however, body lacks spots and the caudal fin is not deeply forked, the base of the anal fin is longer than the head length (see Ref. 3221).

species.name: Headwater chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and undercut banks of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  Maximum length is presumably about  38 cm TL (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Headwater darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains its greatest abundance in small (1-2 m wide) to medium (3-5 m wide) upland gravel and cobble streams where it is found mainly in moderately-flowing to swift shallow riffles and runs (Ref. 47261).  Adults and juveniles are encountered in pools over gravel and bedrock but not as common there unless the pool is in or near a spring (Ref. 47261).

species.name: Headwater killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Headwater livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heald’s skate
species.description: Inhabits upper continental slope (Ref. 114953). Length of adolescent males between 38.0-50.6 cm TL, smallest juvenile 13.8 cm TL (Ref. 75649).

species.name: Heart pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs and collected from large coral rubble pieces lying on soft bottoms below the reef slope. Solitary and only single specimens were collected at any given time. Apparently exhibits a similar behaviour to T. meranyx which co-occurs with this species, and has a similar depth distribution (Ref. 102609).

species.name: Heart-finned goby
species.description: The species sampling site has a moderately swift current and rocky substratum. It appears to be rare compared to the sympatric Sicyopus zosterophorus and Stiphodon sp. (Ref. 127458).

species.name: Heavy lips fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in the littoral zone of the lakes and streams, while the adults inhabit the middle and lower water layers of the lakes. Individuals return from the lake to streams to spawn in June; parental fishes spawn several times from July to September every year. The males dig pits with their anal fin rays and lay the eggs in the pit. Threatened by habitat degradation, water pollution, over-exploitation and invasion of exotic species (most notably, Micropercops swinhonis) (Ref. 89909).

species.name: Heckel’s Orontes barbell
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hector's clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly amongst brown algae (Cystophora) in rock pools at the low tide level and subtidal areas. Sometimes found on seaweed exposed at low tide. Swims towards cover and positions itself like drifting algae (heads up tail down position, sculling with the pectoral fins) when disturbed.

species.name: Hedinichthys grummorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hedinichthys macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heemstra goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand and mud bottoms near coral reefs (Ref. 30573); generally solitary (Ref. 5213).  An invertebrate feeder (Ref. 41878).

species.name: Heemstras' frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heemstra’s lanternbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heinemann's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear forest brooks under forest cover (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Helcogramma alkamr
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in a wide array of habitats; clear and turbid water, between  0-20m depth, amongst coral rock and rubble with some sand, and in a high energy tidal environment amongst large boulders and coral heads (Ref. 75031).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma aquilum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found among rocky boulders and in surge channels to a depth of about 6 m (Ref. 9849).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma billi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on rock surfaces and under ledges; common at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 6211).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma cerasina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma ellioti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky boulders from depths of 2 to 5 m, common at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 6211).  They live in small groups, each comprising a male and several females (Ref. 48636) on rock surfaces and under ledges and  tidepools (Ref. 75031).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma ememes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma larvata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma maldivensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma microstigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma nesion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma rharhabe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma serendip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky bottoms (Ref. 75031).  Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma shinglensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on coral stones and weeds of intertidal zones (Ref. 94009).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogramma striatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear coastal reefs with moderate currents (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Usually in small groups on sponges or reef outcrops.  They feed on zooplankton (Ref. 48636).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 13227.

species.name: Helcogramma williamsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky shore areas with sand channels at depths of 1-3 m (Ref. 94457).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helcogrammoides antarcticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114) along exposed rocky coast (Ref. 49110).

species.name: Helcogrammoides chilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles feed  on copepods and shifts to diet of amphipods as adults (Ref. 94105).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Helen Reef pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a vertical wall covered with sponges, small hard corals, ascidians, huge sandy-floored cave (ca 20 m wide and 5 m high, floor at 27 m) with sea-fans and hydroids at entrance, with sand/rock/patch reef below cave, at 22-34 m depth (Ref. 80731).

species.name: Helen's goby
species.description: Specimens were collected in small crevices at the base of low volcanic rock cliffs with sand substrate (Ref. 95673).

species.name: Helen's klipfish

The stomachs of the specimens examined were more or less filled with mollusks, usually bivalves (Ref. 7432).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Migrates upstream when water levels begin to rise at the beginning of the flood season and moves downstream as water clears at the end of the flood season.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Heller's barracuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly nocturnal (Ref. 4887).

species.name: Helmet triplefin

Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. A typical inhabitant of black or clear waters, usually in forest streams with moderate to swift current flow over firm sand or gravel bottoms (Ref. 7462). Often swims on one side in undulating movements (Ref. 35381).  Feeds mainly on terrestrial insects, particularly ants (Ref. 7462).  Nocturnal (Ref. 6868).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deeper rocky areas and tree roots (Ref. 37771).  Species caught throughout the year.  Enters flooded forest during the months of high water (July-October).  Feeds on fish, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 9497).

species.name: Hemibagrus olyroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Kapuas Lakes Area in Kalimantan Barat, Indonesia, fishermen reported that this species occurs in the upper reaches of main rivers among wood debris and sunken trees and logs (Ref. 56749).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid rivers and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Hemibagrus sabanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to large rivers.  Feeds mainly on spiders, various insects and insect larvae (Ref. 6868).

Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing streams with turbid water and a substrate of mud and gravel at elevation.
Feeds mainly on arthropods (Ref. 93057).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on exogenous insects, aquatic insect larvae, shrimps and other crustaceans, as well as fishes.  In Cambodian Mekong, it moves into flooded forest to spawn and the young are first observed in August, with the adults returning to rivers in November and December.

species.name: Hemibagrus wyckii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in large rivers with fast flowing water over muddy substrate (Ref. 56749).  Appears to be restricted in the middle reaches of rivers (Ref. 40801).  Feeds on insects, prawns and fishes.  Sold fresh in the markets (Ref. 33813).

species.name: Hemibagrus wyckioides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large upland rivers.  Common in areas with rocky bottoms and irregular depths (Ref. 12693).  Apparently does not migrate but reproduces locally and enters the flooded forest during high water in July-October (Ref. 38441).  Feeds on insects, prawns, fish (Ref. 33813) and crabs (Ref. 38441).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Maximum weight reported for an individual caught in Mae Klong River, Thailand, reached 86 kg (J-F. Helias, pers.comm., 07/2002; see photo Hewyc_u0.jpg).

species.name: Hemibrycon divisorensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens were collected at the tributaries of río Tapiche which are about 2-3 m wide with crystalline water, 0.3-0.5 m deep, medium water current, sandy substrate, and with moderate amount of riparian vegetation.  This species has a typical aquasperm with a spherical to slightly ovoid nucleus , suggesting that the species is non-inseminating.  It was not possible to verify the presence of spermatozoa in the ovaries due to the lack of mature females.  Mature males possess bony hooks on rays of all fins, except the caudal fin; the presence of which may represent a secondary sexual character (Ref. 75799).

Occurs syntopically with <i>Bryconamericus emperador, <i>Astroblepus sp., <i>Pimelodella sp. and <i>Characidium sp.  Feeds on adult and larval insects, nematodes, isopods, and unidentified arthropod fragments.  The presence of  autochthonous and some allochthonous items in the guts suggests that this species is insectivorous with considerable plasticity in its diet (Ref. 98056).

species.name: Hemichromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in both forest and savannah biotopes (Ref. 5644); present in littoral riverine habitats and permanent floodplain lagoons with clear water. It feeds on shrimps, small fishes (Ref. 52307) and insects. The species controls large swaths of territory, even larger than those controlled by Hemichromis elongatus; breeding is similar to Hemichromis elongatus (Ref. 52307). A nesting substrate spawner which breeds in the early summer. Pair-bonding well defined (Ref. 52307). Used for tilapia control (Ref. 4537). Maximum TL was recorded at 26.5 cm.

species.name: Hemigrammus changae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow-flowing streams at "aguajales" (wetlands dominated by Mauritia flexuosa palms) which typically possess black water, a large amount of decayed organic matter, and are typically shallow. The type locality was a formerly a gold mining area that is in the process of recovery due to the implantation of a private conservation concession. This species is also recorded from oxbow lakes and, in Bolivia, from lakes and streams at the llanos (seasonally flooded savannahs). It is sympatric, and in some localities syntopic with Hemigrammus lunatus, but the latter species is more commonly found in floodplain lakes from white water rivers, a type of habitat where H. changae is apparently uncommon (Ref. 120197).
