Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus machadoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing, low-gradient streams and small rivers, with clear, sometimes slightly dark-stained waters and bottom composed mainly of sand and clay. Also found in clear water wetlands. In igarapé Barreiro and at some sites at the rio Guaporé, this species seemed to prefer its surrounding with abundant aquatic vegetation (Ref. 96864).

species.name: Hemigrammus mahnerti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reported to reach 8 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Hemigrammus matei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus megaceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus melanochrous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus micropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus mimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus neptunus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from black-water rivers, but may also occur elsewhere.

species.name: Hemigrammus newboldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus ora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamp near the water surface (Ref. 57781).

species.name: Hemigrammus orthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus parana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fish is abundant in backwater margins from 0.3 to 1.3 m depth where it occurs in association with Poaceae and macrophytes (Ceratophyllum sp., Egeria densa, Eichornia spp., Ludwigia sedorde and Salvinia species. Stomach contents of two specimens consist of Spirogyra species, Cladocera, sediments (sand) and unidentifiable organic matter (Ref. 74938).

species.name: Hemigrammus pretoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus rodwayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Particularly abundant in coastal creeks and floodplains where it is supported by a certain salinity level.  It is vulnerable to a trematode parasite which induces a characteristic cutaneous reaction.  Reproduction in captivity has been successful (Ref. 12225).  Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Hemigrammus rubrostriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus schmardae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reported to reach 5 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Hemigrammus silimoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is about 50 m wide and 1.7 to 2.0 m deep, with swift-running, crystal-clear waters and with bottom comprising of sand and rocks.  Reported to occur in areas of slack current near the river bank.  Gut contents include algae and other vegetal matter (Ref. 78749).

species.name: Hemigrammus skolioplatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus stictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).  Maximum length reported to reach 6 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Hemigrammus taphorni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemigrammus tocantinsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams, in semi-lentic and lotic shallow areas (up to 1 m deep) with riparian vegetation composed by trees and shrubs. This new species was collected syntopically with Aspidoras albater, Astyanax sp., Characidium stigmosum, Corumbataia veadeiros, and Trichomycterus sp. Five specimens (UFRGS 11300, 25.1-27.1 mm SL) with stomach contents mainly composed by Diptera (pupae) and allochthonous insects, but also found were autochthonous insects and digested vegetal matter in a lesser amount (Ref. 84462).

species.name: Hemigrammus tridens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).  Maximum length reported to reach 3.5 cm TL (Ref. 2059).

species.name: Hemigrammus ulreyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).  Maximum length reported to reach 5 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Hemigrammus vorderwinkleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reported to reach 4 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Hemigrammus yinyang
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in moderately large (2-6 m wide) streams, with clear water, carrying little suspended sediment.  Also collected from dark-colored waters or muddy, silt-laden waters (Ref. 82434).

species.name: Hemigymnus sexfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on coral reefs and adjacent habitats, on sand and coral rubble. The fish take a mouthful of sand and gravel from the substratum, where small fossorial prey are sorted out within the mouth and pharynx, and inorganic fragments are forcefully ejected from of the mouth. May also feed opportunistically on larger prey (crabs, echinoids, molluscs, ophiuroids, polychaetes) (Ref. 93095). Large breeding males in the Red Sea observed to exhibit h a reversal of the black-and-white barred color pattern of the body similar to H. fasciatus (Ref. 34222).

species.name: Hemileiocassis panjang
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon confluens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in riffles and rapids (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Hemimyzon ecdyonuroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a small river about 60 m wide, with a succession of rapids over rocks and deep pools over sandy bottom. Caught in rapids with a current velocity exceeding 1 m/s with other rheophilous fish (species of Garra, Annamia, Hemimyzon, Homaloptera, Schistura, and Nemacheilus (Ref. 42935).

species.name: Hemimyzon formosanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon khonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon macroptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Hemimyzon megalopseos
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Hemimyzon nanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected in riffles, about 5-10 m wide, on waters less than 20 cm deep; bottom with algal growth (Ref. 30340).

species.name: Hemimyzon papilio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapids and fast flowing water, under large stones (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Hemimyzon pengi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids and fast flowing water, under large stones (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Hemimyzon pumilicorpora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon sheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon songamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon taitungensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon yaotanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemimyzon yushanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heminodus philippinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep benthic species of limited commercial value inhabiting warm tropical seas along continental shelf edge and slope.  Bony scutes reduce commercial value (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Heminoemacheilus hyalinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heminoemacheilus zhengbaoshani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemiodontichthys acipenserinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sandy bottom where it feeds on worms and micro-crustaceans.  Mature males develop a huge labial veil and teeth with spoon-shaped crow (versus pointed ones in females and juveniles).  Unlike most Loricariidae, they don't have well developed odontodes on the snout and pectoral fins.  During reproduction, the males bear a cluster of eggs fixed to their lips, which they provide with ventilation during movement.  About one week after hatching, the alevins leave their parent's protection (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Hemiodus amazonum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus atranalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus goeldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus huraulti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapidly flowing waters where other members of the Hemiodidae are also found (Ref. 12225).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus iratapuru
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemiodus jatuarana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemiodus langeanii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow-flowing stretches of the rio Amana and igarapé Porquinho (1.0-2.5 m deep) and in artificial ponds (4.0-5.0 m deep and 40-70 m in diameter) resulting from gold-mining activities.  The Rio Amana and its tributaries are characterized by clear water (not stained by humic acids) but turbid due to excess of fine suspended solids (clay) as a result of mining activities along river margins and/or bottom such as dredging (Ref. 91067).

species.name: Hemiodus microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Iteroparous synchronous spawner (Ref. 51777).

species.name: Hemiodus orthonops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus parnaguae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus sterni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus ternetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Iteroparous synchronous spawner (Ref. 51777).

species.name: Hemiodus thayeria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemiodus unimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast-flowing rivers over rocky substrate.  Abundant in the lower part of rivers.  Feeds on detritus and periphyton.  Mature at about 11 cm; breeds during the rainy season (Ref. 12225). Iteroparous synchronous spawner (Ref. 51777).

species.name: Hemiodus vorderwinkleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hemipsilichthys gobio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers, with clear water, moderate to strong current, and a substrate of rocks, loose stones and gravel (Ref. 57859).

species.name: Hemipsilichthys nimius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens were collected in small coastal streams flowing through well-preserved Atlantic forest; in localities between 100 and 370 m a.s.l., always in rocky substrate with fast flowing, clear water, under direct sunlight, and depths between 10 and 50 cm.  Underwater observations indicate that this species is most active during the night, grazing on the bottom (Ref. 57859).

species.name: Hemipsilichthys papillatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a small, shallow stream, with clear water and moderate to strong current.  Bottom formed by rocks, loose stones and gravel.  Forest and grass usually present on the margins (Ref. 45132).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon byssus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits streams of lowland forest and peat swamps. In streams with clear water, the body is lighter in color while in tannin stained waters, the body tends to be darker colored, at times appearing black (Ref. 94086).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon chrysopunctatus
species.description: Females bear live young (Ref. 58777).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon kapuasensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Females bear live young (Ref. 58777).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon kecil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with submerged bank vegetation and clear water of pH 7.0 flowing over rocky, sand and silt substratum. Tends to form school in small groups of about 3 to 5 individuals at the surface, preferring quiet pools and dwelling near or under overhanging bank vegetation. Syntopic with Osteochilus vittatus, Rasbora elegans, Systomus binotatus (Cyprinidae), Betta patoti, Trichopodus trichopterus (Osphronemidae), and Channa lucius (Channidae).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon kuekenthali
species.description: Females bear live young (Ref. 58777).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon phaiosoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rivers.  Females bear live young (Ref. 58777).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon pogonognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in peats and lowland forest streams (Ref. 57235).  In fresh and brackish water.  Females bear live young (Ref. 58777).  Uncommon aquarium species (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Hemirhamphodon sesamum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemirhamphodon tengah
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemisalanx brachyrostralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemisilurus heterorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Stomach contents consist of small fish and prawns (Ref. 56749).  Processed as smoked fish (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Hemisilurus mekongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large upland rivers (Ref. 12693) and enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Found in rapids and in deep slow reaches (Ref. 37771).  Feeds on worms, plants, animal debris and insects.  Sold fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Hemisilurus moolenburghi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hemitaeniochromis brachyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The distinctive lower-jaw teeth, with their outwardly and anteriorly angled crowns are similar to those of other haplochromine cichlids that have a paedophagous diet (Ref. 91204). The conservation status is unknown; it may normally inhabit deeper water than has generally been sampled over rocky substrates; and the widely separated localities of the two type specimens at least demonstrate that the species is not restricted to a single circumscribed area (Ref. 91204).

species.name: Hemitaeniochromis urotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups over shallow sandy substrates (Ref. 267).  Hunts in pairs or in large groups (Ref. 3817).

species.name: Hemitriakis complicofasciata
species.description: Claspers of most males are almost fully elongate and calcified at about 76 cm TL; while females are mature and pregnant at about 76 cm TL.  Embryos less than 22 cm TL with only external yolk, most that are more than 22 cm TL with substantial internal yolk.  Litter size from 5-8 with 2-4 embryos per uterus.  Five pregnant specimens contained a total of 29 embryos (9 females and 20 males) and each embryo were covered separately by embryonic membrane (Ref. 55581).

species.name: Hemitripterus villosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Henderson triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky shores (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Henochilus wheatlandii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on plants (Ref. 598).

species.name: Henonemus intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Henonemus macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Henonemus punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Henonemus taxistigmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Henonemus triacanthopomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hepburn's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the intertidal zone, where they hide beneath rocks (Ref. 637 and 559).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hephaestus komaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hephaestus obtusifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in high altitude (200-400 m elevation) fast-flowing mountain streams with gravel or rock substrates.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hephaestus tulliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found abundantly in faster flowing sections of rivers, including riffles, over gravel, cobble and rocky bottoms.  Sexual maturity is reached at about 13 m for males.  Spawning occurs from July to October.  Feed on a variety of macroinvertebrates, including crustaceans, aquatic and terrestrial insects, and algae (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hephthocara crassiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Hephthocara simum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Hepsetus occidentalis
species.description: The capture, in the Senegal River, of an individual measuring 510 mm SL has been mentioned, but not confirmed; the collections of the Museum of natural History in Paris include a head that is said to belong to a specimen collected in the Cavally River measuring 700 mm TL and wighing 4.000 g (Ref. 2914, 81278).

species.name: Heptapterus carnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus exilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus mandimbusu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the type locality, this species occurs in stream with clear water, current velocity, and structure consisting of sequences of pools of 1 to 1.5 meters and shallow riffles, surrounded by native vegetation (Ref. 116411).

species.name: Heptapterus mbya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus multiradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus mustelinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus ornaticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus qenqo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits well-oxygenated rivers and streams, with gravel substratum and moderate to rapid flowing waters. Individuals usually shelter under large rocks.  Apparently solitary and only a few specimens are usually captured per collecting site (Ref. 86258).

species.name: Heptapterus stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heptapterus sympterygium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herichthys molango
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Laguna Azteca, characterized by a depth of 16 m, transparency of 1-3 m, surface temperatures of 16-27°C, and surface pH of 7-8. Does not occur sympatrically with other native cichlids. Feeds mainly on filamentous algae. Threatened by the introduction of tilapia and centrachids (Micropterus salmoides and Lepomis spp.) (Ref. 94458).

species.name: Herichthys pame
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water over a rocky substrate with hardness above 100° dH and pH between 7.8 and 8.3. Sampled together with Herichthys tamasopoensis, H. steindachneri, Xiphophorus montezumae, and Gambusia panuco, among other species of fishes. Based on three specimens examined, stomach contents include detritus (5%), filamentous algae (20%), snails (70%), and unidentified materials (5%) (Ref. 94458).

species.name: Herichthys pratinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is syntopic in the lower courses of the Rio el Salto with H. cf. carpintis, Astyanax mexicanus, Xiphohorus nezahualcoyotl, and Poecilia mexicana along with other species of fishes in higher reaches (Ref. 94458).

species.name: Herichthys tepehua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herichthys teporatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herklotsichthys ovalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heroina isonycterina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in headwaters of major river drainages.

species.name: Heros liberifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is adapted to lentic environment with flooded forest habitats as the typical biotopes. It has no narrow habitat requirement as it is observed not only in clearwater and extreme blackwater habitats, but also in whitewater habitats.  It can thrive in a wide range of physico-chemical environmental conditions (pH 4.1-6.1;  conductivity 4-15 μS/cm).   It spawns in the flooded riparian forest during the flood season. At the start of the dry season, it leaves the riparian forests, which mostly dry up, and spends the low-water season among submerged logs, trunks and branches. During the low-water season, it usually seeks shelter in the crevices and gaps found between the boulders (Ref. 114589).

species.name: Heros notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heros spurius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herre's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herre's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs and rocky shores in 0-12 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Herre’s pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with dip-net or in surface plankton samples. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also found among Xenia soft coral in 1-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Herring cale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near the surface in high energy surf zones along rocky shores, these areas are often dominated by brown macroalgae.

species.name: Herwig lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic; occurs in the upper 100 m at night.

species.name: Herzenstein's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herzenstein's rough sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant at depths beyond 60 m (Ref. 2058). Iinhabits muddy bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Herzensteinia microcephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Herzog's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear and flowing brooks in the mountainous rainforest of the inland plain (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish. Bottom spawner, 1 month incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hessfeld's toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hetereleotris bipunctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hetereleotris diademata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hetereleotris dorsovittata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A single specimen was collected in the large inner lagoon of main island (Farasan Archipelago), at the base of an isolated small coral patch, at 1m depth (Ref. 116594)..

species.name: Hetereleotris exilis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The holotype, a mature female with numerous developed eggs in the ovary, was dredged at
53 m depth.  No habitat information is known (Ref. 84003).

species.name: Hetereleotris kenyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hetereleotris nebulofasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hetereleotris poecila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Hetereleotris psammophila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed on sand bottom close to coral reefs and found to be active at night.  It was also observed in Naama Bay, Gulf of Aqaba at depth of 8 m.  When disturbed, it quickly retreated, but not trying to hide or burrow in the sand (Ref. 94944).

species.name: Hetereleotris readerae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in rocky areas with some coral (Ref. 57078).

species.name: Hetereleotris vulgaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteristius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.

species.name: Heterobranchus boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diet of adults consists of fishes. Juveniles feed on insect larvae and other invertebrates (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Heterobranchus isopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. size in West Africa reported as 510 mm TL (Ref. 57129).

species.name: Heterocharax leptogrammus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heterocharax macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heterocharax virgulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heterocheirodon jacuiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lentic waters over sandy bottom environments.

species.name: Heterocheirodon yatai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heterochromis multidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Old males can exhibit a remarkable head profile with a well-developed hump; probably a biparental substrate spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Heteroclinus kuiteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with rocks and algae in shallow water (Ref. 76776).

species.name: Heteroconger balteatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows tail-first into the sand; feed on zooplankton, in regions of current (Ref. 33408).

species.name: Heteroconger camelopardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteroconger chapmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteroconger congroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from larvae.

species.name: Heteroconger tomberua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Heterogobius chiloensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteromormyrus longilateralis
species.description: Found along well-vegetated and steep banks of the river; they therefore possibly prefer undercut banks with structure such as roots (Ref. 85059).

species.name: Heteromormyrus pauciradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteromycteris matsubarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Heteroplopomus barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms.

species.name: Heteropneustes kemratensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Heteropneustes longipectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Heteropneustes microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur mainly in swamps and similar still, often turbid waters (e.g. irrigation ditches). Form loose schools of about ten individuals of approximately the same size. Enter brackish water. Can survive temperatures up to 39.8°C (Ref. 7256). An omnivore with nocturnal feeding habits. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205). Very easily maintained in captivity. Sympatric with H. fossilis which is more abundant in the type locality. Best method of catch is dewatering of small water holes during drought period.

species.name: Heteropneustes nani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in ponds, ditches, canals, flooded rice fields, swamps, marshes, waterlogged areas and rivers. Its air-breathing apparatus enables it to survive in low water depth, even in turbid and oxygen deficit conditions. During the winter season the fish can live in semi-liquid mud and when the mud dries up they burrow to the bottom of fissures and crevices formed by the cracking mud. Recorded physicochemical parameters during the study period are the following: water temperature 18-28°C; pH 6.5-7.5; dissolved oxygen 4.5-5.0 mg/l; water transparency 45-60 cm at 1.0-1.8 m depth.  This fish is able to deliver a stinging protein (known as poison) emanated from the venom glands around the pectoral spine, and is reported to be neurotoxic and hemolytic (i.e. destruction of red blood cells) in humans, causing local numbness, inflammation and severe painful physical conditions on the affected limb (warm water bath, application of lukewarm turmeric paste, ejection of blood, and traditional herbal medicine are commonly used for healing).  Still, its flesh is of good table quality and nutritional value. rich in iron and low fat, and a valuable source of protein (Ref. 94657).

species.name: Heterotilapia cessiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Hexagramme de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky inshore areas, common on kelp beds, also on sand bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on crustaceans, polychaete worms, brittle stars, mollusks, and small fishes (Ref. 28499).  Young are food of steelheads and salmon (Ref. 6885).  Frequently caught by shore and skiff fishers and speared by divers (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Hexanematichthys henni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hiatt's basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic and rarely seen (Ref. 90102).  Adults are found in shallow wave-washed seaward reefs; also in sheltered rubble reef slopes to at least 20 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hiatt's longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive in sheltered reefs to about 20 m depth (Ref. 48635); a few species collected from reef crevices in 8-34 m (Ref 90102).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hick's toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters.

species.name: Hidden basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef crests and lagoons (Ref. 48635); also near coral heads (Ref. 1602). Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hidden bristlemouth
species.description: Bathy- to abyssopelagic (Ref. 58302).  No apparent vertical migration has been observed (Ref. 4463).

species.name: Hidden ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 45255).  More data needed.

species.name: Hiddenbulb dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi- and mesopelagic with most captures above 225 m fishing depths (Ref. 58302).

species.name: High cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in intertidal areas under rocks (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Green algae is an important food item but may also feed on polychaete worms, crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 6885).  Breathes air (Ref. 31184) and can remain out of water for 15-25 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).

species.name: High-finned dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on trawling grounds, often found on sand or rubble bottoms.

species.name: High-finned glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not very well known, except for specimens collected in 1920.

species.name: High-hat Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in various reef habitats, but often on sponges or reef outcrops (Ref. 48636). Also found in intertidal pools (Ref. 13227) and on corals and rocks (Ref. 37816). They feed on zooplankton (Ref. 48636). Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240). Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114). The most common and most widely distributed among Enneapterygius species (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth reported from Ref. 13227.

species.name: Highback chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Highbrow rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Highcrest triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from inshore continental waters (Ref. 12476).  Adults inhabit bays and sheltered lagoons, close to reef base, on a silty sand or mud substrate, often on stones and dead corals of the same color.  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  This is the  first tripterygiid that has been described from the Red Sea (Ref. 88983).

species.name: Highfin bigeye dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep trawling grounds (Ref. 3132). Found in shelf edges (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Highfin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Highfin cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Highfin carpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 3814, 10294).

species.name: Highfin catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and smaller streams, frequently in slow-flowing, turbid conditions (Ref. 5259, 44894),  and also in lakes and lagoons (Ref.  2847).  Sometimes found in brackish estuaries (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on aquatic plants, benthic crustaceans, insect larvae, bottom detritus (Ref. 5259)  and also fishes (Ref.  2847).

species.name: Highfin deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Highfin dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Highfin dragonfish
species.description: Feed on small crustaceans (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35904).

species.name: Highfin glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds, ditches and pools.  Enters brackish waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Highfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on shallow mud or mud-sand bottoms in turbid and generally brackish water near estuaries (Ref. 13628).  Also encountered in weedy backwaters (Ref. 7251) and hyper-saline waters (Ref. 13628) with salinity ranging from 0.15 to 37.2 ppt (Ref. 97140).

species.name: Highfin lizardfish
species.description: Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Found on the continental rise and the abyss, commonly below 2,000 m, in water colder than 4°C.  Larvae are probably pelagic in near-surface midwaters.  Solitary, lurking bottom feeder.  Probably piscivore (Ref. 4964).

species.name: Highfin moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow reefs, including tidepools (Ref 90102); in turbid waters with muddy substrates (B. Haze, pers.comm., 11/2023).

species.name: Highfin parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Highfin red banner blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral and rocky coral reefs and even on harbor pilings, but not in high-energy zones. Males occupied barnacle shells and worm holes, empty cirripede shells placed among dead Millepora, while females were on the hard surface, in crevices and on corals, especially Montastrea annularis. Apparently this species avoids high-energy areas, going deep when necessary (Ref. 125603).

species.name: Highfin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Have a thick glandular tissue on posterior margin of fin spines which is believed to be venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Highfin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools, sometimes runs, of sandy and rocky creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Highfin shrimpgoby
species.description: The species has been reported to occur from seagrass beds with sandy-mud bottoms (Ref. 119508).

species.name: Highfin slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental edges (Ref. 13707); benthic on sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Highfin velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Highland darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Highland Rim Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Highland shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Highland splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and ponds.

species.name: Highland stoneroller
species.description: Inhabits rocky riffles, runs and sometimes pools of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Highland swordtail
species.description: Inhabits fast-flowing waters in sandy bottoms with rocks and dense plant growth.

species.name: Highlands long-finned eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably caught locally, but no separate statistics available (Ref. 9828).

species.name: Highlands rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in hilly or mountainous terrain between about 200 and 1525 m elevation.

species.name: Highlight hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 4739).  Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Does not exhibits vertical migration (Ref. 4462).  Feeds on copepods, ostracods, euphausiids, amphipods, decapods (Ref. 4739).  Photophores develop in adults over 16-18 mm SL (Ref. 4739). Minimum depth from Ref. 004054.

species.name: Highscale shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs and pools of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Highseas lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic species; found in the upper 24 m at night (Ref. 4066) and 532-1000 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Highsnout melamphid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In the sub-arctic region, young may be found at depths between 50-300 m while older individuals occur at depths between 200-500 m (Ref. 6885).  Further south, in the transition zone, young are found from 200-300 m and older individuals between 200-500 m (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae and eggs (Ref. 36655).

species.name: Higuchi’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hilda's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast-flowing water over rocks with water ferns (Ref. 52193). Possibly an occasional subsistence catch (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Hildebrandt's elephant-snout fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hilde’s darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hillstream loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hillstream spineless eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas of the stream where water is moving very slow.  Spends most of its time lying at the bottom, either buried in mud or clinging to some submerged vegetation along the edges of the streams.

species.name: Hilomen's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a sheltered habitat of mixed coral, algae, sand and gravel (Ref. 85096).  Found in small groups or solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Himalayan glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds, ditches, pools and rivers (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Himantolophus albinares
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Himantolophus azurlucens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males and larvae unknown (Ref. 43997).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Himantolophus brevirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Himantolophus compressus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only two female specimens (Ref. 7406).

species.name: Himantolophus cornifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males unknown (Ref. 40877).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.  Most recent record was from 29°25'S that was recovered from the stomach of a beached sperm whale (Ref. 85522).

species.name: Himantolophus crinitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens taken in bottom trawls at 600-610 m (Ref. 86949).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimen collected at depth of approximately 350 m (Ref. 86949).
