species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in bottom trawls (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Himantolophus mauli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in bottom trawls and open pelagic nets in 400-750 m (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Himantolophus melanolophus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Himantolophus multifurcatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males unknown (Ref. 57659).

species.name: Himantolophus nigricornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Himantolophus paucifilosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens caught in bottom trawls at depths of 600 to 1540 m (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Himantolophus pseudalbinares
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens caught in bottom trawls (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Himantolophus rostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Himantolophus stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Himantura leoparda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly inshore and coastal, but on the continental shelf to depths of at least 70 m.  Birth size is about 20 cm DW (Ref. 76961).

species.name: Himantura pareh
species.description: Environment needs verification.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Hime diactithrix
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft-bottom grounds (Ref. 75183).

species.name: Hime formosana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hime microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hinano’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly from shallow reefs. At Moorea, collected almost exclusively from patches of rubble around shallow lagoon reefs.  Also found in tidepools and adjacent coral reef; rocky shore with porous volcanic rock and large table corals in water beneath rocks (Ref. 94084).

species.name: Hinano’s perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected (with hand nets) and have been observed in highly complex habitats on walls and ledges within mesophotic ecosystems, suggesting that the species does not inhabit shallow coral reefs (Ref. 122130).

species.name: Hinds' dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms.

species.name: Hinomaru perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is only known from Izu Ocean Park, where it has been collected and photographed on rocky reefs at depths of 48-60 meters (Ref. 117635)

species.name: Hintonia candens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066).  Juveniles found in the upper 100 m (night), adults mainly below about 200 m (night).

species.name: Hippichthys albomaculosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hippocampe d'estuaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit seagrass and marine algae areas of estuaries and seaward reefs; also on steep mud slopes. Found in open water and attached to drifting Sargassum up to 20 km from shore. Adults in pairs (Ref. 48635). Benthic to pelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 85309). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Not shown to be monogamous in the laboratory (Ref. 30915). Very popular aquarium fish. Highly valued species in traditional Chinese medicine (Ref. 30915). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35416).

species.name: Hippocampe flúte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow sandy or mixed sand, rubble, or coral areas of reef flats and lagoons, also sometimes on seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 6.5-7.0 cm SL. Usually in pairs or may form small aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hippocampe géant Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal.  Occur in offshore waters, mostly captured by dredging at 10 m or deeper.  Occasionally caught at surface.  Are often camouflaged within the branches of gorgonians and black coral trees where they are seen to curl their tail around the branches (Ref. 5227).  Have been found in the stomachs of Pacific yellowfin tuna and bluefin tuna (Ref. 30915).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hippocampe hérissé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare inhabitant of shallow sheltered reefs, found among clumps of algae or in seagrass beds.  Large adult pelagic and probably associated with drifting debris.  Associated with sponges and sea-squirts (Ref. 30915, 58302).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Feeds on zooplanktons and small crustaceans (Ref. 89972). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Use in traditional Chinese medicine is increasing with the rise in patent medicines (Ref. 30915).  Not common in the aquarium trade (Ref. 30915).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Hippocampe rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally in coastal waters; often around man-made structures (Ref. 26938). Usually attached to gorgonians or seagrasses but may occur in floating Sargassum or swimming freely in midwater (Ref. 9710). Those that live in Sargassum usually have bony protuberances and fleshy tabs that may serve as camouflage. Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420, 35422). Move into deeper waters during winter (Ref. 36630). Feeds by sucking in small organisms, using its long face as a pipette (Ref. 26938); like small crustaceans (Ref. 27549). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Length type refers to Height (= from top of coronet to the tip of straightened tail).

species.name: Hippocampe épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass beds at depths of more than 6 meters (Ref. 75989).

species.name: Hippocampus tyro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coarse calcareous sand and coral (82040).

species.name: Hippoglossina montemaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hippoglossina mystacium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hippopotamyrus castor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hippopotamyrus paugyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hippopotamyrus pictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hircan crested loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality of this species, Zarrin-Gol stream, is about 2 m wide, with substrate consisting of coarse gravel and boulders, fast-flowing and semi-transparent waters without submerged vegetations (Ref. 103421).

species.name: Hirondelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are moderately common in shallow water in areas of surge.  Found in clear waters (Ref. 27584), over sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 27000, 57392).  Occasionally enters lagoons and river estuaries (Ref. 57392).  Form schools (Ref. 27584, 57392).  Small specimens are regularly caught at night from steep rocky shores.  Adults feed on small crustaceans, mollusks and fishes (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Hirtella carinata
species.description: Inhabits small rivers and creeks.  Collected at elevation from 200 to 796 m above sea level, in small headwater streams emptying into the lower portion of the Rio Pardo drainage.  Found in clear water stretches of moderate to rapid water current, 1.0-5.0 meters wide, a few centimeters to one meter deep, and with bottoms of rocks, pebbles, organic debris, and usually small amounts of sand.  Captured within, or near, the Serra Bonita Reserve Complex, a Private Natural Heritage Reserve  (R.P.P.N.), which consists of a consortium of privately owned properties, approximately 7,500 hectares and represents one of the last remnants of moist submontane forest in the region.  The area around the reserve is composed of approximately 50% primary forest and the rest is a mosaic of forests in advanced stages of recovery mixed with cabruca (cocoa trees planted under natural forest canopy) and small areas of pasture. This apparently indicates that this species inhabits streams in pristine or good condition.  Occurs syntopically with other fish species including some unidentified or possibly undescribed species of <i>Astyanax, <i>Characidium, <i>Geophagus, <i>Hypostomus, and <i>Trichomycterus (Ref. 97864).

species.name: Hirundichthys ilma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hirundichthys indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in surface waters over the depths 390-7219 m, usually 2000-6000 m (mean 4129 m) (Ref. 93339). Juveniles of this species under 10.0 cm SL were caught in all seasons, indicating a year-round spawning of this species, with a highly pronounced peak in the summer and autumn months. Mature fishes appear at 16.0 cm SL or more (Ref. 93339).

species.name: Hirundichthys socotranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus acuen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat areas in creeks of headwaters of the rio Xingu basin in places of shallow clear waters with low current.  Found associated with vegetation that covers the bottom and the border of the headwaters (Ref. 106073).

species.name: Hisonotus aky
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus alberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in tributaries, and is associated with marginal vegetation.  The largest specimen observed is 3.41 cm, standard length (Ref. 128921).

species.name: Hisonotus armatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow to moderate flowing watercourses, with clear to brown water over sandy bottom and in marginal or submerged aquatic vegetation. Sympatric with Hisonotus laevior throughout its distribution (Ref. 78747).

species.name: Hisonotus bocaiuva
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus bockmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus brunneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus carreiro
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus charrua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus chromodontus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in flat areas in creeks of headwaters of Rio Tapajós in places of shallow clear waters with low current and sandy substrate. The holotype of this species was encountered in a creek severely altered by human activities; alongside a trail with very shallow water, the margin deprived of vegetation at the opposite side of swampy area, where vegetation was mainly represented by Tipha and Grammineae (Ref. 75061).

species.name: Hisonotus depressicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus depressinotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus devidei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, clear and swift-flowing water, 50-100 cm deep composed of rocks, sand and macrophytes substrates. This species is relatively abundant at the sampled locality (Ref. 128922).

species.name: Hisonotus dinizae
species.description: Found in small shallow streams with clear and swfit-flowing water, ca. 0.5-2 m depth with marginal vegetation (Ref. 128923).

species.name: Hisonotus francirochai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus heterogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus hungy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stream with two different environment, one which has the natural vegetation of the region and the other one which has introduced coniferous trees.  This fish occurs in the portion of the stream where a plantation of small coniferous trees exposes the brook completely to sunlight (Ref. 72404).

species.name: Hisonotus iota
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus laevior
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow to median flowing watercourses, with clear to brown waters running over a sandy bottom and occurs in marginal or submerged aquatic vegetation (Ref. 86691).

species.name: Hisonotus leucofrenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus leucophrys
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits median to fast flowing watercourses of clear water, with stones and sand on the bottom, and are found in aquatic, partially submersed, vegetation islands composed by grass (Ref. 80996).

species.name: Hisonotus maculipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus megaloplax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus montanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hisonotus montanus is found at high altitudes, about 850 m above the sea level, and represents the species of Hisonotus occurring in the most elevated portions of the rio Uruguai basin (Ref. 80996).

species.name: Hisonotus nigricauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus notopagos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus pachysarkos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in rivers with marginal or submerged vegetation (Ref. 128933).

species.name: Hisonotus paulinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus prata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus ringueleti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in between aquatic plants (species of Ludwigia and Potamogeton) and on leaves of terrestrial plants hanging into the water (Ref. 75967). Occurs in a small, shallow creek with muddy soil and clear, slow-flowing water and also in creek with regions of rapid and slow flowing water, with loose stones, and gravel at the bottom and with dense vegetation in the margins (Ref. 75967).

species.name: Hisonotus taimensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus thayeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hisonotus vespuccii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with marginal vegetation in the rio São Francisco and in three of its tributaries, rio das Velhas, rio Paraopeba and rio Formoso; seems to be abundant through all rio São Francisco basin (Ref. 114934).

species.name: Hisonotus vireo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hispaniola molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams over shallow riffles.

species.name: Hispaniola pupfish
species.description: Inhabits saline lakes (Ref. 13498).  6.6 cm max SL (Ref. 13498).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hispaniolan gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in springs entering large brackish and salt water lakes.

species.name: Hispaniolan rivulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits headwater streams. Associates with Poecilia and Limia species in small, sand-bottomed creeks with fast currents (Ref. 13498). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hispidoberyx ambagiosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from five specimens (Ref. 51652).  Probably benthopelagic (Ref. 51652).  Feeds on shrimps (Ref. 51652).

species.name: Histiobranchus australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Histiodraco velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the sublittoral and continental shelf.  Biology unknown.

species.name: Histiophryne pogonia
species.description: This species appears to occur within reef habitat and may be more active at night. Two procured specimens were observed to live peacefully together in an aquarium for many months (suggesting that Histiophryne may not be cannibalistic or as aggressive as Antennarius and Histrio) (Ref. 89955).

species.name: Hitch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, ponds, sloughs, backwaters and sluggish sandy pools of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Hittitic spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hiva basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected over rocky substrata, usually at depths greater than 25 m; with the use of rotenone and quinaldine (Ref. 48242). Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 89972).  FishBase common name agreed by authors.

species.name: Ho's sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hoedeman's Hypopygus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hoedt's waryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 7300, 75154) and epipelagic, associated with island slopes (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hoese's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tidepools and rock and coral reefs in lagoons and reef slopes (Ref. 59013).

species.name: Hoese's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel or mud bottoms of the lakes and small nearby tributaries.

species.name: Hoese's mudbrotula
species.description: Occurs along rocky shores at shallow depths.  A female specimen (AMS 15330-037, 42 mm SL), contained 3 embryos, 11-16 mm SL.  The species is pale except for some weak pigmentation on top of head (Ref. 57886).

species.name: Hoese's sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from silty sand near large rocks.

species.name: Hoese's silhouette goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms, close to shore.

species.name: Hoeven's snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water and lagoons (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Hofmann's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hofrichter's clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species inhabits intertidal pebble beaches and probably shows passive emergence behaviour. It occurs in sympatry with G. orientalis throughout its distribution and on the island Corfu with G. adriatica (Ref. 123696).

species.name: Hokkaido skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 12.0 cm long and 9.0 cm wide (Ref. 41253).

species.name: Holanthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holanthias caudalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky regions, 50 to 100 m deep (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Holbiche arabique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype which was found on the continental slope of the Arabian Sea.

species.name: Holbiche artouca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slopes (Ref. 244).  Poorly known (Ref. 244).  Probably caught with bottom trawls (Ref. 30573).  Maximum length reported refers to an immature specimen (Ref. 244). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fairly common on the upper continental slopes, usually over mud or other soft sea bottom (Ref. 9996).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore to offshore shark found on the continental shelf.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Dental sexual dimorphism exists, with adult males having teeth at least twice as high as adult females as well as much longer and narrower mouths.

species.name: Holbiche bouffie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fairly deep water on or near the bottom on the outer continental shelf and uppermost slope (Ref. 244).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.  Can expand itself with air or water (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Size at sexual maturity according to literature and specimens studied, for males 36.0 cm and for females less than 42.1 cm with maximum size at least 421 cm TL (Ref. 80388).

species.name: Holbiche brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 244).  Found over muddy or sandy bottoms (Ref. 27436).  Feeds on small true shrimps, euphausiid shrimps, squids, and small fishes (Ref. 244). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche campèchoise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Maximum length is of immature holotype.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche chuhu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype which was found at 537 m depth.  Length is from an immature specimen, might reach at least 50 cm TL.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche cyrano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slopes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche damier
species.description: Found in crevices and caves of rocky reefs during the day, but may move to adjacent sandy areas at night (Ref. 12951).  Reported from 18 m to 220 m depth (Ref. 12951).  Feeds on fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 12951).  Adults segregate by sex (Ref. 12951).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  244 cm record from New Zealand possibly due to confusion with another species (Ref. 244).  Can expand itself with air or water (Ref. 244).

species.name: Holbiche des plages
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and uppermost slope, on soft bottoms, from close inshore to 290 m (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on small crustaceans, bony fish, and cephalopods (Ref. 5578).  Although commonly caught by shore anglers, it is not generally considered a game fish (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Holbiche des vases
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope on or just above muddy substrates (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on cephalopods, small bony fishes, and crustaceans (Ref. 5578).  Probably caught with bottom trawls (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Holbiche fantôme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slopes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche gatussau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small bony fish and cephalopods (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche glabre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Just recently described.  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche grandes oreilles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slopes.  Oviparous, with one egg per oviduct laid at a time.  Sexual dimorphism in adults unusually well-developed.

species.name: Holbiche gressouillette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf from close inshore in shallow to deeper water.  Oviparous, hatching at about 14 cm (Ref. 6871).  Can expand itself with air or water.  Caught by commercial bottom trawlers but of no use to fisheries at present.

species.name: Holbiche grise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater bottom shark found on the insular slopes off the leeward islands.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Poorly known.  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche indienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the uppermost continental slope.  Probably a dwarf species.  Oviparous (Ref. 50499).  This species could possibly attains a maximum size of 50.0 cm TL, with males reported (Ref. 26842) to reach length at maturity at 36.7 cm TL. A 45.0 cm female was found gravid and have two egg cases, one in each uterus, containing visible embryos (85.1-86.2 mm) with attached yolk sac. Stomach examined contains crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 95495).

species.name: Holbiche isard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope, on or near the bottom (Ref. 244).  This species has been reported to prefer temperate to cool temperate waters, but may also be found in subtropical waters; apparently prefer 200-300 m depths on the west coast and 100-200 m depths on the south coast; and, a common by catch of demersal trawlers (Ref. 75585).  Feeds mainly on pelagic bony fishes, also fish offal, hagfish eggs, crustaceans, and cephalopods (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche japonaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology little-known.  Oviparous.  Utilized for oil, human consumption and fishmeal or fish cakes.

species.name: Holbiche kiwi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 26346).  Feeds on bottom crustaceans (Ref. 244).

species.name: holbiche laineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holbiche malaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slopes.  Poorly known.  Oviparous, probably one egg per oviduct laid at a time.  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche mannequin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slope.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche mignonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slopes.  Feeds on small fishes, squid and crustaceans.  Mode of development uncertain.  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche mouchetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known but wide-ranging bottom-dwelling shark found on continental and insular shelves (Ref. 11146).  Probably caught with bottom trawls (Ref. 30573).  Live-bearing (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found generally at depths of more than 1000 meters (Ref. 56212).

species.name: Holbiche nébuleuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Poorly known.  Maximum length might be over 23 cm TL.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche papoila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope.  Maximum length unknown, adolescent at 51 cm TL.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Usually caught in deep exploratory trawls, and has no commercial interest (Ref. 117245).

species.name: Holbiche petite queue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental outer shelf and upper slope.  Prefers fine white calcareous material as substrate.  Feeds on small bony fishes and cephalopods.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche petites ailes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope. Oviparous, apparently laying one egg per oviduct at a time. The most common Apristurus species in the Gulf of Mexico, along with A. laurussonii.

species.name: Holbiche platnez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype.  Maximum length presumably comes from an immature specimen.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche porc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope, on or near the bottom (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small bony fish, shrimp, squid, and possibly other sharks (Ref. 5578). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche pâle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare catshark, only known from the holotype taken from the Makassar Straits slope at a depth of 655 m (Ref. 244).  Maximum length reported ( >21 cm TL) based on a juvenile specimen (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche quagga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves, (Ref. 244), on or near the bottom (Ref. 30573).  Attains a maximum size of 37.0 cm TL; female of 36.8 cm TL was gravid and contained eight egg cases, four in each uterus (Ref. 86593).  Feeds on shrimps.  Collection by deep-sea shrimp trawlers may indicate that the species could have a wider depth distribution, possibly down to 280 m (Ref. 86593).   Not utilized at present (Ref. 244).

species.name: Holbiche râpe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope.  Feeds on a variety of small fish (e.g. lanternfish) and invertebrates.  Oviparous.  Possesses an enlarged gill region which is an adaptation to areas with low dissolved oxygen levels.  Has a high concentration of squalene in its liver which affords it neutral buoyancy.  Regularly caught by bottom trawlers but not utilized at all.

species.name: Holbiche salamandre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 559).  Liver has a high concentration of squalene (Ref. 559).

species.name: Holbiche sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slopes primarily on mud, but also on rock bottoms.  Feeds on bottom invertebrates.  Oviparous, with a single egg per oviduct at a time.  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Holbiche soufflue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and upper slope, preferring areas with sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on benthic animals, mainly crustaceans and cephalopods, but also bony fishes, and other elasmobranches (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Can expand with air when disturbed (Ref. 244).

species.name: Holbiche spectre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche tapir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the eastern Pacific upper continental slope.  Oviparous, with a single egg laid per oviduct.

species.name: Holbiche tigrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, from close inshore to deeper water (Ref. 244).  Feeds mainly on small bony fishes and crustaceans, also cephalopods and small elasmobranchs (Ref. 244).

species.name: Holbiche torazame
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known deepwater bottom shark.  Oviparous with one egg per oviduct.

species.name: Holbiche têtard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slope and outermost shelf.  The expanded branchial region of this shark suggests that they are adapted to bottom areas with low dissolved oxygen levels.  With little information available, reproductive mode could either be ovoviviparous (Ref. 244, 53776) or oviparous, paired eggs are laid (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche tête molle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare shark known only from two specimens taken on the insular slopes, on or near the bottom (Ref. 244).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche ventrue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelves and upper slopes from inshore to deeper waters.  Prefers rocky, algal-covered areas of kelp beds.  Nocturnal.  Feeds on bony fishes, alive and dead, and probably crustaceans.  Can inflate its stomach with water or air.  Oviparous.  Can live in tanks for several years and females can lay eggs in captivity.  Occurs in aggregations while resting, sometimes piled one on top of the other.  Sometimes caught by sport divers but not used.

species.name: Holbiche voile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poorly known deep-water bottom-dwelling shark inhabiting insular slopes (Ref. 11146).  Possibly oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche à gorge tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the uppermost continental slopes (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods (Ref. 5213).  The adult males are larger than females, a characteristic unusual among sharks (Ref. 244).  Manifests partial sexual segregation.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche à grande tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water, probably near the bottom (Ref. 11146).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449). First record of a cartilaginous fish manifesting rudimentary hermaphroditism (Ref. 53905).  Biology little known (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Holbiche à joues noires
species.description: A poorly known deep-water bottom-dwelling catshark found on mud bottoms of the upper continental slopes (Ref. 11146).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Holbiche à longues nageoires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poorly known deep-water bottom shark (Ref. 11146).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: holbiche à sexe blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holbiche à taches noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf; sublittoral zone above 100 m (Ref. 11230).  Oviparous, but with several egg-capsules retained in the oviduct until the embryos reach an advanced stage before they are laid which might be regarded as being intermediate between oviparity and ovoviviparity. Diet unknown, but presumably dominated by small invertebrates and fishes. Caught irregularly by demersal longline fisheries operating offshore. Utilized for its meat but of limited value due to its small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Holbiche à taches rouges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore shark found on the continental shelf.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Sexual dimorphism is evident in dentition of male species (Ref. 49562).

species.name: Holcomycteronus aequatoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic at bathyal and abyssal depths (Ref. 56809).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 4103.

species.name: Holcomycteronus brucei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024). Stomach remains include crustaceans (benthic isopod Storthyngura sp. 1.5-2.5 cm long) and an unidentifiable isopod) (Ref. 75736). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Holcomycteronus digittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Holcomycteronus profundissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Holcomycteronus pterotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Holcomycteronus squamosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous (Ref. 6555). Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Holdridges toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stagnant waters or creeks with low current velocity between 35 and 620 m elevation; in temperatures from 21 to 37°C; swims in small groups over muddy bottoms.  Feeds on terrestrial insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Hole goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand patches (Ref. 37816) and fine rubble flats adjacent to reef to about 10 meters depth.  Usually occurs on light coloured sand and is often partly burried (Ref. 48637).  Uncertain if it associates with invertebrate burrows.

species.name: Holiday darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Ulocentra habitats of bedrock and gravel pool areas in small creeks to moderate-sized rivers. Abundant in cool upland streams, but extends into warm-water habitats in the Conasauga River. Usually associated with lush growths of Podostemum (a river weed), where its green banding provides good camouflage. Observed perched high on bedrock profusions with few river weed growth (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Holland's Toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hollandichthys multifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hollandichthys taramandahy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lateral puddles of rivers and very small tributaries with shallow and lentic black waters, with mud and leaf on the bottom, and very dense riparian vegetation. Larger individuals measuring 7.0-8.0 cm SL were observed isolated and small specimens measuring 3.0-4.0 cm SL were encountered in groups of 3 to 6 fishes. Feeds on spiders, ants, beetles, and insect parts. Other fish collected along with this species include Astyanax laticeps, Astyanax sp., Cyanocharax itaime, Cyphocharax voga, Gymnotus sp., Hyphessobrycon luetkenii, Mimagoniates rheocharis, Phalloceros spiloura, and Steindachnerina biornata (Ref. 94715).

species.name: Holleman's frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holleman's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species collected from rock pools (Ref. 11441).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Holleman’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves of reef slopes also with overhangs and crevices; in areas with sand, some rubble and gorgonians, small, hard and soft corals, Tubastrea, sea whips, some black coral, sea fans, tunicates, sponges, some hydroids (Ref. 109919).

species.name: Holocentre rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in reefs and rocky areas from the shoreline to 200 m depth (Ref. 2683).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27000. Nocturnal (Ref. 6537).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6746).

species.name: Holocentre rouge (Sargocentron rubrum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reefs (Ref. 9710); silty reefs or wrecks in lagoons, bays, or harbors (Ref. 27370), may occur in aggregations; also found hidden in caves and cracks of rocks during the day (Ref. 12382, 48635), usually in areas subject to strong currents (Ref. 48635).   Intertidal observations were also reported (Ref. 49162).  Feed mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps (Ref. 2334), also preys on small fishes (Ref. 12382).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6746).  Spine of preopercle venomous (Ref. 2334). Solitary or in groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Holohalaelurus favus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holohalaelurus grennian
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holtbyrnia conocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Holtbyrnia melanocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homaloptera bilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in torrential streams.

species.name: Homaloptera confuzona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homaloptera ocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homaloptera ogilviei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forested streams with black waters.

species.name: Homaloptera orthogoniata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forested streams with black waters (Ref. 7050), usually with some current and wood debris (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Homaloptera parclitella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homalopteroides avii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homalopteroides indochinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit high gradient streams.  Like other members of the genus, it probably Feeds on benthic insects.

species.name: Homalopteroides manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing parts of hill streams and rivers; on water bodies full of shingles, pebbles, stones and rocky (Ref. 44442).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in mountain streams (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Homalopteroides nebulosus

species.name: Homalopteroides smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit high gradient streams over fast bedrock, cobble runs and rapids while juveniles in slower stretches of gravel and exposed tree roots (Ref. 12693).  Found in rapid-running mountain streams of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feed on aquatic insect larvae,  particularly Odonatans (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Homalopteroides stephensoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in both fast flowing water on rocks and in slower water on logs or other woody debris (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Homalopteroides tweediei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in moderate currents with living and dead vegetation.  May move into seasonally flooded areas with moderate currents.  Probably feeds on small aquatic insects and zooplankton.  Not fished commercially (Ref. 12693).

Taken at depths greater than 60 cm in riffles of a large stream, about 20 m wide flowing through a degraded hill forest. Other fish captured with this species and in similar habitat type include Acrochordonichthys melanogaster, Akysis fuscus, Glyptothoax 'major', Neogastromyzon nieuwenhuisii, Gastromyzon punctulatus, Homaloptera nebulosa, H. stephensoni, H. zollingeri and H. ophiolepis (Ref. 33004).

species.name: Homatula disparizona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with clear water, slow current and rocky bottom (Ref. 93166).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homatula wuliangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams of mountain valleys in areas with swift current over rocky and stony substrates, interspersed with sand and gravel in higher elevation reaches (1781 m asl) and in areas with slower current in the lower reaches (1274 m asl) (Ref. 93044).

species.name: Homodiaetus anisitsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Homodiaetus banguela
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Honess' glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Honey blue eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds and small streams near the sea; water typically dark (tea-like) with sand or mud bottom (pH=4.5-5.8, upper limit of water temperature 27.5°-32.5°C). Occurs in slow-flowing, tannin-stained creeks and coastal dune lakes in sandy country (locally known as 'wallum'). Found along grassy banks, often among reeds or water lilies (Ref. 44894). Closely related to Pseudomugil signifer.

species.name: Honey-bee pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Honey-head damsel
species.description: Adults inhabit lagoons and coastal reefs, usually in silty areas (Ref. 4966). The true D. prosopotaenia ranges from Singapore to Sulawesi while the yellow-breasted variant ranges from Irian Jaya to eastern Australia and Vanuatu (Ref. 48636). May be found solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Honeycomb moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in seagrass beds and banks; rarely in bays and not occurring on coral reefs.

species.name: Honeycomb podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive (Ref. 48635); lives among corals of shallow reef flats and lagoons (Ref. 1602).  Also found under dead coral pieces but quickly sneaks away when looking underneath (Ref. 48635). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Honeycomb rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on or near bottom, usually shallower than 70 m (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Honeycomb toby
species.description: Occurs in clear lagoon and seaward reefs, Ref. 48637.  Found  with sponges at various depths (Ref. 48637).  Prefers sheltered areas in the form of holes in dead and living corals.  Solitary or paired.  Feeds on sponges, polychaetes, filamentous algae and on smaller quantities of tunicates, crustaceans, echinoderms and corals.

species.name: honeycomb whipray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on soft substrates.  Viviparous, with histotrophy.  Few biological information is available, diet presumably consists of crustaceans and small fishes.  Caught occasionally in demersal tangle nets; meat, skin (of high value) and cartilage are utilized (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Hong Kong catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in streams, ponds, ditches and reservoirs.  They prefer deeper pools and tend to hide under thick mats of vegetation; are nocturnal feeders foraging on small fishes, worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 44091).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hongkong butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rocky and coral reef areas (Ref. 9710), where they are found in pairs and small groups (Ref. 48636).  Feed on algae (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hongshuia banmo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hongshuia microstomata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hongshuia paoli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hong’s tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on recovered landings where this species is included in an assemblage of fish species which generally live at, or about depths shallower than 100 m, this fish is a shallow-water species inhabiting depths shallower than 100 m (Ref. 126065).

species.name: Honshu pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small caves in sublittoral rocky reefs. Reported from tide pools to depths of at least 25 m offshore, but mostly seen in shallow depths (Ref. 48635). An active cleaner that shares crevices with shrimps, large mud crabs and sometimes moray eels (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in pairs near sponges and Diadema sea urchins (Ref 90102). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Spawns from the end of May to September.

species.name: Hooded fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found above gently sloping bottoms with scattered low outcrops of rocks and rubble (Ref. 116195).

species.name: Hooded triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit surge-swept reef margins (Ref. 1602).  Found on rock surfaces under ledges (Ref. 13227) of coral reefs covered with algae (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hoodwinker ocean sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poisson. This species likely exhibits a similar biology to the other Mola species whereby feeding takes place during deep dives. Stomach contents of three specimens consisted of salps (Thetys vagina and Pyrosoma sp.) and the remains of a nectonic siphonophore, and in one instance, a 3 × 5 mm Styrofoam ball. All dissected specimens were heavily infested with parasites, particularly in the intestines (cestodes) and in the liver (likely larval Trypanorhynch cestodes). Gonadal shape differs between the sexes; the ovary is singular and ball-shaped, the testis are paired, elongated and rod-like and do not appear to frill during maturation. Migrations and spawning grounds, eggs, larvae and pre-juveniles are unknown (Ref. 115933).

species.name: Hooghly croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hooghly halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hook jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hook-nosed sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered bays and estuaries (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Hookcheek dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hookfin cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits rocky and weedy areas with scattered coral outcrops.  Rarely seen.  Usually occurs in pairs (Ref. 11894).

species.name: Hookhorn sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Hookskate
species.description: Inhabits mud-bottom habitat on the upper slope, generally in waters deeper than 350 meters. Mainly feeds on small bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Stomach contents include one specimen of Mullus argentinae, remains of a teleost fish and predominance of Myctophidae fishes. Sympatric with other chondrichthyans, Etmopterus bigelowi, Squalus aff. blainvillei, and Dipturus leptocauda (Ref. 56543). Oviparous (Ref. 50449). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hooktail skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on upper and mid-continental slope (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Biology little known. Males reaches maturity by ca. 107cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Hopbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hoplarchus psittacus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).  Also found in swamps and lakes; feeds on aquatic insects and crustaceans during high water, also on fishes during low water seasons (Ref. 40602).  Maximum length 35 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Hoplostète de Darwin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives close to or on the bottom of the upper continental slope.  Prefers hard substrates.  Young specimens feed on small shrimps and fish (Ref. 4784).  A deep sea species, nonetheless, the young are often found near the coast (Ref. 9137).  Utilized as fishmeal and source of oil in eastern central Atlantic (Ref. 3695).

species.name: Hoplostète noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives near the bottom in deep water, from 200 to at least 500, but possibly to 1000 m depth.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 3695).

species.name: Hoplostète orange
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep, cold waters over steep continental slopes, ocean ridges and sea-mounts.  Shallow range of usual occurrence from Ref. 27121.  Appears to be dispersed over both rough bottoms and steep, rough grounds where it feeds on crustaceans and fish.  In New Zealand, the main prey include mesopelagic and benthopelagic prawns, fish, and squid, with other organisms such as mysids, amphipods and euphausiids occasionally being important (Ref. 9072).  Juveniles feed mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 27075, 27076).  Grows very slowly and is one of the longest lived fish species known.  Based on parasite and trace-element analyses, orange roughy  is a sedentary species with little movement between fish-management zones (Ref. 27089).  Little is known of the larvae and juveniles which are probably confined to deep water (Ref. 27088).  The fishery targets sporadically formed dense spawning and non-spawning aggregations.  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988). Because of severe overfishing the species has been listed as threatened by the Australian Government in 2006.

species.name: Hoplostète scutelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Lives close to the bottom (Ref. 27121).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hoplunnis schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hoplunnis sicarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the substrate but not burrowing (Ref. 35597).  Oviparous (Ref. 35597).  Planktonic leptocephali (Ref. 35597).

species.name: Hoplunnis similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hora danio
species.description: Found in rice fields, small ponds and pools in hill streams (Ref. 4832).  Collected from streams with fast flowing, clear water, over a substrate with rocks, sand and pebbles (Ref. 36341).  Most specimens obtained in late March 1997 appeared to be sexually mature (Ref. 36341).

species.name: Hora razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Hora white carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns during the monsoon months.

species.name: Horabagrus nigricollaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams at upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Horadandia brittani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal floodplain (Ref. 94541).

species.name: Horaglanis abdulkalami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a well with pH 7.2, conductivity 180ìS and dissolve oxygen 2mg/l and soft lateriate bottom comprising of small pores and channels (Ref. 92945).

species.name: Horaglanis alikunhii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Horalabiosa joshuai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Horalabiosa palaniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Horiomyzon retropinnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Horn dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy bottoms of bays (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Horn-nosed boxfish
species.description: Inhabits rubble substrates in channels between sheltered inner reefs or in deep sandy lagoons around coral patches (Ref. 48637). Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Generally uncommon species (Ref. 9710) that inhabits coral reefs and flat bottoms in coastal areas.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Horned blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with mollusks, sponges, and anemones (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Horned goby
species.description: Collected on rubble-sand patches at the base of isolated coral blocks near the margin of Al Fahal reef in central Red Sea (near Thuwal, Saudi Arabia). Individulas were found living inside small holes in large pieces of dead coral rock covered with short algae at a depth of 8 m. Two other specimens were collected at a depth of 15 m in May 2017 at the same locality. Also observed in other localities at depths of about 5 m (Ref. 126737).

species.name: Horned lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic, found between 375-750 m during the day; between 40-225 m at night (maximum abundance at 100 m depth) (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Horned rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Horned searobin
species.description: Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.  Neither anterolateral glandular grooves nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Horned tentacle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Horned whiff
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hornless blenny
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters,on sand and rocks. Form relatively tight groups perched over coral 
heads, often as separate groupings of IP females and pale TP fish, while territorial black males are found alone in burrows, usually challenged by passing pale TP individuals (Ref. 125603). Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Hornyhead chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Horrible rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarely encountered (Ref. 26363).

species.name: Horse-shoe leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on offshore reefs.  The black horse-shoe marking along flanks is diagnostic for this species (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Horseface unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species found in coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710). Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Horsefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Horsehair eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 43688).

species.name: Horsehead tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Most common of Japanese tilefishes (Ref. 559).

species.name: Horseshoe butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hortle's whipray
species.description: Demersal  inshore; commonly found over shallow intertidal mud flats and in estuaries in only several metres depth. Viviparous, with histotrophy. Presumably feeds on crustaceans, molluscs and small fishes. Caught regularly, but usually avoided, by beach seine fisheries operating in intertidal habitats. Possibly adversely affected by mangrove loss. Utilized for its meat, and possibly also for its skin and cartilage. (Ref.58048).

species.name: Hose blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hosokawa's coral blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 42594).  Found among the branches of both living and dead corals on a shallow coral reef (Ref. 35866).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hotlips pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from lagoons as well as from oceanic drop-offs (Ref. 46430).  Forms schools and feeds on plankton (Ref. 46430).

species.name: Hotlips triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at depths of 6 m and shallower on exposed rocky coasts (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hottentot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water over rocky bottoms.  Feeds on seaweeds, echinoderms, crustaceans, mollusks and worms (Ref. 3688).

species.name: Hottentot bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky substrate.  Feeds on benthic organisms like worms, ascidians, crustaceans, mollusks and algae (Ref. 5213).  Rarely caught by shore anglers.  Esteemed food fish.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Hottentot bronze
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near rocks in coastal waters.  Feeds on ascideans, crustaceans, and algae.  Good food fish but not sufficiently abundant to be of commercial significance.  Sold fresh.

species.name: Hourglass basslet
species.description: This species lives in or hovers above small rocky rubble on gradual slopes at depths and when approached by the submersible, it disappears into the rubble. Observed often in pairs (Ref. 113814).

species.name: Hourglass triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in intertidal pools (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hovering goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy or coral rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Inhabits 'U-shaped' burrows.  Often in pairs.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Hovers head down near burrow (Ref. 9710).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Howella pammelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken from the stomach of a Carcharhinus.

species.name: Howella parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Howella zina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Howong betta
species.description: Mouth brooder (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Howson's coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon coral reefs, sheltering among dense branches of Acropora corals, especially A. longicyanthus (Ref. 125638).

species.name: Howson's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-rubble bottom, around low rocky outcrops (Ref. 36661).  Occurs in pairs (Ref. 36661).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Hozukius emblemarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep rocky bottoms.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Hozukius guyotensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur near seamounts (Ref. 34817).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Huan’s goatfish
species.description: Occurs most probably in shallow soft bottom reached by artisanal fisheries (Ref. 130857).

species.name: Hubb's pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mesopelagic or bathypelagic species (Ref. 6601).  The single known adult  (holotype) was taken in haul between 657 to 0 m; most larvae have been taken in haul in the upper 500 m and in waters as shallow as 60 m.  Probably feeds on other midwater fishes (Ref. 6691).  Presumed to be synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 10755).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Hubers knife livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, fast-flowing waters (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Hucho bleekeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing streams with sandy and gravel substratum.  Carnivorous; feeds on fishes, insects.

species.name: Hucho ishikawae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the substrate in clear waters of pools below waterfalls and rapids.

species.name: Huchon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary, inhabits deeper regions of swift flowing streams with oxygen rich waters.  Adults are territorial but not solitary (Ref. 26170).  Carnivore.  Juveniles feed mainly on invertebrates and adults mostly on fishes, but also prey on amphibians, reptiles, small mammals and waterfowl (Ref. 26170).  Important sport fish with minimum size of catch from 50-55 cm.  Transplantations of young artificially incubated and reared fish have not been successful.  Depletion of stocks due to overexploitation, industrial pollution, waterway redirection and badly designed or non-existent fish ladders in dams and reservoirs.  Territorial, but migrates short distances upstream for spawning (Ref. 556).  Reported to be one of the biggest freshwater fishes of the world, reaching  a length of over 2 m and weight of over 100 kg (Ref. 26170); which is probably erroneous (A. Mangold, pers. comm.).

species.name: Hudson's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow reefs (Ref. 37816).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Huguenin’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Produces an offensive odor upon capture (Ref. 559).

species.name: Human's fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in gradual rubble slope next to shore at depths of 10-18 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Humboldt grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hummingbird lampeye
species.description: Found in shallow and vegetated zones near the banks of small rivers and creeks (Ref. 47311).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hump-back [White] sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottom (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Hump-back bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominant food is the lake-fly in its larval aquatic stages (Ref. 246). Also feeds on plants; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307). Max. length of 27.5 cm presumed to be TL.

species.name: Hump-backed mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. While functional habitats are yet to be elucidated, T. remadevii inhabits the middle to upper reaches of the River Cauvery and some of its tributaries. Mesohabitat utilization is known to incorporate shallow high velocity rapids to deep, slow flowing pools, with substrates typically composed of bedrock and boulders (Ref. 123478).

species.name: Hump-head
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms in rather shallow water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Hump-headed blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow shore line water of intertidal reef flats from 0.5 to 1.5 m depth where the substrate consists of a thin carpet of algal turf and sand (Ref. 205).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Humpback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawning from June till the first half of July; fecundity 192,000 eggs.

species.name: Humpback anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poisson d’eau profonde. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302). Males dwarfed and non-parasitic (Ref. 4491). Caught with plankton nets (Ref. 559). Capable of catching and swallowing prey larger than itself, as witness the approximately 24.0 cm SL specimen of Chauliodus sp. in the stomach of a 6.6 cm SL individual (NMNZ P 14537) (Ref. 58502). Larvae are found primarily in upper 100 m (Ref. 36493). Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36493). Eggs are presumably contained in floating gelatinous rafts (Ref. 36493).

species.name: Humpback batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental reefs (Ref. 9710).  Adults usually moderately deep on open substrates with sparse reef or coral heads. A solitary species, but occasionally in pairs or small groups. Small juveniles also in deep water and the zebra-pattern serves well as camouflage when sheltering with crinoids (Ref. 48637).  Juveniles in shore waters; adults in deeper water. Possible to breed in the aquarium (Ref. 130623).

species.name: Humpback cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A euryhaline species (Ref. 59012), often found in freshwater and estuaries (Ref. 4329), shallow sheltered inshore reefs or river mouths, among clumps of algae or algal covered rubble.  Found in aggregations (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Humpback cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Humpback chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, rocky runs and flowing pools.  The hump at the back of the head directs fish to maintain position in the swift water (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Humpback hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No data on habitat and biology, but presumably marine in coastal waters and perhaps entering estuaries.

species.name: Humpback Handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Humpback largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predatory species, most active during twilight and at night (Ref. 52307). Feeds primarily on nocturnal mormyrid and schilbeid fishes (Ref. 27496). Breeding takes place at the beginning of summer (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Humpback nohu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Usually hiding among branches of corals, from near shore to 24 m.  Feeds mainly on crabs and shrimps (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Humpback waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Humpback whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Humpback whitefish
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters near shore (Ref. 5723), lower reaches of rivers with slow current, large lakes with tributaries, floodplain lakes, deltas and estuaries, brackish waters (Ref. 59043).  Migrates up to more than 1,200 km inland for spawning (Ref. 5723).  Overwinters near river mouths (Ref. 5723).  There are non-migratory freshwater populations.  Adults feed mostly on mollusks, crustaceans and chironomid larvae (Ref. 28219).

species.name: Humpbacked cardinalfish
species.description: Adults inhabit mangrove estuaries, tidal creeks and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).  Usually found in brackish water or freshwater of river mouths. Nocturnal (Ref. 7300), euryhaline species (Ref. 59012).

species.name: Humpbacked coralbrotula
species.description: Large dominating individuals were observed to make attacks toward smaller fish, which were hiding below rocks or any other shelter provided.  One male was observed to flip backward the cover of the copulatory organ so that the organ can be exposed while swimming (Ref. 57884). Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices to at least 20m depth, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Humpbacked snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Humphead cichlid
species.description: Rock-dwellers, often in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Omnivorous, feed on shellfish (snails and mussels) and fish (Ref. 6770). Food intake of mouth brooding females is for nourishment of both themselves and the young (Ref. 33980). Aquarium keeping: several females for one male; minimum aquarium size  >200 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Humphead thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling.  Undoubtedly confused with other species in the past.  More data needed.

species.name: Humpnose unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs. Diet consisted a high proportion of the green alga, Caulerpa.

species.name: Hunchback scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters.

species.name: Hureau's flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.

species.name: Hurghada sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Hutchin's mudbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hutchin's toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty inshore reefs in 3-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hutchins' anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected using rotenone or box dredge on sandy mud, sponge, and seagrass (Ref. 59208).

species.name: Hutchins' blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the surge zone in limestone holes just below the intertidal range. Common in areas where Pocillopora damicornis is present on the reefs (Ref. 529). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hutomo's anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep water species, forming small aggregations with large coral heads at the base of deep slopes in current prone areas.  Usually in depths of 40+ m depth (Ref. 48635). Often in silty conditions, in 30-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Huysman's righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9792).

species.name: Hyaline cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The 4.7 cm SL holotype found with nearly ripe eggs (Ref. 11356). Solitary among Sinularia soft corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Hyaline fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species; prefers living and breeding in caves or underground rivers (Ref. 38444).

species.name: Hyalobagrus flavus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyalobagrus leiacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyalobagrus ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat and streams (Ref. 84801).  Occasionally seen in aquarium trades (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Hybopsis rubrifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel pools and runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Hydrolagus barbouri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hydrolagus bemisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hydrolagus eidolon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Hydrolagus lusitanicus
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Maximal length type is pre supra caudal fin length.  
Nothing is known on the biology of the species.
Body uniform rose to light brown with few small irregular light and dark spots; point of snout and region between the eye and the pectoral fin whitish; fins violet blue.

species.name: Hydrolagus pallidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).  Depth range along the mid-Atlantic ridge (Ref. 83979, C.Cotton pers.comm. 03/10).

species.name: Hydrolycus armatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hydrolycus tatauaia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hydrolycus wallacei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyena blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found beneath rocks at shallow depths (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Hygophum bruuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hylopanchax leki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in a small shady stream (Ref. 94189).

species.name: Hylopanchax moke
species.description: Found in calmer parts of larger forest streams (Ref. 94189).

species.name: Hylopanchax multisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits shallow creeks inside dense forest areas (Ref. 123864).

species.name: Hylopanchax ndeko
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small shady streams and rivers (Ref. 94189).

species.name: Hylopanchax paucisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hylopanchax silvestris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hylopanchax thysi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow creeks (Ref. 123864).

species.name: Hymenocephalus antraeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Hymenocephalus barbatulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus billsam
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus grimaldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Hymenocephalus hachijoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus iwamotoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus lethonemus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 26282.

species.name: Hymenocephalus longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.

species.name: Hymenocephalus longipes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus nesaeae

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
