species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus semipellucidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus striatissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hymenocephalus striatulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds mainly on pelagic organisms, copepods (Pleuromamma sp., Oncaea conifera, Xanthocalanus sp., Aetideidae spp.); also on small fish, chaetognaths, gammarids (Lysianassidae), shrimp (Bentheogennema pasithea), and mysids (Paralophogaster glaber); benthic polychaetes, including family Polinoidae (Ref. 9949).

species.name: Hymenocephalus torvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypancistrus contradens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypancistrus debilittera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypancistrus furunculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypancistrus inspector
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from rocks and rapids.  Stomach contents include algae and detritus; also seeds (dicotyledonous and monocotyledonous seeds) (Ref. 41483).

species.name: Hypancistrus lunaorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypancistrus zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypanus berthalutzae
species.description: Mostly a coastal species, usually at the continental shelf, and reported to occur in localities up to 250 km off the coast (Ref. 123757).

species.name: Hypergastromyzon eubranchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing rocky streams (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Hypergastromyzon humilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyperoglyphe macrophthalma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyperopisus bebe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits both still and flowing waters; breeds in the flood season; feeds on mollusks (Ref. 28714).  Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head and on the ventral and dorsal regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located  (Ref. 10011).  Its electric organ discharge (EOD) is steroid-sensitive (Ref. 10763; 10764).  Fecundity value of 18,924 eggs has been reported for this species (Ref. 10607).

species.name: Hyperostotic gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphalophis devius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphen barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in floodplains, pools and shallow streams with vegetation.  Feeds on detritus, algae, seeds, small invertebrates (Ref. 7248) and aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 13337).  Migrates upriver to breed after heavy rains (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon acaciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon agulha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon albolineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon amapaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In small Savanna creeks, over sand and gravel.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon amaronensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over organic detritus and decomposing vegetation, apparent water color was brown to black, low dissolved oxygen (0.42-0.75 mg/l), as was conductivity (42-43 μs) and oxygen saturation (5.3-10 %), slightly acidic pH (6.0-6.2). Five stomachs of cleared and stained specimens indicate a diet mostly composed of algae, Clorophyta, Vlothix (47.72% N, 22.72%V); also present are Cladocera, Alonella (20.45% N, 13.63% V); Clorophyta, Spirogyra (17.04%N, 9.09%V); insect parts (9.09%N, 18.18%V), dipteran larvae, Tabaridae (5.47% N, 5.47% V); Ephemeroptera, Oligoneuridae (1.13%N, 4.54%V) and unidentified digested material (27.27%V) (Ref. 84248)..

species.name: Hyphessobrycon arianae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon auca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon balbus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon borealis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A gregarious fish living near the bank of the river with shallow water and very slow current (57781).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon brumado
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with relatively rapid water current, running over rocky and sandy bottoms at elevated altitudes (971 and 1.048 m a.s.l.).  Stomach contents of three specimens include filamentous algae, fragments of vascular plants, adults and two distinct larvae of Diptera (Chironomidae and Simuliidae), larvae of Trichoptera, adult of Formicidae, Aranae, and fragments of unidentified arthropods (Ref. 85847).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon cachimbensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon condotensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon copelandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently found in waters with slow current or the counter current zones of small creeks with clear water and sandy bottom.  It occupies the upstream portion of rivers before a waterfall.  Its capture in great numbers suggest a gregarious behavior (Ref. 12225).  Its reproduction in captivity has not been reported (Ref. 27188).  Maximum length 5.0 SL (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon cyanotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon ecuadoriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest pools.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon eilyos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon elachys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon epicharis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon ericae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits small to medium-sized clearwater terra firme streams (i.e., streams that are not inundated during the flood season).  Its type locality is characterized by a shallow first order clearwater stream, with sandy bottom and abundant aquatic vegetation. However, this species is often collected in sections of the stream that lack aquatic vegetation.  Four specimens of this species have unidentified vegetal matter and insect remains in their stomach.  Insect items that are recognizable include winged and wingless ants, and a small aquatic beetle (Ref. 116179).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon heliacus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected only in lentic marginal portions of the stream, on muddy bottom with plenty of submersed vegetation (Ref. 42626).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimen 5.0 TL max length (Ref. 2059).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyphessobrycon kayabi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality, Lagoa Azul, a terra-firme lake near the margin of the Rio Teles Pires, connected to it, with crystal-clear water, fed by springs at the bottom of the lake, and large stands of
subaquatic macrophytes.  Stomach content analysis based on three specimens reveals that this species feeds mostly on vegetal matter (macrophyte fragments, unicellular and filamentous algae), and a smaller proportion of other organisms (testate amoebae, Cladocera, aquatic Hemiptera, Chironomidae larvae, unidentified invertebrate eggs).  Observed during snorkeling sessions to browse on the periphyton growing on the surface of large submerged macrophytes leaves (Nymphaeaceae).  Occurs syntopically at Lagoa Azul with other characids including <i>Thayeria sp., <i>Hemigrammus sp., <i>Moenkhausia ceros, <i>M. cotinho, <i>M. colletti, and <i>M. cf. lepidura, as well as several cichlids, anostomids, poeciliids, and stingrays (Ref. 94770).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon montagi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found only in clear-water terra firme streams, i.e., streams dissecting the uplands, above the periodically flooded igapó forest, as the Igarapé Socó Barroso, the type locality.  These streams have width ranging from 0.80 to 20 m, moderate water current (0.1-0.7 m/s), clear,
sandy bottom with pebbles, mud, leaf litter, and submerged logs, often also presenting aquatic macrophytes, pH ranging from 5.8 to 7.44, and water temperature ranging from 24.9° to 29.1°C.  Ripe oocytes were observed in females collected in March and August (Ref. 97524).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon myrmex
species.description: Found where water is transparent and the river bottom is composed of stones, sand and a moderate amount of vegetal debris. The type locality which is a hydroelectric reservoir (PCH Divisa) built in 2010 in the Rio Formiga, occupy an area of 6·8 km2. Before the dam was built, this place would have resembled the adjacent up and downstream areas of the river, i.e. a relative narrow (10–15 m wide) and shallow (maximum depth approximately 1·8 m in some sites) river stretch, with rapid waters and rifles. Stomach contents revealed a diet based on filamentous algae (c. 10%), vascular plant tissue (c. 6%), microcrustaceans (c. 10%), Chironomidae larvae (c. 10%) and Ephemeroptera nymphs (c. 64%). It may be considered an omnivorous species based on the main food resources exploited, but may have tendency toward invertivory. Approximately 50% of the analysed specimens had parasitic isopods (Cymothoidae) associated with the tongue. Specimens with this parasites exhibited a bag-shaped lower jaw, tongue atrophy and softening of the cartilaginous tissues (Ref. 128641).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon pinnistriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a second order stream, known as an igarapé, and surrounded by secondary forest in regeneration. The bottom of is mainly composed of silt, with litter on the margins and few branches and trunks of a diameter greater than 10 cm. In the pools, there is flocculant sediment that is easily disturbed from submerged litter and macrophytes were found at sites with a little more water flow. Most individuals were only observed in more lentic environments, swimming in small schools of 5 to 20 individuals. Individuals also observed to swim alone and together with other species of Characidae, such as Moenkhausia phaeonota and Hyphessobrycon heliacus near igarapé margins with depth ranging from 20-40 cm. Individuals were also sometimes observed foraging among the submerged litter in the igarapé margins. This species also inhabits faster water, no vegetation and substrata consisting of sand and mud (Ref. 118106).

species.name: Hyphessobrycon togoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Buenos Aires province, this species is reported to be found in the Salado River and in ponds, marshes and creeks within the Salado basin. The Chascomús, Lobos and Lacombe lagoons are extensive water-bodies with abundant floating and submerged vegetation). These lakes are a portion of a lenthic environment system which is one of the most remarkable features of the wet pampa. Hyphessobrycon togoi is not abundant with respect to other species occurring in these lagoons, but it is sometimes caught in canals and flooded areas near the lagoons. The Salado River crosses Buenos Aires Province from northwest to southeast, running for ca 690 km in the Pampasia and finally draining into Bahía de Samborombón. The new species was also reported from Matanza River, a highly polluted environment draining into the Río de la Plata, where some of the most densely populated areas of Argentina lies along the middle and lower sections of this river, coupled with a high and complex industrial concentration (Ref. 57841).

species.name: Hypnos monopterygium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and offshore, ranging from the intertidal to 240 m depth (Ref. 9910, 12951).  Found buried on sand and mud bottoms; sometimes found stranded out of water by the tide but is capable of  surviving  for hours (Ref. 9910).  Feeds on crabs, worms, and fishes. It was reported that larger fishes, similar size to themselves have been found in the stomachs of Coffin rays, ingested whole through the large gape (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Maximum length probably to 92 cm TL (Ref. 9910). Both sexes mature at 40-48 cm TL; born at ca. 8-11 cm TL (Ref. 114953). A slow-moving species which uses its electric organs to stun prey.  Also stuns people when accidentally stepped upon or handled (Ref. 9910).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarely attains a length of 20 cm (Ref. 27188). Rheophilic species occurring in very sunny rapids with strong current and rocky bottom (Ref. 35381); inhabiting largest part of freshwaters, from headwaters to upstream of the lower falls, with rocky substrate consisting of boulders, stones, gravels, and sand; the exposed wet rocks are also often covered by the Podostemaceae Mourera fluviatilis and Apinagia richardiana (Ref. 90186).

species.name: Hypostome (Hypostomus ventromaculatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the lower reaches of rivers within the limit of the brackish water and the first rapids (Ref. 35381). Very abundant in estuaries; prefers dead tree trunks and the vast zones of flooded vegetation (Ref. 27188). Also occurs on the muddy bottoms of the banks occupied by Montrichardia arborescens, moving together Loricaria cataphracta and Pimelodus blochii according to the tide. May use its stomach as an accessory breathing organ. Feeds mainly on unicellular algae and then on protozoa, rotifers, nematodes and arthropods as accessory food items (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Hypostome (Hypostomus watwata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A permanent resident of esturial and littoral area (Ref. 90186); in coastal areas and brackish waters of the lower reaches of rivers. Can be caught along the banks with muddy bottom occupied by plants like Laguncularia racemosa, Avicennia germinans and Rhizophora mangle Ref. 35381). Benthic (Ref. 58302). As part of its reproductive behavior, excavates and creates burrows for egg laying (Ref. 82067).

Grazing during the day were occasionally observed. Small fish forage during the day and night, always in shallower areas. Individuals feed mainly on periphyton from rocky substrates, but also explore from submerged logs and branches (Ref. 97225).

species.name: Hypsolebias longignatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection site is a broad seasonal swamp close to the Pacoti River, a small, isolated coastal basin of NE Brazil with shallow part of the swamp 0.4-0.8 m deep.  It has dense aquatic vegetation and slightly turbid water.  Gut contents include amoebas and small aquatic arthropods, with larvae of Odonata and Chironomidae, a small Ostracoda and Cladocera specimens (Ref. 78710).

species.name: Hypsolebias lopesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias macaubensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias magnificus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 5 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hypsolebias martinsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known only from the type locality, found in annual pools of the Brazilian semi-arid habitat. No aggressive behaviour was observed, proving to be very peaceful and not too prolific species (Ref. 108434).

species.name: Hypsolebias mediopapillatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias nitens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal lagoons (Ref. 89836).

species.name: Hypsolebias notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, ? months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hypsolebias nudiorbitatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias picturatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias pterophyllus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sympatric with Hypsolebias picturatus in some temporary pools along its entire geographical range (Ref. 89836).

species.name: Hypsolebias radiosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias radiseriatus
species.description: Occurs in seasonal swamps (Ref. 89836).

species.name: Hypsolebias sertanejo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in parts of the seasonal pools more exposed to sunlight, but often with dense aquatic vegetation (Ref. 89836).

species.name: Hypsolebias shibattai
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a typical annual pool with substrate composed of clay and sand with
slightly turbid water, and dense aquatic vegetation consisting of large stands of <i>Utricularia sp. and <i>Nymphaea sp.  Occurs sympatrically with two other annual rivulids (<i>Cynolebias sp. and <i>Hypsolebias sp.)   The pool has average depth of 80 cm, with the deepest portions about 1.2 m deep, slighty acidic water (pH 6.5), a low electric conductivity (22 μS/cm)., and water temperature of about 30°C at the surface and  approximately 26°C at the deepest portion and shaded banks (Ref. 94796).

species.name: Hypsolebias splendissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow temporary pool in flat plains, in shadier area densely occupied by aquatic vegetation.  Maximum length based on type specimen, to be replaced with a better reference (Ref. 119423).

species.name: Hypsolebias tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hypsolebias trifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a typical annual pool with many aquatic plants of the genera <i>Echinodorus, <i>Utricularia, and <i>Nymphaea.  The pool has about 800 m length and 300 m width, 1.60 m maximum depth, substrate consisting of clay, and transparent and slightly dark color water.  This was the only fish species encountered at the pool, which was shared with many aquatic insect larvae and several tadpole species (Ref. 111470).

species.name: Hypsopanchax jobaerti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly close to vegetated zones along river banks in the gallery forest (Ref. 59344).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Hypsopanchax stiassnyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Currently only found in Kambambe River, a 2-5 meter wide, fast flowing tributary of Lulua River, bottom with sand and pebbles, bordered by gallery forest; the water is brownish with total dissolved ion concentration of 3 ppm and pH 6.2 (Ref. 103403).

species.name: Hypsopsetta macrocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyrtl's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, flowing streams, turbid rivers, lakes and stagnant pools.  Also inhabits billabongs (Ref. 44894).  Shoal forming species (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, crayfish, prawns, mollusks, worms and crustaceans (Ref. 44894).  In northern populations, breeding occurs at the beginning of the wet season (January to March) in shallow sandy areas in the upper reaches of streams.  The spawning habits of interior populations are unknown.  Further research on the many geographic populations is required as there is a strong possibility that Hyrtl's Tandan may actually represent more than one species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Hysteronotus megalostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Hyuga fanray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic ray species that is narrow-ranging (Ref. 114953). According to local divers in Miyazaki, this species  often occurs on very shallow sandy bottoms, at depths as shallow as ca. 1 m, in the summer season off the Nichinan Coast, Miyazaki.  It is frequently captured by set net within a depth of ca. 50 m from early spring (March) to autumn (November).  It was observed by a local fisherman and a fish merchant (pers.comm.), that this species was not included in almost daily set net catches (depth ca. 8-50 m) from November to March in 2007-2008 in northern Miyazaki (Kadokawa Bay) and southern Miyazaki (Meitsu, Nichinan Coast) which indicate that the species avoids lower sea temperatures in the winter season (Ref. 86259). Males mature from ca. 20 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Hémiramphe dissemblable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow water around mangrove in sheltered bays (Ref. 26367).  Early juveniles are neustonic and float on the surface of estuarine mangroves (Ref. 43081).

species.name: Hémirhombe de baie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Hémirhombe oval
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat sand bottoms (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 28023).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Hémirhombe à nageoire longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More information needed.

species.name: Hémirhombe à taches claires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Hétérocongre pointillé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in colonies on clean sandy slopes exposed to currents.

species.name: Hétérocongre tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found on sandy slopes below 15 m; withdraws into its burrow when approached.  Usually in colonies containing up to several hundred individuals. Adults feed on zooplankton (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Iberian barbel
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabit middle and lower reaches, in deep and slow water, with abundant submerged plants (Ref. 11240).  Feed on invertebrates, plants and fish (Ref. 26100).  Juveniles prey on invertebrates while large adult individuals are mainly piscivorous.  Spawn probably in May-June (Ref. 59043). Threatened by pollution, habitat destruction, introduction of new species (Ref. 26100) and water abstraction (Ref. 59043).  Attains up to about 80 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Iberian nase
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits middle stretches of rivers in areas with current.  Can survive in reservoirs.  Occurs in groups, especially during pre-reproduction migration (Ref. 59043).  Also found in lakes (Ref. 26100).  Feeds on vegetal matter, small invertebrates and detritus (Ref. 59043).  Spawning occurs in spring in shallow water, on gravel and sometimes on timber pilings in the river.  Threatened due to the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Iberochondrostoma almacai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The new species is a rheophilic fish, inhabiting Mediterranean-type streams that have typical seasonal habitat heterogeneity, and low to medium flowing clear waters. The species has a short life-span living up to four (4) years, and becomes sexually mature early at the age of two years, irrespective of sex. However, 81.5% of males are mature at 70-80 mm total length, whereas only 50% of females are mature at 80-90 mm total length.  Magalhães (2002) also noticed high fecundity, apparently strongly correlated with total body length, with estimates of up to 3,999 eggs at 100 mm total length; egg size ranges from 1.12 to 1.43 mm and is independent of total body length.  Spawning occurs early in the year, from January to April (Ref. 55426).  Breeds in shallow riffle habitats with fast-flowing water.  May be confined to very small pools during summer (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Iberochondrostoma lemmingii
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in the middle reaches of streams with moderate current and abundant aquatic vegetation (Ref. 59043) and in the lower reaches of rivers with slow current and abundant submerged plants (Ref. 26100).  Feeds on invertebrates, plants (Ref. 26100) and zooplankton (Ref. 59043).  Spawns from March to May.  Threatened due to water abstraction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Iberochondrostoma lusitanicum
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in coastal rivers and terminal segments of main rivers (Ref. 26100).  Occurs in middle and lower reaches of streams, with slow current and underwater vegetation.  Forms large spawning aggregations (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Iberochondrostoma olisiponense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iberochondrostoma oretanum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water with sand and rock bottom in stretches with slow current and underwater vegetation.  Reaches up to about 9 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Iberocypris palaciosi
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits middle reaches of rivers, with abundant aquatic vegetation and moderate to fast current, with rocks or gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  A short-lived species which also occurs in rivers on the low plains, with little current and at high altitudes.  Is threatened due to habitat destruction, pollution and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).  Possibly of hybrid origin (Ref. 59043).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Icana cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ice goby
species.description: Adults ascend rivers in the spawning season without feeding, and dies after spawning. Adults retain larval characteristics, a major factor contributing to its neotenic characteristics is the delayed development of the thyroid system (Ref. 101248).  Caught for food.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 24.5 cm (Ref. 7094). Inhabits open water and fringing vegetation. Feeds on Caridina and fish fry (Ref. 28714).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ichthyocampus carce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively still waters (Ref. 12693).  Most frequently found in rivers, streams and estuaries.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males maybe brooding at 7.8 cm SL (Ref. 5316).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and small zooplankton.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Ichthyococcus polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species, adults mainly found at depths between 500-750 m (Ref. 3988).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches a length greater than 40 cm TL (Ref. 598).

species.name: Icèle spatulée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or sandy-mud bottoms with stones with salinities of 24.7-34.2 ppt (Ref. 4698).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds mainly large bottom invertebrates, rarely small mollusks (Ref. 4698).

species.name: Ide
species.description: Usually inhabits large lowland rivers and nutrient-rich lakes. Adults are solitary while juveniles are gregarious. Undertakes migration to tributaries to spawn in moderate current on gravel or submerged vegetation. Feeds on various aquatic and terrestrial animals and plant material. Larger individuals feed mainly on fishes. Feeding larvae and juveniles thrive in a wide variety of shoreline habitats and leave the shores for deeper waters when growing. Reported to sometimes hybridizes with Aspius aspius (Ref. 59043). Its flesh is not tasty (Ref. 30578). Aquarium keeping: at least 10 individuals; minimum aquarium size >200 cm; not recommended for home aquariums (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Idenburg tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rainforest streams, rivers and creeks.  Often found in hilly or mountainous terrain to elevations of at least 800 m.

species.name: Idiacanthe ruban
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic in depths exceeding 500 m (Ref. 7249) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Females undergo diel vertical migrations (Ref. 7249).

species.name: Idiastion hageyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to occupy steep boulder and sediment-laden bottoms, along 60° slope (Ref. 75873).

species.name: Idiastion kyphos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Idiolychnus urolampus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic in nearshore areas or at seamounts (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Idukki Mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is characterized by rocky substratum (patches of cobbles, boulders and gravelly sand occur at certain places) and intermittent occurrence of moderately dense riparian vegetation. Syntopic with Anguilla bengalensis bengalensis, Danio malabaricus, Rasbora daniconius, Garra mullya, Dawkinsia filamentosa, Haludaria fasciatus, Pristolepis malabaricus, Etroplus suratensis, E. maculatus, Mesonoemacheilus triangularis, Xenentodon cancila, Mastacembelus armatus, Macrognathus guentheri (Ref. 94429).

species.name: Igarapé catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams that are permanently flowing and well-oxygenated (Ref. 56211).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slopes and seamounts (Ref. 41299).  Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded stomach contents with sea urchins, brittle stars, and grains of sand (likely ingested during their feeding on the benthos) (Ref. 127986).

species.name: Ikara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms of the shelf and the uppermost slope (Ref. 5578).  Depth range from 17-300 m, and up to depth of 462 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feed on all kinds of benthic animals, also on fish offal (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 4.2-4.6 cm long and 2.7-2.9 cm wide (Ref. 41250).  About 40-72 eggs are lain by an individual in a year (Ref. 41250).  Caught by ski-boat anglers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Iksookimia hugowolfeldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iksookimia koreensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Iksookimia longicorpa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in clear, slow moving shallow water over sand or small pebbles, or stagnant areas along upper and middle river courses.  The species consumes a wide variety of food, including most aquatic algae, small crustaceans and aquatic insect larvae.  The spawning season is supposed to be in May.

species.name: Ili marinka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Issyk-kul proper, spawning occurs over stony bottom, from May until mid July.  Captured by fishermen during spring until autumn near the shore.  Enters the tributaries of the Issyk-kul in spring, at the end of April and the beginning of May (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Iluocoetes fimbriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from the intertidal zone and brackish areas out to about 600 m (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Ilyophis arx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the lower continental slope at 1,465-2,070 m (Ref. 6726).  Carnivorous, feeding primarily on galatheid crustaceans (Ref. 6726).  Probably spawn in June-July (Ref. 6726).

species.name: Ilyophis nigeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 26895.

species.name: Ilyophis robinsae

species.name: Ilyophis saldanhai

species.name: Imai's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes in 50-70 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Imamura's ghost flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Imitator blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Imitator cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools.

species.name: Imitator damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer reef slopes (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Imitator dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically observed and collected from a current-swept rubble field where individuals are perched on small 5-10 cm long pieces of coralline-algae-encrusted coral rubble, and would quickly retreat under the rubble when approached (Ref. 115492).

species.name: Immaculate damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky or weedy inshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Immaculate dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154). Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Immaculate puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits weedy areas, often in estuaries; seagrass beds (Ref. 41878) and mangrove areas in 1-1.5 m. Solitary (Ref. 90102). Specimens caught by trawling over silty bottoms in 17 m. (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Immigrant goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was observed in vegetated [Lessepsian seagrass Halophila stipulacea (Forsskål) Ascherson, 1867] soft bottom and sloping habitats and also prefers areas where the water movement is limited, such as in sheltered bays. Populations were observed at 5-20 m depth but were more abundant at 7-15 m depth with approximately 1-3 individuals per sq.m (Ref. 119377).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks of moderate current velocity between 80 and 980 m elevation, over sand, gravel or mud substrata.  Feeds on aquatic insects especially dipterans (Ref. 36880).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. species.name: Imperial goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large vertical burrows of crustaceans on sloping silty sand and mud bottoms in 15-20 m (Ref. 90102). Seen together with Apogon, Acanthocepola Gymnothorax, Nemipterus, Muraenichthys, Yirrkala, Priolepis, Oxymetopon species, Oxymetopon cyanoctenosum, Yongeichthys criniger, Amblypomacentrus breviceps, and unidentified gobiids, flatfish, muraenids.

species.name: Imposter fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary in coastal, lagoon, and outer reefs, 1-10 m deep (Ref. 90102). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). A mimic of Meiacanthus smithi (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Imposter lanternfish
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Imspringer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal flats and rock shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Inanga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in a wide variety of habitat, but mostly in still or slow-flowing waters, mainly in streams, rivers and lakes within a short distance of the sea.  Can survive in salinities up to 50 ppt.  Feed on aquatic and terrestrial insects, and crustaceans.  Adults typically migrate downstream into estuaries during high spring tides in autumn to spawn on fringing vegetation.  Spawning does not occur beyond the river estuaries, making this species 'only marginally catadromous' (Ref. 46888).  Many perish after spawning but some survive  another year.  Eggs develop out of water for two weeks and hatch upon the arrival of the next spring tide.  Newly hatched larvae spend their first 5-6 months at sea before returning to fresh shoals of whitebait during spring.  An important component of whitebait fisheries throughout the Southern Hemisphere (Ref. 44894).  Utilized fresh and eaten fried (Ref. 9988, 44894).

species.name: Inayat’s goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Incan cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Incandescent basslet
species.description: Apparently a cryptic species, collected in small rocky  crevice along a steep limestone coral reef drop-off (Ref. 120708).

species.name: Incara multisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Incised gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reefs (Ref. 7300).  Usually caught in less than 200 meters depth (Ref. 54394).

species.name: Incisilabeo behri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in upland reaches of the Mekong. Inhabits rocky stretches of the main stem of Mekong during the dry season and moves into tributary streams during high waters (Ref. 12693). Found in riffle and slow deep reaches (Ref. 37769). Herbivorous, feeding on algae, phytoplankton and periphyton. Not known to persist in impoundments (Ref. 12693). At Stung Treng below the Khone Falls, the species migrates upstream at the start of the rainy season in May-June and downstream in the dry season from November to February. At Sambor and Kratie as well as just south of Khone Falls, it moves downstream at the onset of the rainy season and upstream in the dry season. The reason for such movement seems to be the presence of the important tributary system, Sekong-Sesan-Srepok rivers. Fishermen reported that this fish migrates from this system into the Mekong during receding water and migrates upstream the tributaries during the rainy season, possibly to spawn. Upstream the Khone Falls, this fish begins migrating upstream in the dry season (February-May) and continues into the beginning of the rainy season. This movement may, in fact, be two separate migrations: a dry season non-reproductive migration of smaller fish and an early rainy season migration of larger fish in spawning condition. Undertakes upstream migrations from Khone Falls all the way to Chiang Khong in northern Thailand which are triggered by the increase of water levels and the change in water-color from clear to red-brown. Migrates upstream in schools together with other cyprinids such as Labeo cf. pierrei, Cirrhinus microlepis, Labeo chrysophekadion and Cyclocheilichthys enoplos as well as the loach, Botia modesta (Ref. 37770). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Incomati chiselmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in cool rocky flowing-water habitats; occurs in schools of up to 50-100 fishes (Ref. 52193). It scrapes `aufwuchs' and benthic invertebrates from rocks (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Occasionally caught by anglers (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Incomati suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky rapids and cascades in altitudes of 900-1,200 m; prefers deeper waters (30-60 cm) over cobbles (Ref. 26172, 52193). It feeds on benthic invertebrates such as mayfly and caddis fly nymphs, blackfly and midge larvae and small snails (Ref. 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Breeds during summer and is a partial spawner (Ref. 52193). Increasing extraction and regulation of river water as well as pollution threaten this species (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Inconnu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Occurs in coastal brackish waters near mouths of rivers, but usually in rivers or some land-locked lakes (Ref. 4779).  At the sea, it is found throughout basin in pelagic zone with temperatures below 18° C and 20-50 m deep (Ref. 59043).  Juveniles and adult overwinter and forage at the sea.  Encountered in large lowland rivers during migration (Ref.  59043).  Adults feed mostly on small fishes; young eat aquatic insect larvae and planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 4779).  During spawning migration, it feeds little if at all (Ref. 27547).  Spawns on gravel shallows (Ref. 59043).  Flesh is white, sweet and slightly oily (Ref. 27547).  Sold fresh or frozen.

species.name: Inconsistent dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inconspicious barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, sandy and vegetated areas.  Feeds on insect, weeds and vegetable debris (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Inconspicuous blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mangrove swamps and saline creeks (Ref. 9786, 44894). Occurs infringing coastal mangroves in brackish or marine waters. Aggregations shelter among submerged roots or inundated leaves and branches (Ref. 44894). This is a planktivorous species which adapts well to freshwater environment. May occur in large schools, frequently in muddy waters. Sympatric with P. cyanodorsalis over part of its range (Ref. 9786). Probably more widespread, but has escaped notice due to its small size and largely inaccessible habitat (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Indawgyi stream catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian bandfish
species.description: Caught by commercial deep-sea shrimp trawler in bycatch landings (Ref. 88162).

species.name: Indian blind catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in wells.  Migrate from one well to another through underground water channels (Ref. 43626).

species.name: Indian blue ricefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs near the coast, but may live in freshwater as well as in brackish habitats.

species.name: Indian Bunquelovely
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian carplet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds, ditches, nullahs and slow moving streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Indian coolie-loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow slow-moving waters with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Indian deepsea herring
species.description: Needs better reference.  Andaman Sea, 11°31'40"N, 92°46'40"E, Investigator station 115, 188-220 fathoms.

species.name: Indian deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms.  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Indian dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian fanray
species.description: A narrow-ranging species confined to continental shelf and possibly a benthic species (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Indian frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species that occurs to a depth of at least 25 m.

species.name: Indian gagata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fresh and tidal rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Indian glass barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the middle-depth area of streams, ponds and tanks.  Occurs in shallow and relatively deep areas of streams, both in still and relatively fast-flowing waters.  Form shoals with 15-30 individuals.  Spawns at dusk or dawn in shallow water with about 30 eggs scattered at a time; egg hatch within 24 hours.  Feeds mainly on insects, but also takes plants (Ref. 6028).  Rarely seen in markets, probably used to make prahoc.  Occasionally imported in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Popular for ornamental purposes (Ref. 44325).

species.name: Indian glassy fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sluggish and standing water.  A common species proliferating in impoundments.  Most abundant during the rainy season.  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 12693), worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Breeds everywhere during the rains.  Builds a nest and guards its young.  Rare in markets and often found in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Indian gold-ring bristle-tooth
species.description: Inhabits sheltered inner reef crests and slopes. Usually among large corals or in gutters, singly or in small groups (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Indian golden-barred butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Indian handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on muddy substrates (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Indian hook-teeth moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian hump head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Indian longtailed sand-eel
species.description: Inhabits river mouths and coastal lagoons.

species.name: Indian megamouth dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian mimic goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs and coral areas. Mimics and aggregates with Lutjanus kasmira during the day. Disperses at night to feed.

species.name: Indian mottled eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in freshwaters, but also occurs in estuaries and in the sea during early life and near maturity (Ref. 4832).  Occurs in freshwater streams, pools and reservoirs and commonly found in mud substrates of tanks and in deep rock pools of rivers (Ref. 41236).  Most common eel in Indian inland waters.  There exists a good export market for both live elvers and eels.  Highly prized as food fish because of its nutritional value.  Fish mucous from live fish mixed with rice or wheat flour is used as medicine for arthritis (Ref. 44150).

species.name: Indian mud moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and river mouths (Ref. 4832, 48635). Found usually in muddy estuaries, also enters lower portion of rivers, in 1-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Indian mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Indian Ocean mimic surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow lagoon and seaward reefs, in areas of mixed coral, rock or sand. Juveniles mimic the cryptic Centropyge eibli (Ref. 9710, 48637).

species.name: Indian Ocean slender mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184) found on mud flats (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Indian Ocean twospot cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow protected water, sheltering among the spines of Diadema sea-urchins in groups of up to about 30 individuals (number depends on the size of the urchin and the length of the fish). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Indian ornate dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear coastal and inner reefs.  Shallow coral and algae habitat.  Usually mixes with other species when feeding (Ref. 48636).  Females form small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Indian perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian potasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit freshwaters and tidal rivers.  Its bright color and small size attract aquarists.  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Indian ring skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205); approximately 6 cm long (Ref. 114953).  Utilized for its meat (Ref.58048).

species.name: Indian river shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in middle and upper reaches of rivers.  Also occur in ponds, beels, ditches and inundated fields (Ref. 1479).  Minimum depth assumed based on it being a surface feeder, maximum depth based on study site in Bangladesh (Ref. 128398). More data needed.

species.name: Indian sabertooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species (Ref. 4478).  Feeds on other midwater fishes (Ref. 4763).

species.name: Indian sabretooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at 0-800 m (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36017).

species.name: Indian sail-fin surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon and seaward reefs to depths greater then 30 m; juveniles in sheltered inner reef areas (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Adults usually occur in pairs. Juveniles solitary and commonly among staghorn corals in lagoons or protected reefs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Indian sharpnose ray
species.description: Occurs on continental shelf and feeds on bottom-dwelling organisms (Ref. 4832).    Apparaently move inshore to breed and with litters of probably 2 pups (Ref. 114953). Taken sa small bycatch by trawls off India (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Indian signalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian spaghetti-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow hill streams, buried in mud (Ref. 4832).  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Indian spotted coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary in caves or under large overhanging corals to about 20 m depth (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Indian torrent catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pebbly beds in swift currents at the base of hills (Ref. 4833).  Found among rocks and boulders on the bottom of fast flowing upland streams.  Diet consists of aquatic insects.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Indian unpatterned moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian velvetchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indian white spotted moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from three type specimens collected by demersal trawl at about 200 m depth (on the basis of holotype, not known for paratypes) (Ref. 121832).

species.name: Indienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sporadic distribution (Ref. 48635).  Occurs only at oceanic islands.  Inhabits clear waters of steep drop-offs; rarely seen in less than 30 m.  It has been taken in depths of 120 m and may occur deeper.  Also found in caves and crevices.  Often swims upside-down against the roofs of caves or archways (Ref. 37816). Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Indifferent eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indigo hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting coral reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Indo-Pacific barracudina
species.description: Adult specimens were caught by bottom trawl at an estimated depth of ca. 300 m based on other fishes collected in the bycatch (Ref. 128666).

species.name: Indo-Pacific ocellated flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indo-Pacific shorttail conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Indo-Pacific slender worm-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in loose sand and fine gravel (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302) and burrowing species found in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Indo-Pacific snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Indo-Pacific tropical sand goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in small groups (Ref. 90102). Found over sandy and muddy bottoms, often in weedy areas of intertidal zone; also in  mangroves, estuaries, lagoons and rivers (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Indochinese sheatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainstreams and tributaries (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on insects and small shrimps (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Indonesia weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often seen in weedy reefs typically in cooler waters in areas of upwelling (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Indonesian Angel Shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indonesian damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs where currents are strong.  Often in large schools that cloud the water above the rocks when feeding on zooplankton.  They nest among the rocks (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Indonesian deep-sea worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indonesian eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Indonesian flag dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Indonesian flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in near-shore surface waters, never spread to open sea (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Indonesian gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore. Its biology is probably similar to A. chacunda.

species.name: Indonesian goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit mangrove estuaries as well as clear rainforest streams near the sea (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Indonesian Houndshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably occurring on the outer continental shelf and upper slope.  Females have litters of 6-11 where reproductive mode is viviparous, with histotrophy (no yolk-sac placenta); size at birth about 28- 30 cm TL (Ref. 80994).

species.name: Indonesian leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland streams and peats (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Indonesian longfinned eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only plain-colored, long-finned eel found in the Indonesian area.  Commonly found under rocks in clear fast-flowing streams (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Indonesian numbfish
species.description: The biology of this species is largely unknown, but presumed to feed on small benthic invertebrates as do other numbfishes.  Females are presumed to be sexually mature at 30.6 cm TL; max length of 16.0 cm TL is that of an  adolescent male (Ref. 116737).

species.name: Indonesian ocellated flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sand bottoms.

species.name: Indonesian sawtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found swimming in loose groups around rocky outcrops, usually in high energy zones. Sometime solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Prefer the areas with cool up-wellings (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Indonesian sharpnose ray
species.description: Demersal on the continental and insular shelves of up to approximately 40 m depth.  Birth size is 7.0 - 9.0 cm WD (Ref. 110363).

species.name: Indonesian shortsnout spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently occurs on or near the bottom of upper continental and insular slopes, but depth distribution is undetermined; probably on shallower water than its congeners.  Presumably feeds on small fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans.  Viviparous, with yolk-sac dependency.  Gives birth to 3 -10 pups, but gestation period is unknown.  Males mature at about 43 cm TL and females by 61 cm TL; with largest embryo measured at 18 cm. The species is a very common catch component fo the demersal longline fishery in deepwater areas in eastern Indonesia.  It is caught for its meat, fins and liver oil (Ref. 58042).

species.name: Indonesian shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal inshore on inner insular shelf. Feeds on small crustaceans and probably small bony fishes. Males mature at 70-72 cm TL, females at 75 cm TL. Females have litters of 4-13 pups (Ref. 114953). Caught by fisherman using small demersal gill and trammel nets, and small demersal longlines (Ref. 72461).

species.name: Indonesian Speckled Catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to be caught occasionally by demersal fisheries, but no depth distribution information is available (Ref. 59315).

species.name: Indonesian wobbegong
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The depth range of this species is not well defined; specimens observed at fish markets
were presumably caught by longline fishers operating in deeper parts of the continental shelf.  It probably prefers deeper colder water with a single shallow water observation from the east
coast of Bali where cold-water upwelling is common.  All males (n = 43) mature by ca 90 cm TL; smallest mature female recorded at 94 cm TL, two pregnant females recorded at 104 and 108 cm TL, smaller of the two pregnant females contained 4 mid-term embryos between 13 and 14 cm TL (Ref. 84278).

species.name: Indoreonectes evezardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species.

species.name: Indostomus crocodilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from blackwater stream, close to the bottom, among submerged vegetation.

species.name: Indostomus spinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow to standing waters from among roots of shore vegetation and thick beds of leaf litter (Ref. 38647).  Found in streams, lakes and swamps (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Indus catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Indus snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountains streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).  Found usually in large deep and rapid flowing rivers, above 2566 m (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Inegocia ochiaii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inexplicable shrimpgoby
species.description: Found in silty sand of shallow protected reef flats and lagoons (Ref. 34765).  Occurs in sheltered coastal sand flats and in estuarines (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Inflated whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Inhaca fringelip
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iniistius auropunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas; quickly dives into the sand when threatened (Ref. 39775).

species.name: Iniistius brevipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iniistius cyanifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iniistius evides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy open areas near shallow reefs at about 5 m.  Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Iniistius geisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iniistius spilonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iniistius trivittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles in coastal waters along reef edges on sand or rubble, or open patches on reef.  Adults mainly in deep outer reef habitats where they occur in small loose group along sand ridges (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Iniistius verrens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inimicus gruzovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Inimicus japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Food fish (Ref. 559).  Commercially cultured in Japan.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Inimicus joubini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inimicus smirnovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inkomati mountain catfish
species.description: Occurs in flowing sections of rivers with rocky substrates (Ref. 123712).

species.name: Inlecypris jayarami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Innerspotted sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary on sand at base of coral overhangs (Ref. 90102). Specimens collected from sand or sand and rubble substrata.

species.name: Inpa tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Inquiline snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the mantle cavity of the scallop, Placopecten magellanicus (Ref. 51661). Benthic species (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Inscribed wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow rocky reef areas and associated with kelp (Ecklonia) beds. Collected at depths of 17 m (Ref.26203).

species.name: Inshore hagfish
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230).  Usually buries itself in bottom mud (Ref. 26686). Migrates into deeper water to spawn (Ref. 51361, 51374).  This is the only member of the family having a seasonal reproductive cycle (Ref. 51361).  Food fish in Japan.  Hide is processed into leather and exported worldwide, usually as 'eel' leather.

species.name: Insignia prawn-goby
species.description: Inhabits brackish tide pools (Ref. 1602) and sandy mangrove habitats (Ref. 37816). Also found in sand rubble bottoms in 2-10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Insular bunquelovely
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Insular pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits turtle-grass beds, usually in coves on the seaward sides of islands (Ref. 5521).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Intermediate cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in reefs over sand or mud bottoms.  Solitary in caves to 20 m depth (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Intermediate flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Active during the day (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on bottom-living animals.  Also caught by divers.

species.name: Intermediate flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic surface waters.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Intermediate lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Interochromis loocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on debris (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Interrupted dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tidal areas of small streams in mangrove swamps. Forms aggregations near surface of marine lake, tidal streams and mangrove areas (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Investigator perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Investigator pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Some specimens have been taken in surface tow nets and with nightlight and dipnets; others taken in a dredge sample (Ref. 5316).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Found in sand, mud and coral bottoms in 2-45 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Iodotropheus declivitas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iodotropheus stuartgranti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ioichthys kashkini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iotabrycon praecox
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ipnops meadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ipnops murrayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Ipojuca catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iporanga tooth carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iran cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iran cave barb
species.description: Cave-restricted fish.  Max. length (Yazdan Keivany, pers. comm., 2003).

species.name: Iranian Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on bottoms covered with stones and boulders and with rapid currents (Ref. 104815).

species.name: Iranocichla hormuzensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to salty streams (Ref. 12251, 36597), rarely in freshwaters (Ref. 36597), which are constantly warm, unshaded, usually with muddy bottoms, with little vegetation other than encrusting algae, and are subject to massive flooding during winter rains (Ref. 12251, 36597). Stomach contents consist of various algae (including diatoms) and detritus, indicating that it feeds on bottom deposits (Ref. 36597) and by scraping aufwuchs (Ref. 12251, 36597). This maternal mouthbrooder can brood up to 38 large eggs; females carry eggs in March (Ref. 12251, 36597). Because of the restricted range of this fish and the continual warfare and oil pollution in the area, this fish may be well on its way to extinction (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Iranocichla persa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iraq blind barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Co-exists with another cave fish species, Caecocypris basimi, in a sinkhole at the Sheik Hadid Shrine (Ref. 5326).

species.name: Ira’s snook
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was observed in the more saline waters, close to the outlet channel of the lagoon to the sea, as confirmed by local fishermen. It was also found in the center of the lagoon. None of the specimens collected from the lagoon were preserved, and these were lost, but a picture of the largest individual (53.55 cm SL) was taken (Ref. 121036).

species.name: Irian Jaya rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rainforest creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Iridescent glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, streams and lakes (Ref. 56749).  Found in sluggish rivers and floodplains of the lower Mekong.  Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 12693) and insects (Ref. 9497).  Reported to be a mouth brooder.  Occasionally seen in markets.  Its bright coloration makes it a desirable aquarium fish (Ref. 12693).  Used as feeds for caged fishes (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Irina’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most Trimma species are found between 10-30 m, with relatively few occurring in depths shallower than this. In this case of Trimma irinae, this species occur at depths below about 50 m (Ref. 95906).

species.name: Irish pollan
species.description: Lacustrine, in open waters (Ref. 59043). Feeds on bottom invertebrates and on semi-pelagic crustaceans (Mysis relicta), and also on their own eggs (Ref. 6258). Status of threat: Threatened by eutrophication, introductions and warming of lakes. Only remaining abundant population in Lough Neagh (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Irksone eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarest species of the genus; known only from the holotype (Ref. 43688).

species.name: Ironcolor shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, vegetated, sand-bottomed pools and slow runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans (amphipods, cladocerans, and ostracods), aquatic insects (caddisfly, midge, and mayfly larvae, and corixids), and terrestrial insects (ants), and filamentous algae (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Irrawaddy river shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Irvineia orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds at least in part on insects (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Irvineia voltae
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des schilbeidae. Probably carnivorous, feeding at least partly on small crustaceans (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Isbrueckerichthys alipionis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Isbrueckerichthys calvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually along the bottom among rocks and stones, just under small waterfalls, of a small creek flowing through a landscape of mixed open field, riparian vegetation and forest, sometimes with a very degraded margin.  The stream has rocky bottom, with small to medium-sized rocks, loose stones and gravel and some small pools along the streams with sand and mud on the bottom (Ref. 57731 ).

species.name: Isbrueckerichthys duseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Isbrueckerichthys epakmos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species inhabits the clear headwaters of rivers, in moderate to strong current, on bottoms with loose stones and sandy patches, 700m above the sea level in the main remnant of the Atlantic Forest, southeastern Brazil (Ref. 52250).

species.name: Isbrueckerichthys saxicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually on the bottom among rocks and stones in a small creek flowing through a landscape of mixed open fields and riparian vegetation, sometimes with a very degraded margin.  The stream has rocky bottom with small to medium-sized rocks,  loose stones and gravel, sometimes with sand and mud on the small pools bottoms, and has clear to turbid and moderate to strong flowing water (Ref. 57731).

species.name: Isbrücker's Hypopygus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ischikauia steenackeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ishikawa's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools.  Eggs are deposited in the peribranchial cavity of sea squirts (Ref. 34819, 41071).

species.name: Isichthys henryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head, the dorsal region and some parts of the ventral region; absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located.  Electric organ discharge (EOD) rates are of low frequency and sexually dimorphic as to waveform (Ref. 10011).

species.name: Isis goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on gorgonians, commensal (Ref. 43239). Exclusively associated with Isis hippuris in 1-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Island frillfin
species.description: Inhabits rocky tide pools and along water's edge, but mostly on unsheltered shores.

species.name: Island frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Island goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral or rocky habitats (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Island gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This occasionally schooling species inhabits shallow rock and coral reefs (Ref. 510).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Island gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Island kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky areas, subtidal and to 49 m depth (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Island longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef (Ref. 75154) and tide pools (Ref. 27772).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Island Sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 128120).

species.name: Island triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Isle of Pines rivulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits permanent and temporary waters, preferring clear water without much aquatic vegetation and frequenting bottoms of small stones or course sand. Hides in the substrate, often staying for considerable periods of time. Largest adults were taken from small puddles in rice fields that had dried up after irrigation was suspended. Associates with Gambusia punctata, G. puncticulata and Cichlasoma tetracanthus (Ref. 13498). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Iso flosmaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore and in tide pools.

species.name: Isorineloricaria acuarius
species.description: The holotype was collected on a sandy run with moderate flow, in Rio Portuguesa . It was a nuptial male with breeding odontodes, suggesting that January is within the time of spawning as was suggested for A. ammophilus. It appears to be restricted to white waters (Ref. 129253).

species.name: Isorineloricaria tenuicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Isorineloricaria villarsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Issyk-kul naked loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawning occurs during the first half of June (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Issyk-kul' minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Isthmian goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is found in brackish coastal areas with a rock and algae substrate.  It was collected in large numbers, 30-80 per lot by Dawson in 1972 and 1974, from the Gatun locks of the Panama Canal and Limon Bay, the Atlantic entrance to the canal (Ref. 104557).

species.name: Isthmian priapella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in loose aggregations in eddying currents or rapids, even leaping up out of the water to capture flying insects.  Young occur in large number in the crevices of rocks along the banks, out of the current.

species.name: Isthmoheros tuyrensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A detritivore-herbivore that occurs in slow-moving waters (Ref.  114771).

species.name: Isthmus goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms in 3-15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Istiblennius flaviumbrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Istiblennius rivulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in very shallow water (as shallow as 10 cm) on rocky shores (Ref. 9962).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Istiblennius steindachneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Istigobius campbelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in sandy bottoms of shallow waters.  Also observed to live solitarily or in small schools near crevices or under stones.  Occurs at 21.5 °C (Ref. 4959).

species.name: Istigobius hoshinonis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on sand or mud bottoms in shallow water.  May be solitary or in small schools near crevices or under stones.  Lays its eggs under shells where males care for the young; spawning took place from May to July.

species.name: Italian bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic waters on low-lying plains, with little current (Ref. 26100).  Inhabits well oxygenated, clear montane and hilly streams and small rivers.  Feeds on drifting insects or invertebrates fallen on waters surface. Threatened due to the pollution, impoundment of streams and invasion by non-native species (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Italian spring goby
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. A short-lived species (less than 2 years) which occurs in small and karstic springs and streams, densely vegetated channels and slow-flowing streams (Ref. 59043); with constant water temperature, on sand or gravel with or without vegetation, also in silty areas, provided that the water remains clear (Ref. 26100).  Feeds on small invertebrates.  Spawns after first winter (February-July); females may spawn more than once during this season.  Males defend the eggs deposited in cavities under stones, plant material or shells.  Postlarvae pelagic.  This species is threatened by water abstraction, which lowers the water table and habitat destruction caused by desiccation of some springs (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Itapoá toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis agreste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a mid-small size river with width up to 8 m, in a moderate slope with clear and cold water, with transparency of about 2 m. The river is characterized by mainly turbulent water flow , with alternating areas of currents and pools, though a predominance of moderate to strong drifts. The substrate is composed of rocks and sand. Collected together with Astyanax bimaculatus (Linnaeus), Callichthys callichthys (Linnaeus), Geophagus brasiliensis (Quoy & Gaimard), Rhamdia quelen (Quoy & Gaimard) and Poecilia reticulata Peters (Ref. 94155).

species.name: Ituglanis amazonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives mainly in little forest creeks with notable current and a sandy-rocky substrate.  It is not known whether it feeds on flesh or blood of living animals or it lives on carrion.  Opercle hooks enable it to cling to and to dig little tunnels into its prey's flesh (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Ituglanis amphipotamus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing medium-sized river, running over rocky and sandy bottoms at approximately 40 m above sea level.

species.name: Ituglanis apteryx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis bambui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper mainstream tributaries inside a cave, near the sinkhole end (Ref. 55401).  A solitary species with swimming activity on the bottom, in midwater and sometimes extending to the surface (Ref. 55401).

species.name: Ituglanis boitata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is often associated with clear water, rocky bottom, and small current streams and rivers in the middle and upper portions of three drainages (the rio Araranguá, rio Mampituba and rio Tramandaí basins) and has never been found in lagoons or surroundings swamps of the coastal plain (Ref. 104908).

species.name: Ituglanis cahyensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brown waters with moderate flowing current and sandy or gravel bottom.  Feeds on insect larvae, nymphs and organic matter (Ref. 57703).
