species.name: Ituglanis compactus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis eichorniarum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis epikarsticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools in a set of rimstone dams (wall-shaped barriers of calcite, aragonite or other chemical deposits that impound water pools), 10-30 cm deep and with rocky bottom (Ref. 55401).  A solitary species, swimming on the bottom, along the walls and sometimes at the surface of the pools (Ref. 55401).

species.name: Ituglanis goya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis gracilior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis guayaberensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis herberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis ina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis macunaima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis mambai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subterranean stream inside the cave with slow to fast-moving-waters, 10-90 cm deep on average, and bottom composed basically of sand, silt, some gravels and boulders.  Occurs solitarily with swimming activity on the bottom and sometimes in the midwater.  Exhibits cryptobiotic habits, hiding intro the gravels and under boulders when disturbed, and showing a negative response to carbide and flashlight.  Prefers slow-moving pools (Ref. 75008).

species.name: Ituglanis metae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis nebulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis paraguassuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis parahybae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis parkoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis passensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small riffles with slow current 15-20 cm deep on average.  Exhibits crypto-biotic habits, hiding in the gravel bottom or under limestone blocks.  No observed agonistic behavior (Ref. 46923).

species.name: Ituglanis proops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ituglanis ramiroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a side pool five meters above the main stream level, formed by water percolating from the rock.  A solitary species, swimming on the bottom and displaying rare events of surface swimming (Ref. 55401).  Exhibits weak cryptobiotic habits, sometimes hiding under boulders, but not burying in the silt (Ref. 55401).

species.name: Ivano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms close to coral reefs.  Occurs in small groups.  Juveniles are solitary (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Iwame trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ixinandria steinbachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in fast flowing waters between 15 and 65 cm depth, especially in places with filamentous algae, in mountainous areas at altitudes ranging from around 200 to 2900 meters above sea level.  During the day, it occurs in fast flowing and highly oxygenated waters, with stony bottom, usually hiding under the stones (Ref. 86762).

species.name: Iyidere goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a stream with fresh, running water and a bottom with rounded pebbles, at an altitude of 11 m above sea level and 3.4 km away from the sea. Syntopic species found with this species were Alburnus bipunctatus, Barbus tauricus, Capoeta banarescui, Chalcalburnus chalcoides, Chondrostoma colchicum, Cobitis splendens; Lampetra lanceolata, Leuciscus cephalus, Liza aurata; Mugil cephalus, Rutilus frisii, and Salmo labrax (Ref. 75708).

species.name: Izmir chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing to standing water (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Izmir mminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Izmir nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and in water courses on low plains, with little current.  Is threatened due to pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Iznik loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Iznik shemaya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Izu dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coarse sand, sometimes with broken shells and coral rubble (Ref. 11666).

species.name: Izu Islands triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on beach rocks (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Izu ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on coarse sand, sometimes with algae or rubble (Ref. 11666).

species.name: Izu scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf; in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Izu stingray
species.description: Occurs in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 7445).  Almost with certainty to occur deeper than 20 m (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Işıklı gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jabarichromis pfefferi
species.description: Adults inhabit lakes, often solitary (Ref. 86760).  Feed mainly on shrimps (Ref. 30769).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Jacareí toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jack Dempsey
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae. Occurs in swampy areas with warm, murky water.  Found in weedy, mud-bottomed and sand-bottomed canals and drainage ditches (Ref. 5723).  Prefers coastal plains and slow moving waters of the lower river valleys (Ref. 7335).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and fish (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Jackson's barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and streams, both temporary and permanent; feeds on insect larvae and bottom debris (Ref. 4903). Upstream spawning migrations reported from Lake Rukwa drainage (Ref. 27292).

species.name: Jacuhy pleco
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jae barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jaggedhead gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater species (Ref. 9771).  Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Bony scutes reduce commercial value (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Jaguar dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A very aggressive species that readily attacks the camera when it sees its own reflection.  Mainly found on deep coastal slopes with remote sponges and crinoids in about 30 m depth and often occurs in pairs (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Jaguar guapote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, preferring turbid waters and mud bottoms of the highly eutrophic lakes (Ref. 7335).  Found in springs and ponds over detritus and sand bottom (Ref. 5723).  Commonly found in very warm, oxygen depleted inundation lakes (Ref. 8978).  Highly predaceous, feeding mainly on small fishes and macroinvertebrates (Ref. 7335; 44091).  Oviparous, spawns in batches (Ref. Highly esteemed as food fish (Ref. 44091).  Maximum length 63 cm TL (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Jaguar livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on photo submitted, this species grow up to 8.0 cm TL and live for up to 7 years in captivity (P. Petersen, pers.comm. 12/2022).

species.name: Jamaican killifish
species.description: Inhabits shallow (1.5 m), crystal clear waters (pH 8.2) with a bottom of sand and some soft patches of silt.  Hides among submerged and floating aquatic vegetation.  Feeds on damselfly and dragonfly nymphs, other aquatic larvae, ostracods, copepods and snails.  Eggs measure 1.2-1.4 mm in diameter and hatch in about 9 days (Ref. 13498).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Jamal's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits frequently dense thickets of staghorn Acropora corals, encrusting layers of Galaxea corals, or rocky debris at depths of about 9-16 m. Either encountered solitarily or in loose groups of 2-4 individuals that range over an area of about 1.5-2 m. Observed to occasionally enter sponges of the genus Callyspongia. Its color pattern and behavior indicate a mimetic relationship with the common damselfish Chromis retrofasciata with which it co-occurs (Ref. 74994).

species.name: Jambeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jamei’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: James's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in middle and upper reaches of rivers.  More data needed.

species.name: Jameson's seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Estuarine species, usually in sponges (Ref. 9002).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Jamuna ailia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Jamur Lake grunter
species.description: Adults occur in a shallow lake with clear water and moderate aquatic vegetation (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Janbruin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in shallow rocky areas, but also found down to 80 m.  Flesh excellent.

species.name: Jandira toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Janet's shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly on steady sloping, sandy-rubble seafloor which is exposed to moderate to strong currents (Ref. 123124).

species.name: Jansen's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Apparently occurs at least at moderate depths (Ref. 54393).   A poorly known species; no habitat information and no recent sightings (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Janss' pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and reef crevices.  Also found in sheltered inner reefs, usually in caves with sponges and below large plate corals.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Very active cleaner and has cleaning station that is visited by apogonids and damsels where adults work in pairs (Ref. 48635).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018. Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: January tetra
species.description: Poisson. Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: January toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in shallow, flowing and standing waters that can warm up considerably. Occurs in company with other livebearers, such as Poecilia vivipara and Jenynsia lineata. A photo of this species taken from Santos channel, state of São Paulo, Brazil has a maximum length of 3.3 cm SL (photo by T. Vaske, Jr.).

species.name: Japan surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In clear lagoon and seaward reefs, usually in shallow exposed areas.  Found in small to large aggregations (Ref. 48637). Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102).  Feed on algae (Ref. 128523).

species.name: Japanese Amago
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are buried in unguarded nests (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese armorhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles pelagic, adults benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Japanese barracudina
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154). Feeds on small fishes rather than shrimps (Ref. 121637).

species.name: Japanese blacktail triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal rock pools and upper subtidal areas.  They feed on algae (Ref. 9173).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Japanese blue-spotted seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Important food fish.

species.name: Japanese butterflyray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottom in shallow waters (Ref. 11230).  Feeds on benthic animals.  Spines covered with skin with poisonous glands.  Ovoviviparous.  Used as 'kamaboko' material (Ref. 637). Caught often by demersal trawl, trammel and gillnet fisheries, and occasionally using tangle nets.Utilized for its meat, but of limited value due to its typically small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Japanese chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms and deep offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi- and mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Japanese codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rough, rocky bottom along the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Japanese cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy bottoms (Ref. 559).

species.name: Japanese deepwater clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese dory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Japanese dragonet
species.description: Inhabits coral and rocky reefs.  Found on algal covered rocks and boulders (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Japanese dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore and offshore species, demersal in intertidal habitats to depths of at east 220 m (Ref.58048). Found from the intertidal to the uppermost continental slope (Ref. 9862, 11230).  A carnivore feeding on benthic animals.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Caught occasionally by inshore, demersal longline fisheries. Utilized for its meat and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Japanese filamentous dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese fluvial sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom-dwelling fish of mountain streams.

species.name: Japanese fold dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms of rocky or coral reefs (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Japanese gissu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters.

species.name: Japanese gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling near shore over sand or mud, preferring warmer water than Konosirus punctatus. A filter-feeder; takes minute algae or organic matter. Breeds around May in Japanese waters.

species.name: Japanese gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larger individuals are found in deeper waters.  Feeds on euphausiids, prawns, benthic fishes, isopods, and polychaetes.

species.name: Japanese grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, estuaries and reaching up to middle parts of rivers, apparently able to tolerate freshwater (Ref. 189, 11230). Lives in not really clean water but not really turbid water either (Ref. 12218). Goes to the deep water areas of rivers at night (Ref. 12218). Planktivore (Ref. 12218). Spawns around three times in a lifetime and spawning occurs in between reeds (Ref. 12218). In Ariake Sound, Japan it breeds from May to August, the fishes running about 15 km up the Chikugo River and spawning in freshwater, the spherical eggs floating down and hatching near the river mouth. Its relatively large size makes it a more esteemed food fish than most Coilia. Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Japanese highfin deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf edges (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Japanese huchen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually inhabits lower and middle reaches of rivers and lakes.  A sea-run form is found in the eastern coast of Hokkaido.  Young feed mainly on aquatic insects while fishes more than 30 cm are completely piscivorous.  Spawns in spring in river branches, where the female lays 2,000-10,000 eggs on sandy or gravelly bottom.

species.name: Japanese icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Marine species which enters rivers and estuaries (Ref. 26334, 37812).

species.name: Japanese inflator filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottoms with green seaweed (Ref. 9137).  Secretive on deep coastal slopes, usually among soft corals (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on algae and crabs (Ref. 9137).  Capable of inflating its body like puffers (Ref. 9710, 48637).

species.name: Japanese lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Japanese lates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles ascend rivers.  Commercially cultured in Japan.

species.name: Japanese leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep muddy substrates from about 30 meters depth, but some individuals were found drifting with large Sargassum rafts over deep water, well away from the shore (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Japanese lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottoms with broken coral, shell, pebbles, and gray mud.  Feeds on bottom-living animals.

species.name: Japanese longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow to deep waters (Ref. 559), on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Rarely seen by divers but more commonly encountered in shallow waters (Ref. 90102).  Feeds mainly on amphipods, polychaetes, bivalves, gastropods and ophiuroids (Ref. 13374).  Minimum depth of 5 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Japanese lowfin deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese ornate dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently confined to coastal waters in rocky areas with seaweeds (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Japanese perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep trawling grounds to at least 200 m (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Japanese pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in inlet waters, occasionally entering brackish waters. Fingerlings are often seen in brackish river mouths (Ref. 58920). Move offshore with growth. Breed in the sea (Ref. 58920) from March to May; attach eggs to rocks in shingly areas at depths of around 20 m. Liver and ovaries extremely toxic, intestines slightly toxic; flesh, skin and testes not poisonous. Juveniles resemble Takifugu niphobles (Ref. 637). A prized food fish in Japan. Said to be commercially cultured in Japan at present. Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). One of the first vertebrates whose genome has been sequenced completely, 31,059 genes coding for 33,609 proteins (Ref. 58917).

species.name: Japanese pugnose grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon in depths shallower than 400 m.  Frequents waters of 5-7°C.  Polychaetes and euphausiids compose 30-60% of the diet of specimens from Japan, and prawns of minor importance.

species.name: Japanese pygmy seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poisson. This species was not associated with a particular host. It has been observed in association with mixed soft coral, Halimeda sp. (coralline algae) and hydroids on rocky reef walls and large boulders in both exposed and semi-sheltered locations (Ref. 118476)..

species.name: Japanese roughshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype trawled from a depth between 225 and 270 m (Ref. 31258).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese rubyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf area (Ref. 5213). Found to feed mainly on shrimp of the family Sergistidae and also on small mesopelagic fishes of the family Myctophidae, Astronesthidae and Paralepididae (Ref. 33669).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Japanese seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Japanese seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Zostera seagrass beds; also in estuaries. Length type refers to height (= TL - head length). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Japanese shortspined scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese sleeper ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and offshore (Ref. 9913, 11230).  Found on sand, often near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951).  Biology little known (Ref. 9913), but locally common in Taiwan and Japan (Ref. 114953). Produces 4-6 pups per litter. Maturity size of males known at 25 cm TL.  Not utilized for food. Capable of producing a moderate shock to humans (Ref. 114953).  Does not do well in aquariums (Ref. 12951).

species.name: Japanese slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in open water of impoundments and their tributaries, in fresh and brackish water.  Primarily a brackish water species (Ref.33312).  Anadromous (Ref. 37812).

species.name: Japanese snake blenny
species.description: Adults inhabit deep waters but rises to the surface at night.  Rare species (Ref. 559).  They live in tubes in fine sand or mud and rise to the surface at night where they fall prey to pelagic fishes (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Japanese soldierfish
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Japanese spiny dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japanese swallow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Hardy aquarium species; takes standard food such as chopped beef, freeze-dried shrimp, mysids, etc.  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Forms permanent harem groups composed of a single male  and several smaller females (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Japanese tenspined silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to inhabit the vicinity of river mouth basins, which may be considered strongly related to a minimum winter sea temperature of 16°C (less than 100 m depth).  Specimens were collected in inlet basins, river mouth basins, or on shallow sandy bottoms strongly affected by freshwater from nearby river mouths.  However, this species rarely occurs in the shallow coastal area with almost no freshwater effect.  One specimen (MUFS 9584, 135 mm SL, 3 July 1993), had a clearly matured or water-hardened (transparent) egg, giving an indication of the spawning season of the species (Ref. 58476).

species.name: Japanese thread-sail fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy or muddle areas (Ref. 9137).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Can also be found at 30 m depths (Ref. 11230).  A carnivore which feeds on fish and crabs (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Japanese velvet dogfish
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Japanese wedgefish
species.description: This species is currently known only from nearshore to offshore waters and have been collected by set net from 15-35 m, but was also reported to have been taken at 135 m by bottom trawl.  Based on photos of landed individuals, this species probably attains close to 3 m TL. The captive female individual held for at least 15 years in the Kagoshima City Aquarium reached to 2 m TL. This wedgefish is occasionally landed at fish markets in Kagoshima Prefecture and used for culinary purpose. Reported catches of the species were very rare in the East China Sea and is apparently restricted distribution and increasing rarity indicate that the species should immediately be included in the IUCN Red List CR “Critically Endangered” category, together with other congeners (Ref. 123186).

species.name: Japanese whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sporadic distribution (Ref. 48635), but mostly in deeper offshore waters.  Sometimes enters shallow estuaries or harbors (Ref. 48635).  Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Feeds on small shrimps.  Rarely caught.

species.name: Japigny kirschbaum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with Anostomus brevior and Cynopotamus essequibensis (Ref. 86967).

species.name: Japonoconger africanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic fish, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Japonoconger caribbeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japonoconger sivicolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Japonolaeops dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Marketed salt-dried.

species.name: Japonolycodes abei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters.

species.name: Jaquiá toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jari toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jarocho goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found between 3-25 m depth on high profile coral reefs typically dominated by Montastrea cavernosa (Linneaus), M. annularis (Ellis and Solander), Colpophyllia natans (Houttuyn) and skeletal reef framework. Elacatinus jarocho joins E. atronasus (Böhlke & Robins) as the only two species in the genus to school in the water column. Small to large aggregations (12-60 individuals) of E. jarocho were normally found close to the reef near high profile corals or overhangs. Such reef structure presumably provides shelter from direct sunlight because aggregations were usually observed in darker, shaded areas rather than in direct sunlight. Individuals of E. jarocho, unlike E. atronasus, were never observed stationary on any substrate, but rather hovered continuously about 5–25 cm above the reef, frequently in association with Coryphopterus hyalinus Böhlke & Robins or C. personatus (Jordan & Thompson). This species was not observed to clean other species or interact in other symbiotic relationships. Small and large individuals coexisted in the same aggregations and did not display territorial or hierarchical behaviors. Individual fish would often, though not always, move slowly toward cover when approached to less than 1 m by scuba divers (Ref. 58341).

species.name: Jarocho hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: This species currently has no information on ecology except that it is found in shallow waters less than 20 m, where it is hooked by fishermen (Ref. 92994).

species.name: Jaunet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs.  Often seen in schools near outcrops or drop-offs, often with other species (Ref. 9710), of up to about 30 to 40 individuals.  Small juveniles on shallow algae reef, often near freshwater run-offs (Ref. 48635).  Feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs, other crustaceans, cephalopods and some planktonic items.

species.name: Jaunet (Lutjanus vitta)
species.description: Genre de poissons. Adults are found in the vicinity of coral reefs, also areas with flat bottoms and occasional low coral outcrops, sponges, and sea whips.  They occur singly or in groups of up to about 30 individuals.  Feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs and other benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Jaunet à deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 9710, 48635) and outer reef slopes (Ref. 37816, 48635).  They sometimes form large schools of more than 100 individuals.  Often solitary (Ref. 48635).  Feed mainly on small fishes and crustaceans.  Generally uncommon (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Jaunet à une tache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef areas, usually close to shelter in the form of caves, large coral formations and wreckage.  Usually solitary; occasionally occurring in small groups.  They feed mainly on fishes and benthic crustaceans, primarily crabs (Ref. 37816) at night.  Flesh is sometimes ciguatoxic, and commonly so in Tuvalu (Ref. 9513).

species.name: Java damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit silty rubble reefs of lagoons and offshore areas.  They occur in small loose groups (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Java loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams with muddy bottom, among shore vegetation or leaf litter (Ref. 56749).  Found near the bottom in sluggish parts of rapidly flowing streams.  Usually occurs as scattered individuals over sand substrates in fairly shallow water.  Probably spawns in flooded forests in very shallow water.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Not fished commercially (Ref. 12693), but used as food for caged fishes (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Java rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky shores (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Java spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrowing species (Ref. 7300).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Java stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare and unknown species (Ref. 9863).

species.name: Javaen barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers of all sizes, but mainly in smaller streams, canals and on floodplains.  Occasionally found in impoundments, but usually stays in the flowing streams leading to the impoundment.  Moves into seasonally inundated areas and breeds at the start of the rainy season.  Young of the year appear in streams in July and August.  Adults leave the floodplains when the water recedes in December or January (Ref. 12693).  Captured from the wild for the ornamental fish trade in Thailand (Ref. 6459).  Marketed fresh or made into prahoc along the Tonle Sap (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Javan ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, apparently entering rivers and brackish water.

species.name: Javan pearlside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Javan whipray
species.description: Apparently benthic on soft bottoms near coast (Ref. 114953); inshore coastal habitats near mangroves, close to heavily human populated areas, thus making it accessible to fishers. Males mature at 17-18 cm WD while females at 18 cm WD. Size at birth 5-9 cm WD (Ref. 130662). Caught by trammel nets (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Javanese monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on sand or mud bottoms near reefs in depths up to about 30 m (Ref. 130620).

species.name: Javanese ricefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ditches, canals, ponds.  Occurs at the surface in habitats with dense growth of aquatic plants.  Feeds on small crustaceans, insects and protozoans (Ref. 12693).  Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Javanese snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow moving streams and rivers, as well as lakes, ponds (Ref. 12693) and swamps (Ref. 57235).  A common species in forest streams (Ref. 56749).  Often found in areas with plenty of aquatic vegetation, as well as submerged woody plants.  Feeds on fishes, prawns, and crabs and slightly less on shrimps.  Marketed fresh and often alive (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Javelin pipefish
species.description: Found in shallow coastal areas with algae or Zostera sp. Some specimens have been recorded from tide pools. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may brood at 6.9 cm SL.

species.name: Javelin rainbow sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Javelin spookfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous (Ref. 35626). Bathypelagic at about 400-800 m (Ref. 96339).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Javelin whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Javichthys kailolae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jawed Limia
species.description: This species was collected only from mountain springs that lead to the lake, apparently an endorheic drainage. Site collection is a clear water path with slow current exiting the lake (water temperature 29.9 °C and conductivity 321 microS/cm on the June 5, 2019). Occurs on muddy bottoms and some semi-submerged and submerged vegetation growing near the banks. Sympatric with Gambusia beebei, Limia miragoanensis, L. immaculata, L. nigrofasciata, L. garnieri, L. islai), Nandopsis haitiensis and two species of African cichlids introduced in the lake (Oreochromis aureus and Tilapia sp.) (Ref. 128734).

species.name: Jaya
species.description: Inhabits streams and ponds in plains and mountainous regions (Ref. 41236).  A tasty food fish but rare in the catches.

species.name: Jayakar's seahorse
species.description: Espèce d'hippocampes. Found in seagrass beds, e.g. Halophila spp. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Jaydia albomarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jaydia catalai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Jaydia erythrophthalma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jaydia hungi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from 62 m depth (Ref. 33021).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Jaydia novaeguineae
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Usually lives on sand bottom in shallow waters from depths of 22-62 m.  Trawled specimens were
collected from 40-55 m on an open sandy area (Ref. 99978).

species.name: Jaydia quartus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jaydia striata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon reefs.

species.name: Jaydia striatodes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Jaydia tchefouensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jeanpol's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks in the forested savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Jebb's siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered waters of lagoons and bays (Ref. 11890). Occurs in groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Jeboehlkia gladifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jeff’s snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow-water estuarine, in mangrove creeks and muddy tide-pools, at 0-1 m; also in marginal habitats such as by boat ramps and overgrown drains. Associated with P. aquilonius, P. eos (minor overlap) and P. melanosticta (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Jelly-head fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Jellybean tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jenkins' blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes encountered in shallow rocky areas.  Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Jenny creek sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silt-bottomed to rock-bottomed pools and runs of small to medium rivers.  Occasionally found in impoundments.

species.name: Jensen's lanternfish
species.description: High-oceanic and mesopelagic.  Found in the upper 85 m at night (Ref. 4066).

species.name: Jenyn's tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal areas (Ref. 36453).  Mainly feeds on polychaetes; also on other benthic preys such as gammaridean amphipods, cumaceans, and mysids.  A "smell and touch" kind of predator, little is known regarding its ecology (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Jenynsia darwini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in brackish water lagoons in sand-spit areas; Phalloptychus januarius and Poecilia vivipara were found in the same habitat (Ref. 128887).

species.name: Jenynsia sulfurica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A sulfide-tolerant species currently found restricted to the lagoon and ponds in Laguna La Quinta. The surrounding environment has elevated temperatures (39˚-50˚C), low dissolved oxygen concentrations (0.25-5 mg/L) and elevated levels of SO4 (990 to 1015 mg/l).  Adults were found mostly in the deepest ponds while juveniles were found schooling in small, shallow ponds (Ref. 120686).

species.name: Jespersen's hagfish
species.description: Occurs in muddy bottoms.  Eggs taken from a damaged specimen in various stages of maturation , elliptical up to 23.6 X 8.5 mm; all eggs are in mesenteries and no anchor filaments were found (Ref. 54824).

species.name: Jester goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jewel fish
species.description: Savannah associated species which prospers in a range of lentic habitats (Ref. 5644, 52307), tolerant of a wide range of water quality parameters and found in both very soft waters and highly saline ones (Ref. 52307), including brackish water lagoons, large lakes and riverine flood plains (Ref. 5644). Occurs near vegetation beds and fringes. Feeds on Caridina and insects. Pair-bonding (Ref. 52307) substrate spawner (Ref. 28714, 52307), ripe and spent fish are common early in the flood season (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Jewel killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, swampy parts of brooks and small streams under forest cover on the inland plains rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Jewelled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats as well as shallow lagoon and seaward reefs.  Also found in estuarine areas with algae-rich rubble patches on reef flats and slopes.  Intertidal to a few meters depth (Ref. 48636).  Usually found in areas of mixed coral, sand, and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Found solitary in weedy areas on rocks and coral outcrops (Ref. 90102).  Feed by scraping off algae (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Neither fang nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Jewett's coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from rocky bottoms, including tide pools (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Jewett’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jianchuan stone loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a spring with clear water, 14.4°C water temperature, pH 7.854, altitude 2172 m.  One specimen with gammarid shrimps and copepods in the stomach (Ref. 84390).

species.name: Jigsaw moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky or sandy shallow waters.

species.name: Jimbaran shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal inshore on inner insular shelf. Mainly feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 114953). The smallest pregnant female observed from this species was 74.7 cm TL; with pregnant females having 6-11 embryos, birth size unknown, but embryos well developed at 13 cm TL (Ref. 72461). Males mature at 77-80 cm TL. Females produces litters of 6-11 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Jimenez’s sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow inshore waters (Ref. 116660).

species.name: Jinshaia abbreviata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Jinshaia niulanjiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type of maximum size refers to body length (Ref. 86999).

species.name: Jinshaia sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Jipe tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poisson. Found in lakes and rivers (Ref. 4967). Chiefly a browser of periphyton in the lake, but additionally feeding also on bottom deposits and associated phytobenthos (Ref. 30832). A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 54046, 55060, 118638). Occasionally territorial (Ref. 2). It supports artisanal fisheries in lakes and dams across the Pangani catchment, with the largest fisheries in Lake Jipe and Nyumba ya Mungu (Ref. 118638). IUCN conservation status is critically endangered due to its restricted range and evidence of declining stocks between the 1970s and 2000 (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Jissah sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Joan's fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A group of 10-15 individuals were sighted and observed on rubble bottom at the base of a moderate slope. Observed twice during late afternoon where males were chasing females and engaging in courtship displays in which dorsal and pelvic fins were fully erect (Ref. 44110). Often exported from Bali in the aquarium trade. Appears to be undescribed, closely related to C. rubriventralis from the Red Sea (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Johnius cantori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnius distinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy and sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Johnius fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnius gangeticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and estuaries.

species.name: Johnius goldmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnius grypotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The most common species of Johnius (Johnius) in Chinese waters (Ref. 10101). Sandy-muddy bottoms and muddy bottoms from 25-110 m depth (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Johnius novaehollandiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnius philippinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnius taiwanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnson's gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Juveniles less than 6.1 cm SL were caught at depths of 70 - 110 meters.  Most specimens have sand grains inside the mouth indicating occurrence on open, predominantly sandy substrata (Ref. 54394).

species.name: Johnson's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over dense algal beds of deep lagoons.  Feeds on zooplankton 1-2 m above the bottom (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Johnsonina eriomma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Johnston Island damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found clear water, inner to outer reef crests in rich coral habitat (Ref. 48636). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Common in passages, frequently associated with Acropora, Stylophora, or Pocillopora coral heads or a single head of Pocillopora eydouxi (= Pocillopora grandis). Usually seen solitary (Ref. 48636). Feed on benthic algae and probably coral polyps. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 13550).

species.name: Johnston snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds small fishes, crabs, and prawns (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Inhabits sand bottoms among coral reefs in 2-23 m.

species.name: Johnston's topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the surface and among weeds in which it seeks refuge and food (Ref. 5595).  Prefers standing or gently flowing water as in river backwaters, floodplains (Ref. 7248), swamps (Ref. 7248, 47311), creeks and pools (Ref. 47311). Usually found in small shoals near the surface, among fringing vegetation; usually abundant when present (Ref. 47311, 52193). It feeds on small invertebrates like mosquito larvae and daphnia (Ref. 52193). A serial spawner, laying eggs which attach to vegetation (Ref. 52193). When food is abundant, breeding occurs daily over an extended period (year-round where conditions are suitable) (Ref. 7248, 52193).  6 cm max TL (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Johnston's weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on low reefs on sand with tall vegetation, from intertidal to 50 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Jolo dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand bottoms to 3 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Jonah's icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed mainly on fishes and krill (Ref. 5200).

species.name: Jones’ pony fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jonklaas' s loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not enough is known of the biology of this species. Inhabits shallow, slow-flowing rivulets, heavily shaded, with leaf debris (Ref. 11966). This fish is not visible from the water surface, being concealed beneath leaf debris. It is too rare to be of value to the aquarium trade which in any case exports large numbers of the superficially similar Lepidocephalus thermalis.

species.name: Jordan's cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Jordan's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit seagrass beds and sandy bottoms of trawling grounds (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Jordan's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually between 40 and 250 m on bottoms of mud, sand, and pebbles.

species.name: Jordan's triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth (Ref. 84006).

species.name: Jordan's tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found on substrata of sand, rubble, or small coral heads near reefs (Ref. 2334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Jordan’s red deepwater scorpionfsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Joturo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers.

species.name: Juan Deriba killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow temporary pools, partially covered by floating leaves and plant foliage. Soft bottom with mud over compact, dark brown to blackish clay (Ref. 128719).  This species adapts remarkably well to stress. It can leap out of water to escape predators and stay attached to some foliage for several hours (Ref. 128720).

species.name: Jugular blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Julian galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on rocky shores of lakes.  Bottom-dweller of upland lakes and associated streams, frequently under and around rocks on gravel substrates (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, small crustaceans and mollusks.

species.name: Julidochromis dickfeldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on rocks and rubble; very stationary and territorial.  The center of the territory is a crack or fissure in the rock.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans which are picked from rocks and very occasionally from drifting matter (Ref. 6770).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Julidochromis marksmithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in a rocky habitat but where there are sandy areas close by (Ref. 115482).

species.name: Julidochromis marlieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. These fish are hardy, peaceful toward other species and highly intelligent.  They are microfeeders and not carnivorous.  In the wild, they often stay in deep water and never come to the surface to feed.  They never swim in midwater but are typical rock-dwellers.  Ventures into the open but never far from the rock cover.  Breeds in crevices and caves (Ref. 6770). Monogamous pairs are most common (Ref. 54944).

species.name: Jumbie teta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams, from highly turbid standing water over a heavy clay substratum to free flowing clear water over gravel.  Algae-eater (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Jumping tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: June sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly most common in deep waters of Utah Lake.  Used tributaries of lake for spawning (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Adults are pelagic and feed on aquatic invertebrates in the mid-water column.  Juveniles inhabit emergent vegetation, apparently as refuge from predators (Ref. 35293).

species.name: Jungle toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba abramoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A gregarious species which frequently occurs in small creeks with sandy bottoms or in canals with silty bottoms (Ref. 12225).  Occurs in all types of habitats (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Jupiaba acanthogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba ajuricaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a black-water, terra-firme forest stream about 4-5 m wide and 0.5-1.0 m deep, with a predominantly sandy bottom.  Also found in a large oxbow lake (Ref. 81201).

species.name: Jupiaba anterior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba anteroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba apenima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba asymmetrica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba atypindi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba citrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba elassonaktis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba essequibensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba iasy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba keithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in the upper reaches of rivers.  Frequently occurs in counter current zones or in calm zones of cascades and creeks with sandy bottoms (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Jupiaba kurua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a clear water river.  Omnivorous, feeding on insects, fish, Podostemaceae fragments and filamentous algae (Ref. 80698).

species.name: Jupiaba maroniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the middle and the upper reaches of rivers and creeks with sandy and rocky bottoms (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Jupiaba meunieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the middle  and upper reaches of rivers.  Prefers rapidly flowing water of rivers and creeks with sandy and rocky bottoms.  Herbivorous (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Jupiaba minor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba mucronata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba ocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably solitary.  Appears to prefer areas with rapid water movement (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Jupiaba paranatinga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba pinnata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba pirana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba poekotero
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected exclusively by seining beaches in pools immediately downstream of waterfalls or rapids, but not in the rapids themselves (Ref. 54762).  Apparently avoids small forest streams (Ref. 54762).  Feeds on filamentous algae, fragments of Podostemaceae, terrestrial and aquatic Hemipterans, adults and larvae of Trichopterans and odonate nymphs (Ref. 54762).

species.name: Jupiaba polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba poranga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba potaroensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba scologaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba yarina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jupiaba zonata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Jurua anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in middle and upper reaches of rivers.  The numerous and rather long gillrakers armed with fine setae, together with the very long and highly coiled gut suggest a microplanktonic diet.  More data needed.

species.name: Jutjaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton.  Rarely caught by anglers.  Flesh is good to taste (Ref. 6641).

species.name: Kaalpens goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal areas, entering estuaries and freshwater (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Kabeyawan sand eel
species.description: The single specimen was collected by a trap net operated by a local fisherman who targeted glass eel species of Anguilla. It was collected together with other snake eels, such as Lamnostoma sp. and Ophichthus sp., and was probably chasing the fish larvae to the river mouth (Ref. 127464).

species.name: Kabili bumblebee goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fresh and brackish waters, in areas of aquatic vegetation, including mangrove roots (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Kachira Blue
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kafue killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 5 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kaguya’s dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs singly or in small groups in silty areas, with sand or mud-bottom or low-relief reef at depths ranging from 30-60 m (Ref. 129594).

species.name: Kai Island deepwater dragonet
species.description: Found on the shelf edge (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Kai stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds over sand bottom.  Feeds mainly on fishes.

species.name: Kai stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 236 m (Ref. 9863).  Maximum length based on an immature male (Ref. 9863).

species.name: Kailash Chandra’s snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kailola's hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear shallow creeks with gravel bottoms.

species.name: Kailola’s deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kaja’s sixgill sawshark
species.description: A female specimen (117 cm TL) was found gravid with about six eggs (based on radiographs). The size at birth estimated to be around 35 cm TL and was based on the four near-term embryos of 31.8-32.9 cm TL (Ref. 122027).

species.name: Kakatoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal bays and deep lagoons (Ref. 48636).  Inhabits seagrass beds or dense beds of algae.  Well-camouflaged and easily overlooked (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on these or the associated epiphytes.  Caught nets and other types of artisanal gear.

species.name: Kakatoi blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602), in slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 48636), often solitary but may sometimes occur in small groups (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Males common in atolls where they live mainly around the inner and outer edges of barrier reefs at depths of about 30 ft; females prefer deeper habitat (Ref. 4821).  Small juveniles in groups are found inshore on algae reef habitat (Ref. 9710, 48636) and sometimes enter silty, murky environments (Ref. 5490).  Feed by scraping algae from rocks and corals (Ref. 5227).  Are protogynous hermaphrodites (Ref. 55367).  Caught with nets and other types of artisanal gear.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).  In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Kakatoi brisant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of clear lagoons, channels, and outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).  Generally solitary (Ref. 1602).  Juveniles in small groups on algae and coral reefs inshore (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  Males maintain small harems and pair spawn (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Kakatoi lézard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs and is usually found on patch reefs or rocks (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Kakatoi rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Grazes on benthic algae.  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).

species.name: Kakatoi vareur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep outer reef slopes, channel slopes, and lagoon reefs (Ref. 1602). They are benthopelagic at 2-60 m (Ref. 58302). They are usually solitary but may occur in pairs. Juveniles are encountered in coral-rich areas of lagoon reefs, where staghorn Acropora corals abound (Ref. 1602) and also in algae reefs or seagrasses (Ref. 48636, 41878). Adults rove across the reefs by day and rest in reef caves and under coral ledges at night (Ref. 31343). Primary food are mollusks, fishes, sea urchins, crustaceans, and other invertebrates. They are one of the few predators of toxic animals such as sea hares, boxfishes and crown-of-thorns starfish (Ref. 1602). They are oviparous with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). They are sold in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). This species is captured by hook-and-line and by spear, and is occasionally marketed for food. Juveniles are occasionally seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 9823). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Kakuk's coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs, but has also been caught 230 mm inside an ocean blue hole in the Exuma Cays, Bahamas.  The eye is not particularly small, indicating that it is not a very specialized cave species.  A 6.1 cm SL female specimen caught from San Salvador Island contained 50 immature embryos (4 mm length) and 40 eggs between 0.2-0.4 mm in diameter (Ref. 55786).

species.name: Kalabans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit torrential hill-streams in shallow waters (Ref. 4832). They migrate to warmer regions of lakes and streams during winter (Ref. 40974). Used commonly by anglers as bait for Raiamas bola and Tor putitora. Herbivorous (Refs. 40948, 56237). Highly esteemed as food.

species.name: Kalambo suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Caught in water with rocks and boulders, little waterfalls and rapids, not in more quiet streams; nothing is known in detail on its diet, but it seems to be omnivorous; nothing is known on the breeding habits (Ref. 27292).

species.name: Kalbar rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in forest streams and clear black waters (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Kaleidos wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen collected from a depth of 30 m (Ref. 30829).  Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in rubble slopes with mixed low algae and invertebrates, usually in current-prone channels.  Juveniles and females form small groups.  Males usually seen singly, moving over large sections of reef (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Kali colubrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kali falx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kali indica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The shallowest depth record is based on a single Gargaropteron-staged individual which was taken in the Yucatan Channel, in 0-124 m (Museum:  RHB 1290).

species.name: Kali kerberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most adults have been taken in hauls in depths exceeding 1,000 m but a number of adults have been taken in hauls in depths between 500 to 1,000 m (Ref. 6944).

species.name: Kali macrodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most adults were caught at depths exceeding 1,500 m (Ref. 6764).

species.name: Kali macrura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All adult specimens have been taken in hauls to depths exceeding 1,000 m.  Gargaropteron-stage specimens unknown (Ref. 6944).

species.name: Kali parri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The 5 known adults were from hauls to depths exceeding 1,500 m.  A single Gargaropteron-stage specimens, 4.56 cm SL, taken in a haul 0 to 304 m (Ref. 6944).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Kalimantan ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, perhaps entering estuaries.  More data needed.

species.name: Kalimantan river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers.

species.name: Kalimantania lawak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kaluga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers and lakes. Adults do not spawn every year but at least every other year. With increasing age, the spawning interval increases to three, four and more years (Ref. 593). Feed on invertebrates in the first year then switch to juveniles of pelagic fishes, e.g., Oncorhynchus keta, at age 3 to 4 yrs., kaluga feed on adult fishes (Ref. 40142).

species.name: Kalyptodoras bahiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on crabs.

species.name: Kamaka rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kami barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kami's perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kammal thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling and occurring mostly inshore.  More data needed based on correct identifications.

species.name: Kamohara grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kampen's ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, but also enters rivers and tolerates water of low salinity.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans and fishes; also amphipods.

species.name: Kampoyo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the lower reaches of rivers to the deepest habitable parts of the lake (Ref. 4967). Inhabits a variety of habitats (Ref. 52142). Feeds on small demersal cichlids (Ref. 52142) during the night (Ref. 5595). Juveniles mainly feed on trophic eggs released by the female (Ref. 36945), whilst the male helps the young in searching for invertebrates in and around the nest (Ref. 36945). Mutualistic relationship with cichlids concerning defense and feeding of young of both the cichlid and B. meridionalis (Ref. 52146). Symbiotic relationship of parasitized host-parasite eater exist with Pseudotropheus crabro, which eats away necrotic tissue and parasites, but also steals eggs (Ref. 42778). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Can produce sound as Amia or Synodontis species (Ref. 42447). Considered as a delicacy when smoked, making it one of the most highly priced fishes of Malawi (Ref. 52150).

species.name: Kanakorum catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare inshore catshark found on coral reefs (Ref. 11146).

species.name: Kanawha darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast gravel and rubble riffles of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Kanawha minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rubble and gravel riffles and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Kane's cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kanekonia florida
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kanekonia pelta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kanglang fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kanmu dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kapala lanternfish
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Kapala stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kapala whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Kappa reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Kappie blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit estuaries.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Kapuas river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and streams with clean and moderately fast waters (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Kara tadpolefish
species.description: Collected by pelagic trawling, 0-30 m above the eastern slope of the Novaya Zemlya Depression (193 m deep); suggesting the pelagic habitat of this species. According to field study, the surface water temperature at the locality was 5-7°C, thermocline was situated at a depth from 20 to 30 m, and water temperature of the whole water mass below up to bottom was negative (-0.6 to -0.7°C), salinity 33.31-34.33 ppt from surface to bottom. Most likely that this species inhabits the layer closely below the thermocline where zooplankton organisms produced large concentration there; that is, in water of negative temperatures (Ref. .116680)

species.name: Karen's sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kariba tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools (Ref. 2, 54048). Is mainly diurnal; salt-tolerant (Ref. 2). Feeds mainly on (filamentous) algae (Ref. 2, 12524, 13337, 52307, 54048) and diatoms, as well as higher plants (Ref. 2, 52307), dipterous larvae, cladocerans, copepods (Ref. 2), aquatic and terrestrial insects, shrimps, worms (Ref. 12524, 13337, 54048) and mollusks (Ref. 54048). Mouthbrooder; spawns several times per year (Ref. 12524, 13337, 54048).

species.name: Karimunjawa dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef slopes at about 20 m depth (Ref. 48635). Solitary, in pairs or small groups around coral or rock outcrops (Ref 90102).

species.name: Karin's coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices to at least 16 m depth, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Karnella's rover
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Karomo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males were seen scooping up algal debris from the bottom, and occasionally they moved to the adjacent weed beds and rasp epiphytic algae (Ref. 2). A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 2, 118638); males defend territories in shallow water, building a small platform of fine sand in the centre of a small pit (Ref. 118638). Important in swamp fishery (Ref. 4967), and an important component of the fisheries catch in Lakes Sagera and Nyamagoma; potential as an aquaculture species (Ref. 118638). The IUCN status is critically endangered, based on small range, fishing pressure and habitat degradation (Ref. 118638). Excellent to eat; occurs in shallow water; common but localized (Ref. 53528).

species.name: Karonga tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in all kinds of habitats; it has been observed in shallow vegetated bays, in intermediate habitats, over sand, and in purely rocky biotopes (Ref. 5595). At most locations it is found at shallow levels, rarely deeper than 10 metres (Ref. 5595), but it can be present from the surface waters to depths of 40-50m (Ref. 118638). It feeds on phytoplankton and on diatom sediment on the sand; the so-called 'multitooth' morph at Cape Maclear grazes from rocks and might harvest the loose aufwuchs (Ref. 5595). A maternal mouthbrooder; males defend territories from shallow water down to at least 28m; males dig pits, which are sometimes huge craters with a small raised platform of fine sand (Ref. 118638). It is an important component of the fisheries catch in Lake Malawi (Ref. 118638). The IUCN conservation status is rated as endangered, based on declining fishery catches due to overfishing (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Karrer's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Karsten totoyensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over mud and sand bottoms.  Its small size and deep-dwelling habitat makes collection a difficult task (Ref. 43739).

species.name: Karun barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kasatkia memorabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore to depth of 26 meters (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Kasawala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A semi-pelagic species (Ref. 4967), found in all kinds of habitats but seen mostly in shallow water; it is abundant in the southeastern arm of Lake Malawi, where it occurs in shallow, vegetated bays (Ref. 5595). It feeds on phytoplankton and sometimes from the sediment on the sand; diatoms constitute the major part of its diet (Ref. 5595). Major component of the fisheries catch in Lake Malawi (Ref. 118638). IUCN conservation status is endangered, due to declining population trend (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Kasenye lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in open water, and also among bordering vegetation in the shore regions and swampy lagoonal parts of Lake Albert (Ref. 47311).

species.name: Kashgarian loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow currents in lakes and pools over muddy or sandy bottom (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Katavi mouthbrooder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Katherine's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known at depths ranging from 10 to at least 40 m at exposed outer reef areas than in lagoons or harbors.  Occurs in aggregations.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Kathetostoma binigrasella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 86516).

species.name: Kathetostoma canaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kathetostoma fluviatilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type specimen was collected from the Manawatu River (Ref. 26272).

species.name: Katibasia insidiosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Katrana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Katria katria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers with sand and gravel bottom and scattered boulders.

species.name: Kaup's sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters and enters estuaries.

species.name: Kaupichthys japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected in a pool surrounded by coral heads with fine sandy bottom.  Apparently spawns in the summer (Ref. 41416).

species.name: Kavirondo barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Keel-belly tadpolefish
species.description:
The holotype was collected in the southwestern part of the Kara Sea, by pelagic trawling at surface layer 0-30 m above the 120 m depth where the surface water was warm (6.0 - 7.7°C); with a sharp termocline detected from 19-23 m, and the temperature dropped to negative
values, and then it stay negative (-0.64°C) down to the bottom. Salinity also changed from 32.72ppt at surface to 34.6% at near bottom layer. Most likely that this species stay in cold water below the termocline layer, where the forage zooplankton organisms are concentrated.
Amphipod specimen was also found in throat of the fish , which might suggest that it  feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 116680)..

species.name: Keelcheek bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer parts of the continental shelves and the upper parts of these slopes (Ref. 37343).

species.name: Keeley’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Keeling deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Keletaona's Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kellogg's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coralline areas from near shore to the outer reef slope at a depth of at least 24 m (Ref. 57406).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Kelloggella oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kelloggella tricuspidata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kelp clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Clings to strands of kelp (often high in kelp canopy) or eelgrass with its disk; moves to seek food or cover.  Rarely found in tide pools.

species.name: Kelp gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rests on kelp, usually high up in kelp canopy at depths to about 12 m.  Feeds on small crustaceans.

species.name: Kelp klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in kelp beds at low tide.  Attains over 10 cm.

species.name: Kelp perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among giant kelp, usually up in kelp canopy.  Feed on small crustaceans, especially ones that live on kelp.  Also a cleaner which picks external parasites from other fishes.  Usually occur in large aggregations in summer (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Kelp pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among attached or drifting kelp (Macrocystis) (Ref. 126547), rarely in bays (Ref. 2850). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Kelp poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Crawls over bottom and climbs rocks faces with its pectoral fins (Ref. 2850).  Body often covered with small sponges and seaweed, which provide camouflage (Ref. 2850).  Demersal spawner in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Kelp rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on or near bottom in kelp beds or rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Kelp sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kelp weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal algae and kelp reefs (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in kelp and weed areas of shallow rocky reefs exposed to strong surge and wave action (Ref. 33616).  Feed on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 9003).

species.name: Kenting sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kentrocapros aculeatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Kentrocapros eco
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kentucky darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Kenyaconger heemstrai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Kenyan chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer reef slopes (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Keppi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found throughout the lake, but seems to prefer zones with submerged wooden or stone structures (Ref. 52307). Usually forms schools at the surface; feeds mainly on epiphytic and epilithic filamentous algae, and the diatoms, rhizopods, rotifers and organic debris found among them; adults feed by opening their mouths very wide and applying them to the surface of the rock as though sucking the material in (Ref. 2). Lacks marked sexual dichromatism when sexually active (Ref. 81260). Both sexes are possible incubators (Ref. 52307). Forms temporary pair bonds (Ref. 81260), for the entire duration of incubation/broodcare (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Kerala mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hide under rocks and boulders in swift-flowing clear water hill streams (Ref. 1479).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Kerlèche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lower reaches of slow-flowing rivers, but can also be found in still pools (Ref. 9696),  on sandy bottoms of ponds, pools and ditches.  Adults are nocturnal which burrow into mud during dry periods and strong frosts.  Usually, burrows are 20-30 cm deep, occasionally down to 70 cm during dry periods (Ref. 59043).  During the day, they stay buried in the sand.  Feed on insect larvae and small mollusks.  Seldom captured with hook and line (Ref. 30578).  Are sensitive to pollutants which accumulate in the sediment (Ref. 11941).  Facultative air-breathers (Ref. 27368).  A female specimen measuring 30.7 cm TL was recorded from Netherlands (Ref. 114650).

species.name: Kermadec clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the intertidal and subtidal waters of the Kermadec Islands, including Raoul Island and L’Esperance Rock. Most of the specimens collected using ichthyocides were from rock pools and from shallower subtidal areas (down to 9 meters) over rock and coral rubble. A single specimen has been observed and photographed at 28 meters in depth (Ref. 124119).

species.name: Kermadec dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs (Ref. 93112).

species.name: Kermadec rattail
