species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Kermadec scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Kermadec spiny dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kermadec triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in tidal pools (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Kersin barbell
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kertomichthys blastorhinos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kessler's gudgeon
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit fast-flowing piedmont rivers with large areas of sand bottom.  They live in groups. Juveniles and adults are active during day. Preyson a variety of benthic invertebrates, usually catching drifting prey.  Spawning occurs in shallow areas over gravel, sand or plant material in fast-flowing water. Gradual decline is expected due to on-going economic development. Are sensitive to organic pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kessler's loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kessler's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs where the bottom is sand, sand-and-stone and sand-and-silt.  Stays at a depth range of 3-15 m during the winter months.  Spawns from mid May until the end of June, over sand and stone bottom, 3-5 m depth, as well as in shallow inlets and tributary mouths.  Eggs are deposited under stones and are guarded by the male.  Males are larger than females.  (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Key blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surge channels in coral reefs with high relief (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Key brotula
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The species prefers shallow algae habitats at depths from 0 to 8 m, except for a single record off North Carolina (USNM 223537) caught at a depth of 31-33 m.  A 44 mm SL female specimen (ANSP 148378) contained 2 embryos (12 mm TL) and 15 eggs (diameter 0.3 mm). A 37 mm SL female (ANSP 148378) contains 3 embryos of 8 mm TL, 1 embryo of 4 mm SL, and 10 eggs, 0.5 mm in diameter.  The embryos have black eyes, but no pigmentation on head and body,
probably due to bleaching (Ref. 57883).  A cryptic species, locally abundant (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Key goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Key silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pond waters of varying salinity.

species.name: Key worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds from bays and mangroves to offshore reefs.  Adults move to open sea to spawn.

species.name: Khaki flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Khandalla minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hill streams with sandy and gravelly bottom (Ref. 26727, 41236).

species.name: Khanka gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coarse sandy bottoms of lakes (Ref. 38401). Feeds on aquatic insects, gammarids, small gastropods and zooplankton (Ref. 38401). Adults spawn at the end of June (Ref. 1441 as G. ussuriensis).

species.name: Khanka spiny bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Khavalchor catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit slow moving turbid streams (Ref. 41236).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Khavli barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Kiamichi shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, flowing pools of clear creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Kibiti Lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kibonde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore areas of the lake down to 30 m depth and feeds mainly on crabs (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Kichulchoia brevifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pebble-covered bottoms of shallow, fast flowing streams, less than 80 cm deep and about 1-3 m wide.  Feeds on insect larvae, algae and plant matter.

species.name: Kidako moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Occurs in crevices in shallow reefs.  Often snatches game from divers.  Used as food fish in some districts in Japan.

species.name: Kijimuna goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kikambala nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and temporary pools (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2-4 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kikori River Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from slightly brackish water at two collection sites of the Kikori River (Ref. 84817).

species.name: Killarney shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are pelagic in lacustrine areas (Ref. 59043).  The females are larger than males.  They spawn in June to July on gravel bars and gravelled shallows around large islands of the lake.  Feed mainly on zooplankton.  Population occupies a very small range and is threatened by eutrophication (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Killi
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Two color morphs, chocolate and gold, are in the aquarium trade (Ref. 4537).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Killi des mangroves
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow, mud-bottomed ditches, bays, salt marshes and other brackish-water environments; also crab burrows (Ref. 5723), moist leaf litter, decaying mangrove logs (Ref. 93034). Can withstand heavy pollution of fresh or salty waters and shares its biotope with Poecilia vivipara which is much more abundant (Ref. 35237). Usually found in water with low oxygen content (Ref. 7251). Either male or hermaphroditic, females don't seem to exist. Only about 5% of a population are born as males; after 3-4 years about 60% of the (self-fertilizing) hermaphrodites transform into secondary males by losing female structure and function. The proportion of males depends on the environmental temperature. Below 20°C, majority are males, above 25°C all are hermaphrodites (Ref. 35237). It is the only known naturally occurring, self-fertilizing vertebrate (Ref. 13056, 35237). Not a seasonal killifish. Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kimberley archerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Strictly restricted to freshwater areas, penetrating well inland or approximately 300 km upstream from the sea (Ref. 27655). Occurs in deeper pools where its swims near the surface, patrolling the shoreline for insects (Ref. 27655).

species.name: Kimberley blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral and coral rock reefs at 1-15 m (Ref. 10700).  Found in turbid coral reefs.  Almost exclusively benthic (Ref. 36661).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Kimberley catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to turbid coastal reefs of mainland Australia and nearby islands (Ref. 31103).  Presumably nocturnal (Ref. 31103).  Feeds on gastropod mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 31103).

species.name: Kimberley grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock pools and vegetated river margins over sand bottom.  Feed mainly on filamentous algae (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.5, H=10, 28°C, egg layer, peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Kimberley mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among vegetation or submerged roots in rivers, creeks and billabongs where water is calm (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Kimberley spangled perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear, flowing streams over sandstone bottoms.  Also found in open rocky pools with minimal aquatic vegetation (Ref. 44894).  Feed on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 5259, 44894) but is considered an omnivore (Ref. 7300).  Breeding presumably takes place during the dry season (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Not much known on its biology (Ref. 2906).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.8, H=8, 28°C water temperature, egg layer and a peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Kindia killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Not a seasonal killifish.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: King demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in 1-6 m (Ref. 7247) and in coastal to outer reef crests to depths of about 20 m (Ref. 48636). They occur solitarily or in groups in reef margins and upper seaward slopes subject to mild surge (Ref. 9710).  Feed mainly on algae.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: King dory
species.description: Occurs in offshore waters (Ref. 9258).  Juveniles pelagic in surface waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: King goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shoreline reefs and intertidal flats with sand, mud, or silt bottoms in 0-2 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: King snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore water from 15-365 m depth.  Commonly caught by anglers near oil rigs.

species.name: King-of-the-salmon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 2850).  Also found near shore, but large adults sometimes feed on the bottom (Ref. 2850).  Small individuals feed on copepods, annelid worms, and fish larvae; larger individuals feed on copepods, euphausiids, small pelagic fishes, young rockfishes, squid, and Octopoda (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36610).

species.name: Kinmei dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in channels (Ref. 33412).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Kinneret bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives near the surface in large schools, with occasional forays to deeper waters (Ref. 11031).  Spawns in November to March.  Females attach eggs separately on rocks (Ref. 11030).  Diet limited to zooplankton, essentially copepods and cladocerans.

species.name: Kirk's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the intertidal zone of exposed rocky shores, often out of the water (Ref. 11441).  They actively shuttle back and forth between rock pools and air (skipper) (Ref. 31184).  Breathe air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Kissing loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kissing prochilodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kithulgala danio
species.description: Found mainly in well-shaded areas of shallow, slow-flowing streams (Ref. 118056).

species.name: Kiunga bleheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kiungululu tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The maximum reported total length is 19.5 cm (Ref. 2, 118638); the maximum standard length of 19 cm (Ref. 4967) is not correct (G.F. Turner, pers. comm.). A maternal mouthbrooder; males defend territories in shallow water, digging a pit among branches and roots of reeds (Ref. 118638). Like Oreochromis hunteri, this species appears to be confined to a single lake without an outlet (Ref. 4967). The single population of this species is probably very small and vulnerable and is likely to support a sustainable fishery; the small adult size of the species would suggest minimal potential for aquaculture (Ref. 118638). Its IUCN conservation status is critically endangered, based on risk of siltation and water level fluctuations due to drought; in addition, populations are likely to have been impacted by the stocking of the lake with Coptodon rendalli and Tilapia sparrmanii, which are both presently abundant (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Kiwi hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Kiyi
species.description: Inhabits open water.

species.name: Kiyo’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bottoms with coarse sand, broken shell, volcanic gravel, and small rocks with dead algae.

species.name: Kizilirmak sportive loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Klamath Lake sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy shores of lakes.

species.name: Klamath largescale sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, impoundments, and rocky pools and runs of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Klausewitz' garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in colonies containing hundreds of individuals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Klausewitzia ritae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.

species.name: Klunzinger's mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Klunzinger's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef margins and seaward slopes (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Knaacks cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kner's stareater
species.description: A mesopelagic species (Ref. 51500).

species.name: Kner's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal reefs with mixed weed and coral; often on turbid, silty areas. Usually seen on floor of caverns or under ledges. Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Kneria angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kneria ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kneria katangae

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic algae scraper (Ref. 27609). Maximum TL was recorded at 5.5 cm (Ref. 89001).

species.name: Kneria ruaha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum total length recorded is 68mm; inhabits cool quiet streams; feeds on detritus; no marked spawning period (Ref. 26644).

species.name: Kneria rukwaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum total length recorded is 7.44cm TL (Ref. 26644). Mostly found in stagnant pools and moderately flowing streams, only rarely in fast flowing currents; omnivorous; a female of 6.55cm TL releases about 400-500 ripe eggs of a diameter of 1.2mm (Ref. 27292). Apparently no marked spawning period (Ref. 44637). Male reported to change its coloration at night, being very pale with dark spots along the midline of the body (Ref. 27292).

species.name: Kneria sjolandersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kneria stappersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kneria uluguru
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum total length recorded is 5.31cm TL; inhabits clear streams and rivers with very fast current to more gentle waterflow, but more numerous in the quieter stretches; omnivorous, but feeds mainly on algae and aufwuchs rasped off from stones; apparently no marked spawning season (Ref. 26644).

species.name: Kneria wittei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upland streams and pools; hardy and can survive some time out of water (Ref. 4967). Rare, but abundant in its habitats (Ref. 36901).

species.name: Knife livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits waters of low to moderate velocity, between 0 and 300 m elevation.  Lives on creeks of more than 0.5 m deep, in ditches and near shorelines of large rivers.  Generally swims in small groups at a depth of 20 cm.  Insectivorous, the young eat mainly aquatic insects and the adults feed specifically on terrestrial insects (Ref. 36880).  Found in a rapidly flowing rainforest stream (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Knife razorfish
species.description: A solitary species (Ref. 90102) that inhabits reef flats and shallow lagoons, in sandy, current-swept areas with rubble and weed (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Capable of diving into the sand with the approach of danger.  Rarely caught by fishers or aquarium collectors (Ref. 9823).

species.name: Knife-snouted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate offshore depths.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Knifejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Knipowitschia iljini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the deep regions of the Caspian Sea (Ref. 26334).  Does not occur in freshwaters (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Knipowitschia montenegrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in river shallows with slow current and in pools remaining in gravel pits after river flooding. The substrate consists of gravel, covered with fine sediment and overgrown by dense filamentous algae (Ref. 75974).

species.name: Knipowitschia mrakovcici
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which inhabits lakes.  Is threatened from its range due to pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Knobchin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools and shallow rocky reefs.

species.name: Knobfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in cool to cold spring-fed creeks and rivers with cobble bottoms (Ref. 83416).

species.name: Knobsnout parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky areas of coastal waters.  Found in small groups (Ref. 9710).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in areas of moderate to strong current and present even in the torrential flow of waterfalls.  Juveniles measuring up to 2.4 cm SL occur at sandbars marginal to waterfall pools.  Feeds only on Chironomidae larvae based on 3 stomach contents (Ref. 75965).

species.name: Knodus victoriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Knothead parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on algae from hard substratum (Ref. 9710).  Forms small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Knysna sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An estuary sand dweller occurring in tidal parts of rivers (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Knysna seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays and estuaries among submerged vegetation; diurnal (Ref. 4281, 30915).  Can tolerate salinities from 1-59 ppt (Ref. 30915).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Length type refers to Height (= from top of coronet to the tip of straightened tail). Breeding in the aquarium is possible (Ref. 130565).

species.name: Koaro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly clear streams, often deeply shaded and relatively fast-flowing, although it sometimes occurs in lakes, particularly in Tasmania.  In New Zealand and parts of Tasmania, juveniles occur in marine waters, presumably the larvae are washed out to the sea.  The existence of a marine stage is regarded to be facultative rather than obligatory in Australia.  Swims near the bottom, usually around the cover of rocks and logs.  More common in uploads (Snowy Mountains, Otway Ranges, central Tasmania) than at lower elevations (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Kobayashi's bristlemouth
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Kobayashi's triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kobe flounder
species.description: Lives on sand and shell bottoms and feeds on bottom-living animals.  Sexually dimorphic characters develop at about 5 cm SL.

species.name: Kochichthys flavofasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Koefoed's searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Koester
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs frequently among rocks in depths of 1 to at least 20 m (Ref. 4319).  Commonly caught by anglers (Ref. 4319).  Flesh excellent (Ref. 4319).

species.name: Koheru
species.description: Adults feed on zooplankton (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Kokani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic (Ref. 58426).  Occurs in open ocean and lakes and migrates up to coastal streams to spawn (Ref. 86798). There are two forms, the anadromous form known as the sockeye and the landlocked form (with a much smaller maximum size) known as the kokanee (Ref. 27547).  Upon emergence from gravel, fry at first tends to avoid light, hiding during the day and emerging at night (Ref. 27547).  In some populations, sockeye fry go to the sea during their first summer but most spend one or two (rarely three or four) years in a lake before migrating (Ref. 30333).  In a few streams of the Copper River drainage in Alaska, young sockeye stay in the stream (Ref. 27547).  Once in the lake, the young spend a few weeks inshore, feeding largely on ostracods, cladocerans and insect larvae.  The fish then become pelagic and move offshore, where they feed on plankton in the upper 20 m or so (Ref. 27547).  Seaward migration follows with the young individuals first staying fairly close to shore, feeding mainly on zooplankton, but also on small fishes and insects (Ref. 30343, 30346).  With growth, they head out to sea and fish become important in the diet (Ref. 27547).  Kokanee are confined to lake-stream systems, and most of its life is spent in the lake (Ref. 27547).  They feed mainly on plankton, but also take insects and bottom organisms (Ref. 1998).  Kokanee, wherever they are native, have been derived from anadromous populations, and each kokanee population apparently has evolved independently from a particular sockeye run (Ref. 30338, 30339).  Offspring of kokanee occasionally become anadromous, and sockeye offspring occasionally remain in freshwater (Ref. 27547).  Lifespan of the kokanee varies from two to seven years in different stocks (Ref. 27547).  The sockeye is one of the most commercially important Pacific salmons; the kokanee is primarily a sport fish but also makes excellent food and in some areas well regarded as food for large trout (Ref. 27547).  Marketed fresh, dried or salted, smoked, canned, and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Kokani noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably feeds on mesopelagic or benthopelagic zooplankton (Ref. 87053)

species.name: Kokoda glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits high altitude streams 300-400 m in elevation (Ref. 2847) and occurring in areas with good vegetative cover (Ref. 6398).  A carnivorous and egg laying species which tolerates the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.5, H=10, 26°C water temperature (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Kokoda mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, clear, rainforest streams, in foot-hills with an altitude of about 280-350 m.

species.name: Kokraimoro tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little information is available about the type locality other than that it was a rapids area in the northern portions of the Rio Xingu (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Kokuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kola rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is located about 11 km upstream from the sea with the main river making a gradual transition from a broad, mangrove-lined tidal stream with brackish conditions to an exceptionally narrow and steep-walled, limestone channel in woodland habitat with pure fresh water. This species was found nearly 100 m beyond the navigable (via small outboard boat) limit of the stream (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Kolpotocheirodon figueiredoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in areas with moderate water current.  Occurs mostly in a riffle at a narrow stretch of rio Pratinha, the type locality of this species.  Stays at midwater, swimming against the current, probably feeding on food items drifting downstream.   One individual was observed picking with its mouth on a large boulder in a cave entrance (Ref. 76978).

species.name: Kolpotocheirodon theloura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.

species.name: Komodo cardinalfish
species.description: Usually on sheltered reefs, with abundant coral.  May form large aggregations near the bottom.  Usually hovering close above dense branching corals or feeding high above in currents on zooplankton (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Komodo damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found in surge-affected shallows with a variable-sized boulder substrate (Ref. 31117).  They stay close to shelter (Ref. 31117).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Komodo fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered bays, along mangrove and rocky shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Komodo viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Komodo whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small schools, 20-30 individuals, over rubble slopes at 12-25 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Kongoro lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers, brooks, and shallow parts of river drainages (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Koningsberger's herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters and enters inlets and lower reaches of rivers.

species.name: Konti barb
species.description: A fast growing and valuable species for stocking in even temporary waters.  Does not breed in ponds.

species.name: Konye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on algae, small insects and fish eggs (Ref. 52307). Also kleptoparasite of freshwater crabs (Ref. 53950). Ovophilic mouthbrooder with both sexes as possible incubator; from aquarium observations: a few days prior to spawning, both partners remain close together for much of the time; the genital papilla of the female is clearly visible immediately before spawning and is much broader and larger than the male's; females are normally more successful than males when it comes to brooding the fry; when mouthbrooding, which ends about 3 weeks post-spawning, the specimens are relatively shy and prefer to lie silently near the bottom in secluded areas; once free swimming, juveniles normally do not return to the parent's mouth again (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Kopua kuiteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kopua nuimata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Koragu tank goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in lakes and backwaters of the lowland plain, but also occasionally found in main river channels (Ref. 2847).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Korean bittering
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean bonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, on rock bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Commercially cultured in Japan.  The species can be easily reared in aquaria (Ref. 5474).

species.name: Korean sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Korean seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in floating Sargassum and weeds on shallow soft bottom habitats (Ref. 117115).

species.name: Korean skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449, 81217).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Maximum length for female from Ref. 26574.

species.name: Korean Snake eel
species.description: Burrows into sandy, muddy substrate using its hard pointed tail (Ref. 86398).

species.name: Korechika's dwarfoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Koreocobitis naktongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottom of fast-flowing upper streams (Ref. 42956).

species.name: Korhi barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper part of large streams and rivers along the base of the ghats (Ref. 41236).  Has been introduced into reservoirs and lakes in peninsular India (Ref. 4832).  Prefers rocky streams and fast flowing rivers.  Feeds on debris and plant matter (Ref. 44149).  Spawns in the upper Cauvery.

species.name: Korogwe tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 118638). There is evidence of hybridization with native Oreochromis jipe in northern Tanzania, and non-native O. niloticus in southern Tanzania (Ref. 118638). Of only minor importance to artisanal fisheries (Ref. 118638). Maximum standard length of 18 cm (Ref. 4967) is not confirmed (Ref. 2, G.F. Turner pers. comm.); maximum total length reported as 20.8 cm (Ref. 2, 118638).

species.name: Kosciuszko Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Collected from cold and clear water in small flowing creeks (0.6-1.1 m average width, 0.1-0.2 m average depth, 0.5-0.6 m maximum depth) and from an on-stream lake (Blue Lake). All sites during winter are covered by snow and ice for an extended period of time. Substrate in the creeks consisted of bedrock, boulder, cobble, gravel and sand while the lake with cobble, pebble, gravel and silt.The fish is collected among rock, undercut banks and overhanging grasses in the creeks, mainly from pools. In Blue Lake, collected among small cobbles and from within 2 m of the shoreline (location and habitat in deeper water unknown). All sites without emergent or submerged aquatic vegetation or overhead shading. Collected at a density of 4.5 fish/m2 in Carruthers Creek, 2.5 fish/m2 along the edges of Blue Lake, and 1.5 fish/m2 in an inflowing tributary to Blue Lake. It is the only native fish species so far recorded from within its range, although Galaxias olidus is presumed to be present nearby. It is collected in Carruthers Creek with an unidentified native spiny crayfish Euastacus sp. (possibly E. rieki) (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Koshi Nangra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kosi rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Kosogol grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small in size, mature at a length of 17-20 cm TL (Ref. 593).  Omnivore, feeding predominantly on plankton (Ref. 41072).

species.name: Kosswig’s barb
species.description: Occurs in fast-flowing reaches of rivers and feeds on small animals (Ref. 94477).

species.name: Kotaka’s argentine
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs over muddy and sandy bottoms, at depths of about 150-300 m; young specimens
collected at 146-234 m (Ref. 84005).

species.name: Kotlyar's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kottelat rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from midwater to surface in pools of small upland streams (Ref. 12693).  Feed on insects (Ref. 33813).  Spawning sites are found in rivers and ponds (Ref. 33813).  Mature adults probably breed during the rainy season.  Not seen in markets.  May possibly seen be used in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Kottelatia brittani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kottelatlimia hipporhynchos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various habitats, with different substrates (including peat), but most abundant in streams with clear tannin-stained water on white sandy bottom; observed resting on the sand substrate or diving into it. This species has occasionally been collected at the same localities as Kottelatlimia pristes, but it does not occupy the same habitat, the latter was not observed on sandy substrate but on or inside peat, soil and leave litter (Ref. 79884).

species.name: Kottelatlimia katik
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kottelatlimia pristes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kotthaus’ deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Koumansetta hoesei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coral-reef species that is usually seen hovering a short distance above the substratum in lagoons and seaward reefs. Usually solitary, but sometimes seen in a small group, where each individual is at moderate distance from the others. From the food items found in the gut of one specimen of Koumansetta hectori (filamentous algae, harpacticoid copepods, amphipods, ostracods, and nematodes) a similar benthic, omnivorous diet may be expected for this species (Ref. 119548).

species.name: Kraemeria merensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of this family burrow in shallow marine to estuarine areas with fine coral sand or muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 48316).  Of no commercial interest but may be taken incidentally (Ref. 48316).

species.name: Kraemeria nuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kraemeria tongaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Members of this family burrow in shallow marine to estuarine areas with fine coral sand or muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 48316).  Rare species (Ref. 559).  Of no commercial interest but may be taken incidentally (Ref. 48316).

species.name: Kranji drombus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Krasyukova's perch
species.description: Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Krauss' blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are cryptic among coral and rubble on reef flats and upper portion of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Krefft's dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Most specimens taken in depths less than 1000 m with bottom trawls (Ref. 86949).  Maximum depth reported in Ref. 10977. No male specimens are known.

species.name: Krefft's frillgoby
species.description: Inhabits shallow seagrass beds, rocky estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Krefft's smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic to benthopelagic (Ref. 4460).  Mesopelagic at 1000-1600 m (Ref. 58302).  Bottom trawl captures between 1,000-1,600 m and mid-water captures between 1,600-3,200 m (Ref. 4460).

species.name: Krefft's snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Kreiser’s Killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The area where the species was collected from are both characterized as small tributaries ranging from 0.8 to 4 meters in width with stones (from pebbles to boulders) as the dominant substrate; estimated canopy cover of both localities 70-80%; and both creeks feature a variety of run, pool, riffle, rapid and small waterfall habitats (Ref. 91935).

species.name: Krempf's flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Kribi killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and swampy parts of brooks in the humid coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Omnivorous and egg-layer (Ref. 31267).

species.name: Kribia kribensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum reported total length 5.7 cm (Ref. 57413).

species.name: Kribia leonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kribia nana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum standard length reported 49 mm (Ref. 81660).

species.name: Kribia uellensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kriete's tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater fish commonly collected on mud substrates on the outer continental shelf.  Little is known concerning its ecology (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Krishna carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep large rivers in upland regions (Ref. 41236).  Adults prefer deep rocky pools, mostly hide under bedrocks and boulders; while juveniles prefer pools and riffles (Ref. 43631, 44151).  Feed on allochthonous plant  materials and debris (Ref. 44151).  Breed after the monsoon, when river gets stabilized; fries available during February and March (Ref. 44151).

species.name: Krobia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rivers.

species.name: Krobia petitella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a black water river with pH ranging from 4.2-7.1, conductivity of 2.0-39.0 μS , temperature of 25.0-33.3°C, current velocity typically ranging from 0.1-0.3 m/s, dissolved oxygen of 5.1-6.7 mg/L and Secchi depth 0.7-1.0 m (Ref. 93940).

species.name: Krobia xinguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kronichthys heylandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kronichthys lacerta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kronichthys subteres
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with rocky and sandy bottom, in places up to 0.8 m deep and with water flow up to 30 cm per second.  Forages both during the day and at night.  Grazes on microscopic algae, mostly diatoms and green algae growing on rocks and submersed vegetation.  Occasionally takes chironomid and simuliid larvae, as well as tiny crustaceans.  Before grazing on a patch with dense sediment, the fish makes wiggling head-down movements which raise sediment, to be blown away by the water current.  When grazing algae off the substrate makes vigorous mouth movements, and moves by jerky movements probably related to its mouth making alternate grazing and attaching to the substrate.  Leaves conspicuous grazing marks on exposed rocks.  May re-graze a given spot by moving backwards.  Density may reach about 1 fish per square meter in stream stretches shaded by the forest and 2.5 fish per square meter in sunny stretches (Ref. 26630).

species.name: Kroyer's deep-sea angler fish
species.description: Maximum size observed for free living males is 1.3 cm (Ref. 10524).  Males are parasitic, females oviparous with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36494).  Eggs are presumably contained in floating gelatinous rafts (Ref. 36494). Minimum depth from Ref. 037729.

species.name: Krusensterniella maculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Krusensterniella multispinosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Krusensterniella notabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Krusensterniella pavlovskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the outer shelf (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Krynicki's loach
species.description: Occurs in the upper montane reaches of rivers.  Scarce but possibly overlooked (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kryptoglanis shajii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in subterranean streams. Observed to inhabit an open water body, over the paddy fields and water sources feeding paddy fields. Found mainly hiding between submerged vegetation present on the sides of the water body (Ref. 92081). Specimens collected from 5.5-m-deep well containing water where it is situated on the slope of a hilly terrain and receives water from groundwater springs, subterranean. Female individuals (4.95-5.44 cm SL) collected had distended bellies containing mature eggs. In the laboratory, the fishes thrive on Artemia nauplii and minced earthworms (Ref. 86813).

species.name: Kryptolebias brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water streams within forest at about 50 cm deep (Ref. 52503).  Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kryptolebias campelloi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kryptolebias caudomarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Kryptolebias gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in creeks and swamps in open vegetation areas, in shallow water (about 5-10 cm deep), both in clear and tea colored water (Ref. 72398).  Feeds mainly on ostracods and terrestrial arthropods, but also takes copepods and decapods (Ref. 72398).

species.name: Kryptolebias hermaphroditus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A hermaphroditic species.

species.name: Kryptolebias ocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptolebias sepia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in primary forests with a very dense canopy cover and appears to inhabits only extremely shallow parts of small creeks in hilly areas. Occurs outside the main stream in swampy areas directly adjacent to creeks.

species.name: Kryptopterus baramensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptopterus cheveyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and canals (Ref. 12693).  Enters flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on larvae of chironomids and ephemeropterans as well as zooplankton and fishes.  Sold fresh or smoked and large individuals may be put on ice and shipped to Thailand (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Kryptopterus cryptopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptopterus geminus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large rivers with turbid waters (Ref. 27732) and in streams and canals (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on fish, prawns, insects and their larvae (Ref. 12693).  Spawns during the early part of the rainy season.  The young move toward the seasonally flooded habitats and are first seen in August.  Marketed fresh or smoked on a skewer.

species.name: Kryptopterus lais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and main rivers (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on small fishes and prawns (Ref. 56749).  Usually processes as smoked or salted fish (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Kryptopterus lumholtzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptopterus mononema
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptopterus palembangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mainsheams and peat adjacent areas.  Important food fish in northeast and central Thailand, sometimes seen in aquarium trade (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Kryptopterus paraschilbeides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates and small fishes. In the Cambodian Mekong, the fish migrates into the flooded forest during high water periods and returns to the rivers in November where they remain until March (Ref. 55768).

species.name: Kryptopterus piperatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a small river under primary forest cover and with a moderate current, turbid water and with many fallen trees and a muddy substrate.  Also found in areas with clear water and substrate consisting of sand and gravel (Ref. 52489).

species.name: Kryptopterus sabanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kryptopterus schilbeides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, canals, ditches and swamps.  Moves into flooded forests during high water periods and returns to rivers in November where they remain common at least until March.  Feeds on small fishes, prawns and insect larvae.  Marketed fresh or smoked (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Kryptopterus vitreolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow moving to standing, brown to black, water (Ref. 93176).

species.name: Kuban barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain and piedmont streams, with strong current, sand, gravel or rock bottom.  Less abundant in lowland stretches and estuary. Larvae and small juveniles feed predominantly on chironomids and algae while larger juvenile and adults prey on a variety of benthic invertebrates and small fish.  Spawns on gravel bottom.  Widely distributed and abundant, but rare in lower Kuban since construction of Krasnodar dam (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kuban long-barbelled gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits high-gradient stretches of large rivers with fast (not turbulent) current and gravel or sand bottom.  Nocturnal, found near shores at night on mud or sand bottom. Appears to  spawn early and have a short spawning period. Only large juveniles were encountered in July (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kuban's nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits piedmont and montane rivers with strong current and gravel bottom.  Occurs most of the year in the middle or upper stretches of rivers and moves downstream in winter to lower stretches or larger tributaries.  Feeds predominantly on detritus, but also takes periphyton, benthic invertebrates, especially during first year of life.  Spawns at sites with gravel or hard sand,  with rapids and swift current (up to 1.5 m/s), 0.2-1.0 m deep, in clean water with high oxygen concentrations.  Very sensitive to water quality, especially turbidity (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kubuna hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear rivers and small tributary streams over mud, sand and rocky bottoms.

species.name: Kudersky parketnik
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 6 specimens. But specimens might have been misidentified especially with Muraenolepis microps (Ref. 74968).

species.name: Kudo's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuhlia petiti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Kuhlia salelea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuhlia sauvagii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuhlia xenura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brackish water, tide pools, over sand, and near rocks and reef in estuaries, back-reefs, or areas of strong surge (Ref. 58302).  Inshore species, often seen in schools (Ref. 41640).  Adults nocturnal (Ref. 41640).

species.name: Kuiter's damselfish
species.description: Adults inhabit flat or sloping sand bottoms with sparse coral outcrops (Ref. 31106), where they make burrows amongst rubble for nesting (Ref. 48636).  Found solitary (usually juveniles) or in pairs (adults), hovering a short distance from the bottom (Ref. 31106).  Likely to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 31106).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 48636). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Kukumai
species.description: Inhabits muddy bottoms with preference for depths 100 to 140 m.  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 1967).  Oviparous (Ref. 205). Both male and female guard the eggs (Ref.  52177).  An important food fish (Ref. 4537)

species.name: Kulbicki's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Kulbicki’s pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Male carries the eggs in a brood pouch (Ref. 205). Found in coastal reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Kululu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer shallow areas near the edges of the lake (Ref. 52307). Occurs in schools at the surface; stomach of specimens which were examined contained organic debris; benthic and epilithic diatoms, and sponge spicules were nearly always present and many had inorganic particles in the stomach; individuals were seen shoveling sand into the mouth, moving it about in the buccopharynx, then spitting out the sand and making swallowing movements (Ref. 2). Lacks marked sexual dichromatism when sexually active (Ref. 81260). Probably a biparental ovophilic mouthbrooder that forms little to no (Ref. 52307) and only temporary pair bonds (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Kumaon snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Kumawa rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality lies at an altitude of 1,050 m and consists of a small ephemeral lake basin, approximately 1000 m long and 600 m wide. During dry periods, it consists of small creek that emerges from limestone rocks on the edge of the basin and flows for 500-600 m before draining underground. The maximum width of this remarkably clear creek varies from about 1-2 m, with a maximum depth of 30-50 cm, and average depth of about 10-20 cm. Late early March 2013, most fish, particularly large adults, were concentrated in rocky pools near the end of the creek, just before it disappeared into the ground. But conditions had changed dramatically due to heavy rainfall during a second visit near the end of March where the creek was then inundated, forming a small lake and consequently, the fish is more widely dispersed (Ref. 95068).

species.name: Kumba calvifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba dentoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba gymnorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba hebetata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Kumba japonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba maculisquama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba musorstom
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kumba punctulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuna goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in exposed sandbeds (Ref. 93936), An elusive species for It occupies an obscure habitat:and was collected in deeper water than is usually surveyed, it was far from reef substrate, and the area is subject to some siltation from the Panamanian mainland.  The species is also not particularly different-looking from the usual sand-bed gobies that it would not attract attention (Ref. 58754) .Depth at 15 - 20 m (Ref. 58754), range given by B. Victor (pers.comm. 10/18).

species.name: Kunapari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A plankton feeder occurring mostly in swamps or flooded grounds of coastal zones, either in turbid or clear  stagnant water (Ref. 35237).  Possesses very long and very fine branchial archs which allow it to filter microorganism-rich waters of the flooded savannas and swamps which are its preferred habitats (Ref. 27188).  Males are larger than females, attaining maturity between 17 and 22 cm.  Reproduction takes place during the rainy season (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Kunar snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams.

species.name: Kunming catfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This carnivorous species lives in the edge of the lake with plenty of waterweeds where it stays at bottom of water by day and comes out to the surface seeking food by dawn and dusk (Ref. 45563, 117912).  It relies on the macrophytes for shelter, the disappearance of which from the lake exposed these big fishes in the shallow water which resulted to  increased mortality from its natural enemy and human beings. Predation of eggs and juveniles by the introduced
species in the lake may also play an important role (Ref. 117912).

species.name: Kupang cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154). Solitary or in groups, adults in pairs. Also found in sheltered rocky reefs in 2-15 m, often in silty conditions (Ref 90102).

species.name: Kupang pony fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kura barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Kura bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kura chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kura goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kura gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kura nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on plants, flying insects and larvae of aquatic insects (Ref. 41168).

species.name: Kura shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poorly studied species which occurs in brackish water (Ref. 593).

species.name: Kurchatov's notoliparis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuria labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers.  They spawn during the southwest monsoon.  Do not normally breed in ponds.  Artificial breeding done through hypophysation.  Cultured in ponds along with other carp species.

species.name: Kuronezumia dara
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuronezumia endoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuronezumia macronema
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Kuronezumia paepkei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Kuronuma's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Kurt's coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 5396.

species.name: Kuschakewitsch loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mature females are at least 5 cm TL.  Eggs are about 1 mm in diameter (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Kutubu hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An extremely abundant species which forms schools along shallow margins of the lake in both open water or amongst aquatic vegetation.

species.name: Kutubu tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the type locality; specimens captured in 1983 from shallow water with a soft, muddy bottom and abundant aquatic vegetation.

species.name: Kutum
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. A semi-anadromous species which occurs in large brackish estuaries and their large, freshened plume waters, coastal lakes connected to rivers and lowland stretches of large rivers. Can tolerate salinities up to 7-12 ppt. Landlocked populations live in lakes or reservoirs. Larvae and early juveniles take zooplankton, algae and insect larvae as food while adults feed on molluscs, Rhithropanopeus crabs and other benthic invertebrates. Feeding ceases while migrating, spawning and overwintering. Breeds in small rivers or streams with heavy current on gravel bottom. Begins migration to rivers in second half of October (Black Sea, rarely in Caspian Sea). When rivers are covered with ice, spawning migration stops and continues when ice breaks up or even under ice in February-April. Spawns in April-May. Adults migrate back to estuaries to forage immediately after spawning. Juveniles move to estuaries during first summer in August. Landlocked populations undertake migration in springs from lakes or reservoirs or middle stretches of rivers to tributaries or upper reaches (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Kwangtung skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in the sublittoral zone, 30-100 m on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 6.5 cm long and 4.0 cm wide (Ref. 41249). FB name from Ref. 10932.

species.name: Kwazulu sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from a large cave by hand net or spear (Ref. 107896).

species.name: Kyushu bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Küçük Menderes spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Kızılırmak killifish
species.description: Inhabits a wide range of freshwater habitats, ranging from springs and small streams to large dam lakes (Ref. 98396).

species.name: L'empereur du Vanuatu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, clear streams with rocky bottom; the species utilizes presence of  heavy rains to migrate to the sea or to the river.  The mature specimens were collected at an altitude of 300 m.  Few specimens were found to have fed on aquatic insects and crustacean (Ref. 75882).

species.name: La Lucha blind catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A troglobitic species (Ref. 52912).

species.name: La Palma pupfish
species.description: Area of collection, Charco La Palma, during spring has water temperature of 21°C, clear with muddy bottom easily roiled; algae predominant, with some submerged terrestrials, and formerly with swampy outlet that extended 2-3 m 'downstream' SE, is now dry (Ref. 26729).  Not a seasonal killifish and difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: La Palma silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: La Plata croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Important food fish.

species.name: La Plata skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 24 m (Ref. 26282). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 57911).

species.name: La Preciosa silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: La Queche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep, open pools and channels of turbid, lowland rivers; small lakes and impoundments (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on surface and aquatic insects, crustaceans, mollusks, small fishes, frogs, shrew, and mice (Ref. 10294).  Migrates upstream in the spring to spawn and feed.  Moves downstream in the fall.  Mainly nocturnal.  Preyed upon by birds, some mammals, and other fishes.  Marketed smoked.

species.name: Labeo alluaudi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 16.5 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Labeo alticentralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo angra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, lakes and ponds (Ref. 4832).  Important food and sport fish (Ref. 40948).

species.name: Labeo annectens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL recorded: 48.5 cm (Ref. 2801). Occurs in flowing rivers; consumed as food (Ref. 11970).

species.name: Labeo baldasseronii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo barbatulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in middle and lower reaches of the Congo basin with rapid water flow (Ref. 26192).

species.name: Labeo batesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young specimens (up to 2.5 cm SL) are recorded from the Benito River in Cameroon (Ref. 1440). Most of the individuals examined were collected from areas with rapidly flowing water (Ref. 26190). Maximum TL recorded: 19.0 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Labeo boga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers and their tributaries, above tidal influence (Ref.  41236).  Spawns in  flooded rivers (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Labeo bottegi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo brachypoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: close to L. coubie and L. walkeri (possible synonymy but few available data to confirm) also to L. curriei.

species.name: Labeo caeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo camerunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo chariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo curchius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo curriei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 21 cm (Ref. 2801). Affinities: distinguished from other Labeo species by its high body and the # and form of the gill rakers.

species.name: Labeo cyclopinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo degeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Labeo dhonti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo dyocheilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in clear active currents of large rivers (Ref. 4832).  A migratory species (Ref. 37772).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).

species.name: Labeo erythropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bottom depths of large rivers in lower Mekong, including the upper edge of the freshwater tidal zone.  Typically found in fairly fast currents, although it is encountered in the seasonally sluggish Tonlé Sap in Cambodia.  Enters flooded forests, preferring areas with at least some current.  Herbivorous, feeding on bottom algae, phytoplankton, periphyton and detritus.  Large fish are marketed fresh, smaller ones are made into prahoc.  Known to proliferate in impoundments (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Labeo falcipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo filiferus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo forskalii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in rocky areas (Ref. 28714, 47905). Feeds on phytobenthos, debris and mud; juveniles may feed on zooplankton (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Labeo fulakariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo greenii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo horie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo indramontri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).

species.name: Labeo kawrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).  A prolific breeder and spawning commences on the onset of south-west monsoons (Ref. 4832).  Suitable  for aquaculture (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Labeo kibimbi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo kirkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapid waters and swampy areas (Ref. 26192).

species.name: Labeo latebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recovered on soft-bottomed in-shore habitats, in quite shallow water (Ref. 116769). Long intestines partly filled with small particles suggest that this species is browsing the upper sediment layers on the riverbed for Aufwuchs and organic material (Ref. 116769).

species.name: Labeo lineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Lake Tanganyika and larger rivers (Ref. 4967) .Lives over mud bottoms close to sand banks.  The adults are often captured  over sandy bottoms in deep water (Ref. 26190).

species.name: Labeo lividus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum standard length reported: 160.5mm (Ref. 26190).

species.name: Labeo longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Labeo lualabaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo luluae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo macrostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo maleboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo meroensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found in flowing shallow water over sand, and submerged shore vegetation (Ref. 75742).

species.name: Labeo microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo mokotoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo moszkowskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo nandina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and beels (Ref. 1479).  Occurs in the upper reaches of large rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Labeo nasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapid water habitats (Ref. 1440).

species.name: Labeo nigrescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo nigricans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.

species.name: Labeo nunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo pangusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rivers, lakes and ponds (Ref. 4832); in active currents of large streams and upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).  Feeds mostly on algae and diatoms (Ref. 44151).  An excellent foodfish (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Labeo parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stony river beds and in mountain pools formed by small brooks (Ref. 4906). Maximum TL was recorded at 51.5 cm (Ref. 12456).

species.name: Labeo pellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo pierrei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Labeo pietschmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species can be found in the Juba River, a permanently flowing river through acacia woodland; the fish were caught in a shallow stretch where the water flows rapidly over shingle (Ref. 32347).

Is a partial piscivore:  specimens smaller than 15 FL mainly eat insect larvae and zooplankton, but also some fish. species.name: Labeobarbus wurtzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Barbus wurtzi has differences in meristic and morphometric characteristics depending on which population; body depth varies between 26-33% in Guinean rivers and 34-43% in the Cavally and Nipoué rivers; the caudal peduncle length-height ratio is approximately 100% in Cavally-Nipoue and reaches an average of 140% in Guinean rivers; population east of Ivory Coast has intermediary characteristics such as number of scales above and below the lateral line: 4.5 in Guinea and Ivory Coast, 3.5 in western part of Ivory Coast and east of Liberia (Ref. 2940). Maximum TL was recorded at 27.5 cm (Ref. 2801).

Chironomid and centropogomid larvae, mites, ostracods and other small invertebrates comprise a small proportion of the gut contents (Ref. 4889).

species.name: Laboute's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rubble patches of seaward and back reef slopes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Labracoglossa argenteiventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mid-water of rocky reefs.  Forms schools.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Labre a poitrine jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in clear lagoon and seaward reefs from the lower surge zone to a depth of 30 m (Ref. 1602).  Usually in areas with mixed rubble, coral, or rock and sand (Ref. 9710).  Usually solitary among large corals.  Small juveniles swim with their head down, keeping dorsal and anal fins erected, and may seem like the face of a larger fish when viewed from side on by a predator (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).   Occasionally seen in fish markets and aquarium trade.

species.name: Labre a` barre rouge
species.description: Found in areas with hard substrates, including rocky ledges and patches of dead corals or rocks lying on silty sand bottoms (Ref. 128563).

species.name: Labre banane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is reported to be found on deep offshore reefs as adults, but juveniles may occur as shallow as 9 m (Ref. 75973).  Also, adults inhabit the vicinity of coral and rocky reefs, often over sand or rubble in deeper water.  Feed mainly on benthic invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 9823).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  An excellent food fish (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Labre bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on the surge zone of coral reefs or rocky coasts (Ref. 9710, 58534).  They occur singly or in pairs (Ref. 9710).  Tiny juveniles swim with head towards the bottom and slowly undulate the body, looking like a floating leaf in the current (Ref. 48636).  Young feed primarily on small crustaceans and polychaetes, adults switch to larger crustaceans and mollusks as well as polychaetes (Ref. 1602).  They bury at night (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Occasionally trawled (Ref. 30573).  Not common in fish markets.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Labre californien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefer rocky bottom, particularly in kelp beds.  Often feed on hard-shelled organisms such as sea urchins, mollusks, lobsters and crabs.  Spawning occur during the summer and the eggs are pelagic (Ref. 9311).  Live to more than 50 years of age.  Each individual functions first as a female but changes to a male at a length of about 30 cm.  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Flesh is white,  of good quality and marketed fresh (Ref. 9311).  The large teeth can cause serious bite wounds.

species.name: Labre capitaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A large and economically valuable species, monandric and a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 93709).  Adults are found over open bottoms or coral reef areas (Ref. 5217).  Often encountered  where gorgonians are abundant (Ref. 13442).  Feed mainly on mollusks, also crabs and sea urchins (Ref. 3726).  Flesh highly esteemed; marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 3726).  Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Labre diane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral rich areas of seaward reefs (Ref. 5213). Reported to be associated with the mushroom Heliofungia actiniformis (Ref. 91291). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Labre exquis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over rubble or low patch reefs in areas of current (Ref. 9823); also on reef edges and around bommies with rubble zones (Ref. 48636); often in moderately large groups and mixed sex during feeding on zooplankton well above the substrate. Males often display to each other (Ref. 48636). Reported to be associated with the mushroom coral Heliofungia actiniformis (Ref. 91291). Feeds on zooplankton in the water column (Ref. 9823).

species.name: Labre iris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep rocky areas.  Feed on crabs, gastropods and polychaetes (Ref. 4742).

species.name: Labre masqué
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit semi-exposed reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Common in areas of mixed sand, and rubble that are subject to mild surge (Ref. 1602, 58466).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles shallow on rubble amongst large bommies or protected open patches on reef crests and swim as if were a leaf floating along the bottom; large adults move along over large reef section, usually in pairs and typically turn or shift large pieces of rubble or debris that they grab and pull with their mouth or push over with their snout.  Often, while one works the piece, the other grabs exposed prey.  They are sometimes called rock-mover wrasse, but they don't move real rocks (Ref. 48636).  Highly territorial (Ref. 9823).  Feed on mollusks, sea urchins, brittle stars, polychaetes, and crabs (Ref. 5213); feeding is done by overturning large rocks to expose target preys.  The young imitate drifting masses of algae (Ref. 2334).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9311).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Labre mèche blonde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 40 m.  Territorial around prominent coral formations called 'cleaning stations' (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles generally solitary and quite secretive in caves while adults may wander over a large area in search of other fishes with ectoparasites (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Labre nain d'herbier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet (Ref. 30573) seagrass beds and algal flats.

species.name: Labre oiseau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 90102) that inhabits coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Also in rocky reefs (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5374).

species.name: Labre pointillé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found at moderate depths (50 m).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Labre rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs, usually deeper than 20 m to at least 42 m (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles are solitary and adults form small groups, each with several females and a dominant male (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Labre rouge
species.description: Mainly found over rocky bottoms of insular areas (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Labre sik-lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in seaward reefs among coral branches.  Also in clear coastal waters, dense coral habitats on shallow reef crest or slopes to depth of about 20 m.  Usually occurs in small loose groups.  A shy species, usually swimming amongst the protection of coral branches (Ref. 48636).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans  (Ref. 1602).  Secretive (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Labre à barre noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky and reef-like areas, rich in algae (Ref. 26999).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 5292).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Labre à deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common around rubble and sand in steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710), and drop-offs, usually adjacent to very deep water.  They form small aggregations in soft bottom habitats with sponges and soft corals.  The group usually comprising juveniles and females which are dominated by a large male (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Labre à dos jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reefs over bottom of coral rubble or heads of small finely branched coral.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Usually occurs in moderately large groups in depths of about 20-25 m (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Labre à grosses lèvres
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs.  Juveniles occur inshore, found among branching corals while adults found in areas of mixed sand, rubble, and coral (Ref. 9710).  Large adults in deeper water (Ref. 48636).  Maximum length beyond 45 cm TL is unlikely, with largest measured individual at 37 cm TL (Ref,    Feeds mainly on small invertebrates, especially crustaceans, polychaete worms, mollusks and brittle stars (Ref. 9823).  Diet changing from primarily demersal planktonic crustaceans to hard-shelled invertebrates with growth (Ref. 37816).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Labre à queue de comète
species.description: Inhabits outer reef slopes or deep clear lagoons among rubble or clumps of algae; also in seagrass beds (Ref. 1602, 41878, 58302).  Often in sheltered estuaries and harbors (Ref. 48636).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Labre à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in areas of mixed coral, rubble, consolidated limestone, and sand of seaward reefs; also in soft coral or sponge habitats (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).   Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Labre à tache pectorale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602); common in clear shallow waters at 1-8 m; large individuals occasionally at greater depths below 27 m (Ref. 75973).  Juveniles occur solitary in caves or under ledges and act as cleaners by picking at bodies of other fishes (adults occasionally do this) (Ref. 1602); occurring regularly at depths of 14-26 m (Ref. 75973).  Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled, invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 9823).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Not commonly marketed.  Occasionally seen in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Labre à trois taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas of reef flats, lagoons, and semi-protected seaward reefs.  Juveniles shallow in protected coastal waters; adults to about 30 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on sand and rubble dwelling invertebrates (crustaceans, mollusks, forams, polychaetes, fish eggs, and small fishes).
