species.description: One of the bagrid catfish species known to be endemic to the Mahakam River drainage. Found in streams with a moderate or fast flowing current with clear, sometimes tannin-stained, water (Ref. 121927).

species.name: Leiocassis saravacensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leiocassis tenebrica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing forest stream with clear water, 80% canopy cover, cascades up to 4 m high and a substrate consisting of sand, silt and rock (Ref. 57084).

species.name: Leiocassis yeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leiognathus parviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leiognathus robustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leiopotherapon plumbeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leister sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lemaitre's mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow zones of lake.  Reported to live in brackish coastal waters.

species.name: Lembeh rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lemon damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear lagoon and seaward reefs among branching corals. They occur in small aggregations.  Feed mainly on algae and planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Lemon ghost flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf and in the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Lemon Guppy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lemon pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over limestone rock and rubble slope with scattered patches of sand and small holes, crevices, and caves, with some scattered scleractinian, gorgonian and soft corals;  the water was clear, with low to moderate currents.Collected by rotenone & vacuum device (Ref. 126105).

species.name: Lemon-striped pygmy hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was observed on a gentle slope, over clean rubble, in a highcurrent area (Ref. 82450).

species.name: Lenok
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A slow-growing fish which inhabits rivers.  A cold water fish and never goes to the ocean; finds deep cold waters during summer; can be found under the ice in late fall and winter (Ref. 12218).  Feeds on larval and adult insects, amphipods, small fish, frogs, mice and salmon spawn (Ref. 593).  During spawning the body turns to a dark red and the dorsal and pectoral fins change to a rainbow of colors (Ref. 12218).

species.name: Lentipes adelphizonus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing, clear streams with rocky and boulder-strewn bottom (Ref. 57053).

species.name: Lentipes andamanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lentipes argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift, clear high gradient stream with a rocky and boulder-strewn bottom.  Presumed to be amphidromous as the other members of the subfamily (Ref. 97410).

species.name: Lentipes caroline
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lentipes crittersius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected above a series of waterfalls, together with Sicyopus discordipinnis and Stiphodon birdsong (Ref. 39342).

species.name: Lentipes dimetrodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift, clear mountain stream, above several waterfalls, with rocky and boulder-strewn bottom, together with Stiphodon birdsong, several species of Sicyopterus and S. mystax (Ref. 39342).

species.name: Lentipes ikeae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small and rapid mountain stream with a rocky bottom and boulder-strewn at an altitude ranging between 310 and 488 above sea level.  Presumed to be amphidromous as the other members of the subfamily (Ref. 97410).

species.name: Lentipes kolobangara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, clear, high-gradient streams with a rocky and boulder-strewn bottom between 50 and more than 600 m above sea level (Ref. 109045).

species.name: Lentipes mekonggaensis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in a swift, clear high gradient stream with a rocky and boulder-strewn bottom
at the edge of oil palm plantation (388 m above sea level).  Presumed to be amphidromous as the other members of the subfamily (Ref. 97410).

species.name: Lentipes mindanaoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lentipes multiradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lentipes solomonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in clear, rocky streams running through rainforest from 30-230 m elevation (Ref. 79611).

species.name: Lentipes venustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mountainous terrain in cool, clear and fast flowing streams at elevations from about 100 to at least 600 m.  Collected at depth ranging between approximately 0.5 and 1.3 m.  Usually observed resting on the bottom attached to rock surfaces by their pelvic sucker (Ref. 77028).

species.name: Lentipes watsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with cobbles, boulders and sand bottoms in clear water with slow to very rapid flow through open forest.

species.name: Lentipes whittenorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly amphidromous (Ref. 26364).

species.name: Leobarbus batesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leon Springs pupfish
species.description: Inhabits margins of spring-fed marsh pools; most common away from vegetation (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on diatoms, amphipods, and ostracods (Ref. 79012).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Leopard blenniella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from an inner portion of reef flat in small, irregular sand pool, between limestone outcrops with coral fragments, at 0.1 m (Ref. 9962).  Adults are found in intertidal zone (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Leopard blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on clear coastal reefs, often in bays and semi-exposed habitats (Ref. 48636). Found on the seaward edge of reefs, among corals like Acropora, Pocillopora, Seriatopora, Porites, and Millepora where they feed on coral tissues (Ref. 1602). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Males prepare nesting sites by overgrazing a patch of coral (Ref. 9710). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Leopard catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Leopard cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leopard corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons-chats. Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leopard darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel and rubble runs of clear, small to medium rivers.

species.name: Leopard dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Leopard Epaulette shark
species.description: Usually encountered on coastal fringing reefs and patch reefs during night diving, although it is sometimes seen during the day, sheltering under rocky outcrops or tabular corals (Ref. 83755).

species.name: Leopard goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in living coral colonies; one of several small fishes that lives among the tentacles of living corals (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Leopard jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, on rubble or soft bottoms.  Reported to have bitten waders, but usually harmless.

species.name: Leopard mandarin fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leopard numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from shallow and sandy bottom area. The 33 cm TL pregnant female has a total of 12 embryos with 2 females and 10 males, measuring between 6.2 and 6.8 cm TL (Ref. 116153). Males mature at ca. 18 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Leopard pleco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal; feeds on algae (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Leopard searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow-water bays.

species.name: Leopard sharpnose puffer
species.description: Lives in deep water habitats, usually along deep drop-offs in caves at more than 30 meters depth (Ref. 48637). Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Leopard skate
species.description: Maximum length observed was 139 cm TL (Ref. 89865).

species.name: Leopard snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leopard splitfin
species.description: In small creeks with dense vegetation; feeds on algae.

species.name: Leopard squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers floodplain drainage river and large lagoons (Ref. 7248).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leopard toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore water on deeper rocky reefs.

species.name: Leopard whipray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal on soft substrate inshore (Ref.58048). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Size at birth about 20 cm WD and 92 cm TL (Ref. 90102).  Caught occasionally in the demersal tangle net, bottom trawl and longline fisheries. Utilized for its meat, skin (high value) and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Leopard whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Leopard wirrah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300), on reefs (Ref. 127767).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Lepadichthys bilineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a tide pool (Ref. 103877).

species.name: Lepadichthys ctenion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepadichthys erythraeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from the base of a coral block on a reef flat with mixed sand and flat rock with patches of dead corals, from within live coral head in a sheltered bay, from a fringing reef at a depth of 1-3 m and from an isolated coral block. All were collected in close association with sea urchins of the genus Diadema, utilizing the long spines for shelter (Ref. 103877).

species.name: Lepadichthys frenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky shores and coral reefs, usually under Diadema setosum.

species.name: Lepadichthys sandaracatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidamia natalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Lepidammodytes macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus attenuatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common cichlid of the shallow intermediate habitat (Ref. 46829, 52921). Has been caught at a depth of 25 m  (Ref. 53528). Usually solitary and hovers well above the ground; prefers sand and digs large crater-shaped nests, even when there rocks offering good shelters nearby, a fact that shows that the choice of a nest site can be very revealing of a species ecology (Ref. 6770). Carnivorous, preys on fish (Ref. 6770, 53528). Also feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives as pairs and digs a pit on the sand floor, where the female stays in one or more snail shells  (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary; are rock-dwellers and do not roam the wide open sandy bottoms.  Carnivorous, preys on fish (Ref. 6770, 54948).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus hecqui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shell-dweller (7343).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus kamambae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in transition zone between rocks and sand at 15 m depth; habitat consists of sparsely scattered stones of 0.2-2 m in size on white sand bottom; hunts prey on the open sand floor; feeds mainly on cichlid fish juveniles (Ref. 91764).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus kendalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rock-dweller (Ref. 6770, 7343, 46829). Usually solitary (Ref. 6770, 46829), covers large distances while cruising through habitat searching for prey (Ref. 46829). Does not roam the wide open sandy bottoms; carnivorous, preys on fish (Ref. 6770). Piscivore; found in shallow water as well as deeper than 40 metres (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus meeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has probably never been imported because of its narrow distribution at Katibili Bay (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus mimicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly along the rocky coast; feeds exclusively on fishes and mainly on young and sub-adults of cyprichromine cichlids; when hunting for prey, it exhibits aggressive mimicry by changing its body coloration; seems to breed in rather deep water (> 30 m); probably monogamous (Ref. 76873).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus profundicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary, are rock-dwellers and do not roam the wide open sandy bottoms. L. profundicola lives deeper than L. elongatus or L. kendalli and is seldom found near the surface. Carnivorous, feeds on fish (Ref. 6770, 54948).

species.name: Lepidiolamprologus variostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat characterized by a steeply dropping and craggy rock cliff with terrace-like flats covered by deposits of sand and detritus and with many horizontal and vertical, narrow cracks; compressed body and short pectorals indicate a life in narrow, vertical cracks (Ref. 47366).

species.name: Lepidion capensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 6606).

species.name: Lepidion guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidion natalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Rarely collected.  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Lepidobero sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys alkaia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys arunachalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys barbatuloides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys birmanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small, clear, swift streams with sandy bottoms (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on worms and insect larvae along with some algae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys coromandelensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear streams with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys eleios
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Three sampling sites of this species are characterized by deep water, very slow current, dense shore vegetation, large extents of floating mats of plants, and bottom composed of mud or clay covered with a layer of vegetal debris. Collected from leaf litter, from among the dense vegetation or by scraping the underside of the 'floating' vegetation using a tray net . The following fish species were collected in the same micro-habitat: Oreichthys sp., Pethia erythromycter, Heteropneustes fossilis, Chaudhuria sp., Mastacembelus pantherinus, Monopterus cuchia, Indostomus paradoxus, Badis corycaeus, Dario hysginon (Ref. 117200).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys furcatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland wetlands (Ref. 57235).  Usually inhabits swamps, river sides, shallow lakes and reservoirs among dense vegetation (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys goalparensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in slow-flowing streams with vegetation (Ref. 83671).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys hasselti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-moving, shallow waters of canals and inundated floodplains (Ref. 12693), usually on or in muddy substrates (Ref. 43281).  Lives in swamps and rivers including peats (Ref. 57235).  Also found in mountain streams, preferring sandy or gravelly bottom (Ref. 51717).  Occurs in running waters of lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Preferred food is zooplankton but occasionally feeds on some algae.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys kranos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalichthys zeppelini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocephalus nanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species seems to prefer large rivers (Ref. 95334).

species.name: Lepidocephalus spectrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidocharax burnsi

species.name: Lepidocharax diamantina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidoperca inornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lepidophanes gaussi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic (Ref. 4479).  Found at 425-850 m during the day and  nyctoepipelagic at the surface and down to 175 m (maximum abundance at 51-100 m) (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Lepidotrigla abyssalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy mud bottoms.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy-mud bottoms.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 93 m (Ref. 33021).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 70  (Ref. 33021).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 271 m (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Lepidotrigla papilio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays and coastal marine waters, over the continental shelf (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Lepidotrigla pectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 309 m (Ref. 33021).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. The body is slender and covered with large deciduous scales above the lateral line and cycloid scales below the lateral line.  Throat, chest and breast are scaleless.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of about 82 m (Ref. 33021).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Leporacanthicus triactis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to inhabit burrows (Ref. 82067).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus acutidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).  Males are sexually mature at 1 year while the females become mature at 2 years.  Reproduction is from November to March with a peak from December to March.  The female spawns 100,000 to 200,000 eggs (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Leporinus affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in sand holes of fast-flowing creeks.  Feed on plants, fruits and leaves (Ref. 36801).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus agassizii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus alternus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus altipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species prefers black-water rivers, and is found in tributaries of the Amazonas river basin, such as the Arapiuns and Negro rivers, and in the Orinoco river basin (Ref. 130734). Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers.  Some specimens were collected near bedrock outcroppings and banks (Ref. 96504).

species.name: Leporinus aripuanaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus badueli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal rivers (Ref. 36801).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus gossei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live upstream, in creeks where there is an alternating zone of swift rapids and canals with deeper calm waters. They occur in the company of Leporinus granti (Ref. 12225). Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Leporinus granti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in large numbers at the entrance of creeks where the bottom is sandy or muddy and the current is fast or slow (Ref. 27188).  Juveniles occur in calm, shallow waters, in counter current zones or in the shelter of plants (Ref. 12225).  Omnivorous.  They possess enzymes which enable them to digest chitin, pectin, hemicellulose and mucopolysaccharides.  Individuals are easily captured with hook and line with small hooks (Ref. 27188).  Reproduction takes place from December to June (Ref. 12225).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).  Known among aquarists, this fish is considered turbulent in captivity (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Leporinus guttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in clear water streams, near waterfalls or in a cofferdam just above a waterfall (Ref. 80699).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Lives in upper layer of waters of the plains of cold temperate zone.  Often stays in slow-moving rivers, lakes or still waters, moves fast and sprightly (Ref. 45563).  Feeds on siliceous algae, filiform algae and aquatic insects (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Leuciscus ukliva
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slows-flowing and still water (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in water bodies on the low plains, with little current.  Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Leucobrotula adipata
species.description: 7 specimens known (Ref. 36126).

species.name: Leucos albus
species.description: Prefers  to inhabit sub-lacustrine springs of Lake Skadar, where large numbers of fish gather during the winter period.  Coexists with <i>Leuocos basak in Lake Skadar, with 20:1 proportion in favor of <i>Leuocos basak (Ref. 96829).

species.name: Leucos aula
species.description: Found in canals, swamps, lakes and streams with slow current and dense vegetation (Ref. 59043). Prefers to inhabit lakes and still waters of rivers; does not thrive in moderately to fast flowing rivers (Ref. 96829). Lives in groups. Omnivorous, feeding mainly on insect larvae, other invertebrates, algae and aquatic macrophytes. Spawns in small groups composed of one female and several males. Deposits eggs on aquatic vegetation (Ref. 59043). Age at first maturity is 1+ or 2+ for males and 2+ for females; maximum age observed is 7+ years (Ref. 96829). Abundant, but locally declining due to the introduction of Carassius gibelio, Ctenopharyngodon idella and Silurus glanis ( in lakes). There are introduced populations locally responsible for extirpation of Rutilus rubilio (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Leucos basak
species.description: Occurs in a wide range of habitats such as warm streams and rivers with moderate to slow current, lakes, backwaters, swampy areas, and artificial water bodies (Ref. 59043).  Sympatric with <i>Leucos albus in Lake Skadar (Ref. 96829).  Feeds on plankton and plant material.  Spawns over gravel and stones and in flooded areas and lakes.  Eggs are sticky, yellow-orange which hatch in 9 days at 13-17°C (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Leucos ylikiensis
species.description: Inhabits lakes (Ref. 59043).  Prefers still water.  May reach up to 20 cm TL according to local fishermen. The maximum length observed in all materials examined collected on April, was for a female of about 15 cm TL, aged 3+, with eggs of about 1.0-1.2 mm of diameter, all of equal size (a sign of a probable single spawning reproductive habit).  Spawning season probably takes place  from March to May (Ref. 96829).

species.name: Leuroglossus callorhini
species.description: A recent reference acknowledging the validity of this species is needed.

species.name: Lewis' round herring
species.description: Usually an inshore schooling species.  More data needed.  Used as bait in the tuna fishery. Found in coastal waters, sometimes forming large active schools at surface near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Lezia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with bottom and pelagic trawls.  Adults are pelagic or epibenthic (Ref. 7097) mostly in shallow waters.  They feed mainly on schooling fishes (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Liberian swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Contrary to what is suggested by its morphology, this species is not cavernicolous; it burrows in mud, never very far from the sea (Ref. 57291). The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Liberty molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liche
species.description: Found on outer continental and insular shelves and slopes (Ref. 247).  Mainly found on or near the bottom but readily occurs well off the substrate (Ref. 247, 58302).  Often pelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found singly or in small schools (Ref. 6871).  Feeds mainly on deepwater bony fish, but also skates, other sharks (etmopterids in Ref. 123656), cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 5578).  This bioluminescent shark (currently the largest luminous vertebrate) emit light ventrally to counterilluminate which might be used to illuminate the ocean floor while searching/hunting for prey; or to stealthily approach prey, using counterillumination camouflage, before striking fast when it is close enough (Ref. 123656). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 10-20 young born at 30-42 cm (Ref. 26346).  Used for its squalene liver oil, leather and meat, as well as for fishmeal (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Lichen moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Lichtenstein's Seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to height.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Licorice gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing creeks among vegetation.

species.name: Licoricemouth cucumberfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lidole
species.description: Occurs in all kinds of habitats but is mainly found in open water away from the coast (Ref. 5595). The most pelagic of the Lake Malawi Oreochromis species (Ref. 2, 87, 4364, 4916, 4967). Forms schools (Ref. 2, 2781). Feeds on phytoplankton (Ref. 2, 87, 5595, 10402, 42295, 52161). Female mouthbrooder (Ref. 2). It is suspected that Oreochromis lidole is now globally extinct, as it has not been positively recorded since 2007 (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Lidwill's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish water (Ref. 559, 43239).  Occurs in schools near the surface (Ref. 559).

species.name: Lieu de Norvege
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species probably occurring in midwater.

species.name: Lifehouse dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shoals, reefs and lagoons in 0-28 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Light cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays in schools of several dozens of individuals (Ref. 35381).  Occurs in creeks with sandy bottoms with slow or strong current (Ref. 27188).  Swims mostly in backwaters and hides itself under logs or rocks.  Its 'locking' mechanism built with its bony plaques, which permit it to keep three spines erected, is a good passive defense mechanism.  Lifespan can last for 7 years.  (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Light dusky rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collection depth between 6-370 m, deepest recorded depth at 675 m.  Large adults common along the edge of the continental shelf at 100-300 m where the species is targeted for commercial use.  Captured in the offshore trawl fishery.  Males and females captured by trawl surveys vary widely in maturity during the summer (May-July) (Ref. 53613).

species.name: Light's bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Does not exhibit diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4778).  Spawning is probably year-round, peaking from late spring to early summer (Ref. 4778).  Photophore complement complete at about 15-17 mm SL (Ref. 4778).

species.name: Lightheaded dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow waters, inside fringing reefs (Ref. 5471).

species.name: Lightning-man threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on a mixed rock, sand, and algae bottom (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lightnose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 26340).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Smallest recorded specimen 8 cm TL. Males reaches maturity at ca. 32 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Lignobrycon myersi
species.description: Black water species.  Feeds on mosquito larvae and other aquatic invertebrates.

species.name: Lilac pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Limace acadienne
species.description: Females are mature at 5.4 cm TL (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Limace ardente
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably feeds on comb jellies, cnidarians, salps and crustaceans (Ref. 12204).  Spawning believed to occur almost year round (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Limace atlantique
species.description: Known from tide pool areas to subtidal; usually 2 meters or less, rarely to 90 meters (Ref. 51661).  Benthic species.  Feeds on crustaceans and worms (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limace de Crozet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported in depths of 700 - 1,134 meters (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Limace de Duhamel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limace de Kerguelen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mature female observed in early summer (December) with 216 eggs from 2 to 3.5 mm (Ref. 45488).

species.name: Limace de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the subtidal zone to less than 300 m (Ref. 4702).  Feeds primarily on crustaceans, occasionally fishes and polychaetes (Ref. 4702).  Spawns in the winter (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Limace de Neelov
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limace des laminaires
species.description: Commonly lives in large clusters of kelp (Ref. 7251).  It prefers bottom types like pebbles, stones or boulders, mud and sand (Ref. 5951).  Benthic species.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426); especially amphipods (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Limace gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limace gélatineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud bottoms (Ref. 5951).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Maximum depth reported at 1800 m (Ref. 58426) and 2,500 m (Ref. .  Feeds on benthic and pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 4702), and worms (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limace marbée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among seaweeds or rocks (Ref. 7251).  Often found in empty scallop shells (Ref. 7251).  Benthic species.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426), such as amphipods and crabs (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Limace noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep, cold water (Ref. 4702).  Maximum depth reported at 4009 m (Ref. 58426).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on pelagic amphipods, benthic gastropods, and mysids (Ref. 4702).

species.name: Limace pote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limace à filaments
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limace à large ouie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 1.45 cm SL fry was caught in the mesopelagic zone (Ref. 44814).

species.name: Limace à longues nageoires
species.description: Epibenthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426). Maximum depth reported at 1322 m (Ref. 41470).

species.name: Limace à longues nageoires (Careproctus reinhardti)
species.description: On muddy bottoms (Ref. 4702).  Maximum depth reported at 1750 m )Ref. 58426).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on benthic and pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 4702) and fishes (Ref. 58426).  Female lays about 300 eggs with a diameter of 4.5 mm (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Limace à museau noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic; feeds on comb jellies and cnidaria (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limace à mâchoire oblique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only 2 specimens. Holotype was found in two pieces in the stomach content of one Dissostichus eleginoides Smitt, 1898 caught between 550 and 1345 m deep off Crozet Is. Paratype is a juvenile collected by net in mid-water at about 350 m deep off Kerguelen Is. (Ref. 47264).

species.name: Limace à ventre sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs measures 2.5-3 mm diameter (Ref. 11892).

species.name: Limande
species.description: Adults live mainly on sandy bottoms, from a few meters to about 100 m.  Feed mainly on crustaceans and small fishes.  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Marketed fresh, dried or salted, smoked and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled.  microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Limande carline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Limande du Japon
species.description: Adults feed on hydroids, worms, mollusks, and brittle stars (Ref. 6885).  Marketed frozen and eaten fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Limande plie rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit soft muddy to moderately hard bottoms (Ref. 5951).  Feed predominantly in daytime on organisms living in, on or near the bottom; shrimps, amphipods, crabs, sea urchins and snails (Ref. 12232).  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).

species.name: Limande sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Lives most often on stony bottoms.  Feeds on a variety of small invertebrates, but polychaetes seem to dominate.  Apparently they do not feed in wintertime (Ref. 9900).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Limande sole du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Adults occur on mud bottom (Ref. 2850).  They move into deep water in winter (Ref. 2850).  Produce large amounts of slime which may cover other fishes when caught in trawls (Ref. 4925).  Marketed as mink food (Ref. 4925) or as fillet (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Limande à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sandy to muddy bottoms (Ref. 7251).  Prefer depths of 37 to 82 m at temperatures of 3-5°C (Ref. 6263).  Feed mainly on polychaete worms and amphipods, shrimps, isopods and other crustaceans and occasionally small fish such as sand lance and capelin (Ref. 12232).  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Marketed fresh or frozen; eaten steamed, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Limande-plie du Japon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limbert achigan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, inshore waters, living on or near the bottom, often congregating in masses around wharves, wrecks and submerged seaweed.  During winter they become torpid and remain inshore under rocks in shallow water (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Limbert du Pacifique oriental
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9274).  Depth range based on holotype (Ref. 9274).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35928).

species.name: Limbert guineen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental shelf and slope.  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 3548).

species.name: Limbert royal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 6687).

species.name: Limbochromis robertsi
species.description: Only found in small, shallow and well-shaded forested creeks with flowing waters; diet consists primarily of detritus and algae, and to a lesser degree shrimp eggs; pair-bonding cave spawner; facultative, larvophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307). Maximum TL was recorded at 10.0 cm (Ref. 5657).

species.name: Limnichthys rendahli
species.description: Better reference needed.

species.name: Limnocottus godlewskii
species.description: A common sculpin of Lake Baikal which is known to occur over a silty bottom.  Spawns in January and February (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Limnotilapia dardennii
species.description: Coastal species which occurs over sand more than rock.  Juveniles inhabit shallow water mostly over sand in mud flats; adults inhabit deeper water and are especially abundant near the rocky slopes.  Is omnivorous, but mainly vegetarian (feeds on phytoplankton, algae, and plants) (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Limones splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limpid cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Limpid-wing flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species.

species.name: Lindman's grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species.  There is insufficient data to show if this species occurs along coasts or whether it is estuarine and not freshwater (Ref. 9822).  Found in estuaries and tidal reaches of rivers (Ref.12693).

species.name: Lindo toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Line knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Line-spotted barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a wide range of habitats from small streams to large rivers.  Moves upstream to spawn in flooded grassy areas (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Lineblotch wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups on coastal reefs mixed sandy and rocky bottoms at 2-10 m  (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Linecheek tank goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers of the lower Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lined barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from swamps and open areas with standing waters and submerged grasses (Ref. 37849).  Quite common in clear, black waters (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Lined chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found singly or in loose aggregations above the upper edges of outer reef slopes with rich coral growth.  Often at the entrance of large caves or near its ceiling (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 48636. Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Lined chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, often near riffles and vegetation (Ref. 5723); also found in small upland creeks over sandy substrates.  Feeds on chironomid larvae and pupae, and larger aquatic insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Lined clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with Strongylocentrotus franciscanus. Adults feed mainly on amphipods but captive specimens also feed on isopods which live commensally on the urchin (Ref. 33548). Oviparous, with attached, demersal eggs and planktonic larvae (Ref. 36496).

species.name: Lined cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lined dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found in or near crevices of coral or rock of shallow reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Lined fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimicked by Petroscirtes fallax and by the young Scolopsis bilineatus. Poisonous canines provide considerable protection from predators.

species.name: Lined grunt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore on rocky bottoms (Ref. 11441). Stomach contents of specimens collected from Iraq composed mainly of mollusks, sponges and tunicates (Ref. 97537).

species.name: Lined grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky creeks and small rivers flowing through rainforest.  Adults congregate in deep holes below rapids.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lined hover goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among mangroves (Ref. 1602) and in lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Lined javelinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy areas in coastal waters (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Lined rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the intertidal zone of rocky shores, rocky reef flats (Ref. 9710), including rock pools, harbors and mangrove zones (Ref. 48636).  They graze algae on rocks by groups (Ref. 90102).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lined silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appear to live in shallow waters in cays or close to shore.  Nothing is known of its biology (Ref. 9760). Sometimes found in brackish marine lake (Ref 90102).

species.name: Lined stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from two specimens taken by trawl (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Lined topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and other vegetated standing water bodies, and quiet pools and backwaters of streams.

species.name: Linedfin rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in tidepools (Ref. 54980). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Linesnout goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only shallow-water sponge-dwelling Elacatinus found in the Gulf of Honduras (Ref. 50538).

species.name: Linespot cardinalfish
species.description: Solitary or in small groups on open sand during night and in coral crevices during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Linespotted ufipa barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lingue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft muddy and sandy bottoms, but never on rocks, gravel or shells. Juveniles live along the coasts at shallow depths (4-6 m); adults migrate to deeper waters, generally to between 110 and 130 m, and in some instances, to over 550 m. Juveniles live in scallops (Placopecten magellanicus) and remain close to scallop beds until they mature (Ref. 9988). They prefer temperatures of 8-10°C (Ref. 5951). Feed on shrimps, amphipods and other crustaceans, also on squid and herring, flatfish, mackerel and others. Utilized fresh, dried or salted and frozen; also small fish are used for fishmeal ; eaten steamed, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988). Maximum depth reported from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Lingue bâtarde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly from 350-500 m depth on muddy bottoms.  Feed on crustaceans and fish (flatfishes, gobies, rocklings) (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Liniparhomaloptera disparis
species.description: Adults occur in babbling bottom of mountain streams (Ref. 26563). Utilized for food (Ref. 89718). Length type refers to body length (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Link's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on silty mud flats among the aerial roots of mangroves (Ref. 37816). Also found in stream mouths or occasionally in saline lakes in 0-3 m (Ref. 90102). Max. length (Edward O. Murdy, pers. comm., 1998).

species.name: Linophryne arborifera
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10762).

species.name: Linophryne arcturi
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10762).

species.name: Linophryne bipennata
species.description: Males unknown (Ref. 42949).

species.name: Linophryne brevibarbata
species.description: Parasitic males.

species.name: Linophryne coronata
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10762).

species.name: Linophryne escaramosa
species.description: Males unknown (Ref. 42949).

species.name: Linophryne lucifer
species.description: Caught in high latitudes by commercial bottom trawls at about 300-600 m, with open pelagic trawls fished at maximum depth of 1000 m (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Linophryne maderensis
species.description: Only 3 females known.  Males unknown (Ref. 13578).

species.name: Linophryne parini
species.description: Known only from a single specimen taken from a depth between 1,200-1220 m.  Males parasitic on females.

species.name: Linophryne polypogon
species.description: Only 1 female known.  Males unknown (Ref. 13578).

species.name: Linophryne quinqueramosa
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Linophryne racemifera
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10762).

species.name: Linophryne sexfilis
species.description: Only 1 female known.  Males unknown (Ref. 13578).

species.name: Liobagrus hyeongsanensis
species.description: A nocturnal species that inhabits the bottom stratum of running waters with moderately fast currents, in upper streams and valley streams.  Generally occurs in shallow water (0.3-0.8 m deep) with large or small stony or pebbly substrates. Lays 60-110 eggs, measuring 2.8-3.3 mm in diameter (Ref. 104914).

species.name: Liobagrus reinii
species.description: Captured from under cobbles and boulders, interstices in bedrock, and in clumps of roots of terrestrial vegetation along banks (Ref. 56675).

species.name: Lion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along exposed reef margins and outer reef slopes.  Has been observed at depth of 183 m in Hawaii (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Secretive during the day and hides in holes and crevices of surge channels.  Feeds at night on crustaceans, crustacean larvae, polychaete worms, and small fishes.  Spine of preopercle venomous.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Lionhead cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; feeds primarily on algae; pair-bonding, cave spawning species (Ref. 52307). Aquarium keeping: in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Liopropoma aragai
species.description: A single specimen taken from about 100 m deep.

species.name: Liopropoma danae
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Liopropoma erythraeum
species.description: Collected in about 100 m on a bank off Okinawa.

species.name: Liopropoma flavidum
species.description: Known only from one specimen taken at a depth of 58 m..

species.name: Liopropoma japonicum
species.description: Found on the shelf and shelf edge, on rocky bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Collected at a depth of about 100 m.

species.name: Liopropoma maculatum
species.description: Collected up to 280 m deep, over rocky bottom.  May occur in shallower waters of Japan (Ref. 6180).

species.name: Liparis adiastolus
species.description: Occurs in shallow water and estuaries (Ref. 50520).

species.name: Liparis agassizii
species.description: Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 28160).

species.name: Liparis alboventer
species.description: Known only from the type specimens collected from silty sand bottom.

species.name: Liparis bikunin
species.description: Known from shallow waters.

species.name: Liparis burkei
species.description: Found in shallow waters (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Liparis chefuensis
species.description: Specimens collected from muddy bottom (Ref. 27965).

species.name: Liparis curilensis
species.description: Found in tide pools to 10 meters (Ref. 51661).  Maximum length questionable (Ref. 50520).

species.name: Liparis eos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis fishelsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis frenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis grebnitzkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the intertidal zone (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Liparis kusnetzovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known in shallow reef waters (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Liparis kussakini
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées. Inhabits tide pools (Ref. 51661). Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Liparis latifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis mednius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tide pools and shallow water (Ref. 51661).  Length assumed to be SL.

species.name: Liparis meridionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis micraspidophorus
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées. An intertidal species (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Liparis miostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from shallow waters (Ref. 28160).

species.name: Liparis newmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liparis punctulatus
species.description: Maximum depth reported at 20 m (Ref. 28160).

species.name: Liparis schmidti
species.description: An intertidal species (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Liparis tessellatus
species.description: Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Lipeo livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 45800).

species.name: Lipogenys gillii
species.description: Feed mostly on organic material contained in bottom sediment drawn up by the sucker-like mouth [RF doubts this is a detritus feeder; the elaborate mouth without teeth looks like a specialization for extracting soft-bodied benthic invertebrates out of the ground; also, there are no gill rakers to filter detritus (Ref. 50674)]. No obvious sexual dimorphism; a female of 37.5 cm SL was still immature (Ref. 50674).

species.name: Lippu bourricot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary and found hiding in reefs and caves during the day (Ref. 9114).  Juveniles appear in late summer and swim in schools.  A nocturnal feeder on reef invertebrates (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Lippu caruco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottoms of shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Lippu casse-paille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic over hard surfaces of the continental shelf (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Lippu croupia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840. Inhabits larger patch reefs and quickly sloping rocky bottoms. Often near the shelter of caves, ledges, or wrecks (Ref. 9710). Feeds at night on crustaceans, mollusks, smaller fish, and the long-spined urchin, Diadema. Marketed fresh.

species.name: Lippu drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottoms of shallow coastal waters.  Also caught with trammel nets and harpoons.  Considered a valuable food-fish.

species.name: Lippu du roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal waters, frequently in rocky reefs and occasionally over sandy bottoms (Ref. 9114); often near kelp beds.  Juveniles form schools in littoral pools (Ref. 9114).  Feed on crustaceans, mollusks and bryozoans.  Pelagic spawner (Ref. 56049).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Lippu grosse tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic over hard, rock and rubble bottoms (Ref. 9114).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9114).

species.name: Lippu rondeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Inhabits reefs and rocky bottoms.  Feeds at night on mollusks, echinoderms, annelids, and crustaceans (Ref. 3798).  Young pick parasites from the bodies of larger fishes (Ref. 5521).  Young are popular aquarium fish (Ref. 7251).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Lippu tricroupia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in brackish estuaries and adjacent areas, over sandy or muddy bottoms.  Sometimes caught in marine waters.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 3798).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3798).

species.name: Lipspot moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal reef flats, usually found in less than 5 m water depth, but ranges to deep water rubble reefs (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Lipstick darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lipstick dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coral and rock areas (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Lipstick goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky mid-hill streams with fast flowing water.  They adhere to the sides of submerged rock through sucking discs.  Occur usually in water 50-150 cm deep.  Carnivore.  Sudden, heavy rainfall with an accompanying drop in water temperature induces spawning, usually in a cavity excavated in sand in the shelter of a stone.  Eggs hatch in the event of another heavy rainfall.  Larvae are swept downriver to the sea, mature adults migrate upstream to spawning grounds.  Possibly amphidromous (Ref. 26364).

species.name: Lipstick leporinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lissocampus bannwarthi
species.description: Occurs in shallow water.  Found among small rocks on sand bottoms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 10.9 cm SL.

species.name: Listrura costai
species.description: Found mostly in narrow (about 1 m wide) and shallow (about 50 cm deep) clear water stream located in a swampy plain area densely vegetated with grass. Captured at night or dusk, suggesting a nocturnal habit (Ref. 91744).

species.name: Listrura depinnai
species.description: Found in a swamp with clear black water, mud and litter bottom, covered with a large amount of emerging vegetation adjacent to a dense and isolated fragment of wetland forest.  Collected at a shallowsite (about 10 cm water depth above nearly 50 cm depth of submerged litter deposits) among the emerging vegetation.  Other fishes captured in the same swamp include species of <i>Cynopoecilus and <i>Gymnotus aff. pantherinus, both are potentially new species (Ref. 94748).

species.name: Listrura picinguabae
species.description: Inhabits narrow and shallow (about 20 cm deep) streams in a dense tropical forest (Ref. 57477).  Encountered buried in litter bottom (Ref. 57477).

species.name: Listrura tetraradiata
species.description: Specimens collected from a small, clear water forest stream, shallow (ca. 40 cm deep), with large rocks on banks, gravel and sand on the bottom.  Stomach contents include copepods and insect larvae and mites (Ref. 41513).

species.name: Lithochromis xanthopteryx
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky substrates.  Restricted to places with large, very steeply sloping boulders, where it inhabits the immediately inshore slope between 0.5 and at least 5 m water depth and lives in crevices between boulders, including rock pools within emerged rocky reefs.  Stomach content analyses of males showed a seasonally variable diet of insect larvae, filamentous Cyanophyta, Bryozoa, prawns, detritus and juvenile fish (Ref. 27668).

species.name: Lithogenes wahari
species.description: Inhabits moderately high gradient forest streams with clear water, swift current, and exposed bedrock substratum. At the time of collection, the water color of the Río Cuao was clear to light green (Ref. 83588).

species.name: Lithoxus lithoides
species.description: Inhabits stony rivulets (Ref. 6868).  Clings to rocks in the rapids (Ref. 2037).

species.name: Little Baikal oilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found beyond 1,000 m depth.  Both males and females often occur on the surface.  In January and February, this fish is often found at a depth range of 300-500 m, in March and April, it is found between 100-120 m.  Reproduction takes place in February until March.  There are indications that the females perish after spawning.  The larvae stay dispersed between the surface and 500 m; they do not undergo daily migrations (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Little bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species, found primarily below 200 m depth (Ref. 36655).  All studied specimens were reported to have been sampled by nonclosing gears from the depth of more than 2000 m that one cannot conclude about the exact sampling depth and the depth range of this species; notably, larger specimens occur deeper than young ones (Ref. 117119). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36655).

species.name: Little clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow weed and seagrass reefs, mostly intertidal (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Little Colorado spinedace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy runs and pools of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Little conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom, on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Little conger eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Little croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shallow, muddy or sandy mud bottoms of estuaries and its adjacent areas.

species.name: Little dory
species.description: Occurs on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Little fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in offshore reefs.

species.name: Little galaxias
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, wetlands, shallow lakes, billabongs, small creeks and artificial earthen
drains at low elevation (mean 100 m above sea level, typically 22-176 m above sea level).  Inhabits mostly shallow areas (mean maximum depth 1.1 m, typically 0.5-2.0 m), with still to low water velocities (or often backwaters in faster flowing conditions) and partial shading (mean 27 %, typically 5-50 % surface cover).  Occasionally found in inland with slightly saline waters.  Water quality measurements at the time of collection indicate this species can thrive in a broad range of conditions:  water temperatures 5.2-26.9 °C; dissolved oxygen levels of 20-263 % saturation; pH of 5.3-9.3; water electrical conductivity of 94-13,620 μS/cm and turbidity of 1-96 NTU .  Usually  collected together with other native fish species, particularly <i>Nannoperca australis (65 % frequency), <i>Galaxias maculatus (12 % frequency), and burrowing crayfish (e.g. <i>Engaeus spp., <i>Geocharax spp.) (18 % frequency).  Often found with introduced fish species <i>Gambusia holbrooki (Ref. 104902).

species.name: Little gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Little hooded triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit surge zones of exposed reefs (Ref. 1602), on rock surfaces and under ledges (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Little pineapple fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: Little Pygmy Perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is rare and restricted in its range. Inhabits tannin stained, acidic and shallow Melaleuca rhaphiophylla streams (Ref. 93277).

species.name: Little rainbow wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on rocky reefs in shallow water (Ref. 26203).

species.name: Little rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat is shallow (<50 cm) comprising small Pandanus lined spring fed creeks over sandy soils with strong lateral connectivity to densely vegetated peat swamp and side-channel areas. Swamp and channel habitats can be seasonal or retract to refuge holes. Water transparency ranges from clear (streams) to heavily stained, indicative of water quality parameters in the dry season including pH 6.0–6.5 (noted also as 5.0: Armstrong 1995), temperature 23–24°C, water conductivity 15–30 ìScm-1 and general hardness and carbonate hardness <10 ppm. Occurs with regionally ubiquitous Melanotaenia nigrans and Mogurnda mogurnda and other swamp dwelling fish including Pseudomugil gertrudae, Oxyeleotris nullipora, Porochilus obbesi, Denariusa bandata, and Ophisternon gutturale. Little else is known on the biology of this species other than records of spawning and behaviour in captivity, where it is observed as extremely shy, which is viewed as an adaption to shallow habitat (Ref. 121823).

species.name: Little rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the subtidal zone but may be found in rock pools at low tide (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Little scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs deep along drop-offs in caves and on rock walls, but in some locations with strong currents in shallow water amongst sponges (Ref. 48635). Also found in sand and mud bottoms in 42-110 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Little tailband cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reefs or rocky substrate with caves and ledges at depths of less than 12 m (Ref. 10632); to 40 m (Ref, 126002).

species.name: Little weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in estuaries and sheltered inshore waters at depths usually less than 15 m; also found in grass beds and common around shallow rocky reefs.

species.name: Little weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs, tide pools, and deep estuarine habitats.

species.name: Little wolf
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 7300, 75154) and planktonic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Little-eye round herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually an inshore schooling species, feeding on zooplankton.

species.name: Little-eyed skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Littlefin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to be estuarine, but perhaps ascends rivers or migrates into coastal waters.  The minute teeth and rather numerous gillrakers suggest a diet of small planktonic animals.  The species is probably uncommon as there seems to be only four preserved specimens.

species.name: Littletooth sandeater
species.description: Encountered only in shallow sandy and intermediate habitats when breeding, and disappeared in the same area after the season.  Probably migrates to deeper levels when not breeding.  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Littoral Crozet spiny plounderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by hand from the littoral zone, under stones (Ref. 83990).

species.name: Littoral cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species found on shallow reefs (Ref. 34024).  Benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Livebearing fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Liver-colored moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lizard cabillus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms among coral reefs.

species.name: Lizard catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep-reef habitat on the continental slope, generally in depths greater than 250 meters (122-435 m), with deepwater gorgonians, hard corals, tube sponges, crinoids, ophiuroids, and a great number of sympatric scyliorhinid shark Scyliorhinus haeckelii (Ref. 56497). Oviparous (Ref. 50449); with one egg per oviduct laid at a time. Egg capsule grayish olive (fresh) to brownish (fixed), with filamentous superficial texture (Ref. 56497).

species.name: Lizard triplefin
species.description: Adults inhabit rocky shores and steep slopes.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 11482).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Needs better reference.

species.name: Lizardfish goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on a calcareous sand and dead Halimeda spp. algal rubble area, with dispersed shallow calcareous rock ledges (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Li’s lanternshark
species.description: Smallest mature male examined is 32.5 cm TL. The largest female examined with developing ovaries and uterus (representing a maturing stage), suggesting that mature females apparently attain sizes larger than 40.0 cm TL. Some specimens have whole lanternfishes (family Myctophidae) inside their stomachs, as observed under X-radiographs (Ref. 130841).

species.name: Llanolebias stellifer
species.description: Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Llori's grotto goby
species.description: Individuals were collected from sampling stations located on red algae beds, which is one of the most widespread types of habitats of the shallow continental shelf of the Balearic Islands at depths between 50 and 80 meters. The sampling stations have very similar epibenthic communities in which predominant algae species on the basal stratum belong to the families Corallinaceae (with Lithothamnion corallioides, Lithothamnion valens, Phymatolithon calcareum and Spongites fruticolus among the most abundant) and to Peyssonneliacea (with Peyssonnelia rubra and Peyssonnelia inamoena among the most abundant), and on the erect stratum to Phyllophoraceae (with Phyllophora crispa). With Peyssonnelia spp. having a high biomass, the sampling stations can be classified as Peyssonnelia beds, a frequently occurring habitat in the south west of Mallorca, and the south of Menorca. These beds are frequently associated with open bays characterized by fine sediments, even mud, where calm periods alternate with periods of eddy forming currents. Speleogobius llorios was found in a sheltered area, without significant currents (Ref. 125634).

species.name: Lloyd's slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Loach goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively steep gradient coastal streams in hilly or mountainous terrain. Feeds on algae and diatoms; effectively clings on rocks and boulders with its broadened pelvic and pectoral fins and flattened head and snout (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Loach minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, often vegetated, riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Lobed dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Lobed river mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very little available data.  Possibly ascending some way up rivers.  Probably taken incidentally or as part of subsistence fisheries in rivers.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lobed stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Lobefin snailfish
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées. Ranges from tide pools to shallow water near shore (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Lobejaw ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, presumably able to tolerate some lowering of salinity. Pelagic (Ref. 68964). More data needed.

species.name: Lobel's lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms (Ref. 7438).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Lobetoothed piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare (Ref. 12225).  Possesses powerful dentition that can cause serious bites.

species.name: Lobisomem
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, mesopelagic species (Ref. 4479, 75154).  Occurs deeper than 1,000 m during the day and nyctoepipelagic at the surface and down to 175 m (Ref. 4479).  Probably spawns in autumn-winter in the western North Atlantic (Ref. 4775).

species.name: Lobocheilos bo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are common in shallow, fast flowing areas with gravel substrate  (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Lobocheilos cornutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos cryptopogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from midwater to bottom depths in canals, ditches and small streams of floodplains, and more commonly in larger rivers as the temporary water bodies dry up.  Migrates into seasonally inundated land during rainy season, where it feeds on algae, periphyton and phytoplankton.  Most likely used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lobocheilos davisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at bottom depths in large and medium-sized streams.  Probably feeds on periphyton and phytoplankton like other species of this genus.  Probably used to make pharos (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lobocheilos delacouri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small to medium-sized high-gradient streams.  Feeds on periphyton and phytoplankton (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lobocheilos erinaceus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos falcifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos fowleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large and medium-sized rivers.  Feeds on periphyton and phytoplankton (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lobocheilos ixocheilos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos kajanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos lehat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos melanotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large and medium-sized rivers.  Feeds on periphyton and phytoplankton which it scrapes from rocks.  In the Mekong of northern Cambodia schools of this species were observed to make scrape marks on rocks about 1 cm wide and 7 or 8 cm long.  These marks begin at about a depth of 20 cm and become more and more dense on deeper surfaces.  Probably spawns at the onset of the rainy season.  Used to make nook mama.  Occasionally seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Lobocheilos nigrovittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos ovalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos quadrilineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large and medium-sized rivers as well as streams. Diet is probably similar to other species of Lobocheilos (Ref. 12693). Found browsing on algae growing on rocks in clear, shallow water (Ref. 1632).

species.name: Lobocheilos rhabdoura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at bottom depths in large and medium-sized streams (Ref. 12693).  Usually inhabits streams with relatively swift current, rapids (Ref. 43281).  Enters flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on periphyton and phytoplankton.  Probably spawns at the onset of the rainy season.  Used to make nook mama.

species.name: Lobocheilos schwanenfeldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos tenura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches up to at least 14 cm SL (Ref. 75626).

species.name: Lobocheilos terminalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos thavili
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos trangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lobocheilos unicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches up to about 30 cm SL (Ref. 75626).

species.name: Lobochilotes labiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the largest cichlids in the lake.  Usually observed near rocks, but suspected to roam the sunken sand plains in search of bivalve mollusks, crabs, and other invertebrates (Ref. 6770), often in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Lobulogobius bentuviai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs in freshwaters and sometimes brackish waters in slow to fast current waters to the base of the first falls. Usually occurs in clear waters with sand, gravel or rock bottom. Feeds on algae, detritus, worms, gastropods and crustaceans. Close biology to A. guamensis. Amphidromous species. Adults migrate to the mouth of the rivers for reproduction. Females spawn on the rocks' surface where the males fecund the eggs. Males protect the eggs until they hatch (incubation lasts 24 to 70hrs). Larvae, translucid, are then carried into estuaries or sea. They come back after they spent 150 to 165 days in seawaters (Ref. 57749). Also Ref. 4343.

species.name: Loche (Sicydium plumieri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loche (Sicydium punctatum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found abundant in rivers of coastal volcanic topography (Ref. 12113).  Adults spawn in rivers with coarse substrate, building nests under stones (Ref. 33036).

species.name: Loche asiatique
species.description: Poisson d'eau douce. Occurs in rivers, lakes and ponds. Also in swamps and ricefields (Ref. 27732, 119549). Prefers muddy bottoms, where they hide in the muck and leaf litter with only their heads sticking out; prefers muddy bottoms of streams and ponds; in Hawaii, can also be found under mats of honohono (Commelina diffusa and California grass (Brachiara nuatica); feeds on worms, small crustaceans, insects, insect larvae, and other small aquatic organisms (Ref. 44091).

species.name: Loche bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found around isolated coral heads in lagoons or bays, but also caught on outer reef area.  According to Myers (1989, Ref. 4538) it usually swims out in the open, several meters above the bottom.  It is readily caught by anglers at night.  Feeds mainly on sand-dwelling fishes and crustaceans such as snake eels and box crabs.  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Loche crasseuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons marins de la famille des serranidae. Often found in coral-rich areas of lagoon and outer reefs; in caves and large crevices to swim through (Ref. 48635).  Most abundant around islands, particularly atolls.  Usually in small schools but may be solitary (Ref 90102).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (portunid crabs) and fishes, sometimes on cephalopods and gastropods.  In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).  This species is important in artisanal fisheries, but occasionally implicated in cases of ciguatera (frequently ciguatoxic in the Marshall Is., Ref. 37816). It is now uncommon at localities with heavy spearfishing, but popular in the aquaculture industry of Singapore, where it is known as 'marble grouper'. It is caught with hook-and-line, spear, and traps (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Loche de rivière
