species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in slow-flowing and still waters with fine sandy substrate (Ref. 9696).  They occur in the Baltic Sea at salinities of up to 5 ppt (Ref. 59043).  Filter sand for food particles (Ref. 36876).  Nocturnal, stays hidden under rocks or buried in the sand or mud during the day (Ref. 30578).  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Spawn in spring; scatters eggs into mats of plant material (Ref. 36876).  Eggs are found attached to gravel and weed in shallow, flowing water (Ref. 41678).  Larvae hide under vegetation and in debris until beginning of exogenous feeding (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Loche franche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in flowing stretches of streams and medium-sized rivers with gravel to stone bottom, but also in a variety of other habitats, including sandy canals and lake shores.  Larvae are benthic.  Larvae and small juveniles prefer sand bottom and slow current, shifting to gravel bottom and fast current when growing.  Adults prey on relatively large benthic invertebrates such as gammarids, chironomids, insect larvae.  They breed on gravel, sand or among aquatic vegetation.  Tolerate moderate organic pollution and stream canalization and very sensitive to pollution by heavy metals (Ref. 59043).  Sensitive to pollution and low oxygen levels, therefore, its presence in a river can be taken as an indication of good water quality (Ref. 6111).

species.name: Loche géante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The largest bony fish found in coral reefs (Ref. 9710). Individuals more than a meter long have been caught from shore and in harbors. Common in shallow waters. Found in caves or wrecks; also in estuaries. Juveniles secretive in reefs and rarely seen (Ref. 48635). Benthopelagic and benthic (Ref. 58302). Feed on spiny lobsters, fishes, including small sharks and batoids, and juvenile sea turtles and crustaceans. In South African estuaries, the main prey item is the mud crab, Scylla serrata. Unconfirmed reports of fatal attacks on humans. Nearly wiped out in heavily fished areas (Ref. 9710). Large individuals may be ciguatoxic (Ref. 37816). In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). It is not common enough to be of commercial importance; rare in some places due to spearfishing; also caught with hook-and-line and spear (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Loche pakistanaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hill streams at a minimum altitude of 190 m.  Prefers rocky and gravelly pools of streams (Ref. 12045).

species.name: Loche pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loche ponctuée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in outer reef flats and shallow lagoon (Ref. 37816).  Reported to be taken in a trawl, thus presumably caught somewhat deeper than 7 m.  Also reported to occur in reefs at a depth of about 30 m (Ref. 5213).  Because of its small size and apparent rarity, it is of little or no commercial importance. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Loche rayon de miel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary fish, in coastal and offshore reefs usually in less than 20 m depth (Ref. 90102); also very common in shallow lagoon and semi-protected seaward reefs. Juveniles are common in thickets of staghorn Acropora corals. Feed on crustaceans and fishes. Increase of piscivory with age is observed in this species. Neither opercular spine nor anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406). Current information in the table (dangerous fish) do not match; needs verification. Cultured under experimental conditions in the Philippines (Ref. 4757). In the Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). It is important to artisanal fisheries because of its abundance in shallow water and caught with handlines, fish traps, and spear (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Loche rouge du large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in depths of 70 to 220 m on outer reef slopes; the young in depths of 20 to 40 m (Ref. 89707).  Also caught with vertical longlines.

species.name: Loche sanguine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rich coastal to outer reefs, usually along deep walls with caves, rich with invertebrate growth such as large sponges or soft corals (Ref. 48635). They occur singly or in small groups (Ref. 90102). A secretive species which are active nocturnally in shallow water and diurnally in deeper water (Ref. 5222). They are often seen with the cleaner shrimp Periclimenes elegans (Ref. 37816). Adults feed mainly on fishes (Ref. 5222) and reach sexual maturity at 25 cm SL (Ref. 89707). Probably of commercial interest to certain local fisheries. Are caught with hook-and-line, traps, and spear (Ref. 39231). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Loche saumonée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A generally common species (Ref. 9710).  Adults are benthic and benthopelagic in a variety of coral habitats (Ref. 58534, 58302) from tide pools to depths of at least 40 m; preferring the 1 to 10 m reef zone. Juveniles prefer shallow, protected coral thickets (Ref. 37816).  Mature adults are found in social units comprising up to 12 adults, including 1 dominant male and each group occupies a specific area (up to 2,000 sq. m.) that is defended by the territorial male and subdivided into secondary territories, each inhabited by a single female (Ref. 39231).  At times, they may also be solitary (Ref. 90102). Adults feed mainly on fishes (75-95%) and to a lesser extent on crustaceans. In the Red Sea, they feed early in the morning and late afternoon (Ref. 6775) but in Madagascar, they appear to feed more at night (Ref. 6774). They are implicated in ciguatera at some of the islands in the Pacific region. They can be seen in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). They are important to artisanal fisheries throughout the Indo-West Pacific region and often caught with hook-and-line, spear, and in traps (Ref. 39231).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Loche saumonée (Plectropomus leopardus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral-rich areas of lagoon reefs and mid-shelf reefs (Ref. 6390, 48635). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Inactive at night, hiding under ledges (Ref. 9710). Juveniles have a demersal existence in shallow water in reef habitats, especially around coral rubble (Ref. 27259). Adults feed mainly on fish (Ref. 6390), juveniles feed on small fish and invertebrates such as crustaceans and squid (Ref. 27261). A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367). Form several spawning aggregations on a reef occurring around the new moon (Ref. 27259). Eggs float just below the surface (Ref. 6390). Larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6390). P. leopardus is used in cage culture; P. maculatus in Ref. 3081 was probably a mixture of P. maculatus and P. leopardus; the Plectropomus sp. used for the experiments reported in Capra et al., 1988 (Ref. 4719) consisted predominantly of P. leopardus, with some P. maculatus (M.F. Capra, pers. comm.). On the Great Barrier Reef, its maximum lifespan is 14 years (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Loche à bandes dorées
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found in deep waters, a specimen was caught at 250 m from Tahiti, French Polynesia. Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 089707).

species.name: Loche à bords blancs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An active swimmer usually found on outer reef slopes and channels adjacent to deep water.  Hovers above the bottom and probably feeds primarily on fishes (Ref. 9710).  It is uncommon and usually solitary, however Myers (1989, Ref. 4538) reported of occasional sightings of groups of 3 or 4 fish. Solitary, hovering in midwater (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Loche à hexagone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in exposed outer-reef areas in relatively shallow water.  Well-camouflaged grouper, solitary (Ref 37816).  Feeds mainly on fishes and crustaceans (stomatopods and brachyuran crabs) (Ref. 5222). This fish is too small to be of commercial importance except as a food fish in artisanal fisheries. It is caught with hook-and-line, traps, spear, and gill nets (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Loche à peau de serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the outer slope of coral reefs. Fourmanoir (1971, Ref. 6828) found ophichthid eels, Leiuranus phoenixensis, in the stomachs of his type specimens. May be of some importance to artisanal fisheries and it is rarely caught because of its preference for deep water.

species.name: Loche à taches blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky or coral-rich areas of deep lagoons, channels and outer reef slopes; usually in or near caves (Ref. 089707).  Solitary (Ref 90102). Juveniles are found in tide pools.  Feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 6113).  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). Caught with hook-and-line, spear, and in traps and probably of some importance to fisheries in areas where it is common (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Loche à taches claires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inner coastal and lagoon reefs, also in brackish waters where it occurs in ledges and caves (Ref. 5213). Adults usually found deeper than 20 m (Ref. 48635). Solitary (Ref 90102).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 89707).  A cryptic species which is not very common, but of some interest to fisheries in Japan (and probably elsewhere). Caught with hook-and-line, spear, and traps (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Lochon tétard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwater, estuaries, inshore and mangrove (Ref. 86252).  Adults occur on soft mud bottoms of rainforest creeks to elevations of at least 150 m.  (Ref. 2847, 44894).  They favor undercut banks for retreat.  Probably has a pelagic marine larval stage (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Locusthead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loeme lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers, brooks and swamps in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 59344).  Difficult to maintain in aquaria (Ref. 31267).

species.name: Lofty triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in and about coral reefs and rocky shores in clear water (Ref. 7251).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lohit snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loki whip-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to live only on sea whips and gorgonian corals (Ref. 9002). Occurs usually with Junceela fragilis in Indonesia, that found inshore on somewhat silty reefs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Loktak loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lollipop darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky and sandy pools of headwaters and creeks (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Lombarte's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lombok goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lombok sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected using rotenone, one site is a drop-off  point with numerous small caves and some sand and rubble (Ref. 75879)..

species.name: Lombok Swallowtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lombok viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary in reef crevices and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Lompénie de Fabricius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy to rocky bottoms, often in seagrass or algae; rarely, if ever, found in intertidal area (Ref. 51666).  Feeds on crustaceans, worms, clams, and fish eggs (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lompénie naine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms, generally preferring water below 0°C and salinities above 30 ppt. (Ref. 10571).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 10571).

species.name: Lompénie tachetée
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Adults, juveniles, and late postlarvae are found on sandy and mud to pebble bottoms, usually in less than 170 meters (Ref. 2850, 51666, 120227), while early postlarvae are pelagic (Ref. 120227). Food consists of polychaetes and crustaceans (Ref. 10571). They are an important prey for pelagic (as larvae) and benthic (as adults) predators (Ref. 120226). Sexual dimorphism is more pronounced after maturation with males displaying faster somatic growth (Ref. 120226). This marked dimorphism may well be linked with behavioral dissimilarities between males and
females, and is most likely associated with different roles during the breeding season with only adult males have large canines at the tip of upper jaw. It is assumed that males are territorial and defend their spawning sites, whereasfemales guard eggs within her partner’s territory (Ref. 128434).

species.name: Lonchogenys ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lonchopisthus higmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms.  Feed on small decapods, shrimps and fishes.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Lonchopisthus lemur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found below 200 m (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Lonely clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lonely coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Long barbeled grunter
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The species is apparently restricted to river mouths and coastal rocky to sandy bottoms of less than 50 m depth. The smallest specimen (MUFS 22226, 46 mm SL) was collected in a river mouth, while larger specimens were captured by set net or small trawl between 5-50 m depth over rocky or sandy bottoms.  Between 1960-1980, the species were observed by Miyazaki SCUBA divers to be solitary and common in small caves, holes, and under overhanging rocks along the Nichinan coast, Miyazaki, southeastern Kyushu Island, from late
summer to winter. However, in recent years (post 1990) the species has been only rarely observed (Ref. 56360).

species.name: Long fin Kerala barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This edible species can also be utilized as an ornamental species fish.  It was collected from a polluted water channel flowing through the heart of the Kayamkulam city, and is considered to survive to some extent in contaminated water bodies (Ref. 103709).

species.name: Long green wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in kelp and other weedy areas at 2-25 m (Ref. 123183).

species.name: Long lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-sand bottoms (Ref. 9824, 48637) and algae-reef substrates in coastal bays to deep offshore (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Long nosed arched cory
species.description: Occurs sympatrically with C. arcuatus.

species.name: Long nostril jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long pectoral fin flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long pectoral-fin minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers and lakes at medium to shallow depths.  Juveniles feed on insects while adults on fish (Ref. 12693).  Move towards the flooded forest when the water is high and returns to the river as soon as the water level starts to subside (Ref. 12693).  Good flesh but fairly soft and with numerous bones.  In Laos, it is usually grilled, simmered with padek and made into Ponne pa.  Usually marketed fresh and probably exported to Thailand (Ref. 12693).  Widely distributed but greatly reduced in numbers probably throughout its range.  Extremely sensitive to gillnetting and perhaps also to pollution (Ref. 12369).

species.name: Long snout flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottoms.  Lives mainly at depths of about 200 m (Ref. 9558).

species.name: Long snouted barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occur in rivers, streams, ponds and lakes.  Usually found in flowing water, particularly with a pebble substrate (Ref. 6028).  Feeds on detritus, algae and higher plants (Ref. 6028).  Useful in guinea worm control.

species.name: Long tom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits still or flowing rivers, from tidal reaches to far inland.  Also found in some impoundments (Lake Argyle,WA).  Often shelters among overhanging vegetation or submerged roots.  Adults are infrequently found in coastal marine waters (Ref. 44894).  Occurs in larger streams.  Surface-dwelling predator of small fishes, insects (Ref. 205, 44894) and crustaceans (Ref. 44894).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Spawning is believed to occur sometimes between September and December.  The presence of juveniles well inland and in impoundments suggests that it may spawn in freshwater (Ref. 44894).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Long tongue sole
species.description: Adults live mainly in shallow muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelf, sometimes entering estuaries and tidal rivers (Ref. 1479, 48637).  Usually deeply buried in the substrate during the day, but out and hunting at night (Ref. 48637).  They feed mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed mostly fresh and frozen; also dried-salted (Ref. 9895).

species.name: Long whiskered Kerala catfish
species.description: The river stretch of the type locality is highly sinuous, generally rocky with deep pools at certain locations and has bed materials generally of coarser grade and of very low sand content.  The pools have sporadic patches or fillings of sand deposits (Ref. 96965).

species.name: Long whiskers catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily a brackish water fish that enters and lives in fresh water.  In freshwater, adults occur mainly in larger water bodies (rivers and streams) with mud or clay substrates, and rarely found in smaller streams.  Form schools of 10 to 25 individuals.  Diurnal.  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Long-barbel sheatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river and streams.  Feeds mostly on small fishes, along with prawns and insect larvae.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693); processed as smoked or salted fish (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Long-fin glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mainstreams, tributaries and marshlands (Ref. 58784).  A carnivorous species which feeds on crustaceans and insects (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Long-fin goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-fingered icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on fishes and krill.  Larval pelagic phase is long in late winter (Ref. 28943).

species.name: Long-finned cambeva
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams in the Atlantic forest; backwaters with no flow to 0.44 meter per second water flow.  Dwells mostly in pools beneath small waterfalls in steep hill streams flowing over rocky and sandy substrates.  Density varies from 3 to 25 individuals per square meter.  At densities of 18 to 25 individuals per square meter, fish aggregates in loose groups of up to 30 individuals; largest ones tend to be solitary and territorial.  Nektonic, active both during daytime and at night; juveniles and small adults of up to 9 cm TL are more active at daytime, whereas larger ones are active mostly at night.  Uses visual, tactile, and chemo-sensory orientation to feed on bottom-dwelling aquatic and terrestrial arthropods in the water column or on the surface.  Diet includes immature aquatic insects, crustaceans, adult terrestrial winged insects whole or fragmented, as well as carrion.  Forages mostly by scanning the bottom, the barbels touching the substrate, but visual oriented drift feeding is also employed by individuals up to 5 cm TL.  While foraging may bury into sand or plant debris and sifts through opercular openings and mouth.  Reproduces at the onset of rainy season (austral summer).  Mature oocytes about 0.2 cm diameter; pterigyolarvae range 1-1.5 cm TL.  Spotted color pattern differs consistently between stream populations, an indication of genetic differentiation (Ref. 50917).

species.name: Long-finned charr
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep waters close to the bottom (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Long-finned cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-finned goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas of fine sand and shallow lagoon reefs at depths less than 3 m, rarely at depths greater than 6 m.  Adults usually in pairs, constructing burrows under rubble.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884, 48637).  Feeds on small invertebrates (e.g. copepods, amphipods, ostracods, nematodes, and foraminiferans) by sifting mouthfuls of sand.

species.name: Long-finned gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Long-horned golden-lined fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit a completely dark cave environments (Ref. 128063).

species.name: Long-jawed river garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries, lowland rivers and tributaries.  A shoal-forming species which swims near the surface.  Feeds on insects (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Long-nosed gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Long-rayed dwarf monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Long-rayed sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reef slopes and deep outer reef lagoons in current channels.  Usually in large groups with several large males (Ref. 48636).  Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102).  Found hovering above sandy slopes.  Usually forms a harem of one male-phase fish and about a dozen female-phase fish (Ref. 37240).  Normally buried when no current is running (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Long-rayed weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which is common in soft bottom communities with seagrass.

species.name: Long-snout dace
species.description: Inhabits streams and rivers, sectors with current and clear water, in deep pools.  Feeds on vegetal matter.  Spawns in stretches with swift current and pebble bottom.  Reaches up to about 40 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Long-snout dwarfgoby
species.description: Observed on coastal reefs exposed to significant terrigenous influences (freshwater influx and sedimentation) and from moderate to strong currents. Individuals on coralline algae and dead coral substrates (Ref. 126577).

species.name: Long-snout gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Most specimens taken in trawls have sand grains inside the mouth indicating occurrence on open, predominantly sandy substrata (Ref. 54394).

species.name: Long-snout tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on continental shelf, collected on muddy substrata or a mixture of mud and sand. Caught by bottom trawls (Ref. 109580).

species.name: Long-snouted African spurdog
species.description: Minimum size at maturity of this species is approximately 73.0 cm for females and 65.0 cm for males.  Females have between 4-9 pups per litter (size at birth is around 21.0-30.0 cm, with the smallest free-swimming neonates measuring 23.0-23.5 cm TL.  Reported to feed mainly on bony fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 116246).

species.name: Long-snouted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal algal beds, as well as wharves and pilings.  Usually at depths less than 7.5 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males probably brooding at about 24-25 cm TL.

species.name: Long-snouted tongue sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-spine anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-spine pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes or vertical walls with many small caves (Ref. 13694).

species.name: Long-spined glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brackish-water, mangrove, estuarine and freshwater-stream habitats, usually within 20 km of the sea (Ref. 2847).  They occur at temperatures ranging from 28 to 32°C.  Found in schools and migrate to freshwater.  Mainly diurnal.  A predominantly marine or estuarine spawner.  Caught by hand and scoop nets (Ref. 7242).

species.name: Long-tail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups in sandy estuaries (Ref. 48636) and also in sand bottoms to 37 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Females much smaller in size (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth of 3 m reported from Ref. 48636.

species.name: Long-tail tripodfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy flats of coastal waters.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Long-tailed butterfly ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught often in demersal trawls, and occasionally by trammel net. Utilized  for its meat, but of limited value due to its typically small size (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Long-tailed catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.

species.name: Long-tailed groppo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-tailed river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small catfishes, insects, decapod crustaceans, and parasitic cestodes and nematodes (Ref. 34195).

species.name: Long-tailed snailfsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Long-tailed wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along steep seaward reefs (Ref. 37816).  Specimens collected at 42 and 60 m (Ref. 1692).

species.name: Long-threaded dragon fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Long-toothed false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reef slopes.

species.name: Long-whiskered catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, ponds, lakes, channels and reservoirs (Ref. 4833).  Predatory, adults feed on small fishes and worms (Ref. 44149).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same genus (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longanalus macrochirous
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longarm brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Inhabits coral reefs and is a live-bearing species (Ref. 5521).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 5521.

species.name: Longarm flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longarm grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on euphausiids, prawns, and small fishes (e.g. myctophids).

species.name: Longarmed snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longbarb dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 4468) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Longbarb scaly dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep oceanic waters to more than 1,000 m depth (Ref. 4783).  Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Longbarb whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longbeard grenadier
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longeye conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longface eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves or coral rubble along steep drop-offs or channel walls. Feeds on larvae of crustaceans and fish eggs (Ref. 89972). Secretive (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Longfin Baikal sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin barracudina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longfin beach salmon
species.description: This species is apparently pelagic, entering or living in the lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 129587).

species.name: Longfin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from rocky and rubble shores with algal mats to reefs and seagrass beds.

species.name: Longfin boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Longfin burrower
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the intertidal to at least 16 m.

species.name: Longfin codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental slope (Ref. 1371). Many specimens taken from a whale stomach (Ref. 1371). Gut content of a 3.86 cm SL specimen contained a large number of grasping spines of arrow worms (Chaetognatha spp.), while a 4.01 cm SL specimen contained 6 individuals of the copepod Metridia pacifica (Ref. 87085).

species.name: Longfin Cucumberfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy and rocky runs, flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Often occurs near cover (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Longfin damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs of sheltered lagoons and inshore areas.  Territorial and pugnacious (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Longfin darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Longfin dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species that inhabits steep outer reef slopes, in areas with dense coral growth (Ref. 9710). Solitary, sometimes seen entering sponges (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longfin dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic migrating into epipelagic at night (Ref. 35904).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35904).

species.name: Longfin fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fringing reefs, over coral or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on zooplankton in the water column (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Longfin fairygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms in 20-35 m (Ref. 90102). Hovers above the substrate (Ref. 44093).

species.name: Longfin flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longfin grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas (Ref. 2850); entirely subtidal (Ref. 48978).

species.name: Longfin handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin Irish lord
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin killie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Longfin lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 4066) at 80-300 m at night, 675-1000 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442). Depth range in Psubarctic Pacific gyres around 100-500 m (Ref. 51600).

species.name: Longfin lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 4066, 58302), found between 400-930 m during the day and between 18-1,050 m at night (with maximum abundance at 50-100 m and 500-700 m at night) (Ref. 4479).  Larvae and juveniles non-migratory at least near the Canary Islands (Ref. 4479).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Longfin largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common, occurs in permanent floodplain lagoons and backwaters.  Active at night, preying on small fish and insects such as dragonfly nymphs (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Longfin mullet
species.description: Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longfin pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually live 305 m or more below the surface but move upward in the water at night, sometimes to relatively shallow depths.  Are believed to be rapid swimmers, skillful at avoiding nets, which would account for the scarcity of large adults in research collections.  Juveniles feed heavily on crustaceans, while adults feed mainly on fish (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Longfin perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic (Ref. 2334), shallow-water species collected with the use of ichthyocides (Ref. 26833).  Secretive amongst small boulders or bommies on coastal sand slopes with rich invertebrate and algae growth (Ref. 48635). Solitary in crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longfin pike
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in bays over rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Longfin sawtail cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 439 m (Ref. 13292).

species.name: Longfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in intertidal areas and to 38 m depth, in rocky areas and kelp (Ref. 2850).  Frequently hangs vertically on rock faces (Ref. 2850).  Active and highly territorial during the breeding season (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Longfin shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in the upper and lower reaches of big rivers and also in estuarine zones of mixohaline waters (Ref. 2880). The only Brycinus species to penetrate small rivers and streams (Ref. 2880), but such specimens are always smaller than those in large rivers (Ref. 80290). Aquarium keeping: in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51150).

species.name: Longfin threadtail Anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by bottom trawls and appears to be found at the shallower end of these depths (62-228 m), in the southern part of its range (Ref. 127477).

species.name: Longfin velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by scallop trawls over predominantly sandy bottom, with some scattered shell and rubble. Brown algae Padina sp. and smaller amounts of the rubble and seagrasses Halophila ovalis and H. spinulosa, were recorded in the catch (Ref. 57897).

species.name: Longfin work eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfin worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfingered scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 4313).  Very secretive in coastal coral reefs and rarely seen by divers, even at night (Ref. 48635). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longfinned coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfinned flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longfinned hagfish
species.description: Occurs on soft bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Longfinned mullet
species.description: Found in coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 40488).  Form shoals over mudflats (Ref. 40488).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longfinned sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a patch of sand in a reef at a depth of 9 m (Ref. 75879)..

species.name: Longfinned triplefin
species.description: Adults are commonly found in sheltered areas shallower than 5 m.  Typical in shallow habitats in coastal mainland areas and seldom on offshore islands.  Mainly found under rocks.  They feed on a range of benthic invertebrates including ophiuroids, archaeogastropods, trichoptera and errant polychaetes  (Ref. 84084).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  They are caught by slurp guns and handnets (Ref. 84086).

species.name: Longhead darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky flowing pools, usually above and below rubble riffles of clear, small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in creeks (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on small crayfishes and mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Longhead flathead
species.description: Found in inshore areas (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longhead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longhead grunt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species apparently inhabiting deeper waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 47695).

species.name: Longheaded eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore waters (Ref. 9862).  Probably feeds on hard-shelled and bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 114953). Often found in  brackish waters (Ref. 4832).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Caught occasionally by bottom trawl and inshore demersal gillnet fisheries off Jakarta. Utilized for its meat, but of limited value due to its rarity and small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Longhorn armored gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longhorn blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow rocky areas (Ref. 5521).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Longhorned mobula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and oceanic waters (Ref. 30573); solitary of aggregations, sometimes with 50 or more individuals (Ref. 90102).  Not known to penetrate the epipelagic zone (Ref. 9911).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 30573).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Longiculter siahi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits middle and upper water levels of large and medium-sized rivers (Ref. 12693).  Little is known about this species, but it is apparently uncommon or at least localized in distribution.  Probably a filter feeder (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Longjaw bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic and bathypelagic at 340-1200 m depth (Ref. 36665).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36655).  Significant morphological variation between Indo-Pacific and other populations.

species.name: Longjaw blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Longjaw goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud and rock bottoms near shore in 0-4 m (Ref. 90102). Found in coastal waters, estuaries (Ref. 4833), tidal rivers, canals and creeks (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans and insects.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Longjaw grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably estuarine, like other Coilia species, but more data needed. Found in estuaries and tidal reaches of river (Ref. 12693). Marketed fresh, dried, dried-salted, or made into fish sauce or fish balls (Ref. 9822).

species.name: Longjaw minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species occurs in small schools, often in clear, shallow (up to 50 cm) streams in slow to moderate runs; prefers sandy to sand mixed with gravel substrates (Ref. 57709).

species.name: Longjaw mudsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tidal flats, bays and coastal sloughs.  Prefers mud bottom in shallow water.  Non-emerging air-breather (Ref. 31184).  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  Males guard the eggs which are found attached to the walls of brood chamber (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Longjaw shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered coastal bays, lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 48637). Also found in sand-rubble bottoms in 1-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longjaw silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longjawed galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longlip jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Longlure flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near reefs, in gullies, or cave entrances on sand or coral- or rock-rubble bottoms at 3-57 m depth (Ref. 57759).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Longlure frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow reefs (Ref. 9710).  Commonly found in areas with sponges; background hue of the fish conforms to that of the dominant sponge in the areas and the ocelli look like openings in the sponge.  Feed mainly on fishes, but also eat crustaceans (Ref. 13442).  A voracious predator, with many color phases used for camouflage.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).  Most common frogfish in the West Indies (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Longnaze rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the lower slope, continental rise and upper abyss, primarily between 4° and 2°C isotherms.  Feeds on polychaetes, crustaceans, echinoderms and echiurids.  Hovers above or rests on bottom.  Long slender pectorals are commonly held erect pointing upward and forward, these may serve a sensory function (Ref. 6727).

species.name: Longnose armoured searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prejuveniles and juveniles less than 6.1 cm SL usually found at 350 to 400 m depth; adults usually at 400 to 650 m (Ref. 51211). Taken from the bottom with temperatures ranging from 10 to 11°C (Ref. 51211).

species.name: Longnose batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found typically on sandy bottoms (Ref. 27549).

species.name: Longnose conger
species.description: Collected using beam trawl (Ref. 7446).

species.name: Longnose cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed on open sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 81834).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longnose darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel runs and riffles of small to medium clear rivers.

species.name: Longnose deep-sea skate
species.description: Adults inhabit the continental slope (Ref. 26346).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 8.8 cm long and 4.7 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Longnose greeneye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on fishes and sometimes sepia (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Longnose grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lentic and lotic freshwater (Ref. 7300). Swim close to the bottom of moderate to swift flowing streams, over rock or sand. Retreat quickly to crevices when threatened (Ref. 44894). Herbivorous species (Ref. 7300). Feed on filamentous algae, scraped from hard surfaces using specially modified dentition. Form shoals, often mixed with S. rastellus (Ref. 44894). Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longnose gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare deepwater species (Ref. 9771).  Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longnose killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found around mangroves and on tidal flats where vegetation is sparse and short (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Longnose knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in deep water of the main channel of the Lower Orinoco.

species.name: Longnose little warty catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from clumps of vegetation in streams with flowing waters. Sympatric with P. verruisus. Nocturnal (Ref. 13847). Recorded from fast-flowing, well shaded swamp-forest streams with acidic waters, and dense growth of submerged vegetation. Feeds on minute invertebrates and uses its dexterous and strong pelvic fins to move about (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Longnose poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longnose sawtail cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longnose seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel or sand bottoms around shallow reefs (Ref. 559); muddy estuaries and near mangroves, tolerating brackish waters (Ref. 48635).  Occur singly or in pairs (Ref. 128523).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longnose shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy, sometimes muddy, shallow runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Longnose snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longnose sooty grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit larger streams, occurring in rocky pools.  Occur in small to large pools of slow-flowing streams and major river channels, usually over rocky substrates.  Larger specimens occur in deeper water (Ref. 44894).  Feed on crustaceans, insects and small fishes.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longnose stonebasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Kyoga abundant among or near water lilies (Ref. 49805) and in Lake Victoria it occurs in shallow, inshore waters over sandy and rocky shores (Ref. 4903, 97924), seasonally over muddy bottoms adjacent to papyrus swamps or deep water near rocky islands (Ref. 9606, 97924). Feeds on bottom and in marginal vegetation; insectivorous (chironomid larvae, Povilla, Odonata larvae), but arthropods, oligochaetes and fish eggs are also eaten (Ref. 12526). Uses sensitive pointed addition to chin for testing holes in mud, papyrus roots and between stones to locate underwater insects (Ref. 36900). Rotates body to almost vertical position, searches substrate and grabs prey into mouth; produces weak electric organ discharge for navigation and to warn off other organisms (Ref. 97924). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Breeds twice a year during the rainy seasons, and migrates up rivers to spawn (Ref. 10608).

species.name: Longnose surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 33204).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Its small and numerous pharyngeal teeth suggest a diet that consists mainly of filamentous algae (Ref. 33204).

species.name: Longnosed stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longray cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longray fangjaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species, showing marked stratification of size with depth, with the largest individuals deepest (Ref. 4869); also bathypelagic (Ref. 5951).  Exhibits diel color change, darkening slightly at night (Ref. 4769).  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Longray ghost flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom (Ref. 75154) of the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longrayed whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longsnout blacksmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Usually caught in small aggregations (Ref. 6345).  Exhibits daily vertical migrations (Ref. 6345).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 6345).

species.name: Longsnout boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf, most commonly in depths less than 40 m (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on brittle stars, polychaetes and brown algae (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Longsnout butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep coral-rich reefs and drop-offs (Ref. 47838).  Feed on small invertebrates.  Often seen nibbling on the tube feet of sea urchins or the tentacles of tubeworms (Ref. 9710).  Unlike some chaetodonts it does not pick parasites from the bodies of other fishes (Ref. 5521).  Solitary, sometimes in pairs (Ref. 47838).  Seek  refuge when approached (Ref. 47838).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longsnout distichodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longsnout flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy regions of bays and offshore areas.  Flesh of very high quality but individuals taken are not often sufficiently large to make preparation worthwhile (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Longsnout No-line Scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longsnout pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens from midwater and bottom trawls.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 14.6 cm SL.

species.name: Longsnout prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore (Ref. 2850); possibly the deepest-living lumpenine (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Longsnout seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon in most areas, but may be locally common in certain places. Usually attached to gorgonians or seagrasses but may occur in floating Sargassum or swimming freely in midwater (Ref. 9710). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35409). Length type refers to Height (= from top of coronet to the tip of straightened tail). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Longsnout spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Longsnout stinger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand, rubble and mud bottoms in 1-50 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longsnout weedy scorpionfish
species.description: Most probably found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 106976).

species.name: Longsnouted catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters over soft bottoms (Ref. 7300).  Feeds on detritus, prawns, soft-bodied organisms, and mud (Ref. 38478).

species.name: Longspine bellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 5213, 75154) and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longspine burrfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms to at least 30 m (Ref. 9680).  Presumably feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 9680).  Frequently trawled but not marketed (Ref. 9680).

species.name: Longspine cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Usually only found at night to depths of 25 m (Ref. 48635). Solitary and secretive (Ref 90102).

species.name: Longspine chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longspine combfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Longspine flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Longspine shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coarse sand at the base of a  reef slope at a depth of 26 m.  Associated with burrowing alpheid prawns (Ref. 26237).

species.name: Longspine silverbiddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow inshore coastal waters on sandy bottoms and in estuaries.  Maintain discrete, single species' schools (Ref. 13682).

species.name: Longspot shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from silty sand habitat (Ref. 75862).

species.name: Longtail catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longtail cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Longtail cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy substrate of coastal areas (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Longtail goby
species.description: Inhabits shallow sand or mud bottoms of bays and estuaries.  An intertidal species that actively shuttles back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).  For food ingestion it leaves the home pool during low tides, takes a mouth full of mud and returns to its pool where it washes out the mud through its gill membrane and swallows particles  which are sieved by the gill rakers (Ref. 92840). Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Longtail ilisha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longtail seamouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 4264) collected from muddy and sandy bottoms of estuaries and bays.  Known to 'walk' over the bottom using its tentacular pelvic fins.  Juveniles expatriate to tropical regions; adults mainly found in muddy estuaries where they pair.  Sometimes they are seen partly buried but also feed during the day.  Sometimes found floating on the surface (Ref. 48635). Sometimes occurs in seagrass areas (Ref 90102). Feeds on small benthic organisms (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Longtail shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling in coastal waters and ascending rivers to breed. Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 58784). Presumably its biology is similar to that of T. ilisha, but the fewer gillrakers suggest that it takes larger food organisms. A protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Longtail slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longtail spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly riverine species, but also occurs in lakes near river mouths and in vegetated fringes and in swamps (Ref. 80296). Also found in rapids where it hides among rocks (Ref. 85214). Essentially a sedentary fish, nocturnal and usually waiting for its prey to swim or drift within range whereupon fish will dart out of its shelter to seize it (Ref. 89002). Feeds on aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 80296), lithophilic insects (Ref. 12526), fish (Ref. 13624, 27292), shrimps (Ref. 246, 80296), oligochetes and occasionally vegetable matter (Ref. 80296, 89002). Breeds during flood season, in inundated areas (Ref. 80296). Eggs yellow and large, probably spawned among water weeds (Ref. 89002).

species.name: Longtail tentacle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Longtail tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and shallow coastal waters (Ref. 7251); mainly on silt and soft mud substrates (Ref. 26268).  Little is known of its ecology (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Longtail weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs inshore (Ref. 75154). Apparently restricted to moderately high-energy coastal locations with dominant stands of brown macroalgae such as Phyllospora comosa and Ecklonia radiata.

species.name: Longtailed jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens taken from flat sandy bottoms.  Feeds on benthic and planktonic invertebrates.

species.name: Longtailed shortfaced eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 6534).

species.name: Longtailed slopefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is frequently consumed by the lutjanid Pristipomoides zonatus at Pathfinder Reef, Mariana Archipelago (Ref. 9831).

species.name: Longtrunk conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky or sandy bottoms (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Longue girelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit seagrass beds and algal-covered flats, occasionally in lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 30 m (Ref. 1602, 41878, 48636). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Usually solitary. Juveniles secretive in seagrasses or attached Sargassum; adults usually in small loose aggregations, but occasionally form large schools to spawn (Ref. 48636). Feed mainly on crustaceans, mollusks, sea urchins (Ref. 37816) and other hard-shelled prey. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Longue-flûte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in protected coastal shallows over or among algae, seagrasses (Ref. 41878), or floating weeds (Ref. 1602).  Juveniles occasionally found near the surface (Ref. 4281).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Used in Chinese medicine to extract Hailong, one of the important drugs (Ref. 12206).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35416).

species.name: Loosejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Loosescale smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Looseskin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Looseskin eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Tolerates wide range of depth (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Lophiobagrus aquilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Concealed mostly among rocks during daytime.  Nocturnal habits prevail (Ref. 45232). Of no food value (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Lophiobagrus asperispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype collected at depth of 9-20m (Ref. 93972). May represent a deep-water specialist (Ref. 75075, 78218, 93972) of the benthic or sublittoral region (Ref. 75075). Found mostly among rocks; of no food value (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Lophiobagrus brevispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly among rocks.  Of no value as food fish (Ref 4967).

species.name: Lophiobrycon weitzmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most of the specimens were caught in a flooded/marshy area draining into the stream, with little current on a muddy bottom with a large amount of decomposing litter. Few specimens were caught in the stream itself, in a margin area of slower current under riparian vegetation over a bottom of rocks, pebbles and sand, with submerged litter only on the bottom of the larger and deeper pools. The species eats mainly aquatic and terrestrial arthropods. Sexual dimorphism (Ref. 52251).

species.name: Lophiodes beroe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly occurred on dead coral Lophelia pertusa rubble and seemed to prefer this habitat that is deep and difficult to sample probably explains how this species escaped detection (Ref. 58471).

species.name: Lophiodes bruchius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Lophiodes fimbriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found in sandy areas  about 15 m deep (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Lophiodes gracilimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophiodes miacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Lophiodes monodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophiogobius ocellicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophiosilurus alexandri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophocampus ocellatus
species.description: Occupies the upper middle strata of the water column along the sides of slow-flowing, perennial rivers and usually occurs among marginal weeds and roots (Ref. 6028).  Probably feeds on zooplankton in the wild.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 8.5 cm SL.

species.name: Lophodolos indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophogobius cristulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophonectes mongonuiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lophotus machadoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loquette antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loquette d Amérique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on worms, crustaceans, molluscs, sea squirts, sea urchins and fishes (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Loquettine à queue claire
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loquettine à queue noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Loraxichthys lexa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Encountered in pools and fast water channels (Ref. 93320).

species.name: Lord Howe conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lord Howe Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Lord Howe Island butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky reefs with corals (Ref. 9710).  Feed on small invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lord Howe Island flounder
species.description: Lives on silty sand bottoms and feeds on bottom-living animals.  Only known from specimens collected from divers.  Sexually dimorphic characters possibly develop at about 6-7 cm SL.

species.name: Lord Howe longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lord Howe pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lord Howe sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lord Howe Threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lord's Tasmangoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit brackish estuaries or freshwater reaches where there are mud bottoms.  Sometimes captured in estuarine tide pools where it buries itself in the sand (Ref. 44894).  Adults migrate to lower marine estuarine areas to spawn in spring.

species.name: Lorentz catfish
species.description: A poorly known species so far recorded only from the type locality.

species.name: Lorentz River Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lorentz's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lentic and lotic freshwater.  They inhabit backwaters, swamps and turbid channels of large rivers (Ref. 2847).  Found in small to large pools over rock and sand, usually in more open, unshaded sections of streams.  Water temperature typically ranges between 25° and 30°C (Ref. 44894).  Omnivorous species (Ref. 7300).  Feed on benthic algae.  Juveniles have been collected in September, suggesting that spawning occurs in the early to middle wet season (November to February) (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lorentz's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loreto cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loreto panda cory
species.description: Occurs mainly in lotic habitats characterized by muddy-brown color, soft bottom of clay and sand where it is relatively abundant (Ref. 58938).

species.name: Loreto tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lori's anthias
species.description: Usually in small groups on drop-offs from 30 to 60 m or in the vicinity of caves or ledges of steep outer reef slopes. Feeds on crustacean larvae and fish eggs (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Loricaria apeltogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria birindellii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria cataphracta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Loricaria clavipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria coximensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gut contents of one specimen contain only seeds which conforms with previous observations of granivory in other species of Loricaria (Ref. 90156).

species.name: Loricaria holmbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria lata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria lentiginosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria luciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in flowing water habitats ranging from small, seasonally intermittent streams (arroyos) to large permanent rivers.  Collected from the following localities:  repeatedly in small order streams with clear water in the upper rio Miranda drainage within the boundaries of the Parque Nacional da Serra da Bodoquena;  in and above riffles at depths of 0.3-1.5 m in the Aquidaban and Tebicuary drainages; in black water at the edge of the main river channel in swift current over sand and mud substrates in the rio Negro at the southern end of the Pantanal wetlands; along the shore over substrates of sand, silt and mud, at a depth of less than 1.5 m using seine at night in the lower rio Paraná (Ref. 94550).

species.name: Loricaria lundbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in black-water habitats.  Aquatic insect larvae of family Chironomidae, sclerotized body parts of unidentified insect larvae, organic detritus and sand were found in the stomach contents of a single specimen measuring 7.66 cm SL (Ref. 79031).

species.name: Loricaria nickeriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria parnahybae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sandy substrate (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Loricaria piracicabae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria pumila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reportedly collected using bottom trawls at depths from 3 to 29 m and at distances of 15 to 1500 m from the shoreline, as well as over silt and organic detritus.  Aquatic insect larva, sclerotized body parts of unidentified insects, organic detritus and sand were found in the stomach contents of a single specimen measuring 7.31 cm SL (Ref. 79031).

species.name: Loricaria simillima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricaria spinulifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to prefer deep channels of large black water rivers.  Reportedly collected with the use of bottom trawls at depths from 1.5 to 28 m and at distances of 10 to 750 m from the shoreline, as well as over substrates of sand, mud, and organic debris.  Aquatic insect larvae, organic detritus and sand were found in the stomach contents of a single specimen measuring 12.06 cm SL (Ref. 79031).

species.name: Loricaria tucumanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys acutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys anus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys brunneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys cashibo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys castaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys chanjoo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys derbyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys edentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys hauxwelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys labialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Loricariichthys maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ditches (Ref. 6868) and ponds (Ref. 11229).

species.name: Loricariichthys melanocheilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys microdon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys nudirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys platymetopon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys rostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys stuebelii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loricariichthys ucayalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lorna drum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Robert Eakins, pers. comm., 2003).

species.name: Lortet’s barbell
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Losera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and streams (Ref. 188), also lakes (Ref. 41580). A small predator, feeding on shrimps, mayfly nymphs and little fish (Ref. 41580, 54749).

species.name: Lost pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lost River sucker
species.description: Found in lakes, impoundments and deep pools of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Lost shark
species.description: Maximum length (43.3 cm TL) is that of a juvenile female; size at birth likely close to 34.0 cm TL, since late-term embryo was fully developed and a 37.0 cm TL juvenile had a faint umbilical sca (Ref. 119369).

species.name: Lotella fernandeziana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow, rough bottoms (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Lotella tosaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Matures at 12 cm TL.

species.name: Lotte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits marginal vegetation and floodplains.  Feeds on insects and small fish (Ref. 28714). Maximum SL reported 50.0 cm (Ref. 31256) larger than maximum TL 45.5 cm (Ref. 81648).

species.name: Louise's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Louisiade sand-goby
species.description: Occurs in sheltered silty-sand bottoms of fringing reefs and lagoons i(Ref. 130975).

species.name: Loup de Bering
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms (Ref. 559).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 28499).

species.name: Loup à tête large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters in midwater; adults also near bottom from 60-970 m, mainly 100-900 m (Ref. 4694).  Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on sea gooseberries, medusas, small fishes, also echinoderms, crustaceans and mollusks (not so hard-shelled) (Ref. 4694).  Spawns at great depths (Ref. 44162).

species.name: Louvereau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and epipelagic; found near surface or in deep water (Ref. 10821).  Apparently solitary (Ref. 9314).  Feed mainly on jellyfishes, ctenophores, and other gelatinous planktonic animals (Ref. 2850, 6885).  Spawning starts at the end of spring and during the summer (Ref. 9314).  Juveniles unlike adults in that the median fins are longer and further forward, the mouth toothed and the body and fins black-spotted (Ref. 6517).  Rarely found in markets (Ref. 9314).

species.name: Lover's Lake killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Endangered and endemic species found in Bermuda with highly fragmented populations and a very limited range. Found only in a limited number of isolated brackish water ponds and appear to form loose schools consisting of equally sized individuals (Ref. 59051). This species is regarded as omnivorous opportunistic feeder (Ref. The main predators to Bermuda’s endemic Fundulus populations include a variety of birds (mostly herons), and fishes (eastern mosquito fish Gambusia holbrooki, gray snapper Lutjanus griseus, American eel Anguilla rostrata). Additionally, it is believed that the introduced and invasive red-eared terrapin Trachemys scripta elegans is a significant predator in a limited number of ponds (Ref. 59051). Non-annual killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Lowcrown seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lowe's leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Loweina interrupta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic.

species.name: Loweina terminata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neustonic to mesopelagic;  at the surface at night and to 825 m during day (Ref. 58302).

species.name: lower Amur grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species spawns in rivers of the Amur Basin from the middle to the end of May, 7-10 days before the T. grubei flavomaculatus. The autumn downstream migration in tributaries of the lower Amur takes place from September to October. The range of the food components of the Lower Amur grayling in the Anyui River in July is represented by various zoobenthos organisms. The most weight part in the food boluses of fish older than the age 3+ is represented by mayfly and stonefly larvae, imago caddis and bugs. The composition and the frequency of occurrence of different organisms in the food boluses of the Lower Amur grayling. Comparison of the feeding spectra in the Lower Amur and yellow-spotted graylings caught in the same stations did not reveal any significant differences in the diversity of the food components (Ref. 57969).

species.name: Loweye snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Almost ripe eggs about 4.1 mm in diameter (Ref. 42734).

species.name: Lowfin dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from lagoons on silty sand and rubble substrata (Ref. 75638).

species.name: Lowfin moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lowland cichlid
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in both fast flowing rivers and still waters (Stawikowski & Werner, 1998).

species.name: Lowland livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in brackish and salt water, but also occasionally in fresh water.

species.name: Lowland shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand- and silt-bottomed pools and runs of creeks and small rivers. Often occurs near vegetation (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Lowveld largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers standing or slow-flowing pools with marginal vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52307), thrives in impounded waters (Ref. 7248). Preys on small fish, insects and other invertebrates, including snails (Ref. 7248, 52307). Male clears small nest and attracts female with quivering display (Ref. 7248). Eggs laid in several bouts (Ref. 7248) and fertilized before female collects them (Ref. 7248, 52307). Agamous maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307). Batch spawner.

species.name: Lowveld suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sandy stretches of flowing rivers where it lives over sandbanks, burying itself in the sand (Ref. 52193). It feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 7248, 52193). Breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Loyalty deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lualaba lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and quiet, vegetated parts of brooks, rivers and lakes (Ref. 47311).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Lubbock's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Lubbock's coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults solitary or in pairs on algae-encrusted coralline coastal reefs (Ref. 90102) and on shallow reef flats with mixed rubble and corals where usually found on boulder-shaped corals (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Lubbock's gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles have been observed cleaning many other fish species (Ref. 98447).

species.name: Lubbockichthys myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species was observed (by R. Myers) to hover within half a meter of the side of the cave (the cave with a large chimney with 3-4 m opening in a shelf about 20 m, and a large opening in the adjacent wall from about 36 to at least 50 m).  Seeks refuge (darts) into a hole when approached within 2-3 meters (Ref. 76877).

species.name: Lubin austral
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled below 200 m (Ref. 4241).  Young are found in warmer and more northern waters.

species.name: Lubin brutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species.  May be a species complex (J.A. Moore, pers. Comm.).  Trawled below 300 m off South Africa and New Zealand (Ref. 4241).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lubin la crête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36655). There is significant morphological variation between populations (Ref. 4241).

species.name: Lubricogobius exiguus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore to moderate depth on muddy substrates, usually with small outcrops of rubble or debris (Ref. 48637).  Collected from muddy sand bottom (Ref. 45340).

species.name: Lubricogobius tre
