species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the bottom of the strait covered with a thick layer of soft silt and is polluted with domestic waste and waste from langouste and pearl farms (broken shells).

species.name: Lucaya cavebrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an anchialine cave which is connected to the sea via a submerged passage which opens into a tidal saltwater creek.  The upper about 14 m in the cave consists of freshwater (22 °C), separated from a lower, slightly warmer (23-25 °C), salty layer by a distinct halocline. The holotype was taken in a depth of 12 m, which must then most likely to be freshwater; some where collected from one or two inland sink holes (Ref. 57878).

species.name: Lucifuga inopinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Type specimen found under a rock ledge at 202 m depth on a sea mount (Ref. 33021, 34024).

species.name: Lucifuga simile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found in caves (Ref. 34024). Found together with L. subterranea and L. teresinarum (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Lucifuga teresinarum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species found only in caves (Ref. 34024). Found together with L. dentata and L. subterranea (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Lucigadus acrolophus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lucigadus borealis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lucigadus lucifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lucigadus nigromarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lucigadus potronus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus albanicus
species.description: A long-lived species which occurs in lentic waters (Ref. 26100).  Inhabits lakes and lower course of rivers, with mud to sand bottom.  Feeds on algae, plant material, insect larvae and detritus.  Spawns in both lakes and their tributaries.  Individual females spawn with 3-7 males on sandy beaches, especially near estuaries of tributaries. Larvae and juveniles form small monospecific schools in bays and harbours (Ref. 59043). Threatened due to habitat destruction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Luciobarbus biscarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus bocagei
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits the  middle and lower reaches of streams with slow current (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, detritus (Ref. 59043), plants and fish (Ref. 26100).  Considered a long-lived species (Ref. 26100).  Attains a maximum size of about 80 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Luciobarbus chelifensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus graecus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and streams with stone and gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in water bodies in low-lying plains with little current. Feeds on invertebrates and algae.  Threatened by water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).  Size reaches up to at least 50 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Luciobarbus graellsii
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits lower and middle reaches of rivers with slow current, preferring areas with vegetation and shore cover.  Migrates upstream areas with faster current and gravel or stone bottom for spawning (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on invertebrates and plants (Ref. 26100) and algae (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Luciobarbus guiraonis
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in water bodies of low-lying plains, with little current (Ref. 26100).  Most common in the middle and  lower reaches of rivers.  Moves upstream stretches during spawning season (Ref. 59043).  Threatened by pollution, habitat destruction and introduction of new species (Ref. 26100).  Attains maximum size up to about 50 cm SL and lives up to at least 7 years (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Luciobarbus lanigarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus leptopogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom dweller that feeds mainly on benthic organisms.  In Lake Tiberias the main food items are chironomid larvae and oligochaetes, while gastropods form only a minor part of the diet.  Spawns January to March in shallow waters of small streams, eggs being deposited on gravel.  Very tasty fish but the spawn is toxic (Andrey Mazlin, pers. comm., 2003).

species.name: Luciobarbus magniatlantis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast mountain rivers with current (Ref. 114101).

species.name: Luciobarbus mascarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus nasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Luciobarbus numidiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus pallaryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus setivimensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobarbus steindachneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in water bodies on low-lying plains, with little current (Ref. 26100).  Also inhabits upper reaches of rivers with slow current.  Preys mainly on planktonic crustaceans, supplemented by insects and algae (Ref. 59043).   Threatened by pollution, habitat destruction and introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).  Size reaches up to at least 40 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Luciobrama macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in rivers and lakes.  The fish, under 300 mm long, generally live in upper and middle layers of water and those larger generally live in middle and lower layers of water.  They have the habit of semi-migration between rivers and lakes (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Luciobrotula bartschi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Shallowest depth range at about 250 m (Ref. 95664).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Luciobrotula brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobrotula coheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciobrotula corethromycter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not often encountered but probably locally abundant (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Luciobrotula lineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Luciobrotula nolfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Luciocephalus aura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in freshwater swamp forest habitats (Ref. 56386).

species.name: Luciocyprinus langsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciocyprinus striolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to prefer large, deep rivers without much current (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Luciogobius adapel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciogobius albus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits underground waters near the sea.

species.name: Luciogobius ama
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a tide pool.

species.name: Luciogobius brevipterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Luciogobius dormitoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype, collected from the tidal region of a small river (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Luciogobius elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky coasts with pebbles.

species.name: Luciogobius fluvialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the middle reaches of river on a gravel substrate composed of pebbles of 3-5 cm in diameter and containing less than 5% of sand, where freshwater springs flow from between the pebbles (Ref. 86963).

species.name: Luciogobius fonticola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the river mouth on a gravel substrate composed of sand and pebbles, where freshwater springs flow from gaps between the pebbles (Ref. 86963).

species.name: Luciogobius grandis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky coasts.

species.name: Luciogobius koma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Luciogobius pallidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits underground waters near the sea.

species.name: Luciogobius parvulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools with pebbles.

species.name: Luciogobius platycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky coasts.

species.name: Luciogobius ryukyuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among gravels at the rapids which are in the most lower reaches in the freshwater area on the river (Ref. 86740).

species.name: Luciogobius saikaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward rocky coasts.

species.name: Luciosoma bleekeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in rivers (Ref. 12975).  Occurs at the surface of flowing waters.  Inhabits flooded forests and moves into permanent water in November and December as flood waters rapidly recede.  Feeds mostly on exogenous insects as well as some small crustaceans and fish.  Used to make pharos (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Luciosoma pellegrinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in deeper, slower water.  An active fish, in constant motion at the surface of the water, feeding on material dropping into streams and has been observed leaping clear of the water to prey on material dangling above water (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Luciosoma setigerum
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occur in river mainstream and low gradient tributaries with logs and leaf litter on the bottom (Ref. 7050).  Found at the surface of flowing waters.  Feed mostly on fish (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Luciosoma trinema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in river mainstream and low gradient tributaries with logs and leaf-litter on the bottom (Ref. 7050). Feeds on insects and small fishes such as Rasbora spp. (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Lucretia's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with leaf, shell and organic debris (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Ludong hillstream loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from hillstreams with swift current over bottom of gravel. Individuals swim slowly and usually inhabit the bottom of water. Associated species collected were cyprinids, Carassius auratus auratus, Cyprinus carpio, Pseudorasbora parva Yunnanilus jinxiensis; eleotrid Micropercops compressocephalus; and silurids Silurus asotus, Silurus cochinchinensis (Ref. 87910).

species.name: Luetken's lanternfish
species.description: Oceanic species (Ref. 4066).  Found between 375-750 m during the day and between 40-325 m at night (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Lufubuchromis relictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river, about 15 m wide with an estimated depth of 50 cm, rocky with patches of sand and gravel and with few patches of submerged vegetation (Ref. 122072). It is suggested that this species feeds on insect larvae and detritus (Ref. 122072). It is a maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 122072).

species.name: Luika barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 5.2 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Luminescent cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate (Ref. 7300) and benthic species (Ref. 75154) recorded from the upper continental slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: Luminous cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and coastal reefs, among corals and rocks (Ref. 4329, 127962). Lives sympatrically with A. notatus (Ref. 76833). Forms large schools (Ref. 559).  Feeds during the day in currents above reefs as well as at night (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Luminous conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental shelf over soft bottom (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Luminous deepsea cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Luminous lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.  Found between 425-850 m during the day and in the upper 100 m at night.  Small specimens found in the upper 50 m (night).

species.name: Luminous slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Lumpenopsis pavlenkoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lumpenopsis triocellata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shelf edges and continental slopes (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Lunartail puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly marine, occasionally enters estuaries (Ref. 4833). Occurs over sandy bottoms, often on coastal reefs; feeds on a variety of marine invertebrates (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Lunate goldie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms small aggregations and found on outer reefs in 40-75 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found near the bottom from inshore waters to at least 54 m depth, but may form schools near the surface (Ref. 5217).  Juveniles are found on muddy bottoms brackish estuaries and in coastal marine waters (Ref. 5217).  Adults feed on small fishes and crustaceans.  Good food fish and marketed fresh.

species.name: Lune (Selene vomer)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow coastal waters, usually over hard or sandy bottoms.  Juveniles may be encountered in estuarine areas (Ref. 9626) and off sandy beaches (Ref. 5217).  Found in schools, but may be encountered in small groups or in pairs (Ref. 26235).  Adults feed on small crabs, shrimps, fishes, and worms.  Flesh has excellent flavor (Ref. 5521).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Lune (Trachinotus baillonii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur near surface waters of lagoon and seaward reefs, in surge zones along sandy beaches (Ref. 48635, 90102).  They always move in schools at the edge of the surf near the reef, usually in pairs or small groups in surface waters (Ref. 48635).  They feed on small fishes (Ref. 9710).  They are occasionally taken by trolling and line fishing.

species.name: Lune d'argent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays, mangrove estuaries, tidal creeks, and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847, 44894, 48636); occasionally in silty coastal reefs (Ref. 9710). It feeds on plankton and detritus (Ref. 5213, 44894). Commonly seen in large schools (Ref. 44894, 52193); small juveniles either solitary or in small aggregations (Ref. 48635). Usually only juveniles enter freshwater (Ref. 52193). Highly territorial (Ref. 9710). Caught with throw nets (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Lune pleine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters including estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 5213).  Seldom enters freshwater.  Juveniles can be kept in the aquarium (Ref. 4833).  Caught with throw nets (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Luneur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper coastal waters near the bottom on both the continental shelves and around major island groups; sometimes in river estuaries (Ref. 47690, 48635).  Found in schools (Ref. 47690, 48635).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5213).  Readily dries in air without salting (Ref. 4375, 48635).  Caught in trawls and by beach seine, but mainly by trawling, often incidentally. Marketed fresh and dried (Ref. 47690).  Minimum depth from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Lussion à menton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from 50-1000 m (ref. 04473) and up to 1032 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Epipelagic to bathypelagic (Ref. 58426); also mesopelagic (Ref. 5951).  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and occasionally planktonic organisms (Ref. 5759).  Spawns from March to September, larvae near the surface (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Lutea sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marine and estuarine waters (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Luther's prawn-goby
species.description: Found on sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710). Lives symbiotically with alpheid shrimps (e.g.Alpheus djiboutensis) and photographed with Ptereleotris arabica (https://www.oceandocs.org/handle/1834/10331?locale-attribute=ru, sent by A. Volkers).

species.name: Luther's spiny loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Luthulenchelys heemstraorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lutjan aimable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults mainly inhabit coral reefs.  Sometimes forming large aggregations around rocky outcrops during daylight hours.  They disperse to feed at night (Ref. 9710).  Usually marketed fresh.

species.name: Lutjan rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs, including sheltered lagoons and outer reefs (Ref. 30573). Usually found singly, often adjacent to steep outer reef slopes, but occasionally found in groups (Ref. 9710). Feeds mainly on fishes, but also take shrimps, crabs, amphipods, stomatopods, gastropods and urochordates. Large fish from oceanic areas in the western Pacific are often ciguatoxic, e.g., in Tuvalu (Ref. 9513). Caught mainly with handlines and bottom longlines (Ref. 9821). Utilized fresh and dried-salted (Ref. 9987). Juveniles mimic Chromis damselfishes (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Lutjan à bandes noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs where it usually occurs singly or in small groups.  A shy species that moves around quickly through coral channels in hunt for small fishes (Ref. 48635).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Lutjan à lignes jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit offshore coral reefs and trawling grounds. Trawled to depth of almost 100 m (Ref. 48635). Frequently encountered in large schools with other Lutjanus species (Ref. 9710). Feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Lutjan à tache unique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults probably frequent coral reef areas; juveniles found in mangrove estuaries (Ref. 30573).  Feed on fishes and benthic invertebrates including shrimps, crabs and cephalopods.  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Lutjanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms and coral reefs (Ref. 55, 57393, 81653).  Also common in brackish lagoons and occasionally in rivers (Ref. 55, 81653), especially juveniles (Ref. 57393).  Feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 55, 81653).

species.name: Lutjanus (Lutjanus fulgens)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Also found in deeper offshore waters.  Feed on fishes and crustaceans.

species.name: Lutjanus alexandrei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adult standard length is greater 20 cm (Ref. 57982).

species.name: Lutjanus indicus
species.description: This species was observed in coral-reef habitat; generally encountered solitary or in small groups in about 5-15 m depth. It is also taken by trawlers in deeper water (to at least 50 m) and usually appears in fish markets. Few information on juvenile habitat, but suspected to be similar to L. russellii where young are found in brackish mangrove estuaries and lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 93093).

species.name: Luzon righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Luzonichthys williamsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over coral rubble (Ref. 8524).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycaspine à chevrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on clams, cumaceans and worms (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycenchelys albeola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys bullisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys callista
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on bivalves, gastropods, and crustaceans.

species.name: Lycenchelys camchatica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycenchelys chauliodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys cicatrifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycenchelys fedorovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic infaunal and epifaunal predator.  Feeds mainly on amphipods, with polychaetes, isopods and an ostracod of minor importance.  Females above 25 cm SL contained ova (Ref. 37539).

species.name: Lycenchelys folletti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on a juvenile specimen.  Feeds on gastropods.

species.name: Lycenchelys hadrogeneia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys hippopotamus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys imamurai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters off Peru (Ref. 78516).

species.name: Lycenchelys incisa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys lonchoura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycenchelys maculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys makushok
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycenchelys monstrosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycenchelys platyrhina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy substrates with a bottom temperature of -1°C (Ref. 4695).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycenchelys volki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycenchelys wilkesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycenchelys xanthoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665). Known from a few banks and seamounts at 880–1056 m depth in the Ross Sea, Antarctica and from a single location in the Weddel Sea, at 771–793 m depth (Ref. 82287).

species.name: Lycengraulis figueiredoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycengraulis limnichthys
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to reach 28 cm TL (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Lycian spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from an irrigation canal draining water from a stream.  Population may have dropped dramatically due to water abstraction in large quantities from the stream and from the canals (Ref. 83419).

species.name: Lycodapus australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodapus derjugini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodapus dermatinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodapus microchir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodapus poecilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycode arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft bottoms (Ref. 13534).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds mainly on epibenthic animals and does not seem to burrow much for prey.  Smaller fish prey on smaller species like amphipods, isopods and small bivalves while larger fish prey on shrimps, euphausiids and fish (Ref. 13532).

species.name: Lycode blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycode brun noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycode commune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on mud or sand (Ref. 5951); benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on molluscs and cumaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode d'Adolf
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426). Length type assumed SL.

species.name: Lycode de Hureau
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycode de la mer blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycode de Laval
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud and sand (Ref. 5951); benthic.  Feeds on bottom invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode de Lütken
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud bottoms (Ref. 4965). Benthic; feeds on invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 58426). The holotype was known to contain a species of Cottunculus and another fish (Ref. 4965).

species.name: Lycode de mcallister
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on fishes (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode de paamiut
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode de sars
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy bottoms (Ref. 35388).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on polychaetes, crustaceans and bivalves (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Lycode de terre-neuve
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on sponge remains, worms, molluscs, pycnogonids, crustaceans and brittle stars (Ref. 58426).  Species forgotten in CLOFNAM (10007) and FNAM (4695).

species.name: Lycode glaciale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 58426), bottom crustaceans (isopods, amphipods), ophiurids, cephalopods.  Reproduces probably in early autumn.  About 500 demersal eggs of 7 mm diameter (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Lycode murène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on muddy bottoms at 622-1,175 m, with temperatures below 0°C.  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Lycode obèse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also abyssobenthic on muddy bottoms (Ref. 6950).

species.name: Lycode plume
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow, inshore soft bottoms, mostly in brackish waters with salinities of about 15-27 ppt. (Ref. 4695).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on isopods, bivalves, polychaetes (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Lycode polaire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695).  Buries into the mud tail first (Ref. 4695).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 4695); mainly of amphipods (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Lycode polaire (Lycodes turneri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycode pâle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds mostly on endobenthic prey such as small bivalves, polychaetes and small crustaceans in addition to detritus.  It seems to get the bulk of its food by burrowing in the sediment (Ref. 13532).  Ripe females recorded in September in the Kara Sea (Ref. 4695).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycode quadrillée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on clams (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode à arc
species.description: Occurs on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on polychaetes, mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Lycode à carreaux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives at temperature of 0-5°C.  Off Greenland it measures 50 cm and off Scandinavia rarely over 25-30 cm (Ref. 35388).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds mostly on endobenthic prey, with shrimps and euphausiids becoming the more prominent prey as the size increases (Ref. 13532).  Prefers warmer waters (Ref. 13534).  Large eggs of 6 mm diameter are deposited on the sea floor.

species.name: Lycode à deux lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).  Switches feeding habits with increasing size.  Smaller eelpouts eat mainly endobenthic prey, larger individuals feed more on epibenthic prey (Ref. 13532).

species.name: Lycode à oreilles
species.description: Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695). Benthic (Ref. 58426). Feeds mainly on epibenthic animals. With increase in size, shrimps and euphausiids are ingested in greater quantities but unlike L. reticulatus, its ingestion of smaller prey items does not decrease. Changes in feeding habit with size are relatively small (Ref. 13532).

species.name: Lycode à selles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Lycode à trois taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).  Smaller individuals prey on smaller species like amphipods, isopods and small bivalves while larger ones prey on shrimps, euphausiids and fish (Ref. 13532).

species.name: Lycode à tête longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on mud or sand (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Lycode élan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottom, collected at ca 1200 m depth (Ref. 87479).

species.name: Lycodes akuugun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species were collected in hauls dominated by Atheresthes stomias, Theragra chalcogramma, Hippoglossus stenolepis, and Sebastes alutus; also with Lycodes diapterus and L. concolor. Bottom temperatures of collection sites ranged from 3.3-4.3 °C. Stomach contents of 2 specimens has partially digested sea urchin tests (Ref. 56970).

species.name: Lycodes albonotatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes bathybius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes caudimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from holotype data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodes fulvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodes heinemanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data of Lycodes (Furcimanus) taranetzi (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodes japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodes jenseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes macrochir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes matsubarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycodes microlepidotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes microporus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes nakamurae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes nishimurai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Lycodes ocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data.

species.name: Lycodes paucilepidotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes pectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes sadoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycodes semenovi
species.description: Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Lycodes tanakae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes teraoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes toyamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains over 40 cm TL.

species.name: Lycodes uschakovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes yamatoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodes ygreknotatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodichthys antarcticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodichthys dearborni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodonus flagellicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms with temperatures below 0°C. Feeds on small crustaceans like Themisto, Podocerus and Hemilamprops (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Lycodonus malvinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycodonus vermiformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lycogrammoides schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lyconodes argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic juvenile phase (Ref. 58452).

species.name: Lyconus brachycolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 12204, 58452) found on the muddy slope of the continental shelf (Ref. 6524).  Juveniles are captured from 150-700 m depth range (Ref. 58452).  Biology unknown (Ref. 12204).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 58452.

species.name: Lyconus pinnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles were found from 150-700 m depth range in deep ocean; adults in the continental shelf and seamounts (Ref. 58452).  Poorly known, rare species (Ref. 1371, 58452).

species.name: Lycozoarces regani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lyre goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur mainly in muddy backwaters of bays and estuaries, often in foul waters.  Also found on muddy bottoms of fresh water (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Lyre-tail dart-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in reef habitats from shallow coastal slopes to outer reef lagoons and slopes below drop-offs to 50 meters, among rubble (Ref. 48637).  Occurs in pairs and its burrow may be in coral rock or sand.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). They tend to form large, though diffuse, colonies; may be due to a propensity to aggregate or may be a result of the ecological requirements for the species (for which type of substratum, current pattern, and water depth among the most important) which restrict the areas of settlement of the postlarvae.

species.name: Lyrefin pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers pH=6.6, Hardness=6, temp.=24°C with rocks, plants and driftwood in the aquarium environment.  An egg laying, peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).  Bottom spawner, 2 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Lyretail dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal patch reefs on soft bottom slopes.  Highly territorial and aggressive.  This and related species have been known to bite the camera housings of divers and kill aquarium tank mates (Ref. 9710). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Lythrypnus alphigena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen.

species.name: Lythrypnus brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from large rocks covered with algae, sponges, and bryozoans on a sand bottom (Ref. 34188).

species.name: Lythrypnus cobalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Lythrypnus lavenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen collected in 137-142 m.

species.name: Lythrypnus mowbrayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most collections taken from the bases of patch reefs or coral encrusted boulders with undercut ledges (Ref. 34188).

species.name: Lythrypnus solanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from one specimen.

species.name: Lécaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More commonly found from 30 to 100 m, mainly on mud and gravel bottoms, but also on sand and rock.  Feed on shrimps, crabs, mollusks, small fish, polychaetes and cephalopods.  Migrate to the open sea only after the first year of life.  Eggs are pelagic.   Larvae and juveniles are associated with jellyfish.  Upon maturity, small chin barbel characteristic of juveniles disappear (Ref. 53061).  Spawn in batches (Ref. 51846).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted, smoked and frozen; eaten steamed, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Légine antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 89402).

species.name: Légine australe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At 12-15 cm TL, semi-pelagic juveniles become demersal at 150-400 m depth (Ref. 55957).  Adults migrate to deeper habitats at depths greater than 1,000 m (Ref. 55957).  Utilized as food fish (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Lémonème de Giunée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant around 300 m over soft bottom (Ref. 1371).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 26999.

species.name: Lépadogastère de Candolle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the lower intertidal zone with the algae Himanthalia and Laminaria (Ref. 4489).

species.name: Lépadogastère de Gouan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal species (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Lépadogastère à deux tâches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled over soft mud bottom.  Feeds mainly on benthic organisms (Ref. 12577).  Inhabits shallow water on rocky bottoms and bivalve banks.  Spawns in June - July, egg measures 1.5 mm.  Larvae are pelagic (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Lépadogastère à petite tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in littoral and sublittoral zones.

species.name: Lépisosté de Floride
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in sluggish mud or sand-bottomed pools of quiet lowland streams and lakes.  Usually found near vegetation.

species.name: Lépisosté à museau plat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit quiet pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers, swamps, lakes and overflow areas of large streams.  Often occur near vegetation and submerged logs.  Feed on other fishes and insects.  Spawning occurs over vegetation or other submerged objects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Lézard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental shelves, often on sandy beaches and rarely in estuaries (Ref. 244).  Reported to enter freshwater and recorded several times from Cambodia as far upstream as the Great Lake (Ref. 12693).  Occurs near the surface in shallow waters (Ref. 12693).  Feeds mainly on small pelagic and benthic bony fishes, also cephalopods and other invertebrates (Ref. 244).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized fresh and possibly dried salted for human consumption and for fishmeal (Ref. 9997).  The 178 cm specimen recorded off Africa is possibly based on some other species (Ref. 9997).

species.name: Lézard (Synodus saurus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily in insular waters (Ref. 4964), on sand and sand-rock bottoms (Ref. 6808).  Feeds mainly on other fishes, but may also prey on other animals (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Mabul sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by handnet (Ref. 75879).

species.name: Macau sole
species.description: A coastal and estuarine species, ascending some large rivers, including the Mekong (Ref. 12693).  Lives in silty sand or muddy substrates in sheltered coastal waters (Ref. 48637).  Found on the bottom, where it feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Macclesfield dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macclesfield longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macculloch's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland swamps and small streams, usually in clear, acidic waters with ample cover in the form of log debris or aquatic vegetation. Occurs at temperatures ranging from 24-30° C (Ref. 5259). Found in clear waters of small creeks and Pandanus swamps. pH range is 5.5-7 (Ref. 44894). Commonly co-occurs with Melanotaenia splendida and is often found in association with other wetland fish species particularly Pseudomugil gertrudae and Oxyeleotris nullipora (Ref. 121823),

species.name: Macedonia shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Landlocked, lacustrine, pelagic, in upper water layers during summer and descending to deeper layers in winter.  It spawns at 1-2 years, near shores above gravel or coarse sand, with most individuals spawning more than one season.  Spawning starts when temperature reach about 19-20°C,  in July to August (Ref. 59043).  Adults form schools in the epilimnion during summer and tend to congregate in shallow waters near shores.  They feed on plankton (cladocerans and copepods) and small fishes (Ref. 10545, 59043).  It is threatened by water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Macedonian vimba
species.description: Inhabits rivers and streams, usually with relatively swift current (Ref.  59043).  Also occurs in  lakes and lowland water courses with little current.  Feeds on invertebrates and plants (Ref. 26100).  Spawns among stones in large rivers (Ref. 59043). Threatened due to habitat destruction, angling and water abstraction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Machaca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, rivers and streams between 0 and 600 m elevation.  The young feed on terrestrial and aquatic insects, leaves, fruits and seeds but become mainly herbivorous when adult.  Eggs are deposited in nests located in sand bottoms of streams.

species.name: Machida's coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Macleay's crested pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 13.6 cm SL.

species.name: Macleay's glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along the vegetated margins of streams and swamps, often among dense aquatic vegetation (Ref. 44894).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans as well as on aquatic insects, juvenile fishes and algae (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Maconde aden
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Maconde bonche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Marketed fresh or made into fishmeal (Ref. 3288).

species.name: Maconde lumineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Marketed fresh or reduced to fishmeal.

species.name: Maconde lèvre mince
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud bottom (Ref. 26999).  Most abundant at about 200 m (Ref. 6916).  Feeds on pelagic crustaceans like euphausiids, mysids and decapods (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Maconde sombre
species.description: Marketed fresh or made into fishmeal (Ref. 3288).

species.name: Macquarie notoliparid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrocephenchelys brachialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrocephenchelys nigriventris
species.description: Four adult females of the 28 specimens taken from northeastern and southwestern Taiwan were with mature ovary and eggs at small body size (180–221 mm) (Ref. 129313).

species.name: Macrocephenchelys soela
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus aureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus caudiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus circumcinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams to peats (Ref. 57235).  Found in medium to large-sized rivers and flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Nocturnal, feeding on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 13371).  Commonly seen in aquarium trades and fish markets (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Macrognathus dorsiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus keithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in leaf banks or under log debris or rocks (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Macrognathus lineatomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus malabaricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal rivers, streams and inundated ponds and paddy fields (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Macrognathus meklongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus morehensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus pavo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus pentophthalmos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrognathus semiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A burrower (Ref. 39392).

species.name: Macrognathus taeniagaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing and standing water habitats.  Often found in impoundments.  During the daytime, it spends much of its time mostly buried in silt, sand or fine gravel.  Usually only the snout and eye protrude from the bottom.  Emerges at night to feed on benthic insect larvae, crustaceans and worms.  Also caught with push-nets and set-nets.  Sold fresh and often seen in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Macrognathus tapirus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers among leaf litter or dense vegetation, over muddy substrate (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on insects and crustaceans (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Macroparalepis affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to bathypelagic, young mainly at the surface and to 200 m, adults at 400-2,000 m (Ref. 4473).  Carnivorous (Ref. 5759).

species.name: Macroparalepis brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on planktonic organisms, rarely on small fishes (Ref. 5759).

species.name: Macroparalepis danae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macroparalepis longilateralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macroparalepis nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropharyngodon cyanoguttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropharyngodon marisrubri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropharyngodon moyeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives around boulders on sandy bottom with heavy growth of algae.

species.name: Macropleurodus bicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the littoral and sublittoral regions, especially where the bottom is hard, only rarely over mud (Ref. 5662). Feeds mainly on snails and insect larvae (Ref. 558) as well as on detritus and phytoplankton (Ref. 28676). In combination, the introduction of top-predator Lates niloticus (and probably other species of Lates), together with intensified fishing efforts, appear to be responsible for the virtual disappearance of this species over the last 20 years (Ref. 26184).

species.name: Macropodus baviensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropodus erythropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small hill streams along heterogeneously structured shores with many overhanging shrubs and submerged roots (Ref. 42924).

species.name: Macropodus hongkongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the mountainous regions as well as lowland habitats (Ref. 42924).

species.name: Macropodus lineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropodus oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropodus phongnhaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropodus spechti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in all kinds of hill stream habitats and along diverse structured margins or backwaters of large rivers, as well as in small streams and irrigation channels on farmland (Ref. 42924).

species.name: Macropsobrycon uruguayanae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macropsobrycon xinguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrosmia phalacra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrospinosa cuja
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Macrotrema caligans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Maculabatis astra
species.description: A demersal species found  inshore, over muddy bottoms or mangrove flats to 140 m depth.  Litters of 1-3 pups. Feeds mainly on prawns and crabs (Ref. 114953).  Birth size for this species is about 17-19 cm WD (Ref. 76963).

species.name: Maculabatis macrura
species.description: This species is mainly benthic on soft bottoms, from inshore to at least 60 m. Feeds mainly on small prawns. Size to at least 85 cm WD or 220 cm TL. Males mature at ca. 46-48 cm WD while females at about 64 cm WD, born at ca. 18 cm WD (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Madagascan dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Madagascar guitarfish
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Madagascar numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found over predominantly muddy substrata (Ref. 93929). Maturity size of males at ca. 27 cm TL; birth size at ca. 14 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Madagascar pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth between 600 and 605 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Madagascar skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on upper insular slope (Ref. 114953). Holotype taken from a depth between 300-850 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca.  55 cm TL, females at ca. 57 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Madagascar sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Madagascar wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Madang dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on soft bottom in the deeper parts of the lagoon, where this species is possibly restricted to in the Madang area at depths of approximately 30-40 m (Ref. 97649)..

species.name: Madang sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand at the edge of an isolated coral head in 30 m in the type locality (Ref. 75879).

species.name: Madeira butterfly ray
species.description: Holotype measured 167 cm WD (Ref.  4439).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Madeiran smooth-head
species.description: Benthic species (Ref. 51024, 75154); juvenile mesopelagic (Ref. 51024).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Madhava’s stream loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a small stream about 2 m wide, flowing through sparsely-inhabited tea plantations, at an elevation of about 1000 m above sea level and with substrate consisting of pebbles and gravel. Prefers the faster-flowing areas of the stream. Occurs syntopically with the cyprinids Devario malabaricus (Jerdon), Puntius titteya (Deraniyagala), Pethia nigrofasciata (Günther), Rasbora dandia (Valenciennes), Rasboroides rohani (Batuwita, Silva & Edirisinghe), and the osphronemid Belontia signata (Günther). The introduced guppy Poecilia reticulata Peters was also recorded from this stream (Ref. 116162).

species.name: Madras
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs, occurring in both shallow lagoons and on outer reef slopes.  Frequently found in large aggregations around coral formation, caves or wrecks during the day.  Juveniles inhabit seagrass beds around patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs, stomatopods, cephalopods, and planktonic crustaceans.  Also take a variety of algae (Ref. 4821).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Madras goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably occurs on sandy bottoms (Ref. 125842).

species.name: Madura goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fresh and brackish waters (Ref. 4833). Browses on diatoms; not active at low tide, staying in burrows made by Alpheus bisincisus and others.

species.name: Maeklong chameleon catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on crustaceans and benthic organisms (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Maeklong sheatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mainstream (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on insects and small shrimps (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Magadanichthys skopetsi
species.description: Occurs in the littoral zone influenced by brackish waters; collected from under stones exposed at low tide.  Female individuals collected contained ripe eggs (diameter ca 3 mm); 41-73 eggs (Ref. 55721).

species.name: Magadi tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur at temperatures ranging from 16.0-40.0 °C (Ref. 2). Feed actively in the evening. Young O. alcalicus grahami eat eggs as they are shed by the female, and much of the time and energy of the territorial male is occupied in driving them off. Feed on invertebrates, at the surface (Ref. 2).

species.name: Magdalena blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Magdalena river stingray
species.description: Prefers shallow muddy bottoms with turbid waters (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Magdalena rivulus
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Magela hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing, shallow creeks with sand or gravel bottoms.  Forms large shoals.  Feeds from the substrate on algae, microcrustaceans, aquatic insects and detritus Breeding is opportunistic, with peak activity early in the wet season (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Magellan plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in shallow, inshore waters, but may be found from 40-50 m.  Occurs in tide pools, under rocks and among kelp (Ref. 5191).  Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041).

species.name: Magellan skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Magenta dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers above coral or rubble and inhabits steep outer reef slopes and outer channel walls. Solitary or in small, loosely scattered groups at base of steep dropoffs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Maghreb barbel
species.description: This species can inhabit rivers of varying typology within its distribution range; upstream it is substituted for the trout, and in the lower courses of rivers and calm currents it is locally highly abundant; the species is also present in reservoirs (Ref. 107580). From April to May the species migrates upstream to headwaters for spawning (Ref. 107580). Its spawning migration has been affected by dams, which present physical barriers to upstream migration; the presences of exotic species in reservoirs, as well as poor water quality in the lower courses, due to fertilizers and pesticides, have probably been primary causes of the decline in its population (Ref. 107580).

species.name: Magister argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found shallow warm water, over muddy bottom (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans, also marine worms and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister au nez rétroussé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species found over muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on marine worms and other epibenthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).  Occasionally in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans, also worms and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister bâillant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow water, over muddy bottom (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister creux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in warm water, over muddy bottom (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on zooplankton (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister fourche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, over soft, muddy bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Abundant in brackish estuaries (Ref. 5217).  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans, often hunting in schools (Ref. 4537, 35237).  Mostly used in the manufacture of sub-products (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Magister gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters to about 50 m depth (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Magister lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in warm shallow water, over sandy and muddy bottom (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in warm shallow water, over sandy bottom (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water, including littoral pools (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister Pizarro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow open waters and in bays, over muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on planktonic organisms (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister tiyeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters, also present in river estuaries (Ref. 3702).  Feeds on bottom-dwelling organisms (Ref. 3702).  Mostly used in the manufacture of sub-products (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Magister à tête lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, over sandy and muddy bottom; also in estuaries (Ref. 9118).  Found in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Magister étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over hard sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters to about 20 m depth.  Also common in river estuaries.  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans.  Not marketed for human consumption.

species.name: Magma fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species apparently inhabits steep slopes comprised mostly of volcanic rubble (Ref. 116593).

species.name: Magnificent dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Magnificent rabbitfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and feeds on algae and small invertebrates.  Adults occur in pairs, juveniles secretive in corals (Ref. 48637). Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102). Maximum depth from Ref. 027115.

species.name: Magnificent snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow water and occasionally at the surface over sand and coral (Ref. 40867).  Benthic in crevices and on sandy or rocky substrata (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Magnificent splendid perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species which seeks the cover of caves and crevices at night and when disturbed.  Often found on rocky reefs in coastal waters (Ref. 33616).  Presumably feed on plankton.

species.name: Magnus' prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on open sand bottoms of clear water reefs (Ref. 9710).  Lives with alphaeid shrimps in burrows.

species.name: Magpie morwong
species.description: Inhabits shallow protected reef and sandy areas, sometimes entering estuaries (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Magpie perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on mollusks, polychaetes and algae (Ref. 2156).

species.name: Mahanadi razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the lower reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Mahanadi scribbled goby
species.description: Local communities have been consuming this species and holds a high commercial value, as they are sold at a high price in both fresh and dry forms. Considering its market value, possible extent of exploitation, and area of occurrence, it needs special conservation attention for sustainable utilization (Ref. 130910).

species.name: Mahia whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes (myctophids), and crabs, among other items (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Mahogany goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mahogony snapper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear shallow waters over rocky bottoms in the vicinity of coral reefs, less frequently in sandy or seagrass areas.  They often form large aggregations during the day.  They feed at night mainly on small fish, shrimps, crabs and cephalopods (Ref. 78464).

species.name: Mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper part of clear fast flowing large jungle streams and rivers in upland areas (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Mahseer (Tor douronensis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Kept in ponds or cages in open water.  Seldom seen in markets (Ref. 7050).  Multiple spawner (Ref. 56317).

species.name: Mahseer (Tor putitora)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit streams, riverine pools and lakes.  Found in rapid streams with rocky bottom (Ref. 41236).  Omnivorous, feeding on fish, zooplankton, dipteran larvae and plant matter (Ref. 40948).  Juveniles subsist on plankton while fingerlings feed mainly on algae (Ref. 40948).  Ascend streams to breed over gravel and stones and returns to perennial ponds after breeding.  The most common Himalayan mahseer and a very attractive sport fish, with excellent food value.  Specimens over 30 cm and 5 kg in weight are rarely caught in recent times (Ref. 41236).  Threatened due to over harvesting and habitat loss (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Mahseer (Tor tambra)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).

species.name: Mahseer (Tor tambroides)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit pools and runs over gravel and cobble in rivers flowing through undisturbed forests (Ref. 12693).  Juveniles were most commonly collected in or near rapids (Ref. 27732).  Found in small rivers and streams during the dry season.  Move downstream at the onset of the rainy season, but generally avoid turbid waters.  Mature individuals migrate upstream after two months and spawn in July near the mouths of small streams that the young subsequently ascend.  Omnivorous, feeding on both animal and vegetable matter, at times consuming toxic fruits in flooded forests, making them temporarily inedible.

species.name: Mai-ndombe dwarf sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A lacustrine species in acid waters (Ref. 188).

species.name: Maidague défense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats and lagoon reefs, in areas with seagrass or mixed sand, rubble, and coral (Ref. 9710).  They often form small aggregations (Ref. 8631).  Juveniles occur inshore and usually form small groups in estuarine seagrass beds.  Adults can be found in inner as well as outer reefs and are territorial (Ref. 48636).  Feed mainly on hard-shelled prey including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Maigre africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adult fish found mainly near shore beyond the surf zone, occasionally going inshore.  Juveniles exclusively found inshore.  Juveniles recruit to estuaries at about 30 cm TL.  An important food fish (Ref. 11025).

species.name: Maigre arabe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maigre argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters in sandy, muddy bottoms (Ref. 75716).  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 2113).  Marketed fresh and dried.

species.name: Maigre d'Afrique du Sud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.  Juveniles are found on sand or mud substrate and the adults predominantly on reef (Ref. 12200).  Spawns in the winter (Ref. 12199).  An important food fish.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Maigre d'Amoy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal waters over muddy bottoms.  Forms small schools.  Also caught with bottom trawls and hand lines.  Marketed fresh and dried salted; swim bladder dried (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Mailed butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relatively common on exposed seaward reefs; occasionally on shallow lagoon reefs in areas of rich coral growth and clear water.  Juveniles in protected coral areas (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  In pairs in Indonesia but schools in some Pacific locations (Ref. 48636).  Often in pairs during breeding and feed mainly on scleractinian coral polyps.  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Mailleur
species.description: Adults are found mainly in rapidly flowing streams and rivers, preferring heavily vegetated  habitats (Ref. 26130).  They occur in warm springs and their effluents, weedy canals and ponds (Ref. 5723).  They feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Used for genetics research (Ref. 4537).  Especially the red varieties are very popular aquarium fishes (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping:  the males aggressive towards each other;  minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Mainland's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Associated with alpheid shrimp which burrows on shallow reef flats (Ref. 26168, 58302).

species.name: Majan croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Majestic shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits silty-sand bottoms in sheltered waters, singly or in male/female pairs. Shares the same burrows with unidentified species of Alpheus, a snapping shrimp (Ref. 75784).

species.name: Makaire bec fin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Further study is strongly needed to clarify the validity of this species.  Probably oceanic.  Length has been transferred from 'Body length' to FL (* 0.15).

species.name: Makaire noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, usually found in surface waters above the thermocline, often near shore close to land masses, islands and coral reefs.  Feed on fishes, squids, cuttlefishes, octopods, large decapod crustaceans and mostly on small tunas when abundant (Ref. 9668).  The flesh is of good quality; marketed refrigerated or frozen and prepared as sashimi in Japan (Ref. 9308).  Also Ref. 9692.

species.name: Makaire à rostre court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and epipelagic, found above the thermocline (Ref. 9308).  Feeds on fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans.  Also caught as a by-catch of long lines with hooks intended for tuna.  Marketed frozen and prepared as fish cakes and sashimi in Japan (Ref. 9308).  Also prepared as sausages.

species.name: Makira Rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Tributaries harbouring this species are generally shallow, clear, and cool, with a moderate rate of flow, and low turbidity; the substrate ranges from rocky (small rock to large boulders) to somewhat sandy (Ref. 84245).

species.name: Mako à longues nageoires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species that probably approaches land to give birth (Ref. 13574, 58302).  Epipelagic (Ref. 58302).  Presumably feeds on schooling fishes and pelagic cephalopods (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous, embryos feeding on yolk sac and other ova produced by the mother (Ref. 50449).  With 2 pups in a litter (Ref. 247).  Potentially dangerous because of its large size and big teeth (Ref. 13574).  Utilized fresh, frozen, and dried or salted for human consumption (Ref. 247); meat (lower quality), fins (high value in adults), jaws (highly prized), skin and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Makunaima guaporensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Makunaima guianensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear water streams, running over sand and silt bottoms. Inhabits slow to moderate water current, less than 1m deep. Feeds on aquatic insects (caddisflies larvae, chironomids pupae and Odonata nymph) and arthropods (Ref. 100733).

species.name: Makunaima multidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malabar black-backed barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malabar danio
species.description: Found in a variety of habitats from boulder-strewn mountain torrents to small pools in dry zone streams.  Most common in flowing water than in reservoirs and tanks.  Forms medium sized shoals and prefers flowing water.  Feeds on terrestrial insects and detritus.  Spawns in shallow water, among marginal weeds and roots usually after heavy rains.  Eggs are light orange and sticky; more than 200 eggs are laid and hatch in 1-2 days.  Fry are free-swimming on fifth day.  Exhibits cannibalism on eggs (Ref. 6028). Rarely reaches 12 cm (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Malabar leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear and rapid streams.

species.name: Malabar mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malabar pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches less than 2.5 cm TL.  Probably one of the endangered species.  Maximum length of 15 cm TL in Ref. 13614 is erroneous; length needs better source (RF).

species.name: Malabar ricefish
species.description: Found in estuaries, but can live temporarily in freshwater.  Inhabits quiet rocks and corners of creeks and backwaters.  Can withstand a wide range of salinity varying from 4.36 to 1.35%  (Ref. 48443).  Breeds easily throughout the year peak period during July and August.  Larvicidal fish and eats mosquito larvae at the early instar stages.  A suitable fish in malaria infected areas (Ref. 48443).

species.name: Malabar snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malabar spinyeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pools and running waters.

species.name: Malabar swampeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in marshy areas, paddy fields, ditches and ponds (Ref. 41236).  Burrows in the bottom of ditches and pools (Ref. 4833).  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Malacanthe bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outer reef slopes, hovering above the bottom.  They swim often high above the substrate to pick prey from the substrate with their excellent eyesight (Ref. 48635).  Tends to swim away from its pursuer rather than enter its burrow (Ref. 1602).  Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 9710), adults form monogamous pairs (Ref. 37816). Maximum depth from Ref. 027115.

species.name: Malachigan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in bottoms of medium to large rivers and lakes (Ref. 557, 10294). Adults feed on aquatic insect immatures such as mayflies (Hexagenia), amphipods, fish (especially shad and young drum), crayfish and mollusks. Larval stages of drum consume larvae of other fishes, while young fishes utilize zooplankton (Ref. 10294). Known to produce sound. L-shaped otoliths are collected as 'lucky stones' (Ref. 557). Utilized fresh and can be pan-fried and broiled (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Malacho
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide range of salinities; mature adults and early-life history stages in offshore marine habitats and where spawning is presumed to occur; and transforming larvae and subadults in estuaries, as far up as the oligohaline zone, as well as hypersaline lagoons (Ref. 83481).

species.name: Malacocephalus boretzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacocephalus luzonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacocephalus nipponensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacocephalus okamurai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacocottus gibber
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacoctenus africanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters with rocky substrate (Ref. 7404), both during the spawning season and outside of it; it is less cryptic than Malacoctenus carrowi (Ref. 98055).

species.name: Malacoctenus carrowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected using anaesthetic (quinaldine or clove) oil sprayed into horizontal cracks in rock faces or below large stones at about  10-13 m depth. Additional animals were seen when overturning big stones at 10-16 m and one individual was photographed at night, resting on open rock in water only 3 m deep (Ref. 98055).

species.name: Malacoctenus costaricanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacoctenus erdmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surfaces of rocks, in depressions, and among clumps of algae, among broken coral debris and rocks in only a few feet of water (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Malacoctenus mexicanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacoctenus polyporosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacoctenus sudensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacoglanis gelatinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malacosarcus macrostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults probably bathypelagic or abyssal benthic (Ref. 51654).

species.name: Malagarasi sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and might become important in dams (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Malagarasi tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and swamps (Ref. 4967). It feeds on the soft, flocculent bottom deposits, which consisted of finely divided plant material and many protozoa, bacteria, algae and detritus (Ref. 2, 52307); the young were feeding on fish offal near canoe-landings (Ref. 2). A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 118638). A locally important species in artisanal fisheries (Ref. 118638); it contributes to swamp fishery (Ref. 4967). Recorded from aquaculture ponds near Kigoma (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Malagasy blue-spotted guitarfish
species.description: Occurs in shallow coastal waters to at least 80 m. All juvenile specimeans ranging in size from 17.7 - 60.3 cm TL, the size at birth ca. 18 cm TL and based on unretained specimens, this species grows to more than 100 cm TL (Ref. 124452).

species.name: Malagasy skinny spurdog
species.description:
A mesopelagic species, where its distribution indicates that it is a warmer-water species
associated with the Mozambique and Agulhas currents (Ref. 116247).

species.name: Malakichthys barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malakichthys griseus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malakichthys similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malakichthys wakiyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes, among others (Ref. 559).  Caught in depths of less than 150 m (Ref. 637).

species.name: Malapterurus barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus cavalliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing it known about its biology (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Malapterurus leonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus melanochir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus minjiyria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Largest specimen encountered in museum collections was 320mm SL; Sagua (1987) reported sizes up to 510 mm SL (Ref. 57130).

species.name: Malapterurus monsembeensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female reaches up to 42.0 SL; carnivorous, feeding on fishes, crabs, and other aquatic creatures (Ref. 44050).

species.name: Malapterurus occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus oguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An upland species, generally not found in lowland habitats, where it appears to be replaced by M. beninensis (Ref. 81645).

species.name: Malapterurus punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus shirensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus stiassnyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus tanganyikaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Limnetic electric catfish (Ref. 44050). Voracious piscivore (Ref. 36901, 44050, 78218) feeding on cichlids (Ref. 36901, 44050). Encountered in the littoral zone down to a depth of 50 m; especially common in bays or near the mouths of rivers (Ref. 36901).

species.name: Malapterurus tanoensis
