species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female reaches up to 20.4 SL; nothing reported on the biology or natural history of this species (Ref. 44050).

species.name: Malapterurus teugelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterurus thysi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malapterus reticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is known to be cleaners of Scorpis individuals, feeding of buccal isopod ectoparasites (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Malarmat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from 50-600 m (Ref. 10780) and from 288-848 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Gregarious.  Occurs on muddy or rocky bottoms of the shelf.  Digs the mud with its rostrum, searching for prey; stands and walks on the bottom with its free pectoral rays.  After a pelagic existence, the juveniles live in coastal waters before migrating to deeper waters (Ref. 6556).  Minimum depth range taken from Ref. 27000.

species.name: Malawi eyebiter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in vegetated areas in shallow water.  Feeds on small fishes, mainly juvenile Utaka or other shoaling species (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Malawi spinyeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in shallow water on rocky areas and over sandy bottoms.  Probably feeds on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Malawi squeaker
species.description: Poisson. Found among the rocks during the day and moves around the area at night.  Feeds on insects, crustaceans and other invertebrates (Ref. 5595).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Because of its bony head, this species is often not marketed in Malawi where it is relatively common and considered a favored food of fishermen.  Marketed in Kyela (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Malawi thick lip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore rocky areas all round the lake, where it feeds on insects (Ref. 267).

species.name: Malay combtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in primary peat.  Bubble nest builder species (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Malay glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits river and lowland stream in peat adjacent areas (Ref. 57235) and flooded forest (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on insects (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Malayan deepsea boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Malayan eel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on crustaceans.  Eggs with cruciform hooks on the surface. Inhabits coral reefs among crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Malayan flying barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malayan lanternfish
species.description: Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066, 75154).  Found in the upper 85 m at night.

species.name: Malayan leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow or standing waters, among bushes of shore vegetation (Ref. 27732).  Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers and flooded fields (Ref. 12975), lakes, ponds and swamps (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on filamentous algae, submerged land plants, fruits and seeds with some aquatic insects and crustaceans (Ref. 12693).  Undertakes lateral migrations from the Mekong River to the floodplains during the flood season and back again at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770).

species.name: Malayan silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species  collected from a  shallow seagrass bed at approximately 1.5 m depth (Ref. 39283).

species.name: Malayochela maassi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest creeks without current, swamps forest and vegetation along river banks (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Malaysian deepsea herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maldague robuste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary (Ref. 5213).  Found on deeper coral and rocky reefs.  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 5374).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Maldives Slopefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth of capture, 218 m, is available for only one collection.

species.name: Maldives sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Malenesian blue devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in sheltered seaward coral reefs and lagoons (Ref. 31117), in aggregations within Acropora sp. and Seriatopora histrix (Ref. 41819). Presumably feeding on zooplankton (Ref. 31117). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Malihkaia aligera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast riffles over gravel and cobble at about 60 cm depth. Syntopic with Bangana sp., Garra sp. (Cyprinidae), Psilorhynchus brachyrhynchus (Psilorhynchidae), Homalopteroides rupicola (Balitoridae), Acanthocobitis sp., Schistura malaisei, S. nubigena, S. sikmaiensis (Nemacheilidae), Batasio procerus (Bagridae), Amblyceps murraystuarti (Amblycipitidae), Pseudecheneis brachyurus (Sisoridae) and Mastacembelus armatus (Mastacembelidae). Stomach contents contained insects (Ref. 116725).

species.name: Malpelo barnacle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty barnacles and worm or mollusk tubes on rocky reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Maluti minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and riffles of clear streams.  Feeds on aquatic insects.  Breeds in summer, laying eggs in crevices and between cobbles and pebbles.  Juveniles form shoals in large pools and in side channels.  Adults are solitary or occur in small groups (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Mamfe killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mamila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy or sandy bottoms. Feeds on small fishes and larger benthic invertebrates. Most abundant species of Nemipterus in bottom trawl catches from the South China Sea.

species.name: Mamila arabe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, found in inshore waters usually on shallow sandy bottoms close to coral reefs (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms and fishes (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Mamila aurore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or mud bottoms in offshore waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  No major fishery exists.

species.name: Mamila dos noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found associated with reefs (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Mamila griffée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on coral reefs. Adults occur on most reef habitats, usually in pairs, and juveniles inshore or in lagoons or rubble zones (Ref. 48635). Occurs singly or in small aggregations. Feeds on small fishes and benthic invertebrates. A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 9785). Juvenile mimics poison-fanged blenny Miacanthus grammistes, Batesian mimic (Ref. 90102). Caught mainly by handline and live specimens captured by hand net for the aquarium export trade; no major fishery exists (Ref. 9785). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus hutsonae on the pectoral fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Mamila joues blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in inshore turbid or weedy waters, usually on sand or mud or rubble bottoms close to reefs, in depths to about 30 m (Ref. 92980), as well as offshore areas (Ref. 9785).  Seen solitary, but may school deep (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Mamila lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand or mud bottoms in offshore waters (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Mamila mignonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand or mud bottoms in offshore waters (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Mamila rosée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on  sand or mud bottoms in offshore waters (Ref. 30573, 48635).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Mamila Saint Pierre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters usually on coral reefs or sand or mud bottoms close to reefs (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, echinoderms and fishes (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Mamila à bande dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs close to reefs (Ref. 9785).  Adults at moderate depths in small, loose groups.  Juveniles solitary and in sheltered bays along reef edges with rubble or coarse sand (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Mamselle armée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species inhabiting shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9118).  Enters estuaries and river mouths (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Mamselle blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters over sandy and muddy bottoms.  Moves to the nursery and feeding areas in estuaries during summer months and sometimes enters freshwaters.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, worms and occasionally fishes.  Mostly used as bait.

species.name: Mamselle bleue
species.description: Mostly restricted to clear, sheltered, shore waters with luxuriant plant growth, usually from 3-10 m depth.  Adults feed mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Mamselle caimuire
species.description: Common over muddy and sandy bottoms in inshore waters.  Juveniles are also found in rocky areas.  Feeds mainly on shrimps.  Seldom marketed as a food fish; mostly used as bait (Ref. 3702).

species.name: Mamselle noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species found near the bottom, often in caves and crevices of exposed coasts and open bays (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on crabs (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Mamselle ronco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and river mouths (Ref. 9118).  Introduced into the Salton Sea, a warm, relatively shallow, and highly saline lake (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on fishes, small shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Mamselle rouio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, over muddy and sandy bottoms.  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Important food fish.

species.name: Mamselle épée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, estuaries and river mouths (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on crustacean larvae, small shrimps and fishes (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Manacled sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays, tide pools and among kelp (Ref. 2850).  Previously thought as rare species, but relatively common in some areas, especially kelp beds (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 6885).  Can cling to bottoms or pilings with its pectoral and pelvic fins (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Manaia pygmy pipehorse
species.description: This species is observed in mixed habitat on a vertical rock wall covered in encrusting coralline algae, bryozoans, sponges, solitary corals, and turf algae, which faced a rocky outcrop exposed to the open ocean. The rock wall was subject to moderate ocean swell as was evident from the accumulated debris of detached and decomposed algae on the sandy to rubble bottom of the channel at 17-18 m deep. The holotype was collected below the Ecklonia radiata kelp line and it was observed moving about in close proximity to another individual of the same species, which appeared to represent a male-female pair. (Ref. 125308).

species.name: Manamo anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large schools together with juvenile Anchovia surinamensis and slightly larger juvenile Lycengraulis batesii, which appear to feed on the Anchoviella. Mature by about 2 cm SL; a female of 2.5 cm had 157 large eggs in the ovary. This is evidently a progenetic species (adult at juvenile stage).

species.name: Manantial roundnose minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, sometimes runs, of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers.  Found among filamentous algae (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Manchurian gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Manchurian spiny loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mancilik dwarf loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mancoglosse antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit the lower continental shelves with surface-dwelling larvae and juveniles (Ref. 11892).

species.name: Mancopsette sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported at 1,186m (Ref. 57178).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mancuernas silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mandarin Pleco
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mandarinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow protected lagoons and inshore reefs (Ref. 1602, 48636).  Found on silty bottoms with coral and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Usually in small groups spread over small area (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413).  Well-known aquarium fish.  (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Mandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivore, feeds on insect larvae, mollusks and detritus (Ref. 13868).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Maximum size 325mm TL, 230mm SL (Ref. 57223).

species.name: Manduba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rivers in overgrown backwaters where the current is not too strong. Reported to be nocturnal. Feeds on fish and crustaceans. The flesh is esteemed for its very fine flavor. Frequently captured with nets, with males difficult to release from the nets because of its strong dorsal spine that is bordered with denticles (Ref. 27188).  During reproduction, the mandibular barbels and dorsal spine of the male change, and a copulatory organ appears at the anterior level of the anal fin.  Fertilization is internal, the female being capable of keeping the spermatozoids inserted in the epithelium of her genital tract (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Manducus greyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Manducus maderensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Exhibits diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4769); found between 400-800 m during the day and near the surface at night (Ref. 3991).

species.name: Maned blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the tidal zone, on very shallow reefs and in rock pools (Ref. 12484).  Feed on red and green seaweeds, hydrozoa, rock mussels and small crustaceans (Ref. 12484).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Suitable subject for nature study (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Maned cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy bottom at depths of 20-40 meters; usually deeper than its congeners (Ref. 51666).  Oviparous, eggs are guarded by the female parent (Ref. 58332).

species.name: Maned goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4343) and  in estuaries (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Manefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in midwaters in temperate latitudes.  Fish remains have been found in manefish stomachs (Ref. 4525).  From fry catches, it apparently reproduces in the subtropical zone (Ref. 95096).

species.name: Manetail snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken from great depths, rarely from shallow muddy bottoms.  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 637).

species.name: Mangalore houndshark
species.description: Occurs in outer continental shelf and upper slope, semi-pelagic (Ref. 114967).

species.name: Mangar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mangarinus waterousi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mangeur d'hommes
species.description: Found abundantly near the edge of continental and insular shelves, but also in the open sea and occasionally inshore (Ref. 244).  Often found in deepwater reefs and near insular slopes (Ref. 244).  Littoral and epipelagic, in the open sea or near the bottom at 18-500 m (Ref. 58302).  It is quick-moving and aggressive (Ref. 244).  Solitary (Ref. 26340); often associated with schools of tuna (Ref. 244).  Feeds mainly on fishes, but also squid, paper nautiluses, and pelagic crabs (Ref. 244; 37816).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Regarded as dangerous to humans (Ref. 9997).  Flesh utilized fresh and dried-salted for human consumption; its hide for leather; its fin for shark-fin soup; its liver for oil (Ref. 244).  2 to 14 young, 73 to 87 cm, are born per litter (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Mangeur d'hommes (Carcharhinus limbatus)
species.description: An inshore and offshore shark found on or adjacent to continental and insular shelves (Ref. 244).  Often off river mouths and estuaries, muddy bays, mangrove swamps, lagoons, and coral reef drop-offs (Ref. 244).  Bottom associated or pelagic (Ref. 58302).   Young common along beaches (Ref. 9710).  Active hunter in midwater (Ref. 5485).  Feeds mainly on pelagic and benthic fishes, also small sharks and rays, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 5578; 37816).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Produces litters of one to 10 young  (Ref. 26938, 1602).  Incriminated in very few attacks but dangerous when provoked (Ref. 244).  Often taken by shore anglers (Ref. 5485).  Used fresh for human consumption, hides for leather, liver for oil (Ref. 244).  Parthenogenesis has been observed in a captive female (Ref. 80664).

species.name: Mangeur d'hommes (Galeocerdo cuvier)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found near surface to depths of 140 m (Ref. 26938); in Tahiti from 0-350 m (Ref. 89972). Occurs on or adjacent to continental and insular shelves, frequenting river estuaries, off wharves and jetties in harbors, and in coral atolls and lagoons (Ref. 244). Bottom-associated, sometimes pelagic (Ref. 58302). Also off oceanic islands far from other islands and continental land masses (Ref. 244). Makes excursions in the open ocean, but is not a truly oceanic species (Ref. 244). Nocturnal feeder on other sharks, rays, bony fishes, marine mammals, tortoises, seabirds, sea snakes, squids, gastropods, crustaceans, detritus (Ref. 9997), also including toxic or armored fish species such as Lactoria cornuta or Diodon hystrix, porpoises, whales, sea turtles, cephalopods, domestic animals and humans (Ref. 37816). It also feeds on carrion and garbage, including cans, pieces of metal and burlap bags (Ref. 26938). Second only to Carcharodon carcharias in recorded attacks on humans with at least 27 documented attacks sourced to it . One specimen, reportedly taken off Indo-China, weighed 3,110 kg and measured 740 cm (Ref. 9987). May be kept in an aquaria, but does not last for more than a few months (Ref. 244). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Up to 80 young of 51 to 104 cm are born per litter (Ref. 1602). Valued for its meat, fins, hide and liver oil (Ref. 9997) and also for its jaws and cartilage (Ref. 58048). Often used for fishmeal (Ref. 9997). Utilized fresh, dried-salted, smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987). Species from the Persian Gulf and Oman Sea has a max size of 750 cm TL (Ref. 47613).

species.name: Mango angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species (Ref. 9710) found singly or in small groups in exposed outer reef slopes and occasionally in clear lagoon reefs.  Prefers areas of mixed dead and living corals with numerous shelter holes and passages (Ref. 1602).  Feeds mainly on benthic algae.  Forms harems of 3-7 individuals.  Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Mango tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been known to occur at 9°C; occasionally form schools; territorial (Ref. 2). Adults prefer open waters but juveniles and breeding adults are found inshore (Ref. 4999). Often associated with beds of submerged vegetation in Sudd lakes; feed on algae and fine organic debris; bi-parental mouthbrooder (Ref. 28714). Lacks marked sexual dichromatism when sexually active; forms temporary pair bonds (Ref. 81260). Maximum size recorded at 41.0 cm TL (Ref. 2756).

species.name: Mangrove blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on coastal waters, including mangroves and estuaries (Ref. 26340).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mangrove cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangroves and sheltered (often salty and brackish) coastal areas in 0-3 m depth (Ref. 90102).  Occurs in aggregations (Ref. 48635).  A nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Mangrove dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sand and mud bottoms from brackish mangrove areas to a depth of 15  m in coral reef lagoons (Ref. 1602, 48636).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Mangrove gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tidal creeks under high-storied red mangroves.  Vulnerable because of its highly specific habitat requirements.  Viviparous.

species.name: Mangrove goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow estuaries with freshwater run-off or lower reaches of rivers on mud banks.  Small groups were observed sitting on the bottom as tides were coming in, quickly diving into the mud when approached (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Mangrove molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mangrove whipray
species.description: Found in mangrove areas, also over sand or sand and rubble in lagoons near reefs to depth of 85 m on the continental shelf (Ref. 9840).  Feeds on small fishes, bottom dwelling crustaceans, and large infauna (Ref. 9840).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449), with histotrophy. Caught regularly, but in low numbers, by demersal tangle net and bottom trawl fisheries. Utilized for its meat, skin (high value) and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Mannar croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mannar jawfish
species.description: It is found in reefs, on living and dead coral, sand and rubble (Ref. 128946).

species.name: Mante aiguillat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, possibly in oceanic waters (Ref. 9911). Pelagic (Ref. 58302). Occurs singly or in groups (Ref. 9911). Feeds mainly on euphausiids (mainly Nictiphanes simplex), and to a lesser extent on copepods and crustacean larvae. May also feed on small fishes. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Acoustic tracks record the species to spend time above the thermocline at night to feed on krill (H. Dewar, pers.comm. 05/2000). Very common by-catch of the gillnet fisheries targeting skpjack tuna (Katsuwonus pelamis). Utilized for its gill filter plates (very high value), meat, cartilage and skin (Ref.58048).

species.name: Mante de Munk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic species forming schools in coastal and oceanic waters, but also found near the bottom.  Found singly, in small groups, or in schools (Ref. 12951).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans, but also takes small schooling fishes (Ref. 12951).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Gestation period unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Mante vampire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal and oceanic waters, but more common near the coast (Ref. 9256).  Found singly or in small groups (Ref. 12951).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 12951); mostly small shrimp-like animals (Ref.58048).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught occasionally in the tuna gillnet and in harpoon fisheries. Utilized for its gill filter plates (high value), meat, cartilage and skin (Ref.58048). Can leap out of the water.

species.name: Manus fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs, usually in sheltered inshore reefs (Ref. 41819); described as a gregarious species, with schools as large as 40-50 individuals, some retreating into crevices when disturbed (Ref. 123060),  Also in steep outer reef slope (Ref. 90102);  typically found in 25-55 m near vertical walls or caves (Ref. 123060). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Many spotted cory
species.description: Omnivorous.

species.name: Many-band sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in harbors and coastal waters (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Many-banded cardinal-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species which occurs inshore, over soft bottom (Ref. 7300). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Many-banded pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common among coral and in reef caves and crevices; usually found in pairs.  Nearly always seen swimming upside down against ceiling of caves (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Many-eyed snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand near coral reefs (Ref. 37816, 48635). Also found in rubble bottoms in 2-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Many-fingered grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and estuaries, but the extent of its movements into the sea or up rivers is not known.  Scarce in museum collections but this may not reflect its actual abundance.

species.name: Many-lined cardinalfish
species.description: Found in deep and shallow lagoons with coral heads (Ref. 8631). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Many-lined leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Many-lined pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species has been observed by SCUBA divers from 10 m to 25 m on the sandy bottom along the south coast of Amami-oshima Island of the Ryukyu Islands (Ref. 107899).  Feeds on corals, mollusks, and other sand-dwelling invertebrates (2935).

species.name: Many-lined sweetlips
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 47695).

species.name: Many-ray cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from near the surface to 55 meters in protected reef structures (Ref. 54832). Solitary inhabitant of reef crevices, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Many-spined butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit seaward reefs (Ref. 9710); apparently a deep dweller, collected and observed only on a small section of a well-developed coral reef ('The Bear', off Gannett Ridge, north side of Pitcairn); collected with spears and rotenone (Ref. 4858).  Feed on zooplankton.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Many-spotted lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy substrates in coastal bays to deep offshore (Ref. 48637).  Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Many-spotted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in shallow rubble lagoons with algae and seagrasses.  Often intertidal, and usually in only a few meters depth (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Many-toothed snake moray
species.description: Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthic at 1-15 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Manyara tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes (Ref. 4967); small bodied forms are present in Lake Eyasi, Lake Manyara and Lake Sulungali, while large bodied forms can be found in Lake Kitangiri and Lake Singida (Ref. 4967, 118638). It is microphagous (Ref. 54840). A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 2, 118638). Limited potential as an aquaculture species, it comprises a high proportion of the catch in lakes where it is found (Ref. 118638). IUCN conservation status is endangered, due to restricted distribution, drought and overfishing (Ref. 118638). There is some indication of hybridization with Oreochromis niloticus and O. esculentus (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Manyas shemaya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Manyas spirlin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear fast running water with cobble and pebble substrates. Collected together with Capoeta tinca, Barbus oligolepis, Squalius cii, Vimba vimba, Chondrostoma sp., Rhodeus amarus, Oxynoemacheilus sp. and Alburnus sp. (Ref. 91784).

species.name: Manyband goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in backwaters (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Manyline perch
species.description: A benthic species (Ref. 75154), generally taken from caves (Ref. 1602) with rotenone used for collection (Ref. 1602). Also a ledge dweller and secretive (Ref 90102).

species.name: Manylined grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen.

species.name: Manyscale Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gut material from a 5.85 cm specimen were found to be the remains of hemipteran insects (Ref. 84817).

species.name: Manyscaled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Manyscaled flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Manyspined ctenopoma
species.description: Occurs in vegetated riverine backwaters, floodplain lagoons, swamps and isolated pans (Ref. 52193). It feeds on any suitably small creature, including insects, shrimps, and small fish; well camouflaged; hunts by slowly stalking prey (Ref. 52193). May congregate in groups to breed; the eggs are scattered around and not guarded (Ref. 52193). Can endure warm stagnant waters and is known to leave the water and move overland to alternative sites in wet weather or at night (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Manyspotted flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in neritic surface waters.  Feeds on zooplankton and small fish (Ref. 9839).

species.name: Manystriped blowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore waters and offshore soft bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Highly toxic and is responsible for amputation of swimmers toes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Maori basslet
species.description: Occurs in elevated rocky habitat with ample cracks or holes into which the fish retreated upon approach of the submersible (Ref. 117905).

species.name: Maori chief
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles found in rock pools.  Feeds on squids, other invertebrates, and small fishes.

species.name: Maori wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal bays to offshore reefs, often in loose aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Map cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maquereau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in cold and temperate shelf areas, forms large schools near the surface.  They overwinter in deeper waters but move closer to shore in spring when water temperatures range between 11° and 14°C.  Mainly diurnal, it feeds on zooplankton and small fish.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769).  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  The species is traded fresh, frozen, smoked and canned.  Eaten fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Two stocks in north-east Atlantic:  North Sea (east) and British Isles (west).  North Sea stock decreased dramatically in the 1960's because of direct overfishing.  Recruitment has been poor and unstable.  After spawning, the adult feed very actively moving around in small shoals (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Maquereau (Scomberomorus cavalla)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in outer reef areas.  Larvae are encountered in surface waters of 26.3° to 31°C and 26.9 to 35 ppt.  Feeds primarily on fishes with smaller quantities of penaeid shrimps and squids.  Large schools have been found to migrate over considerable distances along the Atlantic US coast, water temperature permitting.  It is an important species for recreational, commercial, and artisanal fisheries throughout its range.  Most of the catch is processed into steaks or sold fresh, or sometimes canned and salted.  Also prepared smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Potentially ciguatoxic in certain areas (Ref. 9710).  Sometimes called "Kingfish" (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Maquereau blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults and juveniles feed mainly on zooplankton, with relative importance of larger organisms such as cephalopods, crustaceans and small pelagic fish increases with the size of individuals. Caught mostly in purse seine and pelagic trawl fisheries which target sardine and/or anchovy. Usually a by-catch but when availability of target species is low, this species provided an alternative income (Ref. 121850)

species.name: Maquereau bonite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm waters (Ref. 2683). Forms school close to the shore (Ref. 9987). Enters coastal lagoons and feeds on clupeids particularly Ethmalosa fimbriata. Reproduces in July to August (Ref. 5377). Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). Utilized fresh, dried-salted, smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Maquereau d'Atka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found at the demersal zone and near surface over reefs and hard bottoms from intertidal zone to about 2.360 ft (719.8 m).  It is preyed upon by other fishes, sea birds and marine mammals (Ref 114183).

species.name: Maquereau de l'Indo-Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal bays, harbors and deep lagoons, usually in some turbid plankton-rich waters. Form schools. Feed on phytoplankton (diatoms) and small zooplankton (cladocerans, ostracods, larval polychaetes, etc.) (Ref. 9684). Small groups were seen eating eggs of Cheilio inermis straight after spawning (Ref. 48637). Adult individuals feed on macroplankton such as larval shrimps and fish. Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). Generally marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried-salted, and smoked; also made into fish sauce (Ref. 9684).

species.name: Maquereau des îles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic, neritic species, occurring in waters where surface temperatures do not fall below 17°C. Forms schools of equally sized individuals. Feeds on the largest zooplankton organisms, thus complementing the planktonic food spectrum of the other two Rastrelliger species.

species.name: Maquereau tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 9340) and also in oceanic waters (Ref. 9563).  Minimum depth reported at 87 m (Ref. 58489); fishing depths to 265 m (cited in Ref. 58302).  Schooling by size which may include jack mackerels and Pacific sardines.  They are plankton feeders filtering copepods and other crustaceans, but adults also feed on small fish and squids.  Also caught with encircling nets (Ref. 9340).  Marketed fresh, dried-salted, smoked, canned and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Maquereau trapu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An epipelagic, neritic species that tolerates slightly reduced salinities in estuarine habitats and in areas where surface temperature range between 20° and 30°C. It forms schools of equally sized individuals.  Batch spawning is believed to extend from March through September. Feeds chiefly on microzooplankton with a high phytoplankton component.  Marketed fresh, frozen, canned, dried salted and smoked (Ref. 168, 9684).

species.name: Maracaibo river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers shallow muddy bottoms with turbid waters (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Maracaibo toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maraena whitefish
species.description: Forages along coasts. Also reported from deep, oligo-mesotrophic lakes. Feeds on benthic prey (crustaceans, molluscs, large insect larvae, small fish). Spawns in shallow water, in rapids or small rivers or over firm sediments in lowland rivers and estuaries. Northernmost stocks undertake the longest migrations between spawning and foraging grounds. In the northern part of the range, individuals may travel as much as 700 km between these areas (Ref. 59043). Growth parameters from Russia suggest a maximum age of 20 years (Ref. 56506) . Members of the genus Coregonus readily hybridise with other Coregonus species and populations (Ref. 89548).

species.name: Marasri's thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably marine, pelagic and coastal, but its very close similarity to T. aestuaria and T. brevicauda suggests that it may also enter estuaries. More data needed.

species.name: Maratecoara formosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seasonal lagoons in a typical savannah area (Ref. 57947).  Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Maratecoara gesmonei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maratecoara lacortei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seasonal swamps, lagoons and pools in typical savannah areas or transitional regions between savannah and forest (Ref. 57947).  Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Maratecoara splendida
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seasonal lagoon in a savannah region (Ref. 57947).

species.name: Marathon minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits springs, swamps, and canals.  Occurs usually among vegetation or under shore cover.  Feeds on a wide variety of aquatic invertebrates, algae and detritus.  Reaches up to about 6.5 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Maraval toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maravatío shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a spring that is highly degraded and used for recreation. The spring has growing aquatic plants of the genus Ceratophyllum and substrate composed mainly of sand and gravel with many boulders at athe bottom of the pool and mud in the stream. Other fish species found in the spring include the native goodeids Girardinichthys multiradiatus and Goodea atripinnis, and the introduced cichlid Oreochromis sp. and the poeciliids Poecilia reticulata and Heterandria bimaculata (Ref. 84762).

species.name: Marble goby
species.description: Found in rivers, swamps, reservoirs and canals.  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Feeds on small fishes, shrimps, aquatic insects, mollusks and crabs (Ref. 6459).  Considered a delicacy over much of eastern Asia.  Exported fishes command a high price (Ref. 12693).  Maybe the largest species of the goby-like fishes.

species.name: Marble knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marble-mouthed frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs in 1-10 m, resembles algal-covered rock (Ref 90102).

species.name: Marbled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds and coral reefs. May be found associated with the sponge Verongia fistularis (Ref. 13628). Sexual dimorphism in the shape of the head and dorsal fin (Ref. 5521). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Polygynous males guard the eggs which are spawned by several females in nests (Ref. 55842).

species.name: Marbled cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species.  Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300) over rocky bottoms (Ref. 1602).  Also found in outer reefs in mixed rich coral and algae rubble slopes (Ref. 48635). Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Marbled cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Marbled Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marbled dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft bottom among algae or seagrass (Ref. 111072).

species.name: Marbled eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marbled flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore over the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Max. length (Bernard Yau, pers. comm., 2000).

species.name: Marbled flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms in coastal areas (Ref. 9137, 11230). Carnivore, feeds mainly on polychaetes (Ref. 53305).

species.name: Marbled fortescue
species.description: Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Marbled freshwater whip ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and large rivers, often far upstream.  Usually found over sandy substrates where it feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Marbled headstander
species.description: Poisson. Adults feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).  Consumed locally (Ref. 42843).

species.name: Marbled lyretail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, swampy parts of brooks and small streams in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish. Bottom spawner, 1 month.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Marbled moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually on or near coral reefs in up to 30 m depth, but occasionally to 137 m.

species.name: Marbled mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic species; occurs in rivers and streams with moderate current and gradient (Ref. 51677). Mostly associated with upper drainages of rivers; in clear and well-oxygenated water (Ref. 27292). Generally associated with large rocks or mixed cobble and rock substrates (Ref. 51677). Carnivorous, feeds predominantly on benthic aquatic insects (Ref. 51677); insect larvae, worms and other invertebrates are taken (Ref. 27292). Iteroparous, with asynchronous ovarian development (Ref. 51677).

species.name: Marbled plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals over 10 cm SL feed primarily on mysids and to a lesser extent on isopods.  Fish below 10 cm SL feed almost exclusively on gammaridean amphipods (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Marbled reef-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in crevices in shallow water to 121 m (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Uncommon inhabitant of reef flats and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Marbled sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft-bottomed runs of clear, cold creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Marbled seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Marbled snailfish
species.description: Inhabits subtidal to 225 meters (Ref. 51661).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Marbled stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found above 100 m on sandy gravel bottom (Ref. 11230).  Lives on muddy substrates and rarely observed (Ref. 48636).  Hides in sandy bottoms and sucks up animals with sand and debris into the mouth.

species.name: Marbled stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over moderately soft bottoms, from less than a meter to 24 m deep.  Common in shrimp trawls (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Marbled swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anguilliform, has no pectoral and ventral fins; its dorsal and anal fins are vestigial (Ref. 27188).  Adults inhabit streams, ponds, canals, drains, rice fields, both clear and turbid water (Ref. 11225).  Nocturnal (Ref. 11225).  Carnivore (Ref. 26543). The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Its being a facultative air-breather (Ref. 1468) explains, at least in part, why it is often missing from faunal inventories.  At the start of the dry season when there's a decline in water level, it digs a tubular burrow in a bank or on the bottom.  This burrow, which is for the most part sub-horizontal , can have several diverticula, followed by a vertical section which leads to the exterior by only one opening.  Although breathing is slowed down, the fish remains active and flees if it is disturbed (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Marbled whipray
species.description: A freshwater species; may be found in estuaries (Ref. 9840).  Poorly known (Ref. 32457).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Marblefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits weedy reef slopes (Ref. 9002). Feeds on algae (mainly red, Ref. 86913), and the small invertebrates living amongst it.  A poor food fish with its flesh described as coarse with a rank flavor (Ref. 86913).

species.name: Marbré de la côte ouest
species.description: Found inshore over sandy bottoms.  Feeds on sand mussels, worms and crabs.  Protandrous (Ref. 4332), but some specimens with both male and female gonads well-developed at the same time (Ref. 3198).  Commonly fished between October and March (Ref. 36731).  A popular angling fish and an important food fish.

species.name: Marbré du Cap
species.description: Found over sandy substrate, in estuaries and oceanic waters.  Enters lagoons (Ref. 3198).  Feeds bottom invertebrates, including worms, crabs and shrimp (Ref. 27121).  Spawns in the sea but uses estuaries as nursery grounds.  Prime angling fish.  Important food fish.  Sold fresh and whole in markets.

species.name: Marcellino toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcelogobius janetarum
species.description: Collected exclusively from small caves and rock crevices with a specimen observed lurking out of a small cave before it was collected, whereas the other four known specimens were retrieved after spraying clove oil (a fish anesthetic) into rock crevices on vertical walls covered with the coral Tubastrea caboverdiana (Ref. 118256).

species.name: Marcia's anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Marcusenius abadii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius altisambesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius annamariae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to be entomophagous (Ref. 42492).

species.name: Marcusenius bentleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius brucii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius caudisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Water current was moderate to fast in sections of the rivers where Marcusenius caudisquamatus was collected (Ref. 95448).

species.name: Marcusenius cuangoanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius cyprinoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, lagoons, reservoirs and (irrigation) canals; a bottom feeding insectivore; breeds during the flood season and enters the floodplain for this purpose (Ref. 28714).  Shows three 'preferred' modes of intervals between electric organ discharges (inter-EOD) when at rest:  10-35 ms, 50-120 ms and 200-350 ms (Ref. 10833).

species.name: Marcusenius deboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius desertus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The riverbed where this species is found, is sandy or rocky, occasionally with steep cliffs bordering the river (Ref. 113652).

species.name: Marcusenius devosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius dundoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius elegans
species.description: Found in a series of stagnant pools; some pools were quite deep and inhabitated by hippos who could dive; the river banks were high and steep, and difficult to climb when wet, revealing high water and violent current at some times in the year (Ref. 93659).

species.name: Marcusenius friteli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius furcidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Females can produce as many as 9200 eggs (Ref. 10606).

species.name: Marcusenius fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius ghesquierei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius greshoffii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius kainjii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very rare (Ref. 3034). Caught along the shore of the lake (Ref. 13861).

species.name: Marcusenius kaninginii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water, ±1-2 m), near the shores; it has been collected at stations with low water velocity, near roots of vegetation or dead wood and at places with foliage-shade (Ref. 113607).

species.name: Marcusenius krameri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals of this species were found in groups; during the day they were commonly encountered below undercut river banks, especially in dense networks of tree roots or reed beds along the stream margins; places with shallow water and slow-flowing reaches of rivers and streams are especially attractive to them (Ref. 95448). Large numbers of small juveniles were found in bushes of aquatic reeds and floating grass on the periphery of the river or in side channels (Ref. 95448).

species.name: Marcusenius kutuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius leopoldianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius livingstonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet water in rivers; moves on to flood plains to breed (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Marcusenius lucombesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in aquatic weed beds, marginal vegetation and root-stocks of bank vegetation in headwater streams through to floodplain margins (Ref. 95448).

species.name: Marcusenius macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius mento
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius meronai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius ntemensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius nyasensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in swampy places with muddy bottom (Ref. 5595).  Lagoons and sheltered rivers and flood plains (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Marcusenius pongolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. During the day Marcusenius pongolensis is often encountered below undercut river banks, especially in dense network of tree roots; places where there is a countercurrent seem to be especially attractive; in Swaziland it has been observed high up in river systems with rapid water flow and rocky substrate in Swaziland (Ref. 75962).

species.name: Marcusenius rheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius sanagaensis
species.description: Espèce de poisson. Found in raceways with sandy bottoms of larger rivers (50-200 m), in the tree savannah and the more or less degraded semi-tropical forest.

species.name: Marcusenius schilthuisiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius senegalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius stanleyanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marcusenius thomasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: close to M. mento and M. furcidens.

species.name: Marcusenius ussheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: M. meronai. Relatively close to M. furcidens which is found in the same geographic setting in Côte d'Ivoire. A fractional spawner (Ref. 10605; 10606).

species.name: Marcusenius wamuinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the freshwaters near Banana up to Kindonda village, and in some smaller coastal rivers of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ref. 121662).

species.name: Mardi Gras wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over claystone, sponge, and coral substrata. Adults were observed in small schools along the reef crest mixed with Thalassoma bifasciatum, juvenile Bodianus rufus, and Chromis multilineata, while small juveniles ((12-18 mm TL) were observed in mixed schools with juvenile Clepticus parrae. It feeds mainly on calanoid copepods and other plankton. During courtship, terminal phase males: raise the dorsal 'flag' while approaching a female and keep the dorsal fin erect while in close proximity to her; primarily use pectoral ‘'labriform' propulsion for locomotion unless making rapid rushes at a female from a distance, in which case the caudal fin and body are used for rapid propulsion to pursue her; typically circles the female with dorsal fin flared, also periodically flaring the caudal lobes; and, were observed to nip the female on the fins. Agonistic interactions were also observed between males, approaching each other with flaring gill plates and jaws, and rapidly fanning their pectoral fins (Ref. 75768).

species.name: Mareike’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Margaret's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Margaretha's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Margarita blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Margay pencil catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rheophilic species which  dwells on limonite rocky bottom streamlet with pebbles and sand, and pools with muddy bottom and accumulated plant debris.  Crepuscular and nocturnal, it forages on the bottom and picks mostly benthic prey.  Feeds on immature aquatic insects (ephemeropterans, trichopterans, and plecopterans) with larger individuals preying on small tadpoles (Ref. 51380).

species.name: Marginate dascyllus
species.description: Adults are usually associated with the corals Stylophora pistillata, Stylophora wehisi, species of Acropora and Porites. Monogamous (Ref. 52884). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Margined anthias
species.description: Forms schools and found in outer slopes in 35-65 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Margined coralfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Usually solitary.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Margined dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water in areas of living hard and soft corals (Ref. 26137); sometimes in relatively silty areas (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Margined sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble and gravel riffles.

species.name: Margined tonguefish
species.description: Often found in deepwater soft mud substrates on outer continental shelf and upper continental slope (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Margrethia valentinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic, mesopelagic species.

species.name: Marguerite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow reefs and generally occurs singly or in pairs.  Feed mainly on zoantharians, polychaete worms, gorgonians and tunicates.  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Marg’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This 'twilight zone' species are restricted to deeper reefs in the 65-70 m depth range.  The species has been collected only from a single locality (despite extensive collections made) and this may be due to the very unusual microhabitat  which consisted of a very gradual reef slope to 70 m depth, exposed to strong upwelling from the nearby very deep (>1000 m) waters surrounding it.  Collected specimens were sheltering beneath the large barrel sponges that dominated the reefscape (Ref. 96671).

species.name: Maria's tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, rocky streams in deeper pools, usually in hilly or mountainous terrain.

species.name: Mariana snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was reported to be abundant at depths of ca. 7,000-8,000 m and video records showed large aggregations of different-sized individuals attracted to the bait (mackerel) and fed on swarms of amphipods. Smaller individuals were caught at greater depths and no individuals were seen at depths below 8,200 m, which is apparently the physiological depth limit for teleosts. Ripe females had eggs up to 9.4 mm in diameter, among the largest teleost eggs recorded; 0.4 mm smaller than the largest record. Eggs were unsorted within gonad, with the largest eggs free and interspersed within a matrix of smaller eggs. No developmental structures were visible within even the largest eggs. Two distinct size classes of eggs present with up to 23 large eggs (>5 mm) and up to 851 small eggs of less than half the diameter of the larger size class; rarely in intermediate stages. Individuals with only small eggs had maximum egg sizes ranging from 0.7 to 1.4 mm. Genital papilla is visible in freshly collected males, and is oriented anteriorly (Ref. 116641). . A self-powered robot that can dive into the ocean's deepest trench was largely inspired by the bones in the skull of P. swirae (Ref. 124589).

species.name: Marianas rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the intertidal zone of rocky shorelines (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Marico barb
species.description: Forage fish (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Marigane noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, ponds, sloughs, and backwaters and pools of streams (Ref. 1998, 10294).  Usually occurs among vegetation over mud or sand, most common in clear water (Ref. 86798).  Forms schools (Ref. 1998).  Feeds early in the morning, from midnight to 2 am (Ref. 1998).  Individuals up to 16 cm feed on planktonic crustaceans and free-swimming, nocturnal, and dipterous larvae; larger individuals feed on small fishes (Ref. 1998, 10294).  May be preyed upon by other fishes (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Marignan aile noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal reef flats and lagoon and seaward  reefs to depths of at least 20 m.  Found singly or in small groups in coral-rich areas (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps.  Large spine at the corner of preopercle is venomous.  It raises or flashes its distinctly marked dorsal fin to startle possible predator (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Marignan ardoisé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in subtidal reef flats, also in lagoon and seaward reefs below the surge zone to depths of at least 26 m.  Often occurs in large aggregations during the day in areas of rich foliaceous or cavernous coral growth (Ref. 30573).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on plankton such as crab larvae.  Caught at night (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Marignan cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaching at least  21.4 cm TL.

species.name: Marignan coq
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coral reefs, as well as deeper offshore waters (Ref. 3724).  A nocturnal species, hiding in deep crevices or under coral ledges during the day; at night it usually moves over sand and grass beds, taking mainly crabs and other small crustaceans (Ref. 3634).  Capable of producing sounds (Ref. 6537).  Spawning documented as far north as North Carolina in May (Ref. 27549). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3724).

species.name: Marignan de Panama
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hide under conspicuous rocks and small caves during the day.  Form small groups on rocky and occasionally soft substrates or near the surface at night.  Feed principally on crustaceans.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36626).  Appear occasionally in markets and marketed fresh.

species.name: Marignan jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marignan ombré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually inhabits coral-rich areas of drop-offs and steep channel slopes from below the effects of surge to over 25 m.  Occurs singly or in small groups, sometimes with other species (Ref. 9710, 48635).  A nocturnal species hiding in caves or beneath ledges by day, feeds on plankton such as crab larvae at night.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Marignan poklé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected waters at depths greater than 25 m, often in silty reef areas than well developed coral reefs with clear water (Ref. 12419). Tends to hide in caves or crevices during the day that capture by trawling was unexpected (Ref. 5378).  Usually seen in pairs, but occasionally schools in some oceanic locations (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Marignan rouge et argent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the most common of the squirrelfishes that occurs in outer reef areas, also encountered in lagoons and drop-offs from less than 2 to 40 m; either solitary or in groups (Ref. 27370).  Nocturnal, feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps.

species.name: Marignan rouget
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and shallow protected reefs, often in dead reef areas (Ref. 9710).  Secretive during the day (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Marignan soleil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hide in small caves or in crevices and cracks of rocks during the day.  At night, they feed on small crustaceans in the intertidal zone, less than 3 m in depth.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36626).  Appear only occasionally in markets where it is sold fresh.

species.name: Marignan violacé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons, channels, and semi-protected seaward reefs rich in corals. Relatively common near arborescent Acropora or layered Porites rus corals. Feeds on plankton such as crab larvae. Marketed fresh (Ref. 3418).

species.name: Marignon soldat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal (Ref. 37108), inhabits clear reefs (Ref. 5217).  Found near mouths of caves and holes (Ref. 26938); at night they usually move to sandy areas and grass beds to feed on crabs, shrimps, gastropods and brittle stars (Ref. 3724).  Marketed fresh but not popular as a food fish (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Marilyna darwinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marilyna pleurosticta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marine goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow estuaries on silty sand or mud, usually in burrows under rocks (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Marine gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs in coastal bays and estuaries, often in silty habitat (Ref. 9002).  Secretive (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Marine sailfin silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit mangrove swamps close inshore.  Nothing is known of its biology.  This species is too small to be of any commercial value but may be taken as food by young of commercial fish species (Ref. 9836).

species.name: Marini's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore down to at least 20 m deep (Ref. 189).  Presumably feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 189).  Eggs recorded off Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil in July and late August to early September, oval in shape and 0.94-1.02 by 0.68-0.83 mm (Ref. 189).

species.name: Marion's spiderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic at 692-1420 m (Ref. 58302).  Adults bathybenthic on continental slope and rise at temperatures generally warmer than 4°C while larvae are pelagic near the surface.  Feeds on mysids and decapods.  Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 3590).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Marjorie's hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in clear flowing streams where it is common along the vegetated margin.  Generally in shallow water over sandy or gravelly substrates.  A shoal-forming species.  Capable of multiple spawnings between September and January (with peak activity early in the season).  It has reproduced in captivity (Ref. 44894).  Feeds mostly on aquatic insects and their larvae, micro-crustaceans, algae and fish eggs (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Marjorie's Wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marked goby
species.description: Found in very shallow, muddy bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 13628).  Sometimes found in the intertidal zone (Ref. 13628).  Euryhaline species (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Markiana geayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Markiana nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marleyella maldivensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marmalade Razorfish
species.description: Inhabits areas with sandy bottoms (Ref. 5292) or rubble; juveniles often at less than 15 m depth, adults usually in deeper water (Ref. 86997).

species.name: Marmara barbel
species.description: Occurs in swift flowing water, with stone and pebble bottom and collected together with the following species: Alburnoides bipunctatus, Alburnus cf. carinatus, Barbus niluferensis, Rhodeus amarus, Squalius cii, Vimba vimba, Cobitis puncticulata, Cobitis fahirae, and Proterorhinus semilunaris (ref. 80049).

species.name: Marmara goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer small, low oxygenated and permanent waters with lots of vegetation (Ref. 86351).

species.name: Marmara sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms shoals at the water surface, feeding on pelagic crustaceans and cyprinid eggs (Ref. 12259).

species.name: Marmorated medaka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Marmorated zipper loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maroon clownfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoons and outer reef slopes. Feed primarily on planktonic copepods, a variety of algae, echiuroids, and sipunculoids. Diurnal species (Ref. 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Entacmaea quadricolor, Heteractis aurora, Heteractis crispa, and Stichodactyla mertensii (Ref. 5911). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Marquesan parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inner bays and outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Marquesan rockstripper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in surge-zone (Ref. 54980).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Marquesan sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic (Ref. 58302).  Forms schools in coastal waters.  Dominant species in beach seine hauls.  Used as tuna bait (Ref. 6822).  First reported case of clupeoid poisoning was in 1978 in the Hawaiian Is., probably caused by a planktonic dinoflagellate (Ref. 45133).

species.name: Marquesas butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky and sandy bottoms.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  In aquarium trade (Ref. 9210).

species.name: Marquesas dart
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The adult specimens were collected from the surf zone (Ref. 120856).

species.name: Marquesas ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marrero’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marsh killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in grassy backwaters and brackish bays, not along open beaches.  Also found in fresh water (Ref. 7251). Omnivorous and feeds on small fishes, insects, small crustaceans, plants, annelid worms and mollusks (Ref. 93252). Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Marsh knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in floodplains of large rivers, where it is frequently collected together with  <i>Rhamphichthys drepanium and <i>R. marmoratus.

species.name: Marshall Is. dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Solitary or in pairs under ledges or in caves (Ref 90102).

species.name: Marshall Islands moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral and rubble of shallow wave-washed reefs.

species.name: Marshall slopebrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marsha’s lanternshark
species.description: Occurs on sandy bottom. A 21.3 cm TL male was found to be maturing; birth size uncertain with 3 smallest individuals (9.7-11.6 cm TL) and the smallest with scar slightly open suggesting closeness to birth size (Ref. 119149).

species.name: Martenstyn's barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits unshaded, rocky, mid-hill streams (Ref. 11966). Larger individuals form small groups of 5-10 fish, inhabiting relatively deep (1-5 m) rock pools at the bottom of cascades, usually sheltering behind boulders in very swift flow. Juveniles occur mainly in the shallow (< 1 m) areas of larger streams with sand or gravel substrates. Sympatric with Labeo fisheri over its known range.

species.name: Martina’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Marukawichthys ambulator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep-water species.

species.name: Marukawichthys pacificus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Marvelous dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected between 0-700 m over bottom at 1,370-1,700 m (Ref. 42989).

species.name: Mary carp gudgeon
species.description: Maximum size based on type specimen (Ref. 128732).

species.name: Mary River cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mary's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently confined to outer reefs with vertical walls throughout the Palauan islands and is most abundant in caves and under overhangs between 20-30 m. It was collected from a huge cave (ca. 15 m wide, 4 m high) and surrounding area with sand/silt floor at 27 m, hydroids, some hard coral, sea fans, sponges and ascidians (Ref. 109919).

species.name: Maryland darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky riffles of creeks.

species.name: Masago snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish waters (Ref. 43239); in intertidal estuarine habitats and river mouths, mud flats and mangroves. A reported small species apparently spawned in May and August and fed mostly on copepods and amphipods. Associated with several Pseudogobius, especially Pseudogobius pocilosoma (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Masca
species.description: Occurs in sandy and muddy substrates. Apparently associated with Stromateus brasiliensis and Discopyge tschudii (Ref. 34015). Oviparous (Ref. 50449). Max length (Itamar Alves Martins, pers. comm., 2002).

species.name: Masca du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from close inshore and shallow bays to the slope (Ref. 5578). Feeds on small fish and a wide variety of invertebrates (Ref. 27121). Oviparous (Ref. 50449). Produces egg-cases that are spindle shaped, with broad horizontal flanges (Ref. 36731). This species is known to host on its gills monogenean parasites Callorhynchocotyle callorhynchi (Manter, 1955) (Hexabothriidae) and Callorhynchicola multitesticulatus Manter, 1955 (Chimaericolidae) on its gills (Ref. 124045, 124046). Sold commercially as 'silver trumpeter' (Ref. 3180) and considered a delicacy in southern Africa (Ref. 27121). Minimum depth reported from Ref. 7403.

species.name: Masca laboureur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on continental shelves to depths of at least 200 m (Ref. 6871).  Migrates into large estuaries and inshore bays in the spring to breed (Ref. 6871).  Feeds mainly on shellfish (Ref. 26346).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).  Flesh is of good eating quality.  Males have a small, club-like protuberance on the head and also long copulation organs near the pelvic fins (Ref. 557).

species.name: Mascarene goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Mascarene Red Seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mascarene sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mascarenichthys heemstrai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually observed in catches from the back reef lagoonal and tide pool environments and rare to nearly absent from the main and outer reef environments where Dinematichthys indicus is found (Ref. 76869).

species.name: Mascarenichthys microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mascarenichthys remotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mascota jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Masked angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic over rock and sand (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 122680.

species.name: Masked garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Masked goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools near large coral columns and heads.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35408).  Hovers above bottom in caves and shaded areas in reefs (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Masked greenling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Caught by anglers (Ref. 559).

species.name: Masked Hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Masked julie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rock-dwelling.  Usually solitary, territorial.  Feeds on microorganisms (Ref. 6770).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Masked pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which is found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Masked prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the littoral and sublittoral zones; apparently nocturnal and lives in rock crevices (Ref. 26664).

species.name: Masked puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich fringing reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Masked shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal sand slopes (Ref. 8631).  Found in mangroves and bays (Ref. 4833).  Found in coastal sand slopes and estuaries and usually at moderate depth of about 20 meters on deeper slopes (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Masked stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in soft sandy bottom, where it waits for prey, with only the eyes, nose and mouth protruding.

species.name: Masked stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Maskinongé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in clear vegetated lakes, quiet pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 205, 10294).  Solitary, lurking hunter on other fishes as well as on ducklings, muskrats, and snakes. Oviparous, spawn in spring as the ice melts (Ref. 205).

species.name: Masquerader hairy blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Massuti's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by beam trawl, on red algae beds in the circalittoral coarse sand bottoms from around 50 m to almost 80 m depth. There are mainly two type habitats: the Peyssonnelia beds, mainly located in the south west of Mallorca and south Menorca, and the maërl beds, mainly located in the Menorca Channel area. Visible from radiographed stomachs of specimens were uncrushed molluscs (bivalves and snails) (Ref. 114858).

species.name: Mastacembelus alboguttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus albomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, over rocky zones (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus apectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a complex rocky habitat, consisting of multiple layers of rock, at a depth of 3-7 m (Ref. 86808).

species.name: Mastacembelus aviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rock, sand, or mud (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus brachyrhinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus catchpolei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus crassus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids with rocky bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus cryptacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum reported total length 354mm (Ref. 57415, 81678).

species.name: Mastacembelus cunningtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in littoral zones with rocky, sandy or muddy bottoms (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus decorsei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus dienbienensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus ellipsifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters with sandy, rocky or muddy bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus flavidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus greshoffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over rocky bottoms in rivers and lakes, also in rapids (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus kakrimensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles of a small river with bottom consisted of rock boulders with aquatic vegetation (Ref. 55095).

species.name: Mastacembelus latens
