species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus liberiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL observed was 383mm (Ref. 57415).

species.name: Mastacembelus loennbergii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus micropectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters with rocky bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus moorii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits littoral zone.  A very secretive fish which hides between rocks or in the sediments (Ref. 4967). Piscivore (Ref. 52177).

species.name: Mastacembelus nigromarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum reported TL was 443mm (Ref. 57415).

species.name: Mastacembelus notophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus oatesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus ophidium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy shores.  A very secretive fish which hides between rocks or in the sediments (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Mastacembelus pantherinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus paucispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapids where the bottom is predominantly coarse sand (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus plagiostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters with a rocky bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus platysoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal regions with a rocky bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal in distribution; habitat is rocky bottom, flagstone, rock slides and pebbles (Ref. 56055).

species.name: Mastacembelus praensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus reygeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among rocks at depths from 0 to 10 m (Ref. 82667).

species.name: Mastacembelus robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected mostly from the rapids.  For specimens of the Lower Congo River basin (mainstream),  water temperature was recorded at a range of 24.7-29.0°C, air temperature at 23.3-30.0°C, D.O. 8.0 mg/l, and  pH 7.0-7.5   (Ref. 28147).

species.name: Mastacembelus sanagali
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow streams with a sandy bottom (Ref. 6060). Maximum reported total length 252 mm (Ref. 81678).

species.name: Mastacembelus seiteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow streams with sandy bottoms (Ref. 6060). Maximum reported total length 392 mm (Ref. 81678).

species.name: Mastacembelus sexdecimspinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All type specimens were caught in the region of the rapids characterized by a swift current of crystal clear water flowing over a predominantly rock, stone or gravel substrate with small areas of coarse yellow sand; however, this species is also found in a wide variety of habitats such as turbid, sandy lagoons with a sluggish flow of water, heavily shaded, rocky or pebbly, clear swift streams, and exposed, pot-holed bedrock pools (Ref. 81678). Maximum reported TL was 271mm (Ref. 57415, 81678).

species.name: Mastacembelus shiloangoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams (Ref. 52436). Maximum reported total length 151 mm (Ref. 81678).

species.name: Mastacembelus simbi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, marginal habitats among rocks and rock rubble close to rapids or fast flowing water. Appears to be sympatric with or at least in close proximity to, Mastacembelus brichardi, Mastacembelus brachyrhinus and Mastacembelus crassus in Lenga Lenga where the holotype and part of paratypes were collected. Also caught elsewhere with Mastacembelus congicus and Mastacembelus paucipinnis. A 6.12 cm SL female specimen had about 15-20, seemingly mature, ovarian eggs with a maximum size of about 1.0 mm diameter. The occurrence of these large eggs may indicate that reproductive activity occurs in July, the period when the specimens were collected. Sexually mature at about 6.0 cm SL (Ref. 84205).

species.name: Mastacembelus strigiventus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus taiaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum reported TL was 304mm (Ref. 57415).

species.name: Mastacembelus tanganicae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters with a rocky bottom (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Mastacembelus thacbaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus tinwini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus traversi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus triolobus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus trispinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus undulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastacembelus unicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in upland streams but also reported to occur in lakes during dry season (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Mastacembelus zebratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore waters.  A very secretive fish which hides between rocks or in the sediments (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Master's catfish
species.description: A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs over soft bottoms of inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Mastiglanis asopos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mastigopterus imperator
species.description: A rare species inhabiting the deep-sea floor in the tropical to temperate waters (Ref. 43943).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Masuda's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 76829).

species.name: Masuda’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf edges (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Masui's shrimp-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal to outer reef sand slopes to 40 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Specimens collected from sandy bottom at 35 m depth (Ref. 26157).

species.name: Matador triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mataeocephalus adustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mataeocephalus cristatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mataeocephalus hyostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Matajuel blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily a shallow-water benthic species found on sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 5246).  Builds mounds of rubble and shell fragments near reefs and grass beds; enters its mound head first when frightened (Ref. 5246).  Feeds mainly on stomatopods, fishes, polychaete worms, chitons, sea urchins, sea stars, amphipods and shrimps (Ref. 3644).  Tends to bite when handled (Ref. 5246).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5246).  Between 1995 and 2000, at least 7 specimens have been traded as aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Matajuel nez-court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits barren, open areas of outer reef slopes.  Occurs in pairs over rocks or sandy areas adjacent to reefs (Ref. 5213).  Usually lives in a burrow of their own construction, often under a surface rock on sand (Ref. 48635).  Has pelagic stage to at least 5 cm, hence smaller juveniles are not seen on the substrate (Ref. 48635).  Benthic and Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9119).

species.name: Matano medaka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Matcheek warbonnet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow subtidal rocky areas (Ref. 2850); on sandy bottom in rocky areas near shore at depths of 70 meters (Ref. 51666).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Matote noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found close to shore on hard-bottom habitats, occasionally entering brackish water.  Adult male territorial and active during the day to feed and rests in crevices at night.  Prefers temperatures above 10°C.  Spawning was noted in June-July in Canadian waters, but appears more protracted (April-July) in coastal waters of Virginia, USA.  Feeds mainly on mussels, gastropods, other mollusks and crustaceans.  This species has gained popularity as a prized food and sport fish (Ref. 6486, 4926, 41297).  Investigation on the diel and seasonal activity patterns of the adult tautog in its southern range were conducted using ultrasonic telemetry (Ref. 41297).

species.name: Matsubaraea fusiformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms along shore lines (Ref. 37438).  Abundant  around the low water line spring tide.  Caught by small beam trawl and push net at depths not exceeding 5 m deep.  Feeds mainly on mysids (Ref. 37434).

species.name: Matsuichthys aequipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Matsuno's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maude's shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits tide pools and mud flats of brackish to fresh waters (Ref. 37816).  Also found on rubble patches on coastal reef (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Maugean skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The total available habitat is less than 300 km2 and initial surveys suggest that the population is likely to be less than 1000 individuals (Treloar pers. comm.).

species.name: Maugé’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maul's searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maul's waryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559, 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mauligobius nigri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4343).  Although possibly entering estuaries, this species is more likely a benthic inhabitant (Ref. 57403, 79590) of marine intertidal zones (Ref. 27000, 57403, 79590).  Collected in shallow water among large lava-pebbles under strong wave action, and smaller examples came from a boundary area between rocks and sand at 2-4m depth (Ref. 39517). Maximum total length reported 8.7 cm (Ref. 57403).

species.name: Mauritanian shortface eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf on muddy substrates.  Feeds on small annelids, bivalves and crustaceans (Ref. 6721).

species.name: Mauritian damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs exposed to wave action (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mauritian gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs with little coral and found near crevices and holes (Ref. 9710).  They occur singly (Ref. 510).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mauritius dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maurolicus amethystinopunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maurolicus rudjakovi

species.name: Maurolicus stehmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species occurring over the continental slope at about 200 m depth, coming to near the surface at night.

species.name: Maurolicus walvisensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mauve goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral rubble and sand (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Mauvelip threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known about the habits of this species. Minimum depth from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Mawson's dragonfish
species.description: Specimens larger than 26 cm TL were breeding. Spawning seems to take place in autumn or early winter. Feeds mainly on benthic and benthopelagic organisms such as fishes (Trematomus spp.), the decapod Crangon antarcticus, mysids, gammarid amphipod and polychaete worms (Ref. 5192). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Maxillicosta reticulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found on sandy bottoms into which they dig backwards, sometimes with only the head in view (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Maxweber's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive, inner reefs (Ref. 48635); commonly collected from coral bottoms at less than 4 m, but has been collected as deep as 36 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Maya gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers.

species.name: Maya hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is often found among the mangrove roots that grow over shallow seagrass beds. The colors of H. maya and the tunicate, Clavelina puerto-secensis, (growing on mangrove roots) are quite similar and perhaps this hamlet has evolved camouflage coloration against this tunicate. It has also been observed on several occasions that this species attacks small silversides (Jenkinsia lamprotaenia) which form diurnal aggregations among the mangrove roots (Ref. 88139).

species.name: Maya needlefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Maya pupfish
species.description: Feeds on fishes (Ref. 99405).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Mayaheros aguadae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mayaheros zebra

species.name: Mayan tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mayland's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a small creek in hilly terrain at an elevation of 450 m (Ref. 2847).  An omnivore and egg laying species which is considered a peaceful community fish preferring the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=10, 26°C water temperature, rock, plant and driftwood cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Maylandia aurora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intermediate zones of Lake Malawi, being particularly common along the rock-sand interface; occasionally it occurs in purely rocky habitats which are close to sand; most numerous between 2 and 5 m depth (Ref. 6256). Territories are held by males, usually over the upper surfaces of medium-sized and large rocks, but a small proportion of males occupy less prominent sites and some defend areas at the base of rocks where they dig sand-scrape nests; females, juveniles and non-territorial adult males occur singly or in groups of up to 30 individuals (Ref. 6256).

species.name: Maylandia barlowi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sediment-rich areas.  Feeds from the sediment-rich biocover on rocks and also from plankton in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Maylandia benetos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia callainos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the lake (Ref. 12251).

species.name: Maylandia chrysomallos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia cyneusmarginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia emmiltos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia flavicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia flavifemina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in sand-rock interface over slabs, over pockets of sand among the rocks and occasionally over broken rock (Ref. 6256). Males are territorial and chase mainly conspecific males from their territories, with a territory normally consisting of a space between the rocks often with a sandy bottom; males at the bottom of the reef usually burrow from beneath a rock to create a spawning cave (Ref. 76849). Females are often solitary or sometimes occur in small groups, rarely numbering more than 3 individuals (Ref. 6256, 76849). Juveniles and non-territorial adult males occur singly, in pairs or in small groups of 3-8 fish (Ref. 6256). Feeds from the sedimentrich aufwuchs on the rocks from which it rakes diatoms and loose algal strands (Ref. 76849).

species.name: Maylandia glaucos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia hajomaylandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in the sediment-rich rocky biotope and is frequently occurs over sand in the intermediate habitat.  Feeds on plankton in the open water.  Remains close to rocks while foraging.  Territorial males feed from rock biocover (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Maylandia koningsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is a deep-water form and is usually found at depths greater than 15 m (Ref. 127491).

species.name: Maylandia lanisticola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is a facultative cleaner; it has been observed to feed on periphyton and to clean parasites from Lethrinops cf. lituris; additionally, it has been observed to clean parasites from Cyrtocara cf. fenestrata and Cyrtocara cf. picta (Ref. 36956). The host fish approaches the cleaner and positions itself with its dorsal fin oriented toward the cleaner, and permits the cleaner to remove ectoparasites from its fins and skin (Ref. 36956).

species.name: Maylandia lombardoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sediment-rich regions and is often found over sandy and muddy patches between rocks.  Abundant in waters > 10 m (Ref. 6256).  Feeds by brushing the loose algae from the rocks and also on plankton in open water (Ref. 5595).  Aggressive males exhibit territoriality over sand-dug nests.  Females, juveniles and non-territorial adult males occur singly or in small groups (Ref. 6256).  All males have only one eggspot on the anal fin (Ref. 47814).

species.name: Maylandia mbenjii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia midomo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia mossambica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia nigrodorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia nkhunguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia pambazuko
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia phaeos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia pulpican
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the intermediate zone; rocks and sandy habitats; between 4 and 30 m deep; males territorial; females are solitary or form small groups; feeds on aufwuchs and plankton in the water column (Ref. 58703). Spawning sites are holes in the sand beneath a rock (Ref. 79521).

species.name: Maylandia pyrsonotos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at rocky shores (Ref. 27596).

species.name: Maylandia sciasma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia tarakiki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia usisyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maylandia xanstomachus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the sediment-free rocky habitat, usually at exposed sites.  Feed from the biocover on the rocks by combing loose material from the aufwuchs (Ref. 5595).  Mouthbrooding by females (Ref. 53335).

species.name: Maylandia xanthos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Maynea puncta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from the intertidal zone and subtidal kelp beds to at least 101 m depth (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Mazarunia charadrica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in the entire upper Mazaruni River basin, and especially in tributaries with rocky substrates and rich in rapids.  Collected from black water sites with fairly high transparency (0.55-1.0 m Secchi depth), none to relatively fast currents (0-0.6 m/s), temperature (21.7- 24.5°C), pH (4.4-4.8), dissolved oxygen (5.2- 9.3 mg/L) and very low conductivity (<10 µS). Ref. 91746).

species.name: Mazarunia mazarunii
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Mazarunia pala
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in or near the main upper Mazaruni River channel in localities with sandy or slightly muddy substrates with structure formed by submerged or emerging grass and other
riparian vegetation and some drift wood.  Appears to move at night into shallow, flooded banks with terrestrial vegetation (Ref. 91746).

species.name: Mbam killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Mbipia lutea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits exclusively the shallow waters (0-2 m) of gently sloping small rock boulder shores, particularly surf protected habitats like small bays.  Adult males keep territories at 0.5 m depth under the roots of floating reed mats, but also in large and deep pools between the rock stacks.  Found over stone-sand mixed substrate.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae, but takes also insect larvae.

species.name: Mbipia mbipi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits various stony and rocky habitats, including stone-sand mixed substrates.  It is generally more abundant at gently sloping shores with small and medium sized rock boulders.  Females, non-territorial males and subadults are gregarious and forage in groups.  Feeds on a variety of food items such as diatoms, filamentous epilithic algae, detritus, insect larvae and Bryozoa.

species.name: Mbozi suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: McAdam's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive in reefs during the day and usually seen only at night (Ref. 48635).

species.name: McCosker's flasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes, over rubble, algae, or coral (Ref. 9710). Occurs in small groups of mix sexes but females outnumber males greatly (Ref. 48636).  Swim close to the bottom and females swim in small groups.  Males swim around them and often hurry from one area to another where there are groups of females.  Some juveniles are secretive and often single or small groups amongst the rubble (Ref. 48636).

species.name: McCosker’s grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: McCosker’s no-line scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimens were collected from a very steep rocky wall area with white sponges and stony corals, galathiid crabs, large ateleopodids (Guentherus altivela), morids, scorpionfish (Pontius), and catsharks at 515 m depth. It was observed to be solitary and not associated with other animals (Ref. 116601).

species.name: McCosker’s worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by bottom trawlers (Ref. 92296).

species.name: McCulloch's bandfish
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: McCulloch's hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: McCulloch's scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: McDowall’s Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. It is the only species  found within its restricted range. It is recorded from a cool, clear flowing, heavily shaded and shallow (0.5 m) freshwater river, 3-5 m wide, with a substrate of sand, silt and clay, and areas of cobble and pebble. The instream cover was provided by logs, branches and bank and vegetation overhang, and pools ranged from 1-2 m in depth. It was recorded at densities of 0.15-0.18 fish/m2  and was collected with the native species Shortfinned Eel and East Gippsland Spiny Crayfish (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Mcgrouther's coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: McGrouther’s flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: McGrouther’s ghost flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: McGrouther’s triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mchenga conophoros
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forages in the water column, feeding mainly on zooplankton.

species.name: Mchenga cyclicos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forages in the water column, feeding mainly on zooplankton (Ref. 27597).

species.name: Mchenga eucinostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore areas of the lake, where it is common over wave-washed sandy bottoms, and feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 267).  Parental care is provided by mouth-brooding females (Ref. 33611).

species.name: Mchenga inornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on plankton, and basied on the shape and the silvery coloration, probably lives over sand in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mchenga thinos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forages in the water column, feeding mainly on zooplankton (Ref. 27597).

species.name: McMillan's cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare and poorly known species inhabiting the lower continental slope (Ref. 26346).

species.name: McMillan's whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Meadia roseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Medialuna ancietae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mediterranean grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range is reported at 1000m-3000m.  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6187).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mediterranean spiderfish
species.description: Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 6688)

species.name: Medusa blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers shallow coral reefs or rocky bottoms around oceanic islands.

species.name: Medusablennius chani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Medusafish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near surface and to at least 91 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Young are abundant offshore, often among jellyfish (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Megacataetyx niki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Taken in a bottom trawl (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Megadontognathus cuyuniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megadontognathus kaitukaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus garmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus muyscorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Charles W. Olaya-Nieto, pers. comm., 2002).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus obtusidens
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit medium to large rivers accomplishing very long reproductive and feeding
migration in rivers of the Paraná basin (Ref. 93038).  They also occur in ponds.  Omnivorous (Ref. 79585).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus piavussu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus reinhardti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megaleporinus trifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Megalobrama elongata
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Megalobrama mantschuricus
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Usually does not occur in main channel of the river but in the system of auxiliary waters with aquatic vegetation and conditions suitable for feeding and reproduction (Ref. 51498).  Feeds principally on mollusks, but also takes filamentous algae, higher plants, crustaceans, insect larvae and small fish (Ref. 51498).

species.name: Megalobrama pellegrini
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Megalocentor echthrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalodoras guayoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalodoras uranoscopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups and occasionally forms schools. Inhabits rivers. Is mainly diurnal. Feeds on the fruits of Licania longipetala and Astrocaryum jauary. Also feeds on pulmonate snails (Ref. 9086).

species.name: Megalomycter teevani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment needs verification.  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Megalonema amaxanthum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalonema argentinum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches at least 27.1 cm SL (Ref. 36506).

species.name: Megalonema orixanthum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalonema pauciradiatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reaching at least 3.8 cm SL (Ref. 36506).

species.name: Megalonema platanum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalonema platycephalum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on beetle larvae,  fish scales and catfish spines (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Megalonema psammium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalonema xanthum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Megalonibea fusca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy-muddy bottoms of continental shelves (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Meganthias kingyo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Meiacanthus fraseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Meiacanthus kamoharai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on algae and zooplankton (Ref. 559).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Meiacanthus phaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Meiacanthus tongaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Meity’s pygmygoby
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Observed and collected from a nearshore reef which almost has no exposure to waves or
currents, on a silty sand and rubble slope (Ref. 118315).

species.name: Mekong blind sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuarine areas, including the high estuarine tidal zone.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Sold fresh, often in mixed catches in the Mekong delta (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Mekong delta dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The Song Hau Giang which is a branch of the Mekong River also known as the Bassac River is fairly clear, slow flowing (current about 0.2 ms-1) and wide (2 km) with a sand and silt bottom. This species has also been collected from brackish habitats and is the third species of Indo-Pacific callionymid known to inhabit freshwaters (the other species being Callionymus fluviatilis and T. tsukawakii) (Ref. 87929).

species.name: Mekong flying barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in ditches, canals and ponds often in areas with extensive growth of submerged aquatic plants (Ref. 12693).  Encountered mainly in stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals as well as in medium to large rivers of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds on zooplankton and insects.  Sometimes sold fresh and used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Mekong stingray
species.description: Obligate freshwater stingray that occurs over sandy substrate in large rivers.  Feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 32457).

species.name: Mekong tiger perch
species.description: Inhabits mainstreams and large tributaries (Ref. 58784).  Feeds on fishes and shrimps (Ref. 58784).

species.name: Mekongina bibarba
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mekongina erythrospila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapidly flowing water in medium and large-sized rivers (Ref. 12693). Inhabits slower deeper reaches during dry-season (Ref. 37769). Prefers rocky stretches with rapids and a fast-flowing current (Ref. 37770). Feeds on aquatic chlorophytes (Ref. 37769 ), periphyton and phytoplankton (Ref. 12693). Migrates in big schools, comprising several hundred fish, usually together with other cyprinids and loaches such Hypsibarbus spp., Scaphognathops spp., Cirrhinus siamensis and Botia modesta (Ref. 37770). Sold fresh, sometimes dried or salted (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Mekongina lancangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found syntopic with Bangana lippus (Fowler, 1936) during the early flood season, where both share similar body shape and size, as well as a black blotch on the base of the caudal fin. Mekongina lancangensis is readily distinguished from B. lippus in having a rostral cap split into 19-27 papillate lappets (vs. rostral cap smooth) and upper lip degenerated and is discontinuous from the lower lip (vs. upper lip developed, continuous with lower lip) (Ref. 79744).

species.name: Mekran blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Melamphaes contradictorius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gonadal maturity stage II-III for of  3.1 cm SL male (Ref. 117111).

species.name: Melamphaes ebelingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juvenile fish of this species were reported to be seined with closing fishing gear at depths of 290-1060 m, while  adults were seined at depths of 1483-1548 m.  It was suggested that unlike adults, juveniles perform vertical migrations (Ref. 90261).

species.name: Melamphaes eulepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled at depths below 200 m (Ref. 4241).

species.name: Melamphaes eurous
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes falsidicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens of this species were sampled by open-mouth nets at 2500-0 m depth range and by bottom trawls at 700-790 m (Ref. 87970).

species.name: Melamphaes indicus

species.name: Melamphaes janae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults can be found at depths below 200 meters; juveniles taken at depth of 150 meters (Ref. 51657).

species.name: Melamphaes kobylyanskyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes laeviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults trawled in 400 - 500 meters (Ref. 51657).

species.name: Melamphaes leprus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found at depths of 15 - 300 meters (Ref. 51657).  Specimens captured by bottom trawling at 1550 m depth; reported night catches of juveniles at 150-300 m  depth and more (Ref. 87970).

species.name: Melamphaes macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults caught below 400-500 meters; juveniles in shallower water (Ref. 51657).  Specimens were sampled by open-mouth nets at depth range of 1500-0 m; the minimal sampling depth was 62 m (individuals with SL = 12.7-13.3 mm) (Ref. 87970).

species.name: Melamphaes manifestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes nikolayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes occlusus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes papavereus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from one specimen caught in the Bay of Bengal with a nonclosing net at 0-1000 meters depth (Ref. 117121).

species.name: Melamphaes parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is caught by open-mouth nets at 4228-0 m, with original sampling done by closing-mouth nets at 1000 m (Ref. 87970).

species.name: Melamphaes proximus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gonadal maturity at stage III for males (5.05 cm SL) and stage IV for female (9.3 cm SL) (Ref. 117111).

species.name: Melamphaes pumilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melamphaes spinifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found below 400 - 500 meters; juveniles at depths of 100 - 200 meters (Ref. 51657).

species.name: Melamphaes succedaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gonadal maturity at stage IV for both male and female of  4.1 cm SL male (Ref. 117111).

species.name: Melamphaes typhlops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found at depths below 500 - 600 meters; juveniles below 50 meters (Ref. 51657).

species.name: Melamphaes xestoachidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanocetus eustalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanocetus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens captured by open nets fished at maximum depths of 1200-2000m (Ref. 86949).

species.name: Melanocetus polyactis

species.name: Melanocetus rossi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only specimen was collected at 390 m depth.

species.name: Melanocharacidium auroradiatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanocharacidium compressum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits, rivers with sand and mud bottom in turbid and green water.

species.name: Melanocharacidium depressum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapids over rocky areas.

species.name: Melanocharacidium dispilomma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper reaches of rivers.  Its  biotope consists of rapidly flowing creeks where the substrate is rocks and stones (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Melanocharacidium melanopteron
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanochromis baliodigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is typically found at intermediate depths over the rock-sand interface, in crevices and caves at depths around 20 meters (Ref. 26078). It appears to be an opportunistic feeder, eating smaller fish and catfish eggs (Ref. 26078).

species.name: Melanochromis chipokae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It prefers sandy patches among rock (Ref. 5595). In general, only solitary individuals are encountered, wandering through the intermediate habitat searching for larger invertebrates and, perhaps, small fishes (Ref. 89864). It may have suffered over-fishing by collectors of ornamental fishes because this species was rather common in the aquarium hobby more than 20 years ago (Ref. 89864).

species.name: Melanochromis dialeptos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky habitats and feeds primarily on loose attached algae (Ref. 26078).

species.name: Melanochromis heterochromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanochromis kaskazini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the intermediate habitat; not territorial; hunts larger invertebrates and small fishes; small foraging groups frequently seen (Ref. 80784).

species.name: Melanochromis lepidiadaptes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow intermediate zone.  Feeds in packs, primarily on the scales of other fishes (Ref. 26078).

species.name: Melanochromis loriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The preferred habitat is mostly rocky with little sand, and the majority of individuals occur at a depth ranging between 5 and 20 meters (Ref. 6307, 89864). It is an omnivore, feeding mainly from the Aufwuchs on rocks; in addition to algae also cichlid fry and catfish eggs are observed in the stomach contents (Ref. 89864).

species.name: Melanochromis melanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky substrates (Ref. 6307).

species.name: Melanochromis mossambiquensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gathers in foraging groups feeding from the aufwuchs of the small rocks of the intermediate habitat; territoriality is rare, but quarrels between males in breeding coloration occur (Ref. 80784).

species.name: Melanochromis mpoto
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Melanochromis mpoto is a non-specialized, non-territorial cichlid, which lives in rocky and intermediate habitats; often seen at depths of 20-40 m (Ref. 89864). It lives a predatory life but has also been seen feeding on plankton; larger specimens appear to be mainly opportunistic piscivores (Ref. 89864). Adults are usually solitary but quick to form small 'packs' of up to a dozen individuals when hunting opportunities arise; such packs can contain more than a single male in breeding colouration; these small packs move quickly through the habitat, apparently causing commotion among small prey fishes and invertebrates, and scavenging on anything that seems worth consuming (Ref. 89864). Mouthbrooding females are solitary and sometimes found in water shallower than 10 m (Ref. 89864).

species.name: Melanochromis robustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the very shallow, less than 5 m deep, rocky habitat at the islands of Chinyankwazi and Mumbo in Lake Malawi (Ref. 89864). It has an opportunistic feeding behaviour in which the species is attracted to visible particles floating in the water column rather than collecting food by systematically browsing from the rocky substrate (Ref. 89864). Males in breeding colouration energetically defend spawning sites, which are located inside caves and crevices between the rocks, against conspecific males; male territories have an estimated diameter of 2-3 meters (Ref. 89864). Mouthbrooding females remain solitary and stay close to the rocky substrate (Ref. 89864).

species.name: Melanochromis simulans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanochromis wochepa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, rocky habitat; mostly seen solitary; not uncommon; males do not defend territory, but displays between males are frequent and short of duration; feeds from aufwuchs on rocks from which it picks algal strands and diatoms (Ref. 80784).

species.name: Melanorivulus aithogrammus
species.description: It is found in rivers.  The largest specimens are 2.8 cm in males, and 1.75 cm in females, standard lengths (Ref. 128908).

species.name: Melanorivulus amambaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found in a small natural drainage, direct tributary of the Rio Amambaí, not deeper than 50 cm and with low flow in an area totally exposed to the sun, parallel to BR 487 highway. The region has a smoothly undulating terrain and the area of occurrence is at an altitude of 327 m a.s.l.. The drainage has a clayey substrate, which gives an orange water colour when disturbed. Only Gymnotus aff. carapo Linnaeus, 1758 was found co-occurring with this species (Ref. 119399).

species.name: Melanorivulus apiamici
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus atlanticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal plains (Ref. 101434).

species.name: Melanorivulus bororo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly in a shallow swamp, about 10-20 cm deep, within a forest (Ref. 76975).

species.name: Melanorivulus crixas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the shallowest parts of a small stream, about 10-20 cm deep, where the larger specimens are found in places with more dense aquatic vegetation and juveniles in places more exposed to sunlight. It is a typical stream of central Brazil, locally known as Vereda or Buritizal (i.e. streams dominated by the buriti-palm Mauritia flexuosa L.), with orange clay bottom, in open vegetation of the Brazilian Cerrado and water was clear, with pH 5.3 (Ref. 59346).

species.name: Melanorivulus cyanopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus dapazi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus decoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Melanorivulus egens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus faucireticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds with clear water, about 1.5 m deep, connected to shallow creeks of about 0.05 m deep (Ref. 75134).  Adults stay close to the surface of the ponds, near emerging aquatic plants while a few juveniles occur in shallow creek (Ref. 75134).

species.name: Melanorivulus giarettai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at the surface, close to amphibious vegetation at stream bank, with clear to slightly turbid water (Ref. 75625).

species.name: Melanorivulus illuminatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in interconnected pools, about 30 cm deep, with clear water (Ref. 78126).

species.name: Melanorivulus imperatrizensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus interruptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded in a typical Cerrado area, inserted into the urban area of Campo Grande town at an altitude of 594 m a.s.l.. It was found in a small first order creek, but was only captured in border areas with dense aquatic vegetation, mainly grasses. The biotope, which is locally called 'veredas', a freshwater ecosystem comprising streams bordered by the buriti-palm, typically found in the Cerrado Biome, has moderate current speed. However, the area where the species was recorded is formed by small backwaters, with a clayey substrate and with a maximum depth of 10 cm. This species is encountered in areas exposed to the sun as well as in areas shaded by trees, mainly buritis-palm (Mauritia flexuosa). The region also has a slightly undulating terrain and according to the classification of Koppen-Geiger has rainy summers and dry winters (Ref. 119399).

species.name: Melanorivulus ivinhemensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marginal areas of small first order streams and in wetlands completely exposed to the sun on a slightly undulating terrain at altitudes ranging from 267 to 315 m a.s.l. One of the wetlands was deep (about 70 cm of maximum depth), with muddy substratum and turbid water, while in the other localities wherein the species was recorded, the areas were shallow, not exceeding 20 cm depth, in crystalline waters with a clayey substrate. Eight species recorded to be co-occurring with were: Aphyocharax dentatus, Pyrrhulina australis, Hyphessobrycon anisitsi, Hyphessobrycon eques, Serrapinnus kriegi, Cichlasoma dimerus, Hoplerythrinus unitaeniatus and Moenkhausia sanctaefilomenae (Ref. 119399).

species.name: Melanorivulus javahe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the shallowest parts of small streams, about 10-20 cm deep, locally known as Veredas or Buritizais (the streams are dominated by the buriti-palm Mauritia flexuosa), with orange clay bottom, in open vegetation of the Brazilian Cerrado. During the collection of the type series, the water was clear, pH 5.8 (Ref. 59346).

species.name: Melanorivulus kayabi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow portions of streams and swamps, usually about 0.10-0.30 m deep, with clear water (Ref. 76937).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow pools and creeks adjacent to a stream which is about 10-20 cm deep; with orange clay bottom, in open vegetation of the Brazilian Cerrado and water was clear, pH 6.2 (Ref. 59346).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Melanorivulus schuncki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs generally near stream banks, in shallow places (5-50 cm) and sites where the water had high transparency. It usually inhabits lentic streams, but sometimes also near the bank of lotic streams, where the environment conditions resemble those of lentic water habitats. It was also found in the shallow parts of the Curiaú lake, a peculiar environment formed only during the rainy season (January to June) when Curiaú River overflows from its main channel. In the areas north of the Amazonas River, the streams were directly exposed to sunlight as they flow over a savanna vegetation region, characterized by the presence of the buriti palm Mauritia flexuosa, and the water was hyaline or slightly yellow; south of the Amazonas River, this species was always found close to the forest border, in lentic black water streams, with high water transparency. Both the northern and southern populations are often sympatric with the poeciliid Fluviphylax palikur, the cichlid Laetacara sp., juveniles of the erythrinid Hoplerythrinus uniteniatus and a great variety of lebiasinid species (Ref. 82137).
