species.name: Miner's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This cryptic species was only observed in close association with a particular species of tube sponge that is provisionally assigned to the genus Theonella. Using an underwater lightsource, the goby could be seen peering out from the darkened recesses of the exhalent pore of the sponge, but would quickly retreat deep into the canal structure. This behavior made it difficult to photograph in situ or to capture by hand, even with the use of anesthetic clove oil. The sponge was commonly observed on current-exposed walls and steep slopes in the 15-25 m depth range; a visual survey of approximately 200 individual sponges revealed only 10 of this new species (Ref. 121769).

species.name: Mini cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits lagoons and outer reefs in relatively clear water; usually with soft corals or gorgonian fans (Ref. 11893).  Forms small schools (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Mini-clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from only one specimen.

species.name: Mini-fin work eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal species found at depths of less than 3300 m.  A specimen collected with fully ripe eggs suggests that it is a small species (Ref. 96531).

species.name: Mini-molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Miniature snubnose goby
species.description: Inhabits coastal brackish lagoons, known from brackish lakes and salt pans. May co-occur with P. melanosticta (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Minigill snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A recent reference acknowledging the validity of this species is needed.

species.name: Minipizza batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the shelf and shelf edge (Ref. 11230).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Minkley's cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium conditions:  pH=8, H=50, 24°C water temperature, omnivore, egg layer, needs plant and rock cover, not easy to raise in tanks.  Feeds on snails and small fishes (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Minnow-nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to occur in fast flowing creeks and rivers (Ref. 26100).  Inhabits slow-flowing streams and lakes.  Abundant in lakes.  Can colonize still water bodies (shallow clay pits without gravel, sand, current, waves or tributaries.   Enters subterranean waters.  Spawns on submerged plants.  Threatened due to its retricted range, water abstraction and pollution.  Populations sharply declined in the 20th century because of habitat destruction and pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Minor clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools of benches and outer reef flats (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Minor scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 4313) that inhabits reef flats, in areas of mixed sand and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Venomous spines. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Minous andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Minous longimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Minous quincarinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the shelf edge on sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Minous usachevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Minute clingfish
species.description: An intertidal dweller, tiny and light pink in life (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Minute dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Minute flagfin dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Minute goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Minute leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from mixed sand-coral habitats.  Lives mainly on coastal reefs and most often found on outcrops of coral in sheltered sandy bays subject to moderate tidal currents (Ref. 48637).  Occurs singly or in groups among the branches of gorgonians, soft corals, or finely-branched fire corals (Ref. 37816, 48637).

species.name: Minute mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather that actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Minute triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in tide pools; in shallow water on beach rock, brown algae and coralline algae.  Apparently associated with coralline rocky shore or reef flat (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Minute wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in aggregations above outer reef slopes.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Minyclupeoides dentibranchialus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A gravid female was collected at 2.15 cm SL (Ref. 75047).

species.name: Minyichthys brachyrhinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Minyichthys inusitatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to favor depths greater than 30-40 m (Ref. 35628).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Miracle triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found  in coral reef areas, on reef slopes close to the outer reef (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Miraflores goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, silt, or mud bottoms of bays, estuaries and tidal creeks.

species.name: Miragoane gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mirina Molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mirogrex hulensis
species.description: A bottom feeder, its diet consisting partly of mollusks.  Spawned from February to April.

species.name: Mirror dory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in deeper trawling grounds of the continental shelf and slope, close to the sea bed (Ref. 559).  Caught by Japanese trawlers during winter (Ref. 559).  Excellent food fish.

species.name: Mirror shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, sandy, and muddy pools and backwaters of high-gradient creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Mirrorbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  The limits of its distribution are marked by the 10°C isotherm and the 34, 8 %o isohaline (Ref. 6542).

species.name: Miry's demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Misaki grenadier
species.description: Feeds primarily on euphausiids, prawns, and isopods (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Misaki worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow tide pools to a depth of 80 m (Ref. 104540).

species.name: Misgurnus buphoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Misgurnus mohoity
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Misgurnus multimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Misgurnus nikolskyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Misgurnus tonkinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Misol snake eel
species.description: A benthic and burrowing species that lives in coral rubble bottom (ecological information needed) (Ref. 127429).

species.name: Misool rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not very well known, however, 23 specimens were collected in 1948 from an island stream.

species.name: Mississippi silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually at surface of clear, quiet water over sand or gravel (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Mississippi silvery minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools and backwaters of low-gradient creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous, probably open substratum spawners like congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Missouri saddled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fast gravel and rubble riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Oviparous, spawn in batches (Ref. 58430).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Misspelled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mistaken pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with heavy cover of hard corals (Acropora, Pocillopora, Millepora, plate corals, lettuce corals star and cactus corals), variety of sponges, sea whips, ascidians, alcyonarians, tunicates, hydoids (in caves), soft corals, gorgonians, brown encrusting algae; and also on steep reef slopes and almost vertical walls with several large caves with sand/rubble floors, undercuts and small platforms (Ref. 116838).

species.name: Mitchell gudgeon
species.description: Inhabits still or slow-flowing waters, usually in rocky pools.  Occurs in streams.  Usually found close to submerged sandstone boulders, but occasionally seen hovering in mid-water (Ref. 44894).  Solitary, often hovering over submerged sandstone boulders, but sometimes forms loose aggregations in mid-water.  Males are more colorful and slightly larger than females.  Attractive species well suited for captivity, but is unknown to aquarists (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Mitchell’s Emperor
species.description: Found in an area consisting of a gully with volcanic black sand and rubble bottom, from the shoreline shallows to about 30 m depth on a relatively steep slope. About 10 individuals (size from about 10.0-20.0 cm SL) were observed around a large submerged tree trunk, lying horizontally across the gully in 20-25 m depth. When pursued with a spear, the fish retreated down the slope. Thus, it is possible that the species is normally found in deeper water, accounting for the lack of previous observations by us despite many hours of diving near the type locality over the past two decades, routinely to  depths of 40-50 m (Ref. 124781).

species.name: Mitotic stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known of its biology (Ref. 6871).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mitsukuri's sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools in shallow waters on sandy bottom, diving into the sand when threatened (Ref. 637). Probably taken by trawl net and handnet (Ref. 123825).

species.name: Miuroglanis platycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mixobrycon ribeiroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Miyake bigeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rocky bottom areas.

species.name: Mizola toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mnanzini nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moa gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moapa dace
species.description: Inhabits pools of Moapa River and feeder springs over gravel, sand and mud (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Mobile chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in larger, moderately clear to turbid rivers and the lowermost parts of their major tributaries below the Fall Line in the Mobile Bay basin. These areas have moderate to strong water current and bottom comprising of a combination of gravel, sand and silt. Inhabits sympatrically with Macrhybopsis etnieri (with no evidence of hybridization) over a 40-km section of middle Cahaba River in Fall Line area of Alabama (Ref. 116539).

species.name: Mobile logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mochizuki's seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mochokiella paynei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mochokus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mochokus niloticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mock blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky bottom with algal growth.  Forages on benthic and algae-dwelling crustaceans, mostly amphipods.  Males defend territories and probably tend harems.  Sexually dimorphic, red color on head and fore-body of males displayed during breeding season (Ref. 43466).

species.name: Mocosa ruff
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Modicus minimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coarse, mixed shell-bryozoan and brachiopod bottoms (Ref. 27099).

species.name: Modicus tangaroa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coarse bryozoan-shell bottoms (Ref. 27099).

species.name: Modoc sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow mud-bottomed pools of cool creeks (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Moema apurinan
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moema beucheyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality at the time of collection was composed of an elongated ephemeral pool measuring about 40 m long, 20 m wide, and 1.2 m deep, with brown water and dense aquatic vegetation.  Other fish fishes found were only annual fishes such as <i>Spectrolebias filamentosus and <i>Pterolebias longipinnis (Ref. 110333).

species.name: Moema funkneri
species.description: The type series were collected from an ephemeral pool measuring approximately 15 m long, 5 m wide, and 0.3 to 0.9 m deep, with dense aquatic vegetation, brown, turbid water with the following characteristics (measured on late morning): total dissolved solids: 112 ppm, pH 7.1-7.3, german hardness 5-9 dGH, temperature at the surface: 29.1°C. Another fish was present, Pterolebias longipinnis (Ref. 130493).

species.name: Moema hellneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length of Moema spp.: Males 17 cm TL; females considerably smaller (Ref. 89704).

species.name: Moema heterostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moema kenwoodi
species.description: All specimens were collected from a single small, shallow (about 5-8 cm deep) temporary pool, with leaf and mud substratum, and it is adjacent to and subject to seasonal inundation by a small stream. The water was dark brown with temperature approximately 24°C and with a pH of 6.8. Other fishes present were Apistogramma rubrolineata and Hoplosternum thoracatum (Ref. 130458).

species.name: Moema nudifrontata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moema ortegai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small temporary ponds fed by small streams that may dry up in the dry season. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 110392).

species.name: Moema pepotei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moema piriana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 8 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moema portugali
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 8 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moema quiii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length of Moema spp.: Males 17 cm TL; females considerably smaller (Ref. 89704).

species.name: Moema staecki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moenkhausia affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia agnesae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia andrica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia atahualpiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia aurantia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams and semi-lentic and lotic shallow areas (up to 0.8 m deep) with riparian vegetation composed by trees and shrubs.  The streams are characterized by transparent water, and bottom with rocks, stones, and sand in some stretches.  The main food items in the stomach contents of five specimens are Hymenoptera, Hirudinea, filamentous alga and digested vegetal organic matter (Ref. 96859).

species.name: Moenkhausia australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia barbouri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia bonita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in marginal backwaters with low current speeds (about 0.1 m/sec) in up to 1 meter depth.  Occurs primarily near the water surface, swimming in schools up to 10-30 individuals.  Stomach contents and observations indicate that this species feeds mainly on terrestrial insects (dipterans and coleopterans) from the surrounding riparian forest.  The insects are captured via surface picking and drift feeding (Ref. 51265).

species.name: Moenkhausia britskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia browni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia celibela
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia ceros
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia chlorophthalma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Discovered in small creeks near headwaters of rio Curuá, these portions are isolated by large waterfalls (Ref. 84462).

species.name: Moenkhausia chrysargyrea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant and very ubiquitous; found throughout the length of rivers (Ref. 12225).  Prefers slow moving waters of small creeks where the substrate can be very variable (sand, rocks, plant debris) (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Moenkhausia collettii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow flowing areas of the main stream, over muddy bottoms (Ref. 12225).  Considered gregarious and peaceful.  Its reproduction in captivity would have been carried out for the first time in 1988 (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Moenkhausia comma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia copei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia cosmops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its type locality is a clearwater, moderately fast flowing, large stream (4-5 m wide, 0.5 - 2 m deep), mainly with sandy bottom (Ref. 72399).  Except one specimen taken at the main channel of the stream, all specimens were collected at backwaters, near marginal macrophytes (Ref. 72399).  Forms large schools (>50 individuals) at the river bank, sheltered among dead, submerged saplings (Ref. 72399).  Insects (mainly ants), vegetal matter and algae are found in the stomach contents (Ref. 72399).

species.name: Moenkhausia costae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia cotinho
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia crisnejas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia dasalmas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams, occurs in semi-lentic and lotic shallow areas (up to 1.0 m deep) with riparian vegetation composed by trees and shrubs. The area of collection is around 800 m above sea level. The streams have transparent water; bottom with rocks, stones, and some stretches with sand; collected syntopically with Aspidoras albater, Astyanax sp., Characidium stigmosum, Corumbataia veadeiros, Hemigrammus tocantinsi, and Trichomycterus sp. Stomach contents (UFRGS 11194, 3:24.4-27.3 mm SL) were mainly composed by Hymenoptera, Coleoptera (adults) and some fish scales, but autochthonous insects and digested vegetal organic matter (seeds) were also found (Ref. 86678).

species.name: Moenkhausia diamantina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits blackwater rivers.  The type locality (rio Toalhas) of this species has a sandy and rocky bottom, with little riparian and submerged vegetation (Ref. 75036).

species.name: Moenkhausia diktyota
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia doceana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia dorsinuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in a typical white-water river with not too much current and vegetated, muddy banks.

species.name: Moenkhausia eigenmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia eurystaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia forestii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia gracilima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia grandisquamis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is typical of rapidly flowing waters, in cascades and creeks with sandy-rocky bottoms, where it is very abundant. Can also be found in calm waters. It can escape its predators by effecting dramatic leaps out of the water. It is a gregarious species which swims constantly near the surface of the water, on the look out for its food in the company of Bryconops melanurus (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Moenkhausia hasemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia heikoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia hemigrammoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers clear waters and counter current zones of the rapids and the creeks with a rocky bottom.  It is a gregarious species and its bright colors make it a potential aquarium species (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Moenkhausia hysterosticta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia icae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia inrai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in the principal rivers where it constitutes one of the dominant species.  May also occur in creeks (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Moenkhausia intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Can jump out of the water to escape predators.  Feeds on small crustaceans; otherwise omnivore.

species.name: Moenkhausia jamesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia justae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia lata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia latissima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia lepidura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 42843).

species.name: Moenkhausia levidorsa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia lopesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia loweae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia margitae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In slow-flowing or still waters over gravel or mud.1

species.name: Moenkhausia megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia melogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia metae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia miangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia mikia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia moisae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers creeks or zones with rapid current over sandy bottoms alternating with zones of slow water movement and silty bottoms (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Moenkhausia mutum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia naponis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia newtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia nigromarginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia orteguasae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia ovalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia pankilopteryx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia parecis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality of Moenkhausia parecis is a small small "terra-firme igarapé" (= highland creek) with little preserved riparian vegetation and surrounded by large plantation fields (mostly soy and corn), near Vilhena, Mato Grosso. This stream has 1.5-2.5 m width and and 0.3-0.8 m depth, clear water, swift currents, and a bottom composed of sand and dead leaves. M. parecis forms small groups of 10-15 individuals, swimming in midwater. It is syntopic with Ancistrus verecundus, Bryconops piracolina, Cetopsorhamdia sp. 3 (cf. Bockmann & Slobodian, 2013: 25), Corydoras sp., Hyphessobrycon lucenorum, Hyphessobrycon aff. melonostichos and Pyrrhulina sp. The stomach contents of four paratypes consisted of ants, scales, unidentified insect fragments, seeds, unidentified vegetal fragments and sediments (Ref. 109906).

species.name: Moenkhausia petymbuaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a waterfall pool (Ref. 56956).

species.name: Moenkhausia phaeonota
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia pirauba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in clear-water creeks and small tributaries of larger rivers, such as the Rio Culuene, Rio Curuá and Rio Teles Pires.  Usually found in shadowed pools between rapids with well-preserved riparian vegetation. Stomachs of 5 specimens from Tapajós and Xingu basins had a predominance of allochthonous items, adults of terrestrial insects (Coleoptera, Curculionidae; Hymenoptera, Formicidae; Diptera), insect aquatic larvae (Trichoptera, Ephemeroptera; Diptera, Chironomidae), fish remains (Characiformes) and plant fragments (Ref. 83482).

species.name: Moenkhausia plumbea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Discovered in small creeks near headwaters of rio Curuá, these portions are isolated by large waterfalls (Ref. 84462).

species.name: Moenkhausia pyrophthalma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia rubra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia schultzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia shideleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia simulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia surinamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in rapidly flowing waters, sympatric with Astyanax abramoides. The two are difficult to distinguish (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Moenkhausia tergimacula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia tridentata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moenkhausia xinguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moero lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swampy, shallow parts of lakes and river drainages (Ref. 3788, 47311).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Moffit's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Moga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lakes and rivers with slow to moderate currents, between 5 to 200 m elevation (Ref. 36880).  Juveniles feed on aquatic insects, while adults feed on bottom detritus, seeds and leaves.  Also naturally feed on snails and other mollusks, but will accept a variety of food in captivity (Ref. 44091).  Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Moggel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Closely resembles L. capensis in coloration and in having well developed anterior barbels. Survives temperatures below 10°C. Found mainly in standing waters, shallow dams and muddy shallow areas such as in large impoundments. Juveniles feed on small invertebrates while adults feed on detritus and mud. Valued as an important, nutritious food source and is recommended for use in wastewater aquaculture in combination with other aquatic organisms (Ref. 6465).

species.name: Mogurnda aiwasoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mogurnda arguni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively clear and slow-flowing Wahisewar stream, a tributary of Togarni River, with patchy aquatic vegetation.  Occurs syntopically in the stream with other fishes such as <i>Melanotaenia ammeri, <i>Pseudomugil sp., <i>Glossamia arguni and several gobiioid fishes including <i>Redigobius chrysosoma, <i>Mugilogobius mertoni, <i>Eleotris melanosoma, <i>Periophthalmus weberi, and <i>Oxyeleotris nullipora (Ref. 95614).

species.name: Mogurnda kaifayama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mogurnda kaimana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a small mountain lake, Lake Furnusu.  Most of its paratypes occurred adjacent to a rocky shore among aquatic vegetation and submerged <i>Pandanus roots.  Other fishes found in the lake are provisionally identified as <i>Neosilurus brevidorsalis (Plotosidae), <i>Craterocephalus sp. (Atherinidae), <i>Melanotaenia mairasi (Melanotaeniidae) , and <i>Oxyeleotris nullipora Eleotridae (Ref. 95614).

species.name: Mogurnda maccuneae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly observed around the mouth of the Soro river over beds of matted algae Nitella pseudoflabellata and the eel grass Valisneria natans. Specimens collected with the use of handnets while using SCUBA (Ref. 36923).

species.name: Mogurnda magna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common among aquatic plants and over rocky bottom along the shoreline of lakes Laamora and Aiwaso (Ref. 26385).

species.name: Mogurnda malsmithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mogurnda mbuta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mogurnda mosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is on the southern edge of Lake Kutubu near Gesege Village and consists of dense reeds.  The species was collected with handnet (Ref. 36923).

species.name: Mogurnda pardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common among aquatic plants and over rocky bottom near the shore (Ref. 026385).

species.name: Mogurnda wapoga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small, swampy pond on the floodplain with clear, still and very shallow water and with bottom composed of soft mud covered with leaf litter (Ref. 36751).

species.name: Mojarra de Bulha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mok's sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mola carplet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in ponds, canals, beels, slow-moving streams, nullahs and paddy fields (Ref. 41236).  Development of oocytes is asynchronous, are fractional spawners (Ref. 94282).

species.name: Mole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Molas are distinguished for their distinct morphological characters which include reduced/fused caudal elements, presence of a clavus in place of the caudal fin, absence of a swim bladder and a degenerate, cartilaginous skeleton (Ref. 86435). Adults are found on slopes adjacent to deep water where they come in for shelter and for seeking cleaner fishes. They are usually shy. However, they may become familiar with divers in some locations (Ref. 48637). Individuals often drift at the surface while lying on its side but can swim actively and are capable of directional movements otherwise (Ref. 86435). They swim upright and close to the surface. The dorsal fin often protrudes above the water. Females are larger than males (Ref. 86435). This species has been filmed in 480 m depth with the help of a camera equipped with baits (Lis Maclaren, pers. comm. 2005). Adults eat fishes, mollusks, zooplankton, jellyfish, crustaceans and brittle stars (Ref. 4925, 5951, 48637). A live colony of the cirripede Lepas anatifera were found attached to the anterior portion of the sunfish's esophagus that was stranded in the south coast of Terceira Island, Azores Archipelago in 2004. This association has apparent advantages for the goose barnacles such as a regular intake of food and protection both from hydrodynamic hazards and from predators: but for the sunfish, it is not clear whether it is neutral, of advantage or causes feeding problems since the attachment may obstruct the sunfish's esophagus (Ref. 55063). The sunfish is registered as the heaviest bony fish and as the one with the most eggs in the Guinness Book of World Records (Ref. 6472). Generally this species is not used as food fish; some people consider it as a delicacy (Ref. 30573). The fish can be utilized fresh and can be broiled (Ref. 9988). Some parts of the fish are used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Molas may contain the same toxin as puffers and porcupine fish (Ref. 13513). They do not adapt well in captivity (Ref. 12382, 37040). Juveniles are victims of California sea lions in Monterey Bay (Ref. 37040).

species.name: Mollase atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in midwater over the continental slope.  Mostly found from 365-550 m depth, but enters shallower water in the northern part of range (Ref. 7251); prefers salinity of 33.4-34.7 ppt. (Ref. 5951).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Feeds on foraminifera, copepods, and ostracods (Ref. 9731).

species.name: Mollers lantern shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably demersal (Ref. 31367) on upper continental slopes (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), size at birth about 15 cm (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Mollison's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Molliénésie á voilure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in still or gently flowing warm water of small creeks and drains (Ref. 44894).  Occurs in ponds, lakes, sloughs, and quiet, often vegetated, backwaters and pools of streams (Ref. 5723) and also in coastal waters (Ref. 7251).  Abundant in tidal ditches and brackish canals.  Feeds mainly on algae (Refs. 7251; 44091), also consumes animal material: rotifers, small crustaceans (such as copepods and ostracods) and aquatic insects (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects, plant  matter.  The black variety (Black molly) is a very popular aquarium fish and is marketed throughout the world (Ref. 1739).  In the aquarium it feeds on green algae and also readily accepts dried food (Ref. 1672).  Minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Molly (Poecilia vivipara)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Widespread in mildly brackish water in canals and drainage ditches at the edges of swamps, but rarely found in freshwater.  Feeds on mosquito larvae and has at times been used for control in ponds and reservoirs (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Molo snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Moltrecht's minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A medium sized fish that prefers shallow waters of sluggish streams or ponds with inflow water.  It usually hides between dense aquatic vegetation to avoid predation.   Feeds mainly on small aquatic invertebrates, any sizable floating organic fragments and surface-drifting terrestrial insects.  A common food fish.  Threatened by degradation of habitat (construction of hydroelectric power caused drastic diel fluctuation of water level (release and refilling of water) thus preventing growth of aquatic vegetation).  It can now be found only in several streams near its type locality and is diminishing progressively, unless measures are undertaken to rescue remaining populations and to restore their habitats (Ref. 84731)

species.name: Moluccan cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species.  Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300); usually in silty habitat on mud slopes, in lagoons, and sheltered reefs.  Usually seen in pairs or schooling, comprising numerous pairs when adult (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Moluccan moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive in coastal reefs and usually only seen out at night (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Moluccen cardinal
species.description: Nocturnal species which inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).  Most specimens were collected from deeper waters (Ref. 58519). In pairs or groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Mombasa pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (5-20 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Monarch damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon reefs in areas of scattered live coral thickets interspersed with open areas of sand and dead coral (Ref. 4966).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Mongo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only found at greater depths (Ref. 52307). Predatory (Ref. 81260). Probably an ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Mongolian grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in landlocked basins. Usually with T. arcticus, with which it possibly interbreeds (Ref. 593). Omnivore, occasionally predatory. In autumn and winter it forms large shoals at the entrance of rivers and streams into lakes (Ref. 41072).

species.name: Mongolian redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monkeyface prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common inshore, in tide pools or shallow rocky areas, from the intertidal zone to 24 m depth.  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and algae.  Breathes air (Ref. 31184) and can remain out of water for 15-35 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).  Demersal spawners in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Commonly caught by 'poke-poling', a method using a long bamboo pole with a very short wire leader and baited hook.  Good eating.

species.name: Monocentris neozelanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monochirus atlanticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This demersal species is found on sand and mud bottoms on the continental shelf (10-250 m), and also occurring frequently near plant growth. Common length between 10 and 15 cm SL. Taken in by bottom trawls and shore seines. Marketed fresh in some countries, rejected in others (Ref. 109259).

species.name: Monochirus trichodactylus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monochrome chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a steep drop-off near shore (Ref. 54758).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monocle coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in loose small groups in shallow waters 2-10 m deep, on steep gutters covered with algae (Ref. 90102).  They occur in  shallow waters, and are collected at depths less than 5 m. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Monodactylus kottelati
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in coastal seas (Ref. 42969).

species.name: Monognathus berteli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length measured from tip of snout to base of urostyle.

species.name: Monognathus bertini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens were caught in the water column far above the bottom (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus boehlkei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens were taken in closing nets, one between 2500 and 3500 m with a bottom depth of 4563 m and the other specimens between 10-3- m above the bottom with soundings from 2960-5430 m (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus bruuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype was captured with a ringnet, at a depth of about 4000 m (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus herringi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monognathus isaacsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monognathus jesperseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimen examined contained shrimps in its stomach (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus jesse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monognathus nigeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Four "Discovery" specimens were taken in closing nets between 1510 and 3910 m depth, three of these 1500-2000 m, and one 23 m above the bottom.  The "Vityaz" specimen was taken between 3000 m and the surface (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus ozawai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic, caught in an open ring trawl (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus rajui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monognathus rosenblatti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monognathus smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotypes and paratypes of M. smithi were caught in the water column in a closing net at 4200 and 5200 m, with a sounding at 5800 m (Ref. 34506).

species.name: Monognathus taningi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Monolene atrimana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monolene danae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monolene megalepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monolène asaedae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monolène d'Acapulco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 9281).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Monolène de Mertens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms.

species.name: Monolène du large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Monolène du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy, sandy, or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9281).  Marketed fresh and also utilized as fishmeal (Ref. 9281).

species.name: Monolène à petite bouche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 2683.

species.name: Monomitopus agassizii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus americanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus conjugator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus garmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus kumae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus magnus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Feed on euphausiid shrimps, gammarid amphipods, fish scales and a midwater myctophid (Ref. 31446).  Feeding probably takes place on or just above the bottom, utilizing both benthic and benthopelagic crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 31446).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus malispinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 1,865 m (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus metriostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Usually found on the continental shelf (Ref. 3686).  Oviparous (Ref. 3686).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 705 m (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus pallidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809). Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monomitopus torvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus bicolor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus dienbienensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus digressus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus eapeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in subterranean waters and wells.  A true cavernicolous form living in subterranean waters.  Enters wells through subterranean springs (Ref. 4833).  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus ichthyophoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monopterus luticolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found during attempts to collect caecilian amphibians; they were dug from moist to wet soil, usually inundated by the neighbouring water body; the sites were immediately adjacent to both lotic and lentic aquatic habitats (Ref. 116049).

species.name: Monopterus rongsaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by soil-digging searches with bladed hoes for fossorial caecilian amphibians; at a depth of ca. 40 cm in moist, rocky soil in a secondary forest, approximately 4 km trekking distance from Double Decker living roots bridge in Nongriat.  It  was unearthed  ca. 50 m from an unnamed stream with some ground vegetation (herbs and bushes) that was cleared before digging (Ref. 118582).

species.name: Monopterus roseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave-restricted species.  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Monostichodus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 11 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Monostichodus lootensi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 5.7 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Monostichodus mesmaekersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monotocheirodon drilos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monotocheirodon kontos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs sympatrically with Monotocheirodon drilos (Ref. 94699).

species.name: Monotocheirodon pearsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monsoon Fairy-wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected and observed in depths of about 18-37 m; the habitat appears to be localized to sloping rubble bottoms with scattered, low outcrops of rock or coral and occasional large coral outcrops (Ref. 112597).

species.name: Monster cardinal-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species which occurs over soft bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Monster shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected sand slopes (Ref. 37816). Lives in clear coastal and inner reefs on rubble flats and slopes (Ref. 48637). Found in burrows together with Alpheus bellulus. Depth range 10-30 (Ref 90102).

species.name: Montano's Rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal zone rocky shorelines (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Montanus tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Monte Bello seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154). Holotype caught at the surface, clinging to Sargassum fragment (Ref. 42735). Maximum length is based on a straight-line length measurement from upper surface (ignoring spines) of first trunk ring, to tip of tail (Ref. 42735). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Montecristo cichlid
species.description: Inhabits lower and middle reaches of rivers.

species.name: Monteiri's bulldog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mooi's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs in 0-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Moon dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy-muddy bottoms in offshore waters (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Moon fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in large rivers of the Sudan region (Ref. 7095).

species.name: Moon-spotted shrimp goby
species.description: Based on a photo taken from the Philippines, it is reasonable to assume that it is associated with burrows made and occupied by alphaeid shrimps (albeit no visible evidence of the shrimp in the image), as is the case in all it congeners for which information is available (Ref. 53948). Found in sand-rubble bottoms in 5-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Mooneye cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref.34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Moonlight gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds and swamps (Ref. 43281).  Occurs in shallow sluggish or standing water habitats with a lot of aquatic vegetation.  Common in the floodplain of the lower Mekong.  Feeds on zooplankton, crustaceans and aquatic insects (Ref. 12693).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Moonlighter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on offshore rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Juveniles found in estuaries, small protected coves in very shallow depths, large adults more in the open (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Moonstone Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually frequents deep reefs with some sponge and coral cover, reaching 86 m, although sometimes recorded at shallower depths of 25 m. Associates with species of the genera <>Sacura, Pseudanthias, Tosanoides and Pseudolabrus (Ref. 120429).

species.name: Mora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from the upper continental slope (Ref. 9563).  Occasionally found at 50 m.  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans, mollusks and other invertebrates as well as food of terrestrial origin, including garbage.  Probably a winter and early spring spawner (Ref .  4774). Minimum depth from Ref. 106682.

species.name: Morari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and ponds in plains and mountainous regions (Ref. 41236).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mordocet
species.description: A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612) found in shallow waters of rocky coasts.  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).   Mostly active at daytime during high tide.  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, especially gastropods, barnacles and amphipods, and algae (Ref. 31184).  Also, diet of crabs, polychaetes, isopods, copepods, limpets, mussels and small molluscs (Ref. 94105).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs measuring 1.5 mm (Ref. 35388) are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawning takes place in April - August (Ref. 35388).

species.name: More têtard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Highest catches at 235 m.  Females attain larger sizes than males.  Larger individuals of both sexes move into deeper water.  Utilized mainly for fishmeal; can be fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Moresby mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland streams and swamps and also occurs at elevation about 500 m.

species.name: Moreton Bay ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling species which occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Morid cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic or benthopelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  The species is the largest  in the family, an exceed 2 m in length (Ref. 31777).

species.name: Moride de vase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are often taken in or near scattering layer (Ref. 36399).  Food habits change from feeding near the bottom to picking plankton from pelagic waters (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36399).

species.name: Moride noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near bottom (Ref. 36399).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36399).

species.name: Moride péruvien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More information needed.

species.name: Moride à grande tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 9316).  Adults usually collected in midwater trawls and in the stomachs of deep-feeding predators (Ref. 31160).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36399).

species.name: Moringua abbreviata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Moringua macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy mud flats and river mouths (Ref. 47843).

species.name: Mormyre
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Ivindomyrus marchei)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Ivindomyrus opdenboschi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Marcusenius moorii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Mormyrops nigricans)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Mormyrops zanclirostris)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyre (Paramormyrops longicaudatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its preferred environment is large rivers, where it inhabits shallow regions with rapids (Ref. 81635).

species.name: Mormyre (Petrocephalus simus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head and on the ventral and dorsal regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located  (Ref. 10011).  Found schooling with other species having identical electric organ discharge (EOD) waveforms (Ref. 10460).  A fractional spawner (Ref. 10605, 10606). Entomophagous (Ref. 51193).

species.name: Mormyre (Stomatorhinus walkeri)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrids
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: look-alike of M. subundulatus and M. tapirus. Feeds on insects and larvae (Ref.13851). Generates electric organ discharge (EOD) of long duration that seems to correlate with territorial behavior of the species (Ref. 10460; 10601).

species.name: Mormyrops attenuatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops batesianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops breviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: morphologically similar to M. anguilloides (Ref. 2915).

species.name: Mormyrops caballus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: M. oudoti (Ref. 2915).

species.name: Mormyrops citernii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops curtus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops curviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops engystoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops furcidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops lineolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops mariae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops masuianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops microstoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops oudoti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: M. caballus (Ref. 2915).

species.name: Mormyrops parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrops sirenoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus caballus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus casalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus caschive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom feeding insectivore; feeds mainly on chironomid larvae (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Mormyrus cyaneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus felixi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus goheeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus iriodes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in most areas of the lakes and rivers from which it has been collected (Ref. 49805). Generalist feeder (Ref. 12526, 49805). Insectivorous as juvenile, adults eat Caridina, small fishes, and Povilla and Odonata larvae (Ref. 12526). Prawns, water weed and oligochaetes have also been found in the stomach (Ref. 49805). Mabybe spawns in rocky riverine habitats (Ref. 12526).

species.name: Mormyrus macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus niloticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus ovis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus subundulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus tapirus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: Mormyrus rume and Mormyrus subundulatus, Mormyrus tapirus with longer snout, longer anal fin and 10-15 scales on caudal peduncle.

species.name: Mormyrus thomasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mormyrus tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles were observed to live within várzea along the shores of the main river, whereas adults are inhabitants of main river channels (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Moro imberbe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often rather abundant on the upper slope (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Moro subantarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper slope.

species.name: Moro svelte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Food consists of free-living small animals, such as crustaceans and squids.  This species is reportedly being caught by trawl in temperate waters of Australia (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Moro trapu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental and insular slopes (Ref. 5208), as well as seamounts (Ref. 31160).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 5208.

species.name: Moro à nageoires noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Living from the inner shelf, in far southern South America, to depths beyond 1000 m.

species.name: Moroco
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Morrison's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in algal covered rocks of seaward reefs; rarely in less than 25 m in most coral reef areas (Ref. 1602, 48636).  Minimum depth from Ref. 90102, common minimum depth from Refs. 1602, 48636, 34765.

species.name: Morrison's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154). Common over flat bottoms covered with dense Halimeda (Ref. 31119) at depths 23-35 m. Forms mixed aggregations with an undescribed Paracheilinus

species.name: Morse Knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Buried in the sand during the day, emerging at dusk and remain active until just before dawn (Ref. 10809).  Field observation showed that the electric organ discharge (EOD) rate of this species start rising just before sunset, increasing to over 2-folds just after dark when the fish comes out of the sand, and decreasing when the fish returns to the sand well before dawn.  Experimental studies suggest internal control of this cyclic behavior (Ref. 10810).  There is evidence of fractional spawning; fecundity count was 65 eggs (Ref. 10644).

species.name: Mortensen’s darter dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Mortimer's happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various habitats and dams; feeds on insects, snails and plants; breeds in spring and early summer; males construct a sand-scrape nest in shallow water (Ref. 7248). Agamous, ovophilic (Ref. 52307) maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 7248, 52307). Females mouthbrood eggs and larvae (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Morue arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with ice (cryopelagic or epontic), found mainly in offshore waters, at or beyond the edge of the continental shelf (Ref. 1371). Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 58426).  Of little economic value (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Morue arctique (Eleginus nawaga)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the coastal sublittoral zone of the White Sea and Arctic coasts of Europe where it reflects a broad adaptation to the ecological conditions of the Arctic (Ref. 1371).  Found at shallow depths, along shores with soft, muddy bottoms, close to the ice and on the continental shelf (Ref. 1371).  Often caught in greatly freshened and at times completely fresh water, entering mouths and tidal zones of rivers and traveling upstream (Ref. 1371).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and worms, but takes small fishes (Ref. 1371).  Taxonomic problems to be solved.

species.name: morue de Murray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The Murray cod is one of the world's largest freshwater fish (Ref. 6390).  They live in a wide range of habitats, from clear, rocky streams to slow flowing, turbid rivers and billabongs (Ref. 27498).  They are generally found in waters to 5 m deep, in sheltered areas with cover from rocks, timber or overhanging banks.  Adult fish are carnivorous, having a diet of invertebrates, fish, amphibians and occasionally reptiles, birds and aquatic mammals (Ref. 27498).  The young feed on zooplankton.  Spawning takes place from spring to early summer.  Murray cod are territorial, their 'territory' associated with a specific hole, snag (large woody debris) or area of a river or lake (Ref. 27498).  Juveniles may undertake migrations (Ref. 6390).  Threatened due to over harvesting and habitat loss (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Morue de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly along the continental shelf and upper slopes (Ref. 1371). Form schools (Ref. 9988). They appear to be indiscriminate predators upon dominant food organisms present (Ref. 1371). Young probably feed on copepods and similar organisms (Ref. 27547). Adults feed on fishes, octopi, and large benthic and benthopelagic crustaceans (Ref. 1371); also worms. Parasites of the species include sealworm (Phocanema decipiens) in flesh, copepod (Lernaeocera branchialis) on gills and cestode (Pyramicocephalus phocarum) in the intestine (Ref. 5951). Marketed fresh and frozen for human consumption (Ref. 2850), and also dried or salted and smoked (Ref. 9988). Eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, micro-waved and baked (Ref. 9988). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Minimum depth from Ref. 054440.

species.name: Morue rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually on soft muddy or sandy bottoms.  Also on rocky bottoms, in estuaries, bays and continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  In New Zealand, most abundant in 200 to 300 m along the edge of the continental shelf.  May be found at depths exceeding 700 m (Ref. 9258).  Feeds primarily on fishes, cephalopods, crabs and other crustaceans.  Utilized as frozen fillets as well as fish blocks; eaten steamed, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Morue-lingue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from the intertidal to 475 m depth (Ref. 6793).  Adults are found near rocks, inshore and to 427 m (Ref. 2850).  Young occur on sand or mud bottom of bays and inshore areas (Ref. 2850).  Both migratory and non-migratory populations exist (Ref. 6885).  Adults feed mostly on other fishes but also take crustaceans, octopi and squid (Ref. 4925).  Young feed on copepods and other small crustaceans (Ref. 6885).  A very important sport and commercial species (Ref. 2850).  The liver is rich in vitamin A (Ref. 6885).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Has sharp teeth and gill rakers that can cut fingers if handled.

species.name: Morénesoce bio-bio
species.description: Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9323).  Feeds on invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9323).  The flesh is of excellent quality (Ref. 9323).

species.name: Morénésoce commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, including estuaries; sublittoral above 100 m (Ref. 11230).  Feeds on benthic fishes and crustaceans (Ref.  9830).  Nocturnal.  Known to attack fishers or anglers after being captured (Ref. 6590).  Also caught by drift net and bag (dol) nets.  Marketed mainly fresh.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Morénésoce coungré
species.description: Inhabits bays and estuaries.  Found over muddy bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Feeds mainly on benthic animals (Ref. 3793).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 3793).

species.name: Morénésoce indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters and estuaries, on soft bottom (Ref. 30573).  Feeds at night, on bottom fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 30573).  Marketed mainly fresh.  Caught also by bag (dol) net.

species.name: Morénésoce jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters and in estuaries, over soft bottoms.  Nocturnal, feeding mainly on bottom fishes and crustaceans.  Marketed mainly fresh; no separate statistics available (Ref. 7238; 9830). Minimum depth assumed from its ecology.

species.name: Mosaic corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mosaic leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on deep offshore reefs down to about 140 m, while juveniles occur in estuaries and on coastal reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Mosaic moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A secretive species that inhabits coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710, 75154).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Mosaic skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal species found on continental slope. Lengths of smallest mature male 27 cm TL, smallest postnatal juvenile 8 cm TL. Life history unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Mossback velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, in soft bottom.

species.name: Mosshead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612).  Commonly found in tide pools and shallow rocky areas, often in strong surf (Ref. 2850).  Can leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Sometimes encountered resting on rocks out of water, but usually found under rocks or among seaweeds (Ref. 2850).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Mosshead warbonnet
species.description: Usually in intertidal and subtidal rocky areas (Ref. 2850, 51666).  Sometimes hides in crevices and tubeworms holes with only head protruding (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Mossul bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mostelle de fond
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic to pelagic over muddy bottoms.  Mostly found between 100 and 200 m.  Feeds mostly on planktonic crustaceans (copepods, euphausiids, shrimps, amphipods) but also on small fish and various eggs and larvae (Ref. 1371).  Caught mainly for reduction to fishmeal (Ref. 3383), trout pellets, fodder (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Mostelle de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons marins. Found on hard and sandy-muddy bottoms near rocks at 100-650 m, but sometimes taken at greater depths (Ref. 1371).  Nocturnal, hiding between rocks during the day (Ref. 1371).  Feed on small fish and various invertebrates (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Mostelle à plumet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant in waters deeper than 750 m and feeds mainly on benthic organismsm  crustaceans and also on polychaetes. Caught singly but also in aggregations of more than 100 individuals (Ref. 1371). Parasites of the species include trematodes, cestodes, nematodes, acanthocephalans and copepods; attached in the intestines, gills and fins (Ref. 5951). Minimum depth (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Moswaren rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mote
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Motelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in offshore waters on mud, shell and coral bottoms.  Feed on crustaceans.  Spawning occurs in February.  Occasionally sold in markets.

species.name: Motelle arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Found offshore in deep water, always on soft bottoms of gravel, sand, mud, shells, and stones.  Occurs in water temperatures close to or below 0°C.  Feeds on decapod, amphipod, and euphausiid crustaceans, sometimes fishes are included in the diet (Ref. 9985).

species.name: Motelle nordique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone, on sand or mud bottoms.  Feed mostly on decapod crustaceans, lobsters, crabs, mysids and polychaetes (Ref. 3663).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Spawning may take place in deeper waters (Ref. 57987).

species.name: Motelle à cinq barbillons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612).  Generally close to the shore, not descending to great depths beyond the limits of the distribution of green algae (20 m), preferring rock bottoms but also living on sandy, muddy, and shell gravel bottoms.  Feed mainly on crustaceans, sometimes also on algae, polychaetes, gastropods and occasionally, small fish.  Occurs in temperatures ranging from 8 to 24°C (Ref. 4944).

species.name: Motelle à grands yeux de l'Atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on or near the bottom at depths of a few hundred meters.  Feed on crustaceans (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Motelle à quatre barbillons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sedentary bottom dwellers on muddy sand between patches of hard substrate, or on the soft, smooth ground of deep sinks on the continental slopes of both sides of the North Atlantic.  Feed on flatfishes, amphipods, decapods, copepods, mysids, shrimps, isopods and other small crustaceans.  Spawn in the Baltic Sea (Ref. 35388).  Mixed with soups and other products hot-smoked (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Motelle à taches blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in intertidal rock-pools while adults occur in sublittoral areas (Ref. 79721).  Feed on decapod crustaceans and algae (Ref. 3663).

species.name: Motelle à trois barbillons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms but also on mud, sand and gravel.  Feed on shrimps, crabs, isopods, small fish, mollusks and polychaetes (Ref. 1371).  Spawn during spring and summer in the Mediterranean.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Motelle à trois barbillons (Gaidropsarus mediterraneus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives generally at shallow depths near the shores on rocky bottom with aquatic vegetation to 60 m depth.  Feeds on fish, crustaceans, worms and algae.  Sold fresh in markets, also made into fish meal (Ref. 1371).  Caught as a by-catch by various fishing gears (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Moth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mother-of-pearl pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand, rubble or vegetation; two specimens taken from floating Sargassum. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mottled bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mottled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on the rocky shores of coastal waters (Ref. 5298). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mottled cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore in reef areas (Ref. 7300) among Acropora corals (Ref. 37816). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Mottled conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mottled cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reported to reach 280 m depth (Ref. 7251).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mottled eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 9862).  Inhabits mangrove creeks and protected sandy channels to a depth of at least 18 m; relatively uncommon (Ref. 37816).  Active swimmer, travelling long distances; feeds on crustaceans and molluscs (Ref. 68964). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught occasionally by bottom trawl, tangle net and inshore gillnet fisheries. Utilized for its meat, but of limited value as it is not frequently landed (Ref. 58048). Presumably utilized for human consumption in the western central Pacific (Ref. 9862).

species.name: Mottled eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults rarely in coastal swamps, with a wide temperature tolerance.  Shy and secretive, and is found in greatest abundance in mud substrates of dry zones.  Most often found in deep rock pools in rivers in the wet zones.  Probably feeds on small fish, crustaceans, worms and mollusks.  Species is too large for use in the aquarium trade, however is a welcome food fish when caught.

species.name: Mottled false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mottled hagfish
species.description:
From observations of baited videos, this hagfish is much less active feeding on the bait, and is less inclined to produce slime; possible that the colour pattern of this species offers good camouflage in deep-sea reefs or habitats
composed of sand patches over hard substrate, which was also abundant in the Three Kings area (Ref. 115309).

species.name: Mottled jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits an elaborate burrow, often fairly deep (12 inches), and with a terminal chamber; the vertical shaft  lined with coral and shell fragments.  An oral brooder (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Mottled loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear water, swift flowing streams with rocky, pebbly and sandy bottoms (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Mottled mojarra
species.description: Adults prefer sandy shores.  Young are more widespread.

species.name: Mottled moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow areas among corals (Ref. 37816).  A gonochoristic species (Ref. 32169).

species.name: Mottled skate
species.description: Commonly found near coast. Demersal on inner continental shelf. Feeds mainly on fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 114953). Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 14.5-16.0 cm long and 7.0-7.5 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253, 41298). Males reaches maturity at ca. 47 cm TL, females at ca. 69 cm TL; young hatch at 9-10 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Mottled soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky reefs, sheltering in caves and crevices but also encountered in the open (Ref. 11482).  Lies motionless, often on its side, hidden in dark recesses.  Actively hunts at night, preying on small fish (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Mottled sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected sandy bottoms of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Mottled spinefoot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits algal and seagrass flats and shallow lagoon and coastal reefs (Ref. 9710, 11230).  Forms schools.  Mainly diurnal.  Juveniles feed on filamentous algae, adults feed on leafy algae and seagrasses (Ref. 9710).  Commercially cultured in Japan.  Commonly found in large estuaries (Ref. 9002).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Mottled triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are abundant on rocky reefs from 10 to 25m, recorded from 2 to 33m (Ref. 84085). They occur in low tide pools and subtidal areas and prefer overhangs and holes containing sponges and bryozoans (Ref. 9003).  Juveniles are found in shallow waters, while adults are more abundant in deeper waters.  They feed mainly on crustaceans and small gastropods (Ref. 13227).
