Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mottled twister
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found predominantly in tide pools and upper subtidal areas.  Are solitary.  They feed mainly on amphipods, isopods, polychaetes, and small gastropods.  Males may defend small breeding territories during the breeding season (Ref 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Moulton’s handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mountain barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mountain chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with clear to muddy water over substrates of sand, silty mud, rocks and boulders (Ref. 33475).

species.name: Mountain clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mountain Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live mainly in small, clear, flowing streams with gravel or sand bottoms from near sea level to about 1800 m elevation.  May be cryptic, living among log debris and boulders, or sometimes found in loose shoals in more open conditions.  Also occur in small upland tarns where they may be found shoaling in open water.  Tolerant of very cold water, they have been collected from a tarn surrounded by deep snow.  Life cycle (maximum life span of about 4 years) is restricted to fresh water.  Feed on benthic and drifting invertebrates.  Mature individuals breed in spring (sometimes extending to autumn); adults move upstream into shallow riffle areas to lay their demersal, adhesive eggs over rocky bottoms (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Mountain grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit cobble and gravel bottom streams and deep pools below rapids and waterfalls (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mountain hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively fast-flowing streams, usually forming schools in rocky pools or quiet backwaters.

species.name: Mountain madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clean rocky riffles, shoals and runs of small to large rivers.  Often found near vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on larvae of aquatic insects, dominated by mayflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Mountain molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mountain rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits high altitude headwater tributaries at elevations between 790-1600 m (Ref. 2847).  Is an omnivore and egg laying species, considered a peaceful community fish and prefers the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.8, H=16, 19°C water temperature; rock, plant and driftwood cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Mountain redbelly dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Mountain shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky pools and runs of clear creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mountain stream sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools at the foot of rapids or waterfalls (Ref. 11225).

species.name: Mountain swordatail
species.description: Inhabits fast flowing creeks in mountainous areas up to 1200 m elevation.

species.name: Mourine américaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species found on continental and insular shelves; enters bays and estuaries; forms huge schools inshore (Ref. 114953).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates and molluscs (implicated in damaging seagrass beds) (Ref. 93252, 114953). Jumps occasionally, landing with a loud smack, probably as a territorial display.  Migrates south in large schools that disappear off northern Florida, USA and are not reported from Caribbean Is.; tagged fish have been recovered in northern South America (Ref. 7251).  Population in the Gulf of Mexico migrates clockwise; schools of up to 10,000 rays leave west coast of Florida for Yucatan, Mexico in the fall (Ref. 7251).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Mourine du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over soft bottoms, near rocky or coral reefs; also near reef drop-offs (Ref. 12951). They occasionally swim near the surface and may jump out of the water. Often in schools, sometimes associated with Aetobatus narinari, the spotted eagle ray (Ref. 12951). Adults feed on benthic crustaceans and mollusks. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Mourine javanaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays, estuaries, and near coral reefs (Ref. 12951), over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Usually solitary or in small aggregations (Ref. 114953).  However, large schools with up to 500 individuals have been reported (Ref. 12951). Feeds on clams, oysters and crustaceans (Ref. 12951).  Lives to over 2 years in captivity (Ref. 12951).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Edible (Ref. 30573). Caught mainly by gill net fisheries (Ref. 114953), occasionally by bottom trawl, demersal inshore gillnet and tangle net fisheries. Utilized for its meat (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Mourine ticon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species found inshore over sandy bottoms from nearshore to about 20 m depth.  Feeds mainly on molluscs (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Pups 38-48 cm disc width at birth (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Mourner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mournful dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from reef caves, reef overhangs and slopes (Ref. 56434).

species.name: Mourning pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mourning tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is a gregarious species.  Occurs over sand and rocks, in swift flowing waters where it swims rapidly and incessantly.  Feeds on both plants and animals (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Mousetail knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mousey klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal pools.  Gravid females bloated.

species.name: Moustache jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rubble-sand bottoms near coral reefs and rocky areas. and it has been observed in burrows or resting on the bottom (Ref. 129348).

species.name: Moustache longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky or rubble bottoms (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Moustached rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mouth almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit still or gently flowing water of streams, pools, lakes, swamps and reservoirs, usually in well vegetated, shallow margins.  Tolerant of temperatures to at least 38°C and pH range of 4.5-8.1 (Ref. 44894).  Commonly found in rivers, creeks and lagoons.  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Solitary, carnivore.  Most of its time is spent sitting motionless among plant cover waiting to ambush small fishes and crustaceans.  Aquatic and terrestrial insects are also consumed (Ref. 44894).  Males are mouthbrooders (Ref. 205).

species.name: Moutham's goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. General description of the bank where the specimens were taken, is shallow sand on eroded flat rock with scattered patches of green algae (Ref. 58005).

species.name: Moyer's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reef slopes, usually on rubble and sand near large coral formations (Ref. 48636).  Found in small loose groups and usually a large male dominates sections of reef (Ref. 48636).  Small groups occur with one adult male (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Mozambique cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in loose aggregations between branching corals or coralline rocks (Ref. 9710), and seaweed in protected waters to a depth of 15 meters (Ref. 54391).  Relatively common (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Mozambique fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs in areas with poor to moderate coral growth; often over coral rubble (Ref. 9710). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mozambique knifejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef areas and feeds on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Mozambique sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth  range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Mrigal carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fast flowing streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).  Can tolerate high levels of salinity.  Juveniles are omnivorous to about 5 cm TL, adults are almost entirely herbivorous.  Feed on plankton, but also grazes on algae.  Spawning occurs in marginal areas of the water body with a depth of 50-100 cm over a sand or clay substrate.  A 6 kg female can lay a million eggs (of 1 mm diameter) (Ref. 6028).  Widely cultured in India but fails to breed naturally in ponds, thus induced breeding is done.  Fishery harvests 40 cm fish weighing 1000 g and of about 3 years.  A very active fish that thrives in ponds but spawns in swift rivers.  Fingerlings are in great demand for stocking ponds between July and November (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Mt. Nimba lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers, swamps, and brooks in mountainous areas (Ref. 3788, 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Mubi rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits narrow, crystal clear streams in closed-canopy forest, flowing through limestone hills (Ref. 26387).

species.name: Muckraker
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This species is an inhabitant of estuaries and has been taken over fine sediments near mangroves.
Starks (1913) commented that it was not found in rocky tidal pools (Ref. 55435).

species.name: Mucurilebias leitaoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Mud blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mud darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sluggish riffles over rocks or debris in small to large rivers; also lowland lakes (Ref. 5723), creeks, swamps and reservoirs (Ref. 10294).  Feeds mainly on midge and blackfly larvae (Diptera); small fish consumes more microcrustaceans (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Mud flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, inshore region.

species.name: Mud goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs, inhabits sand or mud bottoms of coastal reefs in 5-30 m (Ref. 90102). Collected from the turbid silty mud bottom off a river mouth.

species.name: Mud pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an area consisted of pieces of metal wreckage and discarded tyres on mud bottom; it either rested on the bottom or hovered in midwater in the shady recesses of the wreckage or tyres (Ref. 100512).

species.name: Mud reef-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A territorial species that inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Found over silty bottoms near or under overhanging corals.  Feeds by sifting the sediment through its gill rakers (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Mud skate
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth between 405-420 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 6.7 cm long and 4.7 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Mud sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, estuaries (Ref. 4967) and mangrove creeks (Ref. 10812).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).  Maximum size recorded in West Africa was 8.3 cm TL (Ref. 57413).

species.name: Mud sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs over mud and detritus in vegetated sloughs, lakes, and pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Mud-dwelling moray
species.description: Found on mud bottom with scattered rocks in 15-32 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Mudbank filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy substrates in sheltered coastal bays (Ref. 48637). Also found in sand bottoms of trawling grounds in 15-50 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Muddy arrowtooth eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the slope and upper abyssal zone.  Feeds on annelids and crustaceans.

species.name: Muddy damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are observed around rock outcrops with flat silt-sand bottom (Ref. 31101).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Mudfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in inundated areas.  Bury themselves in the mud when the pools are drying up.  Feed mainly on fish and mollusks; also crustaceans, diatoms, detritus and bottom organisms (Ref. 248). Omnivorous and reproduction takes place in the rainy saison (Ref. 78218). Max. size for West Africa and Lower Guinea: 650mm TL (Ref. 57129, 81644).

species.name: Mudslope goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection area consists of moderately sloped (about 20 degrees) mud substratum (the slope begins in approximately 1.5 m depth and flattens out at about 18 m). The featureless bottom has numerous burrows occupied by a variety of fishes and invertebrates, including Acentrogobius vanderloosi. About eight individuals were observed on the lower section of the slope (15-18 m ) and only widely scattered, solitary individuals were seen, each of which was invariably associated with a muddy burrow, into which it retreated when approached (Ref. 100513).

species.name: Mueller's flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Mueller's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in tide pools and close to edge of rocky shores at low tide.   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Mugil brevirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugil longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugil margaritae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugilogobius abei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms of estuaries and coastal freshwater streams not far from the stream mouth; probably fresh water tolerant (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius adeia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from Lake Matano where it was observed to stay close by or seek shelter in empty shells of the gastropod Brotia gemmifera (Ref. 43716). Feeds on tiny short-spired gastropods (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius cagayanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugilogobius cavifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on mud and sand in brackish to freshwaters, often in mangroves (Ref. 58302).  Adults feed primarily on worms and other small benthic invertebrates; breeding habits are unknown  (Ref. 44091).

species.name: Mugilogobius fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow small mangrove creeks and pools; often concealed among leaf litter (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius flavomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is rare and has been found only in low salinity waters (0.1-0.4 psu) in the estuaries of northeast Taiwan (Ref. 118215).

species.name: Mugilogobius hitam
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to hide in the warm shallows, deep among coarse gravel substrate.  Occurs syntopically with <i>Mugilogobius latifrons and <i>Glossogobius flavipinnis in shallow gravel habitats (Ref. 97638).

species.name: Mugilogobius karatunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugilogobius latifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to freshwater, in three tectonic lakes of central Sulawesi (steep-sided, deep lakes with aquatic vegetation and with native fish fauna generally restricted to the shallow sides) (Ref. 43716). Usually found in very shallow water in Lake Matano, in less than 50 cm depth, typically among pebbles (Ref. 43716). Also in shallow, muddy bays protected from wind and wave disturbance, or where vegetation is thick such as rice paddy or Chara-filled water buffalo wallows (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius lepidotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found exclusively on sandy bottoms (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius myxodermus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ditches, ponds and puddles at Wuchow (Ref. 35840).

species.name: Mugilogobius nuicocensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugilogobius paludis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mangroves, entering the lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Mugilogobius rexi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers above the substrate, in a slightly diagonal position, with caudal fin curved to one side. Inhabits water at least a meter's depth, over silty substrate, near clumps of aquatic plants and the freshwater mangrove Barringtonia racemosa (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius tagala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugilogobius tigrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow small mangrove creeks and pools (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Mugilogobius wilsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected mostly from tidal streams and muddy mangrove creeks and may not travel very far up into more brackish habitats.  Could be kept in captivity for some weeks in seawater; can feed on live brine shrimp (Ref. 43716).  Spawn in fresh water in captivity.  Eggs hatch in 6-7 days at about 27°C (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Mugilogobius zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mugura grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured at depths from 200 to more than 600 m (Ref. 95664).  Feeds primarily on polychaetes with crustaceans of minor importance (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Muiron pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reef of inshore waters.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Muksun
species.description:
Anadromous, semi-anadromous, lacustrine, lacustrine-riverine, and riverine stocks have been reported. Most stocks are migratory, spending most of year at sea, sometimes rather far from coast (Ref. 59043).  Stays mainly in the lower reaches of the rivers (Ref. 593) with slow current, large lakes and their tributaries, floodplain lakes, deltas and estuaries, marine waters with salinity up to 6-10%. Enters rivers in July - August and reaches spawning sites by October - November. In larger rivers, moves upriver up tp 2000 km (average speed 20 km/day). Spawns for the first time at 6-14 years, 47-50 cm SL. Spawns in rapids or shallows, at 1-2°C, when rivers start freezing. Adults leave spawning sites in winter (Ref. 59043). Eggs are buried in unguarded nests (Ref. 205). Eggs hatch in 150-180 days; peak hatching usually in April. Juveniles feed on plankton in winter (during which they do not cease active foraging) and benthic invertebrates in summer (Ref. 59043).  
Status of threat: Important commercial species but rapidly declining (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Mulet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow coastal waters (Ref. 27121), including estuaries (Ref. 2683, 57400, 81659), lagoons (Ref. 57400), tidal rivers (Ref. 3573), freshwater and supersaline environments (Ref. 81659).  Feed on plankton and detritus (Ref. 28587).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Shows a remarkable adaptation to hyperhaline environments (up to 97‰ in the Sine Saloum in Senegal)(Ref. 57400).  Specimens from tropical East Atlantic reaching maximum of 280 mm SL and common to 180 mm SL (Ref. 81659).

species.name: Mulet (Crenimugil seheli)
species.description: Found in coastal waters but enters estuaries and rivers where they feed on microalgae, filamentous algae, forams, diatoms, and detritus associated with sand and mud (Ref. 9812). Form schools. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Also caught using stakenets, barrier nets, and pouch nets during spawning; also taken as bycatch (Ref. 9812). Marketed fresh and perhaps salted, boiled (Thailand), canned or frozen (Australia); roe salted (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet (Dajaus monticola)
species.description: Inhabits pools and runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Adults live in freshwater rivers and streams.  Young are encountered occasionally in brackish waters.  This is the only mullet that ascends far inland and spends all its adult life in freshwater (Ref. 11225).  Tend to be few and solitary in upper streams, but form uneven schools in larger streams at lower elevations (Ref. 11225).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Usually spawn during the rainy season (Ref. 42119).  Caught and consumed by local populations in some parts of central America.

species.name: Mulet (Mugil curema)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy coasts and littoral pools but also occurs in muddy bottoms of brackish lagoons and estuaries.  Sometimes penetrate rivers.  May also be found on coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles are common in coastal waters and are known to find their way to estuaries and coastal lagoons.  Growth in juveniles is moderate (30-40 cm in 4 years).  Adults form schools (Ref. 9321).  Feed on microscopic or filamentous algae and small juveniles of planktonic organisms (Ref. 9626).  Reproduction occurs between March and August.  Spawn several million eggs provided with a notable yolk (Ref. 35237).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Maximul size 910 mm TL for western Central Atlantic specimens, eastern Central Atlantic specimens may reach 350 mm TL and commonly reach 250 mm TL (Ref. 81659). An important foodfish, it is marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 9321).

species.name: Mulet (Neochelon falcipinnis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline, tolerating conditions varying from hypersaline to freshwater; favours sandy or muddy substrates (Ref. 81659). Very common in coastal lagoons and estuaries (Ref. 2683, 57400, 81659). Also caught in hypersaline environments (Ref. 57400) and freshwaters (Ref. 7399, 57400, 81659) several kilometres upstream in rivers (Ref. 81659). Feed on plankton and detritus (Ref. 28587).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Spawning may occur in lagoons or in the sea (Ref. 81659). Possibly reaches up to 500mm FL (Ref. 57400, 81659).

species.name: Mulet (Osteomugil cunnesius)
species.description: Occur in shallow coastal waters, including estuaries and backwaters, frequently enters freshwater.  Form larger aggregations during spawning which takes place at sea.  Young individuals enter tidal rivers.  Feed on organic matter contained in sand and mud (Ref. 30573).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh and salted.  Decays rapidly, but well liked when fresh.

species.name: Mulet (Osteomugil robustus)
species.description: Inhabit coastal waters including estuaries (Ref. 5213).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet (Parachelon grandisquamis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in lagoons and estuaries; an extremely euryhaline species (from 0-66‰), but preferring areas close to the sea in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 57400), often with muddy substrates (Ref. 81659). Inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries and brackish lagoons (Ref. 2683), including mangroves (Ref. 2683, 81659), creeks, estuaries, inundated mudflats (Ref. 81659) and freshwater rivers (Ref. 7399).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Maximum reported size 297 mm FL, but possibly up to 400 mm (Ref. 57400, 81659).

species.name: Mulet (Paramugil parmatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seas, estuaries, and rivers.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet ailé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, estuaries; sometimes ascending rivers into fresh water (Ref. 9812). They prefer slow moving waters or still lagoons (Ref. 9812). Often found in turbid water, over muddy substrates, and with well-substantiated aquatic vegetation (Ref. 9812). They feed on microalgae, detritus, terrestrial plant material, and aquatic insects (Ref. 9812). Perhaps catadromous (Ref. 9812). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy shores, tide pools and rocky surge areas (Ref. 9812).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Form schools.  Feed on seaweeds and some crustaceans at daytime.  Tend to move inshore to surface waters at night (Ref. 9812).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Caught at night with strong light and scooped up with hand nets (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet banae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 2683, 7399, 57400), estuaries (Ref. 2683, 7399, 81659), inshore marine waters and lagoons (Ref. 81659).  Also in high salinity waters (up to 73‰)(Ref. 57400).  Feeds on phytoplankton and detritus (Ref. 28587).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Maximum FL reporded 260mm (Ref. 57400), maximum SL 260 mm, common length 200 mm SL (Ref. 81659).

species.name: Mulet bobo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the upper reaches of rivers but enter brackish waters where spawning probably occurs.  An important food fish in some areas.  Herbivorous and scrapes algae from stones on the bottom with its fleshy lips, although sometimes eats prawns (Ref. 36880).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Migrate from the upper reaches of rivers during months of high rainfall  to the sea-river transition zone to spawn (Ref. 13802).

species.name: Mulet boxeur
species.description: Found in coastal waters, over sandy or muddy areas of lagoons, reef flats and tide pools; enters harbors (Ref. 9812).  Schooling species, swim at various depths along reefs, to about 20 meters but usually much shallower. Feed on detritus containing algae and microscopic animals, by scooping up the upper layer of sand or mud and filtering through the gills (Ref. 48637).  Omnivorous (Ref. 6113).  Form large schools before spawning, at the beginning of the ebb tide (in June), over shallow, open areas of the lagoon slope (Ref. 9812).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawning occurs in large aggregations after dark.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9812).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Mulet caréné
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur mainly in marine coastal waters.  Also found in inlet waters and estuaries of rivers (Ref. 559).  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet chiraya
species.description: A shallow-water, schooling species which enters estuaries and freshwaters.  Spawn at sea.  Juveniles may be found in rice fields and mangrove swamps (Ref. 9812).  Feed on small algae, diatoms, and other organic matter, both living and detrital, taken in with sand and mud.  Fries feed on copepods and floating algae.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh, boiled (Thailand), canned or frozen (Australia); roe marketed salted (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet comorien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit freshwaters, but may occur in estuaries (Ref. 2830). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet de Thoburn
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in shallow waters, most commonly in areas of mangrove development and shallow embayments.  Often seen scraping algae from lava rocks or browsing on filamentous algae (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  More data needed.  Probably caught incidentally with other mullets.

species.name: Mulet des îles du Cap Vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic (Ref. 7399).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet Diassanga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximal length observed during the redescription is 43.9 cm SL (Ref. 89987). It seems to be a rare and large species throughout its distribution; only specimens > 25 cm were observed so far (Ref. 89987). It status for the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is recommended as "Data Deficient" (Ref. 89987).

species.name: Mulet dos vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools in shallow coastal waters and enters lagoons, estuaries, and fresh water to feed (Ref. 9812).  Juveniles may enter rice fields and mangroves (Ref. 9812).  Feed on small algae, diatoms and benthic detrital material taken in with sand and mud; fry take zooplankton, diatoms, detrital material and inorganic sediment (Ref. 9812).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawning occurs at sea.  Also caught with stakenets (Ref. 9812).  Marketed fresh and salted.

species.name: Mulet grande gueule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky littoral zones.  Feed on algae that grows on  rocks by scraping it off with its specialized teeth.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Probably caught incidentally with other mullets.  May be found in Panama markets.

species.name: Mulet hospe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal marine and estuarine areas (Ref. 9321).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Incidentally caught with other species of mullets (Ref. 9321).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 9321).

species.name: Mulet joue d'or
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters, estuaries, lagoons, and sometimes entering tidal rivers.  Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549). Feed on small algae, diatoms, and other organic matter.  Spawn at sea.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Sold fresh in markets; the roe is highly valued.

species.name: Mulet labeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic, found inshore, at mouths of rivers and sewage  effluents but not entering brackish and freshwater (Ref. 7465).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet labéon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal waters, mainly in reef flats and shallow lagoon reefs; often in silty habitats Form schools at the surface (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Usually swimming in surface waters near freshwater run-offs.   Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Used as live bait in pole-and-line tuna fishing (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet lesète
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  More data needed.  Probably caught incidentally together  with other mullets.

species.name: Mulet mignon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 5217).  Adults are found in shallow depth near sand; juveniles often in rockpools (Ref. 86997). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in large schools, sometimes in deep offshore waters (Ref. 2804).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet otomebora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. School in shallow coastal waters; enter lagoons, estuaries, and rivers to feed (Ref. 9812). It feeds on plant detritus, microalgae, minute benthic organisms, and organic matter in sand and mud; juveniles feed on planktonic algae (Ref. 9812). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Also caught with stakenets and is marketed fresh (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet parassi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in brackish estuaries but also in marine and hyper-saline waters (Ref. 5217).  During reproduction, they gather in small groups at the mouth of coastal rivers and creeks.  Reproduction occurs in the early part of the year.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Eggs which are rich in yolk are spawned by the millions.  Upon hatching, juveniles move up to the swamps and coastal rivers over long distances, to seek for food and to protect themselves against predators (Ref. 35237).  Marketed fresh or salted (Ref. 5217).  The roe is marketed salt-pickled and dried and considered a delicacy (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Mulet perlé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools of upland creeks and small rivers, and also ponds and lakes. Usually found over sand or gravel (Ref. 86798). Feeds on copepods, cladocerans, chironomids, beetles, filamentous algae, and Chara (Ref. 1998). Spawns during the spring (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Mulet perlé du nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools of creeks and small rivers, ponds and lakes.  Usually found over sand or gravel (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Mulet so-iny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coastal waters as well as freshwater regions of rivers (Ref. 41299).  Very common in the rivers discharging into Peter the Great Bay; enter freshwater.  Large concentrations of fry-of-the-year measuring 3.1-6.2 cm in the mouths of rivers in August.  Length in the Black Sea is usually 20-30 cm but may reach 43 cm; length in the Atlantic Ocean may reach 50 cm (Ref. 2058).  Omnivorous (Ref. 9137).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Alien Invasive: In Azov Sea, it is now the most abundant mugilid species. Along shores of Black Sea, its expansion corresponds to a sharp decline of native species of Mugilidae, which it apparently replaces (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Mulet sudafricain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, mainly off rocky points and sandy beaches; may enter estuaries which serve as nursery areas (Ref. 27121). Feed mainly on diatoms and detritus, but also on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 27121). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). A primary target species of the inshore net fishery and much of it is sold salted and dried and known as 'bokkoms'. It is also an important exhibit species in public aquaria in South Africa. It is parasitised by the monogenean Gyrodactylus molweni on the external body surface (Ref. 124050).

species.name: Mulet tade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in marine waters, but enters estuaries and backwaters.  Feed on small algae, diatoms, and other organic matter, both living and detrital, taken in with sand and mud.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawning takes place at sea.  Also caught with stakenets.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Mulet à cornes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Mostly found in tiny, intermittent streams.  Young feed on small aquatic invertebrates while adults consume small fish, crayfish and other large invertebrates (Ref. 10294).  One of the most common fishes in eastern North America (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Mulet à grandes écailles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in shallow coastal waters, and from brackish water to freshwater regions of rivers (Ref. 41299).  Form schools (Ref. 40448); in larger aggregations during spawning, which takes place at sea (Ref. 2830).  Feed on small algae, diatoms, forams, benthic polychaetes, crustaceans, mollusks, organic matter and detritus; fry feed on copepods and floating algae (Ref. 40448).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Caught mainly during the spawning season and is sold fresh; the roe is highly appreciated.

species.name: Mulet à queue bleue
species.description: Found in coastal waters, including estuaries and rivers (Ref. 5213). Young fish frequent estuaries and also ascend rivers and coastal creeks (Ref. 2847). It feeds on algae, diatoms, detritus, and crustaceans (Ref. 9812). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Caught during the spawning period (Ref. 9812). Other methods include the use of stakenets, pouch nets, and barrier nets (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Mulet à queue carrée
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoons, reef flats, estuaries, and  coastal creeks, in shallow coastal areas and protected sandy shores (Ref. 40488). Usually within tidal influence, but may enter fresh water, ascending 10 km into rivers (Ref. 40488). Forms large schools, frequently in mangrove areas (Ref. 2334). Juveniles may be found in rice fields and mangroves and may be used as bait fish (Ref. 9812). Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205). Feeds on phytoplankton, small algae and detritus organisms (Ref. 89972). Caught in cast nets, stake
nets, beach seines, and gill nets; marketed fresh and salted; boiled (Thailand), canned or frozen (Australia). Roe also marketed salted and juveniles used as bait fish (Ref. 9812)..

species.name: Mulet éventail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal water, brackish lagoons and lower reaches of rivers (sometimes in freshwater) (Ref. 3791).  Feed on small algae and other organic matter (Ref. 3791).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Mulet œil de perdrix
species.description: Inhabit shallow protected sandy to muddy areas of reef flats and shallow lagoons while juveniles have been encountered in tide pools (Ref. 205).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh and used as live bait in pole-and-line fishing for tuna (Ref. 9812).

species.name: Multi-barred cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations, often among branching corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Multi-thread dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Multibar citharine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers vegetated margins of rivers and oxbow lagoons or shallow lakes; picks small invertebrates and epiphyton from stems of plants and roots; breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Known to make seasonal movements onto floodplains during rainy season (Ref. 13337). Maximum size about 45mm SL; attractive and peaceful aquarium species (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Multibarred shrimpgoby
species.description: Collected specimens were found near the wreck of a Japanese ship on a silty sand bottom in 4 m depth. Observed generally in pairs that share their burrows with a very active, unidentified species of alpheid shrimp (Ref. 92356).

species.name: Multibarred triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 11482).   Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Multicolor angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes, typically in small tracks of rubble between areas of rich coral growth (Ref. 33482).  Benthopelagic at 20-90 m (Ref. 58302).  Cryptic.  Herbivorous (Ref. 33482).  Feeds readily in aquaria.  Forms harems of 3-7 individuals.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Multicolour dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Found in or near holes (Ref. 9710).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413).

species.name: Multipore dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in a midwater trawl (Ref. 42989). Reported maximum length of 3.1 cm SL was based on a subadult specimen (Ref. 42989). Preliminary maximum length assumed as 6.5 cm TL.

species.name: Multisaddle pygmy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A single individual was found together with Trimma chledophilum at the base of a sloping mud bottom, among pieces of metal wreckage. This species was invariably seen sheltering in a small enclosed 'grotto', either resting on the bottom or hovering a short distance above it. This holotype was the only individual encountered in the area despite 38 hours of diving in the immediate vicinity of this site and possibly the main population inhabits deeper waters farther from shore (Ref. 100512).

species.name: Multispine damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur outside the lagoon, usually in deeper surge channels on the leeward side of reefs in the Capricorn Group, Queensland, Australia. Ubiquitous at Lord Howe Island (Ref. 7247). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Close relative of N. mitratus (Ref. 90102). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Multispine giant stingray
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Multispine skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Multispotted goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Multispotted lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic; found between 74-400 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Exhibits size stratification with depth.  Sexually mature from about 62 mm (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Mumburarr whipray
species.description: Juveniles were recorded from lower reaches of rivers at depths of 2.2-8.7 m; salinity 14.6-33.1; turbidity 367->1000 NTU.  Subadult specimens were from depths of 10-20 m.  An adult female (161.0 cm DW, 174.0 cm disc length) aborted a late embryo which was estimated to be ca. 26.5 cm DW on capture. Juveniles (5) measured 39.o - 67.2 cm DW, 43.0-72.0 cm DL, while a late adolescent male measured 103.0 cm DW,  This stingray could be traditionally hunted for food and the caudal sting can be used as a traditional knife. (Ref. 110274).

species.name: Muna jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silt/sand bottoms in brackish habitats near mouths of freshwater tidal streams in 0.5-1 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Munro's hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fluviatile and estuarine habitats.  Does not appear to school in large numbers nor does it seem to be abundant.  Biology unknown (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Muraena appendiculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Muraenesox yamaguchiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Muraenichthys elerae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Muraenichthys gymnopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit warm shallow seas (Ref. 7050), in rocky reefs (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Muraenolepis andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Muraenolepis evseenkoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mural goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal sand and rubble flats, often near mangroves (Ref. 48637).  Occur in areas of fine sand in shallow lagoon reefs.  Adults occur in pairs while juveniles were often seen in small groups.  Feed on small invertebrates by sifting mouthfuls of sand.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Breeding pairs are commonly found sharing a single burrow (Ref. 56281).

species.name: Murdy’s sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on gentle slope of mixed sand and small coral rubble substrate and exposed to frequent currents and coldwater upwelling. It has not been seen at depths less tha 60 m. Collected with the use of clove oil and hand nets (Ref. 118652).

species.name: Murray hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and billabongs, most frequently around aquatic plant thickets.  Omnivorous, feeds on algae, insects and tiny crustaceans (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Murray River rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, creeks, drains, ponds and reservoirs.  Occurs usually in still or slow-flowing conditions (Ref. 7300).  Inhabits streams, backwaters of larger rivers, drainage ditches, overflow ponds and reservoirs.  Usually congregates along grassy banks or around submerged logs and branches (Ref. 44894).  Omnivorous (Ref. 7300).  The most southward-ranging rainbowfish and the only species adapted to low winter temperatures (normally about 10°-15°C).  There is evidence that numbers are drastically reduced during winter drought when water temperatures dip below 10°C.  Suitable for outdoor pond culture in temperate climates (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Murray's abyssal anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 58302) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Males dwarfed, non-parasitic (Ref. 4491).

species.name: Murray's armoured gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deepwater species (Ref. 9771).  Bony scutes reduce commercial value (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Murray's smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mursa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Murty's sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms; form schools and protect themselves from their predators (tuna Euthynnus affinis and carangids) by burrowing (Ref. 93118).

species.name: Murène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasional among rocks and rubble to depths of at least 10 m.  They stay concealed among rocks, waiting for prey to come along.  Are active predators which feed on crustaceans and fish (Ref. 5377).  Possibly  consumed in subsistence fisheries (Ref. 3254).

species.name: Murène (Gymnothorax buroensis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow lagoon and seaward reefs, primarily found in the surge zone (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Lives between rocks and corals.

species.name: Murène (Gymnothorax intesi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Murène (Muraena melanotis)
species.description: Espèce de murènes. Lives in shallow rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683) and feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 3254).

species.name: Murène anneau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species and solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting outer reef slopes.  Occurs under ledges and in holes of reef slopes (Ref. 37816).  Has the habit of puffing its head like a cobra when approached (Ref. 37816).  Secretive and nocturnal (Ref. 48635).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Murène bijou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often seen in shallow water.  Remains under cover in rocky crevices during the day.  Feeds mainly at night on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 6852).  Constantly opens and closes it mouth, an action required for respiration, not a threat (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Murène brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in crevices (Ref. 58302). Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène brune (Gymnothorax unicolor)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf, on rocky coasts, rough sand, gravel, crevices, small caves and shadowed zones (Ref. 3256).  Feeds on small crabs and gastropods (Ref. 3254).

species.name: Murène canarienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range based on the 3 known specimens all of which have been collected from rocky bottom.  May inhabit deep waters.

species.name: Murène châtaigne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses during day; forage in the open at night.  Constantly opens and closes its mouth--an action required for respiration, not a threat (Ref. 5227).  May occasionally wander into open sandy areas about 10-20 m from cover.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fishes and are highly responsive to stimuli emanating from wounded or distressed prey at distances exceeding 20 m (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Murène cobra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms (Ref. 26999) of coastal waters.

species.name: Murène d'eau douce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic and lotic freshwater (Ref. 7300) and found in estuarine and marine habitats (Ref. 6028).  Usually found within 20-30 km of the sea at a maximum elevation of about 30-40 m (Ref. 2847, 44894).

species.name: Murène de Bayer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species that inhabits benches and seaward reefs.  Secretive in reefs, sometimes seen at night (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on fishes.  May bite by accident or when provoked.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène de Calìfornie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found common among rocks; lives in crevices or holes, usually with only head protruding.  Very common in shallow reef areas (Ref. 35581).  Feed mostly at night on crustaceans, octopuses and small fishes.  Long-lived.  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Murène de Java
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon and seaward reefs.  Commonly seen species along deep drop-offs and slopes in Indonesian waters (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles more secretive and occur on intertidal reef flats (Ref. 37816).  It feeds primarily on fishes and occasionally on crustaceans.  This is the largest Indo-Pacific moray eel (Ref. 30404), perhaps reaching 3 m in length.  Because of its position at the top of the reef's food chain it is often ciguatoxic.  Attacks humans when provoked (Ref. 3132).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 10713. Solitary in reef holes (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène de Madère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on shelf, rocks and deep coral zones (Ref. 3256).

species.name: Murène de Méditerranée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A nocturnal and territorial species (Ref. 12382), commonly lurking in holes, and writhing snakelike through crevices, under rocks or corals.  Feeds on fish, crabs and squid (Ref. 12382).  It seldom attacks unless provoked (Ref. 3256).  A gonochoristic species (Ref. 32169).  Utilized fresh and eaten broiled, boiled and baked; the skin can be used for leather (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Murène dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting coral reefs and rocky shorelines. Usually at depths of 60 m (Ref. 26938). One of the most common and easily recognized morays of the West Indian reefs, active during the day and sometimes hunting together with other predators (Ref. 42064). This species has been called Muraena miliaris (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Murène dragon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky reefs.  Common in warm-temperate waters (Ref. 9710).  Benthic at 1-35 m (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène du golfe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses.  Constantly opens and closes its mouth, an action required for respiration, not a threat (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Murène enchainée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) found commonly on reefs and rocky shore areas. Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5521). At Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, off NE Brazil, forages for sally lightfoot crabs (Grapsus grapsus) on exposed reefs at ebb tide and in tide-pools mostly at daytime. Able to withstand up to 30 minutes out of water while foraging, uses four main tactics both in and out of the water. Searches for prey at pool rims and rock bases poking into crevices and holes, stealthily approaches previously sighted prey, chases prey and ambushes prey from under rocks and crevices. Hunting success varies with employed tactic, but overall success is about 50%. May move up to 6 meters in about 1 hour while foraging on the exposed reef. Its crab hunting is mostly visually guided and a fish darting nearby a stealthily foraging moray may cause it to miss the strike; the missed crab may be chased up to 5 m on the reef. Able to strike with its body partly or entirely out of the water, usually strikes from a distance of 5 to10 centimeters. Small crabs are swallowed whole, whereas larger ones are torn apart by a combination of tugging, rotating, knotting, and thrashing movements. Handling time is related to prey size, the largest crabs (carapace width 2.3-3.2 times larger than moray’s head width) broken up and swallowed within 90 to 240 seconds. Attracted to plastic or rubber decoys dragged on a nylon string nearby, striking at these (Ref. 50922).

species.name: Murène fantôme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand or rubble bottoms. Also in Shallow water, often in tidepools (Ref 90102). Nocturnal, feeds on small reef organisms (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Murène grise
species.description: Poisson d'eau de mer. A benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Murène grise (Gymnothorax vicinus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting rocky shores and reefs where water is clear.  Most active at night (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).  May cause serious wounds (Ref. 5217).  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Murène jaunâtre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Lives in holes and crevices of seaward reefs from the surge zone to over 26 m. Solitary and secretive in reef crevices; seldom seen (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène maculée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic between rocks and on sand and mud substrates.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses.  Constantly opens and closes its mouth--an action required for respiration, not a threat (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Murène mignonne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Considered one of the smallest morays in the world (Ref. 28023).  Benthic on sand and between rocks.

species.name: Murène noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) common on shallow reefs and along rocky shores.  Caught incidentally and consumed fresh or salted in some localities (Ref. 3255).

species.name: murène noire (Muraena augusti)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Murène obscure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Murène ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) commonly found on deep soft bottom areas and banks, rarely on coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Also in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 42064).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 42064).  Probably consumed fresh or salted (Ref. 3255).

species.name: Murène octavienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives between rocks, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses during the day; forage in the open at night.  Constantly opens and closes its mouth-an action required for respiration-not a threat (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Murène ondulée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species on reef flats among rocks, rubble, or debris and also occurs in lagoons and seaward reefs to depths of 26 m or more.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942. Cavernicolous (Ref. 8593, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal species that feeds on fishes, octopi, and probably crustaceans.  Reported to be an aggressive species and prone to bite.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Murène panaméenne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intertidal zone up to 20 m in depth.  Inhabits rocky, crevice-rich and reef habitats.  Feeds mainly on fishes and crustaceans like crabs, lobsters and shrimps (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Murène poivrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats and rocky intertidal shorelines.  Feed on small fishes and crustaceans, sometimes leaving the water in pursuit of prey (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Simultaneous hermaphroditism is confirmed for this species (Ref. 103751).  Caught with various nets (Ref. 30573). Solitary (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène robuste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water and feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 3254).

species.name: Murène ruban
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lagoon and seaward reefs.  They are secretive species normally hidden in sand or rubble, sometimes with only its head protruding.  Feed on small fishes (Ref. 9710, 48635, 75154, 89972).  Juveniles all black, males have yellow dorsal fin and females change to a nearly all yellow color, but usually with blue in the posterior (Ref. 48635).  Only moray that undergoes abrupt changes in coloration and sex:  it is a protandrous hermaphrodite, i.e., functioning males reverse sex to become females.  Protandry is diagnosed based on colouration, but not confirmed (Ref. 103751).

species.name: Murène serpent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, shallow-water habitats.  Feeds on crustaceans, small shrimps and young crabs (Ref. 3254).

species.name: Murène tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) abundant in shallow rocky and grassy areas and on coral reefs; less common in turbid bays or harbors. Its bite is very dangerous (Ref. 5217).  Active during the day, sometimes together with other predators.  Feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 42064).  Usually seen with its head protruding from a hole and the rest of its body concealed (Ref. 26938).  Observed to be unusually aggressive towards man (Ref. 86997).  It has been traded as aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Murène tachetée (Uropterygius polystictus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare snake moray that has been collected on reef flats (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Murène tatouée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters, on coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 30573).  Simultaneous hermaphroditism is confirmed for this species (Ref. 103751).

species.name: Murène tigre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Found on sand and between rocks (Ref. 9324).  Extremely secretive.  Usually only seen at night (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène verte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic and solitary species (Ref. 26340) occurring along rocky shorelines, reefs, and mangroves (Ref. 3255).Usually found shallower than 30 m (Ref. 26938).  Due to its large size and aggressiveness, the bites of this moray are particularly dangerous (Ref. 3255).  Feeds mainly at night on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 42064).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 3255).  Large individuals are ciguatoxic (Ref. 3255).

species.name: Murène vibora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives between rocks in littoral pools.  Not frequently seen.  Feeds on crabs, lobsters and mollusks and possibly on other soft-bodied invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Murène vipérine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with strong surge such as benches, outer reef flats and reef fronts (Ref.  9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Very secretive during the day; feeds on fishes and octopi at night (Ref.  9710).  May bite by accident or when provoked.

species.name: Murène voie lactée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs from depths of 1 m to at least 36 m.  Prefers very shallow depth and juveniles often in intertidal zones (Ref. 30404).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Often seen hunting during low tide among partly exposed reefs (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on fishes, also on crustaceans, by day and probably also at night (Ref. 13550).  Caught with various nets (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène zébrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A secretive inhabitant of sandy and rocky bottoms, crevices and ledges of seaward reefs.  It feeds primarily on xanthid crabs, but also on other crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Benthic from 1-39 m, usually at <4 m (Ref. 58302).  Possibly a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32169).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Murène à bandes brunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear waters of lagoons and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Adults feed on fishes and crustaceans, mainly at night.  Nervous and aggressive (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène à bord blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms until at least 10 m in depth.

species.name: Murène à bord jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Along drop-offs (Ref. 48635). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Occurs in coral or rocky areas of reef flats and protected shorelines to seaward reefs. Feeds on cephalopods (Ref. 30573), fishes, and crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Most often appears on the reef after a fish has been speared during daylight. The regularity and promptness of such appearances make it clear that G. flavimarginatus is especially sensitive to stimuli emanating from an injured or stressed fish (Ref. 13550). Eaten in some parts of the Indo-Pacific (Ref. 12484). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797. Solitary and curious, usually seen with head protruding (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène à bordé blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Solitary in crevices, usually seen at night (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène à cou taché
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at reef flats and outer reef slopes to a depth of at least 20 m. Feeds on fishes, cephalopodes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).  Unlikely to be encountered without the use of ichthyocide (Ref. 1602, 37816, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Possibly a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32169). Common, but highly cryptic and seldom seen (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène à dents aiguillées
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits exposed seaward reefs to a depth of 14 m or more (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Solitary in crevices, rarely seen (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène à deux trous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand and between rocks (Ref. 9324).

species.name: Murène à longue queue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy ocean bottoms (Ref. 6934) and estuarine areas (Ref. 2334), but sometimes found in rivers (Ref. 2334) and inner bays (Ref. 37816).  Feeds mainly on a variety of small fishes and crustaceans.  Known to extend itself vertically from a burrow with its head held horizontally beneath the surface, rising and falling with the tide (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh and consumed locally (Ref. 3258). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Murène à pommettes noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear seaward reefs of oceanic islands to a depth over 25 m (Ref. 9710).  Common on reef walls and steep slopes with holes (Ref. 30404).  Inhabits porous coral rock which it shares with swarms of anthiases (Ref. 37816). Feeds on fishes and octopi (Ref. 89972). Territorial and will bite when provoked (Ref. 30404).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Murène à queue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9324).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Murène à taches blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep, rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses.  Constantly opens and closes its mouth, an action required for respiration, not a threat (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Murène à taches noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and outer reef slopes of continental reefs (Ref. 9710).  One of the two largest of Indo-Pacific morays.  Often in holes with cleaner wrasses or shrimps (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on cephalopods and small fishes (Ref. 30573).  Large adults may be aggressive (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Murène à tête jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons, reef flats and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602, 48635).  Prefers protected inshore waters among dead corals, common in harbors and small caves (Ref. 30404).  Probably nocturnal (Ref. 1602).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 9710).  Possibly a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32169).  Current age of a captive individual is 18 years, which exceeds 100 cm and approximately 10 lbs (owner Mark Palermo, pers. comm. 07/12).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Murène étoilée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between rocks and corals of intertidal reef flats, also in shallow lagoon and seaward reefs to depths of at least 10 m (Ref. 9710, 58302). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Nocturnal (Ref. 68964).  Feed mainly on crustaceans.  Protogynous hermaphroditism unconfirmed for this species (Ref. 84746). Safely kept with small aquarium fishes (Ref. 9710). Solitary, seen usually in the open or with only head exposed (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Muscadine Darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Percina smithvanizi is a relatively common darter in undisturbed streams above the Fall Line in the Tallapoosa River. However, it has disappeared in disturbed streams and impoundments associated with mainstream dams on the Tallapoosa River. It has also disappeared from most of the headwaters of the Little Tallapoosa River in Georgia. The species was regarded as vulnerable by Freeman et al. (2005).

species.name: Muscat dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Muscat sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Museau noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over sand in clear vegetated lakes and pools of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Mushroom goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarely enters freshwaters (Ref. 26334).  Inhabits inshore habitats, brackish lagoons, estuaries and lower part of large rivers; usually associated with rock bottom or sunken trees.  Spawns at 2 years, from December to April where females can repeat spawning during a season.  Feeds mostly on crustaceans (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Mushroom scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits primarily offshore islands and infrequently caught in continental waters (Ref. 5521).  Also found in clear water over sand and turtle grass; less common around coral reefs (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Mushroom-coral pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs, usually along the bottom of shallow drop-offs, and in small groups on the solitary coral. Apparently commensal with solitary corals (e.g. Fungia echinata). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also found among tentacles of mushroom corals (often Heliofungia actiniformes ) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Mussel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky areas (Ref. 37955), inhabiting holes and crevices, often in burrows of boring clams or tubes of marine worms, also in mussel beds (Ref. 2850).  Mostly sedentary and territorial (Ref. 2850).  Demersal spawners in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Musso carite
species.description: Adults are found in shallow coastal waters in small schools, generally near the bottom (Ref. 9283).  They feed on squid, small crabs, small fishes and polychaetes (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Musso corcovade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow coastal waters in small schools near the bottom (Ref. 9283).  They feed on small squids, shrimps, polychaetes and small fishes (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 9283). Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Musso lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over continental shelves (Ref. 5217).  No real fishery (Ref. 51310).  Edibility not known (Ref. 51310).

species.name: Musso pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal waters up to at least 50 m depth (Ref. 9283).  They generally form schools near the bottom (Ref. 9283).  Juveniles are encountered near the surface (Ref. 9283).  They feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Mustelus minicanis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Mustèle arctique à trois barb.
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic; feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Mutant wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes over rubble with patches of live coral (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Muzzled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal and brackish waters among rocks and mangroves (Ref. 9710).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Highly tolerant to adverse environmental conditions, self-reproducing population living between rocks in natural  oil seeps in Venezuela (Ref. 56126).

species.name: Mweru hump-backed bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds mainly on insects and their larvae, but also (in small quantities) on crustaceans and molluscs (Ref. 52307).  Maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 52346) that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307). Marked intolerance to oxygen lack (Ref. 246).

species.name: Mya Than Tun’s perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mya's klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal areas.

species.name: Myaka
species.description: Genre de poissons. Prefers open water regions at greater depths, but ventures into the more shallow areas of the lake for spawning, which normally occurs during the rainy season; mainly feeds on phytoplankton and small insects; probably ovophilic mouthbrooder; males occupy a tertitory of ca. 50 cm and it is often possible to find large numbers of males in a limited area (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Myctophum fissunovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic; nyctoepipelagic at the surface.

species.name: Myctophum lychnobium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neustonic to mesopelagic at 1 m and greater depths (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Myctophum ovcharovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myer's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral and rubble habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Myers mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myers' icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on fishes (Pleuragramma antarcticum) and euphausiids (Euphausia crystallorophias). Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 52020).

species.name: Myers' pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from young and juvenile specimens.

species.name: Myersglanis jayarami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myersina papuanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myersina yangii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylesinus paraschomburgkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylesinus paucisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylesinus schomburgkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myleus altipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myleus knerii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myleus latus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myleus micans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myleus pacu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed essentially on Podostemaceae (Lacis), more rarely on seeds (Caladium). During the rainy season, they undertake grand migrations to small creeks to reproduce (Ref. 12225). An important food fish. Possesses powerful dentition that can cause serious bites.

species.name: Myleus setiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylochromis anaphyrmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on sandy coasts and prefers that portion of the sandy coast where a thin layer of silt supports a rich fauna of snails (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis balteatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives over open sand in shallow water.  Feeds on invertebrates that are taken from the sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis chekopae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, sandy shores; in shallower part of range it is the most abundant species; feeds on cladocerans, copepods and algae (Ref. 41276).

species.name: Mylochromis ensatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy shores; rare species (Ref. 41276). Feeds on invertebrates found in the sand (Ref. 79521).

species.name: Mylochromis epichorialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocks at preferred depths of 0 to at least 30 m.  Have been observed feeding on crabs and from the sediment on the rocks (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis ericotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy substrate.  Feeds on invertebrates and probably on phytoplankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis formosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not always seen in sandy areas.  Feeds predominantly on small fishes and invertebrates.  Occurs singly, males are territorial (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dwells in sandy bottoms and feeds from the sediment layer on the substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis labidodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers shallow sandy areas with the bottom covered partly with small rocks and pebbles.  Feeds by turning small stones and checking what is underneath (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Mylochromis melanotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy shores with Vallisneria (Ref. 267).

species.name: Mylochromis mola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water off sandy beaches and feeds on mollusks (Ref. 267).

species.name: Mylochromis obtusus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylochromis plagiotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylochromis semipalatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylochromis spilostichus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy substrate.  Piscivorous.  Feeds by chasing fish close to the substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Myloplus arnoldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus asterias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus levis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus lobatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus lucienae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in rapids, but is also recorded for slow-flowing habitats such as backwaters and lakes (Ref. 114774).

species.name: Myloplus planquettei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus ternetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers lentic waters where the river banks are steep.  Feeds on the leaves of river plants.  During the short rainy season, a third of its diet  consists of flowers and seeds which they find in the flood zones of the forest (Ref. 12225).  The small larvae are zooplanktivores.  Reproduction is asynchronous and lasts year round.  However, spawning frequency is clearly higher during the rainy season.  Is a likely candidate for fish breeding studies (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Myloplus tiete
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Myloplus torquatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylossoma acanthogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Mylossoma albiscopum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.
