species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers open water in the mainstream and backwaters where it feeds on zooplankton and aquatic insects (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Namib happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sandy habitats with vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52307).

species.name: Nandus andrewi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nandus meni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives in the freshwater ecosystem of Noakhali and is widely distributed in ponds, ditches, canals, flooded rice fields, swamps, marshes, waterlogged areas and rivers. A very tenacious species that can live in foul water and a surface dweller that consumes insects, algae and small fish. Breeding period varies from April to September. During the study period, the physicochemical parameters were recorded as follows: water temperature 18-28 °C, pH 6.5-7.5, dissolved oxygen 4.5-5.0 mg/l and transparency 45-60 cm for a water body 1.0-1.8 m deep. In the study area, it represents 15-20% of the total Nandus catch (Ref. 93873).

species.name: Nandus mercatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nandus oxyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in swamps and sluggish waters (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Nandus prolixus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nangra bucculenta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nangra nangra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper reaches of  rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Nangra ornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nangra robusta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannacara adoketa
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae. Collected from a small stream in inundable forest.  Surface water temperature  was 24°C, dissolved oxygen 1.8 mg/l and maximum depth was 28 cm.  Maximum length 10 cm TL (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Nannacara bimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannacara quadrispinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannacara taenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannaethiops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinguished from Neolebias by its always complete lateral line (Ref. 2936). Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Nannaethiops bleheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax altus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum SL recorded is 37 mm (Ref. 81638).

species.name: Nannocharax angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.7 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 4.6 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax dageti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 7.8 cm (Ref. 7094). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 13614).

species.name: Nannocharax fasciolaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax hadros
species.description: Found in a shallow water zone with a high current over the rocky substrate (Ref. 127100)

species.name: Nannocharax hastatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax hollyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax latifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax lineomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax lineostriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.5 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax luapulae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax maculicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax micros
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax minutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.3 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax monardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax niloticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 5.2 cm (Ref. 7094).  Occurs in running water with vegetation (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Nannocharax occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax ocellicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 4.2 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax procatopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 13614).

species.name: Nannocharax pteron
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax reidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax rubensteini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax rubrolabiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under rocks, in riffles of moderately large rivers (30-50m) in the savannah zone, in areas where there is a strong current (>1m/sec); in all sites where collection took place, there was a rather restricted gallery of shrubs and small trees on the river banks; water was greenish with a transparency of about 50 cm, neutral pH (6.5-7.5), with a high content of dissolved oxygen (6.5-7.5 mg/l) and a rather low conductivity (35-45 µS/cm); water temperatures were between 23 and 25 °C at noon (Ref. 26632).

species.name: Nannocharax schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax signifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a narrow forest stream with dense vegetation on its banks and with bottom substrate of mud, sand, leaves, roots and drift wood; also found in larger streams with only spare vegetation in the form of small bushes and solitary trees and with bottom substrate consisting mainly of sand and gravel (Ref. 85591).

species.name: Nannocharax taenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax uniocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.4 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Nannocharax usongo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens collected on logs in areas of relatively rapid water movement; logs had a very rugged surface due to being partially decomposed by wood eating Povilla (Ephemeroptera) larvae; individuals were spaced singly and moved very rapidly around log surface, but always with close contact to it and never reaching out into the free water column; first ray of pelvic fin very thick, which is adaptation to cling on wood in strong current; mouth subinferior and blunt (Ref. 80507).

species.name: Nannocharax wittei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannocharax zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens collected inshore in areas of relatively calm water among fine twigs of a fallen tree; these twigs were not reaching soil, but remained attached to the crown of the fallen tree and reaching into the free water column; specimens sometimes rested on the fine twigs, but mostly were seen moving or hovering in the free water column in a water depth of aproximately 50-100 cm, well above the bottom which consisted of leaflitter, sand and fine detritus (Ref. 80507).

species.name: Nannochorax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannochorax (Nannocharax ogoensis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannoglanis fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannopetersius ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannopetersius lamberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannopetersius mutambuei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannoplecostomus eleonorae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type-locality, the Rio da Lapa, is a moderately sized (8-12 meters wide), fast-flowing, clear-water river, with a predominantly rocky bottom, running across the savannah-like cerrado vegetation.  Also known in the São Domingos karst area, situated immediately below the river resurgences of several tributaries of the Rio São Domingos, including the Rio da Lapa.  Not recorded within the subterranean river stretches (Ref. 92524).

species.name: Nannoptopoma spectabile
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannoptopoma sternoptychum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannosalarias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found solitary or in small groups in seaward reef crests and outer reef slopes in exposed shallow reef fronts subject to mild to moderate surge (Ref. 48636, 90102).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 2 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Nannostomus anduzei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannostomus erythrurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannostomus grandis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannostomus marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Nannostomus mortenthaleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannostomus nigrotaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannostomus rubrocaudatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nannoxyropsis acicula
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Collected from clear to blackwater creeks with moderate water current, bottom composed
of stones, gravel and mud or clay in parts, and moderate amounts of marginal vegetation (Ref. 116855).

species.name: Nannoxyropsis ephippia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small to medium-sized streams with moderate current and riparian forest, water ranges from moderately turbid (e.g., Essequibo mainstem), to clear (Yuora), to black (Burro Burro).  Most of the collecting localities are composed of a variety of substrates with sand being particularly common (Ref. 110244).

species.name: Nanobagrus armatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanobagrus fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanobagrus immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanobagrus lemniscatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanobagrus nebulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Nanobagrus stellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanobagrus torquatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanocheirodon insignis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on mosquito larvae (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Nanochromis consortus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Nanochromis minor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanochromis nudiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Nanochromis parilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large numbers in areas with slowly-flowing waters along the banks of the Congo River near Brazzaville and Kinshasa; does not seem to prefer the more rapidly-flowing parts of the river, even though Roberts & Stewart (1976) viewed it as a moderately rheophilic species (Ref. 52307). Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020). Cave-spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Nanochromis splendens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanochromis teugelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nanochromis transvestitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-spawner (Ref. 52307). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Nanochromis wickleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at sandy beach interspersed with flat laterite terraces; 1-2 m deep (Ref. 57505).

species.name: Nansen goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia ahlstromi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotype which is about 9.5 cm SL is an adult bearing eggs (Ref. 5123).

species.name: Nansenia atlantica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia boreacrassicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia iberica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic.  Three specimens known (2 females, 1 damaged) (Ref. 36163).

species.name: Nansenia indica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Nansenia macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species.

species.name: Nansenia megalopa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A specimen of 12.65 cm SL had ripe ovarian eggs (Ref. 5123).

species.name: Nansenia oblita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns during winter in the Mediterranean.

species.name: Nansenia obscura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia pelagica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Nansenia tenera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nansenia tenuicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Naoko's Fairy Wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narc angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed within interstices of cracks and caves along vertical drop-offs at depths below 100 m.  Natural diet is unknown but accepts a wide range of food (Ref. 26238).  Forms pairs or small groups.  Almost never exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Narcine westraliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Feeds on benthic worms and other invertebrates (Ref. 6871).  Reaches maturity at ca. 18 cm TL (Ref. 114953); size at birth 7 cm (Ref. 6871).  Taken by prawn fishers (Ref. 6871). Occasionally caught as trawl bycatch (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Narcinops ornata
species.description: A benthic species found offshore on mid-continental shelf. Reaches maturity at ca. 18 cm TL.  Biology little known (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Narcissus pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in patch reefs on sandy rubble (Ref. 123182).

species.name: Narino toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrow barred grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds.

species.name: Narrow striped rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrow worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in tide pools and mangrove swamps (Ref. 637). Also seen in sand bottoms near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Narrow-barred butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are similar to adults.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Narrow-body righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Narrow-headed Altai osman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently similar to other piscivirous form of Altai osman with individuals having a long life duration (more than 40 years); reaching maturity at 8-9 years at body length of 20-24 cm. The young feed on plankton with fish as predominant food in the diet of the adults. Spawning occurs in May and June, with eggs laid on the sand, pebble, vegetation (spawning time and place partly coincide with O. potanini (Ref. 57727).

species.name: Narrow-lined puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy substrates, usually shallow coastal slopes to about 20 meters depth and in shallow estuaries (Ref. 48637).  Occurs in estuaries, sheltered reef flats, and lagoons to a depth of more than 17 m.  Common in seagrass beds and sandy areas; juveniles found among mangroves (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Narrow-lined siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations among crinoids (Ref 90102).

species.name: Narrow-mouthed Natron tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It inhabits the springs and some spring-fed creeks near the southern and south-eastern shores of Lake Natron (Ref. 32272). It co-occurs with Alcolapia alcalicus and Alcolapia latilabris (Ref. 32272). Observed to nibble at stones and gravel, probably taking mainly algae for food; omnivorous, taking insects from the water surface as well (Ref. 32272). A maternal mouthbrooder: males defend spawning territories among rocks in shallow water (Ref. 32272, 118638). Potential as an aquarium fish (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Narrow-tail goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrowbanded sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The following observations were reported for this species: adept at burrowing beneath the sand and swims beneath the sand; adults spend the winter months in moderately deep water, gradually move to shallower water in spring and on reaching maturity during summer months, collect in the vicinity of river mouths, where they spawn; the young, as soon as the yolk-sac is absorbed, make their way into the estuaries and gradually work up these even to far beyond the limit of the tide (e.g. in Hunter River); considered a delicious pan-fish, equal in flavor to Solea solea; prefers shellfish and worms that live on and in the substrate (Ref. 57560).

species.name: Narrowbar reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Narrowbar swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrowbody Handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrowfront tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and smaller streams, usually where currents are relatively swift (Ref. 5259).  Also lives in still or gently flowing water of pools and side channels. A solitary species (Ref. 44894).  Feed on mollusks, insects, prawns (Ref. 5259, 44894) crustaceans and worms (Ref. 44894).  Spawning period coincides with the rise of the monsoonal floods (Ref. 38147, 44894).  Adults migrate upstream into shallow riffle zones where they spawn in pairs.  The demersal eggs lodge in crevices on the bottom and hatch 2-3 days later (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Narrowhead catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Narrownape barbelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic inhabitant of sand-rubble bottoms next to reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Narrownecked oceanic eel
species.description: Meso- to bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on small fishes and crustaceans.  Eggs and leptocephali are planktonic (Ref. 35591).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Narrowtail moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in less than 0.5 m (Ref. 10713). Usually in sand and mud bottoms to at least 15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Narrowtail stingray
species.description: The depth occupied by this species is unknown as most material were collected in fish markets, but probably mainly coastal.  A 69.5 cm DW adult male  weighed ca 12 kg.  Size at birth apparently variable;  83.0 cm DW female delivered a full term embryo  with small umbilical scar; however, other retained specimens, 26.1 cm DW still had a substantial yolk sac, while in another 19.3 cm DW  specimen the umbilical scar was barely visible.  All these young specimens have large mid-scapular tubercles and well-developed denticles over most of the dorsal disc; a small embryo with yolk sac (16.5 cm DW) had prominent mid-scapular tubercles, but other denticles are just starting to form on the disc (Ref. 84288).

species.name: Naru eagle ray
species.description: Found in shallow waters at water temperature above 15-17°C; in winter months, the species leave the shallower bays for nearby sea where water temperature is above 15°C brought by the Kuroshio current-derived warm waters (Ref. 94821).

species.name: Nasal-bar pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptobenthic, epibenthic. Collected on drop-offs, either sloping or vertical with caves. Apparently tends to congregate in loose schools close to the shelter of caves and sea fans, to which they retreat when approached, and seem to be most abundant at about 20 meter depth range. Often form mixed schools with Trimma tevegae (Ref. 55345).

species.name: Nasal-flap moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at night in coral reef habitat at a depth of 18 m (Ref. 123128).

species.name: Nasca bigeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens collected along rocky drop-offs or taken by hook and line at undetermined depths over bottoms of about 240 m.

species.name: Nascent membranehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Maximum depth from Ref. 106682.

species.name: Naseux des rapides
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits rubble and gravel riffles (sometimes runs and pools) of fast creeks and small to medium rivers as well as rocky shores of lakes (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Young up to 4 months are pelagic (Ref. 1998).  Form schools (Ref. 1998).  Feeds on mayflies, blackflies, and midges (Ref. 1998).  Spawns over pits in loose gravel substrate (Ref. 51972).  Widely used as bait in the USA (Ref. 1998).  Artificially propagated in Minnesota, USA in long narrow ponds having weak water flow (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Naseux léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing pools and gravel runs of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Also occurs in rocky margins of lakes (Ref. 86798).  Young-of-the-year feed mostly on dipterous larvae; yearlings feed on aquatic insect larvae (mostly Ephemeroptera and <i>Diptera) during the months of June and July switching to terrestrial insects in September; adults more than 2 years also feed on aquatic insect larvae, (Ephemeroptera and Diptera), terrestrial insects, and earthworms (Lumbricus) displaced from the soil (Ref. 1998).  Spawning occurs early July (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Naseux moucheté
species.description: Espèce de poisson. Occurs in rocky riffles, runs and pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers; rarely in lakes (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Naseux noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294, 86798).  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 54729, 10294), diatoms and other algae (Ref. 54725).  Considered as an attractive aquarium pet and propagation through artificial fertilization is practical (Ref. 54725).

species.name: Nash's barb
species.description: Inhabits large hill streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Nasique à éperons oranges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal and sheltered reef flats in small groups and schools in oceanic locations (Ref. 48637). Also found in rocky bottoms in about 5-30 m (Ref. 90102). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 37792).

species.name: Naso maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic and mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Naso tergus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species feeds on benthic crustaceans and bivalves, indicating that this fish feeds on marine organisms living on the sea floor.  Caught by bottom gill-net and hook and line at  70-80 m depth (Ref. 87782).

species.name: Nason bossu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep coastal, usually in small groups but occasionally in large schools (Ref. 48637). Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102). An uncommon species found in seaward reef slopes (Ref. 9710, 48637), also along rocky shores (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  Caught with nets (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Nason jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reef slopes (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Usually seen in large schools (Ref. 90102). Mainly diurnal, it feeds on zooplankton such as crab larvae, arrow worms, pelagic tunicates, and occasionally filamentous red algae.  The species is never poisonous (Ref. 4795).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Nason loupe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 37792).  Feeds on leafy or fleshy algae and zooplankton (Ref. 37792).  Found singly or in small groups (Ref. 37792).

species.name: Nason à gros nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep lagoon and seaward reefs.  Found forming loose schools along upper regions of deep drop-offs (Ref. 48637).  Forms mid-water aggregations off steep slopes during the day to feed on zooplankton.  Usually found alone or in pairs.  Omnivorous.  Has the ability to show or hide its blue markings (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Nason à rostre long
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles occur in clear, shallow lagoon reefs at depths as little as 1 m; adults rarely seen in less than 25 m, encountered off outer reef drop-offs in small schools (Ref. 30573, 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on large zooplankton during the day and shelter within the reef during the night; also benthic algae (Ref. 30573, 48637).

species.name: Nason à éperons oranges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas of coral, rock, or rubble of lagoon and seaward reefs, Ref. 48637. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Adults usually in small groups. Juveniles in shallow rocky reefs, sometimes in small aggregations mixed with other acanthurids of similar size (Ref. 48637). Feed mainly on leafy brown algae (Sargassum and Dictyota). Sometimes in large aggregations (Ref. 37792). Very seldom poisonous (Ref. 4795). Pair-spawning has been observed.

species.name: Natal anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal, pelagic and schooling species; its presence in estuaries suggests that it can tolerate brackish water (Ref. 189). It is common along shore and in estuaries (Ref. 5430). It feeds on plankton, mainly copepods (Ref. 58304). It spawns in summer, usually at sea (Ref. 58304).

species.name: Natal angler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on fishes (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Natal dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near large boulders or lying still against greenish weed.

species.name: Natal duckbill
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Natal electric ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer shelf and upper slope (Ref. 5578). Life history unknown. Males reaches maturity at ca. 17 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Natal fingerfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters from the shore line to at least 20 m depth (Ref. 9492).  Prefers rocky banks (Ref. 12484).  Diurnal (Ref. 12484).  Feeds mainly on small, benthic invertebrates (marine worms, crabs and mollusks), but also squid and small fish (Ref. 12484).  Mainly caught with spears (Ref. 9492).  Marketed fresh, whole (Ref. 9492).

species.name: Natal flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud bottoms; probably a small species.

species.name: Natal knifejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal rocky and coral reefs to a depth of 100 m; juveniles pelagic in currents (Ref. 4332).  Benthic omnivores. May live longer than 10 years. Spawning occurs throughout the year (Ref. 57746).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9660).

species.name: Natal mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among cobbles and rocks in swiftly flowing water (Ref. 52193). Active at night, feeding on benthic stream invertebrates such as mayfly and midge larvae (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer (Ref. 52193). Iteroparous, with asynchronous ovarian development (Ref. 51405). Preyed upon by trout and is now scarce in certain streams (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Natal rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in groups or solitary in the intertidal zone of rocky shorelines (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Natal sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore and offshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Natal snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Natal tongue-fish
species.description: Inhabits shallow waters (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Natal topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore vegetated areas of lakes and well-vegetated streams (Ref. 52193). It feeds on aquatic insects, such as mosquito larvae and algae (Ref. 52193). A serial spawner, laying eggs on vegetation (Ref. 52193). Potential mosquito control agent (Ref. 7248). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Natal weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nato
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and rivers (Ref. 41640).

species.name: Natterer's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably riverine or estuarine.  More material and data needed.

species.name: Naude's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons and seaward reefs; on rubble and reef rock (Ref. 1602); also over coral patches interspaced with fine sandy bottoms, occasionally form small schools (Ref. 37688).  Feeds on copepods, ostracods, and radiolarians (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Nautla cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fast-flowing river over stony bottom, or slower stream, with pH 7.4, dGH 5, KH 6, 26C.

species.name: Navigobius dewa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An epibenthic species found in sandy and muddy bottoms on the steep slope. Adults form epibenthic schools, comprising 10-300 individuals (in Kagoshima Bay) (Ref. 83368).

species.name: Nazas chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nazas pupfish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nazas shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nazas sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ncheni type haplochromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water (Ref. 5595, 55954) and prefers sandy bottoms, also with vegetation (Ref. 5595).  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Neamia xenica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neblinichthys brevibracchium
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neblinichthys echinasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neblinichthys peniculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found  rio Carapo with rapids complex. Collected from 100 m above the lower extent of the rapids as well as a rapids complex further upstream (Ref. 93221).

species.name: Neblinichthys pilosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neblinichthys roraima
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from creeks with substratum of rocks, small stones, and fine sand, without aquatic vegetation.

species.name: Neblinichthys yaravi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nebulous dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coral reefs to about 10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Nebulous snake eel
species.description: Inhabits sand and weed bottoms, also in tidepools (Ref 90102).

species.name: Neck banded blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in calcified polychaete tubes (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Nectamia zebrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Needle toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An insectivorous fish which lives in waters of low to moderate current velocity, rarely in strong current, from 3-540 m elevation; in temperatures 23-32°C.  Inhabits midwater or near the surface in brooks and creeks; sometimes in shallow waters of large rivers (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Needlespine coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from coral-enclosed area and reef bordering eel-grass flat (Ref. 13690). Also found among branches of hard corals including Echinopora horrida, E.mammiformis and Hydnophora rigida (Ref 90102).

species.name: Needletooth cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Neglected triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at depths of 7 m and shallower, in surge channels and exposed coasts of rocky boulders (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Negros pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud and reef flats (Ref. 205); benthic (Ref. 75154).  Solitary, in pairs or small groups in sea crevices or sheltering among sea urchin spines (Ref 90102).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Negros sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected on sand in 4.5-15 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Nehu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic (Ref. 58302).  A schooling species living close inshore and entering bays, inlets, estuaries, canals and even penetrating into fish ponds, thus able to tolerate a wide range of salinities.  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustacean larvae.  Breeds throughout the year, with a peak in summer, spawning at night (between 2200 and 0200 hours) in bays and estuaries (Ref. 189).

species.name: Neighbor portholefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species collected by commercial mid-water trawl (Ref. 121634).

species.name: Neil's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in small, well-shaded, slow-flowing streams with mixed sand, silt and rock bottoms; also in deeper rocky pools in gorges.  Water is typically fresh and clear, between 21° and 28° C, with a neutral or slightly basic pH (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Neiva
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neko-gigi
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are guarded by the male (Ref. 45232).

species.name: Nelson's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  More data needed.

species.name: Nemacheilus anguilla
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Nemacheilus arenicolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Usually associated with sandy substrate with moderate current (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Nemacheilus banar
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Adult specimens have been collected in fast-flowing rivers with rock or large-sized gravel substratum; juveniles from sandy substratum in moderate current.

species.name: Nemacheilus binotatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits streams with moderate to strong current over sandy or pebble substrate.  Feeds on may-flies.  Observed to form small  troops of up to 20 individuals above the substrate around large rocks.  This is in contrast with most of the nemacheilines which live solitary under stones.  A female measuring 4.16 cm SL with distended belly and ripe ovulae, about 0.7 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Nemacheilus chrysolaimos
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Nemacheilus cleopatra
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits fast flowing water on open sand substratum.

species.name: Nemacheilus corica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear waters, hill streams with sandy bottom (Ref. 1479).  Collected in a large river with high, turbid monsoon flow and with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).

species.name: Nematolebias papilliferus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small freshwater temporary pools, 10-40 m of diameter, about 50 cm deep, in floodplains of streams and lagoons or along the vast floodplains of lower rio São João, which are sometimes close to the sea (about 100 m).  Substrate of compact, soft reddish brown mud; water hyaline, yellow or dark orange brown, usually not turbid.  These pools are dry twice a year, once during winter, usually from July to August, and again during summer, usually from February to March.  During dry season, all fish die and eggs undergo in diapause within the substrate.  Eclosion happens at the onset of wet season, usually March-April and September-October  (Ref. 42934).

species.name: Nembwe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles occur mostly on the floodplain and in lagoons and secondary channels, but larger adults appear to prefer mainstream habitats, like deep main channels and permanent lagoons,and are associated with in-stream structures such as woody debris, macrophyte beds, reeds, and eroded clay cliffs on outside bends of the rivers (Ref. 7248, 94654, 128638). Large specimens patrol open water of rivers and lakes, never very far from shore (Ref. 246) and live in well-vegetated quiet waters or near submerged trees or rocks in the lee of the river’s main current, lunging out to capture prey (Ref. 5614). Predator on fish but also feeds on aquatic and terrestrial insects, shrimps and small crabs (Ref. 13337). Adults often feed on squeakers (Ref. 7248, 13337, 94654). Mouthbrooder (Ref. 246, 13337, 13721) and multiple spawner (Ref. 13337). Constructs shallow nest on sandy or muddy substrate in shallow water (Ref. 13337). Reported to have adverse impact on native fish species in Zimbabwe (Ref. 94654).

species.name: Neolamprologus bifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at depths from 30 to 45 metres (Ref. 93973). Rarely found in water shallower than 30 metres (Ref. 46829, 93973). Most often found at bottom edge of rocky habitat where it meets the sandy/muddy substrate; most often seen solitary (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Neolamprologus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on plankton (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus brichardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Plankton feeder (Ref. 54948).  Breeding pair establishes its territory which is defended in a joint effort (Ref. 7343).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Neolamprologus buescheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at depths greater than 20 metres, but some specimens found in water as shallow as 10 metres; cave brooder and cave dweller, rarely venturing more than 30 cm from its cave; frequently several individuals can be seen together (Ref. 46829). Mainly feeds on insect larvae (chironomids), but some other invertebrates are eaten as well (Ref. 94007). Forms pairs but strict bonds are not observed in captivity; when spawning in captivity, this species defends a small territory by aggressively chasing away intruders (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus cancellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallow (2-7 m depth), rocky bottom (Ref. 56628).

species.name: Neolamprologus caudopunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers above the substrate to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 7343).  Needs sand to build its nest.  Forms a protecting and warning group of sexually inactive individuals around the breeding community (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus chitamwebwai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Highly stenotopic, restricted to rocky habitat; occurs in exposed parts of rocky shores, with large boulders (1-2 m in diameter) on a steep slope, with some sand in between the stones, and no bivalve shell accumulations or other rubble present; presence of sand is mandatory; water with high visibility and low sedimentation rates; most common at depth between 10 and 20 m; strong site fidelity and small home range; ingests sediment and spits it out through mouth (Ref. 74422).

species.name: Neolamprologus christyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rather common in habitats where rocks border larger stretches of sand, normally in water with a depth of less than 10 metres (Ref. 46829). In captivity, this species is an aggressive cichlid which can be only kept with larger or very active tank mates (Ref. 7343). Feeds on invertebrates like crustaceans, small mollusks, worms and insect larvae (Ref. 7343, 46829).

species.name: Neolamprologus crassus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus cunningtoni
species.description: Usually solitary.  Prefers to swim close to the sand bottom.  Digs large crater-shaped nests, even when there are rocks offering good shelters nearby, fact that shows that the choice of a nest site can be very revealing of a species ecology.  Carnivorous, preys on fish (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Neolamprologus cylindricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers shallow, rocky habitats; in the recesses of the rocky biotope (Ref. 7343, 46829). Normally found in the upper 10 m of this biotope (Ref. 46829). Feeds on invertebrates such as shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 46829), in the biocover or in the recesses of the substrate (Ref. 7343, 46829). Solitary (Ref. 46829). Substrate spawner; raises fry in seclusion (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus devosi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gut contents included some detritus, freshwater shrimps, ostracods, and soft bodies of snails (Ref. 50569).

species.name: Neolamprologus falcicula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not rock-bound, may migrate through the very shallow waters of the lake.  Although the gut contents indicate a shrimp menu, this species has been known to ambush young cichlids.  A substrate spawner which has often been observed to spawn in empty snail shells found on the sand floor (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus furcifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary; lives in dark recesses of rocky habitat; moves on vertical sides of large rocks or on undersides of overhanging rocks with belly very close to substrate and using large pectoral fins; feeds on macro-invertebrates like crustaceans and insect larvae which are found in the slits, cracks, holes and crevices of their habitat (Ref. 7343, 46829). Always observed in shady parts of rocks; might be nocturnal; large eyes may be adaptation for enhanced night vision (Ref. 95525).

species.name: Neolamprologus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus helianthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers the shallow, rocky habitat; maintains close contact with rocky substrate; adults do not form schools; omnivorous (Ref. 47158).

species.name: Neolamprologus leleupi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in the recesses of the biotope.  Feeds on invertebrates found in the biocover or in deep recesses of the substrate (Ref. 7343).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Neolamprologus leloupi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus longicaudatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Present in the rocky habitats (Ref. 46829) at a depth of 12-15 m (Ref. 28629). Most often found solitary; feeds on invertebrates, seen more often outside caves of the rocky substrate than N. buescheri (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Neolamprologus longior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus marunguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the rocky habitat (Ref. 46829, 93978), at a depth of 25-35 m (Ref. 93978).

species.name: Neolamprologus modestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary although many individuals may be observed at one time. Feeds on small snails that specifically live on the biocover (Chytra kirki, Spekia zonata, Paramelania demoni and Tanganycia rufofilosa). Also feeds on the eggs of the killifish, Lamprichthys tanganicanus. Leaves the rocky biotope to breed in the sandy bottom (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus mondabu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary although many individuals may be observed at one time. Occurs in the rocky biotopes. Feeds on the eggs of Lamprichthys tanganicanus. Leaves the rocky biotope to breed in the sandy bottom (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus multifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shell-dweller; each individual has its own shell.  Congregates in large groups but stay as pairs in very small territories.  Pairs have their shells very close together.  Feeds on plankton that slowly pass by above the colony (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus mustax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates found on the biocover or in deep recesses of the substrate.  Substrate spawner, raises its in seclusion (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the crevices of the sediment-rich biotope.  Feeds on mollusks which are crushed with the pharyngeal bones (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus nigriventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intermediate habitat, which consists of a sandy bottom with numerous rocks (Ref. 46829, 93979). Occurs at depths from 15 to 45 metres and maintains close contact with rocky substrate (Ref. 93979). Crustaceans, insect larvae, copepods, snail fragments, algal strands and sand grains were found in stomach (Ref. 46829, 93979). Highly developed lateral line system as an optimized method of prey detection (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Neolamprologus obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the crevices of the sediment-rich rocky biotope (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus olivaceous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Moderately gregarious; usually a few fish found together (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Neolamprologus pectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is not very colorful (Ref. 12251). Lives in the intermediate habitat, which is characterized by a sandy bottom with numerous rocks; maintains close contact with rocky substrate; ventral part of body remains just few millimeters above substrate while fish follows contours of rock; rare cichlid; occurs at dephts deeper than 15 m; highly developed lateral line system for prey detection (Ref. 46829). Crustaceans, insect larvae, copepods, snail fragments, plant material and sand grains found in stomach (Ref. 46829, 93980).

species.name: Neolamprologus petricola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The stomach of one specimen was observed to contain insect larvae (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus pleuromaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Breeds in caves in captivity (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus prochilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs deep down the rocky slope (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus pulcher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sediment-rich regions.  Breeds in pairs, with both male and female defending the territory in a joint effort (Ref. 7343).  About 20-60 eggs are produced and deposited in crevices (Ref. 36877).

species.name: Neolamprologus savoryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the sediment-rich regions.  Congregates in groups (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus schreyeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shy, rock-dwelling species, living deep inside rock crevices; never seen in the open; spend all of their time hiding (Ref. 6770). Usually found at levels deeper than 20 m (Ref. 46829). Lives in the crevices of the sediment-rich rocky biotope; its enlarged molar-shaped teeth indicate a diet of hard substances (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus sexfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The contents of the intestines which were examined indicate a carnivorous diet (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with large shell beds; also found among rubble of rocky habitats but only at deeper levels (deeper than 25 m); around shell beds species can be found as shallow as 10 metres (Ref. 46829). Maximal depth is 45 metres (Ref. 93981). Prefers shells to holes created by piling up pebbles and small stones; almost always found in colonies; spawning takes place inside the femal's shell (Ref. 46829). Copepods, ostracods, insect larvae, algal strands and sand grain found in stomach (Ref. 93981).

species.name: Neolamprologus splendens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolamprologus timidus
species.description: This shy species is observed at depths varying from 2 to 40 m in a dark rocky biotope, and encountered in pairs defending a territory over a dark cave difficult to access; the territory was often located to a large rock or boulder, which, if large enough was inhabited also by other species like Neolamprologus furcifer and Julidochromis regani; almost always found upside down in cave with belly close to substrate (Ref. 95525).

species.name: Neolamprologus toae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds at night on insect larvae (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Neolamprologus tretocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rock-dweller (Ref. 6770). Occurs in the intermediate habitat (Ref. 46829). Caught at depths between 1 and 10 m; average depth is 5.15 m (Ref. 53528). Feeds mostly from the sandy substrate in areas characterized by small rock and pebbles (Ref. 46829). Its prey consists of invertebrates that live in the sand (Ref. 52921). Eats insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 46829), but also feeds on snails (Ref. 6770, 7343, 46829). Has strong teeth on the lower pharyngeal bone, typical of a snail-crushing cichlid (Ref. 52921).

species.name: Neolamprologus ventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs above substrate consisting of sand, detritus and mud; also found in terrace-like edges and recesses in rock faces, between large rocks and in rock failures (Ref. 93985). Most often seen solitary and at bottom edge of rocky habitat where it meets the sandy/muddy substrate; rarely found in waters shallower than 30 metres (Ref. 46829). Has been observed at a depth of 60 m; copepods, insect larvae, algae, sand and snail remnants have been found in stomach  (Ref. 93985).

species.name: Neolamprologus walteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Highly stenotopic, restricted to rocky habitat and prefers sheltered areas; habitat features gentle slopes with small stones or rubble, cemented by calcite, with fine sediment in spaces between rubble, and stones with stromatolite growth; often associated with bivalve shell accumulations covering large areas (always Pleiodon spekii), shells are cemented together and provide many small spaces for refuge and breeding; most common at 7 to 15 m depth and locally very abundant; excavates crevices that function as refuges; substrate spawner forming large congregations; ingests sediment or plankton; poor disperser; home range 20-200 cm in diameter (Ref. 74422).

species.name: Neolamprologus wauthioni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shell-dweller (Ref. 6770, 7343), or at least a shell-spawner (Ref. 6770). Dwarf species (Ref. 6770). Found over muddy areas; feeds on small invertebrates, like shrimp and insect larvae (Ref. 7343). Specimens have been caught at a depth of 35 m and in area with many Neothauma shells (Ref. 53528, 94008). Shrimp remnants found in stomach (Ref. 53528).

species.name: Neolebias axelrodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolebias gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Neolebias kerguennae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.3 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Neolebias philippei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 3.7 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Neolebias powelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolebias spilotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolebias trewavasae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 5.3 cm (Ref. 7094). Occurs in fringing vegetation; omnivorous browser, consumes plant fragments, algae, protozoans, rotifers, small crustaceans and insects (Ref. 28714).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolissochilus soroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools of clear forested streams and rivers.  Often develops a sharp edge on the lower jaw, which is used for scraping rocks as it grazes (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Neolissochilus spinulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in fast flowing streams and rivers with rocky bottom (Ref. 41236), mainly in the middle of streams.  Omnivorous.  Adults feed mainly on filamentous green algae, lesser on chironomid larvae, crustaceans and water beetles (Ref. 40961).  They migrate upstream during the breeding season where spawning takes place on stones and gravel (Ref. 41864).  Spawning occur  from April to October with a peak in August to September.  Males mature at 9 cm.  Flesh is considered delicious and market demand is great.

species.name: Neolissochilus stevensonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species.

species.name: Neolissochilus stracheyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear forested streams and rivers (Ref. 12693).  They occur in swift flowing streams (Ref. 43281).  Disappear when human activities degrade aquatic habitats, as seen in other members of the genus (Ref. 12693).  Are predators primarily, but also feed on some types of plant matter, particularly fruits (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Neolissochilus subterraneus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cave inhabitant. Juveniles inhabit close to the cave entrance, subadults and adults occur deeper, at least 100 m from the entrance. Juveniles occupy the whole water column, from surface to bottom.  Subadults and adults stay close to the bottom and midwater, usually in slow current. The stomach contents of 18 cm specimen include organic detritus, possibly bat guano, and calcareous ooze of the limestone weathering.

species.name: Neolissochilus sumatranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neolumpenus unocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen taken from the stomach of a Gadus macrocephalus.

species.name: Neomerinthe bauchotae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neomerinthe beanorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Have a thick glandular tissue on posterior margin of fin spines which is believed to be venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Neomerinthe kaufmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neomerinthe megalepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neomerinthe pallidimacula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Neomerinthe rufescens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Offshore species (Ref. 10482).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Neomyxine biniplicata
species.description: In 73 m depth.

species.name: Neon goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral heads.  Removes ectoparasites on skin and fins, in the mouth and in the gill chambers of greater fish like groupers and others (Ref. 92840).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Neonoemacheilus assamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Neonoemacheilus labeosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. A female measuring 5.67 cm SL has ovaries with ovulae about 0.6 mm in diameter; 2 females (6.18-6.63 cm SL) with ovulae about 1.0 mm in diameter (Ref.  39226).

species.name: Neonoemacheilus mengdingensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Neonoemacheilus morehensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Neonoemacheilus peguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Neophrynichthys heterospilos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neoplecostomus bandeirante
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neoplecostomus doceensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water rivers, varying from small to medium sized, with rocky outcrops forming small waterfalls and substrates of rocks and sand.  Occurs at the bottom of the rivers among the rocks (Ref. 106072).

species.name: Neoplecostomus espiritosantensis

species.name: Neoplecostomus watersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear water, at the bottom of the rivers among and beneath the rocks (Ref. 119403).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neosalanx pseudotaihuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small transparent fish feeding exclusively on zooplankton. Commercially important in many lakes and reservoirs. Fish spawn in spring and die thereafter.

species.name: Neosalanx reganius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the tidal areas of the rivers above the salt front, 16-20 km upstream from the river mouth and sometimes found in areas with low seawater concentrations (Ref. 37303). Planktivorous fish. Feed on calanoid copepod, Sinocalanus sinensis which is the most dominant prey item; cyclopoids, Daphniasp. and decapod mysid (Ref. 57041).

species.name: Neoscorpaena nielseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neosho madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel riffles and runs of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Neosilurus coatesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neostethus amaricola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus bicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus borneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus ctenophorus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus djajaorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected over a muddy bottom, in a slightly turbid irrigation ditch relatively near the sea (Ref. 44355).  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus geminus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the type locality, this species was collected together with other fishes: Ambassis sp., Scatophagus argus, Tetraodon leiurus, Gobiopterus brachypterus, and Brachygobius doriae and Neostethus borneensis. The brackish water was clear and brown (Ref. 95599).

species.name: Neostethus lankesteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus palawanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal areas.  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus thessa
