species.name: Neostethus villadolidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in mangrove and nipa swamps (Ref. 280).  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neostethus zamboangae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal areas.  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).

species.name: Neotrygon ningalooensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Neotrygon orientalis
species.description: This species found demersal, inshore to mid-continental and on insular shelves. Accurate depth range is not available but probably found usually inshore at depths less than 100 meters.  Reported pregnant females contained only a single pup with size at birth of ca.12.0 cm (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Neovespicula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possesses venom glands at the base of some of the spines (Ref. 6192).  Of no commercial interest but appear from time to time in the aquarium trade (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Neozoarces steindachneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaweed areas along the coast.

species.name: Nepalese minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits hill streams and rivers (Ref. 6351).  Prefers high-gradient streams.  Adheres to rocks in rapid waters with the use of its unbranched rays in the pectoral fins and the transverse folds of skin along the belly (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Nepalese snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insects and plankton (Ref. 40948).

species.name: Neretva dwarf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear karstic springs, lakes, slow-flowing streams and small rivers.  Longevity is less than 2 years. Spawns after first winter with males defending the eggs in cavities under stones, plant material or shells. Juveniles are free swimming while adults are benthic.  During summer droughts, this species may survive in underground waters (Ref.59043).

species.name: Nerophis ophidion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit algal zone or eel-grass (Zostera) (Ref. 6733). Adults spawn in May - August . Feed on small crustaceans and fish fry (Ref. 35388). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Consistent paternity is ensured despite brooding of embryos on the outside the male's body. Events of cuckoldry by sneaker males is ruled out through genetic paternity analyses based on molecular markers (Ref. 81011). Each male carries eggs from a single female but females may deposit eggs on several brooding pouches (Ref. 81011).

species.name: Nesogobius greeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand around sea grass beds and around rocky reefs (Ref. 76773).

species.name: Nesogobius maccullochi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy areas in bays and estuaries, from the intertidal to depths of a few meters  (Ref. 76773)

species.name: Net-throat grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Netdevil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are mesopelagic and bathypelagic (Ref. 36495).  Larvae are primarily mesopelagic (Ref. 36495).  Males are parasitic, while females are oviparous with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36495).  Eggs are presumably contained in floating gelatinous rafts (Ref. 36495).

species.name: Nettastoma falcinaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from 1070-1100 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Nettastoma syntresis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Netted frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettenchelys bellottii
species.description: The species was described from two small specimens, 1.45 and 2.4 cm TL, with the larger one selected as the lectotype, and it is clearly a larval Nettenchelys (Ref. 106144),

species.name: Nettenchelys dionisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic feeder.

species.name: Nettenchelys erroriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettenchelys exoria
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettenchelys inion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettenchelys paxtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettenchelys taylori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nettoyeur à bande bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral rich areas of inner lagoons and subtidal reef flats to seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Feeds on crustacean ectoparasites and mucus of other fishes (Ref. 9823, 48636).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Stays in stations where other fish come to be cleaned.  Cleaning intensity is not related to client size or commonness (Ref. 28019).  Cleaning stations are occupied by a pair of adults, a group of juveniles or a group of females accompanied by a dominant male where a female becomes a functional male if the dominant male disappears (Ref. 5503).  Some adults solitary and territorial.  An unfamiliar visitor is usually greeted by dance-like movements with the tail maneuvering the back part of the body up and down.  Juveniles behave this way when divers approach closely (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth range of 1 meter in Ref. 27115.

species.name: Network reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices  (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Network slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Network triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky shores.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae  (Ref. 11482).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Network wobbegong
species.description: No male adults are known, but a male adolescent, 50.3 cm TL (Ref. 76939).

species.name: Neumann's suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in the cool waters of mountain streams (Ref. 5595); found.in rocky riffles and rapids as well as pools (Ref. 52193). It feeds on the biocover of rocks and grazes on algae (Ref. 5595). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Neumayer's barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Caledonian deep-water goby
species.description: A deep-water goby species collected with bottom trawls at 264-350 m depth (Ref. 128939).

species.name: New Caledonian longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Caledonian righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Caledonian soft-coral pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected among Sargassum on rocky substrate at 2 m (Ref. 75989).

species.name: New Caledonian striped triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: New Caledonian triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in outer slopes and reef flats (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 1.5 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: New Guinea blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rainforest creeks and large streams in relatively flat lowland terrain.

species.name: New guinea minidartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small aggregations above coral thickets; inhabits sheltered shoreline and lagoon reefs in 2-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: New Guinea mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184) which inhabits brackish mangrove and nipa palm areas, sometimes enters the lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847. 44894).  Occurs in the margin of estuaries and tidal creeks (Ref. 44894).  Actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: New Guinea tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in either small tributaries of the alluvial lowlands or in creeks and small rivers in hilly terrain.  Prefers deeper pools that are often littered with logs and branches.

species.name: New Guinea thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and associated lagoons, in clear or turbid water; also in brackish estuaries (Ref. 44894). A riverine species reaching nearly 900 km up the Fly River, but also down to the estuary. Found in main river channels as well as smaller tributaries (Ref. 2847). It forms shoals in deeper water of lagoons. Breeding biology is poorly understood, but it seems likely that spawning takes place in fresh water as juveniles have been collected from the upper reaches of some Queensland rivers. The diet consists of small crustaceans, fishes, insects and some plant material (Ref. 44894). Piscivorous (at least as large adults), recorded as feeding on Clupeoides papuensis and Melanotaenia nigra in the Fly River. The only anchovy that is restricted to mainly freshwater habitats (Ref. 44894). The largest anchovy known so far.

species.name: New guinea viviparous brotula
species.description: Rare species, found on coral-sand bottom (Ref. 34024).  Benthic (Ref. 75154). Cryptic and solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: New Guinea worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Guinea wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An inshore species inhabiting shallow coral reefs (Ref. 9823), with patches of sand and rubble (Ref. 37816), also along upper part of slopes and on reef crests with Acropora corals. Adults occur in small loose groups of females with dominant male nearby. Juveniles occur solitary in corals (Ref. 48636). Feed on benthic invertebrates. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Occasionally seen in fish markets and aquarium trade.

species.name: New Guinean frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal reef flats (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).

species.name: New Guinean hairtail
species.description: Environment needs verification.

species.name: New Guinean pelican flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Ireland dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Ireland stingaree
species.description: Maximum length known only from the holotype and only known specimen, a juvenile male (Ref. 51067).

species.name: New Providence cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dark inland caves, brackishwater sinkholes, and marine blue holes (Ref. 27158. 57878).

species.name: New River shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: New Zealand black goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock pools and deeper reefs, usually in narrow crevices where fine silt accumulates.  Secretive and usually only the head is seen protruding out of the crevice; will retreat when disturbed.

species.name: New Zealand blue cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky areas to a depth of 150 m (Ref. 9258).  Carnivore which feeds mainly on small fish and  crabs.  Feeds by stalking its prey and swallowing it whole.  Adults are home-ranging  (Ref. 26966). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 58489.

species.name: New Zealand blueback sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species in coastal waters. The biology probably resembles that of S. muelleri from which it has not usually been distinguished in earlier studies. Tends to occur in the bottom or midwater except during summer when surface shoals may appear; extends to deeper water in summer and retreats to close inshore for spawning during winter (Ref. 9258). Reported from surface (Ref. 188) to 72 m (Ref. 58489).

species.name: New Zealand dory
species.description: Occurs on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: New Zealand giant sawbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental slopes, seamounts and submarine rises with collection depths recorded between about 140 and 760 m, but most often 250-400 m (Ref. 92805).

species.name: New Zealand gray sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is a shallow-water species that occurs in 1.5-40 m, with majority of specimens (70 of 81) examined were caught between 11 m and 20 m (8 of 81 collected in 1.5-5.0 m, 2 of 81 taken at 21 m; and only 1 was taken at 40 m. Little else is known about the ecology of this species (Ref. 123823).

species.name: New Zealand grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Now extinct (Ref. 57073).  The last recorded specimen was brought to the British Museum in the 1930's (Ref. 57073).

species.name: New Zealand ling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock pools and shallow coastal waters; secretive species (Ref. 30464).  Feeds on small invertebrates and fish (Ref. 9003).  Probably nocturnal (Ref. 9003).

species.name: New Zealand orange perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: New Zealand pygmy sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to be solitary and possibly, a territorial species. Inhabits broken rocky reefs with holes, crevices, and small caves; perches on rocky ledges partly overlain by silty sand or shell debris. Reported to be often collected underwater sharing caves with much larger black gobies Gobiopsis atrata. Its small size, cryptic habit, semi-transparency, and camouflage coloration make this fish very difficult to locate underwater; though readily collected with rotenone ichthyocide while scuba diving. The habitat of this species in New Zealand is very similar to that of T. adela in Australia, which is restricted to rocky reefs, often in silty turbid waters, at 1-24 m depth. May be collected using slurp gun or hand collected following controlled use of rotenone ichthyocide (Ref. 57647).

species.name: New Zealand rough skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 26346); usually in coastal waters (Ref. 9258).  Found partially buried in sand (Ref. 26346).  Feed on fish, shellfish, crabs, and worms (Ref. 114953, 26346).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.2-12.7 cm long and 6.3-8.3 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41308).

species.name: New Zealand roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on mid-water crustaceans, squid and fishes.

species.name: New Zealand smooth skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 26346).  Usually found in deeper waters to 200 m (Ref. 9258).  Mainly feeds on benthic decapods and bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 150 cm TL. This species is said to be long lived and slow growing (Ref. 114953).

species.name: New Zealand sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, generally at depth of less than 50 m.  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).

species.name: New Zealand sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters, from beaches down to 110 m or more. Has an apparently long spawning season (July to January) around the South Island, but not a fractional spawner. Eggs are present in mid-summer near Clutha River mouth (but samples may have included S. antipodum). More data needed.

species.name: New Zealand topknot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found among large brown algae in rock pools and subtidal areas.  They feed on algal dwelling crustaceans and small fish (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: New Zealand torpedo
species.description: Found on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 26346).  Feeds on fish, probably at night (Ref. 26346).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: New-moon cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nez rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift clear high gradient streams with slab and boulder strewn bottom, some course gravel may be present.  Observed swimming in strong currents rather than being attached to rock surface like other species of Sycidiinae in the environment (Ref. 47442).

species.name: nez rouge (Lentipes rubrofasciatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia africana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia aspidentata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia brevirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia burragei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia cliveri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia cyrano
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia ectenes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Nezumia evides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia holocentra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia infranudis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Nezumia investigatoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia kamoharai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia obliquata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Nezumia rara
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia semiquincunciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia suilla
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia tinro
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia toi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia tomiyamai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nezumia umbracincta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Although most captures have been made with bottom trawls, specimens have recently been taken in midwater trawls fished close to the bottom, suggesting forays to the water column by individuals of different sizes (Ref. 11953).

species.name: Nezumia ventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nga lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams, brooks and swamps in drainage systems.  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Niangua darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Its eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Nibea coibor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nicaragua gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and lakes. A filter-feeder, its feeding and breeding habits presumably similar to other Dorosoma species. More data needed.

species.name: Nicaraguan mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected only on three occasions in the mouth of slow-moving streams, in brackish or fresh waters within a few meters of the sea.  Swims in small groups near the surface over sandy or muddy bottoms at temperatures of 25-26°C.  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Nichols' worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nicholsina collettei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, on seagrass and algal bottoms (Ref. 7360). Nicholsina usta collettei subspecies recognized from the east Atlantic (Ref. 11064).

species.name: Niebuhr’s goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at shallow depths (Ref. 95469).

species.name: Nielsen's catetyx
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nielsen's mudbrotula
species.description: Occurs on rocky shores down to 17 m, most commonly deeper than 5 m (Ref. 57886).

species.name: Nielsen's righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Niger barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on crustaceans, insects, molluscs and organic debris; in the Jebel Aulia Reservoir, annual spawning coincides with the onset of the floods; fecundity estimates ranged from 72 x 1,000 at 33 cm (4 yrs.) to over 14 x 10,000 at 74 cm (8 yrs) (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Niger tetra
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, insects and crustaceans.  In aquaria, female lays up to 1000 eggs, after vigorous driving by the male, which hatch in 30 to 34 hours (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51150).

species.name: Nigerian fangtooth pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and streams, also in the man-made Lake Volta, but only in the most riverine parts (Ref. 188). It feeds on small fishes, including its own juveniles, and aquatic insects (Ref. 188, 2246). Possibly migrates upstream to breed (Ref. 188). It enters artisanal fisheries, but catches are small (Ref. 188).

species.name: Night aulonocara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives over sand and feeds on sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Night sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky inshore reefs. They prefer wave-cut rock ledges or limestone shorelines and tide pools in regions with surf. Feed mainly on algae but adults also consume Zoanthus and hydroids while juveniles also feed on copepods (Ref. 9626). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3139).

species.name: Night smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small shrimp-like crustaceans (Ref. 4563).  Caught during the spawning season (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Nightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal streams, lakes and ponds.  Inhabit clear or darkly tannin-stained water of rivers, streams, swamps and lakes, usually near the cover of rocks, aquatic plants or woody debris (Ref. 44894).  Cryptic during the day under stones or among vegetation, but actively feeding at night on various crustaceans, small fishes, aquatic insects and gastropods (Ref. 44894).  Migrate to spawn in small side creeks after winter rains (August and September) (Ref. 6994).  Males reach maturity after their first year, female after their second (Ref. 6994).  Maximum life span is about six years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Nijssen's Hypopygus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nikhil’s torrent catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from among the stones, not the sandy portions, of the moderately flowing river (Ref. 112632).

species.name: Nikolay's lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Nile bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Polypterus bichir bichir likes shallow water and will often lie basking fo hours near the surface, but when swimming the fish is very pliant, and can turn and twist like an eel (Ref. 4904). The eggs are deposited in weeds, where the adult fish guards the eggs and young (Ref. 36900). It feeds on bottom-feeding fish (Ref. 36900) and is essentially piscivorous (Ref. 367).

species.name: Nile killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small bodies of water and shallow weedy parts of larger water bodies, swamps, irrigation ditches, brooks and small rivers (Ref. 47311).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139). Eggs develop in about 14 days in captivity and young reach sexual maturity at age of about 7-8 months (Ref. 47311).

species.name: Nile labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most closely resembles L. horie, with which it has often been confused (Ref. 1440).

species.name: Nilgiris barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper portion of large streams and rivers below the ghats (Ref. 41236). Migrates upstreams during floods and spawns in the upper reaches of streams (Ref. 4832). Omnivorous; feeds on allochthonous plant materials, seeds, terrestrial insects, Chironomous larvae and small benthic mollusks (Ref. 44151).

species.name: Nimbapanchax maeseni
species.description: Found in brooks, pools and small streams in the forested savanna (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish; very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nimbapanchax melanopterygius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in small puddle at the bank of Cavally River with water temperature 24°C and in a small, slow flowing creek with a maximum depth of 60 cm and a water temperature of 25°C; water at the latter location was stained slightly brown, creek covered by small trees and bushes and its bank by herbaceous plants (Ref. 82704).

species.name: Nimbapanchax petersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow brooks, shallow pools and shallow parts of swamps on sedimentary soil in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nimbapanchax viridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small streams, mainly in the weedy parts, in the forested savanna (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nimbochromis linni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the rocky (Ref. 5595, 55922) and intermediate habitats (Ref. 55922).  Piscivorous; observed ambushing fish prey (Ref. 5595, 55922).

species.name: Nimbochromis livingstonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in all kinds of habitats but is more common in vegetated areas of sheltered bays (Ref. 5595).  Prefers soft, muddy bottoms but is also seen in purely rocky environments (Ref. 5595, 55922).  Feeds on fish (Ref. 5595).  Has been observed to mimic as dead and then feed on small fish that get close (Ref. 3817, 13371, 55922).  Is usually solitary and territorial (Ref. 3817).

species.name: Nimbochromis polystigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common in mixed rock-sand habitats and vegetated areas (Ref. 55922). Occurs in small groups in rocky areas with beds of Vallisneria and Potamogeton (Ref. 3817). Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 267). Hunts in pairs (Ref. 3817) or in large groups (Ref. 3817, 55922). When singly, sometimes ambushing prey by lying motionless on the substrate, but not on its side (Ref. 55922).

species.name: Nimbochromis venustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy substrates (Ref. 5595, 55922).  Juveniles may be found in shallow water near rocks while adults forage in deeper regions with sandy substrate (Ref. 5595).  Feeds on small fish (Ref. 5595, 55922) and invertebrates (Ref. 55922).  Half-grown individuals have been observed to remain motionless, partially buried in the sand, waiting for small fishes to come within reach (Ref. 55922).

species.name: Nine ray toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ninebar prawn-goby
species.description: Occurs in shallow sandy expanses in or near seagrasses.

species.name: Nineline goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow areas with clear water and coral formations (Ref. 13628), often in close association with the sea urchin Echinometra lucunter. Possesses a ventral sucking disk which allows it to adhere to the rock beneath the test of an urchin with only the head showing among the spines of urchins. When disturbed they retreat farther beneath the urchin, and if the urchin is removed it rapidly darts beneath the test of a neighboring one. Feeds mainly on the tube feet of sea urchins (Ref. 33548)..

species.name: Ninespine batfish
species.description: Inhabits coastal reefs. Often occurs ion silt-sand bottoms of coastal trawling ground in 10-40 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Ningu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Anadromous species; ascending both large rivers and streams during floods and spawning in floodwater pools or inundated grasses at margins of rivers (Ref. 105018). Upstream migration at beginning of rains (Ref. 36900) in fairly compact shoals (Ref. 52083). Permanent river populations exist (Ref. 52083). Lake Victoria: in shallow, inshore waters and influent rivers (Ref. 34291). Lake Kyoga: in open waters away from water-lily zone (Ref. 4903). Specialized feeder on epilithic and epiphytic algae (Ref. 12526). Also feeds on rotifers growing on the body of other fishes (Ref. 34291). Caught with weirs and in baskets (Ref. 4967). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ninja lanternshark
species.description: The larger individuals of this species were collected at greater depth than smaller specimens, suggesting a positive relationship between size and depth, as has been observed in E. princeps. The largest paratype (51.5 cm TL) contains five ova ranging from 25.6 to 34.2 mm, with no embryos apparent. The immature male paratype has claspers at the earliest stage of development, suggesting that maturity for males is attained at a greater size. Viviparous with litter sizes apparently consist of at least 5 pups with post-partum lengths less than 177 mm TL (Ref. 106129).

species.name: Niobichthys ferrarisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nipponocypris koreanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Niwaella delicata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Niwaella laterimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Niwaella longibarba
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Niwaella multifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Niwaella xinjiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nkhomo-benga peacock
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with scattered rocks on a sandy bottom.  Feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nkupe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift flowing water, rapids or quiet, deep, sandy or rocky pools (Ref. 13337). Found only in the mainstream of larger rivers and even in Lake Kariba prefers more riverine habitats; omnivorous, feeds on insects, snails, small fish, and aquatic plants; breeds in summer, moving upstream to suitable sites (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Noble goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shoreline waters at depths over 6 m (Ref. 3921).  Benthic in reefs and coral rubble (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Noble lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 4066).  Found between 475 to over 900 m during the day and between 100-500 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Maximum abundance found between 300-500 m at night.  Sexually mature from about 11.2 cm (Ref. 4479).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Minimum depth from Ref. 4066.  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Nocturn goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Common in areas with fine sand to muddy bottoms at the bases of inner lagoon and coastal reefs.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884, 48637). Feeds on small invertebrates and organic matter (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Nocturnal pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Free-living adults are found on the outer shelf, usually deeper than 64 m over muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 36487).  Oviparous, with specialized vexillifer planktonic larval stage, and benthic tenuis larval stage (Ref. 36487).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Noline scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5755).  Female specimens (4.70-5.59 cm SL) taken from the Emperor Seamounts have mature gonads filled with relatively large eggs of several developmental stages with the most developed eggs are ca. 0.4 mm in diameter (Ref. 92340).

species.name: Nomorhamphus aenigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from the river that belongs to the Malili River basin. The type locality is approximately 10 m in width and 1.5 m in depth, partially shaded by forest canopy, and has mud and gravel bottom. Associated species: Nomorhamphus rex, Oreochromis niloticus, Oryzias dopingdopingensis, Osteochilus vittatus, Redigobius penango, Telmatherina sp. (Ref. 123153).

species.name: Nomorhamphus bakeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus brembachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus ebrardtii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus hageni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus kolonodalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A viviparous species collected from a variety of habitats including small, clear, cool mountain streams with rocky, muddy bottoms; shallow pools (0.02-0.50 m); muddy shorelines among tangles of roots; the base of small waterfalls among reeds; and under riverine canopies.  (Ref. 45130).

species.name: Nomorhamphus lanceolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a stream of about 7-9 m wide and 50 cm deep, partially shaded by forest canopy, with a bed of sand and gravel (Ref. 97329).

species.name: Nomorhamphus liemi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on flying insects (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Nomorhamphus manifestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus megarrhamphus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus philippina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus pinnimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus rex
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small, fast flowing river of few meters width that are partially covered by forest canopy, with gravel and sand bottoms. Occurs with Oryzias celebensis, Telmatherina cf. bonti, Anabas testudineus, Channa striata, Trichopodus pectoralis, Trichopodus pectoralis, Mugilogobius sp., Aplocheilus panchax, and Poecilia reticulata (Ref. 91778).

species.name: Nomorhamphus rossi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus sagittarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from three streams (Sungai Mangolo, Sungai Tawo-Tawo and Sungai Watumbasi) in Sulawesi Tenggara, Indonesia.  There are two sampling sites for Sungai Mangolo:  one is about 6-8 m wide and 10-100 cm deep with a sandy and rocky bottom and clear water at the type locality near the Scout Camping Ground of the Forestry Department area; and the other one is about 5-7 m wide, 10-50 cm deep and moderate running with a few boulders and stones at this point, is covered by rain forest canopy and with murky water due to traditional gold mining in the area.  Sungai Tawo-Tawo is about 3-5 m wide and 10-50 cm deep at the sample site and characterized by a sandy and gravel bottom and by clear water with much riparian vegetation.  The Sungai Watumbasi is 1-3 m wide, 10-30 cm deep and characterized by a muddy-sandy bottom (Ref. 97329).

species.name: Nomorhamphus sanussii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus towoeti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nomorhamphus viviparus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nonbanded whipfin mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Noodlefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Noreil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Christine Pöllabauer, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Norfolk cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Norfolk Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on outer reef slopes around boulders or occasionally on coral patch reefs (Ref. 125611).

species.name: Norin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected in a karstic river with fresh, oligotrophic, running water.  The adults collected only in the main current at the greatest river depth (5.5 meter); bottom was clear gravel laterally becoming muddy; the juvenile (paratype) was collected in shallow waters, among vegetation (Ref. 55951).

species.name: Norman's lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A savannah dwelling species found in, or close to, vegetated parts of small rivers, brooks, and swamps (Ref. 7372, 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Norman's smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Normichthys herringi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Normichthys yahganorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with the Antarctic Intermediate Water.  Biology unknown (Ref. 5161).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Noronha cleaner goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the archipelago islets; in cleaning stations on coral heads, sponges, and rocky substrata, with up to 15 individuals present in large stations, particularly those on sponges. Recorded to clean about 30 species of fish clients, including large carnivores such as shark (Carcharhinus perezi) and smaller carnivores (grouper Cephalopholis fulva), besides small clients like the planktivorous damselfish (Chromis multilineata) and zoobenthivorous butterflyfish (Chaetodon ocellatus) (Ref. 79614).

species.name: Noronha frillfin goby
species.description: Collected from reef crests and bottoms, and shallow tidepools everywhere in Fernando de Noronha and Atol das Rocas, up to 3 m deep. Observed in solitary, pairs or in large groups of up to 20 individuals, often in reef crests with rough waters, and eventually in sheltered sandy bottoms. Feeds mainly on small invertebrates, but also on small fishes. The eggs are guarded by territorial males, and their agonistic behaviour. Associated with several species of small fishes: blennies Scartella itajobi, Ophioblennius trinitatis, Entomacrodus vomerinus; labrids Malacoctenus sp., Labrisomus kalisherae, Labrisomus conditus; and the goby Coryphopterus glaucofraenum (Ref. 128474).

species.name: Noronha scaly blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow reefs where it preys on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 123106).

species.name: Noronha wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally a plankton-eater. Found on deep reefs (40-60 m), where it is recorded inside the lumen of tubular sponges (Ref. 39606). At Fernando de Noronha and Trindade Islands, groups of 10-450 initial-phase individuals clean other fishes in the water column close to the reef bottom and pinnacles (Ref. 36301, 49354). Also at Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, juveniles follow foraging green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and pick off particles stirred from the bottom by the turtle’s activity (Ref. 51385). Fish clients include about 20 species of surgeonfishes, damselfishes, parrotfishes, grunts, and even small groupers such as coneys. Occasionally, a coney (Cephalopholis fulva) preys on isolated Noronha wrasses out and away from the cleaning stations. Coastal individuals were never recorded cleaning. Strictly diurnal, this wrasse is one of the last reef fishes to emerge from nocturnal shelters and one of the first to retreat (Ref. 36301). Initial-phase individuals are predominantly dark-brown and white, whereas terminal-phase males are blue and purple. A group-spawner throughout the year, adult females form harems dominated by a few terminal-phase males. Pair spawning is also recorded for this wrasse (Ref. 49354). Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Noronha’s scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: North African shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species undertakes anadromous breeding migrations from the sea, where it spends most of its life, into the freshwater sections of rivers; it can also live permanently in brackish water (Ref. 10538). Males migrate upriver at 3-4 years, females at 4-5 years; it starts entering rivers when temperatures reach 14-18°C, mainly in May, and spawning commences when temperature rises above 20°C in May and June (Ref. 59043). The spawners return downstream immediately after spawning, but many die after spawning; most juveniles migrate to river mouth in first summer and remain at sea until they mature (Ref. 10538, 59043). Spawning occurs close to estuaries in fresh and brackish water (Ref. 59043). In the marine and brackish water habitats, this shad consumes small fishes, such as species of Engraulis, Sardina, and Sardinella, and small benthic crustaceans, mainly isopods and amphipods (Ref. 10538).

species.name: North American naked sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26938).  Occurs from shoreline to 183 m depth (Ref. 5521).

species.name: North Atlantic codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: North Atlantic slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water, 150-600 m, on muddy bottoms.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, mainly worms and crustaceans (Ref. 53643).

species.name: North Caucasian bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits water bodies with slow to fast current, preferring places with slow current.  Abundant in middle and lower parts of large rivers and their tributaries, reservoirs and swampy creeks; also in brackish water at river mouths, in estuaries and coastal lakes.  Frequently schools in upper water layers.  Feeds on plankton, insect larvae, and seeds.  Spawns in shallow water at depth of 0.1-0.5 m.  Lays sticky eggs, 1.4 mm in diameter, on submerged plants, rarely on pebbles (Ref. 59043).

species.name: North Caucasian longbarbel gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and rivers stretches with fast current and gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Feeds on Trichoptera larvae (Ref. 59043).  Spawns at the end of May (Ref. 1441).

species.name: North New Guinea rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: North Pacific daggertooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of depths, sometimes near surface (Ref. 2850) to below 2,000 m.  Larger adults inhabit colder water toward the poles, whereas, the young and smaller adults inhabit more temperate regions (Ref. 35956).  Feed on mollusks, crustaceans, marine worms, coelenterates, salps, and fishes (Ref. 4525, 6885).  Its distensible body wall and large stomach can accommodate prey up to half of its own length.  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35956).  Preyed upon by albacore, Pacific lancetfish, halibut, steelhead salmon, blue shark, pomfret, and whales (Ref. 6885).

species.name: North Pacific deepsea herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: North Pacific lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, migrating to the surface at night (Ref. 559).

species.name: North Pacific lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: North Pacific squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky soil of deep waters (Ref. 9137).  Benthopelagic in or near crevices and caves of rocky substrates (Ref. 58302).

species.name: North-west hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Essentially an estuarine species and coastal species, co-occurring with C. pauciradiatus, C. mugiloides and Atherinomorus endrachtensis. Biology not known except that it can withstand very high salinities. Probably taken as food by larger commercial species. (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Northern Australian longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern bastard codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottom.  Rarely seen during the day.  Swims close to the bottom at night.

species.name: Northern blue devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic species which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  They inhabit coral reef and rock reef (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Northern cavefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Blind and depigmented.  Despite the lack of eyes it does respond to light and moves away from it (scotophilia).  Inhabits subterranean water or caves which have consolidated mud-rock substrates in shoals and silt-sand substrates in pools but is more often found in caves with uniform silt-sand substrates (Ref. 34868).  Has low reproduction rate and broods eggs in gill cavity for up to 4-5 months (Ref. 557; 34868; 27795).  Can live for 2 years without food because of low metabolic rate (Ref. 5326).  Top predator.

species.name: Northern checkmark cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate flowing waters of the middle and upper river valleys.  Occurs in small groups, usually 10-30, staying relatively close to large rock formations.

species.name: Northern clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal rocky areas among algae, and on kelp (often high in kelp canopy) (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 6885).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Northern fatnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow-water estuarine, estuaries of rivers, streams and mangroves, at depths of 0–1 m, especially in mangrove habitats (Ref. 126575). Adults also found in the sea (Ref. 4833). Feed on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Northern fraildisc clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal, may remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Better reference needed.

species.name: Northern kahawai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Northern kongnose cory
species.description: Inhabits spring with water current.

species.name: Northern lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Adults move upward in large numbers at night (Ref. 28499).  Feed on fishes, copepods and euphausiids (Ref. 11712).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Lipid content is 15.6 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 90.9 % in total lipids (Ref. 9197). Minimum depth from Ref. 82347.

species.name: Northern leatherside chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sluggish pools and backwaters, usually over mud or sand, of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Northern medaka
species.description: Occurs in ponds, marshes, and streams, such as irrigation canals amid paddy fields in flat alluvial lowlands. Well adapted to aquatic life on temporary floodplain wetlands (Ref. 89067).

species.name: Northern mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally lives in slow-flowing, shaded streams, in rocky pools or well-vegetated sections.  Also found in swampy areas.  Occurs at altitudinal range from near sea level to at least 1200 m.

species.name: Northern pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 35929).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35929).

species.name: Northern plains killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters (Ref. 52299).  Omnivorous.  Spawning occurs in small pools over sand and gravel bottom in water 6-10 cm depth (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Northern rainbow wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep shelf waters (Ref. 530).

species.name: Northern Rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat where found is highly variable, including rivers, creeks, swamps, marshy lagoons, lakes, and reservoirs.  Usually forms aggregations at or near the surface of deeper pools in stream habitats, especially where there is aquatic vegetation or log debris (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Northern river shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern rivers catfish
species.description: Prefers main river channels, but also occurs in lakes and on the floodplain. Feeds mainly on large crustaceans (Macrobrachium and Caridina), fishes, aquatic and terrestrial insects, nymphs and detritus. Occurs at temperatures ranging from 26 to 32°C. Mainly diurnal.

species.name: Northern rock flathead
species.description: Found on the continental shelf, inshore region (Ref. 7300).  Apparently associated with aquatic vegetation.  Has been taken by trawl at depths from 15 to 46 m, frequently found at depths of 10 m or less (Ref. 9790).

species.name: Northern rock sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand, also together with gravel and mud (Ref. 37594).

species.name: Northern rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Northern ronquil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually among rocks (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Northern sawtail shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits littoral rocky bottom (Ref. 559), and in protected bays on silty substrates among debris (Ref. 48635). Solitary among crevices of coastal reefs to 15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Northern sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft or shell bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on shrimps (Ref. 4925). Occurs at minimum depth of 9 m (Ref. 06885).

species.name: Northern sennet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern smoothtongue
species.description: Adults are generally found at depths greater than 150 m during the day.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604), which are distributed in the sub-arctic gyre south to about 47°N (Ref. 6848).

species.name: Northern snubnose garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species that extends into fresh water.  Occurs in brackish estuaries, but frequently found in the lower, tidal portions of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847).  Considered an excellent food fish taken by commercial and recreational fishers (Ref. 9843).

species.name: Northern snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occupies shallow-water estuarine, found in tidal rivers, mangrove creeks and muddy tide-pools, at depths of 0–1 m, on sandy mud, mud and mangrove roots, logs and leaf litter. It is found among a variety of mangroves, e.g. Aegialitis, Avicennia, Ceriops, Exoecaria, Rhizophora and often in marginal habitats such as small drainage creeks that runs through exposed salt flats. Associated with other species in its microhabitat or location in northern Australia including a minor overlap with Pseudogobius eos around Brisbane) (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Northern spearnose poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern spiny dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northern stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cleithral spine with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Found inshore, at depths to 36 m (Ref. 55313).

species.name: Northern studfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits margins, pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Most commonly found in shallow sandy backwaters of clean rocky creeks.  18 cm max TL  (Ref. 5723).  Adult feeds on aquatic insect larvae and snails (Ref. 10294).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Northern sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy pools of headwaters, creeks, and small to medium rivers.  Usually found near vegetation (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Northern tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in relatively fast-flowing, rocky streams in hilly or mountainous terrain.

species.name: Northern tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and shallow coastal waters (Ref. 7251); with mud substrates.  Sexual maturity occurs at approximately 4 cm SL (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Northern trout gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range environments from desert bores and muddy swamps to clear jungle streams.  Inhabits rivers, creeks and billabongs, in quiet or slowly flowing sections among vegetation or rocks.  Young fish feed mostly on microcrustaceans.  Adult fish prey upon insects, crustaceans, worms, mollusks, fishes and plant materials.  Spawns during the rainy season (November to March).  Female produces several batches of 100-500 eggs which are deposited on rocks or logs.  The males guards and fans the eggs until hatching, which takes about 8-10 days.  The population on the Barkly Tableland (Northern Territory) may eventually prove to be a separate species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Northern tubelip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in rich coral reefs in clear coastal to outer reef habitats.  Adults feed on coral polyps but may also clean (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth range from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Northern whitefin gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottom of moderately flowing lowland rivers and prefers sand bottom. A nocturnal species feeding on insect larvae and other larger benthic invertebrates (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Northern yellow-spotted Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Northland mudfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ephemeral areas that dry out over summer and autumn months, where it aestivates in damp areas or under tree roots and logs (Ref. 43717).

species.name: Northwest Australian whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs close to reefs in offshore waters (Ref. 9785).  Solitary or small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Northwest black bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, often entering estuaries.  Popular angling species usually caught with hook and line and sometimes taken by trawlers (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Nose stribed cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nosestripe klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live among stones in tidal pools.  Viviparous (Ref. 51409).

species.name: Nosestripe sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is generally found in calm environments on sand or rubble near reefs.   A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 057562).  Minimum depth of 3 m reported from Ref. 57562.

species.name: Nosey dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among corals and seagrasses (Ref. 9710); and around a large boulder in a macroalgae dominated biotope, mixed with large sponges and sparse encrusting hard corals on rock platform (Ref. 88695).

species.name: Notable whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on gastropods, bivalves, polychaetes, and percarid crustaceans.

species.name: Notacanthus abbotti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notacanthus indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notacanthus spinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notal lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.  Found in about 700 m during the day and below 60 m at night.

species.name: Notarius armbrusteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notarius biffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore marine and brackish waters, and high salinity estuaries (Ref 54794).

species.name: Notarius cookei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notarius insculptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notarius luniscutis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notched flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawling over sand and mud bottoms to 130 m (Ref.9790).

species.name: Notched mud carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rapids and in slow flowing water (Ref. 37771). It may be the single most abundant species in the Mekong basin and is certainly an ecological keystone species. Collected in numerous tributaries as small as 2-3 m wide in widely separated localities in Thailand, Laos and Cambodia. In terms of absolute numbers, it is the most abundant fish species in the major migrations that occur in the mainstream of the Mekong River below Khone Falls every December-February and May-July, where there is an important artisanal fisheries. Probably the single most important forage or prey species for many piscivore fish species present there, and may also be heavily preyed upon by the local dolphin, Orcaella brevirostris . Is one of the lead species in the massive migrations of cyprinid fishes moving up the Mekong mainstream in the Khone Falls area. Most of these falls represent an impassable physical obstacle to the migrators, but they can be avoided by going up one or two of the large "hoo" or channels (most importantly Hoo Sahong) and smaller pathways, thus by-passing the impassable falls and more difficult rapids. Employs a strategy, "the ever-changing leadership strategy for finding the pathway of least resistance", which can only be successful when very large numbers of individuals are migrating. As the migrating fish move upstream, the leading fish are blocked or fail to find a way onwards, some fish turn back and look for other routes. Therefore the leadership of the migrators is constantly changing, until some leaders are successful in getting past obstacles and take large numbers of followers with them.

species.name: Notched triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky substrate (Ref. 13227) and on roofs of caves at 10-30 m (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Notchheaded marblefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs (Ref. 5755).  Feeds on seaweeds (Ref. 5755).

species.name: Notchlip redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Notchspine brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky reefs.  A 5.9 cm SL female (USNM 263738) contains about 60 eggs, 0.4-0.6 mm in diameter and 140 embryos, 4-5 mm TL, with 2 rows of 2-3 large spots along anal and dorsal fin bases (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Notchtail stargazer
species.description: Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Notchtongue goby
species.description: Inhabits tide pools and shore waters, including mangrove areas (around muddy substrate near mangrove roots) and sheltered seagrass beds (rock and turtle grass) (Ref. 7251, 85559).

species.name: Nothobranche de Rachov
species.description: Poisson. Found in water-filled depressions in the floodplains of rivers; water depth is variable and decreases as the dry season progresses, eventually drying out completely (Ref. 85866). Littoral vegetation usually consists of grasses; aquatic vegetation may consis of Nymphea, Ottelia, Lagarosiphon and Utricularia species; occasionally, the swamps are used by local inhabitants to cultivate rice (Ref. 85866). Very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius albertinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ephemeral pools and marshes as well as small river systems (Ref. 123150); the type locality is an isolated pool, about 1 m at the deepest point, in an area that was overgrown by reeds (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius albimarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In shallow waters among weeds.

species.name: Nothobranchius angelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools and marshes (Ref. 122068).

species.name: Nothobranchius annectens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small, temporary, weedy pools (Ref. 41296).

species.name: Nothobranchius attenboroughi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The distribution area of Nothobranchius attenboroughi overlaps with those of N. sagittae and N. serengetiensis, but syntopic occurrences are rare (Ref. 123150). Found in isolated temporary pools in a seasonal stream system; in turbid water, the bottom of the pool, less than a meter at the deepest point, not visible (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius balamaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pool in a seasonal stream course, less than 1 m in depth, with turbid and slow flowing water; riverbanks were covered by grass with remnants of Miombo vegetation (Ref. 127332).

species.name: Nothobranchius bellemansi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality comprised a pool in a clay depression containing a few centimeters of standing water in the savannah floodplains southeast of the Nuba mountains; these depressions become filled during the rainy season, with certain deeper parts retaining water for longer periods (Ref. 97568).

species.name: Nothobranchius boklundi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality was at the time of collection of the type material a pond about 100 m in diameter with a depth of about 1.5 m in its centre (Ref. 84038). The water was light clay grey in color, slightly turbid and aquatic vegetation which includes a species of Nymphea (Ref. 84038).

species.name: Nothobranchius brieni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from temporary pools and swamps (Ref. 3788, 59344). Bottom spawner (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius chochamandai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality was a large ephemeral pool formed in a river bed, as a standing fragment of the seasonal river, at the collecting point about 100 m wide, and about 1.5 m deep at its deepest point; all collecting took place in the same general habitat; most parts of the habitat were heavily overgrown by grass and aquatic vegetation consisted of Nymphea species; water slightly turbid, whereas at shallower parts the bottom of the pool was visible; water temperature around noon 25.3°C, pH 7.30 and it contained 20 ppm of total dissolved solids (Ref. 97353).

species.name: Nothobranchius cooperi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is a micropredator, feeding on small aquatic crustaceans, worms, insect larvae and other zooplankton (Ref. 117281). The species appears to qualify as vulnerable (B1bii) according to IUCN criteria (Ref. 117281).

species.name: Nothobranchius derhami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools less than 1 m deep and with aquatic vegetation; the water was light clay grey and turbid, with a pH of 7.6 and temperature ranging from 25-31°C depending on the position in the water column (Ref. 123202).

species.name: Nothobranchius ditte
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius eggersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools and swamps (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2-3 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius elucens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an isolated pool in a shallow depression on a floodplain (Ref. 123810). It is a micropredator, feeding on small aquatic crustaceans, worms, insect larvae and other zooplankton (Ref. 123810). Nothobranchius elucens is recommended to be listed as vulnerable (Ref. 123810).

species.name: Nothobranchius fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius flagrans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius flammicomantis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius foerschi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 2-4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius fuscotaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius geminus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually at the surface of pools preying on small food items (e.g. small insects) that fall on the water surface.  These pools from which the species were collected are ephemeral and usually dry up seasonally (Ref. 42930).

species.name: Nothobranchius hassoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ephemeral pools with turbid water (Ref. 53530).

species.name: Nothobranchius hengstleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type locality is a temporary pool of about 6 m long, 1.5 m wide and 0.10 m deep; no aquatic vegetation present, only dry grass along the shore; water brown and turbid; pH 7.5; no other fish present (Ref. 58960).

species.name: Nothobranchius hoermanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a shallow ephemeral pool with a diameter of about 10 m and about 50 cm at the deepest point; the water was turbid, the bottom of the pool not visible (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius insularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius itigiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is an ephemeral pool formed in the marshy terrain drained by the Mlumbi and Kisigo streams; an extensive pool of about 50 m wide; the water was turbid, the bottom of the pool not visible (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius ivanovae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swampy area; described from a residual pool in the dry bed of the Karira stream (Ref. 92886).

species.name: Nothobranchius janpapi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small pools and swamps in the floodplains.  Lives near the water surface (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius jubbi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It occurs in temporary pools, swamps and ditches or rain pans, usually without connection to river courses (Ref. 30558).  The adults die when waterbodies dry out with low rainfall (Ref. 30558).  Males display to attract ripe females, pair off and spawn, grasping the female by folding over the large dorsal and anal fins (Ref. 30558).  Spawning occurs daily for an extended period with a few eggs laid at a time (Ref. 30558).  It is a bottom spawner (Ref. 27139, Ref. 30558) and development is suspended when the water bodies dry out (Ref. 30558).  The eggs hatch the following rainy season when the pan fills, the fish growing to maturity in a few weeks (Ref. 30558).  It are aggressive predators on insects and other aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 30558); therefore it is used for mosquito larva control (Ref. 30558).  It is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139) and thus a popular aquarium fish (Ref. 30558).

species.name: Nothobranchius kadleci
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The altitude of collection sites ranged from 24-82 m above sea level (Ref. 83370). It is found in small temporary pools varying from 3.5-2150 m², with a maximum depth of 100 cm, very turbid water and soft muddy bottom; littoral vegetation was present in the pools, sometimes with scarce Nymphaea vegetation (Ref. 83370).

species.name: Nothobranchius kardashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius kilomberoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits water levels close to the substrate of pools.  These pools are ephemeral and usually dry up seasonally.  Collected from areas of pools with the highest grass density (Ref. 42930).

species.name: Nothobranchius korthausae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools, swamps, ditches and small streams (Ref. 3788, 97277). Temporary pools and streams; distinctively more abundant in temporary pools; open savanna-like vegetation and gallery forest (Ref. 83284). Bottom spawner, 1-3 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius krammeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Described from an ephemeral pool which measures approximately 350 m in diameter and no more than 0.75 m deep at centre; banks densely covered with water lilies (Nymphea spp.); water brown, slightly turbid with neutral pH (Ref. 79559).

species.name: Nothobranchius krysanovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ephemeral pools and swamps on floodplains; water level in the habitats is subject to seasonal changes and generally the water disappears completely during the dry season (Ref. 85866). Grass vegetation is usually found near the habitat margins; much of the swamps may be utilised by local inhabitants for the cultivation of rice; aquatic vegetation may comprise Nymphea, Ottelia, Lagarosiphon and Utricularia species (Ref. 85866). It has an annual mode of reproduction (Ref. 85866).

species.name: Nothobranchius kwalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius lourensi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius lucius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools and swamps and has an annual mode of reproduction; observations on captive specimens indicate that it can be predatory to smaller fish, although this behavior is not obligatory (Ref. 83514).

species.name: Nothobranchius luekei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius makondorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Annual species; found in water-filled depressions on the floodplain of rivers and creeks or remnant pools of seasonal creeks; water in all pools turbid; during dry season, pools mostly dry up; usually no aquatic vegetation, but grasses may be present only at the margins of the water bodies; if aquatic vegetation is present, it may include Nymphea, Ottelia, Lagarosiphon, and Utricularia species; no associated fish species were observed (Ref. 83514).

species.name: Nothobranchius malaissei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, with unknown months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius matanduensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius milvertzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The accompanying fauna of the ephemeral pools consisted of non-annual species, such as Barbus haasianus, Lacustricola moeruensis, Protopterus sp. and Pseudocrenilabrus cf. philander (Ref. 95524). The type locality was a large ephemeral pool formed in a river bed, as a standing fragment of the seasonal river, about 50 m long and 10 m wide, and about 2 m deep at its deepest point; the edge of the habitat was heavily overgrown by grass and the aquatic vegetation consisted of Nymphea species; the water was brown and slightly turbid, whereas at shallower parts the bottom of the pool was visible (Ref. 95524). Eggs slightly oval, measuring 1.27-1.36 mm on average, with short filaments on chorion (Ref. 95524).

species.name: Nothobranchius mkuziensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius moameensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an ephemeral pool, circular with a diameter of about 10 m, and less than a meter at the deepest point; in turbid water and the bottom of the pool not visible (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius neumanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, X months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius niassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pools of seasonal streams, less than 50cm deep, with no vegetation, and with leaf litter and gravel as bottom substrate; on type locality the water was light clay gray, slightly turbid with low conductivity (Ref. 91043).

species.name: Nothobranchius nikiforovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species meets criteria B1ab(iii) for Vulnerable as conservation status; the increasing pressure on land and water resources of wetlands will continue to result in habitat degradation and represent an important threat to the species, raising vulnerability in terms of conservation status (Ref? 123990).

species.name: Nothobranchius nubaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in residual pools of seasonal rivers and rainwater filled depressions (Ref. 82677). The present disjunct distribution pattern of Nothobranchius nubaensis can be explained by the dynamics of the changing rain pattern and climatic conditions over the vast plains of central and southern Sudan and south-west Ethiopia (Ref. 82677).

species.name: Nothobranchius occultus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius ocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. bottom spawner, with unknown months of incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius oestergaardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality was at the time of collection a pond about 15 m in diameter and circa 1.5 m deep at its centre, extending on one side into the grass for about further 10 m and with a depth of 0.5 m (Ref. 86819). The aquatic vegetation consisted of a Nymphea species; the water was light clay grey and turbid, with pH 6.1 and conductivity 207 µS/cm (Ref. 86819).

species.name: Nothobranchius ottoschmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools and marshes (Ref. 122068).

species.name: Nothobranchius palmqvisti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools in floodplains, swamps and temporary ditches (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 2-4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius pienaari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in temporary pools and swamps in the floodplains of several rivers flowing into the Indian Ocean south of the lower Zambezi River; usually found in water-filled depressions in the floodplains of rivers and bordering swamps; water depth is variable with the progress of the season (Ref. 85866). Aquatic vegetation may consist of Nymphea, Ottelia, Lagarosiphon and Utricularia species (Ref. 85866).

species.name: Nothobranchius polli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools, water-filled depressions ("dembos"), temporary swamps and ditches in floodplains (Ref. 59344).  Bottom spawner, 4-6 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius prognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius rosenstocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Populations of this species have been found scattered over a large area in the Luapula River basin; specimens have been found mainly in shallow and vegetated parts of small, slow-flowing rivers which empty into swamps; the species was also collected from so-called "dembos" or water-filled depressions; all habitats were temporary and only filled with water during the wet season and for a short period afterwards, the bottom substrate of which were usually silt or clay with a high humus content (Ref. 53985).

species.name: Nothobranchius rubripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner; 2-4 months incubation; very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius rubroreticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools, swamps and ditches (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius rungwaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools (Ref. 122068).

species.name: Nothobranchius ruudwildekampi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type specimens originate from temporary shallow pools in open savanna area, with some shrubs near the pool margin; the water was brownish hyaline, slightly turbid, and water plants were abundant; pools were shallow, about 50 cm deep in deepest parts, but 5 days after collection, one pool was entirely dry (Ref. 83284).

species.name: Nothobranchius sagittae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, seasonal pools and swamps (Ref. 98818).

species.name: Nothobranchius sainthousei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ephemeral habitats in the floodplain between the small seasonal Chimbembe and Kusake rivers; about 5 km southwest of the confluence of the Luapula with the Luongo (Ref. 116789). The ephemeral pools were about 5-10 m wide, and less than 1 m deep at the deepest point; the aquatic habitat was heavily overgrown with grass (Ref. 116789). The water of pH 6.98 contained 15 ppm of total dissolved solids; it was brown and turbid, so the pool substratum was only visible at shallower depths; the water temperature measured at midday was 23.0°C (Ref. 116789). The conservation status of Nothobranchius sainthousei is uncertain, but appears to qualify as vulnerable (Ref. 116789). Stomach contents of adult wild-caught specimens show that N. sainthousei is a micropredator, feeding on small aquatic crustaceans, worms, insect larvae and other zooplankton (Ref. 116789).

species.name: Nothobranchius seegersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in seasonal pools; the type locality was at the time of collection a small and very shallow pond, about 3x5 m wide and 0.25 m deep, without aquatic vegetation, in the open woodland; the water was brown and very turbid (Ref. 87047).

species.name: Nothobranchius serengetiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in seasonal pools and swamps (Ref. 98818).

species.name: Nothobranchius skeltoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius sonjae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seasonal pools and marshes (Ref. 122068).
