species.name: Nothobranchius steinforti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools, swamps and rice fields (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, X months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius streltsovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an ephemeral pool located near a culvert measuring approximately 6 m x 6 m, less than 50 cm deep, and without aquatic vegetation; the water was light clay grey and slightly turbid with low conductivity, pH 7.9 and temperature approximately 26°C (Ref. 116792).

species.name: Nothobranchius symoensi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools, swamps and ditches (Ref. 59344).  Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Nothobranchius taiti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ephemeral pool and swamps of Apapi River system. This species is a micropredator, feeding on small aquatic crustaceans, worms, insect larvae and other zooplankton (Ref. 128031).

species.name: Nothobranchius torgashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a seasonal ditch, less than 1 m deep and without aquatic vegetation, the water light clay grey and turbid with a pH of 8.3 and temperature varying from 25 to 30°C (Ref. 116436).

species.name: Nothobranchius usanguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nothobranchius venustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a temporary pool about 10 m wide, more than 20 m long, and about 1 m at the deepest point; the water was turbid, the bottom of the pool not visible (Ref. 123150).

species.name: Nothobranchius virgatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits temporary pools and channels in and around foothills of the Nuba mountains and bordering the Sudd wetland; feeds on cladocerans, copepods, ostracods and insects (Ref. 28714). Annual species; eggs resist desiccation during dry season (Ref. 97278). Bottom spawner, 3-6 months incubation (Ref. 27139). Sexual maturity reached in 5 weeks (Ref. 59344).

species.name: Nothobranchius wattersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothobranchius wattersi occupies seasonal water pools that are briefly connected owing to seasonal flooding by summer rains and isolated later in the season before eventually desiccating; these pools are characterized by fine black or grey-coloured clay-rich soils typically comprising silt, mud and fine sand, roughly in that order of abundance, and eggs are laid in the uppermost layers of this substratum (Ref. 92979).

species.name: Notholebias cruzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Notholebias fractifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notholebias vermiculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notocheirus hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently planktophagic, with Drepanopus forcipatus (calanoid copepod) as its main food; has very low fecundity (only 71 maturing ova found as mean value); and has four parasites - two species of Acanthocepha (larvae of Corynosomia sp. And adults of Hypoechinorhyinchus sp.), one undetermined Trematoda and a larva of undetermined ectoparasitic copepod (Ref. 56210).

species.name: Notoglanidium akiri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoglanidium depierrei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoglanidium maculatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoglanidium pallidum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoglanidium pembetadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found between large rocks and pebbles covering the bottom of the Kouilou-Niari River at Pont du Niari (Ref. 94483).

species.name: Notoglanidium thomasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoglanidium walkeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notolabrus cinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on mollusks and small crustaceans (Ref. 26203). Recorded at depth of 15 m (Ref. 58932).

species.name: Notoliparis antonbruuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoliparis kermadecensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to be abundant in its known depth range (6456 to 7554 m) (Ref. 129455).

species.name: Notolycodes schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notophycis fitchi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notopogon armatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoraja azurea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on continental slope (Ref. 114953). Length of smallest mature male 53.5 cm TL and smallest juvenile 19.3 cm TL (Ref. 75642). Occasionally caught by deep-sea trawlers (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Notoraja fijiensis
species.description: Found on nearby insular slope. Life history unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Notoraja hirticauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notoraja lira
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal, possibly on hard bottoms (Ref. 114953). Described from a single juvenile male, 41.5 cm TL (Ref. 75642).

species.name: Notoraja longiventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal species found on mid-insular slopes. Known from few specimens. Hatching size at ca. 17 cm TL. Life history unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Notoro skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Notoscopelus bolini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, mesopelagic species.  Probably found deeper than 1,000 m during the day, occurs at 12-200 m at night (maximum abundance at 45-50 m).  Nyctoepipelagic at surface and down to 125 m (Ref. 4775).

species.name: Notoscopelus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, found between 375-1,000 m during the day and between 45-150 m at night.  Spawns from winter to spring.

species.name: Nototheniops nybelini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nototheniops tchizh
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Notothénia queue longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length taken from asymptotic length in Ref. 7226; length type assumed as TL. Bottom browser, feeding mostly on gelatinous and crustacean plankton (Ref. 47657).

species.name: Notothénia siouna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males guard the nesting sites (Ref. 57915).

species.name: Notropis imeldae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Novacula razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper drainages of rivers and reservoirs (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Nsess
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer the more open regions of the lake; vagabonding, fast-swimming species; ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307). Predatory; reported to kleptoparasitize the freshwater crab Potamon africanus (Ref. 81260). Prefers small fish, shrimp and insect larvae (Ref. 52307). Aquarium conditions: pH=9, H=25, 30°C water temperature, omnivore, egg layer, needs rocky cover and substratum, not easy to raise in tanks (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Nuakata shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on a flat muddy bottom in a sheltered bay with a mangrove shoreline. It is presumed to live in burrows and, like other members of the genus, is associated with snapping shrimps of the genus Alpheus Ref. 119393).

species.name: Nuchequula glenysae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nuchequula longicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nuchequula mannusella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nueces roundnose minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, sometimes runs, of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers.  Usually occurs among filamentous algae (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Nukta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large streams and rivers with sand and boulder bed (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Numbray
species.description: Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 9913).  Mainly feeds on crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 114953). Biology little known (Ref. 9913) but reported to produce 4-6 young each gestation (Ref. 114953).  Adult males and females known at 15 cm TL; common size reported to reach 35 cm TL (Ref. 114953). The electric organs present on disc are used to stun the prey.

species.name: Nursalim flasherwrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits semi-sheltered areas, exposed to periodic strong currents; invariably associated with gradual rubble slopes at depths ranging from about 5-50 m or more, but most abundant between about 20 and 35 m. Large aggregations, of about 30 males and several hundred females, were occasionally encountered in only 6 to 10 m at Triton Bay (Ref. 74967).

species.name: Nurse tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, lakes, irrigation canals and fringing vegetation; feeds on zooplankton, Caridina, insects, snails and vegetation (Ref. 28714). Dwarf populations are described in lake basins: Lake Turkana, B. n. nana Pellegrin, 1935 and Lake Chad, B. n. dageti Blache and Miton, 1960 (see Ref. 2880).

species.name: Nurseryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mangrove-nipa swamps, brackish estuaries and slow-flowing turbid rivers.  Feed on small fishes, shrimps and crayfish.  The male carries the eggs around like a bunch of grapes attached to a hook on the head, called forehead brooding (Ref. 36739, 44894).  Esteemed table fish (Ref. 2158).

species.name: Nusa penida viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of rocky crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Nusa Tenggara deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nutcracker prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in soft bottoms at depths of 45 - 490 meters; usually on outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Nutting's hatchet fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds Globigerina, foraminiferans and copepods (Ref. 26165). Minimum depth from Ref. 58302.

species.name: Nutty snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: NW Australian deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nyanza barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes and rivers. In the Lake Victoria system it appears in rivers and lake-side streams during rains, and in dry season along shores of the lake (adults) or in floodwater pools (juveniles) (Ref. 104796). Anadromous (Ref. 104796). Likely to spawn twice a year; floodwater pools appear to be spawning grounds; breeding may also occur among grasses at river edges (Ref. 104796).

species.name: Nyassachromis boadzulu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in shallow water over open sand floors; also found near small rocks and rubble on the bottom (Ref. 5595).  Feeds exclusively on zooplankton (Ref. 267).

species.name: Nyassachromis breviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sand but males need small stones for nest construction which is not common in the genus.  Feeds on phytoplankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nyassachromis microcephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sandy vegetated areas in shallow water.  Forms small schools in midwater.  Feeds on plankton in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nyassachromis nigritaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been seen on open sand at a depth of about 15 m.  Feeds on zooplankton in midwater (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nyassachromis prostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Nyassachromis purpurans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy areas.  Feeds on plankton in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nyassachromis serenus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intermediate sand-rock habitat but also occurs over open sandy areas.  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Nybelin's Porogadus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Nybelinella brevianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum size based on holotype (Ref. 116600).

species.name: Nybelinella brevidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 5,160 (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Nybelinella erikssoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Viviparous (Ref. 6527).

species.name: Nymph goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices in 4-16 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Nzoia barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and rivers during floods, in floodwater pools during dry season; probably two breeding seasons coinciding with rains; floodwater pools and shallow pools in lake-side streams are spawning grounds (Ref. 104796). Feeds on debris, algae, higher plant material, insects and other organisms (Ref. 12523).

species.name: Négrillon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats and lagoon reefs. Frequently occur in colonies associated with live or dead branching staghorn coral (Acropora). Feed on algae, gastropods, sponges, and copepods. Territorial, maintain and 'weed' filamentous algae patches growing on dead coral (Ref. 9710). They attack human intruders without hesitation, sometimes taking painful nips. Particularly aggressive during reproductive periods. The species emit clicking noises during aggressive encounters. Oviparous, males tend the nest visited by several females (Ref. 59295).

species.name: Néon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Néon (Neolebias unifasciatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 5.3 cm (Ref. 7094).

species.name: Néon bleu
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, small insects, crustaceans and plant matter.  In tank, female lays a relatively small number of eggs, which hatch in about 24 hours (Ref. 7020).  Most popular aquarium fish.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Néon du pauvre
species.description: Poisson. Found in clean, sluggish coastal stream amongst hydrophytes (Ref. 85799).  Can survive in water temperature as low as 5°C.  Feed on zooplankton and detritus.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Néon rose
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plants (Ref. 7020).  Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).  Maximum length reported to reach 4 cm TL (Ref. 7020).  A popular aquarium fish (Ref. 598).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Nérophis lombricoïde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal to about 30 m (Ref. 6733), among rocks or holdfasts and lower branches of algae (Ref. 4509).  Spawn in the summer months.  Become sexually mature at an age of 2 years.  Feed on small crustaceans and fish fry (Ref. 35388).  Larvae are attached to the ventral surface of the males (Ref. 42359).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Parental care is exclusively paternal (Ref. 42359).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Nérophis tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 6733).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Oarfifsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Warmer-water distribution, within 15° of the Equator. Large adults sometimes kill themselves by swimming out of the water onto beaches; occurrence of such strandings may be linked to certain areas, seasons or months and often in spates. With a unique adaptation of self-amputation (autotomy) of the posterior part of the body past the vent which may involve only the caudal fin (or one to a few small adjacent vertebrae) or as far anterior as just before the abdomen; apparently occurs several times during its lifetime (serial autotomy) but do not damage any vital organs and are usually survived except in strandings. All records over 1.5 m long have bodies shortened by autotomy and may exhibit a healed-over stump or "terminus"; still, many specimens found with fresh (with a ragged appearance very different from a healed termini) incomplete self-amputations of the posterior part of the body, notably not consistent with shark bites; the lost part is never regenerated. Species of this Regalecus attain lengths of 7-8 meters and this is well established by documented specimens. Oftentimes sighted vertically suspended head-up in clear oceanic or inshore waters with the rays of the two dorsal fin crests usually extended vertically upward while the pelvic fin rays may be horizontally spread outward and away from the body (Ref. 92949). This is hypothesized to be a feeding stance that visually allows the fish to spot the silhouette of its potential prey against the skylight (Ref. 49905). Feed on euphausiid crustaceans, small fishes and squid (Ref. 6738). Toothless protrusile jaws work to suction krill-laden water into its oro-branchial cavity and retained in the gullet by the long, spiny and bristly gill rakers (Ref. 92949). Occassionally associate in pairs (gender undocumented) but no record of group larger than three or of schooling behavior (Ref. 92949). Spawning occurs between July and December and larvae are encountered near the surface (Ref. 9337). Spawns in the North Pacific Ocean, in an area west of the Marianas Islands; also possibly in South Africa near Durban (Ref. 92949). In Guinness Book of Records as longest bony fish (Ref. 6472). Also caught with encircling nets and marketed fresh (Ref. 9337). Reputed to be unpalatable because the flesh is tasteless or otherwise unappetizing (Ref. 92949). Underwater footage shows them slowly swimming vertically, head up, with a stiff body, only undulating the dorsal fin, and with photophores on their appendages. The mouth can be protruded for capturing prey (RF, pers. comm. 2013). A rare species mainly offshore, sometimes drifting to coastal regions (Ref. 41299). Length based on occurrence record from Taiwan.

species.name: Oaxaca killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Oaxaca livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Obama anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found living among small holes in a hard limestone bottom covered with crustose calcareous algae, in areas of apparent ancient shorelines (undercut limestone ledges adjacent to sandy bottom.  Male specimens were taken by hand nets, each of which were in association with a single, presumed female (Ref. 114834).  FishBase common name coined by authors.

species.name: Obama’s Teleogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from a few rock outcrops located along a 40 km stretch of the middle Congo River, just upstream of Pool Malebo, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In August 2011, when water levels in the main channel of the middle Congo River reached an historic low (July-September 2011), a series of rocky outcrops, which in previous (and subsequent) years had been completely submerged, became partially exposed and accessible for sampling; and it was only on these that specimens of Teleogramma obamaorum were collected. Since only very few rocky outcrops were located, and most of the shoreline was comprised of sandy or reed-fringed banks, this suggests that the short stretch where all T. obamaorum specimens were collected may represent the entire distributional range of the species. The stomach and full length of gut of all collected specimens contained small, intact shells of two species of rissooidean gastropods (superfamily Rissooidea) but in most cases, no other food items were present; a few individuals with some disarticulated remains of ephemeropteran nymphs. The male and female of this species are monomorphic and distinguished externally only by examination of the genital papilla. A female individual, although collected while reproductively active, also appeared to lack the pronounced red flush of color on the belly (reported to be observed with females of other Teleogramma species and most chromidotilapiines). Fecundity appears to be low, the largest female examined (6.38 cm SL) contained only 19 ovoid eggs measuring approximately 0.02 cm in height and 0.18 cm at widest girth and the smallest female (5.19 cm SL) contained 15 eggs of a similar size (Ref. 104438).

species.name: Obbes' catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in slow-flowing streams, backwaters, swamps and lily lagoons, usually among aquatic weeds such as eel grass (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Also found in lakes (Ref. 2847).  Feeds on insects, prawns and mollusks (Ref. 5259, 44894).

species.name: Obese dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Oblada
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious, forms aggregations over rocky bottoms or seagrass beds (Zostera and seaweeds). Omnivorous but feeds mainly on small invertebrates (Ref. 3688). Important food fish.

species.name: Oblique butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on vertical rock faces (Ref. 13121).  Usually in small aggregations of up to about 6 individuals (Ref. 47838).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Oblique-banded cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Rocky and rubble reef, secretive under pieces or in the back of low caves (Ref. 48635). Solitary and cryptic, hides under ledges and rocks (Ref 90102).

species.name: Oblique-jaw thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling, occurring mostly inshore and entering estuaries and also Lake Chilka in India, thus able to tolerate lowered salinities. More data needed based on correct identifications. If this is the species being referred to in Ref. 6841, then the young feeds on surface plankton, chiefly on prawn larvae, but also small fishes (e.g. Stolephorus) and cypris. Apparently common.

species.name: Oblique-lined dottyback
species.description: A cryptic species found in or near holes of coral and rock reefs, occurring on tide pools, lagoonal reefs, and reef slopes (Ref. 9710, 37748). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Obliquebanded stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud or clay bottoms.

species.name: Obliquichthys maryannae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky reefs at depths of 1- 50 m (Ref. 13227) and usually seen schooling up to 5 m above substratum, although often seen resting in crevices (Ref. 84085).

species.name: Obliquogobius cirrifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from fine-sandy bottom (Ref. 75138).

species.name: Obliquogobius cometes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water (Ref. 42915).

species.name: Obliquogobius fulvostriatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Obliquogobius megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only specimen collected by beam trawl at 290 m depth (Ref. 75138).

species.name: Obliquogobius turkayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken between 434-496 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Obliquogobius yamadai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It has been suggested that some specimens were possibly captured from sandy or sandy-mud bottoms in the center and/or western parts of Tosa Bay at the depths of 30-100 m (Ref. 75138).

species.name: Oblong ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oblong slipmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inner reef flats and silty coastal waters to a depth of 20 m or more.

species.name: Obscure damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon, coastal and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), usually on open rubble patches (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Obscure dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Obscure flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud or sand bottoms (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Obscure Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Generally found at low to moderate elevations (lowland to foothill reaches) in different stream types, ranging from slower-flowing, clear to turbid, medium to larger rivers (4-20 m average width), gently or moderately fast flowing smaller creeks (0.5-4.0 m average width), also in anabranches, billabongs and some wetlands, including disconnected pools in drying water courses. It is recorded from shallow riffle areas along the edge of pools as juveniles, to deeper (0.1- >1.2 m average depth), more open water habitats in pools as adults, although also usually in glides. Often found among dense aquatic vegetation and timber debris, occasionally in the open in midwater or just under the surface. Recorded often at densities up to 0.7-1.6 fish/m2, but can be very abundant in swamps, billabongs and isolated pools (up to 8.0 fish/m2). Collected with a diverse range of fish and decapod crustacea, commonly with Galaxias olidus, Galaxias arcanus, Gadopsis marmoratus (River blackfish), Nannoperca australis (Southern Pygmy Perch), Retropinna sp. (Australian Smelt), Philypnodon grandiceps (Flatheaded Gudgeon), Common Freshwater Shrimp and Common Yabby. It appears to have high physico-chemical tolerance as recorded from isolated pools with high water turbidity or salinity levels (e.g. Wimmera and Glenelg river systems), or stagnant, refuge pools with high loads of dissolved organic carbon from leachates of Eucalyptus leaves (e.g. Marne River) and upper Avoca River system. It has been found to be infected with the parasitic copepod Lernaea cyprinoides, and can be lightly to heavily infected with small grey to black cysts, possibly trematode metacercariae, embedded in the skin of the head or trunk, or in the fins. A small number of fish were recorded with a short, thin, white worm, coiled and pointed at both ends, from amongst fat deposits around the stomach in the body cavity, others with small ulcers on the body. Deformities recorded of fins (dorsal, pectoral, and pelvic), jaws and posterior margin of the gill cover, and some with curvature of the spine (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Obscure garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on silty bottom (Ref. 33408).

species.name: Obscure goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from freshwater and brackish habitats, from mangrove creeks to a lily-covered lake (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Obscure jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Obscure pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline species (Ref. 58920).  Adults migrate to freshwater to spawn (Ref. 58920).

species.name: Obscure ruff
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Obscure swamp eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a variety of habitats from standing water in small muddy pools to clear running water in streams and larger bodies of water such as lakes (Ref. 79717).  The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Obscure triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from offshore islands and coastal rock stacks.  Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Obtuse sandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms.

species.name: Occella iburia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Occella kasawae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Occella kuronumai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Occidental blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ocean triggerfish
species.description: Common near drop-offs of seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Occasionally in shallow water. Solitary or in small groups in open water. Often associated with Sargassum (Ref. 9710). Feeds mainly on large zooplankton. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 13121.

species.name: Oceania fantail ray
species.description: This species probably occur mainly inshore, with types collected from surge channels in fringing coral reefs, to at least 18 m depth (Ref. 110363)..

species.name: Oceanic flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oceanic lightfish
species.description: Epi- to abyssopelagic (Ref. 58302) but usually mesopelagic, mainly found at 200-400 m by day and upper 100 m by night (Ref. 4778).  Both juveniles and adults exhibit diel vertical migration (Ref. 4778).  Feeds mainly on copepods, feeding intensively in the afternoon to early evening (Ref. 4778).  Adult photophore complement attained at about 18-20 mm SL (Ref. 4778).

species.name: Oceanic pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sub-adults and adults are demersal and have been found among gravel and coral rubble.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 5.4 cm SL.

species.name: Ocellate cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on muddy bottoms.  Adults are sometimes caught by trawl nets, but the young are rather rare (Ref. 559). Mximum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Ocellate damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Comprises several color forms, or geographical variations (Ref. 48636).  Adults are found in mixed coral and rubble areas of  lagoon and seaward reefs from the lower surge zone to a depth of 40 m (Ref. 1602).  Solitary (Ref. 37816).  Feed on filamentous algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Ocellate duckbill
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ocellate eel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal pools to 3 m.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans.  Eggs with cruciform hooks on the surface.

species.name: Ocellate frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore trawling grounds and may enter cray pots.

species.name: Ocellate skate
species.description: Benthic (Ref. 51024).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ocellate soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral heads of lagoon and seaward reefs from 3 to at least 15 m (Ref. 1602). Solitary or in pairs, seldom seen (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ocellate spot skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom-dweller that feeds on invertebrates and bony fish.  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 4.8-6.6 cm long and 2.9-3.7 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253, 41298).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).

species.name: Ocellate triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are said to be associated with red coralline gravel and shell substrates (Ref. 13227).   Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ocellated blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore among algae and rocks; usually shallower than 70 meters, but recorded to more than 300 meters (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Ocellated cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found in shallow sheltered lagoons and harbors, hiding among rocks, rubble, or clumps of brown algae (Ref. 1602).  Nocturnal species. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ocellated damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 9710), probably subject to surge to 20 m depth. Poorly known species that is seldom seen. Probably overlooked because of the drab appearance. Juveniles unknown and probably have large ocellus like N. thoracotaeniatus (Ref. 48636). Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Ocellated dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602); in sheltered rocky reef habitats in few meters depth, usually in small loose groups (Ref. 48636).  Occurs in rubble and algal turfs (Ref. 90102) and tidepools (Ref. 111072). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Ocellated dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found resting only on the substrate at the mouth of a river in an estuary (Ref. 116739).

species.name: Ocellated flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelves.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 30463, 48637) and small benthic animals.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Ocellated frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Largest species of frogfish in western Atlantic (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Ocellated killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Ocellated labyrinth fish
species.description: Inhabits both temporary and permanent streams and swamps (Ref. 4903). Feeds on insect larvae and crustacea (Ref. 4903, 12526). Juveniles are found in interstitial pools in papyrus.  Browses on plant tissues with ostracods, dipteran larvae, beetles, mollusks and debris (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Ocellated pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble patches of shallow sheltered reefs (Ref. 37816).  Found to a depth of 12 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ocellated pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds, beels, canals and rivers (Ref. 1479).  Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers of the lower and middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).

species.name: Ocellated shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty near shore reefs, often stream mouths in 1-5 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ocellated snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with black and clear waters (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Ocellated spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapids and fast flowing waters over rocky substrate (Ref. 6060).

species.name: Ocellated splitfin goby
species.description: Collected on a gentlly sloping sand-calcareous bottom with scattered small calcareous rocks and ledges. It is also collected from fresh volcanic deposits, a submerged pyroclastic flow, mostly rocks with thin layer of dark sediments, scattering of small rocks, ledges and various sessile invertebrates (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Ocellated tonguefish
species.description: Inhabits sandy substrates, also those submerged beds of aquatic vegetation, in clear shallow waters near coral reefs.  Little is known of its biology since its captured infrequently and generally in small numbers; most captures were a single fish (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Ocellated tonguesole
species.description: Occurs in shallow water from tidal pools; rockpool with rock, algae and rubble (Ref. 123824).

species.name: Ochetobius elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochmacanthus alternus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochmacanthus batrachostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochmacanthus flabelliferus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochmacanthus orinoco
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochmacanthus reinhardtii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ochre-striped cardinalfish
species.description: Found in small aggregates among or near mounds of branching corals such as Porites cylindrica or P. nigrescens (Ref. 1602). Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35404).

species.name: Ochreband wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near substratum, over open bottoms of silty sand and coral rubble (Ref. 12420).  Juveniles in small groups.  Adults only seen solitary.

species.name: Ochrebanded goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits coastal waters down to 100 m.  Usually occurs in schools.  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 2110).

species.name: Ocmulgee shiner
species.description: Inhabits sandy and rocky runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Ocosia fasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental edges.

species.name: Ocosia possi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ocosia ramaraoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ocosia spinosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ocosia vespa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental edges.

species.name: Ocular blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoons to 15 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Common around coral reefs.  Adults manifest both sexual and geographic variation.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ocular coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ocynectes maschalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools.

species.name: Ocynectes modestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools.

species.name: Oda's skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water (Ref. 8630).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.7-5.9 cm long and 3.2-3.3 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: Odontamblyopus lacepedii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A species that creates elaborate burrows in mud.  Its burrows are tunnel-shaped, vertical, and extend to depths of 50-90 cm into the substrate; 4-9 other smaller tunnels radiate from the primary tunnel and connect to the outside.  Feeds on a variety of food including bivalves, crustaceans, cephalopods, and small fishes (Ref. 45323). At low tide, this fish is a facultative breather (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Odontamblyopus rebecca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontamblyopus roseus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontamblyopus rubicundus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Odontamblyopus tenuis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontanthias chrysostictus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over rocky bottoms in fairly deep water (Ref. 559).

species.name: Odontanthias dorsomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontanthias elizabethae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over hard substrates with holes (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Odontanthias flagris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper rocky reefs (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Odontanthias grahami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontanthias hensleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontanthias katayamai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontanthias rhodopeplus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper rocky reefs (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Odontanthias unimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper rocky reefs (Ref. 39231).

species.name: Odontanthias wassi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontaspide féroce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on or near the bottom of the continental and insular shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 6871); sometimes in shallow water (Ref. 6871).  Tagging showed the species dives up to 2,000 m at Malpelo Island, Colombia (S.Bessudo, pers.comm. 06/09).  Feeds on small bony fishes, squids, and crustaceans (Ref. 13568).  Uses its long body cavity and large, oily liver to regulate buoyancy.  Ovoviviparous, embryos feeding on yolk sac and other ova produced by the mother (Ref. 50449).  Not implicated in attacks on people (Ref. 247).  Flesh utilized for  human consumption and liver for its high squalene content (Ref. 247); utilization of fins, jaws and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Odonteleotris canina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes argentinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes bicudo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in exclusively freshwater lakes of the coastal laguna system (Ref. 47314).

species.name: Odontesthes brevianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in schools in caves and inlets very close to the surface or under piers (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Odontesthes hatcheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes humensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes incisa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes ledae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs almost exclusively in freshwater lakes, but also found occasionally in brackish water lagoons (Ref. 47314).

species.name: Odontesthes mauleanum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes mirinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes nigricans

species.name: Odontesthes orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes perugiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes piquava
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs exclusively in freshwater (Ref. 47314).

species.name: Odontesthes platensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes retropinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes smitti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes wiebrichi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontesthes yucuman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from reservoirs or immediately downstream of three Hydroelectric Power Plants of the rio Uruguay basin (Itá, Machadinho and Monjolinho). Occurs sympatrically with O. bonariensis (Valenciennes) and O. humensis de Buen in the upper rio Uruguay (Ref. 116661).

species.name: Odontobutis haifengensis

species.name: Odontobutis obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Takes up life at the bottom right after hatching; spends its whole life in freshwater.

species.name: Odontobutis platycephala

species.name: Odontostilbe avanhandava
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in rivers.  The largest specimen is 7.07 in standard length (Ref. 128907).

species.name: Odontostilbe dialeptura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stagnant puddles, ditches and creeks of low to moderate velocity, between 20 to 90 m elevation.  Herbivorous and feeds on "aufwuchs", diatoms, filamentous algae and seeds (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Odontostilbe dierythrura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe ecuadorensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe euspilurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe fugitiva
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe littoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe microcephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum size for females from Ref. 128907.

species.name: Odontostilbe mitoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe nareuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in oxbow lakes, river or small river habitats in forest with whitewater or turbid-white water and bottom consisting of sandy or muddy substrate with sticks, logs and leaves (Ref. 57085).

species.name: Odontostilbe pao
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the llanos, savannas and white water, together with the cheirodontines Cheirodontops geayi and Odontostilbe pulchra (Ref. 75063).

species.name: Odontostilbe paraguayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe parecis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in translucent water of quiet to medium flow, sandy bottom with pebbles and a depth of 1-1.2 m (Ref. 57085).

species.name: Odontostilbe pequira
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Odontostilbe pulchra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe roloffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe splendida
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy and sandy bottom and water depth nearly 1 m (Ref. 75063).

species.name: Odontostilbe stenodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostilbe weitzmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at lapa stream near the mouth and along the seawall of rock and the bridge of the road.  The largest specimens observed were 4.39 cm for males and 5.08 cm for females (Ref. 128907).

species.name: Odontostoechus lethostigmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Odontostomias masticopogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 27000).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Odontostomias micropogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, at least in young stages; possibly benthopelagic when large.  Occurs mostly close to the continental shelf.

species.name: Offshore cardinalfish
species.description: Benthic species which occurs over soft bottom (Ref. 75154). Found in sand/silt bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Offshore lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Absent from the shore zone.

species.name: Offshore pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens known only from plankton samples collected by midwater trawl or surface dipnet.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Offshore tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Ogasawara gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ogasawara sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools in underwater rock recesses in groups of up to ca. 10 individuals, associated with very large numbers of Pempheris schwenkii being observed in the same rock recesses (Ref. 123196).

species.name: Ogcocephalus cubifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found on sandy, muddy, or rocky bottoms.

species.name: Ogcocephalus notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ogcocephalus porrectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ogilby's ghost flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Temperate species which occurs in the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Ogilby's hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters, including bays and estuaries (Ref. 36661); can tolerate salinity as low as 3 parts per thousand (Ref. 9760).  Usually in schools (Ref. 36661).  Feeds on amphipods, copepods, isopods, crab and barnacle larvae, polychaetes, gastropods, chironomid midges, hymenopterans, ants, foraminiferans, and plant matter (Ref. 9760).  Opportunistic feeder (Ref. 9760).  Probably used as bait and for fishmeal (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Ogilby's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not very well known, however, 7 specimens were collected in the lower reaches of a river in 1907.

species.name: Ogilby's weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly in shallow weedy areas in green or brown weeds (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Ogilbyina salvati
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from around coral rubble, patch reefs, rocks and coral heads in tidal pools and shallow lagoon areas to depths of are least 5 m (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Ogilbys ghostshark
species.description: Occurs in the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205). Caught with bottom trawls but not utilized at present although its meat is of high quality (Ref. 6871, 9904) but of low value (Ref.58048).

species.name: Ogre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58426).  Adults occur mainly between 500 and 2,000 m, but ranging from near the surface (young) to 5,000 m.  Form schools, swim in small groups or solitary.  Carnivorous (Ref. 27155), feeding on crustaceans when young and on fish mainly when adults (Ref. 4737).  Serve as food for pelagic fishes such as tuna, albacore, and marlin (Ref. 5951).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36624).

species.name: Ohrid gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups in lakes, usually on sand to pebble bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ohrid minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes and brooks, in shallow still waters (Ref. 59043).  Is threatened due to pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Oibita catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oidiphorus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Oidiphorus mcallisteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from 2 specimens.

species.name: Oily bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Okaloosa darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit vegetated sand runs of clear creeks (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Okamejei leptoura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits upper continental slope (Ref. 114953). Length of adolescent males 32.7-46.3 cm TL, some individuals with no clasper development at 35.6 cm TL; males mature at 39.4-48.6 cm TL, with smallest juvenile at 14.7 cm TL (Ref. 75645).

species.name: Okamejei mengae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Okamejei philipi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Okamoto’s deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Okapi goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits isolated patch reefs surrounded by fine white sand (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Okavango robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shoals in shallow, vegetated marginal and floodplain habitats.  Appears to prefer a swampy environment to open water (Ref. 13337).  Feeds on small aquatic insects and other invertebrates.  A partial spawner, breeding during high-water periods (Ref. 7248).  Known to migrate up rivers and on to floodplains during flood season (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Okavango suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky rapids as well as in fringing vegetation in the mainstream current.  Feeds on small invertebrates and algae from the surface of rocks and plants (Ref. 7248).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Okavango tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and floodplain habitats, especially enriched pans and well-vegetated shallow littoral margins of drainage rivers.  Feeds on detritus, soft plants and insect larvae.  Males establish a territory and attract a ripe female to form a pair bond.  Females construct a saucer-shaped nest in which eggs are laid and fertilized then tended mainly by the female while the male guards the territory (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Okefenokee pygmy sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, heavily vegetated sloughs and small sluggish streams, usually over mud. Oviparous, eggs are deposited in aquatic vegetation, preferably on strands of Ceratophyllum sp. when available (Ref. 58020).

species.name: Okhotsk skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 8.5 cm long and 6.7 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Okinawa chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Okinawa flap-headed goby
species.description: Inhabits intertidal pools and silty bottoms of estuaries (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Okinawa goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among staghorn Acropora corals in lagoons and hovers among or above the branches and also rests on them (Ref. 1602, 48637); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Occurs in aggregations of 5-15 individuals.

species.name: Okinawa seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young individuals are frequently found in brackish waters (Ref. 637).  Commercially cultured in Japan.

species.name: Okinawan silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found along the open coast or sometimes in the inner parts of bays (Ref. 92894).

species.name: Okinawan yellow-fin seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Large and fully matured adults are caught around coastal waters of Okinawa Island in midwinter, observed when fishery of this species is carried out by using set nets, gill nets, and bottom long-lines. Juveniles smaller than 10 cm) occur near shore from late spring to mid-summer. Almost nothing is known about the larvae and juveniles in spite of the commercial importance of this species in Okinawa Island, Japan (Ref. 75207).

species.name: Oktedi rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams of 300-500 m elevation 900-950 km upstream from the sea (Ref. 2847).  Is an omnivorous egg layer, generally peaceful community fish which prefers the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.3, H=12, 23°C water temperature with rock, plant and driftwood cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Okumus trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oldman klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in weedy tide pools and subtidal areas.

species.name: Olga cory
species.description: Prefers clean, clear water with current.

species.name: Oligobrycon microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligolepis cylindriceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in brackish waters in river deltas.  Feeds on zooplankton, crustaceans, insects and insect larvae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Oligolepis dasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligolepis formosanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligolepis jaarmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near the river mouth.

species.name: Oligolepis stomias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus acutirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus amome
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus bolivianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus brevioris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus hepsetus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Inhabits shallow, densely vegetated microhabitats in small streams or along the banks of larger rivers (Ref. 106564).  Feeds mostly on fishes (Ref. 598).  Two rodents (Sigmodontinae) were found in the stomachs of two individuals in different rivers located in the southern Brazilian Atlantic Rain Forest, in March and November 2010. These represent the first records of this species feeding on mammals (Ref. 106564).

species.name: Oligosarcus itau
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus jacuiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus jenynsii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 79585).

species.name: Oligosarcus longirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus menezesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus paranensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus perdido
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river where the upper portion is located on a carbonate plateau of about 68 km long.  The river in the plateau is dammed by calcareous tufa deposits, forming 1 to 6 m tall sequences of waterfalls.  The substrate is composed of many logs, branches and whole trees ling on whitish calcareous clay.  Inhabits stretches with sluggish to still waters and appears to occur in low densities.  Adults are active from dusk to around 21:00 from near the surface to 2 m deep and always solitary and observed resting after this time along the vertical rocky banks.  They remain hidden during the daylight hours.  Young fish are observed active during the day, in small groups of 5-6 individuals (Ref. 72405).

species.name: Oligosarcus pintoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus planaltinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus platensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus robustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oligosarcus schindleri

species.name: Olive barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rivers, streams, lakes and backwaters.  Tolerant of salinity.  They form schools in groups of four or five to several dozens (Ref. 6028).  Feed on aquatic insects, fish, algae and shrimps.  Spawn in running waters among submerged boulders and vegetation (Ref. 4832).  Small fish have limited demand in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Olive cory
species.description: Feeds on insect larvae.

species.name: Olive darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately deep boulder riffles and runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on hydropsychid caddis larvae and heptageniid mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Olive dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among corals.  Minimum depth reported from (Ref. 27115).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413).

species.name: Olive rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes found well off bottom, in or near kelp or over rocky reefs (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Olive skiffia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit thickly planted shores.  Cultivated almost exclusively in scientific institutions.

species.name: Olive snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water (Ref. 40865).  Probably spends most of the day in a burrow along the river bank and forages actively at night for small fishes (Ref. 12693); in soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Olive wide-eyed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.

species.name: Olive-tailed flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms of the continental shelf at a depth range of 15-95 m (Ref. 3476).

species.name: Olivegreen ufipa barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Olmec blind catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species.

species.name: Olmec priapella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow to fast-moving water. Mainly carnivorous, feeding on insects, insect larvae, small crustaceans and planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 89993). Found along with Xiphophorus hellerii and Poecilia mexicana.

species.name: Olomina toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An insectivorous fish generally inhabits waters of low to moderate current velocity; between 10 and 900 m elevation; at temperatures of 19 to 34°C; in surface or midwaters of brooks, streams.  Occasionally found in shallow waters of rivers (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Olympic mudminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet water with dense vegetation or other cover over mud and debris; also in cool, brown waters of bogs and swamps.

species.name: Olyra astrifera
species.description: Inhabits river with relatively clear water, substratum composed mostly of sand and small boulders, width of 62 m, depth from 0.5-4.5 m and 80-90 % riparian cover mostly overhanging vegetation.  Encountered in exposed bamboo roots along the edges of the bank with leaf litter and small grasses (Ref. 93959).

species.name: Olyra collettii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly wrongly attributed to the South-American fauna.  This species clearly belongs to South Asia.  It is possible that accidental mixing of specimens and or labels resulted in the assignment of this species to a Neotropical location (Ref. 55745).

species.name: Olyra horae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species.

species.name: Olyra kempi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers with swift flowing, clear water and with bottom of rocks and boulders (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Olyra longicaudata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small rocky streams at the base of hills.

species.name: Olyra saginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a shallow stream with moderate to strong current and substrate composed of sand, pebble and rocks.  Occurs in association with the following fish species:  <i>Badis spp. (Badidae), <i>Rasbora rasbora (Cyprinidae), <i>Garra spp, (Cyprinidae), <i>Glyptothorax chimtuipuiensis (Sisoridae), <i>G. caudimaculatus (Sisoridae) and <i>Pseudolaguvia nubila (Sisoridae) (Ref. 96386).

species.name: Oman blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky bottom.  Seen under ledges swimming upside down (Ref. 11441).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Oman bullhead shark
species.categoryName: Heterodontidae (Bullhead, horn, or Port Jackson sharks)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oman butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Oman cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens were collected from tide pools.

species.name: Oman cownose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic in the open ocean and often aggregating in large shoals (Ref. 114953). .  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Oman dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oman freshwater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oman goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly associated with a sessile invertebrate.

species.name: Oman jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Oman moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oman numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 114953). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018. Maturity size for females at ca. 31 cm TL; birth size at ca. 11 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Oman porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, over rocky bottom.

species.name: Oman sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Oman’s eyebrow goby
species.description: Occurs on shallow mudflat at Yeti, near the mouth of Wadi Aday (Muscat Area, northern Oman), which drains into the Gulf of Oman. Associated with the following species: Favonigobius reichei, Cryptocentroides arabicus, Planiliza klunzingeri and Terapon jarbua (Ref. 128815).

species.name: Omble de fontaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, cool, well-oxygenated creeks, small to medium rivers, and lakes (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Anadromous in some populations (Ref. 86798).  In its native range, general upstream movements have been observed in early spring, summer and late fall; downstream movements, in late spring and fall (Ref. 28546, 28548, 28549, 28550).  Some fish, popularly known as salters, run to the sea in the spring as stream temperature rises, but never venture more than a few kilometers from river mouths. It may remain at sea for up to three months (Ref. 28546, 28549, 28551).  Feeds on a wide range of organisms including worms, leeches, crustaceans, insects (chironomids, caddisflies, blackflies, mayflies, stoneflies and dragonflies (Ref. 5951), mollusks, fishes and amphibians (Ref. 3348, 10294); also small mammals (Ref. 1998).  Stomachs of some individuals contained traces of plant remains (Ref. 1998).  There are reports of introduced fish reaching 15 years of age in California, USA (Ref. 28545).  Cultured for food and for stocking (Ref. 27547).  Extensively used as an experimental animal (Ref. 1998).  Marketed fresh and smoked; eaten fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Omble à tête plate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep pools of large cold rivers and lakes (Ref. 5723).  Most common in high mountainous areas where snowfields and glaciers are present (Ref. 5723).  Rarely anadromous (Ref. 5723, Ref. 51243).  Lacustrine form matures in lakes and spawns in tributaries, where young reside for one to three years (Ref. 10367).

species.name: Omble-chevalier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Occurs in the sea along coasts, estuaries, rivers, and lakes with cold, clear water (Ref. 59043). Found in deep runs and pools of medium to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798). Anadromous forms spend a considerable time of their lives at sea; non-migratory populations remain in lakes and rivers (Ref. 4779).  Anadromous populations enter rivers to breed during fall and winter (Ref. 86798). Freshwater populations feed on planktonic crustaceans, amphipods, mollusks, insects and fishes (Ref. 4479).  Anadromous individuals feed little in freshwater and never feed during migrations.  Spawning usually takes place on pebble to stone bottom in lakes.  Riverine stocks spawn in rivers with slow current (02.-0.8 m/s), but there are some riverine anadromous stocks (in Norway) which spawn yearly in fast-flowing waters of riffles (Ref. 59043).  Extremely sensitive to water pollution (cold water and oxygen oriented) (Ref. 2163).  Marketed fresh, smoked, canned (Ref. 27547), and frozen.  Eaten sautéed, broiled, fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Parasitized by tapeworm (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Ombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits submontane reaches of rivers with a hard sand or stone bottom and well oxygenated, cold and fast-flowing water (Ref. 59043).  Prefers running, well-oxygenated waters of rivers (Ref. 30578).  In Scandinavia, it occurs in clear lakes and freshened part of northern Baltic basin.  Usually lives in hollows behind boulders and shaded water under overhanging vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Gregarious, forms schools (Ref. 2196).  Feeds mainly on insects (Ref. 9696), nymphs, small worms and crustaceans (Ref. 30578).  Breeds in shallow stretches, usually 20-40 cm deep, or riffles, with moderate current of about 0.5 m/s and clean gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Can be captured with natural bait (insect larvae) or with artificial fly.  Very sensitive to pollution (Ref. 30578).

species.name: Ombre arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open water of clear, cold, medium to large rivers and lakes.  Enters rocky creeks to spawn (Ref. 5723).  Occurs in piedmont and montane cold streams, rivers and lakes with high oxygen concentrations (Ref. 59043).  Forms schools in moderate numbers (Ref. 9988).  Young feed on zooplankton with a gradual shift to immature insects; adults feed mainly on surface insects but also take in  fishes, fish eggs, lemmings, and planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 1998).  Spawns in montane streams with heavy current on shallows with rock-gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).  Utilized fresh and can be fried, broiled, boiled, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Ombrine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mud and sandy bottoms of the shelf and upper slope (Ref. 4780), 14° to 15° C (Ref. 36731).  Feed on small shrimps, worms and other bottom invertebrates (Ref. 4780).  Sold fresh and dried salted (Ref. 3490).

species.name: Ombrine (Umbrina cirrosa)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky and sandy bottoms in coastal waters.  Juveniles enter estuaries.  Feed on bottom invertebrates.

species.name: Ombrine d'Argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Especially abundant at about 100 m depth (Ref. 27363).  Found over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Ombrine de Bussing
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ombrine de Steindachner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Ombrine de Wintersteen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water, has only been caught at a depth of 2 m (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Ombrine des Galapagos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky or sandy coasts and in bays, from near the shore to a depth of at least 18 m (Ref. 9118).  Considered a good food fish (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Ombrine fusca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species (Ref. 27000).  Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Juveniles may occur in littoral areas.  Feeds on shrimps, worms and other bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 4780).  Sold fresh (Ref. 3490).

species.name: Ombrine polla
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottom (Ref. 9118).  Juveniles also littoral pools (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on fishes, crustaceans and bivalves (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Ombrine pétote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the surf zone along sandy beaches, but in clear water.  Also occurs over muddy bottoms in estuaries and sometimes near coral reef areas.  Feeds on small crustaceans washed out of sand by the surf (Ref. 5521).  Large specimens are marketed mostly fresh; smaller ones are used as bait.

species.name: Ombrine rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy areas along beaches.  Marketed fresh or salted, or sold for bait.

species.name: Ombrine à longue aile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy coasts and bays, also in littoral pools (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on crustaceans and worms (Ref. 9118).  Considered a good food fish (Ref. 9118). Sold fresh and its meat is highly valued (Ref. 55763).

species.name: Ombrine à nageoire jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy areas, often in surf zones, bays and tidal sloughs.  Feed on fishes, crustaceans, marine worms and bivalves (Ref. 9118)  Often caught by surf fishers.  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Ombrine épineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy coasts and bays, also in the surf zone (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on crabs, other crustaceans and marine worms (Ref. 9118).  Good food fish (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Omega lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Omegophora cyanopunctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Omisco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, deep flowing pools of creeks, and rivers (Ref. 5723).  Usually found over sand (Ref. 5723).  Moves into the shallows of lakes at night  to feed and moves back to deeper water as dawn approaches (Ref. 1998).  Feeds on insect larvae, amphipods and fishes (Ref. 1998).  Important forage fish (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Omn guitarfish
species.description: Apparently a benthic species on inner continental shelf. Unknown life history.  Maturity size unknown but a male was found mature at 50 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Omo lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Omobranchus anolius

Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus aurosplendidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rocky shore areas.  Adults feed on algae and detritus (Ref. 9137).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus fasciolatoceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults rarely enter brackish water.  Attain less than 8 cm TL.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus hikkaduwensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus loxozonus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in rocky shore areas.  Attain less than 8 cm TL.   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus smithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus steinitzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omobranchus zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in mangroves and brackish waters (Ref. 4833).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Omosudid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic at 700-1830 m (Ref. 58302).  Probably swift swimmers, which can avoid nets, captured singly or in small groups (Ref. 6692).  Carnivorous, feed on squids and pelagic fishes (Ref. 6692).  Oviparous and are synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 84733).

species.name: Omox blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species, living among the roots of mangrove trees (Ref. 559).  Also found in estuaries and stream mouths (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

Moves into seasonally flooded habitats during periods of high water and can usually be found around submerged woody vegetation.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recently collected specimen found in shallow blackwaters in a peat swamp heavily disturbed by logging activities.

species.name: Ompok pluriradiatus

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large, slow flowing rivers and lakes (Ref. 52514) and swamps (Ref. 56749).  Juveniles sometimes occur in smaller streams (Ref. 52514).  Feeds on smaller fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 52514).

species.name: Ompok siluroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams and rivers of all sizes with currents ranging from sluggish to moderate (Ref. 12693).
