species.name: Ompok sindensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ompok supernus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs most frequently in large slow-flowing rivers and lakes.  Migrates into inundated forest during periods of high water, where it can be found around submerged woody vegetation. Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 52514).

species.name: Ompok weberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Onaç spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oncorhynchus formosanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at temperatures below 15 °C.  Feeds mainly on insects.

species.name: One spot toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: One-and-a-half-stripe hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found on rocky areas cleared of sediment.  Feeds on eggs (Ref. 5595).

species.name: One-eyed blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A relatively rare species found in shallow weedy areas.

species.name: One-spot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: One-spot moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surge-swept seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Mostly found in oceanic islands (Ref 90102).

species.name: One-stripe anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in or near caves and ledges of seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Adults swim upside-down (Ref. 37816, 48635). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: One-stripe spinyeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in running and stagnant waters (Ref. 4833).  Found in fresh and brackish waters and deltas of large rivers, common in ponds and slow flowing rivers with vegetation in plains (Ref. 41236).  Inhabits still waters with silt or mud substrate.  Believed to be common in rice paddy fields.  Nocturnal feeder, on insects and worms.

species.name: One-striped fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs, usually on sheltered inshore reefs (Ref. 41819) which occur mainly solitarily (Ref. 48636). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimicked by Cheilodipterus parazonatus and juvenile Scolopsis margaritifer (Ref. 90102) and juvenile Cheilodipterus zonatus (Ref. 9710). Also mimicked by the apogonid C nigrotaeniatus which is much more widespread and adapts in coloration to various Meiacanthus spp. Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: One-striped poison-fang blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on reef slopes with large soft-coral communities (Ref. 48636).  They form groups usually among gorgonians or black coral (Ref. 90102) in shallow protected reefs.  Relatively common and broadly distributed.  Feed on zooplankton.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Onefin skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 800 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 57911).  Max. width (Teodoro Vaske Jr., pers. comm., 2002).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males are unknown (Ref. 37039).

species.name: Oneknife unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally uncommon species found in steep outer lagoon and seaward reef slopes (Ref. 9710, 48637). Maximum depth reported at 40m (Ref. 37792) Occurs singly or in large schools (Ref. 9710, 48637). Usually seen swimming steadily along upper edges of drop-offs in pursuit of plankton (Ref. 48637). A semi-pelagic fish that feeds on zooplankton, but remains over or near reefs. Also feeds on algae (Ref. 30573). It is cleaned by Labroides and sleeps on reefs at night, taking on a disruptive mottled pattern (Ref. 10671). Caught with nets (Ref. 30573).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock and coral reefs and may be found in tidepools at depths of 6 m and shallower (Ref. 90102). Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Onespot waspfish

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water but also lives in silty water.  Occurs in swift currents over bedrock, large boulders and cobble substrates covered with periphyton. Feeds on algae and animals living in the algae. Shares habitat with <i>Mystacoleucus obtusirostris, <i>Osteochilus vittatus, <i>Poropuntius deauratus, <i>Channa gachua, <i>Yasuhikotakia morleti, and <i>Acantopsis dialuzona. The following water conditions were recorded:  Dissolved oxygen 82.7−91.4%; conductivity 12−25 μS.cm-1 ; and flow velocity 0.12−0.77 m/s (Ref. 102622).

species.name: Onychostoma krongnoense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lotic habitats of main streams with clear water. Prefers erosional zones such as runs and riffles with swift currents over periphyton covering bedrock, large boulders and cobble substrates when foraging. Shoals preferably the depositional zones such as fast flowing pools with detritus and fallen leaves (habitats alternate in rapid succession).  Found syntopic with <i>Poropuntius sp., <i>Neolissochilus stracheyi, <i>Annamia normani, <i>Schistura spp., <i>Glyptothorax sp. and <i>Channa gachua. Also shares habitat in the lower reaches of Ea Krong No with <i>Poropuntius sp., <i>Tor spp., <i>Lobocheilus delacouri, <i>Crossocheilus reticulatus, <i>Garra fuliginosa, <i>Garra cambodgiensis, <i>Gyrinocheilus aymonieri, <i>Annamia normani, <i>Schistura spp., and <i>Channa gachua. Feeds on pinnate diatoms (Order Bacillariales) and filamentous algae such  <i>Spirogyra sp., <i>Mougeotia sp., and <i>Oedogonium sp. (Ref. 102622).

species.description: Occurs in clear hill streams with gravelly or rocky bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Opsarius kanaensis
species.description: Found in fast-flowing stream and river with clear water, gravel or cobble bottoms; associated with Schistura manipurensis, Pethia meingangbii, Glyptothorax granulus, Channa marulius, Rasbora ornatus, Devario aequipinnatus, Acanthocobitis zonalternans, Botia histronica (Ref. 126981).

species.name: Opsarius koratensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs in large, quiet and deep, often turbid waters (Ref. 37788). Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975). Reported to occur over gravel substrate in clear, swift, small streams up to rapidly flowing stretches of large rivers.  Feed on insect larvae, especially trichopterans.  Rarely seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Opsarius maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Opsarius nelsoni
species.description: Inhabits clear gravelly streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Opsarius ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Opsarius pectoralis
species.description: Occurs in terrestrial streams with very cold water and stony and rocky bed (Ref. 93114).

species.name: Opsarius pulchellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over gravel substrate in clear, swift, small streams up to rapidly flowing stretches of large rivers.  Feed on insect larvae, especially odonatans.  Rarely seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Opsarius putaoensis
species.description: Associated fish species from the type locality: Psilorhynchus brachyrhynchus, Opsarius barnoides, Garra bispinosa, Placocheilus dulongensis, Homalopteroides rupicola, Schistura sikmaiensis, Schistura malaisei (Ref. 121827).

species.name: Opsarius sajikensis
species.description: Occurs in fast flowing waters with clear water, cobble, pebble and sandy bottoms. Found together with the following species: Acantopsis spectabilis, Paracanthocobitis tumitensis, and P. zoanlternans, Badis ferraris, Botia histronica, Synchrossus berdmorei, Channa marulius, Gonorhynchus burmanicus, Devario aequipinnatus, Garra gravelyi, Lepidocephalichthys guntea, Mastacembelus armatus, Macrognathus morehensis and others (Ref. 126953).

species.name: Opsarius shacra
species.description: Found in rivers and streams (Ref. 4832).  Collected in large river with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).

species.name: Opsarius signicaudus
species.description: Inhabits mountainous areas in fast-flowing streams and small rivers with clear water and gravel or cobble bottoms. Juveniles occur near shallow shorelines and behind large rocks where the flow is slower. Sympatric with Barilius koratensis, Poropuntius melanogrammus, Mystacoleucus marginatus, Garra spp., Rasbora cf. rasbora, Rasbora paucisqualis, Microdevario kubotai, Crossocheilus siamensis, Labiobarbus sp., Acanthocobitis zonalternans, Schistura spp., Nemacheilus pallidus, Botia morleti, Glyptothorax spp., Batasio tigrinus, Xenenthodon sp., Parambassis siamensis, Tetraodon sp. (Ref. 93076).

species.name: Opsarius tileo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams and rivers with pebbly or sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Orange angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic species found in reefs (Ref. 58302); in coral bottoms of channels and over reef slopes (Ref. 9710); also in areas with rubble bottom (Ref. 4858).  Often in small loose groups on inner reefs in low patches of brittle corals and coralline algae mix that is shared by damselfishes and small wrasses (Ref. 48636).  Herbivorous (Ref. 33482).  Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Orange bellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf and slope. Identification of Notopogon species are difficult because body shape and development change with age and perhaps sex (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Orange blotched eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy bottoms (Ref. 95408).

species.name: Orange brotula
species.description: Rare, shallow water inhabitant (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Orange cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species, occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Orange chromide
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons and small streams.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Often found among marginal roots and weeds in lagoons and some dry zone tanks (now relatively rare in the latter habitat).  Feeds on fish fry, zooplankton and algae.

species.name: Orange clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rock pools at low tide and sub-tidally.  Found clinging under rocks or boulders in more sheltered areas.  Feeds on amphipods, gastropods, and fishes.  Takes cover when disturbed.

species.name: Orange clinid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock pools and subtidal area down to 30 m. Usually found living on brown algae (Carpophyllum and Cystophora). Feeds on small weed dwelling crustaceans.

species.name: Orange croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Orange dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species, quick to take shelter. Found on offshore coral and rocky reefs from shallow depths down to about 25m (Ref. 68964). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413, 130616).

species.name: Orange dwarf toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orange eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orange eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species inhabiting shallow reefs (Ref. 34024).  A benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Orange finned toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in currents of low to high velocity; in brooks and streams between 25-1270 m elevation; in temperatures of 17-35°C.  Swims in small groups at all depths, over rock or sand substrata.  Reproduces continuously all year round.  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects, especially ants and termites (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Orange goggle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known only from the holotype which was collected at 14-16 m depth, from a steep coral-reef sloping down to about 30 m depth, where the upper half of the slope with short steps covered with hard and soft corals, and the specimen was collected at the entrance of small with cave (Ref. 121824).

species.name: Orange margin butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was observed in areas of basalt substrata (e.g., basalt talus, blocky lava, lava tubes and pillows, basalt boulders) and in limestone habitats (primarily limestone holes and ledges). Observed also in the vicinity of an unidentified antipatharian coral, near Cirrhipathes spiralis (Linnaeus), and Antipathes dichotoma Pallas. This species in association with limestone ledges and discontinuities representing ancient shorelines, almost in all cases, the fish were found underneath, inside of, or in close proximity to small undercut overhangs or caves, often swimming upside-down in association with the roof of the overhangs and caves. However, there are no obvious associations with other species, such as antipatharian corals, other corals and sessile invertebrates, or particular fish species; although certain species, such as Odontanthias fuscipinnis (Jenkins, 1901) and the wrasse Bodianus sanguineus (Jordan & Evermann, 1903), these species tend to occupy the same depth and habitat. Collected with hand nets during deep dives using mixed-gas, closedcircuit rebreathers (Ref. 116690). FishBase common name agreed by authors.

species.name: Orange notothen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds primarily on fish eggs.  Other less important food items are amphipods, decapods, fishes, isopods, polychaetes and nemerteans.

species.name: Orange perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563) near rocky reefs (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Orange pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rock crevices or caves.  Probably reaching 17-18 cm SL.  Males mature at about 15 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orange reef-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky estuary reefs, in small caves, usually in pairs (Ref. 9002). Cryptic (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Orange river mudfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a variety of habitats:  quiet well vegetated backwaters, standing open waters, flowing open waters, sandy-rocky stretches and rocky rapids.  Their preferred habitat is flowing rocky channels.  Bottom feeder which grazes algae and organic detritus (Ref. 6465).  Breeds in summer, gathering in large numbers in shallow rocky rapids where eggs are laid.  Larvae hatch after 3 or 4 days.  May live up to 8 or 9 years (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Orange scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Orange seam snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orange snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamp forest (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Orange spotted damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on shallow coral reegs in calm areas (Ref. 124650). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orange wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Inhabits depths up to at least 50 m (Ref. 26203).

species.name: Orange-banded scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs with sandy substrata.  Depth extension 25-30 for underwater photographs taken off Izu Peninsula and a single specimen reported to be collected from Okinawa Trough at 205 meters (Ref. 54394).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Orange-black dragonet
species.description: Collected from a sandy bottom (Ref. 35443).  May occur solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Orange-freckled flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orange-fringed largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in pools and quiet stretches of rivers with sandy substrates and dense marginal vegetation.  Feeds on small fish and aquatic insects (Ref. 6465). Agamous, ovophilic (Ref. 52307) maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 7248, 52307), the female carries the eggs and larvae (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Orange-red pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear coastal reefs, near sponges (Ref. 48637).  Usually hovers upside-down in small caves in coral reefs. Forms small loose groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Orange-socket surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow reefs, both in lagoons and outer reef areas.  They frequently move in groups.  Juveniles found between soft corals in lagoons at depths of up to 2 m (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Adults in groups, often mixed with other similar species (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Orange-spotted clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orange-spotted goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand and rubble patches, located on ledges of steep seaward or lagoon reef slopes or at the base of these slopes.  The fish lies on the bottom, retreating into crevices when threatened (Ref. 31115). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Orange-spotted sand-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms of caves of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602, 48637).

species.name: Orange-spotted therapon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orange-spotted toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small loose groups on shallow coastal sand flats and in estuaries.  Often sleeps during the day by burrying itself under the sand with just eyes exposed (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Orange-striped goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms of inshore bays and lagoons from about 3 to at least 20 m and uses a vertical, tube-like burrow of an unidentified invertebrate for refuge (Ref. 1602).  Occurs in coastal and inner reefs on sand and rubble flats to about 20 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Feeds by sifting mouthfuls of sand to capture small invertebrates and organic matter (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Orange-striped shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the outer reef slopes; often found in pairs, hovering a few centimeters above the sandy bottom at the entrance to its burrow. Symbiotic with the red-and-white barred shrimp, Alpheus randalli (Ref. 40962).

species.name: Orange-striped wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mixed coral, rubble, and sand slopes along the bases of steep protected seaward reefs (Ref. 37816).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Orangeback bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and reef areas.  Occurs in pairs (Ref. 9710).  Synchronously hermaphroditic.

species.name: Orangeback fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups along reef edges with rubble patches in depths to about 25 m.  Juveniles in small groups in shallower depths (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Orangebanded gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Most specimens taken in trawls have sand grains inside the mouth indicating occurrence on open, predominantly sandy substrata (Ref. 54394).

species.name: Orangebar anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300), near small patch reefs at the bases of drop-offs (Ref. 37816). Forms aggregations (Ref 90102).  Female max length (Ref. 48242).

species.name: Orangebeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orangebelly darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit gravel and rubble riffles and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Orangebelly goby
species.description: Inhabit open sand or shell-hash bottom with scattered small rocks (Ref. 39827).

species.name: Orangedotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Orangeface angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Least known (Ref. 48636).  A rare species that inhabits deep rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Orangefin anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit passages and outer reef slopes. Known to occur at 25°C. Feed chiefly on planktonic copepods, algae, echiuroid and sipunculoid worms, and pelagic tunicates. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Entacmaea quadricolor, Heteractis aurora, Heteractis crispa, Heteractis magnifica, Stichodactyla haddoni, and Stichodactyla mertensii (Ref. 5911). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Orangefin barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors clear-flowing waters, usually headwater streams with rocky habitats; feeds on insects (Ref. 7248, 52193). Known to ascend tributaries and move only onto floodplains in rainy season (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Orangefin darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast, rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in small streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on dipteran larvae (midges and blackflies) (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Orangefin madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of clear, swift, small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Orangefin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 3814, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Orangefin tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims incessantly.  Common and ubiquitous but is more frequently encountered at low tide in creeks with swift-flowing waters.  Feeds on plants and various invertebrates (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Orangefin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs or shallow rocky areas (Ref. 559) in groups, pairs or solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Orangefinned snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orangeflag blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers the low-energy habitats of protected mid-shelf reefs in Belize, with TP preferring holes in dead coral substrates, most often the coiled shells of dead vermetid gastropods. All specimens were collected in less than 5 m depth, with the single IP Honduran specimen collected on the lee side of Utila in a relatively protected area, in less than 5 m depth (Ref. 78428).

species.name: Orangehead anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in harems.  Minimum depth range from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Orangelined bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported as sometimes congregating beneath piers and near jetties and not often sighted during the day (Ref. 27767).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Orangelined wirrah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Orangemouth lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in and around reefs.  Found to depths over 12 m (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on small fishes.

species.name: Orangesided goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral formations surrounded by white sand (Ref. 5521).  Found singly or in pairs on small coral heads and sponges; also on rocky substrates (Ref. 46821).

species.name: Orangespotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky areas along quiet shores, usually in less than 3 m depth.  They feed on polychaete worms, crustaceans and filamentous algae (Ref. 5521).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Orangespotted goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty open bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Shares burrow with alpheid shrimp, usually in open bottom in less than 9 m depth.

species.name: Orangespotted puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orangespotted snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orangespotted soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orangespotted sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet pools of creeks and small to large, often turbid, rivers; usually near brush (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on microcrustaceans and aquatic insect larvae, principally chironomid dipterans (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Orangetail dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found in or near holes of coral or rock (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Orangetail filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Solitary among coral and rubble (Ref. 90102). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Orangetail shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and silt-bottomed pools and runs of headwaters, creeks and small rivers, usually along undercut banks and debris (Ref. 86798). Occurs in reduced current, under overhanging vegetation or an overhanging bank, around stumps or roots, or occasionally under floating debris caught on snags or trailing brush of Smilax or Vitis vines (Ref. 40813).

species.name: Orangethroat darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow gravel riffles, sometimes rocky runs and pools, of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Adults feed on midge and blackfly larvae, mayfly nymphs, isopods, amphipods, and caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).  Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 36980).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Orangethroat pikeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas in worm tubes.

species.name: Orbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water, over mud bottoms.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9616).

species.name: Orbiculate cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to coastal waters, forming small aggregations among mangroves, rocks, debris, or piers of shallow sheltered shorelines.  Feeds at night (early evening and just before day break), primarily on planktonic crustaceans.  Courtship and spawning occur fortnightly (shortly before new moons and full moons).  Eggs are incubated by the male for about 8 days.  Larval phase pelagic.  Sexual maturity is attained at 7 cm by males and at 6 cm by females (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Ordinary snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. a cryptic species that lives in sandy substrates (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ordway's brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit caves and crevices of rocky reefs (Ref. 11482). Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205). Grow to at least 10 cm (Ref. 11482); size of Brotula species is given as 'at least 75 cm' in Ref. 34024, which is followed here until better information becomes available (RF).

species.name: Oregon chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sluggish sand- and gravel-bottomed pools and backwaters of creeks and small rivers.  Often found in vegetation and sometimes in ponds and impoundments (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Oreichthys andrewi
species.description: Occurs mainly in open water with silt as the substrate and with little or no aquatic vegetation (Ref. 95042).

species.name: Oreichthys coorgensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in the headwaters of the Cauvery in Karnataka, in close association with submerged vegetation and debris in shallow waters, with little or no current, along the margins of swift running hill streams (Ref. 99423).

species.name: Oreichthys cosuatis
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in ditches, ponds, streams and canals (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Oreichthys crenuchoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreichthys duospilus
species.description: Occurs in a shallow, sluggish stream with a mixed sand and gravel bottom and scattered large boulders (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Oreichthys incognito
species.description: Found in shallow river with rapid flow over a substrate of gravel and cobbles and with river banks composed of stands of <i>Pandanus and other riparian vegetation.  Collected close to the bank among submerged vegetation (Ref. 99423).

species.name: Oreichthys parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in hill stream (Ref. 57235).  Usually found in clear, slow-flowing water (Ref. 43281).  Apparently a widely distributed species but overlooked because of its small size (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Oreochromis angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreochromis ismailiaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreochromis lepidurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Microphagous, using plankton (Ref. 2, 55074). Maternal, ovophilic mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Oreochromis mweruensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young Oreochromis mweruensis feed on epiphytic filamentous algae in swampy areas (Ref. 2), but also accept small invertebrates and zooplankton, a tendency they lose with age (Ref. 52307). Adults feed on filamentous algae and detritus (Ref. 52307) and bottom deposits, but those that migrated to the deeper northern end feed almost exclusively on plankton (Ref. 2).

species.name: Oreochromis saka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at a temperature range of 21.5-29.0 °C (Ref. 2).  Inhabits very shallow and vegetated regions.  Feeds on diatoms and debris collected  from the bottom and from between vegetation (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Oreochromis salinicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreochromis upembae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Oreoglanis colurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis delacouri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis frenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis heteropogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis hypsiurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis infulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in a steeply sloping rainforest stream 1-3 m wide; only in waterfalls where the fish were found adhering to vertical surfaces of rocks (Ref. 49549).

species.name: Oreoglanis insignis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis jingdongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis laciniosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis lepturus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis macronemus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mountain streams.

species.name: Oreoglanis majusculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis nakasathiani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis pangenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis setiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oreoglanis sudarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis suraswadii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis tenuicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a rocky, fast-flowing stream (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoglanis vicinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 83406).

species.name: Oreoleuciscus dsapchynensis

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky reefs with algae and coral (Ref. 9710).  Solitary or in groups (Ref. 9710).  Feed on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Oriental fringe stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from coastal waters of East Asia (Ref. 121635).

species.name: Oriental Goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Oriental lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Oriental maori wrasse
species.description: Found in coastal to outer reef habitats; juveniles often in crinoids or soft corals at moderate depths (Ref. 48636). Probably occurring deeper than normal diving depths (Ref. 35918). Reported to be associated with the mushroom Heliofungia actiniformis (Ref. 91291). Occurs among dense cover of coral rubble or algae. Feeds mainly on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans. Known in outer reef lagoons to deep slopes with other invertebrates (Ref. 9002). Females swim in small groups (Ref. 48636). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Oriental sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orinoco eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orinoco sailfin catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams and lakes (Ref. 44091) and in weedy, mud-bottomed canals (Ref. 5723).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal, feeds on algae (Ref. 13371), but will also feed on worms, insect larvae, and other bottom-dwelling aquatic animals (Ref. 44091).  Spawning period peaks once a year (Ref. 56986).  Reproductive behavior includes digging of burrows for egg laying (Ref. 82067). May exhibit male parental care (Ref. 56986).

species.name: Orinocodoras eigenmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orissa razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from the lower reaches of rivers, ponds and ditches (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Ornamented dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand bottoms near outer ocean reefs (Ref. 33412, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Ornamented goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large (5-10 m2 ), flat, sandy areas surrounded by live coral at about 14-15 m (Ref. 116128).

species.name: Ornamented wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs, coral-rich areas with sand patches (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds primarily on small benthic crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Ornate angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools along steep current-swept outer reef drop-offs from 45 to at least 97 m.  Forms harems of 3-7 individuals.  Feeds on plankton.  Rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).  At Canderawasih Bay common depth range is 20-25 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Ornate bagrid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ornate bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits calm waters of swamps and rivers (Ref. 11970).  It feeds on worms and insect larvae when young, but takes larger food, mainly fish, when adult (Ref. 27292).  It mainly hunts at night (Ref. 27292).  In general they are more or less solitary fish and do not form schools (Ref. 27292).

species.name: Ornate cowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters, more commonly in depths less than 20 m (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Ornate ctenopoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum total length reported 8.0 cm (Ref. 6803).

species.name: Ornate eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in muddy bays and banks and on coral reefs from close inshore to 110 m depth (Ref. 9862).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught in bottom trawls, gillnets, seines, and fish traps (Ref. 9862, Ref.58048).  Utilized for its meat and cartilage (possibly used as "filler" in shark fin soups as with other large eagle rays) (Ref.58048).

species.name: Ornate Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Recorded from cool, well-shaded and clear-flowing, small upland creeks and moist gullies along mountain ranges (e.g. Dandenong Ranges, GDR, Otway Ranges), larger, forested foothill streams to larger rivers at lower elevation. The streams occupied usually range in size from 0.5-8.0 m in width (up to 20 m), with 0.05-0.30 m average depth, with pools 0.3 to > 1.2 m in depth, with a complex instream substrate ranging from clay and sand to bedrock, boulder and cobble. Instream cover usually relatively plentiful, consisting of rock, large and small timber debris, aquatic vegetation, and vegetation and bank overhang. It is also known from drier river systems, including ephemeral tributaries, to the north-west and west of Melbourne (e.g. Plenty, Maribyrnong, and Werribee rivers), where individuals are able to persist in small and large, isolated and sometimes stagnant pools. Also able to persist in small streams within upland catchments in the north-east of their range (e.g. upper Yarra River system) that are often covered by snow for varying periods of time during winter (Ref. 98815). It is usually recorded at densities up to 04-1.5 fish/m2 , though can be very abundant in isolated pools (up to 3.0 fish/m2). Recorded in sympatry with Galaxias brevipinnis, Galaxias maculatus, Galaxias truttaceus, and historically possibly with Galaxiella pusilla and Neochanna cleaveri (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Ornate goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species that inhabits mangroves and silty, rocky areas; occasionally found in rubble reef areas.  Only single individuals were observed; many individuals found scattered over a small area (Ref. 420).  Found primarily in lower estuaries, usually in mangroves.  This is the species of the genus that is found farthest inland.  Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Ornate pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats where it is found in seagrass areas, among coral rubble and algae-covered rocks.  Juveniles occur with round-leafed seagrasses on sand slopes, usually settling from pelagic state at about 8 cm long.  Adults on sand or algae covered reefs to about 25 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ornate prawn-goby
species.description: Inhabits shallow sandy areas among seagrass (Ref. 1602) and in silty lagoons amongst rubble (Ref. 30404).  Lives in burrows with alpheid shrimp species with dark bands on back (Ref. 30404). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Ornate rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coastal streams and often found in stagnant pools or streams with little or no flow.  Inhabits creeks, backwaters of larger streams, ponds and dune lakes.  Usually found in sandy coastal country (locally known as 'wallum') in slow-flowing, tannin-stained waters.  Prefers the cover of submerged logs and branches, grassy banks, reeds and lily roots (Ref. 44894).  Occurs at temperature and pH ranging from 20°-28° C and 5.4-6.5 respectively.  Eggs are laid among plants each day during the breeding season.  Feeds on insects and their aquatic larvae, microcrustaceans and algae.  Popular aquarium fish which readily breeds in captivity (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Ornate shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ornate skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ornate sleeper-ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in warm-temperate or subtropical waters approximately 310 km of coastline with very narrow continental shelf (10-36 km wide to the 200 m isobath), however, the few sightings were all inside the 50 m isobath; on reefs with sandy or gravelly areas from close inshore to less than 50 m depth, including patches of appropriate habitat on inshore and offshore rocky banks and reefs.  Apparently an infauna or meiofauna feeder, feeding on  polychaete worms (including a tube-worm) and at least one small shrimp-like crustacean (Ref. 75572).

species.name: Ornate slippery goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand, silt, and rubble bottoms, takes refuge in dead shells, worn tubes, tunicates and empty bottles (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Ornate slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ornate Snake Eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Ornate snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a small stream with shaded forested banks flowing down a steep hill and with clear, fast running water (Ref. 75135).

species.name: Ornate stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology not known.

species.name: Ornate threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on mud or sand bottoms.  Most abundant in depths of 20 to 50 m.  Feeds mainly on small shrimps, squid, small fishes and benthic animals.

species.name: Ornate velvetfish
species.description: Found inshore, in soft bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Orontes bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orontes bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orontes dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orontes minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In slow-moving or still water amidst stones and vegetation.  Feeds on algae and aquatic invertebrates.  Spawns between February and April (Ref. 13609).

species.name: Orontes nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orontes phoxinellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orontes spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orpheus dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small to larger streams and rivers with standing water to moderate current (Ref. 57141).  Found mainly in pools (Ref. 57141). Feeds in the water column and in the upper layers on fallen terrestrial insects but it is otherwise omnivorous (Ref. 57141).  Spawns in shallow areas with gravel bottom.  Some populations are under threat due to water abstraction in dry season (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Orphie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters, but also found in coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on small fishes (Ref. 6530).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orphie carène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length refers to body length.  Inhabits surface waters (Ref. 2683). Circumglobal in tropical seas and divisible into five subspecies (Ref 90102).

species.name: Orphie carène (Platybelone argalus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore; particularly abundant around islands (Ref. 5217); schools in sheltered parts of the reef (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on small fishes.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orphie carène (Platybelone platyura)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore surface waters but is particularly abundant around islands (Ref. 9682).  Probably the most common needlefish of reef flats, lagoons and bays where it occurs in groups of a few to several dozen.  Carnivorous, feeding mainly on small fishes; marketed fresh (Ref. 9682).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Orphie carène (Platybelone pterura)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly at the surface of offshore waters, but also in coastal waters (Ref. 9279).  Abundant around islands (Ref. 9279).  Feeds mainly on small fishes (Ref. 9279).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).  Usually caught with the help of artificial lights (Ref. 9279).

species.name: Orstom dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Ortega's Hypopygus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Electric organ discharge: Data available from eight specimens in type series, from the vicinity of Jenaro Herrera, Loreto, Peru. Hypopygus ortegai generates a tetraphasic EOD ranging in duration from 1.17 to 2.11 ms (mean 1.73, N = 7), and with a PPF ranging from 1.408 to 1.869 kHz (mean 1.661, N = 7). Mean pulse rate during the day ranges from 44.7 to 56.8 Hz (mean 50.3, mean CV 0.91, N = 8), and during the night from 59.2 to 65.5 Hz (mean 62.1, mean CV 2.87, N = 8) (Ref. 88778).

species.name: Orthochromis gecki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a river which has a rocky bottom with patches of gravel and sand, and is about 15 meters wide and about 50 cm deep (Ref. 122085). This species seems to be a maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 122085).

species.name: Orthochromis indermauri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in part of river which is rocky with some patches of sand and gravel, about 20 meters wide and on average 50 cm deep (Ref. 122085). This species is benthic-rheophilic and prefers stretches of fast flowing water where it is found between and among large rocks or patches of gravel (Ref. 122085). It is a maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 122085).

species.name: Orthochromis kalungwishiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307). Collected from clear, fast-flowing waters. The type series was taken from down to 2 m depth close to the shore, over rocky bottoms. Water temperature was 20.7 °C, pH 6.8, conductivity 25.7 µS, dissolved oxygen 9.3 mg/l (Ref. 26626).

species.name: Orthochromis kasuluensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rather slow running water, in a section bordered with dense vegetation and in a small shallow stony brook with rather swift water; seems to be more common in fast flowing water between the stones; detritus eater; female mouthbrooder (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis katumbii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic-rheophilic maternal mouthbrooder with clutch sizes, in captivity, of between 25 and 30 eggs (Ref. 122085).

species.name: Orthochromis kimpala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a river which has a rocky bottom with some patches of sand and gravel, about 5-8 meters wide and on average about 50 cm deep (Ref. 122085). The species appears to be benthic-reophilic (Ref. 122085).

species.name: Orthochromis luichensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small and moderate swift running waters; feeds on plant matter; mouthbrooding species (Ref. 28096).

species.name: Orthochromis luongoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Orthochromis malagaraziensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Essentially riverine with tendency to colonize quieter waters; near bands of reeds and vegetation fringing the river; very small eggs, plant and insect debris and small crustaceans found in stomach; most probably a mouthbrooder (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis mazimeroensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water rivulets with sandy and stony bottoms; sand, plant debris and algae belonging to Bacillariophyceae, Chlorophyceae and Cyanophyceae found in stomch and gut; mouthbrooder (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis mosoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often encountered in swift running waters, but occasionally in more quiet rivulets; numerous algae belonging to Bacillariophyceae, Chlorophyceae and Cyanophyceae found in gut; mouthbrooder (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis mporokoso
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic-rheophilic species (Ref. 122085).

species.name: Orthochromis polyacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Orthochromis rubrolabialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively clear, swift and shallow water with rocky bottom; found near the ground trying to hide between the stones and boulders; probably mouthbrooding (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis rugufuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among vegetation roots and wood at the edge of a small brook, with relatively gentle water flow, crossing a woodland area (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthochromis stormsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; mainly feeds on algae and aufwuchs, animal matter is rarely taken; polygamous, ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Orthochromis torrenticola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Orthochromis uvinzae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic species, confined to swift running waters; feeds on algae particularly belonging to the Bacillariophyceae and Chlorophyceae and some Cyanophyceae; mouthbrooder (Ref. 28906).

species.name: Orthodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, backwaters and sluggish pools of small to large rivers.  Usually found in warm turbid water (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Orthopristis forbesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools above rocky, boulder strewn reefs, slopes and hard substrate with good water movement.  May mingle with yellowtail grunts and golden-eyed grunts (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Orthospinus franciscensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Orthosternarchus tamandua
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oryzias asinua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small pools and along the shore that was an extensive floodplain with clear water, slow to swift current and temperature of 26°C. Lives with a native species of halfbeak, Nomorhamphus sp., a possibly native Clarias sp., and the exotics Puntius binotatus, Trichopodus trichopterus, and Oreochromis sp. (Ref. 94271).

species.name: Oryzias bonneorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelvic-brooder, in which females carry an egg cluster until hatching (Ref. 126777).

species.name: Oryzias curvinotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Oryzias eversi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality where the species occurs is a karst pond of 30-40 m length, up to 10 m width and approximately up to 4 m depth, with calm and crystal clear water, with single in- and outflow and surrounded by rain forest.  The pond is used by local people as a natural swimming pool (Ref. 91779). A pelvic-brooder, in which females carry an egg cluster until hatching (Ref. 126777).

species.name: Oryzias hadiatyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits blackwater lake which is almost circular and only a few meters deep, surrounded by rain forest. The introduced predatory snakehead, Channa striata, occupies the same shallow shoreline habitats of this species and appears likely to cause threats (Ref. 85098).

species.name: Oryzias haugiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in habitats strongly influenced by tides.

species.name: Oryzias hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in low hilly area at elevations of 700 to 1000 m.

species.name: Oryzias luzonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Oryzias mekongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow permanent standing water of ditches, canals and ponds.  Most commonly found in water that has dense growth of submerged aquatic macrophytes with finely divided leaves.  Feeds on plankton.  Caught only with fine-meshed nets or when larger nets pull out large amounts of plants, trapping the fishes in them.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).  Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Oryzias melastigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish waters and estuaries, usually in shallow lagoons and swamps among roots and mangroves along the margins of waters, and readily adapts to freshwater conditions and even spawns in freshwater (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Oryzias nebulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in the morning in clear water over a bottom of sand, pebbles and fallen branches and during night time from a boat traveling along the lake shore, including the mouth of the tributary stream (Ref. 54508). Infested with parasitic copepods, Lernaea sp. (Ref. 54508).

species.name: Oryzias pectoralis
species.description: Found in rice paddies (Ref. 27658), swamps and sheltered areas of slow flowing rivers (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Oryzias sinensis
species.description: Adults occur in swamps, marshes, rice fields, backwaters, stream stretches with stagnant water and dense vegetation (Ref. 59043).  In Fuxian Lake, China, they are found in upper and middle layers of shallow coastal waters (Ref. 26717).  Adults feed mainly on filamentous algae and zooplankton (Ref. 26717).  They mature in 3 months time.  Spawning occurs between April and September when temperature rises above 26°C.  Can tolerate temperatures from 0 to 42°C, surviving winter under ice (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Oryzias soerotoi
species.description:
The type locality, Lake Tiu in central Sulawesi, is surrounded by trees and mountains and 
is characterized by a muddy substrate, and calm and transparent water, but darkly stained by decaying vegetation.  Juveniles and young fish occurs in shallow habitats with dense vegetation (Ref. 103734).

species.name: Oryzias songkhramensis
species.description: The species was collected in clear water from ditches and paddy fields by dip nets in the Songkhram and Mekong River basins. The area of collection is a small ditch, 3-6 m wide and 0.5 to 2 m deep, Substrate ranges from sand to detritus or mud. Associated species include Trichogaster trichopterus, Trichopsis vittatus, Rasbora rubrodorsalis, Channa striata and Machrobrachium lanchesteri; aquatic plants Nymphaea lotus, Jussiaea repens and Hydrilla verticillata. Water quality in the area: 27.5-28.7 ºC, conductivity 41.5-124.4 μm/l, dissolved oxygen 2.05-3.97 mg/l, pH 7.1-7.9 and salinity 0.1 ppt (Ref. 84389).

species.name: Oryzias timorensis
species.description: Non-annual breeder.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Oryzias wolasi
species.description:
Inhabits slow to swift-flowing freshwater stream with a substrate of mud, small rocks, and plant debris with emergent grasses and a shore of mud, rocks and grass.  Also found in a relatively cool (24°C), swift-flowing stream along Sumbersari Falls and a warmer (26°C), springfed
coastal stream (Ref. 94271).

species.name: Ossubtus xinguense
species.description: Feeds on aquatic macrophytes and filamentous algae (Ref. 26700).  In the aquarium it will feed on flakes and frozen food, but will also hunt down a large shrimp.  Females are aggressive towards other females and can have several males in following (Calum Chalmers, pers. comm. 2007).

species.name: Ostenfeld's lanternfish
species.description: Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4066, 75154).  At night, juveniles found in less than 100 m while larger individuals below 160 m.

species.name: Osteobrama belangeri
species.description: Occurs in rivers and lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Osteobrama cotio
species.description: Adults occur in rivers, lakes, ponds and ditches (Ref. 41236).  Possibly useful as larvicide (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Osteobrama cunma
species.description: Inhabits rivers and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Osteobrama neilli
species.description: Occurs in fast flowing clear streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Osteobrama peninsularis
species.description: Occurs in rivers and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Osteobrama vigorsii
species.description: Inhabits fast flowing clear streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Osteochilus brachynotopteroides
species.description: Found in a lake.  Like other members of this genus, this species probably feeds on periphyton, algae, phytoplankton as well as leafy plants such as aquatic macrophytes.  Most likely caught with seines, castnets and traps (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteochilus chini
species.description: Ubiquitous in slow water habitats feeding on detritus and algae.  Form schools up to 200 individuals (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Osteochilus enneaporos
species.description: Found in upland areas with fast flowing waters (Ref. 56749).  Probably migrates into seasonally flooded forests.  Feeds on periphyton, phytoplankton and algae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteochilus intermedius
species.description: Occurs in rivers and small streams in the swamp forests (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Osteochilus jeruk
species.description: Occurs in a variety of conditions:  in flowing water; in clear black or turbid brown water; over muddy, sandy or gravelly substrate.  Valued for its tasty flesh (Ref. 39912).

species.name: Osteochilus kahajanensis
species.description: Found in upland streams over stony and gravel bottom, with clear and fast flowing water (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Osteochilus lini
species.description: Found at midwater to bottom depths in large and medium-sized streams.  Moves into flooded forests or open fields and begins to re-enter rivers in October.  Young of the year are first seen in August.  Feeds on periphyton, phytoplankton and some detritus.  Usually used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteochilus melanopleura
species.description: Occurs at midwater to bottom depths in rivers, streams, canals and swamps.  Large individuals also occur in impoundments.  Moves into seasonally flooded habits that supply its preferred diet of mostly periphyton as well as leafy plants like aquatic macrophytes and inundated land plants.  Also feeds on phytoplankton, filamentous algae and benthic algae.  Begins to return to the river  in October, with numbers steadily increasing until January, when they begin to decline again.  Large individuals are sold fresh or dried and salted, smaller ones are made into prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteochilus microcephalus
species.description: Lives in highland streams to lowland rivers and peats (Ref. 57235).  Found in a variety of habitats, but frequently in sluggish, turbid waters (Ref. 43281).  Occur in midwater to bottom depths in rivers, streams, canals and swamps.  Moves into flooded forests and grassland during the flood season.  It returns to the rivers later, with highest numbers appearing from December to February.  Used to make prahoc and nuoc mam (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteochilus partilineatus
species.description: Found in a large and deep black water forest stream with running water.

species.name: Osteochilus serokan
species.description: Known only from a swamp near the mouth of Sungai Lembang.  Taken from very dark water 0.3-1.0 m deep with many fallen leaves and branches, over muddy substrate.

species.name: Osteochilus sondhii
species.description: Lives in hill streams.

species.name: Osteochilus spilurus
species.description: Common and abundant in creeks and small water bodies in the forest (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Osteochilus waandersii
species.description: Usually associated with clear, relatively fast flowing waters, with gravel to stony bottom (Ref. 27732).  Juveniles all found in the overhanging bank vegetation and near the soft substrate banks (Ref. 34011).  Moves into flooded forests adjacent to upland streams during periods of elevated water levels (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Osteomugil formosae
species.description: Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ostorhinchus ishigakiensis
species.description: Found among Zostera colonies.

species.name: Ostorhinchus pallidus
species.description:
This species occurs in aggregations, usually mixed with other apogonids. Hovers about 
1-2 m above the bottom at depths of 18-30 m (Ref. 114921).

species.name: Ostorhinchus parvulus
species.description: Found in schools around rocky reefs in bays (Ref. 559), in current-prone areas (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Ostorhinchus pselion
species.description: Found in reefs.

species.name: Ostorhinchus quinquestriatus
species.description: Known only from deeper water (Ref. 58479).

species.name: Ostorhinchus relativus
species.description: Found in rocky substratum, in sheltered bays and along exposed shores (Ref. 41638).  Usually in aggregations (Ref. 41638).

species.name: Ostorhinchus sinus
species.description: Specimens have been collected in very shallow water (one from a tide pool) at the head of deep bays (Ref. 41638).

species.name: Ostorhinchus urostigmus
species.description: Found in coastal reef slopes (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Ostracoberyx dorygenys
species.description: Rarely caught.

species.name: Ostrich goby
species.description: Occurs among corals.

species.name: Otjikoto tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep sinkhole lakes (100 m deep or more, e.g. introduced population in Lake Otjikoto, Namibia) with moderately clear water and with water temperatures ranging from 19 to 27°C (Ref. 6465). Omnivorous (Ref. 52307), but feeds mainly on algae and diatoms (Ref. 6465, 52307). Generally congregate, breed and feed from the near-vertical shores.  Use narrow shelves for breeding, with established and defended territories, both parents guard and tend eggs.  Threatened due to depletion of local groundwater resources and impact of introduced species (Ref. 7248).  Individuals tend to display different color patterns ranging from pure black to mottled black and blue, pink and white (Ref. 27829). Biparental open-spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Otocinclus cocama
species.description: Found in a medium size creek with clear water and lost of marginal vegetation (Ref. 57860).

species.name: Otocinclus mimulus
species.description: Found in stream with dark, slightly turbid water, flowing through a landscape of mixed low forest and pasture (Ref. 52874). Collected at the margin of an open field, but the stream flowed through dense low forest left along its bank and providing shadow (Ref. 52874). Usually occurs in areas with sandy bottom, bank vegetation entering water or with marginal aquatic plants, dark, clear or slightly turbid water and limited associated fauna (Ref. 52874). Mimics Corydoras diphyes (Ref. 52874). Mimicry is unusual because the two species occupy different microhabitats and it is hypothesized to operate with a primarily visual predator moving between the microhabitats, tentatively identified as the cichlid Crenicichla lepidota (Ref. 52874).

species.name: Otocinclus tapirape
species.description: Inhabits well-oxygenated, slow to moderate flowing waters, often near river banks (Ref. 46820).  Feeds on algae (Ref. 46820).

species.name: Otolithe bobo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters over mud bottom (Ref. 3593, 57396, 81656), very close to the shore (Ref. 57396). Also enters estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 3593, 81656), where reproduction takes place (Ref. 57396).  Moves farther offshore to about 100 m for spawning during rainy season from December to February; feeds on (juvenile) fish, shrimps (Ref. 28587, 81656) and other crustaceans (Ref. 81656).

species.name: Otolithe camerouonais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters over mud bottoms.  Feeds on small shrimps, worms and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3665).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 2683.

species.name: Otolithes arabicus
species.description: The largest specimen observed was 34.3 cm, standard length (Ref. 128934).

species.name: Otopharynx antron
species.description: Cave-dwelling; males have been observed defending small caves with sandy bottom mostly against conspecific males (Ref. 82798). Unicuspid teeth suggest diet of larger invertebrates or even fish (Ref. 82798).

species.name: Otopharynx argyrosoma
species.description: Lives over sand in shallow as well as in deeper regions.  Feeds on small invertebrates and plankton taken from the sand or from the water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx brooksi
species.description: Has been seen over sand near rocks.  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx decorus
species.description: The young are very common on Namalenje Island, Malawi at an average depth of 6 m.  Feeds on invertebrates being sifted from the thin layer of sediment on the substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx lithobates
species.description: Inhabits caves; found in rocky habitats; feeds on the droppings of mainly herbivorous species; picks up edible morsels from the substrate; also seems to be attracted to large catfishes, from which it may eat wastes as well (Ref. 5595). Feeds on droppings of cave-dwelling catfish Bagrus meridionalis (Ref. 82798).

species.name: Otopharynx ovatus
species.description: Normally seen in midwater, over rocks or sand.  Feeds on the eggs of other cichlids (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx selenurus
species.description: Occurs over sandy substrates.  Move around with large sand-digging species and feed from the particles thrown up by the large hosts (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx speciosus
species.description: Probably lives over sandy substrate. Caught in fairly deep water off sandy beaches. Piscivore, feeds on fish like Engraulicypris sardella (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx spelaeotes
species.description: This species has a preference for large caves and is therefore often found in rocky habitats that consist of large boulders (Ref. 82798). Most individuals are seen solitary and often at a depth of more than 10m (Ref. 82798). The mode of feeding consists of scavenging material lying on the rocky substrate of their environment (Ref. 82798).

species.name: Otopharynx tetraspilus
species.description: Inhabits vegetated shallow waters in sheltered bays.  Feeds on algae and small crustaceans (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otopharynx tetrastigma
species.description: Found in shallow vegetated areas.  Feeds on invertebrates such as insect larvae and small crustaceans found in the weedy environment (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Otothyropsis biamnicus
species.description: Commensal with midge larvae (Chironomidae) which are attached to the gill opening or more rarely to the posterior process of the cleithrum (Ref. 93039).

species.name: Otothyropsis piribebuy
species.description: Found on marginal vegetation (Ref. 87312).

species.name: Otuno
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ouachita madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky pools, backwaters and runs of clear swift creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Ouachita shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky pools of small to medium rivers.  Often occurs near vegetation (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205),

species.name: Ouitouche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel- and rubble-bottomed pools and runs of small to medium rivers, and also lake margins (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Outer-reef damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at the upper edges of steep outer reef slopes.  They occur singly or in small groups.  Feed on zooplankton and algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Outrigger triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep seaward reefs.  One collection outside Micronesia was made at 15 m (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). Exhibits sexual dimorphism (Ref. 37816).  Taken occasionally by bottom fishing (Ref. 1602).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Ouwen's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal creeks with gravel and boulder bottoms.

species.name: Oval damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  Feed mainly on plankton (Ref. 9334).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Oval electric ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Oval-spot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral-reef slopes in the protected bays, found solitary on muddy or sandy-mud bottoms with dead-coral rubbles under the heavy growth of corals (Ref. 75136).

species.name: Ovate chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer coral or rocky reefs; seldom in shallow waters (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Ovate sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand and mud bottoms in coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, especially crustaceans.  Marketed fresh, frozen, and dried-salted (Ref. 9893).

species.name: Owens pupfish
species.description: Occurs in marshes, vegetated sloughs and backwaters of Owens River.  7.2 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium.  4 cm max TL (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Owens sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty to rocky pools and runs of creeks.

species.name: Owston's slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Owstonia crassa
species.description: Caught by beam trawl.

species.name: Owstonia sibogae
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Ox-eyed oreo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Oxeye oreo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young oceanic; adults near bottom (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Oxleyan pygmy perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds, dune lakes and creeks, usually among aquatic weeds (Ref. 6398).  Lives in swamps with prolific sedge growth, gently flowing streams and dune lakes in areas of coastal heathland (wallum).  Water is often darkly tannin-stained and acidic (pH 5.4-6.5) with temperature range from 12° to 28°C (Ref. 44894).  Feeds primarily on aquatic insects and their larvae (Ref. 5259).  Also consumes microcrustaceans and algae.  Breeding season extends from October to May, when water temperatures rise above 20°C.  The breeding habits and biology are similar to other nannopercids, but this species takes only 4-5 months to attain sexual maturity (Ref. 44894).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=8, 26°C water temperature, egg layer, plant and rock cover, peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Oxuderces dentatus
species.description: Occurs in brackish water of estuaries and in the freshwater tidal zone.  Lives on intertidal mudflats often covered with a thin film of water (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Oxycheilinus lineatus
species.description: Occurs on deep reefs (Ref. 56651). Feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Oxydoras kneri
species.description: Omnivorous, feeding mainly on insects, crustaceans, mollusks, other invertebrates and some vegetable material (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Oxyeleotris altipinna
species.description: Relatively common among dense vegetation near the shore of Lake Aiwaso, but apparently rare at Lake Laamora and Werfyang Creek (Ref. 26385).

species.name: Oxyeleotris caeca
species.description: Inhabits limestone caves and sinkholes in the hilly terrain of the Upper Kikori River System of Papua New Guinea (Ref. 26384)

species.name: Oxygaster anomalura
species.description: Found at the surface of small mountain rivers with complete or nearly complete forest canopy.  Diet consists largely of exogenous insects and chironomid larvae.  Very rare in fish markets (Ref. 12693, 57235).

species.name: Oxygaster pointoni
species.description: Occurs at the surface in medium-sized rivers. Diet is probably similar to O. anomalura including chironomids and small mollusks. Rarely seen at fish markets.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus elsae
species.description: This species is usually found in fast flowing parts of rivers with cobble substance. It is associated with the following species: Alburnus atropatenae, Barbus cyri, Carassius gibelio, Capoeta capoeta, Hemiculter leucisculus, Pseudorasbora parva, Rhinogobius similis, Rhodeus amarus, Romanogobio macropterus and Squalius turcicus (Ref. 119504).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus galilaeus
species.description: Found in shallow waters near the lake shore, among stones and roots of willows (Ref. 92318).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus leontinae
species.description: Occurs at higher altitudes in the Jordan River basin, which might indicate that it is adapted to colder water.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus parvinae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The river at the Sefidbarg sampling site measures 5 m wide, with substrate consisting of coarse gravel and small boulders, and semi fast-flowing and semi-transparent waters.  The riverbanks are composed of some vegetation (Ref. 115530).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus persa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus phasicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus pindus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in creeks and streams with stone bottom and in riffles (Ref. 59043).  Seems to prefer clean and clear water with stony, gravely or sandy bottoms, with quite fast current (Ref. 55660).  Also found in stream sections characterized by quieter and shallow areas (Ref. 55660).  A short-lived species which inhabits highland water courses (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus seyhanicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus shehabi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus theophilii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper part of stream, with current and clear, cold water (Ref. 59043).  Hides among the stones of the substrate.  Stomach contents of a 6.32 cm SL female consists of aquatic insects larvae (Ref. 57755).  Water abstraction may pose threat to its population (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus tongiorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus veyseli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a slow flowing creek with stony and sandy substrate and during the sampling, the stream's width was 2.5 m, its depth 17.0 cm, the water temperature was16°C and current 0.6 m/s (Ref. 119376).

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus zagrosensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxynoemacheilus zarzianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyrhynchus tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology is unknown (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Oxyropsis acutirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyropsis carinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyropsis wrightiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyurichthys chinensis
species.description: Habitat unknown (Ref. 103856).

species.name: Oxyurichthys guibei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyurichthys mindanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft muddy bottoms (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Oxyurichthys rapa
species.description: Specimens were collected over mud and rock substrate at depths between 0-0.5 m (Ref. 103856).

species.name: Oxyurichthys takagi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyurichthys tentacularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, enters rivers and lagoons (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Oxyurichthys viridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyurichthys visayanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oxyurichthys zeta
species.description: Specimens are photographed hovering over a dark soft substrate. One individual at Lovina Beach, Bali, appears to be at the entrance of a large burrow (made by another organism).

species.name: Oyapock eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically occurs in rocky zones of main rivers during periods of low water level (Ref. 27188).  Often caught in quiet zones of cascades with sandy-rocky bottom.  Males who appear not to develop s frontal hump have long filaments on their caudal fins, as well as the dorsal and ventral fins (Ref. 35237).  Maximum length 25 cm SL (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Oyster blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in mangroves, pilings and rocky shores, often in silty water.  They feed on crustaceans, hydroids, bryozoans and pelecypods (Ref. 5521).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Oyster goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Oyster pearlfish
