species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302, 75154) found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154). Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Commensal inquiline in the giant oyster Pycnodonta hyotis (Ref. 4104).

species.name: Oyster pompano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Ozark bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear rocky pools and creeks and small to medium rivers, usually near stream bank, large boulders or brush.

species.name: Ozark cavefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit subterranean waters of quite small cave streams.  Preferred habitat in these caves is chert rubble though individuals are also found in areas of silt-sand substrates.  Stomachs examined contained copepods which constituted about 70-90% by volume with the balance being primarily small salamanders, crayfish, isopods, amphipods and young of their own species (Ref. 34868).  Eggs are carried in gill chambers of females (Ref. 205).  Threatened by overfishing (Ref. 10172).

species.name: Ozark chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits riffles, runs, and current-swept pools over gravel and rubble in clear, small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Ozark logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ozark madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, cool, swift rocky riffles and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Ozark minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel-bottomed and rubble-bottomed flowing pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Rarely found in large rivers.

species.name: Ozark sculpin
species.description: This species prefers cool clear brooks and moderate to large streams and rivers usually with rapid flow and gravelly or rocky bottoms. Within these environment, it typically occurs in shallow, gravel-bottomed riffles or shoal regions with strong current. It is reported to often occur in thick growths of watercress (Nasturtium officina. Little is known of its biology. Feeds also on crayfish (Orconectes); larvae of Trichoptera (Hydropsychidae), Plecoptera, Ephemeroptera, Diptera (Chironomus, Simulium), gastropods, elmid beetles and miscellaneous animal material, including other individuals of C. hypselurus (Ref. 121014).

species.name: Ozark shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy runs and flowing pools, often near riffles, of clear fast-flowing small to medium rivers.

species.name: Pabdah catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear as well as muddy rivers, streams, ponds and lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pabo catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, ponds and lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pachycara alepidotum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic fauna of sampling area diverse in deep-sea corals, echinoderms, molluscs, and crustaceans (Ref. 57887).

species.name: Pachycara caribbaeum
species.description: Known from two bathyal collections at chemosynthetic environments; depth ca. 2300 m (Ref.112624)

species.name: Pachycara cousinsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara crossacanthum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara dolichaulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters off Peru (Ref. 78516).

species.name: Pachycara garricki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara goni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara karenae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara matallanasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara mesoporum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara microcephalum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in abyssal depths (Ref. 11954).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pachycara nazca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pachycara pammelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara priedei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara rimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara saldanhai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara shcherbachevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from a single specimen taken in the western Indian Ocean (Bay of Bengal) (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Pachycara sulaki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara suspectum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachycara thermophilum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachychilon macedonicum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in marshlands, lakes, and water courses on the low plains, with little current.  Threatened due to water abstraction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Pachypanchax arnoulti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in  wide range of habitats: swamp whose water is clear, tannin stained, acidic, soft and deficient in dissolved substances; small creek whose water is clear, colorless, with a neutral pH, moderate hardness and deficient in dissolved substances. Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects and preyed upon mostly by fish-eating birds and dragonfly nymphs (Ref. 57724).

species.name: Pachypanchax patriciae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small rivers that are tannin stained, acidic, very soft and deficient of dissolved substances, with compacted clay/sand bottoms, overlain with organic detritus.  Also found in large rivers with a markedly seasonal hydrological regime, substantial flood plains and water ranges from clear to turbid water, but are not tannin-stained, are less acidic, harder and carry a greater concentrations of dissolved minerals (Ref. 57724).  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects and preyed upon mostly by fish-eating birds and dragonfly nymphs (Ref. 57724).

species.name: Pachypanchax sakaramyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks in the mountainous area (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pachypanchax sparksorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow areas of rivers where it seeks shelter along the banks or among rocks. Feeds on small shrimps and terrestrial and aquatic insects.  Preyed upon by aquatic insects and fish-eating birds (Ref. 57724).

species.name: Pachypanchax varatraza
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of habits: stream flowing under relatively intact forest cover at an altitude of 70 m above sea level consisting of a series of quiet pools with clay/sand bottoms, interspersed with short stretches of flowing water over sand/ gravel bottoms and with very turbid water; and stream flowing through modified low-altitude rain forest at an altitude of 30 m above sea level consisting of clay/sand bottom, interspersed with patches of bedrock with clear water and moderate current (Ref. 57724).  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects (Ref. 57724).

species.name: Pachypops pigmaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachypops trifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Pachypterus acutirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pachyurus calhamazon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachyurus gabrielensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachyurus junki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachyurus paucirastrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachyurus squamipennis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pachyurus stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed coastal, pelagic and schooling.  Recorded only from bays and estuaries.  The eggs are oval with a small knob.

species.name: Pacific anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is generally commensal with the anemone Heteractis magnificus (Quoy & Gaimard, 1833) at depths between about 4-10 m (Ref. 85065). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pacific astronesthid fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slopes and sea mountains (Ref. 41299).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pacific barracudina
species.description: Epipelagic to bathypelagic, from 50 (larvae and juveniles (Ref. 47377)) to more than 2,000 m (older youngs and adults (Ref. 47377)) (Ref. 4056).

species.name: Pacific barrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Adults found in deeper water, at depths greater than 100 m (Ref. 559).  Plankton feeder (Ref. 12115).

species.name: Pacific beakfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually solitary.  Constantly swims over rocky reefs, boulder strewn slopes and along walls.  Occurs more commonly in shallow water (Ref. 5227).  Feeds on algae and invertebrates (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Pacific bearded brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults benthopelagic to 650 m depth, juveniles common on reefs (Ref. 34024).  At depths of about 40-75 m, adults are found deep on mud and broken shell bottom (Ref. 36413).  Smaller silvery specimens taken far out at sea in the epipelagic (Ref. 34024).  Caught occasionally (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with late post-flexion and transformation stage larvae found in midwater (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pacific beardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Inhabits sandy and muddy areas (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Pacific black scabbardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles mesopelagic at 146-190 m at night, 300-1100 m during day; adults benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pacific blackchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and bathypelagic (Ref. 6604).  Adults usually found below about 1,000 m, but juveniles found between 500-800 m.  No evidence of vertical migration (Ref. 6604).  Feed mainly on small crustaceans.  Sexually mature from about 15.2 cm (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36062).

species.name: Pacific blackdragon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559).  Migrates to the surface at night and return to the depths at dawn.  Feed mainly on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35926).  Exhibit extreme sexual dimorphism, with larvoid males (Ref. 35926).

species.name: Pacific blue eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, cool, fast-flowing streams and also brackish mangrove estuaries.  Inhabits tidal mangrove creeks or fringing coastal mangrove and around offshore islands.  Also common in clear, forest streams.  Water temperature varies between 15° and 28°C, with the lower end of the scale applicable during winter over the southernmost part of the range.  The pH fluctuates from 5.5-7.8 according to habitat conditions.  At least 15 geographical varieties have been recognized, but detailed morphological studies reveal there is only one species  (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Pacific bronze Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on planktons (Ref. 89972). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pacific bullethead parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species, observed in schools on seaward reefs or rocky substrata. Stomach contents include benthic algae (Sargassum, Ulva, Zonaria, Gelidium, Amansia, Polysiphonia, Herposiphonia, Gelidiella, Griffithsia, and Hypnea. It is also known to eat the tough alga Turbinaria (Ref. 86689).

species.name: Pacific croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and rivers (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Pacific crown toby
species.description: Occurs in sheltered habitat, often on open sand and rubble bottom near reefs; but appears to be far less common than C. coronata (Ref. 83660). Solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pacific Domine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific doubleline clingfish
species.description: This species is usually commensal with crinoids, rarely associated with rocky substrate near sea urchins (Ref. 130914).

species.name: Pacific drummer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pacific eagle ray
species.description: This inshore species in coastal bays and estuaries, to offshore occurs solitary or in large schools. It feeds mainly on bivalves, also shrimps, polychaetes and other fishes. Size usually less than 130 cm, size unknown at birth and when it matures (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Pacific fanfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic.  The species is very rare and most likely seen as stomach content of large predatory fishes, such as tunas.  Young probably inhabits shallow, adult deep water.

species.name: Pacific fat sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit estuaries, stagnant ditches or creeks of low current velocity between the sea and an elevation of 30 m.  Benthic and most abundant on sandy and muddy bottoms.  Ingests much mud and  detritus, although also filter plankton (Ref. 36880).  Found in shallow inshore areas; typically in freshwater but moves freely into the sea.

species.name: Pacific footballfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pacific foureyed fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fresh water to full salinity coastal lagoons.  Used in eye research.

species.name: Pacific goby
species.description: Found in crevices and caves (Ref. 2334, 9360), usually under loose debris (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Pacific gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky and coral reefs exposed to mild to moderate surge (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  They occur solitary among boulders (Ref. 48636).  Territorial in areas where filamentous algae cover rocks and dead coral (Ref. 9710).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Pacific grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic mid-slope species, that appears to wander off slope bottoms into midwater (Ref. 1371).  Adults feed on small fish, euphausiids, prawns, amphipods and cephalopods (Ref. 1371).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36385).

species.name: Pacific halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools at the surface of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Pacific hatchet fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4739, 58302), mainly at 300-650 m (Ref. 4054), 170-500 m at night and 350-600 m during day (Ref. 58302), commonly 1-600m (Ref. 035838).  May make short diel migrations (Ref. 4739).  Smaller individuals feed on copepods and ostracods; larger ones feed on euphausiids, salps and chaetognaths (Ref. 4739).  Adult complement of photophores acquired at about 14 mm SL (Ref. 4739).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35838).

species.name: Pacific headlightfish
species.description: Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442) at ≥ 90 m (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Pacific jellynose fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on prawns (Ref. 27550).

species.name: Pacific leaping blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in moist shaded pockets of pitted limestone in the spray zone above the water line (Ref. 34765).  Leaps from hole to hole when disturbed (Ref. 34765).  Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pacific longnose parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits turbid lagoons more than outer reef areas.  Usually seen in aggregations; females usually in small groups (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.  Large adults may occur to depths of at least 40 m.

species.name: Pacific molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide variety of standing and flowing waters, but prefers those with dense algal growth and other aquatic vegetation.

species.name: Pacific mud eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific pearlfish
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Adults inhabit the body cavity of pearl shells (Pinctada), pen shells (Pinna), and cockles (Laevicardium). Oviparous, with pelagic vexillifer stage larva, and benthic tenuis stage larva (Ref. 36487). Also found in following shells in the Gulf of California: Megapitaria squalida, M. aurantiaca, Laevicardium elatum and Spondylus princeps (Ref. 38407).

species.name: Pacific portholefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at 15-650 m (Ref. 58302).  Exhibit diel vertical migrations, juveniles and adults found at 300-800 m by day and often reach the surface at night (Ref. 4769).  Early stages at 450-610m (Ref. 035800). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35800).

species.name: Pacific redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns from May to September.  Spent adults descend to sea after spawning.  Immature specimens occur in the mouths of rivers the whole year round; the young descend to the sea upon attaining a length of 7-9 cm (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Pacific reef bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky crevices.  Feeds mainly on small fishes and benthic crustaceans (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Pacific rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in surf-swept seaward reefs.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pacific seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in brackish waters of estuaries and inlets, coastal rivers and tidal creeks, occasionally entering lower sections of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).  Juveniles inhabit protected bays and estuaries (Ref. 47715).  Usually occurs singly or small groups, but may migrate in schools (Ref. 48635).  A popular angling species, often caught with hook and line (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Pacific shafted bonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific silverstripe halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore, coastal and estuarine; found along sand beaches, in lower tidal streams and mangroves.  Usually encountered in schools at the surface of the water (ref. 42105).

species.name: Pacific sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers, creeks and lakes from the brackish swamps to sea level to 115 m elevation.  Young are very abundant near the coast, suggesting reproduction in marine or brackish waters.  Eats crustaceans and fish (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Pacific spadenose shark
species.description: Adults are found in shallow, inshore waters, most abundant near large freshwater outflows, e.g. Pearl River estuary (Hong Kong) and the large Borneo drainage systems (Ref. 84283).

species.name: Pacific spiny lumpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly inshore; often found at low tide attached to rocks (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Pacific spookfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Maximum length 130 cm without caudal filament (Ref. 26346).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pacific squaretail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pacific staghorn sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found near shore, especially in bays and estuaries; most frequently on sandy bottom (Ref. 2850).  Intertidal individuals breath air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Can leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Although some individuals may spend their entire life in highly saline waters (Ref. 28693), some newly metamorphosed young move from the estuarine spawning sites to completely fresh water and may remain there for up to 6 weeks (Ref. 27547).  Adults apparently tend to remain in the shallow lower estuary, or farther offshore (Ref. 27547).  Feeds mostly on crabs, shrimps and amphipods, but also takes larval, juvenile and adult fishes, as well as polychaete worms, mollusks and other invertebrates (Ref. 4930).  Expands its gill covers and produces a low-pitched humming sound when stressed (Ref. 6885).  Considered a nuisance by anglers (Ref. 27547).

species.name: Pacific viperfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Migrate upward at night (Ref. 28499).  Feed on small planktonic crustaceans, arrow worms and fish (Ref. 28499).  Has photophores on belly arranged in a row (Ref. 2850).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35898).  Also caught with bottom trawls.

species.name: Pacora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in estuaries and lower part of streams.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 35237).  An important food fish. Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Pacu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Invades the flooded forests to feed on nuts and seeds which fall from trees (Ref. 32894).  Reaches around 50.0 cm SL (Ref. 81048).

species.name: Padanian goby
species.description:
Espèce d'animaux. Found in streams with moderate flow over pebble beds, from altitudes of 400 m to sea level, and also at lake edges (with dense vegetation or coarse gravel, Ref. 59043).   Spawns for the first time at 1  year; spawning season in April to July, when temperature reaches 20°C; females may repeat spawning during a season.  Adhesive eggs deposited between stones, shells and aquatic plants and males guard the eggs until hatching.  When spawning and defending the nest, males produce sounds.  Feeds on a variety of benthic invertebrates (Ref.59043).
Territorial, usually burrows under flat stones.  A short-lived species which is threatened by pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100). Known to be invasive in Italy and has massively expanded its range south since the last decades (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Padded clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in very shallow water along rocky shores that may be exposed to surf (Ref. 13442).  May enter narrow cracks and crevices (Ref. 13442).  Feeds on limpets, crabs, chitons, crustaceans, fishes and polychaete worms (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Padded sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from intertidal areas to 55 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Paddlefish cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in  deep caves (Ref. 9710), usually where little light is left (Ref. 48635). Solitary in caves (Ref 90102).

species.name: Paddlenose chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare (Ref. 11228).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Paddletail onejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 96339).

species.name: Paedocypris carbunculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with slow current, usually forming small shoals approximately up to 100-200 individuals, most abundant near or under overhanging structures or submerged vegetation.  The type specimen was collected in a small stream, 3-6 m wide and 0.5 to 2 m depth, with substrate ranging from sand to detritus and peat, with flowing blackwater (Ref. 78740).

species.name: Paedocypris micromegethes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from peat swamps (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Paedocypris progenetica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the smallest fish and vertebrate known, with the smallest mature female measuring a mere 7.9 mm (Ref. 56152).

species.name: Paere
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic, epipelagic species frequently solitary or forming small loose aggregations rather than compact schools.  Feed on fishes and squids. Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769).   An important sport fish in some areas (Ref. 9340).  Marketed fresh, salted or spice-cured slices of meat; also frozen (Ref. 9987).  Flesh of very good quality (Ref. 9684). Minimum depth from Ref. 005227.

species.name: Pageau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on inshore waters, on various bottom (rock, gravel, sand and mud) to 200 m (Mediterranean) or 300 m (Atlantic) and move to deeper waters during winter.  Omnivorous, but feed mainly on benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 3688).  Protogynic hermaphrodites, females become males first in their third year with sizes of about 17 cm.  Important food fish.

species.name: Pageot acarne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit various types of bottoms, especially seagrass beds and sand down to 500 m depth, but more common between 40 and 100 m.   The young are found nearer to the shore.  Omnivorous, but prefer worms, mollusks and small crustaceans (Ref. 3688).  Important food fish.

species.name: Pageot d'Arabie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over various grounds (Ref. 30573).  Omnivorous with preference for carnivorous diet (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Pageot du Natal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy-muddy bottoms at a depth of about 150 m (Ref. 5213).  Omnivorous species but prefers worms, mollusks, and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).  Grunts when removed from the water.

species.name: Pagetodes atkinsoni
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pagetopsis macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found more commonly at depths from 5-40 m.  Adults feed mainly on fishes and krill.

species.name: Pagetopsis maculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larval pelagic phase is long (Ref. 41551).

species.name: Pagre berda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in estuaries, relatively uncommon in freshwaters (Ref. 52193). It feeds on invertebrates, including worms, mollusks, crustaceans and echinoderms (Ref. 5213), and small fish (Ref. 3670, 52193). Breeds in winter at sea (Ref. 52193). Protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367). The flesh is excellent; sold fresh in markets. It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus australis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Pagre commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults Inhabit hard (rock and rubble), sandy or muddy bottoms on the continental shelf and the upper slope to about 200 m depth, but not often descending beyond 150 m.  The young found nearer to the coast than the adults.  Feed on mollusks and fish (Ref. 3688).  Important foodfish.

species.name: Pagre commun (Pagrus pagrus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rock, rubble, or sand bottoms (young frequently found on seagrass beds and the continental shelf (Ref. 47377)) down to about 250 m depth, often above 150 m. In southwest Brazil found in 160 m depth (Ref. 47377). Feeds on crustaceans, fishes, and mollusks (Ref. 3688). Its toxic nature is uncertain (Ref. 4690). Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987). Reported weights of caught individuals were between 9 to 17 kgs (9-10 off the west coast of Greece) (Hans Bollnert, hassebollnert@yahoo.gr, pers.comm. 12/09). It is parasitised by the monogeneans Anoplodiscus longivaginatus and Anoplodiscus richiardii (species inquirenda) on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Pagre cramoisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and muddy-sandy bottoms.  Feeds on a wide range of benthic invertebrates and on fish.  Two spawning seasons, early summer and autumn.  Utilized for human consumption especially in the East China Sea where it is caught mostly by trawlers.  An important food fish.

species.name: Pagre dentchien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow, clear, warm, coastal waters over coral reefs. Often near the shelter of elkhorn corals and gorgonians (Ref. 9710). Juveniles are encountered over sand bottoms with or without seagrass (Thalassia), and over muddy bottoms of lagoons or mangrove areas. Young sometimes enter brackish waters. Sometimes form resting aggregations during the day. Feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs, worms, gastropods and cephalopods. Considered a good food fish, it is marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 55). Maximum length for female taken from Ref. 3093.

species.name: Pagre double bande
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in small groups.  (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh or dried.

species.name: Pagre fine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky bottoms.  Juveniles inhabit shallow waters, common over sand or muddy bottoms.  Feed mainly on fishes, shrimps, crabs, worms, cephalopods, and some planktonic items including urochordates and gastropods.  Marketed fresh and eaten steamed, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Heavily exploited in American waters where it is now closely protected; shrimp fishing, accused of destroying young snappers, is currently restricted.

species.name: Pagre rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults Inhabit hard bottoms (rock or rubble); the young occur near the coast.  Feed mainly on mollusks including cephalopods, and also on crustaceans (Ref. 3688).  Important food fish.

species.name: Pagre tête noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in bays, shallow rocky reefs, and in brackish waters (Ref. 41299). Feeds on mollusks and polychaetes. Spawns in the spring and summer months (Ref. 41299). It is parasitised by the monogenean A. spari on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Pagre à nageoires jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits warm shallow and coastal waters, often entering river mouths and estuaries (Ref. 93743). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus australis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Pahranagat spinedace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in spring outflows (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Pahrump poolfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm springs about 25°C springs, usually in deep holes (Ref. 86798).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pailona austral
species.description: A rare species inhabiting lower continental slopes (Ref. 26346), also on insular slopes in large schools near the bottom which are segregated according to size and sex, and feeds on cephalopods and bony fishes (Ref. 247).  Up to 36 young in a litter, ths size at birth between 32 and 36 cm (Ref. 247).  Used for fishmeal and liver oil (Ref. 6871).  Minimum depth from Ref. 247. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pailona commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slopes and abyssal plains (Ref. 6871).  Feeds mainly on fish (including sharks) and cephalopods (Ref. 6871), also gastropods and cetacean meat (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205),  with 13 to 29 young per litter, born at 27-31 cm (Ref. 26346); 32-35 cm TL in North Atlantic (Ref. 98315).  Utilized as fishmeal, dried and salted for human consumption, or as a source of squalene  (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Pailona rapeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on upper continental slopes, on or near the bottom (Ref. 247).  Feeds on fish and cephalopods (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 16- 28 young born at 27-30 cm (Ref. 26346).  Caught in trawls or longlines set at depths greater than 400 m (Ref. 55584).  Flesh is high in mercury (Ref. 6871).  Utilized as fishmeal and source of squalene (liver oil) (Ref. 6871). Maximum depth from Ref. 55584.

species.name: Pailona à long nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A fairly common species found on continental and insular slopes (Ref. 6871), on or near the bottom (Ref. 5578).  Feeds mainly on fish and cephalopods (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 4-8 young in a litter (Ref. 6871), born at 28-35 cm (Ref. 26346).  The flesh is high in mercury; utilized as fishmeal and source of squalene (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Painted anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in aggregations above steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Painted catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pool and run areas of swift streams (Ref. 12045).  Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Painted dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer slopes around isolated rock and coral outcrops in 28-36 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Painted frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow sheltered reefs (Ref. 9710).  Adults usually with sponges; juveniles openly on sand or reef, mimicking small sponges or nudibranchs (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).

species.name: Painted greenling
species.description: Found in rocky areas, from the intertidal to 49 m (Ref. 2850). Sleeps on the oral disc, leaving the anemone (Urticina lofotensis) by day but returning every night (Ref. 45560). Commonly encountered hovering motionless by divers (Ref. 2850). Feeds on crustaceans, polychaetes, small mollusks and bryozoans (Ref. 4930). Neither anterolateral glandular grooves nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Painted hornshark
species.categoryName: Heterodontidae (Bullhead, horn, or Port Jackson sharks)
species.description: Specimens ranged from 35.5-60.1 cm TL, an immature male at 43.2 cm TL and mature ones at 55.5-60.1 mm TL (Ref. 129794).

species.name: Painted latchet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Excellent food fish but rarely caught (Ref. 9771).

species.name: Painted maskray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 6871, 75154).  Size at birth about 11 cm WD (Ref. 6871).  Exists as two color forms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Painted moki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Feeds on small invertebrates that are sifted then sucked up from sediment.

species.name: Painted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Painted rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies habitat considered among the most scenic freshwater environments found at the Aru Islands, consisting of small, rainforest brooks with quiet pools interspersed with cascades to 3-4 m high.  The habitat has excellent water clarity and stream channels composed of relatively smooth limestone with minimal aquatic vegetation, but abundant shelter for fishes in the form of log snags (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Painted stinger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Painted stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reefs, estuaries, sheltered to turbulent reefs (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Painted swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from fish market (Ref. 86282)

species.name: Painted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Paintedface dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs in shallow fringing reef which is subject to significant terrigenous sedimentation and relatively warm water due to the limited circulation in the large bay of Teluk Saleh. Often found resting on live massive coral colonies (Ref. 115282).

species.name: Paiute sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble and gravel riffles of cold creeks and small to medium rivers.  Also found in rocky shores of lakes.

species.name: Paiva's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer the tunnels drilled by ship-worms in submersed branches of bank vegetation.  At ebb tide, may seek vacant hollows and endure hours out of the water.  They feed on isopod and amphipod crustaceans.  Occasionally, they swim like a half-waterlogged leaf moving in the slow current.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205).  Egg clutches found within drilled tunnels by ship-worms are attended by the male (Ref. 49399).  Sexually dimorphic males with higher dorsal fin and prominent flap on its anterior edge.  Territorial males adopt a dark color while flashing the bright turquoise spot on dorsal fin.  Contests are size-dominated and may be restricted to displaying dark colors and turquoise spot, or the opponents may enter in physical combat, nipping at each other. Larvae hatch at about 3.5 mm and settle at about 8 mm SL (Ref. 49399).

species.name: Pajama cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms aggregations among the branches of Porites nigrescens and P. cylindrica in sheltered bays and lagoons (Ref. 1602, 48635). Disperses at night to feed close to the bottom (Ref. 9710). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35407). Popular aquarium fish (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Pajama pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species appears to be restricted to relatively shallow (3-10 m) reef areas protected from wave exposure. Type specimens were collected exclusively from within beds of Halimeda macroalgae growing beneath branching Acropora coral stands. It is apparently the only species of the genus to be limited to this habitat (Ref. 96671).

species.name: Pakhorukov rockling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pakoko wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by hand nets and rotenone (Ref. 97238).

species.name: Palaeoplex palimpsest
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in river which is rocky with sandy to muddy patches, about 25 m wide, and with an estimated depth of approximately 1.5 m; the shoreline is fringed with dense vegetation; the species seems to prefer stretches of slow flowing water as it was neither observed nor collected in the small rapid-like stretches of the river (Ref. 122072). The molariform teeth of the lower pharyngeal jaw suggest that this species feeds at least partly on molluscs which are crushed by the pharyngeal jaws (Ref. 122072).

species.name: Palatogobius grandoculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018. Occurs in coral rubble and sand (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Palatogobius incendius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep reefs, schooling at the top or bottom of vertical walls, with a stretch of sand and small rocks, at depths of 88 to 201 meters.  The largest specimens were 2.22 cm for males and 2.15 cm for females (Ref. 128886).

species.name: Palau grenadier
species.description: Females with ripe eggs were taken in mid-December.  Captured in fair numbers during exploratory fishing on the Kyushu-Palau Ridge, but not known from any other area.

species.name: Palauan deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It may be possible that the species may occur in deeper water and migrate to shallow water for spawning or feeding (Ref. 58473).  Reported from a cave facing the drop off of the fringing reef of Palau at a depth of about 20 m (Ref. 93890).

species.name: Palauan primitive cave eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave species (Ref. 87802).

species.name: Palawan lentipes goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was commonly observed with many other goby species and two cyprinid species at the reaches below the first waterfall of Estrella Falls. It was more abundant at the reaches above the waterfal, a habitat it occupies together with Sicyopus zosterophorus. In the Olanguan Falls which consists of continuous waterfalls along the course of one stream. this species co-occurred with many other goby species, a cyprinid species, and two Kuhlia species (Ref. 125534).

species.name: Pale cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky areas from 3-30 m, but possibly much deeper.

species.name: Pale catfish
species.description: This species occupies main channel of rivers and streams, either with turbid waters and high sediment loads or with transparent waters and few nutrients.  It prefers pools and slow-flowing waters of different depths and has plant material deposits and heavy substrates such as rocks and stones which serve as shelter for this fish during the day (Ref. 108688).

species.name: Pale clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups, among the bases of the arms of some comasteroid crinoids (e.g. Himerometra robustipinna), or feather stars, and in surge channels (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Pale cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Feed on gastropods (Ref. 31524).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pale deepsea lizardfish
species.description: A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Pale dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs around small isolated rocks or corals on sandy bottoms.  Found singly or in pairs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Pale fortescue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pale perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pale rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur near the surface of ponds, canals and streams.  Often found in turbid waters.  Probably feed mostly on exogenous insects and also on some algae.  Spawning sites are found in rivers and ponds (Ref. 33813).  Mature adults probably breed during the rainy season.  Occasionally sold fresh.  Probably used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pale sand catlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water with a sandy bottom (Ref. 94654). It feeds on small invertebrates, including mayfly nymphs and caddis fly larvae (Ref. 94654).

species.name: Pale sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms near reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pale skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom-dweller that feeds on invertebrates.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 35 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Pale smiling whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pale snipe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pale spotted catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Pale threadtail snipe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Diurnal migrations (Ref. 51024).  Feeds on crustaceans.  Oviparous, strong sexual dimorphism (Ref. 3247).

species.name: Pale toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pale tropical skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer continental shelf and upper slope. Probably feeds on small bony fishes (Ref. 114953).  Observed lengths of adolescent males between ca. 47.0 (tail tip damaged) and 64.4 cm TL, smallest juvenile 15.0 cm TL (Ref. 75649) to 17 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Pale Usisya aulonocara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among the sediment covered rocks.  Feeds on soft-bodied invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pale white-spotted triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow waters (Ref. 27223) and reefs in 0-8 m depth (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pale wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in steep outer reef slopes to at least 74 m depth (Ref. 34765), with large caves and rich invertebrate growth.  Occurs in small groups of females and dominating male (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Pale yellow tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly from moderate to fast-flowing, gravel-boulder bottom creeks in mountainous tributaries of the Ok Tedi River.

species.name: Pale-barred coris
species.description: Found in coastal to outer reef habitats in deep gutters or along reef margins (Ref. 48636).  Inhabits rocky and coral reefs, in areas with rubble, weed and sand (Ref. 9710).  Found solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pale-edged stingray
species.description: Feed on bottom-dwelling organisms (Ref.50449); primarily small crustaceans, but also  small fishes (Ref.58048).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Pale-spot whip ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters and river mouths (Ref. 45255).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Paleback darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow, rocky pools of headwaters and creeks, and vegetated springs (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Paleback goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic, benthic and found on sandy bottoms near rocks or corals (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Palebar hogfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. A common species of deeper rock and coral reefs of South Africa.  Reported to feed mainly on sea urchins, crabs, gastropod mollusks, and other hard-shelled invertebrates, which are
crushed in the powerful pharyngeal plates that are studded with large molariform teeth.

species.name: Palebarred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic inhabitant of crevices and caverns in 1-56 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Palebelly searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Palefin batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Palefin dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Palefin sawbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from the continental slope (Ref. 9563) and shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Palefin threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms.

species.name: Palegold searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and benthopelagic at 850-1500 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Palehead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from rocky and rubble shores with algal mats to reefs and seagrass beds.

species.name: Palelipped surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear seaward reefs near drop-offs (Ref. 9710, 48637). Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Palemarked feia goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic; found in coral reefs and sand bottoms (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Palemouth snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Palenose cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Palenque priapella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapidly flowing, preferably torrential waters. Usually found in shallow waters about 20 to 50 cm deep. Feeds on insects. Lives along with livebearing Xiphophorus alvarezi only in the Rio Palenque.

species.name: Palepore snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 42734, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Palespotted corydoras
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Palestriped cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species, occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Paletail damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Palezone shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clean, clear waters of flowing pools and runs (Ref. 31523).  Found over bottoms with fractured bedrock, cobble, and gravel mixed with clear sand (Ref. 31523).  Reaches a maximum length of less than 6 cm SL (Ref. 31523).

species.name: Pallaoro's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found between gravel and small boulders in very shallow infralittoral waters, just by the shore, at a maximum depth of 1 m; a typical cryptobenthic fish (Ref. 124191).

species.name: Pallid basslet
species.description: Inhabits shallow lagoon and seaward reefs from 6 to 40 m (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Pallid chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow unimpounded rivers with bottoms consisting of sand and gravel, combined with occasional small rubble, and water clarity ranges from relatively clear to moderately turbid (Ref. 116539).

species.name: Pallid cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pallid eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in midwater, from near surface at night to about 800 m during the day (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Pallid pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Free-living and benthic or pelagic (Ref. 58302).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Pallid pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reef slopes and lagoons.  Found along reef margins with rubble (Ref. 48637). Also found in caves and crevices, often on drop-offs in 3-35 m (Ref. 90102).  A relatively rare species in collections, usually been taken in lots of one or two specimens (Ref. 100726)..

species.name: Pallid rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species endemic to the Red Sea; nothing is known of its habits nor habitat preferences (Ref. 9962). According to traits of family where it belongs, it is oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pallid shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and silty pools of medium to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Pallid sturgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit large, deep, turbid river channels, usually in strong current over firm sand or gravel (Ref. 10294, 58490).  They feed on aquatic insect immatures, particularly caddisfly larvae, and small fish (Ref. 10294).  Threatened due to over harvesting and habitat loss (Ref. 58490).  No length type given but assumed to be in TL.

species.name: Pallid whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pallidochromis tokolosh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf areas near the bottom (Ref. 55949).  Predatory (Ref. 26712).

species.name: Pallidus rasbora
species.description:
Found in shallow, slow-flowing, densely shaded lowland rain-forested streams with a sandy-silt
substrate (Ref. 94541).

species.name: Paloa villadolidi
species.description: This species is found in the tidal zone within or around mangroves in estuaries, and where four of the seven specimens were found hovering in small tidepools around the roots of mangrove trees [Bruguiera gymnorhiza (L.) Savigny] within the forest at night. The substrate of the tidepool was mud, and a thalassinid mud lobster, Thalassina anomala (Herbst, 1804) made a burrow system around the tidepool. Other fish species observed in that tidepool include Bostrychus sinensis, Eleotris melanosoma, Mugilogobius chulae, and Pisodonophis boro). One individual was found inside a polyvinyl chloride pipe buried in the muddy gravel bottom along the main course of the stream during the daytime, and this site was approximately 10 m from the mangrove. Another individual was collected from the burrow of an unknown builder on muddy substrate using a suction pump during the daytime. One juvenile specimen was found in a similar tidepool on Ishigaki Island, Japan. (Ref. 129074).

species.name: Palomas pupfish
species.description: Occurs in springs, ciénegas, shorelines and cutoff channels of rivers and creeks, even colonizing ephemeral canals and ditches along roadsides (Ref. 43452). Distinct pairing during breeding. (Ref. 205).  Demersal eggs with adhesive threads (Ref. 205).

species.name: Palutrus reticularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inner reef flats (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Palée
species.description: Lacustrine. Males reproduce initially at 3-4 years, females at 5. Spawns on gravel near shore or, depending on population, in depths up to 50 m. Spawning time depends on depth and apparently on temperature at that location, from November to December in shallow water to February in deepest places (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pam's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found common at depths between about 13 and 20 m, on sheltered reef slopes where it formed aggregations of up to 10-30 individuals, among live and dead corals (predominantly tabulate acroporids), and in shady crevices (93848).

species.name: Pama croaker
species.description: Found in coastal waters, estuaries and rivers (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Pamphylian spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Streams inhabited are fed with surface water and drain into the Mediterranean Sea. The riparian vegetation of the 15- to 17-km-long stream includes emergent aquatic plants and other trees; with bottom covered with sand, gravel and partly mud. The Aksu River is about 140 km long and begins from Eğirdir and Kovada Lakes. The bottom of the Karaöz region of Aksu River is completely covered with gravel and sand, and its riparian vegetation also includes emergent aquatic plants. Associated species found at some localities (Aksu River) include Anguilla anguilla, Cyprinus carpio, Capoeta antalyensis, Vimba vimba, Clarias gariepinus, and Aphanius mento. On the other hand, species living in the Ilõca and Kömürcüler streams are A. anguilla, Capoeta angorae, Alburnus baliki, and Salaria fluviatilis. Specimens were collected with portable electroshocker (Ref. 58389).

species.name: Pampus punctatissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 42717).

species.name: Pamvotis chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with flowing, clear water.  Attains up to about 30 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pan sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and tidal rivers (Ref. 4833).  Also found in freshwater rivers (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Panama blackcheek shy blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (5-15 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Panama croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panama lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic near the coast (Ref. 31442).  Adults form dense aggregations at night (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Panama lightfish
species.description: Found in the epipelagic and mesopelagic zone (Ref. 35839).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35839).

species.name: Panama snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at a minimum depth of 500 m upon reaching 5 cm in length (Ref. 54657; 82347). Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Panama toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks and brooks of low to moderate velocity and sometimes is found in brackish tidelands. Found in brackish and freshwater between 0 and 15 m elevation. Forms schools in shallow waters and is also syntopic with P. turrubarensis. Insectivorous and eat many hymenoptera (Ref. 36880). Occurs along with other livebearers such as Poeciliopsis elongata and Neoheterandria tridentiger in mangrove swamps.

species.name: Panama triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in shallow rocky areas.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 11482).   Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Panamanian eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers moderate to fast flowing water over a substrate of small stones, sand, rocks and leaf debris from the forest canopy (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Panamanian greenbanded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panamanian jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits burrows in sand-rubble areas.  Feeds on benthic and planktonic invertebrates.

species.name: Panamanian tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panamanian worm blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic species found among weed on rocky reefs.

species.name: Panamic clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Panamic cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panamic dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals were seen poised 10-20 cm above small mounds encircling the small openings to their burrows. It was also observed in burrows always close to a reef or  grouped in small colonies on gently sloping mud-sand bottoms usually hundreds of meters from any rocky substrata. Juveniles were collected with quinaldine from the same burrows as adults they darted into. Often two adults or an adult and one or two juveniles were seen to occupy the same burrow. Individuals when prevented from entering their own burrow, would sometimes swim away rather than enter neighboring burrows (Ref. 75966).

species.name: Panamic frillfin
species.description: Inhabits high, sandy-bottom tide pools along rocky coasts (Ref. 5592).  Maximum length for female (Ref. 87607).

species.name: Panamic redhead goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs, usually found near Eucidaris thouarsi. Known as facultative cleaners (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Panamius panamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately flowing water over a substrate of small stones, sand, rocks, and leaf debris from the forest canopy.  Feeds on aufwuchs.

species.name: Panaqolus albivermis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaqolus albomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaqolus changae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaqolus claustellifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaqolus dentex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaqolus nix
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught mostly in cofferdams at the construction sites of the hydroelectric power plants of Santo Antônio and Jirau (former Santo Antônio and Jirau rapids) in rio Madeira. Most specimens were collected at depths of 3.1-11 m and 4.1 to 8.5 m using trawl nets, indicating preference for deep-water habitats with strong current (Ref. 104707).

species.name: Panaqolus purusiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaque armbrusteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaque bathyphilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaque cochliodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded maximum length and weight of a captive individual from the middle course of Magdalena River in Colombia, 45 cm SL and 1.45 kg, respectively (A.F. Echeverri (pers.comm. 04/09).

species.name: Panaque schaeferi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panaque titan
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Panatella silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Preferred habitat appears to be deeper enclosed atoll lagoons, reefs, coastal waters and harbors.  May gather in schools at night when attracted to light but generally not found in very large numbers.  May be taken as food by larger commercial species (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Panay anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known to be abundantly landed at the fish markets during July to September (Ref. 121596).

species.name: Panay ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pancake batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bare sandy bottom where, during the day, it rests partly covered by a thin layer of sand (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Panchax de Playfair
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small fresh and brackish water streams.  10 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Also inhabit ponds.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and fish (Ref. 7020).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pandaka bipunctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pandaka trimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish waters (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Pando tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a blackwater river with no aquatic plants, except for bladderwort Utricularia; pH 5.9 and conductivity of 15 μS/cm (Ref. 82662).

species.name: Pangani barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Juvenile mouths very variable and may develop rubber lips (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Pangani haplo
species.description: Inhabits rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Pangani nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothobranchius vosseleri was observed from a wide variety of habitats, including ephemeral pools, temporary creeks, man-made ditches and small, probably permanent, streams; bordering vegetation of grasses and stands of Typha and Cyperus were found at all localities (Ref. 96650). It is an annual species, its annual reproduction was confirmed in the aquarium; eggs are, after a short courtship, deposited in the bottom substrate, which is mainly silt with an addition of decayed plant material (Ref. 96650). Like all other known Nothobranchius species, the eggs survive the dry season by delayed hatching; the majority of eggs are hatchable 8 to 10 weeks after spawning; growth is fast, after 6 to 7 weeks of age the young fishes may reproduce (Ref. 96650).

species.name: Pangani robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lagoons, mostly quieter stretches of rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Pangani suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 4967). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pangas catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Occurs in high estuary (freshwater tidal zone) as juveniles, moving to brackish water as sub-adults, and finally as adults to river mouths and inshore areas (Ref. 12693).  Longevity given as 10 years (Ref. 2686) but appears too low.  Feeds on snails, other mollusks (Ref. 1479) and plants (Ref. 4833).  Reared for consumption in Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam; excellent food fish with very white fine grained sweet flesh (Ref 2686).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pangasius bocourti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from large rivers (Ref. 12693).  Found in rapids and also in deeper slower reaches (Ref. 37771).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Feeds on plants (Ref. 9497).  Spawns at the onset of flood season and the young are first seen in June, averaging about 5 cm by mid-June.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pangasius conchophilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large rivers (Ref. 12693) and enters flooded forests (Ref. 9497). Found in rapids and in deep slow reaches (Ref. 37771). Juveniles feed on prawns and insects; subadults and adults on prawns, insects and particularly mollusks which are more predominant in stomach contents than in any other Pangasius species (Ref. 7432) and on plants (Ref. 9497). Migrates into the middle Mekong along the Thai-Lao border as water levels and turbidity begin to increase. Reproduces early in the flood season and juveniles of 6 to 7 cm are taken by late June (Ref. 12693). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pangasius djambal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bears strong resemblance to P. bocourti but has different gill-raker counts and coloration. Diet consists mostly of benthic insect larvae and worms, with some free swimming insects, submerged plants and seeds (Ref. 12693). Undertakes upstream and downstream migrations in the Mekong mainstream (Ref. 37770). Length type for maximum size is assumed in TL.

species.name: Pangasius elongatus
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. An omnivorous fish, feeding mainly on benthic animals such as mollusks and crustaceans.  During rainy seasons, Mekong specimens feed on fruits and various debris (Ref. 46915).
A single 63 cm SL gravid female was observed at Ban Hang Khone in Laos (Ref. 9497).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pangasius humeralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius kinabatanganensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius krempfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Migrating but the direction is unknown.  Dietary habits have not been studied.  Taxonomy of this species may be problematic (Ref. 12693).  Unique among pangasiid species in the Mekong in spending a major part of its life in marine coastal waters.  Migrates into the Mekong River (but not into any other rivers) in order to breed (Ref. 12369).  Regarded to be anadromous (Ref. 12369).  It was hypothesized that at least two populations in the Mekong undertake migration (Ref. 37770).  One population migrates during May-September from just south of Khone Falls upstream to spawning grounds along the mainstream Mekong all the way to Chiang Khong near the Lao-Thai-Myanmar border.  The other population migrates downstream from around Stung Treng to unknown spawning grounds somewhere between Stung Treng and Kompong Cham in Cambodia during the spawning season between May and August.  When water level starts to fall in October, the fish moves back to the main river to initiate an upstream dispersal migration, reaching the stretch just below the Khone Falls.  Stays in deep pools within the mainstream during the dry season (Ref. 37770).  Only two specimens of the fish were collected  on April 5, 1956 and September 10, 1957 in Beihai City, Guangxi (Ref. 45563).  Another on November 22, 1963 at Shanwei City of Guangdong Province (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Pangasius kunyit
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper waters. Occurs sympatrically with P. krempfi in the Mekong delta. It is considered as a candidate species for aquaculture and its reproduction in captivity has already been achieved in the Mekong delta, Viet Nam (Ref. 33567).

species.name: Pangasius lithostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius macronema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, lakes and reservoirs (Ref. 43281). Found in rapids (Ref. 37771). Forms large schools. Moves into tributary streams and flooded forests along with many species of cyprinids and other species of visually oriented catfishes such as P. pleurotaenia when water transparency decreases. Feeds on mollusks and chironomid insects (Ref. 12975), small fish and prawns (Ref. 56749). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pangasius mahakamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small specimens (smaller than 15 cm) were collected in brackish water in the river delta, while larger ones were found in the upper part.  No vegetation were found at the banks, relatively strong current, deep and turbid water.  An omnivorous fish, feeding mainly on insects and small fruits.  Spawning periods unknown (Ref. 46915).

species.name: Pangasius mekongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius myanmar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius nasutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975) and lakes (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Pangasius nieuwenhuisii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The stomach of the holotype contains very hard seeds of higher plants Ref. 7432).

species.name: Pangasius polyuranodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes and rivers (Ref. 56749).  Occurs in estuaries and lower reaches but has also been observed in the upper reaches during the rainy season.  Species is omnivorous with a tendency to opportunism (Ref. 46915).

species.name: Pangasius rheophilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from freshwater near the mouth; inhabits large pools near the sea, with deep and turbid waters.  In the upper reaches, inhabits torrential areas with clear water (altitude 200-400 m).  Immature specimens occur all over the basin; mature ones apparently present only in the upper reaches  in running water.  Mature ones observed to be able to cross major waterfalls by jumping out of the water.  Reproductive behaviors unknown.  Predominant in the stomachs of small specimens  were mollusks; large specimens with skeletal remains of small cyprinid species and fruits (Ref. 40416).

species.name: Pangasius sabahensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangasius silasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio agma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio alcoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, black or brown water swamps in open areas.

species.name: Pangio alternans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits black water streams under forest cover with quite swift current.

species.name: Pangio ammophila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow part of a medium-sized clear water stream, up to 200 m wide and up to at least 2 m deep with sand, gravel and stones as substrate. Its type series was collected from a shallow part of the river with a fast current over medium-sized rounded stones and sandy patches as substrate.  Caught only from sandy areas (Ref. 93057).

species.name: Pangio anguillaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in hailstone to peat carals (Ref. 57235).  Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Inhabits sand or leaf-litter in river stretches with slow current (Ref. 27732).  Occur near the bottom over sand or silt substrates in debris and decaying vegetation.  Spends much of its time buried in the sand or slowly foraging across the surface.  Breed in very shallow water with a lot of vegetation, most commonly in flooded forests or grasslands along the water edge.  Feeds mostly on benthic invertebrates.  Not fished commercially.  Occasionally seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Highly esteemed food fish in northern central Thailand (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Pangio apoda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio atactos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio bhujia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species was collected from a six-meter-deep homestead well that is used for drinking and irrigation purposes, as well as from a channel (<0.4m depth) connecting a pond to an adjacent paddy field located ca. 200 m away from the well; the pond with laterite rock walls had a substrate with a mix of sand and clay and covered with decayed leaves. Individuals with eggs were collected from the channel with reduced water flow. Species also occurring in the channel and paddy field included Pseudosphromenus cupanus, Channa striata, Rasbora dandia, and Aplocheilus lineatus (Ref. 121819).

species.name: Pangio bitaimac
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio borneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Pangio cuneovirgata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to peats in dense litter falled canals (Ref. 57235). Found among submerged vegetation along shores of stream with moderate current and clear and relatively cold water. Occurs sympatrically and syntopically with P. kuhlii in the Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and Java.

species.name: Pangio doriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland wetlands including peats (Ref. 57235).  Found among leaf litter in slow flowing streams under forest cover (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Pangio elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio filinaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from fast-flowing clearwater forested streams (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Pangio fusca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio incognito
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio lidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio longimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits standing water with sandy bed (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pangio lumbriciformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio malayana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest streams.

species.name: Pangio mariarum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio muraeniformis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shaded forest streams with acid water.  Lives among dense submerged vegetation and leaf litter (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Pangio myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lowland stream and peats (Ref. 57235).  Size up to 10 cm SL in aquarium-reared individuals (Ref. 43281).  Popular aquarium fish (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Pangio pangia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow moving rivers with sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pangio piperata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams, usually in thick leaf litters.

species.name: Pangio pulla
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits blackwater streams with moderate swift current.

species.name: Pangio robiginosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pangio semicincta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in forest streams with muddy bottoms and dense shore vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Nocturnal, secretive species in creeks, living near the bottom among vegetation.  Feeds on benthic organisms (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Pangio signicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stream with slow current, muddy gravel bottom with clear water but dark brown and with lots of algae and aquatic vegetation (Ref. 57993).

species.name: Pangio superba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in forest streams with muddy bottom and leaf litter accumulations (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Paniai gudgeon
species.description: Found in lakes and outlet streams at elevations of 1640-1750 m.  The only fish species found in its range and is used as bait for catching crayfish, an important source of food for the local population.

species.name: Pantanal dwarf catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An air-breather, inhabiting clear water streams with sandy to muddy bottom, up to 2.5 m deep with water flow up to 30 cm/sec.  Forages at twilight and night, moving little and preying mostly on chironomid larvae and tiny oligochaetes.  When disturbed may bury itself in the sand, diving quickly headfirst and making lateral movements with body.  Hides during the day amidst the exposed root tangle and basal portions of submersed aquatic vegetation, and among plant debris on the bottom.  A sample of 874 individuals (7.7-16.4 mm SL) taken at the end of the rainy season contains six sexually dimorphic males (14.0-14.6 mm SL) and several presumably adult females (12.8-16.4 mm SL) with up to 300 immature oocytes in each ovary.  Sexual ratio of 28 adults (11.9-14.1 mm SL) taken at random is 0.86 males to 1.14 females (Ref. 39865).

species.name: Pantanal eartheater
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and lagoons with sandy to muddy bottom.  Forages by plunging its protrusible mouth into the sandy or muddy bottom, filling it with sediment, and sorting out food inside the mouth.  The bulk of the mouthful is expelled through the opercular openings and the 
mouth, producing a cloud of sediment (substrate sifting).  This feeding mode leaves a series of pits and mounds on the bottom.  Feeds on insect larvae, crustaceans, plant debris and loose scales (Ref. 40396).  Discourages piranha attacks by watching the predator, a tactic used when 2-5 fish feed in groups and the individuals take turns as the "watchman".  Confronts an approaching piranha by charging towards the predator with an open mouth and erect dorsal fin (Ref. 9080).

species.name: Pantanal parasitic catfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found to exhibit parasitic traits (Ref. 6868).  Inhabits rivers with sandy to muddy bottom.
Forages both during the day and at night seeks the gill chambers of larger fishes, especially catfishes.  Enters and leaves the gill chamber during the host's ventilating movements:  feeds on blood drawn from the gill filaments and may stay in the gill chamber for 1-3 min; when gorged with blood, moves to the bottom and buries itself in the sand.  A single large catfish tethered on the river bank may feed thousand of these parasitic catfish over a period of up to 6 hours.  Two females, 1.8 cm TL, caught in January (wet season) had about 150 mature oocytes each, and one male 2.0 cm TL had well-developed testes.  Large numbers of this fish may kill fishes tethered by fishermen (Ref. 40386).

species.name: Pantano cichlid
