species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in intertidal areas  (Ref. 31184), like tide pools, rocky slopes, and places where there are boulders on the bottom (Ref. 5521).  Actively shuttle back and forth between rock-pools and air (Ref. 31184).  They breathe air (Ref. 31184) and can remain out of water for up to 2 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).  Feed mainly on algae (Ref. 13442). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pearl cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Quite popular with aquarists.

species.name: Pearl danio
species.description: Lives in hill streams (Ref. 4832).  Found in running waters of lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Occurs at the surface of small, clear streams (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on exogenous insects and some zooplankton (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in fish markets, but popular in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Pearl darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pearl dwarfgoby
species.description: Found on all coastal reefs on inshore coastal and lagoonal reefs, including those subject to significant sedimentation (8 m down to at least 30 m), where it frequents complex reef habitat with abundant live coral or rugose rubble areas (Ref. 130976).

species.name: Pearl goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in turbid coastal areas near river mouths at less than 1 m to at least 12 m,  Ref. 48637.

species.name: Pearl gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps and streams, usually among dense vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Found in lowland swamps with acidic water (Ref. 57235).  An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Pearl of Likoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over rocky substrate (Ref. 6307).

species.name: Pearl perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters in moderate depths to 90 m on the continental shelf particularly close to submerged reefs, rock ledges or rough bottom (Ref. 27621).  This species is stated to be a midwater feeder (Ref. 27621).  The inside of the mouth is black and may luminescent at night (Ref. 27621).

species.name: Pearl stingray
species.description: Dasyatis margaritella is the most common littoral stingray on the West African coast and it enter lagoons, shallow bays and estuaries (Ref. 7397, 81259). Most likely feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Pearl wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky substrate of inshore areas.  They also inhabit tide pools and relatively deeper water (Ref. 55080).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on crustaceans, including shrimps, amphipods (gammarids and caprellids), copepods, ostracods, isopods, and brachyuran crabs.  Other food items include sipunculids, gastropods, chitons, and occasionally ophiuroids and echinoids, tunicates, algae, foraminifera, and fish material.  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pearl-spot chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral or rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Pearl-spotted fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Pearl-spotted killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water among vegetation, where it  feeds on insect larvae, crustaceans, and algae.  Breeds during the warmer months of the year.  (Ref. 13609).  8 cm max TL (Ref. 11028).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pearlfish
species.description: Common species (Ref. 34024).  Occurs in or near shallow seagrass beds.  Lives in body cavity of sea cucumbers during daytime and leaves host at night. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 34024.

species.name: Pearlscale angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons and seaward reefs, mainly in coral rich areas (Ref. 1602). Feeds on algae. Oviparous (Ref. 240), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Frequently exported through the aquarium trade. Form hybrids with Centropyge eibli and C. flavissima at areas of sympatry. Mimicked by juveniles of the acanthurid Acanthurus pyroferus (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Pearlscale butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Clear coastal to outer reef slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 48636). Found around staghorn corals. The only member of the family with a crosshatch pattern of dark lines on the sides. Generally seen below 15 m depth and occurs singly or in pairs. Feed on small benthic invertebrates and algae, similar to C. mertensii (Ref. 37816). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pearlspot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily found in brackish water but known to tolerate fresh or marine waters for short periods (Ref. 48490).  Found in large rivers, reservoirs, lagoons and estuaries.  Feed on filamentous algae, plant material and insects.

species.name: Pearly cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal, often silty reefs or shallow lagoons, forming schools just above branching corals (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Pearly goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs on open sand or silty sand bottom or on sand and rubble in the vicinity of reefs or rocky outcrops (Ref. 54393).

species.name: Pearly lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, nyctoepipelagic at the surface and to 950 m and generally found between 475-850 m during the day (Ref. 4479).  Neustonic to mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Lipid content is 3.8 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 10.6 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).  Females reach sexual maturity at 4.8 cm, males at 3.5 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Pearly perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Pearly prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in soft bottoms on outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Pearly rasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in shallow, cool, clear, quiet, heavily shaded forest streams, usually with a silty substrate and often in areas with a large amount of leaf debris in the water.  Feeds on terrestrial insects (Diptera and Coleoptera, see Ref. 6469) and detritus.  Males slimmer and brightly colored than females.

species.name: Pearly rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pearly sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal coral reefs with moderate wave action (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pearly tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Poorly known and rarely seen but probably inhabits deep waters (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pearly-finned cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species.  Occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).  Lives in holes in the mud during the day.  Usually trawled near river mouths (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Pearly-spotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in inshore, usually silty habitat on sand or mud near shallow reefs and seagrass beds (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Pearlycheek cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Pearse's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather that actively shuttles back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Pebbled butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over reefs and rocks (Ref. 58302).  Feed mainly on coral polyps, also polychaete worms and small shrimps.  Usually seen in pairs.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Peckoltia bachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at the edge of medium to large rivers among submerged twigs and grasses, usually in flow (Ref. 77026).

species.name: Peckoltia braueri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift riffles among very large boulders (Ref. 54521).

species.name: Peckoltia brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia caenosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing muddy streams.  Also encountered inside submerged, hollow logs during the day (Ref. 77026).

species.name: Peckoltia capitulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in swift current at a single place of Approuague River.  During the time of collection, the river was very turbid as a result of illegal gold mining activities (Ref. 90183).

species.name: Peckoltia cavatica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with large number of lateritic rocks (Ref. 54521).

species.name: Peckoltia compta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia ephippiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia furcata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia greedoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia lineola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky riffles (Ref. 77026).

species.name: Peckoltia lujani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia oligospila
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia otali
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rapids, it occurs mostly in sunny and shallow clear water, swiftly flowing currents, with medium- sized rocks substrate (Ref. 90183).

species.name: Peckoltia pankimpuju
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia sabaji
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in medium to large rivers among boulders, usually in runs and riffles. Small individuals may be found hidden in the holes of lateritic rocks in pools and most specimens were collected at night. The largest individual was captured in a gill net in the main stem Essequibo and this individual apeared to be moving from deeper water into the shallows where there were exposed boulders (Ref. 50590).

species.name: Peckoltia simulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small forest creek tributaries on sandy and graveled bottom with rocks, woods and leaves (Ref. 90183). Collected with other species such as of Ancistrus cf. leucostictus, Ancistrus. aff. temminckii, Guyanancistrus longispinis, Farlowella reticulata, Rineloricaria stewarti, and Otocinclus mariae (Ref. 90183).

species.name: Peckoltia vermiculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peckoltia vittata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens from Venezuela were collected from rocks in runs (Ref. 77026). Nocturnal species; feeds on algae (Ref. 13371).  Aquarium keeping:  feeds on plants and roots; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Pecos gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated springs and effluents.

species.name: Pecos pupfish
species.description: Occurs in springs, sinkholes and pools of streams.  6 cm max TL  (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pectenocypris balaena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small forest streams.  Collected in open areas, usually with flooded grasses.  Feeds on phytoplankton (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Pectenocypris korthausae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pectenocypris micromysticetus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pectinantus parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pectinochromis lubbocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pectoral podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Pedder galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky lake margins and occurs to a lesser extent around submerged vegetation and log snags.  Usually around rocks and boulders on lake margins in darkly tannin-stained water.   Juveniles shoal in open water near lake margins.  Spring spawning occurs in small feeder streams.  Eggs are deposited in sheltered positions among vegetation, rocks or woody debris and take about 3-4 weeks to hatch.  Sexual maturity is reached after the second year but most fish breed in their third or fourth year (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on crustaceans and insect larvae.  Spawning probably occurs in spring as juveniles are numerous during summer months.

species.name: Pegasus laternarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults lives on muddy bottoms, often collected at depths of about 50 m; larvae are planktonic.  Rarely seen diving, except a few localities in Japan where they occur in sheltered muddy habitats (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Peipsi whitefish
species.description: Inhabits lakes and rivers.  Spawns mainly in southern coastal part of Lake Peipus and northern part of Lake Teploe, but also enters some rivers to spawn (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pelagic basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the open ocean.  Spends the day in midwater from 305-1,829 m depth and migrates near surface at night (Ref. 2850).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pelagic cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pelagic porcupinefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic throughout its life history (Ref. 592, 48637).  A schooling species.  Feeds on larger zooplankton and fish larvae (Ref. 9680, 48637).

species.name: Pelagic scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pelagic worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelagocephalus coheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelangia mbutaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelasgus epiroticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which occurs in lakes and lowland water courses, with little current.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Is threatened due to pollution and water abstraction.  Spawns in May and June (Ref. 26100).  Reaches up to about 10 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pelates qinglanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Peled
species.description: Freshwater and estuarine.  Lacustrine, fluvial and anadromous forms exist (Ref. 593). Lives up to 13 years (6 in dwarf form). Feeds on zooplankton (mostly crustaceans), benthic animals (especially insect larvae and mussels, also algae) and insects from surface. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pelican Knifefish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Electric organ discharge known from two sexually mature
females and three sexually mature males. The two female specimens exhibited a lower Fo (1.242–1.243 kHz) than the three male specimens (1.337, 1.387 and 1.396 kHz) (Ref. 80384).

species.name: Pellegrin's barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 11.5 cm (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Pellona altamazonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pellonale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and streams (Ref. 188). It forms large schools in lower courses of rivers (Ref. 2244, 43836), and is very abundant in brackish water habitat (Ref. 86940).

species.name: Pelmato
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020). In the river Sombreiro (Nigeria) observed to mainly feed on diatoms, algae, higher plants and detritus (Ref. 52307). Pair bonding (Ref. 52307), cave-spawning (Ref. 52307, 81260), substrate brooder (Ref. 81260). Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Pelmatochromis buettikoferi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivorous, feeding on small items like detritus and insect larvae; probably an open substratum spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Pelmatochromis nigrofasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Open substratum spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Pelmatochromis ocellifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelteobagrus eupogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelteobagrus intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelteobagrus tonkinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peltorhamphus tenuis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal coastal waters on sandy or sandy-mud bottoms. Small juveniles are caught at depths similar to those of adults, but juveniles are known to inhabit shallow water, not shallow-water inlets, perhaps reflecting an avoidance for areas with soft, silty substrates. Prey consumed may be similar to is congeners based on jaw morphology and mouth size, thus feeding on small small epibenthic and infaunal invertebrates such as crustaceans, molluscs, and polychaetes (Ref. 123823).

species.name: Pelvic-spot wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in still coastal waters, where brittle corals grow high.  Occurs in small groups that feed actively among the lower and dead parts of the corals with coralline algae.  Easily overlooked because of its small size.  Length to 6.5 cm, but usually much smaller (Ref. 48636).  Always hides or stays close to its shelter (Ref. 90102).   A secretive species.  Feeds on amphipods and other small invertebrates.  Rarely found in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Pelvicachromis drachenfelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is restricted to pure freshwater of low conductivity and pH (Ref. 97630).

species.name: Pelvicachromis kribensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pelvicachromis roloffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found primarily in smaller rivers and creeks, although it may also be found in shallows waters near the banks of larger rivers; pair-bonding cave spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Pelvicachromis sacrimontis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In aquaria, this species is a monogamous, pair bonding cave-spawner (Ref. 119364).

species.name: Pelvicachromis silviae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In aquaria, this species is a monogamous, pair bonding cave-spawner; frequently imported to Europe and North America for ornamental fish trade; seems not to be rare (Ref. 93865).

species.name: Pelvicachromis subocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding (Ref. 52307), cave-spawning (Ref. 52307, 81260), substrate brooder (Ref. 81260).

species.name: Pelvicachromis taeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-spawning, substrate brooder (Ref. 81260). Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Pemba chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep outer reef slopes.  They are found in small loose groups near shelter often above reef pinnacles (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pempheris adspersa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal, retreats to large surge pools or channels open to the sea during the day and usually under overhangs or ledges in small schools.  Juveniles occur amongst weed along rocky shores in late summer.  Feeds on plankton and benthic organisms (Ref. 26966).  Adult diet observed consists of amphipods (45%), mysids (20%), polychaetes (20%), isopods (7%), and crab larvae and ostracods (8%) which are taken out of the water column c. 4-5 m from the bottom.  Juveniles that are less than 40 mm are diurnal feeders, mostly feeding on small copepods.  Some groups were observed to enter rivers by night in summer and swim well upstream into mangrove forests to feed on crab larvae, shrimps, amphipods, and other zooplankton (Ref. 88976).  The smallest identified gravid female was 8.56 cm SL and the largest 12.3 cm SL. Gravid females were found among collections made in mid November into February.  These observations agree with reported observations that spawning occurs from November through February and that juveniles settle in January through April (Ref. 88976).

species.name: Pempheris japonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs in shallow waters; not forming large schools (Ref. 43239). Active at night and spends the day in caves (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Pempheris malabarica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pempheris molucca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and rocky areas (Ref. 27550).  Enters estuaries (Ref. 27550).  Feeds on crustaceans and polychaete worms (Ref. 27550).

species.name: Pempheris nesogallica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pempheris nyctereutes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with set nets.

species.name: Pempheris otaitensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef and rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pempheris rapa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pempheris rhomboidea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Pempheris sarayu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pempheris schreineri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pempheris xanthoptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species.  Juveniles form large schools.  Tasty food fish.

species.name: Penang betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small fast flowing forest streams (Ref. 13061).  Inhabits mainly overhanging bank vegetation, submerged leaf litter and exposed roots of bank vegetation (Ref. 13220, 56613).  Mouth brooder (Ref. 13061).

species.name: Pence's squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pencil cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults benthic on the continental slope and collected with bottom trawls (Ref. 7321).  Juveniles are pelagic in depths of 130-145 and 350-425 m (Ref. 9563).  Feed on small fishes and planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 4738).  Oviparous (Ref. 4738).

species.name: Pencil coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slopes (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Pencil snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pencil weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on rocky reefs with thick growths of brown macroalgae at depths of 10 m; also in areas of only moderate wave action.

species.name: Penguinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reported to reach 8 cm TL (Ref. 1672).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Peninsular clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peninsular hilltrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams, rivers and lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Penn's thrush eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pennahia ovata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pennant flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Pennant goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pennant goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Pennant pearlside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pennant-tailed suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky riffles and rapids (Ref. 52193). It feeds on insects such as mayfly nymphs and blackfly larvae grazed from rocks (Ref. 52193). Its spines protect it from predators such as trout (Ref. 52193). Breeds during the summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Is an occasional aquarium species (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Pennyfish
species.description: Occurs in small, slow-flowing streams and swamps where there is dense aquatic vegetation (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Tolerant of temperatures between 25° and 38°C, and a pH range of 4.5-8.1 (Ref. 44894).  Feeds primarily on aquatic insects and micro-crustaceans (Ref. 5259, 44894).  The smallest ambassid in Australia, with a life span of probably 2-3 years.  Sexual maturity is attained at the end of the first year and breeding has been recorded in the wet season in flooded swampy lagoons (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Penopus japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Penopus microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Penpoint gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal areas, especially in tide pools (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of the water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 6885).  Pairs are found coiled around egg masses (Ref. 4925).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Pentaceros quinquespinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pentecost Sicyopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in clear, high gradient streams with rocky bottom.  It lives on the bottom, on top of rocks, and often seen swimming in open water in the current between rocks or in large pools.  Like its congeners, it is presumed to spawn in freshwater, the free embryos drift downstream to the sea where these undergo a planktonic phase, and before returning to the rivers to grow and reproduce (Ref. 85524).

species.name: Pentherichthys atratus
species.description: Also mesopelagic.  Males dwarfed and non-parasitic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Pepperdot tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected by trawlers operating in deep waters, on the continental shelf and/or continental slope. Landed catch also contained S. orientalisand other deep-sea fishes known to occur at depths of about 300-400 m (Ref. 82202).

species.name: Peppered chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peppered corydoras
species.description: Found in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Peppered dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found to be abundant in small coral limestone islands, with small shallow lagoons and steep outer slopes to deepwater, on submerged volcanic peaks (Ref. 94781).

species.name: Peppered goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sponge-dwelling goby which inhabits loggerhead sponges, 1-2 ft in diameter, at depths of 12-28 m. Generally co-occurs with Evermannichthys metzelaari (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Peppered horseface loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peppered maskray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Size of new-born specimens 90-105 mm DW (Ref. 76964).

species.name: Peppered shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and sluggish runs of small to medium rivers; often in quiet water near vegetation (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Peppered spinefoot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and channel reefs (Ref. 9710), usually near steep slopes and harbours (Ref. 48637).  Usually seen in pairs.  Feeds on benthic seaweeds (Ref. 9813).

species.name: Pepperfin cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peppermint angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ledges, caves, and rubble areas of steep seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48391).  Never or rarely exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Peppermint armour goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing streams.

species.name: Peppermint bass
species.description: A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting deep recesses of coral reefs.  Common, but secretive and rarely seen (Ref. 9710).  The maximum size for this species is about 8 cm standard length or 100 mm TL (value from Ref. 26938) (P.Heemstra, pers.comm. 12/09).

species.name: Peppermint goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coral heads in fairly deep water.  Usually solitary, but sometimes swims close to reef in small groups.

species.name: Pepperminteye dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on sandy slopes, coral patches, and lagoons (Ref. 94740).

species.name: Peprilus crenulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuarine and coastal marine waters at depths of up to 136 meters.  Probably does not form large schools for though it is common in the catches of artisanal fisheries (notably in Brazil), it is always in small numbers (Ref. 116249).

species.name: Peprilus xanthurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perak river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and canals including peat tributaries, feeding mainly on zooplankton and insect (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Percarina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups in fresh and brackish waters with salinities up to 7 ppt, abundant at depths around 5 m over black mud.  Feeds predominantly on benthic invertebrates. Spawns in coastal waters close to river mouths, over mud bottom.  Spawning occurs in May-June.  More or less abundant in lower reaches of rivers and coastal lagoons but increased salinity resulting from reduced flow in all large rivers, which are now dammed, may pose threat to its population (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Percarina maeotica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal fresh and brackish waters with salinities up to 7 ppt, and river mouths. Occurs in groups. From about 6 mm SL feeds actively on planktonic crustaceans, at 16-40 mm on larger copepods and mysids, and from second year of life on Knipowitschia longecaudata, Clupeonella cultriventis, benthic worms, molluscs and insect larvae. Attains first sexual maturity at 1 year of age. Spawns in at least saline part of Gulf of Taganrog in June-July. Adults migrate to open sea soon after spawning. Eggs are released over mud bottom. Eggs hatch in 2 days and larvae first lie on bottom, moving to the surface at 4 days (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 50 cm; prefers flowing water over rocky bottoms (Ref. 7094). Feeds on vegetation and periphyton (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Perchaude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, ponds, pools of creeks, and rivers.  Also found in brackish water and in salt lakes.  Most commonly found in clear water near vegetation; tends to shoal near the shore during spring (Ref. 9988, 10294).  Feeds on immature insects, larger invertebrates, fishes and fish eggs during the day.  Preyed upon by fishes and birds (Ref. 1998).  Spawns between February and July in the northern hemisphere and between August and October in the southern hemisphere (Ref. 10999).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Marketed fresh or frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled or baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Perche
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottom and on Posidonia beds. Feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5506). Also found in muddy and algal or seagrass overgrown substrates. Reported to be a simultaneous hermaphrodite, which tends to spawn from early spring to early summer (Ref. 91154).

species.name: Perche chinoise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers (Ref. 26334).  Are demersal piscivores which have very specialized feeding habits--as soon as they start feeding, they feed solely on fry of other fish species.  Typical of stalking predators, they rely on vision for following the movement of prey before leaping forward and snapping at the victim.  Prey consist mostly of diurnal fishes whose eyes have color vision and high acuity but cannot function at night.  The habitat of the  Chinese perch is usually rich in macrophytes and might be very turbid during rainy season (Ref. 28033).

species.name: Perche de mer pourpre
species.description: Found primarily on continental reefs (Ref. 9710).  Form aggregations on outer reef slopes to depths over 30 m (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans and fish eggs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perche grimpeuse
species.description: Prefers forest regions (Ref. 7393, 57414).

species.name: Perche grimpeuse (Microctenopoma nanum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum total length reported 8.0 cm (Ref. 6803).

species.name: Perche Macquarie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and flowing streams usually in deep holes with rock or gravel substrates (Ref. 5259). Inhabits cool, clear water of rivers, lakes and reservoirs. Prefers slow-flowing, deep rocky pools. Solitary, swimming near the bottom or in mid-water, but form small shoals during the spawning season (October to December) (Ref. 44894). Forms large shoals near shore. Fry feeds on zooplankton; adult on aquatic insects, crustaceans and mollusks. Male matures at 20 cm (2 y), female at 30 cm (3 y). Spawns upstream in spring or early summer; eggs hatch in 13-18 days; larvae of 7 cm TL (Ref. 5259). Moves into areas just upstream of shallow riffles over gravel or rocky bottoms to spawn. The female releases demersal eggs which sink into cracks in the substrate. Fish in reservoirs move into flowing feeder streams to spawn. Sexual maturity is reached after 2 years (20 centimeters) for males, 3 years (30 centimeters) for females (Ref. 44894). Tolerates temp. down to 9°C (Ref. 7276). Infected by nematodes and copepod Lernaea cyprinacea (Ref. 7315).

species.name: Perche maori
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally encountered in coral reefs or shallow inshore flats (Ref. 30573).  Found singly or in small groups (up to 15 to 20 individuals).  Adults on deep coastal slopes; juveniles on shallow algae-reef flats, often near freshwater run-offs (Ref. 48635).  Feed on fishes, cephalopods and benthic crustaceans (Ref. 30573).  An excellent food fish.  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253). Caught with handlines, traps, and gill nets, occasionally trawled; important to artisanal fisheries and marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9821). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Perche rouget
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on fishes and larger invertebrates such as squids, shrimps and crabs; also takes planktonic organisms, including pelagic urochordates.  An important food fish in some areas.  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 55).

species.name: Perche à raies bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered lagoons and exposed, outer slope coral reefs.  Frequently encountered in large aggregations including 100 or more individuals at moderate depths, usually in 30-40m, like in some Pacific locations (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles solitary and shallow in protected bays with algae and rubble substrates.  They feed mainly on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4533).

species.name: Perche écarlate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit both coastal and offshore reefs. They tend to be associated with sponge and gorgonian-dominated habitats on the North West Shelf (Ref. 28006), and hard mud areas of the Arafura Sea. In Australia, they frequently form mixed shoals with L. erythropterus. Juveniles tend to inhabit shallow inshore waters and larger fish live in deeper waters (Ref. 27260, 27264). Juveniles also occur in mangrove areas and seagrass beds (Ref. 128523). Feed mainly on fishes, with small amounts of benthic crustaceans, cephalopods and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6390). They forage mostly at night (Ref. 6390). Caught mainly with handlines, bottom longlines, and bottom trawls (Ref. 9821). Marketed fresh, dried-salted (Ref. 55) and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Perche-brochet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit large, turbid rivers and eutrophic lakes, brackish coastal lakes and estuaries.  Feed mainly on gregarious, pelagic fishes.  They attain first sexual maturity at 3-10 years of age, usually at 4.  Undertake short spawning migrations. Individuals foraging in brackish water move to freshwater habitats.  Migrations up to 250 km have been recorded.  Homing is well developed, even nearby populations may be relatively isolated.  Spawn in pairs at dawn or night.  Spawning occurs in April-May, exceptional from late February until July, depending on latitude and altitude when temperatures reach 10-14° C on spawning grounds (Ref. 59043).  Popularly fished by sport fishers.  Its flesh is succulent (Ref. 30578).  Utilized fresh or frozen and eaten steamed, broiled and microwaved (Ref. 9988).  An individual weighing 19 kg was reportedly caught in 1959 in Starnberger, Bavaria, Germany (Peter Admicka, pers. Comm.  E-mail:  peter.adamicka@oeaw.ac.at).

species.name: Percichthys chilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percichthys laevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percichthys melanops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percilia gillissi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percilia irwini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percina apina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitats of this species differ between reproductive and non-reproductive periods. Both sexes in  in reproductive condition were most often found in swift runs of depths about one meter or less with predominant gravel and cobble substrates. On many occasions, adult males were collected in shallow, swift riffles with gravel bottoms during late April to early June. In summer months, adult males and females occurred in swift runs and in pool areas with substrates free of silt. Subadults were only encountered in pool habitats and were usually accompanied by adult females (Ref. 116752).

species.name: Percina brucethompsoni
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Observed to seasonally occupy two different types of habitats. In spring season, breeding individuals typically occurs in gravelbottomed and cobble substrate riffle areas and swift chutes and runs of up to approximately 1 m deep.  Inhabits deeper pool habitats for the remainder of the year.  Also reported to inhabit deep, swift riffle areas with rocky substrates
and thick growths of <i>Podostemon heterophyllum in spring.  During fall, a single specimen was collected from a sluggish siltbottom pool at the confluence of the Ouachita River and Lake Ouachita.  Also observed to have preference for a late-summer microhabitat of upstream edges of runs that invariably included slight surface agitation and a high
percentage of cobble substrate.

species.name: Percis matsuii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy-sand bottom.

species.name: Percocypris pingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Percocypris regani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A predatory species (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Percocypris tchangi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perdix cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found among rubble of reef flats and 'dead' reefs (Ref. 1602, 58302).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Secretive (Ref. 48635), nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Eggs are incubated orally (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Periophthalma prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal to outer reef sand slopes to 35 meters depth (Ref. 48637); on sandy areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Inhabits burrows with alpheid shrimps (Ref. 11441).

species.name: Periophthalmodon septemradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Periophthalmus chrysospilos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184) found in brackish mangrove and nipa palm areas (Ref. 7050).  Actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Periophthalmus magnuspinnatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies elevated, vegetated mudflats (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Periophthalmus malaccensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Periophthalmus pusing
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide-dominated coastal system with relatively low wave action; also within the mangrove forest, it was found in a variety of microhabitat types in seaward and higher mangrove areas as well as within, and on sloping banks of tidal creeks. Found syntopic with congeners P. argentilineatus and P. malaccensis (Ref. 111149).

species.name: Periophthalmus spilotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from the intertidal mudflat of the Suir river of Tebing Tinggi I., Sumatra. Associated with Periophthalmus novemradiatus and P. gracilis (Ref. 35996).

species.name: Periophthalmus variabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Periophthalmus walailakae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mangrove forests (Ref. 49729).  Builds burrows 9-13 cm wide and 100-120 cm deep (Ref. 49729).  Nocturnal, leaving the burrow to feed in the evening and returning in the morning (Ref. 49729).

species.name: Perissodus eccentricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic species (Ref. 6770) occuring in the rocky habitat (Ref. 46829). Scale-ripper (Ref. 6770, 46829). Caught at depths from 60-100 metres (Ref. 93918), but has also been seen in the shallow rocky habitat (Ref. 46829). Breeding behaviour is interesting as it involves a pair bond even though they are mouthbrooders in which the female broods the eggs (Ref. 466829). Come to shoreline to release their fry (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Perissodus microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Scale-eating. Prefers fish that feed from the algal layer or fish which are inattentive, the usual prey being Tropheus and Pseudosimochromis (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Perissodus paradoxus
species.description: Frequently seen solitary in rocky habitats but usually hunts in packs of more than 500 individuals at great depths.  Feeds on the scales of fish (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Peristedion altipinne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with deepwater trawls in depths between 100 and 200 m on the Brazilian shelf (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Peristedion amblygenys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peristedion barbiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Needs better reference.

species.name: Peristedion crustosum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on soft-bodied invertebrates and worms (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Peristedion ecuadorense
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peristedion greyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peristedion imberbe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peristedion nesium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected with otter trawls at depths between 110 and 180 m, over sandy substratum.  However, it was not present in hauls made along the same transects at lesser depths.  Typical demersal fishes collected in the same hauls include Paralichthyidae, Triglidae, Anthiinae, Ophichthidae, Aulopidae, Ococephalidae and Malacanthidae (Ref. 86275).

species.name: Peristedion orientale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the shelf edge.

species.name: Peristedion paucibarbiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peristedion riversandersoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Peristedion unicuspis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Peristedion weberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perle du Suriname
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Though not so abundant, it is often caught in the quiet zones of cascades with G. harreri (Ref. 35237). Lives in mud and sand-bottomed canals. Maximum length 30 cm TL (Ref. 5723). Omnivorous, with a tendency towards herbivory, searches for food by digging into the substrate with its protractile mouth. Can emit sounds through its pharyngeal teeth though it is not known whether it is a form of communication or not. Spawning takes place on a flat stone or in a hole dug in the sand. Parents generally take the eggs into their mouths until hatching occurs three days later. At night or when faced with danger, the alevins seeks shelter in the mother's mouth. Parents take care of their siblings for several weeks (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Perloeil courte dorsale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mesopelagic or bathypelagic species (Ref. 6601).

species.name: Perloeil longue dorsale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults mesopelagic (below 500 m); larvae in upper 200 m (Ref. 5174).

species.name: Permitin spiny plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perpeire
species.description: Occurs in bays, lagoons and shallow coastal waters.  Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Perpeire a quatre taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9330), on sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 11482).  Utilized fresh or as fishmeal (Ref. 9330).

species.name: Perpeire chausson
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottoms with mud or rubble, near the coast up to a depth of 46 m.  Occasionally exploited with encircling nets.  Utilized fresh or as fishmeal.

species.name: Perpeire chaussure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms of shallow waters, including estuaries.  Utilized fresh or as fishmeal.

species.name: Perpeire de Delsman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud and rubble bottoms.

species.name: Perpeire de sable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sandy bottoms.  Possibly exploited occasionally by trawlers in Panama and Colombia.

species.name: Perpeire dentu
species.description: Inhabits soft bottoms, from within the vicinity of mangrove areas up to a depth of 29 m (Ref. 9330).  Feeds on large benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 9330).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 9330).  Max. length size of female from Ref. 105273.

species.name: Perpeire des Caraïbes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.

species.name: Perpeire du Golfe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sandy bottoms.

species.name: Perpeire frange
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9330).  Common in estuaries (Ref. 9330).  Feeds on big, benthic invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 9330).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 9330).

species.name: Perpeire grande gueule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms of trawling grounds and bays (Ref. 11482); commonly found in estuaries; sometimes enters freshwater.  Feeds on big benthic invertebrates and small fishes.  Utilized fresh and frozen.

species.name: Perpeire gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits soft bottoms (Ref. 9330); from the littoral zone (35 m, shallowest depth reported in Ref. 9330) up to 600 m (Yañez and Barbieri, 1974.in Ref. 82251:833). Common depth range was taken from a study done in northern Chile. Stomach contents include mainly the squat lobsters (Pleuroncodes monodon and Cervimunida johni) and the deep-sea shrimp (Heterocarpus reedi) (Ref. 82251). Exploited on a local level with trawl nets and is utilized fresh or as fishmeal.

species.name: Perpeire langue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized fresh and is said to be an excellent foodfish.

species.name: Perpeire lisse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 2683, 81290) and brackish water of estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 81290, 81683), also ascending rivers (Ref. 81683) and entering freshwater (Ref. 2683). Feeds on fish, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Perpeire longue aile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or sandy-muddy bottom (Ref. 9750).  Utilized fresh.

species.name: Perpeire met-des-dieux
species.description: Inhabits soft bottoms, from shallow estuaries up to a depth of 44 m (Ref. 9330).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 9330).

species.name: Perpeire pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft or rocky bottoms.  Exploited on a local level with trawl nets and is utilized fresh or as fishmeal.

species.name: Perpeire pélican
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the deeper continental shelf to depths of almost 1,000 m (Ref. 27121).  Found on sand, mud and clay bottoms (Ref. 4417).  Feeds on larger benthic animals (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30573.

species.name: Perpeire queue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud, sand, or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9281).  Utilized as fishmeal (Ref. 9281).

species.name: Perpeire zingua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms.  Marketed fresh and may also be utilized as fishmeal.

species.name: Perpeire à grandes écailles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy areas of the continental shelf.  Feeds on crustaceans, polychaetes, and other benthic animals (Ref. 9824).  Marketed fresh and sometimes dried (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Perpeire à queue tachetée
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Perrooquet bossu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9338).  Occurs in small aggregations over reefs.  Feeds by scraping the substrate for coralline red algae, and probably on coral polyps.  Only caught occasionally (Ref. 9338).

species.name: Perroquet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seaward slopes and reef flats (Ref. 90102).  Usually associated with outer reefs but will enter shallow water in protected areas.  Often in large schools (Ref. 9710).  Grazes on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).  Also caught with nets and other types of artisanal gear (Ref. 2689).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Perroquet (Sparisoma cretense)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In shallow water along rocky shores.  Feed on algae and small invertebrates (Ref. 6761, 56146). Herbivore species with specialized pharyngeal bones and muscles (Ref. 52194, 52195).  Breeding occurs from July to September, with juveniles recruiting in late summer in Portugal (Ref. 56146).

species.name: Perroquet aile-noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in seagrass beds in shallow, protected waters.  Feeds primarily on epiphytes and seagrass blades, leaving crescent bite marks.  Darts into seagrass when frightened (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet arabe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs, in areas with high coral cover (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs.  Young are commonly found in mangrove areas.  Feeds mainly on benthic algae (Ref. 3802).  Known to have a home cave to which it retires at night or when danger threatens; makes use of the sun as an aid to locating the cave.

species.name: Perroquet azur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky, boulder strewn reefs and slopes.  Commonly occurs in reefs with reef building stony corals.  Feeds by scraping algae from rocks and corals (Ref. 5227).  Uncommon species.  Only caught occasionally.

species.name: Perroquet banane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 10 m (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Also found in lagoons and coastal and outer reefs to 20 m deep (Ref. 90102). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972). Occurs singly (Ref. 4821).  May also form groups (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet basto
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and seagrass beds.  Juveniles or primary-phase fish can rapidly assume a mottled pattern as it comes to rest on the bottom.  Spawning is usually a group activity in similarly colored males and females (Ref. 5521).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Perroquet beriquete
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in shallow coastal areas, especially in rocky coasts with macroalgae.  May be solitary or swim in loose schools (Ref. 5227).  Feeds by scraping or breaking off chunks of the reef and digest the algae that grows within, or they feed directly on algae (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Perroquet bicolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs and clear lagoons (Ref. 1602), at depths of 1-30 m.  Occurs in groups of females with one male (Ref. 90102) form harems; while juveniles are usually solitary (Ref. 9710).  Males are territorial.  Goes to several changes during growth and very large females change sex to the brightly colored male.  Small juveniles usually in dense coral and algae habitats (Ref. 48636). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs.  Juveniles generally solitary; large adults often school together. Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet bleu (Scarus coeruleus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs. Juveniles found on Thalassia beds (Ref. 13628). Feeds on benthic plants and small organisms in the sand (Ref. 5521). Forms large spawning aggregations (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet bossu bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found around deep rocky reefs up to a depth of at least 30 m (Ref. 9710).  Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 9710).  Also caught with nets and other kinds of artisanal gear.  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Perroquet braisé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitary or in pairs in seaward reefs (Ref. 90102).  Usually over rocky or coral substrates, at boulder-strewn slopes at the base of high-island cliffs where it may occur in large schools.  Large adult usually on upper parts of deep slopes, but seen to about 35 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  An uncommon species (Ref. 9338).

species.name: Perroquet candelamoa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal regions associated with coral reefs and reef flats.  Forms groups consisting of a terminal phased individual and numerous individuals in the initial phase (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  Caught with nets and other artisanal gear.  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Perroquet capitaine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow fringing reefs.  Usually in areas with dead coral and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Forms small groups (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on benthic algae.  Also caught with nets and other kinds of artisanal gear.  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Perroquet commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs to at least 25 m depth (Ref. 1602).  Found over corals (Ref. 5213, 58652).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Initial-phase fish stage usually form small feeding schools (Ref. 2334).  Graze on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).  Secrete a mucus cocoon (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Perroquet de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky coastal areas (Ref. 7360).  A herbivorous species with specialized pharyngeal bones and muscles (Ref. 52194, 52195). Occurs in shallow water (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Perroquet de la Mer Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs around small coral heads or dead coral rock on silty sand of inshore reefs (Ref. 9710).  Solitary species (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet de Sinai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef slopes (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Perroquet des Carolines
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal reef flats, and lagoon and seaward reefs to a depths of at least 27 m (Ref. 1602). Found in coral, rubble, seagrass (Ref. 41878, 58302) and weedy areas (Ref. 9710). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Found singly or in small groups (Ref. 9710). Feeds on a variety of benthic encrusting algae, e.g., Padina (Ref. 37816) and seagrasses. A protogynous hermaphrodite which may only have secondary males. Caught with nets and other types of artisanal gear.

species.name: Perroquet du Golfe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perroquet faucille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep seaward reef slopes to at least 20 m depth (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae.  Also caught with nets, and other kinds of artisanal gear.  Sold mostly fresh in markets.

species.name: Perroquet feu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs with clear water (Ref. 13628). Young may be found in seagrass beds and other heavily vegetated bottoms. Feeds mainly on soft algae, but has been observed to graze on live corals like, Montastraea annularis (Ref. 6496). Produces a significant amount of sediment through bioerosion using its strong beak-like jaws and constantly re-growing teeth (Ref. 6485). Protogynous; strictly diurnal, spends the night sleeping on the bottom (Ref. 5221). Found singly or small in small groups.

species.name: Perroquet globeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons, seaward reefs, and reef flats (Ref. 90102).  More common in outer reef habitats than in protected waters.  Spawns in groups or in pairs. Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972). Caught mainly with traps, nets and other types of artisanal gear.

species.name: Perroquet joue blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear coastal and inner reefs (Ref. 48636); in lagoons and channel reefs (Ref. 2334).  Feeds by scraping algae from the substrate (Ref. 26993). Females usually in small groups and maybe mixed with other species when feeding; males solitary nearby (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet lune bleue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty protected reefs, over sand and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae.  Also caught with nets and other artisanal gear.  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Perroquet marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered bays, harbors and lagoons (Ref. 48636).  Inhabits seagrass areas or areas with hard substrates heavy with algal cover.  Usually occur in small groups.  Unlike other parrotfishes, males and females look very similar and do not change sex (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on seagrasses and algae (Ref. 30573).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Perroquet marguerite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the most widespread parrotfishes, but highly variable and some geographical forms that are probably subspecific (Ref. 48636).  Inhabit both coral rich (Ref. 58652) and open pavement areas of shallow reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 5213), as well as drop-offs, behaving differently in various areas (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles found in coral rubble areas of reef flats and lagoons (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles and individuals in the initial phase form large groups that migrate great distances between feeding and sleeping grounds (Ref. 9710).  Feed on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth range reported taken from Ref. 30874.  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Perroquet mauve
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found on exposed outer lagoon and seaward reefs, usually in rich coral habitats.  Generally solitary. Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).  In Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Perroquet moiré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral and rocky reefs and grass bed areas to depths of about 30 m (Ref. 9710).  Occurs singly or in small groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on marine angiosperms and epiphytic algae.  Caught mainly with traps, nets and other types of artisanal gear.

species.name: Perroquet mâchoiron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in groups on the outer reef (Ref. 30573).  Caught with nets, and other types of artisanal gears.

species.name: Perroquet noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from rocky coastal reefs to seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Often in schools, feeding with surgeonfishes by scraping off algae from rocks or dead coral (Ref. 9710).  Marketed fresh and salted (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Perroquet océan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in large groups (Ref. 90102).  Adults usually seen along the reef margin of seaward reefs while juveniles and subadults are found in shallow protected reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 26993).  Occurs to a depth of over 50 m (Ref. 1602).  Adults and subadults form groups, juveniles usually solitary (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Perroquet pourpre-marron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water, often over sand or weed bottoms with coral heads (Ref. 9710).  Found in pairs or small groups (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet princesse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on bottoms with coral or rock (Ref. 13628). Juveniles often occur in association with Thalassia. Forms large feeding aggregations and feeds on plants. Sleeps in a mucus cocoon (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Perroquet périco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and adjacent habitats.  Feeds on algae scraped from rocks or dead coral.  Sleeps in a mucus cocoon (Ref. 9710).  Often seen in groups of one super male with several young adults, most of which are probably females (Ref. 26938).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Perroquet rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shallow, clear waters, generally over Thalassia beds (Ref. 13628). Also found rocky or coral areas (Ref. 13628). A schooling species. Feeds on plants. A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367). Super males spawn individually with striped females, while sexually mature males in the striped phase spawn in aggregation.

species.name: Perroquet rayé (Scarus schlegeli)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs from 1 to over 50 m depth.  Adults are common in areas with rich coral and high vertical relief (Ref. 9710, 48636).  A solitary species (Ref. 90102).  Juveniles may school with other species.  Form feeding aggregations on rubble and mixed rubble-coral slopes rather than on flats.  Females often in schools of mixed species when feeding, males usually seen separate (Ref. 48636). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972). Males exhibit territorial tendencies.

species.name: Perroquet ronille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected coral slopes (Ref. 9710).  Individuals in the terminal phase form harems (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).

species.name: Perroquet tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs, young usually in adjacent seagrass beds.  Often rests on the bottom (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on plants.  Solitary or in small groups.  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Perroquet tatoué
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often seen in small schools on exposed reef flats and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 90102. Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Perroquet tricolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs, in areas with dense coral growth (Ref. 9710) up to at least 30 m.  Usually solitary, sometimes in groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).

species.name: Perroquet tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).  Uncommon (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet tête ronde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary (Ref. 90102) in shallow reefs, on flats and reef fronts or rocky shores of high islands (Ref. 9710); also on mixed algae rubble and rich coral patches (Ref. 48636). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 30573). Caught with nets and other kinds of artisanal gear. Sold mostly fresh in markets (Ref. 3488). Close relative of S. spinus of the Pacific but has allopatric distribution (except Bali) (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Perroquet vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs and adjacent habitats, the young especially in seagrass beds.  Juveniles or primary-phase adults rapidly assume a mottled pattern with which they blend with the substratum when they come to rest on the bottom.  Feeds on benthic algae and seagrasses.

species.name: Perroquet à bandes rouges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).  Solitary and wary species (Ref. 9710).  Caught with nets and other kinds of artisanal gear.  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Perroquet à cinq selles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow lagoon reefs, in areas with dense coral cover (Ref. 9710).  Individuals in the initial phase form groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on algae by incessant grazing in coral reefs (Ref. 5503).  Marked sexual dimorphism.

species.name: Perroquet à joue pâle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward coral (Ref. 58652) and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710); inner reefs with rich coral habitat (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 3488).  May occur in small groups of 1 TP with 1 to 3 IPs  (Ref. 9793). Caught mainly with traps, nets and other types of artisanal gear.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet à lèvre bleue
species.description: Inhabits seagrass beds and weedy areas with sand (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on seagrasses (Ref. 9710).  Buries in the sand to sleep in a mucus tube (Ref. 9710).  Protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Perroquet à museau rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty coastal and offshore areas to 20 m deep (Ref. 90102).   Inhabits rocky and coral reefs from tidal pools to at least 10 m deep.  Form schools with 30 to 40 individuals.  Grazes on benthic algae and corals (Ref. 2935).  Reproductively active terminal males become bicolored (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Perroquet à points rouges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic grazer of algae (Ref. 3488).  Caught with nets and other types of artisanal gear.

species.name: Perroquet à six bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on exposed outer reefs, sometimes in very shallow water (Ref. 2334).  Juveniles occur among coral and rubble of lagoon reefs.  Grazes on benthic algae (Ref. 30573).  Generally solitary (Ref. 1602).  Often in schools of mixed species when feeding (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Perroquet éclipse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal reefs (Ref. 9710) and outer reef slopes at depths of 6-15 m (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on algae by grazing on sand or coral rubble (Ref. 9710).  Wary and usually found singly (Ref. 9710).  Often seen in markets.

species.name: Perroquet émeraude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 52834.  Inhabits seagrass beds and open bottom, mostly in shallow water.  Larger adults live in deeper water.  Not commonly marketed for food (Ref. 52834).

species.name: Persara gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic. Feeds by filtering plankton (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Persian cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Persian carpet sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Persian chub
species.description: Max. length (Hamid Reza Esmaeili, pers. comm., 2004).

species.name: Persian dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Persian mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow coastal waters (Ref. 13710).  Feed on detritus, minute benthic invertebrates and algae (Also Ref. 13710).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Persimmon eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in dead bottom-drifting kelp or eelgrass that accumulates in submarine canyons and deep basins.  Usually found at less than 210 m depth.  Feeds mainly on amphipod crustaceans (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Perth herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in estuaries; also found in coastal embayments.  A filter-feeder.  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 33617).  Used mainly for bait in the rock lobster fishery in Western Australia (Ref. 33617).

species.name: Perugia's limia
species.description: Found in streams.

species.name: Perulibatrachus aquilonarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Perulibatrachus kilburni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral rubble and sandstone bottom.

species.name: Peruvian chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs; no information on depth range available (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Peruvian eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Depth range assumed based on other members of the group (RF).

species.name: Peruvian eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish tidal rivers and fresh water.  Found in muddy burrows.

species.name: Peruvian grunt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in open water above rocky, boulder strewn reefs and slopes and hard substrate with good water movement (Ref. 5227).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and floating organic matter (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Peruvian hake
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the shallow continental shelf to the upper continental slope (Ref. 1371).  Sometimes found off the bottom or in midwater (Ref. 1371).  Marketed fresh and frozen and also used for fishmeal (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Peruvian longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 9 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Peruvian skate
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth of 980 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Peruvian stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peruvian tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pervagor marginalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky reefs to depths of 25 m.

species.name: Pervagor randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coral reefs to depths of 10 m or more.

species.name: Peten molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Peter amicuscaridis
species.description: It was observed that only single specimens were found at the entrance of burrows of the axiid shrimp Axiopsis serratifrons; in depths from 7 m to 25 m (P. Wirtz, pers.comm. in Ref. 79573). Stomach contents visible on the radiograph of the holotype show at least 6 snails of different families: one of Sinozona sp. (Scissurellidae), and several which most likely belong to Rissoidae and Limacinidae (Schwabe, pers.comm. In Ref. 79573).

species.name: Peter wirtzi
species.description: Only single specimens were observed at the entrance of burrows of the axiid shrimp, Axiopsis serratifrons; at 16 m depth over coarse sand (Ref. 79573).

species.name: Peter's clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores.  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Peter's goby
species.description: Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Peter's toby
species.description: May be solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Petersius conserialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy river courses and floodplain lakes with bushy shorelines with forested or grassy margins (Ref. 127953).

species.name: Peters’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia atra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sluggish streams (Ref. 58118).

species.name: Pethia aurea
species.description: Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Pethia canius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia dikhuensis
species.description: The type locality had a water depth of 0.5 m, with numerous boulders and rocks. Co-occurring with this species include: Balitora sp., Amblyceps cerinum, Garra sp., Mustura sp., and Lepidocephalichthys sp. (Ref. 129302).

species.name: Pethia expletiforis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia khugae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively faster, clear-water streams (Ref. 58118).

species.name: Pethia longicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flooded temporary pools, riffles and runs with boulders and gravel as substratum with riparian vegetation. Occurs together with other species of <i>Salmostoma, <i>Devario, <i>Danio, <i>Rasbora and <i>Acanthocobitis (Ref. 96889).

species.name: Pethia lutea
species.description: Occurs in riffles and runs with boulders and gravels as substratum.  Encountered only in clear unpolluted river stretches with well oxygenated waters and were not observed in pools and ditches.  Adults are mostly found in association with submerged vegetation.  Occurs together with other fish species of genera <i>Salmostoma, <i>Devario, <i>Dawkinsia, <i>Garra, <i>Puntius, <i>Systomus and <i>Anguilla (Ref. 96472).

species.name: Pethia macrogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A ripe female specimen measuring 4.96 cm SL has eggs in single ovary, with egg size up to 0.6 mm in diameter (Ref. 75627).

species.name: Pethia muvattupuzhaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia nankyweensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia ornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and beels.  This implies that the fish can live both in lotic and lentic environment (Ref. 98590).

species.name: Pethia poiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia pookodensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from 27 specimens (Ref. 78621).

species.name: Pethia rutila
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pethia sanjaymoluri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At Rawet, this species occupied the main river channel beneath riparian vegetation and submerged boulders and silt as substratum. It was found among aquatic vegetation. It co-occurred with the following fishes: Salmostoma boopis (Day 1874), Devario aequipinnatus (McClelland 1839), Rasbora daniconius (Hamilton 1822), Aplocheilus lineatus (Valenciennes 1846), Notopterus notopterus (Pallas 1769), Mastacembelus armatus (Lacépède 1800), Puntius sophore (Hamilton 1822), and Rohtee ogilbii Sykes 1839. At Bhor, it was encountered in ponds and ditches formed by boulders in the main river channel, with no riparian vegetation and with substratum composed of basalt bedrock and silt. It was observed to co-occur with the following fishes: Nemacheilus denisoni (Day 1867), R. daniconius, Garra mullya (Sykes 1839), S. boopis, Lepidocephalichthys thermalis (Valenciennes 1846) and D. aequipinnatus (Ref. 107652).

species.name: Pethia setnai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pethia sharmai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pethia stoliczkana
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Pethia striata
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Formed small groups of three or four individuals in shallow pools beneath dense riparian canopy. Usually found together with other cyprinid species such as <i>Puntius sahyadriensis and <i>Dawkinsia arulius.  A few juveniles were also observed with <i>Pethia setnai in shallow pools (Ref. 104010).
The type locality was a pool-riffle sequence in a small gently flowing clear water stream with a pH of 6.1 and water temperature of 25.5°C. The stream at the type locality has a width of 7 m and a depth of 0.6 m. The run-riffle sequence just below the type locality has a flow velocity of 0.2 m/s. This species was collected in an altitude range between 660-910 m ASL. <i>Ochlandra sp., <i>Ficus sp., and <i>Elaeocarpus tuberculatus dominated the land vegetation, providing 80% shade. The substrate was composed of leaf litter mostly with <i>Lagenandra sp., bamboo leaves, and clay.
