Other fishes commonly found at the type locality included the following:  <i>Devario malabaricus, <i>Salmophasia boopis, <i>Garra mullya, <i>Barilius canarensis, <i>Barbodes wynaadensis, <i>Tor khudree, <i>Dawkinsia arulius, <i>Puntius sahyadriensis, <i>Osteochilus nashii (Cyprinidae), <i>Batasio sharavatiensis (Bagridae), and <i>Nemacheilus denisoni (Nemacheilidae) (Ref. 104010).

species.name: Pethia tiantian
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a small hill stream, about 3 m wide on average,  flowing through low forest,  with grass and shrub along banks and over a varied bottom with rock, gravel and sand (Ref. 54351).

species.name: Pethia yuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petilipinnis grunniens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petit chien bleu
species.description: Found inshore and offshore, on continental and insular shelves and adjacent deep water (Ref. 244).  Common at bays, river mouths and in harbors; avoids sandy beaches and the surf zone, coral reefs and rough bottom, and surface waters (Ref. 244).  Coastal-pelagic, but usually bottom associated at 1-280 m (Ref. 58302).  Sometimes in oceanic waters (Ref. 9997).  Known to make extended seasonal migrations in some parts of its range (Ref. 6871).  Feeds mainly on bony fishes, also small sharks, cephalopods, and shrimps (Ref. 5578), rays and gastropods (Ref. 5213). Youngs feed heavily on crustaceans such as blue crabd and mantis shrimp (Ref. 93252).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Sexual dimorphism is evident in thickness of skin layer of maturing and adult females (Ref. 49562). Females live as long as 21 year; males 15 years (Ref. 27549). Populations are segregated by age.  Young readily kept in aquaria (Ref. 244).  Utilized for human consumption, for leather and oil (Ref. 244).  Marketed fresh, smoked, dried-salted and frozen; fins are valued for soup (Ref. 9987).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).  Records to 300 cm TL uncertain (Ref. 9997).  TL to 300 cm (Ref. 26938).  Angling: an inshore fish and a good light-tackle fighter (Ref. 84357).

species.name: Petit diable
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and oceanic waters (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 30573).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Generally found in schools, leaping out of the water (Ref. 11228). Caught rarely in the tuna gillnet fisheries. Utilized  for its gill filter plates (high value), meat, cartilage and skin (Ref.58048).

species.name: Petit diable de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de raie. Found in- and offshore areas (Ref. 106604). Usually small, although it attains a maximum length of 200 cm.  Lives in groups and swims either close to the bottom or at the surface.  The cephalic horns serve as a funnel to bring food near the mouth.  Its behavior is rather sluggish at the surface; however, they can swim rapidly and make impressive leaps out of the water.  They are actually inoffensive when they are not disturbed or are not wounded.  Feeds on small fish and plankton (Ref. 5377).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 4442).

species.name: Petit dragon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lagoons often among algal or seagrass beds (Ref. 5503).  Found on sand or silt bottoms, frequently in bays or estuaries (Ref. 3132).  They are opportunistic feeders that collect mainly epifaunal and interstitial invertebrate prey, e.g., crustaceans and worms from the sediment-water interface (Ref. 31134).  Shed their skin in one piece with a rapid jump periodically to rid themselves of accumulated ballast (Ref. 31134).  Adults usually in pairs on muddy substrates (Ref. 48635). Has a monogamous mating system with close-pair bonding (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Petit nègre
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly carnivorous (Ref. 13810).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Petit poisson chien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet streams, sloughs, swamps and other wetlands over sand, mud and debris, often among dense vegetation.  Juveniles also found among aquatic vegetation, often forming schools of 10-12 individuals (Ref. 39069).  An introduced species in Europe which usually occurs in small isolated ponds and peat bogs (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, larvae remain in algal nest for about 6 days (Ref. 39067).  Spawning takes place in April and May (Ref. 30578).  Feeds on insect larvae, worms, mollusks, crustaceans alevins.  Experimental studies show that this species can tolerate acidic environment, particularly, at ph values ranging from 4.0 to 7.0 where no mortality or significant changes in blood plasma osmolarity and haematocrit was observed (Ref. 59260).

species.name: Petit poisson-crocodile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand and mud (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Petit porc-épic
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow reefs to open, soft bottoms. Also in areas with rocky substrata. Sometimes form groups (Ref. 9710, 48637). Occur on open muddy substrates as well as on rich soft-bottom and coral reefs. Juveniles often with floating Sargassum rafts. Young and sub-adults may form small groups (Ref. 48637). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Juveniles pelagic to about 6-9 cm. Solitary. Feed on mollusks, sea urchins, hermit crabs, and crabs at night (Ref. 9680). Relatively poor swimmers (Ref. 9710). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Captured at the surface using a hand net (Ref. 26165).

species.name: Petit sar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious.  Inhabits the upper portion of the continental shelf from the coastline to 100 m depth, but especially from 30 to 50 m.  Occurs on various types of bottom.  Sometimes forms sizeable aggregations.  Feeds on small benthic mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 4781).  Important food fish. Minimum depth range from Ref. 113561.

species.name: Petit sigan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coral reef flats.  Found in rivers (Ref. 12792, 48637).  Occurs in small schools (usually less than 10 individuals).  Juveniles gather in larger numbers in corals with algae-grown at their bases (Ref. 48637).  Initially, they browse on fine textured, e.g. filamentous algae, switching to coarser algae with increasing size.  Both adults and juveniles are diurnal feeders (Ref. 4666).  Fry are marketed fresh, pickled in brine or made into fish paste (Ref. 9813).  Can inflict painful stings (Ref. 4690).

species.name: Petit squale-chagrin
species.description: A common deepwater dogfish of the outer continental shelves and upper slopes, on or near the bottom.  Adults feed on bony fishes and squid.  Males mature by 80 cm TL (Ref. 94782).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized dried salted for human consumption and probably for fishmeal and liver oil (Ref. 247).

species.name: Petit sébaste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky bottoms, close to the shore, between 10 and 150 m, but also recorded at 760 m (Ref. 4570).  Live in shoals and moves closer to the shore in the summer (Ref. 35388).  Feed on various small crustaceans and young fishes (Ref. 4570).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Petit wiwa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found around exposed seaward reefs of isolated high islands such as the northernmost Mariana and Bonin Is. Feeds on Sargassum and Turbinaria algae. Valued as a food fish, but not in Hawaii (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Petit-bec
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear to turbid vegetated lakes, swamps, oxbows, sluggish streams of all sizes (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on insect larvae, filamentous algae and microcrustacea (Ref. 10294).  Spawning occurs underneath flat rocks, in cavities; nest spawner (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Petite anguille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum reported total length 388 mm (Ref. 81678).

species.name: Petite anguille (Mastacembelus niger)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow  waters (Ref. 6060). Maximum reported total length 387 mm (Ref. 81678).

species.name: Petite lamproie de ruisseau
species.description: Lamproies américaines non parasitaires de la famille des petromyzontidae. Freshwater, in streams and lakes (Ref. 89241). Inhabit clean, clear gravel riffles and runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 3814).  In Delaware, occurs in small streams with relatively slow current, usually 0.03 m/s or less, with water temperatures throughout the year 4.0-19.0 °C, dissolved oxygen 5.6-14.0 ppm, and pH 6.0-7.3. In Kentucky, occurs in small to medium size, clear creeks with sand-gravel substrate, either among debris (adults) or in mud banks with silt deposits (ammocoetes) (Ref. 89241). Ammocoete larvae occur in spring-fed wetlands and quiet pools and backwaters of small, sandy or muddy bottom streams (Ref. 3814).  Larval period varies from 2.5 to at least 5.4 yrs. Metamorphosis in early September and maybe even mid- to late August. In Maryland, metamorphosis has been reported as late as February  (Ref. 89241). Adults enter riffle areas to spawn at 10-16°C water temperature (Ref. 10294).  Non-parasitic (Ref. 3814). Fecundity, 572-3,816 eggs/female and relative fecundity, 373-687 eggs/g body weight. Egg diameter, 0.66-1.36 mm. In Delaware, spawning occurs at the end of March at a water temperature of 13.8 °C, dissolved oxygen 11.6 ppm, and pH 6.6. In Maryland, spawning occurs from 10 April to 10 May when the water reaches 16 °C. Both sexes participate in nest building. Stones up to 2.5 cm in diameter are moved using their oral disc. Nests are circular or oval, 15-2 cm in diameter and about 7 cm deep. They are built in streams 4.5-.3 m wide and 15-1 cm deep with a substrate of sand and fine gravel. From 2-5 lampreys share a nest. Up to two males will spawn with one female. Average size at hatching, 3.4 mm TL. Modal length at age 1 is 27-8 mm TL and at age 2 is 50 mm TL. Most growth occurs during the spring season, intermediate growth in summer and fall and very little during winter. In Kentucky, mean length at age 1 is 39 mm TL, at age 2 is 65 mm TL, and at age 3 is 89 mm TL (Ref. 89241).

species.name: Petite limace de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from intertidal to 30 m, often under stones or clinging to algae.  Feeds primarily on crustaceans; gammarid amphipods in intertidal; shrimps and small crabs in subtidal areas.  Spawns in winter; young are also found in the Wadden sea (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Petite mancopsette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported in Ref. 5105 is 240m.

species.name: Petite poule de mer arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud, gravel or stone bottoms at temperatures below 0° C (Ref. 4701).  Young occur in shallower water (Ref. 4701).  Benthic; feed on crustaceans and oikopleura (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Petite poule de mer atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stony bottoms (Ref. 4701).  Benthic species.  Feeds on crustaceans, oikopleura and fishes (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Petite poule de mer douce
species.description: Benthic; feeds on worms, crustaceans and molluscs (Ref. 58426).  Also Ref. 12204.

species.name: Petite rascasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rocky littoral habitats.  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4570).  Flesh is tasty and used in making 'bouillabaisse' (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Petite rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore in reef areas (Ref. 7300).  Commonly found among weeds in tide pools (Ref. 4329).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Petite sole jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Demersal on sandy bottoms of continental shelf and slope.  Feeds on a wide range of bottom-living organisms, mainly crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, cumaceans), bivalve mollusks, and polychaetes (Ref. 3397).

species.name: Petite vive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Littoral and benthic, on sandy, muddy or gravelly bottoms, from a few meters to about 150 m (in winter).  Rest on the bottom, often buried with eyes and tip of first dorsal fin exposed.  Considered as the most dangerous of the European weevers, both for its poison and for its frequent occurrence very near to beaches (Ref. 4675). There are venom glands on the first dorsal fin, which is totally black, and on the gill cover (Ref. 6790).  Also Ref. 57406.

species.name: Petrocephalus ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. bane and P. sauvagii.

species.name: Petrocephalus arnegardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus balayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus bane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open water and vegetated areas of lakes, lagoons and irrigation canals; females grow larger and are more frequently caught than males (Sudan); chiefly insectivorous, feeding on the bottom and in vegetation (Ref. 28714). Affinities: P. ansorgii, differ only by the small eyes, the thick caudal peduncle, numerous teeth on lower jaw and the uniform silvery color (P. ansorgii has a spot on the dorsal fin).

species.name: Petrocephalus binotatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus boboto
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus bovei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. pellegrini. Generates electric organ discharge (EOD) of short duration that seems to correlate with aggregative behavior of the species (Ref. 14060; 10601). EOD temporal pattern cues have been shown to play a role in species recognition for P. bovei (Ref. 10600). A ratio measure between olfactory and visual receptor areas suggests that this species relies more on visual than olfactory information (Ref. 10839). A fractional spawner (Ref. 10605; 10606).

species.name: Petrocephalus christyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus cunganus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus degeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms shoals and frequents sandy or gravelly bottoms on lake shore; feeds on algae, plankton and small underwater insects (Ref. 36900).

species.name: Petrocephalus frieli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus gliroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus grandoculis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus haullevillii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus hutereaui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus keatingii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus leo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus levequei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: appearance close to P. tenuicauda; difference in number of soft rays.

species.name: Petrocephalus longianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type locality (Lufubu River) is a braided rocky channel with dense riparian forest; water flow rapid, but also deep pools providing slacker flow areas; substrate is rocky but with considerable amounts of leaf litter; some sections with mats of aquatic water ferns and mosses and filamentous algae (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus longicapitis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to prefer quiet reaches of oxbow lakes or arms with dense vegetation on borders; where it occurs in the main river channel, sand and gravel substrate mainly with occasional rocky rapids; during the day associated with marginal cover in holes in banks, root stocks and aquatic weed beds (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus magnitrunci
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a shallow floodplain lagoon; substrate is mud; vegetation is dense emergent grasses and water lilies (Nymphea sp.); water depth up to 2 m; lagoon flooded during winter flood cycle and dry during the low water period (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus magnoculis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rather strong currents; dicotyledonous trees, extensive reed beds and semiaquatic bushes dominate the river banks, which are rocky or sandy depending on the inside or outside bank (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus mbossou
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus microphthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus odzalaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus okavangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hardy and eurytopic species, common in both swamp and river (Ref. 79613). Collected under papyrus root stocks in the Guma Lagoon (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus pallidomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. bovei.

species.name: Petrocephalus pellegrini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: can be mistaken for P. bovei, only difference is its small eye and shorter anal fin base.

species.name: Petrocephalus petersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat of type locality is a medium-sized stream, sand substrate with lots of leaf litter and marginal grass; prefers freshwater (<1% salinity) (Ref. 91771).

species.name: Petrocephalus pulsivertens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The EOD waveform of Petrocephalus pulsivertens resembles an inverted-polarity version of the 'typical' Petrocephalus EOD (Ref. 85331).

species.name: Petrocephalus sauvagii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: Same color as P. soudanensis, but distinguished by mouth position, number of teeth and eye size; same morphology as P. bane and P. ansorgii (Ref. 2915).

species.name: Petrocephalus schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus soudanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. sauvagii.

species.name: Petrocephalus squalostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus steindachneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus stuhlmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus sullivani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus tenuicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. levequei.

species.name: Petrocephalus valentini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrocephalus zakoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrochromis ephippium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the shallow precipituous rocky habitat, which is characterized by rocks piled on top of each other forming a complicated network of caves and crevices (Ref. 46829). Herbivore; feeds on algae which are scraped from rocks Ref. 6770, 46829). Maternal mouthbrooder; males strongly territorial (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Petrochromis famula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary adults are usually found over rocks.  Feed by scraping rock biocover (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Petrochromis fasciolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found over rock, either solitary or in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Feed by scraping rock biocover (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Petrochromis horii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on rocks (Ref. 95531).

species.name: Petrochromis macrognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic species between rocks near shore (Ref. 35773). Occurs in the upper 2-3 m of the water column (Ref. 7343, 46829, 52921). Feeds by scraping loose algae from the vertical faces of boulders in turbulent water (Ref. 6770, 46829). In order to cope with the movement of the surge its feeding speed is fast; very shy species; males are territorial and hide in large caves when threatened (Ref. 46829). Often solitary but more than 2 individuals may be seen at once (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Petrochromis orthognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found over rocks, either solitary or in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Feed by scraping rock biocover (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Petrochromis polyodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in small communities.  Usually found over rocks either solitary or in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Feed by scraping rock biocover (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 7248, 86760).

species.name: Petroscirtes marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Petroscirtes springeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Petrotilapia chrysos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Scrapes algae from the rock over which it lives.  Found foraging in the water column presumably on both phytoplankton and zooplankton.

species.name: Petrotilapia flaviventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrotilapia genalutea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky habitats.  Feeds by using the teeth to comb loose algae from the substrate (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Petrotilapia microgalana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Petrotilapia species have broad, fleshy lips with numerous slender teeth that are used to comb the algae on rocks for diatoms and loose algal strands (Ref. 6256, 87181). Adult Petrotilapia males establish territories; females, juveniles, and non-territorial males are found either singly or in schools throughout the rocky habitat (Ref. 6256). Petrotilapia microgalana males patrol territories at an average depth of 10-15 m; females are usually encountered in the upper region (Ref. 79521). It inhabits the deeper rocky environments of Lake Malawi (Ref. 87181).

species.name: Petrotilapia mumboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrotilapia nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky habitats.  Feeds from the sediment-free biocover on miniscule diatoms that use the algal strands as substrate.  In deeper waters, this species feeds from the vertical faces of rocks (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Petrotilapia palingnathos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Normally found in the shallow but not wave-washed habitat (Ref. 87181).

species.name: Petrotilapia pyroscelos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petrotilapia tridentiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits very shallow, rocky biotopes.  Feeds by using the tricuspid teeth and large mouth to feed from the sediment-free biocover (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Petrotilapia xanthos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Petulanos intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Petulanos plicatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Petulanos spiloclistron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Petén tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pez demonio
species.description: Found mostly in the mesopelagic area (Ref. 35904).  Possibly undergoes vertical migration (Ref. 35904).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35904).

species.name: Pfaff's lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers, brooks, swamps and shallow parts of larger bodies of water (Ref. 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Phago boulengeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Phago intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Phalacronotus apogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large rivers with turbid waters (Ref. 27732), streams, canals (Ref. 12693) and lakes (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on pelagic fishes in midwater to upper depths (Ref. 12693).  Spawns just prior to the rise in water levels and moves into the flooded riparian forests and probably out into the floodplains during high water levels.  Young of the year are first seen in July and start to move back to the rivers in October, where they remain common until January (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Phalacronotus bleekeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, streams and lakes as well as in impoundments (Ref. 12693).  A migratory species (Ref. 37772).  Undertakes lateral migrations from the Mekong River into smaller tributaries and into the floodplains at the start of the flood season, returning back to the main river channel when the water begins to recede at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770).  Migrations are triggered by the first rainfall at the end of the dry season, as well as water level changes.  Lunar cycle affects also the movements.  Returns to the river from the floodplain and tributaries on, or immediately before, the full moon (Ref. 37770).  Feeds on small fishes, shrimps and aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 6459).

species.name: Phalacronotus micronemus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, streams, and lakes as well as in impoundments.  Feeds on pelagic fishes and shrimps.  Sold fresh or smoked on a skewer (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Phalacronotus parvanalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Phallic blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand-weed areas.  Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Phallobrycon adenacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the main channel of rivers with fast flowing and rather shallow clear waters, with abundance of rocks and thick sand (Ref. 81937).

species.name: Phalloceros aspilos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Phallostethus cuulong

species.name: Phantom goby

species.name: Phantom shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the main channel of Rio Grande, usually over sand and often in turbid water (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Pharaoh’s moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usual habitats of this fish are crevices and shelters of fringing seaward reefs, and  may be seen out of shelter at night only.  Female specimens as small as 22.3 cm were found with large eggs. Males appear to mature at larger sizes than females (Ref. 121606).

species.name: Pharaon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epimesopelagic species. Juveniles and fry observed exclusively within the central-circle current and its periphery; large adults caught mainly in boreal and sub-arctic waters. Feeds mainly on small and moderate-sized mesopelagic fishes; the largest Paralepis coregonoides and Arctozenus risso, had body length of 28-30 cm; a specimen caught from the southern region of Reykjanes Ridge had 12 individuals of Sebastes mentella ranging from 4.5-5 cm. Stomachs of those caught in the Mid-Atlantic Ridge have small squids (Ref. 31260).

Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Pherallodichthys meshimaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often inhabit intertidal or subtidal reefs (Ref. 47249).  Fish-egg eaters (Ref. 54616).  Most species  reported to feed on zooplankton or benthic animals (Ref. 28114).  May change its feeding habits when growing to an obligate fish-egg eater targeting demersal egg spawners (Ref. 54616).

species.name: Philippiines spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on or near the bottom of upper continental and insular slopes.  Viviparous with yolk-sac dependency; gives birth to 4-16 pups, gestation unknown.  Feeds mainly on small fishes, cephalopods, and crustaceans.  Usually caught by demersal longline fisheries operating in deepwater.  Marketed for its meat, fins, and liver oil which has a high value (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Philippine anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling, although the three type (and only known) specimens were caught after 20 months of sampling.  Evidently rare.

species.name: Philippine cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes occurs in schools of Rhabdamia gracilis (Ref. 1602). Rarely noticed because of small size (Ref. 48635). Occasionally collected with ichthyocides (Ref 90102).

species.name: Philippine catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lowland streams (Ref. 57235), swamps, ponds, ditches, rice paddies, and pools left in low spots after rivers have been in flood (Ref. 2854, 57235).  Usually confined to stagnant, muddy water (Ref. 1479).  Found in medium to large-sized rivers, flooded fields and stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals (Ref. 12975).  Undertake lateral migrations from the Mekong mainstream, or other permanent water bodies, to flooded areas during the flood season and returns to the permanent water bodies at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770).  Can live out of water for quite sometime and move short distances over land (Ref. 4833).  Can walk and leave the water to migrate to other water bodies using its auxiliary breathing organs.  The Lao use this fish as lap pa or ponne pa.  Feed on insect larvae, earthworms, shells, shrimps, small fish, aquatic plants and debris (Ref. 6459).  An important food fish (Ref. 4833) that is marketed live, fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Recently rare, being replaced by introduced African walking catfish (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Philippine chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare and limited to the upper slope.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).  Biology and utilization unknown in the area (Ref. 9904).

species.name: Philippine dark velvetchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The habitat is likely to be dominated by a muddy rocky bottom (Ref. 76777).

species.name: Philippine darkthroat dragonet
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Philippine dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower reaches of rivers and sheltered reefs (Ref. 37816).  Found in small groups on silty reefs to about 10 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Philippine guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males mature at ca. 56 cm TL, females slightly larger. Unknown life history (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Philippine luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bioluminescent.

species.name: Philippine slender flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from one depth of 197 m.  Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Philippine snubnose halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species (Ref. 9843), characterized by a sandy bottom with patchy seagrass beds and was collected in Indonesia together with the silverbiddy (Gerres sp.) and silverside (Atherinomorus sp.) (Ref. 126046).

species.name: Philippines chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit seaward reef slopes (Ref. 9710), with caves and large crevices.  Congregated in groups in caves when not feeding on plankton away from the reefs.  Often see well away from shelter and in spread-out schools (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Philippines dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and shallow reef areas in 0.1-1.5 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Philippines dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal sand-flats (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Philippines moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Philippines viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabitant of reef crevices, cryptic and solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Philippines worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic species, inhabits sandy substrates (Ref 90102).

species.name: Philippines wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in coastal sand and rubble reef, usually flat substrate with remote coral bommies in current zones.  Mixes with various other fishes in open water to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Phillips's garra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky areas of hill streams, almost always in fast-flowing water. More common in deeper and more heavily shaded areas of clear-water streams. Occurs sympatrically with G. ceylonensis in its limited range. Feeds essentially on algae in captivity. This species is easy to maintain in aquarium.

species.name: Philypnodon macrostomus

species.name: Phoenix devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found exclusively in surge zone of seaward reef margins (Ref. 9710). They occur in or near Acropora or Pocillopora coral patches (Ref. 1602). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). A solitary territorial herbivore (Ref. 1602). Feeds on benthis algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Pholidapus dybowskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seaweed beds near shore (Ref. 43239).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow rocky runs and riffles of clear rivers, at an altitude of 900-1200 m above sea level, and depths from 0.2 to 0.4 m (Ref. 52116, 52193). It feeds on invertebrates such as mayfly nymphs and caddis fly, blackfly or midge larvae grazed from rocks (Ref. 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Breeds in summer (Ref. 7248, 52193). Distribution in southern Africa is restricted and may be threatened by alteration of its habitat (Ref. 52116), by water extraction, river regulation and sedimentation (Ref. 52193).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in lowland water bodies, with little current (Ref. 26100).  Inhabit streams with clear water and enter subterranean karstic waters during winter or droughts.  Spawn in shallower parts of streams where females probably lay 2-3 portions of eggs.  Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and introduction of exotic species;  limited data suggest that its decline in the last 10 years is likely to continue due to water abstraction and introductions of exotic species (Ref. 59043).

Occurs in association with salmonid fishes or cyprinids of barbel zone.  Feeds on invertebrates, algae and detritus.  Spawns in shoals over clean gravel bottom in flowing water (Ref. 59043).

The water in the wells is used locally for human consumption.  This fish is often mistaken for parasitic leeches  " sanguijuelas" due to its bright, blood-red color  and vermiform shape. For this reason, this is killed upon incidental capture when extracting drinking water from wells.

species.name: Phycis du Golfe

species.name: Phycis tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found onshore, most common between 110 and 185 m.  Feed on crustaceans, and possibly fish and squids.  Juveniles spend part of their time in estuaries.

species.name: Phycocharax rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected mainly in dammed portions of the rio Braço Norte where it can be considered highly abundant. Appears to be uncommon in the lotic stretch of rio Braço Norte downstream of the dam, where only three specimens were collected. At the type locality (the igarapé do Arnaldo, a small tributary which was flooded during the damming of river), this species was the most abundant comprising 77% of all specimens collected. Found syntopic at Braço Norte reservoir with other species of Characiformes such as Cyphocharax cf. spilurus (Curimatidae), Leporinus friderici (Anostomidae), Serrapinus aff. micropterus, Astyanax aff. bimaculatus (Characidae), Hoplerythrinus unitaeniatus (Erythrinidae), Gymnotiformes like Gymnotus diamantinensis (Gymnotidae), and Cichliformes, i.e., Aequidens sp. and Apistogramma sp. (Cichlidae). Co-occurs with the following Characiformes: Leporinus desmotes (Anostomidae), Hemiodus quadrimaculatus (Hemiodontidae), Astyanax aff. bimaculatus , Bryconops sp., Jupiaba polylepis , Jupiaba paranatinga , Moenkhausia hasemani , Serrapinnus aff. micropterus (Characidae); and with a single species of Siluriformes, Hypostomus sp. (Loricariidae). Males and females have well-developed gonads during rainy and dry seasons. Oocytes in varied sizes were present in the gonads, suggesting multiple spawning of females. Feeds on algae and vegetal matter (Ref. 116744).

A 9.6-cm specimen appears to be a sexually mature, where the right ovary, about 26 mm long (27.1%SL), contains approximately 130,000 eggs (count based on extrapolation from wet weight) each about 0.3 mm in diameter (Ref. 53300).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a small tributary, about 2 m wide and 30 cm deep at the sampling site, running into the Nangunhe River. Not encountered in the mainstem of the Nangunhe River. Co-occurred with two nemacheilids, Schistura cryptofasciata and S. disparizona, both were found in the mainstem (Ref. 116525).

species.name: Physoschistura chulabhornae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a stream with mixed sand, gravel, pebble, silt, mud and rock bottom, and with clear running water, elevation is 764 m above mean sea level, and with annual rainfall over 1450 mm. Surrounding landscape has semi-evergreen forest, plantations, and agricultural crops (mainly corn, cabbage and tomato). Water temperature was 17°C, air temperature 20.5°C, pH 7.7, DO 6.5 mg/l, and conductivity 20 μS. Averaged stream width 4 meters, and water depth 40-60 cm. Specimens were collected during the daylight by electro-fishing. Other species collected at the type locality were Schistura breviceps, Schistura maejotigrina, Oreoglanis siamensis, Scaphiodonichthys burmanicus, Opsarius pulchellus, Garra cambodgiensis, Puntius brevis, Puntius stoliczkanus, Monopterus albus, Channa gachua and Devario sp. A 3.0 cm SL female (MARNM 3999/14) contained 260 large eggs (0.6 mm diameter) (Ref. 94424).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from 15-170 m but up to depth of 328 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504). Inhabit Posidonia beds and muddy bottoms. Occur in schools except during breeding (Ref. 7081).

species.name: Picarel guetteur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic.  Found over rocks or gravelly bottoms (Ref. 7349).  To depth of 200 m (Ref. 7349) and from 327-464 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Breeding stock approach the coast in summer (Ref. 6518).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 6518).

species.name: Picarel queue noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over the continental shelf (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Picarel à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic (Ref. 7349).

species.name: Picasso noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in shallow outer reefs subject to surge (Ref. 9770, 48637).  Commonly found over barren rock or the spur-and-groove zone where there is a mixture of bare rock, rubble, and coral.  Juveniles on algae reef (Ref. 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on algae, detritus, mollusks, crustaceans, worms, echinoderms, fishes, sponges, foraminiferans, and eggs.  Territorial.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Also taken by drive-in nets (Ref. 9770).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Picasso triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy and rubble areas of coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles are commonly found on reef flats (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 30573).  Caught with artisanal gear, mainly pots (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Picot renard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sometimes territorial, occurs in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs. Often among staghorn corals (Ref. 90102). Usually occurs singly or in pairs, but juveniles and subadults occasionally occur in large schools among Acropora where they feed on algae growing on the dead bases of the coral branches. Capable of inflicting painful stings (Ref. 4690, 48637).

species.name: Picot à lignes bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of lagoons and seaward reefs. Juveniles form schools. Pairs form at 7 cm; but these pairs continue to form loose schools, sometimes with juvenile scarids, to feed in areas being flooded by the tide. At 20 cm, isolated pairs in deep water lagoons or on drop-offs at reef-edges feed on benthic seaweeds (Ref. 9813, 48637). Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Very closely related to the blue-spotted S. virgatus (Valenciennes) and apparently hybridizes at times with it in the Indo-Malayan region (Ref. 2334). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Picot à lignes bleues (Siganus puellus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, coral-rich areas of clear lagoons and seaward reefs. Individuals up to 7 cm SL forms large schools in shallows, lagoons and outer reef flats, particularly in areas dominated by luxurious growths of Acropora. Adults occur in pairs. Juveniles feed on filamentous algae, adults on algae, tunicates, and sponges (Ref. 9813, 48637). Can inflict painful stings (Ref. 4690).

species.name: Picot à taches oranges
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear lagoons and seaward reefs.  Juveniles live in schools of up to about 50 fish with pairing commencing as small as 15 cm, but fish may still be schooling at 22 cm SL; older fish live in pairs.  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 9813).  Adults on deep coastal reefs, juveniles in shallow estuaries (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Picotee goodeid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Picotee livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lushly vegetated sections, slowly flowing and standing marshy peripheral  areas of rivers.

species.name: Picturesque dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms of shallow sheltered reefs (Ref. 9710).  Secretive in rubble below living coral (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Forms small loose groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pictus cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  not recommended for home aquariums; minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539). Average life span in captivity is said to be 4-8 yrs (https://aquaticmag.com/freshwater/fish/pictus-catfish-information/). In one case, this catfish lasted 18 yrs (1999-2017) in an aquarium (Roel Hurkens <rhurkens@gmail.com>, Pers. Comm.).

species.name: Piebald horseface loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Piebald madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainstream rivers of small to medium size and the lower reaches of their major tributaries (Ref. 55397). Most commonly associated with moderate velocities, moderate depth (about 60 cm), clean sand or clay substrata and cover in the form of leaf packs, brush and log jams (Ref. 55397).

species.name: Piebald sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Piedmont darter

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered coastal reefs, usually forming small aggregations (Ref. 48637).  Also found in mud and sand bottoms of trawling grounds (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Pig-nosed pony-fish
species.description: Found in estuaries (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Piglet sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal pebble beaches, where it might be found even above the waterline during low tide, and rarely occurs in fields of larger boulders (Ref. 123696).

species.name: Pigmouth carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers, channels and culture ponds (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pigmy leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries, coastal reefs and offshore islands (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Pigmy scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with rubble or mixed sand and rubble, within or near coral reefs (Ref. 48236, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 89972). Venomous spines (Ref. 1602). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Pigmy smelt
species.description: Lives in small, deep, thermally stratified lakes. When this species occurs with Osmerus mordax, it usually spawns later in the year, feeds on smaller food items, grows more slowly, matures earlier in life, and has a shorter life span.

species.name: Pignosed arrowtooth eel
species.description: Found on the upper continental slope (Ref. 5235), over soft substrate (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pigsnout pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Specimens have been taken from a coral knoll and from reefs.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be mature at about 5-5.5 cm SL.

species.name: Pike asp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers river channels.  Rarely found in lakes.  Feeds on fish.

species.name: Pike characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in black and clear water streams and rivers, as well as lagoons and other off-channel habitats associated with whitewater rivers (Ref. 52916).  Prefers slow currents and a silty or sandy bottom.  Like other species of the genus, it is a formidable predator (Ref. 12225).  Strict piscivore; however, it consumes insects during the dry periods of the year (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Pike cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pike icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed mostly on fishes and krill.

species.name: Pike silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand bottoms (Ref. 26550).

species.name: Pike's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pikehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams and flooded forest among dense vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Found in  primary peats swamps.  Mouth brooder (Ref. 57235).  Highly protrusible jaws.  The premaxillae can extend about 1/3 of the head length.  Prey is captured by the fish making a rapid lunge and surrounding the prey with the open mouth.

species.name: Pikehead hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  A schooling species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pilbara eelblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky mud pools (Ref. 42960), in limestone reefs, with Sargassum and mainly sandy or muddy bottoms (very little coral) in less than 1 m depth (Ref. 51685).

species.name: Pile perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky shores, often around kelp, pilings and underwater structures (Ref. 2850).  Feed on hard-shelled mollusks, crabs and barnacles (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pillaia kachinica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate to fast flowing clear water with aquatic vegetation with mud mixed with small stones bottom.

species.name: Pillai’s anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pillar wire eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pillard épineux littoral
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under rocks on the beach or in tide pools, but may also be found deeper (down to 80 m) among kelp and other algae (Ref. 5191).  Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041).

species.name: Pillard épineux profond
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range:  80-180 m (Ref. 5191).  Feed on small crustaceans and common in littoral of all sub-Antarctic islands (Ref. 42041).

species.name: Pillow velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, in soft bottom (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Pilote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species with a semi-obligate commensal relationship with sharks, rays, other bony fishes and turtles (Ref. 5217).  Young are usually associated with jellyfish and drifting seaweed (Ref. 2850, 9563).  Feed on scraps of host's left over, parasites and excrement; also on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 5288).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).  Captured at the surface using hand nets (Ref. 26165).

species.name: Pilote (Remora remora)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually associated with sharks but also attaches itself to other large fishes, sea turtles and even ships (Ref. 2850, 58302); found in gill chambers, fins and body surface (Ref. 5951).  Sometimes free-swimming (Ref. 2850).  Younger individual is more active as parasite pickers (Ref. 26938).  Feeds on parasitic copepods (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Pima hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep pools and quiet backwaters of fast-flowing gravel-bottom river.

species.name: Pima River rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits headwater mountainous streams with an elevation of more than 800 m in a relatively broad (1 km width) valley (Ref. 2847).  An egg laying omnivore which prefers rock, plant and driftwood cover and the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.5, H=10, 26°C water temperature (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Pimelodella geryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to be smaller than P. cristata. P. geryi and P. cristata share the same biotope. Inhabits the high and middle parts of rivers, in zones with more or less fast flowing water and a rocky substrate (rock clusters consisting of pre-Cambrian pebbles, shales). Lies hidden under rocks, letting its barbel out to auscultate the exterior world. Emits growling sounds regularly (alarm signals?) and goes stalk-hunting frequently scouting around its hiding place. The population is organized in a hierarchical structure based on size, with markedly aggressive behavior. The juveniles are found mostly in seasonal little tributaries. Diet changes according to size: small crustaceans, insect larvae and adult, and fish. This slow-growing species can live for more than 10 years in the wild (Ref. 35381).

The notable number of individuals caught during inventory is indicative of its gregarious behavior. In March and April, all females larger than 5.8 cm are mature. Like all Pimelodella living in Guiana, the pectoral and dorsal spines are located with a poisonous mucus that can cause painful injuries (Ref. 35381).

Individuals were observed calmly swimming near the bottom, in the midwater and near the surface.  Elusive fishes and apparently photophobic (Ref. 55501).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. In shallow lagoons.  Feeds on benthic organisms.

species.name: Pimelodus absconditus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large or small rivers, streams and lagoons.  Feeds on larvae of chironomids and ceratopogonids, both larvae and adult terrestrial Coleoptera, ants, mollusks and other fishes.

species.name: Pimelodus albicans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimelodus maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Omnivorous (Ref. 79585).

species.name: Pimelodus microstoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimelodus multicratifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is widepread throughout the rio Ribeira de Iguape drainage, ranging from the altitudes of 3 m above sea level at the rios Pariquera-Açu and Pariquera-Mirim in the lower stretch of the rio Ribeira de Iguape, to 250 m above sea level at the rio Catas Altas in the high stretch of the river basin. It was found mainly in the large rivers like Ribeira de Iguape, Catas Altas, Pariquera-Mirim and Turvo; rivers of the high stretch have clear water running over rocks and sand; rivers of the low stretch have a turbid water, and in some case, acid black water like the rio Momuna, at the sandbank forest near the mouth of the rio Ribeira de Iguape into the sea. At the type locality, this species occurs syntopically with the following species: Cyphocharax santacatarinae, Hoplias malabaricus, Oligosarcus hepsetus, Hoplosternum littorale and Crenicichla iguapina (Ref. 86673).

species.name: Pimelodus mysteriosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimelodus navarroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on other fishes and terrestrial insects that fall into the water (Ref. 26543).  Considered a good food fish (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Pimelodus ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in principal river beds, in upstream parts of rivers, downstream rapids, in backwater zones or on stony bottoms of pools with dead tree trunks.  Active at dusk.  Piscivorous.  Emits loud grumblings (Ref. 35381).  Secretes toxic mucus and the wounds caused by its pectoral spines are very painful.  The female can preserve spermatozoids  by coating them with original maternal secretions and inserting them in the epithelium of its genital tract (Ref. 27188).  The presence of sperm in the mucus of the female's genital tract is indicative of internal fertilization (Ref. 35381).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimple pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs on mixed algae and coral to about 20 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pimpled lumpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimpled snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A partially digested specimen (discarded) was found in the stomach of a Malacocottus zonurus collected from central Aleutian Islands (Ref. 124469).

species.name: Pimélode charu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimélode crapaudin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pimélode manguru
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous (Ref. 79585).

species.name: Pinafore goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools (Ref. 2798).

species.name: Pinda moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on reef flats as well as lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 43 m.  Benthic to 40 m (Ref. 58302, 75154). Cryptic (Ref 90102).Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Pindani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow areas, mostly over sand but territorial males stay close to rocks (Ref. 5595). It feeds from the biocover on the rock and sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pindu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predatory; reported to kleptoparasitize the freshwater crab Potamon africanus (Ref. 81260). Mainly feeds on shrimp and insect larvae; ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder; in aquarium, males have been observed moutbrooding albeit rarely (Ref. 52307)

species.name: Pineapple rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pinecone fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dorsal and pelvic spines robust with a locking mechanism similar to sticklebacks and some catfishes (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Pinewoods darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel riffles and current-swept vegetation in creeks.

species.name: Pinewoods shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs and flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably open substratum spawners like congeners.

species.name: Pinge brésilien
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des pinguipedidae.

species.name: Pinge chilien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. On muddy bottoms or sandy and rocky bottoms.  Spawns during spring.

species.name: Pinge namorade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deeper waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 27569).   Also sandy, rubble and rocky bottoms and shallow rocky reef (Ref. 57919).

species.name: Pinge oriflamme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rubble bottoms near reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on small invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9710).  There is an indication that the species is a protogynous hermaphrodite.

species.name: Pinge pintade
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and rubble bottoms of shallow lagoon and protected seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Also Ref. 58652.

species.name: Pinhead pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Lives within holothurians (e.g. Thelenota ananas and Bohadschia argus) (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Pinjalo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reefs and rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573). They are found in schools over shallow depths of a few meters in open ocean reefs.  In most areas they are found in deep waters and are usually trawled to 100 m depth (Ref. 48635).  They feed on benthic and planktonic invertebrates (Ref. 30573), and possibly small fishes.  Marketed fresh or dried-salted.

species.name: Pinjalo rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often form schools (Ref. 90102).  Inhabit reefs and rocky bottoms.  They feed on benthic and planktonic invertebrates and possibly small fishes.  Marketed fresh or dried-salted.

species.name: Pink anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Mainly diurnal. Non-burrowing. Monogamous (Ref. 52884). A protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32166). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Heteractis magnifica (usually), Heteractis crispa, Macrodactyla doreensis, Stichodactyla gigantea (Ref. 5911). In Bali they occur together with the closely related Indian Ocean species A. akallopison and have even been found sharing the same anemone (Ref. 48636). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413, 35418, 35420).

species.name: Pink blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pink cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays under ledge overhangs and other shaded, reclusive areas on rocky reefs and slopes during the day.  Feeds in the open at night.  Often mingles with other cardinal fish (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Pink corydoras
species.description: Omnivorous.

species.name: Pink flabby whalefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Normal diurnal distribution is between 700 and 1200 m The shallowest diurnal capture (500-600 m) is of one of the smallest specimens (4.3 cm) and the deepest (1500-1600 m) is of one of the largest (20.4 cm), indicating a trend for the diurnal depth to increase with increasing size (Ref. 9791).  Nocturnal distribution is between 110-700 m (Ref. 9791).  Feeds on decapods and euphausiids (Ref. 6715).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pink flasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on bases of steep outer reef slopes, above coral or rubble (Ref. 9710).  Forms schools.  Maximum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Pink frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental shelves and slopes, from approximately 200 m and below (Ref. 10756).  A solitary species (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Pink Handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains at least 99.5 mm SL (ca. 136 mm TL); smallest specimen examined 68.5 mm SL (Ref. 82446).

species.name: Pink happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers deep main river channels and floodplain lagoons (Ref. 7248) with sandy bottoms (Ref. 7248, 52307). Feeds primarily on snails, bivalves and insect larvae (Ref. 7248, 52307), rarely also on fish or plants (Ref. 52307).  Ovophilic (Ref. 52307), female mouthbrooder (Ref. 7248, 52307), breeds in early summer (Ref. 7248). Up to 700 eggs may be laid per female and per brood; males construct shallow, rounded pits approximately 20-30 cm in diameter, preferably in regions containing vegetation (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Pink lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Pink maomao
species.description: Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Benthopelagic and benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on plankton and small nekton.  Occasionally caught on small hooks when fishing in midwater without sinker and make excellent eating (Ref. 30464).  Its abundant gillrakers and stomach contents characterize it as an opportunistic pelagic polyphagic-zooplanktivorous predator (Rojas et al. 1998a, c) (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Pink pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and flats in depths less than 1 m, among the brown alga Cystoseira sp.; has also been trawled at a depth of 45 m. Males mature at about 11.5 cm SL. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). Males carry the eggs in their brood pouches (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pink rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Pink seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons appartenant à l'ordre des perciformes. Adults occur offshore (Ref. 2850).  Usually found in deeper water than other surfperches (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pink snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pink squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in relatively deep waters of outer reef slopes and has been collected on reef flat and lagoon patch reefs.  Feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps at night.  Spine of preopercle venomous.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Pink stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pink wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from muddy littoral and estuarine habitats (Ref. 81289).  Burrows in shallow muddy and sandy bottoms (Ref. 7251).  Postlarvae and early juveniles (to ca 2-2.5 cm SL) may occur in surface plankton to distances of 15 km or more offshore; subadults and adults occasionally found swimming near the surface at night (Ref. 10815).

species.name: pink-banded fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aggregate on coral reefs or rocky or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Pink-belly wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reefs and rocky shores, usually in weedy areas exposed to surge (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Feeds on benthic crustaceans, mollusks, polychaetes, forams, fishes, and fish eggs (Ref. 1602).  One of several similar species that have near identical juvenile and female stages (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Pink-lipped moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters freshwater (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Pink-speckled shrimpgoby
species.description: Found on silty bottoms of coastal reefs and inner reef flats (Ref. 9710).  Inhabits coastal waters, including mangroves, large tidal pools or inner reef lagoons, on sand and rubble substrates (Ref. 48637). Also found in sheltered sand and mud bottoms to 10 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Pinkbreast siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Pinkeye mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often occur in small groups in deep pools where stream flow is slow.  Inhabit deep, gently flowing sections of rivers.  Also occur in estuaries and coastal seas during spawning runs.  Tolerant of temperatures between 9° and 27°C.  Form small shoals (Ref. 44894).  Mainly herbivorous.  Feed on filamentous green algae, microscopic plants and animals as well as detritus.  Also consume benthic invertebrates.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawn in estuaries or at sea following a downstream migration in summer.  Peak spawning activity is in February.  Sexual maturity is reached after 4 years at a length of about 30 centimeters.  Maximum life span is approximately 14 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Pinkfin Alestes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pinkhead frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Pinkrose rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually at around 200 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Pinktail chalceus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is very active and is always moving.  Frequently found in well oxygenated waters (Ref. 12225).  Occurs mainly near the surface and at times jumps out of the water.  Feeds on worms, insect larvae and small fishes (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Pinktail triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in seaward reefs to depths greater than 60 m (Ref. 9710, 48637), with rich invertebrate growth (Ref. 48637).  Common in coral-rich areas exposed to currents (Ref. 1602).  Usually at moderate depths in small loose groups (Ref. 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Diet consists mainly of algae and detritus but also takes in crustaceans, octopuses, sponges, and fishes (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Also taken with drive-in nets.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9770).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Pinkthroat corydoras
species.description: Very abundant. Lives in the upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 35381). Frequently occurs over sandy bottoms traversed by strong currents. Most probably lives in schools as it is often captured in groups (Ref. 27188). Often found with C. approuaguensis and C. cf. brevirostris (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Pinniwallago kanpurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Pinocchio dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in vertical drop-off with caves and sandy and slope with some Halimeda (Ref. 92345).

species.name: Pinpoint lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442); minimum depth of occurrence is 500 m upon reaching about 5 cm length (54657).  Feed on euphausiids (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Pinstripe cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups. Found in caves and ledges on coastal reefs in 3-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Pinstriped basslet
species.description: A secretive, ledge dweller species (Ref. 90102); benthic (Ref. 75154). and found in caves and crevices (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Pinstriped blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pintail fairy-wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with flat or gently sloping bottoms with scattered low outcrops of rock and coral (Ref. 108439).

species.name: Pipe fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur along the bottom in stagnant waters of canals, ditches and swamps.  A sedentary, slowly moving species that spends most of its time resting on the bottom.  Feeds on worms and other slowly moving benthic invertebrates.  Relatively inedible, because of its small size and strong body armor.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near piers and wharves to offshore depths of 62-120 m.  Specimens have been taken over bryozoan and coarse shell bottom; juveniles in surface plankton tows.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 9.95 cm SL.

species.name: Pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One specimen collected on rubble bottom (Ref. 51183).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Piquitinga anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters, but also entering brackish water.  More data needed (Ref. 189).  Found in markets (Ref. 37032).  Largely utilized as bait for commercial fishery, oil, flour, and also canned fish (Ref. 103984).

species.name: Piquitingue du Pacifique
species.description: More data needed.

species.name: Pirambeba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and estuaries.  Feeds on the fins of other fish.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Dies at less than 11°C.  Its reproduction in captivity has been carried out (Ref. 12225).  Although armed with strong, sharp teeth, it is however not dangerous to man.  When captured with fishing nets, it must be released because it attacks the other fish caught in the net (Ref. 27188).  Of the few piranhas which have escaped from aquaria in the USA, only this species was able to establish a breeding population in Dade County, Florida which was eradicated in 1981 (Ref 1739).

species.name: Pirapitinga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles mimic Serrasalmus nattereri. Feeds on insects and decaying plants (Ref. 32894). Possesses powerful dentition that can cause serious bites (Ref. 4537). An important foodfish (Ref. 12202).

species.name: Pirate blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the shoreline to deep rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Pirate perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually occur over mud in swamps, vegetated sloughs, ponds, lakes, backwaters, and quiet pools of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref 5723, 10294).  Nocturnal feeders.  Feed on aquatic insects, small crustaceans, and occasional small fish including their own young (Ref. 10294).  Eggs in nests are guarded by both parents (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pisidian spring minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pisodonophis copelandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pisodonophis hijala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pisodonophis hypselopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pit sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Pit-head sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand bottom.  Uncommon.

species.name: Pita skate
species.description: Found in shallow water over soft substrate (Ref. 13710).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pitcairn angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock and coral reef at depths of 30 to at least 60 m.  Occurs in aggregations that swim high above the bottom; harems of 2-5 individuals.  Feeds mainly on zooplankton, although some benthic material is probably consumed (Ref. 4858).  Almost never exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Pitcairn Sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling fish, 25-30 individuals, found over sand with high ripple marks; fast swimmers and capable of rapid changes in direction; swim in perfect unison. Preyed upon by larger pelagic fishes such as Carangoides ferdau and other species of Ammodytoides (Ref. 37585).

species.name: Pitgum lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Pithead
species.description: Probably an autumn or winter spawner (Ref. 11892).

species.name: Pitre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near rocks, mainly in eel-grass beds.  Adhesive eggs laid by one or more female in nest of algae built by male (Ref. 4742).  Males grow faster than females (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pitted stonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds (Ref. 57406).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Pituna brevirostrata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pituna compacta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium.  Bottom spawner, 5 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pituna obliquoseriata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a temporary swamp in a savannah area (Ref. 57947).

species.name: Pituna poranga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits temporary swamps, usually in open areas of savanna vegetation (Ref. 57947).

species.name: Pituna schindleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seasonal pools in savannah area (Ref. 57947).

species.name: Pituna xinguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a temporary swamp (Ref. 57947).

species.name: Placidochromis acuticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Placidochromis acutirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Placidochromis argyrogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Placidochromis boops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Placidochromis borealis

species.name: Plagiotremus spilistius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Plagoptère argenté
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in fast sandy runs and pools of small to medium rivers, usually in warm turbid water (Ref. 86798).  Most commonly found in shallow, moderately flowing water over shifting sand substrates (Ref. 26186).  Spawning in the Virgin river begins in April to May and continues through August (Ref. 26186).

species.name: Plagusie de Norman
species.description: Inhabits mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Plagusie de Vanmelle

species.name: Plagusie à queue noire
species.description: Occurs on mud or sand bottoms of the continental slope and shelf (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Plain basslet
species.description: Collected from an outer reef slope off Cranked Island. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Plain cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky reefs (Ref. 11482).  Seeks shelter during the day (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks and other small invertebrates (Ref. 37955).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 2850.

species.name: Plain dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups. Found in outer slopes on rocky substrates with rich encrusting invertebrate growth including sponges and gorgonian sea fans (Ref 90102).

species.name: Plain helmet gurnard
species.description: Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Plain maskray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore on continental shelf and feeds on bony fishes and crustaceans. Litters of 1-3 pups, born at 12-14 cm WD (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449)

species.name: Plain pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Plain sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters (Ref. 2850), on sand and mud bottoms from intertidal zone to depths often not greater than 80 m; seldom caught deeper than 150 m (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Plain snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Plain squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The spines are said to be poisonous (Ref. 4537). Found in pools and slow flowing reaches of perennial and seasonal rivers; prefers riverine habitats to floodplains; shelters in holes or crevices or on the underside of logs, frequently in an upside-down position (Ref. 52193). Active at night, feeds on detritus and plant matter such as seeds as well as small invertebrates like insects and snails, and will scavenge readily (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer during rainy periods (Ref. 7248, 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Plain thicklip loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits slow current, backwater of streams or lakes over sandy and gravel bottom (Ref. 51717).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Matures at 70 mm SL or more (Ref. 57754).

species.name: Plainfin sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in estuarine areas (Ref. 36453).

species.name: Plains killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sandy runs, pools, and backwaters of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers.  Tolerates extremely alkaline and saline streams, and often found where few other fishes can survive.  Buries headfirst in sand and orients itself with only mouth and eyes are visible.  This habit may protect the fish from intense sunlight or may help avoid predators, detect potential prey, or stream desiccation.  10 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Plains topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in springs and their effluents, and in quiet to flowing pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Usually found near vegetation.  7 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).
