species.name: Poisson-crayon (Nannostomus bifasciatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious.  Forms schools of about a dozen individuals.  Frequently occurs upstream in counter current zones.  Is an omnivore with a tendency to feed on insects (Ref. 12225).  Crepuscular.  Appreciated by aquarist notably for its tendency to live in groups and for it habit of swimming with the body oriented upwards.  Reproduces in captivity.  The spawned eggs, which are fixed to vegetal substrate, do not receive parental care (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Poisson-crocodile de Beaufort
species.description: Lives on sand or rubble substrates of sheltered or semi-exposed reefs to a depth of at least 8 m (Ref. 9710).  Well camouflaged on reefs (Ref. 48635). Also found in coral reefs and mangrove area in about 1-12 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-crocodile à tête large
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken over sand associated with rocks and coral reefs to about 30 m (Ref. 9790).  Buries itself partially in the sand for camouflage.  Feeds mainly on crabs and prawns, also on fishes. Also found in sandy fringe of coral reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-dragon gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poisson-fantôme robuste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This uncommon species is found in coastal reefs and weedy areas (Ref. 5463) or lagoon reefs, often on algal flats or seagrass beds (Ref 90102). Monogamous, always in pairs (Ref. 52884).  Females carry the eggs in their pelvic fins that are modified to form a brood pouch (Ref. 205).  Feed on small crustaceans (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Poisson-feuille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats, outer reef slopes, current-swept channels, and rarely on lagoon reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Solitary and usually immobile among algae or seagrass but effects hip movements resembling that of a leaf falling down from a tree.  Molts twice a month with the skin breaking off first in the head region.  Has the habit of mimicking a dead leaf by swaying from side to side (Ref. 37816).  Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 9710); also feeds on larvae (Ref. 5503).  Venomous spines.

species.name: Poisson-feuille Peau-Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow subtidal areas among weeds.  Rocks back and forth (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Poisson-guitare chola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow, soft bottoms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Flesh considered low quality (Ref. 5217).  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Poisson-guitare du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from the surf line to about 70 m depth (Ref. 5578), also reported as common in shallow waters to at least 75 m depth (Ref. 114953); also enters estuaries (Ref. 27121). Feeds on crustaceans, bivalves, polychaete worms and small bony fishes (Ref. 5578). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature at ca. 59 cm TL, females at 62-65 cm TL; born at ca. 23 cm TL. Produces litters of 2-10 pups (Ref. 114953). Taken by surf anglers (Ref. 3919). Flesh highly esteemed (Ref. 3919). It is parasitised by the monogeneans Pseudoleptobothrium christisoni on the dorsal skin surface (Ref. 124055) and Neoheterocotyle robii on the gill lamellae (Ref. 124054).

species.name: Poisson-guitare du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly coastal, benthic species with unknown biology (Ref. 114953). May reach 170 cm TL (Ref. 12951). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Poisson-guitare fouisseur
species.description: A coastal and benthic species found on sandy and muddy bottoms, intertidal zone to at least 80 m depth.  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans and small fishes.  Maximum length would probably reach up to 265 cm TL, common at about 200 cm TL.  Males mature at 138-154 cm TL, females at 153-164 cm TL. In the Mediterranean Sea, males mature at smaller size, about 100-110 cm TL and females at about 110 cm TL.  Size at birth about 34 cm TL.  Produces litters up to 20 pups (more common 6-7 pups) (Ref. 114953).   Ovoviviparous, one or two litters per year, of 4-6 embryos.

species.name: Poisson-guitare marbré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in shallow waters over soft bottom (Ref. 9262).   Adults feed on prawns and crabs, juveniles mainly amphipod crustaceans (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Poisson-guitare nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This benthic inshore species is found over soft bottoms to at least 50 m; feeds on benthic crustaceans and polychaetes. Gestation last about a year, produces litters of 1-8 pups in autumn (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Maturity size for males at 43-45 cm TL, females at 42-48 cm TL; birth size at 13-16 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Poisson-guitare nez blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in shallow waters over sandy bottoms (Ref. 9262).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Produces litters of 1-6 pups. Females mature at ca. 48 cm TL, males at ca. 51 cm TL; born at 19 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Poisson-guitare rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally in rocky areas mainly shallower than 10 m, moves offshore onto soft bottoms in autumn and winter; but may also be found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 37955, Ref. 114953). Reported from tide pools (Ref. 12951). Relatively docile, harmless rays that are easily approached by divers (Ref. 48844). Feeds mainly on mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 37955). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449), with 4 to 11 pups in a litter (Ref. 51576). Maturity size of males at 64-70 cm TL, females at 57-77 cm TL; birth size at 15-18 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Seldom buries itself in sand. This species is a commercially important part of artisanal fisheries (Ref. 114953). Etymology: The genus name comes from the Greek za, meaning intensive, and pteryx, meaning fin, in reference to the vertical fins being larger than those of skates. The species name comes from Latin, meaning made rough, in reference to the numerous stellate prickles on its back. (Ref. 48844).

species.name: Poisson-guitare spatule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms of bays, seagrass beds, estuaries, and near rocky reefs. Nomadic and gregarious. Found singly or in aggregations (Ref. 12951). Burrows in sand during the day, feeds on crabs, worms, clams and small fishes at night (Ref. 12951). Ovoviviparous, with 6 to 28 pups in a litter (Ref. 48844). Females mature by 7 years at 87-99 cm TL; males reaches 91-110 cm TL; birth size at 20-24 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Etymology: The genus comes from the Greek word rhine, meaning shark, and the Latin word batis, meaning ray, in reference to its body form being intermediate between that of a shark and a ray. The species name comes Latin, meaning produced, in reference to its pointed snout (Ref. 48844).

species.name: Poisson-guitare à lunaires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic and more or less stationary in inshore coastal waters.  Feeds on fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587).  Ovoviviparous. Females have litters of 2-3 pups. Males mature at ca. 46 cm TL, females at ca. 52 cm TL; birth size at ca. 15 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Poisson-guitare épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fine sand to mud bottom, often near kelp beds and sometimes abundant on mud flats of coastal bays.  Often buries itself in bottom sediments.  Ranges from the intertidal zone to 50 m depth (Ref. 12951).  Solitary or in small groups, gathers in shallow bays, lagoons, and off beaches (Ref. 12951, Ref. 114953).  Feeds on small sand-dwelling crustaceans, worms and mollusks.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449), with 1 to 15 pups in a litter (Ref. 48844), mainly in August (Ref. 114953).  Possesses ampullary electroreceptors with a region of maximum sensitivity of 5-15 Hz (Ref. 10011).

species.name: Poisson-guitarre tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and weedy bottoms, sometimes near patch reefs.  Also found along beaches from shoreline to depths of 30 m (Ref. 26938).  Usually buried in the sand or mud.  Feeds on mollusks and crustaceans.  Ovoviviparous, with up to 6 in a litter (Ref. 12951).  Size at birth 20 cm (Ref. 12951).  Generally uncommon (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Poisson-hachette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Poisson-hérisson à points jaunes
species.description: Found in coastal waters in the vicinity of reefs (Ref. 9680).  Lives in seagrass habitats and coastal slopes with sponges.  Active during the night (Ref. 48637).  Nocturnal and solitary (Ref. 9680), usually found under ledges during the day (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles pelagic (Ref. 30573).  Feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 9680).  Not usually marketed (Ref. 9680).

species.name: Poisson-lampe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually on or near coral reefs (Ref. 7251).  Rare, most often found from seagrass beds (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Poisson-lampe (Dinoperca petersi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reefs to a depth of 50 m; juveniles in rocky shores (Ref. 4332).  Also found under ledges and cave entrances.  Makes a loud drumming sound.

species.name: Poisson-lapin à queue tronquée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small schools in very shallow water close to the bottom.  Prefer hard bottoms of compacted sand with rock or coral debris.  Solitary adults and groups of 3 or 4 adults have also been observed.  Feed on a wide range of benthic algae.  May suddenly stop and erect its fins (dorsal, anal and pelvic) presenting an encircling array of spines to potential predators; these spines are venomous.  A food fish that is occasionally poisonous (Ref. 4537).  Probably does not adapt well in captivity (Ref. 12382).  A thermophilic species (Ref. 120766). Minimum depth from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Poisson-lune lancéolé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poisson-marabout austral
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the epimesopelagic layer of the southern ocean circumglobally. Only fry and juveniles were observed in subtropical waters; large adults encountered in sub-Antarctic and Antarctic waters. Capable of shedding teeth and reducing gastrointestinal tract prior to spawning. Monocyclic, that is, they die after the first spawning (a reproductive strategy that evolved as a result of the large distance between feeding and spawning areas). Main food is Notolepis coatsi which are 15-38 cm in length and weighs to 57-90 g (Ref. 31260).

species.name: Poisson-paille africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 114953). Occurs in shallow coastal waters, more or less stationary.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Adults feed mainly on small bony fishes and invertebrates. Females have litters of 2-5 pups. Maturity size unknown but born at 79-85 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Poisson-papier couteau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, perhaps entering estuaries (Ref. 9336).  Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 9336).

species.name: Poisson-papier de Dove
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, perhaps entering brackish water (Ref. 9336).  Feeds mainly on small fishes (Ref. 9336).

species.name: Poisson-papier dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal areas, but also in lagoons and off river mouths, perhaps entering water of lowered salinity (Ref. 12225).  In Southwestern Atlantic preys on proportionally large clupeoid fishes and caridean shrimps.  Fishes are distinctively folded in the stomachs of this herring, in about 90% of the cases with their heads and tails pointing head-wards the predator.  This herring stands out as the only small-sized species among the predaceous fish-eating clupeiforms.  The well developed canine-like teeth are likely related to a piscivorous diet and may play a role in the folding and orientation of fish during prey handling and swallowing (Ref. 51383).   Spawns during the northern winter (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Poisson-papier guyanais
species.description: Occurs inshore, off river mouths, in estuaries, and some distance up rivers in freshwater (e.g., up Coppename River near Wilhelmina Mts, Suriname).  Found over sand and mud bottom (Ref. 5217).  Possibly spawns in rivers.  Utilized as a food fish at some localities (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Poisson-papier jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 9336), including estuaries to a depth of 50 m (Ref. 96339).

species.name: Poisson-papier tarture
species.description: Found close to shore and also entering estuaries (e.g. Aluhaluh on Barito River in Kalimantan, Indonesia). Ascends rivers into the tidal zone (Ref. 12693). Feeds on mysids, Pseudodiaptomus and copepod eggs, also prawns and other small crustaceans, bivalve eggs and larvae, amphipods and small fishes. Spawns in late February or early March to July or August (around Karwar, India). Used as fish meal or fertilizer (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Poisson-papier vaqueira
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Either living in rivers or entering rivers from the sea (Ref. 9336).

species.name: Poisson-papier vénézuélien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters inshore, probably entering estuaries.

species.name: Poisson-papier équatorial
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters, perhaps entering water with low salinities (Ref. 9336).

species.name: Poisson-papillon côtelé du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in monogamous pairs in coastal coral-rich areas (Ref. 47838, 48636).  Juveniles hide among branches of small corals, often in lagoons (Ref. 9407).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed solely on live corals (Ref. 47838).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon de l'Atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral reefs. Prefer to feed on eggs of Abudefduf saxatilis (Ref. 9626) but also on polychaete worms, shrimps, amphipods and hydroids. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon de l'île de Pâques
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in algal covered rocky reefs.  Juveniles in tide pools, observed to pick bodies of other fishes for parasites (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon de Sainte-Hélène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in shallow waters. Usually observed in pairs or large groups. Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205). Called a cunning fish since it can nibble the bait from a hook without taking the hook into its mouth. The juvenile Thalassoma sanctaehelenae has been observed cleaning the cunningfish of its parasites (Ref. 5288).

species.name: Poisson-papillon de Smith
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in algal covered rocky reefs often in large aggregations (Ref. 9710).  A mid-water plankton feeder (Ref. 4858).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon de Tahiti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon reefs, usually solitary or paired.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon du nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow, coral reefs with clear water (Ref. 9626).  Develop dusky bands at night.  Generally common (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon grains de millet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow reef flats (Ref. 205).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Form schools at midwater to feed on plankton and benthic invertebrates.  Also on shallow seamounts.  Oviparous.  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon japonais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow rocky reefs.  Spawning occurs in groups at sunset when water temperature is 23°C (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon marqué
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually seen in pairs, frequently in association with plate-like heads of Acropora coral. Feed mainly on coral polyps. (Ref. 4858). Territorial (Ref. 9710). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon quadrillé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon species found in areas of rich coral growth of lagoon and protected reef flats and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Often in pairs (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Feed on sea anemones, polychaetes, and octocorallian and scleractinian coral polyps.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  In captivity, this species should be fed algae stones and the so-called 'feeding stones' which are prepared by spreading the food pulp over the stone.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Poisson-papillon robuste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over rocky areas in inshore waters (Ref. 6943).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-papillon soyeux noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear and outer waters; usually  more than 10 meters deep.  Adults form schools of more than 10 individuals and migrate over a wide area.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Occasionally kept in captivity by Japanese aquarists but is rarely exported.

species.name: Poisson-papillon à tache ovale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In coastal reef slopes rich with hydroids and anemones.  Small juveniles secretive in coral thickets (Ref. 48636).  Usually solitary and relatively uncommon.  Feed on coral polyps and invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-perroquet bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles usually solitary; adults may form schools (Ref. 9710). Females smaller (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on algae, and inhabits on reef edge (Ref. 6113).

species.name: Poisson-phare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in and outside the coelacanth caves during the day, and at night it usually ascends to the coral reef at depths of 3-20 m (Ref. 58472).

species.name: Poisson-pingouin
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, small insects and crustaceans.  In the tank, female lays a large number of eggs, which hatch in about 20 to 24 hours (Ref. 7020).  Maximum length reported to reach 6 cm TL (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Poisson-pipe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among corals or sea fans in lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 30874).  Adults in pairs or small aggregations when in the open or in safe places at night (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Poisson-ruban licorne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 4165), oceanic, mesopelagic species.  Occasionally stranded in shallow water (Ref. 9563).  Capable of discharging a black ink from an ink-sac in the cloaca when alarmed.  Adults feed on fishes (anchovies) and squids (Ref. 6740).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36608).  Found in stomachs of tunas (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Poisson-scie commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A euryhaline species (Ref. 57533).  Inhabits inshore coastal waters to moderate depth, also around off lying islands.  Found also in estuaries, lagoons, river mouths, and even freshwater.  Feeds on fishes and bottom-living animals.  Ovoviviparous.  Apparently can reproduce in freshwater (Ref. 57533).  Freshwater populations occur to about 750 km up Amazon River; populations in Lake Nicaragua may be non-migratory (Ref. 7251). Reaches sexual maturity at 8-10 years and females have litters of approximately 1-13 pups. Young spend much of their early life in rivers up to 400 km from the sea (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Poisson-scie grandent
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms of shallow coastal waters, estuaries, river mouths, and   freshwater rivers and lakes. Usually found in turbid channels of large rivers over soft mud bottoms (Ref. 2847, 44894). Adults usually found in estuaries and young ascend into fresh water. Large adults can also be found in fresh water, but are rarely caught (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on benthic animals and small schooling species.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  The saw is used for grubbing and attacking prey as well as for defense.  The saws sell as tourist souvenirs (Ref. 7248).  Occasionally caught by demersal tangle net and trawl fisheries in the Arafura Sea; possibly extinct in parts of the Indo-Pacific; highly susceptible to gill nets. Utilized for its fins and meat (both of very high value), and skin and cartilage (Ref.58048). Attains 4.6 m total length (Ref. 52193).

species.name: Poisson-scie trident
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore and intertidal species, but may cross deep water to reach offshore islands; also ascends rivers and can tolerate fresh water (Ref. 9859). Commonly seen in bays, lagoons, estuaries, and river mouths.  Also found in rivers and lakes (Ref. 12951). Feeds on fishes and shellfishes (Ref. 58784). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Gravid females reportedly carry as many as 20 embryos, which require a year of gestation (Ref. 27549).  Uses its saw to stir the bottom when feeding on bottom invertebrates and to kill pelagic fishes (Ref. 9859). Utilized as a food fish; oil is used to make medicine, soap and in leather tanning (Ref. 6871).  Adults stuffed for decoration (Ref. 6871). Reported to be aggressive towards sharks when kept in tanks (Ref. 12951). This species is currently protected in several areas as populations are under severe threat (Ref. 81624).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion d'Eschmeyer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A popular aquarium fish, together with Rhinopias frondosa, are collected from Southeast Asian waters, imported to Japan where these are traded separately as different morphotypes (Ref. 57714). Found in coral reefs and ruble bottoms in 18-55 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion de Maurice
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer intertidal reef flats and shallow lagoon reefs exposed to wave action. Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion de Poos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary on rock or coral bottoms in 1-40 m (Ref 90102). Feeds on fishes (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion du Mozambique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with mixed sand and rubble in reef flats, shallow lagoons, and channels.  Hides during the day, ventures out in the open at night.  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion à guenilles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reefs (Ref. 9710); usually taken by diving in protected areas of bays or lagoons, often where the fish can be well camouflaged in areas of algae, seagrass or sponge (Ref. 42181, 48635).  Venomous spines. Occurs along continental margins or islands associated with continents, not at true oceanic islands (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion à piége
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and rubble under ledges of seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  The dorsal fin mimics a tiny fish and is used as a lure (Ref. 9710).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion à tache jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef crests with rich coral growth (Ref. 48635). Typically found among the branches of Pocillopora corals in surge areas of seaward reefs (Ref. 1602). Also observed between the branches of the fire coral Millepora and Styllophora (Eran Brokovich, pers. comm. 03/02). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Poisson-scorpion à épines courtes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas of rich coral growth from near shore to the outer reef slope (Ref. 4313).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Cryptic.  Venomous spines (Ref. 4313).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Poisson-tapir sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302) and epibenthic (Ref. 58426).  Not uncommon in depths around 180 m off Iceland and Greenland.  Individuals with nearly ripe eggs have been found in late autumn off Iceland.  Mostly found at depths well below 200 m, but enters slightly shallower water on Grand Banks in Canada (Ref. 7251).  Feeds primarily on sea anemones (Ref. 4449).

species.name: Poisson-tapir épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic invertebrates, especially amphipods, polychaetes and mysids (Ref. 6728).

species.name: Poisson-taureau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits main channels, pools, backwaters of small to large rivers, lakes, and impoundments (Ref. 86798).   Feeds on cladocera and cyclopoid copepods supplemented with midge larvae (Ref. 10294).  Oviparous (Ref. 205). Prefers water with depth of less than 5 m (Ref. 121623).

species.name: Poisson-volant du Japon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the neritic zone (Ref. 11230).  Spawning school captured with gill-net in early summer.  Common and commercially valued.  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: poisson-éléphant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs close to the bottom where it probes for food with the long snout.  Territorial and usually aggressive towards members of its own species.  This behavior has been shown to involve electric organ discharge (EOD) activity (Ref. 10011).  Feeds mostly at night on worms and insects (Ref. 7020), probably aided by electro-sensory inputs (Ref. 10011).  Electroreceptors are distributed over the entire head, the dorsal and ventral regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located (Ref. 10011).  Sex-related EOD characteristics in this species has been demonstrated in the laboratory with freshly imported samples during the breeding season; such EOD dimorphism changed with time in captivity (Ref. 10764; 10766).  Lead nitrate in water significantly increased EOD rate and selectively altered the EOD waveform of this species (Ref. 10469).  Dubbed a `hearing specialist' having auditory abilities in the range of 100-2500 Hz, with `best frequencies'  between 300 and 600 Hz (Ref. 10830).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 150 cm; not recommended for home aquariums (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Poissons soldat rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A nocturnal species found in small, loose groups in caves or under ledges of reef flats, lagoons, and outer reef slopes.  Feeds on plankton such as crab larvae (Ref. 12419).

species.name: Poissons soldat rouge (Myripristis seychellensis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens found in caves.

species.name: poissons-main tachetés
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf and inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  Occurs in coarse to fine sand habitats in depths of 5-40 m (most commonly 5-10 m).  Often found in shallow, shell-filled depressions or near rocks of low relief projecting from the substrate (Ref. 30684).  Length only preliminary, replace with better value (RF).  Egg masses contain about 80-250 eggs, about 1.8-2 mm in diameter; egg capsules about 3-4 mm diameter.  Newly hatched juveniles are about 6-7 mm SL, attaining at least 9.0 cm SL (about 13.0 cm TL), with adults commonly about 6.0-7.5 cm SL (Ref. 72490).

species.name: Poissson-couteau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare and little is know of its biology. Occurs in rapidly flowing water over a sandy bottom together with Leporinus granti, L. maculatus and Crenicichla multispinosa. Its dispersed capture suggests a solitary behavior (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Policante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 117245.  Epibenthic and feeds on coelenterates, worms and crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Polka dot waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled over muddy bottoms.

species.name: Polka-dot batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from water's edge to 70 m depth.

species.name: Polka-dot cusk-eel
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 37039.

species.name: Polka-dot ribbonfish
species.description: Epi- (Ref. 58302) and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4506).  Feeds upon various organisms like small fish, squids, octopus, and crustaceans (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Polka-dot splitfin
species.description: Poisson. According to aquarists, the species prefers live food. Thought to be extinct in the wild as their spring area has been claimed. Males can be recognized by a notched anal fin. Live bearers producing 10-20 offspring and breed several times per year. Source: https://aquainfo.org/breeding-chapalichthys-pardalis/

species.name: Polkadot dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polkadot pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poll's bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This entomophagous fish lives in swamps and zones of flood (Ref. 41580).

species.name: Pollimyrus adspersus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: P. isidori.

species.name: Pollimyrus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus cuandoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species prefers to hide in weeds if present, floating or not, often high up in water column, sometimes even at the surface under a water lily leaf in bright sunlight; also found on rocky bottom, hiding in crevices and holes (Ref. 94890). It will often not struggle in weeds brought to shore, so as not to raise attention (Ref. 94890).

species.name: Pollimyrus eburneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus guttatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus maculipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus marianne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast-flowing areas of river with rapids and rocky bottom where there is little cover, except for crevices and rock holes, and also from dense reed beds on sandy bottoms and weak current (Ref. 50438).

species.name: Pollimyrus nigripinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possesses electroreceptors over the entire head, the ventral and dorsal regions of the body, but absent from the side and the caudal peduncle where the electric organ is located (Ref. 10011).

species.name: Pollimyrus pedunculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus petricolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: sympatric with P. isidori.

species.name: Pollimyrus plagiostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus pulverulentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus schreyeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus stappersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pollimyrus tumifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyacanthonotus africanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at bathyal and abyssal depths.  Feeds on benthic polychaetes, cnidarians, amphipods (Ref. 4449).

species.name: Polyacanthonotus merretti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polycentrus jundia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polygon moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters in rocky habitats.

species.name: Polygon perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected (with hand nets) in highly complex reefs predominantly covered by coralline algae and sponges and crevices of steep reef walls, indicating that this species probably has a wider Pacific distribution and all known individuals have been observed or collected at mesophotic depths, suggesting as with most of its congeners, this species does not inhabit shallow coral reef habitats (Ref. 122130).

species.name: Polyipnus asper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus asteroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus bruuni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus danae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Polyipnus fraseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Polyipnus indicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known specimens are less than 5.5 cm SL (Ref. 4054).

species.name: Polyipnus inermis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus laternatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus limatulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to prefer the pelagic environment.

species.name: Polyipnus matsubarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus meteori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at depths of 0 to 1770 meters.  The largest specimen observed was 3.07 cm, standard length (Ref. 128944).

species.name: Polyipnus oluolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus omphus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus ovatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus parini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus spinifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens have been collected above 150 m in Suruga Bay, Japan (Ref. 26382).

species.name: Polyipnus stereope
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus surugaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyipnus unispinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polylepion russelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep waters (Ref. 3921).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Polymetme andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polymetme elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polymetme thaeocoryla

species.name: Polymixia fusca

species.name: Polymixia longispina

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polynemus bidentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polynesian pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polynesian sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polynesian triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polynesian wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found well above the bottom of exposed seaward reefs (Ref. 9710) away from lagoons and sheltered bays (Ref. 123182). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Polypera simushirae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequently occurs in the upper bathyal zone.  Predominantly piscivorous (Ref. 26947).

species.name: Polyplacapros tyleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polypterus congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This carnivorous fish lives in streams, lakes and zones of flood (Ref. 4910, Ref. 41580).  In Lake Tanganyika it is mostly found at the mouth or delta of rivers and lagoons (Ref. 36901).  Not commercially important (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Polypterus mokelembembe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polypterus teugelsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant in densely shaded rainforest streams (Ref. 51884).

species.name: Polyspina piosae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Polyspondylogobius sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in brackish water, river mouths and tidal pools, but also near the bottom in shallow, sandy bays.

species.name: Poma snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in moderate to swift , transparent to turbid and cool running water with low to moderate depth and various substrates as gravel pebbles, cobbles and medium to large boulders. River banks consist of a mixture of sand, soil, and stones that lead to frequent soil erosion. The following associated fishes were observed: Garra birostris, G. annandalei, Crossocheilus latius, Chagunius chagunio, Neolissochilus hexagonolepis, Tor putitora, Bangana dero, Labeo pangusia, Puntius ticto, Barilius bendelisis, B. barna, Devario aequipinnatus, Danio dangila, D. rerio, Badis sp., Psilorhynchus balitora, and Botia rostrata (Ref. 116756).

species.name: Pomacentrus atriaxillaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pomacentrus bipunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs in lagoonal habitats on coral reef substrates, often on pinnacle or patch reefs at depths between 5 and 43 m (Ref. 54758).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pomacentrus caeruleopunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pomacentrus cheraphilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit silty reefs around coral and rock outcrops (Ref. 86257).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pomacentrus flavioculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on both outer reefs and in lagoons, often adjacent to steep coral formations with abundant ledges and overhangs. Common in depths of about 4-30 m. (Ref. 116673).

species.name: Pomacentrus microspilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on silt-affected coral reefs, in loose aggregations that apparently feed on zooplankton above the reef (Ref. 75750).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pomacentrus yoshii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Pomadasys bipunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pomadasys guoraca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pomadasys ramosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along sandy shores and over mud bottoms in shallow water, in mangrove areas.

species.name: Pomadasys schyrii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pomatoschistus montenegrensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. P. montenegrensis lives in the slow current shallows of the Moracă River and in pools remaining in gravel pits after river flooding. The substratum is like gravel, covered with fine sediment and overgrown by dense filamentous algae, within which gobies are concealed (Ref. 75173).

species.name: Pomegranate pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along a rubble terrace adjacent to a drop off at 25 m (Ref. 123182).

species.name: Pompaneau africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal areas with reefs or rocky outcrops (Ref. 3197).  They are found normally in pairs on reefs but may be solitary or form schools (Ref. 5213, 90102).  Juveniles in sheltered bays.  Adults feed on mollusks (mussels) and crabs (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Pompaneau argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal waters (Ref. 9283).  They are common in shallow water and feed mainly on  mollusks, but also take crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 9283).  Juveniles are frequently encountered in estuaries and feed on a variety of benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Pompaneau chevron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow coastal areas and estuaries (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Pompaneau colombe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal waters, usually forming schools in shallow inshore sandy areas (Ref. 9283).  They feed on mollusks, crustaceans, other invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 9283).  Excellent for human consumption.  Minimum depth range based on estimate; to be replaced with a better reference.

species.name: Pompaneau du Plate
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pompaneau fin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore sandy areas and also clear waters around reefs and rocky areas (Ref. 9283).  They feed on small invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Pompaneau indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coastal waters (Ref. 3287).

species.name: Pompaneau né-bé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 2683). Enters brackish waters for reproduction and ascends rather far up the lower courses of rivers (Ref. 4225, 57392). Unique in spending the whole live cycle in myxohaline environment, without a marine phase; seasonality of recruitment seems to indicate that favourable conditions for reproduction and larval survival are limited to the dry season although sexual maturity occurs all year round (Ref. 81654). Feeds on fry and young shrimps up to 125 mm fork length, diet of larger specimens mainly malacophagous (bivalves), the shells of which are crushed with well-developed pharyngeal jaws (Ref. 81654). Also feeds on fish, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 28587). Maximum fork length recorded was 610 mm (Ref. 57392).

species.name: Pompaneau pierrot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300), in sandy surf zones; juveniles in shallow surf zones (Ref. 4332).  Adults feed on crabs, mussels, and worms (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Pompaneau tachete
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal marine species (Ref. 2683, 57392) occurring down to 100 m depth (Ref. 57392), frequently entering estuaries (Ref. 2683, 57392) and ascending lower courses of rivers (Ref. 57392).  Maximum length possibly up to 100 cm (Ref. 57392).

species.name: Pompaneau éclatant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near islands (Ref. 9283).  They generally form big schools (Ref. 9283).  Not directly targeted for fishing (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Pondoland sailfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pongo characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pontic spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small brooks to large rivers, in flowing or still waters on sand, silt or mud bottoms (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ponticola cephalargoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to brackish water habitats; endemic to Black and Caspian Seas (Ref. 92840).  Found inshore, on pebbles or gravel, and also some offshore banks; migrates to shallows in spring (Ref. 4696).  Eggs deposited under and between stones (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Pontinus corallinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pontinus helena
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pontinus rhodochrous
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Michael N. Trevor, pers. comm., 1999).

species.name: Pontinus tentacularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pontoh's pygmy seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hippocampus pontohi has been observed on the coralline algae Halimeda, as well as on the hydroid Aglaephenia cupressina (Müller and Severns, pers. comm.). Severns noted it particularly in areas where Halimeda is growing on reef walls. It has been recorded at a number of areas in Indonesia (Bunaken, Cape Sri, Sorong, Wakatobi, Lembeh Straits), at depths of between 11-25 m particularly on vertical walls or in rock fissures on current-swept walls where it will tend to occur on the side of the fissure that faces away from the current, but in all cases where there is some upward current (Müller, pers. comm.) and has been seen swimming over a fungiid coral (Hardt, pers. comm.). Hippocampus pontohi is commonly found in pairs and, like H. denise, is relatively active in the morning and late afternoon when it is not in direct sunlight (Müller, pers. comm.). Two of the specimens examined were pregnant and each contained approximately 11 embryos (Ref. 79848).

species.name: Pool barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers, streams and ponds in plains and submontane regions (Ref. 41236).  Collected from a large river with high turbid monsoon flow and with diverse substrate consisting of sand, mud, gravel, pebble, cobble, and boulders (Ref. 85713).  A very plentiful shoaling fish.  They remain small in domestic aquaria and become mature at 7 to 8 cm (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Poor man's tropheus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits both lakes and rivers.  Proliferates in rivers with medium to high velocities.  Found between 35 and 535 m elevation (Ref. 36880).  Feeds on aufwuchs which cover rocks and submersed trees and filaments of algae.

species.name: Popeye grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on pelagic forms (Ref. 1371).  Too small for fresh consumption (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Popeye lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic and mesopelagic, found in 525-725 m during the day and in 10-150 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Popeye shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, gravel-bottomed, flowing pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Popoche chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Popondetta blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found in clear, moderate to fairly rapid flowing streams in both shaded rainforest or sunlit, exposed sections.  The altitudinal range is from about 30-300 m (Ref. 2847).  An egg laying omnivore and a peaceful community fish which prefers the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.7, H=14, 28°C water temperature and some vegetative cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Popta's buntingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are attached to the body, between the pelvic fins (Ref. 31267).

species.name: Poptella brevispina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear waters of creeks with sandy bottoms.  Reproduction takes place during the rainy season (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Poptella compressa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poptella longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poptella paraguayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf, commonly near reefs (Ref. 26998, 9563).  Feed mainly on invertebrates (Ref. 26998).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten steamed, pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Seen in small aggregations but school in deep water where commercially trawled (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Porc-épic bécard
species.description: Inhabit clear protected reefs with sponge and algal habitats.  Often in large sponges during the day (Ref. 48637).  Usually over sand and mud bottoms to at least 170 m (Ref. 30573).  Occasionally on reefs (Ref. 9680).  Active at night, feeding among reefs (Ref. 48637).  A nocturnal species (Ref. 9710) that presumably feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates (Ref. 9680, 48637).

species.name: Porc-épic de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly over sand and mud bottoms.  Feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates such as mollusks (Ref. 2718).  Sale of this species is banned in some countries due to belief that this species is poisonous (but documented proof is lacking).  Not consumed in Africa.

species.name: Pored sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools (Ref. 2850). Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Poreface longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porehead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poreless dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually seen in aggregations; inhabits mangroves, sometimes adjacent to coral reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Poreless goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poreless gudgeon
species.description: Found in backwaters of rivers, small creeks, swamps, and lily lagoons, usually among thick aquatic vegetation over soft mud bottoms.  Females lay about 30 eggs (2 millimeters in diameter) on the ceiling of overhanging rocks or crevices.  These are guarded and fanned by males until hatching, which takes about 8 days (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Porichthys bathoiketes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porichthys kymosemeum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Porichthys oculofrenum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porichthys pauciradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Needs better reference.

species.name: Porichthys porosissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Porky
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porochilus argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in slow-flowing streams over sand or rock bottoms (Ref. 5259).

species.name: Porocottus allisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults Inhabit sea-well beds. Minimum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 56557).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools (Ref. 44254).

species.name: Porocottus minutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porocottus quadrifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porocottus tentaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porogadus atripectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  This species is caught mostly between 1800 and 4000 m, rarely up to 1200 m on the lower reaches or the base of the continental slopes. Apparently, it does not appear to venture away from the slope for more than about 500 km (Ref. 125143). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus caboverdensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A deep-water species that has only been caught below 4480 m in the Cape Verde Basin off northwestern Africa. It occurs with two other deep-water species, P.mendax and P. turgidus (Ref. 125143).

species.name: Porogadus catena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus dracocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porogadus guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthopelagic species at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809). Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  This species ventures out for about 800 km from the continental break and occurs primarily between 1800 and 3300 m but two specimens were caught in very shallow water at 245 m or near the surface. The reason for the unusual shallow catches are not known (Ref. 125143). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus melanocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus mendax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porogadus nudus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus promelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porogadus trichiurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Porogadus turgidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porogobius schlegelii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, in the intertidal zone (Ref. 4343), in brackish and freshwaters, particularly estuaries, coastal lagoons, mangrove swamps (Ref. 4343, 57403, 79590), creeks and lower river basins (Ref. 57403). Tolerant of fresh waters and may ascend rivers, although less common in these habitats; may establish burrows in subtidal mud (Ref. 79590). Feeds on fish, lamellibranchs, phytoplankton and detritus (Ref. 28587).

species.name: Poromitra agafonovae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra atlantica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found mainly below 400 - 500 meters, to 800 - 1,000 meters; juveniles as shallow as 50 - 100 meters (Ref. 51657).

species.name: Poromitra coronata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra crassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra cristiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This was caught by non-closing fishing gear in water horizons of 1000-0 to 2000-0 m (Ref. 83719).

species.name: Poromitra curilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seined with non-closing fishing gear in the water horizon of 8000-0 m; and one catch was performed with a dip net near water surface (Ref. 83718).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were seined using non-closing fishing gear, the largest depths of capture were 1650-0 m, and the smallest depths were 50-900 m (Ref. 83719).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra jucunda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens seined with unclosing fishing gear (Ref. 84090).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species, adults trawled at depths below 400 m, juveniles below 150 meters.  There is significant morphological variation between Indo-Pacific and other populations.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36655).

species.name: Poromitra nigriceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were seined with non-closing fishing gear in the range of depths 3000-0 m and with bottom fishing gear is seined at 1640-2000 m (Ref. 83719).

species.name: Poromitra nigrofulva

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poromitra unicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with non-closing fishing gear that precise depths of its occurrence is undetermined.  Depths of catches are 200-0 minimum and 5300-0 maximum (Ref. 83717).

species.name: Poropanchax luxophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers and brooks in the swampy primary and secondary rainforest on the coastal plains (Ref. 3788, 57259). It feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020). It is not a seasonal killifish and very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Poropanchax pepo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a stagnant channel, with sand and bolders, located approximately 180 meters from the main channel of the Congo River (Ref. 122044).

species.name: Poropanchax stigmatopygus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porophryne erythrodactylus
species.description: This species usually found in subtidal rocky-reef habitat dominated by small filamentous and foliose algae Zonaria, Corallina, Amphiroa, and Laurencia (often with some Sargassum spp.), a few scattered larger seaweeds, including Ecklonia radiata and Sargassum spp., and large patches of filamentous or foliose algae. Vertical or sloping walls on the deep edge of nearby reefs are inhabited by ascidians, corals, and sponges, the latter including Spongia sp., Tedania anhelans, Ephydatia fluviatilis, Darwinella australiensis, Chondrilla australiensis, Mycale australis, and Holopsamma laminaefavosa. It is most often found closely associated with small sponges, blending in with the gray coloration of Psammocinia sp. or the red or yellow coloration of Darwinella sp., or nestled next to fan-shaped Echinoclathria leporina. The black ‘‘osculum-like’’ spots typically present on gray color morphs of the new species presumably aid in the mimicry of sponges as well (Ref. 97600).

species.name: Poropuntius alloiopleurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length reaches to at least 40 cm SL (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Poropuntius angustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in small streams, in forest and in shallow water (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Poropuntius bantamensis

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams and rivers at foot hills (Ref. 41236).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).

species.name: Poropuntius kontumensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear mountain brooks and streams in forested areas.  Feeds on insect larvae.  Not known to migrate and does not persist in impoundments.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Poropuntius krempfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length reaches up to at least 13 cm SL (Ref.  43281).

species.name: Poropuntius laoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear forested streams.  Not found in large rivers and does not persist in impoundments.  Not known to migrate.  Feeds mainly on insect larvae.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches up to at least 9.2 cm SL (Ref.  43281).

species.name: Porotergus duende
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known mainly from the main channels of large whitewater rivers such as the Rio Solimões(Amazon) and Río Ucayali. In the Tefé region, it was encountered only during the rising water period in January and February, and captured in waters of 2–4 m depth on beaches of alluvial silt and fine sand.  Based on examined stomachs of four specimens, this species feeds exclusively on small, autochthonous, benthic insect larvae (of micro-caddis fly, biting midge and beetle). Most specimens had loose sand grains in the stomach (larger than the grains of sand in the caddis fly jackets), suggesting foraging on sandy substrates; one stomach contained many endoparasitic nematodes.  All four specimens captured in the Tefé region had maturing, but not fully mature, gonads, suggesting that spawning occur during the rising water period, typical of riverine apteronotids (Ref. 83661).

species.name: Port Curtis mossback
species.description: Found inshore, in soft bottom (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Port Hedland tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Collected from a depth of 200 m (Ref. 9069).

species.name: Port Jackson glassfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic and lotic freshwater, as well as in mangrove areas (Ref. 7300).  A small schooling species also found in estuaries and coastal marine waters (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Port Phillip pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock pools and estuaries.  Found among vegetation.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 9.35 cm SL.

species.name: Porte-écuelle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores.  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Porte-écuelle des oursins
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles about 1-2 cm SL are often observed in association with sea urchins and in beds of Posidonia oceanica. Adults found hidden under stones covered with red calcareous algae and empty shells of mussels near Posidonia and Cymodocea nodosa beds. Among Posidonia, the species is often sympatric with Opeatogenys gracilis (Ref. 28715).

species.name: Porte-écuelle grêle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Robert A. Patzner, pers. comm., 1999).

species.name: Porte-épée de Monterrey
species.description: Used for genetic studies.

species.name: Porthole livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in irrigation canals (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Porthole pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Porthole shovelnose catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rather rare, confined to the deeper and slow-moving parts of large rivers together with some Loricaria and Potamotrygon. Its body shape and color pattern are perfectly adapted to the muddy bottom where they stay (Ref. 35381). Feeds on benthic organisms and fish. The position of the eyes and the shape of the mouth of this piscivorous fish give to its stalking mode of hunting (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Posidonichthys hutchinsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on leaves of Posidonia australis, a marine angiosperm. Appears to be most common from just beneath the surface down to about 2 m..

species.name: Poso halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Postel's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Pot-bellied leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).

species.name: Potamarius izabalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males carry the eggs in their mouth (Ref. 205).

species.name: Potamobatrachus trispinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers (Ref. 26631).

species.name: Potamoglanis anhanga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in places with mud and roots of aquatic plants of a small stream, mainly composed of sandbanks (Ref. 116750).

species.name: Potamoglanis hasemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in roots of aquatic plants (Ref. 116750).

species.name: Potamoglanis johnsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in roots of aquatic plants (Ref. 116750).

species.name: Potamoglanis wapixana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marginal vegetation of small streams (Ref. 116750).

species.name: Potamorhina altamazonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Potamorhina laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms big schools (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on detritus (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Potamorhina latior
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Potamorhina pristigaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Potamorhina squamoralevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Potamorrhaphis eigenmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Potamorrhaphis labiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type used is body length (BL), measured from the anterior margin of the nasal bone to the hypural plate (Ref. 92518).

species.name: Potamorrhaphis petersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Potamotrygon boesemani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
