species.name: Potamotrygon schuemacheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Potomac sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers, often near vegetation.

species.name: Potosi pupfish
species.description: 5.9 cm max SL (Ref. 12193).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pouch snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Poulamon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal, brackish and fresh water, landlocked in several lakes.  Feeds mostly on small crustaceans, (especially shrimps and amphipods); also worms, small mollusks, squids and fishes (smelt, sticklebacks, striped bass, alewives, shed, herring and sculpins (Ref. 5951))  (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Poulamon du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally found over sand (Ref. 1371).  May enter brackish water (Ref. 1371).  Young move into shallow waters in summer and fall, whereas adults usually stay in deeper waters (Ref. 28499).  Feeds on shrimps, amphipods, isopods, gastropods, mussels and fishes (Ref. 1371).  An important prey species (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Poule d'eau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in shallow protected coastal waters to deep, somewhat silty habitats. Often with deep shipwrecks (Ref. 48637).  Adults are found singly or in small groups and occasionally in large schools in some areas.  Juveniles occur singly or in small groups among mangroves and inner sheltered lagoons  while adults move out to open waters over sandy areas of deep lagoons, channels, and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 30 m.  Feed on algae, invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Pourceau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Pourceau dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in areas with rocky bottoms (Ref. 5374).  Juveniles have been observed in 3 m (Ref. 75973).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pourceau des îles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in areas of rock and rubble bottoms associated with sand or reef-like areas.  Protogynous hermaphrodite, with obvious sexual dichromatism (Ref. 5292).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Juveniles remove ectoparasites from other species (Ref. 86997).

species.name: Pourceau dos noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs, rarely at depths greater than 24 m (Ref. 9710). Feed on crabs and small shellfish (Ref. 3726). Juveniles pick parasites from other fishes (Ref. 9710). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). May hybridize with Spanish hogfish, B. rufus (Ref. 40096). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3726).

species.name: Pourceau du Natal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky areas.  Feed mainly on  mollusks, crustaceans and sea urchins (Ref. 5374).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pourceau espagnol
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky or coral reefs (Ref. 9710). Feed on brittle stars, crustaceans, mollusks, and sea urchins (Ref. 9710). Juveniles actively pick parasites from larger fishes (Ref. 5521). A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. ). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). May hybridize with spotfin hogfish, B. pulchellus (Ref. 40096). Marketed fresh (Ref. 3726). Maximum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Pourceau mexicain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky or coral areas (Ref. 9311).  Sometimes also found on sandy  bottoms and where marine plants abound (Ref. 9311).  Solitary or forms aggregations of only a few individuals.  Feed on crabs, brittle stars, mollusks, and sea urchins (Ref. 9311).  At night, they agglomerate in cracks and crevices of rocks and caves to sleep (Ref. 9311).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9311).  Starts life as a female, later becoming a functional male.  Males defend temporary reproductive territories called leks. Sex change may be due to local social conditions, but it may also have a genetic component, since the reversal occurs over a limited size range (Ref. 28023).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Powan
species.description: Lacustrine, in open water. Feeds on crustaceans and insects (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Powder-blue panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small rivers, mostly in quiet parts (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139); prefers aquaria with rocks, plants and driftwood (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Powellichthys ventriosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Power's deep-water bristle-mouth fish
species.description: Epi- (Ref. 58302) and mesopelagic, mostly found at 300-600 m during the day and at 50-350 m at night (Ref. 3988, 58302); both juveniles and adults make diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4778).  Feed on small crustaceans (Ref. 4778).  Adult photophore complement attained at about 19 mm SL (Ref. 4778).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35839).  Spawning takes place throughout the year in Mediterranean (Ref. 37473).

species.name: Prado toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Praealticus dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Praealticus margaritarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky shore areas, exposed to surges (Ref. 559).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Praealticus tanegasimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit surge, rocky shore areas.  Grow to less than 14 cm TL. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Praematoliparis anarthractae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Prairie chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Predaceous chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Predatory carp
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit rivers and lakes.  Feed on insects, crustaceans and smaller fishes.

species.name: Prespa minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits still waters of lakes and lake shores, with abundant aquatic vegetation. Population has declined due to the introduction of alien species (Pseudorasbora parva, Rhodeus amarus). Maximum size reaches up to about 5.5 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pretty goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pretty shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and clay-bottomed pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Price's damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to be reef-associated (Ref. 48494).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Prickle triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pricklebreast poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud or sand bottom.

species.name: Pricklefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults probably benthopelagic (Ref. 51654).  Larvae taken at 30 m (Ref. 51654).  Benthic crabs Malacostraca were found in the stomachs of 3 specimens SL 8.5-9 cm from Madagascar Ridge (Ref. 10920).

species.name: Prickly anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Prickly croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries and rivers (Ref. 9772).  A food fish.

species.name: Prickly deep-sea skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 26346).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Prickly fanfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles probably found up to a depth of 200 m (Ref. 4388).

species.name: Prickly footballfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Prickly lanternfish
species.description: Neustonic to mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  High-oceanic, nyctoepipelagic at the surface and down to 125 m.  Found between 425-750 m during the day.  Sexually mature from about 65 mm (Ref. 4479).  Proximate analysis (excluding head) reveals that lipid content is 2.0 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 17.2 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).

species.name: Prickly leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in weedy areas of coastal reefs (Ref. 9710) and trawling grounds.  The flesh is good for human consumption.

species.name: Prickly pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Probably brooding at 15.4 cm SL.

species.name: Prickly skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of about 1,093 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Prickly snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Prickly toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Primitive archerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams and swamps, usually with abundant overhanging vegetation.  Breeds in the early wet season, as small juveniles have been recorded in the late wet (Ref. 44894).  A rare species.

species.name: Princess anthias
species.description: Large aggregations occur on steep outer reef slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 4538, 48635).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Princess pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a quiet, sheltered bay (Ref. 55345). Inhabits sheltered bays in 9-26 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Priocharax ariel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits still waters of shaded rain forest streams (Ref. 28825).

species.name: Priocharax britzi
species.description: Specimens were collected from a small lake approximately 15 m wide and 35 m long, apparently isolated from the main channel of the rio Ipixuna and where the water level was low as sampling occurred during the dry season (September). It is possible that this lake connects to the main channel in the wet season. Collection was done near the shore at depths varying from 0.5–1.0 m, when the bottom was muddy with patches of leaf litter. Vegetation around the lake was composed mainly of dead logs and branches. Collected with the characiforms Carnegiella marthae, Hemigrammus sp., Hyphessobrycon rosaceus. Iguanodectes spilurus, Microcharacidium sp., Nannostomus digrammus, Nannostomus eques; the catfish Amblydoras affinis; the knifefishes Brachyhypopomus beebei, Microsternarchus bilineatus; the cichlids Apistogramma cf. pulchra, Biotoecus opercularis and Crenicichla cyanotus (Ref. 124594).

species.name: Priocharax marupiara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found along banks of aquatic plants (e.g., Elodea sp.) in a blackwater pond approximately 10 × 5 m, separated during the dry season by only a few meters from the stream, with both connected in the rainy season. They were very abundant and found with the arowana tetra Gnathocharax steindachneri; the aphyoditeine tetra Axelrodia stigmatias; the tetras Hemigrammus bellottii, H. microstomus, H. vorderwinkleri, Hyphessobrycon bentosi, an unidentified Hyphessobrycon sp.; the freshwater hatchetfish Carnegiella strigata; the toothless characin Curimatopsis macrolepis; juvenile wolffish Hoplias malabaricus; the pencilfish Nannostomus marginatus, Pyrrhulina sp.; the miniature thorny catfish Physopyxis lyra; the callichthyid armoured catfishes Megalechis picta, M. thoracata; the loricariine armoured catfish Rineloricaria sp.; the bigeye cichlid Acaronia nassa; juvenile saddled cichlid Aequidens tetramerus; the pike cichlid Crenicichla sp. Despite sampling efforts in all mesohabitats other than the pond, this was not found in the main channel. In the 2021 expedition, the pond was littered with a large amount of garbage (e.g., bottles, plastic bags) (Ref. 128833).

species.name: Priocharax nanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in the black acidic waters of the Rio Negro basin around the submerged vegetation at depths of about 1 m or less and from an area exposed to the sun in warm, shallow water, approximately 50 cm deep (Ref. 96862).

species.name: Priocharax pygmaeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shaded or partially shaded rainforest stream.  The bottom was clay with much leaf litter and without submerged plants.

species.name: Priocharax toledopizae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in black water systems including small streams and ponds close to the streams and were collected along the margins where riparian vegetation was still present, especially among roots of buriti (Mauritia flexuosa). It was collected with the following species: arowana tetra Gnathocharax steindachneri; sailfin tetra Crenuchus spilurus; the tetras Bryconella pallidifrons, Hemigrammus melanochrous, H. schmardae, Hyphessobrycon agulha, Jupiaba abramoides, Moenkhausia collettii, M. comma, M. melogramma, M. mikia; the neon tetra Paracheirodon innesi; the freshwater hatchetfish Carnegiella strigata; the headstander Chilodus punctatus; the toothless characin Curimatopsis sp.; the wolf-fish Hoplias malabaricus; the pencil fish Nannostomus marginatus; the callichthyid armoured catfish Corydoras arcuatus; the three barbled catfish Pimelodella sp.; the loricariine armoured catfish Rineloricaria sp.; the saddled cichlid Aequidens tetramerus; the dwarf cichlid Apistogramma juruensis; the glass knifefish Eigenmannia sp.; the sand knifefish Gymnorhamphichthys rondoni; and the rivuline killifish Laimosemion sp. Most sampling localities that were visited in 2021 had signs of anthropogenic impacts such as degragation of the riparian vegetation and litter accumulation (e.g., bottles, plastic bags) (Ref. 128833).

species.name: Priocharax varii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected between 14:00 and 17:00 in a small tributary of the Rio Jamari, close to a bush of submerged macrophytes in a slow flowing part of the Rio Preto, approximately 200 m above rapids. It was collected with Apistogramma resticulosa, Axelrodia lindeae, Axelrodia stigmatias, Hemigrammus bellottii, Hyphessobrycon aff. sweglesi, Leporinus sp., Nannostomus trifasciatus, Odontocharacidium aphanes and Satanoperca sp. Three of these species are considered miniature: the characids Axelrodia lindeae, A. stigmatias and the crenuchid Odontocharacidium aphanes. This species and the three miniatures are mostly transparent, and with the larger Hemigrammus bellottii which has a predominantly translucent body in life, an ‘almost invisible league’ for the Rio Negro was proposed by Carvalho et al., 2006 (Ref. 128847 in Ref. 128819).

species.name: Priolepis ailina

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Priolepis boreus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Priolepis cinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hides in caves and crevices (Ref. 9710), also among corals or rock (Ref. 37816). Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottom at depths between about 40 and 100 m (Ref. 75864).

species.name: Prison goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic, intertidal in pools, sometimes in mud (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Pristella ariporo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a flooded savannah associated with the Rio Aiporo (Ref. 128489).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens have been collected in rocky areas at 100-200 m depth.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Privitera's fairy basslet
species.description: Collected on a very steep reef with ledges and caves and observed in aggregations within about a meter of the substratum (Ref. 48242). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).  FishBase common name coined by authors.

species.name: Problematic lanternfish
species.description:

species.description: Espèce de poissons. During rainy season, has been collected in tangled roots of epiphytic plants that support a diverse fish assemblage.  Feeds on insect larvae  and parts (Ref. 102656).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Proeutropiichthys macropthalmos

species.name: Proserpine shiner
species.description: Found in rocky runs and pools of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Benthic insectivore.  Feeds on dipterans, lepidopterans, trichopterans, ephemeropterans, and coleoterans (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Prosomyleus rhomboidalis
species.description: Occurs along the calm banks of main rivers and also near the rapids. During the rainy season when growth is maximal, it feeds on fruits and consumes the seeds of palm trees like Euterpa oleracea, Taralea oppositifolia, Mauritia flexuosa and other plants like Inga sp. and Psidium sp. which they crush with their strong jaws. During the dry season, their diet consists more of aquatic plants like Mourea fluviatilis and Apinagia richardiana and gastropods and fish (Ref. 12225). Its flesh is excellent but it is preferable not to consume it at the end of the rainy season because then its flesh is very high in fat (Ref. 27188).

species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in middle reaches of rivers and main tributaries, in piedmont, with moderate to swift current, over gravel bottom.  Occurs in groups.  Omnivorous, feeding mainly on aquatic insects and epilithic algae.  Undertakes small spawning migration in large groups towards main tributaries. Spawns in swift current on gravel (Ref. 59043).  Reported to spawn in March-May (Ref. 26100) and in May-June (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to the introduction of other species and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers areas with gravel and overhanging vegetation in slower places of swift, clear streams; rocks and gravel usually coated with detritus.  Dives into the substrate when threatened, with its eyes, mouth and first dorsal fin above the gravel.  Feeds mainly on small freshwater crustaceans, especially transparent shrimp which are abundant. Ref. for amphidromous (Keith et al, in press 2014).

species.description: Collected in one sample at 113 m on a coarse sand bottom with many deep sea oyster shell remains (Neopycnodonte cochlear). Arnoglossus thori Kyle, 1913 was the most abundant fish species associated with this species (Ref. 106320).

species.name: Protomelas annectens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common at depths of about 10 m.  Prefers shallow water and is usually found together with large, sand-dwelling cichlids.  Opportunistic feeder that is attracted to any moving object that stirs up some sediment (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Protomelas dejunctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed feeding on plankton in the water column and foraging on attached algae.  Males establish breeding territories on rocks; one female captured had young in her mouth (Ref. 26731).

species.name: Protomelas kirkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow vegetated inshore areas of the lake where it is commonly found around patches of Vallisneria. Feeds on invertebrates including the small gastropod, Gabiella stanleyi (Ref. 267).

species.name: Protomelas krampus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is observed feeding on eggs and fry while stealing them from mouth-brooding females of other cichlid species; the paedophage rams these females from above on the snout and the brooding females may release some eggs or larvae upon this impact; the brood can then be snatched by Protomelas krampus (Ref. 122325). The inclined position of the mouth enables the fish to immediately grab the brood since it is already in a good position relative to the prey after ramming from above (Ref. 122325).

species.name: Protomelas labridens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in relatively shallow water (Ref. 267).  Feeds on small snails and invertebrates found on the vegetation (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Protomelas macrodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the two specimens collected was from an extensive shallow sandy area with Vallisneria beds. Stomach content consisted of a gastropod and a ceratopogonid larva (Ref. 267).

species.name: Protomelas marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow vegetated areas.  Feeds on algae and debris of vascular plants.  Ingestion of small invertebrates is possibly incidental (Ref. 267).

species.name: Protomelas pleurotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in vegetated areas between rocks and sand.  Feeds on invertebrates that it locates in the sand by blowing into the upper sediment layer (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Protomelas similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow vegetated areas; feeds on macrophytes and algae (Ref. 267).

species.name: Protomelas spilonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors a sediment-free rocky habitat, where it stays in midwater about one meter away from the substrate.  Is normally found just below the surface, rarely deeper than 5 m.  Mostly seen at places where the rocky coast drops steeply.  Feeds on invertebrates taken from the water and on insects that fall into the water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Protomelas spilopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon.  Structure of mouth and pharyngeal dentition suggest that it is a paedophage (Ref. 267).  Mouthbrooding by females (Ref. 53335).

species.name: Protomelas triaenodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been caught over sandy bottoms (Ref. 5595).  Frequently taken in ad hoc trawl hauls at 10-15 m but has been found at 35 m (Ref. 267).

species.name: Protoptère éthiopien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit river and lake fringes, swamps and floodplains (Ref. 28714). In the Lake Victoria basin found in open lakes and marginal swamps, while in the Lake Tanganyika basin only found near rivers and deltas (Ref. 4967). Juveniles occur in matted roots of papyrus (Ref. 34291). Adults able to survive in streams and swamps that are completely dry for long periods of the year, withstanding desiccation on floodplains by aestivating in cocoons until the next rains, breathing air by a small passage leading to the outside (Ref. 45484). Obligate air-breather (Ref. 126274) under laboratory conditions (Ref. 34291), but under certain conditions lungfish in the wild may not be obligate air-breathers and the use of aerial respiration may be a function of ecological as well as physiological factors (Ref. 58531). Mature individuals breed during the flood season (Ref. 28714). One or several females spawn in burrows which are dug and cleaned by the male, who later guards the eggs and the young. Principal diet of adults and sub-adults consists of mollusks, but small fishes and insects are also eaten in small quantities; young individuals less than 35 cm TL feed almost exclusively on insects (Ref. 34291).

Males reaches maturity at ca. 83-98 cm TL; smallest known specimen at 24 cm TL; hatching size possibly at ca. 24 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

Found in deep rubble slope areas on reefs, the first specimen collected by the 1997 ‘Twilight Zone’ Expedition (BPBM, John Earle diving with Richard Pyle) at 80 to 90m depth in the famed Blue Holes dive site in Palau. Several individuals have been collected for the aquarium trade from similar depths in Majuro. However, the particularly deep habitat is very poorly sampled and surveyed and that the species may well have a wider range. Another deep-water wrasse, Cirrhilabrus earlei was also discovered on the same dive in Palau as P. zeus, and is also collected for the aquarium trade by the same commercial collectors in Majuro, and these are mainly shipped to Japan (Ref. 102105).

species.name: Pseudolaguvia muricata

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in large and medium-sized rivers (Ref. 12693).  Found in rapids and in deeper slower reaches (Ref. 37771).  Common in the middle Mekong before the flood season where it is found in the lower reaches of tributary streams along with most of the cyprinids which would be found in the main stream of the Mekong when the water is clear.  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects along with small amounts of plant matter.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pseudolaubuca engraulis

species.name: Pseudolithoxus kinja
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow (depth <1.5 m), fast-flowing water over a substrate of eroded bedrock, living among narrow cracks between rocks, and were abundant at the sampling site. However, this type of habitat was not frequently encountered on the lower Nhamunda, and the species was not found associated with more common woody-debris sites, or rocky sites lacking any appreciable water current. Water temperature 28.3C and conductivity 6 mS/cm. Syntopic fishes encountered during the night survey were species of Leporinus, Symphysodon, Cichla, Pimelodella, Tatia, Dekeyseria, Peckoltia, Lasiancistrus, and this species was the dominant loricariid in this habitat (Ref. 119352).

species.name: Pseudophallus elcapitanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from rivers and coastal creeks of low to moderate current velocity.  Generally occurs near shorelines among grasses or undergrowth.  Sometimes found in tidelands near stream outlets; in rivers it reaches 20 m elevation.  Food consists of small aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).  Probably reaching 19-20 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 9-10 cm SL.

species.name: Pseudophallus mindii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens were collected from freshwater habitats, but there are some caught from estuaries and mangrove areas; while planktonic juveniles have been collected well offshore at sea.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Brooding males present in collections from all months except November, December, February, and May (Ref. 30499).

species.name: Pseudophallus starksii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, streams or upper reaches of estuaries.  Maximum upstream elevation of 61 m.  Most common in depths less than 3 m.  One specimen reported from a presumably marine habitat.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pseudophoxinus callensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudophoxinus drusensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large dense populations, among stones and vegetation, in small ponds and streams.  Feeds on plants and small animals.  Spawns between April and June.

species.name: Pseudoqolus koko
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in main river channel on a stony substrate at two meters depth (Ref. 90183). Collected together with the hypostomins Hemiancistrus medians, Peckoltia otali and Pseudancistrus barbatus, and with the loricariins Harttia guianensis, Loricaria cataphracta and Rineloricaria stewarti (Ref. 90183). The gut contents of one specimen consisted mostly of intact sponge fragments and spicules (Ref. 117193).

species.name: Pseudorasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in a wide variety of habitats, most abundantly in well vegetated small channels, ponds and small lakes (Ref. 59043).  Adults occur in cool running water.  Feed on small insects, fish and fish eggs (Ref. 30578), and plant material (Ref. 59043).  Usually breed in habitats with still or very slow-flowing water (Ref. 59043).  Females spawn 3-4 times in a season (Ref. 59043).  Males clear the surface of the spawning site and guard the eggs until they hatch (Ref. 59043).  Regarded as pest which competes with the fry of other species due to its high reproductive rate (Ref. 1739).

species.name: Pseudorasbora elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorasbora interrupta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorasbora pugnax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep irrigation canals and ponds (1-2 m depth) with emergent plant growth.  Spawns from late March to early July and preferentially lays eggs under stones (< 200 cm3 volume) in shallow water (< 40 cm depth)  (Ref. 103407).

species.name: Pseudorestias lirimensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorhombus binii

species.name: Pseudorhombus ctenosquamis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorhombus megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 9774).  Feeds on crustaceans and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Pseudorhombus micrognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorhombus neglectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, on mud and sand bottoms of continental shelves (Ref. 9774).  Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9774).  Marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Pseudorhombus oculocirris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorhombus russellii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudorhombus tenuirastrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Feeds on small benthic animals.  Caught mainly with prawn and bottom trawls.

species.name: Pseudorinelepis genibarbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small sluggish streams, floodplain lakes and large rivers generally in very soft water (Ref. 89711). Water quality measurements from Ushpa Caño showed that the water was very low in oxygen, but neutral (pH 7.0). Was observed to breathe air and when disturbed, would swim through the water column remaining neutrally buoyant.  The species is not an obligate air-breather and does not routinely gulp air in well-oxygenated aquaria. Minimum temperature from Ref.13614.

species.name: Pseudoscopelus aphos

species.name: Pseudoscopelus cordilluminatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A meso- to bathypelagic, from 537 to 1164 m (mean 954 m) (Ref. 85782).

species.name: Pseudoscopelus lavenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to bathypelagic; from 325 to 2700 m (mean 1631 m) (Ref. 85782).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to bathypelagic, from 893 to 1223 m (mean 1027 m) (Ref. 85782).

species.name: Pseudoscopelus pierbartus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to bathypelagic; juveniles are known from 50 to 1025 m (Ref. 85782).

species.name: Pseudoscopelus sagamianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudoscopelus scriptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A meso- to bathypelagic species found at 250-1,370 m (mean 786 m); juveniles to about 30.0 mm are known from 95 to 590 m (Ref. 85782).

species.name: Pseudoscopelus scutatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudosetipinna haizhouensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudosimochromis babaulti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is one of the smallest and hardiest species in Lake Tanganyika along with Pseudosimochromis marginatum (Ref. 6770). Known from sandy and rocky areas (Ref. 7343). It is very intolerant of any other rockgrazer, less so of the other species, and very territorial and aggressive toward its conspecifics (Ref. 6770). It cleans off a patch of ground between rubble to breed (Ref. 6770). Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Pseudosimochromis curvifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary adults inhabit rubble areas in shallow water, most often not exceeding 10 m depth and never exceeding 10 m.  Feed on the biocover (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Pseudosimochromis margaretae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated areas near the rocks and stones in the littoral region of the lake; area of collection was strewn with harbour debris, and was heavily vegetated with macrophytes and algae-covered rocks; collected at 2-6m depth (Ref. 49183). Inhabits shallow sediment-rich habitats (Ref. 46829). Feeds on algae which is picked from the rocks (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Pseudosimochromis marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Medium-sized fish (Ref. 93886). Inhabits shallow sediment-rich habitats (Ref. 46829). Adults inhabit rubble areas in shallow water, often solitary (Ref. 6770). Feeds on biocover (Ref. 6770), which is picked from the rocks (Ref. 46829). Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Pseudosinocyclocheilus jinxiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep pool of a spring. Syntopic with Cyprinus carpio Linnaeus 1758, Silurus asotus Linnaeus 1758, Carassius auratus (Linnaeus, 1758), Opsariichthys bidens Günther 1873, and Yunnanilus jinxiensis Zhu, Du & Chen, 2009 (Ref. 93154).

species.name: Pseudosphromenus dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic environment (Ref. 41236).  Found in ditches and swamps.  Eggs shrink to the bottom and were then collected by one or both parents and were embedded among the foam bubbles in the nest (Ref. 41595).

species.name: Pseudostegophilus haemomyzon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudostegophilus nemurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is said to become attached to the gills, anal region and fins of dead, dying, or disabled fishes (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Pseudotanganikallabes prognatha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotatia parva
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotocinclus juquiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotocinclus parahybae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotocinclus tietensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotothyris ignota
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal drainages from Iguape in São Paulo state to São João do Rio Vermelho in Santa Catarina state, Brazil. Occurs sympatrically with Pseudotothyris obtusa in small coastal drainages in Iguape, Cananéia, and Ilha Comprida, which are adjacent to Ribeira de Iguape basin (Ref. 116384).

species.name: Pseudotothyris janeirensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a lentic environment, regionally known as açude, a kind of water reservoir. It is uncommon for Pseudotothyris and for the majority of the members of Hypoptopomatinae to occur in this type of habitat (Ref. 116384).

species.name: Pseudotothyris obtusa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotrichonotus altivelis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms of about 30 m depth; has been observed to dive into the sand.

species.name: Pseudotrichonotus caeruleoflavus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on  sandy bottoms, usually in areas of cool upwelling (Ref. 118515).

species.name: Pseudotrichonotus xanthotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Pseudotropheus benetos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over the rock-sand interface, sand and rocky habitats (Ref. 26078). An algae browser with a long, beak-like snout occurring in the upper rocky habitat (Ref. 80784).

species.name: Pseudotropheus brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the sediment-free rocky habitat in the upper 3 m.  Tends to hide in caves and crevices.  Feeds on ants, flies, algae and plankton taken from the stirred-up material in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus crabro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in all kinds of habitats but if most frequently found in large caves or near large boulders. Feeds on anything that is available but is specialized in cleaning parasites from the catfish Bagrus meridionalis (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus cyaneorhabdos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly observed over small to medium sized rocks between 5 and 10 mm.  Typically feeds on zooplankton and epibenthic invertebrates.

species.name: Pseudotropheus elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In some places, this species commonly inhabits open sandy areas which are usually below 10 m (Ref. 6256 mentions samples caught in trawls from 6-76 meters). It feeds by picking invertebrates from the silty layer that covers the sand in many places (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus fuscoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the upper part of the sediment-free rocky habitat, where it remains very close to the rocks.  Rarely found below 5 m.  Feeds on algae (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus galanos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotropheus interruptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found over large rocks and slabs at depths ranging from 5 to 12 meter (Ref. 26078). It reportedly feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 26078).

species.name: Pseudotropheus livingstonii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives mainly over sand where it finds refuge in the empty shells of the gastropod, Lanistes nyassanus. Also found in intermediate habitats and rarely over rocks. Usually territorial over gastropod shells. When found away from its shell, it is usually solitary or in small groups of less than 5 individuals. Feeds from sand, taking epipelic algae (Ref. 6256).

species.name: Pseudotropheus lucerna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among the beds of Vallisneria in sheltered bays. Feeds by brushing loose algal strands from rocks, sand, and plant leaves (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus novemfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow areas in sheltered bays.  Stays mainly in the upper 4 m and lives close to small rocks and vegetation.  Feeds on loose algae taken from plant leaves (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotropheus perileucos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed over rock-sand interface as well as purely rocky habitats.  Feeds on attached algae, in the sand substrata, and on plankton (Ref. 26078).

species.name: Pseudotropheus perspicax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotropheus purpuratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pseudotropheus tursiops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the upper part of the sediment-free rocky habitat.  Found mostly on exposed rocky shores with a mean depth of 5 m.  Feeds by combing loose strands of algae from the biocover (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Pseudotrypauchen multiradiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by trawl in 9-12 fathoms over muddy bottom. Associated fishes include Saurida, Platycephalus, , Kuhlia, Trichiurus, Aluterus, Lagocephalus, apogonids, and cynoglossids (Ref. 45319).

species.name: Pseudotylosurus angusticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pseudotylosurus microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pseudoxiphophorus attenuata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Psilodraco breviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns apparently during autumn and early winter; hatching probably during winter (Ref. 5192).  Synchronous spawner (Ref. 50743).

species.name: Psilogobius randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Psilorhynchus amplicephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits river with more water current and sandy bottom.  Prefers sandy substrate with horizontally placed pectoral fin suited to withstand the water flow (Ref. 75068).

species.name: Psilorhynchus arunachalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Psilorhynchus brachyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Psilorhynchus breviminor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from algae mats on which the species seems to be resting/feeding. The type locality is s cool, fast-flowing stream, with sand and gravel substrate, moderately shallow 30 cm deep. Associated to this species include species of the genera Acanthocobitis, Schistura, Danio, Puntius, and Barilius (Ref. 78700).

species.name: Psilorhynchus chakpiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a cool, shaded and swiftly flowing river with a gravel bottom, rocky bed substrate and numerous riffles.  Usually occurs on sandy substrate with pectoral fins spread horizontally while feeding at the bottom and adhering to rocks while at rest (Ref. 93984).

species.name: Psilorhynchus gokkyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Found in a swift-flowing stream with dense bank and overhanging vegetation, and a substrate of sand, gravel and small boulders (Ref. 85329).

species.name: Psilorhynchus hamiltoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Psilorhynchus kaladanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate to fast flowing water with sparse vegetation and a substrate of pebbles, sand, gravel and small boulders (Ref. 102605).

species.name: Psilorhynchus khopai
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate- to fast-flowing sections of the river with sparse vegetation and a substrate of
pebble, sand, gravel and small boulder.  Occurs together with <i>Glyptothorax spp.,  <i>Garra spp., <i>Schistura spp. and <i>Batasio convexirostrum (Ref. 95676).

species.name: Psilorhynchus konemi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Psilorhynchus maculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Psilorhynchus magnaoculus

species.name: Psilorhynchus piperatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Found in a swift-flowing river with dense riparian vegetation and a substrate of sand, gravel and small boulders (Ref. 85329).

species.name: Psilorhynchus rahmani

species.name: Psilorhynchus tenura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams, preferring cobbled substrate.  Found attached to cobbles with their expanded pectoral fins and free swimming in shallow waters with medium flow (Ref. 78734).

species.name: Psilorhynchus tysoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in swift flowing water of shallow to moderate (50-100 cm) depth over a substrate of sand and gravel; water parameters measured at this locality at time of collection include: 21C, pH 7.5, KH 3, GH 0 (Ref. 110241).

species.name: Psilotris boehlkei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in coral-reef habitats (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Psilotris celsus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in coral-reef habitats (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Psilotris kaufmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in coral-reef habitats (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Psychedelic frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found at a depth of 5-7 m, within 100 m of the commercial jetty in the harbor at Ambon City (its type locality that was previously well known to divers as the ‘‘Twilight Zone,’’ because of the presence of many rare animals); currents varied from virtually nonexistent to strong; visibility varied between about 10 and 30 m; sea floor in this location slopes gently near shore, but more steeply below 10 m, quickly reaching a depth of 100 m or more; aside from the coral rubble, the bottom was littered with a variety of human refuse; and both individuals were consistently found hidden among coarse coral rubble, usually encrusted with ascidians, sponges, and coralline algae (Ref. 80493).

species.name: Psychrolutes inermis
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes.

species.name: Psychrolutes macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes.

species.name: Psychrolutes marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes. Feeds mainly on benthic animals, polychaetes, small crustaceans, and mollusks (Ref. 27363).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Richard Field, pers. comm., 2000).

species.name: Pteragogus aurigarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaweed beds and rocky reefs (Ref. 42722).

species.name: Pteragogus clarkae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pteragogus trispilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with rotenone or spear in areas with sand bottom with detached brown algae or small coral patches and rocks.  A very cryptic species, hence difficult to photograph underwater. The small sample of stomach contents from the holotype contained foraminiferans and from the 7.35 cm paratype consisted mainly of crushed remains of small gastropods, some foraminiferans, and unidentified crustacean fragments, including a small crab chela. Also from the very large stomach of the 4.4 cm paratype, it was found to contain the remains of a moderately large shrimp, so this fish does not feed exclusively on tiny prey (Ref. 93522).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Pteragogus variabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptereleotris cyanops
species.description:
This species was collected from the bycatch landings of single day trawlers operated at the 
depth of 30-40 m along the Chennai coast at the distance of 20 to 60 km, which stretches from Mahabalipuram in south to Ennore in Northern Tamil Nadu, Bay of Bengal (the area is characterized by natural boulders and coral reefs) (Ref. 123270).

species.name: Ptereleotris melanopogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand or sand and rubble bottoms.  Burrows occasionally. Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Pterobrycon landoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterochromis congicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly a predatory species (Ref. 52307). Minimum TL was recorded at 17.5 cm (Ref. 5685).

species.name: Pterocryptis anomala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer boulder-strewn, fast-flowing streams (Ref. 55706).  A nocturnal species which hides among rocks and submerged plant roots during the day (Ref. 55706). Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Pterocryptis barakensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterocryptis berdmorei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterocryptis bokorensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small upland streams (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pterocryptis burmanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterocryptis cochinchinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit streams.  They feed actively at night on small fish, crustaceans and insects.

species.name: Pterocryptis gangelica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams with gravelly and sandy bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pterocryptis indica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams with gravel bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Pterocryptis inusitata

species.name: Pterocryptis torrentis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in small  fast flowing upland streams (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Pterocryptis verecunda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterocryptis wynaadensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast flowing rivers, canal and streams, hides in holes and rocks.  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 44149, 44151).

species.name: Pterodoras rivasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterogobius elapoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hover along rocky shores.

species.name: Pterogobius virgo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms.

species.name: Pterogobius zacalles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow rocky bottoms from 5m down to 30 meters (Ref. 37679).  They are solitary dwellers and live around nests buried under stones (Ref. 37679).

species.name: Pterogobius zonoleucus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools near rocky shores.

species.name: Pterolebias hoignei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shaded pools (Ref. 13284).  Bottom spawner, 7 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pterolebias phasianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Pterolebias zonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in open sunlit waters (Ref. 13284).

species.name: Pteronemacheilus lucidorsum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a fast flowing stream about 4-10 m wide and 0.5 m deep during late dry season.  The stream has substrate consisting mainly of stones up to 60 cm diameter (Ref. 87201).

species.name: Pteronemacheilus meridionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits river with slow current and occurs in the crevices of gravel (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Pterophyllum altum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  May reach about 20 cm in height (Ref. 12251).  Maximum length 18 cm TL (Ref. 13371).

species.name: Pterophyllum leopoldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.

species.name: Pteropsaron dabfar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by a beam trawl over hard, sandy, rocky bottom (Ref. 95663).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be found in rivers with strong current but prefers backwaters (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on detritus and periphyton on submerged trunks and aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Pterygoplichthys weberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pterygotrigla urashimai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit gravel bottom of streams (Ref. 9671).  Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Ptychidio longibarbus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychidio macrops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Ptychobarbus dipogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychobarbus kaznakovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in main streams and tributaries of large rivers (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Ptychocharax rhyacophila
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear streams with sand and granitic rocks bottoms covered by dense mats of the plant <i>Apinaga multibranchiata (Podostemaceae) in areas of fast water.  Feeds on larvae of aquatic insects such as simuliids and trichopterans that were found among the podostemacean plants.  A few ants and spiders were also found in the stomachs.

species.name: Ptychochromis curvidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromis ernestmagnusi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a region which is characterized by humid, lowland rainforest; with a steep overall profile, and a generally rocky to sandy substrate (Ref. 83427).

species.name: Ptychochromis grandidieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromis inornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected in shallow, clear, moderate to swift flowing water; also from deeper pools or from under overhanging banks and vegetation.  Diet highly variable, apparently an omnivore (Ref. 41510).

species.name: Ptychochromis insolitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromis loisellei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromis mainty
species.description: Diet is largely unknown, but stomach contains gastropod shells (Ref. 105395).

species.name: Ptychochromis makira
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Although once common throughout the region of Maroansetra, Ptychochromis makira has suffered a severe decline in abundance in recent years, according to local fishermen (Ref. 57663). They report that the species is now rare (Ref. 57663).

species.name: Ptychochromis oligacanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromis onilahy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromoides betsileanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ptychochromoides itasy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The largest specimen caught was in the immature stage (Ref. 53256).

species.name: Ptychochromoides vondrozo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the deep, seasonally turbid, and moderate to fast-flowing rivers in the immediate vicinity of Vevembe (Ref. 39915). These habitats are characterized by a relatively sandy substrate, with regions of small to large rocks and boulders, where there are areas of relatively still water and deep pools, in addition to swift flowing water (Ref. 39915). Specimens were captured with hook and line using Odonata larvae (Ref. 39915).

species.name: Ptérois nain
species.description: Common in reef flats and shallow lagoons, in areas with weed-covered rocks on sandy substrates.  Adults often found on sponges and juveniles are sometimes found in small aggregations on remote bommies with 10 or so individuals (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal.  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Ptérois ocellé
species.description: An uncommon inhabitant of clear waters rich in corals to depths of  40 m or more.  Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972). Secretive and usually observed at night.  During the day in caves and sponges, and usually well out of sight (Ref. 48635).  Venomous spines.

species.name: Ptérois zèbre
species.description: Found on coral, rubble, or rock bottoms of reef flats (Ref. 9710); also in coastal to outer reef habitats in sheltered lagoons and in caves, sometimes in small aggregations.  Usually shallow, from 3-60m (Ref. 30874) but also reported to 80 m depth.  Pelagic stages travel great distances and expatriate to sub-tropical zones (Ref. 48635).  Spawned in captivity (Ref. 37816).  Spines with poison glands (Ref. 125576).

species.name: Ptérois à antennes
species.description: Poisson. Occurs in lagoon and seaward reefs.  Hides in crevices under rocks and coral formations during the day and hunts at night.  Typically with head towards the safety of their hide-out or narrow passage (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on shrimps and crabs.  Venomous and capable of inflicting a painful sting.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.  Solitary or in groups, under ledges and holes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Puan spine loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puck pinnata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably bathypelagic.

species.name: Pudgy pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef caves and crevices in 8-70 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Puerto Rico coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known from a single male specimen collected over sand and rock covered with calcareous algae and not on coral reefs (Ref. 55786).

species.name: Puffcheek blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from rocky and rubble shores with algal mats to reefs and seagrass beds.

species.name: Pug-headed mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal and amphibious air-breather that actively shuttles back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Pug-nosed pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in grass beds (Posidonia and Zostera). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may be brooding at 13.85 cm SL.

species.name: Puget Sound rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reefs and rocky shorelines and found in loose congregations hovering above the bottom or resting among caves and crevices (Ref. 27436).  Seeks shelter in areas of strong current (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Flesh is tasty and flaky, but since it is rarely caught, it is seldom used as a food fish (Ref. 2850, 27436).  May be used as bait for large rockfish, lingcod or cabezon (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Puget Sound sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal and subtidal areas, on rocks or vertical rock faces (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Pugheaded pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154). Associated with dendrophyllid corals and the coral Galaxea musicalis (Ref. 1602, 37816). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pugjaw wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in soft muddy and sandy bottoms in shallow waters.

species.name: Pugnose bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pugnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate sponge dwellers. Live deep within canals of the sponges, near the openings to the incurrent canals. Sponges provide species with protection from predators and an available food source in many invertebrates. Eggs found within sponge or small plankton brought through incurrent pores (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Pugnose grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Closely related to S. hirundo (eastern Atlantic) and S. pumiliceps (Indian Ocean). A more thorough study using adequate numbers of specimens should be done to distinguish the three.

species.name: Pugnose pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A semi-pelagic and insular species commonly found in shallow turtle-grass beds (Ref. 5521).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pugnose shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually occur over sand and mud in clear vegetated lakes and vegetated pools and runs of creeks and rivers.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pumpkin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pundamilia igneopinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in rocky substrates.  Inhabits moderately steep ( restricted to slightly offshore areas beyond 2 m depth) and steep rocky shores (inhabiting immediately inshore waters where it lives in deep and wide gaps between big boulders) with medium sized to very big boulders.  Feeds on algae and detritus.

species.name: Pundamilia macrocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptically, most likely solitarily living species.  Inhabits moderately steep and steep rocky shores at depths between 2 and at least 10 m.  On moderately steep slopes it is usually encountered somewhat offshore.  On steep slopes it occurs immediately inshore among boulders and in deep rock pools, sometimes at less than 2 m depth.  Feeds on insect larvae, epilithic sponges, ostracods, plankton, detritus and snails.

species.name: Pundamilia nyererei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the close vicinity of rocky shores and rocky islands (Ref. 4983).  Feeds on algae and insects (Ref. 13624).

species.name: Pundamilia pundamilia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Confined to rocky substrates.  A cryptic species inhabiting moderately steep and steep shores with medium to large boulders, where it lives in large crevices between rocks, predominantly in shallow waters and in rock pools within emerged rocky reefs.  Feeds mainly on benthic insect larvae, especially Ephemeroptera, but occasionally takes zooplankton, small fish and Bryozoa.

species.name: Pungitius bussei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pungitius hellenicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit spring-fed streams and ponds, with temperature rarely rising above 20° C and dense vegetation.  Feed on small aquatic invertebrates and fish larvae.  Spawn in May-June.  Males build a nest and guard the eggs until hatching.  Threatened due to habitat alteration and water abstraction.  Attain a maximum size up to about 4.5 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Pungitius modestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams and ponds that are refreshed by abiundant cold spring water from the bottom with temperatures ca. 16°C year-round. This fish tends to hide in water grasses and usually remains still, suspended just above the bottom. The adults feed mainly on amphipods (e.g. Jesogammarus jesoensis) that are extremely abundant in the type locality. The larvae, on the other hand, feed on tubificids, while 30-day old juveniles on chrironomids and copepods. Breeding season peaks in May, with courtship behavior occurring at night, but may also be observed in the daytime. Reported observation stated that usually, females spawn at night between 21:00 and dawn (Ref. 124673).

species.name: Pungitius polyakovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pungitius stenurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pungtungia herzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pungtungia hilgendorfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pungtungia shiraii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pungu maclareni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in smaller groups (Ref. 52307) in shallow waters of lake shore (<4 m deep)(Ref. 26185). Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (mayfly, caddis and chironomid midge larvae) (Ref. 26185) and the endemic sponge Corvospongilla thysi (Ref. 53950, 58527, 81260), but diatoms and terrestrial macrophytes are also sometimes eaten in quantity (Ref. 26185). Maternal (Ref. 52307) mouthbrooder (Ref. 13614, 52307, 58527).

species.name: Pungwe chiselmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky rapids of cool, clear mountain streams (Ref. 52193). It scrapes algae and insects from the rocks (Ref. 52193). Breeds in spring-summer, young found in deep pools below rapids (Ref. 7248, 52193). Occasionally caught by anglers and subsistence fishers (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Punjab razorbelly minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntang goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102). Inhabits muddy bottoms of shallow, turbid marine to brackish coastal inlets and estuaries.  Also lives in shallow coastal waters, large tidal pools, mangroves, siltty lagoons and brackish lakes (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Puntigrus anchisporus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntigrus navjotsodhii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntigrus partipentazona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits midwater to bottoms depths of small streams and weedy impoundments.  Most abundant in impoundments with dense growth of aquatic macrophytes.  Feeds mainly on zooplankton, along with some aquatic insect larvae and plant matter (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Puntigrus pulcher
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntio barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntioplites bulu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at midwater to bottom depths in large lowland rivers and lakes.  Moves into the flooded forests when water levels are high, feeding mainly on submerged plants as well as on some filamentous algae and insects which occur on the plants.  Feeds also on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 56749).  Formerly common, but has become very rare recently (Ref. 12693).  Spawns in rivers (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Puntioplites falcifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large upland rivers. Seems to avoid standing water. Little is known about its biology. Like other members of the genus, it probably feeds mainly on plant matter and occasionally on insects and insect larvae (Ref. 12693). Also reported to prefer deep pools in the river and to migrate into streams, canals and lakes during the flood season. Migrates in large schools (Ref. 37770). Migrates together with Cosmochilus harmandi, Cirrhinus spp., Labeo chrysophekadion and Bangana sp (Ref. 37770). Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Puntioplites proctozystron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large, slow flowing rivers (Ref. 43281).  Commonly found in standing and slowly moving water of streams, canal, ditches and reservoirs.  Moves into flooded forests and marshes during high water periods.  Usually occurs around submerged aquatic or inundated terrestrial vegetation where it consumes some algae but mostly insects and zooplankton.  Larger fish are marketed fresh while smaller ones are used to make prahoc along the Tonlé Sap, Cambodia (Ref. 12693).  Reaches more than 30 cm in length (Ref. 4792).

species.name: Puntioplites waandersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large river habitats.  Primarily herbivorous, feeding on aquatic macrophytes, inundated terrestrial vegetation and filamentous algae along with some insects (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Puntius ambassis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and ponds in the plains (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius aphya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius arenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius bramoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius brevis
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Usually found in slow moving or standing water (Ref. 27732).  Occurs in floodplains, canals, ditches and small sluggish streams.  Proliferates in impoundments, and lives in areas with abundant aquatic vegetation.  Feeds on crustaceans, tubificid worms, algae and zooplankton.  Moves into newly inundated land during flood season and spawns there (Ref. 12693, 57235).

species.name: Puntius burmanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius cauveriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius crescentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius didi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stream with fast flowing, clear, brownish water and with bottom consisted of mud mixed with stones (Ref. 54351).

species.name: Puntius erythromycter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius jerdoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits running waters (Ref. 4832).  Occurs in deeper part of large streams below the ghats (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on debris, leaf litter and other plant matter; column and bottom feeder (Ref. 44149).

species.name: Puntius katolo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius khohi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius madhusoodani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius mahecola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow-flowing sand-mud substrate parts of rivers, in water up to a depth of about 2 m (Ref. 55031).

species.name: Puntius manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius masyai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small streams and weedy lakes.  Occurs from midwater to bottom levels in shallow water.  Feeds on small crustaceans, worms and zooplankton (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Puntius meingangbii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius melanostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius morehensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius mudumalaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hill streams (Ref. 41236).  Reported to reach 225 cm (may be an error) (Ref. 43637).

species.name: Puntius muzaffarpurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius nangalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits littoral areas of lakes (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius narayani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius padamya
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in an artificial pond (Ref. 79001).

species.name: Puntius parrah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water streams and inundated paddy fields (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius paucimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius pinnauratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius pugio
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds and streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Puntius punjabensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius sealei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from rivers and streams (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Puntius snyderi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius sophoroides
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius speleops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only known cave fish in the genus Poropuntius. Apart from reduction of eyes and pigmentation, this species has not deviated greatly from riverine surface-dwelling species of the genus (Ref. 35912).

species.name: Puntius spilopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius stigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius takhoaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius tetraspilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius thelys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puntius ticto
species.description: Poisson. Found in still, shallow, marginal waters of tanks and rivers, mostly with muddy bottoms.  They browse close to the substrate in shallow water.  Feed on crustaceans, insects and plankton.  About 150 eggs are laid in batches of about 20 at a time; eggs hatch in about a day, and fry are free-swimming the next day.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Puntius waageni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Punyit dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Pura chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sloping, rocky bottom exposed to strong currents (Ref. 78145).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Pure cusk
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Purity snailfish
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Purple brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Inhabits rocky areas of shallow waters (Ref. 2850).  Hides in dark caverns and crevices during the day, active at night (Ref. 2850).  Gives birth to live young (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Purple chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Purple dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms groups among branches of Acopora coral, inhabits sheltered reefs in 8-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Purple eagle ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare offshore species (Ref. 9862).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Purple eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to be an inshore burrower found in muddy benthos (Ref. 120675).

species.name: Purple eyebrowed tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on deep outer reef habitats; flat sandy or weedy areas. Rarely seen by diving and is usually caught on lines from deep water (Ref. 48636). Usually found solitary, in rubble bottoms near seaward reefs. C. melanostigma is a junior synonym (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Purple labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in strong-flowing rocky stretches of larger perennial rivers (Ref. 52193). It grazes algae and `aufwuchs' from rocks and firm surfaces including the backs of hippos, leaving characteristic tracks (Ref. 52193). Migrates upstream in swollen rivers to breed (Ref. 7248, 52193). Can occur as either sail-fin or normal varieties (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Purple mbuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools (Ref. 4364).

species.name: Purple reeffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in steep outer slopes and deeper patch reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Purple sand tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand and rubble patches of steep seaward slopes.  Usually in pairs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Purple spaghetti-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries.  Reported to occur in rivers (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Purple tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitarily in shallow coral reefs and seagrass beds.  Feed mainly on hard-shelled prey including crustaceans, mollusks and sea urchins (Ref. 9823).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  An excellent food fish.

species.name: Purple-black skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Purple-boned wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found 1-2 m above rock and coral bottoms and feeds on zooplankton.  Males territorial and haremic.

species.name: Purple-scaled perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species apparently occurs on rocky reef bottom or slope in the mesophotic zone. Judging from other specimens (Parapercis spp., Plectranthias kamii, P. sheni, Helicolenus hilgendorfii) collected by anglers together with this species, these were taken at depths of 200 m or below (Ref. 124021).

species.name: Purple-tip Anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in trawls at depths ranging from 110-119 m, and with two other species likely form mixed-species aggregations in the water column well above the bottom, feeding on plankton (Ref. 127477).

species.name: Purplebelly skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Purpleface largemouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in a broad range of habitats from mainstream margins to floodplain channels and lagoons; preys on insects and small fish, including mormyrids and barbs, which are taken near the bottom; breeds in spring and early summer at low water before the annual floods arrive; relatively few eggs are laid and mouthbrooded; matures after 1-2 years (Ref. 7248). Agamous, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307). Also caught with drawnets.

species.name: Purplelined wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Purplemask angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710); in ledges and caves (Ref. 48391). A shy species, not easily approached at close range (Ref. 4537). Usually observed singly, almost always upside down in reef caves (Ref. 47838); also forms pairs or small groups (Ref. 48391). Natural diet unknown (Ref. 48391). Sometimes forms hybrids with Centropyge multifasciata (Ref. 48391). Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade.

species.name: Purplemouthed conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms.

species.name: Putao snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Putra’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently rare and relatively deepwater with specimens collected between 35-70 m. It appears to be a solitary species, with only 1 or 2 specimens collected from each site. Three of the collection sites were steep reef walls exposed to significant current, with individual specimens observed perched upright in small crevices in the coralline-algae-encrusted wall. Two other collection sites were in the mixed coral rubble and sand at the base of steep reef slopes in 35 m depth, with individuals resting on top of medium-sized rubble pieces and disappearing under the rubble when closely approached (Ref. 119475).

species.name: Puzanovia rubra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puzanovia virgata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Puzzled toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species.

species.name: Pycnochromis abruptus
