Aggregates in shallow waters ca. 10-20 m deep during summer and autumn months, dispersing to deeper waters during winter (Ref. 114953).  Buries itself with only eyes protruding (Ref. 12951).  Nocturnal, moves to shallow bays at night to feed; prefers worms, but may take juvenile snake eels, anemones, and, small crustaceans (Ref. 12951).  Produces broods of 4 to 15 young (Ref. 26938). Reaches ca. 45 cm TL. Both sexes mature by 27 cm TL; birth size at ca. 11 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Can discharge between 14 and 37 volts.  Contact with the skin can produce a severe electric shock.  In addition to the main electric organ, this species possesses a bilateral accessory electric organ (Ref. 10011) speculated to have a possible role in social communication (Ref. 10489).  Reported to taste good, but not fished commercially.  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Raie électrique géante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water on sandy bottoms, sometimes adjacent to reefs (Ref. 12951).  Found buried in the sand during the day (Ref. 12951).  Moves into shallow bays at night to feed; prefers polychaete worms, but may take sea squirts (Ref. 12951). Produces litters of up to 15 pups. Maturity size of males at ca. 36 cm TL; birth size at ca. 11 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie électrique ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A nocturnal and solitary species found on sand and rock bottoms, in bays and on coral reefs (Ref. 12951).  Feeds on small crustaceans, worms, and fishes (Ref. 37955). The smallest adult males known ca. 15 cm TL, females ca. 18 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie électrique vermiculée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, on soft bottoms in protected coastal areas. Males mature at ca. 19 cm TL; born at ca. 6 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie épineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on insular shelves and slopes. Mainly feeds on benthic invertebrates and bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Young hatches at ca. 17 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie équatorienne
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Raie étoilée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit inshore waters (Ref. 3167).  Depth range to 170 m (Ref. 04426), and from 333-343 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feed on all kinds of benthic animals (Ref. 3167).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 4.5 cm long and 3.0 cm wide (Ref. 41304). Minimum depth range (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie étoilée antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental and insular shelves, as well as upper slopes. Feeds mainly on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Reaches maturity at 80-90 cm TL; birth size at ca. 20 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsule measures 116.5 mm long and 80.0 mm wide (Ref. 41249). Utilized as fishmeal and possibly not utilized for human consumption due to extreme roughness of its squamation (Ref. 5159).

species.name: Raie-guitare mauritanienne
species.description: A benthic species with presumably very restricted distribution range (Ref. 114953). A larger male of 275 cm TL (without the caudal fin) was observed in March 1998 at Agadir (reported not collected by an IMROP fishery observer).  Caught by trammel net (Ref. 109576). The species was known from a few specimens caught in shallow water in Banc d'Arguin sandy shoal (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raie-papillon bécune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons, but occasionally also in greater depths.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Raie-papillon californienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm-temperate to tropical shallow bays and beaches (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 37955).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Has a small venom apparatus which has limited use as a defense organ (Ref. 37955).  Maximum length reported to reach 150 cm (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Raie-papillon du Natal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs off sandy beaches, muddy estuaries and offshore banks.  Found singly or in large groups (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on a variety of fishes, crabs and polychaete worms (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Ability to change markings and color to blend into environment (Ref. 3263).  Caught by offshore trawlers (Ref. 5578).  Caught by shore anglers, it is prized for its strong fight when hooked, often released (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Raie-papillon glabre
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Prefers neritic waters of the continental shelf and 
usually found on soft bottoms.  May enter brackish 
estuaries or hyper-saline lagoons (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on 
fish and shrimps (Ref. 28587); other crustaceans and clams 
(Ref. 27549). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Generally 
marketed salted (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rail goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Railroad Valley springfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in warm (35°C) springs.  6 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Rainbow cale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly restricted to exposed coastlines with rocky reefs covered with brown macroalgae and areas with broad-leafed seagrasses, such as Posidonia.

species.name: Rainbow characodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear springs with plant growth.  Feeds on algae.

species.name: Rainbow cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and swampy areas with muddy bottoms.  Feeds on considerable ooze, detritus and filaments of algae (Ref. 36880).  Forms pairs; both sexes territorial. Tolerant of high temperatures and able to survive in small water bodies during dry periods. (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rainbow gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rainbow happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors deep permanent floodplain channel and lagoons, with sandy bottom and vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52307). Feeds on aquatic insects, crustaceans and snails (Ref. 7248). Ovophilic, agamous (Ref. 52307) female mouthbrooder (Ref. 7248, 52307). Males construct a nest where the eggs are initially laid; mature at 10-12 cm length; useful snail control agent (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Rainbow jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Rainbow minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over small pebbles in shallow running waters where the bottom is mainly sand (Ref. 4832).  Also found in a slow moving stream with a sandy bed (Ref. 93866).

species.name: Rainbow seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky shores, often at edges of kelp beds, occasionally over sand but not in surf (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).  Caught mostly by rocky shore fishermen.  Aggregates in the fall.

species.name: Rainbow sharkminnow
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Observed over sandy substrate (Ref. 27732).  Found near any type of solid surface at midwater and bottom depths in streams and rivers.  Moves into seasonally flooded habitats and returns to the rivers as floodwaters recede.  Feeds on algae, periphyton, phytoplankton and some zooplankton.  Popular in aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Rainbow shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravelly riffles and pools (sometimes sandy pools) of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in springs, and small, clear streams (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Rainbow slender wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Found in sand patches of shallow reefs but has been reported to occur up to a depth of 100 m (Ref. 530).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rainbow tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rainbow wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs, normally high above the bottom.  Swims with worm-like movements.  Feeds on various invertebrates.  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rainford's butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas of sparse coral growth.  Feed on algae and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 2334).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Heavy algae growth should always be maintained in the aquarium.

species.name: Rainford's dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools among mangroves and in coastal inlets, associate with P. formosus (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Rainfordia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found in caves of coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Secretive (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Rainwater killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated quiet water and usually swims several inches below surface of water.  7 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on larval crustaceans (mainly cyclopoid and harpacticoid copepods), mosquito larvae, small worms, and mollusks (Ref. 79012).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Raja Ampat Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is generally found around isolated, small coral and rock outcrops in both silty and clear water reef environments, usually in about 10-45 m depth (sometimes seen as deep as 60 m).  Occurs solitarily or in small loose groups, is relatively curious and easy to photograph, though it invariably retreats into crevices or under coral heads when approached too closely (Ref. 89094).

species.name: Raja dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered reef slopes (Ref. 44113).  Forms aggregations of 10-20 individuals among branching coral (Ref. 44113).

species.name: Raja rouxi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the shelf and upper slope waters (Ref. 4426).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ram cichlid
species.description: Poisson. Used in behavioral studies (Ref. 4537).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Rama rama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rama Rao's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from both silty sand and rocky bottom; also from areas with coral (Ref. 42181). Inhabits rock or coral bottoms in 1-60 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rambou léopard du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard bottoms (rocks, shell rubble, boulder and gravel strewn slopes).  Glides over the bottom with wave-like motion when moving (Ref. 5227).  Not commonly caught (Ref. 9281).

species.name: Ramcarat grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters, but also entering estuaries (although its tolerance to salinities seems not to have been recorded).

species.name: Ramu rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ranch silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rancurel's lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers and brooks in the swampy rainforest on coastal plains (Ref. 7372, 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Randall's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in inshore and offshore rocky reefs in 5 to 30 meters in small to large aggregations (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Randall's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 12 m (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Randall's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Randall's fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in caves or coral rubble areas along steep drop-offs or channel walls (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found in small groups (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Randall's frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).

species.name: Randall's goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Randall's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral reefs.

species.name: Randall's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Randall's prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on patches of carbonate sand of clear water reefs (Ref. 9710). Usually in rubble caves Lives with an olivaceus prawn with short white transverse marks (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Randall's puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Randall's threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 30573).  No major fishery exists, but a large population is believed to occur in the Persian Gulf.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Randall's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky boulders of exposed coasts (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Randall's viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, found near reef-sand interface (Ref. 34024).  A 3.8 cm SL female specimen found to be gravid (Ref. 34024). Cryptic and solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Randall's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble bottoms (Ref. 11903) and coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Randall’s fold dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Randall’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes, often on rubble, rock and sand bottoms in 6-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Randall’s tilefish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gentle rubble slopes; constructs impressive rubble mounds over its burrows, which range from about 50-70 cm in height and 1.5-2 m in diameter and typically, the fish are seen hovering a short distance from their home mound, with up to six individuals using a single mound.   The fish when approached closely or frightened by spear shots, quickly retreat
into the burrow, which is located near the apex of the mound (Ref. 85568).

species.name: Ranong guitarfish
species.description: Caught individuals: males at 49.4 and 50.3 cm TL were immature and the largest female (51.1 cm TL) was most probably at late adolescent or early mature stage of development (Ref. 123963).

species.name: Ranta Goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ranzania
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 2850), epipelagic (Ref. 2340), and generally solitary (Ref. 9317).  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 4424).

species.name: Rao's hover goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove swamps and inlet waters (Ref. 559); shallow coastal waters with mud, sand, or rock bottoms (Ref. 1602). Forms aggregations near surface (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Rapa Nui splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a rocky patch reef surrounded by a large sandy area at a depth of 83 m, using hand nets and transported alive to the surface in a perforated-plastic collecting jar (Ref. 120585).

species.name: Rapa triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow depths, including intertidal pools (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical to somewhat flattened (Ref. 240, 94114).

species.name: Rapanui cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rapanui flagtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from along an exposed rocky shore, in large tide pools, and over sand near rocky shores (Ref. 41640).  Often found in aggregations (Ref. 41640).

species.name: Rapanui goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Stomach contents include a juvenile spiny lobster (Panulirus pascuensis) and small crabs (Ref. 54393).

species.name: Rapanui goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected near reef or rocky bottom in depths of 17-21 m (Ref. 41653).

species.name: Rapanui lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on rock and sandy bottom with rotenone and with about 250 m hook and line (Ref. 80927).

species.name: Rapanui nibbler
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rapanui sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rapanui seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rapson's ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rare velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype which may be at a transitory larvae and juvenile stage with a length of 0.85 cm SL (Ref. 35981).  Maximum length value is preliminary and is assumed to be twice the length of the only juvenile specimen reported.

species.name: Rasbora amplistriga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Rasbora api
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel-bottomed mountain streams, moderate flowing turbid rivers, and acidic blackwater peatswamps. Occurs sympatrically with Rasbora jacobsoni, R. truncata, and R. cf. sumatrana in the Kluet and Alas river basins (Ref. 85846).

species.name: Rasbora aprotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora arundinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various types of habitats such as gravel-bottomed mountain streams, moderate-flowing turbid rivers, and muddy backwater pools. Occurs sympatrically with Rasbora api, R. kluetensis (only in the Kluet River), R. jacobsoni, and R. truncata (only in the Alas River) (Ref. 94947).

species.name: Rasbora atranus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora atridorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora baliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora bankanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits forest streams (Ref. 13061).  Restricted in peat, found in marginal areas (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Rasbora bindumatoga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mountain streams and moderate-flowing turbid rivers with gravel bottom. Sympatric with Rasbora api (Ref. 94947).

species.name: Rasbora borneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Kapuas Lakes Area, Kalimantan Barat in Indonesia, it is only collected in the Kapuas mainstream and it is reported to enter lakes during the wet season (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasbora bunguranensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora cephalotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large streams and rivers with black water (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasbora cryptica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora dies
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora dorsinotata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora ennealepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora everetti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora gerlachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora haru
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora hosii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers small creeks with flowing water, often over stony substrate (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasbora hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast flowing areas or near riffles (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Rasbora jacobsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora johannae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small high gradient forest streams with gravel to cobble bottoms and with very little or no emergent aquatic vegetation. Its most common co-inhabitants were the balitorid Nemacheilus spiniferus and the cyprinid Puntius binotatus.

species.name: Rasbora kluetensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs sympatrically with Rasbora api, R. jacobsoni, and R. cf. sumatrana (Ref. 94947).

species.name: Rasbora kobonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Rasbora kottelati
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland streams and swamps, with tannin-stained, brownish to black, acidic freshwater of pH 4.1- 6.1.

species.name: Rasbora labiosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rivers and streams (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Rasbora lacrimula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora laticlavia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small to moderate-sized streams with a good pool riffle structure with pebbly to sandy substrate with many fallen tree trunks.

species.name: Rasbora maninjau
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora meinkeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora nematotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora nodulosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs sympatrically with Rasbora cf. sumatrana in the Seumayam River (Ref. 85846).

species.name: Rasbora notura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora ornata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora patrickyapi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, slow-flowing swampy areas next to the flowing blackwater streams.  Occurs in lowland peat swamps and degraded heath forest with a substrate made of a mixture of peat and silica sand (Ref. 82329).

species.name: Rasbora reticulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora rheophila
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora rubrodorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing waters, ditches and shallow ponds (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Rasbora rutteni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora sarawakensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers moderately fast flowing waters in small forest streams (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasbora semilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora septentrionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is one of the northernmost ranging species of Rasbora (Ref. 36949). Reaches up to at least 5.7 mm SL (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Rasbora spilotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora subtilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Kalimantan Lakes Area in Kalimantan Barat, Indonesia, it is common along lake shores and in shallow, open areas (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasbora sumatrana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and creeks with moderate to swift, relatively cold and well-oxygenated water (Ref. 7050).  Lives in hill streams to lowland peats (Ref. 57235).  Found in medium to large rivers and brooks of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Occurs in running waters of lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).

species.name: Rasbora tawarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora taytayensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora tobana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora trifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora truncata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species mostly inhabits moderate-flowing turbid rivers. In streams with fast-flowing water, it tends to form school at the stream margins or the pool regions along the river banks. It occurs sympatrically with Rasbora api and R. cf. sumatrana (Ref. 94947).

species.name: Rasbora tubbi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora tuberculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, slow to swift water in a small creek in a hilly area, flowing through a succession of riffles over large boulders and deeper pools (Ref. 12804).

species.name: Rasbora vaillantii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora vietnamensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower reaches of rivers, streams with strong current in mountain areas, lakes, and ponds (Ref. 93745).

species.name: Rasbora volzii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora vulcanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora vulgaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rasbora-ciseaux
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in lakes, swamps, slow flowing areas of rivers, usually in open areas (Ref. 27732, 57235).  Seems to prefer habitats in forest (Ref. 56749).  A common resident of surface waters in streams, canals, ditches and occasionally of reservoirs in lowland areas (Ref. 12693).  Inhabits medium to large rivers, flooded fields and brooks of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds mostly on exogenous insects (Ref. 12693), also takes worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Not seen in markets, but popular in aquarium trade (Ref. 12693, 57235).

species.name: Rasborichthys helfrichii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, rivers and streams (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Rasboroides rohani
species.description: Occurs in shallow, slow-flowing, shady streams with sandy-silt substrate and dense leaf litter in submontane forest. Sympatric with other fishes: Pethia nigrofasciata, Puntius titteya, Belontia signata and Rasbora microcephala (Ref. 94541).

species.name: Rascasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on hard bottoms (Ref. 4510).  Feeds on fishes and shrimps (Ref. 5377).  Females appear to remain smaller, up to 38.4 cm TL in the Canary Islands (Ref. 55964).  Males are heavier and larger (Ref. 55965).

species.name: Rascasse (Scorpaena stephanica)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand, mud and rock bottoms (Ref. 2683). Carnivorous (Ref. 43448).

species.name: Rascasse (Trachyscorpia echinata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over muddy sand bottoms (Ref. 4570). Probably oviparous with eggs extruded in floating gelatinous masses. Feeds on deep-sea benthic crustaceans, cephalopods and fishes (Ref. 43448).

species.name: Rascasse aile-longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters.  Found on soft bottom.

species.name: Rascasse arc-en-ciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common but inconspicuous species (Ref. 9341). Found in cracks, crevices, under ledge overhangs and other recesses on rocky reefs, steep slopes, and especially on walls. Small individuals often stay near the protective spines of long spined urchin, Diadema mexicanum (Ref. 5227). Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Rascasse blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand and mud (Ref. 2683).  While buried, it waits for its prey, attracting them by means of its appendage.  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Rascasse bossue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This solitary species inhabits the outer edge of the reef (Ref. 583). Usually beneath ledges or near entrance to caves (Ref. 42181). Benthic (Ref. 58302). A prized food fish with population greatly reduced in main Hawaiian islands due to fishing pressure, especially by spear fishermen. Stomach contents include small fishes (holocentrid, acanthurid and Aulostomus chinensis) (Ref. 42181).

species.name: Rascasse brésilienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in bays, harbors, and on the continental shelf.  Inhabits soft bottoms.  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Rascasse californienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs in rocky areas of bays and along shore, especially in caves and crevices (Ref. 2850).  Prefers depths less than 26 m (Ref. 121641).  An excellent food fish (Ref. 2850).  Venomous spines in the dorsal, anal, and pelvic fins (Ref 13513).  Minimum depth range based on occurrence (Ref. 121641).

species.name: Rascasse crapaud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 9341).

species.name: Rascasse d'Accra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud or sand bottom.  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 4510.  Possibly occurs to a depth of 500 m (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Rascasse d'Angola
species.description: Found on sand or mud bottom (Ref. 4510) of coastal waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Rascasse de Cadenat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually  measures less than 10 cm TL (Ref. 4510).  Occurs on muddy sand and gravel.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 4570).

species.name: Rascasse de Folgor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably found over rough bottom (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Rascasse de Madère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 2683); rocky areas and favours habitats with generous brown algal growth, rocky depressions and ledges and small boulders (Ref. 95708).  Feeds on crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 4570).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Rascasse de Messine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed and captured in rocky caves (J.M.N. Azevedo, pers. comm., 03/02).

species.name: Rascasse de Norman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottom (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Rascasse du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rascasse du Sénégal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow rocky areas (Ref. 4570).

species.name: Rascasse joueur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms between 5 and 157 m depth.

species.name: Rascasse longnez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hard bottom.

species.name: Rascasse maculée de Polynésie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rascasse marbrée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rascasse monchetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are demersal while juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Eggs are probably released in buoyant gelatinous mass (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Rascasse noire
species.description: Found mostly in shallow coral reef and rocky areas.  Lies motionless on the bottom (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mostly on other fishes and crustaceans.  Moderately common below about 5 m depth to at least 55 m.  Displays characteristic bright white spots on dark background of pectoral axil when disturbed (Ref. 49392).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).  Eaten locally and said to taste a bit like chicken.  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Rascasse ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms of the continental shelf.  Primarily known from trawls over prawn-grounds but divers looking in suitable habitats can come across them, especially at night.  During the day it buries itself deep in the sand with just the eyes exposed.  When disturbed, it spreads its long pectoral fins with the bright upper color to deter predators.  It uses its fins to corner prey and has sensitive barbels below the mouth to detect those buried in the substrate (Ref. 48635).  Fin spines venomous (anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406))  (Ref. 30573).  Sold in small quantities either fresh or dried and salted in markets.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Rascasse profonde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Among all scorpionfishes, it is structurally best adapted for mid-water existence (Ref. 11015).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, amphipods and sergestid shrimps (Ref. 28023).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland at least in anal-fin spines (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Rascasse péruvienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 9341).

species.name: Rascasse richichi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Have a thick glandular tissue on posterior margin of fin spines which is believed to be venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Rascasse rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An upper slope species (Ref.  10482).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Rascasse scorpion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water and seaweed-covered reefs as well as on open, sandy areas (Ref. 5592).  An opportunistic predator, this cryptic fish lies unseen on the reef top waiting for small fishes to pass by (Ref. 5592).  Although the flesh is of excellent quality, it is not utilized commercially due to its venomous spines (Ref. 9341).

species.name: Rascasse serran
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom, at a bottom temperature range of about 5.5°-12.5°C and usually at a depth of about 400 m. They live on or near the bottom but feed in the water column (Ref. 47377). Specimens usually brought to the surface with the stomach everted. Stomach contents included parts of bathypelagic crustaceans of family Oplophoridae, Oplophorus sp., and an amphipod (Ref. 11015). Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Sold in small quantities in markets. Minimum depth range taken from Ref. 27000.

species.name: Rascasse sonore
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rascasse tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Rascasse à dos tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Considered a good  food fish (Ref. 9341).

species.name: Rascasse épineuse du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from off Puerto López, Manabí, Ecuador and it is  probably a deepwater species, presumable rarely caught by the longline fisheries off Puerto López.

species.name: Rascasse épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft substrate.  Have a thick glandular tissue on posterior margin of fin spines which is believed to be venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Raseux-de-terre gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers; and shores of lakes (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Raseux-de-terre noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in sandy and muddy, sometimes rocky, pools of headwaters, creeks, and small to medium rivers; and in sandy shores of lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Adults feed on midge larvae, mayfly nymphs, caddis larvae, and microcrustaceans; young on entomostracans and tiny midge larvae (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Rason deux taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably inhabits open sandy bottoms and dives head-first into the sand with the approach of danger (Ref. 5374).  Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Rason ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms of coastal areas and also in areas with some seagrass or algae.  Ranges to a depth of over 18 m (Ref. 9710).  Usually in large spread-out groups on upper slopes of sand and mud banks with males defending its section that has numerous females (Ref. 48636).  Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).  When threatened, it dives head-first into sand; may take some time to emerge again.  Feeds mainly on hard-shelled prey, including mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 5374).  Minimum depth taken from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Rasp coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in association with Acropora loripes and Acropora elseyi; commonly in pairs (Ref. 36585); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Feeds on copepods, forams, and unidentifiable flocculent material (may represent in part the remains of coral tissue) (Ref. 36585).

species.name: Raspback skate
species.description: Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.6-13.2 cm long and 7.6-8.6 cm wide (Ref. 41298, 41253).

species.name: Raspthorn sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.2 cm long and 3.1 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Rasptooth dogfish
species.description: Espèce de requins. Holotype taken from a depth of 360 m (Ref. 26282).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Raspy river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rass' snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rastrinus scutiger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ratabulus megacephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawling at depths of 79 to 261m.  Recorded by Galathea Station 539 as being dredged over gravel (Ref. 9790).

species.name: Ratabulus ventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ratan goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to brackish water habitats (Ref. 92840). Reported to enter fresh waters (Ref. 58342).  Occur inshore, over stones and gravel.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and fish (Ref. 4696).

species.name: Rathbunella alleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ratnagiri minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ratsirakia legendrei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs strictly in freshwaters of highlands and oriental versant (Ref. 6802).

species.name: Rattail skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably taken by offshore trawlers (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ravenous cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Uncommon species found in coastal waters (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy and muddy bottoms of outer continental shelf and upper slope, also found at shallower depth 20m. Feeds mainly on bony fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205); egg cases ca. 20-30 cm long (Ref. 114953). Reaches maturity at ca. 13 years (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Raymond's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear, rainforest creeks over gravel and cobble bottoms (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Razor wrasse fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet sandy bottoms beyond the reef (Ref. 583).  Benthopelagic or benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Razorback sucker
species.description: Occurs in silt-bottomed to rock-bottomed backwaters near strong current and deep pools in medium to large rivers, and impoundments.

species.name: Reader's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from tidal pools, lagoon patch reefs and reef slopes at depths from about 0.3 to at least 30 m (Ref. 59013). Benthic, also found in coral and rock reefs (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Reader's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually found in back reef leeward areas (Ref. 100726).

species.name: Rearbar cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups. Found in caves and ledges in 18-37 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rearfin wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen collected from a rock pool (Ref. 46206).

species.name: Reba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear rivers and tanks, ponds, beels, and inundated fields.  Feeds on plankton and detritus.  Grows fairly rapid.  Breeds in flooded shallows from June to September.  A prolific breeder, laying about 3 million ova per female.  A suitable species for aquaculture.  Contributes 10 to 15% of the fishery in Cauvery.

species.name: Reba carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit large streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).  Also found in tanks, canals, ponds, beels and inundated fields (Ref. 4832, 94287).  Primarily feed on plankton and detritus, but may also take in mud, vegetables, crustaceans and insect larvae (Ref. 4832, 94287).

species.name: Recep's chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift and clear flowing water over cobble and pebbles. Collected together with Capoeta umbla (Heckel, 1843), Cyprinion macrostomum Heckel, 1843, Squalius sp., Oxynoemacheilus sp., Garra rufa (Heckel, 1843) and Garra variabilis (Heckel, 1843) (Ref. 94737).

species.name: Rechin
species.description: Found in coastal and offshore waters but not oceanic (Ref. 5578).  Adults are commonly found at depths of 200-400 m, young in shallower waters (Ref. 5485).  A seasonal migratory species over parts of its range (Ref. 6871).  Common component of the catch of the shark longline fishery (Ref.58048). Feeds on bottom and pelagic bony fish, sharks, skates, rays, cephalopods, gastropods, crustaceans, sometimes mammalian carrion and inorganic objects (Ref. 5578).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449); with litter size number from 3-14 (Ref. 27549).  Large adults are potentially dangerous (Ref. 4716, 6871).  Utilized fresh, dried-salted, frozen and smoked for human consumption; hides for leather; fins for sharks-fin soup; and liver oil extracted for vitamins (Ref. 244).

species.name: Rectoris longibarbus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a temporary pool of water spilled from a karst cave during the annual rainy season. (late June to August). Sympatric with Rectoris posehensis, Yunnanilus jingxiensis, Pseudogyrinocheilus longisulcus and Cophecheilus bamen (Ref. 93096).

species.name: Rectoris longifinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rectoris luxiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Rectoris mutabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rectoris posehensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid current in rivers.  Length type refers to body length.

species.name: Red Anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and lagoon reefs. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Entacmaea quadricolor (usually) and Stichodactyla gigantea (Ref. 5911). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Red barbier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red barred killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivorous and egg-layer.

species.name: Red blotch perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shelf and the shelf edge, on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Food fish.  Found over sandy-silt bottom (Ref. 559).

species.name: Red breast cichlid
species.description: In addition to soft bottoms of the lake, inhabits rivers between 0 and 850 m.  Abounds more in stagnant waters although also found in strong current.  Browse on soft bottoms picking up aquatic insects, especially diptera (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Red brotula
species.description: A common cryptic species (Ref. 34024).  Found in rocky areas (Ref. 2850).  Live-bearers with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36488).  Flesh considered sweet and fine-textured but rarely available (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Red Canarese barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large streams and rivers below the ghats (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Red clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in close association with the sea urchin Echinometra mainly for protection. Feeds primarily on benthic crustaceans like amphipods, but harpacticoid copepods and ostracods are also eaten (Ref. 33548).

species.name: Red coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red deepwater scorpionfish
species.description: Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  The dorsal spine contains poison glands which can inflict painful wounds (Ref. 11015).

species.name: Red devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and rarely enters rivers (Ref. 7335).  Feeds on small fish, snails, insect larvae, worms and other bottom-dwelling organisms (Ref. 44091).  Females tend clutch of eggs (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Red dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A miniature, deep-water species collected at ledge and spur and groove habitats from 12.2-28.7 m and 9.4-10.4 m depths. This species co=exist with Eviota epiphanes in the spur and groove habitat at 12.2-15.2 m but not shallower. It is one of the smaller Eviota species with females having mature eggs at 1.1 cm SL size (Ref. 38034).

species.name: Red eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat unknown.

species.name: Red eye barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly larger, clear-water streams descending from the central mountains, close to the areas in which these reach the coastal floodplain.  Substrates of the these streams are composed of granite, pebble or sand (Ref. 79817).

species.name: Red filament threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms.  Occurs in groups and feeds on small bottom-living animals.  Regarded as a trash fish and used mainly for fish meal or animal feed.

species.name: Red fin barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red fin labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large streams and rivers in the upper reaches (Ref. 41236).  Found in reservoirs and still waters (Ref. 11966).

species.name: Red finned kuruva
species.description: The type locality of this species in Manimal River at Venpala, is less than 50 m wide and 1- 5 m deep; bank height about 1 m with respect to the general water level in summer season. Sediments in this stretch are generally silty clays with occasional patches of sand. The channel bed is blanketed by mud dominated sediments. The stretch of this river is covered by moderately dense riparian vegetation (Ref. 104747).

species.name: Red garra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in different habitats such as rivers, lakes, small ponds, and small muddy streams.  Hides under and among stones and vegetation.  Bottom dweller, feeding on aufwuchs.  Said to also occur in hot ponds where they feed on the skin scales of bathers, reducing illnesses such as neurodermitis.

species.name: Red gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the intertidal and subtidal, in exposed surge areas (tidal surge channels) and to 18 m depth.

species.name: Red gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563). Two forms exist in New South Wales, Australia. The inshore form is dominant in depths less than 300 m and the offshore form is most common in deeper waters (Ref. 30468). Juveniles of both forms are caught near the edge of the continental shelf by fishers targeting royal red prawns (Haliporoides sibogae) in Australia, but their full distribution is unknown (Ref. 6390). Reproduction in ocean perch is distinctive in that fertilization is internal (Ref. 6390, 34817). Feed on squid, shrimps and fish (Ref. 6390). Head and dorsal-fin spines are venomous (Ref. 33616). Sold whole and chilled on the domestic fresh fish markets (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Red handfish
species.description: Espèce de poisson. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Red icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Indian fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Red Irish lord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually near shore in rocky areas (Ref. 2850), from intertidal areas to 275 m depth (Ref. 6793).  Adults feed on crabs, barnacles, and mussels (Ref. 6885).  Good eating (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Red jewelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotype's stomach was examined and found to be empty, with no trace of biological material and the gonads were analyzed macroscopically, indicating it to be an immature female (Ref. 109715).

species.name: Red little gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red lizard fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coastal reef flats (Ref. 48635) in sandy or rocky places.  A carnivore which feeds on fish (Ref. 9137). Pelagic spawner (Ref. 35298).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Red mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and runs over gravel and cobble in clear rivers in forest areas (Ref. 12693).  Omnivorous, feeding on vegetable matter such as fruits, as well as fish, crustaceans and other invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Occasionally caught, but never in large numbers (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Red moki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Red morwong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found on exposed rocky reefs down to about 30 m; juveniles on coastal reefs, amongst algae.

species.name: Red naped wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 42722).

species.name: Red neon blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Pangani barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimens of Barbus venustus were caught in shallow water among open stands of the emergent grass Paspalidium geminatum in the Nyumba ya Mungu reservoir; it was taken in July and August at the onset of the dry season but with the lake level still close to its maximum (Ref. 48244). Gut content includes cladocerans, insect fragments, plant material and fine sand (Ref. 48244).

species.name: Red parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon inhabitant of clear lagoon and seaward reefs, usually seen along drop-offs (Ref. 9710).  Solitary.

species.name: Red patched grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mixed sandy and muddy bottom (Ref. 27973).

species.name: Red pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found offshore, on deep reefs or islands (Ref. 9002).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Red pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Red piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in creeks and interconnected ponds in Matto Grosso, Brazil, where it influences distribution and feeding of other fish (Ref. 9080) and in areas of high primary production in Rio Machado and Rio Negro (Ref.9096).  Adults feed mainly at dusk and dawn.  Feeds on insects, worms and fish (Ref. 7020).  Medium-sized to large individuals (15-24 cm length) forage mainly at dawn, late afternoon and night up to about 2200H, whereas smaller fish (8-11 cm) are active mainly during the day (Ref. 9080).  Teeth replacement on alternating sides of jaw allows continuous feeding.  Its powerful dentition  can inflict serious bites.  Has a highly evolved auditory capacity and  a 'lurking', then 'dashing' behavior during daytime.  Shows hierarchies within small schools (Ref.  9077).  Available information on body composition of 'piranha caju' flesh is 8.2% fat, 15.0% protein and 4.4% ash (Ref. 9251).

species.name: Red rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit a lake in a hilly area of about 75 m elevation.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 100 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Red River pupfish
species.description: Inhabits shallow, sandy pools and runs of headwaters, creeks, and small to medium rivers.  Often found in extremely shallow and hot (to 37°C) water (Ref. 5723).  Consumes midge and other insect larvae (Ref. 79012).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Red River shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy, turbid channels of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on terrestrial insects (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Red rock cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms (Ref. 9563).  Known in shallow estuaries from muddy environments to offshore reefs in kelp reef (Ref. 9002).  Nocturnal species and juveniles are occasionally seen in large rock pools.  Feeds on a wide variety of invertebrates, mainly on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 9003).

species.name: Red sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26334).  Found under stones near the shore to a depth of 140 m.  Most abundant in autumn and winter at  a depth of about 100 m (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Red Sea anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Sea demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Red Sea eightline flasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of seaward reefs to depths greater than 25 m (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Red Sea elongate ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Sea flappy snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is seined on shallow sand bottom, at 0.5-1 m.  Apparently very rare, or rarely encountered by divers or snorkelers, possibly also due to its cryptic burying habits (Ref. 103840).

species.name: Red Sea flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Sea halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common around reefs (Ref. 30573). Max length was from photo contributed by Valeriy Konstantinovitch Biryukov, taken at Hurghada , Egypt.

species.name: Red Sea hardyhead silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on zooplankton, small bottom-living invertebrates (Ref. 5980).

species.name: Red Sea lanternbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red sea lionfish
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottom of coral reefs (Ref. 123589).

species.name: Red Sea longnose filefish
species.description: Inhabits coral rich fringing reefs and feeds on Acropora polyps (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Red Sea mimic blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mimics Meiacanthus nigrolineatus (Ref. 9710). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Red Sea nymph cardinalfish
species.description: This species was observed at night, usually in the vicinity of a cave. A single individual at Dahab was observed solitary, although a large group of specimens was collected from the cave in Obhur, Jeddah suggesting that the species living in small groups in crevices (Ref. 125402).

species.name: Red Sea roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Sea silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by purse and bag seines and rotenone (ref. 92894).

species.name: Red Sea soldierbream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually caught on reefs, and feeds on benthic organisms and according to D. Golani (HUJF), this species is collected in deeper waters at 100-400 m (Ref. 124569).

species.name: Red Sea spiny basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected on a small reef platform (about 3 x 1 m), with small corals on sand, on steep coral reef slope. The coral slope with mixed patches of corals and caves and extended down to a depth of 30 m, becoming a sandy slope below this depth (Ref. 95091).

species.name: Red Sea spiny dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red Sea stonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic inshore on sand and rocky reefs (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Red sea torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Biology little known. Probably reaches ca. 40 cm TL; males mature before 23 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Red Sea whitespotted moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Red Sea worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red seam snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams (Ref. 27732).  Adults inhabit medium to large rivers, brooks, rapid-running mountain streams and stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals (Ref. 12975).  Feed at night on small fish, insects and crustaceans (Ref. 85309).  Exhibit parental care, with the male brooding eggs and fry in his mouth (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Red seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs to at least 35 m depth (Ref. 33839).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Red shiner
species.description: Inhabits silty, sandy, and rocky pools and runs, sometimes riffles, of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Can tolerate siltation and high turbidity (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects, and algae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Red snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red snout emperor
species.description: Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102).  Thought to occur on soft bottoms near reefs and presumed to feed on benthic invertebrates and fish.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Red splodge
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red star-eye dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected or observed across a depth range of 8–30 m and were found under large pieces of coral rubble long a gentle slope on an inner patch reef. These were never observed in the open, but only found under coral rubble and living within the interstices of the reef (Ref. 122934).

species.name: Red stripe barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red striped lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams, brooks, rivers and swamps in drainage basins.  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Red tail wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 58302).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  A single male usually found with a group of females (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Red tailed tinfoil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at midwater depths in large and medium-sized rivers and floodplains.  Feeds on various plant and animal matter.  Commonly found near villages where it feeds on organic detritus disposed of by humans (Ref. 12693).  Reported to be occasionally poisonous, causing vomiting, due the fruits it eats (Ref. 12369).  Colonizes inundated forests and adults migrate back to the river in October.  Young of the year follow thereafter when the water levels recede.  Large-sized  fish are marketed fresh while smaller ones are used to make prahoc and nuoc mam (Ref. 12693).  Popular fish in the aquarium trade where it is sold under the name of "tinfoil barb" (Ref. 12693).  Captured from the wild for the ornamental fish trade in Thailand (Ref. 6459).  Cultured in floating cages in Viet Nam (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Red tonguesole
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone (incl.  semi-enclosed sea areas) on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Red top williamsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in very shallow rocky biotopes, usually at exposed sites.  Mostly found in the upper 2 m.  Feeds mainly from the water column; on plankton when this is available and on insect larvae and other invertebrates that appear in the open water.  Has also been observed feeding from the biocover on the rocks (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Red triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually solitary on corals and rocks in lagoons and bays from 0.5-12 m or deeper (Ref. 88983).

species.name: Red velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef and weed beds (Ref. 75154) of inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Red Victoria nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in marginal, ephemeral, zones of permanent water bodies such as flowing creeks in papyrus swamps, small streams and dead river branches (Ref. 26661, 59344). Usually inhabits the more shallow and quiet parts between bordering vegetation; occasionally in temporary pools (Ref. 26661). Occurs in low water temperatures (21.8°C on average) (Ref. 97291). Incubation period of eggs in captivity is 4-8 weeks and young reach maturity at about 8 weeks (Ref. 59344). Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Red viviparous brotula
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024). Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices to at least 15m depth, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Red zebra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas (Ref. 40897).  Males territorial (Ref. 40897).  Feeds on algae (Ref. 40897).  Aquarium keeping:  many females for one male; minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Red-anal triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-banded prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Moderately common in patches of coarse carbonate or volcanic sand of outer lagoon and seaward reefs.  Occurs in pairs and burrow with a yellow species of prawn.  Minimum depth range reported taken from Ref. 30874. Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Red-barred rubble goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons and on the 'reef top' (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Red-belted anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in aggregations around isolated coral heads and rubble patches (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles enter harbors and often on silty rocky reefs (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Red-blotch pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-blotched river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-bodied triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually found in open tide-pools and areas with strong regular surges generated by wave swells. Individuals often inhabit the surface of large rocks, but also slits and holes in large rocks, at depths of less than 25 m (usually less than 15 m). Spawning at Shikoku is reported to occur from early morning until about 10 am starting in June (Ref. 118055).

species.name: Red-cheek wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in small groups in rocky reefs with little coral cover (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Red-cheeked fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs singly or in small groups around coral outcrops of clear outer reef slopes.  Males are territorial and haremic (Ref. 9710).  Total length for females from Masuda & Allen, 1993 (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Red-earth pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in crevices of coral rock walls, reefs, and on sand/rubble bottoms (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Red-eye wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal to outer reef lagoons on rubble and coral habitats (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Red-fin fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rubble on outer reef slopes up to at least 30 m depth (Ref. 31269). Closely related to C. flavidorsalis and females look almost identical (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Red-finned killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-finned mud carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to be restricted to marginal or temporary habitats, including roadside canals.  Has never been seen in flowing water habitats.  So far as known, it does not occur sympatrically with other species of the genus.

species.name: Red-finned rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relative common in a variety of habitats including tannin-stained creeks in lowland rainforest, larger streams in more open areas and mountain tributaries to an elevation of about 400 m above sea level.  Occurs in quiet shaded pools, as well as sunlit sections of larger streams and relatively fast-flowing mountain streams.

species.name: Red-finned triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on reef's surface, often in weedy areas, and on algal-covered rocks or on rubble.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Red-gold Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Several individuals were observed darting under low, rocky overhangs and larger coral rubble pieces on this current-swept, low-relief slope (Ref. 89054).

species.name: Red-lined hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-Lined Jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected on the edge of a 200 m-wide channel between the mainland and a small island, where the area is exposed to periodic strong currents associated with tidal fluctuation. It is characterized by relatively rich coral grading to rubble in deeper water with a maximum depth of about 50 m. It has a series of vents, at depths of about 2-35 m, which releases large volumes of freshwater and the abrupt salinity changes are visible due to the blurring effect of the fresh- and seawater mixture. About 10 burrows of this species were detected on rubble bottoms in about 20-25 m depth during the 2006 and 2007 visits. The two type specimens were taken from their burrows using a clove oil-alcohol solution (Ref. 75148).

species.name: Red-lined pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Usually lives in caves and crevices of outer reef slopes (Ref. 2334).  Inhabits deep lagoon and protected seaward reefs (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Red-lined sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over fine, silty or muddy sand bottoms, Ref. 48637. Usually in pairs (Ref. 90102). Sifts large mouthfuls of sand to feed and dig its own burrow.

species.name: Red-lined wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups (Ref. 90102) in seaward reefs to at least 35 m depth, usually in areas of mixed coral and reef rock with sand patches (Ref. 9710).  Also in reef crests and slopes on rocky or rubble-algae substrates (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Red-margined wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep coastal to outer reef drop-offs and steep slopes.  Occurs over rubble or sandy bottoms with small isolated patch reefs of low profile.  Juveniles solitary among large rubble, usually in 2-30 m depth.  Adults in loose aggregations in moderate depths, usually 40 m or more around patch reef (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Red-sashed hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Photos of individuals taken with maximum size up to about 30 cm SL (Ref. 75973).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Red-speckled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit exposed seaward reefs where it usually shelters at bases or among the branches of Pocilloporid corals (Ref. 1602). Feeds on benhic algae (Ref. 89972). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Red-spot mudsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-spot perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-spotted bandfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the shallowest water, compared to other cepolids.  Lives on muddy substrates, deep as well as in shallow protected estuaries (Ref. 48635).  Caught by dredge, but not valued as food fish (Ref. 559, 637).

species.name: Red-spotted pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble slopes at the base of vertical cliffs.  Typically hovers vertically or obliquely, several centimeters above the bottom (Ref. 31115).

species.name: Red-striped cardinalfish
species.description: Found in shallow coral reefs around lagoons and sheltered bays (Ref. 36661).  In small groups, usually sheltering near long-spined urchins or large anemones in seagrasses (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Red-striped coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446).

species.name: Red-striped rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Red-striped toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in brackish water but also found in freshwaters of tidal creeks and rivers (Ref. 2847).  Very common in some mangrove areas (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Red-striped wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually inhabits areas of sand covered with dense scattering of small scale rubble composed of either volcanic rock chips or calcareous algae, at depths to at least 30 m. Small numbers of individuals found on sand at sand/reef interfaces. Species of Halichoeres melanotis and H. malpelo occur in the same habitat, on continental mainland and Isla Malpelo, respectively (Ref. 75895).

species.name: Red-Tailed Silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers well-shaded, quieter sections of small streams at altitudes of 300 to 650 meters above sea level; not collected in low altitude habitats in the Mananjary basin, probably because of increased silt loads and higher water temperatures due to deforestation in the area around the town of Mananjary; observed swimming in loose, size-graded associations of up to a dozen individuals; juveniles usually found in the shallows, adults frequent deeper water (Ref. 76768).

species.name: Red-tipped halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit estuaries (Ref. 4833), rivers (Ref. 43641) and marine waters (Ref. 45255).  Frequently found in mangrove areas (Ref. 43081).

species.name: Red-wing fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Before the 1990s, this species was a very important component of the local fishery.  Its population is shrinking quickly.  No adult specimen was found during the 2004 field survey.  The primary threat might be the introduction of icefishes (Family Salangidae)  based on survey conducted (Ref. 80016).

species.name: Redback dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitary or in small groups on sand-rubble bottoms 50-120 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Redback longface wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, in areas of mixed sand, rubble, and coral (Ref. 9710). Often found in areas with Halimeda algea. May be solitray or form groups. East indian reef fishes of this species are mostly young and rarely larger than 10 cm (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Redback sand tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually lives in very deep water adjacent to reef drop-offs (Ref. 48635); also on sandy and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).  Builds large rubble mounts (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on zooplankton. Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Redband darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams and springs (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Redband wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, algal-covered reefs, particularly at offshore localities (Ref. 26203).

species.name: Redbanded perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary fish found in deep holes and rock ledges which rarely strays far from its refuge.  Feeds on small fishes, crabs and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Redbanded rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Redbanded weever
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Redbar sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits near shore, sand rubble bottom with scattered rock and coral outcrops in about 2-20 m, often in less than 8 m, solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Redbar triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the intertidal and shallow coral-reef habitats (Ref. 114928).

species.name: Redbarred sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly occurs at moderate depth on open rubble reef flats, but occasionally more shallow on outer reef habitats (Ref. 48636).  Usually on rubble or sand near coral reefs (Ref. 42740) solitary or forms small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Redbelly dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among branching and encrusting corals (Ref. 9210) in lagoon reefs at depths of 10 or more (Ref. 37816, 48637). Forms groups among branches of Acropora coral (Ref 90102).

species.name: Redbelly triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in and about coral reefs and rocky shores in clear water. (Ref. 7251).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Redblotch basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along outer reef slopes (Ref. 8894).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Solitary and cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Redblotch razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy open area at 10-20 m, solitary or forms loose groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Redbreast acara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers (Ref. 12965).  Known to leap from the water to land on nearby buoyant  vegetation to escape predators, but this may in turn, make them vulnerable to aerial hunters (Ref. 40103).  Maximum length 8 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Redbreast sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rocky and sandy pools of creeks and small to medium rivers; rocky and vegetated lake margins (Ref. 5723).  Adults feed on terrestrial insects and both immature and adult aquatic insects, particularly larger varieties such as mayflies and dragonflies.  Juveniles consume benthic organisms such as dipteran larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Redcap triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow water and tidal pools (Ref. 13227).  They feed on gastropods (Ref. 94105).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Redcheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Redchin panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swampy areas along the coast, quiet parts of brooks and slow flowing river in the coastal lowlands (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Redcoat soldierfish
species.description: Four known specimens. Caught with a gill net in 114 m off Itsoundzou Island (Ref. 58472).

species.name: Redeye barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers marshes and marginal vegetation of streams, rivers and lakes; active in subdued light and at night (Ref. 7248, 52193). It feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Redeye bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 205); also found in upland streams (Ref. 10294).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Redeye chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in spring, spring-fed headwaters and creeks.

species.name: Redeye gaper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the specimens (NCSM 41116) represents a new size record for the species (25.5 cm SL, 30.5 cm TL), and another (GMBL 02788) represents a southerly range extension (31°23.94'N). All specimens observed exhibited similar behaviors of sitting on the bottom on top of dense beds of dead coral (Lophelia pertusa) (Ref. 58471).

species.name: Redeye goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers in groups above branches of certain Acropora corals in shallow lagoon reefs, Ref. 48637.

species.name: Redeye labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shoaling species (Ref. 94784). Found in both sediment-free and sediment-rich rocky biotopes; favors clear, running waters in rocky habitats of small and large rivers, also found in lakes and dams over rocky areas (Ref. 5595, 52193).
