Utilized as food (Ref. 247); for its meat and fins. Caught frequently by demersal gillnet, longline and trawl fisheries operating in insular and continental shelf waters (Ref.58048).

species.name: Requin-chabot birman
species.description: Feeds on small bony fishes (Ref. 43278).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-chabot camot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs, rocky shores, and mangrove estuaries.  Free-living at 10.1 cm TL.  Feeds on squid, shelled molluscs, crustaceans, and snake eels (Ref. 43278).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Of minimal interest to fisheries (Ref. 43278).  Caught rarely by demersal trammel and trawl fisheries operating inshore.  Utilized for its meat and possibly fins, but of limited value due to its small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Requin-chabot de Hasselt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore bottom-dweller (Ref. 13575); on rock and coral reefs (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 13575).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 13575).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Requin-chabot gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore bottom shark (Ref. 247).  Often found in estuaries (Ref. 4832).  Probably feeds mainly on invertebrates (Ref. 247, 43278).  Oviparous (Ref. 43278, 50449).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 171).

species.name: Requin-chabot grivelé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known bottom shark, probably common on coral reefs (Ref. 247); tide pools and sea grass beds in 0-12 m (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-chabot marquéterie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow coral reefs of the continental shelf (Ref. 247).  Probably mainly feeding on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6871).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-chabot moine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known inshore bottom shark of singular and unique appearance (Ref. 247).  Probably found on coral reefs (Ref. 247). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-chabot ocellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in shallow water of coral reefs (Ref. 6871).  Often in tide pools (Ref. 13575).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6871).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Squirms when captured but cannot readily escape (Ref. 247).  Survives well in aquariums (Ref. 6871). Has the ability to survive low oxygen conditions by switching of non-essential brain functions; apparently an adaption for hunting in tide-pools with low oxygen (Ref. 52022).

species.name: Requin-chabot taches blanches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common but little-known inshore bottom shark (Ref. 247); found on rocks and coral reefs (Ref. 90102). Feeds on bony fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 43278).  Oviparous (Ref. 43278, 50449). Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 247) and used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).  Caught by multiple hook and line and trawl (Ref. 47736).  Caught rarely by demersal gillnet fisheries operating inshore (Ref.58048).

species.name: Requin-chabot à taches bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-chabot élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common, but little-known inshore sluggish bottom shark (Ref. 13575) found on sandy and muddy bottoms of coastal waters, bays and inlets and rocky and coral reefs.  Probably mainly feeds on bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 13575), also small fishes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 247).  Possibly may occur in fresh water in the lower reaches of the Perak River in peninsular Malaysia (Ref. 43278).

species.name: Requin-chabot épaulette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known inshore bottom shark, probably on coral reefs (Ref. 247). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-hâ aile blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An little-known inshore tropical shark found in coastal waters (Ref. 13563). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-hâ dochizame
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs close inshore and offshore down to at least 100 m depth.  Presumably feeds on small fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans.  Ovoviviparous, with 8 to 22 young in a litter.  Size at birth about 20 to 21 cm.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Requin-hâ long nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known tropical shark found on the uppermost insular slopes (Ref. 13563) at depths of 250-475 m (Ref.58048). Stomach contents of a specimen included small Macrouridae (Hymenocephalus sp., Nezumia sp., Ventrifossa spp.), crustaceans (Penaeoidea, Munidae) (Ref. 127459) and cephalopods (Ref. 244). Viviparous, placental (Ref. 50449). Caught irregularly by the small-scale demersal longline fisheries operating in deepwater. Utilized for its meat and fins, but of limited value due to its small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Requin-hâ voile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 244).  The only known specimen was taken at a depth of 73 m, probably near the bottom (Ref. 244). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Requin-hâ à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and slope.  Water temperature:  16-25°C.  Oxygen level:  0.2-2.4 ppm.  Feeds on bony fishes (mostly lanternfishes) and cephalopods.  Sexual dimorphism by size exists.  Viviparous (with a yolk-sac placenta), with probably 2 to 10 young in a litter.  Utilized fresh for human consumption.

species.name: Requin-hâ élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves (Ref. 244).  Feeds on bony fishes and cephalopods (Ref. 6871).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 244).

species.name: Requin-tapis cordonnier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on the continental shelf (Ref. 6871).  Frequents rocky and coral reef areas.  Biology almost unknown.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 6871).  May possibly grow to 200 or 300 cm TL.

species.name: Requin-tapis moustache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known bottom shark found inshore (Ref. 247); usually in sand or sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230); also on rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 43278).  Nocturnal in habits (Ref. 247).  Feeds on fish and presumably bottom invertebrates (Ref. 247), including lizardfishes, cutlassfish, horse mackerel and other jacks, goatfishes, groupers, tilefishes, sea robins, whiting, parrotfishes, sea bream, croakers, also skates, shark egg cases, cephalopods, and shrimp (Ref. 43278).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 43278, 50449), with up to 20 young in a litter (Ref. 247).  Wobbegongs should be regarded as potentially dangerous because of its formidable dentition (Ref. 247, 13577).  Used for human consumption (Ref. 247).  Kept in aquaria in Japan and the United States (Ref. 43278).

species.name: Requin-tapis paste
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common bottom shark of  inshore continental waters, on algal-covered rocky areas and coral reefs (Ref. 247).  Nocturnal, resting on the bottom during the day and prowling on its reef habitat at night (Ref. 247).  Presumably feeding on bottom invertebrates and fishes but diet unrecorded (Ref. 13577).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Attacks waders and fishers in tide pools (Ref. 247).  Interest to fisheries limited; its skin very tough and attractively patterned and utilized for leather (Ref. 13577).

species.name: Requin-tapis savetier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, commonly inshore (Ref. 247).  Presumably feeds on bottom invertebrates and fishes, but diet still unrecorded (Ref. 13577, 43278).  Probably ovoviviparous (Ref. 13577, 43278).  Wobbegongs should be regarded as potentially dangerous because of their formidable teeth (Ref. 247, 13577).

species.name: Requin-tapis tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, from the intertidal down to at least 110 m (Ref. 247).  Commonly on coral and rocky reefs, under piers, and on sand bottom (Ref. 247).  May occur in water barely deep enough to cover the fish, and has been observed climbing ridges between tide pools with its back out of water (Ref. 247).  Nocturnal (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bottom invertebrates (Ref. 247), including crabs, lobsters and octopuses (Ref. 43278), and bony fishes (Ref. 247), like sea bass, scorpionfishes and luderick (Ref. 43278).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 43278, 50449), with up to 37 pups in a litter (Ref. 247).  Known to bite people that step on it or put their feet near its mouth, and can and will bite when molested and provoked (Ref. 247).  Flesh highly regarded and sometimes utilized for human consumption (Ref. 247).  Skin sometimes utilized for leather (Ref. 247).  Regarded as pest by lobster fishers (Ref. 247).

species.name: Requin-vache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental and island shelves and slopes, occasionally near surface or inshore from 0 to 700 m depth.  Feeds on small to medium-sized bony fishes and occassionally on crustaceans.  Viviparous, with 13-26 young in a litter (Ref. 125614).  Size at birth measures to about 40-43 cm TL (Ref. 94780).  It is taken as bycatch within its range, but is not commercially important (Ref. 125614).  Utilized for its fins, meat and liver oil but of little value due to its relatively small size (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Resistencia toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Resplendent angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The habitat of this species consists of rock and rubble at depths of from 15 m to at least 40 m.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35409).

species.name: Reticulate boxfish
species.description: Inhabits clear coastal reefs in rich invertebrate habitat on shallow crests or upper zone of slopes to about 15 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Relatively uncommon inhabitant of coral rich areas of seaward reefs.  Sexually dimorphic (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Reticulate dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Reticulate goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on live coral (Ref. 11441); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446).

species.name: Reticulate hookjaw moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Lurks in holes, crevices and dark recesses.  Constantly opens and closes it mouth, an action required for respiration, not a threat  (Ref. 5227).  Despite its large size, this fish is not consumed as food (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Reticulate knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers calm waters with dense vegetation.

species.name: Reticulate loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks with rocky and gravel bottoms (Ref. 12045).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Reticulate moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from moderate depths along outer continental shelf.

species.name: Reticulate sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually inhabits rubble and gravel-bottomed pools and riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers, but can shift to other habitats depending on the environmental conditions and composition of fish communities. Where Cottus rhotheus and Cottus aleuticus do not occur, this species occupies riffles; at localities where all occur together, it shifts to pools (ref. 86798). Has been observed in slow moving and still waters with muddy substrates, but identification is uncertain (K. McAllister & M. Young, pers. comm. 07/04/20).

species.name: Reticulate spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reticulate toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reticulate triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reticulate unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reticulated corydoras
species.description: Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Reticulated fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs (Ref. 41819) and sheltered lagoons (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Reticulated jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Reticulated moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type specimens were captured at night on a sand-rubble bottom adjacent to coral reef at a depth of 16 m (Ref. 123128).

species.name: Reticulated pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water reefs near sand or seaweed areas.  Also found in estuaries and protected muddy bays; juveniles in mangroves and entering the lower reaches of streams (Ref. 9407, 48637). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Adults at moderate depths, often laying on the mud during the day (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Reticulated sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) commonly on deep coastal slopes, from the shallow rocky shore to the deep soft bottom zones (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Reticulated shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Retroculus lapidifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In adults, males are larger, with extended dorsal, anal and pelvic fins (Ref. 37197).

species.name: Retroculus septentrionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured mainly in the rapids of rivers (Ref. 35237)..

species.name: Retroculus xinguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12965).  Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 13614).

species.name: Retzer’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reunion angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Unknown to the aquarium hobby; its maintenance is probably similar to that of A. trimaculatus.

species.name: Reverse gland lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neustonic to mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Reversed skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of about 1,500 m (Ref. 26282). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Revillagigedo barnacle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small benthic reef fish which is common in shallow water, but also occurs to depths of at least 31 meters (Ref. 81029).

species.name: Revillagigedo sea chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rexea alisae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Reynald's grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal and tidal stretches of rivers, but apparently no data on salinity tolerances.  Its presence above Barrackpore on the Hooghly in India suggests that it can live in freshwater.  Larvae feed on copepods;  thereafter mainly on copepods, but also on prawns, larval decapods and other crustaceans.  Breeds in the lower parts of estuaries.  The time and duration of the breeding season reported vary for different estuaries in India.

species.name: Rhabdalestes aeratis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdalestes brevidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdalestes septentrionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Group of melanophores above base of anal fin more pronounced than that observed for Micralestes species (Ref. 2880).

species.name: Rhabdalestes yokai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdamia nigrimentum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdamia spilota
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims in tight pairs (Ref. 48635); observed to occur in large aggregation around rocky outcrops with gorgonian fans and crinoids on steep slopes.  Swims actively during the day above isolated coral heads to feed on zooplankton (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Rhabdoblennius nigropunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rhabdolichops caviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep river channels, other fluvial habitats and lagoons (Ref. 9394).  Feeds mainly on copepods (Ref. 9394).

species.name: Rhabdolichops eastwardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops electrogrammus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops jegui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops lundbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is common in the main channel of the whitewater rivers of the Tefé region where it was found both in trawl-net samples at depths of 10-18 m and also, very abundantly, on sandy and muddy beaches sampled with seine nets. It occurs with R. eastwardi, caviceps, and electrogrammus, but not with nigrimans or navalha. The preferred habitat of this species is turbid river water with electrical conductivity in the range of 80-150 µScm-1. Mature males and females were found during the rising water phase of the Amazon River and were encountered among many other immature specimens on beaches. There in no information about the breeding habits of this species. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates-mainly larvae of Trichoptera and Ephemeroptera larvae, also of Coleoptera and Chironomidae. Some specimens had also ingested large amounts of adult Conchostraca (Ref. 55969).

species.name: Rhabdolichops navalha
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known only from the main channel of the low-nutrient blackwater Rio Tefé. Apparently, the species is a benthic specalist. It is captured in trawl nets where it occurs with Rhabdolichops eastwardi, troscheli, caviceps, nigrimans, and electrogrammus, except lundbergi. Its diet consists of small planktonic crustacean primarily Cladocera and Copepoda, but also small Conchostraca and Ostracoda (Ref. 55969).

species.name: Rhabdolichops nigrimans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops troscheli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdolichops zareti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhabdosargus niger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Imported into Korea from Indonesia as frozen commercial food (Ref. 94713).

species.name: Rhadinoloricaria bahuaja
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the main river and major tributaries, always over sandy beaches.  Stomach contents include larvae of aquatic insects, small seeds and debris.  The holotype (male, 11.59 cm SL) carried 53 fertilized eggs (3.2-3.4 mm diameter) on its lips and another specimen was carrying 31 unfertilized eggs (3.1-3.4 mm diameter).

species.name: Rhadinoloricaria macromystax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhadinoloricaria papillosa
species.description: Occurs at the bottom of Rio Negro (Ref. 128857).

species.name: Rhadinoloricaria rhami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhadinoloricaria stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella aymarae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella cainguae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over rocky bottoms in a clear water stream, approximately 0.5 - 1 m deep, with pools around 3 m deep, running through a densely forested area (Ref. 75872).  Tends to be gregarious as individuals were observed in dense group under large stones (Ref. 75872).

species.name: Rhamdella eriarcha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella exsudans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella jenynsii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella longiuscula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella montana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella rusbyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdella zelimai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small to medium-sized streams with clear water running on a bottom composed of boulders, stones and gravel (Ref. 98446).

species.name: Rhamdia argentina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia enfurnada
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia foina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia guasarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The cave where the fish was collected is near the margin of Río Guasare and is the source of a spring during seasonal rains; its lower conduit has a 280 m course, 2-3 m wide and 1-2 m high, narrowly communicating with the access gallery.  The underground river is permanently fed by a spring about 60 m into the lower gallery.  At the time the collection was made, the average depth of the water course was 1.5 m with deeper pools along its course where the catfishes were observed (Ref. 80467).

species.name: Rhamdia humilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia itacaiunas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia jequitinhonha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia laukidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia muelleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia nicaraguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rivers and creeks between 20 and 1160 m elevation in currents of low to moderate velocity, with stony bottoms and substrata of sand and mud.  Feeds mainly on aquatic insects,  seeds and small fish (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Rhamdia poeyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia schomburgkii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdia xetequepeque
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdioglanis frenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdioglanis transfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdiopsis krugi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in the upper phreatic zone of a large karstic area (over 300 km2) including limestones
and quartzites, which is connected to surface through caves.  Inhabits lentic waters formed by the water table inside the caves, varying from large, partially illuminated lakes to isolated pools. Mainly solitary.  Observed swimming up to about 35 m depth, but it usually aggregates between the surface and 10 m.  Reported to show preference for substrate, concentrating in the rocky walls.  Strictly a carnivorous species which feeds on invertebrates found near or on the bat guano (Ref. 86271).

species.name: Rhamdiopsis microcephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamdiopsis moreirai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhamphochromis esox
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the open water (Ref. 5595). Widely distributed in shelf and rocky reef zones, usually where the bottom is fairly shallow; rarely found offshore; small juveniles widely distributed in the littoral zone in swampy, sandy and rocky habitats; adults regularly encountered near sandy beaches in the shallows (Ref. 55949). Feeds on fish species like the small Utaka and the lake sardine Usipa (Engraulicypris sardella) (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Rhamphochromis ferox
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at fairly deep levels of the open water.  Piscivorous (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Rhamphochromis lucius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the open water but is usually caught in deep levels. Piscivorous, Readily caught using Usipa (Engraulicypris sardella) as bait (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Rhamphochromis macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on the shelf zone; occasionally found off reefs; but not commonly recorded from the middle of the lake (Ref. 55949). Moves in the open water but stays 2-5 m above the substrate; feeds on fish like the small Utaka and Usipa (Engraulicypris sardella) (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Rhamphochromis woodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reef and shelf zones, and offshore in the pelagic zone (Ref. 55949).  Few specimens were collected near rocky shores.  Occurs in small groups (Ref. 5595).  Piscivorous (Ref. 5595, 55949).  Female mouthbrooder (Ref. 55949).

species.name: Rheocles vatosoa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in the upper and middle reaches of the Lokoho river in the general vicinity of the town of Andapa.  Found predominantly in clear streams over gravel or coarse sand bottoms.  This streams are characterized by soft, slightly acidic to moderately alkaline water; total and carbonate hardness values < 1°DH and pH 6.8-7.5.  Collected from both rapidly flowing rivers and small brooks.  Stomach contents almost exclusively of macerated insect remains, most of terrestrial origin.  A few remains of aquatic insect larvae suggesting a somewhat opportunistic feeding (Ref. 42716).

species.name: Rheocles wrightae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rheoheros coeruleus
species.description: A current-loving fish which prefers the montane habitat.  Feeds upon aufwuchs and the encrusted invertebrates (mostly small crustaceans).

species.name: Rhexipanchax kabae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small streams and brooks (Ref. 3788, 57259). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Rhinecanthus abyssus

species.name: Rhinobatos nudidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Offshore on insular shelves of the Central Indian Ocean, distribution probably restricted (Ref. 114953). Maximum size is actually unknown, presumably a small- to moderate-size species given that the half-meter holotype is sexually mature (Ref. 55722). Biology is unknown, more specimens needed (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Rhinobrycon negrensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rhinoceros leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal reefs and enter estuaries.  Often in silty habitat and usually on slopes with low rubble reef and rich invertebrate growth, ranging to moderate depths (Ref. 48637).  Found on  weedy and sandy areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Often found in pairs (Ref. 9710). Sometimes solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102). Juveniles hide or shelter near seawhips or seapens (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Rhinocerus triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear coastal reefs with algae covered rocky boulders, usually in small groups (Ref. 48636).  They occur in very shallow depths on rock surfaces and under ledges (Ref. 48636).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rhinodoras armbrusteri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. There were individuals encountered during the day hiding in cavities in lateritic boulders submerged in less than three meters of water.  An adult specimen was observed at night in a swift shallow run over bedrock (Ref. 75166).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit middle to upper reaches of rivers, and are especially found in open and shallow areas.  Breeds from June to August and makes a spawning bed (nest).  Eggs are protected by the male.  As soon as they hatch, the juveniles live on the river bottom.  Not amphidromous.  Food fish.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found both upstream and in estuaries.  Carnivorous.  Spawning season from July to October.  Eggs are laid under stones in river shoals.  Larvae travel in both river and the sea, and return to rivers from September to November.  Caught by small trap nets in rivers, but not in abundance.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected both in small streams and larger rivers, among stones and boulders, with moderate to swift current (Ref. 33279).  Feeds on zooplankton and insect larvae.  Occasionally marketed fresh in mixed catches (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Rhinogobius milleri

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow riffles with depth 20-40 cm, substratum of small pebbles and slow to moderate water flow (Ref. 79879).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs preferably in a hill-stream habitat with moderate to slow current over small to medium-sized pebbles and water depth ranging from 15-70 cm (Ref. 94987).

A non-diadromous species, restricted in non- or slow-flowing freshwater habitats throughout the life cycle (Ref, 119678).

species.name: Rhinogobius tyoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow freshwater areas with mud bottoms and aquatic vegetation, such as ponds, marshes, reservoirs, canals, creeks of middle or lower reaches of rivers. A non-diadromous species, restricted in non- or slow-flowing freshwater habitats throughout its life cycle (Ref. 119678).

in the sampling area is 3,400 mm/year and average temperature is 25.5° C (Ref. 100824).

species.name: Rhodes minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which inhabits lakes, rivers, springs, and associated wetlands (Ref. 26100).  Found in slow-flowing stretches of streams, especially roots of trees, bank cavities and among vegetation.  Larvae occur along banks among vegetation.  Feeds on  aquatic invertebrates and algae, mainly on plant material in summer.  Juveniles and adults die in large number during summer and autumn drought.  Spawns among aquatic vegetation, especially filamentous algae.  Threatened due to water abstraction in dry season and habitat destruction (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rhodeus albomarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a hill stream with bottom consisting of mud mixed with stones, low water level, and depth mostly less than 100 cm. Collected from the upper portion of the stream.  Spawns in summer from June to August, several times during the spawning periods, and usually releases 10-20 eggs at one time.  Lives in host mussel <i>Ptychorhynchus murinum (Ref. 95613).

species.name: Rhyacoglanis seminiger
species.description: Found in very fast-flowing rapids with clear waters over a substrate composed almost exclusively of quartz sand and small rocks, with the river margins covered by riparian forest (Ref. 128485).

species.name: Rib-bar cardinalfish
species.description: Found over open bottom.  Sold in fish markets as part of trawl catches and utilized as food in the Philippines and India (Ref. 58479). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ribbed tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud bottoms.  May inhabit burrows.  Fished between 200 and 400 m (Ref. 5503).

species.name: Ribbon basslet
species.description: Solitary and secretive in reef crevices in 60-80 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Ribbon goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Ribbon prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under rocks in intertidal areas and to about 12 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on crustaceans, and red and green algae (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Ribbon reefgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reefs or areas with soft bottoms.

species.name: Ribbon shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet, usually turbid, mud-bottomed or sand-bottomed pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ribbon snailfish
species.description: Occurs from near shore (also in tide pools)  to 183 m depth (Ref. 2850, 51661).

species.name: Ribboned pipefish

Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Richardson's sardinella

species.name: Richer’s dragonet

species.name: Ridgeback skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Capture depth unknown, but probably from deep slopes of the Sulu Sea and adjacent waterways.  the largest paratype (SUML MMLM 018) was measured in 1999 at 896 mm TL (Compagno et al., 2005) and shrank to 878 mm TL when measured a decade later. Of the two known males, one was sexually mature (621 mm TL) and the slightly larger holotype was at a late adolescent stage (657 mm TL); birth size unknown (Ref. 94808)..

species.description: Mainly in the marine waters of the lower estuaries, along the coast and off river mouths (Ref. 40908).

species.name: Ridgehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found mainly below 150-200 m (Ref. 6747).  Larvae and juveniles primarily found in depths as shallow as 35-40 m (Ref. 36655).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36655). Collections were done mainly by using nonclosing nets (Ref. 117121).

species.name: Riffle chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Riffle Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish not able to undertake diadromous migrations. It was collected at a density ranging from < 0.01-0.80 fish/m2, but as individuals are usually hidden amongst or within the substrate in fast-flowing areas which are difficult to sample, these values are considered a gross underestimate of its relative abundance. Also recorded from cold to relatively cool, clear water in flowing creeks to large rivers (1.0-20.0 m average width), usually in shallow (0.1-0.4 m average depth), fast-flowing and high energy riffles and runs, although juveniles have been recorded moving upstream through slow water along the shallow edges of pools. The substrate in riffles and runs are mainly a complex of abundant cobbles and pebbles, with smaller amounts of bedrock, boulder, gravel and coarse sand. Fish are typically found within the diverse substrate, either amongst or under rocks on the stream bed, or deeper in the interstitial spaces of the substratum. It is usually not associated with aquatic vegetation, but have been found amongst small and large timber debris. Adults often are solitary; juveniles and younger adults observed in loose shoals of 50+ individuals, moving upstream during the day in shallow, slow-flowing water along the edge of pools, between riffle habitats: fish 3.8-6.6 cm LCF were recorded moving upstream in the Acheron River and individuals < 5.0 cm LCF observed along the edge in the Steavenson River (Goulburn system) in late May 2001; and, individuals 4.9-6.7 cm LCF were collected moving upstream along the edge of a long pool in the Mitta Mitta River (upper Murray system) in late June 2002. This suggests active upstream dispersal by younger age-classes of fish. Individuals from the Steavenson River, downstream from Marysville, were found with cysts, possibly trematode metacercariae, embedded in the skin of the trunk and fins. This species is often collected with the native species Gadopsis bispinosus (Two-spined Blackfish), Galaxias olidus s.s., Euastacus armatus (Murray Spiny Crayfish), Euastacus crassus (Alpine Spiny Crayfish), a shrimp (Atyidae) and including the alien species Brown Trout and Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), and less often with the native Galaxias oliros (Obscure Galaxias) and Broadfinned Galaxias (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Riffle minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble runs and riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Riffle sculpin
species.description: Inhabits sand and gravel riffles of headwaters and creeks; also in sand-gravel runs and backwaters of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Rifian barbel
species.description: This species is ubiquitous and inhabits streams and rivers with substrata ranging from sandy to stony, being absent only in small streams near the sources of rivers and in shallow waters; it is also present in reservoirs (Ref. 107580). The spawning period is variable, but usually takes place in April and May; the species migrates upstream to spawn in cold and oxygenated waters where the females excavate a nest in the gravel (Ref. 107580). It is a common species; however, its distribution area has been extensively transformed due to construction of dams, which also hamper upstream migration during the spawning period (Ref. 107580).

species.name: Rifle cardinal
species.description: Occurs mainly in shallow waters and tide pools (Ref. 58479). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178. Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rift pygmygoby
species.description: This species was observed hovering in aggregations up to 15 individuals near the roof of caves and moving to shelter in the cave roof when approached by divers (Ref. 129378).

species.name: Rigid boxfish
species.description: Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Rigilius goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 90102). Occurs in sandy areas with living corals and coral rubble in clear waters, Ref. 48637.

species.name: Rikuzen flounder
species.description: Found on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Rimicola eigenmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the intertidal and shallow subtidal to 15 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Feed almost exclusively on tiny crustaceans (Ref. 4930).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36496).  Eggs are demersal attached to stones or cobbles (Ref. 36496).

species.name: Rimmed-scaled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Rimspine searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on the continental slope.

species.name: Rineloricaria aequalicuspis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks to large rivers with shallow to deep water, dwelling among bottom rocks and stones (Ref. 40941).

species.name: Ring-backed pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among brown and red algae in sheltered reef habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ring-eye pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected with rotenone (Ref. 13702).  Inhabits coastal and outer reef slopes (Ref. 37816, 48637). Benthic, occuring singly or in loose groups, and a plankton-feeder; with prolonged pelagic larval duration of 33.9 days (= 24% of maximum lifespan) and linear post-larval growth; daily mortality rate ranging from 2.9% to 6.3%; sex ratio of 1:1.6 male/females)  (Ref. 87294).

species.name: Ringed blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rich coral tops of drop-offs (Ref. 9710) to at least 175 m. Associated with Condylactis gigantea (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Ringed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ringed moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ringed toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Ringed torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental shelf in shallow water to at least 15 m deep. Presumably feeds on small invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Males mature at ca. 32 cm TL, females at ca. 35 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Ringtail cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ringtail maori wrasse
species.description: Usually solitary in coral rich areas of clear lagoon and seaward reefs.  Hovers well above the bottom (Ref. 9710, 48636).  Young secretive in soft corals and hydrozoans (Ref. 48636).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9823).  May be ciguatoxic (Ref. 37816).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Ringtail pike cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in creeks, but sometimes captured in rivers, specially during the dry season.  A formidable predator; it consumes essentially aquatic insects, fish and plant material.  Not very popular among aquarists because of its aggressive behavior (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Ringtail snailfish
species.description: Occurs from intertidal areas to 73 m depth (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Ringtail tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rio anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species occurring in coastal waters.  Recorded in salinities of 7.94-31.31 ppt in the Santa Cruz canal, Pernambuco, Brazil.  More data needed based on correct identifications.

species.name: Rio Grande chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  Occurs usually near brush (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Mid-water carnivore; feeds on zooplankton, aquatic and terrestrial insects, crustaceans, juvenile fish, and a limited amount of detritus (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Rio Grande darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit gravel and rubble riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Rio Grande shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and flowing pools of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Rio Grande silvery minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and backwaters of low-gradient creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous, open substratum spawners (Ref. 205, 35784).

species.name: Rio Grande sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, runs and riffles of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Rio Napo cory
species.description: Forms schools. Occurs sympatrically with C. elegans.

species.name: Rio Negro pygmy anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species collected some distance up a low-gradient swampy tributary of the Rio Negro (the Rio Jufari), Brazil and in the main river, in both cases the water generally darkly tinted, acid (pH 4-5) and low in dissolved ions.  Feeds on dipteran larvae and pupae; also cladocerans.  Males mature at 1.43-1.62 cm SL; females at 1.59-1.82 cm.  Ovarian eggs are creamy or pale orange.  A female of 1.73 cm had 20 eggs in the single ovary in January.

species.name: Rio pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small freshwater temporary pools in floodplains of streams and lagoons.  These  pools are shallow with compact, soft reddish brown muddy bottom and dry twice a year, during winter, usually from July to August, and during summer, usually from February to March.  During dry season, all fish die and eggs undergo in diapause within the substrate.  Eclosion happens at the onset of wet season, usually March-April and September-October  (Ref. 42934).  This species was introduced in California (Ref. 4357).  Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Rio skate
species.description: A coastal species found on sand, mud or gravel bottoms (Ref. 26375).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks and fishes (Ref. 26375).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rio Verde catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ripon barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Victoria drainage: inshore waters and affluent rivers (Ref. 4903, 34290). Young occur in shoals (Ref. 36900) in riverine habitats while adults occur in both riverine and lacustrine habitats (Ref. 34291). Swims upstream to spawn (Ref. 36900), probably in swift, rocky upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 34291). Feeds on gastropod molluscs, insects, plants, fishes and crustacea (Ref. 12526). In lakes Edward and George: in shallow water (Ref. 4903). In Rusizi River system: migrates to small upstream rivers to spawn (Ref. 87863). Oviparous (Ref. 205). A food fish for humans (Ref. 4537), but not of great economic importance (Ref. 4903).

species.name: Rippled blaasop
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably pelagic.

species.name: Rippled coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Marine species usually living on coral reefs but also recorded from pools, freshwater streams or lagoon mouths (Ref. 4343). Preys on copepods (Ref. 92840). Found on tabletop Acropora corals (Ref. 1602); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Monogamous (Ref. 52884). The male takes care of eggs deposited on a coral branch (Ref. 32163). Has the ability to change sex in both directions to favor reproductive success (Ref. 32163).

species.name: Rippled klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in weedy tide pools.

species.name: Rippled rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal (Ref. 31184, 48636).  Adults are common in areas with large rubble pieces which are often used to built breakwaters or to support jetty-pylons (Ref. 48636).  They hide in cracks or holes when not feeding.  They jump out of the water in energetic skippings to another pool when pursued (Ref. 2158, 48636).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  They breathe air when out of water (Ref. 31184). Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Ripplefin tonguesole
species.description: Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Ripsaw catfish
species.description: Occurs over mud in streams and lakes.  Forms schools (Ref. 9084).  Feeds on detritus, chironomid and ephemeropteran larvae, and crustaceans (Ref. 9096).  Known from temperatures ranging from 24-29.8 °C, pH range of 5-9, and an alkalinity range of 42-142.

species.name: Rita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and estuaries, preferably muddy to clear water (Ref. 1479).  Prefers backwater of quiet eddies (Ref. 12045).  Feeds on insects, mollusks, shrimps and fishes (Ref. 1479).  A very good food fish.

species.name: Rita chrysea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and large streams (Ref. 41236).  Spawning occurs during the monsoon months (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Rita gogra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Rita kuturnee
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Rita macracanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rite dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters and estuaries, on mud and sand bottoms, to depths of 200 m (Ref. 30573).  Juveniles common in brackish water (Ref. 9774).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 5213).  Mainly sold fresh (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Rite du Natal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms.

species.name: Rite javanais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow continental shelves with muddy and sandy substrates.  Feeds on benthic  animals.  Marketed mostly fresh.

species.name: Rite malais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the muddy and sandy trawling grounds of the continental shelf.  Feeds on benthic organisms.  Sold mostly fresh in markets.

species.name: Rite targeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on clay, sand and mud bottoms of the continental shelf.  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 5213).  Mainly sold fresh.

species.name: Rite à trois taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on muddy-sandy bottoms (Ref. 9330).  Commonly caught with trawls in the Gulf of California (Ref. 9330).

species.name: Rite à trois taches (Pseudorhombus triocellatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelf.  Feeds on benthic organisms.  Sold fresh and dried salted in markets.

species.name: Rite éventail
species.description: Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms,  from 4.6-79 m depth.  Usually buried in bottoms.  Feeds almost exclusively on crustaceans.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9330).

species.name: Rivas's limia
species.description: Collected at depth of 5-10 cm over organic mud.

species.name: River blackfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in clear, flowing streams with abundant cover (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Prefers streams with gravel bottoms and abundant snags.  Also occurs in lakes and reservoirs (Ref. 5259).  Tolerant of slightly brackish conditions (10 p.p.t.) in the tidal reaches of rivers, and a temperature range of 5°-25°C.  Home-ranging; remaining within about a 20-30 meters stretch of water throughout the life span (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 5259) ; also on mollusks (Ref. 2156).  The spawning season runs from November to January.  A popular angling species in the south, but large fish are rare.  Highly susceptible to overfishing, due to its home-ranging behavior and low fecundity (Ref. 44894).  Flesh is oily and not very good eating.

species.name: River carpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Adult feeds on organic detritus (Ref. 10294).

species.name: River cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small, benthic species inhabiting pool and run areas of streams (Ref. 12045).  Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: River catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).

species.name: River chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and flowing pools of small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: River darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky riffles of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults usually occur in deep swift riffles while young in shallow riffles and runs (Ref. 5723).

species.name: River Diamond mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: River dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the bottom in the lower courses of rivers.  Feeds on worms, zooplankton and  phytoplankton.  Occasionally marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: River garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: River goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear streams and rivers over sand and gravel, but also found in turbid waters with muddy bottoms.  Prefers clear flowing, well oxygenated streams.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae (Ref. 13444).

species.name: River pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers with tidal influence. Found in association with submerged aquatic macrophytes, primarily the eelgrass Zostera capensis (Ref. 26174). Sympatric with Syngnathus acus in the eelgrass beds (Ref. 26174). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: River Plate sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably confined to freshwaters and brackish waters of lagoons, estuaries and the lower reaches of rivers.

species.name: River sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pelagic species preferring close proximity to substrate and seeking out slacker areas such as backwater, eddies and pools below riffles (Ref. 116496). It occurs in shoals and prefers well-aerated, open water in flowing rivers, favouring the upper stratum (Ref. 7248, 52193, 116496). Feeds from water column on planktonic crustaceans and insects, such as midges and ants (Ref. 7248, 52193, 116496). Breeding occurs in early summer; appears to migrate up streams in spring to breed where it is found in tributaries (Ref. 7248, 116496).

species.name: River shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and main channels of medium to large rivers, usually over sand and gravel (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on cladocerans and a variety of immature aquatic insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: River stone carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs mainly in the edges of sandy streams.  Common near emergent or overhanging vegetation (Ref. 4832).  Prefers pools and run areas of mountain streams (Ref. 12045).

species.name: River tonguesole
species.description: Inhabits rivers (Ref. 5297).  A freshwater species found well above the tidal zone.  Stays on the bottom where it feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Riverine goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Riverweed darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Rivulus azurescens
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a steep mountain creek under primary forest canopy with clear swift running water,
stony cascading profile, no aquatic vegetation, temperature 20 °C at 19.45 hours and pH 5.8 (Ref. 95022).

species.name: Rivulus berovidesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small mountain streams with bottom substrate basically composed by stones, sand and dead leaves; no aquatic vegetation in the area (Ref. 101368).

species.name: Rivulus carolinae
species.description: The type locality, a black water creek was located in primary forest under a thick canopy and where water depth was only a few cms, likely due to the flat terrain. The creek is divided into several smaller streams and covered a wide stretch of the forest floor. Rivulus carolinae was taken in leaf litter in the shallowest parts of the stream (Ref. 130065).

species.name: Rivulus flammaecauda
species.description: The type locality, a black water creek was located in primary forest under a thick canopy and where water depth was only a few cms, likely due to the flat terrain. The creek is divided into several smaller streams and covered a wide stretch of the forest floor. Rivulus flammaecauda was more abundant in deeper, open areas (Ref. 130065).

species.name: Rivulus formosensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open areas highly exposed to sunlight (Ref. 75995).

species.name: Rivulus monticola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear to slightly turbid, rather fast flowing brooks having a depth of up to about 70 cm.

species.name: Rivulus pivijay
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rivulus ribesrubrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rivulus tomasi
species.description: Collected alongside a fast running part of a creek that flows down a boulder-strewn area, with a fall of approximately one in every five meters, a place where people find leisure and can slide down the rocky face.  This rocky open area is surrounded by a primary forest. This species lives between tree roots and fallen leaves attached to boulders at the edges of the stream, and between boulders. It was also collected a in places where the water ran slower, but was not found in still water surrounding the rocky waterslide.  At the time of collection (September 2006), the water at the collecting site was clear, pH 7, 27.6°C, conductivity was <1 μS/cm. (Ref. 94444).

species.name: Rivulus xi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rize trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small pools of streams with cold, clear and very swift flowing water, with high concentration of dissolved oxygen and substrate consisting of rocks, stones and few pebbles.  Spends whole life and spawns in the upper reaches.  Does not undertake migration during spawning period.  Spawns in September-October.  Overwinters into sand or gravel or under rocks and stones in small streams.  Seems to stop feeding during winter as all specimens collected in winter had empty stomach (Ref. 85599).

species.name: Road cory
species.description: Captured in the upper reaches of rivers.  No information is available on the biology of this fish (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Roanoke bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky and sandy pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Roanoke darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast gravel and rubble riffles (adult), gravel-bottomed pools and runs near riffles (young) of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Roanoke hog sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles, runs and pools of creeks and small rivers.  Often found over sand in slow current.

species.name: Roanoke logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel and boulder runs of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Roatan goby
species.description: A deep-reef goby collected from rariphotic depth ca. 237 m, found on a silt-covered boulder with small 3-10 cm diameter caves and crevices (Ref. 129296).

species.name: Robert's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Robert's river garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rainforest streams.

species.name: Roberts’ gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robert’s Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robia legula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robins' moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mixed coral, sand and weed bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Robinsia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robinsichthys arrowsmithensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known specimens were trawled from deep water (92-596m), along the edge of the bank, which consists of hard substrate (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Robin’s ghostshark
species.description: Espèce de chimères de la famille des chimaeridae. This species is likely to occur beyond 2,000 meters. Fragments of possible crab appendages recovered from a digestive tract indicate a diet of crustaceans and other benthic fauna (Ref. 116866).

species.name: Robust armoured-gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Robust assfish
species.description: Benthopelagic at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).   Of the 36 female specimens caught, 3 with 0.5-1.0 mm eggs.  No identifiable stomach contents were found (Ref. 84269).

species.name: Robust blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from three type specimens collected in the surge zone among large boulders at the Baton Is., Philippines. Probably oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive based on family traits (Ref. 205).

species.name: Robust cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).

species.name: Robust cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robust gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robust icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shelf waters of islands and caught in 2 bottom trawls at depths of 126 and 270-310 m, together with C. rhinoceratus, C. rugosus, C. panticapaei, C. bospori, C. irinae and C. mithridatis. Most specimens were caught at depth of 126 m in an area with abundant benthic fauna and the alga Macrocystis pyrifera. Apparently a primarily piscivorous predator (inferred from the single row of gill-rakers and similar to its congeners). Females mature at about 29-31 cm TL (25-27 cm SL); the post-spawning SGM VI-III is clearly detected in females larger than 31 cm TL and the SGM III - in the smaller, firstly maturing ones. The SGM of the males examined varied from stage II to early stage III in the specimen of 32.5 cm TL. Spawning and pre-spawning SGM were absent. Spawning period apparently takes a place from autumn to the beginning of winter (Ref. 90862).

species.name: Robust jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is occasionally encountered in the fish market and its flesh is reported to be relatively good.  It is taken incidentally in bottom trawls and by hook and line at 30-50 m (Ref. 81517).

species.name: Robust klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal weedy areas.

species.name: Robust mangrove goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud bottoms of estuaries, marine lakes and occasionally in the vicinity of reefs (Ref. 90102). Common in marine lakes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Robust mora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302) found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Robust pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males known to brood at 31.4 cm TL.

species.name: Robust pygmy-stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow quiet waters in light-colored sand (Ref. 9002).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Robust ribbongoby
species.description: Inhabits deep mud slopes subject to strong currents, usually in excess of 15 meters depth. Adults are solitary or in pairs while juveniles form small groups that resemble Ptereleotris when small (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Robust smallmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Robust soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in protected waters with silty sand and rubble bottoms.

species.name: Robust tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on continental shelf with captures from muddy substrata or a mixture of mud and sand (Ref. 126065).

species.name: Robust worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably a shallow water species (depth of occurrence unknown) (Ref. 104540).

species.name: Rocas gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow outer reefs and lagoons (Ref. 7247); in rock pools, from the surface to depths of at least 50 m (Ref. 13121, 58184), usually around rocks and rubble (Ref. 13121).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rocha's sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Rocio gemmata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rocio ocotal
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rocio spinosissima
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers.

species.name: Rock blackfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 33839).  Found in small groups under ledges and in caves (Ref. 33839).  Can quickly change from its uniformly dark color pattern to a blotchy coloration (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Rock blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow, weed-covered rocky reefs, including tide pools (Ref. 11482).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rock cale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow exposed rocky shores, aggregating in high-energy zone, just below foaming surface to depths of about 10 m (Ref. 9002); in kelp and weed areas (Ref. 86913). Feed on either loose or attached weeds and algae (Ref. 9002); mainly consisting of Corallina pilulifera, together with smaller quantities of Ulva actuca, Jania and filamentous species such as Sphacelaria sp. (Ref. 86913).

species.name: Rock carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in slow flowing deep water in rocky substratum.  Carnivore, feeds mainly on zoobenthos (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Rock clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky areas.  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Rock cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs in the continental shelf and in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Often found in caves (Ref.9002).

species.name: Rock damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in very shallow water in the surge zone of exposed rocky shores (Ref. 3921).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed mainly on benthic algae and occasionally on small invertebrates (Ref. 3921).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rock darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Rock flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore and over reefs (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Rock greenling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in shallow rocky areas, especially on exposed coasts (Ref. 2850).  Often captured by shore fishers (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Rock ling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon and benthic species in rocky habitat (Ref. 34024).  Restricted to estuaries, shallow bays and coastal reefs (Ref. 33847).  Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Juveniles are found in seagrass beds in estuaries while adults inhabit caves and rocky recesses (Ref. 33847).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Important as a recreational fish (Ref. 33839).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Rock pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and rocky or coral reefs.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rock prickleback
species.description: Found in rocky areas, from intertidal to 18 m depth, mostly on exposed coast (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184).  Feed mainly on algae (Ref. 6885).  Oviparous, eggs are laid in several clumps or masses which are guarded by the male (Ref. 58332).  Breathe air (Ref. 31184) and can stay out of water for 17-23 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).

species.name: Rock sea bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers hard bottom, rocks, jetties and ledges.

species.name: Rock-catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky habitats in flowing water, favoring rapids.  Feeds on invertebrates, especially insects, taken from rock surfaces; larger specimens also take small fish.  Rarely caught by anglers (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Rock-pool blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the shallow littoral zone, in areas exposed to sunlight, between algae-covered pebbles.  Feed almost exclusively on algae (Ref. 5981).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Mature nesting males actively defend territory, court females and provide parental care to eggs (Ref. 94113).

species.name: Rockcut goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, rocky areas.

species.name: Rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are residents of intertidal zone with homing behavior (Ref. 32612) found in pools with rocks or boulders.  May leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Feed mostly on invertebrates, particularly crustaceans and mollusks.  They breathe air when out of water (Ref. 31184) and swim with an eel-like motion (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rockhead
species.description: Inhabits intertidal areas and to 18 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Frequently caught in tide pools (Ref. 28197).  Its food consists mainly of tiny crustaceans (shrimp and crab-like creatures) which are picked from the bottom or very close to it (Ref. 4930).  Demersal spawner in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Rockpool blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in intertidal areas, with homing behavior (Ref. 32612).  Also found in subtidal rocky areas.  Demersal spawners in nearshore habitats (Ref. 56049).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Eggs are guarded by the male (Ref. 32612).  Non-emerging air-breathers (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic (Ref. 58302), occurring in  rocky shores exposed to surf; dwell in holes and crevices to escape heavy wave action (Ref. 205).  They feed on algae, detritus and small invertebrates.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rocksucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on sea urchins and limpets (Ref. 6614).

species.name: Rockwall clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the surge zone along rocky shores (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Rockweed gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal (Ref. 31184), commonly found in rockweed (Fucus) masses, in tide pools and inshore areas. May remain out of water under rocks or seaweed (Ref. 31184). Feeds on small crustaceans and mollusks. Breathes air (Ref. 31184) and can stay out of water for 5-20 hours if kept moist (Ref. 51276).

species.name: Rocky kurper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky streams, favoring marginal habitats where the current is slow.  Preys on insects, crabs and small fish.  Is preyed upon by introduced predators such as bass and sharptooth catfish.  Breeds in summer.  Males guard the eggs and larvae which are found on the substrate (Ref. 41595).  Upon hatching, larvae adhered permanently to the substrate at the nesting site (Ref. 41595).

species.name: Rocky shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear water rivers and streams of moderate to high gradient with gravel and rubble substrates.

species.name: Rocote
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A generally active and free-swimming rockfish found in midwater above a rocky reef or steep shoreline; occasionally huddling motionless among caves and crevices (Ref. 27436).  Young are found in shallow water (Ref. 2850).  Form schools (Ref. 2850).  Feed mostly on small pelagic crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten pan-fried, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Roeboexodon geryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboexodon guyanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Relatively rare.  Encountered in creeks with rapidly flowing water over a sandy substrate.  The particular form of its dentition allows it to feed on the scales of the other fish (Ref. 12225).  See color photo in Ref. 12225.

species.name: Roeboides affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides araguaito
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides biserialis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides bussingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides carti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers slightly turbid standing water.  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Roeboides dientonito
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides dispar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides ilseae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit stagnant sections or stretches of low to moderate current in streams between 10 and 660 m elevation (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Roeboides loftini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides margareteae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides myersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides numerosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides occidentalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides oligistos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides prognathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inlets and backwater of rivers and slow-flowing streams.  Forages mostly at twilight, stalking larger fishes to feed on their scales.  Approaches its prey stealthily and usually aims at prey's flank.  Its translucent body likely favor this stealthy approach.  Strikes at prey mostly with its mouth closed, dislodging the scales with its stout, external and forward directed foremost premaxillary and dentary teeth.  These teeth are often worn and sometimes missing, the differential teeth wear indicating right or left-handedness of a given individual (Ref. 28733).  The jarring strike dislodges a few scales which are swallowed immediately if taken in the mouth, or are picked up as they sink.  Besides scales, it feeds on aquatic insects.  Juveniles up to 3 cm still do not bear the stout external teeth, hence feed mostly on insects and tiny crustaceans (e.g. ostracods) (Ref. 40383).

species.name: Roeboides sazimai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roeboides xenodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roestes itupiranga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roestes molossus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roestes ogilviei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rofen's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found along exposed rocky shores (Ref. 54980). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rofen’s barracudina
species.description: Off southern Taiwan, the smaller specimens were collected by mid-water trawl (<100 m depth) while the larger ones usually caught by demersal trawl (> 300 m), which may suggest that the adults shift to deeper waters with growth/age (Ref, 123138).

species.name: Rogadius fehlmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rohteichthys microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rolland's demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur singly or in small groups in lagoons, harbors, and outer reef slopes.  Found among corals and coral rubble (Ref. 9710).  Feed mainly on zooplankton.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  DNA analysis suggests that this species could be divided to three species at least, i.e. fish from (1) Andaman Sea, (2) Indo-Australian archipelago, and (3) New Caledonia and southern Coral Sea are distinct species. Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Roman nose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and rivers of lowland regions, above tidal influence. Collected from generally clear waters (sometimes in turbid waters), over bottoms usually consisting of gravel, sand and some mud. Feeds mostly on algae (Ref. 26669, 44894) and bottom detritus. Little is known of the life history, but it probably has a marine larval stage. Only recently described, although it has long been misidentified as Awaous crassilabrus, a species that does not occur in Australia (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Romanogobio amplexilabris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Romanogobio banaticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Romanogobio benacensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups in a wide variety of habitats such as large lowland rivers, canals, warm streams and lakes. Avoids very fast waters and usually found on sand bottom (Ref. 59043). A short-lived species which inhabits running clean waters with gravelly or sandy bottoms (Ref. 12291). Preys on a variety of small invertebrates. Life span is about 4 years. Threatened due to pollution, river-bed alterations and competition from introduced Gobio gobio (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Romanogobio elimeius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits main course of large rivers and main tributaries, in relatively deep water, with sand bottom and near riffles.  Attains up to about 10 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Romanogobio johntreadwelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Romanogobio parvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in turbid waters with very strong current (Ref. 52363).  Occurs in large, high-gradient river stretches with fast but not turbulent current and gravel or sand bottom.  Active at night where it stays near shore on mud or sand bottom.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, mainly Trichoptera larvae.  Appears to spawn late and to have a long spawning period.  Many small juveniles are observed in July (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Romanogobio vladykovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottom of moderately flowing large and medium size lowland rivers, preferring sand bottom.  Also found in lake. Juvenile may occur in backwaters.  Active at night, feeding on insect larvae and other large benthic invertebrates. Populations most likely have declined due to construction of large reservoirs on Danube in 20th century and have stabilized at a moderate level since (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rombou cyclope
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms of the continental shelf.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Rombou de canal
