species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms of the continental plateau (Ref. 5217, 5377).  Feeds on worms and crustaceans.  Exhibits sexual dimorphism (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Rombou de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rombou de plage
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow muddy bottoms from the coastline to 75 m depth; also in brackish estuaries and hypersaline lagoons (Ref. 5217).  Inhabit mainly coastal waters and tidelands, but abundant in waters very near the sea to a few meters elevation with wholly freshwater ichthyofauna (Ref. 36880).  Feeds mainly on zooplankton and zoobenthos  (Ref. 13196).  Taken with beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rombou de St. Hélène
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud, sand, gravel and shell bottoms.  Marketed fresh and dried salted.

species.name: Rombou du Pacifique
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 9281).  Utilized fresh (Ref. 9281).

species.name: Rombou lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear sandy areas near mangroves, among seagrass, coral or rubble (Ref.9710).  Most common flounder around coral reefs (Ref. 26938).  Often partially buried in sand, occasionally on hard bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Feeds mainly on small fishes but also on crustaceans and octopuses.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rombou léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or silty sand, and muddy bottoms of inner reef flats and seaward reefs; juveniles frequently found in tide pools (Ref. 9824, 48637).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 5213).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4537) and processed into fish meal (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Rombou noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays, lagoons, and shallow coastal waters.  Found on soft bottoms of continental shelf to a depth of about 90 m, more common between 10-50 m (Ref. 5217). Feeds on crustaceans, polychaetes and mollusks (Ref. 36453).

species.name: Rombou ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas with coral rubble or seagrasses, usually near patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Shallow coastal waters to depths of 110 m (Ref. 26938).  Lies motionless on the bottom, moving only when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Larvae are attracted to lights at night but are difficult to see because they are transparent (Ref. 26938).  About one-third of the diet consists of fishes; the rest of its food is crustaceans:  crabs, shrimps, amphipods, and mantis shrimps (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Rombou ovale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 9824).  Found in sandy and muddy areas of the continental shelf (Ref. 5213).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9824).  Most sexually dimorphic characters develop at about 8 cm SL (Ref. 9824).  Marketed fresh or used in making fish meal (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Rombou podas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters, over sandy and muddy bottoms of the continental plateau (Ref. 5377, 12382).  Feeds on benthic small fishes and invertebrates.  Reproduction occurs between May and August.  Small individuals adapt well in aquariums but require sufficient bottom areas (Ref. 12382).

species.name: Rombou rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 9281).

species.name: Rombou tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.  Bycatch of shrimp trawl fisheries (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rombou tropicale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy bottoms of coastal coral reefs (Ref. 5213, 48637), generally in shallow water (Ref. 9281).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Hunt mostly at night, but also active during the day.  Often crawling over low rocky reef (Ref. 48637).  Occasionally rest on bare rock (Ref. 1602).  Feed on fishes, crabs and shrimps.  Collected by divers (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Rombou à quatre yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms of the continental shelf.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Roncador catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rondeau brème
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found over mud bottoms in mangrove sloughs and on vegetated sand bottoms, sometimes in brackish water and occasionally also in coral reef areas near mangroves.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (small bivalves, crustaceans), as well as on plant material.

species.name: Rondeau mouton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and estuaries.  Freely enters brackish waters; sometimes enters freshwaters (Ref.  26938).  Commonly found around pilings.  Caught by anglers from jetties or rocky shores (Ref.  9988).  Feeds mainly on mollusks and crustaceans.  An excellent food fish.  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref.  9988).

species.name: Rondeletia bicolor
species.description: Espèce de plantes.

species.name: Rondonacara hoehnei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12965).  Adults exhibit biparental care (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Ronquillo's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  Not common in museum collections, so perhaps not very abundant.  More specimens and data needed.

species.name: Roosevelt's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas with rock or algae cover (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Rooster snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from large tide pools.

species.name: Roque toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rose groppo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rose Island basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reefs and in caves with rich invertebrate growth in walls (Ref. 48635); feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 1602). Cryptic and seldom seen (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rose tadpolefish
species.description: Collected by bottom trawl at  140 m with bottom water temperature at -0.9°C, salinity 34.18 ppt over sandy silt and clay bottom (Ref. 116680).

species.name: Rose-veiled fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly in mesophotic coral ecosystems and likely to occur in greater depths. Like other Cirrhilabrus species, it frequents rubble bottoms scattered with loose coral cover (Ref. 125961).

species.name: Rosefin barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and riffles in clear rocky streams (Ref. 52193). It feeds on aquatic and adult flying insects and takes trout flies (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Rosefin rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a variety of habitats, but seems to prefer large rivers with slow current (Ref. 27732).  Common along shores in large rivers (Ref. 56749).  Found at or near the surface in clear waters of rivers and streams.  Generally prefers a depth of about 5 m.  Feeds mainly on exogenous insects, some small crustaceans and algae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Rosefin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on insects taken in midwater areas and from the surface (Ref. 10294).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably open substratum spawners like congeners.

species.name: Rosefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rosenberg's jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy/mud bottoms in 1-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rosenblattia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rosenblattichthys nemotoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rosen’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected at Caño Bravo in the Río Apure drainage of Venezuela, from a white water habitat over a substrate of sand and clay covered with leaf litter and at water depths of up to 1.5 m (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Rosethorn rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Often caught on commercial longlines set below 108 m (Ref. 27437).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Rosette river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rosette torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roswitha's toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small rivers; adults found in schools (Ref. 42972).

species.name: Rosy barb
species.description: Poisson. Adults inhabit lakes and fast flowing hill streams (Ref. 4832, 41236).  One of the hardiest of the barbs, undemanding and beautiful; most impressively colored during the mating period, when the normally silvery male takes on a rich claret flush and the slightly larger female becomes more luminous.  Can be kept together with other small fishes.  Feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020, 44894).  Prolific spawners that tolerate low water temperatures (Ref. 44894).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Rosy basslet
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 51183).

species.name: Rosy bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow ponds and marshes of plains, and adjacent irrigation canals (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Rosy blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide variety of shoreline habitats and patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Found in sponge beds in shallow waters and grassy areas (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Rosy clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky areas near the shore (Ref. 11482).  Territorial (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Rosy cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rosy curimata
species.description: Feeds on detritus (Ref. 12371).

species.name: Rosy deepsea boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf and continental slope.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rosy dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and rubble bottoms adjacent to coral reefs or rocky areas (Ref. 33412).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Rosy dwarf monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on sand-rubble bottom (Ref. 123359).

species.name: Rosy flagfin
species.description: A demersal species found on sandy bottom (Ref. 105374).

species.name: Rosy grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits trawling grounds.  Rarely caught, by handline from depths deeper than 100 m (Ref. 559).

species.name: Rosy Jewelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rosy razorfish
species.description: Most common in open sandy areas.  Feeds on small sand-dwelling invertebrates.  Dives head first into the sand when frightened.  Generally common (Ref. 9710).  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rosy rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught fairly often by sport fishers using small hooks (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Rosy roughy
species.description: The mature female specimen (24.7 cm SL) with well-developed eggs and the male specimen (21.4 cm SL) with well-developed testes; females (19.5-20.9 cm SL) with mature eggs, suggests that this species is a small species, which reproduces at a length c. 20.0 cm SL (Ref. 129008).

species.name: Rosy sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon.  Found in intertidal and subtidal areas.

species.name: Rosy tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rosy triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs at depths of 10 m or shallower (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rosy weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaweed belts along the coast.

species.name: Rosy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Rosylip sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal (Ref. 31184) and inhabits tide pools and rocky inshore areas on exposed coasts (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Rosyside dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky flowing pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  Usually occurs in small clear streams (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Rotengle italien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in well vegetated lowland rivers, backwaters, oxbows, ponds, and lakes. Feeds mainly on macrophytes and terrestrial insects. Spawns on submerged plants when temperature rises above 18° C. May form locally hybrid populations with introduced Scardinius erythrophthalmus. Attains a maximum size of up to about 40 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rothschild's barracudina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302, 75154).

species.name: Rotuma lewisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rotuma triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit exposed rocky and coralline boulders of coasts (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rotund blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Roucaou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters near rocky or sandy bottoms.  Feed on benthic invertebrates.  Solitary (Ref. 2683).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Males build dish shaped nests and guard the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rouffe africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near islands (Ref. 27000).  Feeds on planktonic salps, cephalopods and small fishes (Ref. 11228).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 11228.

species.name: Rouffe antarctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common over or near rocky areas at 100-300 m (Ref. 9258). Generally, blue eye remain close to the sea bed during the day and move up in the water column at night, following concentrations of food (Ref. 6390). The fish are found over rough ground and at the edges of canyons and steep drop-offs. Blue eye appear to prefer cold water as part of their general behavior (Ref. 6390). Juveniles inhabit surface waters, sometimes in association with floating debris (Ref. 6390). Feed primarily on the pelagic tunicate Pyrosoma atlantica which is found near the sea bed during the day but dispersed throughout the water column at night (Ref. 7129, 30454). They also feed on squid, mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 30455, 30454) and fish ranging from small lanternfish (Myctophidae) to large fish such as gemfish (Rexea solandri). Juveniles consume small planktonic and sedentary organisms (Ref. 30456). Marketed fresh and frozen; exported to Japan for sashimi; eaten steamed, fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Rouffe chiffon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at the edge of the continental shelf and near oceanic islands (Ref. 6942).  Adults are demersal on the continental slope in 800 to 1,000 m; subadults and juveniles found in surface waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Rouffe des méduses
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on medusae and ctenophores (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Rouffe impérial
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers deep water at the edge of continental shelves and around oceanic islands; larger specimens near the bottom (Ref. 4542). Young are epipelagic and associate with floating jellyfish, including Physalia (Ref. 4542). Adults are caught on hooks baited with fish or squid. Its white flesh is reported to be good-tasting (Ref. 4542).

species.name: Rouffe indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found  in deep water, forming small schools (Ref. 30573).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rouffe rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shelf and slope waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on rocky bottoms and (near shore) coral reefs, as well as in brackish lagoons and sometimes in lower courses of rivers (Ref. 2683, 57393, 81653). Maximum reported size only 200mm TL in Ref. 57393.

species.name: Rouget
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the coastal waters of the continental shelf, over sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 4845).

species.name: Rouget barbet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on  gravel, sand and mud bottoms of the continental shelf.  Depth range from 10-300 m (Ref. 07313) and up to depth of 328 in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on small benthic crustaceans, worms and mollusks (Ref. 4845).  Marketed mainly fresh (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Rouget barbet (Mullus surmuletus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on broken and rough grounds but also found over sand and soft bottoms at depths less than 100 m.  Depth range from 5-60 m (Ref. 07313) and from 305-409 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feed on benthic organisms such as shrimps and amphipods, polychaetes, mollusks, and benthic fishes.  Spawning occurs from May to July, eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 4845).  Marketed fresh and frozen for steaming, pan-frying, broiling and baking (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Rouget-barbet argentin
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Marketed fresh.

species.name: Rouget-barbet bandeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs to over 25 m (Ref. 9710).  Found on sandy or weedy bottoms (Ref. 30573); rarely at depths of more than 40 meters (Ref. 54393).  Usually seen solitary but often several individuals nearby (Ref. 48636).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and worms (Ref. 54393).

species.name: Rouget-barbet doré
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found on coral (Ref. 58652), rocky, or rubble bottoms of reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 3921).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Juveniles form schools, adults usually solitary.  Feed primarily on small fishes, crustaceans, peanut worms, shrimps, crabs, octopi, and small gastropods during the day (Ref. 3921).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Rouget-barbet double-tache
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. This occasionally schooling species inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs:  juveniles on reef flats, adults tend to occur around rocky or coralline areas of high vertical relief.  Feeds on crustaceans at daytime and on fishes and crab larvae at night.  Also feeds on worms (Ref. 6113).  Occurs in 3 color forms.  The Indian Ocean form has 2 sharply defined wedge-shaped bars become narrower and sometimes end on the belly.  The Indo-Australian form has 3 very distinct dark patches and rows of yellow spots on the sides.  The Pacific Plate form has 2 wide bars that extend to the belly (Ref. 37816).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Rouget-barbet pastille
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Primarily an insular species (Ref. 30573).  Usually solitary, it occurs in seagrass beds (Ref. 41878) as well as over sand, rubble, or coral and rock bottoms of shallow lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 46 m (Ref. 30874).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on benthic animals like crabs, polychaetes and other worms during the day (Ref. 30874), also shrimps, heart urchins, gastropods, pelecypods, foraminiferans, brittle stars, and fishes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Rouget-barbet sellé
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found on sandy bottoms and murky areas of coastal waters (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Rouget-barbet tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters to depths of 90 m (Ref. 9626), especially over sand and rock bottoms in reef areas. Young juveniles often found on beds of seagrass, e.g. Thalassia. Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 9626). Flesh highly esteemed; marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 3792). Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Rouget-barbet trille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sandy and muddy bottoms near the coast and in deep waters as well (Ref. 9322).

species.name: Rouget-barbet à tache noire
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits coastal reefs and estuaries (Ref. 9002); in Indonesia mainly found on deep reefs adjacent to strong currents (Ref. 90102).  Juveniles found in small schools; adults singly or in small aggregations (Ref. 9002, 48636).  May also be solitary.  It is rare in the East Indian region, and found only in cool areas of upwelling; but is common in subtropical latitudes (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Rouget-souris aurore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, entering estuaries (Ref. 30573). Sandy-muddy bottom (Ref. 43239).  Forms schools (Ref. 5213).  Has appearance of sillaginids when schooling (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Rouget-souris bande d'or
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in coastal waters with a muddy substrate.  Forms large schools (Ref. 9987).  Usually fast swimming with short stops to feed (Ref. 48636).  Sold fresh in markets.  Utilized for fish meal.  Valued also for its roe (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Rouget-souris bensasi
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Widespread in sandy regions (Ref. 9137). Minimum depth from Ref. 098481.

species.name: Rouget-souris mignon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 3792).  Juveniles up to 8 cm are pelagic (Ref. 9626).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3792).  Flesh considered good quality; marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 3792).  In southwestern Brazil found in 112 m depth (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Rouget-souris orangé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline (Ref. 12743).  Inhabits sandy lagoons and sheltered coastal waters.  Also found over muddy bottoms (Ref. 5213).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Often in groups (Ref. 9710).  In the north-east coast of India, the male to female ratio was 1:1.5 in most months (Ref. 28761).  Feeds primarily on small crustaceans.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Rouget-souris rayé
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits sheltered, often turbid inshore waters over sand or mud substrates; found near corals (Ref. 5213), in very shallow water, usually in small groups (Ref. 9947).  Reported to cause hallucinations when eaten (Ref. 4690).

species.name: Rouget-souris à bande sombre
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Known to enter lower reaches of rivers. Usually found on sandy bottoms in nearshore areas; usually solitary (Ref. 68964). Forms small to moderately large aggregations at all sizes (Ref. 48636).  Minimum depth from Ref. 3470.

species.name: Rough anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 75154) and temperate species (Ref. 7300) found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Rough bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling in caves and near rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Rough dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Rough flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken by trawling over mud and sand at depths to about 55 m (Ref. 9790).  Juveniles may enter brackish water.

species.name: Rough leatherjackets
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass beds and on rocky reefs. Females of this species may be confused with female Penicipelta vittiger [= Acanthaluteres vittiger] (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Rough leg skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rough oreodory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope, benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rough pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs offshore in warm and temperate waters (Ref. 6697).  May spawn widely in the subtropics (Ref. 6697).

species.name: Rough sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated runs and riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers, usually over mud in clear, fairly deep water (1-2 m).

species.name: Rough shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and gravel-bottomed flowing pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Rough silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along shore and in bays and inlets.

species.name: Rough velvetfish
species.description: Occurs on soft bottom.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rough-head whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by commercial and research vessels.

species.name: Rough-headed dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal and sandy estuaries along seagrass and reef margins, usually in small aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Rough-scaled flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Caught with shrimp bottom trawls.

species.name: Roughback batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore water, usually from 54-125 m depth.

species.name: Roughback sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on sand bottom, also on mud bottom.  Occurs in intertidal areas and up to 142 m depth (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 4925).  Aquarium observations indicate that this is nocturnal (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Roughcheek jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed using shells and rubble to close their burrow opening (Ref. 26893).

species.name: Roughcheek sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from intertidal areas to 27 m depth.  A rare species (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Rougheye rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found offshore (Ref. 27437).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Roughhead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Almost always found in holes of corals.  Feed on amphipods and copepods (Ref. 5521).  Main diet of  benthic harpacticoid copepods (Ref. 94105).   Oviparous (Ref. 56066).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56066).

species.name: Roughhead shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear rocky pools and backwaters of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Roughhead triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit patch reefs and rocky bottoms (Ref. 5521).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Roughlip cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roughlip grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roughnose stingray
species.description: Found most abundant near the coast in regions of high riverine outflow.  Largest immature male was found to be 27.5 cm WD.  No data on size at birth, with smallest specimen 13.2 cm WD of a late male embryo (Ref. 58027). Data for Max.Length of female from Ref.58027. Caught occasionally by bottom trawl and demersal gillnet fisheries operating off Sumatra and Kalimantan. Utilized for its meat and probably its skin (Ref.58048).

species.name: Roughridge pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Roughscale flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9774).  Feeds mainly on small demersal fishes (Ref. 9774).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Roughscale sole
species.description: Genre de poissons. Occurs on mud and sand bottoms (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Roughscale tonguesole
species.description: Inhabits sand and silt bottoms in 3-30 m, sometimes near reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Roughskin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Five known specimens.

species.name: Roughskin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live at the mouths of rivers that fall into the seas along the coasts of the warmly temperate zone of East Asia.  Carnivore.  Can grow to 12-14 cm long and becomes sexually mature in one year (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Roughskin trunkfish
species.description: A secretive species found in holes and crevices in rocky seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Roughsnout ghost pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in algal/rubble reefs and sandy bottoms, often at depths below 10 m (Ref. 90102).  Mostly pelagic until they settle on the substrate for breeding (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Roughsnout grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily a pelagic feeder, feeds primarily on pelagic copepods, but also takes mysids, shrimps, cephalopods, fish, polychaetes and gastropods (Ref. 1371).  Mainly reduced to fishmeal and oil (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Roughsnout whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Roughspine sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on flat bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Roughspine seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Roughspine triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Roughtail skate
species.description: Inhabits deeper waters than hardnose skates and reported to prefer medium to cold temperatures and low oxygen environments compared to its congeners. It is found over a wide range of substrates, from fine sediment to rocky environments. Feeds mostly on benthic  organisms, including annelids, shrimps, crabs, and fishes, with adults preferring fishes, whereas juveniles consume mostly invertebrates (Ref. 126515).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Reported size at maturity for males 74 cm TL and for females 80 cm TL with males growing to at least 90 cm TL and females at least 89 cm TL; with size at birth 9-16 cm TL. Maximum age reported estimated to be 20 years for males and 17 years for females. Egg cases small in size (6.2-7.8 cm TL), colour dark brown and becoming light golden brown on keels, which are smooth and plush-like when touched. Egg cases with long, slender horns at each corner, curving inwardly and slightly overlap at their tips with a distinct crossbar originating midway along the posterior horns in some specimens (Ref. 126515).

species.name: Roughtip grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most numerous at 450 to 730 m in the open Atlantic and at 500 to 800 m in the Mediterranean.  Feeds on small crustaceans (copepods, amphipods, decapods, mysids, etc.) and polychaetes (Ref. 1371)

species.name: Roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal shallow water (Ref. 9872).  Also in Ref. 9137.

species.name: Roule-caillou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles, runs, and pools of headwaters, creeks, and small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Subadults and adults feed on detritus, filamentous algae, diatoms and occasionally on small aquatic insects; young on rotifers and microcrustacea (Ref. 10294). Reported maximum length is 17 cm TL (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Rouleina danae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rouleina euryops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rouleina livida
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rouleina nuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Rouleina watasei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Round hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-migrant.  Dioecious, adult photophore complement acquired at about 20 mm SL (Ref. 4739).

species.name: Round scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Round tail paradisefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology similar to Macropodus opercularis. Reported to be well-adapted to low winter temperatures (4-25°C); adults and juveniles (about 1.5 cm SL), are sometimes active under ice cover (E. Willems pes.comm. 11/12).

species.name: Round whip ray
species.description: Demersal, inshore on continental shelves, frequently in coastal embayments near large river mouths (Ref.58048).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Regionally common by-catch of bottom trawl and beach seine fisheries off southern Borneo. Utilized for its meat, skin and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Round-scaled barbell
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits streams and rivers, preferring stretches with clear water and riffles (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Roundbelly cowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral and rocky reefs of coastal areas (Ref. 9806, 48637).  Also common on offshore sand and mudflats (Ref. 48637).  Young fish occur in oceanic waters, at or near the surface (Ref. 2850); semi-transparent young may enter estuaries (Ref. 3141).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9806).  A large number of juveniles were found in the stomachs of flatheads (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Roundbelly pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species, chiefly near the coast and entering lagoons, where salinities vary with the tides; it is presumably euryhaline, although it may escape high salinities (Ref. 188). Ripe females of 3.5 to 4.0 cm standard length were recorded in Ebrié Lagoon (Ref. 188, 1989).

species.name: Roundel batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottom (Ref. 2850).  Adults feed on small crustaceans and fish (Ref. 4525).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36492).  Eggs are presumably contained in floating rafts (Ref. 36492).

species.name: Roundhead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mangroves and sheltered bays (Ref. 90102).  Occur among corals, rocks, and rubble of shallow waters (Ref. 1602, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Roundhead grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 3587).  Remains of fish have been found in one stomach (Ref. 6187).

species.name: Roundnose knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to reach 70 cm TL (Ref. 81048).

species.name: Roundnose lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic, at 375-650 m by day (most common at 500 m); nycto-epipelagic at surface and down to 200 m (Ref. 4775).  Neustonic at 0-200 m at night (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Roundnose minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools, sometimes runs, of headwaters, creeks, and small rivers.  Often occurs among filamentous algae (Ref. 86798).  Feeds mainly on algae and other plants (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Roundscale goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand, sand/mud or mud bottoms (Ref. 91780).

species.name: Roundsnout Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Typically recorded from clear water in slow to moderately flowing creeks to large rivers (1.0-12.0 m average width and 0.1-0.6 m average depth), flowing through light to heavily forested (and shaded) catchments, consisting mainly of pools, glides and riffles with smaller areas of still backwaters. It is also recorded from modified streams in areas almost completely cleared for grazing. Substrate often consists of bedrock, boulder, cobble and coarse sand with smaller amounts of pebble, gravel and silt. Instream cover is typically provided by rock, timber debris, and smaller amounts of aquatic vegetation, leaf litter and bank and vegetation overhang. Average pool depth ranged from 0.2-1.8 m. It is collected at densities ranging from < 0.1-1.5 fish/m2 and found with other native fish species Shortfinned eel, Anguilla reinhardtii (Longfinned Eel), Retropinna sp. (Eastern smelt), and River Blackfish, native decapod crustaceans, Common Freshwater Shrimp, East Gippsland Spiny Crayfish and Variable Spiny Crayfish (Euastacus yanga), and a native bivalve mollusc (Hyridella sp.). Recorded with the alien species Brown Trout, though probably occupies a discrete micro-habitat (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Roundsnout gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms in coastal marine waters, over the continental shelf (Ref. 33616).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Roundtail chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs, sometimes pools, of creeks and small to large rivers as well as impoundments.  May hybridize with <i>Gila cypha throughout their shared range except in Yampa River (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Roundtooth hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually in shallow inshore waters (Ref. 267).

species.name: Roussette barbichette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on or near the bottom of warm-temperate waters, from the intertidal zone to 256 m (Ref. 5578).  Prefers rocky reefs (Ref. 5578).  Nocturnal (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small bony fish, crustaceans, octopus and polychaete worms (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Readily kept in captivity (Ref. 244).

species.name: Roussette boa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental and insular slopes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roussette brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found close inshore on the continental shelf, often in shallow, rocky areas (Ref. 244).  Feeds on lobsters, crabs and small bony fish (Ref. 5578).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Readily kept in captivity (Ref. 244).  Caught by shore anglers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Roussette cloquée
species.description: Found on the continental slope.  Maximum length is from an immature specimen.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roussette des Galapagos
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. This species were observed living on the bottom above sand or sand and mud substrates, 
in the vicinity of lava boulders, either over flat bottoms or along slopes to 45° (Ref. 89625).

species.name: Roussette maille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf and upper slope on rough, rocky bottom.  Water temperature:  8.5-11.3°C.  Food habits unknown.  Oviparous.  Not utilized at present.  Found in waters 75-550 m deep (Ref. 26938). Lives at depths off 36-230m in the northern portion of its range, and in waters deeper than 460m in its southern range (Ref. 55294). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 55584.

species.name: Roussette naine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slope.  Little is known of its biology.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roussette nuageuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common catshark found on the continental shelf, from close inshore down to at least 100 m (Ref. 244, 11230); with records from the Tsushima Strait at 120 m and Korea Strait at 140 m depth; also known to enter shallow coastal waters (Ref. 120402). Oviparous (Ref. 50449). Adult males are between 36.0-40.0 cm TL (largest reported 77.8 cm TL) while adult female sizes at 37.0-42.0 cm TL (largest 47.8 cm TL). Egg capsules are translucent yellow with smooth surface, with anterior tip slightly concave and posterior tip truncate, with long tendrils (mean values for egg capsule dimensions: 5.5 cm length. 1.9 cm width, n = 3) (Ref. 120402). Interest to fisheries unknown (Ref. 11146).

species.name: Roussette polka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer continental shelf.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roussette rubanée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 5578).  Prefers rocky reefs from the intertidal zone down to 100 m depth (Ref. 5578).  Nocturnal, often found in caves and crevices during the day (Ref. 5578).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, but also bony fish and cephalopods (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Readily kept in captivity (Ref. 244).

species.name: Roussette selle blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the upper continental slope.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Not utilized at present.

species.name: Roussette sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental shelf, in inshore waters (Ref. 244).  Most common in shallow sandy areas (Ref. 244).  Feeds on small bottom-dwelling fish, crustaceans, and cephalopods (Ref. 27121).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught by shore anglers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Roussette taches de son
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is reported to be associated with coral or calcareous algal formations where it possibly lays it egg-capsules.  Stomach contents include squid beaks and skeletal elements of bony fishes.  Reported males with well-developed claspers at about 35.3 cm TL; females as adults from 41.5 cm TL.  Egg-capsules observed to have light amber to yellowish colour, without longitudinal grooves and measure about 6.0 cm in length, 2.5 cm in width (Ref. 107325).  Found on the continental shelf and upper slope.  Oviparous.  Not utilized at present (Ref. 244).

species.name: Roussette thalassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky and muddy bottoms of the continental shelf and upper slope.  Temperature:  11-16°C.  Salinity:  30 ppt.  Oxygen:  1.0-1.6 ml/l.  Feeds on bony fishes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roussette vipérine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore and offshore waters of the continental shelf, on sandy and rocky bottoms (Ref. 244).  Feeds on bony fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught by surf anglers (Ref. 244).

species.name: Roussette à taches brunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Adult size unknown (Ref. 11146).  Habitat and biology unknown (Ref. 244).

species.name: Roussette à taches jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common inshore to offshore catshark.  Prefers to feed on small bony fishes and crustaceans, also cephalopods (Ref. 244).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Roux's pygmy-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove shores and brackish lakes in 0-2 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Royal blue hap
species.description: Found mostly on sediment-rich substrates on deeper regions but is also found in the intermediate sand-rock habitats.  An opportunistic feeder that feeds from the drifting sediment in the water column (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Royal dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal to deep outer-reef drop-offs (Ref. 8631).  Hovers close to coral or rubble (Ref. 9710). Solitary or in small loosely scattered groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Royal gramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in caves or under ledges.  Swim with belly toward substratum, thus under ledges seen upside down.  Feed on ectoparasites of other fishes (Ref. 5521).  Males show various types of nest care behavior (Ref. 35580).  Retreat into recesses when alarmed (Ref. 9710).  Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Royal Splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing water with dense algal growth on rocks.  Also occurs in swamps (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Royal sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species (Ref. 188).

species.name: Royal tetra
species.description: Poisson. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Ruaha lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Ruanoho decemdigitatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in sheltered to moderately exposed areas shallower down to 21 m; less associated with rocky substratum, but may be found under, side or top of rocks.  They are found in offshore islands and coastal mainland areas (Ref. 84086).  They feed on a range of benthic invertebrates including ophiuroids, archaeogastropods, trichoptera and errant polychaetes (Ref. 84084).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rubberlip seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found in rocky areas, also in kelp and near jetties and pilings (Ref. 2850). From Surf zone to 50 m (Ref. 96339). Often in schools (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rubbernose conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rubble goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms.

species.name: Rubicundus lopheliae
species.description: This species is closely associated with the reef structure of the deep-sea reef building coral L. pertusa (Ref. 75169).

species.name: Rubicundus rubicundus
species.description: Only one specimen known.

species.name: Rubinoff's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky areas.  They feed on tiny invertebrates and algae (Ref. 11482).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rubricatochromis cerasogaster
species.description: Probably an open substratum spawner with well-defined pair-bonding (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Rubricatochromis guttatus
species.description: Eurytopic; found most frequently in association with stands of emergent or submerged aquatic plants; particularly abundant in shallower and quieter stretches of large rivers, in small lateral tributaries of such streams, in oxbow lakes and in swampy habitats; even maintains breeding populations in coastal lagoons; absent from rapids zone of streams or in headwaters flowing through montane forest (Ref. 43352). Forest-associated species (Ref. 43352, 52307). Pair-bonding, substrate brooders (Ref. 52307, 81260). Aquarium keeping: aggressive species, requires sufficient space to build territories; omnivore; spawns up to 300 eggs which hatch after 2 days, young are free-swimming after 5 days (Ref. 57572).

species.name: Rubricatochromis lifalili
species.description: Absent from rapids and swampy habitats (Ref. 5644). Primarily found in forested habitats, but also in more savannah-like areas with gallery forests; open substratum spawner with well-defined pair-bonding (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Rubricatochromis paynei
species.description: Hemichromis paynei is found mainly in coastal areas (Ref. 52307). All specimens referred to as Hemichromis paynei in aquarist publications before 2004 do not actually belong to this species; they have definitely been misidentified (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Rubricatochromis stellifer
species.description: Pair-bonding, substrate brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260).

species.name: Ruby cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sheltered reef flats, lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of 17 m or more.  Feeds on small benthic crustaceans at night; cryptic under rocks or deep holes by day.

species.name: Ruby dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas of broken coral rubble interspersed with outcrops of soft and stony corals (Ref. 114910).

species.name: Ruby longfin fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ruby seadragon
species.description: Occurs more offshore in slightly deeper waters; at 50+m with complex habitat of a mixed reef and sandy habitat with two paratypes collected from the continental shelf (Ref. 100032).

species.name: Ruby tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Strongly red in nature, but gets pale in captivity.  Maximum length reported to reach 4 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Rubyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur near sandy or muddy bottom in deep water.  Feeds on larger zooplankton (Ref. 3394). Marketed fresh or frozen and proves to be an excellent foodfish (Ref. 115123).

species.name: Rubynose brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Locally abundant (Ref. 34024).  Juveniles mesopelagic, larger individuals benthic at depths of 600 to 1,000 m (Ref. 34024).  Ovoviviparous with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36488).

species.name: Rubyspot cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabit coral reef (Ref. 75154). Form small aggregations (Ref. 33415). Distinguished from A. cyanosoma by the presence of a single red spot at the midbase of the caudal fin, a higher number of gill rakers, and apparently a smaller maximum size (Ref. 33415).

species.name: Rudis rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on cephalopods, at least at larger sizes.

species.name: Rudolf lates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep waters (Ref. 3636).

species.name: Rufous coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species exhibits a generalised habitat selection and occupies a great range of Acropora corals. It is found in deeper water regions, at lower reef slope and fore reef areas, and is most common in corals such as Acropora samoensis, A. valida and A. secale, but was also observed in Acropora eurystoma and A. pharaonis in the northern Red Sea (Ref. 94082).

species.name: Rufus cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from exposed coral reefs (Ref. 40889). Solitary, also found in outer reef slopes in 15-80 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Rugby hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rummy-nose tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Rush darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rusi blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tidepools and rocky surge areas (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Rusichthys explicitus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rusichthys plesiomorphus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Russell's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Russell’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Russet angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rock, coral, or rubble areas of seaward reefs; juveniles occasionally in 5 m (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on algae and detritus (Ref. 13550).  Oviparous (Ref. 240), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Peak reproductive activity occurs from mid-December through May.  Spawn at dusk during the week before full moon (Ref. 4858).

species.name: Russetfin topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits vegetated sloughs, swamps, and quiet pools and backwaters of streams.  7.8 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Russian bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Russian river tule perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud- to gravel-bottomed pools and runs of small to large, low-elevation rivers and lakes.  Usually occurs near emergent aquatic plants or overhanging banks.  Rarely enters brackish water (Ref. 86798).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rust-banded wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found to depths over 35 m in deep outer reef drop-offs.  Forms aggregations of females and a single dominating male (Ref. 48636).  Planktivores (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Rusty angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward (Ref. 9710), rocky reefs and rubble areas, especially where algal growth is extensive (Ref. 47838).  Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 47838).  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35414).

species.name: Rusty Catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves (Ref. 59315).

species.name: Rusty goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow bottoms of coral reefs with clear water (Ref. 13628).  Usually found on undersides of ledges and roofs of caves (Ref. 26938).  Feeds on minute crustaceans (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Rusty perchlet
species.description: Known only from beam trawls and sled captures. From video camera footage, habitat consist of low relief silty sand/mud with dense patches of crinoids and erect, cup-shaped sponges (Ref. 123579).

species.name: Rusty scaly blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow reefs and tide pools, usually in clear waters where it feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 123106).

species.name: Rusty snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Rusty spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Burrowing species (Ref. 7300).  Inhabits sandy areas.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Rustyside sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of swift mountain creeks and small rivers.  Young occur in flowing pools.

species.name: Rutilus heckelii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A semi-anadromous species.  Occurs mostly in shallow brackish coastal waters.  While at sea, adults are most abundant at depth of 2.5-4.0 m and salinity of 2-4 ppt.  Enters freshwater of estuaries, lagoons and lower reaches of large rivers to spawn.  Commences movement to coast in August and to rivers in September, with a peak in October.  Stops migration by end of November and overwinters in main river or estuaries.  Continues spawning migration with breaking up of ice in March (Dniepr).  Breeds in April-May.  Adults migrate back to estuaries to forage immediately after spawning.  Juveniles move to estuaries during first summer in August.  Reported decline was due to blocking of almost all spawning rivers and decline of brackish areas in Black Sea basin (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rutilus kutum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rutilus meidingerii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in subalpine lakes.  Preys on benthic invertebrates.  Breeds in lake tributaries or streams connecting lakes in shallow areas with current and near shore. Has been extirpated since 1980 from two of five lakes it originally inhabited (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Rutilus stoumboudae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A lacustrine species adapted to still water (Ref. 96829).

species.name: Rutilus virgo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits medium sized to large rivers.  Spawns in fast-flowing water of riffles over gravel or submerged plants.  Attains a maximum size of about 40 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ruwenzori lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the shore regions of lakes and inflowing rivers.  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Rwandese carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rypticus randalli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ryukyu banded silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ryukyu gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 9771), benthic (Ref. 75154) species that inhabits continental shelves and insular areas.

species.name: Ryukyu ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy-muddy bottom (Ref. 27315).

species.name: Rémora blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near as well as far from the coast (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Rémora blanc des marlins
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the body and inside gill chamber of billfishes and swordfishes, rarely on any other fishes (Ref. 2850); also in the gill cavities and mouths of sharks (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Rémora des baleines
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mostly in warm seas.  Attaches itself only to whales and porpoises (Ref. 7251).  One adult couple was recorded attached to the same individual spinner dolphin for a period of about 3 months (Ref. 50801).  A common associate of spinner dolphins at Fernando de Noronha Archipelago, southeast Atlantic, where it occurs year-round.  Recorded feeding on spinner dolphins’ feces and vomits (Ref. 48727).

species.name: Rémora des mantas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Host specific on manta rays, but occasionally attaches to sharks. Often occurs inside gill chamber and mouth of host. Also attaches itself to black marlin, Makaira indica, of the Indo-Pacific Region (Ref. 7251). Rarely free-swimming (Ref. 10791). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Rémora grêle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare (Ref. 4389), oceanic species.  Most often found attached to barracudas but also to other fishes and sea turtles.  Clings to body of host and also found inside gill chambers.

species.name: Réunion seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type is height (=TL - head length).  Found in seagrass beds.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Rêveur cauchemar
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Rêveur fer-de-lance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches depths greater than 1,500 m and probably not uncommon below 650 m (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Rêveur piquant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic; feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Río Salado darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in habitats with moderate turbulence over gravel and small cobble substrate.  Seems to concentrate in vegetated areas when present.  Also found in eddying currents along vegetated or cobble shorelines.

species.name: Röemer's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit large turbid lowland rivers (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sabah damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably widespread in silty coastal regions (Ref. 48636).  Observed to occur solitarily or in small groups that remain close to shelter (Ref. 11891).  Diurnal species (Ref. 52881). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sabah Danio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from rivers.  Adults found mostly in deeper, slower areas, while sub-adults found in riffles and juveniles in cut-off areas (Ref. 34011).

species.name: Sabah dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary and cryptic. Inhabits caves and under ledges of coastal fringing reefs (Ref 90102). This species has been observed to inhabit the tubular sponge Callyspongia aerizusa (Ref. 93553).

species.name: Sabaki tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insects, plants and diatoms (Ref. 2).

species.name: Sabanejewia baltica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in a wide array of habitats from small lowland streams to fast-flowing piedmont rivers with clear water and sand to gravel bottom.  Usually do not occur in large lowland rivers. They are found burrowed in sand, avoiding mud or silt, sometimes in gravel (Ref. 59043).  Mature individuals spawn in batches (Ref. 59043).  Eggs, 1.1-1.2 mm in diameter, lay scattered over sand, gravel or other structures (Ref. 59043).  Absence of external gill filaments in free larvae but transparent bump on forehead prominent (Ref. 59043).  Larvae start to feed after 6 days at 3.1-4.2 mm TL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Sabanejewia bulgarica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large lowland rivers, usually in deep water (Ref. 59043).  Spawning takes place in Danube River and in mouths of some tributaries (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Sabanejewia kubanica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of habitats from small lowland streams to foothill rivers with clear water and gravel bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Sabanejewia larvata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species.  Adults inhabit lakes and lowland water courses with little current (Ref. 12291), on silt bottom with little aquatic vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Feed on invertebrates.  Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Age at first maturity: about 2 years (Ref. 59043).  Population is threatened by pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).  However, recent assessment of threat: least concern (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Sabanejewia romanica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy streams with clean water and moderate to fast current (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Saberfin killie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4-5 months incubation.  Is very difficult, experimented, to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Sabertooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in empty tube-worm snail shells, often extending the head from the opening.  They feed by joining loose groups of look-alike rainbow wrasse and darting out to nip at nearby fish, taking mucus and perhaps small bits of flesh (Ref. 5227).  The skin of larger fishes is the mainstay of the diet, although they are also known to eat eggs (Ref. 28023). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56053).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Sabine shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs and flowing pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Sabre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found near the surface in coastal waters (Ref. 30573), in small schools.  They feed on fishes (Ref. 5213).  Dorsal and anal fins may carry toxins (Ref. 12484).  Generally marketed fresh, may be dried or salted (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Sabre fleuret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found over the continental slope (Ref. 27121).  Juveniles mesopelagic (Ref. 6181, 58302).

species.name: Sabre goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sabretoothed thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine and lacustrine species, but perhaps passing from estuaries into the sea.  More data needed; rather few specimens are in museum collections (Ref. 189).  Often ascends into freshwater (Ref. 12693).  Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers of the lower Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Apparently non-migratory (Ref. 12693), but reported to undertake migrations in the Mekong mainstream (Ref. 37770).  From the Khone Falls to the Mekong delta, it migrates upstream during the dry season from October to March and  downstream at the onset of the monsoon season from May to July (Ref. 37770).  These migrations are reported to be triggered by the receding or rising of the water levels (Ref. 37770).  Feeds on crustaceans, insects and small fishes (Ref. 12693).  Use to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Saccoderma hastata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccoderma melanostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small shady streams (Ref. 26543).  Feeds on mosquito larvae (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Saccoderma robusta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccodon dariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccodon terminalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccodon wagneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccogaster brayae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccogaster hawaii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Rare species, known from a single specimen (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Saccogaster horrida
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This viviparous species was caught on the upper continental slope and this female specimen was with ovaries containing many eggs but no embryos (Ref. 93007).

species.name: Saccogaster maculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Saccogaster nikoliviae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This viviparous species occurs on the upper continental slope. Female specimens have extended ovaries and eggs up to 0.5 mm in diameter; no embryos were observed. A 5.0 cm SL male paratype had a ripe testes and well developed intromittent organ (Ref. 93007).

species.name: Saccogaster parva
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a single specimen (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Saccogaster staigeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Saccopharynx berteli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was caught in an open IKMT between 1100 meters and the surface (Ref. 36344).

species.name: Saccopharynx harrisoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccopharynx hjorti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species has been forgotten both in CLOFNAM (Ref. 27942) and FNAM (Ref. 6718).  Only one specimen is known (Ref. 36365).

species.name: Saccopharynx lavenbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally caught in midwater (Ref. 35599).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and leptocephalus larvae (Ref. 35599).  Degenerative changes in males and females suggest semelparity (Ref. 35599).

species.name: Saccopharynx paucovertebratis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only one specimen known (Ref. 6718).

species.name: Saccopharynx ramosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccopharynx thalassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saccopharynx trilobatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only one specimen (Ref. 36365).

species.name: Sacramento perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in vegetated sloughs, pools of sluggish rivers and lakes; now most common in ponds and impoundments (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Sacramento pikeminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy pools and runs of small to large rivers.  Usually found in clear, warm streams (Ref. 5723).  Voracious minnow with pike-like habits.  Small pikeminnows (less than or equal to 7 cm SL) are found in shallow water with cover and lower velocities.  The microhabitat use of these juveniles is controlled by the presence of large pikeminnows which connotes intraspecific predation.  The microhabitat shift is observed to be significantly influenced by the presence rather than the number of large pikeminnows in the area (Ref. 55069).

species.name: Sacramento sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in pools of clear, cool streams.  Also found in lakes and impoundments (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Sacura margaritacea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large schools in rocky areas.

species.name: Sacura speciosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sad glider
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The holotype was taken from the stomach of a flatfish (Arnoglossus) caught at a depth of 90 m off Natal.

species.name: Sad klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and subtidal areas.  Viviparous (Ref. 51409).

species.name: Saddle bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Synchronously hermaphroditic.

species.name: Saddle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary or in small groups  in fringing reefs to 8 m deep (Ref. 90102).  They inhabit vertical surfaces of cuts along clear reef margins to a depth of 6 m (Ref. 37816). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 6 m reported from Ref. 1602.

species.name: Saddle squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably more common on shelf-edge reefs (Ref. 51183).

species.name: Saddle stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble areas around coral reefs or exposed rocks.  Absent from surf beaches (Ref. 27742).  The reddish-brown bands along the sides of the fish serve as camouflage when the fish partially buries itself in sand (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Saddle wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in clear lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic over coral, rock and rubble (Ref. 58302).  Feed mainly on benthic animals.  Juveniles and adults sometimes act as cleaners (Ref. 9710).  Spawning occur either in aggregations by fish in the initial color phase or in pairs, typically with the terminal male being much larger than the female.

species.name: Saddleback clownfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit silty lagoons and harbors. Monogamous (Ref. 55367). A protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32166). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Heteractis crispa and Stichodactyla haddoni (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420, 35423).

species.name: Saddleback darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs of creeks and small to medium rivers, sometimes in very shallow water (Ref. 3814, 10294). Feeds on pleurocerid (Leptoxis) river snails, hydropsychid caddisfly larvae, midge larvae, and small mayfly nymphs, such as baetids (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Saddleback gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore areas, on mud bottoms among eelgrass and seaweed (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on small mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 2850).  Both male and female guard egg mass (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Saddleback plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphipods were the main food of fishes from the Weddell Sea, although isopods, mysids and polychaetes were important food items (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Saddleback sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal (Ref. 31184).  Occurs in rocky areas and in kelp beds (Ref. 2850).  Usually caught from lower tide pools (farthest from shore) (Ref. 2850).  Can leave tide pools when aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Saddlebanded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saddled bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamps and rivers. Essentially piscivorous (Ref. 9695, 28714). Diet includes snails and crustaceans (Ref. 30488).

species.name: Saddled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and rocky shores.  Often found in crevices, or among weed and rubble (Ref. 13121).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Saddled dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from coral and rubble slopes. Also found in reef slopes and dropoffs around overhangs and rocks in 30-50 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Saddled dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef crevices, frequently on drop-offs, in 10-40 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Saddled galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky lake shore, particularly around man-made groynes or jetties.  Found among aquatic plant meadows near the shore.  Larvae and juveniles inhabit open water on lakes.  Adults feed on insects and crustaceans, pelagic juveniles probably feed on zooplankton.  Breeding is opportunistic (occurring at any time of the year), with a peak possibly occurring late in spring (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Saddled goby
species.description: Occurs among rubble and sand of bays and steep reef slopes (Ref. 37816, 48637).

species.name: Saddled herring smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saddled madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from riffle habitats with gravel, cobble, rubble, or slate substrate; mean depth of 0.2 meters (0.1 - 0.3 m), and stream width averaged 13.6 meters (range 8 - 25 m); mean current readings from the 3 capture sites ranged from 0.59 - 0.76 meters per second.  Riffles are typically occupied during daylight hours when individuals are likely buried within the interstices of gravel.  Based on its small adult size (to 72 mm SL), this species probably lives no longer than 2-3 years.  Preserved females contain mature oocytes from late May to late July; females are mature at sizes as small as 44 mm SL (Ref. 56218).

species.name: Saddled moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives together in fine sediments of the upper continental slope.

species.name: Saddled prawn-goby
species.description: Found on open sand bottoms of clear seaward reefs to at least 20 m (Ref. 9710).  Lives in a burrow with symbiotic alpheid shrimps.  Occurs on sheltered protected reefs, along edges with coarse sand and fine rubble (Ref. 48637). Also Ref. 2334. Also found in sand bottoms of lagoons (Ref 90102).

species.name: Saddled prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saddled sandburrower
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in loose coral sand of shallow exposed seaward reefs and sandy shorelines to a depth of at least 10 m (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Saddled sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary in sand-rubble bottoms with scattered rock and coral outcrops near reefs in 55-80 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Saddled snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy areas and seagrass beds of both lagoon and seaward reefs.  Uses its stiff pointed tail to rapidly burrow backwards into the sand when frightened (Ref. 37816).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on sand-dwelling fishes and crabs and prawns.  Sometimes fully exposed when searching for prey (Ref. 30874).  Rises to the surface to spawn (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Saddled swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sadler's robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Victoria found in shallow inshore areas with papyrus and other aquatic vegetation (Ref. 34290). In Lakes Kyoga and Nabugabo amongst marginal vegetation; believed to run up rivers during rainy season to spawn (Ref. 4903). Present in lake and affluents in the Lake Rukwa basin (Ref. 27292). Feeds on aquatic plants and surface insects (chironomid pupae), rarely on fishes (Ref. 12526). Appears in small quantities in markets (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Saffron anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals of this species were found shoaling together on a deep reef within a meter of the bottom (Ref. 93435).

species.name: Saffron darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Saffron shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bedrock-bottomed and rubble-bottomed pools of clear, fast headwaters, creeks (Ref. 5723) and streams (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Sagami grenadier
species.description: Most common in about 350 to 550 m where water temperatures range from 6° to 12°C.  Feeds primarily on euphausiids, prawns, and isopods.  Spawning probably takes place in early spring.

species.name: Sagamia geneionema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms near the sea shore.

species.name: Sagamichthys gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sagre antillais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the upper continental and insular slopes. Found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 26340). Ovoviviparous with 4 to 5 young in a litter. Maximum size reported in Ref. 106604 after Bigelow & Schroeder (1948). Maximum sizes of 31.5 cm precaudal length (Longley & Hildebrand, 1941) and 50.0 cm TL (Ref. 247) probably refer to the subsequently described and very similar E. robinsi, which attains a greater maximum size according to Schofield & Burgess (1997) (Ref. 106604).

species.name: Sagre brun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A little-known lanternshark, mainly from depths below 900 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sagre chien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slopes at about 366 m depth.  Length given comes from an immature specimen.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sagre diablotin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the insular slopes.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sagre filtre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sagre long nez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outermost continental shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bony fishes including lanternfish, barracudina, synaphobranchid eels, oreo dories, hake, rattails, bathylagids, idiacanthids; also on squids (including histioteuthids and ommastrephids), octopuses, euphausiids, mysids, penaeid shrimp, salps, sponges and ribbonworms (Nemertina) (Ref. 124555).
