species.name: Satyrichthys clavilapis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Satyrichthys laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Satyrichthys longiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Satyrichthys milleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sauclet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Littoral, often near shore.  Gregarious, sometimes occurs in marine lagoons (France) and estuaries (Portugal).  Feed on pelagic copepods and benthic crustaceans (Ref. 5980).

species.name: Saudi Arabian dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters, on coral gravel or silty sand bottom near coral reefs (Ref. 96762)

species.name: Saumarez Gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saumon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphihaline species, spending most of its life in freshwater (Ref. 51442). Occurs in lakes and rocky runs and pools of small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Some landlocked populations exist. Found in all rivers where temperature rises above 10° C for about 3 months per year and does not exceed 20° C for more than a few weeks in summer (Ref. 59043) (preferred temperatures 4-12°C). Juveniles may live in cold lakes in northern Europe (Ref. 59043). Parr (i.e. juveniles) are territorial and are found in the upper reaches of rivers and streams, in riffle areas with strong current and rough gravel bottoms (Ref. 7471). During winter, parr seek refuge in small spaces or under stones during the day (Refs. 59043, 89461). Young remain in freshwater for 1 to 6 years, then migrate to coastal marine waters or even to open oceans where they remain for 1 to 4 years before returning to freshwater  for spawning (Ref. 51442). Adults inhabit cooler waters with strong to moderate flow (Ref. 44894). The Atlantic salmon is reported to live up to 10 years, but most individuals only reach 4-6 years (Ref. 88187). Juveniles feed mainly on aquatic insects, mollusks, crustaceans and fish; adults at sea feed on squids, shrimps, and fish (Ref. 51442). Most populations depend mostly or exclusively on stocking due to degradations of environmental conditions.  Fishing pressure on wild stocks has decreased due to intensive farming but other problems have increased. Farmed salmons escape in large numbers and move to any river and hybridize with wild stocks (Ref. 59043). This species may hybridize with trout (Salmo trutta) (Ref. 59043). Diseases of the species include furunculosis (Aeromonas salmonicida), corynebacterial kidney disease (Renibacterium salmoninarum), enteric red mouth disease (Yersinia ruckeri), infectious pancreatic necrosis virus, bacterial kidney disease, fin rot and fungus infections (Ref. 5951). Marketed fresh, dried or salted, smoked, and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, cooked in microwave, and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Saumon argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The fish occur in the ocean or in lakes; adults return to the rivers where they were born (Ref. 27547).  The young fish emerge in springtime and they usually live in fresh water for 1-2 years (sometimes up to 4 years, Ref. 27547); later they migrate at night to freshwater lakes or to the sea (Ref. 1998).  Epipelagic (Ref. 58426).  The fish that stay more than two years in fresh water and become sexually ripe without ever going to sea, are called residuals; they never spawn (Ref. 27547). Young fish in lakes and rivers eat mainly insects; they stay almost entirely in deep parts of the river and soon become strongly territorial (Ref. 27547). Upon reaching the sea, the smolts remain close to the coast for a certain time, eating planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 27547). As they grow, they migrate farther out into the sea and hunt larger organisms (Ref. 27547) such as jellyfish, squids and fishes (Ref. 58426).  They are hunted by various fishes, birds (mergansers, loons and kingfishers), mammals and lampreys (Ref. 1998).  This kind is traded as fresh fish, dried or salted, smoked, canned, preserved and frozen (Ref. 9988).  They are steamed, grilled, broiled, cooked in the microwave and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Saumon australien
species.description: Poisson du pacifique sud, une des quatre espèces du genre arripis. Inhabit continental shelf waters including estuaries, bays and inlets (Ref. 6390). Found between depths of 30 m (Ref. 33616) and 39 m (Ref. 58489). They enter rivers (Ref. 9002). Juveniles form school in shallow coastal bays and estuaries; adults move in large schools along shores (Ref. 9002), and can move over reefs in depths just sufficient to cover their bodies (Ref. 6390). They form large surface aggregations in deep water (Ref. 6390). Feed mainly on fishes but also on pelagic crustaceans, especially krill (Nyctiphanes australis). Take also food from the seabed. Fish smaller than 10 cm feed predominantly on copepods (Ref. 9072). Utilized fresh, canned and frozen; can be steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Saumon chien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ocean and coastal streams (Ref. 86798).  Migrating fry form schools in estuaries, remain close to  shore for a few months and finally disperse to enter the sea (Ref. 1998).  Epipelagic (Ref. 58426).  Juveniles and adults feed mainly on copepods, tunicates and euphausiids but also on pteropods, squid and small fishes (Ref. 1998).  Adults cease feeding in freshwater (Ref. 1998).  Males and females die after spawning.  The catch is mostly canned but also sold fresh, dried-salted, smoked, and frozen.  Eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).  Utilized for caviar.

species.name: Saumon chinook
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults return to natal streams from the sea  to spawn (Ref. 27547).  Fry may migrate to the sea after only 3 months in fresh water, some may stay for as long as 3 years, but generally most stay a year in the stream before migrating (Ref. 27547).  Some individuals remain close inshore throughout their lives, but some make extensive migrations (Ref. 27547, 44894).  Also found in lakes (Ref. 1998).  Possibly up to 375 m depth (Ref. 6793).  Epipelagic (Ref. 58426).  Food in streams is mainly terrestrial insects and small crustaceans; in the sea, major food items include fishes, crustaceans, and other invertebrates (Ref. 27547).  Young are preyed upon by fishes and birds (such as mergansers and kingfishers); adults are prey of large mammals and large birds (Ref. 1998).  Highly regarded game fish (Ref. 27547).  Flesh is usually red, but some are white; the red meat commands a higher price (Ref. 27547).  Marketed fresh, smoked, frozen, and canned.  Eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).  Viscera said to contain high vitamin A content and used successfully as food for hatchery fish (Ref. 28971, 28977).

species.name: Saumon du Danube
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The fluviatile form generally inhabits headwaters and often maintains a territory; it feeds mainly on insects but also on small crustaceans and fishes.  The sea-run form goes downstream forming schools, and after a short stay in the brackish zone enters the sea where it feeds on small fishes and pelagic crustaceans.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are buried in unguarded nests (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Saumon rude
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found inshore in bays and estuaries over seagrass beds or near areas of seaweed (e.g. kelp), on rocky reefs, and along  ocean beaches.  Juveniles are found in inshore coastal waters, bays and inlets (Ref. 6390).  Feed on small fish and prawns (Ref. 27946).

species.name: Saumon à bosse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An anadromous species which inhabits ocean and coastal streams (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Epipelagic (Ref. 58426). Pelagic at the sea.  In freshwater, lives in Montane and Piedmont rivers with moderate to fast current and gravel bottom. Spawns in riffles or at head of riffles in shallow water with current up to 1.5 m/s, and clean coarse gravel (Ref. 59043).  Spends 18 months at sea after which spawning migration to the natal river or stream occurs; but because the species is less certain of its homing and there is a certain degree of wandering, streams as much as 640 km from natal streams may be used (Ref. 1998, 27547).  Upon emerging from the gravel, fry immediately move downstream and remain inshore for a few months before going out to sea.  Fry may feed on nymphal and larval insects while in fresh water, but may not feed at all.  In the sea, young feed on copepods and larvacean tunicates, its diet shifting to amphipods, euphausiids and fishes as the fish grows (Ref. 27547).  Other food include ostracods, decapod larvae, cirripeds, tunicates, dipterous insects (Ref. 1998, 27547).  Fry may be preyed upon by birds and mammals while adults by marine mammals and large fish (Ref. 1998).  Mostly sold canned (Ref. 1998) but also utilized fresh, smoked, and frozen; also valued for caviar, especially in Japan; eaten steamed, fried, broiled, boiled, microwaved, and baked (Ref. 9988).  The smallest of the true salmon (Ref. 12218).

species.name: Saupe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky substrates and sandy area with algal growth.  Gregarious, sometimes forming sizeable schools.  Young mainly carnivorous on crustaceans, adults almost exclusively herbivorous (Ref. 4781), feed on seaweeds (Ref. 36731).  Protandric hermaphrodite  (Ref. 4781).  Tasty when fresh, but easily softens and is not much esteemed (Ref. 3198).

species.name: Saupe de Mer Rouge
species.description: Caught in shallow coastal waters, mainly in muddy quiet areas.  In the northern part of the Indian Ocean, it is caught all year round and consumed fresh.  In the southern part of the Indian Ocean, it is fished mainly for bait.  Feeds mainly on algae, also invertebrates such as crustaceans and worms.

species.name: Saurenchelys fierasfer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurenchelys lateromaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurenchelys meteori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurenchelys taiwanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurida lessepsianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is found mainly on sandy or muddy substrates to about 100 m, but observed to be more common inshore close to islands or coasts in depths of 20-30 m. Mainly piscivorous.  Spawning season prolonged and occurs nearly all the year round, in the Gulf of Suez with two peaks in December and May (El-Halfawy et al. 2007).  In the Mediterranean, spawning season off the coast of Israel lasts from March to December (Golani 1993), whereas at Iskenderun Bay, Turkey, spawning occurs mainly in two seasons (May-July and September-November) (İşmen 2003). Reported to be important in the trawl fishery of the Gulf of Suez and the Mediterranean coast of Egypt, where it is in a state of high overfishing and severe overexploitation. In the Mediterranean, it was rather uncommon until 1955, when it started to appear in large quantities in bottom trawl catches (according to Ben-Yami & Glaser 1974, Ref. 1289; Bilecenoğlu 2010, Ref. 94612); catches have since remained high, with some fluctuations (Golani 1993, Ref. 38081).  Also reported to be an economically important fish in the Mersin and Iskenderun Gulfs, Turkey and is among the most common species caught in the trawl fishery, comprising almost one-third of the commercial trawl catch in the north-eastern Levant (Ref. 101631).

species.name: Saurida macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy-muddy bottoms, in water shallower than 100 m depth (Ref. 57869).

species.name: Saurida microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters with sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 11230, 41299).

species.name: Saurida pseudotumbil
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurida tweddlei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at depths of 57 to 127 meters.  The largest specimen was 40.10 cm in standard length (Ref. 101339).

species.name: Saurida umeyoshii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental shelves deeper than 100 m (Ref. 57869).

species.name: Saurogobio dumerili
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurogobio gracilicaudatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurogobio gymnocheilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurogobio immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurogobio lissilabris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saurogobio punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually on the bottom of fast flowing water.  Reaches sexual maturity at the age of 1 year. (Ref. 117924).

species.name: Saurogobio xiangjiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sauromuraenesox vorax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Saury
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits surface waters (Ref. 583).

species.name: Sauter parone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length assumed to be 1.5 * 40 = 60 cm TL (RF).

species.name: Sauteur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over soft bottoms of the continental shelf, often inshore and in estuaries.  Also pelagic and encountered throughout the water column (Ref. 9626).  May feed on plankton by ram-filtering.  Juveniles feed mainly on planktonic crustaceans and chaetognaths, to a minor extent on benthic crustaceans and polychaetes, besides scales taken from larger fishes (Ref. 30206, 40402).  Mature females generally spawn in summer.  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 35237).  Marketed mostly fresh.

species.name: Sauteur carsia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore waters at a temperature range of 26.0-29.0 °C (Ref. 4959).  Adults feed mainly on fish.  Usually seen swimming solitary in surface waters (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Sauteur palomette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found mainly in brackish and fresh waters; also over muddy bottoms of coastal marine waters (Ref. 5217). May leap out of the water. They return to the sea to reproduce (Ref. 36880). Dorsal and anal spines bear venomous glands (Ref. 40401). Adults are carnivorous (Ref 40401) while juveniles up to 8.2 cm FL feed mainly on scales taken from larger fishes, also on benthic and planktonic crustaceans, and to a minor extent on smaller fishes and polychaetes (Ref. 40402). Juveniles up to 3.0 cm TL adopt a dark brown color pattern while close to decaying plant fragments, an example of camouflage (Ref. 40401, 46533). Over open, detritus-free and light colored sandy bottom, adopts a contrasting yellowish and dark brown pattern, an example of warning colors. Its conspicuous colors are mimicked by juveniles of the non-venomous grunt Pomadasys ramosus (Ref. 46533).

species.name: Sauteur pelon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, entering estuaries (Ref. 9283).  Dorsal and anal spines of this species are connected to venomous glands that may inflict painful wounds (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Sauteur talang
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, frequently near reefs and offshore islands (Ref. 30573, 48635).  Occasionally found in estuaries.  Usually in small groups (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Feed on fishes, cephalopods, small invertebrates and, other pelagic prey (Ref. 5213, 90102).

species.name: Sauvagesse du nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes, pools and occasionally in runs of small to large rivers.  Large individuals occur in deep water (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on fishes, terrestrial insects, plankton, aquatic insect larvae, and crustaceans while inshore; feeds mostly on fishes while offshore (Ref. 1998).  Male squawfish, prickly sculpins, and newts prey on the eggs (Ref. 1998).  Edible but not well appreciated (1998).

species.name: Savage's birdsnouted whalefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All captures were made with open nets fishing (Ref. 9791).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Savanna tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Savannah darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel riffles, gravel and sand runs of creeks and small rivers.  Often found in vegetation.

species.name: Savon barbu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water coral heads and rocky reefs, over 25 m (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Savon barbu (Pogonoperca punctata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sporadic distribution and habitat specific, preferring large coral heads on slopes prone to moderate currents (Ref. 9137, 48635).  Adults usually in 20+ m depth; juveniles in shallow lagoons or protected bays (Ref. 48635).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Savon de Mer Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and coral reefs.  Hides behind big non-predatory fishes to get to its prey.

species.name: Savon tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear tropical waters to depths of 26 m, but it is found most commonly at 1-2 m (mean maximum depth of specimens collected is 5 m, only 6 were captured deeper than 15 m).  Lives in tide pools, among coral rubble, in patch reefs and shallow spur and groove reef areas, occasionally found on steep vertical walls (Ref. 89885).  A solitary species (Ref. 26340).  Adults are said to prefer clearer waters than juveniles (Ref. 7320).

species.name: Savon à bande jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves and crevices in rocky reefs (Ref. 9710).  Skin contains grammistin which imparts a bitter taste.  The amount of toxin produced increases when the fish is frightened (Ref. 4326). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 09710.

species.name: Savon à deux bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in coastal habitats in semi-silty conditions (Ref. 48635); also found near caves and crevices in rocky and coral reefs from a few meters to at least 100 m.  A predator that feeds on surprisingly large prey, swallowed whole through its expandable jaws (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on fishes.  Secretes the skin toxin grammistin under stress (Ref. 2334).

species.name: Sawback poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Sawback skate
species.description: Lengths of adolescent males ranged from 32.6-34.1 cm TL, with smallest juvenile a neonate 9.4 cm TL; adult males 34.8-40.1 cm TL (Ref. 75643).

species.name: Sawbwa barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Extremely common all over the Inle lake and in the swamps that surround the lake.  Occurs in large shoals among dense vegetation both in clear and in peaty and often foul waters.

species.name: Sawcheek cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coral, sand, or gravel bottoms.  Sometimes associates with sea anemones, possibly as shelter from predators; it also lives in tubular sponges (Ref. 26938, 45560).

species.name: Sawcheek darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs near vegetation in swamps, lakes, sluggish headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Sawcheek scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in muddy habitat that are very sheltered and this is usually deep or very sheltered estuaries. Appears to be one of the more primitive forms and has similar coloration to some members of the genus Scorpaenodes, especially the markings on the head (Ref. 48635). Sometimes caught by trawl net (Ref. 559).

species.name: Sawfin
species.description: Favors deep pools and runs of mainstreams, also impounded waters; young occur in smaller tributaries.  Breeds in summer, congregating in deep pools below waterfalls and rapids.  Feeds on insects and invertebrates as well as algae and detritus mainly off the bottom, leaving characteristic pockets in sand and gravel beds.  Decline in population is due to the introduction of bass, increasing habitat destruction and the impendence of large dams (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Sawfin suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocky riffles and rapids but may be found in rocky pools or intermittent streams during low water conditions; migrates into seasonal streams, climbing damp barriers by clinging with the mouth (Ref. 7248, 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sawlipped catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sawspine catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, estuaries and rivers within tidal influence; among mangroves (Ref. 40908).

species.name: Sawspine dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools with seaweeds and shallow waters down to 20 m.  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 397.

species.name: Sawspine spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sawspine whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sawtooth eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds primarily on crustaceans, and to a lesser extent upon small cephalopods and fishes (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Sawtooth pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may brood at 5.6 cm SL.

species.name: Saya de Malha luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalanago
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Scale croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters, estuaries and in freshwater as far as 500 km upriver from the sea (Ref. 9772, 44894).

species.name: Scale-eye plaice
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scale-eyed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species found on mud bottoms (Ref. 9797).  Feeds on benthic animals (Ref. 9797).

species.name: Scalebeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalebelly eelpout
species.description: Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 4695).

species.name: Scaled belly toothpony
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nothing is known on its ecology except specimens were collected from coastal waters shallower than about 13 m depth along with Gazza minuta (Ref. 39894).

species.name: Scaled sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 50610.

species.name: Scaledcheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Minimum depth from Ref. 089972.

species.name: Scaleless black dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468).

species.name: Scaleless dragonfish
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559).

species.name: Scaleless goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow bottoms of coral reefs, usually less than 5 m (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Scaleless killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Scaleless shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in about 3-10 m depth, often solitary or shares sandy burrow with alpheid shrimp (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Scaleless spiny waspfsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scaleless worm goby
species.description: Found in rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Occurs on mud bottoms of estuaries, and tidal parts of rivers and creeks (Ref. 2847).  Feeds on small crustaceans and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scaleline cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species taken in midwater and bottom trawls (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scalicus amiscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalicus engyceros
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on rocks and sand bottoms (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Scalicus gilberti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalicus hians
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Scalicus investigatoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalicus orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Scalicus quadratorostratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalicus serrulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalloped perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in brackish waters of bays and estuaries, entering freshwater and mangrove-lined tidal creeks (Ref. 4833).

species.name: Scalpel sawtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in groups in shallow, surge rocky areas (Ref. 9710).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Scaly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shoals and migrates upstream during spring and summer.  Prefers warmer areas of rivers and often congregate at the inlets of small tributaries where the temperature is warmer than that of the main river.  Feeds on algae, insect larvae and crabs.  Spawns in fast-flowing stretches of rivers that are algae-free (Ref. 6465).  Breeds in summer, migrates upstream and spawns over gravel beds.  Males mature at about 10 cm FL, females at 15 cm FL (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Scaly boy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow intertidal areas with sandy/mud substrate (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Scaly breasted sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on bottoms that range from rock and gravel to broken shell and fine sand.

species.name: Scaly cheek-hook goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy-mud or silt bottoms at depths of 20-30 m (Ref. 84001).

species.name: Scaly chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs.  Aggregate close to shelter (Ref. 9710).  Feed on zooplankton (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Scaly damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoons, passages, and outer reef slopes.  Feed on zooplankton in the water column, a short distance from the bottom.  They occur singly or in small groups (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Scaly gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported from depths of 26 m (Ref. 58489) to 234 m (Ref. 27469).

species.name: Scaly hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found mainly in coastal waters, but also entering estuaries (e.g. the Hooghly). More data needed, based on certain identifications, since at least some records must have been based on S. tenuifilis. One of the commonest species of Setipinna.

species.name: Scaly osman
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in rocky, mountainous streams and lakes (Ref. 4832).  Found in rivers with swift currents (Ref. 1441).  Feed on benthic plants which are attached on rocks and stones and on associated benthic invertebrates (Ref. 40974).

species.name: Scaly paperbone
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larger individuals apparently occur in deeper water than small ones (Ref. 4525).  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 35934).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35934).  Juveniles makes nocturnal vertical migrations to the epipelagic zone (Ref. 43939).  A planktivorous fish feeding mainly copepods and euphausiids (Ref. 35945).

species.name: Scaly sand darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs of creeks, small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723) and streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds mainly on midge larvae and entomostracans (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Scaly sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sandy areas (Ref. 10275).  Rare species (Ref. 5465).

species.name: Scaly snouted silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scaly stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens usually collected by bottom trawlers at 200 to 800 m depth; longlines between 40 to 100 m depth (Ref. 59152).

species.name: Scaly-belly sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scaly-headed triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species found in crevices or holes during the day.  Adults feed on small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scaly-nape tentacle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalybelly blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalycheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along coastlines, bays and estuaries.  Known to occur in brackish water and may also be found in freshwater.  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates.  Not seen in the markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scalycheek shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on silty-sand bottoms in sheltered water exposed to periodic strong currents. It lives in burrows and presumably, like other members of the genus, is associated with snapping shrimps of the genus Alpheus (Ref. 95856).

species.name: Scalyfin basslet
species.description: Inhabits reefs between 120-250 m depth (Ref. 27481).

species.name: Scalyfin cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Scalyhead goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Scalyhead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in intertidal and subtidal rocky areas, around pilings (Ref. 2850).  Males are territorial (Ref. 6885).  Sexual dimorphism is remarkable (Ref. 74407).  Males guard eggs (Ref. 74407).

species.name: Scalyhead Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal pools in coral reef areas (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scalyjaw koester
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalynape eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scalynape goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal reef slopes, usually on hard corals to about 30 meters depth.  Sometimes found on the mantle of clams and eggs are usually laid on ascidians (Ref. 48637).  Found on gorgonians.

species.name: Scaphiodonichthys acanthopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast flowing, clear waters with stony substrate (Ref. 27732).  Found in clear mountain streams usually under complete forest canopy (Ref. 12693).  Encountered in rapid-running mountain streams of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Feeds mainly on insect larvae along with small amounts of detritus and periphyton.  Apparently breeds after the end of the rainy season after water levels in upland areas have declined, and juveniles appear in catches during April.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scaphiodonichthys burmanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in mountain streams (Ref. 4832), usually under complete forest canopy (Ref. 12693).  Feeds mainly on insect larvae along with small amount of detritus and periphyton (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scaphiodonichthys macracanthus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scaphognathops bandanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the main stream of the middle Mekong during dry season (Ref. 12693) in deep slow reaches (Ref. 37769).  Migrates to smaller streams or floodplains during rainy season (Ref. 12693).  Found also in rapid-running mountain streams (Ref. 12975).  Omnivorous, feeding on detritus, periphyton, worms and insects.  Breeding occurs at the end of the rainy season, as water levels fall.  Marketed fresh (Ref.12693).

species.name: Scaphognathops stejnegeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large river habitats (Ref. 12693).  Inhabits deep slow reaches during dry season (Ref. 37769).  Found in rapid-running mountain streams (Ref. 12975).  Not known to migrate, but may probably leave main stream for flooded forests during the periods of high-water.  Has not been found in any impoundments.  Omnivorous, feeding on detritus and algae along with worms, crustaceans and insects.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scaphognathops theunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scapular goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty reefs in 0-5 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Scardinius acarnanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and large rivers. Early larvae and juveniles often form large schools and frequently in association with Tropidophoxinellus hellenicus. Juveniles feed on phytoplankton while adults on macrophytes. Spawns in March-July. Lays adhesive eggs on vegetation which hatch in 5 days (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scardinius dergle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing and still waters and lakes (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scardinius graecus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and lowland water courses with little current.  Feeds on plants (Ref. 26100). Deposits among vegetation adhesive, spherical and yellow eggs which hatch in 4 days at 25° C (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to water abstraction, pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Scardinius knezevici
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes (Ref. 55977).  Inhabits deep pools and canals in swampy areas along lake shores or in floodplain.  Breeds in April-May.  Attains a maximum size of about 26 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scardinius plotizza
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits well vegetated rivers, backwaters, oxbows, ponds, and lakes.  Attains a maximum size of about 20 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scardinius racovitzai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits densely vegetated, shallow hot spring with mud bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scardinius scardafa
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits lakes and swamps in or near aquatic vegetation. Threatened due to proposed stocking of Scardinius hesperidicus and other cyprinids (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Scarecrow tapertail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Th e holotype was collected shallower than 100 m depth by a mid-water trawl targeting the Sakura-shrimp Lucensosergia lucens (Ref. 123098).

species.name: Scarecrow toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sluggish, but pugnacious when approached closely (Ref. 5521). Dark coloration of the buccal cavity more developed in the larger specimens indicating that this trait is related to growth or maturation (Ref. 54666).

species.name: Scarf triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky bottoms at depths of 6 m and shallower (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scarface blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coral and rock (Ref. 58302).  The most common blenny on shallow reefs.  Adults feed on benthic algae and detritus (Ref. 3921).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scarface rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore species that may be found out of the water at night on rocks.   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scarlet cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Scarlet seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.

species.name: Scarlet shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of clear, fairly fast headwaters, creeks, and small rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably open substratum spawners like congeners.

species.name: Scarlet wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small mobile animals, preferably crabs.  Searches for food among encrusting organisms and algal holdfasts using the large forward-jutting canine teeth to rake its food from the substratum (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Scarlet-banded barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams, descending from the wet zone foot hills, particularly in areas with gravel or pebble substrates, but also in the coastal marshes.  Found in streams and tanks in the dry zone.  Feeds mainly on detritus and algae.  A potential larvicide fish (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Scarletfin blenny
species.description: Found in shallow waters and in calm rocky areas (Ref. 37955).  Inhabits mollusk tubes and barnacles on rocky reefs (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Scartelaos cantoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scartelaos gigas
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scartella caboverdiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in intertidal areas (Ref. 27000). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartella itajobi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow-waters and tide pools of the type locality.  Similar to its congeners, this species is extremely tolerant to salinity and temperature variations.  Some individuals were
also found in small crevices of emerged rocks (2 meters above sea surface), remaining up to 20 minutes out of the water, probably avoiding predators. (Ref. 80496).  Similar to its congeners, this species is oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartella poiti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from 0.1 to 1.0 meter depth inside tide pools and in the surf zone over crustose algae or volcanic reefs. Observed to be extremely tolerant to high salinity and temperature variations. Adults occur with other blennies (Ophioblennius cf. atlanticus and an undescribed species of the genus Entomacrodus, labrisomids (Labrisomus nuchipinnis and an undescribed species of Malacoctenus), the Trindade damselfish (Stegastes fuscus trindadensis), and a Brazilian wrasse (Thalassoma noronhanum) (Ref. 49353). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartella springeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in rock pools (Ref. 5288).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartichthys crapulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the coast, on rocky bottoms (Ref. 10696).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartichthys variolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scartichthys viridis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in tide pools and rocky shore areas. Are primarily herbivorous (Ref. 9032). Selectively feed on the green algae Ulva, Enteromorpha, as juveniles and favor red algae Gelidium as adults (Ref. 94105). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Scarus chinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scarus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scarus obishime
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually seen at depths of 25 m or more.  Feeds on benthic algae during daytime.

species.name: Scatty
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in harbors and estuaries (Ref. 5480); also found in rivers and lagoons.  Forms  shoals (Ref. 5480).  Feeds on detritus and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 30573).  Antirolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Schedophilus griseolineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scheel's lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and brooks, mostly in weedy areas and under forest cover in river drainages (Ref. 3788); also brackish water, river mouths, lagoons and estuaries along the coast (Ref. 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Schelly
species.description: Lacustrine, in open water. Spawns in January to February in shallow bays on stones and gravel. Feeds on crustaceans and insects.  Population in Haveswater strongly declined by water abstraction and cormorant predation (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Schilbe angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe bocagii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe brevianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Occasionally imported from Nigeria to Europe or America for aquarium purposes (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe congensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Might be a species adapted to rapids (Ref. 43912). Max. recorded SL 36.7 cm (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe djeremi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Stomach contents of a specimen from the Upper Sanaga showed the presence of insect remains (adult Hymenoptera,
Odonata larvae and other unidentified aquatic insect
larvae)(Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe durinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe grenfelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivorous or predominantly carnivorous, feeding on fruits, leaves, grains, insect larvae and nymphs, and small fish; very voracious; juveniles found in floodplains during the rainy season, often hidden under floating trunks of trees which seems a favorite place for juvenile Schilbe and numerous other fish larvae; active swimmer, especially during the night, probably resting near the bottom during daytime (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Important species in fishery terms (Ref. 78218). Flesh of this fish very tasty, its price rather elevated (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems confined to lakes and rather large rivers (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe mandibularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riverine and lacustrine conditions; prefers freshwater but has also been recorded from brackish water lagoons in mixohaline water; voracious and carnivorous (Ref. 43912). Feed mainly on (terrestrial) insects (Ref. 6868, 43912) and fish, but also fruits, amphibians, small rodents and Arachnida have been found in stomachs (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe micropogon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe moebiusii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rivers (Ref. 4967).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe multitaeniatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Locally this species might have some value for the fishermen (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe nyongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schilbe tumbanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Confined to larger lakes and rivers; possibly a shoaling species; polyphagous with a frugivorous tendency; stomach contents examined showed the presence of sand, mud, benthic vegetable remains, leaves, fruits and insect remains (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Probably of economic importance locally for fishermen of Lake Tumba; maximum reported TL 280mm (Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe uranoscopus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adapted to riverine and lacustrine conditions; appears to live mainly in the open waters; predatory, carnivorous but not strictly piscivorous; young essentially entomophagous (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205). Especially in the Chad basin of some economic value to the fishermen (Ref. 43912). Maximum reported total length 45 cm (Nile basin)(Ref. 43912).

species.name: Schilbe zairensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Schindler's fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur around lagoons and in adjacent waters (Ref. 52496, 58302).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Exhibit extreme paedomorphism (Ref. 52496).  Planktonic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Schindleria edentata
species.description: Collected at a depth of one meter from a lagoon with sandy bottom and covered with algae and seagrass (Ref. 129305).

species.name: Schindleria multidentata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schindleria pietschmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Planktonic, benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Schindler’s large-toothed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatogobius alleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderate flow in shallow areas of gravel (Ref. 116768).

species.name: Schismatogobius ampluvinculus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the lower freshwater reaches of streams, 50 to 800 m from the upper limit of tidal fluctuations. The habitat is almost the same as that of S. ninja and they were often observed syntopically, and sometimes with Schismatogobius marmoratus. Major syntopic fishes were also the same as those with S. ninja. This species also has camouflage coloration. This species often spreads its pectoral fins and flutters them and although the proximal part of the large black patch on the pectoral fin is covered by white pigmentation on the anterior side, it lacks white pigmentation on the posterior side. Thus, the black patch on the posterior side is conspicuous during the fluttering behavior. They communicate with other individuals by this behavior, but the meaning is unknown (Ref. 125666).

species.name: Schismatogobius arscuttoli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with moderate to fast flowing water in shallow areas of gravel (Ref. 116448).

species.name: Schismatogobius baitabag
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of gravel. The holotype was collected from a bend in the Nagada River in a valley, with slow to moderate flow over sand, gravel, smooth rocks and boulders, with some leaf litter and logs (Ref. 116768).

species.name: Schismatogobius bruynisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatogobius bussoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of rocks and gravel (depth 0.3-0.4 m), just above tidal influence, and sometimes with Schismatogobius bruynisi and S. saurii (Ref. 116448).

species.name: Schismatogobius du Vanuatu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatogobius essi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of gravel (depth 0.3-0.7 m) just above tidal influence, in company with Schismatogobius bruynisi and S. vanuatuensis (Ref. 116768).

species.name: Schismatogobius fuligimentus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow and clear-water riffles with slow to moderate current in rivers with substrate of small to medium gravel.  Elevations of type localities of adult specimens range from 18 m to 250 m, however, it may be an amphidromous species (Ref. 39635).

species.name: Schismatogobius hoesei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatogobius insignis
species.description: Found in shallow bays and river mouths (Ref. 439). Lotic freshwater, torrent dweller, benthic, sand bottom; buries in sand (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Schismatogobius limmoni
species.description: Collected in a freshwater stream which has moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of boulders, gravel and sand (Ref. 123786).

species.name: Schismatogobius marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the lower freshwater reaches of a stream in Japan,150 m from the upper limit of tidal fluctuations, with S. ninja. It was also observed in two other streams on Okinawa Island, located 50 and 600 m from the upper limit of tidal fluctuations. Found in rapids at depths of 5-30 cm and in one case, was observed to swim away in the middle of the water column against a strong current, a behavior not seen in S. ninja and S. ampluvinculus (Ref. 125666).

species.name: Schismatogobius mondo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of rocks and gravel (depth 0.3-0.6 m) just above tidal influence with Schismatogobius bruynisi, S. tiola, and S . vanuatuensis, in the same habitat (Ref. 116768).

species.name: Schismatogobius pallidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatogobius risdawatiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected in freshwater streams with moderate to fast flow,  in shallow areas with gravel and boulders, just above the tidal influence at elevation ranging from 16 to 45 m (Ref. 116448).

species.name: Schismatogobius roxasi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy areas of the middles reaches of rivers.

species.name: Schismatogobius sapoliensis
species.description: Occurs in a freshwater stream with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of rocks and gravel (depth 0.2-0.3 m), just below a waterfall (Ref. 118600).

species.name: Schismatogobius saurii
species.description: Taxon. Recorded from Indonesia in streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of gravel and boulders at depth of 0.4-0.6 m, usually at low altitude (< 10 m), and sometimes with Schismatogobius bruynisi (Ref. 116448). On the other hand, specimens from Japan (as Schismatogobius ninja) were collected from the lower freshwater reaches of the streams, at 50 to 1,300 m from the upper limit of tidal fluctuations; on coarse sand and gravel bottoms of shallow areas (depth usually 5-30 cm) around rapids, a typical habitat was at the ends of the rapids (transitional areas from rapid to pool) with steady flow. This species usually stay on the bottom and often bury half of their body in the substratum, preferring substrates with free gravel granules which can be moved easily by water flow, and do not inhabit silty substrates. Body markings perfectly camouflage them on the gravel bottom of their habitats; thus, are hard to detect if they remain motionless. Occurs with S. ampluvinculus, and sometimes with Schismatogobius marmoratus, but the most abundant syntopic species was Rhinogobius nagoyae; other gobies, such as Stiphodon percnopterygionus, Sicyopterus lagocephalus, Glossogobius illimis and Luciogobius ryukyuensis and amphidromous pipefish, Microphis leiaspis, were also frequently observed with this species (Ref. 125666).

species.name: Schismatogobius tiola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderate to fast flow in shallow areas of rocks and gravel (depth 0.3-1 m) just above tidal influence with Schismatogobius bruynisi and S.vanuatuensis, in the same habitat.

species.name: Schismatogobius tuimanua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderate flow in shallow areas of rocks and gravel (depth 0.4-0.6 m) just above tidal influence (Ref. 116768).

species.name: Schismatogobius vitiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer shallow and clear water riffles with slow or moderate current speed and with a substrate of small boulders and gravel (Ref. 55545).

species.name: Schismatorhynchos endecarhapis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatorhynchos heterorhynchos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismatorhynchos holorhynchos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schismorhynchus
species.description: A benthic species (Ref. 58302, 75154) which inhabits shallow lagoon reefs (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Schistura acuticephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura afasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura albirostris
species.description: Found in a reach of alternating riffles and flowing pools, river width was about 20m, depth to 1m, water clear, substrates generally unembedded and consisting of mixed cobble and gravel. Sympatric with Garra tengchongensis Zhang & Chen, Pseudorasbora parva (Temminck and Schlegel), Schistura polytaenia (Zhu), Schistura vinciguerrae (Hora), Misgurnus anguillicaudatus (Cantor), Oreoglanis insignis Ng and Rainboth, and Pareuchiloglanis macropterus Ng (Ref. 93052).

species.name: Schistura albisella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura alticrista
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura altipedunculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura amplizona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura anambarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura andrewi
species.description: Occurs in a small pool with slow-flowing water and substrate composed of sand, gravel and rocks. Found associated with the following fishes: Schistura nebeshwari, Olyra sp. and Garra spp. (Ref. 97391).

species.name: Schistura antennata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams; restricted to microhabitats with moderate flowing water and never in riffles or waterfalls. Associated with S. hingi and Oreoglanis sp. (Sisoridae).

species.name: Schistura aramis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small forest creek.

species.name: Schistura arifi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura athos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura atra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in crevices between large blocks (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura aurantiaca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura bachmaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a stream with fast running water. Associated with Poropuntius deauratus (Cyprinidae), Pterocryptis cochinchinensis (Siluridae), and Schistura spiloptera. Apparently very rare.

species.name: Schistura bairdi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers in gravel beds and rapids (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Schistura balteata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura baluchiorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura bannaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura bella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a small stream running among piles of pebbles, with clear water depth up to 50 cm and moderate to swift current (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura bhimachari
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura bolavenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura breviceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small stream running among piles of pebbles, with clear water depth up to 50 cm and moderate to swift current (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura bucculenta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles (Ref. 43281).  Inhabits mountain streams over sandy and gravelly bottom (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Schistura callichroma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura callidora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at the mouth of a stream up to 20 m wide with substrate consisting of a mixture of gravel, stones and boulders of up to 30 cm diameter with few larger stones and with a maximum water depth of 50 cm (Ref. 87201).

species.name: Schistura carbonaria
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium-sized rivers in highest abundance in riffles with rocks and gravel substratum and high water velocities (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura carletoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small shallow swift, clear streams with sandy or gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura cataracta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer stretches with swift current and stony or rocky substrate, but also found over sandy substrate (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Schistura caudofurca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura chapaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura chindwinica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura cincticauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura clatrata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura colossa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura conirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura coruscans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles, among stones (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura crabro
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura crassa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura cryptofasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with clear and swift current, rocky bottom (Ref. 56368 ).

species.name: Schistura curtistigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura dalatensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Always found syntopic with S. yersini. Rheophilous and occurs in fast flowing water. Always less abundant than S. yersini. Juveniles found in riffles and along the shore. Adults live in deeper river channels. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates.

species.name: Schistura daubentoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers with sand or gravel bottoms (Ref. 12693).  Found over gravel in shallow water, with moderate current (Ref. 27732).  Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura dayi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, shallow, swift streams with sandy or pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura deansmarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits cave with only stagnant water in the dry season and with reportedly only moderate flow in the rainy season.  Occurs approximately 200 m from the entrance.  Mostly found resting on the bottom, sometimes free swimming, near crevices where they hide if chased.

species.name: Schistura defectiva
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits riffles and creeks (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura deignani
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Schistura denisoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura desmotes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with strong current, depth up to 70 cm and stony substrate with patches of algae and massive of Cryptocorine balansae Gagnepain, a long leaved Araceae (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura devdevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, swift streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura diminuta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the mainstream of Sekong river, from moderate flow, over a sandy substrate (Ref. 88809).

species.name: Schistura disparizona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow and narrow branches of stream, with gravel or stone bottom (Ref. 56369).

species.name: Schistura dorsizona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with relatively clear, fast water and sandy to gravel substrate; stomach of one female specimen contained aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura dubia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over pebbles in small shallow streams.  A female measuring 4.56 cm SL contained ovulae of about 0.9 mm in diameter.  Its stomach contained insect remains (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura ephelis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in riffles, among stones (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura epixenos
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs in stream characterized by forest cover, very narrow, dense cover of branches, bamboos and shrubs. The stream is shallow with depth of 1-30 cm and  bottom covered by thick mud (probably due to the track construction and recent agricultural work), at places with thick
layers of leaf litter (Ref. 117206).

species.name: Schistura fasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura fascimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura fasciolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rapid current of  mountain streams (Ref.  26563).  Length type refers to body length which is assumed to be in TL.

species.name: Schistura fusinotata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from small forest creeks to main rivers (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura gangetica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, clear, swift streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura geisleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in stream with slow current and with depth never more than 30 cm during the dry season.  Also found in shallow riffles over pebbles up to 5 cm in diameter, with clear water and moderate current.  A female measuring 3.12 cm SL contained ripe ovulae about 0.7 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura globiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small forest creeks (Ref. 43281).  Occurs among leaf litter, in 5-20 cm of water, over a clay bottom (Ref. 36949).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, clear, swift streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura huongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits medium-sized rivers, with its highest densities immediately upstream of riffles with rocks and gravel substratum and low water velocities (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura imitator
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast flowing water, rapids; Schistura imitator has always been collected together with S. khamtanhi (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura implicata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in riffles (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura incerta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in streams on the bottom (Ref. 26563).  Length type refers to body length which is assumed in TL.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura isostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water over sandy substrate (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura jarutanini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A troglobitic species, strictly living in cave stream.  Feeds on benthic microorganisms (Ref. 58784).  Known only from the 22 specimens comprising the type series.  Eyes reduced or absent.  Well pigmented.

species.name: Schistura kampucheensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura kangjupkhulensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, swift streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).  A female measuring 3.94 cm SL   has ovaries with ripe ovulae about 1.7 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura kaysonei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura kengtungensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit small, shallow, high gradient streams with cobble or boulder substrates (Ref. 12693).  A ripe female measuring 5.27 cm SL with ovulae 2.4 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura khamtanhi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast flowing water, rapids (Ref. 36949).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.
