species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura klydonion
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura kodaguensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, swift streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura kohatensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura kohchangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit small, shallow, high gradient streams with gravel and boulder substrates in forests.  Diet probably consists of insect larvae and some algae, as seen in other nemacheilines (Ref. 12693).  A female 5.24 cm SL contains ovulae about 0.7 mm diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura kongphengi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer fast flowing waters with stones and boulders (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura kontumensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura laterimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura latidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapids, under boulders, in about 0.6 m of fast flowing water; collected by women using baskets (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura latifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura leukensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow current at the time of collection, but very fast flowing water over smooth basaltic rocks in the rainy season (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura lingyunensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A troglobite, living obligatory in caves (Ref. 86777).

species.name: Schistura liyaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with swift current, big boulders, and rocks. Occurs together with the following fishes: Barilius sp., Devario sp., Pethia sp., Garra sp., and Glyptothorax manipurensis (Ref. 112085).

species.name: Schistura longa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravelly mountain streams (Ref. 51717).

species.name: Schistura machensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura macrolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura macrotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura maculosa
species.description: Inhabits small pool with slow-flowing water and substrate composed of sand, gravel and rocks. Occurs in association with Exostoma cf. barakensis, Garra spp. and Lepidocephalichthys guntea. A female measuring 7.56 cm SL contained ovulae 0.8-1.2 mm in diameter (Ref. 94258).

species.name: Schistura maejotigrina
species.description: Found in a stream near a water fall and terraced rice fields with fast flowing, clear water, width of 3-4 m and depth of 3.75 cm. Occurs over substrates of mixed gravel, mud and sand. Other species encountered at the collection site include Schistura breviceps, S. pridii, S. spilota, Oreoglanis siamensis, Devario sp., Scaphiodonichthys burmanicus and Channa gachua (Ref. 93077).

species.name: Schistura maepaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stream with moderate to swift current over boulders and pebbles.  A female measuring 4.18 cm SL contains ovulae about 0.6 mm in diameter.  Its stomach contents are Diptera larvae and worms, both of very small size (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura magnifluvis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and river backwaters at the driest time of the year (Ref. 39226).  Frequently found in large rivers with stony bottom (Ref. 43281).  A 5.92 cm SL female with ripe ovulae 1.4-1.6 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).  Not caught commercially (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Schistura mahnerti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The stomach of a 4.87 cm SL fish contains several insect larvae of various sizes (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura malaisei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, swift, clear streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura megalodon
species.description: Inhabits river with clear and moderate to fast running water over boulders, rocks, pebbles, sand, and twigs.  Occurs together with <i>Schizothorax malacanthus, <i>Devario kakhienensis, <i>Exostoma labiatum, <i>Misgurnus anguillicaudatus, and <i>Channa gachua.

species.name: Schistura melarancia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles and fast flowing creeks (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Schistura menanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in various habitats, including a large tributary and several smaller streams with moderate to swift current.  Inhabits small riffles (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura minuta
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura mizoramensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow flowing water with a substrate of sand, gravel and rocks.  Occurs in association with  <i>Glyptothorax maceriatus, <i>Garra cf. annandalei and <i>Schistura cf. fasciata (Ref. 98821).

species.name: Schistura moeiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stream with muddy to sandy substrate with a few stones and numerous empty gastropod shells, in depths ranging from 0.05 to 10.5 m.  A female measuring 4.51 cm SL contains ovulae 1.2 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura mukambbikaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura multifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rapid streams and rivers with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura musa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura myrmekia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura nagaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift mountain streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura nagodiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura nalbanti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura namboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant in riffles and rapids, but also found in slow moving sandy river sections  (Ref. 40772).  This species is very resistant to organic pollution and occurs in streams that flow through villages and towns, being often one of the last fish species surviving (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura nandingensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura nasifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from the upland streams (Ref. 117882). The ovaries of a 6 cm SL female contain ovulae about 0.8 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura nebeshwari
species.description: This species usually inhabits brooks and streams with slow to swift current, among small pebbles, stones, and boulders in southern Mizoram. Its holotype was collected from a stream near Phura village near Palak Lake (the Koladyne basin), among small pebbles, in slow current. Three paratypes were caught from the Kolchaw River near Kolchaw in Saiha District, Mizoram. This species co-occurs with the following fishes: Olyra sp. (Bagridae); Barilius profundus, Devario sp., Pethia sp., Garra sp. (Cyprinidae); Schistura scyphovecteta (Nemacheilidae); and Glyptothorax jayarami (Sisoridae) (Ref. 94459).

species.name: Schistura nicholsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow riffles in small streams with fast flowing water over pebbled bottom.  It probably feeds on insect larvae and small amounts of algae (Ref. 12693).  A female 7.84 cm SL with ovulae 1.0-1.2 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura nilgiriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura niulanjiangensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura nomi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on gravel banks (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura novemradiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small creeks (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Schistura nubigena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs together with Malihkaia aligera in fast riffles over gravel and cobble (Ref. 116725).

species.name: Schistura nudidorsum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, fast  water on gravel to pebble substrate (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura obeini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a variety of habitats, but usually associated with fast to very fast waters, on pebble to stone substrate (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura oedipus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species (Ref. 12041).  Collected in a pool of moving water about 1 km from a cave entrance (Ref. 39226).  Mostly found stationary on the muddy bottom at depths from 20 cm to 1 m (Ref. 42927).  Tends to occur in slow moving water during the dry season, but some individuals were observed climbing rapids (Ref. 42927).  Small groups of individuals were frequently found in the pools while isolated individuals were common in rapids (Ref. 42927).  Weakly or not at all cryptobiotic, not remaining under rocks for more than 5 min during the day (Ref. 42927).  Feeds on insects and roundworms (Ref. 42927).  Shows behavioral responses to light, including avoidance and perhaps a residual diurnal rhythmicity (Ref. 42927).

species.name: Schistura orthocauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura pakistanica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura pantherina
species.description: Occurs in flowing water in shallow rubble and gravel riffles (Ref. 93042).

species.name: Schistura papulifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura paraxena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on nymphs of the stonefly family Perlidae (Ref. 115556).

species.name: Schistura paucicincta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 2.91 cm SL female has distended belly which contains ripe ovulae about 1.3 mm in diameter.  Its stomach contains numerous larvae of Coleoptera (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura paucifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura pawensis
species.description: Found in clear and shallow (30-60 cm depth) water above gravel with moderately fast flowing water (Ref. 95079).

species.name: Schistura personata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in riffles, among stones (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura pertica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura pervagata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles and rapids (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura phamhringi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits cool, clean, swift-flowing shaded freshwater streams which flow over a substrate of gravel, cobble and boulders.  Topotypic specimens were collected from a stream among small pebbles in slow current. Occurs together with other fish species including Cyprinidae: <i> Barilius ngawa, <i>Devario acquipinnatus, <i>Neolissochilus stracheyi, <i>Poropuntius burtoni, <i>Garra paralissorhynchus; Psilorhynchidae: <i>Psilorhynchus ngathanu; Nemacheilidae: <i>Schistura khugae, <i>S. reticulata; Sisoridae: <i>Glyptothorax granulus, <i>G. ventrolineatus; Mastacembelidae: <i>Mastacembelus armatus; and Channidae: <i>Channa gachua (Ref. 95580).

species.name: Schistura poculi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and streams with swift current, among large pebbles, stones and boulders (Ref. 39226).  Found in creeks and streams with moderate current and clear water (Ref. 43281).  A 4.82 cm SL female contained nearly ripe ovulae, about 1.3 m diameter; when collected, a 5.22 cm SL female  extruded yellow-orange ovulae; one of them still adheres to its genital opening (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura polytaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura porthos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura prashadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams (Ref. 41236 ).

species.name: Schistura pridii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, torrential hill streams, 0.3-1.0 m deep with gravel bottom and rocky crevices, in mixed deciduous forests, at  950-1120 m altitude (Ref. 51709).

species.name: Schistura procera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small forest creeks (Ref. 43281). Type locality at the time of visit, except in the pool of the waterfall itself: creek with at most 100 cm wide and 5-10 cm deep, over pebbles; other species present: Garra cambodgiensis and Schistura kengtungensis (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura pseudofasciolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura psittacula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in riffles with rocks and gravel and high water velocities (Ref. 40772). Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 40772). Associated with Annamia normani, Schistura huongensis, Mastacembelus armatus, Rhinogobius ocellatus and Anguilla marmorata (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura pumatensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura punctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura puncticeps
species.description: Found only in the mouth of the Nam Paw stream.  Appears to be restricted to the lowest stretch of this stream (Ref. 95078).

species.name: Schistura punctifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, standing to relatively fast water on gravel substrate; collected from very shallow to deeper waters (70-100 cm, with swifter current) (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura quaesita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles and rapids (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura quasimodo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles, among stones (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura rara
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura reidi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most commonly found in swiftly flowing waters.  A female measuring 6.13 cm SL contained ripe ovulae 1.7 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura rendahli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura reticulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura reticulofasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura rikiki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Schistura robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with moderately flowing water, over pebbles, in depths between 10-30 cm.  A female measuring 3.36 cm SL contains ovulae at various stages of development (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura rupecula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow water riffles and spring pools (Ref. 12045).  Found in small streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura russa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in riffles (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura savona
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura scaturigina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura schultzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hill streams (Ref. 12041).  Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura scripta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is known only from its type locality, a stream about 3-4 m wide, flowing through the palm-oil plantations of Nakiyadeniya Estate in an unprotected area of the Gin River basin, elevation ca. 80 m above sea level and where the substrate consists of small boulders and pebbles. It prefers the faster-flowing regions of the stream and was observed with Garra ceylonensis, Rasbora dandia, Belontia signata. It appears to be locally abundant when sampled during a relatively dry period in December 2017 and about 100 adults, including several gravid females, were observed in a stretch of approximately 50 m along the length of the stream. Schistura notostigma was recorded in similar habitats sampled in Udugama about 8 km from the type locality of S. scripta and as presently understood, these two species do not co-occur (Ref. 127984).

species.name: Schistura scyphovecteta
species.description: This species usually inhabits streams with swift current, among big boulders and rocks in southern Mizoram. Topotypic specimens of this species were taken from Kaoao River near New Serkawr village, among big boulders, in fast current. Two paratypes were also caught from the Kolchaw River near Kolchaw. This fish co-occurs with the following species: Olyra sp. (Bagridae); Devario sp., Pethia sp., Garra sp. (Cyprinidae); Schistura nebeshwari (Nemacheilidae); and Glyptothorax jayarami (Sisoridae) (Ref. 94459).

species.name: Schistura semiarmata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).  Prefers slow flowing riffles, a bottom dwelling species.  Found in lowland and wet hollows.  Feeds on detritus and debris matter (Ref. 44325).  Spawning occurs in backwater pools and stagnant water bodies mostly after the monsoon rains (Ref. 44325).

species.name: Schistura sertata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in the creek flowing from Kuang Xi waterfall, in a side arm with quiet water and a quite muddy bottom (limestone clay) (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura sexcauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura sexnubes
species.description: Occurs among rocks along the shallow shores in a water depth of 10-40 cm with moderate to fast current in Mengmenghe River. Syntopic with Schistura cryptofasciata , Glyptothorax laosensis and Clarias sp.. Found also in Nanzhaihe River, characterized by water flow velocity of 0.5 m/s, 21 °C water temperature, and a pH of 5.4 (Ref. 94768).

species.name: Schistura shadiwalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura sharavathiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura shuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura sigillata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in riffles, among stones (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura sijuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in caves.

species.name: Schistura sikmaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with gravelly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura similis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 5.78 cm SL female had insect larvae in its stomach and unripe ovulae in its ovaries (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura sokolovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast running water (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura sombooni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seems to prefer stretches with relatively slow current and gravel or sandy substrate (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura sonlaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in caves.  Forms shoal, feeding on larvae, insects, pests and ants.  Encountered only in July to October.  When water becomes shallow, this species follows water receding into caves (Ref. 92114).

species.name: Schistura spekuli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura spiesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits cave, most commonly found resting on the bottom of shallow pools with flowing water. Sometimes occurs in mid-water, or also co-exists with Neolissochilus subterraneus in deeper areas with little flow. Swims along the surface of pools with its snout raised up, out of the water while moving it head from side to side. Large fish occur in the deeper zone, far from the entrance of the cave.

species.name: Schistura spiloptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, clear, fast-flowing water over rocky bottoms in upland streams.  Seasonal movements slight, if they occur at all.  Feeds on insect larvae, some algae and phytoplankton.  Not caught commercially, but might have possibilities in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).  A 4.32 cm SL female with ovulae 1.5 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura spilota
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 7.17 cm SL specimen has unidentifiable vegetal remains in its stomach (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura striata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Schistura suber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among leaf-litter, in a small pool, in a drying small forest creek (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura susannae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura tenebrosa
species.description: Mostly found in small streams in rubble riffles. Usually collected in areas where riparian vegetation cover was > 50% and included mature deciduous trees, screw pines, bamboo, ferns, tall grasses, Alocasias sp. and a variety of other herbaceous plants. Substrate was composed mostly of small to medium-sized rocks (1-13 cm). Stomach contents of a 4.5 cm SL female consisted of chironomid larvae (Diptera) and a mayfly (Ephemeroptera). The following physico-chemical parameters were recorded in the sampling sites: 7.0 average pH; 8.2 to 8.5 mg/l oxygen; 0 mg/l ammonia; 3.1-9.8 mg/l silica; approximately 10-13 mg/l (pH 4.5) alkalinity; 15 to 48 cm/s velocity; 430 m asl average elevation; 4.8-7.2 m stream width; and 18 to 40 cm depth. Sympatric in the Mae Khlong basin with Schistura aurantica (Ref. 93080).

species.name: Schistura tenura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura thanho
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in riffles (Ref. 40772).

species.name: Schistura thavonei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stretches of streams with riffles (in the sheltered parts with somewhat quieter current), over gravel to stone bottom.  The stomach contents of a 4.24 cm SL fish consist of insect larvae (Ref. 117218).

species.name: Schistura tigrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura tirapensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Schistura tizardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in main rivers, on gravel beds (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Schistura trilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in caves.  Forms shoal, feeding on larvae, insects, pests and ants.  Encountered only in July to October.  When water becomes shallow, this species follows water receding into caves (Ref. 92114).

species.name: Schistura tubulinaris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in stretches with relatively slow current and gravel or sandy substrate; stomach of one female contained arthropod remains (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Schistura udomritthiruji
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the time of sampling, the type locality was a stream with width up to 8 m, but the riverbed would allow a 20 m wide river at high water level, and with calm stretches, depression up to 1 m deep as well as riffles. Riffle consisted of gravel with few larger stones and maximum water depth of 40 cm (Ref. 83421).

species.name: Schistura vinciguerrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small streams with pebbly bottom (Ref. 41236).  Found in channels with very swift current and bare bottom.  The ovaries of a 6.63 cm SL female contain ripe ovulae of about 1.6 mm in diameter (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Schistura waltoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small mountain streams with fast and shallow water.  Feeds on insects and invertebrates, based on the stomach contents of a 5.46 cm SL specimen.  Juveniles were observed to form loose troops of 10-20 individuals (Ref. 39226)

species.name: Schistura wanlainensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Mon Lan Chaung, a large river with approximately 50 m width and very fast water flowing over a stone and boulders bottom. Syntopic with Garra cf. dulongensis, Garra sp., Neolissochilus compressus, Oreinus meridionalis, Semiplotus cirrhosus (Cyprinidae), Acanthocobitis sp., Schistura malaisei (Nemacheilidae), Amblyceps murraystuarti (Amblycipitidae), Glyptothorax sp., Oreoglanis sp. (Sisoridae) and Mastacembelus armatus (Mastacembelidae) (Ref. 116725).

species.name: Schistura xhatensis

species.name: Schistura yersini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in streams and rivers with gravel or rocky substrate and high water velocities (Ref. 40772). Resistant to organic pollution and can survive in streams that flow through villages and towns and exhibit strong signs of human perturbation (Ref. 40772). Most abundant in riffles and rapids with current velocities more than 1 m/s below the surface (Ref. 40772). Found in small high gradient rivers and small mountain streams, as well (Ref. 40772). Often associated with Poropuntius sp., Annamia normani, Schistura dalatensis and Glyptothorax laosensis (Ref. 40772).

They are strict herbivores which feed on plant debris, leaves and algae (Ref. 12225) but are reported as omnivores in Ref. 2060.  The males are mature at 18 cm and the females at 22 cm (Ref. 12225).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).  In the Amazon, the species of this genus are gregarious and undergo migration (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Schizolecis guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with rocky and sandy bottom, mostly in shallows and backwaters up to 30 cm deep, with slow water flow (0.5-10 cm/sec).  Forages mostly during the day with some night activity also recorded.  Grazes on microscopic algae, mostly diatoms and green algae growing on rocks and submersed vegetation; occasionally takes chironomid and simuliid larvae.  Before grazing on a patch with dense sediment, it makes wiggling head-down movements to dislodge sediment.  When scrapping algae off the substrate, it makes vigorous mouth movements, and moves by jerky movements probably related to its mouth making alternate grazing and attaching to the substrate.  Grazing  leaves characteristic, parallel and elongated marks on the substrate.  Density may reach about 0.09 fish.m-2 in stream stretches shaded by forest canopy and 0.15 fish.m-2 in sunned stretches (Ref. 26630).

species.description: Solitary or in pairs. Often on steep slopes in crevices and caves in 10-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi- and mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Schnakenbeck's searsid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic to bathypelagic in southern part of its range and benthopelagic from 365 to 1,200 m in the northern part (Ref. 4461).

species.name: School bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deeper waters around coral reefs.  Forms small groups to feed on plankton (Ref. 9710).  Synchronously hermaphroditic.

species.name: Schooling bumblebee goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits very shallow water of flowing streams, canals ditches and marshes (Ref. 12693).  Occurs from completely freshwater habitats downstream to brackish waters of the estuarine zone (Ref. 12693).  Prefers areas of considerable plant growth (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 12693).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Schooling dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock and coralline ledges and caves (Ref. 9710). In Socotra Archipelago, it is mainly recorded from the north coasts from hard coral communities including those dominated by Millepora and Porites, and encrusting and massive Agariciidae, Pectiniidae, and Mussidae, as well as from mixed communities of macroalgae and hard corals on rock platform and mixed encrusting communities on exposed rock platform, and a near vertical rocky drop off (Ref. 88695). Occurs in colonies. Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413).

species.name: Schoolmate cory
species.description: Widespread along the whole length of the river. Some specimens have been caught in creeks under tidal influence, others at the headwaters of basins (Ref. 35381). Sympatric with C. oiapoquensis.

species.name: Schraetzer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in groups in open sand and mud bottom of large rivers with moderate current.   Nocturnal, feeding on small invertebrates, especially molluscs, usually crepuscular but may also feed at daytime.  Larvae are benthic  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Schroeder's coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary on sheltered reefs with rich coral growth (Ref. 48636, 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Schroeder’s deepsea herring
species.description: Reaches at least 14 cm (Ref. 57190).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits rivers and streams, with fine sandy bottoms. Often collected syntopically with S. operculatum (Ref. 112319).

species.name: Scleronema ibirapuita
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits rivers and streams, inhabits rivers and streams with sand- or gravel-bottoms. The species has not been collected with congeners. The stomach of one specimen had immature aquatic insects and unidentified plant remains (Ref. 112319).

species.name: Scleronema macanuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and streams usually with sandy bottoms. Collected syntopically with S. minutum in some localities. Stomachs of eleven specimens were analyzed where 6 had immature aquatic Diptera (Chironomidae), Oligochaeta, unidentified plant fragments and sand. A study showed that the diet of immature individuals was composed of Chironomidae and Ephemeroptera. Individuals larger than 3.5 cm SL are reported to be capable of spawning and thus are considered adults (Ref. 122319).

species.name: Scleronema mate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. : Inhabits rivers and streams with sand- and gravel bottoms. In the rio Pardo basin, the species is collected syntopically with S. macanuda (Ref. 122319).

species.name: Scleronema milonga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and streams with sand- and gravel-bottoms and has not been collected syntopically with its congeners. Individuals larger than 3.1 cm SL are reported to be capable of spawning and are considered adults. Reported diet composed mainly of immature, autochthonous and benthic insects (Ephemeroptera, Chironomidae, and Trichoptera), in both adults and juveniles (Ref. 122319).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers and streams but has not been collected with its congeners. Stomachs of two specimens contained immature aquatic Diptera (Chironomidae and Simuliidae) and Ephemeroptera (Ref. 122319).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tannin stained blackwater streams (Ref. 12693).  Found in forest covered streams including peat adjacent areas.  Take around three months for free swimming fries (Ref. 57235).  Young individuals feed on insects at the water surface, adults take fishes (Ref. 12693, 57235) and smaller vertebrates (Ref. 56749).  A mouth brooder, young about 6 cm at birth (Ref. 7050, 57235).  Valued as an aquarium fish, its flesh commands a moderate price.

species.name: Scoloplax baileyi
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found in Rio Unini basin, in mid-sized streams within dense forest vegetation and these streams are blackwater throughout most of the year.  During the dry season, some streams carry a small amount of sediment and present higher pH and conductivity values.  Substrate consists of sand and silt and collections done using handnets sweeping stream bottom in depths that ranged
from 0.4 to 1.5 meters.  Stream temperature varied from 24.8 °C to 26.7 °C, pH from 5.2 to 6.5, conductivity from 8.8 to 18.6 µS/cm, and dissolved oxygen from 1.07 to 6.68 mg/l.  Also collected together with this species are at least 40 species, including other undescribed species, from different taxonomic groups (Ref. 92919).

species.name: Scoloplax baskini
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found among leaf litter in small clearwater tributaries of the middle part of rio Aripuanã (Ref. 79026).

species.name: Scoloplax dicra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ox-bow lagoons which have stagnant water and bottom covered with leaf debris and other organic litter; also occurs in cut-off pond with murky water and bottom composing of mixed sand and silt with some organic debris.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms in lagoons and areas close to reefs and mangroves.  Occurs singly or in small aggregations (Ref. 9785).

species.name: Scolopsis curite
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scolopsis de Peter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered lagoons on sandy or muddy bottoms close to reefs.  Occurs singly or in small aggregations.  Adults mainly in depths over 15 m; juveniles solitary and in sheltered coastal habitats (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Scolopsis masqué
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand bottoms close to reefs. Often silty habitats (Ref. 48635). Occurs solitary or in small groups. Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans, mollusks and polychaete worms (Ref. 90102). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus hutsonae on the pectoral fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Scolopsis nacré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms close to reefs. Feed on crustaceans, polychaete worms, mollusks and small fishes (Ref. 3810, 9785). Juveniles may be Batesian mimics of poison-fang blennies, Meiacanthus spp. (M. geminatus and M. vittatus) (Ref. 37816, 90102). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus hutsonae on the pectoral fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Scolopsis rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on coral reefs usually associated with sandy areas.  Adults inhabit outer lagoon reef flats and seaward reefs flats, often in groups.  Juveniles are found singly near the shelter of corals on clear shallow lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).  Adults form schools or small groups (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on small fishes,  crustaceans (Ref. 9710) and benthic invertebrates, primarily polychaetes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Scolopsis à barres obliques
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters around rocky-rubble and seaweed areas of coral reefs, outer slopes and lagoons.  Usually in small groups but may be seen solitary (Ref. 48635, 90102).  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans.

species.name: Scolopsis à taches orange
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms close to coral reefs.  Also near mangroves (Ref. 48635).  Frequently in silty areas with low visibility (Ref. 90102). Occurs often in small groups.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates and small fishes.

species.name: Scopelengys clarkei

species.name: Scopelidé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep water offshore on sandy mud bottom for most of the year, but also gathers in large shoals in deltas of rivers to feed during monsoons (Ref. 9987, 11230).  Spawn 6 batches of broods per year (Ref. 43449).  An aggressive predator (Ref. 9987).  Primarily caught along Maharashtra with the bag-net, better known as 'dol' net.  Operation of this gear is timed to a strong tidal current.  The bag with the mouth set against the current strains the fish which is being retained therein by the strength of the current.  The net is thus retrieved before the tide turns.  Very phosphorescent.  Excellent food fish.  Marketed fresh and dried or salted; consumed pan-fried (Ref. 9987).

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scopelogadus unispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scopelosaurus adleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Individuals of 20-22 cm SL, feeds on various types of plankton, almost exclusively deep-sea copepods of Pareuchaeta. Larger specimens also feed on squid, shrimp, and fish (Ref. 35945).

species.name: Scopelosaurus craddocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably bathypelagic.

species.name: Scopelosaurus gibbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Scopelosaurus herwigi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles epipelagic to mesopelagic in warm currents moving southwest from the equator; adults benthopelagic on slopes (Ref. 6602).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scopelosaurus hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scopelosaurus smithii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larvae are epipelagic, young inhabit the layers between 50-200 m, adults benthopelagic and found deeper than 500 m over continental and insular slopes (Ref. 6552, 6602).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on zooplankton.  Extensive migrations by juveniles and adults, probably for feeding in the subtropical belts.  Spawning occurs in tropical waters, especially in the western part of the Atlantic Ocean (Ref. 6689).

species.name: Scorched croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Scorpaena annobonae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena ascensionis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably does not exceed 5.0 cm TL (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Scorpaena azorica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard bottoms (Ref. 4570).

species.name: Scorpaena canariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena cocosensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena colorata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Scorpaena decemradiata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The collection depth and habitat of this species is unknown (Ref. 122805).

species.name: Scorpaena fernandeziana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena grattanica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena hatizyoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena hemilepidota
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scorpaena jacksoniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rocky coastal reefs (Ref. 93630).

species.name: Scorpaena lacrimata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena melasma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.

species.name: Scorpaena miostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains less than 20 cm TL.

species.name: Scorpaena neglecta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.

species.name: Scorpaena pascuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena pele
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scorpaena petricola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small species with a generally pallid head and body (Ref. 7365).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scorpaena thomsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena tierrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena uncinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaena wellingtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenella cypho
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenodes africanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore, rocky areas (Ref. 4510).

species.name: Scorpaenodes bathycolus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in relatively flat or gradually sloping sand-rubble bottom with scattered rock and coral outcrops in 60 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Scorpaenodes corallinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in coral reefs (Ref. 58302). Solitary and secretive, among corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Scorpaenodes immaculatus
species.description: Only one specimen known (at the date of 20 Feb. 2013).

species.name: Scorpaenodes insularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 4510) and has been collected from caves and crevices (Ref. 13121). Usually found among rocks below 3 m depth, small individuals may inhabit rubble (Ref. 86997).

species.name: Scorpaenodes investigatoris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scorpaenodes muciparus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported from Ref. 39597.

species.name: Scorpaenodes rubrivinctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected and observed from rocky reefs, often in association with sponges, upon the platform and along the margins of the Galápagos archipelago at 200-412 m; photographed at 160-300 m (Ref. 83997).

species.name: Scorpaenodes steinitzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenodes tribulosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenopsis altirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected from coarse sand bottom with broken shell and coral (Ref. 42181).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Scorpaenopsis eschmeyeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Scorpaenopsis longispina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenopsis orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Scorpaenopsis pluralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Apparently feeds on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 42181).

species.name: Scorpaenopsis pusilla
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpaenopsis rubrimarginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpiodoras calderonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpiodoras heckelii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpiodoras liophysus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scorpis chilensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scott's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More common in outer reef areas than sheltered lagoon reefs.  Usually seen in small groups feeding a short distance above the bottom on zooplankton.  These groups are composed mainly of females and juveniles.  Males in courtship, actively swim up to  3 m or more above the bottom with fins fully erect.

species.name: Scottie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit quiet, weedy water (Ref. 5472).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Scowling silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scrapermouth mbuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Scrapes algae off rocks and also takes in small crustaceans and worms (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Scribbled angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal and inner reef areas with rubble, soft bottoms, or open flat bottom areas with rock, coral, sponge, and seawhip outcrops.  May be found in small groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on sponges and tunicates.  Forms pairs or small groups.  Occasionally exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Scribbled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and rivers.  Enters estuaries (Ref. 4833).  Usually associated with streams having a gravel or sand substrates.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae and Diptera (Ref. 6028) and also small fishes and crustaceans (Ref.  12693).  Not seen in market, but probably sold fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion banforense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in brooks with a sandy bottom, with a water depth between 20 and 50 cm (Ref. 44596).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion chaytori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion etzeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brooks and swamps (Ref. 3788).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion fredrodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in temporary pools in a dry river bed and a swampy area crossed by a small creek; water temperature 24-27°C; pH 6.3-6.5 (Ref. 52015).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion guignardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It inhabits quiet brooks, swamps and weedy parts of small streams (Ref. 3788).  It is not a seasonal killifish and difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion liberiense
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brooks, swamps, pools and small streams in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788). Not a seasonal killifish; occurs in coastal lowlands with pure freshwater (Ref. 84174). It is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion nigrifluvi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in quiet brooks, swamps and weedy parts of small streams (Ref. 3788).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion roloffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools, brooks, swamps and small streams, mainly in the shallow and stagnant parts in the coastal rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion schmitti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brooks and small streams in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Scriptaphyosemion wieseae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Present in small rivers and a large rice swamp (Ref. 91031).

species.name: Sculpin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 42552); over rubble or rubble and sand bottom (Ref. 42181).

species.name: Sculpted lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is fairly common along the upper continental slopes between Namibia and southern Mozambique (Ref. 87957); upper slope, on or near the bottom (Ref. 5578). Observed mostly at depths between 450 and 900 m (Ref. 27644), but with records as shallow as 240 m (in Bass et al., 1976: listed as E. lucifer) (Ref. 87957). Feeds mainly on mid-water bony fish, also squid, octopus, shrimp and brittle stars (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Sculptured cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic at bathyal depth (Ref. 56809).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sculptured frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Sculptured goby
species.description: Found in coastal reefs and estuaries, secretly under rocks or in narrow ledges (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Sculptured pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal reef flats.  Also found in seagrass habitats to few meters depth (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 4.6 cm SL (Ref. 30874).  Seen in lagoons and seaward reefs in 0-6 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sculptured seamoth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found inshore of the continental shelf in muddy, silty and sandy bottoms, usually with seagrass; intertidal to 50 m depth (Ref. 75154). Large numbers of individuals are known to congregate in the shallows of estuaries.  The species is capable of burying itself in the sediment and change colors to match the background.

species.name: Scyliorhinus cabofriensis
species.description: Males of this species range in size from 30.8-46.8 cm (n = 8) and females from 27.6-45.0 cm (n = 16). Size of first maturity not exactly defined, however, males have well-developed claspers at 39.3 cm TL and egg-capsules and other evidence that would help establish size of maturity in females without dissection have not been found. Stomach contents include squid beaks and skeletal elements of bony fishes (Ref. 107325).

species.name: Scyliorhinus meadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Sea blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found along surge reef margins.   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Sea carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Sea conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Several similar species throughout the Indo-Pacific (Ref. 48635). Rarely seen and usually at night on sand, rubble and mud bottoms in 3-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sea pony
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to height (= TL - head length). Occurs in eelgrass beds (Zostera sp.) in lagoons. Used in India for traditional medicines. Diurnal. Adults pair-bond and greet on daily basis in the laboratory (Ref. 30915). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sea sweep
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on offshore and deepwater reefs (Ref. 9563).  Feeds at  mid-water on  zooplankton (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Sea trumpeter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Omnivorous species (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sea urchin cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tidal pools among spines of sea urchins (Echinotrix diadema and Diadema setosum) (Ref. 90035).

species.name: Seaboard goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas.

species.name: Seadevil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Seafan blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on surface of hard corals and sea fans on coral reefs, from shallow reef crests to drop offs at depths to 30 m. Exhibit greater habitat specificity than other chaenopsids. Spirobranchus giganteus. Females and immature males move about on surface of or near live corals, particularly sea fans. Breeding males are particularly found only in tubes abandoned by serpulid worms Spirobranchus giganteus. These probably controls their population size (Ref. 51514).

species.name: Seafarer’s ghost shark
species.description: This species is collected by midwater and bottom trawls. Maximum length for females is 64.5 cm BDL, 97.1+ cm TL, and for males 51.9 cm BDL, 83.4+ cm TL. The smallest free swimming individual is 11.8 cm BDL, 25.8 cm TL. Females are mature at 51.9 cm BDL, 76.7 cm TL, while males mature at 36.9 cm BDL, 63.8 cm TL (Ref. 116312).

species.name: Seagrass eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas and seagrass beds, usually bathed by clear, oceanic waters.  Feeds on small fish and invertebrates (Ref. 42064).

species.name: Seagrass wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) in seagrass beds and sandy algal flats of lagoons and mangrove channels.  Secretive amongst the vegetation and well-camouflaged (Ref. 48636, 58466).

species.name: Seagreen darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Seale's cardinalfish
species.description: An uncommon species found among branching corals of sheltered lagoon reefs (Ref.1607).  In small to large aggregations low on the reef.  Rarely seen deeper than 10 m (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Seale's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the intertidal zone of rocky shores, benches, and wave-swept seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Seamount Rudderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The juveniles (6.1-9.9 cm SL) were collected from the epipelagic zone at 30-50 m depth; larger individuals (11.0-56.1 cm SL) occur much deeper in the mesopelagic zone at 525-1438 m depth (Ref. 93030).

species.name: Seapen goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commensal in sponges and gorgonians (Ref. 11432, 48637).Commensal with sea pens and hollow, banching gorgonians (genus Solenocaulon) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Searcher
species.description: Adults are found offshore on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850); and deeper (to 300 m) than other ronquils (Ref. 48889). Reaches more than 38 cm (Ref. 48889).

species.name: Searcher stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottoms.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.

species.name: Searsioides calvala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Searsioides multispinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seaver splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Seaweed blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit eroded basins and limestone boulders covered by an algal mat, sea fans, etc. (Ref. 5521). Sometimes around mangrove roots, young are sometimes found in floating Sargassum (Ref. 26938). Omnivorous, but feed mostly on algae (Ref. 13442). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Seaweed pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in estuaries and in association with Zostera and other vegetation. Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Seba's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected in a sheltered bay on a mainly flat, silty-sand bottom with scattered patches of sea grass and occasional coral rubble in 30 m depth (Ref. 123123).

species.name: Sebae anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters and lagoons. They grow rather large (Ref. 48636). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemone Stichodactyla haddoni (Ref. 5911). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Sebastapistes nuchalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sebastes baramenuke
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes flammeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the bottom.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes hubbsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sebastes ijimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes inermis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed.  Plankton feeder (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes iracundus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes itinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep waters.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes joyneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes koreanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sebastes longispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky coasts.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes matsubarai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky areas (Ref. 559).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes minor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with bottom set nets.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes nivosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes notius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes nudus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 42552).

species.name: Sebastes oblongus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur along rocky coasts.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes owstoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes pachycephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs (Ref. 42552).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes peduncularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from juvenile specimens (Ref. 9341).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes scythropus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes spinorbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes steindachneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools on rocky and sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 559).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes taczanowskii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur near the coast.  May enter estuaries and brackish water.  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes thompsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes trivittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky coasts.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817). Minimun depth reported taken from Ref. 50610.

species.name: Sebastes varispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from juvenile specimens (Ref. 9341).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes ventricosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sebastes vulpes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky shore areas.  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Feed on crabs and fishes (Ref. 9137).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes wakiyai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastes zonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 42552).

species.name: Sebastiscus albofasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky bottoms.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebastiscus tertius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone, on rock bottom (Ref. 11230).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sebol toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Secret goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas with rock or algae cover (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Secretary blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits limestone slopes rather than patch reefs and these slopes are usually dotted with small brain corals, stinging coral, sea fans, whips, and sea urchins (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Sectoria atriceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a small stream about 3-5 m wide, in a narrow valley, up to 60 cm deep with moderate (in pools) to swift (in riffles) current, over sand and pebbles (pools) or boulders and pebbles (riffles).  The stomach and intestine of a 4.17 cm SL fish contained vegetable remains (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Sectoria heterognathos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles were collected in small rivers (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Securicula gora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, beels and canals (Ref. 4832).  Feeds at the surface on insects, insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 1479).

species.name: Segmented blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary on coral outcrops (Ref. 90102).  They inhabit shallow lagoon reefs, on algal covered rocks and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Feed on algae growing at the coral bases.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Maximum depth reported by Ref. 48636.

species.name: Seguro toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Selar aile noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore waters.  Feed mainly on small invertebrates, shrimps and copepods.

species.name: Selar harengule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in shallow coastal waters where it often swims near the surface.  They form dense schools on clear inner reefs, swimming high above substrate (Ref. 48635).  They feed chiefly on shrimps, copepods, decapods and small fishes (Ref. 30573, 90102).

species.name: Selar subari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults form large schools near inshore reefs (Ref. 30573).  Feed on shrimps, copepods, decapod larvae and other crustacean larvae and small fish (Ref. 5213, 90102).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).  Often caught by ski-boat anglers in southern Africa (Ref. 12484).

species.name: Selar à bande dorée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  They form large demersal schools over soft bottom habitats at depths shallower than 50 m.  Sometimes they ascend into freshwater reaches like the freshwater tidal zone in the Mekong delta (Ref. 12693).  Ostracods, gastropods and euphausiids are common prey but small fish are also taken.

species.name: Selenanthias barroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Selenanthias myersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Selene spixii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seleniolycus laevifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably benthopelagic (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Seleniolycus pectoralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seleniolycus robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens caught on  weighted bottom longlines (Ref. 58765).

species.name: Selenotoca papuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Selincuo naked carp
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Reported age of sexual maturity for males is 7 years, females 8 years old, and their life span can exceed thirty years. An omnivorous species consuming a wide range of food sources, including detritus, algae, macrophytes, benthic invertebrates, phytoplankton, zooplankton, and
fish. Reproductive season starts in late March or early April after winter ice thaws, and the main growing season is between April and October. Adults migrate to freshwater tributaries during reproductive seasons, while juveniles spend their first 5 years in rivers and grow in the lake thereafter (Ref. 123179).

species.name: Sellal bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Semaphore rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably occurs on craggy bottom (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Semaphore tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimens reach 7.0 cm TL (Ref. 2060).  Inhabits creeks of low to high current velocity.  Collected in sites between elevations of 10 to 80 m, insectivorous (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Semaphore whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Semaprochilodus brama
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Semaprochilodus kneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Semaprochilodus laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Semaprochilodus varii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims in the rapids.  Undergoes downstream migration during reproduction where it spawns in alluvial waters.  Six months later, the juveniles return upstream.  Individuals are sexually mature at  22 cm (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Semilabeo notabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel bottom in mountain streams (Ref. 26563).

species.name: Semilabeo obscurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seminemacheilus dursunavsari
species.description: Inhabits small stream with sandy and clay bottoms covered by dense vegetation (Ref. 124013).

species.name: Seminole goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in bottom in open stretches of coarse sand. Often hovers over burrow. Also known to inhabit mangrove streams with very fine silt-mud substrate (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Seminole killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open areas of lakes and quiet stream pools.  Young are usually found in schools near vegetation.  16 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Semipelagic torpedo
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Semiplotus cirrhosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Semiplotus manipurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing hill streams with rocky beds, smaller individuals in shallow and fast flowing waters while larger ones in deeper, slower waters (Ref. 42977).

species.name: Semiscaled goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rock or coral bottoms (Ref. 13628); also limestone canyons covered with algal mats (Ref. 5521). Found hiding in recesses at the bases of coral heads as well as burrows of the chiton Choneplax lata (Ref. 46821).

species.name: Semiscaly goggle goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype which was collected from reef flat of a seaward reef (Ref. 121824).

species.name: Semutundu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit lakes, swamps and rivers (Ref. 31256). Widespread in both shallow and deep water (Ref. 34291). Probably associated with rocky bottoms/coarse substrates (Ref. 27490). Mostly active during the night and the twilight hours (Ref. 2060). Juveniles may frequent exposed rocky shores (Ref. 12526). Feed on insects, crustaceans, molluscs and fish; some debris and vegetable matter may also be ingested (Ref. 28714). Moderately important as a food species in Lake Victoria, but becoming rare with the appearance of Nile perch (Ref. 4967). Catches decreased strongly in Lake Victoria after the Lates upsurge (Ref. 34291). Predation by Lates and competition with Lates (for haplochromines) may have played a role in the decline (Ref. 34291). A notably recovery in waters between 3m and 6m depth in Lake Victoria has been reported (Ref. 51900). Second most important food species in Lake Edward, Congo (Ref. 13302).

species.name: Senckenberg rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits creeks and small rivers flowing through primary rainforest and second growth forest and gardens, as well as tree-lined creeks in relatively open savannah.  Syntopic with either <i>Melanotaenia albimarginata, <i>M. aruensis, or <i>M. patoti as well as other fishes such as <i>Craterocephalus, <i>Mogurnda, <i>Glossamia, and <i>Glossogobius (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Senegal goby
species.description: The two female specimens were collected by spraying a solution of clove oil into horizontal cracks in the rock in 19 and 21 m depth (Ref. 123114).

species.name: Senegal minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Senou's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral-reef slopes, in protected bays, and found solitary on muddy or sandy-mud bottoms with dead-coral rubbles In the area. Associated with Its congener, A. atripes (Ref. 75136).

species.name: Sentani gudgeon
species.description: Commonly found throughout the lower altitudes of the Sepik River basin, preferring still waters of floodplain lakes, swamps and inundated floodplain. Rarely found in the main river channel. Feeds mainly on the eleotrid fish Ophieleotris aporos and large crustaceans such as Macrobrachium prawns. Also caught using pots, handlines harpoons, hand nets, scoop nets, and others. Female reaches 39.6 cm SL (Ref. 9162).

species.name: Sentani rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sepia stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and rock bottoms (Ref. 12951, 11230).  Ovoviviparous, with up to 4 in a litter (Ref. 12951).

species.name: Sepik glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flood plain water courses as well as foothill streams to an altitude of about 200-300 m.

species.name: Sepik grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rainforest creeks flowing through hilly or mountainous terrain.  Occur at altitude of 120-1500 m.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sepik rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swampy lagoons, lakes and small side channels of large rivers (Ref. 2847).  The only known floodplain dwelling rainbowfish.  Carnivorous, feeds mainly on small invertebrates taken from mid-water or from surface water (Ref. 46864).

species.name: Sepik River halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and backwaters to river channels, and lower sections of tributary streams.  Caught using harpoons, hand nets, and scoop nets.

species.name: Sequatchie darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seram blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary on dead corals (Ref. 90102) in sheltered bays and lagoons, often silty habitat, amongst mixed algae and coral rubble to about 10 m depth (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Sergeant baker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate, benthic species inhabiting rocky reefs and soft bottoms on the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 9563).

species.name: Sergent ciseaux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral or rocky reefs (Ref. 9334).  They aggregate in large numbers in open water above reefs and feed on zooplankton.  Not strongly territorial as other damselfishes in the area.  They become almost invisible in the darkness of deep water except for its brilliant post-dorsal white spot which gives the illusion of glowing in the dark.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sergent cromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults generally occur in steep slopes and patch reefs. Diurnal species (Ref. 9626), they most commonly form moderate-sized feeding-schools over reef tops, rising above the bottom to feed on plankton, mainly copepods. Often seen with Chromis cyanea (Ref. 9710). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Rarely marketed (Ref. 3139).

species.name: Sergent à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups along upper edges of sheltered drop-offs.  Also found in rocky inshore reefs with moderate to strong wave action.  In roving aggregations and somewhat difficult to approach (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sergent-major de Mer Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit upper edge of outer reef slopes and inshore rocky reefs.  Juveniles associated with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on  zooplankton, benthic algae, and small invertebrates (Ref. 1602).  Often in aggregations (Ref. 9710) feeding at midwater or tending nests among rocks and coral ledges (Ref. 90102).  In large numbers at spawning sites that are timed with large tides that carry their pelagic offspring far offshore (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Seriolella tinro
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serpe du Groenland
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns mainly in spring and early summer.

species.name: Serpent de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoons and coastal waters (Ref. 2683), from near shore to 40 m (Ref. 4455).  Burrows in sand or mud (Ref. 4455).  Feeds on small fishes, crabs and shrimps (Ref. 3651).

species.name: Serpent de mer (Ophichthus cruentifer)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore water (Ref. 7251).  Males mature at 19.7 cm TL and females gravid at 22.7 cm TL (Ref. 40865).

species.name: Serpenticobitis cingulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Found in muddy streams with fairly swift to very swift flowing water.

species.name: Serpenticobitis octozona
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in clear, high gradient mountain streams with very swift current, large boulders and rich and diverse fish faunas.  Also found in other habitats such as with quite rocky bottom and equally high fish diversity and with a more unstable gravelly bottom and much less fish diversity.

species.name: Serpenticobitis zonata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Found in stretches with relatively swift, clear water, with boulders and gravel bottom (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Serpenton acné
species.description: Benthic, the only specimen was taken from a depth of 60 m.

species.name: Serpenton antillais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Serpenton aux dents de marbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms of shallow waters.  Also often associated with mangroves.

species.name: Serpenton blanc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from shore to deep waters, but rare in shallow water (Ref. 7251).  On the continental shelf of South America, this species is said to be common between 5 and 40 m depths (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Serpenton caréné
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms (Ref. 9328).  The specimens were either dip-netted at the surface under night lights or with ichthyocides over sand bottoms of up to 30 m depth (Ref. 27478).

species.name: Serpenton caréné à taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky bottoms.

species.name: Serpenton chevrette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits soft bottoms.  Occurs in bays and backwaters to offshore banks, less commonly to 180 m depth.  The most common eel on Florida shrimp grounds.  Rarely consumed (Ref. 3795).

species.name: Serpenton croûte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, the only specimen known was encountered in the stomach of a Atractoscion nobilis.

species.name: Serpenton cuillère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 10 m.

species.name: Serpenton d'Afuera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 40 m.

species.name: Serpenton de Byrnes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic, the only specimen was taken during low tide in a sand bank.

species.name: Serpenton dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near estuaries and in marine waters (Ref. 5217).  Assumed to live in permanent or semi-permanent burrows with only snout and eyes exposed, darting to feed on other fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 43686).

species.name: Serpenton des rizières
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoons and estuaries, entering freshwater and paddy fields (Ref. 7245, 30573). Common in tidal reaches and nearby upstream areas of coastal rivers (Ref. 12693). Lives in holes in the river bottom and bank and actively forages for small fishes at night (Ref. 12693). Reported to spawn in rice-paddies during the rainy season (Ref. 12693). Caught in bag nets and similar gear.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Serpenton du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 20 m (Ref. 9328).  Burrows in bottoms.  Generally captured from tide pool depths to 155 m (Ref. 31243).

species.name: Serpenton du Panama
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms up to a few meters deep.

species.name: Serpenton enchanté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy areas.  A burrowing species.  Feeds on clams and fish (Ref. 4525).

species.name: Serpenton fuligineux
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms up to a few meters deep.

species.name: Serpenton funèbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms up to a depth of 325 m.

species.name: Serpenton gusano
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and on shallow muddy and sandy bottoms.  Benthic but not burrowing (Ref 35581).  Young are attracted to lights at sea surface.  Adults may often be observed near the surface (Ref. 9328).

species.name: Serpenton imberbe
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud.

species.name: Serpenton jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the shelf, on mud bottoms (Ref. 3397).  A nocturnally-active species (Ref. 48389).  Buries itself in the mud during the day, emerging only to feed at night (Ref. 48389).

species.name: Serpenton léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in coarse sand along the rocky coasts of oceanic islands (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Serpenton manchot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef flats and lagoons to at least 13 m.  Burrows in soft bottoms (Ref. 30573).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Caught in bags or nets, or by digging (Ref. 30573).  Used as shark bait (Ref. 30573).
