species.name: Serpenton mince
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only known specimen was obtained  from dredging on mud bottoms at a depth of 20 m.

species.name: Serpenton miro
species.description: Found on mud and sand bottom of estuaries and coastal lagoons.  Burrows in sand with only the head protruding (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Serpenton nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms, between 100 and 200 m.

species.name: Serpenton olive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and inshore areas of turbid waters.  Marketed fresh and used mainly for bait.

species.name: Serpenton petit
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 20 m.

species.name: Serpenton pointillé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand or mud in shallow water of the continental shelf near bays and lagoons (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Serpenton pointillé (Ophichthus remiger)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sandy and muddy bottoms.

species.name: Serpenton queue molle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A small, burrowing eel which is active over soft sediments at night.

species.name: Serpenton rond
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms up to a few meters deep.

species.name: Serpenton sans nageoires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms, from shallow waters (Ref. 9328); captured by rotenone, dredge and trawl (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Serpenton sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms of shelf waters (Ref. 5217).  Largest specimen examined was 93.3 cm TL, a 100 cm TL specimen was reported (Ref. 54133).

species.name: Serpenton souris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 30 m.

species.name: Serpenton tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms, from shallow waters up to a depth of 25 m.  Can be seen at times in daylight searching for prey under rocks and in crevices over rocky bottoms, or buried completely in the sand when inactive (Ref. 6852).

species.name: Serpenton tacheté (Ophichthus ophis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Lives in a permanent burrow, often in very shallow water.  Heads protrude diagonally from the sand.  Nocturnal.  Feeds on octopus and fish (Ref. 5217).  Bold and easily approached.  Feared by fishers (Ref. 9710).  Rarely consumed (Ref. 3795).

species.name: Serpenton vipère
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms up to a depth of 85 m.

species.name: Serpenton voile
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms, from the intertidal zone up to a depth of 17 m.

species.name: Serpenton à grande nageoire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky bottoms up to a depth of 35 m.

species.name: Serpenton à grandes taches
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.

species.name: Serpenton à longue nageoire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lagoons and estuaries, entering freshwater (Ref. 12693).  Often in tidal channels where loose groups congregate, and usually seen with just the head exposed (Ref. 48635).  Caught most often in tidal areas and estuaries (Ref. 12693).  Caught in bag nets and similar gear.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Serpenton à nageoire longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms up to a depth of 64 m (Ref. 9328).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Serpenton à nez long
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabiting the continental shelf on sand or mud bottom (Ref. 4455).  Buried with only its head exposed (Ref. 27121).  Also found in estuaries (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Serpenton à selles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).  Feeds on small crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 6522).

species.name: Serpenton élastique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottoms, between 1 and 35 m.

species.name: Serrabrycon magoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serran argentin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf in colder waters.  Utilized to some degree for human consumption.

species.name: Serran belles joues
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms, between 15 and 100 m depth.  Probably too small to be of commercial importance.

species.name: Serran bridé
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology not known (Ref. 9342).  Probably of no commercial interest due to a small median size and because it is apparently scarce.

species.name: Serran cabaicucho
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and muddy-sand bottoms. Juveniles and small adults are found on fine sand near the coast.  Lives to about 6 years (reaching a SL of 20 cm).  Feeds on fishes and crustaceans.  A synchronous hermaphrodite.

species.name: Serran cabrilla
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in schools (Ref. 5530).  Known from a temperature range of 14-16 °C (Ref. 9098).  Also caught with trammel nets (Ref. 9342).  An appreciated food fish in Peru (Ref. 9342).

species.name: Serran cagua
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Lives to about 4 years ( reaches 12 cm SL).  Feeds on crustaceans.  A synchronous hermaphrodite.

species.name: Serran camotille
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology and utilization not known (Ref. 9342).

species.name: Serran de Patagonie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serran de roche
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on sand or mud bottom near rocks and eelgrass, from the coast to a depth of 60 m.  A secretive species, it feeds on small fishes and benthic crustaceans during the day (Ref. 9342).  Capable of tolerating ample fluctuations of temperature (from 7.5 to 32°C) and survive extreme cold intervals (Ref. 9342).  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Important game fish caught in bays and harbors (Ref. 9342).  Minimum depth range based on occurrence (Ref. 79604).

species.name: Serran de sable
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays, coastal grassy areas and shallow banks.  Solitary (Ref.  26340) and retreats into shelter when frightened (Ref. 9710).  Neither opercular spine nor anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Popular as a pan fish despite its small size.

species.name: Serran de Sainte-Hélène
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard substrates in shallow waters (Ref. 2683).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 2683.

species.name: Serran des algues
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in or near kelp beds, shallow water and to about 50 m but mostly from 2.4-21m .  Found throughout water column.  Large specimens usually occur in deeper water.  Juveniles feed on benthic invertebrates (especially crustaceans); adults feed on fishes and cephalopods (Ref.9342).  Both juveniles and adults may feed on plankton when abundant (Ref.9342).  Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049).  Also caught with troll lines (Ref. 9342).  Excellent food fish and an important game fish (Ref. 9342).

species.name: Serran des lagunes
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs commonly in coastal waters and also enter estuarine regions (Ref. 36323).  Found over soft bottoms.  Flesh is of good quality and is eaten fresh.

species.name: Serran doré
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms, between 40 and 107 m depth.  An important game fish.

species.name: Serran farlot
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on sand bottom among or near rocks from shallow areas to about 183 m depth, but usually at less than 30 m. Juvenile feed on benthic invertebrates (crabs, bivalves and mysids) and rarely fish; adults prey on fishes (especially Porichthys notatus) and also on crustaceans (Ref. 9342). Pelagic spawners (Ref. 56049). Important game fish (Ref. 9342).

species.name: Serran fil
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottom (Ref. 5217).  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Good food fish (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Serran ganéen
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26999).

species.name: Serran guavine
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand or muddy-sand bottoms.  Probably too small in size to be of commercial importance.

species.name: Serran levant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably a gregarious and plankton-eating fish found near the bottom.

species.name: Serran perroquet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky bottoms in the vicinity of sand.  Reaches a maximum TL of at least 28 cm.  Utilization is not known.

species.name: Serran tatler
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting rocky areas.  Synchronously hermaphroditic.  Feed mainly on shrimps, less on crabs and bivalves (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Serran vieux
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on semi-hard or soft bottoms. Juveniles are often in association with Thalassia. Synchronously hermaphroditic (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Serran violon
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms or isolated reefs (Ref. 9342); usually found near patch reefs on sandy or broken-shell bottoms.  Solitary and diurnal.  Juveniles under laboratory conditions can tolerate low water temperatures, e.g. 9.4°C (Ref. 6852).

species.name: Serran à queue noire
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard bottom.  Carnivorous (Ref. 2739).  Minimum depth range from Ref. 121774.

species.name: Serran à rayures rouges
species.description: Secretive inhabitant of cave recesses (Ref. 9710). Also a ledge dweller (Ref 90102). Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Serran écriture
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the shelf and upper slope on rocks, Posidonia beds, sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 5506). Adults feed on fishes, cephalopods and crustaceans (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Serran écureuil
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bottoms with fine sand.

species.name: Serran épineux
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and muddy-sand bottoms, between 25 and 160 m depth.  Too small in size to be of commercial importance (Ref. 9342).

species.name: Serran-tambour
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over seagrass, sand, mud and rocks (Ref. 2739).  Carnivorous, decapods dominate the diet.  Adapts well in an aquarium (Ref. 12382).  A synchronous hermaphrodite (Ref. 56921).

species.name: Serranilla goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranochromis janus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits areas with slow current with vegetation (Ref. 4967, 52307). No information available on breeding (Ref. 52307, 97233) and feeding (Ref. 52307) behavior.

species.name: Serranochromis spei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranochromis stappersi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranus aliceae
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the deeper portion of coastal reefs, usually below 30 m, and is often observed hovering at a short distance above rocks, sand or rubble (Ref. 95046).

species.name: Serranus drewesi
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a submarine cave (Ref. 118671).

species.name: Serranus heterurus
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranus inexpectatus
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky bottoms (Ref. 118671).

species.name: Serranus maytagi
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranus pulcher
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard bottoms (rock, gravel, coral rubble, or maerl) from about 1 m (juveniles) to at least 30 m depth (Ref. 114584).

species.name: Serranus stilbostigma
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serranus tico
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble fringe of reefs (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Serrapinnus aster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrapinnus calliurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to live in groups of equal ratio for both sexes.  Its biotope depends on the season.  In March, they are captured in great numbers in shallow reed zones with strong current.  In October,  they practically disappear from the same environment (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Serrapinnus heterodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus kriegi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus lucindai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrapinnus microdon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus micropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus notomelas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).

species.name: Serrapinnus piaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in ponds.  Oviparous with distinct pairing (Ref. 205).  Presence of rays with hooks in the anal fin which can serve as contact organs during copulation according to other authors (Ref. 54306).

species.name: Serrapinnus potiguar
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality, the rio Ceará-Mirim, is characterized by clear and transparent water, sandy
bottom high depth 1.2 m, slow to moderate water current and dense floating and submerse vegetation.  Sympatric and synotopic with <i>Compsura heterura, <i>Serrapinnus heterodon and <i>S. piaba in the type locality.  Feeds mainly on vegetal matter and algae, but also takes insects and microcrustaceans (Ref. 96867).

species.name: Serrapinnus sterbai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrapinnus tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrapinnus zanatae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus altispinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus altuvei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus auriventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus compressus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Rio Madeira the index of fecundity is 6400 oocytes (Ref. 26758).

species.name: Serrasalmus eigenmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus emarginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus geryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus gibbus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus gouldingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus hastatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus hollandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus irritans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus maculatus
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in small groups of up to 20 individuals which appear to have a definite range within a pond or a creek.  Observed to be active mainly during the day.  Larger fish extend their foraging until about 9 at night.  where it stays in the shallows near the bottom, sheltered among vegetation (Ref. 9080).  Larvae and juveniles hide and feed within the root tangle of water hyacinths, which also act as a dispersal agent during floods (Ref. 40399).  Larvae feed on
microscopic crustaceans and small aquatic insects; very small size juveniles (about 1.2 cm)
already clip fins of other fishes (Ref. 40399).  Juveniles and adults feed mostly on fins and muscle portions of fishes (Ref. 9080, 40398).  Adults may scavenge on dead mammals, including humans (Ref. 40400).  Attacks on humans with bite outbreaks may occur in dammed
portions of rivers during the breeding season, related to brood protection by the spawning
adults (Ref. 50802).

species.name: Serrasalmus manueli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus marginatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly during the daytime, though some large fish (15-20 cm SL) extend their foraging activity to dusk (about 1800-1900H). Night is spent sheltered among vegetation. Small-sized to medium-sized fish (7-10 cm) are solitary and patrol feeding territories (3-4 square m.) in a way similar to that reported for the scale-eating Catoprion mento. Stalking with some use of plant cover is a frequent mode of hunting employed by S. marginatus. It approaches its prey with a slow, stealthy movement from behind or below. It strikes its prey on the tail or anal fin, of which a piece is clipped out with a jerking motion of the body. This clipping is audible underwater. Lurking is also employed during daytime (Ref. 9080).

species.name: Serrasalmus medinai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus nalseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus neveriensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus nigricans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus nigricauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus odyssei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is reported from the clear- to black-water rivers of the Upper Madeira where it seems to be scarce in white waters. Inhabits the shallow part of the river near the shores especially where dead woods accumulate and scarce in the running part of rivers. Apparently common in syntopy with young S. rhombeus individuals of equal size (Ref. 85594).

species.name: Serrasalmus sanchezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus scotopterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus serrulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus stagnatilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrasalmus undulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrated deepwater scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrated flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken over sand around coral reefs to depths of 11 m; one specimen taken by trawl at 45 m (Ref. 9790). Also occurs on silty sand or rubble bottoms near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Serrivomer garmani
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Serrivomer schmidti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesopelagic species feeding on crustaceans and small fishes.

species.name: Serrivomer à dents courtes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common depth of juveniles around 650-850 meters while subadult and adults are deeper in the water column from 800-1000 meters; no indication of diel vertical migration in juveniles and adults (Ref. 94792).  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Serrivomer à nageoire longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Solitary (Ref. 5951); exhibits vertical migrations during the night.  Feeds on shrimps, other crustaceans and small fishes (Ref. 6722).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Serrulate whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) recorded from the continental slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: Setarches armata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sevan khramulya
species.description: Feeds on detritus.  Juveniles feed on zooplankton and zoobenthos (Ref. 41168).

species.name: Sevan trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce endémique du lac sevan en arménie. The adults spawn in the lake proper at a depth range of 0.5 to 3 m, over fine gravel.  Two spawning stocks are known:  one spawns in the northwestern corner of the lake from the beginning of November till the end of December; the other spawns at the southeastern corner, from the middle or the end of January till the end of March.  This fish approaches the coast twice a year:  from April till July and from October till December.  In mid winter and at the end of summer, it leaves the coasts to stay at greater depth.  Adults feed exclusively on sand hoppers (Amphipoda) (Ref. 593).

species.name: Seven khramulya
species.description: Inhabits mainly the drier parts as well as the upper reaches of rivers in mountains and the lower reaches which sometimes end in marshes or deserts.  Feeds primarily on plants.  Spawns mostly on stony ground in rivers (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Seven pelvic ray flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottoms.

species.name: Seven ray toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seven River's minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits marshy springs, lakes, desert ponds (karasuks) and irrigation ditches (aryks).  Spawns in March and April (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Seven-banded silver biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seven-lined prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species, from visual underwater observations, occurs in rocky substrate, 2.5-11.3 m, at water temperature from 14ºC to 21ºC during July to September. It is a secretive species, and under ordinary condition it seldom leave their shelters under boulders in the daytime and usually with only the anterior part of the body exposed. During the collection, 1-3 fish were usually found under one boulder 0.3 × 0.3 m in size, the common density reached 8 fish/m2. The species is inactive at night, unlike E. hexagrammus which commonly occurs in the same rocky habitat. Specimens of the type series had average body weight 1.425 g (1.100-1.900 g), the smallest collected fish (FEMBSNR 748 juvenile SL 34 mm) had body weight of 0.350 g. Stomachs of collected specimens contained remains of shells of small mollusk Falsicingula mundana (Gastropoda: Discopoda: Falsicingulidae), remains of unidentified fish and lumps of tiny fish eggs (Ref. 86739).

species.name: Sevenband cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species.  Occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Sevenband tonguesole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sevenbar weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sevenstriped cardinalfish
species.description: Common in reef flats and shallow lagoons to a depth of about 4 m.  Also found in rocky reefs (Ref. 93839). Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 1602).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Usually in pairs swimming close to shelter (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Severi’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected in an area characterized by steep banks and a shoreline bordered by dense forest; large amounts of aquatic plants (Family Podostemonacease) were present in the river, with the water being acidic (pH 5.8) and well oxygenated (91% saturation) (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Severns' wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly in open ground areas covered with rubble; may also be found in areas with rock and coral patches (Ref. 35870).  Found in small harems and feeds on material on the substratum (Ref. 35870).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 35870.

species.name: Severtsov's loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mature on the 3rd year of life (Ref. 1441).

species.name: Sewellia albisuera
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits rocky rapids and deep pools over sandy substrates. Also found in rocky pools isolated from the main river.

species.name: Sewellia analis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sewellia breviventralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Very rheophilous, caught in only in rapids with current velocity exceeding 1 m/sec together with other rheophilous fish such as species of Garra, Annamia, Hemimyzon, Homaloptera, Schistura and Nemacheilus. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 40433).

species.name: Sewellia diardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits hill streams. Occurs sympatrically with S. speciosa.

species.name: Sewellia elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in moderately high gradient forested montane stream with large boulders, a coarse gravel or sandy bottom and some logs.  Also found in an extremely high gradient, tumultuous mountain stream with huge boulders and coarse gravel bottom.

species.name: Sewellia lineolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Rheophilous, inhabits rapids and riffles. Found in small streams with large and deep pools covered by submerged plants, provided that small riffles are present between these pools. Occurs also in high gradient streams consisting almost exclusively of waterfalls; in larger rivers, at the upper extremity of riffles where current velocity do not exceed 0.2 m/sec, as well as habitats with high water velocities exceeding 1 m/sec. Often associated with Annamia normani, Balitora sp., Schistura spp., Glyptothorax spp., Anguilla marmorata, and Rhinogobius spp. Stomach contents include benthic invertebrates and algae. Observed to be active during daytime searching in the periphyton on both horizontal and vertical surfaces of stones probably searching for aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 40433). Commonly found in aquarium trade in Finland (Länsman, pers. comm., 25/03/2010, Ref. to find).

species.name: Sewellia marmorata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Collected from streams with shallow rapids; current relatively slow and water very clear; deep pools with detritus and muddy or sandy substrate.  Stomach contents indicate that this species feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 40433).

species.name: Sewellia medius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sewellia patella
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits a river with a succession of riffles over coarse gravel and larger single stones and deep pools over sandy bottom. Rheophilous, caught in only in riffles or rapids with current velocity from 0.6 to more than 1 m/sec. Found with Garra cambodgiensis, Schistura sp. and Homaloptera yunnanensis. Feeds on aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 40433).

species.name: Sewellia pterolineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Sewellia songboensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sewellia speciosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers with rocky bottom, with gravel and stone and sometimes large boulders.  River current is moderate to swift, but the gradient is moderate.

species.name: Sewellia trakhucensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seychelle's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit surge areas of exposed outer reef flats and seaward reefs.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Seychelle's wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seychelles dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic fishes found on sandy or muddy substrates, among weeds and in coral reefs from tide pools and the surf zone (Ref. 96610).

species.name: Seychelles goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from an isolated patch of rock and coral, with sponges and much sand (Ref. 82838).

species.name: Seychelles moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common among rubble, coralline algal debris, and coral heads of shallow wave-washed reefs (Ref. 1602, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Often found in tide pools.  Sluggish eel (Ref. 1623), but may bite when provoked (Ref. 2334).

species.name: Seychelles shrimpgoby
species.description: Found in coarse sand and rubble bottoms of coastal reefs in 1-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Seychelles silver sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually seen in aggregations in the shelter of coral reefs, at times in less than 1 meter depth.  Collected using rotenone and spear (Ref. 106074).

species.name: Seychelles spiny dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among weeds (Ref. 1623).

species.name: Seychelles sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Seyhan dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swift and cold flowing water with cobble and pebble bottom. Collected together with Capoeta angorae (Ref. 93268).

species.name: Seyhan trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Señorita
species.description: Live in kelp and other seaweeds and over rocks. Occurs in intertidal up to 97 m (Ref. 96339). Found usually at depths shallower than 23 m but also caught at depths up to 73 m.  Often form small groups, frequently well off bottom.  When disturbed often burrows in bottom sediment.  Sleep at night buried in sand with head protruding.  Feed on a variety of small invertebrates and also picks parasites from other fishes that come to be cleaned.  No sex reversal.  Pelagic spawner (Ref. 56049).

species.name: Shabout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small to large rivers (Ref. 96964). It can attain sizes of up to 2 m and a mass of 100 kg (Ref. 96964).

species.name: Shadine pisquette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species usually occurring inshore.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Preyed upon by many larger fishes and squids (Ref. 5521).  Important as live bait for scombrids (Ref. 26340).  In 1937, at Kingston, Jamaica it spawns during the winter months.  Travels long distance (Ref. 37032).

species.name: Shadow bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brushy and vegetated, gravel-bottomed, sand-bottomed and mud-bottomed pools of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on small fish (darters, madtoms, minnows), crayfish, and larger insects including dragonfly, mayfly, and stonefly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Shadow bristlemouth
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Shadow goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary (Ref. 90102). Found over silty (Ref. 58652) and muddy bottoms around inner reefs.  Common in mangroves, entering estuaries and rivers (Ref. 4343). Toxin concentrated in the skin; contains 28.7 µg/g tetrodotoxin in the internal organs while the flesh holds 1.7 µg/g (Ref. 5719).

species.name: Shadow toothcarp
species.description: Inhabits waters of all velocities, between 35 and 590 m elevation, with temperatures of 21 to 37°C.  Lives in small groups in brooks, creeks and along the shorelines of rivers where it feeds on detritus, filamentous algae, aquatic insects and ooze.  Probably reproduces throughout the year (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Shaggy angler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits still muddy habitats that are either deep or offshore (Ref. 48635) or shallow rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178. Solitary and often among leaf-eater debris (Ref 90102).

species.name: Shaggy cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty sand, gravel, and pebble bottoms (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Shaggy cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species inhabiting shallow reefs (Ref. 34024).  A benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Shaggy whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Shalyni barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in hill streams (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Shannon galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in the margins of lakes and streams, usually in rocky areas or around vegetation and debris.  Bottom-dweller in shallows of lakes and inlet streams over rocky substrates.  Often sheltering in crevices under rocks, woody debris or among aquatic plants.  May also occur in deeper lacustrine waters.  A nocturnally active, seldom seen species.  Breed in summer (December-January), releasing demersal eggs among rocks at lake margins which hatch in two weeks.  Juveniles swim in midwater feeding on plankton, and colonise the bottom after about six months.  Sexual maturity is attained at the end of the first year; the maximum life span is probably about three years (Ref. 44894).  Feed on insects, small crustaceans, algae and eggs of other galaxiids.

species.name: Shark Bay eel-blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in sand-weed areas (Ref. 36661).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shark mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit muddy freshwaters and mangroves.  May feed on surface algae and insects, but also on benthic organisms.  May breath air and wriggle over mud banks for short distances.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sharkmouth snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sharknose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs with clear waters, preferably in oceanic, insular areas (Ref. 13928).  In pairs near coral heads.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  A cleaner (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.  Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).  Feeds on ectoparasites of fishes (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Sharktail distichodus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distichodus fasciolatus is a bottom-dweller in streams, found near the muddy bottom in lakes, large rivers and their dead-ending branches (Ref. 96324). This species is mainly herbivorous, though insects and nematodes were also found in the stomachs (Ref. 96324). The fry are born near the river banks just before the April or December floods and feed on zooplankton and insect larvae in the flooded zones; adults mainly feed on insect larvae, aquatic plants, leaves and seeds (Ref. 96324).

species.name: Sharm sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sharp-headed wrasse
species.description: Occurs over sand bottom in lagoon (Ref. 7461).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 7461).

species.name: Sharp-nose weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow, low reef on sand with sparse tall weeds in seagrass areas (Ref. 9002).  Feed mostly on weed shrimps (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Sharp-nosed catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on higher plants, including a variety of fruits, but also takes ants, grasshoppers, beetles, small crabs and prawns.

species.name: Sharp-nosed longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found under corals in lagoons (Ref. 559).  Usually occur in water shallower than 3 m on reefs, or in tide pools (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sharp-nosed river mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very little available data.  Possibly ascending some way up rivers.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sharp-nosed sand goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow sandy inner reefs and estuaries (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Sharp-snout lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sharp-spined notothenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on seafloor and spawns during summer (Ref. 45168).  They feed primarily on errant polychaetes, with lesser amounts of amphipods, fish eggs and mollusks.

species.name: Sharp-toothed grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams, preferring deep back waters and slow-flowing portions. Forms shoals in the middle of the water column with Hephaestus jenkinsi Whitley, 1945. Occurs in clear waters over rocky substrates, usually where algae are in abundance. Found in highest abundance during snorkelling in Pitta Creek, 1km upstream from the confluence with the Prince Regent River (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Sharpbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is common in large streams and reservoirs in Hong Kong but not favored as a table fish because the flesh is unpalatable and very bony; abundant in China where it is canned.  The main bulk of the diet includes zooplankton, insects, crustaceans, algae and detritus.

species.name: Sharpchin rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sharpchin slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic, but also probably associated with the bottom (Ref. 35724).  Oviparous, with mesopelagic larvae, probably found in deeper waters (Ref. 35724).

species.name: Sharpfin barracuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Also found in bays (Ref. 9768).  Schooling species.  Nocturnally active (Ref. 9768).

species.name: Sharpfin chubsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Occurs in pools and backwaters of creeks and small rivers over sand or silt.  Often found near vegetation.

species.name: Sharphead darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast, deep rocky riffles in small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Sharphead eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In quiet sections of the river, over sandy bottom.  Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Sharphead perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Temperate species which occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Sharpjawed buntingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Non-annual breeder.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Sharpline cardinalfish
species.description: Found very close to bottom (Ref. 44115). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sharpnose croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 9772).  An important foodfish.

species.name: Sharpnose darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast boulder riffles and runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Sharpnose grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit slow or fast moving water of lagoons, streams and rivers, in clear or turbid conditions.  Most commonly encountered in deeper sections of larger watercourses (Ref. 44894).  Occur in lentic and lotic freshwater.  Herbivorous species (Ref. 7300).  Feed on filamentous algae.  Breed between November and December when water temperatures rise to  about 29°C.  Sexual maturity is attained at 20-22 centimeters (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sharpnose lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sharpnose sand-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sharpnose sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in rocky intertidal and subtidal areas, but also over sand and in eelgrass and seaweeds (Ref. 2850).  May leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Occasionally enters fresh water (Ref. 27547).  Probably feeds on small invertebrates common among seaweed and in tide pools.  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Sharpnose seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore waters (Ref. 2850). From surface to 229 m (Ref. 96339). Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).  Seldom caught by fishers (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Sharpnose shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs of medium to large rivers but is less often found in sand or mud bottomed pools (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on aquatic and terrestrial invertebrates (71% of diet) detritus, plant material and sand.  Batch spawner (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Sharpnose silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sharpnose stingray
species.description: Likely confined to the inner continental shelf (Ref. 9840), over sandy and mud bottoms (Ref. 30573). Recorded from coastal waters and river mouths (Ref. 45255). Feeds on bottom crustaceans including shrimp, crabs and small lobsters (Ref. 5578). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Important food fish, the skin and flesh are dried or used to produce leather for purses and bags (Ref. 9840). Caught in very large quantities in the demersal tangle net, bottom trawl and trammel net fisheries. Utilized for its meat, skin (high value) and cartilage (Ref. 58048). It is parasitised on the dorsal skin surface by the monogeneans Dendromonocotyle citrosa, D. colorni, D. ukuthena (Ref. 124058) and D. lotteri (Ref. 124051).

species.name: Sharpnose tonguefish
species.description: Only two specimens were collected from the deep waters, but It is expected to have wider distributions, horizontally and vertically. Stomach contents include small crustaceans, snails and bivalves. Little else is known about the biology of this species (Ref. 127475).

species.name: Sharpnose weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common along the lower reaches of rocky reefs and drop-offs near the bottom in fine brown and red algae zones or in areas with sparse growths of seagrass.

species.name: Sharpnose worm eel
species.description: Inhabits sand bottoms near reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sharpnose wrasse
species.description: Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs, in caves and crevices (Ref. 9710).  A secretive species.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9823).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Sharpnosed coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef with sand at the base (Ref. 57884).

species.name: Sharpnosed duckbill
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Sharpnosed sawtooth pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and lakes, apparently in both running and still water (Ref. 188), but not swimming upriver in the smaller streams (Ref. 4910). The distribution of this species suggests that it tolerates a wide variety of water conditions (Ref. 188).

species.name: Sharpsnout hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen collected more than 150 years ago at Molucca Islands, Indonesia (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sharpsnout snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Forms congregations in confined sandy areas of sandy bottoms (Ref. 30874) where it buries itself using its pointed snout or its bony, sharp tail.  May feed on small fishes, crabs, and prawns (Ref. 30874).

species.name: Sharpsnout tubeshoulder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also benthopelagic (Ref. 4461).

species.name: Sharpspine skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sublittoral on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).  Feed on invertebrates and bony fishes (Ref. 9908).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 4.9-5.4 cm long and 2.5-2.9 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: Sharptail eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly encountered swimming near the bottom in clear water from harbors to reefs.  More common along continent and in grassy areas (Ref. 7251).  Found in shallow areas to depths of 9 m.  Feeds mainly on crabs.  (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Sharptail goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, enters lagoons (Ref. 4343).  Found in muddy estuaries and coastal bays (Ref. 4833).  Enters lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 2847).  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans and other invertebrates (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Sharptooth seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Sharptooth tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Shoals in clear, flowing or standing, open water; appears to co-exist with the tigerfish Hydrocynus forskalii in open water although it is heavily preyed upon by that predator, particularly those shoals of tigerfish ranging up to 45 cm in length (Ref. 13337). Omnivorous, often feeding from surface waters on winged insects; also takes insect larvae, crustaceans and eggs and fry of other fish (Ref. 13337). Matures after a year; partial spawner of moderate fecundity, with usually fewer than 700 eggs per female; shoals migrate upstream after first summer rains; breeds throughout the summer months; used as forage fish and as bait for tigerfish and pike (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Shaw Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish not able to undertake diadromous migrations. In 2002, it was recorded from a small (0.6-1.4 m average width and 0.15-0.20 m in average depth), cool, clear, alpine creek, flowing through a grassy plain, consisting of pools, glides and riffles, with smaller amounts of small cascades, and with very little shading except that provided by grasses. During the winter the catchment is usually covered by snow for varying periods of time. Substrate consisted of bedrock, boulder and cobble, with smaller amounts of pebble, gravel and coarse sand. The instream cover was provided mainly by rock and from bank and vegetation (alpine grasses) overhang, and pools averaged 0.5 m in depth. Recorded densities of 0.05-0.18 fish/m2 and it is the only native fish species so far recorded from within its range (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Shaw's cowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  Known in rocky reefs, usually fairly deep, including estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Shaw's shovelnose guitar fish
species.description: Found on shallow waters (Ref. 27550).

species.name: Shawnee darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 27671).

species.name: Sheep-pacu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sheepshead swordtail
species.description: Found in fast flowing waters.

species.name: Sheila's damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in exposed rocky shores, common in tide pools (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shelf flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shelf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Shelter cardinalfish
species.description: Benthic species which inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018. Forms groups that shelter among urchins, black corals and gorgonians (Ref 90102).

species.name: Shen's basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Shen’s soldierfish
species.description: No depth recorded from the only country (Taiwan) where it was collected (Ref. 114923).

species.name: Sheppard's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves, ledges and rubble bottoms of outer reefs in 20-70 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Sherborn's pelagic bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on pelagic crustaceans (Ref. 58748).

species.name: Shibukawa’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shield darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit gravel and sand riffles and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Shifted wolf eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Shige shrimpgoby
species.description: Occurs on coastal sand slopes to a depth of at least 35 m (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Shiho's seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported to live in a wide range of habitats, from shallow high-energy algae reefs to soft bottom habitats (Ref. 117115). Length type refers to height (= TL - head length).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shimadai's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered reefs in 3-20 (Ref 90102).

species.name: Shimizu's squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from 2 specimens taken with dynamite in Sulawesi in 1909 (Ref. 27370).

species.name: Shimmering cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools with other Archamia species in coral reef lagoons (Ref. 559). Cryptic, hiding in dark crevices and caves in reefs during the day (Ref. 54391).

species.name: Shimofuri goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline (Ref. 37812). Native to fresh and brackish waters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Shimoni sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from reef flat with dead coral and sand (Ref. 106074). Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Shiner anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shiner perch
species.description: Usually in shallow water, around eelgrass beds, piers and pilings and commonly found in bays and quiet back waters (Ref. 2850).  Also in calm areas of exposed coast (Ref. 2850).  Enter estuaries and brackish waters (Ref. 114138) [noted from freshwaters in Ref. 2850, but it is unlikely or rarely]. Found in loose schools or aggregations (Ref. 2850, Ref. 114138).  Young feed mainly on copepods, while adults eat various small crustaceans, mollusks, and algae (Ref. 27547).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).  Exhibit seasonal onshore-offshore movements (Ref. 27547).

species.name: Shining pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shining tubeshoulder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at 300-900 m (Ref. 58302). Young migrate in association with Cyclothone signata to within 200 m of the surface at night and feed extensively on small crustaceans (Ref. 4525). Oviparous, with large mesopelagic larvae (Ref. 35760).

species.name: Shinohara’s grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shiny loosejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed on crustaceans (Ref. 4525).  Probably spawn in spring (Ref. 35921).  Apparently, undergo diurnal migration (Ref. 35921).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35921).

species.name: Shipwreck pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Numerous individuals were found along the vertical, stern section of the outer hull of the vessel in about 23-28 m depth. The iron hull was completely encrusted with marine growth, especially algae, gorgonians, tunicates, and sponges. The fishes either rested on the bottom or hovered in midwater usually in small groups (Ref. 100512).

species.name: Shirai's spurdog
species.description: Found in shallow waters of the upper continental slope (Ref. 122378).

species.name: Shire tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in very shallow waters around Lake Malawi that are densely vegetated, but also in lagoons (Ref. 5595). It can occur at temperatures ranging from 23.0-42.0 °C (Ref. 670). It feeds on detritus and phytoplankton (Ref. 5595). A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 118638). A large species heavily exploited in Lake Nyasa [= Lake Malawi] and its catchment; males in particular are fast-growing and the species is cultured commercially in Malawi in cages and ponds (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Shirin tooth-carp
species.description: Inhabits Khosroshirin Stream in the uppermost reaches of the Kor River Basin and its connected springs including Paselari and Pahn springs. Paselari spring is composed of muddy substrate with small gravels, and water surface covered by dense filamentous green algae. The surrounding area is vegetated with reed (Phragmatis sp.), rush (Juncus sp.), shrubs and trees. Water current is high in Khosroshirin stream while low in Paselari and Pahn springs. The following mean values of physico-chemical paramaters of three stations from Paselari spring were recorded: nitrates 1.95 mg l-1, nitrites 0.42 mg l-1, phosphates 0.59 mg l-1, ammonia 0.12 mg l-1, dissolved oxygem (DO) 8.92 mg-1, DO% 122.6, total dissolved solids 191.7 mg-1, conductivity 395 μs cm-1, salinity 0.18 0/00, pH 7.9 and water temperature 17.05°C . Collected together with Acanthobrama persidis, Alburnus mossulensis, Capoeta aculeata, Capoeta saadi (Cyprinidae) and Onchorhynchus mykiss (Salmonidae) from Khosroshirin Stream. Threatened mainly by the carnivorous exotic O. mykiss (Ref. 94548).

species.name: Shirley's coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered reefs at 3-12 m deep (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Shirvan roachling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shoal bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shoal chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs of small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Shokihaze goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Native to marine and brackish waters in China, Japan and Korea (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Short alfonsino
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short barbeled velvetchin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs in coastal waters (Ref. 9137) and river mouths; usually over sandy bottoms near rocky shores, from summer to early winter (Ref. 56360).

species.name: Short barbelled catfish
species.description: Inhabits river.  Feeds exclusively on small fishes including clupeids, chanids and melanotaeniids.

species.name: Short barbelled suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Lips greatly enlarged in a big flat sucker; occurs in rapids and fast flowing waters; clings onto stones and can even climb up waterfall; feeds on algae and aquatic insects (Ref. 36900).

species.name: Short boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Short dorsal-fin snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short fin pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 6601, 58302).  Adults have usually been taken in hauls to depths in excess of 500 m although they have also been captured at night in several hauls between 275 to 0 m.  Larvae have been captured in hauls restricted to the upper 100 m and have been captured year-round throughout its range  (Ref. 10755).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35929).  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 35929).  Adults prey on other midwater fishes (Ref. 6691).

species.name: Short river garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in harbors and mangrove areas (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Short tail worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short tapetail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-armed waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Short-bodied arrowtooth eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-body frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-fin goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-finned snailfish
species.description: The sediment from the Agassiz trawl included gray and brown silt and the bycatch was dominated by the holothurians Molpadia sp., Echiura and glass sponges; polychaetes were numerous (not less than 12 species including Travisia sp.). Also gorgonians and alcionarians, as well as ascidia of Culeolus sp., colonies of bryozoans Kinetoskias were few (Ref. 123108).

species.name: Short-hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently purely riverine. More data needed, based on separation from S. phasa.

species.name: Short-headed lantern fish
species.description: High-oceanic (Ref. 4479).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found between 175-550 m during the day and near the surface to about 225 m at night (Ref. 4066, 58302).  Large males partially or non-migratory (Ref. 4066).  Exhibits dwarfing in minimum region off Brazil with a maximum length of about 3.6 cm SL and sexual maturity from about 2.7 cm SL (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Short-headed sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. About 110-200 eggs are contained in both ovaries (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Short-headed tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on recovered landings where this species is included in an assemblage of fish species which generally live at, or about at, depths shallower than 100 m, this fish is a shallow-water species of tonguefish inhabiting depths of approximately 100 m or so (Ref. 126065).

species.name: Short-headed worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, in bays (Ref. 9563); burrowing, on soft bottoms (Ref. 7300).  Caught under surface nightlights, and by trap, trawl, hook-and-line, and is occasionally discovered in fish stomachs; a benthic species living from tidepool depths to 156 meters (Ref. 56887).

species.name: Short-horn triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-jaw goatfish
species.description: The habitat is most probably shallow bottom of the upper shelf reached by traditional artisanal (Ref. 130857).

species.name: Short-jawed lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 7300, 75154), benthopelagic and neustonic between 1 m at night and 856 m during day (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Short-keel pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in freshwater and estuarine habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Brood pouch may be developed at 7.85 cm SL.

species.name: Short-maned Sand Eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand or mud in shelf waters (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Short-maned sand-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Short-nosed flyingfish
species.description: Inhabits neritic surface waters, most abundant off oceanic islands (Ref. 9839). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Short-rod anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 10524).

species.name: Short-snout hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in sheltered coastal bays and clear marine estuaries (Ref. 9002).  Also in schools in rocky, sandy vegetated areas (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Short-snout pugolovka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An almost mature female measuring about 4.0 cm length was caught on July 8, 1915.  It had 60 eggs on both ovaries, each egg was 2 mm in diameter (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Short-snout sand-dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud flats, mostly estuarine or near rivers (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Short-spined goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shoreline reefs and estuaries littered with dead coral blocks on sand, mud, or silt bottoms in 0-2 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Short-striped round herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic school-forming species found near coral reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Short-sword platyfish
species.description: Inhabits fast-flowing water with thick plant growth.

species.name: Short-tail bandfish
species.description: Inhabits depths around 200 m.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Short-tail bristle-tooth
species.description: Inhabits inner to outer reef with rich coral growth, usually on upper part of slopes in 7-15 meters depth (Ref. 48637). Solitary or in groups, grazing on algae (Ref. 90102).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Short-tail doublebar Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-tail Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish not able to undertake diadromous migrations. It is recorded from clear and gently flowing, unshaded, narrow and shallow (1.0 m average width and 0.3 m average depth) creek, consisting predominantly of pools connected by very short sections of shallow riffles. The substrate consisted of clay overlain with fine and coarse sand, with areas of silt, and riparian vegetation had been cleared and consisted of pasture and tussock grass. The instream cover was provided by rock, aquatic vegetation and overhanging grasses and maximum pool depth was 0.9 m (Ref. 98815). The general catchment of the creek at the type locality was disturbed, having been previously cleared for grazing. At the time of sampling (0900 hrs, 14 March 2002) the instream dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration was relatively low (4.2 mg/L) and majority of fish were captured in the shade under the bridge at the head of a pool where, presumably, water of higher DO concentration was flowing in over a short riffle section (Ref. 98815). Recorded at a relatively high density of 2.15 fish/m2, but this was probably elevated above normal levels encountered in an undisturbed stream due to fish congregating in shade and accessing higher quality water (see above). This fish was collected with a native species of freshwater crayfish (Euastacus sp.), the native Common freshwater shrimp and the translocated native Cherax destructor (Common Yabby) (Ref. 98815). Spawning period is unknown, although all mature fish examined in mid-March were in an early stage of gonad development, with gonads filling from 25-50% of the body cavity, and the smallest fish collected measuring 4.94 cm LCF, suggesting spawning during late winter/early spring. One individual was found with small white cysts, possibly trematode metacercariae, embedded in tissue on the inside of both gill covers (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Short-tail grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-tail stingray
species.description: Occurs offshore, on the outer shelf and uppermost slope; sometimes close inshore (Ref. 5578), in very shallow ( 0 m) depths (Ref. 26346). Found on sandy bottoms, in bays, harbors, and near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951). Often in aggregations (Ref. 12951). Feeds on fishes, bivalves, squid, and crustaceans (Ref. 12951). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Reputed to be the largest stingray in the world weighing more than 350,000 g (Ref. 6871). Frequently raises its tail in a scorpion-like fashion when approached, but is considered more as inquisitive rather than aggressive (Ref. 6871). The barbed tail however can inflict a severe or potentially fatal wound (Ref. 6871). Sometimes caught by anglers (Ref. 5578). It is parasitised by the monogenean Heterocotyle tokoloshei in the gills (Ref. 124053)

species.name: Short-tail thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed marine, pelagic and coastal, but at least the juveniles enter mangrove creeks of rivers, thus tolerating lowered salinities.  More data needed.

species.name: Short-tail tripodfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy flat of coastal areas.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Short-tail whipray
species.description: Smallest specimen, immature male at 20 cm WD is postnatal; birth size unknown, but probably ca. 15.0-17.0 cm WD (Ref. 110187).

species.name: Short-tailed hairtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-tailed river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Short-tassel weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 5755).

species.name: Short-tooth moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Short-tooth whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Short-tube scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Shortbarbel pangasius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large and medium-sized rivers, Omnivorous, feeding on animal and plant matter including detritus.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Shortbeard codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortbeard grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep-water species collected by bottom long-line at depths 1036-1163 m by hooks. Visual observations of both type specimens, which were keeping alive in container filled with marine water, demonstrate the maintaining of the mental barbel in a horizontal position parallel to the ground when fishes were immovable. In swimming fishes, the mental barbel was pushed back over or alongside the snout by flowing water. P. brevibarbata evidently belongs to the mostly predatory species, which also opportunistically feeds as necrophage. The stomach of the female, captured 20 January 2010, contained (besides the bait, giant Peruvian squid, Dosidicus gigas) the remains of a large crustacean, probably Antarctic shrimp, Notocrangon antarcticus. State of ovaries with traces of recent spawning corresponds to early SGM VI-III, GSI 1.3. The length, width and depth of the left ovary attain about 44, 18 and 6.5 mm correspondently. The liver fills in length about 1/3 of the abdominal cavity; hepatosomatic index reaches 1.6 (Ref. 92304).

species.name: Shortbelly catshark
species.description: Maximum size of females is unknown. Smallest paratype (33.7 cm TL) with short and soft claspers of 2.5% TL, ranked as immature (maturity stage 1); while holotype and other paratypes (43.2-47.7 cm TL) with long, fully developed claspers (5.8-8.1% TL), ranked as mature (maturity stage 3) (Ref. 97621).

species.name: Shortbelly eel
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters.  Prefers muddy bottoms, often off mouths of large rivers.

species.name: Shortbelly rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of habitats, sometimes in large schools well offshore and off bottom (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic (Ref. 36715).  Adults feed on planktonic animals, mainly krill (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  A very important prey species for predatory fishes and marine mammals (Ref. 2850).  Not marketed due to its small size (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Shortchin stargazer
species.description: Found on sandy bottoms (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Shortdorsal cutthroat eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Shortfin barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in headwater streams with vegetation (Ref. 52193). It feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 52193). Breeds in spring and summer (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Shortfin bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortfin eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy or muddy bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Shortfin false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in seaward and lagoon reefs to a depth of at least 43 m in areas of mixed coral and sand. Also found in reef crevices in about 6-45 m (Ref 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Shortfin flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small bottom dwellers that either pass under or through most commercial trawls.  Biology poorly known (Ref.  33839).

species.name: Shortfin gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Type specimen taken from 38-45 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Shortfin lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms of the continental shelf down to about 60 m.  Feeds on small bottom-dwelling invertebrates and fishes.

species.name: Shortfin minidartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in midwater aggregations of up to 50 individuals; inhabits sheltered waters of turbid lagoons in about 3-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Shortfin molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in warm springs and their effluents, canals and weedy ditches, and stream pools (Ref. 5723).  Food is mainly detritus (Ref. 36880).  Some populations in caves (Ref. 27297).

species.name: Shortfin neoscopelid
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Found over continental and island slopes (Ref. 4481).
Sexual mature at 12 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Shortfin pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in shallow seagrass beds.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shortfin pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortfin sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shortfin sand stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers shallow waters where the sediment size is tiny, especially intertidal areas that have white coral sand.  Never found in waters that are brackish or fresh.  Carnivores, which prey on a variety of benthic invertebrate animals (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Shortfin saury
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, on sand and mud bottoms.

species.name: Shortfin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Shortfin searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Shortfin silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortfin smooth lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along the upper continental slope and caught by bottom trawl at a depth greater than 300m. Sexual maturity in males likely achieved between 31.9 and 40.6 cm TL, and in females, larger than 45.6 cm TL. A cymothiod isopod Elthusa raynaudi was found attached to the roof of the mouth of the holotype (normally occurs in the gill chambers of fishes) (Ref. 86885).

species.name: Shortfin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Shortfin snakeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under rocky ledges and around weeds (Ref. 33839).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Shortfin spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hovers and swims along at slight head-down angle.  Often caught in large numbers and possibly gregarious.  Depth range from 700-2000 m and from 487-1034 m in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).  Feeds on sessile and motile invertebrates such as bryozoans, ophiuroids, amphipods and sponges.  Spawns in June-July in the Mediterranean.  Sexually dimorphic, males generally smaller and with enlarged nasal rosettes (Ref. 4449).

species.name: Shortfin tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, swamps and rivers, including turbid backwaters and clear, flowing tributaries (Ref. 2847).  Inhabits bottom of warm, clear, flowing streams; also lives in billabongs and flooded lagoons (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects, prawns, mollusks and small crayfish (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Reaches sexual maturity at about 12 centimeters (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Shortfinned worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow species (< 50 m) found in among seagrass beds and rocky tidepools (Ref. 104540).  Lives in groups of many individuals.  Feeds on small bottom-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Shortgut fintail snipe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Shorthead barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shorthead cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand and mud bottom (Ref. 81834).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shorthead eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic, relatively stenothermal species (Ref. 119197). Adults primarily feed on krill and amphipods (Ref. 119197).

species.name: Shorthead hagfish
species.description: TBK: demerspelag.

species.name: Shorthead hairfin anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A marine or estuarine species, but perhaps also ascending into freshwater.  More data needed.  Apparently a highly esteemed foodfish at the Rokan River mouth, Sumatra and presumably so in similar localities elsewhere in Indonesia, Malaysia and Sarawak.

species.name: Shorthead seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  Occur in small to large aggregations in weed patches attached to rocks on sand, mostly in Sargassum weeds (Ref. 9002).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: Shorthead snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shorthead sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal, inshore waters, benthic and on soft bottom areas (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Shortheaded tonguesole
species.description: Inhabits silty or muddy substrates in coastal waters to about 25 meters depth.  Usually deeply burried in the substrate during the day, but out and hunting at night (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Shorthorn fangtooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Shortjaw eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Shortjaw kokopu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in freshwater; young in marine and estuarine waters.

species.name: Shortjaw mudsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in high intertidal pools and tidal rivulets of rocky and sandy shores (Ref. 90849).

species.name: Shortjaw saury
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms.

species.name: Shortlight siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms small groups in Diadema sea urchins (Ref 90102).

species.name: Shortlip electric ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found offshore on inner continental shelf. Size usually smaller to 25 cm TL; birth size at ca. 8 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Shortmast sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore and to 73 m depth, on sand and rock bottoms and shallow exposed areas (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Shortnose batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat bottoms of sand, coral rubble, seagrass or mud (Ref. 13442).  Occurs from water's edge to at least 275 m depth.  Feeds on mollusks, crabs, fishes, polychaete worms and algae (Ref. 13442).  May be caught by hand (Ref. 13442).  Rarely used for food (Ref. 26938).  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Shortnose eagle ray
species.description: Male and female mature at approximately 50.0-60.0 mm DW (Ruocco, unpubl. data), and males are typically smaller than females (Ref. 91774).

species.name: Shortnose pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools, reef flats, and shallow sand flats among algae or seagrasses to a depth of 5 m or more.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Shortnose sucker
