species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit mainly tidal mudflats adjacent to turbid, brackish rivers.

species.name: Slender orange perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Slender pike cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rheophilic species which dwells on rocky bottom rapids with water flow up to 1.7 m/sec.  Perches solitary on top of boulders.  Forages on rock surfaces and picks mostly on benthic preys; also feeds on micro-crustaceans (cladocerans, ostracods, copepods), immature aquatic insects (chironomids, ephemeropterans, trichopterans) and minute clams (Ref. 46528).

species.name: Slender pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Slender piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender platanna-klipfish
species.description: Found in coarse gravel areas of the intertidal zone; may be found up to 20 m depth in warmer waters.

species.name: Slender rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large water courses and isolated rocky pools generally bordered with paperbark trees (Melaleuca) which have clear waters and minimal flow during the dry season (Ref. 2906, 44894). Large numbers congregate in shady pools around log snags and submerged branches (Ref. 44894). Feeds on insects and their larvae, small crustaceans and algae. Sympatric with M. splendida australis (Ref. 2906). Prefers the following aquarium conditions: pH=7, H=10, 24°C water temperature; is an egg layer and a peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Slender rasbora
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in a variety of habitats (Ref. 27732):  ditches, ponds, canals, haors, streams, rivers and inundated fields (Ref. 1479).  Inhabits mainly sandy streams and rivers (Ref. 6028).  Found in medium to large rivers and brooks of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  In the Mekong basin, this species is usually associated with large, slow flowing rivers, usually with turbid waters (Ref. 43281).  Sometimes forms large schools.  Feeds mainly on aquatic insects and detritus.  A surface feeder (Ref. 1479).  Spawning sites are found in rivers and ponds (Ref. 33813).  Mature adults probably breed during the rainy season.  Hardy and adaptable in the aquarium.

species.name: Slender redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools in clear, flowing Fold Mountain streams.  Feeds off the substrate on algae, detritus and bottom-living and other invertebrates.  Breeds in summer (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Slender reef-damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs.  A planktivorous species (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Slender ribbonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnally active; inhabits cracks and crevices during the day.  Feeds on small mobile benthic organisms (Ref. 26966), by drifting up to its prey and swallowing it whole with a sideways snap of the large extensible mouth (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Slender sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Slender sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms next to reefs in 6-18 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Slender sawtail catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare, little-known bottom-dwelling catshark found on the uppermost continental slopes (Ref. 11146).  Mode of reproduction unknown (Ref. 11146).

species.name: Slender scalyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on amphipods (mostly Themisto gaudichaudii), copepods, polychaetes, and mysids.

species.name: Slender scorpionfish
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 11015) and continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Slender sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over mud, sand and gravel on lake shores, and in riffles, runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Slender searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on the continental slope.  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Slender shortfaced eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender shovelnose catfish
species.description: Poisson. Collected from both white and black waters; found in floodplain lakes, small creeks (or caños) to large rivers and tidal rivers; on sand, mud, and clay substrates associated with vegetation (e.g. tall reeds, emergent grasses, and root masses of stream-side trees).  Apparently nocturnal and hide in groups along stream margins during the day (Ref. 40631).

species.name: Slender silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Although difficult to see, specimens are easily found by following distinct waving trail they leave behind (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Slender snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand bottoms.

species.name: Slender snipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of habitats, from near surface to near bottom and sometimes in huge schools (Ref. 2850). May range into coastal waters (Ref. 36711). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36711). Seems to be sympatric with Macroramphosus scolopax (Linnaeus, 1758) all around the world (Ref. 89357).

species.name: Slender sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the vicinity of rocky areas (Ref. 4925).  Good food fish but is of little commercial importance due to its small size (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Slender sorcerer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender spongegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 42915). Commensal on foliaceous flattened sponges (Phyllospongia) (Ref. 27362, 48637).

species.name: Slender stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender stone loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in torrential streams.

species.name: Slender stonebasher
species.description: Found in rocky habitats in flowing waters (Ref. 7248, 52193). Feeds on small aquatic invertebrates (Ref. 7248, 52193) such as insect larvae (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Slender tail hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Preys on juvenile cichlids on sandy substrate.  Juveniles are very common in near-shore shallow waters, adults found in deeper waters (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Slender tardoor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along shores and in estuaries. Probably similar to O. tardoore, but more specimens and data needed.

species.name: Slender thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An estuarine species, but presumably also found inshore.  More data needed.

species.name: Slender tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow-water tonguefish occurring at depths of ca. 15 m (Ref. 126065).

species.name: Slender triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Slender unicorn
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal to outer reef slopes, usually swimming along upper edges of drop-offs in small schools (Ref. 48637). Descends from the water column to the reef front to be cleaned by Labroides dimidiatus (Ref. 4974). Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 3145). Forms aggregations, feeding on zooplankton well above the bottom over or in the immediate vicinity of reefs. Males exhibit rapid and striking changes in color pattern during courtship (Ref. 10671).

species.name: Slender unicorn rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Slender walking catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in peats, lakes and lowland forest streams (Ref. 57235).  Found in well shaded forest streams and swamps with acidic waters.  A carnivorous species which feeds at night (Ref.  85309).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Slender weasel shark
species.description: Viviparous (Ref. 50449). Lives in shallow water to 18m depth on the continental shelf (Ref. 93009).

species.name: Slender weed whiting
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found at some distance from the shore, over sandy areas associated with seagrass and low rocky outcrops.  Form small groups at depths of about 15-20 m.

species.name: Slender weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and shallow coastal water with vegetation (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Slender white sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably a marine and coastal pelagic species.

species.name: Slender work eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slender wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found around coral and rock patches in shallow protected sandy areas (Ref. 9710).  Amphipods, small crustaceans, and polychaetes have been reported from the stomachs of Japanese specimens.

species.name: Slender-spined porcupine fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found commonly in shallow bays.  Nocturnal.  Occurs in small aggregations.

species.name: Slenderhead darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel runs and riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on mayfly nymphs (baetids, heptageniids), midge larvae, and hydropsychid caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Slenderline cardinalfish
species.description: Found hovering around a large coral formation (Ref. 44115). Usually in aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Slendertail cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs or rocky slopes.

species.name: Slendertail lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic; at surface at night (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Slendertail moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits corals and rocks of lagoon and seaward reefs.  Mottled moray.  Benthic (Ref. 58302, 75154).  Possibly a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32169).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slickhead brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms.  A 63 mm SL female specimen (USNM 375546) contained 160 embryos, 4-5 mm TL, with three short rows of small pigment spots posteriorly on the body.  No eggs.  A 55 mm SL female (SIO 65-185) contained about 600 eggs, 0.5 mm in diameter (Ref. 57883).

species.name: Slim betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs in peat swamps.  Also found in swamp forest habitats (Ref. 56613).  A bubble nest builder (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Slim flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slim lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Slim minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-bottomed and gravel-bottomed pools and runs of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Slim sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Taken in shrimp trawls (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Slim snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slime flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Slimtail lampfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).
Shallow depth of 100 m taken from Ref. 51600.

species.name: Slimtail skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Slimy cuskeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the interstices of lagoon or seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Body covered with heavy coating of mucus (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Slimy goby
species.description: Inhabits sand-rubble bottoms in 3-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Slimy head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Johnny Labbe, pers. comm., 2000).

species.name: Slimy snailfish
species.description: Espèce d'orchidées. Occurs from intertidal areas to 15 m depth, but usually not in tide pools (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Slinky klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Slippery dick
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in rocky and reef areas in shallow waters.  Less common in seagrass beds.  Feeds on other fishes (Ref. 5521) and gastropods (Ref. 9626).  Forms leks during breeding (Ref. 55367).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).

species.name: Slipskin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore and to 388 m depth (Ref.2850).  Feeds on shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Slit branchial paraliparis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic and epibenthic invertebrates, mainly mysids, gammarid amphipods, and sipunculids.

species.name: Slobbering catfish
species.description: Appears to migrate during high water or flood season.  Nothing is known of its feeding habits (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Slope bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms.

species.name: Slope hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Slope soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear tropical , mean maximum depth of collected specimens was 17 m, only 6  specimens were collected at depths less than 5 m.  This species lives among coral or rocks on steep slopes, vertical walls, or in other areas with large vertical relief, however, a few specimens have been taken among coral heads in shallow flat areas (Ref. 89885).

species.name: Slopewater lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pseudoceanic, found over continental shelves and slopes (Ref. 4066).  Occurs between 325-475 m during the day; between 40-250 m at night  (maximum abundance in 100 m depth).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951).  In the Cariaco Trench, day distribution is at 250 m and at night at 50 m due to anoxic conditions below 400 m and free hydrogen sulphide below 375 m.  Fecundity is about 1,000 eggs per female (Ref. 9504).

species.name: Slough darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in standing or slow-flowing water over mud, often in vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Slow goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic (Ref. 92840). Found in rocky crevices, from tide pools to at least 14 m depth (Ref. 11482).  Larvae usually found around sargassum (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Sluiter's pearlfish
species.description: Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Ascidian commensal (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Small banded rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Small Bengal silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally collected in shallow coastal waters within less than 10 m or from estuaries basins strongly influenced by freshwater (Ref. 39283).

species.name: Small Chinese silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow, coastal sandy and muddy areas associated with freshwater basins (Ref. 30392).

species.name: Small eye golden-line fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species.

species.name: Small goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small green utaka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy habitat at a depth of about 10 m.  Feeds from the silty layer on the sand, on small soft invertebrates (Ref. 5595) and on planktonic and benthic algae (Ref. 267).

species.name: Small headed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on benthic animals.

species.name: Small kob
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small lunate caudal fin croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives near mangroves and reefs on sandy or silty mud bottoms at 1-42 m deep (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 27315.

species.name: Small scale croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Small scale lunate caudal fin croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small scale mud carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large rivers and lowland floodplains (Ref. 12693).  Occurs in riffle and deep slow reaches (Ref. 37769).  Moves out into the flooded forest where it feeds on leafy plant matter, phytoplankton and insects (Ref. 12693).  Migration pattern is markedly different above and below the Khone Falls in the Mekong basin.  Below the falls, it makes an upstream migration from Phnom Penh to the Khone Falls between November and February, consisting mainly of sub-adults of sizes 10 to 50 cm.  From April to July, it migrates in the opposite direction, from Khone Falls and downstream, constituting mainly of sub-adults up to about 50 cm (Ref. 37770).  Above the Khone Falls, from Klong Kaem District, Ubolratchatani in Thailand, fish migrates upstream in February; at Khemmaratch further upstream in Ubolratchatani, it moves upstream in March-April; and at Mukdahan, it goes upstream in May.  However, it migrates downstream at Klong Kaem in June-July (Ref. 37770).  Only downstream migrations are reported in the Mekong Delta in Viet Nam, constituting mainly of juveniles (2-20 cm), with the smallest fish mainly in June-July and fish between 10 and 20 mainly from September to November (Ref. 37770).  From Xayabouri in Laos to Chiang Saen in Thailand, upstream migrations take place from March to August.  This appears to be two distinct migrations:  one of sub-adults measuring 15-50 cm during March-April and another one of larger fishes of sizes 40 to 90 cm during June-July (Ref. 37770).  Not known to persist in impoundments.  Individuals caught with dais or traps are often immediately kept alive in fish cages for future sale.  Marketed fresh and sometimes dried and salted (Ref. 12693).  Known to reach up to 15 kg in Thailand (Jean-Francois, pers. comm. 11/02).

species.name: Small scaled brown slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small scaled nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools.  8 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 3 months incubation.  Very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Small snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally restricted to relatively narrow regions, characterized by humid rainforest climate (Ref. 43157).  Feed on crustaceans, insect larvae and fish.

species.name: Small-eyed abyssal eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from the abyssal zone off southern Japan (Ref. 96071).

species.name: Small-eyed coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The minute eyes are indicative that it could be a cave species, but so far collected only on coral reefs.  A 31 mm SL female was found with a 3.7 mm long bilobed ovary containing 50 eggs, with 0.4 mm diameter (Ref. 55786).

species.name: Small-eyed flathead
species.description: Found in shallow coastal areas and reef flats to about 50 m.  Usually captured by spear fishing or with ichthyocide, occasional specimen taken by trawling (Ref. 9790).

species.name: Small-eyed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among coral rubble.

species.name: Small-eyed loter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish mangrove estuaries, tidal creeks and lowermost reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Small-eyed sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length 13,2 TL (Ref. 42042). Eggs very large, up to 4.25 mm.  About 20 eggs in each ovary.

species.name: Small-eyed whipfin mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small-fin worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small-headed cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) recorded from the continental slope (Ref. 9563, 75154).

species.name: Small-jaw croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries and rivers (Ref. 9772).  Mainly found in brackish or marine conditions, but sometimes penetrates fresh water (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Small-mouth char
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Small-mouth croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Small-mouth righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a depth of 304 m.  Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Small-scale tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More accurate information about geographic distribution, bathymetric distribution and substrata where this species is found needed to better understand the ecology, distribution and life history of this species (Ref. 126065).

species.name: Small-spine tadpole-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fresh and brackish waters with salinity up to 13 ppt.  Maximum depth 50 m, with mature adults at 1-11 m.  Lives for about a year, spawns in May-August in northern Caspian, April-November in eastern Caspian.  Some individuals may spawn for the first time at 6-7 months.  Females probably lay eggs in 3 portions and die after spawning while males probably die 3-4 weeks alter (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Small-toothed perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This rare and deep-water species occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 123218).

species.name: Small-toothed whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found close to the bottom over coral reef areas.  Feeds on small fishes and larger zooplankton, as well as on benthic organisms (Ref. 9785).  Occurs solitary or in small groups.

species.name: Smallcheek snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smalldisc clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores and coral reefs and sometimes associated with Stomopneustes variolaris (Ref. 559) and also Heterocentrus trigonarius.

species.name: Smalldisk snailfish
species.description: Rare deepwater species (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Smalldisk torpedo
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smalldorsal cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smalleye conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smalleye cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species found on shallow reefs (Ref. 34024).  Most common in inshore and back reef environments, associated with crevices of silty coralline rock.  Female specimens with unusually low numbers of large embryos, 1-3, usually 2). One female (3.2 cm SL) contained one embryo (1.4 cm SL in length)  This is among the lowest degree of fecundity observed in tribe Dinematichthyini. (Ref. 76869).

species.name: Smalleye dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a midwater trawl (Ref. 42989).  Maximum length based on a juvenile specimen (Ref. 42989).

species.name: Smalleye lantern shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Smalleye pygmy shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly the smallest living shark (Ref. 6871).  Found near continental and island land masses (Ref. 31367).  Feeds mainly on cephalopods and small midwater bony fishes (Ref. 6871).  Probably makes diurnal vertical migrations from within 200 m of the surface at night down to about 2,000 m during the day (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Smalleye shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy, turbid channels of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on insects, primarily dipterans, terrestrial insects, detritus, and plant material (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Smalleye smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms (Ref. 27363).  Maximum length based on a single specimen (Ref. 27363).

species.name: Smalleye spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Smalleye stingray
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters and river mouths (Ref. 45255).  Found on the continental shelf.  Maximum disc width of about 180 cm.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Litters of a single pup; born at ca. 33 cm WD (Ref. 114953).  Caught very rarely by the demersal tangle net fisheries operating in shelf waters. Utilized for its meat, cartilage and probably also its skin (Ref.58048).

species.name: Smalleye sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a tide pool (large tidal channel) (Ref. 106074).

species.name: Smalleye whip ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Better reference needed.

species.name: Smalleyed guitarfish
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smalleyed round stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallfin lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, epipelagic to mesopelagic, found in 375-750 m during the day and near the surface to 125 m at night (Ref. 4066, 58302).  Adults feed on zooplankton (Ref. 9835).  Caudal glands develop in both sexes from about 1.9 cm (Ref. 4775).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Smallfin redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty to rocky pools and slow runs of small to medium rivers.  Also found in impoundments.

species.name: Smallfin whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smallfinger topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pools and along banks, occasionally in swift water, in highland streams.  A midwater and bottom swimmer, occasionally at or near the surface.  Sensitive to high chlorine content and warm, turbid, poorly oxygenated, stagnant water.  Feeds on diatoms, algae, detritus and insect larvae.

species.name: Smallhead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs over soft bottoms of inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Smallhead dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms with some rock.

species.name: Smallhead eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallhead flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A neritic species.

species.name: Smallhead grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear, fast-flowing streams, frequently in rapids or pools below them (Ref. 5259, 44894).  Benthic feeder:  various shrimps, earthworm, algae.  Maturity:  F, 17 cm SL; M, 23 cm SL.  Spawning:  mid October to early November after rainy periods; temp.  Of 24°C.  Fecundity:  115,000 eggs per female.  Eggs:  pelagic, 4.2-4.3 mm diameter.  Hatching:  36 hours (Ref. 2906, 44894). Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).   Aquarium conditions:  pH=7, H=8, 25°C, rock and plant cover (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Smallhead snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathypelagic (Ref. 58302) and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4465, 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Smallhead sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries and harbors, usually buried in muddy substrate (Ref. 9002).  Move with undulating body when disturbed, reminiscent of distasteful flatworm, thus possibly deterring predators (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Smallknob flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smallmouth electric catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallmouth flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallmouth hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal bays, estuaries and lakes ranging from pure fresh to salinities in excess of seawater (Ref. 9002).  Occurs abundantly in in estuaries around eel-grass thickets, occasionally penetrating the lower freshwater reaches of rivers.  Feeds on tiny crustaceans and insects.  Breeds in spring (September to October).  An annual species (living for only one year), dying shortly after spawning (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Smallmouth redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Smallmouth ronquil
species.description: Inhabits tide pools and shallow inshore areas (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Smallmouth scad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154). Feeds primarily on small invertebrates, primarily microscopic crustaceans and molluscs. Caught mainly on hook-and-line (Ref. 9894).

species.name: Smallmouth silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallmouth squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits virtually all coral reef zones (Ref. 1602). Benthopelagic in or near crevices and holes (Ref. 58302). Common in thickets of staghorn Acropora or in large Pocillopora heads (Ref. 1602). Feeds on small crustaceans, worms, and fishes during the night (Ref. 30874). Spine of preopercle venomous. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Smallmouth yellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in impoundments and rivers.  Prefers clear-flowing waters over sandy or rocky substrates.  An omnivorous bottom feeder.  Diet includes water fleas, snails, plankton, small mussels, insects, small fish, algae and detritus.  Breeds in spring through to midsummer after the first substantial rains of the season.  Migrates upstream to spawn over suitable gravel beds (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Smallmouthed salmon catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing, often turbid rivers and coastal waters.  Also occurs in slow-moving freshwater streams, favours turbid coastal shallows and brackish estuaries (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on gastropod and bivalve mollusks.  The food are swallowed whole (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Smallnose fanskate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 8.1 cm long and 4.6 cm wide (Ref. 41249).  A common by-catch in the coastal and continental shelf bottom-trawl fisheries of the Argentine-Uruguayan Common Fishing Zone; also fished extensively by bottom longline (Ref. 54460).

species.name: Smallpore whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smallscale archerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large rivers (Ref. 27732).  Found along the shores of flowing and standing waters with overhanging vegetation.  This is the more common species of the genus found well upstream from the estuary.  Feeds on terrestrial insects, zooplankton, crustaceans and aquatic insect larvae.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Smallscale bonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallscale bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on offshore reefs, in large schools.  Juveniles found on coastal reefs and near entrance of coastal estuaries with rocky reefs.

species.name: Smallscale cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Remains hidden by day (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Smallscale codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic, probably undergo vertical migration.  Migrates into and out of anoxic water on a diurnal basis.

species.name: Smallscale darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, shallow gravel riffles of small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Smallscale grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallscale hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, inshore waters (Ref. 7300).  Often found in estuaries and recorded in coastal bays (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Smallscale kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smallscale lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smallscale redfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in standing or slow-flowing pools with a soft or rocky bottom.  Thrives in dams and tolerates turbid waters.  Juveniles occur in large shoals, adults in small groups.  Feeds off the substrate on algae and detritus.  Breeds in summer, moving into riffle areas to lay eggs (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Smallscale searsid
species.description: Bathypelagic to benthopelagic (Ref. 4461).

species.name: Smallscale smoothhead
species.description: Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smallscale tonguesole
species.description: A strictly freshwater species found in large rivers.  Found along the bottom where it feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Marketed fresh (Ref.12693).

species.name: Smallscale wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) on coastal slopes with sparse reef formation, inhabiting the open areas (Ref. 48636); also on silty sand or mud bottoms.  Feeds on benthic crustaceans (other stomach contents were polychaete remains and fish scales) (Ref. 12420).

species.name: Smallscale yellowfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 1441)

species.name: Smallscale yellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cool-water species not found below 600m altitude; occurs in deep pools and flowing waters of permanent rivers and in dams (Ref. 52193). It feeds primarily on algae in winter months and aquatic insects in summer months, but also takes mussels, snails, crabs and small fish (Ref. 52193). Breeds during spring and summer, males maturing at a smaller size (170 mm FL) than females (300 mm FL); females grow larger than males (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Smallspine turretfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on flat bottoms in coastal waters.  Juveniles may be pelagic (Ref. 561).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Smallspot moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs in 5-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Smallsucker clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along shallow coastal shores, where it probably clings to rocks of the substratum.

species.name: Smalltail sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 120 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Smalltail wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Engybenthiic, found over coral and rubble, usually at depths greater than 21 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Smallthorn sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.7 cm long and 3.4 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Smalltooth dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 27000) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Smalltooth flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and offshore over sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on various benthic animals (Ref. 9774).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9774) and is considered  an excellent food fish.

species.name: Smalltooth grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens from northwestern Africa feed primarily on faunal organisms, especially polychaetes (90% of contents) and a variety of small crustaceans. Smaller individuals (30-40 mm head length) feed mostly on epibenthic organisms, especially the copepod Aetidopsis carinata (Ref. 6219).

species.name: Smalltooth stingray
species.description: A coastal species (Ref. 4438), that would be capable of migrating into freshwaters (Ref. 81259). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smiler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble flats near reefs (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Smilosicyopus fehlmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smilosicyopus leprurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast-flowing streams.

species.name: Smilosicyopus mystax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smith's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over silty bottom (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Smith's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit live coral patches often in silty areas of lagoons and inshore reefs.  They occur in small to large groups.  Feed in midwater above live coral heads (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Smith's priapium fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A euryhaline species (Ref. 12041).  Found in freshwater habitats in inland floodplains.  Occur in marshes and swamps with plenty of aquatic submerged and floating vegetation.  Feed on minute crustaceans and protozoans.  Fertilization is internal and eggs are attached to the substrate via adhesive filaments (Ref. 43413).  Caught only with the most finely meshed nets.

species.name: Smith's shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-mud bottoms of sheltered bays in 10-23 m (except specimen reported from about 100 m depth) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Smokey chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 9710). Prefer habitat consisting of boulder substrates or mixed rock, rubble, and sand, at depths between about 3 and 30 m (Ref. 125611). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding; eggs demersal and adhere to the substrate, and males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Smoky damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock, rubble or coral reefs usually inshore.  Visits reefs submerged by high tides.  They occur in small loose groups or solitary (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Smoky madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, cool, rocky riffles, runs, and flowing pools of creeks (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Smoky seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Smooth alligatorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found among rocks (Ref. 2850).  Usually caught by shrimp trawlers (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Smooth anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur inshore (Ref. 7300).  Oviparous.  Eggs are attached to each other by a single, flattened, acellular filament and are brooded in a hollow behind the left pectoral fin (Ref. 6773).

species.name: Smooth blaasop
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the shelf edge (Ref. 11230). Closely resembles the Atlantic species L. laevigatus Linnaeus which reaches southern Angola (Ref. 4919).

species.name: Smooth cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Smooth croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 9772).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Smooth deep-sea skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit the continental slope (Ref. 26346).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 3.7 cm long and 2.2 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Smooth dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- (Ref. 10524) and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Males dwarfed, non-parasitic (Ref. 10524). Specimen examined was 9.7 cm SL from Auckland Institute and Museum (AIM 6609) (Ref. 58502).

species.name: Smooth freshwater stingray
species.description: Dasyatis garouaensis is restricted to fresh waters (Ref. 81625). Its conservation status is uncertain, given its restricted distribution in a region with known habitat degradation; this species has apparently become less common after the construction of a dam on the Benue River (Ref. 81625). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smooth gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Type specimen taken from 55 m depth (Ref. 33021).  Better reference needed.

species.name: Smooth handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Smooth lumpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males are said to guard the eggs (Ref. 6885).  Migrate to spawn in littoral waters of Bering Sea in December-June (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Smooth pipefish
species.description: Found among kelp and Zostera sp. In rock pools and shallow coastal waters; sometimes among floating Sargassum. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may be brooding at 7 cm SL.

species.name: Smooth razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons osseux. Found on coastal waters.  Occurs solitary or in small groups in seagrass habitats, inshore or in estuaries (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Largest shrimpfish (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Smooth seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smooth toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal bays on sandy flats, often in very large schools, entering fresh water in estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Smooth tooth blacktip shark
species.description: Known only from the holotype (immature male).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smooth-cheek eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns on the bottom.  A male will spawn with more than one female if there is more than one ripe female around.  If not, he is satisfied to spawn with one partner and to stay with one female forever (Ref. 12251).  Maximum length 25 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Smooth-cheek scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from near shore to 110 m depth (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Smooth-eye blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs.

species.name: Smooth-fin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found among corals (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Smooth-head scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the shore (small individuals) to 90 m depth.  Inhabits muddy bottoms (Ref. 26340).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Smooth-headed catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smooth-nose deepwater cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Smooth-scale goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smooth-skin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in rotenone collections.

species.name: Smooth-snout clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal reefs, usually in ledges with sea urchins (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Smooth-snout flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smoothback guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on benthic inshore areas on continental shelf to at least 76 m depth (Ref. 123963). Also known to inhabit river mouths.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Confused with other species in the Indian Ocean, biology unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Smoothbelly goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit fresh water (Ref. 9304).

species.name: Smoothbelly pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species apparently found in the main stream of the Congo River (Ref. 188). It feeds on small shrimps, mosquito larvae and chironomid larvae (Ref. 188).

species.name: Smoothcheek sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Smoothgum sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from 21-27 m depth.

species.name: Smoothhead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in marginal water-lily and papyrus swamps as well as in marginal weed beds; abundant in high mountain streams and torrents and on the bottom among stones; not found in any situation lower than about 915 m above sea level nor in water of a higher temperature than 18 °C (Ref. 248). In the Rukwa and Malawi drainage they are sometimes found in very cold upland streams (Ref. 78218). These fishes are omnivores, feeding on insect larvae and sometimes also fishes (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Smoothhead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the intertidal (common) and to 13 m depth (Ref. 2850).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Smoothlip clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology not known (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Smoothlip stargazer
species.description: Inhabits sand, rock, and marl bottoms.

species.name: Smoothnose legskate
species.description: A rare species known only from 2 specimens both of which are missing (Ref. 2708).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smoothnose wedgefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species mainly found near the coast in shallow bays and off river mouths.  It is poorly known but probably feeds on bottom-dwelling crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 114953).   Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Smoothscale sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Snaggle-toothed snake-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Assumed to live in permanent or semi-permanent burrows with only snout and eyes exposed, darting to feed on other fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 43686).

species.name: Snail bullhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles, runs and flowing pools of swift streams.  Rarely found in backwaters.

species.name: Snail darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in gravel and sand runs of medium-sized rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in creeks (Ref. 10294). Feeds on small pleurocerid river snails, mostly Leptoxis and Lithasia, as well as some physid snails and limpets; also consumes caddisfly larvae (Glossosoma, Hydropsyche, Brachycentrus), midge and blackfly larvae, and a few mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Snail-fin poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on muddy sand bottoms in 150 m or less.  Adults feed on crustaceans and marine worms (Ref. 28197).

species.name: Snaileater
species.description: Feeds primarily upon snails, but also takes other invertebrates and small fish; ovophilic, agamous, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307). Used for snail and bilharzia control (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snake catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in vegetated areas in shallow and swampy places around the lake.  Occasionally found in cataracts, hiding under rocks (Ref. 248).  The species is omnivorous (Ref. 78218) and feeds on insects (Coleoptera, ants, Chironomid larvae) (Ref. 248 & 5595), plant seeds and other fishes (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand with associated rock and coral reef bottoms and collected with ichthyocides and dredges at depths between 12-100 m  (Ref. 75631).  Largest specimen examined, female at 57 cm TL (Ref. 101270).

species.name: Snake prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow bays and offshore waters (Ref. 2850); on sand mixed with silt, pebbles, and stones to depths of 425; usually shallower than 200 meters (Ref. 51666).  Sometimes takes hooks using marine worms as bait (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Snake River sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snakehead eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Snakehead goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found beneath stones in muddy areas of tide pools.

species.name: Snakehead toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal species (Ref. 4107).

species.name: Snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in intertidal pools and marginal subtidal areas (Ref. 4395).

species.name: Snakeskin sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snakeskin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Snaky klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in pools and subtidal areas.

species.name: Sneaky wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered inner reefs amongst broken coral and rubble. Usually seen in less than 10 m depth, staying well hidden in reefs, but sometimes swimming amongst the long-spined Diadema urchins or in thick algae coverage (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Snooty wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral-rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs at depths of 1 to over 40 m (Ref. 1602, 48636, 58534).  A secretive  species (Ref. 8631, 48636), rarely ventures more than a few centimeters from shelter (Ref. 1602).  A shy species, usually found in pairs when adult (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Snoutscale whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Snoutspot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually paired (Ref. 90102). Inhabits silty sand of shallow protected inner reefs and intertidal flats near mangroves (Ref. 37816).  Also occurs on muddy substrates to about 10 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Snow bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Synchronously hermaphroditic.

species.name: Snow's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit reef flats, benches, and rocky shorelines exposed to strong wave action (Ref. 37816).  They occur solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Snowflake-patched moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mountain streams and rivers (Ref. 41236), preferring to live among rocks (Ref. 4832).  Are herbivores feeding mainly on algae, aquatic plants and detritus (Ref. 6351).  Mature individuals breed during April and May (Ref. 4832).  The flesh of this species is much relished (Ref. 4832).

species.name: Snub-snouted flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snubhose garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Snubnose blacksmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Snubnose darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits current-swept rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae, with mayfly nymphs, caddis larvae, and microcrustacea (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Snubnose emperor
species.description: Found in sandy areas near reefs during daytime, sometimes in small groups.  At night, they are solitary and range over reef-flats and slopes where they feed primarily on echinoderms, mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 2295).  The taxonomy of this species has been considerably confused.

species.name: Snubnose pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in bay and reef localities among eelgrass and algae.  Also pelagic (Ref. 2850).  Males may be mature at 5.9 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Snubnose sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from intertidal rocky areas to about 30 m depth.

species.name: Snubnose snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collection assumed to be over soft substrates, the tow was usually no farther than 300-400 m from known coral habitat. Captured during the trawl included species typical of slope habitat (14 species dominated by Laemonema barbatulum and Helicolenus dactylopterus) and invertebrates (Ref. 75745).

species.name: Snubnose whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27121.

species.name: Snyder's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302) found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Snyderidia canina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An uncommon, free-living species (Ref. 34024) and benthic or pelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Snyderina yamanokami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soconusco gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow flowing water.

species.name: Socorran soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Socorro blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter (Ref. 56053).  Eggs are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56053).

species.name: Socorro clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Socorro serrano
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand-rubble areas (sandy bottom with scattered rocks and corals) used for shelter (Ref. 81032).

species.name: Socotra blue-spotted guitarfish
species.description: Occurs in coastal waters. Size range from 20.8 - 62.2 cm TL, males at size 37.8 cm TL is considered very early subadult (apparently start to mature around this size) and juvenile at  20.8 cm TL; while females at 59.4 and 60.2 cm TL are presumed to be adult  (Ref. 124452).

species.name: Socotra Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is collected mainly from coral dominated communities including those by Millepora, Acropora and Porites; also in a mixed soft and hard coral community on large rock boulders. Other visiual records were done in areas dominated by Galaxea, and encrusting and massive Agariciidae, Pectiniidae and Musside, and at the few fringing reef sites. The species was also sighted on relict reef or spur and groove with mixed macroalgae and hard coral communities, and on mixed macroalgae and/or sparse hard coral communities on rock platform (Ref. 88695).

species.name: Socotra hole-hiding goby
species.description: Collected on rubble-sand patches in sandy areas and in areas with mixed corals and stones or rocks. The holotype and paratypes were found living inside small holes in moderately large pieces of coral rock covered with short algae (Ref. 125392).

species.name: Socotra sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Socotran snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sodwana dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sodwana pygmy seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species remains undetected because of its cryptic behaviour and diminutive size. It is observed in flat sandstone-based coral reefs comprising of low pinnacles, shallow drop offs, and sandy gullies, with the latter being exposed to strong currents. It was found loosely associating with short algal turf, used as a holdfast, which was growing on sand-covered coral bedrock separated by sandy gullies (around 2 meters wide). Ambient seawater temperature averaged ca. 24 °C during the dives, which were conducted in October of 2018. Collectors experienced strong swells on the exposed reefs of 2 Mile Reef during data collection. The holotype and paratype appeared to be a mated pair, found within approximately 60 cm distance of each other on the two dives. Behaviour of the pair was observed prior to collection which was very similar to congeners H. pontohi and H. japapigu. Several individuals, including a small juvenile (ca. 1.0 cm SL), were found in the gullies and observed to be associated with low-growth algal turf. The juvenile, retained the dark colouration of a recently settled juvenile pygmy seahorse (Ref. 122372).

species.name: Soela cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Soela gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soela hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soela whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Soela wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Soft electric ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters (Ref. 26165). Known from few specimens. Size presumably exceeds 30 cm TL. Males reaches maturity at ca. 20 cm TL. Biology and reproduction unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Soft lanternfish
species.description: Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oceanic (Ref. 4066), found between 300-600 m during the day and between 50-300 m at night, exhibiting size stratification with depth (Ref. 4479).  Reach sexual maturity at a length of 3 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Soft leafvent angler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 7300).  A small deep-sea angler fish.  Males dwarfed, becoming parasitic on females (Ref. 10762).  An 8 cm female was found with 3 parasitic males of 18 mm length, attached to her ventral side.  Adult (=parasitic) males are colorless with reduced teeth, jaws, and eyes.  Information on the maximum length of female was taken from Ref. 10762.

species.name: Soft sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes. Occurs in rocky areas, among sponges; also found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Soft-coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on Dendronephthya soft corals, usually at depth of 20 meters or more in areas subject to strong currents. Large corals may play host to several individuals (Ref. 48637). Also found with Sarcophyton soft corals and sea pens in 5-82 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Soft-spined catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools in main river channels and larger creeks. Omnivorous (Ref. 44894). Stomach contents of fish less than 10 cm SL were mainly insects and their larvae, primarily chironomid larvae, ephemeropterans, and trichopterans; small amounts of odonates, unidentified dipterans, ostracods, and filamentous algae. Fish larger than 10 cm mainly ingested trichopterans, ostracods, and chironomids with some amounts of dipterans, odonates, aquatic coleopterans, corixids, Macrobrachium, bivalves, filamentous algae, and detritus (Ref. 27663). Collection of specimens with ripe and recently spent gonads in November suggests that breeding occurs at the commencement of the wet season (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Softcoral pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught by surface dip-nets from coral rubbles and coral heads from 0 to 21.9 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Softcoral seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs at moderate depths. Some corals with which this species associates with also occur in very shallow shaded areas such as below jetties. It may eventually be found inshore (Ref. 80667).

species.name: Softskin smooth-head
species.description: Captured between 1,400-2,100 m in the Atlantic Ocean; 1,120-1,650 m in the Indian Ocean; 585-1,416 off Australia; 1,020-1,540 in Western Pacific; 911-1,187 Eastern Pacific and Bering Sea;  and 800-1,400 m in the Pacific Ocean (Ref. 5003, 57826).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Maximum depth reported from Ref. 4460.  Upper distribution of this species may follow the 4°C isotherm (Ref. 57826).

species.name: Softy hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sohal surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species found in seaward edges of reefs exposed to surge (Ref. 9710). Aggressive and territorial (Ref. 9710). Feeds on various kinds of algae, mainly Sargassum, and fine filamentous green algae. Caught with nets (Ref. 30573); traps and occasionally by trawls (Ref. 68964).

species.name: Soldat anglais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along seaward reefs near or along steep drop-offs with caves (Ref. 9710).  In some areas it may approach the surface (Ref. 9710).  Usually feeds in large groups away from the reefs at night.  Well hidden in caves during the day and rarely seen; often observed at 10-30 m at night (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Soldat à œillères
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in reef flats and shallow lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 12419).  Benthopelagic in or near crevices and caves (Ref. 58302).  Mainly nocturnal.  Feed mainly on plankton such as crab larvae (Ref. 12419).  Secretive, hovering under ledges and in caves (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 240).

species.name: Soldatov's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Threatened due to over harvesting, habitat loss and pollution (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Soldatov's gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soldatov's thicklip gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soldatovia polyactocephala
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soldatov’s lumpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soldier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in inshore waters (Ref. 9563).  Most active at night, lying motionless during the day.  Spawn during August-September and seem to be triggered by an increase in water temperature at the onset of spring.  Smaller individuals feed mainly on shrimps and crabs, while bigger ones are piscivorous (Ref. 2156).  Adults possess venomous infraorbital, preopercular and dorsal-fin spines (Ref. 33616).

species.name: Sole
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 2683, 81682), including estuaries and fresh water lagoons (Ref. 81291). Feeds on (lamelibranch) mollusks, shrimps, crabs and fish (Ref. 28587, 81682). Sold as frozen filet under the name 'filets de sole' (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Sole (Solea senegalensis)
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Flatfish with oval and asymmetric body (eyes on the right side). Interradial membrane on the pectoral fin on the eye
side is of black colour(A). This feature distinguishes it from common sole (Solea soled), which has a big black compact spot on the posterior side of this fin. In the Atlantic, from the Gulf of Biscay to the coasts of Senegal. Less frequent in the Western Meditarranean.
A predominantly littoral species. Benthonic marine species living in sandy or muddy bottoms, off coastal areas up to
100 m depth and in brackish lakes.Feeds basically on benthonic invertebrate, such as larvae from  polychaets and
bivalve molluscs. Also on small crustaceans.Sexual maturity is reached when size is 30 cm. Spawning happens beween the months of March until June.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Sole (Solea solea)
species.description: Espèce de poisson plat. Adults occur at a temperature range of 8.0-24.0°C (Ref. 4944).  Usually solitary.  They burrow into sandy and muddy bottoms.  Retreat to deeper water during winter (Ref. 9988).  Juveniles are found during the first 2 to 3 years in coastal nurseries (bays and nurseries) before migrating to deeper waters (Ref. 92286).  Adults feed on worms, mollusks and small crustaceans at night.  Waden sea is the most important nursery area.  Batch spawner (Ref. 51846).  Recruitment is very variable.  Frequently found pelagically during spawning migrations (Ref. 35388).  Marketed fresh and frozen; utilized steamed, fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Sole (Synapturichthys kleinii)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms; mainly in shallow water (Ref. 3200).

species.name: Sole achire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur mainly in brackish or hyper-saline lagoons (Ref. 5217), on sandy-muddy bottoms of estuaries and in the littoral zone where it hides itself leaving just its eyes out.  Can easily disguise itself in the environment.  Feed on worms, crustaceans and small fishes. Juveniles have a brief planktonic life, moving quickly to the benthic stage.  Growth rate is relatively slow (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Sole adriatique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4537).  Maximum depth from Ref. 122868.

species.name: Sole australe occidentale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larvae are pelagic (Ref. 27121, Ref. 36731), while adults live close to the sea bed (Ref. 36731).  Adults feed on worms, crustaceans, mollusks, and fish (Ref. 27121, Ref. 36731).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4931).

species.name: Sole bavoche
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Adults inhabit coastal waters.  They also enter fresh waters, going hundreds of miles upstream. Migrate downstream to spawn in spring (Ref. 36739).  Larvae move upstream after hatching (Ref. 36739).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Sole d'orient
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand and mud bottoms in coastal waters.  Enters brackish waters (Ref. 6805).  Reported to enter fresh waters (Ref. 4833).  Feeds mainly on bottom-dwelling invertebrates, especially small crustaceans (Ref. 30573).  Marketed fresh, frozen and dried salted.

species.name: Sole de Cadenat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters on sandy bottoms (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Sole de Commerson
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly sand and mud bottoms in coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, especially small crustaceans.  Marketed fresh, frozen, and dried-salted.

species.name: Sole de Frechkop
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy and muddy bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 2683).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sole de Herre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species.  Demersal but may occasionally be pelagic (Ref. 9343).  Prefers sand or gravel substrata in shallow waters and will frequently bury itself.  When lying exposed on the bottom, it can change it color to match the substratum, making it difficult to distinguish from the bottom.  If harassed, it will rapidly dart head first about one or two feet away and dive into the substrata (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Sole de lait
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters, on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on bottom living invertebrates.  Marketed fresh.  Produces a bitter toxic substance from the bases of the dorsal and anal fin rays that deters predation, even by sharks (Ref. 9710) and thus may prove valuable as a shark repellent (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Sole de Mazatlan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in coastal waters less than 20 m depth and enters coastal lagoons and fresh water (Ref. 9047).  Feeds on crustaceans, small fishes, polychaetes, and occasionally detritus (Ref. 9047).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 9047). Benthic species that inhabits coastal waters less than 20m deep. May enter estuaries and freshwater (Ref. 55763).

species.name: Sole de Mer Egée
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sole de profondeur
species.description: Occurs on muddy bottoms of the continental slope (Ref. 2683).  Feeds mainly on polychaetes and some amphipods (Ref. 4710).

species.name: Sole de vase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud bottoms (Ref. 27121).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates and small fish (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Sole du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are abundant in sandy estuaries.

species.name: Sole fasciée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms.

species.name: Sole fluviatile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 9047).  Enters freshwater (Ref. 36798).  Maximum length reported to reach 15 cm TL (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole garde-bouée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shallow sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole langue
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 2683).  Feeds on mollusks.  Sold as frozen filet under the name 'filets de sole' (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Sole langue du Cap
species.description: Usually found at depths less than 100 m, but also recorded on the continental slope (Ref. 27121).  Caught incidentally (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Sole noire
species.description: Frequently captured on the slope of the continental plateau (Ref. 5377).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sole nue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms.  Minimum depth from Ref. 26912.

species.name: Sole ocellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms.

species.name: Sole ocellée (Pardachirus pavoninus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand and mud bottoms of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602, 48637).  Burries itself in the sand (Ref. 48637).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, especially small crustaceans (Ref. 9893).  Extract from sac under the skin is toxic (Ref. 559) and the mucus appears to have shark-repellent qualities.

species.name: Sole pantoufle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found more abundantly on shallow soft bottoms of brackish estuaries or hypersaline lagoons.  Enters freshwaters at least to an elevation of 10 m.  Inhabits rivers and creeks and probably feeds on aquatic insects and crustaceans (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Sole perdrix
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand bottoms (Ref. 5304). Enters lagoons (Ref. 6805). Feeds on mollusks and other invertebrates (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Sole poivrée
species.description: Occurs in shallow coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on bottom-living invertebrates.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Sole pole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on gravel, sand or mud.  Feeds on a wide range of small marine bivalves; mainly on crustaceans such as amphipods, mysids, shrimps, decapods, bivalves and polychaetes (Ref. 4710).

species.name: Sole quagga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 30573).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Sole queue longue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare.  Adults occur over sandy-muddy bottoms of the littoral zone and estuaries.  Little is known of its biology (Ref. 35237).  Maximum length reported to reach 15 cm TL (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Sole ronde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology little known (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole ruardon commune
species.description: Found on sand or mud bottoms (Ref. 2683, 4710) in shallow waters, from the shore to 60 m (Ref. 4710). No information available on diet or reproduction (Ref. 4710). Maximum depth from Ref. 122917.

species.name: Sole réticulée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear waters of oceanic islands; also in bays and mangrove-lined lagoons along continental coasts, on sandy-muddy bottoms (Ref. 5217).  Feeds on invertebrates.  Sexually mature after two years.  Females are bigger than males (Ref. 35237).

species.name: Sole sombre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the littoral zone, down to 20 m depth, and on all sandy-muddy bottoms of estuaries, rivers and coastal streams where it penetrates far enough sometimes.  They hide completely in the sediment, leaving out its eyes, in order to look out for predators and prey.  Feed on small crustaceans and fish.  Reproduction is like to occur between July and September (Ref. 35237).  Maximum length reported to reach 37 cm TL (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Sole tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on shallow muddy and sandy bottoms, near estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 9067).  Regularly penetrating brackish waters (Ref. 9067).  Feeds on crustaceans, small fishes and occasionally, detritus (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole trémail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and penetrates estuaries (Ref. 9047).  Feeds on small crustaceans and polychaetes (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole velue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal, neritic over soft bottoms; usually between 10 and 100 m depth. Feeds on benthic organisms, A bycatch species, caught occasionally to rarely with trawls (Ref. 120290).

species.name: Sole zèbre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in shallow sand and mud bottoms of the continental shelf and creeks.

species.name: Sole à joue tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy and muddy bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 9047).

species.name: Sole égyptienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. On soft bottom in coastal waters.  Feeds on benthic invertebrates, e.g., cnidarians, polychaete worms, and bivalves.

species.name: Sole élancée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand and mud bottoms in coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, especially small crustaceans.

species.name: Sole-langue canarienne
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Sole-langue de Mer Rouge
species.description: Not recorded from a depth of more than 135 m (Ref. 5297).

species.name: Sole-langue du Ghana
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms of coastal waters (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Sole-pedrix commune
species.description: Espèce de poissons plats. Inhabits mud or sand bottoms.  Feeds on a wide range of small bottom-living organisms, mainly crustaceans (amphipods, shrimps), also polychaete worms and bivalve mollusks (Ref. 4710).  Utilized as a food fish.

species.name: Sole-perdrix brune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud and sand of the continental shelf, from the shore down to 250 m (Ref. 4710).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, mainly amphipods and polychaetes (Ref. 4710). Minimum depth range from Ref. 121791.

species.name: Sole-perdrix juive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or muddy sand bottoms.

species.name: Sole-pole
species.description: Found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sole-ruardon du Golfe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 2683).

species.name: Solea capensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Solea heinii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Solea turbynei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in estuaries.  Juveniles are abundant on shallow sand banks (Ref. 3200).

species.name: Soleichthys dori
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleichthys maculosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleichthys multifasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleichthys nigrostriolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleichthys siammakuti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleichthys tubifera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Soleil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rarely found in shallow water, but appears to be the most common squirrelfish in the depth range of 30-60 m or more (Ref. 32).  Reported used as food fish (Ref. 37108).

species.name: Soleil (Sargocentron coruscum)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sandy, rocky and coral bottoms (Ref. 5521).  More common on seaward reefs than on protected reefs.  Retreat into recesses when alarmed (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal (Ref. 37108).  Secretive, found deep in crevices between branches of live corals (Ref. 26938).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 240).

species.name: Solitary duckbill eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded on video tape outside the coelacanth caves at a depth of 278-340 m (Ref. 58472).

species.name: Solitary jawfish
