species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mouthbrooders.  Eggs which are clumped together in a sticky ball get incubated inside the parent's mouth (Ref. 40511).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Solivomer arenidens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Solocisquama carinata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Solocisquama erythrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Solocisquama stellulata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bathymetric range possibly up to 900 m (Ref. 40826).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Solomon fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from deep-reef habitat (Ref. 123060).

species.name: Solomons goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Solomons sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species lives in a relatively unusual habitat, consisting of a nearly enclosed, narrow, dead-end lagoon, with a gradually sloping, white sand bottom with scattered, mainly low-profile, coral formations, occurring  as solitary individuals (Ref. 116121).

species.name: Solor jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand near reefs in 0-35 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Solor triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 27223.

species.name: Somali butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species apparently prefers deeper water, in deep coral rich reefs, often near base of slopes over coral rubble.  Usually solitary or in pairs over open bottoms.  Uncommon (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Somali flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Somali sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on deep coastal slopes and is sometimes trawled in deep water, usually in depths well-over 40 m (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Somalia catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Somalia glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably a schooling species confined to rather large river systems; feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 43912). Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Somalian blind barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A blind fish adapted to a cave-dwelling life (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Somalian cavefish
species.description: A blind species which inhabits underground waters in Somalia (Ref. 2801).

species.name: Somalian giant catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in mud at bottom of rivers.  Latest (March 2000) male specimen caught in rather shallow water on the sandy bottom of the river, which had a very low water level following a long period of drought (in Kenya).  Female (caught later in 2000)  (Ref. 41277).

species.name: Somalian sand diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Someren's suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers fast-flowing upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 96588) with rocks and small boulders (Ref. 105400). Also found in residual pools (Ref. 78218). Mouth and dentition suggest that it is a bottom feeder and algal grazer; probably spawns more than once per year (Ref. 96588). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sonoda megalophthalma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults taken in bottom hauls (Ref. 37473).

species.name: Sonoda paucilampa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to prefer the bathypelagic environment (Ref. 46206).

species.name: Sonora blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reefs, among seaweed.  Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Sonora chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy pools (intermittent during dry season) of creeks and springs (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Sonora clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the rocky intertidal zone (Ref. 11482).  May remain out of water under rocks or seaweeds (Ref. 31184).  Feeds on barnacles, limpets and small crustaceans (Ref. 37955).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Resistant to extreme temperatures (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Sonora goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually on sand bottoms of tide pools and rocky reefs.

species.name: Sonora sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Large individuals occur in rocky riffles and runs at night.

species.name: Sonora topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sonoyta pupfish
species.description: An omnivore feeding on plants, insect larvae and nymphs, water mites, ostracods, their own eggs, sponge, mollusc eggs and some other organisms (Ref. 58358).

species.name: Soot-tail Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reef slopes and dropoffs to 33 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sooty cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sooty darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools and nearby riffles of headwaters and creeks (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Often found in very shallow water less than 4 m deep (Ref. 5723).  Juveniles feed on midge larvae and microcrustaceans; adults on midge larvae, other immature aquatic insects (mayflies, caddisflies, stoneflies), isopods and amphipods (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Sooty grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More commonly found in larger flowing streams in both clear or turbid water.  Adults inhabit particularly the upper reaches of river systems over sandy or rocky bottoms with sparse aquatic plant growth.  Can tolerate acidic conditions (to a pH of 4.0) and temperatures between 12° and 34°C.  Feed on frogs, insects, worms, shrimps, algae, plant roots, and palm berries.  Some adults develop greatly oversized `blubber' lips.  Spawns in summer in response to rising water levels following monsoonal rains.  Group spawning may occur (Ref. 44894).  Spawns in summer when streams begin to rise.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  A good angling species growing to a weight of 4 kilograms.

species.name: Sooty skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 12.5 cm long and 7.5 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Sooty snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sorcière de Facciola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The young are sometimes found in caves, larger specimens caught deeper.  Feeds mainly on decapod natantia (Ref. 4776).

species.name: Sorcière à queue noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in holes on muddy bottoms of continental slope.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 4776).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Soromonichthys stearleyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens were collected from shallow riffles and runs over clean cobble substrate interspersed with sand and patches of a rooted, moss-like aquatic macrophytes. Other loricariids collected in Soromoni Creek with this species were Ancistrus sp., Dekeyseria niveata, Exastilithoxus sp., and Rineloricaria formosa (Ref. 87303).

species.name: Sorong rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sorubim maniradii
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Sostra's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs in 0-40 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Soto la Marina shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Souris de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore waters, deeper waters in winter in Skaggerak, preferring sandy bottoms, rarely with stones.  Maximum depth reported at 270 m (Ref. 28197).  Temp.  range:  4.0-8.0 °C.  Feeds on bottom crustaceans and polychaetes.  Matures after about 1 year; a few spawning in the second year (Ref. 722).  The eggs are laid in seaweed (Ref. 9900).  Spawns in February - April, female laying 2,500-3,000 yellow eggs with a diameter of 2 mm.  Period of development is very long and 6-8 mm long pelagic larvae hatch after 10-11 months (Ref. 35388).

species.name: South African thorny flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: South African zebra sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: South American catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in littoral creeks, over sandy bottoms covered with dead leaves (Ref. 27188).  Inhabits also lakes and rivers, but seems to prefer rivers with a very slight current (Ref. 6868).  Prefers a muddy bottom covered with leaves and decaying wood, the latter providing for hiding places during the day (Ref. 35381).  Feeds on fish and insects (Ref. 27188), benthic zooplankton and crustaceans (Ref. 35381).  Omnivorous (Ref. 79585).  Mainly nocturnal (Ref. 11225).  Possesses poisonous spiny rays.  Its sex ratio is 2:1 in favor of females.  The male's reproductive apparatus includes multi-lobed testicles and accessory organs for secretion and storage.  Fertilization is external.  Non-sticking demersal eggs (1.1 to 2.8 mm diameter) are laid down, hatching after about 48 hours at 22°C.  Ten days later, the larvae weigh approximately 100 mg but growth is slow (0.5 to 1.15 g per day).

species.name: South American freshwater stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwater rivers.  It is an extremely dangerous species.  Maximum length reported in Axelrod et al., 1991 (Ref. 6398)  is 100 cm TL.

species.name: South American lungfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers stagnant waters where there is little current.  Juveniles feed on larval insects and snails.  Adults are omnivorous and feed on aquatic vertebrates, invertebrates such as snails, clams and shrimp, and algae (Ref. 36739).  Can survive low oxygen levels in its habitat by means of its very reduced branchial apparatus.  It possesses two lungs without bronchial tubes.  During the dry period, this species burrows into the mud, to a depth of about 30-50 cm, and seals off the entrance with clay, leaving out 2-3 holes for aeration.  It reduces its metabolism during this period of hibernation.  The fish are obligate air-breathers and will drown if denied access to the surface (Ref. 36739).  During the rainy season, reproduction begins.  The parents gather vegetal debris in a burrow (about 1.5 m long) to create a nest.  During reproduction, males guard the young.  These males can increase the oxygen level in the burrow because during breading season the pelvic fins develop highly vascularized, gill-like, feathery structures which perform a function opposite to those of gills:  they releases oxygen from the blood and take in carbon dioxide; the filaments disappear after the end of the breeding season (Ref. 12225, 36739).  The young look like amphibian tadpoles with four external gills.  During the first weeks of their life they breath only through the external gills; at an age of 7 weeks they become air-breathing and regression of the external gills begins (Ref. 27188, 36739).

species.name: South American silver porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in clean turbulent waters along open rocky coasts, usually in surf areas (Ref. 7251). Juveniles are frequently found in littoral pools between rocks (Ref. 9626). Individuals up to 10 cm are caught in shallow waters, often in sandy shores or in seagrass (Thalassia) beds (Ref. 9626). Maximum weight of 2500 g based on confirmed reports from Uruguay (L.A. Pereira, pers. comm., 6/12/01).

species.name: South Brazilian skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit continental slopes.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Maturity size unknown, 95 cm TL male was still immature (Ref. 114953).

species.name: South caucasian gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: South China leg skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype was taken from sandy-muddy bottom; maximum depth provided by H. Ishihara and Y. Wang (pers. comm. 07/07).

species.name: South Georgia spiny plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly littoral but has been reported to occur as deep as 90 m.  Fishes seen lying motionless on the bottom most of the time.  Major food item:  amphipods.  Also important food are isopods and polychaetes (Ref. 5191).

species.name: South Indian flying barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: South Pacific lanternbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: South Pacific moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from very shallow inshore areas or tide pools to depths of at least 45 m depth (Ref. 13539).

species.name: South Pacific sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-gravel bottom (Ref. 10634).

species.name: Southeast Asian blackstripe dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on silty coastal habitat with remote coral heads to soft bottom at shallow depths to about 25 m (Ref. 48635).  Also found on coral or rocky patches. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Southern African Pike
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers quiet, deep water, like channels and lagoons of large floodplains; juveniles and fry inhabit well-vegetated marginal habitats (Ref. 7248). Adults feed on fish, juveniles feed on small invertebrates and fish (Ref. 7248). Multiple spawner; breeds over the summer months; relatively short-lived, only 4-5 years; also caught with drawnets (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Southern African triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern Atlantic sharpnose-puffer
species.description: Inhabits coral-rich as well as coral-poor areas, and areas with rocky bottoms (Ref. 43205).  Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Often in pairs, hovering over the reef during the day (Ref. 43205).  Feeds on vegetation, sponges, crustaceans, and mollusks (Ref. 42064).

species.name: Southern barred minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, flowing water in rapids or instream pools of rivers (Ref. 26673); frequenting pools below rapids or water flows over sand or gravel (Ref. 52193). It feeds primarily on benthic macroinvertebrates, mainly chironomid and simuliid larvae, and adult insects taken from the surface (Ref. 26673)..Gonadosomatic index indicates that the species is a partial spawner which breeds over an extended period during the spring and summer months (Ref. 26673), spawning several times during the season (Ref. 52193)..

species.name: Southern barred triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rock pools and the upper subtidal zone.  Mostly associated with seagrass beds (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Southern bastard codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on hard bottom, over exposed rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans (Ref. 2156).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Southern bigscale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled at depths below 500 m (Ref. 4241).

species.name: Southern blue catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern bluespotted flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species, recorded from surf beaches, estuaries and in bays (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Southern Burmese river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers.  More specimens and data needed.

species.name: Southern cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Southern Caspian sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schools in the open sea, not approaching shores.  Occurs mainly in the south in winter, migrating to the middle parts of the sea in spring and returning south in November-December.  Found in upper layers in March-April, but descends to 16 to 32 m in summer and autumn.  Feeds mainly on copepods, also pelagic mysids and small fishes.  Breeds in January-September intermittently in the open sea.  Stocks said to be depleted in southern part of Caspian Sea.

species.name: Southern cavefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit subterranean water (Ref. 5723).  Found in caves which are near the water table and are therefore more uniform than other amblyopsid caves (Ref. 34868).  Feed mainly on copepods, amphipods and isopods (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are carried in gill chambers of females (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southern checkmark cichlid
species.description: Inhabits rivers, preferring fast flowing, cooler waters of the mountain runoffs.  Adults occur solitarily or in pairs (Ref. 7335).  Omnivorous, specialized in fresh vegetation (Ref. 30499).

species.name: Southern chimaera
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern Churchill
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing, major, perennial river, bordered by dense, subtropical or tropical vegetation (Ref. 38306).

species.name: Southern clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore waters (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Southern conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in about 100 m depth.

species.name: Southern crested weedfish
species.description: Inhabits areas with weeds, subtidal to about 30 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Southern deepbody
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers and brooks in the gallery forest (Ref. 59344), possibly over rocky substrate (Ref. 7248).  5.5 cm max TL (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Southern demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southern dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern driftwood catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern fiddler ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species that occurs on continental shelf, mainly found on soft bottoms and seagrasses. Feeds on bottom crustaceans, worms, molluscs and small fishes. Produces litters of 2-5 pups. Maturity size of males at ca. 70 cm TL, females at 89 cm TL; birth size at 21-25 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Southern fintail snipe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently entering the upper water column (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Southern flathead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Enters fresh waters (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Southern fraildisc clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern frillfin
species.description: Collected from intertidal rock-pools, where this species is said to dominate the shallow tidepool habitat (Ref. 87607).

species.name: Southern frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore in surface waters of estuaries, bays, inlets and gulfs to a depth of about 20 m (Ref. 9563).  In the South Australian gulfs, southern sea garfish may be found in deeper waters during the colder months (Ref. 27008).  Generally herbivorous, seagrasses and algal filaments comprise about 75% of their food (Refs. 26551, 27013).  Form schools, generally found near the surface at night and close to the bottom over seagrass beds during the day (Ref. 6390).  Post-larvae or young fish less than 1-year-old live in estuaries from March to July then move to inshore marine waters, remaining there for up to 2 years (Ref. 27012).

species.name: Southern Gulf pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens were collected or photographed in sheltered shallow open water at 1-5 m depth over a substrate of a mosaic of patches of brown algae, with Posidonia or Zostera. It appears to have a very limited inshore distribution along patches of moderate energy coastlines with low turbidity and a broken vegetation pattern of seagrass and brown algae. The restricted inshore habitat may be particularly vulnerable to pollutants or exotic marine species. The eggs of this species are deposited in two layers, a basal and then an external layer. A specimen with the greatest recorded number of eggs had 3 staggered rows of 64 basal membranous egg compartments on the tail, with the basal layer of eggs covered by a membrane with matching rows of egg pouches; the second layer with 34 eggs within the brood pouch folds resulted in a total of 98 eggs. Total lengths of larvae at hatching is 1.8 cm (vs. 1.3 cm in S. nigra and 3.2 cm in S. argus. Males of this species have extended brood patches from December to March, and juveniles < 9.0 cm are seen from December to March. Males also can mature at 11.3 cm. The maximum recorded brood was 98 eggs which was far greater than that recorded by for S. nigra which is approximately 25 and for S. argus with 41 eggs (Ref. 75062).

species.name: Southern gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to bury itself completely in the sand during the day, but are fully exposed at night.  Prefers deeper sand channels, away from rubble or seagrasses (Ref. 57438).

species.name: Southern herring smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern hulafish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southern King Weakfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is heavily exploited throughout its range (Ref. 88197).

species.name: Southern leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Southern leatherside chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sluggish pools and backwaters, usually over mud or sand, of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Southern lemon sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow waters, generally at depth of less than 50 m. Found to depth of 385 m (Ref. 27073).  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).

species.name: Southern lesser pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters.

species.name: Southern lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Southern little pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Males may have developed brood pouches at about 4.5 cm TL (Ref. 5316).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southern logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore near reef areas (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southern longfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sandy estuaries, often in seagrass beds (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Southern Mandarin Dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern mountain swordtail
species.description: This species occurs sympatrically with X. mixei and apparently prefers deeper pools; in rapidly flowing river with boulders and riffles (Ref. 52914).

species.name: Southern mouthbrooder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in various habitats, from flowing waters to lakes and isolated sinkholes, e.g., Lake Otjikoto, Namibia (see Ref. 27829); usually prefers vegetated zones. It feeds on insects, shrimps and even small fish (Ref. 52193). Breeds from early spring to late summer; males establish and defend a territory, construct a simple cleared nest and attract ripe females; eggs are laid in the nest, fertilized and collected by the female; the female withdraws to a quiet nursery area to brood the eggs, larvae and juveniles until they are able to fend for themselves (Ref. 7248, 52193). Ovophilic, agamous maternal mouthbrooder; no pair-bonding takes place (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Southern ninespine stickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fresh, brackish and marine waters (Ref.  58342).  Inhabits swamps and slow-flowing streams with dense vegetation. Feeds on benthic invertebrates.  Territorial during spawning season.  Males construct a nest and guard the nest until the young swim away a few weeks later.  Attain first sexual maturity at 1 year of age (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Southern no-line scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern orange-lined cardinal fish
species.description: Found in clear coastal and outer reefs, juveniles in harbors, boulder rock and usually in small aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Southern Pacific moray cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern peacock sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered coastal waters, usually in clean sand habitat (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Southern pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Sedentary fishes that swim slowly and spend much of their time resting on the bottom.  They use the long snout for probing in crevices, seaweed and sand for crabs, worms, and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 30464).  Neither anterolateral glandural groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Southern platyfish
species.description: Adults occur in warm springs, canals and ditches with typically slow-moving water, silt bottoms and weedy banks  (Refs. 5723; 44091, 44894).  Also inhabit creeks and swamps (Ref. 44894).  Feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Refs. 7020; 44091).  Used for genetic research (Ref. 4537).  Several color varieties are popular aquarium fishes, where they attain sexual maturity after 3-4 months and reproduce easily (Ref. 1672).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Southern pond loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern purplespotted gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing or still waters, among weed (Ref. 7327). Occurs in rivers, creeks and billabongs, usually over rocks or among vegetation (Ref. 44894). Feeds on worms, dragonfly larvae, midge and mosquito larvae, crustaceans and mosquito fishes (Ref. 7327). Maturity: F at 4.9 cm, M at 4.5 cm. Sexually dimorphic. Direct pair spawning in rivers and ponds at 19-34°C in Dec.-Feb. A single cluster of demersal eggs laid on a solid substrate, often close to vegetation (Ref. 7276). Spawns during the rainy season (November to March). Females produce successive batches of 280-1300 eggs which are deposited on rocks, logs, or other solid debris. Males guard and fan the eggs until hatching, which takes about 3-9 days depending on temperature (Ref. 44894). Preyed on by Perca fluviatilis and competes with mosquito fish (Ref. 7329).

species.name: Southern pygmy perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lotic and lentic freshwater bodies (Ref. 7300).  Inhabits vegetated margins of streams, billabongs, drains, dams and swamps in still or gently flowing water.  Forms small groups and is a very common prey item for introduced fishes, such as the Redfin perch and trout.  Feeds on small crustaceans, insects and their larvae.  Breeds from September to January, when water temperatures rise above 16°C.  Reproductive habits and biology are typical of the family.  Maximum life expectancy is about 5 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Southern rays bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern redbelly dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, usually spring-fed, pools of headwaters and creeks (Ref. 86798).  Also found in streams (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Southern rock bass
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Needs better reference.  Max. length (Pedro Jimenez Prado, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Southern round skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over soft bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.1-7.6 cm long and 3.2-3.8 cm wide (Ref. 41308). Males reaches maturity at ca. 46 cm TL. Occassionally caught as bycatch and typically discarded (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Southern sand darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Southern sand flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters from shallow bays and inlets to depths of about 100 m over sand, shell grit and mud substrates (Ref. 6390).  Sand flathead are usually solitary but may form loose aggregations (Ref. 2165, 27247).  They sometimes move long distances (Ref. 6390).  They are active foragers and ambush predators (Ref. 6390), occasionally are scavengers (Ref. 6390).  Feed on crustaceans and fish (Ref. 2165). Its fin spines are venomous, can inflict mild to severe pain (Ref. 125684).

species.name: Southern saratoga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in still waters and slow-flowing sections of streams.  They are usually seen near the surface or near shore among aquatic vegetation (Ref. 39857, 44894).  Territorial and aggressive towards other fishes, particularly conspecifics.  Scratches and wounds resulting from fighting arre frequently exhibited by adults captured in the wild (Ref. 44894).  Feed on aquatic and terrestrial insects, fishes, frogs and crayfish.  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 39857, 44894).  Breeding occurs prior to the wet season at temperatures between 20°C and 23°C.  A renowned angling species (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Southern sawtail catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species inhabits deep-reefs in the shelf break and on the continental slope, and is often found in depths greater than 400 meters, with gorgonians, hard corals, tube sponges, crinoids, ophiuroids, and a great number of the sympatric scyliorhinid shark Scyliorhinus haeckelii (Ref. 56495). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Southern smoothhead glass blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed TP males in holes in live and dead coral, as well as in sponges while IP fish are found perched on live corals and sponges, but also on dead coral and encrusted substrates; also the depth range is broad, up to at least 40 m with no particular peak of occurrence (Ref. 125603).

species.name: Southern sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern spearnose poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Southern spotted barracudina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported as by-catch of bottom trawl on the slope of the Kerguelen Plateau (480-800 m) and South-Georgia (Ref. 122005).

species.name: Southern stoplight loosejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only a few were caught above 500 m, thus it appears that this species does not regularly migrate on a diel basis out of the mesopelagic.  With its large accessory orbital photophore (AO), this species likely uses this in employing a far-red visual system as part of its foraging strategy (Ref. 78501).

species.name: Southern striped raphael
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Southern studfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits margins, pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Most commonly found in shallow sandy backwaters of clean rocky creeks.  12 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on snails (Ref. 10294).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Southern tandan
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly restricted to headwater streams in hilly or mountainous terrain.  Prefers clear, fast-flowing streams, usually in deep rocky pools.  Can ascend torrential steep-gradient streams and small waterfalls.

species.name: Southern thorny skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mid- and outer continental shelf and upper slope, occasionally caught deeper to 1000 m. Mainly feeds on benthic invertebrates and small bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsule measures 86.4 mm long and 56.2 mm wide (Ref. 41249). Hatches from egg case at ca. 9 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Southern tidewater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Southern tubelip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reef areas with high coral cover (Ref. 9823).  Adults feed on coral polyps while juveniles take ectoparasites and possibly mucus of  other reef fishes (Ref. 9823).

species.name: Southern velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore in soft bottom, among plants.

species.name: Southern whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally demersal, on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on octopods, fish, and decapod crustaceans.

species.name: Southern yellow croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries to depths of 50 m (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Southseas devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Southwell's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from plankton or night-light collections.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Southwest Atlantic butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns near the coast (Ref. 36453).  Juveniles lives in close association with jellyfishes (Ref. 36453).

species.name: Southwestern goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lower reaches of rivers, estuaries and coastal lakes (Ref. 33616).  Lives on silt or mud  bottoms in quiet waters of brackish estuaries and coastal lakes (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Sovvityazius acer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from silty ground (Ref. 129446).

species.name: Spade sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 3.5 cm long and 5.2 cm wide (Ref. 41249).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spadenose guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found on shallow coastal regions of the Gulf of California to at least two meters depth.  The smallest adult 48.0 cm TL (Ref. 125697).

species.name: Spaghetti eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Young and females burrow in sandy tide pools and reef tracts.  Males inhabit deeper water, possibly pelagic.  Adults emerge at night and sometimes come to lights at the surface (Ref. 26938).  Feed on burrowing  invertebrates that live in the sand (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Spalding's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spangled cichlid
species.description: Considered an easygoing and adaptable fish of long standing  with aquarists.  Is noteworthy among lake mouth brooders by the fact that both parents participate in the incubation of the brood, which implies that the mates are bonded in a monogamous relationship lasting until at least as long as the fry are incubated (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Spangled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spangled perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit forest streams to desert bores under equally variable regimes of salinity (pure fresh to seawater), pH (4.0 to 8.6) and temperature (5° to 44° C).  Occur in billabongs, lakes and dams.  May be encountered in any temporary water in the interior after rains, including wheel ruts of vehicle tracks (Ref. 44894).  Omnivorous, feed on insects, crustaceans, mollusks and plants.  A hardy species that may be capable of surviving droughts by aestivating in wet mud or under moist little on the bottom of ephemeral waterholes.  Spawning occurs on summer nights (November onwards) when water temperatures reach 20°-26°C.  Fish moves upstream in rivers or to the shallows in lakes and ponds to spawn on soft substrates.  The eggs hatch in 2 days and larval development is complete in about 24 days (Ref. 44894).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Neither anterolateral glandular grooves nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Spangled tubeshoulder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 6598, 75154).

species.name: Spangleside neoscopelid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Spaniblennius clandestinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from one specimen but probably a shallow water species (Peter Wirtz, pers. comm. 05/05).  Similar to its congeners, this species is oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spaniblennius riodourensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range of 17 - 30 meters given by Peter Wirtz (pers. comm. 05/05).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spanish minnowcarp
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabits small streams with swift current (often pools in summer) and pebble to rock bottom, usually without submerged vegetation (Ref. 59043).  Reported to occur in lowland streams with a moderate current and abundant submerged plants.  Pelagic filter feeder (Ref. 26100) . Feeds on filamentous algae and small invertebrate.  Migrates upstream to spawn then returns to downstream areas at beginning of summer, where permanent water is retained throughout the year (Ref. 59043).  Due to its threats such as habitat destruction and water pollution (Ref. 26100), a conservation project started under the EU-Life Nature program (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Spanner barb
species.description: Usually inhabits clear mountain streams strewn with rocks and boulders; frequently found below waterfalls (Ref. 2091).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Sparano cory
species.description: Diurnal, found singly or in pairs (Ref. 46825).

species.name: Spare bourriquète
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spare broyeuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters, mainly off rocky shores down to 80 m depth.  Rarely enters estuaries.  Young commonly found in tide pools.  Feeds mainly on mollusks (Ref. 5213).  An important food fish.

species.name: Spare dentue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in middle waters near reefs (Ref. 3507).  Carnivorous.  Sold fresh.

species.name: Spare doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually in schools inshore in summer and offshore in winter.  Feeds on amphipods, worms, sand dollars and young squid (Ref. 4926).  Utilized fresh, smoked and frozen; eaten pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Exported to Japan (Ref. 9988)

species.name: Spare du Natal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore.  May occur singly or in small groups.  Feeds on crabs, hermit crabs, shrimps, bivalve mollusks, squid and sometimes other small fish (Ref. 3670).  Spawns in the summer (Ref. 3198).  Good food fish (Ref. 3198).  Sold fresh and whole in markets.

species.name: Spare gibbeuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters. Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, worms and small fishes (Ref. 5213). Good food fish. Sold fresh in markets. It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus cirrusspiralis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Spare nasique
species.description: Inhabits shallow, rocky coastal areas to 80 m depth. Rarely enters estuaries. Feeds on crabs, crayfish, sea urchins and other hard-shelled animals (Ref. 3670). Takes almost any bait (Ref. 3198). Important food fish. Head considered a delicacy in some areas (Ref. 3198). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus cirrusspiralis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Spare panga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, over soft bottoms (Ref. 27121).  Forms large schools (Ref. 5213).  Sold fresh.

species.name: Spare poignard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky banks (Ref. 3198).  Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, worms, and small fishes.  Seldom caught from the shore (Ref. 3198).  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Spare royal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide range of bottoms.  Young fish occur in very shallow waters of sheltered bays; larger individuals in deeper water.  Feed on benthic invertebrates, mainly mollusks (Ref. 5213).  Important food fish.

species.name: Spare sobaity
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow coastal waters to moderate depths.  Carnivorous.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Spare soldat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over corals in warmer waters and rocky reefs over sandy bottoms; feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 5213, 124569).  Sold fresh, whole or dried in markets (Ref. 3507).

species.name: Spare à front rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on crustaceans, mollusks, worms and small fish.  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Spare à selle blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs above rocky bottoms in deeper water to 100 m but often caught from shore. Juveniles occur in shallow-water beds of seaweed where they feed on minute crustacean (Ref. 3670). Feeds on mollusks, crustaceans, worms and fish. Females transform into territorial males with growth (Ref. 3198). Voracious but sluggish, takes any bait. Good food fish (Ref. 3198). Sold fresh (Ref. 3507). It is parasitised by the monogenean Anoplodiscus cirrusspiralis on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Spare élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters over rocky substrate.  Feeds on mollusks, crustaceans, worms, and small fishes (Ref. 5213).  Sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Spare épineuse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly on mud bottoms.

species.name: Sparidentex belayewi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sparisoma griseorubrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sparisoma tuiupiranga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow areas of tropical rocky reefs. Males establish territories (approximately 8 m2). Juveniles are strongly associated with seaweed beds, occasionally found mixed with Sparisoma radians and Cryptotomus roseus. This species is typically a scraper which grazes upon a large variety of epilithic algae (e.g. Jania, Gelidium, Polysiphonia, consequently ingesting a large quantity of sediment. It is however, very plastic in its feeding habits and is commonly observed browsing over Sargassum. Males and larger initial phase adult individuals perform up to 2400 bites daily with a mean gut turnover of about 2.5 guts day-1, having an important role on local energy flux (Ref. 52151).

species.name: Sparkfin Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species of Manonichthys facultatively enter large sponges. However, no large sponges were observed at the collection sites (Ref. 88961). Found in outer reefs and lagoons in 2-33 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sparsely spotted carpetshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species is likely to occur deeper, 245-435. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Sparsely-spotted stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).  Adults feed on worms, crabs, shrimp, and small bony fishes while juveniles take small crustaceans (Ref. 12951).

species.name: Sparsetooth dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth ranging from 0-200 m (Ref. 10905).

species.name: Spathodus erythrodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly seen in less than a foot of water, this species is found at the very edge of the pebble or rubble shoreline.  Feeds by picking microorganisms from the rock biocover (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Spathodus marlieri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swims over rock bottom for long distances, alone or in pairs, instead of jumping from place to place between pebbles as S. erythrodon does. Feeds by picking microorganisms from the rock biocover (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Spatula-barbeled catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit inshore waters to 20 m deep (Ref. 3236), and restricted to the rocky littoral zone (Ref. 38677). Rest on the bottom with the modified maxillary barbels (Ref. 6868). Nocturnally active meanwhile resting beneath rocks and within interstices in the rock or rubble substrata during the day (Ref. 38677). Oviparous (Ref. 205). First report of bi-parental mouthbrooding among catfishes (Ref. 38677). No value as food (Ref. 4967). Stomach contents examined consist of shrimps, occasionally debris from larval insects, and fish remains which apparently are clupeids (possibly Limnothrissa. Aquarium conditions: pH7.6; hardness of water 12; temperature tolerance 25°C; tank capacity, 60L; food, e.g. live worms, Daphnia; aquarium lighting, as dark as possible as long as fishes are visible; a peaceful, bottom-swimming fish which prefers a set-up with rocks, plants, and driftwood in an aquarium (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Spatular-scale silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur usually along the open coast; rarely seen in lagoons or inner parts of bays and inlets (Ref. 44256).

species.name: Spatulate rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154). Caught with Caelorinchus innotabilis (Ref. 26363).

species.name: Spatuloricaria atratoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria caquetae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria curvispina
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria euacanthagenys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria evansii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria fimbriata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria gymnogaster
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria lagoichthys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria nudiventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria phelpsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on algae and detritus (Ref. 26543).

species.name: Spatuloricaria puganensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spatuloricaria terracanticum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species prefer areas of the river with moderate slopes (between 0 and 3%) over substrates consisting of stones (less than 20 cm of diameter) and sand (observations indicate 80% rocks and 20% sand). Specimens captured at altitudes ranging from 197 to 350 m asl; water varies from high turbidity (316 mg/l total solids) to slightly clear, with pH between 6.4 and 8.2, conductivity between 30 and 302 µS/cm, oxygen concentration between 1.6 and 7.64 mg/l, with percent of saturation between 22.5 to 98.8%, water temperature between 22.5 and 28.58°C. This species has been captured with other species of loricariids (Chaetostoma formosae, C. joropo, Farlowella mariaelenae, Lamontichthys llanero), as well as characids (Creagrutus bolivari, Gephyrocharax valencia, Hemibrycon metae, Odontostilbe splendida), a cichlid (Bujurquina mariae), and apteronotids (Apteronotus apurensis, A. galvisi) (Ref. 119417).

species.name: Spatuloricaria tuira
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the bottom of medium to large rivers, in association with rocky or sandy substrates
in fast-flowing sectors (Ref. 96500).

species.name: Spearcheek cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from a depth of 835 (Ref. 34024).  Benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spearfin goby
species.description: Occurs among rubble and coral of weedy or grassy inner reef flats and silty slopes (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Spearnose grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms.

species.name: Spearnose seabat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spearnose whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spearsnouted grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds primarily on small fish and bottom-living crustaceans.

species.name: Speartail mudgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on mud in shallow brackish waters (Ref. 58302). Also found in sand bottoms in estuaries and stream mouths in 1-4 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Speckled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 56066).  Eggs are attached to the walls of the parent's shelter and are brooded by the male parent (Ref. 56066).

species.name: Speckled chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and gravel runs of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on aquatic insect larvae dominated by midges (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Speckled damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitarily or in small groups in lagoons, reef flats, passages, and outer reef slopes.  Usually amongst coarse rubble or rock (Ref. 48636, 119540).  Feed primarily on pelagic materials, such as copepods, isopods, and pelagic tunicates and opportunistically algae (Ref. 119540).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Speckled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear sandy and rocky pools of creeks and small to medium, usually fast, rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Speckled dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been collected from depths of 0 to 31 m (Ref. 1602). Found in coastal reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Speckled garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Speckled garden-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In dense colonies of about 6 individuals per square meter.  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 33408, 89972).  Diet mainly composed of calanoid copepods, gelatinous plankton, invertebrate pelagic eggs, siphonophores, decapod larvae, fish eggs, particles of organic matter and larvaceans.  (Ref. 33447).

species.name: Speckled killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over sand or mud in backwaters and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.  9.6 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Speckled klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and subtidal areas.

species.name: Speckled madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel-sand runs and rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers, near vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Speckled maori wrasse
species.description: Found solitary (Ref. 90102) in caves of steep outer reef drop-offs from 25 to at least 46 m (Ref. 1602) with rich invertebrate growth such as large gorgonians or soft corals (Ref. 48636).  Feeds mainly on fishes, shrimps and other crustaceans (Ref. 9823).

species.name: Speckled pavon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies deeper littoral areas in lagoons and sandy and rocky banks of the main river channel.  Feeds mainly on small fish (especially characids measuring <10 cm SL) (Ref. 26329, 27531).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Has been introduced to Florida and Texas, but is considered not established yet.

species.name: Speckled piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Speckled puffer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Speckled rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found commonly on deep rocky areas in southern California, USA from 30-366 m.  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).

species.name: Speckled sanddab
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottom, from near shore to 366 m (Ref. 2850).  Little commercial importance because of its small size (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Speckled shrimpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small groups near or among long-spined sea urchins and branching corals.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9710).  Swims vertically, with a head-down position  (Ref. 5462).

species.name: Speckled siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Speckled sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers harbors and bays.

species.name: Speckled stargazer
species.description: Burrows in soft sandy bottom, where it waits for prey, with only the eyes, nose and mouth protruding.

species.name: Speckled swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Speckled tongue sole
species.description: Inhabits sand and silt bottoms of coastal seas, rarely seen near reefs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Speckled worm-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds from bays and mangroves to offshore reefs.  Adults move to open sea to spawn.  The species has considerable regenerative powers (Ref. 5521).  Tidal creeks and brackish estuaries offshore to depths of 7 m (Ref. 26938).  Reported from fresh water in Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and Mexico (Ref. 30499).  Caught for bait fishery with use of ichthyotoxic plants (e.g. 'cunabi') along the north Brazilian coast (Ref. 34896).

species.name: Speckled xingu cory
species.description: Occurs in lotic habitats that have muddy-brown water with clay and sandy substrata. Most specimens were captured in the small forest streams of black or clearwater, or in marginal ponds (Ref. 122129).

species.name: Specklehead cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The two known specimens were collected from under a piece of dead-coral rubble on a gradually sloping sand bottom at 40 m depth (Ref. 118651).

species.name: Specklemouth eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range from type locality data (Ref. 51665).

species.name: Spectacled filefish
species.description: A generally uncommon species found in seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48637) and in harbours.  Usually in rich coral with various other mixed-invertebrate habitat (Ref. 48637).  Found close to shelter (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic organisms (Ref. 3467). Solitary (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Spectacled parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear lagoon and seaward reefs, from the intertidal to at least 45 m (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).

species.name: Spectacled sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand or mud bottoms of estuaries and sheltered shoreline reefs in 0-6 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Spectacled sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly between 100 and 380 m on mud, sand, pebbles, gravel and shell.

species.name: Spectracanthicus immaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectracanthicus murinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectracanthicus punctatissimus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectracanthicus tocantinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectracanthicus zuanoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds actively at night on algae and other food items off periphyton by grazing over rock bottom. Found in rock-bottom areas subjected to backwater and strong currents. Occurs individually or in groups of three, under shelter boulders (adults) and spaces beneath rocks (juveniles), up to 2m deep. Juveniles co-inhabit with other loricariids such as Ancistrus sp., A. ranunculus, Baryancistrus xanthellus, Spectracanthicus punctatissimus , Hopliancistrus tricornis, Parancistrus nudiventris, Peckoltia vittata, and Pseudancistrus aff. barbatus (Ref. 95496).

species.name: Spectrolebias brousseaui
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The locality where the species occurs lies at the plateau area (316 m.a.s.l.), just southwest of Llanos de Mojos, which occupy much of the río Mamoré basin. Water temperature at the surface of the pool was 31ºC, at 1 meter depth was 22ºC, and at the marginal area of the pool, at 15 cm depth, was 35ºC. Only small specimens of Trigonectes sp. were collected syntopically in marginal areas, while specimens of Simpsonichthys brousseaui were collected in the deepest areas, at about 1 m deep. The pool has dark water, pH 6.8 and water hardness 80 ppm (Ref. 93219).

species.name: Spectrolebias chacoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Spectrolebias costai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 6 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Spectrolebias filamentosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectrolebias gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This endemic species is found in river system of Araguaia-Toncantins, with temporary pools surrounded by dense aquatic vegetation.  They were observed in 0.8 meters of water.  The largest specimens examined were 2.08 cm for males and 1.85 cm for females, standard length. (Ref. 119392).

species.name: Spectrolebias inaequipinnatus
species.description: Found only in a seasonal pool that is exposed to sunlight and with aquatic vegetation, clear, slightly tea-colored water (Ref. 79814).

species.name: Spectrolebias pilleti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectrolebias reticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spectrolebias semiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow temporary pool, about 80 cm deep with slightly acidic (pH 6.5) dark water (Ref. 26131).

species.name: Spectrunculus crassus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One specimen from the eastern Pacific was examined and radiographs showed the following stomach contents: detritus, gastropods, crustaceans, ophiurids, remains of polychaetes, foraminifera, sediment, and bivalves.  From individuals with filled stomachs), detritus was found to be 88%, followed by gastropods (52%), crustaceans (44%), and ophiurids (36%).   Observed ontogenetic trend in the consumption of gastropods with 18.2% in specimens less than 45 cm SL (n=11) and 78.6% in specimens greater than 45 cm SL (n=14, Fisher’s Exact Test, P<0.005); all gastropod shells were intact (Ref. 80689).

species.name: Speolabeo musaei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in caves (Ref. 86533).

species.name: Speonectes tiomanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species (Ref. 27297).  A 4.89 cm SL female has ripe eggs (about 1.0 mm diameter) in its gonads (Ref. 37830).

species.name: Sperata acicularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same genus (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sperata aorella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same genus (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sphaerichthys acrostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphaerichthys selatanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphaerichthys vaillanti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small creeks with plenty of wood debris in which it camouflages by its mimicry of a dead leaf, coloration and swimming positions (Ref. 56749).  Observed in pairs (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Sphaerophysa dianchiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphagemacrurus decimalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphagemacrurus gibber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Sphinx dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphinx goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Occurs on sandy or sparse seagrass substrata of protected reefs.  Hovers just above the bottom and takes refuge in a burrow,  Ref. 48637.

species.name: Sphoeroides andersonianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphoeroides georgemilleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sphoeroides nitidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphoeroides rosenblatti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit inshore waters to 4 m depth in brackish-water estuaries, amongst mangroves and river mouths.

species.name: Sphyraena iburiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow coastal water inhabitant (Ref. 54823).

species.name: Sphyraena intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected using gill nets, trawl nets, seining and 'lampara' engine. Stomach contents include remains of cephalopods, Sardina pilchardus or Sardinella aurita, a young Sphyraena sphyraena, and fluid materials. Some were infected in the stomach and gonads by the anisakid nematode Anisakis sp. (Ref. 82428).

species.name: Sphyraena tome
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sphyraena waitii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spicara australe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spicara axillare
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore during bad weather.

species.name: Spicara martinicum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spider-eye puffer
species.description: Inhabit shallow water, often subjected to surge.  Juveniles secretive and remain in holes of outer reef flat and reef margin (Ref. 37816).  Adults on shallow reef flats in high energy zones to about 10 meters depth.  Juveniles among small boulders (Ref. 48637).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed mainly on algae, but also takes polychaetes, sea urchins, brittle stars, mollusks, tunicates, corals, crustaceans and sponges.

species.name: Spikedace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky runs and pools and often occurs near riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Spikefin blenny
species.description: Inhabits empty mollusk tubes on rocky reefs.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Spikefin glass blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Dark males photographed in holes in both live and dead corals, of several species and of different morphologies, including holes embedded among encrusting sponges. The IP individuals are mostly photographed on live coral substrate (Ref. 125603). Depth range given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Spikefin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas with live coral, rubble, and sand (Ref. 9710, 48637, 58302).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Secretive and not associated with burrows or prawns (Ref. 9710, 48637).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Spiketail gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spiketail paradisefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found in ditches, paddy fields and shallow water not far from tidal influence (Ref. 1479).  Prefer stagnant or slow-flowing water with thick vegetation such as grasses, roots and floating plants.  Feed on insects and zooplankton.  A bubble nest builder.

species.name: Spiketail platyfish
species.description: Inhabits fast flowing river with an average depth of 2 m. Occurs with other livebearers, Xiphophorus hellerii and Heterandria jonesi.

species.name: Spikey bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Spiky oreo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit continental slopes (Ref. 9563), forming large shoals over rough ground near pinnacles and canyons (Ref. 6390).  Juveniles are pelagic and tend to be dispersed over smooth grounds (Ref. 6390).  Feed on salps, fish, crustaceans and squid (Ref. 27230).  Eggs float near the surface and larvae also inhabit surface waters (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Spinach pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not well known, few specimens collected upstream 35-100 km from the sea.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spinaker grenadier
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spindle hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, rocky sediment-free habitat.  Feeds on 'aufwuchs' attached  to rocks, but also takes small invertebrates, including zooplankton when this is abundant (Ref. 267).

species.name: Spine bahaba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Spineback guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. More or less stationary in inshore coastal waters to moderate depth. Feeds on benthic invertebrates, mainly crustaceans.  Common length is  60-66 cm TL. Males mature at ca. 42 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous. Produces small litters of 1-3 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spinecheek anemonefish
species.description: Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), found mainly in protected coastal waters and lagoons. Typically found in pairs in which males are much smaller than females (Ref. 48636). Feed primarily on zooplankton and benthic algae (Ref. 4966). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemone Entacmaea quadricolor (Ref. 5911). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35404, 35413, 35420). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Spinecheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty bottoms of inner lagoons and bays (Ref. 9710).  Solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Also occurred in shallow to deep coastal sand and mud flats, usually on the sand near large depression  with burrow in the middle (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Spined anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  Adults frequently visit the lower reaches of  mangroves where neritic conditions are present (Ref. 43081).  More specimens and data needed.

species.name: Spined pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock and coral habitats of lagoons and seaward reefs from the surf zone to a depth of 40 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spined whiff
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Visually orienting ambush predator (Ref. 53012).

species.name: Spineless sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minumum depth reported at 0 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Spineless toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow, sandy estuaries in small aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Spinesnout soldierfish
species.description: Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spinibarbus babeensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus brevicephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus caldwelli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in swift waters (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Spinibarbus denticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in the deep pools of streams.

species.name: Spinibarbus hollandi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus maensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus nammauensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus ovalius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinibarbus vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spiniphryne duhameli
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught with a 3-m Isaacs-Kidd mid-water trawl fished open (Ref. 57704).

species.name: Spinipterus acsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep water species (Ref. 6902).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 25 cm TL, females at ca. 29 cm TL; size at birth unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spintherobolus ankoseion
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower elevations of coastal blackwater streams that drain the surrounding forests.

species.name: Spintherobolus broccae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dark-brown swamp waters.  Appears to be found in somewhat acid waters in relatively lowland areas, in both swamps and slow moving streams, but only in areas where the streams remain unpolluted.

species.name: Spintherobolus leptoura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spintherobolus papilliferus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spiny batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most specimens are taken less than 100 m (Ref. 85070).

species.name: Spiny blaasop
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Spiny cat-fish
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Spiny chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Also found in harbors, lagoons and outer reef slopes.  The only pomacentrid species that lacks a pelagic larval stage.  One of the very few marine fishes where fry are guarded by the parents (Ref. 9710, 48636).  School as they grow and sub-adults are usually seen in small groups.  Adults form pairs and are territorial when breeding (Ref. 48636).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spiny cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools of rocky shores, among rocks and seaweed beds in bays (Ref. 43239).  Oviparous, eggs are guarded by the female parent (Ref. 58332).

species.name: Spiny dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Found around outcrops on sand or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Spiny dreamer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds heavily on crustaceans (Ref. 4525).  Males are not parasitic on females (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Spiny eel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coarse sand bottoms with weed and sponge.  The species has been taken by trawl in 4 to 8 m from Exmouth Gulf and at 60 m in the Arafura Sea.

species.name: Spiny flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow (about 20 m) mud and sand bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9774).  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9774).  Marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9774).

species.name: Spiny grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spiny guitarfish
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Size is based on original stuffed specimen, now in British Museum (Ref. 6902).

species.name: Spiny hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spiny lantern fish
species.description: Neustonic (Ref. 58302).  High-oceanic and mesopelagic; nyctoepipelagic at the surface.

species.name: Spiny pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from the continental shelf (Ref. 9563) from depths between 114 m (Ref. 58489) and 230 m (Ref. (9563). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spiny pugolovka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Does not enter freshwater areas (Ref. 26334).

species.name: Spiny red gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the tropical to warm temperate areas (Ref. 9771), in sandy or sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Spiny sea bat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563, 75154) and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spiny seadevil
species.description: Espèce de poissons abyssaux. Meso- (Ref 58302) and bathypelagic (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Females with long movable teeth outside jaws.  Mature males parasitic on females.

species.name: Spiny searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spiny snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 227 m (Ref. 51661).

species.name: Spiny squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 11897. Solitary and cryptic, found in outer reef slopes of oceanic islands, mainly in the South Pacific (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spiny waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inshore, usually muddy-sand habitat, estuaries and coastal slopes (Ref. 48635). Sways back and forth with current surge, mimicking dead leaves and other debris (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spiny-eye threefin
species.description: Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spiny-tailed leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Spiny-tufted frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives at moderate depths in sponge zones (Ref. 48635); occurs in seaward reef flats. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178. Coral and Rocky reefs in 0-130 m, more common between 30-40 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spinycheek lanternfish
species.description: Type de poisson. Benthopelagic and mesopelagic in slope and oceanic waters, but usually not high-oceanic.  Occurs in the upper 200 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Epipelagic in nearshore areas at 0-856 m (Ref. 58302).  Occasionally seen during dark nights on slopes that are near very deep water.  Attracted by light like moths, becoming disoriented and darting frantically in all directions (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Spinycheek scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Have a thick glandular tissue on posterior margin of fin spines which is believed to be venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Spinycheek seabass
species.description: Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spinycheek soldierfish
species.description: Inhabits deep rocky slopes (Ref. 7251) and reefs (Ref. 51183).

species.name: Spinycoat anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 75154) and temperate species (Ref. 7300) found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Spinyface soldier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic  in or near crevices and caves at 9-348 m (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Spinyfin Perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spinyfin velifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563, 75154) and slope (Ref. 559); also on seamounts (Ref. 559).

species.name: Spinyhead cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A viviparous, benthic species found on the lower continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154, 93007).  Rare species (Ref. 34024).  A 5.7 cm SL  female with full developed embryos (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Spinyhead sculpin
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Spinynose sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and shell bottoms near rocky outcrops (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Spinyskin velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rubble bottoms in 10-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spinysnout pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock or coral habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at about 10 cm SL. Also seen in sheltered water, often on rubble bottoms in 2-12 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spinytail lampfish
