species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Spinythroat scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rough bottom.

species.name: Spirinchus lanceolatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns in rivers.

species.name: Spirlin
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Inhabit streams and rivers in foothills with well oxygenated, fast-flowing water.  All age classes occur in open water of streams and small rivers (Ref. 59043).  Found also in rivers with very calm waters.  Feed on insect larvae and dead insects (Ref. 9696), as well as on crustaceans and diatoms.  Spawn in small groups and lay eggs deep into gravel with swift current.  Locally threatened by stream regulation, trout stocking and pollution.  Attain a maximum size of up to about 13 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Splash tetra
species.description: Feeds on worms, insects and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Splendid darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Splendid dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lagoon and seaward reefs.  Prefers drop-offs, usually close to corals and sponges.  Usually solitary, occasionally in pairs.

species.name: Splendid garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Single to small aggregations (Ref. 48635). Live individually in burrows from which they protrude.  Feeds on drifting plankton (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Splendid hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaward reefs, at the bases of coral heads or on hard bottom (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Splendid killifish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Splendid lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably demersal on the outer continental shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 31367).  Feeds on squids (Ref. 31367).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Splendid pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually associated with offshore coral-reef areas in relatively deep-water habitats over rubble bottoms (Ref. 116679).

species.name: Splendid sea perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 7300), near rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Splendid seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Splendid spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams.  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Split-ray pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species collected from jetty pilings, log debris, and concrete stairs at the water’s edge, at about 1-4 meters.  It apparently have an affinity for sponge-encrusted surfaces, but the general area where it is observed is characterized by extensive silty mud substrata inhabited by a large number of burrowing gobies. It was not previously observed despite nearly 100 hours of scuba-diving  because the collection site is immediately adjacent to shore at a busy shipyard where diving is usually banned during daylight hours. Most of the specimens were found on the inner side of a single pillar of the jetty, which was situated in total shade (Ref. 119492).

species.name: Splitbanded goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits algae-covered rocky or rubble reefs (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Splitfin flashlightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hides during the day and venture out at night to feed, tending to occur along steep drop-offs near caves on dark, moonless nights.  Feeds on zooplankton.  The large, deep water form is occasionally collected by fishing at depths of 200 to 400 m.  Caught with cast nets in shallow waters of the Philippines. Forms aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Splitlevel hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranging into subtropical zones as juveniles expatriate caused by warm currents during pelagic stage (Ref. 48636).  Adults inhabit coral-rich outer reef slopes at depths of 5 to over 20 m, particularly near caves.  Juveniles in caves; adults swim openly about, but usually close to the substrate, and often engage in cleaning larger fishes (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Splitnose rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common offshore, on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Young occur in shallow water, often at surface under drifting kelp (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae and pelagic juveniles (Ref. 36715, 34817).  The biggest individuals are sometimes found in markets where the flesh is sold as rockfish fillet (Ref. 27436).  Rarely caught by anglers (Ref. 27436).)

species.name: Splittail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and backwaters and pools of rivers.  Tolerant of brackish water (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Sponge anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs inshore (Ref. 7300, 75154); associated with sponges (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sponge cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs and rocky bottoms, frequently inhabiting cylindrical sponges like Verongia fistularis, Callyspongia plicifera, and Callyspongia vaginalis (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Sponge ghostgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water on sponges and soft corals in depth of 25 meters or more (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Sponge goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate sponge dwellers. Live deep within canals of the sponges, near the openings to the incurrent canals. Sponges provide species with protection from predators and an available food source in many invertebrates. Eggs found within sponge or small plankton brought through incurrent pores (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Spongy rat tail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spookfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are encased in horny shells (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spoon-snouted catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spot fin parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water on coral reefs with high coral cover; primarily on reef crest and slope habitats (Ref. 72409).

species.name: Spot pangasius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Inhabits deep pools in the river (Ref. 37770).  Found in rapids and riffle (Ref. 37771).  Enters flooded forest (Ref. 9497).  Artificially reared fry of 3.5 mm at 12 hrs., 8.4 mm at 4 days, 8.8 mm at 8 days and 23 mm at 18 days.  Larval teeth present in 12 hr and 4 day larvae.  Feeds on shrimps, small fishes, gastropods and plants (Ref. 6459).  Migrates into floodplains and spawns at the beginning of the flood season (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Spot-fin green barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spot-lined flasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on bases of steep outer reef slopes, above rubble or coral (Ref. 9710).  Found on rubble bottoms that are exposed to strong currents occasionally  (Ref. 90102).  Occurs in small groups (Ref. 2139) of mix sexes but females outnumber males (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Spot-nape butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral-rich areas of coastal reefs, feeding mainly on coral polyps and anemones (Ref. 9710).  Occurs solitarily or in pairs (Ref. 90102). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spot-nape cardinalfish
species.description: In clear lagoons with deep sand slopes, forming schools above remote rock or coral outcrops to 30 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 75154). Forms aggregations (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spot-stripe dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at 45° slope with mixed sand-rubble substrate; at least four male-female pairs were observed, several were solitary (Ref. 56434).

species.name: Spot-tail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow and sheltered waters of swampy bays. Generally restricted to shallow waters where they may be found in various habitats such as over sand, rock or, less frequently, in aquatic weed beds (Ref. 13337). Common in shallow vegetated areas (Ref. 4967). Also found in large rivers and floodplain pans and lagoons. Feeds on insects, tiny fishes, vegetable matters (Ref. 5595) and crustaceans (Ref. 13337). Main predator is the tigerfish (Ref. 7248). Breeds in summer, migrating to spawning sites after rains. Migrates to tributary rivers and floodplains when the rivers come down in spate (Ref. 13337). Known to mass at river mouths while waiting for suitable conditions to trigger off the breeding migrations upstream (Ref. 13337). Used as live bait for tigerfish and large catfish (Ref. 13337). Affinities: B. carolinae, with lateral stripe; B. nigricauda with wide black margin on caudal fin.

species.name: Spot-tail butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most commonly found in reef channels and outer slopes (Ref. 90102). Occur in coral rich areas of reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs. Juveniles inshore. Adults usually seen in pair (Ref. 48636). Feed on soft coral polyps (e.g. Litophyton viridis and species of the genera Sarcophyton, Nephthia, and Clavularia) (Ref. 9710). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spot-tail golden bass
species.description: Inhabits rocky slopes and ledges.  When approached and illuminated by the submersible, it retreated into small caves and crevices (Ref. 95858).

species.name: Spot-tail perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Trawled (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spot-tailed dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found on reef flats and on lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Spot-tailed pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotback goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in reefs and rock outcrops surrounded by sand (Ref. 11482).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spotback loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit fast flowing streams with a rock or pebble substrate (Ref. 116162).  Found usually browsing among pebbles in shallow, flowing water.  Can ascend steep inclines and also occurs in even the highest mountain streams (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Spotback skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsule measures 92-103 mm long and 72-80 mm wide (Ref. 41249).  Utilized as fishmeal (Ref. 6077).

species.name: Spotback wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotbanded scat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal estuaries, river entrances and rock pools (Ref. 9002, 44894).  Inhabits mangrove creeks and the lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).  Anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland (Ref. 57406).  Sometimes sold fresh in markets (Ref. 43044).  Juveniles collected for the aquarium trade (Ref. 43044).

species.name: Spotbelly plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only species of the genus with conspicuous ventral spots.  Adults maybe nesters due to low absolute fecundity (Ref. 52020).

species.name: Spotbelly tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotbreast angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally seen in pairs on steep outer reef slopes, drop-offs (Ref. 9710), in caves or along the bases of boulders (Ref.48636); in  rich coral growth interspersed with sand (Ref. 37816).  Usually occurs in loose groups of females dominated by a male.  Sometimes feeds on plankton high above the substrate (Ref.48636).

species.name: Spotbreast dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from coral reefs in harbours and near mangrove areas (Ref. 81967).

species.name: Spotcheck stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, on rock bottoms (Ref. 11230) or sandy beaches (Ref. 42788); also in estuaries (Ref. 42788).  Good food fish (Ref. 42788).

species.name: Spotcheek blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky or coral bottoms with clear water (Ref. 13628).

species.name: Spotcheek cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal mud flats and reefs to 10 m depth (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).  Very cryptic and rarely seen, even at night (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Spotcheek goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocky substrata where it may be observed "perched" on a rock or cliff face, or protruding from a crevice.  Does not form large aggregations.  Preys upon various benthic invertebrates but will "grab" small planktonic organisms that continually drift in the current and surge (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Spotfin anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble bottoms with strong current.

species.name: Spotfin betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow (about 30 cm deep) near stagnant pools along stream bed with substrate consisting of clay (Ref. 56613).  Occurs also in waterfalls with fast flowing clear water; occupies small pools in tributaries and quiet pools along the main confluence of the river (Ref. 56613).  A mouth brooder (Ref. 56613).

species.name: Spotfin cardinal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Spotfin chub
species.description: Found in rocky riffles and runs of clean small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Juveniles are associated with small gravel substrates and moderate current, while adults are encountered in swift currents and boulder substrates.  Feed on aquatic insects, predominated by midge, blackfly, and caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Spotfin corydoras
species.description: Occurs upstream.  Prefers to live in small, moderately sunny  and shallow creeks with sandy to sandy-muddy  bottoms.  Also occurs on the edges of stagnant zones of flooded forests (dams, lakes).  Populations living on darker substrates have more and larger spots.  Sexual dimorphism is well marked, the pectoral fins in the male are markedly longer and thicker due to the presence of a number of spikelets (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Spotfin cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotfin dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy or sandy bottoms (Ref. 13628).  Neither opercular spine gland nor anterolateral glandular groove with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spotfin fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy bottom; sticks halfway out of holes and when spooked, disappears down into its hole (Ref. 117352). Caught by hand net or clove oil (Ref. 117352).

species.name: Spotfin gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers calm, heavily vegetated coves and inlets.

species.name: Spotfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms.  Shares burrow with alpheid shrimp.

species.name: Spotfin goby cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Surf-dwellers, they occur among the pebbles on the shoreline often solitary.  Feed on tiny crustaceans which are attached to rocks (Ref. 6770).  Exhibit biparental mouthbrooding (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Spotfin hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimens reach  cm TL (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Spotfin jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Continental species (Ref. 26893).

species.name: Spotfin killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits salt marshes.  4 cm max TL (Ref. 7251).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139). Omnivorous and feed on detritus, diatoms and a variety of small crustaceans, insects and worms (Ref. 93252).

species.name: Spotfin scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic in or near coral (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Spotfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand bottom.  Feeds on shrimps (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Spotfin squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A secretive species during the day (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Spotfin surfperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the surface up to 101 m (Ref. 96339). Rarely caught from surf and piers by sport fishermen.  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotfin tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spothead dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spotjaw blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotless lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9824).  Feeds on bottom-living animals (Ref. 9824).  Taken in shrimp trawls (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Spotless nape plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotless plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range:  2,473-2,542 m, the deepest record for Pogonophryne (Ref. 5181).

species.name: Spotless podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef.  Benthic (Ref. 75154). Cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spotless spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality, Manimala River, is highly sinuous and generally rocky with deep pools at certain locations and sand deposit occurring as sporadic patches or fillings in the pools.  It has more or less scanty riparian vegetation.  The river has bed materials generally of coarser grade and very low sand content. The width of the river channel ranges from 45-110 m and water depth in the active channel during summer seasons ranges from 0.5 m-3 m.  This species occurs together with the following fish species:  <i>Anguilla bengalensis, <i>Salmostoma boopis, <i>Danio malabaricus, <i>Barilius bakeri, <i>Gonoproktopterus kurali, <i>Rasbora daniconius, <i>Puntius mahecola, <i>Haludaria fasciatus, <i>Pethia ticto, <i>Dawkinsia filamentosa, <i>Systomus subnasutus, <i>Batasio travancoria, <i>Ompok malabaricus, <i>Clarias dussumieri, <i>Heteropneustes fossilis, <i>Mesonoemacheilus triangularis, <i>Bhavania australis, <i>Xenentodon cancila, <i>Aplocheilus lineatus, <i>Parambassis thomassi, <i>Etroplus maculatus, <i>Etroplus suratensis, <i>Anabas testudineus, <i>Pristolepis malabaricus, <i>Mastacembelus armatus, <i>Macrognathus guentheri, etc. (Ref. 97143).

species.name: Spotlight goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep waters (Ref. 5521).  Found on tube sponges on deep reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Spotlight lanternfish
species.description: Oceanic and mesopelagic, found between 425-750 m during the day and between 40-550 m at night (most abundant below 200 m at night) (Ref. 4066, 4775).  There is size stratification with depth both day and night (Ref. 4775).

species.name: Spotlight rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotnape cardinalfish
species.description: Occur in groups around coral bommies (Ref. 2334).  In Japan, the breeding season is from June to September.  Breeding pairs set up territory which is mostly defended by the female (Ref. 57690).  Mouthbrooding is done by the male parents (Ref. 559 and 637) some of which resort to partial egg cannibalism probably to adjust the brood size to their buccal capacity (Ref. 57690).  Nocturnal species, but courtship and spawning takes place during day (Ref. 7300, 37227, 38747).

species.name: Spotnape ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal and brackish waters (Ref. 41299, 48635).  Aggregates in schools.  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 637).  Commonly caught by anglers (Ref. 637).  Produces sound (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Spotside wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in shallow, quiet water, over a silty to sandy bottom, close to the ocean (Ref. 48399).

species.name: Spotstripe pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotstripe snapper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in tide pools and rocky shores.  Adults spawn in shallow water in spring, supporting evidence of seasonal migration.

species.name: Spottail barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet, well-vegetated waters where it feeds from the surface or on small invertebrates living on plant surfaces (Ref. 7248).  Requires well oxygenated waters and usually not found in small or headwater streams (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Spottail chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spottail darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools and adjacent riffles of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723); also found in streams (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Spottail goby
species.description: Occurs over rubble from shallows of open coasts to nearly fresh water (Ref. 7251).

species.name: Spottail leporinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spottail tonguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays and shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Spottail wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted algae eater
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Found on solid surfaces in flowing waters (Ref. 12693).  Occurs in riffle and rapids during the dry season (Ref. 37769).  Feeds on aquatic chlorophytes (Ref. 37769).  Large adults are often seen in the markets of the upland Mekong (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Spotted and barred blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 559).   Adults live in abandoned worm tubes, solitary or in loose groups (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spotted angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 43239).  FishBase common name agreed by authors.

species.name: Spotted anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted armoured-gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm tropical seas along the continental shelf edge and slope and insular areas (Ref. 9771).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spotted barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from sea level to at least 2000 m above sea level and is commonly found below waterfalls in isolated mountain streams and on small islands inhabited by few other freshwater fishes (Ref. 2091).  Inhabits medium to large rivers, stagnant water bodies including sluggish flowing canals and brooks of the middle Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Found in middle to bottom depths in fairly shallow waters where it feeds on zooplankton, insect larvae and some vascular plants.  Probably does not migrate (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Spotted bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear, gravelly flowing pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 6465); also found in streams, lakes and reservoirs (Ref. 10294).  Juveniles feed on small crustaceans and midge larvae while adults eat insects, larger crustaceans, frogs, worms, grubs and small fish (Ref. 6465, 10294).

species.name: Spotted batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mouth brooder (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Spotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically found in the surge zone of coral reefs from 0-8 m deep (Ref. 529).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spotted blenny (Starksia guttata)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small creeks, swampy marshes, heavily shaded rainforest streams, lily lagoons and backwaters adjacent to major water courses.  Usually found in Pandanus-lined creeks with muddy bottoms.  Aggregations are encountered in areas with abundant vegetation and submerged log debris (Ref. 44894).  Occurs at temperatures and pH ranging from 23°-30° C and 5.2-6.7 respectively.

species.name: Spotted bullhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep rock-bottomed or sand-bottomed pools of small to medium swift rivers and impoundments.

species.name: Spotted cardinalfish
species.description: Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Nocturnal, under ledges or in caves by day (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Spotted citharinid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large, slow flowing vegetated rivers (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Spotted coral croucher
species.description: Inhabits shallow reef crests, usually exposed to moderate surge (Ref. 48635). Common among the branches of pocilloporid corals (e.g. Pocillopora eydouxi, Stylophora mordax) and some species of Acropora.

species.name: Spotted ctenopoma
species.description: An air-breathing species (Ref. 118402).

species.name: Spotted cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found on sandy bottom from the shore to 280 m (Ref. 34024).  Adults often burrow tail-first in sand, live in mucus-lined holes (Ref. 2850), mud, eelgrass and rock rubble (Ref. 36413).  Mostly active at night and on overcast days (Ref. 2850).  Important food for sea lions and cormorants (Ref. 2850).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae and extended pelagic juvenile (Ref. 36413).  Oval, pelagic eggs float in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in fast, rocky riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Spotted dick dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from fringing reefs, gullies with sand, encrusting corals, and algae and large bommie surrounded by coarse sand, coral rock, and algae, both habitats at 0-6 m depth (Ref. 109221).

species.name: Spotted dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow seagrass beds.

species.name: Spotted dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow reefs with mixed algae and coral growth to about 15 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Occurs in coastal and insular areas.

species.name: Spotted eel blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted fanfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep waters.

species.name: Spotted flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Frequents shallow areas in depths of 10 m or less.  Taken in trawl fisheries at depths from 23 to 250 m.  Reported from a trap in the Gulf of Aqaba at a depth of 300 m.  Young to juvenile stages utilize mangrove habitat (Ref. 9790).  Adults occur in silty sand habitats from the shallows to a depth of 300 m (Ref. 37816). Also found in coastal sand patches, near coral reefs but more often on offshore (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spotted frillgoby
species.description: Inhabits intertidal seaward reef flats (Ref. 37816, 48637). Also found in shallow reefs near shore (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Spotted garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is currently known only from the type locality, about 80 km southwest of the town of Kaimana, West Papua Province, Indonesia. The type specimens were obtained from two separate colonies in 13-25 m, wherein each occupy about 50-100 sq. m and containing approximately 50-100 eels. The gently sloped bottom consisted of clean white sand and was more than 200 m from the nearest reef habitat (Ref. 121836).

species.name: Spotted gelatinous cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Viviparous. Relatively often caught by commercial trawlers for it also occurs on the upper continental slope (Ref. 128809).

species.name: Spotted ghoul
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Inhabits sandy bottoms near reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406). Also found in rubble and mud bottoms in 5-90 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spotted goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to forested areas and small, shallow, slow flowing silted streams with leaf debris and thick marginal vegetation.  Stays close to the substrate and is very seldom found in unshaded waters.  Feeds on fish fry, plankton and insect larvae.  Bubble nest builder.

species.name: Spotted green goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur primarily along coastlines and in estuaries, but also found in freshwater.  Occasionally marketed (Ref. 12693)

species.name: Spotted green pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit freshwater streams, rivers and floodplains.  Feed on mollusks, crustaceans, and other invertebrates, as well as some plant matter.  May eat scales and fins (Ref. 12693).  Seen in the aquarium trade but known to be aggressive with its tankmates (Ref. 12693).  Aquarium keeping:  needs salt; minimum aquarium size 60 cm; not recommended for home aquariums  (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Spotted grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Spotted guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal inshore on continental shelf to 70 m depth. Feeds on small crustaceans and fishes. Matures at ca. 62 cm TL; born at ca. 25 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Produces litters of up to 7 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spotted gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf and slope (Ref.9563).  The depth range is indicated 60-320 m in Ref. 89357.

species.name: Spotted halibut
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone above 100 m (Ref. 11230).  Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms in coastal areas (Ref. 9137, 11230).  Cultured and released for fishery in Japan.

species.name: Spotted hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly coastal and estuarine, often schooling with C. capreoli, Atherinomorus endrachtensis and A. ogilbyi. Diet includes crustaceans and diatoms. Breeds from December to March throughout the southern hemisphere. Appears to have a one year life span. May be food fish for larger commercially important fishes.

species.name: Spotted hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small crustaceans, larvae and mosquitoes (Ref. 26543).  Aquarium specimens reach 9.0 cm TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Spotted headstander
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found from subtidal rocky areas to 56 m depth, usually in seaweed.  Female lays white eggs in seaweed, male guards egg mass (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Spotted killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on temporary pools, floodplains, swamps, rice fields, ditches and small streams (Ref. 3788). A slow-moving fish usually found in sections of a river where aquatic vegetation provide some cover (probably as a means of avoiding predators). Feeds on mosquito larvae, small crustaceans and other aquatic organisms (Ref. 6465). Used for mosquito larva control. Collection for the aquarium trade is controlled (Ref. 7248). Bottom spawner, 3-5 months incubation; it is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Spotted knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted knifejaw
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky and coral reefs.  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115, 58302).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Spotted lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Spotted leporinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in creeks with swift water flow, over sandy and rocky bottoms.  Prey on invertebrates (Ref. 12225).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places.  Males tend to remain near the nesting site (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted long-tom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species (Ref. 9682).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow water at depths of 3 m or less (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted metynnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fish feeds on fruits and plants, and in extreme conditions or in captivity, may go for fish, crustaceans or maybe meat, but still are not considered dangerous.

species.name: Spotted minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted mountain trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in still or slow-flowing waters at low elevations close to the sea; most abundant along shore margins in rocky areas.  Found around plants, rocks or logs on the margins of still or flowing rivers, streams and lakes (Ref. 44894).  The species has a marine juvenile stage, indicative of a diadromous life cycle.  Spawning takes place from autumn to winter, among aquatic vegetation.  Newly hatched larvae drift downcurrent and out to sea where they spend their first few months, eventually returning to fresh water during spring among annual whitebait migrations.  In lacustrine and other landlocked populations, adults move upstream into feeder streams to spawn.  The larvae are then swept downstream into lakes (Ref. 44894).  Feeds mainly on aquatic and terrestrial insects.

species.name: Spotted mud carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted notothen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A nearshore benthic species usually abundant in shelf waters of East Antartica (Ref. 122792). Adults feed primarily on amphipods, other fishes, and molluscan larvae, with lesser amount of polychaetes and mysids.  They capture some prey in the water column, but are not cryopelagic.

species.name: Spotted numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 9912).  Occurs over soft bottoms; feeds on bottom-living organisms; possesses electric organs (Ref. 68964). Biology little known (Ref. 9912). Gravid females produces 2-3 pups during each gestation. Males mature at ca. 14 cm TL; born at ca. 6 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spotted perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves.

species.name: Spotted pike-characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted pike-conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Spotted pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually among vegetation in bays and estuaries, but sometimes offshore among floating Sargassum. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may be brooding at 11.2 cm TL.

species.name: Spotted prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in patches or expanses of coarse carbonate sand on outer lagoon and seaward reefs.  Inhabits coastal to outer reef sand slopes to 25 meters depth (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Spotted rainbow wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits high altitude (150-800 m) swamps and creeks.  An egg laying species which prefer the following aquarium conditions:  pH=7.8, H=12, 25°C water temperature.

species.name: Spotted redlined pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on middle and outer reefs (Ref. 100726).

species.name: Spotted ricefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs near the coast but may live in fresh water as well as in brackish habitats (Ref. 27658).

species.name: Spotted righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a depth of 252 m.  Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Spotted rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur along exposed rocky shores (Ref. 9962).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spotted Salta livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted sand catlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fairly shallow water (Ref. 13337).  Occurs over sand, usually buried with just the eyes protruding.  Feeds on minute organisms.  Eggs few (12-16) and large (3-5 mm diameter) suggesting possible parental care (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Spotted sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in steep sand slopes in large aggregations (Ref. 8631).  Hovers above clean sandy bottoms; darts into the sand when disturbed.  Usually slightly silty habitat.  Usually seen resting on substrate, leaving substrate to grab prey from zooplankton floating over, or when displaying (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Spotted sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on rubble bottoms of coral reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Spotted shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found inshore on mid-continental shelf. Biology little known. Maturity size of only two males known at 48-50 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spotted skiffia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used for cancer research.

species.name: Spotted sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers of low to high current velocity and stagnant waters between sea level and 100 m elevation, generally occurs in freshwaters but sometimes in slightly brackish river mouths.  More abundant near the coast and only large individuals are found upstream.  Benthic species that lies waiting for prey, shrimps and fish under stones or overhanging shorelines (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Spotted snailfish
species.description: Occurs in tide pools and other intertidal areas (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Spotted snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found within weed litter at the base and amongst roots of seagrass.

species.name: Spotted sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear water coastal bays on white-sand substrates, shallow to deep water (Ref. 48637).  Lives on sand bottoms.

species.name: Spotted sorubim
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds mainly on fishes (Ref. 26762).  Utilized for human consumption (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Spotted spikefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with still to moderately flowing clear water and mud bottom (Ref. 59043).  Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranging from estuaries to the continental shelf (Ref. 42788).  Feeds on demersal fishes (Ref. 42788).  Minimum depth range from Ref. 121942.

species.name: Spotted stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf and inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Found partly covered with sand near seagrass beds (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Spotted stinkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from coastal waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Spotted sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits long deep pools of small to medium rivers over clay, sand or gravel.  Occasionally found in creeks, large rivers and impoundments (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on organic detritus, copepods, cladocerans, midge larvae and diatoms (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Spotted sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits heavily vegetated ponds, lakes, pools of creeks and small to medium rivers, and swamps (Ref. 205).  Usually occurs over mud or sand.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Feeds on midge larvae, other immature insects, and microcrustaceans such as amphipods and cladocerans (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Spotted thicklip loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spotted tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in still or flowing waters in rocky or mud-bottom areas (Ref. 44894). Occur in warm springs and mud-bottomed to sand-bottomed canals (Ref. 5723). Clearly prefers a herbivorous diet, including algae, higher plants and parts of cassava, but also accepts insects and shrimps (along with their eggs) (Ref. 52307). Consume plant matter. Reache sexual maturity at 10-15 centimeters length. Parents prepare nest site on logs, leaves and other debris. Prolific species (Ref. 52307). The eggs (600-3300 per female) are guarded by the parents and hatch in 1-3 days. Larvae need 6-8 additional days to develop before they can swim freely (Ref. 52307). Parental care of the brood continues until the fish are about (1.5 cm, Ref. 52307) 2.5-3.0 centimeters (Ref. 44894). Occurs in mixed groups composed of individuals of varying size/age, along with individuals of other species (Ref. 52307). Pair-bonding, open (Ref. 52307) substrate brooder (Ref. 52307, 81260) with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307). Maximum size was recorded at 39.4 cm TL (Ref. 40637).

species.name: Spotted tinselfish
species.description: Found on the continental slope.  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spotted whiff
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hard sand bottom from water's edge to 18 m depth, occasionally to 90 m.

species.name: Spotted worm goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky coasts, including tide pools.  Feeds on zooplankton and tiny benthic crustaceans.

species.name: Spotted wriggler
species.description: A benthic, inshore species found in coral reefs (Ref. 75154). Also found in sand patches among reefs and rubble, often in surge areas (Ref 90102).

species.name: Spotted yellowfin seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotted-belly catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed by dive operators in North Sulawesi and Ambon on night dives at depths of 3 to 15 m (Ref. 100516).

species.name: Spotted-gill cardinalfish
species.description: Found in coral reefs, more commonly in aggregations among branching corals (Ref. 36661, 48635).

species.name: Spotted-sail goby
species.description: Collected from oolite sedimentary rock. Also found in sand habitats with rubble, gravel and shells (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Spottedback coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal reefs (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Spottedfin dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs, inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Spottedsail barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear streams and rivers (Ref. 4832).  Found in standing waters, over silt and mud (Ref. 41236).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Spottedtail morwong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commercially cultured in Japan.

species.name: Spottobrotula mahodadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spottobrotula mossambica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spottobrotula persica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spotty
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water, but may reach to depths of 145 m (Ref. 26203).  Feeds on small benthic organisms.  Uses its forward-jutting front teeth to rake food from the substrate (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Spotty blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shoreline reefs and sheltered lagoons (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Spotty seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300), in caves and beneath ledges (Ref. 33839).  Probably also at depths greater than 22 m (Ref. 33839).  Secretive (Ref. 33839).  Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Spotty-bellied greenling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seaweed beds of coastal waters.  Juveniles occasionally seen among floating seaweed.  A food fish; taken by angling (Ref. 559, 637).

species.name: Spotty-fins sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sprat de Madagascar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in freshwaters, possibly tolerating brackish water (Ref. 188); from sea level to about 450m, mostly in smaller rivers and streams and usually in forested areas (Ref. 56161). Probably planktivorous (Ref. 56161).

species.name: Sprat de Malabar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries, lagoons and as much as 10 km up rivers, presumably tolerating a wide range of salinity.  Reported to feed exclusively on rotifers (Ref. 6028).  Marketed fresh or dried salted.

species.name: Sprat des iles Falkland
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species found in coastal waters.  Food item of hakes, sea birds and seals in the Patagonian Falkland waters (Ref. 27363).

species.name: Spratelle de Guinée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found chiefly in rivers and streams, also man-made and natural lakes (Ref. 188); also in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 188, 2683). Apparently able to tolerate moderate or even quite high salinities (Ref. 188). It forms enormous shoals in both inshore and offshore regions of Lake Kainji (Ref. 3034). It feeds on terrestrial and aquatic insects, but also ostracods and entomostracans; stomachs containing clupeid fish scales may represent cannibalism (Ref. 188). Reproduction occurs in rivers and lakes, and may be also in estuaries and coastal lagoons (Ref. 2683). It breeds from July to September in Lake Volta (Ref. 188).

species.name: Spreadfin skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outer continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 114953). Moderately deep water species (Ref. 6902). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 51cm TL, females at ca. 59cm TL; hatching size unknown (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Spring cavefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in springs and caves (but almost always near surface).  They live underground but emerge above ground in springs (Ref. 5723).  Active in springs at night and usually retreat underground during the day.  The few individuals which venture into the spring portions of their habitat may show strong rheotaxis for half to one-minute periods but usually show strong thigmotaxis and hide under rocks or debris (Ref. 34868).  Feed at night on amphipods, midge larvae, tiny worms and micro-crustaceans.  Fecundity averages about 100 eggs per female (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are carried in gill chambers of females (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spring Chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep outer reef slopes and drop-offs with rocky outcrops and small caves and holes, often in association with limestone talus; usually observed in pairs or small groups, feeding low in the water column, and are generally abundant where they are found (Ref. 59379).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Spring pijor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and springs with clear water. Occurs in subterranean water during winter or droughts. Threatened due to water abstraction and introduction of Salmo trutta and Oncorhynchus mykiss (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Spring pygmy sunfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, clay, mud and/or limestone substrate commonly associated with rooted, submerged vegetation (Ref. 58011). Oviparous, eggs are deposited in aquatic vegetation, preferably on strands of Ceratophyllum sp. when available (Ref. 58020).

species.name: Springer's barbelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ingle specimen collected from sloping reef in 15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Springer's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit upper edge of outer reef slopes (Ref. 90102), 0-18 m deep (Ref. 529).  Found in shallow and protected inshore reefs with sparse coral and rich algae growth (Ref. 48636).  Also found in coral reef crevices.  They feed on algae and detritus.   Usually occur in small loose groups but are shy species and are easily missed by divers that are not on the look-out for blennies (Ref. 48636).  Collected from water shallower than 10 m to as great as 18 m in the Ninigo Islands.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Springer's clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coral reefs at 1-10 m deep (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Springer's coralbrotula
species.description: Solitary inhabitant of coral reef crevices between about 8-20 m, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Springer's demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral-rich areas of sheltered lagoon and inshore coral reefs (Ref. 9710). Seen with similar yellow-tailed species, often on the same coral patches. Mostly found in aggregations on coastal reef slopes with low Acropora patches on sand to 30 m (Ref. 48636). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Springer's dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives near reefs on sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth of 0 m reported from Ref. 34729.

species.name: Springer's sand-diver
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in sloping sand bottoms to 73 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Springer's sawtail cat shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Springer's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live on rock surfaces and under ledges, commonly at depths less than 10 m (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Springer's wriggler
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a steep-sided gully with caves.

species.name: Springeratus polyporatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Springer’s coral blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only from a small area in the Kokas District on the northern coast of the Fakfak Peninsula of West Papua Province, Indonesia and relatively common in its coral-reef habitat, perching on a variety of substrates including live corals, tunicates, sponges, and algae. The type locality is at a small, roughly circular islet with a diameter of about 850 m, lying approximately 8 km from the mainland and the surrounding waters have characteristics more typical of estuarine habitats, i.e. with lowered salinity, high turbidity, and sedimentation, and frequently elevated sea-surface temperatures up to about 31°C. It has been suggested that this unusual combination of conditions, and the general geographic isolation of the coral reef areas of the Fakfak Peninsula may account for its suite of microendemic species (Allen et al. 2018, Ref. 118654) (Ref. 120749).

species.name: Springer’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Spurcheek lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic species (Ref. 4066).  Found between 425-750 m during the day and at 40-500 m at night, with maximum abundance at 75 m (Ref. 4479).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Specimens reach sexual maturity at a length of 5.4 cm.  Off southern Brazil found between 500-900 m during the day and 25-300 m at night. (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Squale bouclé du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A large, sluggish shark occurring on continental and insular shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Feeds on a variety of fishes, other sharks, octopi and squids (Ref. 13564).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with up to 114 in a litter (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Squale mignon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably oceanic (Ref. 5578).  The holotype was caught off a beach, but a second specimen was taken in the Atlantic at night between the surface and 502 m (Ref. 247).  Food unknown but may subsist on pelagic fish and invertebrates (Ref. 247).  Probably ovoviviparous with very few young (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squale moustache
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the uppermost continental and insular slopes, and probably the outer continental-insular shelves (Ref. 31367).  Probably feeds on bottom fishes and some invertebrates (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 10 pups in a litter (Ref. 247).  Although not utilized commercially, the liver is relatively high in squalene oil (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Squale nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic, wide-ranging, tropical pelagic species occurring near continental and insular land masses, sometimes over the shelves, but usually over the slopes (Ref. 247).  Displays vertical migrations on a diel cycle, seen at the bottom during the day and travels to 200 m at night (Ref. 247).  Feeds on deepwater squid, lanternfish, gonostomatids and idiacanthids, and probably follows its prey on their diel migrations (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Has well-developed photophores densely covering the ventral part of the body and sparsely seen on the sides and hardly developed on the dorsal surface (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squale pygmée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi-, meso-, and perhaps bathypelagic at 1->400 m (Ref. 58302).  Occurs at or near the surface at night, descending to below 400 m (possibly as deep as 1,800 m) during the day (Ref. 31367).  Feeds on squid, bony fishes, and crustaceans (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 8 young per litter, size at birth between 6 and 10 cm (Ref. 247).  Caught with dip-nets and buckets at night (Ref. 6577).

species.name: Squale savate
species.description: Found on the outer continental and insular shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Usually on or near the bottom but sometimes found well above it (Ref. 5578).  Apparently in large schools (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on pelagic bony fish, squid, octopus and shrimp (Ref. 5578). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Caught very rarely by demersal longline fisheries operating in deepwater of Indonesia. Utilized for its meat, fins (low value) and liver oil (very high value) (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Squale à queue claire
species.description: Prince syrien. Probably oceanic but also near the upper slope (Ref. 5578).  The holotype was caught in a bottom trawl between 457 and 640 m, a second specimen was collected in the open ocean near the surface at less than 25 m (Ref. 247, 5578).  Food unknown but the powerful jaws and sharp teeth suggest that this species can take relatively large prey (Ref. 247).  Probably ovoviviparous with few young (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squale-chagrin bilimélé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 6871, 75154). Presumably ovoviviparous (Ref. 6871). Smallest mature male recorded at 82.5 cm TL (Ref. 76933). Longevity assumed to be high similar to close relative C. zeehaani with estimated longevity exceeding 46 yrs (Ref. 107026).

species.name: Squale-chagrin de l'Atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on or near the bottom of continental slopes; also found pelagically in the upper 1,250 m of water 4,000 m deep (Ref. 31367).  Presumably feeds on fish and cephalopods (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized and fishmeal and dried salted for human consumption (Ref. 247); meat and fins (low value) and liver oil (very high value), and occasionally for its mature eggs (Ref.58048).

species.name: Squale-chagrin à longue dorsale
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A large deepwater dogfish of the outer continental shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bony fish, small dogfish sharks, squids, and lobsters (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Utilized as food fish and as fishmeal (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squale-grogneur chien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 26346) presumably inhabiting the insular slope of New Zealand (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Squale-grogneur commun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species (Ref. 26346) inhabiting continental slopes (Ref. 247).  Usually mesopelagic although taken most often near the bottom (Ref. 10717).  Its razor-edged lower teeth is used to attack and dismember large prey (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Utilized dried salted for human consumption and for fishmeal (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squale-grogneur à queue échan.
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Demersal or pelagic near continental slopes and seamounts in depths of 550-2,000 m (Ref. 6871, 58302).  Also found from the surface to 580 m over deep water (Ref. 26346).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Used dried and salted for human consumption and for fishmeal (Ref. 6871). Caught rarely by longline fisheries operating in deepwater; also caught, but rarely landed, by pelagic tuna longline fisheries (Ref.58048).

species.name: Squale-savate lutin
species.description: Found on the upper continental and insular slopes, on or near the bottom (Ref. 247).  Feeds on small benthic and midwater bony fishes, squid, and crustaceans (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Minimum depth reported from taken from Ref. 5578.

species.name: Squale-savate rude
species.description: Found on the insular slopes.  No record of food items.  Ovoviviparous, size of litter not known but a female with 12 large eggs suggests moderate-sized litters.

species.name: Squale-savate à long nez
species.description: A rare (Ref. 26346) and little-known species found on outer continental shelves and upper slopes (Ref. 247).  Feeds on bony fishes (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Squalelet dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A very rare species known only from few localities in epipelagic waters. Apparently feeds on small epibenthic and epipelagic invertebrates and fish.  Its powerful jaws, big mouth and enormous lower teeth enable it to bite off large portion of its prey in one sweeping motion.  A facultative ectoparasite evidenced by its suctorial lips and feeding apparatus.  It has extremely short snout and anteriorly positioned eyes which allows for binocular vision (Ref. 247).  Caught by mid-water trawl (Ref. 55584).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Has large oily liver which helps it to become neutrally buoyant (`hepatic float').

species.name: Squalelet féroce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species (Ref. 247).  Epi- to bathypelagic at 1-3500 m (Ref. 58302).  Makes diurnal vertical migrations from below 1,000 m in the day to or near the surface at night (Ref. 6871, 58302).  Travels long vertical distances in excess of 2,000 to 3,000 m on a diel cycle (Ref. 247).  Feeds free-living deepwater prey such as large squid, gonostomatids, crustaceans but is also a facultative ectoparasite on larger pelagic animals such as wahoo, tuna, billfishes, and cetaceans (Ref. 247).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with 6-12 young per litter (Ref. 48844).  The cookiecutter shark has specialized suctorial lips and a strongly modified pharynx that allow it to attach to the sides of it prey (Ref. 247).  It then drives its saw-like lower dentition into the skin and flesh of its victim, twists about to cut out a conical plug of flesh, then pull free with the plug cradled by its scoop-like lower jaw and held by the hook-like upper teeth (Ref. 247).  Teeth are shed as a complete unit; the lower teeth are swallowed, perhaps to maintain sufficient calcium levels in its body (Ref. 247).  Interconnection at the bases of individual tooth allows a whole row of teeth to move if one tooth is touched.  This shark is reported to radiate light for as long as three hours after its death.  Not dangerous to people because of its small size and habitat preferences (Ref. 247).

species.name: Squalidus argentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus atromaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with sandy to muddy substrate (Ref. 43281).

species.name: Squalidus banarescui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lentic waters of middle and lower reaches of rivers, on sandy, pebble bottoms (Ref. 41299).  Omnivore (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Squalidus homozonus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus iijimae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus intermedius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes of plains, pools on flood plains, and lentic irrigation canals, on mud or sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 41299).  Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Squalidus mantschuricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus minor
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus multimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus nitens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalidus wolterstorffi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Squalius agdamicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius alburnoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in schools in lowland rivers and lakes.  Feeds on invertebrates, chiefly small crustaceans and insect larvae.  Breeds in April-May among aquatic plants and on stony bottoms in shallow water.  Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).  The species is unique as it represents a stable all-male lineage nested within an almost all-female hybrid lineage (Ref. 49905).

species.name: Squalius albus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in open water.  Grows up to at least 20 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius aradensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An ubiquitous species which inhabits small to medium sized streams with Mediterranean water regime.  May be restricted to very small pools during summer.  Breeds in shallow riffle habitats in fast-flowing water (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius castellanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius illyricus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with swift water and lakes in karstic areas (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in water courses on low plains, with little current.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Threatened due to habitat destruction, pollution and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Squalius janae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from small rivers which become shallow in summer, often partly dried, and where fish survive in remaining pools.  The river flows over a bare limestone bed, alternating with silted pools and the Dragonja section had clear and colorless water, temperature of 21.4°C, pH 8.8, a mineralization of 0.32 gl-1, and has slow current.  No other fishes were caught in the stream.  Both females and males adults with completely ripe gonads, were found in the middle of May and at the beginning of July; post-spawning adults in July. The smallest mature male was 10.14 cm SL and adult males retain the nuptial tubercles until at least August. Stomach contents of specimens collected (April 10, 2009) upstream from the confluence of Dragonja and Pinjevec, contained no food, while those collected at the same date but 5 km downstream, contained algae, plant remains and detritus; the difference is coincident with the spring water temperature rise and start of plant growth in the areas of sampling (Ref. .84537).

species.name: Squalius keadicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits springs and streams with fast flow and open water (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in deeper waters of the river and in the ditches of lowland, preferring places where current is slow.  Found over stony, gravelly and sandy bottoms.  Omnivore.  Feeds throughout the water column (Ref. 26100).  Preys predominantly on aquatic insects.  Eggs are adhesive, 2 mm in diameter (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Squalius kosswigi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius laietanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with clear water, gravel bottom and prefers moderate flowing stretches (Ref. 75108).

species.name: Squalius lepidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rivers and lakes.

species.name: Squalius lucumonis
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in small to medium-sized premontane streams with Mediterranean water regime.  May be confined to very small pools during summer (Ref. 59043).  Inhabits brooks, brooklets and small rivers.  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 26100).  Spawns in shallow riffle habitats in fast-flowing water (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to the introduction of other species, pollution (Ref. 26100), habitat alterations and water abstraction (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius malacitanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with clear waters and gravel bottoms and prefers moderate flowing stretches (Ref. 72459).

species.name: Squalius microlepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes and still water.  Adults prey on juvenile fishes. Spawns along lake shores.  Threatened due to overfishing (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius peloponnensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams to rivers with moderate to swift current.  Feeds on a variety of plant and animal food.  Spawns adhesive eggs of 1.8 mm in diameter in gravel (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius platyceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius prespensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along shores of lakes (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius pyrenaicus
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in rivers and marshlands (Ref. 26100). An ubiquitous species which inhabits small to medium-sized streams with Mediterranean water regime. May be confined to very small pools during summer. Feeds mainly on small arthropods. Spawns on stone to gravel bottom in shallow riffle habitats with fast-flowing water. Involved in the Iberocypris alburnoides hybrid complex (Ref. 59043). Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and the introduction of other species (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Squalius squalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mainly small rivers and streams with riffles and pools. May be confined to very small pools during summer. Also found along shores of slowly flowing lowland rivers, even in very small mountain streams and in large lakes, undertaking spawning migrations to inflowing streams or spawning in very shallow water, over stones close to surf zones. Feeding larvae and juveniles occur in very shallow shoreline habitats. Juveniles are gregarious while adults are more solitary. Feeds on various aquatic and terrestrial animal and plant material. Large individuals feed mainly on fishes. Breeds in shallow riffles with fast-flowing water. Often forms hybrids with Alburnus arborella and Alburnus albidus. Attains up to at least 60 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius svallize
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in streams with swift water, lakes in karstic areas and enters subterranean waters (Ref. 59043). Adults inhabit water bodies on the low plains, with little current.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Threatened due to pollution, the introduction of other species and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Squalius tenellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing and still waters and lakes.  Enters subterranean waters during winter or droughts.  In lakes, adults feed on small fishes.  Threatened due to water abstraction, pollution and its small range. Its sharp decline in 20th century was attributed to habitat loss and pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius torgalensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An ubiquitous species which inhabits small to medium-sized streams.  May be confined to very small pools during summer.  Breeds in shallow riffle habitats with fast-flowing water (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius ulanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalius valentinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams with clear waters and gravel bottom and prefers moderate flowing stretches (Ref. 72459).  Threatened due to water abstraction for agriculture, construction of reservoirs and introduction of exotic species (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squalius vardarensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with flowing, clear water.  Grows up to about 16 cm SL (Ref.  59043).

species.name: Squalius zrmanjae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with swift water and lakes in karstic areas.  Restricted to the lower, almost still part of Zrmanja drainage (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Squaloliparis dentatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squalus brevirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from the continental shelves, sometimes at depths greater than 130 m (Ref. 57879).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 559).

species.name: Squalus lalannei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Square-spot fairy basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aggregations of this species occur a few meters above the edges of current-swept drop-offs (Ref. 4538).  Females and males in separate aggregations or mixed sexes (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles solitary and remain close to shelter (Ref. 37816).  Seldom encountered in the aquarium trade (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Squarechin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Squarehead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers, beels, canals and ponds (Ref. 1479).  Prefers soft substrates where it lies concealed in the soft mire of the river bed.  It depends upon this concealment for protection and will not even move when it is touched lightly.  Lies quietly on the bottom until  some prey comes along (Ref. 6868).  Apparently a worm-like appendix at the fringe of the mouth is used to attract prey (Ref. 50926).  Fairly common in catches, but is not eaten perhaps due to its ugly appearance.

species.name: Squarenose unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep drop-offs of offshore coral reefs or rocky outcrops (Ref. 37792).  Feeds on algae and larger zooplankton (Ref. 37792). Solitary or in groups (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Squarespot rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow reefs (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Squaretail triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squashed face rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Only known from a few specimens.

species.name: Squatina armata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Squatina varii
species.description: Occurs along continental slope (Ref. 114945).

species.name: Squiggly blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in algal ridge and crests between surge channels of exposed seaward reefs (Ref. 205, 58302).  Usually taken in water less than 10 m deep, but has been collected at depths as great as 19 m  (Ref. 529).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 89972). Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Squire's fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Squirrelheaded catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore and turbid brackish waters and tidal reaches of rivers (Ref. 38478).  Probably feeding on mollusks or thick-shelled crustaceans (Ref. 38478).

species.name: Sri Lanka bagrid catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sri Lanka dwarf catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers with mud or sand substrate (Ref. 79815).

species.name: Sri Lanka giant snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occurs primarily in the deep pools in the Mahaweli River and its tributaries. Also recorded from reservoirs in the Mahaweli catchment (Victoria and Randenigala). Around 20 juveniles (ca. 8.0-10.0 cm SL), guarded by a pair of adults, were observed in shallow water (ca. 60-80 cm deep), among submerged roots, close to the bank, at the mouth of a stream draining into Badulu Oya of the Mahaweli basin. The highest recorded elevation from which this species was found was about 500 m asl at Kandy (Ref. 127648).

species.name: Sri Lanka labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs primarily in rivers, but also observed among the fisheries catch in dry-zone reservoirs. The species is largely restricted to the lowland floodplain of both the dry and the wet zones (demarcated by the 2000 mm/yr isohyet) and it was observed also within the tidal influence of estuaries, suggestive of its tolerance of salinity. This species is abundant wherever it occurs but is of minor importance to inland fisheries (Ref. 118635).

species.name: Sri Lanka swamp barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sri Lanka sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often encountered on reefs or rocky substrata in small aggregations (Ref. 106074).

species.name: Sri Lankan flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: St Brandon's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from drop-offs, surge channels and coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 57771).

species.name: St. Brandon’s sandy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: St. Helena chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky or rubble reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: St. Helena deepwater scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its soft white flesh is considered excellent eating (Ref. 5288).

species.name: St. Helena seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably occurs around rocks and coral reefs (Ref. 7423)

species.name: St. Helena Sharpnose Pufferfish
species.description: Occurs in tide pools and to depths of up to 45 m (Ref. 43205). Also found in rocky areas to at least 50 m depth; adults often in pairs (Ref. 86997).

species.name: St. Helena wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment needs verification.

species.name: St. Maarten pejerry
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Staghorn ghostgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on Acropora coral. Usually in 3-15 m, but occasionally to 30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Stalix davidsheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from 17 m depth (Ref. 33021).  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Stalix flavida
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Stalix immaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stalix novikovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stalix sheni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stalix toyoshio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Stalkeye scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stamen dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from a depth shallower than 100 m, by a mid-water trawl that was targeting the Sakura-shrimp (Lucensosergia lucens) (Ref. 121636).
