species.name: Stanaland's sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from silty sand with sparse seagrass area.

species.name: Star pearlfish
species.description: Common species (Ref. 34024). Found in starfishes (mainly) and holothurians (Ref. 4104), usually in a male - female pair (Ref. 11228). Benthic (Ref. 58302). In Micronesia, it prefers the pincushion starfish Culcita novaeguinae for a host. Also known to occur in certain holothurians (Bohadschia argus, Stichopus sp.) on rare occasions (Ref. 1602); for the first time with Isostichopus fuscus along the coast of Ecuador (Ref. 57700).

species.name: Star-spangled goby
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected from the lower intertidal zone on a narrow reef flat exposed to strong wave energy and were found living in small water-filled crevices in the reef pavement. Observed to be fairly abundant on the reef flat where it was collected, with an estimated
five to 10 individuals per m2  in the lower intertidal zone (Ref. 116852).

species.name: Star-spotted perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starck's demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky outcrops and crevices that are frequently situated in sand channels on outer reef slopes.  Common in deeper sections of the outer reef about 20 to 60 m in depth (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Stardrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy to sandy bottoms of estuaries and adjacent areas (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Stareye lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic and mesopelagic species, adults and juveniles usually found at 200-500 m by day and the majority of them migrate into upper 100-200 m at night.  Feeds mainly on small crustaceans.  Dioecious with peak spawning during summer.  Adult photophore complement attained at about 25-27 mm SL (Ref. 4778).

species.name: Stargazer mountain catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers clear, flowing water in rocky habitats (Ref. 52193). It feeds on stream insects and other small organisms off rock surfaces (Ref. 52193). Breeds in summer; juveniles are easily mistaken for tadpoles (Ref. 52193). Preyed upon by trout and probably eels (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Stargazer snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most commonly found in sand and mud, near coastal reefs at depths of 1 up to at least 10 m. Burrows into the sand tail-first until only its eyes and the top of its snout are visible. Sometimes seen with only its head or snout protruding from the sand. More commonly encountered at night but also seen with its head protruding out of the substrate during the day. Observed with cleaner shrimp Periclimenes magnificus on its head. The shrimp would swim off for short periods and then return to this species (Ref. 42180). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 2334).

species.name: Stargazing darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast gravel runs of clear, medium-sized rivers.

species.name: Stargazing minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble runs and riffles of clear, fast creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on dipteran and caddis larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Stargazing seadevil
species.description: Also mesopelagic (Ref. 4494).

species.name: Stargazing stonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud bottoms in estuaries. Also found in sand bottoms of estuaries and coastal waters in 2-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Starhead killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly in the shallow and weedy parts of brooks, small streams and swamps in the rainforest (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Bottom spawner, 1 month incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Starhead topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated standing water bodies and quiet pools and backwaters of streams (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Maximum length 7.8 cm TL  (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on terrestrial insects, snails, small crustaceans, and some algae (Ref. 10294).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Staring pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic (Ref. 6601, 58302, 75154).  Adults have been captured at depths in excess of 500 m, although they have also been captured in the upper 150 m at night.  Larvae have usually been taken in hauls restricted to the upper 100 m.  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 10755).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35929).

species.name: Stark's tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits patches of talus or rubble of steep outer reef slopes. Usually seen in pairs that quickly dive headfirst into their burrow when disturbed. Juveniles occasionally school with similarly colored juveniles of Pseudanthias pascalus. Stomach contents of 6 adult specimens consisted of copepods (31.4% by volume), pelagic tunicates (31%, larvaceans, plus Oikopleura), fish eggs (28.6%), siphonophores (5.5%), larval shrimps (1.2%), fish (0.8%), amphipods (0.7%), unidentified decapod larvae (0.5%), and heteropods (0.3) (Ref. 8991). Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27115.

species.name: Starksia brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species.

species.name: Starksia culebrae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia greenfieldi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia langi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia nanodes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits patch reefs and coral heads in relatively deep water (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Starksia sangreyae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia splendens
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia springeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia variabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia weigti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starksia williamsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stark’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Starry blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow, protected inshore reefs and in estuaries to depths of about 15 m (Ref. 48636); also on sand-weed areas on rocky outcrops.  They form small groups, usually seen near reef rubble margins of coral reefs (Ref. 48636).  Also found solitary on rock or coral outcrops (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Starry clingfish
species.description: Partially digested crinoid pinnules were found in the stomach of a specimen suggesting a diet of L. polyastrous similar to that of L. lineatus (Ref. 129525).

species.name: Starry flying gurnard
species.description: Found on the shelf and shelf edge (Ref. 11230), over sandy bottoms in coastal areas.  Feeds on benthic crustaceans (Ref. 5213).  Rarely used as food.

species.name: Starry goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on algal-coated reef rock and rubble of inner flats and turbid lagoons (Ref. 1602).  Takes refuge in burrows or holes in the reef (Ref. 11441).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972). Solitary or in small group (Ref 90102).

species.name: Starry pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Fairly deep-dwelling pipefish (Ref. 559).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Starry rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually found on deep reefs (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae and pelagic juveniles (Ref. 36715).  Occasionally captured by sport fishers (Ref. 2850). Minimum depth range from Ref. 96339.

species.name: Starry smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found in areas with steeply inclined slopes.  Ovarian eggs relatively large (1.8 mm in diameter) and few (96 in a female of 10 cm).

species.name: Starry toado
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Starrynose stingray
species.description: This species probably prefers shallow, fresh or brackish water habitats (Ref. 84289).

species.name: Stars and stripes leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly in deep coastal reefs, in sponge areas (Ref. 9002).  Young are mainly found with kelp (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Stars-and-stripes snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be found hiding among spines of Diadema.

species.name: Stathmonotus tekla
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steatocranus bleheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear flowing water with rocks, in river pools; found in small groups, up to 20 individuals (Ref. 42983). Likely a pair-bonding, cave-spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatocranus gibbiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; feeds primarily on mollusks (snails); pair-bonding, cave spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatocranus glaber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; seems to feed on diatoms and other small particles; pair-bonding, cave spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatocranus mpozoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding and cave spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatocranus rouxi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding and cave spawning species (Ref. 52307). Maximum TL was recorded at 7.5 cm (Ref. 5696).

species.name: Steatocranus tinanti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding and cave spawning species (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatocranus ubanguiensis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding and cave spawning species; in contrast to congeners, it seems the male guards eggs and
wrigglers, while the female is primarily engaged in defending the territory (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Steatogenys duidae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from small streams.

species.name: Steatogenys ocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stedman barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and rivers at foot hills (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Steelcolor shiner
species.description: Inhabits rocky and sandy runs, less often pools, of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Common near riffles (Ref. 5723, 86798).

species.name: Steene's prettyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthic which occur inshore (Ref. 7300).  They inhabit coral reef (Ref. 75154).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Steene's scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on reef areas (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Stegastes lividus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species; on hard substratum (Ref. 39287).  Adults are collected usually from bays and many from tide pools (Ref. 54980).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Stegastes sanctaehelenae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky or rubble reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Stegastes uenfi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Stegastes xanthurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stegophilus insidiosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A true parasite living in the gill chambers of larger fishes, including catfishes like Sorubim lima. It uses its strong teeth to bite into the gill filaments to suck the blood (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Stegophilus panzeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stegophilus septentrionalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stegostenopos cryptogenes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stein's dwarf snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steindachner's cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers.  Feeds on snails and smaller fishes.  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7, H=3, 25°C water temperature, carnivore, egg layer, needs plant and rock cover, not easy to raise in tanks (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Steindachner's moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow seaward reefs to over 30 m.  Common in holes or crevices at the base of corals or rocks (Ref. 9710).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Steindachneridion amblyurum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Steindachneridion scriptum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Carnivorous (Ref. 79585).

species.name: Steindachnerina atratoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steindachnerina bimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in ponds.

species.name: Steindachnerina dobula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately flowing waters adjoining sandbars.  Stomachs contain bottom detritus.

species.name: Steindachnerina elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steindachnerina leucisca
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steindachnerina quasimodoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steindachnerina seriata
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Collected in flooded areas along the margin of the river among stands of dense aquatic
vegetation (Ref. 88964).

species.name: Steindachnerina varii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to live in groups of a few individuals.  Feeds on algae (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Steindachner’s cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Steinitz' prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy areas of outer lagoon and seaward reefs, with a pale brown or marbled brown and white alpheid shrimp (Ref. 1602).  Also found in estuaries and usually at moderate depth of about 20 meters on deeper slopes (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Steinitz' velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stelgistrum beringianum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A recent reference acknowledging the validity of this species is needed.  Minimum depth reported at 52 m (Ref. 5610).

species.name: Stelgistrum stejnegeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stellar goby
species.description: Inhabits coral rubble in 0-10 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Stellar gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stellar rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rocky shorelines (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Stellate codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum size given for a juvenile specimen which may be paedomorphic (Ref. 37039).

species.name: Stellate pencil wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble zones with prominent kelp and other macroalgae growth. Also collected by hand net and rotenone (Ref. 123183).

species.name: Stellate scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on rocky substrata on a vertical rock wall (Ref. 109716).

species.name: Steller's sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the littoral zone (Ref. 26334), over rocky reefs (Ref. 559).  Enters rivers (Refs. 2058, 37812).

species.name: Stellifer brasiliensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stellifer chaoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand or muddy-sand bottoms of brackish waters and nearby areas.

species.name: Stellifer ephelis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stellifer gomezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stellifer magoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy and sandy bottoms of estuaries with low salinity (Ref. 9626).

species.name: Stellifer naso
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy or sandy mud bottoms of estuaries and its adjacent areas.

species.name: Stellifer venezuelae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy or sandy bottoms of estuaries and it adjacent areas.

species.name: Stemonosudis bullisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on immature specimen (Ref. 37039).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Stemonosudis distans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stemonosudis elongata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epi- to mesopelagic in habitat (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Stemonosudis gracilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species (Ref. 26340) occurring from about 20 m (young) to about 500 m depth.  Known only from juvenile specimens, probably attains more than 20 cm (Ref. 4056).

species.name: Stemonosudis intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The young occur near the surface, adults up to 800 m and more.

species.name: Stemonosudis macrura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic in tropical waters (Ref. 4056, 58302).  Known only from juvenile specimens, probably attains 25 cm (Ref. 4056).  Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 35950).

species.name: Stemonosudis miscella
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stemonosudis molesta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Stemonosudis siliquiventer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenodus nelma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the pelagic zone at the sea with salinity up to 20 ppt.  Inhabits large lowland and piedmont rivers and lakes.  Prefers cold water with temperatures below 16° C.  Forages and overwinters in lower reaches of large rives, deltas, estuaries and sea, sometimes far from coast.  Anadromous or semi-anadromous, living in some rivers and landlocked in some lakes. Undertakes migration to spawn in rivers, moving upstream for long distances, up to uppermost reaches in European rivers.  Populations in the lake migrate into tributaries.  Juveniles prey on mysids, insect larvae and fry, shifting exclusively to piscivory at about 30 cm SL.  Actively feeds on all available fishes.  Spawning takes place over shallow waters with sand-gravel bottom and 2-3 m depth (Ref.  59043).

species.name: Stenogobius alleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater streams.

species.name: Stenogobius blokzeyli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenogobius fehlmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenogobius gymnopomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal waters, estuaries and tidal zone of rivers.  Feed on small fishes, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Stenogobius hawaiiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A poor climber and thus restricted to the lower reaches and adjoining brackish waters; found in both altered and unaltered streams; omnivorous and a benthic feeder on filamentous algae, worms, crustaceans and insect larvae; not highly sought as food by the early Hawaiians (Ref. 44091).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Stenogobius hoesei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from freshwater streams.

species.name: Stenogobius ingeri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and rivers in fresh water near the coast (Ref. 34009).

species.name: Stenogobius kyphosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported from rivers and estuaries over sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 34009).

species.name: Stenogobius laterisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large turbid rivers, lakes, lagoons, backwaters and small lowland tributaries.  Occurs on soft mud bottoms.

species.name: Stenogobius macropterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from brackish and freshwater streams.

species.name: Stenogobius marinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish and near marine waters in intertidal streams and estuaries.

species.name: Stenogobius mekongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and streams.

species.name: Stenogobius ophthalmoporus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from estuaries to lowland rivers and streams in fresh water.

species.name: Stenogobius psilosinionus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from lowland rivers and streams primarily over mud bottoms in fresh water.

species.name: Stenogobius watsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenogobius zurstrasseni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenolebias bellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, ? months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Stenolebias damascenoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Stenolicmus ix
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenolicmus sarmientoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stenorynchoacrum xijiangensis
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Inhabits underground caves connected to the surface river in the Karst area.  Remains in
the underground caves in the dry season and swims upward into the rivers during the flood season (Ref. 95674).

species.name: Step-spot pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits current-prone reefs in 12-70 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Stephanoberyx monae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults probably abyssal benthic (Ref. 51654).

species.name: Sterba's cory
species.description: Found in smaller rivers and tributaries, as well as flooded forest pools with soft, acidic waters. The habitats are characterised by swift flowing water with few plants.

species.name: Sternarchella duccis
species.description: Inhabit deep channels of white-water and black-water rivers (Ref. 13085); collected at low densities. Stomach content analysis indicates that it feeds entirely on the tails and scales of other electric fishes (Ref. 126780).

species.name: Sternarchella orinoco
species.description: Found in deep river channels and most commonly collected in the Amacuro estuary and Llanos floodplains (Ref. 126780).

species.name: Sternarchella orthos
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchella patriciae
species.description: Collected by trawling the river bottom where individuals inhabit deep river channels (10-20 m) during the day and move to shallower water at night to feed near the river margin and over flooded beaches. Stomach content indicates that these fishes feed primarily on larger-bodied (non-planktonic) aquatic insect larvae (e.g. Odonata and Ephemeroptera) and some juvenile fishes (Ref. 126780).

species.name: Sternarchella raptor
species.description:
Inhabit channels of white-water and black-water rivers (Ref. 13085). Stomach contents indicates that this species feeds on the scales and tails of other electric fishes (based on the presence of 
stacked scales, vertebrae and cartilaginous regenerated caudal filament rods) (Ref. 126780).

species.name: Sternarchella rex
species.description: Occurs over substrate comprised of mud and organic debris. Stomachs examined contained unidentified fish scales, skin and fine bones and aquatic arthropods were absent. Caught with seine nets deployed from the middle of the paraná channel to the edge (Ref. 126780).

species.name: Sternarchella schotti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchella sima
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchogiton labiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchogiton nattereri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchogiton porcinum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchogiton preto
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only in channels and major side branches of large whitewater and blackwater rivers (Ref. 75769).

species.name: Sternarchogiton zuanoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchorhamphus muelleri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternarchorhynchus curvirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Curvirostris tube-snouted ghost knifefish.

species.name: Sternarchorhynchus schwassmanni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sternoptyx obscura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Sternopygus aequilabiatus

species.name: Sternopygus branco
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the main channels of major rivers or side branches; not known to occur in seasonally inundated floodplain forests or in forest steams of the Amazon's terra firme. In the Tefé region, this species is caught with beach seines and trawl nets at depth up to 10 meters in areas with weak currents, such as in large eddies, sheltered bays or "paranás" (side-branches of the main river channels that wind their way through the whitewater "várzea" floodplain); occurs syntopically with Sternopygus macrurus in whitewater habitats, but never with Sternopygus atrabes. This species does not occur where currents near the substrate exceeded 0.1 m/sec. At daytime it is usually encountered near submerged structures such as fallen trees and driftwood, and at night it moves into shallower water and away from structures. Specimens are collected on both sand and mud bottoms. It does not live in groups as indicated by electrode surveys and its sporadic occurrence in nets. Sexually mature males were never encountered, but gravid females were found along the edge of whitewater floodplain areas and in paraná channels during the rising water months of January and February. Feeds mainly on autochthonous insect larvae which it encounters on the substrate; the presence of small pieces of wood in many of the stomachs indicate that it forages among organic detritus on the river bed rather than within rafts of floating meadows or marginal macrophytes (Ref. 55493).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in subtidal rocky to sandy areas (Ref. 2850).  Benthic; feeds on crustaceans and worms (Ref. 58426).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is a piscivore that breeds in rocky reefs where territorial males defend the vertical face of a large boulder near the sandy bottom (Ref. 87930).

species.name: Stigmatochromis modestus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found in the rocky habitat.  Feeds by ambushing its fish prey in the dark recesses of the habitat (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Stigmatochromis pleurospilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stigmatochromis woodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Larger specimens are normally encountered over the open sand at deeper levels.  Piscivorous.  Hunts its prey over the sand (Ref. 5595); usually in pairs or in large groups (Ref. 3817).

species.name: Stigmatogobius borneensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish streams (Ref. 56945).

species.name: Stigmatogobius elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow flowing river over sand and pebble substrate (Ref. 56945).

species.name: Stigmatogobius pleurostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stigmatogobius sadanundio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and tidal zone of rivers.  Prefers fresh water, rarely found in brackish water.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates, including mosquito larvae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Stigmatogobius sella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Brunei, both adults and juveniles were encountered frequently in small, shallow and clear, tannin-stained mangrove pools and rivulets among Nypa and Rhizophora roots and litter at low tide, usually well back from the main stream (Ref. 56945). In Indonesia, specimens were also collected from tannin-stained, fresh-tasting water, but a non-mangrove habitat (Ref. 56945).

species.name: Stigmatogobius signifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits blackwater streams (Ref. 56945).

species.name: Stimpson's goby
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Benthic in lower and middle reaches of streams (Ref. 58302).  Adults inhabit mountainous streams.  Are well adapted to exist in swiftly-flowing basalt-bottomed stream habitat (Ref. 26461).  Presence of these species signify water of good water quality (Ref. 44091).  Adults are primarily herbivorous, scraping algae off rocks, while the larvae are omnivorous; occasionally caught with nets ('upena), usually after being stupefied with native plants (e.g. hola and ahuhu), a process requiring partial diversion of the stream to reduce water flow; particularly prized in July and August when the females are gravid (Ref. 44091).

species.name: Stinging catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found mainly in ponds, ditches, swamps and marshes, but sometimes occur in muddy rivers.  Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549).  Can tolerate slightly brackish water.  Omnivorous.  Breed in confined waters during the monsoon months, but can breed in ponds, derelict ponds and ditches when sufficient rain-water accumulates.  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).  In great demand due to its medicinal value. Venomous fish, from its pectoral spines (Ref. 94495).

species.name: Stinging eel catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuaries and along open coasts.  Enters freshwaters of South Africa (Ref. 3879).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 3478).

species.name: Stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon alcedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults and juveniles inhabit freshwater streams, usually in pools. Often form shoals with conspecific individuals and the congeners Stiphodon percnopterygionus and Stiphodon atropurpureus, and occasionally with Stiphodon imperiorientis.

species.name: Stiphodon annieae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found in a clear, high gradient stream with rocky bottom and lives on the bottom of the river, on top of rocks. Assumed to be amphidromous (Ref. 100388).

species.name: Stiphodon atropurpureus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear streams and mainly feed on epiphyte and biofilm on rocks in the wild. Due to its possible amphidromous nature, as known to occur with its congeners (adults live and breed in freshwater streams; larvae hatched drift downstream and develop in marine environments; juveniles return to freshwater streams), blockage of the migration pathway (e.g. construction of dam or culvert in streams) would cause a significant impact on this species. Ensuring no net loss of habitat, keeping the natural stream flow and maintaining the stream-ocean corridor are all essential for preserving this species (in reference to its congeners; see Ref. 82682, 82684, 82689, 82690). Collection conducted by aquarium hobbyists (both private and commercial) also poses a serious threat to Stiphodon species in some regions (Ref. 82684) and this kind of activity should be strictly controlled (Ref. 82694).

species.name: Stiphodon aureofuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, high gradient stream with rocky bottom.  Occurs on the bottom of the river, perching on rocks, between 100 and 400 m in altitude. Assumed to be amphidromous (Ref. 105117).

species.name: Stiphodon aureorostrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams with slow moderate flow (Ref. 84801).

species.name: Stiphodon birdsong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, clear streams with rocky bottoms.

species.name: Stiphodon caeruleus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon de Donna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear and calm streams, sandy or slightly rocky bottom and large pools.  Found on the bottom of the river and observed from 5-10 m high in altitude (Ref. 72456).

species.name: stiphodon de Julien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in a clear, relatively swift rainforest stream, close to the coast.  Sexual dimorphism well developed:  sexual dichromatic color patterns well developed in both sexes; males with longer unpaired fins (Ref. 46975).

species.name: Stiphodon de Mele
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, high gradient streams with rocky bottom and lives mainly on the riverbed, on top of rocks, but also seen swimming in open water in the current between rocks or in large pools; observed from 10 to 100 m high in altitude.  It spawns in freshwater, the free embryos drift downstream to the sea where they undergo a planktonic phase, before returning to the rivers to grow and reproduce (Ref. 82682).

species.name: stiphodon des Marquises
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from clear streams over rock and boulder strewn bottoms close to the coast.

species.name: Stiphodon imperiorientis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit areas of boulders with a rock and gravel bottoms in clear streams (Ref. 28731) and mainly feed on epiphyte and biofilm on rocks in the wild. Due to its possible amphidromous nature, as known to occur with its congeners (adults live and breed in freshwater streams; larvae hatched drift downstream and develop in marine environments; juveniles return to freshwater streams), blockage of the migration pathway (e.g. construction of dam or culvert in streams) would cause a significant impact on this species. Ensuring no net loss of habitat, keeping the natural stream flow and maintaining the stream-ocean corridor are all essential for preserving this species (based on researches on its congeners; see Ref. 82683, 82684, 82685, 82689, 82690, 82692). Collection conducted by aquarium hobbyists (both private and commercial) also poses a serious threat to Stiphodon species in some regions (Ref. 82684) and this kind of activity should be strictly controlled (Ref. 82694).

species.name: Stiphodon incolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon larson
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively swift, clear freshwater streams with rocky bottoms.

species.name: Stiphodon maculidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon martenstyni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Like other sicydiine gobies, Stiphodon martenstyni is probably amphidromous (McDowell, 1992a, 1992b). While juveniles and adults live exclusively in freshwater, adults reproduce in freshwater, the eggs being cared for by males. Eggs in all sicydiine gobies studied usually hatch in about 24 hours (Erdman, 1961, 1986; Beyer, 1989) at which time the fry passively drift downstream and out to sea where they become part of the plankton layer. The time spent out at sea as planktonic fry is unknown. The returning fry can be likened to surfers: that is, when fry are able to detect the crest of waves to their new home. This follows a similar scenario presented in Erdman (1961) for Sicydium Valenciennes, 1837 from Puerto Rico (Ref. 44827).

species.name: Stiphodon multisquamus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear streams and mainly feed on epiphyte and biofilm on rocks in the wild. Due to its possible amphidromous nature, as known to occur with its congeners (adults live and breed in freshwater streams; larvae hatched drift downstream and develop in marine environments; juveniles return to freshwater streams), blockage of the migration pathway (e.g. construction of dam or culvert in streams) would cause a significant impact on this species. Ensuring no net loss of habitat, keeping the natural stream flow and maintaining the stream-ocean corridor are all essential for preserving this species (based on researches on its congeners; see Ref. 82683, 82684, 82685, 82689, 82690, 82692). Collection conducted by aquarium hobbyists (both private and commercial) also poses a serious threat to Stiphodon species in some regions (Ref. 82684) and this kind of activity should be strictly controlled (Ref. 82694).

species.name: Stiphodon niraikanaiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species was observed in a small pool less than 1 m deep and a rapid just below the pool, located 1.5 km from the stream mouth, no major barrier to upstream migration between the stream mouth and this site. The individuals were often shoaled with the abundant S. percnopterygionus and observed scratching on the rock surface for feeding with them. Single individuals of S. atropurpureus and S. multisquamus were also observed at the same site. Other abundant fishes found on the site were amphidromous gobies, such as Sicyopterus japonicus (Tanaka 1909), Awaous melanocephalus (Bleeker 1849), Rhinogobius nagoyae Jordan and Seale 1906, and Tridentiger kuroiwae Jordan and Tanaka 1927, amphidromous pipefish, Microphis leiaspis (Bleeker 1854), and catadromous flagtail, Kuhlia marginata (Cuvier 1829) (Ref. 95104).

species.name: Stiphodon noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The species is found in coastal steams, in clear and oxygen rich water, in the lower course of rivers, up to 50 m in altitude. It prefers rocky substrates, with boulders and pebbles, and slow to medium currents (pools). It feeds on algae and small invertebrates, scraping them of the surface of the rocks. The species is amphidromous. After the reproduction in freshwater, larvae go at sea where they undergo a planktonic life for several months (Ref. 87781). Inhabits large and quite streams, preferring pools and backwater areas. (Ref. 26040).

species.name: Stiphodon oatea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear and calm streams with sandy or slightly rocky bottom and large pools.  Lives on the bottom of the river.  Also observed from sea level to 40 meters high in altitude.  Possibly spawns in freshwater, with free embryos drifting downstream to the sea where they undergo a planktonic stage, before returning to the rivers to grow and reproduce, hence are amphidromous (Ref. 83881).

species.name: Stiphodon ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon palawanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in pools with a substrate composed of a mixture of boulders, gravel, and pebbles with exposed bedrock in some places.  Also found in rapids.  Two cyprinid species, <i>Barbodes palavanensis (Boulenger) and <i>Rasbora everetti Boulenger co-exist very abundantly with <i>Stiphodon palawanensis.  Syntopic with other  common fishes such as two gobioids, <i>Glossogobius illimis Hoese & Allen and <i>Redigobius sp., and a halfbeak <i>Dermogenys palawanensis<i> Meisner (Ref. 104909).

species.name: Stiphodon pelewensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stiphodon percnopterygionus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit small, clear streams with rocky bottoms usually covered with dense mats or clumps of algae (Ref. 28731).  This species produces small pyriform eggs, laid on the undersurfaces of stones in freshwater streams.  Newly hatched larvae are small (0.12-0.13 cm in notochord length) and poorly developed. These migrate downstream to the sea shortly after hatching at dusk, where they develop as pelagic larvae for 2.5-5 months. Pelagic larvae may potentially disperse to distant islands before migrating to freshwater streams when they reach 1.3-1.4 cm standard length (SL) where they grow further and reproduce (Ref. 95104).

species.name: Stiphodon pulchellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively swift streams over boulder and gravel bottoms (Ref. 26366).

species.name: Stiphodon rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, swift streams, sometimes close to the sea.  Collected also above a waterfalls.

species.name: Stiphodon rouge doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift, clear streams over rocky bottoms.

species.name: Stiphodon rubromaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, high gradient streams with rocky bottom and large pools.  Found on the bottom of the river, on top of rocks but also observed swimming in open water in the stream between rocks or in large pools; and observed from 90-200 m high in altitude (Ref. 72457).

species.name: Stiphodon saphir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear swift streams and has been found in streams from near sea level to well above small waterfalls at higher elevations (Ref. 56893).  Usually prefers to inhabit one of boulders and slab bottom streams usually with little or no sand and gravel (Ref. 56893).  Generally found in riffles but on occasion has been collected in swift waters above waterfalls (Ref. 56893).

species.name: Stiphodon semoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small, moderately flowing to swift clear streams with rocky and boulder strewn bottom, usually in sunny areas and has been collected above waterfalls (Ref. 33064).  Common in small rainforest creeks, often in hilly terrain, but usually within 30 km of the sea (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Stiphodon surrufus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit relatively swift streams over boulders (Ref. 26366).  Possibly amphidromous (Ref. 26364).

species.name: Stiphodon weberi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs with S. atratus in fairly wide streams and in rather calm waters, unlike most Stiphodon.

species.name: Stiphodon zebrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a small stream close to the sea.  Habitat is assumed to be similar to other related species which prefer clear rather swift waters in areas of rocks and boulders.

species.name: stiphodon à collier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, relatively swift rainforest streams with rocky bottom, close to the coast.

species.name: Stiphodon élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear, relatively swift rainforest streams, close to the coast (Ref. 26637).  Feeds on algae (Ref. 559).

species.name: Stippled clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common on limestone rocks and ledges in clear shallow water.

species.name: Stippled darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky pools of headwaters, creeks, and less often in small rivers; near springs and debris.

species.name: Stippled gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in seaweed areas of the intertidal zone (Ref. 559).

species.name: Stippled studfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits margins, pools and backwaters of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Most commonly found in shallow sandy backwaters of clean rocky creeks.  12 cm max TL (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Stippled wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stlengis distoechus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stlengis misakia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stlengis osensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stobbs' pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups in caves and ledges. Also found in steep seaward slopes in 10-40 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Stocky anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 75154).  Usually occurs in groups on well-protected reefs of lagoons or bays (Ref. 2334, 48635).

species.name: Stocky Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. Recorded from a small (0.8 m average width and 0.1 m in average depth), cold, clear and fast flowing alpine creek, flowing through an open forest of Eucalyptus, low shrubs and tussock grass, and which is often snow covered during winter. Flow consisted predominantly of riffle and glide, with smaller amounts of cascades. Substrate composed of bedrock, boulder, and cobble, with smaller amounts of pebble and gravel, and sections of silt. Instream cover provided mainly by rock and by bank and vegetation overhang, and pools averaged 0.3 m in depth. Recorded at a density of 1.8 fish/m2 and the only native fish so far recorded from within its range (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Stokell's smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Migrates into the estuaries and lower reaches of rivers during spring.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.description: Espèce de poissons. An oceanic (Ref. 4783) and mesopelagic species (Ref. 4464).  May migrate to near-surface waters at night (Ref. 4783).  Feeds on midwater fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4783).

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Stomias lampropeltis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 27000).

species.name: Stone cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams (Ref. 12045), common in hill-stream (Ref. 6351). Found in mountain rapids (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Stone cockscomb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly intertidal, but may be found at depths as much as 100 m (Ref. 43939); typically found shallower than 50 meters (Ref. 51666).  Often in bays with pebble-rock debris bottoms (Ref. 43939).  Oviparous, eggs are guarded by the female parent (Ref. 58332).

species.name: Stone darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stone flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms in coastal areas (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Stone goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries and backwaters (Ref. 4833).  Common along the margins of streams where the flow is slower (Ref. 41236).  Predominantly found in fresh water, migrating up to torrential streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Stone sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in the littoral zone, occurring exclusively over stone or sand.  Spawns near shore at depths not exceeding 1.5 m, from the end of May to mid July.  About 600 eggs are deposited under stones during spawning.  Spent females move away to deeper waters (10-30m); males guard the eggs until the fry stage (Ref. 2058).

species.name: Stone sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in slow to moderately flowing rivers and streams.  Adults and juveniles (>=5 cm.) with fully developed sucking discs are associated with rocky substrates.  Juveniles are found throughout the water column, generally free swimming in search of food.  Reported to ascend small, rocky streams to breed.  Feeds essentially on algae (diatoms).  Popular with the aquarium fish trade.

species.name: Stone-bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters with rocky substrate.  Feeds on algae and the associated invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Stonelapping minnow
species.description: Inhabits rocky bottoms in swiftly moving water of small and medium-sized streams.  Feeds on periphyton, phytoplankton and some insects (Ref. 12693).  usually abundant; the adults live in loose groups of 4-10 individuals while juveniles 3.0-4.0 cm SL may form loose schools of tens of individuals (Ref. 128869).  Not fished commercially, but occasionally seen in the aquarium trade (Ref 12693).

species.name: Stonogobiops medon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A burrowing species occurring on flat or slightly sloping sand or sand and rubble bottoms. Takes refuge in a burrow constructed by its symbiont alpheid shrimp (a juvenile observed to live with Alpheus randalli). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Stonogobiops pentafasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on slopes of clear and fine sand (usually at about 30 m depth). Lives in symbiotic association with alphaeid shrimps, usually with Alpheus randalli and rarely with A. bellulus. Sometimes found in pairs.

species.name: Storrsia olsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found  in tide pools.

species.name: Storthynx dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow inshore algal reefs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Stott's goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in inshore waters of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Stout argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in continental slope regions.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35612).  Larvae and juveniles pelagic in the upper 200-m layer and more broadly distributed than adults (Ref. 5123).

species.name: Stout blacksmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs at a minimum depth of 550 m upon reaching about 5 cm length (Ref. 54657; 82347). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 35604). Generally mesopelagic and bathypelagic and not ascending to epipelagic depth range (Ref. 96339).

species.name: Stout goby
species.description: Inhabits reef crevices in 5-25 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Stout infantfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recently reported as the smallest vertebrate. Males average 7.7 millimeters long and the gravid female which is 8.4 millimeters weighed 1 milligram.  This pedomorphic species has a life span of only 2 months, has dispensed its fishy appendages such as teeth and scales, and has no pigment except in the eyes (Ref. 52508).  Specimens were collected in oblique plankton net tows (Ref. 52019).

species.name: Stout jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stout longtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species (Ref. 9682).  Inhabit coral reefs (Ref. 75154) and estuaries (Ref. 9002).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Stout rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common in the subtidal zone but may be found in rock pools.  Feed on small fishes such as triplefins (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Stout sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stout slipskin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Stoutspine waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Straightfin barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hardy, prefers quiet, well-vegetated waters in lakes, swamps, and marshes or marginal areas of larger rivers and slow-flowing streams (Ref. 7248, 52193). In shallow, inshore areas of Lake Victoria especially where bottom is sandy (Ref. 4903). Bottom feeder (Ref. 12526), it feeds on a wide variety of small organisms including insects, small snails and crustaceans, algae, diatoms, and detritus (Ref. 7248, 52193). Eaten by large predators like the sharptooth catfish, tigerfish, largemouth breams (Serranochromis species) and birds (Ref. 7248, 52193). Spawns amongst vegetation during summer (Ref. 7248, 52193), in river and streams during rainy season in Lake Victoria basin (Ref. 4903).

species.name: Straightstick pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 5316).  Enters sheltered muddy estuaries where laying out in the open on the bottom (Ref. 48635).  Most specimens from dredge and trawl collections (Ref. 5316).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Solitary on mud bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Strange pike smelt
species.description: Epi- and probably mesopelagic at ca. 15-200 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Strap-weed file-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal algal reefs and estuaries. Sometimes solitary (Ref. 90102). Adults are often in pairs (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Strasburg's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic in rocks along coasts with surf (Ref. 58302). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Strasburg's dascyllus
species.description: Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs.  The two specimens at the Bishop Museum were collected off Matahumu Point, Patu Hiva, Marquesas Islands in 6 to 12 meters (Ref. 7247). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Strawberry darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Streaky clingfish
species.description: Known from only one specimen.

species.name: Stream pipefish
species.description: Adults inhabit streams and rivers.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Streamer fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species, known from only seven specimens.  Occurs in the open ocean habitat (Ref. 4171). Found only in the southern oceans from 25°S to 59°S. Apparently also capable of autotomy, unique amongst lampridiforms.  Early life history stages (eggs and larvae) unknown. Predators, prey, and parasites unknown (Ref. 92949).

species.name: Streamer searobin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from bays and estuaries to the mid-shelf.

species.name: Streamline chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits riffles, runs, and current-swept pools over gravel and rubble in clear small to large rivers (Ref. 86798).  Feeds on periphyton and a wide variety of aquatic insect larvae, especially midges, mayflies, and caddisflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Stretchjaw blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Striate whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Attains a length of more than 60 cm.

species.name: Striated blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow reefs and tide pools.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Striated darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools of headwaters and creeks (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feed on midge larvae and microcrustaceans (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Striated dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among the interstices of overlapping laminar corals or near the bases of whorled corals on coral reef drop-offs in depths of 18-20 m, also in crevices in 15-37 m depth. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Striated frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky and coral reefs, on rocks, sand or rubble (Ref. 9710).  Found in weedy estuaries along the east coast of southern Africa (Ref. 4113). Occurring in marine or brackish waters (Ref. 57225). In the Atlantic, it is found at an average depth of 40 m (Ref. 5288).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Observed to inflate itself greatly like the puffers (Ref. 5521).  Oviparous.  Males have more intense coloration and extended cutaneous appendages than females (Ref. 205).  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773).

species.name: Striated rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky shores and intertidal zone (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Strickland rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not well known, however, was collected in a mountain tributary at 1200 m elevation about 850 km upstream from the sea.

species.name: Strickland river gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rivers, but there is no indication whether it descends to estuaries.  A filter-feeder.  More data needed.

species.name: Strickrott's hagfish
species.description: First record of a myxine record in a hydrothermal vent. Fourth record of a myxine species below 2000m (Ref. 74406). Known from one specimen only, the holotype (in 2007). Possibly, individuals filmed at Grommit, Oasis, and Yaquina vent sites pertain to  the same species (Ref. 74406).

species.name: Strigate parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occasionally occur in groups of up to six individuals (Ref . 7360).  Adults usually found in rocky areas at less than 10 m depth (Ref. 86997). Juveniles occasional amongst weed and rubble patches on sand at 15-18 m depth.  Occasionally eaten (Ref. 5288).

species.name: String eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 43688).

species.name: Stripe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shallow sandy bottoms with clear water (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Stripe-face Calamiana
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stripe-tailed dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky substrata. Sometimes found in tidepools (Ref 90102).

species.name: Stripeback darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit pools, usually with rock bottoms and near riffles, of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Stripeback hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays at an average depth of 10 m in offshore sandy beaches and chases juvenile sand-dwelling cichlids over the open sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Striped barb
species.description:
Inhabits small forest streams, ditches and rivers.  Usually found near the bottom in shallow waters.  Feeds on zooplankton and insect larvae along with some plant material (Ref. 12693);
also worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Striped barbelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits intertidal zone and shallow reefs next to shore in 0-15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Striped bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow lakes, ponds and adjacent irrigation canals of plains; ponds in flood plain (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Striped blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in oyster beds and on hard bottom, retreating, in winter, to deeper water.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Striped boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic over reef and sand (Ref. 58302).  Found in pairs or small groups in deep rocky drop-offs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Striped boga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water.  Forms schools.

species.name: Striped burrfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very common in seagrass beds in bays and coastal lagoons.  Also found on shallow coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Has been traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Striped bystranka
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insect larvae.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide variety of habitats, including grass flats, partially open sand bottoms around the bases of finger and globose sponges, tentacles of anemones, inside live conch shells, and around coral reefs and high relief structures such as artificial reefs (Ref. 26883).  Presumably, striped cardinalfish leaves its daytime hovering places to forage over grass and sand flats at night (Ref. 26883).

species.name: Striped chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped codlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic (Ref. 46075).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 6735).

species.name: Striped coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in loose small groups or solitary, usually in sheltered lagoon reefs at depths of 1-10 m (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Striped cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species found in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Striped dwarf catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit standing and flowing waters.  Usually found among marginal vegetation in lakes and swamps with a mud substrate.  Feed on plants, shrimps, insects, mollusks and fish (Ref. 6028).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped flying barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped giant seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped glass catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to peat habitats (Ref. 57235).  Occurs in shady spots in running waters.  Omnivorous, although larger individuals may prey on smaller fishes (Ref. 6868).  Uncommon in aquarium trade (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Striped gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in a variety of conditions ranging from clear, fast-flowing streams to muddy waterholes.  Inhabits slow-flowing creeks.  Juveniles common in estuaries (Ref. 44894).  Most common at low altitude close to the coast.  Spawns mainly in late summer and autumn at temperature near 21°C.  Feeds on insects, crustaceans and fishes.  The newly hatched larvae are apparently swept downstream, as juveniles are commonly found in estuaries (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Striped hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is  common in the shallow waters of the bay (Ref. 118648).

species.name: Striped headstander
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped hoplo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped jumprock
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy to rocky riffles and runs of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Striped kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among seaweeds, especially in tide pools and kelp.

species.name: Striped killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits bays, estuaries and coastal marshes (Ref. 5723). Feeds on worms, small crustaceans, mollusks and insects (Ref. 93252).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Striped klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and subtidal areas.

species.name: Striped limia
species.description: Found in streams.

species.name: Striped mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along the lake margin among thick vegetation.

species.name: Striped mud carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found at bottom depths in canals, ditches and small streams in large river floodplains.  Migrates up small rivers and streams and out onto floodplains.  Feeds on phytoplankton, periphyton, benthic algae, detritus and some zooplankton.  Most likely used to make prahoc (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Striped mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur mainly in estuaries, congregating over mud-banks (Ref. 2830).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Omnivore (Ref. 97629). Fleshy highly esteemed (Ref. 4393).

species.name: Striped nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seasonal fish with very short life span, typical species of steppe and savannah which need long dry season (Ref. 27292). Occurs in swamps and restwater pools of river floodplains (Ref. 79882), in ditches and despressions in floodplains (Ref. 59344). Bottom spawner (Ref. 79882). Incubation of eggs in captivity is 3-6 months and young fish reach maturity in 6-7 weeks (Ref. 59344). Specimens from central Tanzania introduced in various localities in Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya and other countries, for mosquito control (Ref. 59344).

species.name: Striped panchax
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in streams and reservoirs at high altitudes, and in rivers, wells of the plains, low-lying paddy fields, swamps and brackish waters (Ref. 4833).  Utilized for mosquito control (Ref. 1672).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Striped pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on deep rocky reefs (Ref. 75973).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped pike-characin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped poison-fang blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species found in sheltered lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710, 48636). Several adults together occasionally in close vicinity to each other (Ref. 48636). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Several geographical variations and is mimicked by another blenny Petroscirtes breviceps (Ref. 48636). Both fang and venom gland are present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Striped poison-fang blenny mimic
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal reefs and estuaries to depths of about 10 m (Ref. 48636). May also be found up to 15 m depth in coastal and lagoon reefs in sandy and weedy areas among clumps of Sargassum or other seaweeds. They also take shelter and nests inside small-necked bottles and abandoned worm tubes or shells (Ref. 90102). They feed on small crustaceans, diatoms, and perhaps other plant material associated with such clumps. They use their fangs defensively and will not hesitate to bite if handled, thus, species of this genus are avoided by predators (Ref. 205). Oviparous. Males uses shells but also ring-top cans for nesting (Ref. 48636). Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimic of Meiacanthus grammistes, which like all species of that genus possesses a pair of large grooved fangs in the lower jaw with associated venom glands. These bites are used defensively and Papuan variety is also a possible mimic of Meiacanthus vittatus (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Striped rabbitfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female maximum length given as precaudal length (PCL). Inhabits deep-reefs on the continental slope, usually deeper than 400 meters; with gorgonians, hard corals, tube sponges, crinoids, and ophiuroids. It also shares this habitat with other sharks Heptranchias perlo, Scyliorhinus haeckelii, Galeus mincaronei, Schroederichthys saurisqualus, Squalus sp., and the skate Gurgesiella dorsalifera (Ref. 52554).

species.name: Striped rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Common length:  females usually less than 5.5 cm, males usually more than 6.0 cm in SL (Ref. 9962).

species.name: Striped sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy areas in coastal waters (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Striped seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky coasts and kelp beds, occasionally in sandy surf near rocks (Ref. 2850).  Feed on small crustaceans, worms, and mussels; occasionally on herring eggs (Ref. 4925).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped silver biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters including estuaries.  They form schools (Ref. 5213).  They feed on invertebrates (Ref. 3409).  Fry about 10 cm in length enter the estuaries and stay until they reach maturity (Ref. 34363).

species.name: Striped siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commensal with sea urchins and crown of thorns starfish (Ref. 27362). Occurs in small groups, also found in sheltered reefs and adjacent sand, rubble and rocky bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Striped slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from steep outer reef areas. Forms aggregations with individuals of L. waitei. Inhabits steep outer reefs in 20-40 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Striped stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near reefs, sea grass beds, and sandy beaches (Ref. 12951).

species.name: Striped stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms (Ref. 39597) of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Secretive species, usually found by accident.  Buries itself in the sand during the day.  Usually in shallow sheltered habitats with sparse seagrass beds.  Sits on top of the sand at night (Ref. 48635). Also found in sand or mud bottoms in 10-50 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Striped sweetlips
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Seek shelter in the reef and feed on a variety of benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Striped swordtail
species.description: Inhabits fast-flowing river, preponderantly in stands of water plants or below overhanging shore vegetation.

species.name: Striped topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is found in schools mainly in the shallow and vegetated part of small rivers, brooks and swamps, and in the shallow parts of lakes (Ref. 47311). Uncommon in floodplains (Ref. 52193). It feeds on insect larvae, daphnia and other small invertebrates (Ref. 52193). Typical serial spawner, laying eggs on vegetation (Ref. 52193). Useful as a mosquito control agent (Ref. 7248). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Striped trawl wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Striped triggerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species that occurs in offshore reefs, often seen well above the bottom (Ref. 9710).  Also taken by drive-in nets.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Striped triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are generally more abundant above 10m, but common in areas of broken rock on reefs, rock pools and sub-tidally down to 33 m (Ref. 84085). They feed on benthic invertebrates.  Spawning occurs from May to November (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Striped trumpeter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults apparently prefer broken rocky reefs, rich in 'coral' and other invertebrate life.  Reported to be frequently found over rocky places, especially narrow channels between two cliffs in fjords of New Zealand.  May spawn closer to shore (Ref. 9563) but probably in areas of deeper waters, otherwise they seem to migrate offshore  to spawn (Ref. 85801).  Collected by bottom trawls, dropline, and rod and line (Ref. 76767).  In Australia, adults are found over rocky reefs at depths from 5 to 300 m (Ref. 53584).

species.name: Striped tubeshoulder
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped woodcat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Striped-cheek gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, backwaters, well vegetated slow-flowing creeks and rocky pools (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Stripefin brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024) found to feed on crustaceans (Ref. 32505).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Stripefin eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stripefin poacher
species.description: Found on soft bottom (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Stripefin ronquil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocks and sand on exposed coast at about 6.1-91 m depth.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Male guards eggs.

species.name: Stripenose guitarfish
species.description: A demersal species found inshore on continental shelf. Reports from 366 m are probably erroneous.  Males mature at ca. 58 cm TL, females by 62 cm TL; born at 18-20 cm TL (Ref. 114953).   Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Produces litters of up to 6 pups (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Stripesnout false moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stripetail darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on midge larvae, mayfly and stonefly nymphs, and crustaceans (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Stripetail rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in offshore water on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 6885).  Anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland (Ref. 57406).  Commonly caught with trawls but usually discarded because of its small size (Ref. 2850).  Rarely taken on baited hook in deep water (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Stripey
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Inhabits coastal and lagoon reefs, also in dense aggregations under ledges and in caves during the day (Ref. 9710). Also observed in rocky areas and occasionally in harbours, embankments, and coastal ports. Adults often school in large groups. It ranges between 10 and 30 m depth, but can occur as shallow as 0.3 m to as deep as 300 m (Ref. 123714).  Young feeds on small crustaceans and algae (Ref. 3921).

species.name: Stripped robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, sandy or marshy areas (Ref. 13337).  Shoals in clear, slow-flowing or quiet, well-vegetated waters.  Often found together with the dashtail and the threespot barb and the close similarity of these species suggests mimicry between them.  Feeds on small aquatic and terrestrial organisms.  Preyed upon by tigerfish and observed to be eaten by a small crocodile during an upriver migration (Ref. 13337).  Moves upstream during rains, possibly to breed.  Ovarian egg counts from a large ripe female reach up to 12,000 eggs (Ref. 13337).  Used as bait for tigerfish and largemouth bream (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Stripped weakfish
species.description: A coastal demersal species, but more oceanic than similar species.

species.name: Stromaté argenté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on sand bottom of exposed coasts.  Usually occurs in shallow water near shore and often forms small, but fairly dense, schools (Ref. 4563).

species.name: Stromaté du Japon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are associated with jellyfish, and can occur in small groups. Adults become bottom-dwellers (Ref. 128523).  Tasty food fish (Ref. 559).

species.name: Stromaté du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near the surface of coastal water to over bottom of continental shelf (Ref. 11035).

species.name: Stromaté fossette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms large schools over the continental shelf, except during the winter months when it may descend to deeper water.  Juveniles are generally found under floating weeds and jellyfish.  Often found in brackish waters (Ref. 26938).  Nerito-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Adults feeds mainly on jellyfish (Ref. 26938), squids, arrow worms, crustaceans and worms (Ref. 58426).  Marketed fresh, smoked and frozen; eaten fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).  Mostly frozen and exported to Japan.

species.name: Stromaté lune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic fish forming large schools in coastal bays, inshore waters over the continental shelf and around islands at moderate depths (50 to 70 m) where it occurs throughout the year (Ref. 53006).  Juveniles are found in shallow coastal waters under floating weeds; also in or near brackish estuaries (Ref. 5217).
