The young of less then 10 cm length are often encountered in association with medusae.  Adults feed mainly on jellyfish, small fish, crustaceans and worms while juveniles are plankton feeders.  Caught mainly with otter trawls, also seines; marketed  fresh and frozen (Ref. 53006).  Its flesh is well esteemed.

species.name: Stromaté palomette
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stromaté saléma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stromaté étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Strong spined silver-biddy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected in shallow coastal or estuarine areas (Ref. 41102).

species.name: Strongylura anastomella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Strongylura fluviatilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Strongylura forsythia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal areas and mangrove-lined lagoons where it is moderately common (especially small individuals).  A carnivorous species feeding mainly on small fishes and shrimps (Ref. 50368).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Strophidon dorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Struhsaker's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only on the basis of specimens caught by a shrimp trawl in 99 to 183 meters (Ref. 7247).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Struhsaker's deep-sea smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the outer shelf and upper slope, rarely to 1400 m.

species.name: Stubbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Biology unknown (Ref. 5181).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Stubby lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic species found between 375 and 750 during the day and between 40 and 650 at night (Ref. 4775).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 75154).  Large individuals are non-migratory (Ref. 4775).

species.name: Stumptooth minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturgeon chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand and gravel runs of medium to large turbid rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Sturgeon grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Sturgeon poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, and small fishes (Ref. 4925).

species.name: Sturisoma barbatum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma brevirostre
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma caquetae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma graffini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma guentheri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma lyra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma monopelte
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma nigrirostrum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its natural habitat is described as mostly soft water backwaters in which there are no water plants although the banks are overgrown with Pistia or Eichornia. Branches extending below the surface and driftwood on the bottom serve as surfaces that the fish can scour for aufwuchs and this fish can actually scrape off some of the wood itself as an aid in digestion (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Sturisoma robustum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma rostratum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisoma tenuirostre
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisomatichthys aureum
species.description: Aquarium keeping:  feeds on plants and roots; minimum aquarium size 120 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Sturisomatichthys citurensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisomatichthys kneri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisomatichthys leightoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sturisomatichthys tamanae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stylish Scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Stymphalia chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and streams with flowing, clear water.  Feeds on various plants and animals. Maximum size reaches up to about 21 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Stymphalia minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which occurs in spring and associated wetlands and in lowland water courses with little current.  Feeds on invertebrates and plants.  Is threatened due to water abstraction and habitat destruction.  Spawns in December to March (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Sua bumblebee goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits freshwater streams, canals, ditches and marshes as well as brackish estuarine areas.  Feeds on zooplankton.  Not sold in the markets, but occasionally encountered in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Sublime pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Subnose darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and adjacent riffles of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Subparallel lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Suceur aiguille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This curious fish is so fine that it resembles a brushwood.  Mimetic.  Frequently occurs in shallow creeks (Ref. 27188) that are not so sunny but with a strong current and a rocky substrate.  General activity is poor since it remains hidden in the anfractuosities of logs during the day.  Feeds on periphyton and associated organisms.  The mating couple choose a narrow hole to spawn the eggs (about 50,000 eggs), after having cleaned the substratum.  The male takes care of the eggs (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Suceur aiguille (Farlowella rugosa)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in forest creeks, 4 to 8 m wide, 0.3 to 2 m deep, over sandy bottom with flowing water.  During reproduction, the males have short odontodes restricted to some parts of their snout (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Sucker barb
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found mainly in medium to large-sized rivers (Ref. 12975).  Found in large rivers during the dry season and in floodplain streams and canals during the wet season.  Does not persist in impoundments (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on algae (Ref. 12975), phytoplankton (Ref. 12693), fish and crustaceans (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Sucker fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Sucker throat catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast-flowing hill streams.  Prefers deep riffles and runs over gravel, cobble substrates (Ref. 12045).

species.name: Sucker-belly loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Adults inhabit rapid flowing streams.  Feed on periphytic algae and detritus on rock surfaces (Ref. 33406).

species.name: Suckerlip blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Intertidal, found in rocky shorelines (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Suckermouth catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits the lower part of rivers still under tide influence, and characterized by a quiet flowing water and muddy substrate, and swamps (Ref. 90186). Feeds on algae and small crustaceans.  Is cultured in ponds in Singapore and Hong Kong for the aquarium trade, where it is very popular (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Suckermouth minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble riffles and runs of clear to turbid creeks and small to medium, sometimes large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Sudis hyalina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic to bathypelagic.  Carnivorous.  Probably spawns near the surface in temperate to tropical waters (Ref. 5759).  Has been supposed to be one of the 'cable-biters'; reconstructions from big teeth found in submarine cables suggests that it attains at least 100 cm body-length (Ref. 4474).

species.name: Suezichthys ornatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suggrundus cooperi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suggrundus meerdervoortii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in semi-enclosed sea areas, down to 100 m in sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Sulawesi anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sulawesi coelacanth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably on rocky slopes in deep water of 150-200 m.  Fricke et al. (Ref. 33470) observed two specimens of 120 and 140 cm length in a deep carbonate cave at a depth of 155 m (water temp.  17.8-20.1°C).

species.name: Sulawesi fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in sheltered coastal, lagoon, and outer reefs in 1-10 m; solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).  Collected from a depth of 10 m (Ref. 7401).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Sulawesi moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sulawesi Silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by beach seine in seagrass areas and on mud bottoms (Ref. 92295).

species.name: Sulfur limia
species.description: Found in sulfur spring.

species.name: Sulfurhead Aulonocara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found over sand bordering the rocky reef.  Feeds on small sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 5595).  Females mouthbrood eggs (Ref. 6020).

species.name: Sulphur damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs, in areas with rich-coral growth (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sulphur molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sultan Sazlığı minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sulu eelblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs among crevices, known only from Sulu Sea, Philippines (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sulu fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in small schools along deep outer reef walls, usually swims upside-down on the ceilings of large caves (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Sulu goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty sand and mud bottoms, usually near mouth of streams, occasionally near reefs in 1-4 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Sulu velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble bottoms, frequently neas reefs, in 10-30 m  (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sulu viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky surge area, rocky tidepool.  A 3.9 cm SL gravid female (USNM 376179) with 325 embryos, 0.37 cm TL in length.  Collected by rotenone (Ref. 81230). Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of shallow water (usually <5) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sumatra barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, small crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; not to be kept with long-finned fishes; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Sumatran river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large lakes or rivers (Ref. 12693).  Found in the basin-wide mainstream of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 33813).  Used to produce prahoc and tuk trey (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Sumatran silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the coast and the surface (Ref. 11230).  Occurs in estuaries (Ref. 7050).  Probably important as forage fish.  Nothing is known of the biology of this fish (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Summer sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits hilltop lakes and streams, but is no longer known from its type localities. Individuals spawn once per reproductive season that extends from early June to late July or early August. Preferentially use ephemeral streams for spawning. Arrival at streams is episodic, correlating to precipitation events and appropriate flow. Stream temperature appears to be less important a cue for reproductive behavior than other Catostomus. Females always have pearl organs when in breeding condition; retain drab coloration when spawning. Males develop a gold longitudinal stripe, small gold-colored patch above each eye, and are extensively covered in pearl organs when in breeding condition. Both sexes start to reach sexual maturity at about 4 years. Eggs are about 3mm in diameter (Ref. 83995).

species.name: Sun loach
species.description: Inhabits areas of boulders and cobble of rapidly flowing stretches of large and medium-sized rivers.  Feeds mainly on mollusks and occasionally on other benthic invertebrates.  Occasionally seen in the markets during the dry season.  An extremely aggressive species which is often seen in the aquarium trade (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Sunagocia omanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sunbeam lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442) at 50-600 m at night, 500-1000 m during day (Ref. 58302).  Reported from depths  of 100-500 m in Subarctic Pacific gyres (Ref. 51600). Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Sunburnt pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sunburst Dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary under large Xestospongia barrel sponges on gradual, current-swept reef slopes in 32-45 m, sometimes in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sunda viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cryptic and solitary, inhabits reef crevices in about 0-8 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Sundadanio atomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio axelrodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sundadanio echinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio gargula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio goblinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal peat swamp forests (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio margarition
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamp forests and blackwater streams (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio retiarius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamps and blackwater streams (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundadanio rubellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits peat swamp forests (Ref. 88800).

species.name: Sundasalanx malleti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In turbid, flowing waters over silty, clayey substrates along banks adjacent to mainstream currents and at depths up to 1 m, probably deeper during daylight.  Feeds on insects and crustaceans.

species.name: Sundasalanx megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the mouth of a creek over sandy, silty substrate in flowing turbid water approximately 1.5 m deep.

species.name: Sundasalanx mekongensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly in large rivers with muddy bottom, turbid water and slow to moderate current.  Caught by seine and push net.  In all habitats where it was collected by push-net, it was only present at depths greater than 1 meter, usually at a depth immediately below those at which a slight drop in temperature could be felt.  Located above the bottom, usually above a layer of 10-20 cm loose ooze.

species.name: Sundasalanx mesops
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Downstream from creek mouths in shallows over sandy or silty substrates during daylight hours.  Also in grassy stream banks.

species.name: Sundasalanx microps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sundasalanx platyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers with moderate to fast flowing water with muddy bottom (Ref. 56749).  During the day, they occur usually in water deeper than 1 m, close to the bottom. At night, they form school near the surface along the shores (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Sundolyra latebrosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a hillstream. Found in a crevice between large boulders at the bank of a moderately steep, fast-flowing stream with clear (low turbidity) and slightly alkaline (pH 7.9) water and with substrate consisting of large boulders and cobble. Barbodes cf. binotatus (Cyprinidae) was the only other species collected when the stream was sampled. Reaches up to 20 cm TL based on interviews with the locals (Ref. 104298).

species.name: Sundoreonectes obesus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Sundoreonectes sabanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Sunier's righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Sunny dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in well-developed caves on drop-offs and may be restricted to this habitat (Ref. 39927).

species.name: Sunrise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in Zostera marina or Sargassum beds. Eggs are deposited in the peribranchial cavity of sea squirts (Ref. 34819, 41071).

species.name: Sunrise dartfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sunrise perch
species.description: Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300), on sand or rock bottom (Ref. 11230).  Benthic and benthopelagic on hard substrates (Ref. 58302).  Consumed as food (Ref. 559).

species.name: Sunrise sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No available data re habitat or depth of capture, it is likely to be relatively rare and occupy at least moderately deep habitats (Ref. 116166).

species.name: Sunrise wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Reported to have been encountered it most often in pairs, one individual usually being much larger than the other; appears to be among the deepest ranging of the subgenus Trochocopus, collected at depths of 67 to 238 m, but apparently preferring depths of 100-120 m (Ref. 75973). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Sunset anthias
species.description: Rarely seen because of small size and deepwater habitat.  Usually in depths over 40 m and more common in 50-60 m range where it forms small groups that swim close to the substrate (Ref. 48635); may also occur in aggregations above patch reefs on sand or rubble seaward slopes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Sunset butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feed mainly on coral polyps and small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 2334, 48636).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Adults usually paired during breeding (Ref. 9710), but juveniles solitary (Ref. 48636).  Can adapt  easily to tank life and willingly accept nearly all kinds of food offered.

species.name: Sunset dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sunset fairy-wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sloping rubble bottoms with scattered low outcrops of rock or coral and occasional large coral outcrops. Associated with its congeners, including Cirrhilabrus hygroxerus and four species of undetermined status that are related to C. cyanopleura (Bleeker, 1851); C. exquisitus Smith, 1957; C. punctatusC. temminckii Bleeker, 1853 (Ref. 118280).

species.name: Sunset perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky patch reef surrounded by a large sandy area using a hand nets at a depth of 83 m.  It was then transported to the surface alive in a perforated plastic jar.

species.name: Sunshinefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit outer and seaward reefs.  Feeds on plankton (Ref. 5521).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Supanose rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Super VC-10 hap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Confined to rocky areas where the rocks are covered with a thin layer of sediment.  Usually solitary.  Feeds on insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 267).

species.name: Supreme gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sureyan killifish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Surf blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits well-washed, eroded limestone localities (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Surf eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Burrows in sand in surf areas.

species.name: Surf sprite
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large numbers in boiling surf, close to shoreline. Occurs in large aggregations (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Surf Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow waters, surge channels and tidal pools around fringing reefs where wave action is high; some found in the big surf, oxygen-rich habitat (Ref. 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Surfette commune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most commonly found in surf around rocky headlands and along the shoreline, occasionally also in more still waters of river mouths. Very delicate and do not survive handling. Appear to be able to hybridize with congeners, Iso flosmaris and Iso hawaiiensis. Nothing else is known about this species. (Ref. 9769).

species.name: Surge damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rubble-strewn surge channels, the outermost reaches of exposed reef flats, and the upper submarine terrace at 12 meters. Territorial but they generally occur in groups, and remains close to shelter.  Feed mainly on benthic algae and small crustaceans (Ref. 1602, 37816 ).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Surge dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common but secretive species (Ref. 9710, 48635) found in holes and crevices of exposed outer reef flats and reef margins.  Occurs in pairs and feeds on small crabs, isopods, and copepods (Ref. 1602).  Usually most abundant in high current or surge areas.  Frequently enters the aquarium fish trade and has been bred in captivity (Ref. 37748). Sometimes solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Surmulet pontique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over mud, sand and gravel bottoms of the continental shelf.  Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (crustaceans, worms and mollusks) (Ref. 4845).

species.name: Surubí tigré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs throughout the principal riverbeds and sometimes in the flooded areas of forests. Its biology is similar to that of P. tigrinum but it appears to be more fond of shady streams. Feeds at night on fish (loricariids, cichlids and characoids) as well as crabs (Ref. 6868). Confines its foraging activities to riverbeds. Its yellowish flesh is succulent and like that of other silurids, it is without bones (Ref. 27188). Females reach a more notable size. They become sexually mature at 56 cm, males at 45 cm. Fecundity is estimated at 8 million eggs per kg (Ref. 35381). Utilized for human consumption. See Loubens and Panfili, 2000 (Ref. 34213) for reproductive biology and ecology.

species.name: Suruga fundicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suruga lightfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suruga snailfsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The gonad is pouch-like, translucent whitish, with ovarian eggs 0.35-0.75 [average ± standard deviation 0.50 ± 0.14 (n = 62)] mm in diameter (Ref. 120239)..

species.name: Susan's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found resting on the substrate in shallow (<4.6 m) sheltered habitats, either at patch reefs well back in the bay (no surge, silt, and mud surrounding the coral) or from fouling communities on dock floats (Ref. 38034, 116739).

species.name: Suspicious lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef and sandy bottoms (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Suspiria blenny
species.description: Espèce de blennie.

species.name: Susvva rainbovvfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suttonia suttoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Suwannee bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles, runs and pools, and large springs and spring runs.

species.name: Svetovidovia lucullus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic species (Ref. 2729).

species.name: Swahili goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swales' basslet
species.description: Very secretive in dense brittle coral formation on coastal slopes at depths of about 25 m (Ref. 48635). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Swallow damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky inshore reefs, often near drop-offs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Swallow grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swallow-tail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs of the continental shelf (Ref. 9563) and continental slope (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Swallowtail bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swallowtail dart
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore (Ref. 7300), in surf zones off sandy beaches (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Swallowtail fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Swallowtail shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy, sometimes rocky, pools and runs of creeks and small to large rivers.

species.name: Swallowtail tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swamp barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams, rivers, canals, beels, haors, ponds and inundated fields.  Occurs mainly in shallow water (Ref. 6028).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Swamp blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swamps and rivers.

species.name: Swamp darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in standing or slow-flowing water over mud, sometimes sand; often in vegetation (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Eggs are found attached to the substrate unguarded (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Swamp galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swamps, quiet pools and backwaters, either in open, shallow stretches or the vegetated margins of these areas.  Found around the shelter of rocks and vegetation on the bottom, also in streams draining into lakes (Ref. 44894).  Believed to spawn in winter or spring following rains.  Sexual maturity is reached after one year for males and two years for females.  Fecundity is typically low; spawning females lay between 70-500 eggs in well-sheltered sites (underneath rocks).  The eggs require around 50-60 days to hatch (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on aquatic insects and their larvae, also small invertebrates (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Swamp gudgeon
species.description: Known only from two specimens from the type locality in New Guinea, Indonesia, collected in 1997. Inhabits sago-Pandanus swamp habitat. Attempt to collect specimens in 1998 unsuccessful due to road construction.

species.name: Swamp toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on vegetation and debris in swamps, sloughs and quiet pools and backwaters of streams. Found year-round in open streams which are small and well-shaded with temperatures never exceeding 23°C. In such streams, thigmotaxic tendency is shown by the difficulty in seining these individuals from the roots and debris of their preferred habitat along edges of submerged weed banks which border sand-bottomed channels. This habitat is rich in potential food for C. cornuta like amphipods, ostracods and copepods (Ref. 34868). Eggs are carried in gill chambers of females (Ref. 205).

species.name: Swan Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in slow to moderately swift flowing waters situated in dry scrub country; occurring in aggregations usually in rocky pools or along shallow stream margins around log debris.  Occurs in gently to moderately flowing water of shallow spring-fed creeks (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on insects and their larvae, small crustaceans and algae.  A shoal-forming species, particularly when young.  The entire life cycle takes place in fresh water.  Breeds in its second year during spring.  Maximum life span is about 3 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Swannanoa darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits swift rubble riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Swatow thryssa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably schooling, perhaps mainly in inshore waters. More data needed based on correct identifications. This species is probably hidden in various synonymies, chiefly those of T. hamiltoni which it resembles superficially.

species.name: Sweetwater demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mouth of freshwater or brackish streams.  Found in small groups Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018 but also in Ref. 90102. Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Swellhead snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 294 m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Swift's goby
species.description: This species was found on steep, volcanic-sand slopes; under small pieces of coral rubble and volcanic rock that were often covered with Halimeda algae. Strong thermoclines were frequently encountered between 40-50 m on these slopes, thus consequently this species is likely exposed to temperatures ranging from about 24-29º C (Ref. 122935).

species.name: Swollen-headed conger eel
species.description: A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on soft bottoms on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Swollengut worm eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Swordfin killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium specimens prefer waters with 25°C mean temperature, pH=6.8, water hardness of 10 and areas with rocks, plants and driftwood.  Carnivorous, egg laying and peaceful community fish (Ref. 6398).  Bottom spawner, 5 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Swordsnout grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Size may exceed 50 cm TL.  Feeds primarily on small fish (myctophids), polychaete worms and crustaceans (pagurids, crabs, shrimps, ostracods, and copepods (Ref. 6187).

species.name: Swordspine gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves and insular areas.  Rare (Ref. 9771).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Swordspine rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Swordtail characin
species.description: Aquarium species reach 7.0 cm.  TL (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Swordtail jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty or muddy bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 13628), in burrows (Ref. 9710).  Sometimes found in colonies (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Swordtail platyfish
species.description: Inhabits tranquil zones of slow-flowing waters of ditches, spring areas, marshes and ponds.

species.name: Swordtip gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Sydney cardinalfish
species.description: Found in rocky estuaries to offshore reefs, usually in small aggregations (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Sydney scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy bottom at depth of 14.4 m.

species.name: Sydney skate
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 6871, 75154).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules measure 5.7 cm long and 3.2 cm wide (Ref. 41308). Males reaches maturity at 43-48 cm TL. Biology poorly known; probably have suffered population declines in recent years (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Sydney's pygmy pipehorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in semi-exposed rocky reefs, sparsely covered with bushy red-algae in which the species is extremely well camouflaged (Ref. 54742).  Benthic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Symbolophorus kreffti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, mesopelagic; nyctoepipelagic at the surface.  Sexually mature from about 8.4 cm (Ref. 4479).  Maximum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Symbolophorus rufinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic species found between 425-850 m during the day and nyctoepipelagic at the surface and down to 125 m (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Symphurus arabicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus bathyspilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 51120).

species.name: Symphurus caribbeanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters (Ref. 10879); in sand and mud substrates (Ref. 26268).  Feeds on polychaetes and small, benthic crustaceans.  May be a nocturnal feeder (Ref. 10879).

species.name: Symphurus fallax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus fuscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep water.

species.name: Symphurus gilesii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus hernandezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is apparently is endemic on the outer continental shelf off the Caribbean coast in a relatively narrow depth range (148–301 m) located off Bocas de Ceniza in Magdalena region and Parque Nacional Natural Tayrona in Tayrona region (Ref. 75960).

species.name: Symphurus holothuriae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus hondoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand or sand-mud bottom (Ref. 35979). Unpublished maximum depth given at 1040 m (in Ref. 127475).

species.name: Symphurus kyaropterygium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently inhabits muddy or calcareous mud substrates of inner continental shelf (Ref. 26268).

species.name: Symphurus leucochilus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus lubbocki
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus luzonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus maculopinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype, collected on soft sediments at 561 m;  56 other individuals observed, but not collected, were found on a variety of substrata, including coarse gravel, gravelly sand-shell and gravelly sand, located between 433-561 m on Volcano-19, Tonga Arc, western Pacific.  Considered to be a true vent species since  (Ref. 87974).

species.name: Symphurus maldivensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus microrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably frequents coastal lagoons with sandy bottom.  More studies are needed concerning the ecology of this species.

species.name: Symphurus novemfasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus oculellus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy substrates in coastal bays and deep water (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Symphurus reticulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus sayademalhensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus schultzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Symphurus tessellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish waters, bays and coves (Ref. 36453).  Reported from depths between 247.05 and 274.5 m (Ref. 26912).

species.name: Symphurus undatus
species.description: Benthic on mud (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Symphurus variegatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphurus woodmasoni
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Symphysanodon andersoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Symphysanodon disii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by gillnet  at about 150 m (Ref. 75640).

species.name: Symphysodon tarzoo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synanceia platyrhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synaphobranchus calvus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synaphobranchus dolichorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from larvae specimens; adults not known (Ref. 46206).

species.name: Synaphobranchus oregoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synaptolaemus cingulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Synaptolaemus latofasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Synaptura megalepidoura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synbranchus lampreia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Synbranchus madeirae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The male guards and builds nest or burrow (Ref. 205).

species.name: Synchiropus orientalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Synclidopus hogani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on a broad shallow bank, on coarse sand and gravel substrate, which included numerous fallen leaves and the open shells of freshwater bivalve molluscs. The riverine environment at the type locality is flowing, clear and fresh (being about 5-6 km upstream from the brackish zone), but is clearly subject to tidal influence, with about a 75 cm rise and fall.  Environmental parameters at the time of collection (25 November 2006):  conductivity 59.6-60.6 μS/cm (approximately 30 ppm), pH 6.8, temperature 29°C, dissolved oxygen 6.5 ppm, and turbidity 0.8 NTU.  Stomach contents included fragments of insect larvae and numerous sand grains (Ref. 86741).

species.name: Syncomistes bonapartensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers deeper portions of slow-flowing creeks and rivers, as well as billabongs. Inhabits clear and turbid waters, over muddy to rocky substrates, often where algae is abundant. Adults occur in shoals around snags. Juveniles are mostly found in riffle habitat. Sympatric with Syncomistes holsworthi, S. kimberleyensis, S. rastellus and S. trigonicus. Feeds mainly on filamentous algae along with some detritus and invertebrates. Attains sexual maturity at 120-140 mm and spawns in wet season. Eggs are large about 3 mm and non-adhesive (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Syncomistes holsworthi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer to inhabit deeper and slow flowing areas of creeks and rivers, as well as still waters and billabongs while juveniles occur in shallow, still waters or occasionally in riffle habitat. Usually forms shoals in the middle of the water column around snags, sometimes with Syncomistes bonapartensis. Feeds mainly on filamentous algae that are scraped off rocks with specially modified teeth. Attains sexual maturity at 9.0-10.0 cm. Spawns during the wet season and appears to wait until a major flood event to spawn. Produces non-adhesive eggs that are large, about 3 mm (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Syncomistes moranensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers to inhabit deep backwaters and slow flowing stream areas. Forms shoals in the middle of the water column with Hephaestus jenkinsi. Occurs in clear waters over rocky substrates, where algae are in abundance (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Syncomistes versicolor
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer to inhabit deeper, slow flowing portions of creeks and rivers. Juveniles occupy shallow, still waters or occasionally in riffle habitat.  Frequently encountered shoaling in the middle of the water column around snags, also observed in large schools (> 50 fish) patrolling up and down stream reaches. Occurs in clear waters over rocky substrates, usually where algae are in abundance. There is an apparent segregation by size/age with large adult fishes (> 200 mm) 
appearing restricted to the lower catchment, while juveniles and sub-adults only stay in the upper catchment.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae that are scraped off rocks with its modified teeth (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Syncomistes wunambal
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer to occupy riffle and run habitat, and may form shoals in deep slow water around snags.  Juveniles mostly occurs in riffle habitat. Inhabits clear waters, over rocky substrates, usually where algae are in abundance.  Feeds mainly on filamentous algae that are scraped off rocks with specially modified teeth  (Ref. 119336).

species.name: Syncrossus reversus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Syngnathe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal rivers and estuaries (Ref. 4127).  Seems to be mainly a brackish water species, only occasionally entering fresh water (Ref. 81680).  Has been recorded in waters with a temperature range of 26.0-29.0 °C (Ref. 4959).  Lives among algae where it mimics the coloration of the vegetation.  Feeds on small prey and organic debris.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The incubation of the eggs takes place in a marsupial pouch found in front of the tail of the males (Ref. 5377).  Dawson (1981) reported over 800 postlarvae in a male of 141 mm SL (Ref. 81680).  Maximum reported total length 20.0 cm (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Syngnathe aiguille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal and estuarine waters to depths of at least 110 m (Ref. 4281); on sand, mud and rough bottoms. Common amongst algae and eel-grass (Zostera) (Refs. 4146, 6733, 88187). Feeds mainly on small crustaceans (Ref. 85544). It is parasitised by the monogenean Gyrodactylus eyipayipi on the body surface, inside the flute and male brood pouch (Ref. 124059).

species.name: Syngnathe brun
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds in bays and estuaries, but also enters fresh water (Ref. 7251).  Resident in estuaries during spring through fall, migrates into near shore continental shelf waters during winter.  Found in waters of 4-17 °C.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe commun
species.description: Majority of collections are from freshwater streams and rivers.  Probably reaches 14.5 cm SL.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe courbé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subtidal lagoon and seaward reefs, usually among algae or seagrasses (Ref. 9710).  Most are seen on sand and mud areas, prone to currents; usually soft bottom to about 25 m (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe de Duméril
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal and estuarine waters (Ref. 126547); often found on sandy shores among floating or attached seaweeds (Ref. 6733).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Spawns in summer.  Young are sometimes caught pelagically in the North Sea (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Syngnathe de l'Adriatique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly amongst detritus or vegetation over shallow muddy bottom (Ref. 6733).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe de lagune
species.description: Poisson de la famille des syngnathidae. Euryhaline, found among detritus or vegetation over sand or mud, within a temperature range of 8° to 24°C.  Probably an amphidromous species (Ref. 51243) but migratory behavior needs verification.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Early free-living young measure 23 mm TL (Ref. 6733).

species.name: Syngnathe de Schmidt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic species found near surface of water or in midwater in open sea (Ref. 126547). Feeds mainly on copepods, preferably Acartia clausi, Pseudocalanus elongatus, Oithona nana, and Pseudocalanus parvus (Ref. 10613). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits oceanic and coastal waters.  Sub-adults planktonic, adults probably demersal (Ref. 6733).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe trapu de l'Océan Indien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).  Found in tide pool, seagrass, and coral reef areas.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 3.5-4.0 cm SL (Ref. 5316). Also found in lagoons and seaward reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Syngnathe virgule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal rivers, streams, and estuaries (Ref. 4127).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 9.7 cm SL (Ref. 5316).

species.name: Syngnathe à double menton
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe à larges bandes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer depths of about 25 m or more and is easily overlooked (Ref. 48635).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Solitary or in pairs in caves and crevices (Ref 90102).

species.name: Syngnathe à long museau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore algae-weed rubble or reef areas (Ref. 126547). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe à queue courte
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in relatively shallow (25-150 cm), still to slow-flowing water (Ref. 6028).  Inhabits freshwater streams, rivers and estuaries. Juveniles and subadults are usually found in  estuaries while adults are found upstream in freshwater areas.  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and zooplankton.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693)

species.name: Syngnathe à queue courte (Microphis millepunctatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal rivers, streams, and estuaries (Ref. 4127).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathe à traits jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among algal-matted rock and living corals of lagoon and seaward reefs from the low tide line to a depth of 25 m or more.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Feeds on small invertebrates particularly copepods (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Syngnathe épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically inhabits offshore.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathus carinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be mature at 17.5 cm SL.

species.name: Syngnathus caspius
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Syngnathus chihiroe
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Syngnathus dawsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathus folletti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuaries, algae and rock bottoms (Ref. 126547). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathus insulae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found among algae in depths of 20-34 m, but sometimes among floating Sargassum. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Males may be mature at 12.5 cm SL.

species.name: Syngnathus macrobrachium
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be mature at 8.4 cm SL.

species.name: Syngnathus macrophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be mature at about 10 cm SL.

species.name: Syngnathus makaxi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bottoms with dense algae and seagrass (Ref. 126547). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Syngnathus safina

species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the muddy bottoms down to at least 100 m in lake (Ref. 4967). Feeds on the snail, Neothauma (Ref. 6770). Zoobenthos feeder (Ref. 52177). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Only fish known to practice brood parasitism: it manages to mix it eggs with those of mouthbrooding cichlids. Its larvae grow faster than those of the host and feed on them.

It feeds on typical squeaker diet of detritus, algae and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 52193). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Lives for 4 or 5 years (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Synodontis ngouniensis

species.name: Synodontis nigrita

species.name: Synodontis nigromaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocks or marginal vegetation of flowing riverine channels to lagoons or backwaters (Ref. 7248, 52193). It feeds on a variety of food including detritus, algae and plant material, insects, snails and small fish, and scavenges readily (Ref. 7248, 52193). Eggs and larvae of cichlids have been reported in stomach of this species (Ref. 78218). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Breeds during the summer rainy season (Ref. 7248, 52193), with a peak coinciding with heavy rains in January to March (Ref. 13337). Juveniles move off the floodplains when water recedes (Ref. 13337). Grows to a large size (Ref. 246).

species.description: Occurs in very different biotopes, such as streams with fast or slow-moving currents, with stony or muddy beds, as well as with vegetation.

species.name: Syrman goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, on shelly ground, sand, muddy sand or mud.  May enter freshwaters.  Feeds on crustaceans (mysids, corophiid amphipods), small fish (gobies), bivalves, polychaetes, and chironomid larvae.  Sexually mature at 1 to 2 years (Ref. 4696).  Spawns in March to June with females spawning at least twice during this season.  Adhesive eggs are deposited under or between stones, shells and aquatic plants and males guard the eggs until hatching (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Systomus laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a small freshwater stream, formed by the confluence of certain branches of rivers flowing through the low level regions of Pathanamthitta District. This water body is 30- 37 m wide and <1 to 2 m deep during summer season and is blanketed by mud dominant sediments. This area has been covered by more or less dense riparian vegetation. Co-occurs with the following fish species: Puntius mahecola, Dawkinsia filamentosa, Haludaria fasciata, Rasbora dandia, Heteropneusteus fossilis, Clarias dussumeiri, Wallago attu, and Ompok malabaricus (Ref. 112401).

species.name: Sébaste atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit deep waters (Ref. 4570).  Epibenthic-pelagic (Ref. 58426).  Bear live young.  Gregarious throughout life.  Feed on euphausiids, hyperiids, cephalopods, chaetognaths and small fishes.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 4570).  Longevity was determined from isotope ratios and given as at least 65 years in general and at least 75 years in the waters off Nova Scotia (Ref. 45673).

species.name: Sébaste bocace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found over rocky reefs, but also common on open bottoms to about 320 m (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles are pelagic and settle in near shore nursery areas, then move to deeper habitats (Ref. 36715).  Young form schools (Ref. 2850).  Feed mainly on fishes, including other rockfishes (Ref. 2850).  Ovoviviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715, 6885, 34817). Validated age by radiometry is 37 yrs (Ref. 75794).  A famous sport fish throughout its range (Ref. 2850).  Flesh is of excellent quality when kept chilled (Ref. 27436).  Sold with other rockfish species (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Sébaste boucanier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sébaste capricorne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Sébaste citron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hover in loose groups above rocky bottoms (Ref. 27436).  Pelagic juveniles are found in shallower water (Ref. 27436).  Feed on small fishes and krill (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Validated age by radiometry is 44 yrs (Ref. 49687).  Flesh is of good quality (Ref. 27436).  Sold as fillets (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Sébaste de Bougainville
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Sébaste de corail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles up to 6 cm SL are pelagic (Ref. 9341).  An important game fish (Ref. 9341).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Marketed whole or as fillet (Ref. 9341).

species.name: Sébaste de Cortez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at a depth between 200 and 1,100 m; larvae encountered near the surface; and juveniles sometimes mesopelagic (Ref. 9341).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sébaste du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sébaste du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant in offshore waters (Ref. 2850).  Young pelagic up to age 3 (Ref. 6885).  Grows slowly (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Very important commercial rockfish in the North Pacific (Ref. 2850, 27437).  Marketed as fillets (Ref. 2850).  Utilized fresh and frozen; eaten fried, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Sébaste piment
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults frequent deep rocky reefs as well as sand and mud bottoms; young are pelagic (Ref. 36715) and occur in shallower waters (Ref. 2850).  Feed on euphausiids (Ref. 6885), krill, small squids and fishes (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36715).  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten fried, boiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Sébaste rose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow water; rocky or clay-silt bottom (Ref. 5951). Bears live young. Gregarious during all life. Feeds on euphausiids, decapods, mysids, small mollusks and fishes. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 4570). A long-lived species with estimated life span of 30-50 years, slow growing and has low fecundity. Late juveniles (11-20 cm total length) were primarily associated with boulder reefs that have deep interstices amongst the boulders; as well as in exposed boulders that do not have crevices along their lower margins, but are surrounded by dense patches of cerianthid anemones, Cerianthus borealis. The use of both boulder and cerianthid habitats are either on an encounter basis, regardless of habitat saturation or predation pressure, or because boulder reefs serve as recruitment habitats, and cerianthid habitats serve as a conduit for redfish moving away from saturated boulder reef sites (Ref. 58487).

species.name: Sébaste tigre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky reefs, mainly at depths greater than 10 m (Ref. 27436).  Solitary and territorial, defending a home crevice among rocks (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles pelagic (Ref. 27436).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Quickly changes color when disturbed or when there is a change in lighting (Ref. 6885).  Caught infrequently and incidentally marketed  as rockfish (Ref. 27436).  Flesh firm and tasty (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Sébaste à bouche noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Sébaste à grosse tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300) and on soft substrates (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Sébaste à queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools in open water along steeply sloping shores or above rocky reefs; also holes up amid cracks and crevices of the sea floor (Ref. 27436).  Juveniles found around floats and pilings (Ref. 27436).  Feed on pelagic crustaceans, fishes and squids (Ref. 6885).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Filleted, then sold fresh or frozen, with other rockfishes (Ref. 27436).

species.name: Sébaste épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on soft bottom of offshore waters (Ref. 2850).  Juveniles occur in midwater (Ref. 2850).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are spawned in pelagic gelatinous masses (Ref. 59312).

species.name: Sélar ligne jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found inshore and form large schools on day time.  They disperse at night to feed on planktonic and benthic invertebrates such as crabs and shrimps.  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233, 7300, 90102).

species.name: Séret’s dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sériole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthopelagic in outer reef slopes and offshore banks to 160 m or more.  They form small groups (Ref. 9283, 26235, 58302). Young often seen around floating objects (Ref. 4887, 48635).  They feed mainly on fishes, but also on invertebrates.  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).  May cause ciguatera poisoning, particularly in coral reef areas (Ref. 5217).  Uncommon on East Indian reefs but occasionally found in cool upwelling areas of Lesser Sunda Islands of Indonesia (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Sériole australienne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in inshore oceanic waters often associated with reefs, jetties and pylons (Ref. 6390), sometimes entering estuaries (Ref. 9563).  They Prefer warmer water (18-24°C) although they are occasionally found in cooler water (Ref. 27128).

species.name: Sériole babiane
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are benthopelagic near the coasts (Ref. 5217).  Smaller juveniles epipelagic in oceanic or offshore neritic waters.  Adults feed on squids and fishes (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Sériole bijou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are benthopelagic in coastal areas (Ref. 9283).  Marketed fresh and salted or dried (Ref. 9283).

species.name: Sériole du Japon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults exhibit shoaling habit (Ref. 9988).  They feed on plankton.  Juveniles are found among floating seaweeds (Ref. 12114, 12115).  Collection of young is the basis for prosperous aquaculture in Japan.  Raised in captivity and marketed fresh for sashimi (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Sériole guaimeque
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are pelagic or epibenthic and confined to coastal waters over the continental shelf.  They feed on fishes and shrimps.

species.name: Sériole guinéenne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are generally confined only in coastal waters over continental shelf, from the surface to at least 200 m.  They feed on squids and fishes.  Are confined to areas where surface temperature exceed 25°C, their distribution perhaps influenced by seasonal movements of the 18-27°C water mass along the African coast (Ref. 4233).  Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 4233).

species.name: Sériolelle argentine
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Sériolelle palmée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length estimated from other maximum lengths in Genus; replace with data asap (RF).

species.name: Sôhachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230). Feeds on crabs (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Taaning's lantern fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, found between 325-850 m during the day (most abundant at 400-500 m) and between 40-225 m at night (most abundant 100 m) (Ref. 4479).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951, 75154).

species.name: Taaningichthys paurolychnus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, known only from deeper than 900 m.  Sexually mature from about 65 mm (Ref. 4479).  Bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Tabarestan riffle minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taboga goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove streams with very fine silt-mud substrate (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Tachanovsky's gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus adiposalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus argentivittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus hoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus longispinalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus nitidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus nudiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stay at the bottom of warm waters.  Often enters port and river mouth.  Feeds on small shrimps and fishes (Ref. 41215).

species.name: Tachysurus spilotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tachysurus virgatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tadpole cod
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tadpole coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154). The first video footage of this species was taken from the North West Shelf of Western Australia where it is shown that the fish was on sandy bottom with no rocks visible; and during the 55 s movie, the fish swam slowly for a short distance (about 4-5 times body length) by moving its tail from side to side, stayed motionless for about 20 seconds and then turned right to face the camera by moving the pectoral-fins and the tail at the same time. There were no jet propulsion from the gill openings observed in this individual (Ref. 99940).

species.name: Tadpole goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy creeks draining mangrove samphire plains or freshwater floodplains, also artificial habitats such as water buffalo wallows and concrete drains.  Always seen near the coast in low-salinity environments (0-9% sea water).  Spawned in captivity.  About 30 eggs were laid, which took 9 days to hatch at 25°C.  After hatching the young were observed clinging to the walls of the aquarium, apparently feeding on algae (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Tadpole sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes. Found on soft bottoms and possibly rocky bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Reported near shore (Ref. 2850).  Prefers low temperatures (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Tadpole snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been taken from stagnant bottoms (Ref. 6885). Minimum depth from Ref. 006885.

species.name: Tadpole whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live at midwater as well as benthopelagic levels (Ref. 37108).

species.name: Taei’s Dwarfgoby
species.description: Found on outer reef slopes exposed to waves (Ref. 128853).

species.name: Taeniacara candidi
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Taeniamia bilineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at 12 meters on an isolated coral knoll in a protected shallow embayment with sandy bottom (Ref. 54391).

species.name: Taeniamia flavofasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass beds in shallow water and was collected by trawl between 3 - 13 meters (Ref. 54391).

species.name: Taeniamia kagoshimana
species.description: Observed from shallow coastal reef crests, among corals and in caves, often in less than 10 m depth (Ref. 126002).

species.name: Taeniamia pallida
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taeniochromis holotaenia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and rocky bottoms all over the lake.  Feeds on juvenile cichlids and invertebrates (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Taenioides caniscapulus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taenioides eruptionis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taenioides kentalleni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taenioides limicola
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in soft sediments of estuaries (Ref.43239).

species.name: Taeniolethrinops cyrtonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only one specimen known.  Probably lives over sand and probably filters its prey from the sand by passing it over the gills (Ref. 5700 and 5595).

species.name: Taeniolethrinops furcicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over open sandy areas, usually by itself.  Feeds by filtering the sand through the gills and retaining the insect larvae and other edible material found in the sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Taeniolethrinops laticeps
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taeniolethrinops praeorbitalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly occurs over open sand in shallow water but has also been caught at a depth of slightly more than 50 m (Ref. 54528).  Feeds on insect larvae that are sifted from the sand (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Taeniopsetta radula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Tahitian reef-damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in current-swept and surge areas of seaward and outer channel reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980).

species.name: Tahoe sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in various habitats but most common in large lakes such as Lake Tahoe and Pyramid Lake in Nevada, USA.  Also found in pools along lower reaches of streams.

species.name: Tahuantinsuyoa chipi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tahuantinsuyoa macantzatza
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and streams.  Maximum length 12 cm TL (Ref. 36377).

species.name: Taijiang snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in brackish water habitat of estuary, mangrove and earthen pond (Ref. 94984).

species.name: Tail beacon jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tail-barred rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found along rocky intertidal shorelines, benches, outer reef flats, and reef margins subject to some degree of wave action. Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tail-eye cardinalfish
species.description: Occurs on sand or rubble slopes.  Seen during the day around ledges at the base of large coral formations. In pairs or groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Tail-spot wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on shallow coral reefs and rocky shores (Ref. 9823).  Found solitary or in small groups on sheltered reefs over 15 m depth (Ref. 90102). Feed on small invertebrates such as polychaetes, copepods, isopods and forams (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Tailband toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tailbar cichlid
species.description: Inhabits lower to middle river valleys as well as lakes.  Found over rocks, sand, silt or mud.  Feeds on benthic detritus, aquatic plants and invertebrates (Ref. 7335).  Reported size in captivity  to about 25 cm for males and 18 cm for females (Paul Stevens, pers. comm.).

species.name: Tailbar goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms where the species iscommonly trawled (Ref. 121834).

species.name: Tailed sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taileyed goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Parachaeturichthys spp. Inhabit deep water (Ref. 42915). Rarely enters estuaries (Ref. 4833). Captured by trawls over mud bottom (Ref. 11441). Found to contain tetrodotoxin (TTX) and anhydrotetrodotoxin (anh-TTX) which causes paralytic food poisoning (Ref. 54777).

species.name: Tailface sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among coral and rubble (Ref. 1602)

species.name: Tailjet frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has been collected from tide pools and to outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602).  Benthic species (Ref. 58302, 75154).

species.name: Taillight shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occurs near vegetation in swamps, ponds, backwaters, pools of small to large rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294) and oxbow lakes.  Feeds on microcrustaceans (chydorid cladocerans, cyclopoid copepods, ostracods), rotifers, unicellular algae (desmids and diatoms), and small dipteran larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Tailmark wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102) on muddy bottoms, often deep in front of river mouths where land debris is scattered over the bottom; sometimes takes refuge in the mud burrows of other animals.  Adults were all seen in about 30 m and usually swim fast near the bottom (Ref. 48636).  Feeds on benthic animals (polychaete worms, crustaceans, also small fish) (Ref. 12420).  Minimum depth of 7 m from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Tailspot barracudina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 4056, 58302).  Juveniles are pale and transparent when fresh.

species.name: Tailspot cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tailspot coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in small groups in coastal lagoon and sheltered coral reef habitats 2-30 m deep (Ref. 48636, 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tailspot fangblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral outcrops, coastal reefs. They occur in small or large groups which may exceed 100 individuals (Ref. 90102). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). Mimicked by Cheilodipterus quinquelineatus (Ref. 90102). Minimum depth of 1 m reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Tailspot goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tailspot goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms at depths ranging from 10-120 meters (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Tailspot lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tailspot tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rapidly flowing water with a rocky bottom.  Like other taxa of the same genus, it is omnivorous and feeds on small fish.  Is known to be quarrelsome (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Tailstripe goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taimen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit piedmont and montane cold rivers with high oxygen concentrations.  They prefer to live in deeper holes with slow current for periods of reduced activity (day time, winter), but also lower reaches, estuaries, cold lakes and reservoirs.  Both juveniles and adults are territorial.  Adults frequently occur within their own restricted territory (deep holes below rapids and waterfalls, confluence of small tributaries, below bridge pillar or large rocks, bank excavations), which they abandon only foraging and spawning.  Young individuals do not maintain permanent territory.  Juveniles occur in fast-flowing waters, prey on drifting invertebrates and shift to fish diet after 1-3 years. Adults feed on fishes and terrestrial vertebrates.  They breed in shallow places with fast current on pebble bottom, immediately downstream of large deep pools, often in small river tributaries.  Usually undertake upriver migration for spawning in the upper reaches of tributaries.  Can overcome quite high obstacles while migrating to spawning sites.  Eggs, 5-6 mm in diameter, hatch after 28-38 days.  Alevins stay in gravel until yolk sac is absorbed after 10-15 days while young first remain near spawning site, then move downstream. Larger immature individuals of 2-4 years of age live in same sites as adults but separately below groups of adults or in smaller holes.  Life span reaches up to about 20 years (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to habitat loss, pollution and over harvesting (Ref. 58490), including angling tourism (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Taiwan coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water between rocks, mainly in surge areas (Ref. 57884). Cryptic, solitary inhabitant of shallow water (<6m) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Taiwan guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore and offshore (Ref. 9909).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Biology little known (Ref. 9909).  Utilized where it occurs, but details lacking (Ref. 9909).

species.name: Taiwan ku fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapid flowing streams.

species.name: Taiwan picnic seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taiwan sardinella
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in coastal waters.

species.name: Taiwan shoveljaw carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Taiwan sleeper shark
species.description: This species was collected in canyons surrounded by deep-sea longliner off eastern Taiwan at a depth greater than 500 m (Ref. 123759).

species.name: Taiwan spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taiwan tai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 41299).  Important food fish. In Okinawa (Japan), according to  local fishermen, this species usually reches more thatn 50 cm SL and a buyer from Ryukyu Is. reported that some individuals occasionally attain 65 cm SL (Ref. 124569).

species.name: Taiwan torpedo ray
species.description: Primarily found offshore. Life history unknown. Size reaches at least 62 cm TL; born at ca. 20-25 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Taiwanese barbel moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype collected from a tidal pool.

species.name: Taiwanese blind electric ray
