species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on continental slope. Mainly feeds on polychaete worms (Ref. 114953). Stomach contents include mud and the partial remains of an unidentified polychaete worm, plus unattached polychaete bristles and unidentified small white objects (Ref. 75959). Maturity size of males at 16-19 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Taiwanese deepwater dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shelf edges (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Taiwanese flashlight fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taiwanese moray eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow reef and rocky shorelines, benthic.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and small fishes.  All female specimens were found with ripe ovaries with ova measuring about 0.8-1.0 mm in diameter.  Spawning apparently occurs near or from July- August (Ref. 79874).

species.name: Taiwanese perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught as by-catch of bottom-trawl fisheries (Ref. 125677).

species.name: Taiwanese triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rarely seen species in bycatch of bottom trawlers (Ref. 121638)..

species.name: Taiwanese Wedgefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species that was recently discovered and not well known, but apparently lives in shallow water on the continental shelf. Probably feeds on bottom-dwelling crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 114953). Specimens caught are all immature that most probably the maximum length of this medium-size wedgefish could be less than 150 cm TL (Ref. 94805).

species.name: Tajamar livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu alboplumbeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Flesh, liver, ovaries, testes, skin and intestine toxic (Ref. 42715).  Occur in sandy and rubble areas adjacent to corals and rocky reefs. Observed to bury itself in sand, with only the eyes and parts of the dorsal body being exposed (Ref. 128523).

species.name: Takifugu basilevskianus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu bimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gonad, blood, skin, flesh and liver toxic (Ref. 42715).

species.name: Takifugu chinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu chrysops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu coronoidus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu exascurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu niphobles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. During high tide, mature individuals swim ashore in large numbers and spawn on beaches.  Eggs are left partially buried in sand and rubble (Ref. 240).

species.name: Takifugu ocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles are found in brackish and fresh waters, but adults need marine conditions.  Deadly poisonous to eat.

species.name: Takifugu orbimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Has properties for medicinal use  (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Takifugu pardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore in rock bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Takifugu plagiocellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu poecilonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Euryhaline (Ref. 37812).  Occurs near shore on rock bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Takifugu porphyreus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230).  The skin, gonads, liver, intestines and even the blood contain deadly toxin but still utilized fresh for human consumption, especially in Japan (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Takifugu pseudommus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovaries, liver, skin and intestine toxic (Ref. 43239).

species.name: Takifugu radiatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu reticularis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Internal organs and blood thought to be toxic, toxicity unknown (Ref. 42715).

species.name: Takifugu snyderi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovaries and liver extremely toxic, skin and intestine highly toxic, flesh innocuous or slightly toxic, and testes innocuous (Ref. 42715).

species.name: Takifugu stictonotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takifugu variomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Takita's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Talamancaheros sieboldii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate to fast flowing waters.  Juveniles feed primarily upon aquatic insects while adults feed on vegetable matter such as aufwuchs and algae.  Produces about 200-300 fry (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Talamancaheros underwoodi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Talbot's blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the surge channel zone of exposed outer reefs.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Talbot's demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral-rich areas of seaward reef slopes and deep lagoons (Ref. 9710).  Feed on zooplankton a short distance from the bottom.  Usually seen solitary on mixed coral and rubble patches (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Taliev’s sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy bottoms (Ref. 130169).

species.name: Talismania aphos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a depth of 1,830 m (Ref. 9068).

species.name: Talismania bussingi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Talismania kotlyari
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A specimen was taken from a depth between 980-1,050 m (Ref. 2711).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Talismania okinawensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Talking catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Said to produce toxic fluids.

species.name: Tall-fin goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux.

species.name: Tall-fin shrimp-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on white sand with free rubble (Ref. 30404). Lives in symbiotic association with either Alpheus ochrostriatus and A. randalli (Ref. 30404).

species.name: Tallapoosa darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tallapoosa shiner
species.description: Found in sandy and rocky runs of small to medium rivers, less often in flowing pools (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Tamanka maculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tamanka siitensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from land-locked, freshwater lakes close to the coast (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Tamar River goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet waters of brackish estuaries and coastal lakes; also in lower reaches of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).  Found on sand, silt or mud bottoms, usually in small aggregations (Ref. 9002, 44894).

species.name: Tamarin à bandes noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mostly on coral reefs and reef flats to at least 20 m depth. Juveniles secretive on inshore reefs. Large adults swim openly on reefs, singly or in small loose aggregations (Ref. 48636). Adults feed mainly by taking mouthfuls of sand and gravel, releasing sand from the gill opening after sorting the small animal prey and ejecting the inorganic fragments from the mouth. Gut contents may contain shrimps and 25% the crushed remains of the echinoids Echinometra and Diadema, these were large prey; remaining food material consisted of very small gastopods, bivalves, crabs, ophiuroids, foraminiferans, and unidentified eggs (Ref. 93095). Feed mainly on small crustaceans, mollusks and echinoderms (Ref. 9823). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Tamasopo cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in hard, clear waters with pH 7.8-8.3, over rock substrate.  Found syntopic with <i>Nosferatu pame, <i>N. steindachneri, <i>Xiphophorus montezumae, <i>Gambusia panuco, and <i>Astyanax mexicanus among other fish species (Ref. 99935).

species.name: Tamaulipas shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy channels of large creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Tambopata catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tambour brésilien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur usually over mud and sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters and in estuaries where the nursery and feeding grounds are located.  They feed mainly on worms, crustaceans and fishes.  An excellent foodfish.  Sold fresh and frozen; eaten fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Tambour croca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually over sandy or muddy bottoms in coastal waters to about 60 m depth.  Occurs in nursery and feeding grounds in river estuaries during summer and fall.  Juveniles often stay in the estuarine waters throughout the year.  Feeds mainly on worms, small crustaceans and organic detritus.  A small specimen of this species was caught in Tokyo Bay, Japan, probably brought in with the ballast water of a ship (Ref. 10325).

species.name: Tambour fin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along sandy coasts and bays; also in estuaries, river mouths, and coastal lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans, mollusks and worms (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Tambour jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, including semi-enclosed sea areas, in mud to sandy mud bottom (Ref. 11230).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Tambour rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over muddy and sandy bottoms in coastal waters and in estuaries where the nursery and feeding grounds are located.  Adults form schools.  Feeding habits vary with ontogenic development and season; juveniles feed on benthic migratory crustaceans and sessile boring mollusks while  adults are benthos-feeders and occasionally capture fish (Ref. 27).  Undergoes seasonal migration.  An important food fish which is usually marketed fresh and salted.

species.name: Tambour rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over sand and sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters and estuaries.  Abundant in surf zone.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, mollusks and fishes.  Utilized fresh and frozen; can be pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Tambour voilier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along sandy shores and bays, also in estuaries and lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on shrimps, fishes, mollusks, other crustaceans, and worms (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Tambour à grand œil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal lagoons, estuaries and river mouths; also in deep water far from the coast (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Tambour à gros yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 2113). Found in muddy or muddy-sandy bottoms shallower than 120 m depth (Ref. 43239). Feed on crustaceans and fishes.

species.name: Tami River rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tan bristlemouth
species.description: Meso- to bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  Oceanic, precise depth range dependent upon developmental stage, latitude, season (Ref. 4769).  Does not exhibit diel vertical migrations (Ref. 4769).  Lipid content is 2.3 % in fresh body weight and wax ester is 34.0 % in total lipids (Ref. 9193).

species.name: Tan Hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A 7.02 cm SL specimen of this species, collected 8 July 1990 on reefs off the Discovery Bay Marine Laboratory in Jamaica, had a freshly consumed a cleaner goby, Elacatinus evelynae (16.5 mm SL) in its stomach content (Ref. 88139).

species.name: Tana labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water over sandy bottoms (Ref. 5595, 52161). Is a mud-feeder (Ref. 52161), feeds from the biocover and sediment on the sand (Ref. 5595). Also caught using weirs and baskets; formerly very abundant in Malawi, but now rare except where rivers drain undisturbed soil; possible that silt prevents development of eggs (Ref. 4967). Indications that it may leave the lake and run up rivers to spawn (Ref. 52161).

species.name: Tana sardine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers with swiftly flowing water with large rock outcrops that formed small waterfalls (Ref. 121710). Stomachs dissected from a few specimens were found to contain chironomid larvae, ants, mayflies and various body parts of winged-adult stages of unidentified dipterans (Ref. 121710). Males have breeding tubercles on the top of head, underside of jaws, cheeks, and operculum, with fine tubercles on the pectoral fin and the ventral sides of the body; nuptial males also have an orange patch of pigment in the middle of the lower lobe of the caudal fin (Ref. 121710).

species.name: Tana squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205). Inhabits small streams, main rivers and flooded pools (Ref. 30558). Extremely abundant in ox-bow lakes and river cut-offs in the Lower Tana River (Ref. 39831). Breeding occurs shortly after floods, when ripe fish enter small streams leading to floodwater pools, where they breed; this migration is rather sudden, adult fish migrate in large schools upstream over a period of less than a week (3 to 4 days); one or two additional smaller migrations may occur after the main peak; the stimulus triggering this migration is probably closely connected with rainfall (Ref. 96595).

species.name: Tana-churchill
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanaka's dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reefs, in caves and crevices or beneath overhangs on steep slopes in 20-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Tanaka's snailfish
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone (Ref. 11230). Minimum depth reported at 50 m (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Tanaka's wrasse
species.description: Found in coral reefs but secretive (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Tanakia koreensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanakia lanceolata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanakia latimarginata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mostly in clear and shallow (40-120 cm deep) low to medium-gradient large creeks to medium rivers, over coarse sand to pebble substrates.  Inhabits backwaters or shallow pools near vegetation from autumn to spring.  Large individual are usually collected in rock- and gravel-bottomed riffles during summer. The type series was collected together with the congener <i>T. lanceolata, along with the following species in the subfamily Acheilognathinae:  <i>Acheilognathus macropterus, <i>A. majusculus, <i>A. rhombeus, <i>A. yamatsutae, <i>Rhodeus ocellatus, <i>R. notatus and <i>R. sinensis.  Spawns from April to August.  Spawning males aggresively defend a territory around a mussel-spawning site.  Also collected together with unionid mussels (<i>Unio douglasiae, <i>Anodonta woodiana, <i>Lanceolaria grayana and <i>Solenaia triangularis, though the major host mussels are still not known (Ref. 97360).

species.name: Tanakia shimazui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanakia somjinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tandanus bellingerensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on altitude zone, this species is common to the coastal plain (3-30 m), lowland (31-200 m), and slopes (201-400 m) but occurs occasionally in upland areas (401-700m), and rarely in highlands (701-1,100 m) (Ref. 116005).

species.name: Tandanus tropicanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal rivers (Ref. 96080).

species.name: Tandikan goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found only in the Cayulo River which is a small stream (length approximately 4 km including 1 km of an estuary) flowing into Ulugan Bay on South China Sea-side of the island. The stream system is surrounded by mountains of about 200-400 m above sea level. The Cayulo Falls is composed of a series of small waterfalls, located at the middle reaches of this stream and the species was found at both the lower and upper reaches of this waterfall, as well as pools in the middle of the falls. It was abundant in this site with many other goby species, cyprinids, and a jungle perch species (Ref. 125663).

species.name: Tangachromis dhanisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the dwarf species living in deep water over the sunken sand plains.  Has been caught with drag nets down to 100 m.  Feeds on copepods (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Tanganikallabes alboperca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is likely to inhabit rocky bottoms over a range of depths (Ref. 90118). Feeds on fish eggs, platythelphusid crab, and insect larvae (Ref. 90118).

species.name: Tanganikallabes mortiauxi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in littoral to benthic zones over rocky bottoms; this species may inhabit rocky bottoms over a wide range of depths (Ref. 78218, 90118). It appears to be an opportunistic, generalist predator feeding on eggs of fish species, platythelphusid crabs, atyid shrimps and insect larvae (Ref. 90118).

species.name: Tanganikallabes stewarti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is likely to inhabit rocky bottoms, over a range of depths (Ref. 90118).

species.name: Tanganyika Clown
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky areas (Ref. 53528). Adults occur in the turbulent, highly oxygenated shallow waters of the surf zone; found in the shallows of a gradually sloping rocky coast where some sand is found between the rocks; solitary and to some extent, territorial; heavy body and small swim bladder result in negative buoyancy (Ref. 6770). Feeds on algae which are scraped from the rocks (Ref. 6770, 46829). Both parents brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 52921, 86760).

species.name: Tanganyika killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores, but also found offshore (4967).  12 cm max TL (Ref. 31267).  Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Tanganyika lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers and river mouths, coastal swamps, estuaries and other shallow parts of Lake Tanganyika (Ref. 47311). Occurs in small groups near river banks; found in slow flowing and stagnant water of river mouths and deltas near lakes (Ref. 36901). Feeds on algae, fish scales, termites, chironomid larvae, prawns and copepods (Ref. 43507). Not a seasonal killifish; easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139). Eggs have development time of 14 days in captivity; sexual maturity reached at age of 5 months (Ref. 47311).

species.name: Tanganyika lates
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles live in a specific inshore habitat until they reach 18 cm (Ref. 2216) also found near and in slow flowing affluents (Ref. 36901). Adults found from the littoral to near the limit of the oxygenated zone (Ref. 2216). Solitary, lurking predator, probably favoring rocky bottoms and unspecialized in its fish diet; highly susceptible to intensive fishing (Ref. 2216). Feeds largely on benthic cichlids (Ref. 4967, 36901), but also takes sardines (Ref. 4967). Threatened due to over harvesting (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Tanganyika tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is the dominant tilapiine species in Lake Tanganyika, despite the presence of the normally invasive Nile tilapia (Ref. 118638). It is not normally found far up into inflowing rivers (Ref. 118638). It has been reported to browse the surface film of sheltered waters; stomachs contained large quantities of the diatoms Pinnularia and Navicula with some sand-grains (Ref. 2). A maternal mouthbrooder; males defend territories in shallow water in sheltered sandy or muddy areas, and dig simple pits in the substrate (Ref. 118638). A large fast-growing species well represented in fishery catches in and around Lake Tanganyika; currently being promoted as an aquaculture species and occasionally exported for the aquarium trade (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Tangaroa shrimpgoby
species.description: Occurs in patches of fine sand on seaward reefs and uses alpheid shrimp burrows for refuge.  Found in clear coastal and inner reefs on rubble flats and slopes in 6-20 meters depth range (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Tangerine darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear, fairly deep, rocky pools (usually below riffles) of creeks and small rivers.  Large males often found in rocky riffles (Ref. 5723).  Juveniles feed on mayfly and dipteran larvae, while the adults consume caddisfly larvae (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Tanichthys albiventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected at a small hill stream, about 2 m wide on average, located in the depths of the forest. Water depth varied from approximately 0.4 to 1 m and the bottom consisted of mud mixed with sand. Some aquatic plants (Cryptocoryne crispatula and Blyxa sp.) in the lower part of the habitat. Other fish species found were Oryzias pectoralis, Macropodus hongkongensis and Rhinogobius cf. duospilus (Ref. 125918),

species.name: Tanichthys flavianalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanichthys kuehnei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanichthys micagemmae
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found in a wide, shallow stream with fast current and sandy bottom (Ref. 41279).

species.name: Tanichthys thacbaensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tanzanian tigerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tape blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near coast in beds and clumps of algae (Ref. 51666), in shallow waters down to 6-8 m in sandy grounds (Ref. 102278).

species.name: Taper-tail ribbonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Tapered Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A freshwater fish that is unable to undertake diadromous migrations. It is recorded from a cool, small (0.5-1.5 m), shallow (0.1-0.5 m), clear and slow-flowing, partly shaded freshwater creek in a forested catchment. The substrate consisted mainly of cobbles, with some gravel, bedrock and sand, and the instream cover was provided mostly by rock, also by small amounts of undercut banks, timber debris and vegetation overhang. Recorded at densities of 0.01-0.9 fish/m2  and collected with the native species Broadfinned Galaxias, Shortfinned Eel, Central Highlands Spiny Crayfish, Gippsland Spiny Crayfish and Common Freshwater Shrimp. An individual was recorded with a short, thin, white worm (probably nematode), coiled and pointed at both ends, from amongst fat deposits around the stomach in the body cavity (Ref. 98815).

species.name: Tapertail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 6808). Adults feed on lantern-fishes (Myctophidae) and possibly euphausiid crustaceans (Ref. 6739). Oviparous, with planktonic larvae (Ref. 36609). They have the ability to discharge dark brown fluid from the ink-sac when alarmed.

species.name: Tapertail ribbonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic.  Found at or near surface at night, deeper during the day.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36610).

species.name: Tapertail shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sand-rubble or mud bottoms in 15-48 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Taphorn’s tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tapir du Cap
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 9563).  Feeds on benthic copepods and polychaetes (Ref. 27637).

species.name: Tapir tadpole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tapiroid grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit salt and brackish waters of bays and estuaries, penetrating into fresh water (Ref. 1601).  Juveniles are sometimes found in streams within 5-10 km of the sea (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tarakihi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults demersal on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563) to depths of 450 m (Ref. 33616).  Juveniles tend to live near shallow reefs (Ref. 6390).  Postlarvae inhabit offshore waters and are found in surface waters at night (Ref. 9072).  Average weight is 1800 g.  Feed on polychaete worms, crustaceans, mollusks and echinoderms (Ref. 28626).  Flesh is quite good eating.  Often sold as tiki fillets.

species.name: Target shrimp goby
species.description: Occurs in silty bottoms of lagoon or coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).  Common near areas with  terrestrial runoff (Ref. 1602).  Lives with alpheid shrimps (Ref. 30404).  Found in coastal waters, near reefs on sand with rubble (Ref. 48637). Minimum depth from Ref. 090102.

species.name: Targeur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on stony or rocky ground in the algal zone, and feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 4703).  Spawns in March - June (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Targie naine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky bottoms between 10 and 180 m.  Feeds on small fish and invertebrates (Ref. 4703).  Spawns in April - July (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Tariqilabeo bicornis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives near the bottom of the river and feeds mainly on detritus and filamentous algae (Ref. 28024).

species.name: Tarphops elegans
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tarphops oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tarr's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype which was collected at the base of a drop-off in 15 m.

species.name: Tarred snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Tarsistes philippii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tarumania walkerae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected specimens were deeply buried into massive leaf-litter deposits in isolated pools in the riparian forest (with some sites had no standing water, while other were up to 70-cm deep). All these pools join the main river channel during the high-water season and which possibly allows specimens to move and colonize suitable habitats. The new species so far has only been found in temporary pools, during the low-water period and its whereabouts during the flood season are yet unknown (in large measure due to difficulties in collecting during such time). The only other fish consistently associated with Tarumania walkeri is an undescribed species of the catfish (Phreatobius, although some other species, mostly represented as juveniles, have been sporadically caught in the same pools, (Microsternarchus bilineatus, Brachyhypopomus beebei, Apistogramma sp., Aequidens pallidus, Scoloplax dolicholophia, Microphilypnus amazonicus, Curimatopsis sp., Brycon sp., C. punctatus, Nannostomus eques, Copella cf. nattereri); all of which are probably just stray specimens that accidentally got trapped in the pools because of water-level changes in the hydric cycle. It is likely that this species follows the water-substrate interface along the hydric cycle, thus staying in more superficial layers when there is plenty of standing water and sinking into deep substrate as the water level recedes. This fish feeds on invertebrates, some captured specimens regurgitated whole small freshwater shrimps (Euryrhynchus). Accessory aerial respiration was observed, in the form of air taken via the mouth and held temporarily in the branchial cavity, which, along with the gular region, then becomes noticeably inflated. In the aquarium, the aerial respiration is induced by low-water conditions, observed fish gulped air at surface and kept it in the oral cavity for nearly 35 s before expelling an air bubble to take another gulp almost immediately and the same fish repeated such behaviour up to ten times in sequence. A large live nematode (Goezia spinulosa) was found in the branchial cavity of a specimen and also on the gills and in the intestines. Live specimens can move equally easily forwards and backwards, its pelvic fins can move independently of each other and deflect 180 degrees anteriorly. This fish displays remarkable stability and manoeuvrability in the water column and can remain stationary in contorted positions in narrow spaces amidst irregular substrate (not contacting any surface) (Ref. 116356).

species.name: Tashkent riffle bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tasmanian blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in rock pools and shallow estuaries, commonly under jetties along tops of pylons (Ref. 9002).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tasmanian clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal and rocky estuaries, often under rocks (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Tasmanian codling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 75154).  Described from the original literature only (Ref. 1371).

species.name: Tasmanian mudfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, drains and ponds.  The species is likely capable of aestivation as individuals are sometimes encountered in mud or beneath logs or stones when pools dry up.  Feeds partly on bottom detritus and insects.

species.name: Tasmanian numbfish
species.description: Found on sand or mud bottoms, occasionally near rocky reefs (Ref. 12951).  Feeds on amphipods, shrimp, and worms (Ref. 12951). Produces 1-8 (normally 3) pups during each gestation. Both sexes mature at ca. 20-21 cm TL; born at 9-12 cm TL (Ref. 114953)

species.name: Tasmanian perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Tasmanian ruffe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Subadults are found near the surface over deep water; juveniles occur inshore from surface waters down to at least 50 m (Ref. 9563).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.  Habitat change gradually occur during the growth of the fish, from epipelagic to benthic (mesobenthopelagic), including talassobenthic.  Of no commercial value (Ref. 54802).

species.name: Tasmanian smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits estuaries and the lower reaches of coastal streams (Ref. 44894). Occurs in lowland streams, forming schools that feeds at or near the surface on insects and zooplankton. Found among the annual Tasmanian whitebait migrations in shoals with Lovettia seali and various galaxiids. Most of the life cycle is spent at the sea (Ref. 44894). The species is thought to have an anadromous life cycle involving upstream migration of adults from the sea prior to spawning. Newly hatched larvae are carried on tides out to sea where they develop to maturity (ref. 44894).

species.name: Tasmanian snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Tasmanian whitebait
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal seas, estuaries and rivers.  An annual species, with an anadromous life cycle.  In spring, large shoals of adults migrate from the sea into rivers and estuaries to spawn.  Eggs are deposited on the bottom or among debris.  They hatch in 2-3 weeks, and the fry are swept out to sea where they undergo development.  Adults die shortly after spawning.  Also known as Derwent whitebait (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Tasseled blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in small groups in sheltered turbid coastal reefs (Ref. 90102).  Benthic in algae and fouling communities in estuaries (Ref. 58302).   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tasselfin longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205). Collected specimens from surge channels in 1-4 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Tasselled anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300) to at least a depth of 45 m (Ref. 9563). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Tasselled Threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Associated with yellow sponges.   Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tasselsnout flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters and reef areas (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Tassled coffinfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Edible (Ref. 637).

species.name: Tatia aulopygia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches sexual maturity above 8.0 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia bockmanni
species.description: The single specimen was captured in an area with gravel and rocky bottom, near the margin of the river (F. Bockmann, pers. comm.). The fishes from Bahia were captured by seine at night in a riverine beach in clear, shallow water with sand and gravel bottom in depth less than 1.70 m.  Stomach contents of two specimens were partially digested fragments of insect larvae and nymphs (Ref. 56311).

species.name: Tatia boemia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers with bedrock and loose stones on the bottom (Ref. 26675).  Nocturnal. Reaches sexual maturity above 5.24 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia britskii
species.description:
Found in areas with rocks and rapids near cofferdams in the main channel of the upper rio
Paraná.  Stomach contents include insect larvae, including Chironomidae, and other invertebrate fragments.  Attains sexual maturity at about 3.3 cm SL (Ref. 103263).

species.name: Tatia brunnea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sympatric with Tatia intermedia in some rivers in Suriname and French Guiana and also in the Trombetas river (Ref. 79512). Rather rare, occurs in the slow parts of creeks. May easily be mistaken as juveniles of Glanidium leopardus with which it is distinguished by means of the pectoral spines (having projections vs. smooth) and by the number of rays in the anal fin (8-9 vs. 12-14). Sexual dimorphism in males appear at a length of 3.5-4.0 cm. Its small size makes it interesting for aquarists (Ref. 35381). Reported sizes at sexual maturity are above 5.46 cm SL and above 7.0 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia caxiuanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Attains sexual maturity at 2.93 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia dunni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tatia galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches sexual maturity above 5.42 cm SL (Ref.  79512).

species.name: Tatia gyrina
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is typically associated with blackwater environment, mainly in rivers.  In central Amazon, it occurs both in black and clear waters but only in dense vegetation where there is minimal light.  Field data suggest that this fish inhabits water with low pH, low conductivity and low level of dissolved oxygen.  Reaches sexual maturity above 2.8 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia intermedia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 27188).  Reaches sexual maturity above 5.04 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia jaracatia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tatia marthae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tatia meesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is characterized by fast flowing water over huge boulders.  Found in large pool and backwater area with a substrate of sand, gravel and rubble over bedrock (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia neivai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in semi-lotic environments.  Some individuals were observed hidden within marginal vegetation or found inside crevices of submersed trunks.  Reaches sexual maturity above 4.81 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reaches sexual maturity above 8.0 cm SL (Ref. 79512).

species.name: Tatia simplex
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tatia strigata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in an igarape of rivers, hidden in submerged trunk.  Feeds mainly on juvenile and adult insects.

species.name: Tattoo-chin rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the intertidal zone of rocky shores, benches and surge seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tattooedj jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is probably a deep-water species, similar to its sister-species Opistognathus aurolineatus (reflected in the depth range given) (Ref. 128653). Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Tau sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Taunayia bifasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tauredophidium hextii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).  Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Taurocottus bergii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tawny blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tawnystripe eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Taylor's catfish
species.description: Inhabits upper reaches of shallow flowing streams in turbid waters.  Feeds on pulpy fruits of terrestrial plants and terrestrial insects.

species.name: Taylor's garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty sand and seagrass bottom.  Occurs singly or in small groups (Ref. 48635). Individuals from Cenderawasih Bay, West Papua, Indonesia with slightly smaller spots (Ref 90102).

species.name: Taylor's inflator filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary among seaweed, hard and soft corals, sponges and crinoids. Inhabits coastal reefs in 8-35 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Tazard à larges écailles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Form schools near individual bays and reefs in Barrier Reef waters.  With the rising tide, they move into shallow water over the reef flats, feeding on schools of clupeoid fishes that concentrate there.  Utilized as a food fish.

species.name: Teacher brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Teapa cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teardrop darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723).  Adults feed on midge and blackfly larvae, copepods and cladocerans, and immature mayflies and caddisflies (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Teardrop mosquito
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found near the shore where vegetation is present in both pond and river habitats.  Feeds mainly on benthic, vegetation-associated invertebrates, and on terrestrial shoreline organisms.

species.name: Teardrop threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on mud or sand bottoms in depths greater than 50 m. There is no major fishery for this species (Ref. 3810, 125700).

species.name: Teardrop tubeshoulder
species.description: Bathypelagic to benthopelagic, exceptionally as shallow as 100-120 m (Ref. 4461).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Teared dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tearful dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Photographed or collected from lagoon, slope, and drop-off coral-reef habitats (Ref. 95167).

species.name: Teary monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Techirghiol stickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit springs.  Mature individuals spawn in February - October (Ref. 59043).  Males build, guard and aerate the nest where the eggs are deposited (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tectus lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms of the continental shelf and inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 48635, 75154).

species.name: Tefenni minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telatrygon acutirostra
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Teleocichla centrarchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teleocichla cinderella
species.description: Espèce de poissons de la famille des cichlidae. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 12251).  Maximum length 14 cm TL (Ref. 13614).

species.name: Teleocichla gephyrogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teleocichla monogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teleocichla prionogenys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teleocichla proselytus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Teleocichla wajapi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rapids with clear water and rocky riverbed composed of an array of material, from pebbles to boulders or slabs.  Observed to remain mostly stationary in areas where the water velocity was slower, apparently protected between slabs of rock or close to the river bank (Ref. 93336).

species.name: Teleogramma brichardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding, cave spawner (Ref. 52307). Maximum TL was recorded at 11.0 cm (Ref. 5703).

species.name: Teleogramma depressa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding, cave spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Teleogramma gracile
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding, cave spawner (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Teleogramma monogramma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rheophilic; pair-bonding, cave spawner (Ref. 52307). Maximum TL was recorded at 9.7 cm (Ref. 5703).

species.name: Telescope fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large low tidal pools and surge channels (Ref. 9003). Feeds on zooplankton in the water column (Ref. 120445).  May be found living within soft bodied invertebrates (e.g. salps) (Ref. 9003).  Juveniles probably pelagic (Ref. 48372).

species.name: Telescope shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and flowing pools, often near riffles, of clear creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on terrestrial and surface insects, and immature benthic insects (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Telescope tadpole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Immature female (13.8 cm SL) has small ovarian eggs not more than 1 mm in diameter (Ref. 41470).

species.name: Telescopefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).  The species is rare.  Inhabits deep water.  Famous for its bizarre shape and unusual eyes.

species.name: Telestes beoticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams, preferring cool and swift waters associated with springs (Ref. 59043).  Inhabits clear waters of rivers and lakes  where it forms small schools in the middle or upper layers of the water as well as close to the bottom.  Frequents areas with aquatic plants.  Field observations have shown that adults feed on zooplankton, small insects and larvae (Ref. 12266).  Spawns in January-March (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to pollution, water abstraction and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Telestes comes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telestes dabar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water of river sections that are adjacent to and filled from underground springs. The water is clean with no current (Ref. 89938).

species.name: Telestes karsticus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telestes metohiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes and in water courses at high altitudes and on low plains, with little current (Ref. 26100).  Inhabits streams with clear water.  Enters subterranean waters in karstic areas.  Ripe individuals are encountered in May (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to pollution and habitat destruction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Telestes miloradi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telestes montenigrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide range of habitats from small mountain streams to lake shores.  Reported to feed on plankton and bottom fauna (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Telestes muticellus
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in main rivers and small streams (Ref. 45688).  Prefers to inhabit streams of piedmont and hilly areas, with moderately cold water, but may be found in most habitats.  Feeds predominantly on aquatic invertebrates, also on epilithic algae.  Spawns in areas with swift, shallow waters (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Telestes pleurobipunctatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland water courses with little current  (Ref. 26100).  Also occurs in streams with moderate to swift current, often in cavities along shores.  Feeds predominantly on insect larvae, supplemented by other animal and plant material.  Deposits  adhesive eggs, 1.9mm in diameter (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction (Ref. 26100), and water abstraction which is a serious threat over most of its range (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Telestes polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in water courses at high altitudes and on the lowland rivers, with little current (Ref. 26100). Also occurs in clear streams and springs. Enters subterranean waters during winter or droughts. Omnivorous. Threatened due to water abstraction, pollution and introduction of Salmo trutta. Considered on the very edge of extinction, with a single small population known (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Telestes turskyi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow-flowing and still water.  Possibly enters subterranean waters during winter or droughts (Ref. 59043).  Occurs in water courses on the low plains, with little current and in lakes.  Feeds on invertebrates.  Threatened due to water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Tellia apoda
species.description: Occurs in wells and brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Telmatherina abendanoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Largest of the telmatherinids from Lake Matano; very short gill-rakers (Ref. 7305)

species.name: Telmatherina albolabiosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky habitat in small groups consisting of two to three fish (Ref. 86891).

species.name: Telmatherina bonti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatherina obscura
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatherina opudi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatherina prognatha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatherina sarasinorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatherina wahjui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatochromis bifrenatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is an ideal beginner's fish.  Sometimes found as deep as 20 m depth.  Always solitary in very clear water.  Often seen wandering close to rocks or over coarse sand between rock patches.  Omnivorous (Ref. 54948), feeds on microorganisms (Ref. 6770).  Forms temporary pair bonds; the male defends the territory while the female takes care of her offspring (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Telmatochromis brachygnathus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Telmatochromis brichardi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky habitats; feeds on algae; cave brooder that selects tiny holes in substrate as nesting sites (Ref. 46829). Forms temporary pair bonds; the male defends the territory while the female takes care of her offspring (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Telmatochromis dhonti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Have been discovered over many types of rock substrates even in very muddy water.  Omnivorous, feeds on microorganisms (Ref. 6770).  Forms temporary pair bonds; the male defends the territory while the female takes care of her offspring (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Telmatochromis temporalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are not light shy and swim in the open.  Have been discovered over many types of rock substrates even in very muddy water.  Lives in rather deep water for such small species, specimens having been found as deep as 20 m, although they seem to prefer a range between 5 and 10 m.  Always solitary.  Omnivorous.  Feeds on microorganisms and small fish (Ref. 6770).  Aufwuchs eater (Ref. 54948).  Forms temporary pair bonds; the male defends the territory while the female takes care of her offspring (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Telmatochromis vittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rather deep water for such small species, specimens having been found as deep as 20 m, although they seem to prefer a range between 5 and 10 m.  Swims in the open.  Omnivorous, feeds on microorganisms (Ref. 6770).  Usually solitary but form temporary pair bonds; the male defends the territory while the female takes care of her offspring (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Tembeassu marauna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Temperate scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly on rocky reefs and also on sandy bottoms scattered among rocky reefs (Ref. 118151).

species.name: Ten spotted live-bearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Viviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Ten-tooth wrasse
species.description: Found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Tenant goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate sponge dwellers. Live deep within canals of the sponges, near the openings to the incurrent canals. Sponges provide species with protection from predators and an available food source in many invertebrates. Eggs found within sponge or small plankton brought through incurrent pores (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Tenellus leporhinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tenellus ternetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tenellus trimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tengara catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rivers and ponds in plains and submontane regions (Ref. 41236) in  flowing and standing waters (Ref. 4833).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tennessee dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in gravel-, sand-, and silt-bottomed pools of spring-fed headwaters (Ref. 5723, 10294, 86798).

species.name: Tennessee shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Tentacle dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tentacled butterfly ray
species.description: Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Tentacled dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand of shallow reefs, from tide pools to as deep as 30 m (Ref. 1602).  Also inhabits sheltered reef lagoon habitats, usually in on algae reef near seagrass beds (Ref. 48636).  Occurs solitary in weedy areas and sand-rubble bottoms (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Tenuicephalus melampeplus
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tenuicephalus multitrabs
species.description: The largest number of specimens were caught at great distance from the nearest shelf areas in the central Indian Ocean, nearly 2000 km above the Ninety-East Ridge. It was caught well above the sea bottom indicating that these fishes might obtain a bathypelagic rather than a benthopelagic life style (Ref. 125143).

species.name: Tenuicephalus silus
species.description: Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). The species does not venture far from the shelf break (Ref. 125143). Reproductive strategy possibly similar to other members of this family featuring oviparity, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tenuicephalus squamilabrus
species.description: This species does not seem to venture far away from the continental slopes (Ref. 125143).

species.name: Tephrinectes sinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Tequila splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This fish generally inhabits rivers, but now appears to only occur in one small pond in Mexico.  The locality was at an elevation of 1311 m and specimens were usually caught in the quiet part of the river, at a depth of less than 1 m., with mud and silt, and was nearly continuously stirred by domestic livestock. It was reported that the only known extant population inhabits a spring pool, 4 m in diameter with an average depth of 20 cm. Little is known about the species in the wild. However, in aquaria, sexual maturity can be reached within six to ten weeks and broods are known to number as man as 20-29 offspring, but females in their first year of reproduction are reported to have fewer than ten (Ref. 117910).

species.name: Teramulus waterloti
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Terapon à quatre lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are coastal species often found in brackish waters; common in estuaries.  They croak when taken from the water.  Usually forming schools.  Juveniles in seagrass beds and in mangrove bays (Ref. 48635).  Feed on small fishes and invertebrates.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Terapon à queue rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters, entering brackish estuaries (Ref. 3132) and mangrove areas (Ref. 7300).  Also in fresh waters (Ref. 30573).  Feed on fishes and invertebrates.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Terateleotris aspro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in backwaters (Ref. 27732).  Inhabits gravelly-sandy bottom of a shallow-flowing area just downstream of the exit of river underground course (Ref. 42922).

species.name: Terek barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits piedmont and montane stretches of rivers and streams with stone or gravel bottom.  Occurs from upstreams to uppermost reaches in mountains. Feeds on invertebrates, terrestrial insects and diatoms.  In still habitats, this species takes terrestrial insects and zooplankton as food.  Undertakes upriver migration and spawns in shallow tributaries.  Larvae and yearlings stay in spawning streams while adults migrate downriver.  Abundant in the upper reaches of rivers and invasive in Don drainage (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Terek nase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits piedmont and mountain rivers with strong current and rock to gravel bottom.  Feeds predominantly on detritus and also on periphytic algae and benthic invertebrates, especially during first year of live.   Spawns over hard bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ternate damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common among coral-rich areas of sheltered coastal reefs (Ref. 9710), with algae and staghorn corals to about 15 m depth, especially around the rock islands in Palau, they aggregate with A. curacao. They spawn in groups and each pair claims a small section of the reef (Ref. 7247). Dead coral branches serve as nest (Ref. 90102). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are laid on a cleared section of the coral and guarded by the parents (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Terpuga
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles form large schools near the surface; adults are benthic (Ref. 559).  Utilized fresh, dried or salted and frozen; can be pan-fried and broiled (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Terrassier géant
species.description: Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 12204).  Probably spends part of its life buried (Ref. 12204).

species.name: Terrassier tacheté
species.description: Burrows in soft muddy bottoms from shallow water to 110 m depth. Feeds mainly on benthic infauna found in and around its burrow system; its prey consisting of various amphipods, polychaetes, shrimp and small fish (Ref. 87300).

species.name: Terrassier à six lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud and sand bottoms to depths of about 56 meters; often in brackish waters (Ref. 51666).  Benthic; feeds on worms, crustaceans, sea urchins and molluscs (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Terry's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Terver's lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small rivers and brooks (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Tessellated blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in attached, empty barnacle shells in clear waters, usually on pilings, buoys and rock ledges at or near surface.  Recorded from oil platforms.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Teta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear fast flowing streams and feeds on periphyton (Ref. 11225).

species.name: Tetha’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species occupies a very specific microhabitat and depth range, observed and collected exclusively from a very sheltered and coral-rich lagoon (Kwatisore South Bay) with limited water flow and water temperatures that are commonly elevated above that of the surrounding reef areas (usually 30-31° C). Depth range of occurrence is rather narrow (25-30 m depth) and it was not found either deeper or shallower than this, despite extensive searching. It was found resting and moving about on the surfaces of the extensive foliose and plating coral colonies (mostly Pachyseris and Turbinaria spp. colonies) in the lagoon. Found in association with other coral goby species, including E. atriventris, E. fallax, E. lachdeberei, and Trimma emeryi (Ref. 96307).

species.name: Tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetracamphilius angustifrons
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetracamphilius clandestinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetracamphilius notatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetracamphilius pectinatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetractenos hamiltoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow estuaries, often buried in sand with only eyes exposed.  A schooling species (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Tetragondacnus spilotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus anostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus argenteus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Consumed locally for recovery or during illness.  Carnivorous (Ref. 42843).

species.name: Tetragonopterus carvalhoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus chalceus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in creeks with rapidly flowing water over sandy areas and slow flowing water over plant debris (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Tetragonopterus daguae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus franciscoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus georgiae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occupies the counter current zones of rivers where it hides under the rocks.  It is constantly on the look out for food items that fall into the water (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Tetragonopterus juruena
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus kuluene
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus ommatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus rarus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetragonopterus signatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetranematichthys barthemi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetranematichthys quadrifilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetranematichthys wallacei
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetraodon barbatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the Mekong mainstream as well as in its large tributaries, especially in areas with rocky, sandy or muddy substrates. Often syntopic with Tetraodon suvattii and T. baileyi (Ref. 95519).

species.name: Tetraodon duboisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetraodon implutus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetraodon miurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers; sometimes found in rapids (Ref. 2829). Aquarium keeping: solitary, agressive towards others (René König, pers. comm., 2004) .

species.name: Tetraodon pustulatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles and adults are common in the mainstream river (Ref. 2829). Ventral pocket communicates gill chamber with oesophagus, allowing the fish to inflate its body like a ball (Ref. 57417). Liver and sexual organs are poisonous, but fishermen of the upper Cross carefully remove them and eat the flesh of this species (Ref. 81679). Some references to Tetraodon guttifer in the literature may represent misidentifications of T. pustulatus (Ref. 81679).

species.name: Tetraodon schoutedeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in large rivers (Ref. 2829), i.e. not a brackish water species.  Feeds on benthic animals such as snails and worms.  Solitary, aggressive against conspecifics.  Eggs are deposited on leaves and defended by the male.

species.name: Tetraodon waandersii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tetraroge nigra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 559).  Possess venom glands at the base of some of the spines.

species.name: Tetrosomus stellifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tevegae pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal to outer reefs, typically in small groups in caves (Ref. 48637).  Forms loose aggregations associated with shallow pockets and caves of steep drop-offs.  Hovers in a head-up position (often vertical, posture in the water column) and feeds on copepods (Ref. 1602, 58123).

species.name: Tewara cranwellae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rock pools and pools with sandy bottoms down to 5 m.

species.name: Tex-Mex gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Texan tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Texas logperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).

species.name: Texas pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In coastal lagoon habitats.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Texas shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy runs and pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers.  Usually occurs in clear water (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on aquatic insects and algae (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Texas silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Textile blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common on rocks and in rock pools to a depth of about 0.5 m, only found near the surface in deep rock-pools.  They appear to favor areas subjected to surf.  Feed mainly on algae (Ref. 5288).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Thai anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed coastal, pelagic and schooling, but evidently tolerates lowered salinities (e.g. in the Godavari estuary, India; Songkla Lake, Thailand and Barito River estuary, Indonesia) and possibly such places are its main habitat.  More data needed.

species.name: Thai damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and lagoon coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: Thai gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore and probably entering estuaries. Its biology is probably similar to A. chacunda.

species.name: Thai river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in reservoirs and presumably in rivers (Ref. 188).  Found in standing waters and large rivers.  Feed on planktonic crustaceans.  A nocturnal species which can be attracted to bright lights.  Found in schools during the spawning season (Ref. 85859).  Used to produce prahoc and tuk trey (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Thalassobathia nelsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Thalassobathia pelagica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species, living in close association with the large jellyfish, Stygiomedusa sp. (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Thalassoma cupido
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commercially cultured in Japan.

species.name: Thalassoma heiseri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thalassoma loxum
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thalassoma newtoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thalassoma robertsoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the outer reef slope, frequently in areas where surge is strong (Ref. 31087).

species.name: Thalassoma septemfasciata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Found in rocky and weedy reefs (Ref. 36661).

species.name: Thalassophryne amazonica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Both opercular and dorsal glands are venomous (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Thalassophryne megalops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thalassophryne montevidensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thalassophryne nattereri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Numerous in the estuarine areas of the Brazilian coast; stays motionless in the sandy or muddy bottoms; the venom is injected in the flesh of the victim when pressure is applied on the gland (Ref. 55461).

species.name: Thalassophryne punctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thamalakane barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Favors well-vegetated margins of rivers and lagoons, floodplain pools and backwaters.  Feeds on insects and periphyton.  Breeds in summer, laying eggs on submerged vegetation (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Thaman's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thamnaconus analis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Thamnaconus fijiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thamnaconus multilineatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thamnaconus tessellatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles(?) found near shore on sand bottoms (Ref. 11230). Adults in deep water (see occurrence records).

species.name: Thaumatichthys axeli
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thaumatichthys binghami
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thaumatichthys pagidostomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thazard atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are pelagic in oceanic waters.  Juveniles found beneath jellyfish (Ref. 9563), in epipelagic waters (Ref. 54802).  Rare species with no commercial value (Ref. 54802).

species.name: Thazard Atlantique (Scomberomorus maculatus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Migrates in large schools over great distances along the shore.  Larvae are found in surface waters between 19.6° and 29.8°C with salinities of 28.3 to 37.4 ppt.  Feeds mainly on small fishes (clupeoids and anchovies), few quantities of penaeoid shrimps and cephalopods.  Casting, live-bait fishing, jigging, and drift fishing are also employed in capturing this species.  Aerial spotting is sometimes used in locating the fish.  Marketed fresh, frozen or smoked; eaten pan-fried, broiled and baked.

species.name: Thazard atlantique (Scomberomorus regalis)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most abundant in clear waters around coral reefs, occasionally forming schools. Feeds on clupeoids (Harengula, Jenkinsia and Opisthonema) and atherinids (Allanetta [= Craterocephalus), squids and shrimps. Good food and game fish (Ref. 5521). Utilized fresh, smoked and frozen; consumed pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9987). Sometimes called the "Painted Mackerel" (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Thazard australien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found more commonly in offshore, open waters away from reefs and shoals (Ref. 30199). Form large schools which move close inshore along the coast of Queensland, commonly taken between December and April or May. Feed largely on fishes, particularly anchovies and sardines with smaller quantities of shrimps and squids. Common fork length ranges between 50 to 80 cm (Ref. 168). Sometimes confused with S. niphonius.

species.name: Thazard cirrus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Unlike S. commerson and S. guttatus, S. lineolatus is not encountered in very turbid waters or much reduced salinity. Feeds primarily on fishes. Also taken with midwater trawls, purse seines and by trolling (Ref. 9684). Taken from Oct.-Nov. along the Thai coast, Indian Ocean; in Malaysia Nov.-Feb. in the west coast, Mar.-Jul. in the south, Feb.-Mar. and Aug.-Nov. in the east; in India from May-Sept. with other seerfishes. Marketed mainly fresh; also dried-salted (Ref. 9684). Also consumed as spicy fishballs.

species.name: Thazard coréen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small schooling fishes, such as sardines and anchovies and on shrimps.  This species makes up an important part of the drift net fishery in Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar.  Marketed fresh and dried-salted (Ref. 9684).

species.name: Thazard de Monterey
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is now extinct outside the Gulf of California.  Supports a commercial net fishery close inshore, in estuaries and coastal marshes (Ref. 9987).  Its biology is almost completely unknown.  This fishery operates on a relict of the original population.

species.name: Thazard du Queensland
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Schooling species which moves into inshore waters, bays and estuaries of Queensland during the southern midwinter and early spring. Often inhabit very turbid coastal waters shallower than 30 m (Ref. 6390). Common length 50 to 80 cm FL (Ref. 12241). Seasonally migratory in the Gulf of Carpentaria and form mixed schools with S. commerson over shallow reefs offshore of Queensland. Trolling lines with lures such as metal spoons and cut bait are used by recreational and commercial fishermen. Mostly marketed fresh (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Thazard Kanadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species (Ref. 5313). Forms large schools in the Zanzibar Channel from March to September. Feeds mainly on anchovies (Anchoviella sp.), clupeids (Amblygaster sp., Sardinella fimbriata, Sardinella perforata [= Sardinella albella), other small fishes, squids, and mantis shrimps.

species.name: Thazard nébuleux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Travels 300 km up the Mekong River, above Phnom Penh but believed to reproduce only in marine waters.  Feeds on fishes and swims well upstream river because of easy food availability (Ref. 12693).  No information on biology available (Ref. 9684).  It is a prized food fish in Japan and probably in China as well.  Utilized fresh, dried or salted and smoked; consumed pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Thazard oriental
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore (including semi-enclosed sea areas) (Ref. 11230). Undergoes a spawning migration in spring (March to June) and a feeding migration in fall (September to November) in the Inland Sea of Japan. Feeds on small fishes. Another major fishing gear that is used are set nets. This species is the most important Scomberomorus species in Japan which is cultured and released for fishery. Marketed fresh and especially tasty in winter. Eaten pan-fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Thazard papou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Neritic species found in turbid waters.  Sexual maturity is attained at much less than 30 cm fork length.  The smallest species in the genus.

species.name: Thazard ponctué (Indo-Pacifique)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A pelagic migratory fish inhabiting coastal waters at depths between 15-200 m; sometimes entering turbid estuarine waters; usually found in small schools (Ref. 9684).  Feeds mainly on small schooling fishes (especially sardines and anchovies), squids and crustaceans (Ref. 9684).  Fishing peaks in the months of November and December in Eastern Thailand, late Dec and January in the northern part of the Gulf and January to March in its western part.  Caught with midwater trawls, purse seines, bamboo stake traps, and by trolling (Ref. 9684).  Marketed mainly fresh; also dried-salted (Ref. 9684), smoked and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Small quantities of frozen product are exported to Europe and North America (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Thazard sierra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A schooling species believed to spawn close to the coast over most of its range. Adults occur near the surface of coastal waters to over bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 11035). Adults feed on small fishes, particularly anchovies (Anchoa and Cetengraulis) and clupeids (Odontognathus and Opisthonema). The most abundant game fish along the Pacific coasts of Mexico and Central America. An excellent food fish enough to support a commercial fishery. Marketed fresh and frozen; also used for ceviche (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Thazard tigre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found more commonly around coastal headlands and rocky reefs but are also caught offshore (Ref. 6390).  Juveniles (4.5 to 10 cm length) are commonly encountered during November along the beaches of Townsville, Queensland and grow to twice this size by January.  They are pelagic predators, feeding exclusively on baitfish (sardines and herrings (Ref. 30572).  Caught also with set lines aside from trolling with small lures or cut bait.  Marketed fresh and frozen; eaten fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Thazard-kusara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits open water but often seen swimming near outer reef walls or deep clear-water slopes (Ref. 48637). Found mostly in shallow reef waters where it forms large schools. Feeds on crustaceans and fishes, particularly clupeoids (Sardinella, Thrissocles), and other fishes such as Sphyraena and Balistes. Marketed canned and frozen (Ref. 9684). Its flesh is mild and pleasantly flavored, but brushed with lemon juice prior to cooking to remove the ammonia-like smell (Ref. 9684).

species.name: Theodore's threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms.

species.name: Thepas' sabretooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit weedy areas such as Sargassum beds. They occur in shallow seagrass beds where they hide by pressing itself against a blade of seagrass. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Therese's sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic on sand, rubble or reef (Ref. 58302).  Often buried in sand in caves.  Feeds on small crustaceans (shrimps, crabs, isopods, ostracods, and amphipods, caprellids (Ref. 13070).

species.name: Theriodes sandakanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thermarces andersoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth from holotype record (Ref. 51665).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Thermarces pelophilum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured by the submersible Nautile on the cold seeps of the Barbados accretionary complex (Ref. 30548).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Thermichthys hollisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species known from a depth of 2,500 m and found in thermal vent effluent (Ref. 34024).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Thermobiotes
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thessaly goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The original habitat was described as a spring.  A short-lived species which is threatened due to pollution, habitat destruction and water abstraction (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Thessaly gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found on sand bottom (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Thetis fish
