species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563); usually take below 100 m (Ref. 33839).  Reported at depths of 20-260 (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Thick lipped chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thick-lipped catfish
species.description: Inhabits rivers and feeds on insects and higher plants (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Thickbeard grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds primarily on benthic organisms, especially gammarian amphipods and, to a lesser extent, lamellibranchs, copepods, polychaetes, ostracods, isopods mysids, Natantia, and echinoderms (Ref. 1371).  Minimum depth record from Ref. 1371.

species.name: Thickbody skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on continental slope and upper abyssal plain. Feeds on small benthic invertebrates, adults possibly piscivorous (Ref. 114953). Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Males reaches maturity by ca. 76 cm TL; young hatch at ca. 22 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Produces horny-shelled eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thickhead lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic to mesopelagic, at surface at night (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Thicklip barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large upland rivers. Feeds on benthic organisms and insect larvae (Ref. 58784). Undergoes upstream movement for spawning (Ref. 58784). Little is known about this species due to past confusion with P. jullieni. Apparently migrates together with P. jullieni and has been decimated by the intensive gillnet fishery directed at that species just above the Lee Pee Waterfalls in southern Laos (Ref. 10431). However, further investigation is needed to find out whether it shares the same spawning grounds and times (Ref. 10431).

species.name: Thicklip chub
species.description: Inhabits rocky riffles and runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Thicklip pupfish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Thicklipped happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers rocky habitats (Ref. 7248, 52307). Possibly an ovophilic, agamous maternal mouthbroodar, like other members of the genus (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Thickset tadpole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported at 2150 m (Ref. 51661).  Immature female measures 11.75 cm SL (Ref. 41470).

species.name: Thickskin snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Thickspine roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thicktail chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly found in marshes and backwaters along rivers and lake margins.  Reported to reach a maximum size of 3.2 cm TL (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Thielle's anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat information unavailable.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Breeding in captivity is possible (Ref. 130462).

species.name: Thin snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Size pertains to immature specimen.  Occurs over sand bottoms (Ref. 31243).

species.name: Thin-barred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known specimen was found inside a glass bottle collected along a sandy slope ca. 114 -137 m depth (Ref. 113825).

species.name: Thinbarbel whiptail
species.description: A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Thinbarred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tide pools.

species.name: Thinface cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in well-vegetated swamps and along the edges of rivers (Ref. 6465). Also occurs in fast-flowing reaches over sand and rocks (Ref. 6465, 52307). Feeds primarily on small fish (Ref. 6465, 52307), also on shrimps and insects (Ref. 6465). A female (Ref. 52307) mouthbrooder which breeds in spring (Ref. 6465). Aalso caught with drawnets (Ref. 6465).

species.name: Thinlip barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in upland reaches of large and medium sized rivers (Ref. 12693). Feeds on benthic organisms and insect larvae (Ref. 58784). Undergoes upstream movement for spawning (Ref. 58784). Little is known about this species due to past confusion with P. jullieni (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Thinstribed toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thintail skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype taken from a depth of 500 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thiolliere's lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic and mesopelagic.

species.name: Thiony's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the seafloor near the Peroa natural gas platform, with rhodoliths and other calcareous substrate (Ref. 113825). Also found in a moderately steep slope with short rock ledges, small caves and crevices. Collected on a fine sand and Halimeda rubble substrate in close proximity to an Ircinia sp. sponge and several ca. 1 m diameter boulders covered with encrusting algae and sponges (Ref. 129296). Mininum depth and maximum size for male from Ref. 113825. Maximum depth and maximum size for female from Ref. 129296.

species.name: Thiony’s jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found solitarily, always in small constructed burrows on sandy rubble bottoms. It feeds on small benthic organisms that live near the bottom (e.g., small shrimps) (Ref. 128653).

species.name: Thomas' triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral reefs and intertidal pools (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Thomasen's snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thompson's butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs (Ref. 43239). Occur in schools above steep outer reef slopes at depths below 10 m to 300 m and sometimes above clear lagoon reefs at depths as shallow as 4 m.  Uncommon (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thompson's snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thon bleu du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epipelagic, usually oceanic, but seasonally coming close to shore (Ref. 168).  Tolerates  ample temperature intervals (Ref. 168).  Forms schools by size, sometimes with other scombrids (Ref. 168).  Migrates between June and September in a northward direction along the coast of Baja California, Mexico and California (Ref. 168).  A voracious predator that feeds on a wide variety of small schooling fishes and squids, also on crabs crabs and to a lesser degree on sessile organisms (Ref. 168).  Marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Thon mignon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Predominantly neritic species avoiding very turbid waters and areas with reduced salinity such as estuaries.  May form schools of varying size.  Feeds on a variety of fishes, cephalopods, and crustaceans, particularly stomatopod larvae and prawns (Ref. 9684).  Marketed mainly fresh and dried salted (Ref. 9684), but also smoked, canned and frozen (Ref. 9987).

species.name: Thon papillon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep oceanic waters (Ref. 9563), most abundant in waters of 8° to 10°C. Stomach contents of the specimen from north of the Hawaiian Archipelago include onychoteuthids, ommastrephid squid, vertebrae and fin rays from an unidentified fish, bird feathers and parasitic nematodes (Ref. 11006). Taken as longline by-catch by Japanese fishing for Thunnus maccoyii.

species.name: Thon rouge
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. Oceanic but seasonally coming close to shore. They school by size, sometimes together with albacore, yellowfin, bigeye, skipjack etc. Visual predators (Ref. 88866) preying on small schooling fishes (anchovies, sauries, hakes) or on squids and red crabs. Live up to 40 years in the western Atlantic (Ref. 88822).  Weight up to 900 kg (Ref. 88823). Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 6769). Juvenile growth is rapid (about 30 cm / year) but slower than in other tuna 
and billfish species (Ref. 88867). Adult growth is considerably slower, with about 10 years needed to reach two thirds of maximum length.  Become rare because of massive overfishing (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Thon rouge du sud
species.description: Espèce de poissons. By maturity, most southern bluefin tuna lead an oceanic, pelagic existence (Ref. 6390).  Spawning fish and larvae are encountered in waters with surface temperatures between 20° and 30°C.  An opportunistic feeder, preying on a wide variety of fishes, crustaceans, cephalopods, salps, and other marine animals.  Mostly canned (Ref. 9684).  A specialized fishery for sashimi-quality has been developed recently by New Zealand fishers.  In Japan, it is highly prized for the sashimi markets.

species.name: Thon élégant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An occasionally schooling species which feeds mainly on krill (euphausiids), and also on squids and small fishes.  Juveniles are found between 20 and 35°S at surface temperatures ranging from 19 to 24°C.  Its flesh is paler than that of most true tunas and is very oily, but the cooked meat has fine eating qualities.  Mainly marketed fresh.

species.name: Thonine noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs rarely where surface temperatures fall below 23°C. Its larvae are more frequently encountered at temperatures above 26°C and are practically confined to waters within about 240 miles off the mainland. Inhabits near the surface of coastal waters and offshore waters (Ref. 11035). Form multi-species schools with Thunnus albacares and Katsuwonus pelamis. An opportunistic predator which shares feeding pattern with other tunas and probably compete for food with other species such as yellowfin tuna, common dolphin, oriental bonito, among others.

species.name: Thoracochromis bakongo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis brauschi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly feeds on plants (e.g. Vallisneria aethiopica) but also on algae and detritus; ovophilic, agamous, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Thoracochromis callichromus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds primarily on plants like Vallisneria, but also on snails and insect larvae (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Thoracochromis demeusii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis fasciatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis lucullae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis moeruensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis schwetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species practices buccal incubation (Ref. 11970).

species.name: Thoracochromis stigmatogenys
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thoracochromis wingatii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in both still and flowing waters (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Thorichthys maculipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower and middle river valleys over sandy and rocky substrate.

species.name: Thorichthys panchovillai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thornback cowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic over rubble and sand at 5-132 m (Ref. 58302). Solitary (Ref. 90102). Males are highly territorial (Ref. 9710).  Poisonous in some parts of the tropics (Ref. 7364).

species.name: Thornback sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found on rocky bottom.  Occurs from near shore to 183 m.  Rare.

species.name: Thornback skate
species.description: Occur on soft bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Feed on benthic fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 6871).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 4.4-6.3 cm long and 3.2-3.8 wide (Ref. 41308). Males reaches maturity at ca. 39 cm TL, females at ca. 42 cm TL; young hatch at ca. 10 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Thornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly found in rockpools living within deep crevices and holes or under overhangs. They are rarely seen because of their nocturnal habits and camouflaged colour pattern. In some areas, small groups of thronfishes may be seen resting vertically or even upside down on rock faces. Diet consists exclusively of crabs and prawns. Juveniles are pelagic and distinguished by a silvery color pattern with vertical metallic and reddish brown bands (Ref. 9003).

species.name: Thorntail pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among algae (Ref. 5316).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thorntailed pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs from tide pools to a depth of at least 8 m (Ref. 1602).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thorntooth grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Thorny freshwater stingray
species.description: Benthic species mostly in lakes and rives, found more than 240 km upstream from the sea (possibly also coastal).  The life history and present status of populations in West Africa is unknown.  Type specimens were born after capture of the mother; few specimens exist (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Thorny sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thorny tail skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Thorny tinselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep midwater or near bottom (Ref. 6749); benthopelagic (Ref. 52595).  Caught by bottom trawl, bottom lines and drift gill net (Ref. 87951).

species.name: Thorogobius angolensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Thorogobius rofeni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur offshore, on the upper slope.  Holotype was trawled on mud (Ref. 5299).

species.name: Thorophos euryops
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thorophos nexilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thouin ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore (Ref. 9909) and offshore (Ref. 58784). A carnivorous fish that feeds on large shellfishes (Ref. 58784).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Biology little known (Ref. 9909).  Caught occasionally by demersal tangle net fisheries operating throughout the area. Utilized for its meat, find (both very high value), skin and cartilage (Ref.58048). Marketed fresh and probably dried-salted (Ref. 9909).

species.name: Thracian shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Landlocked, found in a shallow lake, of purely fresh water at its inland extremity and a brackish lagoon at the lower extremity; inhabits mostly the freshwater part.  No data on its biology.  This species is threatened by sewage, industrial effluents, alteration or destruction of spawning sites by agricultural development and increased salinity following the opening of a canal into the sea (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Thread brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Thread eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Thread pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on debris on mud and silt bottom having low, if any relief; individuals reluctant to leave the rock were these were first observed (Ref. 075145).

species.name: Thread shrimpgoby
species.description: Collected by rotenone and spear from silty, sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 75863). Also found in lagoons (Ref 90102).

species.name: Thread-tail basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threaded sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threadfin acara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length 20 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Threadfin anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in groups off outer reef slopes (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Threadfin bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rough bottom, deep reefs.  Feeds on small planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Threadfin cardinalfish
species.description: Dense aggregations (often mixed with other species, like Archamia fucata, A. zosterophora are found above mounds of branching coral Porites cylindrica in sheltered, often turbid bays and lagoons (Ref. 1602, 48635). Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Threadfin catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and estuaries, river deltas and rivers within tidal influence.  Feeds mainly on prawns and other crustaceans, fish, aquatic insects, plant material, and fish scales taken opportunistically (Ref. 38478).

species.name: Threadfin cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in the shallow, rocky habitat; extremely shy; usually found in groups; feeds on algae and has long digestive tract (Ref. 46829). Feeds by scraping rock biocover (Ref. 6770, 46829). Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 46829, 86760).

species.name: Threadfin dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- to abyssopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Threadfin dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threadfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in coastal streams with moderate to fast flow (Ref. 2847).  Usually found in small.  clear creeks, often in rainforest within about 50 km of the sea (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Threadfin leatherjacket
species.description: Lives on trawling grounds.  An excellent food fish.

species.name: Threadfin longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found usually on reefs in less than 8 m (Ref. 27772).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Threadfin mangrovegoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove creeks and estuaries, sometimes well into freshwater influence (Ref. 43716).

species.name: Threadfin mudgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal bays and estuaries on muddy substrates, usually in depths over 15 meters on coastal slopes, but shallower in estuaries (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Threadfin pearl-perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit trawling grounds.  Found more frequently in moderate depths on the continental shelf particularly close to submerged reefs or rough bottom (Ref. 27621).  Feed mainly on crustaceans (Ref. 27621).  Some cuttlefish are also taken (Ref. 27621).

species.name: Threadfin porgy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over a wide range of bottom types from the surface to 100 m, but is more common close to reefs or on rough bottoms.  Small individuals are very common at some localities in shallow, sheltered bays; larger fish often occur in deeper water.  Important food fish.

species.name: Threadfin rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lowland swamps, drainage ditches and streams that have abundant vegetation (Ref. 2847).  Occurs in slow-flowing streams, swampy ponds and billabongs with abundant aquatic vegetation.  Temperature and pH ranges are 23°-28°C and 5.2-6.6, respectively (Ref. 44894).  Most commonly found along the heavily vegetated margins of lily lagoons and small streams.  Feeds mostly on diatoms and micro-crustaceans.  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).  Well established in the aquarium hobby, but its longetivity is relatively brief, averaging only 2-3 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Threadfin sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly on mud bottoms (Ref. 42740).

species.name: Threadfin saury
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottoms of the continental shelf and inshore waters (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Threadfin scat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on algae and sewage (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Threadfin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on crustaceans, including shrimps and isopods (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Threadfin slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 7300).  Oviparous, with mesopelagic eggs and larvae, or probably in deeper waters (Ref. 35724).

species.name: Threadfin smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic to benthopelagic (Ref. 51024).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Threadfin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over loose rubble in seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Forms aggregations to feed on zooplankton.

species.name: Threadless blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in estuaries and freshwater habitats, frequently where mangrove are abundant.  Presence of toxic buccal glands associated with the grooved canines.  This is avoided by predators which even reject it unharmed if they try to ingest it.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Both fang and venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Threadless cheek-hook goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy-mud or silt bottoms at depths of 5-30 m (Ref. 84001).

species.name: Threadnose bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threadsail filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commercially cultured in Japan.  Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115).

species.name: Threadtail anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught in fairly deep water. Found in sandy-muddy bottoms of coastal deep waters (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Threadtail conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Further study is needed to clarify the differences between this species and U. lepturus (Richardson) from the Indo-West Pacific.

species.name: Three point toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Three spot cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits slow moving waters of the lower river valleys and prefers mud and sand bottoms where it lives in the roots and weeds.  Feeds on small fishes, macro-invertebrates and aquatic and terrestrial insects.

species.name: Three spotted tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in both river and swamp habitats and is adapted to fairly fast-flowing rivers (Ref. 6465). Hardy, tolerating fresh and brackish water (up to 20ppt, Ref. 3), preferring slow-flowing or standing water; adults occupy deep open waters, juveniles remain inshore among vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193). Prefers fairly deep, quiet water with some weed cover; hippo pools are a favoured retreat (Ref. 12524, 13337). Forms schools (Ref. 2, 12524, 13337). Mainly diurnal; a detritivore which feeds on fine particulate matter (Ref. 2), including algae (Ref. 246, 12524, 13337, 53992), diatoms, detritus (Ref. 7248, 52193, 53992) and zooplankton (Ref. 7248, 52193). Larger individuals also take insects and other invertebrates (Ref. 53992). Feeding regime is variable, the diet changes according to food availability (Ref. 6465). Female mouthbrooder (Ref. 87, 246, 6465, 12524, 13337). Fine angling and table species (Ref. 6465, 12524, 13337).

species.name: Three-barred mouth almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Three-barred porcupinefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuarine, coastal and offshore reefs to a depth of 50 m.  Nocturnal and solitary.  Feeds on hard-shelled invertebrates.  Not usually marketed.

species.name: Three-by-two garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species mostly found in more turbid inshore waters replacing Hemiramphus far, which is more common in more oceanic waters (Ref. 9843). Inhabits estuaries (Ref. 75154). A high quality food fish well-known in markets of Brisbane, Queensland (Ref. 9843).

species.name: Three-eye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in bays, lagoons and shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Three-eyed pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef walls, often present in groups of up to 20 individuals which are loosely aggregated and perched vertically on the substrate at the back of small overhangs and crevices.  Non-type specimens collected were also nearly always found on steep outer reef walls (Ref. 102609).

species.name: Three-keel pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens have been collected from coral knolls.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Three-line Sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Three-lined blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found solitary or in small groups perched on corals, sponges, and tunicates (Ref. 90102) in coastal reef crests (Ref. 8631, 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Three-lined catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pool and riffle areas of streams (Ref. 12045).  Found in rapid-running mountain streams (Ref. 12975).  Occurs in the basin-wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).

species.name: Three-lined rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often found on exposed reefs with shallow clear water.  Usually swim in loose groups along upper parts of drop-offs or above reef crests (Ref. 48636).  May also be found solitary or in pairs (Ref. 90102).   Minimum depth reported from Ref. 90102.

species.name: Three-lined tongue sole
species.description: Found in the sublittoral zone incl.  semi-enclosed sea areas; inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms of the continental shelf and feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 2107, 11230).

species.name: Three-lips
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Three-lobed suckermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Three-ray dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Three-ribbon wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds and areas of mixed sand, rubble, and algae of inner reef flats and shallow lagoons.  Female length is from Ref. 9137.  Swims in small aggregations over large areas.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 48636.

species.name: Three-spined frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reefs, mangrove estuaries, and offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 3132).  Found over muddy bottoms in shallow estuaries and along coasts.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Three-spined hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Three-spot cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits inshore coral reefs (Ref. 40889).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary, also found in reef crevices and ledges in 1-35 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Three-spot frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in inshore waters near reefs (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Egg clusters are attached to the side of the body of the male parent, either as brooding strategy or as aid in luring other fish for food (Ref. 6773). Solitary, usually under wharf pilings or among debris (Ref 90102).

species.name: Three-striped butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coral rich areas of lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Occur in small groups.  Oviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 52884).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Relatively unknown to American and European aquarists because this species has only been rarely imported.

species.name: Three-striped whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Clear coastal to outer reef crests (Ref. 48635).  Common in shallow sandy rubble and coral reef areas.  Usually in aggregations.  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans and polychaetes during the day (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Three-tentaxles dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was collected from a depth shallower than 100 m, by a mid-water trawl that was targeting the Sakura-shrimp (Lucensosergia lucens) (Ref. 121636).

species.name: Threeband cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a large cave at base of a steep slope, next to shore, in 22 m depth (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Threeband damselfish
species.description: Adults inhabit lagoon and inshore reefs around coral or rock outcrops situated in sandy areas (Ref. 7247).  Solitary (Ref. 37816).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Threeband tonguesole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mature female specimens with elongate ovaries at sizes 9.26 and 9.35 cm SL were examined.  Nothing is known of its life history (Ref. 26267).

species.name: Threeblotched rabbitfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Strictly corallophilic, pairs living in area rich in hard coral, particularly Acropora.

species.name: Threefin velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky reefs and soft-bottom trawling grounds. Also found in sand and rubble bottoms, usually near reefs in 3-4 m (Ref 90102). Minimum depth from Ref. 090102.

species.name: Threelight hatchetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threeline basslet
species.description: Found beneath rocky and coral ledges (Ref. 5521).  Also found in deep reefs and outer wall at depths from 22-69 m (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Threeline damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs and rocky inshore areas (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Threeline prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky and sandy areas among kelp, in crevices, or kelp holdfasts (Ref. 48788).; subtidal (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Threeline tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threeline tonguesole
species.description: Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Threespine bass
species.description: Encountered near the surface at night.

species.name: Threespine cardinalfish
species.description: A temperate species occurring in a wide range of habitats and depths from estuaries (< 40 m) to the continental slope (ca. 100-600 m), but most common in outer shelf and upper slope waters (Ref. 9563, 33616). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Threespine grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threespine seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Threespot barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in a wide variety of habitats, especially where there is vegetation (Ref. 52193), in shallow water near river outlets or close to swampy areas (Ref. 5595). It feeds on insects and other small organisms (Ref. 52193). Used as bait for the tigerfish (Ref. 7248). Breeds in summer, shoals of ripe adults moving upstream in spate after rain; females produce as many as 8,000 eggs (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Threespot chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults form large aggregations high above the bottom in rocky areas around caves and ledges (Ref. 7247).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Collected from 183 m.  Spawn from December to June (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Threespot damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species, solitary, in holes of small rocks on sandy bottom with coral rubbles.  Adults inhabit shallow bays, silty coastal reefs and harbors with sparse coral and algal growth.  Feed mainly on benthic algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Threespot damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs.  They are found within caves at night (Ref. 9626). Often found in tangles of staghorn coral; anywhere there is abundant algae on reefs (Ref. 26938).  Feed mainly on algae but also on harpacticoid copepods, small gastropods, eggs of mollusks, sponges, polychaetes and hydroids (Ref. 9626).  Juveniles subsist on the external parasites of fishes (Ref. 5521).  Adults pugnaciously guard large territories, will chase and nip intruders of all sizes, including divers (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).  Taken incidentally in traps and small-meshed beach nets (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Threespot eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max.  length 30 cm TL (Ref. 2060).

species.name: Threespot flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow mud, sand, and rubble bottoms of the continental shelf (Ref. 9824).  Feeds on benthic animals.  Marketed fresh and used in making fish meal (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Threespot grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky pools of lowland streams (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Aquarium conditions:  pH=7.2, H=10, 26°C water temperature, egg layer, carnivore (Ref. 6398).

species.name: Threespot headstander
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in schools of 10-50 specimens in deeper water. They feed on plants (Ref. 13371).  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Threespot jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threespot leporinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in ponds (Ref. 11229).  Very active during the rainy season, they gain the flooded zones where they are captured with nets.  In dry season, they are confined to the deepest parts of the river where they are captured with fishing rods.  Feed primarily on fruits, seeds and termites.  The food is crushed by four strong teeth on each half-jaw.  (Ref. 27188).  Males are sexually mature at 1 yr, while females are mature at 2 years.  Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).  Reproduction takes place from November to June, with a peak from December to March but mature individuals can be found year round.  Females spawn around 100,000 to 200,000 eggs (Ref. 12225).  The females grow slightly faster than the males; however this difference is clearly perceptible only after 4 years of age.  Its excellent flesh makes it ideal for consumption in spite of its numerous bones (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Threespot torpedo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderately deep water over sandy and rocky substrates and feeds on fishes (Ref. 267).

species.name: Threespotted waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Threestick stingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Threestripe corydoras
species.description: Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Threestripe gourami
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in marshes, swamps and rice fields (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Threestripe pencilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).

species.name: Thripenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults live in subtidal areas and are rarely found in intertidal areas.  They feed on organisms which inhabit encrusting rock growths, with amphipods and hermit crabs being the dominant food items (Ref. 26966).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Thrissobrycon pectinifer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Throatspotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in rocky, boulder strewn areas and walls.  Prefers tide pools and shallow water habitats (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Thryssocypris ornithostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insects (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Thryssocypris smaragdinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thryssocypris tonlesapensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near the water surface.  Highest numbers mainly in the tidal zone of large deltaic branches of the lower Mekong.  Feeds on insect larvae.  Sometimes seen in the markets, but usually used for making prahoc and tuk trey (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Thryssocypris wongrati
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected mostly by large seines with small mesh measuring 2 mm from open water in the Chao Phraya River mainstem. Also found in current in irrigation canals. Observed to form school at the surface of the water, swimming very fast with other species such as Clupeoides borneensis, Rasbora spp., Barilius koratensis, Paralaubuca spp. and Discherodontus halei (Ref. 93051).

species.name: Thumb grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thurla whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Thymallus brevipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thymallus burejensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thymallus mertensii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thymallus yaluensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits very cold and clean rivers.  It has the most beautiful form and fins of a freshwater fish.  (Ref. 12218).

species.name: Thynnichthys polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on insect and fish remains (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Thynnichthys thynnoides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in large rivers, canal, oxbows and floodplains.  Microphagous, feeds mainly on phytoplankton and periphyton with lesser amounts of bottom algae and small zooplankton.  Migrates for spawning to the floodplains when water level is high.  Young of the year are caught as they begin to return to the rivers in October.  In the Tonle Sap, adults make nearly all of the October catch, with larger and larger proportions of young in subsequent months.  Use to make prahoc and nuoc mam (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Thynnichthys vaillanti
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref. 6128).

species.name: Thyriscus anoplus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported at 800m (Ref. 50610).

species.name: Thysanichthys crossotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thysanichthys evides
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 58302) found in coral and rocky reefs in 1-40 m (Ref 90102); and caves (Ref. 10482).

species.name: Thysanophrys armata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species rarely cited in the recent literature, only as material examined (Ref. 29003, Ref. 31147, Ref. 31163), in lists (Ref. 9790) or in keys (Ref. 92921).  Cited in some field guides (Debelius).  Please send references or more studies are needed.

species.name: Thysanophrys longirostris
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Thysanopsetta naresi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on one specimen (Ref. 27363).

species.name: Thysochromis annectens
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, cave-breeding (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Thysochromis ansorgii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, substrate brooder which spawns preferentially in caves or cave-like structures (Ref. 52307, 81260). Maximum TL was recorded at 12.0-13.0 cm (Ref. 5706).

species.name: Thysochromis emili
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in well oxygenated lakes and rivers situated in higher order systems of the Kouilou and Noumbi River basins (Ref. 122428). It occurs over sandy substrate in shallow, less than 0.5 m deep, clear, shoreline waters fringed by abundant overhanging vegetation, deeply undercut banks and root wads (Ref. 122428). It is probably a pair-bonding, cave brooder (Ref. 122428).

species.name: Tibetan stone loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers, streams and standing waters (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Tiburon Peninsula gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits springs and clear streams.

species.name: Tiburon Peninsula limia
species.description: Prefers small shallow flowing waters and adjacent marshy areas rich in vegetation (Ref. 27158).

species.name: Tidepool blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow, weed-covered rocky reefs, including tide pools.   Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tidepool gunnel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools or the intertidal zone to 20 m depth, on sandy-mud bottoms and among rocks of rocky reefs (Ref. 43239); also in eelgrass (Zostera marina) beds (Ref. 559). Sometimes to 200 m depth (Ref. 43239). Feeds on gammarids. Juveniles associate with drifting seaweed (Ref. 12114, 12115). Although rarely used for commercial food, this species is highly valued as fried fish in the spring months in Tokyo and neighboring areas (Ref. 7031).

species.name: Tidepool pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools and reef habitats from 1.5 to 5.5 m.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tidepool sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612), found in sheltered areas and  common in tide pools (Ref. 2850).  In areas with rough surf, it occurs in higher, more sheltered places (Ref. 2850).  Can leave tide pools when aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Shows a tendency to return to its home pool if displaced (Ref. 6885).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Tidepool snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore, in tide pools on exposed coasts (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Tidepool snake moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Abundant on rubble areas of intertidal reef flats.  Feeds on small crustaceans and probably on small fishes as well. Also found in shallow reefs including tide pools (Ref 90102).

species.name: Tidewater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal lagoons and brackish bays at mouth of freshwater streams (Ref. 2850).  IS subjected to wide variation in salinity (1-28 ppt.) and temperature (9-25°C) both within and among habitat types.  The substrate and vegetation can also differ among lagoon, creek and marsh habitats (Ref. 26474).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans, dipteran larvae, gastropods, and invertebrate eggs (Ref. 26474).  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  Males construct nesting burrows (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Tidewater mojarra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Primarily in estuarine waters, in seagrass beds, open sand and mud bottoms, and in mangrove forests (Ref. 51706).  Penetrates freshwater tributaries (Ref. 51706).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 51706).

species.name: Tidewater silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tidal creeks and marshes, in brackish or full sea waters.  Never found in inland waters.

species.name: Tiene’s dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deepwater-reef environment consisting of large foliose and plating corals on a gentle slope and exposed to moderate currents, but otherwise protected from wave energy (Ref. 119773).

species.name: Tiete tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tiger botia
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Usually found in large rivers with a muddy substrate (Ref. 27732) and also with bottom cover of rocks, logs, or even brush piles.  Nocturnal or crepuscular fish.  Feeds on mollusks, benthic insect larvae and worms.  Moves into flooded areas during the rainy season and returns to rivers during November and December.  Sometimes marketed fresh.  Made into prahoc along the Tonlé Sap, Cambodia (Ref. 12693)

species.name: Tiger combtooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Tiger dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep coral covered slope exposed to strong currents and frequent cold-water upwellings. Young individuals were associated with larger coral rubble pieces where they would hide and adults were with deep labyrinthine burrow under larger coral outcrops. Adults usually seen in pairs sharing the same burrow (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Tiger dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tiger fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers warm, well-oxygenated water, mainly larger rivers and lakes; all but the largest form roving schools of like-sized fish; aptly described as fierce and voracious; diet increasingly piscivorous, becoming exclusive fish feeders when above 90-100 mm length; feeds on whatever prey is most abundant but Brycinus, Micralestes, Barbus, and Limnothrissa are favored (Ref. 7248, 52193). Piscivorous, but may also eat Caridina and insects (Ref. 28714). Useful food fish in some areas (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Tiger flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore waters over the continental shelf.  Sometimes entering coastal bays (Ref. 9563).  Tiger flathead are not active fish and will normally rest on the sea bed during the day in areas of mud and sand substrate (Ref. 6390).  They may migrate into the water column at night following prey species (Ref. 27197).  Adults feed mainly on small fish such as silversides and three-spined cardinal fish (Ref.  27193) while juveniles feed primarily on crustaceans including krill.  The young inhabit shallow waters of the continental shelf and move into the outer shelf zone as they reach maturity (Ref. 6390). Its fin spines are venomous and can inflict mild to severe pain (Ref. 125684).

species.name: Tiger goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock faces and tide pools (often under red algae), pilings and surfaces of large sponges.

species.name: Tiger grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit swampy lagoons and backwaters as well as the main channel of turbid rivers (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tiger Limia
species.description: Known only from its type locality, the Lake Miragoane in south-western Haiti. It was collected in a small, clear water path exiting the north end of the lake and in the lake itself. However it little else is known about the ecology, but it seems that it prefers habitats with some submerged vegetation and muddy bottoms. It was sympatric with Gambusia beebei, Nandopsis haitiensis, Limia nigrofasciata, L. garnieri, L. miragoanensis, L. immaculata and some introduced species, such as Oreochromis aureus and Tilapia rendali (Ref. 128733).

species.name: Tiger loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits lakes, rivers and streams, usually close to submerged trees or logs or under floating logs and houses (Ref. 56749).  Found as well in upland streams over stony substrate (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Breeds in small streams in swamp forest (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Tiger pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over mud, sand, rubble and rocky bottoms.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 17.5 cm SL.

species.name: Tiger sandgoby
species.description: Found from three sites within the sheltered waters/embayment of north-east Kangaroo Island (northern Shoal Bay, Western Cove and upper American River). It apparently occupy a narrow strip of habitat at the lower intertidal and start of the sub-tidal over sand and mud with broken shell and sometimes in association with sparse marine eel grass Zostera and the algae Hormosira, but appears not to occupy fringing ribbon weed Posidonia in clean sands of deeper water. Radiographs showed small shells (micro-molluscs) in the stomach content of most fish screened, suggesting a benthic predatory/omnivorous diet (Ref. 118118).

species.name: Tiger sorubim
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in estuarine zones, mainly upstream of the first rapids up to the basin's headwaters.  Nocturnal species which lives in the main bed of slow or fast zones, as well as in the flooded forests, particularly the juveniles., Opportunistic, piscivorous fish which may feed on crabs and shrimps.  At the end of the dry season, they can migrate at the same time as their prey, then return at the end of the rainy season (Ref. 35381).  Most important catfish in gill-net fisheries of Guaporé and Mamoré rivers.

species.name: Tiger tail seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to Height (= from top of coronet to the tip of straightened tail). This species is mainly found in pairs (Ref. 48635) on coral reefs, sponge gardens, kelp, and floating Sargassum. Nocturnal, site faithful. Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 85309). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Life span probably more than 2-3 years. Used for traditional Chinese medicine (Ref. 85309).

species.name: Tiger-fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Hydrocynus species are piscivorous, but may also eat Caridina and insects (Ref. 28714). Affinities: easily distinguished from two other species in West Africa from the number of scale-rows below lateral line, which is 3 instead of 2 (Ref. 81279).

species.name: Tigerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reedy bays and lagoons, at open sandy beaches, throughout the shelf and reef zones (Ref. 55949), and in the open water (Ref. 5595, 55949). Piscivorous (Ref. 5595, 55949). Small specimens mostly feed on crustacean zooplankton, adults predominantly eat larvae and juveniles of small shoaling zooplanktivorous cyprinid Engraulicypris sardella; female mouthbrooder (Ref. 55949).

species.name: Tigerstriped catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigertail skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Tigris asp
species.description: Record length is about 102 cm TL; 150 cm TL and 60 kg are questionable - anecdotal or unverifiable reports (Ref. 93003: http://www.fishing-worldrecords.com/scientificname/Aspius%20vorax/show).

species.name: Tigris bleak
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris cat
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tigris mystus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tigris spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous, possibly with distinct pairing during breeding similar to congeners (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tigris trout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species inhabits clear and very swift flowing water, with stone and pebble bottom (Ref. 87713).

species.name: Tiki soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults thrive in standing waters (Ref. 7248, 12501). Inhabits reservoirs, rivers, creeks, drains, swamps and tidal creeks; commonly over mud bottoms, often in well-vegetated areas (Ref. 44894). Also found in warm weedy pools of sluggish streams, canals, and ponds (Ref. 5723). Most common in blind estuaries and coastal lakes (Ref. 32693), but usually absent from permanently open estuaries and open sea (Ref. 6465) and from fast-flowing waters (Ref. 7248, 12501). Normally not found at high altitudes (Ref. 6465). Able to survive extreme reduction of temporary water bodies (Ref. 2, 27445). Highly euryhaline (Ref. 2, 3, 23, 58, 61, 6465, 12501, 12522, 12524, 13337, 27445, 55352). Grows and reproduces in fresh-, brackish and seawater (Ref. 2, 21, 23, 61, 5214, 27445, 36683, 54362). Can be reared under hyper-saline conditions (Ref. 4537, 44894, 52307). Tolerates low dissolved oxygen levels (Ref. 3, 23, 6465) and can utilise atmospheric oxygen when water oxygen levels drop (Ref. 61, 6465). Mainly diurnal. May form schools (Ref. 3, 4537, 44894). Omnivorous (Ref. 21, 12524), feeds mainly on algae and phytoplankton (Ref. 4537, 7248, 12501, 12522, 12524, 13337, 36683, 44894, 52307) but also takes some zooplankton, small insects and their larvae (Ref. 4537, 7248, 12524, 13337, 44894, 52307), shrimps (Ref. 12524, 13337), earthworms (Ref. 12501) and aquatic macrophytes (Ref. 6465). Juveniles carnivorous/omnivorous, adults tend to be herbivorous or detritus feeders (Ref. 2, 6465, 13517). Large individuals have been reported to prey on small fishes (Ref. 2, 6465, 12501, 12522), and occasionally cannibalise their own young (Ref. 2, 6465). Exhibits considerable plasticity in feeding habits (Ref. 6465, 13544) as well as in reproductive biology (Ref. 13544). Polygamous (Ref. 12524, 13337), maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 1, 5214, 12524, 13337). Reaches sexual maturity at 15 centimeter length (Ref. 44894), but stunted fish may breed at 6-7 centimeters and at an age of just over 2 months (Ref. 52307). Fecundity high (Ref. 55352). Extended temperature range 8-42 °C, natural temperature range 17-35°C (Ref. 3), with salinity-dependent difference in temperature tolerance (Ref. 2, 23). Somewhat aggressive toward other species (Ref. 36683). Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987). Excellent palatability (Ref. 6465), with small head and large dress-out weight (Ref. 61), and filets without small bones (Ref. 57960). Used extensively in biological, physiological and behavioural research (Ref. 7248). Translocated and introduced for aquaculture, sport fishing, stocking man-made lakes and biological control of nuisance plants and animals (Ref. 6465). Eurytopic; a most successful and vagile invader (Ref. 6465).

species.name: Tilapia baloni
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding their brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tilapia brevimanus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood; seems to breed throughout the year; development time of larvae, from deposition of eggs to free swimming stage, takes about 13 to 14 days (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tilapia busumana
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adapted to living in fast-flowing rivers with rapids (Ref. 2). Pair-bonding, open substratum spawner, with both parents guarding the brood (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tilapia pra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy/muddy substrate of mediem-sized rivers (Ref. 84667).

species.name: Tile blanquille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms and feeds on crustaceans, polychaetes and small fish.

species.name: Tile chameau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Most common around 200 m, usually over mud or sand bottom and occasionally over rough bottom (Ref. 9988); prefers temperature of 8-17°C (Ref. 5951).  Feeds mainly on shrimp and crabs, but also takes fish, squid, bivalves and holothurians.  Sensitive to cold water (Ref. 9988), a mass die-off occurred in 1882, after which the species was rare for decades, presumably due to unusually cold water (Ref. 7251).  Marketed fresh or frozen; can be steamed, pan-fried, broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Tile clown
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms.  Marketed mostly fresh.

species.name: Tile de Hubbs
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the bottom, in the area occupied by C. affinis and C. princeps, but prefers shallower waters.

species.name: Tile fin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky bottoms (Ref. 9119).  Also found on soft sand and mud bottoms.  Solitary species.  Digs into the substrate for food (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Tile fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from a depth of 142 m (Ref. 9924).

species.name: Tile grande tête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms, near isolated reefs (Ref. 9119).  Mature females are encountered in April and November in the Gulf of California, Mexico and in September in Colombia, Ecuador and the Galapagos Islands (Ref. 9119).  Marketed fresh or frozen and considered of excellent quality for human consumption (Ref. 9119).

species.name: Tile gris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on mud and rubble bottom.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates (crustaceans, mollusks, polychaetes and brittle stars) and fishes.  Captured mainly from 75 to 200 m deep and occurring to at least 236 m (Ref. 6134).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Tile oeil doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble bottoms.  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and other invertebrates;  occasionally on small fishes.  Flesh not appreciated (Ref. 5217).  Minimum depth from Ref. 47377.  Traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Tile réticulé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-shell bottoms.  Flesh not highly appreciated.

species.name: Tile zebre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Epibenthic.  Has a marked seasonal availability.  Most abundant from June to October at 50-100 m depth (Ref. 7358).

species.name: Tile à raie noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms. Possibly construct burrows in the seafloor sediments (Ref. 101572).  Feeds on invertebrates and small fishes (Ref. 26235).  Marketed fresh and is highly appreciated as a food fish.

species.name: Tile-colored righteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand-mud bottoms.  Very rare.  Feeds on small benthic animals (Ref. 9792).

species.name: Tilesina gibbosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 15 m (Ref. 56557).

species.name: Timika Mouth Almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Common in forest streams in Timika region, Papua New Guinea. Inactive during the day, usually hovering in sheltered locations, frequently among plants, aquatic (50% ground cover, e.g. Vallisneria, Limnophilia), tree roots, and dead branches.

species.name: Timor cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow protected coastal reef crests and lagoons, hiding below corals during the day, but also trawled on soft bottom (Ref. 48635); also under boulders on shallow reef flats.  Nocturnal species. Aquarium breeding is possible (Ref. 130643).

species.name: Timor Sea banjofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Timor wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow coastal reefs, mainly rock substrates with soft coral and algal growth.  Occurs in small loose groups dominated by a large male (Ref. 48636).  May also be found solitary  (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Timorichthys angustus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Timorichthys disjunctus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is viviparous, living near to, or on, the bottom on the deep northwestern Australian Plateau (Ref. 88959).

species.name: Tiny cardinalfish
species.description: Occurs in silty inshore reefs; aggregations observed hovering during the day around both soft and hard coral formations.  An oral brooding male collected at Madang, papua New Guinea, contained 328 eggs, which is a relatively low number for the genus (Ref. 11893).

species.name: Tiny cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tiny goby
species.description: The type specimens were obtained within 100 m of each other on an approximately 20° mud slope.  Two specimens were collected together from the inside of a dead bivalve while the other two were found on either filamentous algae or sponge that covered bottom debris, including a piece of wood and a cement block, and a fifth uncollected specimen was also observed and photographed in the same dead bivalve mentioned above (Ref. 107278).

species.name: Tiny Hawaiian dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Tiny New Guinea longtail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth of 24 m reported from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Tiny pygmy-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mangrove shores, occasionally near coral reefs in 0-2 m. Usually in groups, often hovering in midwater (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Tiny shrimpgoby
species.description: The type locality is a narrow isolated patch reef that rises to within 1 or 2 m of the surface from a depth of about 30 m and approximately 8 solitary individuals were observed at this location on a silty-sand and rubble bottom. It was invariably seen at the entrance of a burrow in company with an unidentified species of alpheid shrimp (Ref. 120714).

species.name: Tiny whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Tippecanoe darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow gravel riffles of medium-sized rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adults feed on midge larvae and baetid mayfly nymphs (Ref. 10294).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Tiquie banded knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens were collected in small, clearwater terra firme forest streams, generally no more than half a meter deep and one meter wide; dipnet was used after being stunned with the aid of barbasco (timbó), an ichthyocide prepared from the root of Lonchocarpus urucu (Leguminosae). This species was collected syntopically with Sternopygus macrurus, Eigenmannia sp. (Sternopygidae), Hypopygus lepturus, Hypopygus sp., Brachyhypopomus sp. (Hypopomidae), and the congeners G. carapo and G. coropinae (Gymnotidae). In the Rio Tiquié basin, G. tiquie and G. coropinae appear to be confined to terra firme streams while G. carapo was recorded from both terra firme streams and from the main channel of the Rio Tiquié (Ref. 83328).

species.name: Tiran sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-10 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Tire track eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flowing waters.  Most often found over gravel substrates where it buries itself during the day.  Feeds actively at night on benthic insect larvae, worms and some submerged plant matter (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Titan cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tlaloc portillorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The specimens were collected from two sites at 1340 m elevation in two small tributaries of the Río Calam in the Ulúa drainage. The creeks were 3-5 m wide, 20-40 cm deep and canopy cover was c. 60%; substratum dominated by large cobble, and creek margins featured emergent macrophytes where the species was collected. Associated fishes Alfaro huberi, Oreochromis niloticus and Rhamdia laticauda (Ref. 84033).

species.name: Toad lumpsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand, broken shell and gravel bottoms (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Toadfish
species.description: Max. length (Eran Brokovich, pers. comm., 2001).

species.name: Toadfish goby
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms in coral-reef habitats (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Toadstool groper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Toba betta
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in peat swamps (Ref. 93059).  Bubble nest builder (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Tobago coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tocantinsia piresi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Largest specimen collected is 38.5 cm SL (Mark Sabaj Perez, pers. comm.;  http://www.scotcat.com/auchenipteridae/tocantinsia_piresi.htm).

species.name: Togean flasherwrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes bottom rubble areas in small groups of mix sexes with females outnumbering males (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Togo Killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in temporary pools and swamps in the savanna (Ref. 3788).  Bottom spawner, 3-4 months incubation.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Tokyo bitterling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tollo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Important food fish and is referred to in books and the popular press.

species.name: Toluca silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomato clownfish
species.description: Poisson. Found in lagoon reefs and embayment. Monogamous (Ref. 52884), protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemone Entacmaea quadricolor (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413, 35415, 35418, 35420).

species.name: Tomato Snailfish
species.description: One 11.6 cm TL ripe male and female specimens were examined:  the smallest female with yolked eggs was 14.9 cm (UW 119817).  For the ripe females, at least two sizes of eggs were present, yolked eggs were 3.5 mm in diameter and smaller white eggs had diameters of 0.5-1.5 mm (Ref. 91047).

species.name: Tombigbee darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tometes ancylorhynchus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tometes camunani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gut contents of large specimens measuring 17.5-38.2 cm SL are composed mainly of leaves of Podostemaceae, and fragments of grass and whole seeds of Myrtaceae and Fabaceae. Two smallest specimens examined measuring 9.08 and 13.3 cm SL feed mainly on fragments of Podostemaceae and benthic macroinvertebrates (Leptophlebiidae, Simuliidae and Chironomidae). All dissected specimens contain Oxyuroid nematodes (Rondonia rondoni) in their gastrointestinal tracts (Ref. 93807).

species.name: Tometes kranponhah
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tometes lebaili
species.description: Espèce de poissons. All specimens captured in rapids upstream. Captured with hooked-lines baited with Podostemaceae, arrows, and rotenone. Podostemaceae seems to be their main diet. Very similar to Tometes trilobatus. Both species are important for Amerindian tribes Wayãpi and Wayana. Could be endangered by human threats like subsistence fisheries, habitat destruction by mining activities, and dams (Ref. 47182).

species.name: Tometes makue
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tometes siderocarajensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rapids associated with rocky outcropping covered in aquatic macrophytes of the families Podostemaceae and Fabaceae, which serve as a food source for this fish. The stomach contents of one large specimen measuring 34.0 cm SL consisted mainly of large pieces of Podostemaceae (leaves and flowers), but also comprised of three small Fabaceae fruits and a cricket (Orthoptera). Occurs syntopically with three other serrasalmid, rapids-adapted species, namely, Mylesinus paucisquamatus, Myleus setiger, and Tometes ancylorhynchus. Commonly captured by local, professional and amateur fishermen in the Itacaiúnas River. One of the most in demand species for game fishing in the region based on fishermen report (Ref. 116762).

species.name: Tometes trilobatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rheophilic species, collected in high courses, especially in zones of rapids.  Associated with Podostemaceae, the rupestral plants characteristic of the rapids of the studied area, observed in abundance in the stomachs (Ref. 43881).

species.name: Tomicodon abuelorum
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in areas with mangrove prop roots, usually attached to, or moving about and feeding from, root surfaces at high tide (Ref. 42103). Stomach contents contained barnacle cirri and barnacle cyprid larvae, Sphaeroma peruvianum, small oysters and other bivalves, amphipods, and harpacticoid copepods (Ref. 42103).

species.name: Tomicodon australis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomicodon briggsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from areas with sand and coral bottom (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon clarkei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from a single specimen (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon cryptus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from high-energy zones of rocky shores, including tide pools (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon lavettsmithi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomicodon leurodiscus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from vertical rock walls (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon prodomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomicodon reitzae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the shallow surge zone (Ref. 50106).  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon rhabdotus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky shallow surge zones (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon rupestris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from rocky shallow surge zones (Ref. 50106).

species.name: Tomicodon vermiculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tominanga aurea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tominanga sanguicauda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomini surgeonfish
species.description: Occurs singly or in small groups along steep coral-rich drop-offs of sheltered coasts (Ref. 48637). Feeds on algae and microfauna living in between the algae (Ref. 89999).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Tomiyamichthys dorsostigma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives symbiotically in sand near fringing reef with an unidentified alpheid shrimp, in shallow waters.  Collected b multi-pronged spears (Ref. 88846),

species.name: Tomiyamichthys fourmanoiri
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomiyamichthys levisquama
species.description: Occurs over mud bottom (Ref. 116701).

species.name: Tommyfish
species.description: Buries itself in areas of broken shell and gravel with only the head exposed.  Darts away and dives into the sand when disturbed.

species.name: Tomocichla asfraci
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tomocichla tuba
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits moderate to fast flowing waters of rivers with high velocity.  Feeds on aquatic plants, algae, and fruits.  Juveniles are partial to aquatic insects (Ref. 7335).

species.name: Tonala catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tondanichthys kottelati
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tongan spiny basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected off a deep slope with a near vertical coral wall with a sandy channel at its base, followed by a steep drop-off (Ref. 75897).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tongareva goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy bottoms of lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of over 9 m (Ref. 37816). Gut examined of a 2.78 cm SL male included remains of mantid shrimps and that of a 2.39 mm SL female included one juvenile specimen of Cabillus tongarevae, indicating possible cannibalistic habit (Ref. 125964).

species.name: Tongue flatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Rare.  Feeds on small benthic animals.

species.name: Tongue sole
species.description: Carnivorous, feeds mainly on benthic crustaceans and fish (Ref. 30433).

species.name: Tonguetied minnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools and runs of creeks and small to medium rivers, often near vegetation or other cover.  Males construct large circular or rectangular nests by piling pebbles carried in the mouth (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Tonkin numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in continental waters, both inshore and offshore (Ref. 9912).  Biology little known (Ref. 9912).

species.name: Tonlesapia tsukawakii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lake with mud substrate (Ref. 56950).

species.name: Tono's wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on open hard-bottom substrates with algae and sparse coral growth, usually in strong current zones.  Juveniles and females in small groups, sometimes with several males of which largest is dominating (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Toothbrush leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass beds and on rocky reefs. Females resemble the rough leatherjacket Scobinichthys granulatus (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Toothed carp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters, brooks and rivers (Ref. 3788).  6 cm SL (Ref. 7372).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Toothed Cuban cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves. Feeds on cirolanid isopods. Viviparous. Found together with L. subterranea and L. teresinarum (Ref. 34024).

species.name: Toothed no-line scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species.

species.name: Toothless blindcat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits subterranean waters.

species.name: Toothless catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in clear, flowing waters.  Often forms aggregations around log snags or in deeper rock pools.  Also occurs in sandy bottoms around the cover of woody debris and in flooded lagoons. Solitary (Ref. 44894).  Feeds on aquatic insects, mollusks, prawns and bottom detritus (Ref. 5259).  Feeds by thrusting its snout into the sandy bottom.  Nothing is specific is known about the breeding biology, but it probably spawns early in the wet season (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Toothless smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Toothless snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Toothy flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bays and coastal waters (Ref. 9002).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Toothy goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among soft coral, sponges, Tridacna, and broad-blade plants (Ref. 2798). Also inhabits coastal bays and reef slopes, found on a variety of host and also on algae from very shallow to at least 30 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Toothy topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits ponds, lakes and streams but prefers clear sluggish streams.  Feeds on the bottom on aquatic vegetation, diatoms, algae and insect larvae.

species.name: Topeka shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet gravel-bottomed and sand-bottomed pools of headwaters and creeks.

species.name: Topgallant blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A moderate-depth species found from 7.6-30 m.

species.name: Topside lampfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, epipelagic and mesopelagic (Ref. 4479).  Found between 375-700 m during the day and between 25-350 m at night (Ref. 4066).  Size stratification with depth during the day only (Ref. 4775).  Juveniles migratory; adults migratory, partially migratory or non-migratory (Ref. 4775).  Feed on copepods, conchoecid ostracods and euphausiids (Ref. 4775).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 31442).  Also Ref. 58302.

species.name: Tor ater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tor laterivittatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Large adults are found in deep pools; juveniles were most frequently found in shallow areas with sandy substrate (Ref. 27732).  Its meat becomes poisonous to eat after feeding on the fruits of certain trees (Ref. 43281).  Reaches up to at least 60 cm SL (Ref. 27732).

species.name: Tor polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams with clear water and usually with slow current (Ref. 13848).

species.name: Tor yingjiangensis
