species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds on insects and their larvae, as well as on molluscs, plants and detritus;  maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis lateralis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds mainly upon insect larvae, plants and fruits, as well as detritus and molluscs (Ref. 52307, 52346). Maternal (Ref. 52307) mouth brooder (Ref. 51193) that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307). Tastes like Nile perch, Lates niloticus (Ref. 51906).

species.name: Tylochromis leonensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Appears to be an exclusively Upper Guinean Province species (Ref. 52346). Inhabits large sandbanks and hardly ever penetrates into small streams (Ref. 53407). Benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds primarily upon insects and their larvae, but also accepts plants (Ref. 52307). Oviphilous (Ref. 53407), maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis microdon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted in its distribution to the lake proper and absent from the surrounding swamps and inundated forest (Ref. 52346). Predominantly a lacustrine form (unusual among Tylochromines)(Ref. 52346). Benthic microphage (Ref. 52346). Feeds mainly upon small organic particles, plants and invertebrates; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swamp-dweller (Ref. 6770). Juveniles are coastal and gregarious while adults wander over the sandy bottoms by themselves (Ref. 6770), in shallow inshore areas of the lake, in lagoons and river mouths (Ref. 4967). Feeds mainly on crustaceans and insects, along with some plants (Ref. 52307), but also a mollusc eater (Ref. 6316, 10616). Maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 1872, 52307) that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307). Females have been observed with about 100 eggs of a diameter of 6 mm (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis praecox
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivorous, prefers small organic particles, regardless whether they are plants or small insects (Ref. 52307).  Opportunistic bentic microphage; probably tolerant of relatively high salinity levels (Ref. 52346). Maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 52346) that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis pulcher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly found in lakes and surrounding swamps and seasonally inundated forests; primarily a benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds upon larger particles, plants as well as insects; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis regani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Mainly feeds on plants and insect larvae; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis robertsi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Opportunistic benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Mainly feeds on plants and insects (as well as their larvae) (Ref. 52307). Female mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307, 52346) that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis sudanensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers algae and plant matter, as well as invertebrates; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307). Maximum total length 26.0 cm (Ref. 42518).

species.name: Tylochromis trewavasae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly feeds on insects and their larvae; maternal mouthbrooder that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tylochromis variabilis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Opportunistic benthic macrophage (Ref. 52346). Feeds on plants, insects and (to a lesser degree) molluscs (Ref. 52307).  Maternal (Ref. 52307) mouthbrooder (Ref. 4910, 52307) that does not pair-bond (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Tympanopleura atronasus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Spawns between mid-to-late October and end of March.  Feeds on small small macroinvertebrates and fish (Ref. 103256).

species.name: Tympanopleura brevis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tympanopleura cryptica
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tympanopleura longipinna
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tympanopleura piperata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tympanopleura rondoni
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlachirus caecus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlachirus lipophthalmus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft muddy-slit substrate. Caught as bycatch of Macrobrachium rosenbergii fishery with the use of a method called 'Belat' (net length ca15 m, mesh about 4-5 cm wide) held in place by long wooden stakes laid around a shallow dip in the river bank during low tide, and left for one tidal cycle before retrieval (Ref. 126196).

species.name: Typhleotris madagascariensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Blind and pigment-free obligate cave-dwelling species; restricted to subterranean habitats (caves, sinkholes, wells) within the Mahafaly Plateau karst formation, as well as isolated locations with Eocene limestone along the coastal plain below and to the west of the plateau, to the south of the large Onilahy River drainage basin (Ref. 93144). Apparently confined in underground waters (Ref. 6802). Attracted by disturbance of water surface (Ref. 94243). Feeds on crustaceans and insects found in caves (Ref. 91201).

species.name: Typhleotris mararybe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Blind, cave-dwelling species; the known habitat, Grotte de Vitane, is a karst formation with nearly vertical walls, whose water level at the time of collection was approximately 10-15 m below the rim; the diameter of the sinkhole was approximately 100 m across at its widest, and 70 m at its narrowest, with more or less shear walls; the heigth of the sinkhole walls to the water level was approximately 50 m on its southern end, and much shallower on the northern end (Ref. 93144). The water was relatively clear, deep, and warm, about 7.5-10 m deep on average; occurs in open water within 1–1.5 m of the surface; upon being chased, all individuals immediately dove toward the bottom (Ref. 93144).

species.name: Typhleotris pauliani
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is restricted to subterranean habitats in coastal regions to the south of Morombe in the vicinity of Andalambezo (Ref. 93144). A cave-dwelling species (Ref. 6802). Feeds on guano and small aquatic insects (Ref. 91201).

species.name: Typhlobarbus nudiventris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species.

species.name: Typhlobelus auriculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected during late afternoon at the peak of the southwestern Amazonian summer when rivers are at their lowest level.  The site was a marginal sand bank forming a small island.  Found in an area with moderate current (approx. 40 cm/sec), depths up to 35 cm, markedly warm water (30-33uC on the surface), horizontal transparency varied between 2.5 and 3.2 m and pH 6.5-7.0.

species.name: Typhlobelus guacamaya
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlobelus lundbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlobelus macromycterus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlobelus ternetzi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Typhlonarke
species.description: Found on the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 26346). Produces up to 11 pups a litter. Males reaches maturity at 35-40 cm TL; birth size at 9-10 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Typical eelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyrannochromis macrostoma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky areas in shallow water (Ref. 267).  Piscivore, feeds by moving around rocks and into cracks in search of its unwary prey, the Mbunas, which are quickly snapped up with the large mouth (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Tyrannochromis maculiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sediment-free rocky habitats in shallow areas.  Piscivore, feeds by ambushing its prey (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Tyrannochromis nigriventer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sediment-free rocky habitats in shallow areas.  Feeds on fish (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Tyrannochromis polyodon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers sediment-free rocky habitats in shallow waters (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Tyrannophryne pugnax
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttobrycon dorsimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttobrycon hamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttobrycon marajoara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from temporary streams, drying completely during the dry season (September to February) and flowing on the rainy season (March to August).  Small groups of adults were found on the bottom and marginal portions of the streams in April.  Juveniles in large schools were collected along the bottom of the stream in August (Ref. 94718).

species.name: Tyttobrycon spinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttobrycon xeruini
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttocharax cochui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tyttocharax metae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams characterized by relatively rapid water current, running over rocky and sandy bottoms at altitudes between 264- 282 m a.s.l., high dissolved oxygen (5.7-7.1 mg/l) and having tea colored water with usually high transparency (Ref. 91745).

species.name: Tyttocharax tambopatensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small black water streams in areas forested by the palm Maurita flexuosa. Usually occurs in the gallery forest areas in pools of small streams of 2-4m wide. The water depth where this species occurs is usually 20-60cm and the current is slow. The bottom is usually sandy but may be pebbly and with much forest debris. Commonly found near the shoreline where they can seek protection from predators among vegetation. Commonly swims near the surface of the water in schools of about 20 to 80 individuals.

species.name: Tåning’s lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic, found between 475-1000 m during the day; nyctoepipelagic at surface and down to 250 m ( maximum abundance at 100 m) (Ref. 4479).

species.name: Télescope arctique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic species.  Found at 250-850 m during the day; at 90-325 m at night (Ref. 4775).  Epipelagic to bathypelagic.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 58426).  Sexually mature when 3cm long (Ref. 35388).

species.name: Téléo noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In moderate to fast, shallow rapids, with clear water and the riverbed composed mainly of large rocks and little accumulated sediment.  Feeds predominantly on of caddisfly larvae (Trichoptera) and other hard-shelled invertebrates (gastropods and bivalves), as well as midges (Diptera: Chironomidae) and mayfly larvae (Ephemeroptera) (Ref. 108975).

species.name: Téraglin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters, over sand muddy bottom. Juveniles enter estuaries. Adults feed on pelagic fishes at night. Often caught with Umbrina canariensis. Feeds on pelagic fish such as mackerel and horse mackerel (Ref. 36731). Marketed fresh, flesh highly esteemed (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Térraba toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits stagnant waters or currents of all velocities between 40-1250 m of elevation; mainly in waters of moderate flow in brooks and creeks at temperatures of 20-23°C.  Feeds on terrestrial insects (Ref. 36880).

species.name: Tétard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and creeks between 25 and 580 m elevation, in currents of high velocity and feeds on fish, fish scales and aquatic insects (Ref. 36880).  Occurs solitarily in streams (Ref. 11225).

species.name: Tétra africain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Affinities: close to B. taeniurus and B. opisthotaenia; body with clearly wider band than the former; dark band starts less forward than in B. opisthotaenia, originating slightly posterior to vertical through dorsal fin origin in B. kingsleyae, but originating at a vertical through dorsal fin origin in B. opisthotaenia (Ref. 80290).

species.name: Tétra aveugle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and sandy bottoms of pools and backwaters of creeks and small to large rivers, and springs.  Feeds on insects, crustaceans and worms (Ref. 7020).  Migrates during winter to warmer areas (Ref. 47195).

species.name: Tétra citron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra de Colombie
species.description: Poisson. In small creeks.

species.name: Tétra de Rio
species.description: Poisson. Inhabits small streams of slow flowing, dark-brown or clear water, shaded by small forests.  Occurs also in small streams with clear water and sandy bottom.  Prefers habitats with vegetation and streams with slow flowing water, living in depths not superior to 50 c and water temperature from 22°-28°C.  Forms relatively numerous schools with agonistic interaction among alpha males. Feeds on small insects, worms and plants.  Female lays around 200 to 330 oocytes on rocks, plants, or submerged debris; after that, the male releases the sperm for fertilization. The eggs hatch in about 2-3 days.  Longevity is around four years (Ref. 96863).  In tank, female lays 200 to 300 eggs which hatch in 2 to 3 days (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra diamant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra fantôme rouge
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms, small insects and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra pingouin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in groups, in calm, shallow waters with humus-laden substrate (Ref. 12225).  Prefers lentic waters and sandy-rocky bottoms of creeks and counter-current zones of principal rivers (Ref. 27188).  Maximum length report to reach 5 cm SL (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Tétra rose
species.description: Poisson. Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra vampire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently carnivorous, probably ichthyophagous.  Maximum length reported to reach 40 cm TL (Ref. 12468).

species.name: Tétra voilier
species.description: Little is known of its biology in its natural environment.  Unlike most Characoids, this species is typically solitary and territorial.  The dimensions of the mouth confirms its predatory habits.  Its food consists mainly of Ephemeroptera larvae, copepods and ostracods.  In the aquarium, only the male guards the spawned eggs.  About a hundred eggs are deposited on the substrate and dispersed by the male (Ref. 12225).  Reproduces by laying eggs on stones or submerged leaves (Ref. 27188).

species.name: Tétra à drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in ponds, ditches, slow flowing streams, both clear and turbid, in both open and shaded areas.  A voracious species which feeds on small crustaceans, insects and mollusks (Ref. 12225).  Gregarious and non-aggressive, it is reputedly easy to rear  and to reproduce in the aquarium (Ref. 27188).  Maximum length questionable (Ref. 38376).

species.name: Tétra-empereur
species.description: Poisson. Feeds on worms and crustaceans (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétra-joyau
species.description: Poisson. A gregarious species which positions itself near the surface between the stems of emerging plants.  It is frequently found in stagnant waters.  They are generally peaceful, but when there are too many of them during feeding, they bite each other's fins (Ref. 12225).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plants (Ref. 7020).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  This species is part of a complex of `blood' tetras, hybrids of which are commonly offered in the aquarium trade.  Aquarium keeping:  aggressive;  in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Tétragonure
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, usually near surface; possibly near bottom.  Perhaps occurs in schools.  Young usually among jellyfishes or inside large salps.  Feeds on jellyfishes and salps (Ref. 2850), also other soft-bodied coelenterates, ctenophores, as well as plankton.  There are conflicting reports that the flesh of this species is poisonous (Ref. 11149).

species.name: Tétragonure atlantique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mostly in the upper 91 m but adults probably deeper (Ref. 7251). Occasionally strays close to shore (Ref. 7251). Young commonly inquiline in pelagic tunicates, especially Salpa and Pyrosoma (Ref. 11149). Feeds on soft-bodied medusae, ctenophores and especially salps; will also take plankton (Ref. 11149). The flesh may be poisonous (Ref. 27121).

species.name: Tétraodon-lièvre de Suez
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 127989.

species.name: Tétraodon-lièvre doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Essentially an inhabitant of marine waters, but enters the mouths of rivers (Ref. 4833). Several organs are very toxic, potentially lethal to humans (Ref. 43448).

species.name: Tétrodon constellé
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Tétrodon nain
species.description: Inhabits reefs and marginal habitats such as seagrass beds (Ref. 43205).  Diet consists of seagrass, sponges, crabs and other crustaceans, mollusks, polychaete worms, sea urchins, starfishes, hydroids and algae (Ref. 13442).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Tête de boule
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy pools of headwaters, creeks, small rivers, and ponds (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Also found in lakes (Ref. 10294).  Can tolerate conditions (e.g., turbid, hot, poorly oxygenated, intermittent streams) unsuitable for most fishes (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on detritus and algae (Ref. 10294).  Spawns in still-water habitats along shores (Ref. 59043).  Introductions consequently caused the spread of the enteric red-mouth disease throughout northern Europe which infected wild and cultured trouts and eels (Ref. 1739).  Maintained a relatively high metabolic rate and level of activity under hypoxic conditions (Ref. 77050).  Individuals  that survived the hypoxic conditions during winter had rapid growth rates after ice-off (Ref. 77048).

species.name: Tête de serpent d'Indonésie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland river and swamp (Ref. 57235).  Usually associated with deep water bodies (Ref. 27732).  Found in large streams and canals (Ref. 4833), with standing or slowly flowing water (Ref. 12693).  Feeds mainly on fish but also takes some crustaceans.  Spawns in small streams with dense vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 4931).  Economic important mainly from capture fisheries (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Tête de serpent strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit ponds, streams and rivers, preferring stagnant and muddy water of plains (Ref. 41236). Found mainly in swamps, but also occurs in the lowland rivers. More common in relatively deep (1-2 m), still water. Very common in freshwater plains (Ref. 4515, 57235). Occur in medium to large rivers, brooks, flooded fields and stagnant waters including sluggish flowing canals (Ref. 12975). Recorded as having been or being farmed in rice fields (Ref. 119549). Survive dry season by burrowing in bottom mud of lakes, canals and swamps as long as skin and air-breathing apparatus remain moist (Ref. 2686) and subsists on the stored fat (Ref. 1479). Feed on fish, frogs, snakes, insects, earthworms, tadpoles (Ref. 1479) and crustaceans (Ref. 2847). Undertake lateral migration from the Mekong mainstream, or other permanent water bodies, to flooded areas during the flood season and return to the permanent water bodies at the onset of the dry season (Ref. 37770). During winter and dry season, its flesh around coelomic cavity is heavily infested by a larval trematode Isoparorchis hypselobargi. Other parasites infecting this fish include Pallisentis ophicephali in the intestine and Neocamallanus ophicepahli in the pyloric caecae (Ref. 1479). Processed into pra-hoc, mam-ruot, and mam-ca-loc (varieties of fish paste) in Kampuchea (Ref.4929). Perhaps the main food fish in Thailand, Indochina and Malaysia (Ref. 2686). Firm white flesh almost bone-free, heavy dark skin good for soup and usually sold separately (Ref. 2686). In Hawaiian waters the largest specimen taken reportedly exceeded 150 cm (Ref. 44091). Very economic important on both cultures and captures throughout southern and southeastern Asia (Ref. 57235).

species.name: Tête de serpent tachetée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in ponds, swamps, brackish water (Ref. 6028), ditches and beels (Ref. 1479).  Adults prefer stagnant waters in muddy streams (Ref. 4833).  Feed on worms, insects and small fish (Ref. 6028).  Accept chopped fish and shrimp in the aquarium.  Breed throughout the year.  Mitochondrial hypertrophy, noted in the double cone of the retina of this species, is considered a basic process in oil droplet formation (Ref. 10557) believed to be an adaptation for enhanced visual contrast detection in turbid waters (Ref. 10407).  Used as live bait for angling larger snakeheads.

species.name: Tête en bas
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps but also found in creeks and rivers.

species.name: Tête en bas rayé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow areas of rivers and creeks, with sandy substrate and a strong current. Feed on algae. Are relatively abundant and are often found together with Leporinus despaxi, Bryconops affinis and Eigenmannia virescens (Ref. 12225). They generally swim with the head oriented downward (Ref. 27188). Distinct pairs breed on densely grown weedy places (Ref. 205).

species.name: Tête en bas rayé (Anostomus ternetzi)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in fast-flowing parts of rivers.  Omnivorous, feed on aquatic plants and insects.  Spawn on the vegetation and on the bottom (Ref. 12225).

species.name: Tête en bas rayé (Caenotropus maculosus)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on largest examined specimen.

species.name: Tête rose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky runs and flowing pools of small to medium rivers.  Common in upland areas and clear streams with fast current.

species.name: U-mark sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silty sand and rubble areas near reefs at depths of 10-40 m (Ref. 2334, 90102).

species.name: U-spot wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uaru
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear streams with a pH of 6.8 (Ref. 12251).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020), but needs plants as supplement (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Uaru fernandezyepezi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In rivers, but never very abundant; not esteemed as food fish.  Maximum length 24 cm TL  (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Ucamara catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected in lakes or lake channels within dense marginal or floating vegetation, sometimes in hypoxic conditions (Ref. 56211).

species.name: Ucayali catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uegitglanis zammaranoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Cave-restricted species. Depth of water at type locality was 1.25 m. The temperature was 24°C, pH 8 and the hardness 300mg/l Ca. To date there are no other data available on the biology of the species (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Uganda nothobranch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in temporary water bodies: swamps, roadside and drainage ditches, pools and depressions downstream of culverts; in turbid to very turbid water; usually no aquatic vegetation present, only some grasses and reeds may be found near the banks (Ref. 26661). Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation (Ref. 27139). Young can reach sexual maturity in 6 or 7 weeks (Ref. 59344).

species.name: Ukkrit’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Captured using rotenone along the coast with beach rock bommie surrounded by sand and patch reef. Area of occurrence may include live corals such as Acropora, Astreopora, Pavona, Porites, Millepora, Pectinia coral, favids and others (Ref. 123489).

species.name: Ukrainian gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams in foot hills and lowlands with moderate current. Size reaches up to about 13 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Ulvaire deux-lignes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among algae on rocky shores and on hard bottom in deeper water, or depth of 55 meters or more (Ref. 51666).  Male guards multiple egg masses (Ref. 58332).

species.name: Umatilla dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble riffles and runs of large rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Umbre de vase
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet areas of streams, sloughs, swamps and other wetlands over mud and debris (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Often found in dense vegetation.  Tolerates drought, low oxygen levels and extremes water temperature (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on aquatic insects, amphipods, isopods, and snails (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Umbrella cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Aquarium keeping:  in pairs; minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).  Eggs are deposited on the ceiling of caves and are tendered by the female parent (Ref. 1672).

species.name: Umbrella conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over soft bottom of the continental shelf (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Umbrina imberbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Umbrina milliae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Umbrina reedi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: uMkhomazi mountain catfish
species.description: Occurs in riffle habitats in perennial streams and rivers (Ref. 123712).

species.name: Umpire Triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Umpqua dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky riffles (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Umpqua pikeminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes and pools and sluggish runs of creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Umpquachub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sluggish sand- and gravel-bottomed runs, pools and backwaters of creeks and small rivers as well as sloughs. Usually found near vegetations (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Unarmed dwarf monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms in offshore waters.  Usually in small groups, in depths over 50 m (Ref. 48635).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Also caught with deep-sea shrimp traps.

species.name: Uncisudis advena
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Maximum length based on immature specimen (Ref. 37039).

species.name: Uncisudis longirostra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uncisudis posteropelvis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uncisudis quadrimaculata
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at 25-600 m (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Undistinguished sabretooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic at ca. 100-1000 m (Ref. 58302).  Larvae (<3 cm SL) and small juveniles are frequently caught in the upper 50 or 100 m.  Most adults are usually taken from depths exceeding 400 m but often between 100-400 m (Ref. 4763).  Feeds on other midwater fishes.  Synchronous hermaphrodites (Ref. 4478).

species.name: Unernak aurore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves (Ref. 11954).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Unernak à grands yeux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves (Ref. 11954).  Minimum depth from type locality data (Ref. 51665).  Benthic (Ref. 58426).

species.name: Unicolor coralgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446). Found among Acopora coral branches, often A.millepora and A.nasuta, also with other species of Gobiodon (Ref 90102).

species.name: Unicolor moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow lagoon reefs and drop-offs as deep as 25 m (Ref. 1602).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Unicolor snake moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in mangrove swamps, brackish rivers, and shallow coral reefs to depths of at least 8 m (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 86942.

species.name: Unicorn crestfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare (Ref. 4165), mesopelagic species found at 1,000 m depth (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Unicorn grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Unicorn sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 30573), on sand or mud bottoms to at least 100 m (Ref. 9710, 11230, 48637).

species.name: Unicornfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Unipa chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from the type locality with rubble and low-profile coral reef substratum at the base of a steep, nearly vertical drop-off, 42 to at least 65 m depth (Ref. 82433).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Unipore snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Probably benthic or benthopelagic (Ref. 42734).  Largest eggs 1.7 mm in diameter, unripe (Ref. 42734).

species.name: Unpolished dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Unspecked hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rivers (Ref. 26703).

species.name: Upjaw barb
species.description: Occurs in swamps and floodplains in shallow densely vegetated still-water habitats.  Feeds on minute planktonic organisms (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Upland bully
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams.  Preys on invertebrates (Ref. 27776). Maximum life-span for both sexes was observed to be 4.5 years (Ref. 46231).

species.name: Upper Grijalva livebearer
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Upper Yenisei grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Upper Zambezi labeo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocks in mainstream and in large soft-bottomed floodplain lagoons.  Grazes algae and aufwuchs as well as detritus.  A shoaling species, breeding in summer, possibly in flooded marginal habitats, as the young fish are caught in large numbers in fish-weirs set across floodwaters receding from floodplains (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Upper Zambezi squeaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Upper Zambezi yellowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers fast water with rocky bottom and seldom occurs over sand or in aquatic vegetation (Ref. 13337). Feeds on aquatic insect larvae, crustaceans, mollusks and small fish (Ref. 13337).

species.name: Upside-down goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on lagoon reefs and hovers upside-down among thickets of the staghorn coral Acropora formosa (Ref. 37816, 48637). Often seen resting on underside of coral branches and makes short forays into water column to feed on planktons (Ref 90102).

species.name: Upside-down pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rocky reefs.  Appear to feed nocturnally, and usually found swimming upside down in caves or under ledges during the day.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  Males carry the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 6.3 cm SL.

species.name: Upsidedown catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Omnivore, feeds on plankton, algae and detritus (Ref. 13868).  May also feed on surface insects, chironomid larvae, benthic crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 28714).  Oviparous (Ref. 205). Maximum size reported as 50.0cm total length in Ref. 3799, but only 26.5cm total length in Ref. 57223.

species.name: Upturned snout rattail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Upwelling dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uranoscope boeuf
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often buried (Ref. 7366) in sand or mud (Ref. 26999).

species.name: Uranoscope bouledogue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on bottom.  Feeds mainly on other fishes.  Young are pelagic and eaten by large predatory fishes such as tunas.  Spine above pectoral fin probably slightly venomous.

species.name: Uranoscope du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uranoscope géant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported from depths between 30 m (Ref. 58489) and 600 m (Ref. 9258). Buries in sea bed until suitable prey passes by.  Utilized fresh and frozen; can be steamed, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Uranoscope miou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often buried in sand or mud (Ref. 7366).

species.name: Uranoscope miraciel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy bottoms, gravel or mud, adults between 5-15 m, juveniles between 0-5 meters on the edge of beaches and protected bays (Ref. 26375).

species.name: Uranoscope tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty, sandy, or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 13628).  Possesses electric organs located in a specialized pouch behind the eyes.  Can discharge up to 50 volts (Ref. 10576).The electric organ discharge (EOD) rate depends on the temperature:  about 500 Hz at 35°C and 50 Hz at 15°C (corresponding to the annual temperature range of the  habitat of this species) (Ref. 10011).  Cleithral spine with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Uranoscope à bordure blanche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and coastal bottoms (Ref. 9710) but is rarely seen because it lies buried in sand or mud most of the time, with only the eyes showing.  When buried, the cirri on the edge of the mouth serve to keep out the sand during respiration.  The oral lure is used to attract the prey within striking range of the mouth.  The shoulder has a venomous cleithral spine; wounds can be serious.

species.name: Uranoscope épineux
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft or rubble bottoms.

species.name: Uranoscopus affinis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uranoscopus archionema
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The large spine on the shoulder is venomous.

species.name: Uranoscopus bauchotae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uranoscopus chinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, down to 120 m on sand or sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Uranoscopus crassiceps
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms of lower continental shelf and at relatively narrow depth range (Ref. 94018).

species.name: Uranoscopus dahlakensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uranoscopus filibarbis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Uranoscopus fuscomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic predator often lying buried up to its eyes in mud or sand waiting for prey to venture close enough to be caught with a swift lunge.

species.name: Uranoscopus japonicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore, down to 260 m, on sand and sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Spend a large part of their time buried in the mud or sand with only their eyes and a portion of the mouth protruding (Ref. 4716).  Cleithral spine with venom gland (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Uranoscopus marisrubri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from 363-383 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Uranoscopus marmoratus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Better reference needed.

species.name: Uranoscopus oligolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max. length (Edward O. Murdy, pers. comm., 1998).

species.name: Uranoscopus rosette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected using rotenone in cove, edge of precipitous reef with numerous caves, rock and coral ledge, over sand and patches of segrasses (Ref. 93135).

species.name: Uranoscopus tosae
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shelf and shelf edge (Ref. 11230).  Hides in sandy bottoms.

species.name: Uranoscopus turbisquamatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Urchin clingfish
species.description: Occurs in rock pools and the subtidal zone. Usually found beneath the spines of sea urchins. Individuals too large to be associated with sea urchins usually found beneath rocks or among shell debris. Feeds mainly on the tube feet and pedicellariae of its host sea urchins, Evechinus chloroticus (Ref. 33548) and on small crustaceans.

species.name: Urmia Lake chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Max length assumed to be TL.

species.name: Urobatis pardalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uroconger drachi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uroconger erythraeus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Urolophus deforgesi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 51067).

species.name: Urolophus neocaledoniensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 51067).

species.name: Urolophus papilio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the continental slope (Ref. 51067).  Adult size unknown (Ref. 51067).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Urophycis mystacea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species occurring around 200 m depth, rarely found above 60 m.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Uropterygius genie
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Uropterygius golanii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Urotrygon caudispinosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Urotrygon cimar
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in tide pools and to a depth of 85 m.  Usually collected in waters shallower than 10 m.

species.name: Ursinoscorpaenopsis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Urucu cory
species.description: Occurs along semilentic stretches of the shore of a moderately large stream (Igarapé da Onça), about 15 m wide, with sand, clay and leaves on the bottom, in addition to emerged vegetation.  Average depth of the stream is 1 m during dry season and 4 m in rainy season (Ref. 83456).

species.name: Uruguay river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently confined to freshwater at mouths of rivers and their lower reaches.  Presumably schooling.

species.name: Uruguay tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lentic environment (Ref. 11229).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Uruguayan eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Urville's longtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species, sometimes entering brackish water (Ref. 9682).  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates >2 mm (Ref. 11889).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Usangu lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in swamps, little streams and brooks in the river drainage (Ref. 3788).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Ussuri catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ussuri sharpbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Usumacinta buffalo
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Weight of 8,405 grams reported for a specimen caught in Misicab Island, Tabasco, Mexico (E.Perusquia as pers. comm., 02/05).

species.name: Usumacinta molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is like other species in the Poecilia latipinna complex, which occurs in shallow, brackish to freshwater coastal areas such as tidal lagoons, lakes, creeks, and pools. It is also found across a range of turbidity (clear to muddy) and substrate types (mud, sand, clay) and is sometimes associated with submerged or emergent aquatic vegetation (Ref. 125334).

species.name: Usumacinta toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs along with Heterandria bimaculata.

species.name: Uswanas’ damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species was found in a typical habitat for the species complex, consisting of sheltered lagoonal reefs associated with large open branching acroporid coral colonies (Ref. 119675).

species.name: Utah chub
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Occurs in lakes, quiet pools of headwaters, creeks and small to medium rivers.  Often found in vegetation over mud or sand (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Utah Lake sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Utah sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, impoundments and streams over silt, sand, gravel or rocks.  Often found near vegetation.

species.name: Utchee rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is found in moderate to fast flowing water, in sections of stream with deep pools separated by short runs; its substrate consists of cobbles and boulders with little fine sediment. Reported to be co-oocurring frequently with purple spotted gudgeons (Mogurnda adspersa), long finned eels (Anguilla reinhardtii) and less commonly with blue-eyes (Psuedomugil signifer), roman nosed gobbies (Awaous acritosis), swamp eels (Ophisternon sp.), grunters (Hephaestus sp.) and exotic guppies (Poecilia reticulata)(Ref. 44137).

species.name: Utiaritichthys esguiceroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults swim in the  main river channel of Rio Juruena, mostly in riffles and rapids. Juveniles occur in calm portions of the Rio Juruena, usually near the margins. Juveniles were reported to feed on aquatic and terrestrial insects and particulate organic matter, while adults almost exclusively on Podostemaceae macrophytes and filamentous algae, both typical of riffles and rapids (Ref. 96883).

species.name: Utiaritichthys longidorsalis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Utiaritichthys sennaebragai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: V-lip redhorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits rocky runs and mud-bottomed to rock-bottomed pools of small rivers.  Also found in impoundments.

species.name: Vachelli's glass perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in brackish waters of bays, estuaries and tidal mangrove creeks, sometimes entering fresh water (Ref. 2847, 44894).  Occurs in lotic and lentic freshwater (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Vacuocua
species.description: Uncommon species inhabiting rocky coastal areas (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Vaillant's anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in middle reaches of rivers.  More data needed.

species.name: Vaillant's grenadier
species.description: Feeds on mysids, pelagic copepods, chaetognaths and small shrimps (Ref. 3587).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 1371.

species.name: Vaillant's smooth-head
species.description: Juveniles possibly mesopelagic to bathypelagic (Ref. 6558).  Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Vaillantella cinnamomea
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Collected from accumulations of leaf litter in sheltered areas of fast flowing streams, with clear water, in forest (Ref. 56749).

species.name: Vaillantella euepiptera
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabit leaf litter off bank of streams with soft clay substrate and turbid water with little current.

species.name: Vaillantella maassi
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce.

species.name: Vairon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Gregarious (Ref. 2196). Found in a wide range of cold and well oxygenated habitats from small, fast-flowing streams to large Nordic lowland rivers and from small upland lakes to large oligotrophic lakes. Usually occurs in association with salmonid fishes (Ref. 59043). Feeds on algae, plant debris (in rivers), mollusks, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 30578). Spawns over clean gravel areas in flowing water or on wave-washed shores of lakes. Overwinters in coarse substrate or in deep pools with low current (Ref. 59043). Migrates upstream for spawning in shallow gravel areas. Important laboratory fish, for research on sensory organs of fishes. Mean maximum age is 6 years (Ref. 41616). Locally threatened due to pollution and excessive stocking of species of Salmo (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Vairon-brochet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in weedy canals and tolerates poorly oxygenated waters and salinity to 40 ppt.  Occurrence in saline (34-37 ppt.) water in Florida seems to be a case of local acclimatization.  Formerly used in medical research.  Total length 14 cm (Ref. 26938).  Mostly freshwater, sometimes brackish (Ref. 26938).  Piscivore (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Valaam whitefish
species.description: Recorded from coastal waters at sea. Lacustrine, at depths greater than 30 m, in Lake Ladoga commonly at 50-150 m (Ref. 59043). Specimens measuring 36-40 cm are more than 5 years old.  Spawns for the first time at 4-6 years (Ref. 59043).  Spawns from the end of November to 20 December (Ref. 593).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are buried in unguarded nests (Ref. 205). Feeds on benthic invertebrates, especially gammarids, molluscs and insect larvae (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Valdivia black dragon fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Also mesopelagic (Ref. 7300).  Caught from deep water in the Hawaiian area.

species.name: Valdivia dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand (Ref. 109259).

species.name: Valencia robertae
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Valenciennea persica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sand near corals and has been observed in pairs.  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Valenciennea yanoi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms of bays and inlets (Ref. 123074).

species.name: Valenciennellus carlsbergi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Valparaiso chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs; no information of depth range available (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Van Heurn's rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanacampus poecilolaemus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Reported from estuaries and shallow weedy bays.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 17 cm SL.

species.name: Vandellia beccarii
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vandellia sanguinea
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vandepoll's molly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanderbilt's cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species which inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Vanderbilt's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in small to large aggregations in exposed outer reef slopes and rocky inshore reefs (Ref. 3921).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Diet consists of zooplankton, especially copepods (Ref. 3921).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Vanderhorstia auropunctata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanderhorstia bella
species.description: Poisson. Collected above fine, silty, sand with small coral patch (Ref. 56674).

species.name: Vanderhorstia cyanolineata
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanderhorstia fulvopelvis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanderhorstia hiramatsui
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanderhorstia kizakura
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy gentle slope below coral-reef drop-off (45 m or more depths), and found to be associated with the alpheid shrimps (Ref. 75057).

species.name: Vanderhorstia opercularis
species.description: Associated with alpheid shrimps, sharing the same burrow maintained by the shrimp (generally as a pair) and guarded by the goby (Ref. 59177).

species.name: Vanderhorstia rapa
species.description: Occurs in coarse sandy bottom around rubble area, and found to be symbiotically associated with the alpheid shrimps (Ref. 75057).

species.name: Vanderloos angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Of all coral reef fishes. this species has one of the most restricted ranges. Occurs in scattered soft and hard corals of rocky bottoms, in vicinity of sunken debris or wharves, in areas of cool upwelling, 22-24 degrees Celsius (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Vandoise rostrée
species.description: Inhabits streams and rivers, sectors with current, clear and cool, in deep pools.  Adults undergo small migrations.  Spawns at night in stretches with swift current and pebble bottom, in deeper pools (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Vanishing silhouette goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vanmanenia crassicauda
species.description: Occurs in rapids, torrents and waterfalls (Ref. 36949).

species.name: Vanmanenia microcephala
species.description: Inhabits rapids, torrents, and waterfalls. Feeds mainly on algae attached to rocks and on organic residues and small aquatic insects (Ref. 120400).

species.name: Vanmanenia pingchowensis
species.description: Adults occur in babbling bottom of mountain streams (Ref. 26563). Utilized for food (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Vanmanenia serrilineata
species.description: Collected in swift creeks under forest cover (Ref. 36949).  Also recorded from a stream with clear water ((16 °C; pH 8.1; 250 μs/cm; measured on 1 January 2011 at 11:00 am) that flowed over boulders and rocks with moderate to fast current. Found syntopic with nemacheilids <i>Schistura macrocephalus and <i>Pteronemacheilus meridionalis, the snakehead <i>Channa gachua, and cyprinids such as <i>Barilius pulchellus, <i>Devario chrysotaeniatus, <i>Poropuntius huangchuchieni, and  <i>Scaphiodonichthys acanthopterus (Ref. 95066).

species.name: Vanuatu goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vardar spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in still waters of lakes, oxbows and backwaters on mud to silt bottom, rarely in flowing water (Ref. 59043). Also occur in marshlands, lowland rivers with little current, springs and associated wetlands (Ref. 26100). A short-lived species. Oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Can be diagnosed from Cobitis elongatoides and Cobitis pontica only by chromosome characters. They cannot be distinguished in the field, except by origin (Ref. 59043). Is threatened due to water abstraction and pollution (Ref. 26100). Current assessment of threat reduced to least concern (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Varech
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) occurring in seagrass habitats.  Sedentary during the day, hiding in crevices or lying among seaweed, sometimes partly covering itself with sand while lying on its side.  Nocturnal feeders of benthic crustaceans.  Estimated eggs per fish is from 157512 to 223706 (Ref. 29).  Small, colorful group; a sequential hermaphrodite (Ref. 26938).  Has been traded as an aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Varech pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water, cryptically colored, secretive species that inhabits seagrass areas. Also found in rocky reefs in depths of 1-50 m (Ref. 89707). Sedentary during the day, hiding in crevices or lying among seaweed, and rely on their effective camouflage to escape detection.  Sometimes partly covering itself with sand.  Nocturnal predators feeding mainly on benthic crustaceans.

species.name: Varech veiné
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A demersal, rocky reef (Ref. 89707) and shallow-water species, cryptically colored and secretive.  Sedentary during the day, hiding in crevices or lying among seaweed, and rely on their effective camouflage to escape detection (sometimes lying and partly covering itself with sand).  Nocturnal predators feeding mainly on benthic crustaceans.

species.name: Variabilichromis moorii
species.description: Gobbles up pieces of the biocover in search of invertebrates (Ref. 7343).

species.name: Variable cory
species.description: Usually occurs in areas with sandy bottom, bank vegetation entering water or with marginal aquatic plants, dark, clear or slightly turbid water and limited associated fauna (Ref. 52874). Mimicked by Otocinclus mimulus; (Ref. 52874). Mimicry is unusual because the two species occupy different microhabitats and it is hypothesized to operate with a primarily visual predator moving between the microhabitats, tentatively identified as the cichlid Crenicichla lepidota (Ref. 52874).

species.name: Variable dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Variable garra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Variable jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sand/rubble bottoms in 0-37 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Variable lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in small rivers and brooks, mainly in the streaming parts on sedimentary soils; in coastal plain rainforests and secondary forests (Ref. 3788, 57259). Not a seasonal killifish. Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Variable platyfish
species.description: Occurs in warm springs, weedy canals and ditches (Ref. 5723).  Feeds on worms, crustaceans, insects and plant matter (Ref. 7020).  Used for genetic research (Ref. 4537).  Aquarium keeping:  minimum aquarium size 60 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Variable sabretooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in seagrass beds of shallow lagoons. Also in Sargassum rafts during or immediately after wet season (Ref. 48636). Replaced by P. thepassi at Solomon Islands (Ref. 90102). They feed primarily on small crustaceans and occasionally on scales from fishes. Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). This form was named by Bleeker (1852) as Petroscirtes bankanensis.

species.name: Variable snake-blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef areas, most commonly in sponge areas from 5-20 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Variable-toothed snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovary pouch-like, translucent whitish, with unripe ovarian eggs (0.20 mm in maximum diameter) (Ref. 120238).

species.name: Varicus bucca
species.description: Rare in collections that little is known about the distribution and ecology (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Varicus lacerta
species.description: Found at the base of a yellow sponge, Dactylocalyx pumiceus, on a rocky outcropping along the deep-reef slope, at a depth of 129 to 143 meters (Ref. 110434).

species.name: Varied-spine goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sandy or muddy bottoms (Ref. 121834).

species.name: Variegate darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit swift gravel and rubble riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found buried in the substrate (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Variegated cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral reefs and seagrass beds of inner bays and shallow lagoons (Ref. 1602); also in dead reef and rubble (Ref. 48635).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Variegated catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Variegated mogurnda
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near shore in shallow vegetated areas.

species.name: Variegated moray eel
species.description: The holotype was reared from 10 June 2002 until 4 February 2005 in a laboratory aquarium. It accidentally crawled out of the aquarium during the night and died. It was dissected and many mature eggs were found in its abdominal cavity. The mature eggs were between 0.8-1.2 mm in diameter, and batch fecundity was about 20,000 eggs. Under microscope, there was the other immature egg group in its ovaries, the diameters of oocytes were about 0.15-0.26 mm. The paratype was also reared until its death on 22 September 2008. Under the microscope, its gonads belonged to immature ovaries, with 2 groups of oocytes with different egg diameter interval ranges: the larger group was 0.17-0.26 mm, while the smaller group was 0.07-0.13 mm. The two specimens were fed with fish and squid meat (Ref. 127463).

species.name: Variegated ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Zostera beds, in sandy bottom or rocky reefs (Ref. 75992).

species.name: Variegated snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in seagrass areas among Amphibolus species with dropped leaves and other organic litter on sand (Ref. 9002). Secretive and extremely well camouflaged (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Variegated spinefoot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef areas with sand and coral rubble, down to at least 15 m.  Juveniles found in mangroves (Ref. 9710).  Adults occur in schools of 10 to 20 or more and feed on algae growing on compacted pavement areas (Ref. 9813).

species.name: Varna gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs only in the upper and middle stretch of a small, slowly flowing stream.  Attains up to about 10 cm SL (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Vatani rohtee
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast flowing streams and rivers (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Veladykov’s tooth-carp
species.description: Collected from an altitude of approximately 2,380 meters on a small plain between high ranges at the easternmost edge of the Zagros Mountains; from a large pool in the upper reaches of the Karun River basin which drains to the head of the Persian Gulf; shallow water at about 4 cm depth; cloudy water over mud and pebbles; with Myriophyllum (Ref. 38795) and Potamogeton sp. which are the dominant aquatic plants used as spawning substrate (Ref. 54276). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139). Parasites ( Trichodina sp., Gyrodactylus sp., Diplostomum spathaceum, Allocreadium isoporum, Allocreadium pseudaspii, Ornithodiplostomum sp., Contracecum sp., and Acanthocephalorhynchoides cholodkowskyi) were found from a collected sample of Aphanius vladykovi in Gandoman lagoon (Ref. 125593).

species.name: Velioglu's chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in swift and clear flowing water with cobble and pebbles. Collected together with Capoeta umbla (Heckel, 1843); Barbus lacerta Heckel, 1843; Alburnus mossulensis Heckel, 1843, Oxynoemacheilus sp., and Salmo sp. (Ref. 94737).

species.name: Vellitor centropomus
species.description: Found in Sargassum belts.

species.name: Vellitor minutus
species.description: Inhabits Eisenia and Ecklonia belts of the littoral zone.

species.name: Velvet angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults found on current prone, semi-open reef flats with gorgonians and seawhips in depths of at least 35 m (Ref. 48636).  Juveniles in sheltered coastal bays (10-15 m) with small coral outcrops on muddy substrates (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Velvet skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom-dweller that feeds on invertebrates.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Males reaches maturity at ca. 50cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Velvet whalefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles mesopelagic, adults benthopelagic.  Presumably feed on crustaceans.

species.name: Velvet whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Velvetnose brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Adults inhabit rocky crevices (Ref. 11482).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Velvety sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits turbid main river channels and swampy backwaters.

species.name: Venefica ocella
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Venefica procera
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Venezuela round stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Venezuelan blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species found on bottoms with coarse sand or rubble and shells of mollusks.

species.name: Venezuelan dwarf numbfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species on continental shelf. Biology unknown. Size known only from few specimens (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Ventral-barred shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits sand-silt bottoms (Ref. 90102); associated with alpheid shrimps (Ref. 96641).

species.name: Ventre citron
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, ponds and sluggish pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers, usually over silt and near vegetation (Ref. 86798). Probably feeds on insects, crustaceans, and plankton (Ref. 1998). Spawning probably occurs in the spring (Ref. 1998). Commonly hybridizes with Chrosomus eos. The hybrids are always females and in some areas are more common than the parental species. Hybrids breed with males of the parental species and consequently can outnumber and even replace one of the parent species (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Ventre rouge du nord
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes, ponds, bogs, and pools of headwaters and creeks.  Usually occurs over silt, often near vegetation (Ref. 86798).  Feeds mainly on algae, but also on zooplankton and aquatic insects. Preyed upon by fishes, kingfishers and mergansers (Ref. 1998).  Spawning occurs in spring or early summer (Ref. 1998).  Used as bait in parts of Ontario and Quebec (Ref. 1998).

species.name: Ventre-pourri
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs almost anywhere in its range but most common in clear rocky streams (Ref. 3814, 10294); also inhabits large rivers, reservoirs and glacial lakes to the north.  Feeds on algae, detritus, entomostraca, and immature insects, especially midge larvae and pupae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Ventrifossa fusca
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Ventrifossa longibarbata
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Venus tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits outer reef slopes, in sand and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Veracruz tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Veracruz whiff
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Verco's pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among weed and seagrass.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males brood at 10 cm SL.

species.name: Verdoeil barbu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found offshore (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Verduya's hap
species.description: Occurs in the open water, sometimes in large shoals (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Verilus pacificus
species.description: Apparently occurs on rocky slopes of islands and seamounts (Ref. 37257).

species.name: Verilus sordidus
species.description: Inhabits rocky bottoms to depths less than 100 m.

species.name: Verlorenvlei redfin
species.description: Spawning possibly occurs around October-December, based on the general patterns of congeners (Ref. 98574).

species.name: Vermeille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common near the edge of the continental and island shelves; also found in deeper waters (below 200 m); usually ascending to shallow water at night.  They feed mainly on fishes, shrimps, crabs, gastropods, cephalopods, tunicates and some pelagic items including urochordates.  Marketed fresh.  Said to be a good food fish (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Vermiculated blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in the intertidal area, actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184).  They breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Vermiculated goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy bottoms of brackish or nearly fresh waters.

species.name: Vermiculated sailfin catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Typically from floodplain lakes, swamps and borrow pits, in poorly-oxygenated waters and must rely on air breathing for long periods of time. Has a specialized (enlarged) stomach which appear to function as accessory respiratory organs (Ref. 58517).

species.name: Vermilion darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vermilion rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow to deep rocky reefs, less common on deep ones (Ref. 2850).  Young inhabit shallow water (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Sold as fillets together with other rockfish (Ref. 27436). Maximum depth and minimum common depth from Ref. 128668.

species.name: Verrue argentée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Verrue au nez-court
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species found along sandy bays and lagoons; rarely in estuaries (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Verrue brillante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Feed mainly on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Verrue bronzée
species.description: Found in coastal and inshore waters.  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates.  An important foodfish.  Sold fresh and dried salted (swim bladder) in markets.

species.name: Verrue canine
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, bays, and estuaries (Ref. 9118).  Feeds on crustaceans, fishes and cephalopods (Ref. 9118).  Considered a good food fish (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Verrue de roche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits caves and crevices or among corals (Ref. 9710).  Solitary or in groups (Ref. 9710).  Feeds at night mainly on shrimps and small fishes (Ref. 9710), and their larvae (Ref. 13442).  Secretive and wary (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Verrue des Galapagos
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Often occurs in large schools or loose aggregations above rocks, small boulder strewn slopes covered with leafy blade algae (Ref. 5227).  Feeds mainly on zooplankton (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Verrue du Pacifique
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species inhabiting coastal waters (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9118).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Verrue rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs usually over mud and sandy mud bottoms in coastal waters to about 60 m depth, more rarely in estuaries.  Feeds mainly on small shrimps.

species.name: Verrue tigre
species.description: Inhabits inshore and coastal waters (Ref. 3490). Carnivorous feeder. Feeds on Acetes spp., penaeid prawns, deep-sea prawns, fishes, stomatopods, mollusks, isopods, copepods and fish larvae (Ref. 53464).

species.name: Verrue titête
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters, usually found over mud and sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 3702).  Also in estuaries (Ref. 3702).  Important food fish.

species.name: Verrue à stries noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters and lagoons (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 9118).  Common in local markets (Ref. 9118). Depth range assumed (RF).

species.name: Verrue à œil jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water, entering estuaries and river mouths (Ref. 9118).  Forms schools (Ref. 9118).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans and pelagic fishes (Ref. 9118).

species.name: Versluys' jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in silt and sand bottoms in 15-45 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Vertical blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Vertical hover goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from one specimen collected in less than 1.5 m in the coastal waters of Pohnpei (Caroline Is.) (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Vespicula trachinoides
species.description: Apparently occurs over soft sand and broken shell bottoms.  Of little commercial interest and seem to be marketed fresh (Ref. 39597).

species.name: Vibranium fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deep shelves consisting of small patch reefs dominated by rhodolith and sponge beds (Ref. 120658).

species.name: Victoria barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Victoria robber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Victoria confined to shallow coastal areas (Ref. 34290, 104654), in water less than 20 m deep (Ref. 12526, 34290). Omnivore, feeding on aquatic plants, surface insects and small fishes, and sometimes on molluscs (Ref. 4903, 12526, 104654). Known to run up rivers and streams in Lake Victoria during rainy season (Ref. 4903). Apparently rare since introduction of Lates (Ref. 4967).

species.name: Victoria snake catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among stones and shingle over the river bed (Ref. 4903, 104773), and in similar places on wave-washed rocky shores of the lake (Ref. 4903, 104734). Preference for rocky or stony substrates, where they hide among the rocks (Ref. 78218). Feeds mainly on lithophilic insects (Ref. 12526, 104773), plants and Copepoda (Ref. 12526), but shows great adaptability in diet (Ref. 12526). Nothing is known about spawning and reproduction (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Victoria stonebasher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In Lake Kyoga in or near water lily swamps (Ref. 49805). In Lake Victoria in shallow inshore waters over both sandy and rocky bottoms, and seasonally over muddy bottoms adjacent to extensive papyrus swamps (Ref. 9606). Predominantly insectivorous, feeding mainly on chironomid larvae (Ref. 12526), but also feeds on small organisms like Ostracoda, Hydracarina (Ref. 9606, 12526), Conchostraca (Ref. 12526) and Diaptomus (Ref. 9606). Crustaceans, gastropods, fish eggs and detritus are also taken (Ref. 9606). Males grow to larger size than females; breeds twice a year during rainy seasons; migrates up the river to spawn (Ref. 10608). Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Victoria tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults feed predominantly on bottom algae, some of the planktonic organisms that are found in their stomachs are probably those which have settled on the bottom or were washed shorewards from open waters but they do feed directly on plankton (Ref. 2). A maternal mouthbrooder, males make complex courtship structures in the substrate (Ref. 118638). Was a major component of the fisheries catch in Lake Victoria (Ref. 118638). Some pond culture attempted (Ref. 118638). IUCN conservation status is critically endangered (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Victorian scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore in rocky reefs (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Victory whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Probably belongs to the upper abyssal area (Ref. 41160).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Vieille
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in littoral (10-20 m) zone around rocks, offshore reefs, and seaweed.  Young often in intertidal areas.  All are born females and change sex when they are 4-14 years old (Ref. 35388).  One (or more) female spawns in nest of algae, built by male in a crevice.  Feed on crustaceans and mollusks (Ref. 4742).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Vieille balayette
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs and adjacent rubble, sand and seagrass habitats (typically along the edges of coral rich fringing reef slopes, Ref. 9710).  Feed mainly on hard-shelled invertebrates, especially mollusks (Ref. 5374).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Vieille ciseau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear channels and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710). Juveniles are commonly found along drop-offs below 18 m (Ref. 9710). Adults usually found near caves while juveniles frequently live inside them. Adults are solitary and feed on algae and small invertebrates. Juveniles have been observed 'cleaning' other fishes. Because of its dentition, it is regarded as a close relative to the parrotfishes (Scaridae), although it behaves like the species of Anampses.

species.name: Vieille d'Arabie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In the Red Sea, it is often found on patchy open reef areas.  Feeds diurnally on fishes (64%, mostly pomacentrids) and crustaceans (36%).  It is a monogamous species, the pair jointly defends a common territory of up to 62 square m (Ref. 6480). Major threats include overfishing, lack of management and habitat loss (Ref. 089707).

species.name: Vieille femme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Juveniles live in estuaries (Ref. 33616) while adults occur in estuaries and on inshore and offshore rocky reefs and seagrass beds (Ref. 9563).  Found either in large schools, in pairs or as solitary individuals (Ref. 33616).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406). Reported to have venomous fin spines without associated venom gland (https://fishesofaustralia.net.au/home/species/445#moreinfo).

species.name: Vieille rouillée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected or silty reef areas (Ref. 89707). Reported to be very habitat speciific, lives in very rich invertebrate habitat in the shore side of inner reefs and difficult to get shots u/w. Largest seen was about 25 cm, but usually smaller up to about 20 cm (R. Kuiter, pers. Comm. 03/2022). Maximum length given 40 cm TL (for confirmation) May undergo protogyny. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Vieille saignante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms associated with gravel and rocky reefs.  Caught as a by-catch of industrial trawl fishing.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vieille triple queue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and seaward reefs at depths of 1 to over 30 m, and relatively common along shallow reef margins with good coral cover (Ref. 9710).  Usually solitary (Ref. 5213).  Feed mainly on shelled benthic invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans, but occasionally take fishes (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Difficult to approach (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles secretive on algae reefs and usually around stinging hydrozoans (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Vieille à selle noire
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on deep reef slopes rich with invertebrates such as sponges and seawhips, but young adults are occasionally seen much shallower (Ref. 48636).  Usually solitary in coral and rocky reefs.  Feed mainly on benthic, hard-shelled, invertebrates such as mollusks and crustaceans.  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Vieille à tache rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in shallow clear water of reef flats and lagoon and seaward reefs, in areas of mixed sand, rubble and coral (Ref. 9710, 58534).  Usually solitary or in small groups (Ref. 9311).  Feeds mainly on demersal planktonic crustaceans and small benthic invertebrates.  Female length is from Ref. 9137.  Replaced by <i>S. albovittatus </i.> in the Andaman Sea (Ref. 90102).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Vieille étoiles bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow protected coastal reefs, in seagrass beds, and in coral-rich areas (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Feeds on crustaceans and fishes (Ref. 37816). Solitary (Ref 90102). Protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 089707).

species.name: Vieja fenestrata
