species.description: Inhabits lakes, preferring mesotrophic waters with a mud or sand bottom.  Some populations have migrated into the lower river valleys with slow to moderate flowing waters.  Feeds mainly on plant and vegetable matter supplemented by invertebrates and aquatic insects.

species.name: Vielle barbe noire
species.description: Found solitary (Ref. 90102) in lagoon and sheltered seaward reefs in coral rich areas (Ref. 1602, 58652).  Possibly to 120 m depths.  Young is more inshore on sheltered reef crests or slopes, usually amongst soft corals or stinging hydrozoans (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on hard-shelled mollusks, crustaceans, and sea urchins (Ref. 27550).  The species is observed to swim with a group of goatfish and change its color to resemble these fish, it then darts out from the group to catch small fish (Ref. 2334).  This species curiously approaches divers closely (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Vielle chocolat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mainly a coastal species (Ref. 48635).  Inhabits silty dead reefs in protected waters. May also be seen on live coral (Ref. 089707). Secretive (Ref. 37816).  Feeds mainly on fish (Ref. 30531) and crustaceans (Ref. 089707).  Courtship and pair spawning were observed by Donaldson (1989, Ref. 6900).  Diandric protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 45317).

species.name: Vielle de la Mer Rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dead reefs in silty areas as well as  silty lagoons; often found in or near caves as adults, while juveniles are more common in coral rubble areas (Ref. 089707).  It could possibly be an aquarium novelty.  Ripe females at 17 to 19 cm SL and a mature male at 22 cm SL were reported (Ref. 6699).

species.name: Vielle lignes bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Like C. boenak, it prefers shallow dead or silty reefs and this may account for the primarily continental distributions of these two species. Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Vielle taches de rousseur
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow waters, usually on silty reefs, midshelf lagoons and backreef areas; feeds on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 089707).  Secretive in corals to about 20 m depth.  Juveniles are found under corals with rubble substrate (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Vietnames snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Villa Lopez pupfish
species.description: The area of collection is arid, with little vegetation, often succulents, also with thick shrubby growth around; the area is dusty, with poor soils and some cultivated fields nearby. Water is clear, bottom muddy; aquatic vegetation includes Chara and Scirpus; banks shrubby or meadowlike (Ref. 26729). Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Villasboas’ tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little information is available about the type locality other than that it was a rapids area in the Rio Xingu, Brazil (Ref. 84053).

species.name: Vine-like sand eel
species.description: Two specimens were reported to have been collected as stranded specimens caused by the extremely low temperatures by a serous cold wave coming from the Arctic. In the type locality, several species of Muraenidae, Ophichthidae, Apogonidae, Syganidae, etc., were also collected at the same time (Ref. 127464).

species.name: Vinson's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Violet cuskeel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species (Ref. 34024).  Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Violet damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow protected areas (Ref. 4391).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Violet demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in lagoons, harbors, and coastal reefs, shallow habitats, deep sand or mud slopes with outcrops of debris or coral rubble pieces, or on rocky substrates in sheltered bays. They usually occur in large aggregations, sometimes forming mixed aggregations with Neopomacentrus sp. Abundant around sponge-encrusted mooring buoys and their anchor lines and occur in smaller colonies around rocks and refuse (Ref. 1602). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Violet goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults prefer muddy bays and estuaries; encountered in fresh water (Ref. 13628), with a salinity range of 0.0 to 25.5 ppt (Ref. 97140).  Also found offshore on muddy bottoms, off mouths of large rivers.  Largest goby in the Caribbean, and the only one with this distinctive eel-like shape (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Violet roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Violet squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon in atoll reef flats, lagoon patch reefs, and steep outer reef slopes.  Solitary and secretive species, occasionally seen in small crevices in clear water habitats (Ref. 48635).  Strictly nocturnal, feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps.  Spine of preopercle is venomous. Usually among rich coral growth (Ref 90102).

species.name: Violon franc
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Caught with all types of inshore gear.  Probably sold fresh in markets.

species.name: Violon jarbua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over shallow sandy bottoms, in the vicinity of river mouths. Enter estuaries and rivers (Ref. 1479, 11230, 44894, 48635), juveniles and adults are often found in freshwater (Ref. 4327). Adults in loose aggregations (Ref. 48635). Juveniles common in sandy intertidal areas; often in tidal pools.  Minimum depth reported is 20 m (Ref. 12260). Found in schools (Ref. 9710).  Omnivorous (Ref. 7300), feeding on fishes, insects, algae, and sand-dwelling invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Spawn in the sea and juveniles migrate into fresh water (Ref. 2847).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Produce sound (Ref. 9137).  Caught on all types of inshore fishing gear including gill nets, traps, handlines, and bottom trawls and  marketed fresh and dried-salted  (Ref. 48274).

species.name: Violon tigre
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal waters (Ref. 5213).  Often found in brackish waters (Ref. 4833).  Juveniles with floating weeds, often far offshore (Ref. 48635).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 5284).

species.name: Viper dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected between 330 and 360 m (Ref. 31259).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Virgin chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and undercut banks of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.  Presumed maximum length is about 38 cm TL (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Virgin dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Virgin spinedace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and sand-bottomed flowing pools and runs of fast and usually clear creeks and small rivers (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Virli coro
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental and insular shelves, often occurring in shallow water close inshore.  Prefers estuaries and shallow bays, especially sandy and algal-covered areas and eelgrass flats.  Feeds on small fishes and probably crustaceans and other benthic invertebrates.  Often solitary, though some may cluster in resting areas on bottom.  Ovoviviparous (aplacental), with 10 to 20 young in a litter.  Meat is regarded as of inferior quality.

species.name: Virli dentu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs off sandy beaches, rocky shores and in shallow bays (Ref. 5578).  Feeds on crabs, lobsters, bony fish and small sharks (Ref. 5578).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Forms schools in summer (Ref. 244).  Hardy and keeps well in captivity (Ref. 244).  Commonly caught by rock and surf sports anglers but not eaten much (Ref. 244).  Meat is dried into shark 'biltong' or jerky which commands a relatively high price (Ref. 244).  Attains 160 cm, TL (Ref. 36731).

species.name: Virli léopard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow water from the intertidal to deeper waters, most commonly in enclosed muddy bays; including estuaries and lagoons (S. Wilson, pers. comm.).  Prefer sandy areas, mud flats, and bottoms strewn with rocks near rocky reefs and kelp beds.  Feed mainly on crabs, shrimps, bony fish, fish eggs, clam necks and innkeeper worms among a large variety of food in its diet.  Form mixed schools.  Ovoviviparous (aplacental), with 4 to 29 young in a litter.  Utilized fresh or frozen for human consumption.

species.name: Virli tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf, mostly inshore.  Possibly to 240 cm.  Probably feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 28023).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449), with about 14 young to a litter.  Size of full-term fetuses 30 to 40 cm.  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Virli à clapet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs from the surf line to close offshore (Ref. 5578).  Feeds mainly on crustaceans (including lobsters), also squid (Ref. 244).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).  Caught by rock and surf anglers (Ref. 5578).

species.name: Virli équatorien
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from two specimens.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Visitor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore, benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Vitiaz dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Vivaneau amarante
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore reef areas over hard bottoms.  Generally solitary (Ref. 9313).  Juveniles are sometimes encountered in shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on invertebrates and fishes (Ref. 9313).  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau ambigu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Vivaneau barbe blonde
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal rocky and coral reefs up to at least 40 m depth (Ref. 9313). During the day they form schools of 30 or more individuals, which sometimes remain stationary (Ref. 9313). Juveniles are seen associated with schools of Chromis atrilobata (Ref. 9313). Feed on invertebrates and fish and may also ingest plankton (Ref.9313). Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau bengalais
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults mainly inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 30573).  They sometimes form small aggregations around rocky outcrops and coral heads during daylight hours.  Feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 30573).

species.name: Vivaneau bleu et doré
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in coastal waters, frequently around rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9313).  They occasionally occur in large schools (Ref. 9313).  Also caught with nets and marketed fresh (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau carpe
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit very shallow coastal habitats, often in large schools near freshwater run-offs (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles often intertidal (Ref. 48635); over sand, silt, or coral rubble bottoms, occasionally in mangrove-lined streams and estuaries (Ref. 9821)  They may enter freshwater to feed (Ref. 245);  on small fish and invertebrates (Ref. 5213). This is a small species commonly utilized in subsistence fisheries and also seen in markets. Caught mainly with handlines, traps, and gill nets and are marketed mostly fresh (Ref. 9821).

species.name: Vivaneau charbonnier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal rocky and coral reefs up to at least 60 m depth (Ref. 9313).  Juveniles may be encountered in estuaries with mangroves and mouths of  rivers (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on big invertebrates (such as crabs, prawns and shrimps) and fish (Ref. 9313).  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau cramoisi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit trawling grounds and reefs.  They are present over shoals, rubble, corals, large epibenthos, hard or sandy mud substrates and offshore reefs (Ref. 6390).  Usually in groups (Ref. 90102).  Juveniles from about 2.5 cm length inhabit shallow waters over muddy substrates (Ref. 6390).  Feed on a broad range of prey dominated by fish, and with small amounts of crustaceans, cephalopods and other benthic invertebrates (Ref. 6390).  They forage mostly at night (Ref. 6390).  They are marketed either gilled and gutted,  whole as fillets, as fresh chilled or frozen product (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Vivaneau cubera
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found mainly around ledges over rocky bottoms or around reefs.  Young sometimes inhabit mangrove areas.  Maximum depth from Ref. 126840.  Feed mainly on fishes, shrimps and crabs (Ref. 55) and lobsters using their strong canines (Ref. 123493).  A wary fish, not easily approached underwater (Ref. 13442).

species.name: Vivaneau d'eau douce
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit freshwater streams and brackish, mangrove-lined estuaries.  Juveniles upstream (Ref. 48635).  Not reported from purely marine habitats.

species.name: Vivaneau damier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit both inshore and offshore coral reefs where they occur singly or in schools.  Small juveniles on shallow protected reef flats and are used in the aquarium trade.

species.name: Vivaneau de l'Indonesie
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit deeper reef areas.  They occur solitarily or in small groups.

species.name: Vivaneau de Papua
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit large freshwater streams. Not reliably reported from marine habitats but may occur in estuaries. Larval stages are probably marine. Juveniles of adolescent fish may occur in mangroves and could be mistaken for the mangrove jack L. argentimaculatus that has a similarly banded pattern in such habitats (Ref. 48635). It is a popular sport fish forming the basis of a safari-angling industry.

species.name: Vivaneau de Randall
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky bottoms in relatively deep water (Ref. 55).  Marketed fresh (Ref. 55).

species.name: Vivaneau de Samoa
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit offshore reefs.  Also deep coastal muddy reef slopes with reef outcrops and often on shipwrecks in depth over 20 m.  Seen singly or in small aggregations (Ref. 48635).  Occasionally seen at depths of 10-20 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Vivaneau de Timor
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rubble reefs.  Usually solitary.  Juveniles on muddy coastal slopes on open substrates with small outcrops of reef debris, usually in depth of 15 m or more (Ref. 48635).  Relatively uncommon (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Vivaneau drapeau
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be found in turbid coastal waters (Ref. 90102).  Adults inhabit coral reefs in both sheltered lagoons and on outer reef slopes.  Often encountered in schools of up to 20 to 30 individuals. (Ref. 55)

species.name: Vivaneau flamme
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms (Ref. 30573) of the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feed on small fishes, squids and crustaceans (Ref. 30573).  Considered an important food fish in some areas.  Marketed fresh and frozen (Ref. 9987).  Highly valued for the quality of its flesh (Ref. 11888). Mnimum depth from Ref. 089972.

species.name: Vivaneau fourche
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coralline and rocky bottoms (Ref. 2683).  Feed on small fishes, squids and crustaceans.  Flesh of good quality.

species.name: Vivaneau garance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over hard bottoms in inshore reef areas up to a depth of at least  80 m (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on big invertebrates and fish (Ref. 9313).  They are marketed fresh or frozen because of excellent quality of flesh (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau huachinango
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over hard bottoms in inshore reef areas.  They form schools in surface waters around Cocos Island, Costa Rica (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on invertebrates and fish (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reef areas over hard bottoms until at least 60 m depth (Ref. 9313).  Tolerant to freshwaters (Ref. 36880).  Form aggregations during daylight and shelter as solitary fish in caverns.  Feed on fishes, shrimps, crabs and mollusks.  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau madras
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 55) in coastal areas and outer slopes.

species.name: Vivaneau mexicain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are encountered generally over rocky bottoms in the vicinity of coral reefs, up to at least 40 or 50 m (Ref. 9313).  Juveniles may penetrate rocky littoral pools  (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on fishes and invertebrates of the bottom (Ref. 9313).  Caught with handlines and marketed fresh (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau minuit
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep slopes of lagoon, channel, or seaward reefs (Ref. 9710), commonly on deep reef slopes and may be in small groups (Ref. 9710, 48635). Juveniles occur singly on protected reef slopes with feather stars, in staghorn corals or large sponges. Occasionally, they aggregate with M. niger. Apparently feed primarily on large zooplankton at night (Ref. 37816); but also feed largely on fishes and crustaceans. Caught with handlines, gill nets, and traps, also speared by divers. Usually seen in markets and sold mainly fresh (Ref. 9821). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Vivaneau nain
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Apparently restricted to freshwater streams and brackish waters, although adults are unknown  (Ref. 55).  Also found in mangrove lined inlets (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Vivaneau noir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mainly rocky bottoms.  Young sometimes found near the surface.  Feed on fishes and benthic organisms, including cephalopods and tunicates.  Flesh of good quality; marketed fresh and frozen.

species.name: Vivaneau queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms.  They feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Vivaneau radis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This is an inshore, reef-dwelling species found over hard bottoms until at least 50 m depth (Ref. 9313).  Adults may form schools consisting of several hundreds of individuals (Ref. 9313).  Juveniles are encountered in shallow waters, including littoral pools and estuaries (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on fish and invertebrates (Ref. 9313).  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vivaneau rose
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over hard bottoms in inshore reef areas.  Generally solitary or in small groups but may occasionally form big schools (Ref. 9313).  Juveniles inhabit estuaries and mouths of rivers (Ref. 9313).  Carnivorous, feed on invertebrates and fish (Ref. 9313).  Marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9313).

species.name: Vivaneau rouge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky areas.  They feed mainly on fishes, shrimps, crabs, cephalopods and planktonic items.

species.name: Vivaneau soleil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs, presumably in shallow water (less than 30 m).

species.name: Vivaneau strié
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit clear coastal coral reefs.  They occur singly or in small groups.  Marketed mostly fresh.  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Vivaneau têtu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs to depths of at least 100 m (Ref. 30573).  Off South Africa they display a preference for slightly silty, turbid regions in the vicinity of sometimes shallow, offshore banks.  Captured mainly at night on coral banks off Mafia Island (Tanzania) in 9 to 12 m and off Zanzibar in about 75 m.  They are active at night feeding over sandy or rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 9773.

species.name: Vivaneau verrue
species.description: Adults are found over rocky bottoms of the continental shelf.  Probably feed on fishes and large invertebrates.

species.name: Vivaneau voilier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over sand bottoms in the vicinity of coral reefs.  Usually seen singly.  They feed on fishes and sand-dwelling crustaceans and mollusks.  Mature individuals aggregate to spawn along seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  They are occasionally seen in markets.

species.name: Vivaneau à queue en croissant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs.  Also found in current or surge zones (Ref. 48635).  Usually seen singly or in small groups.

species.name: Vivaneau à raies bleues
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs where they occur usually solitarily or in small groups of about 5 to 10 individuals.  They feed on fish and crustaceans (Ref. 5213).

species.name: Vivaneau à raies jaunes
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).  Adults inhabit offshore reefs and muddy habitats.  Juveniles are sometimes found in the vicinity of coral reefs, often located close to the shore where silting is moderate and visibility is reduced.  Adults usually very deep (Ref. 48635).  They feed on fishes and a variety of benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Vivaneau écarlate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky bottoms.  Feed mainly on fishes.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vivaneau étoilé
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in the vicinity of coral and rocky reefs.  Usually found solitarily or in small groups.  Sold in Hong Kong live fish markets (Ref. 27253).

species.name: Vivanette bleu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky bottoms often in schools.  They feed on plankton (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Usually marketed fresh.

species.name: Vivanette cacao
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on the continental shelf and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Vivanette japonaise
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms at depths exceeding 100 m.  An important foodfish.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vivanette queue jaune
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms, sometimes forming large schools.  They feed largely on zooplankton (Ref. 30573).  Caught mainly with handlines and bottom longlines and marketed fresh or frozen (Ref. 9821).

species.name: Vivanette sellée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found over rocky bottoms.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vivanette vanuatu
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur over rocky bottoms.  Marketed fresh.

species.name: Vive
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow waters over sandy bottoms, often in less than 50 m deep (Ref. 6790).  Lies hidden in the sediment while waiting for its prey.  Feeds on fish, crustaceans and annelids.  Its venom is not deadly but can cause painful wounds (Ref. 5377).

species.name: Vive araignée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit shallow waters to about 100 m depth, burrowing in the bottom.  Feed on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 3697).  Anterolateral glandular grooves and opercular spine with venom gland (Ref. 57406).  Oviparous, eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 4675).

species.name: Vive du Cap Vert
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky, sandy and muddy bottoms in littoral and coastal waters (Ref. 2683, 6790).

species.name: Vive peigne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2683) in littoral and shallow coastal waters (Ref. 6790).

species.name: Vive rayée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft bottoms (Ref. 2683) in littoral and shallow coastal waters (Ref. 6790).

species.name: Vive à tête rayonnée
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand and mud bottoms on the continental shelf from shoreline to a depth of about 150 m (Ref. 6790).  Oviparous (Ref. 4675).  Eggs and larvae are pelagic (Ref. 4675).

species.name: Viviparous halfbeak
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found mainly in marine waters, but enter estuaries and tidal rivers (Ref. 4833) and mangrove areas (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Vogelkop blue-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits well-vegetated rainforest stream.

species.name: Vogelkop river garfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Volcano pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Volcano shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in outer reef slopes, inhabiting burrows made by alpheid prawns in sand and rubble (Ref. 26237). Also found in sand-rubble bottoms adjacent to seaward reefs in 30-45 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Volcano triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found among exposed boulders of rocky coasts in two volcanic islets in Banda Sea (Ref. 8927, 90102).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Volga dwarf goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This near-pelagic coastal marine species is found in areas with different salinities, including freshwater.  It lives for a year and matures at 18-20 mm SL.  Spawns after first winter, May-June, down to 2-7 m, with females probably laying 2-3 portions of eggs (0.4-1.0 mm), separately attached inside a mollusc shell; and adults dying soon after spawning.  Feeds on small crustaceans (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Volga pikeperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large, turbid rivers and lakes, and brackish coastal lakes and estuaries.  Most active at dusk and dawn.  Feeds on small fish and invertebrates.  Larvae and juveniles are pelagic and feed on zooplankton. Attains first sexual maturity at 3-4 years of age and 20-30 cm SL. Spawns in April-May.  May undertake short spawning migrations (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Volga shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in a wide variety of marine habitats; migrate to delta and lower reaches of large rivers and spawns in main channel. Feeds on a wide variety of zooplankton (e.g. crustaceans) and small fish. Enters rivers with ripe gonads. Eggs are pelagic (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Volga undermouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lowland and piedmont rivers with moderate to strong current and in reservoirs.  Commonly found in river main courses in rapids, sandy shallows and river curves.  Larvae and juveniles with superior mouth prey on small invertebrates. After 3-4 months, juveniles measuring about 3-3.5 cm SL change to adult feeding mode and graze benthic diatoms and detritus from hard substrate in habitats with strong currents.  Breeds on gravel or rock bottom in shallow riffles of larger rivers  or in smaller tributaries with moderate to strong current.  Most of the year in the middle and upper stretches of rivers, moves to lower stretches or to larger tributaries during winter.  Deposits sticky eggs which adhere to gravel.  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Volodichthys herwigi
species.description: Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Vomeridens infuscipinnis
species.description: Biology unknown.

species.name: Voodoo whiff
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May swim upstream to an elevation of 60 m and a straight line distance of some 20 km from the coast.  Found in rivers and creeks.  Feed on crustaceans.

species.name: Vulture sand eel
species.description: A burrowing species of inshore waters, in soft bottom areas (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Sandy bottoms in 2-18 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Waccamaw darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, sandy areas of lake (Ref. 5723).  Eggs are found clustered on underside of stone and guarded by males (Ref. 7043).

species.name: Waccamaw killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur over sand in  lakes, near and away from shoreline.  Often found near vegetation.  Swim a few inches below surface (Ref. 5723).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Waccamaw silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually occur in large schools near surface in open water, over dark sandy bottom (Ref. 35360).  Well adapted to a life of heavy predation (Ref. 35360).  Frequent skipping over the water surface is observed apparently in avoidance of predators (Ref. 35360).

species.name: Wahrindi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum TL was recorded at 47.0 cm (Ref. 57223).  Omnivore, feeds on insect larvae (Ref. 13868) (especially chironomids, Ref. 28714), nymphs, eggs and detritus (Ref. 13868).  Also feeds on molluscs (predominantly, Ref. 4903), fish, bivalves in the Sudd and snails in Gezira irrigation canals (Ref. 28714).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Breeding occurs during the flood season (Ref. 28714).  Utilized for human consumption.

species.name: Waigeo rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams.

species.name: Waigieu sea perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Waistcoat lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. High-oceanic species found between 1-800 m during the day and between 90-600 m at night  (large specimens between 200 and 400 m) (Ref. 4479).  Size stratification with depth at night (Ref. 4775).  Epipelagic to mesopelagic (Ref. 31442).  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and neustonic larvae (Ref. 31442).

species.name: Waite's lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on bottom-dwelling animals.

species.name: Waite's splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually in groups on outer reef slopes (Ref. 27115).  Most commonly occurs in shallow water and most likely seen by divers (Ref. 37816). Forms dense aggregations that feed on zooplankton (Ref 90102).

species.name: Walea pygmy seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in association with the soft coral Nephtea, but has also been observed swimming lengthy distances from one coral to the next (Ref 90102).

species.name: Walindi fairy-warsse
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Walking catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rain forest streams and lowland rivers.  Feeds at night on fish, worms, frogs, tadpoles and crustaceans.

species.name: Walking goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An intertidal species (Ref. 31184) found on sand and mud flats along bay shores.  Also in estuarine areas, swamps, marshy areas and on tidal mud flats (Ref. 5258).  Also found in the freshwater tidal zone (Ref. 12693).  Actively shuttling back and forth between rock pools and air (Ref. 31184). Feeds on algae and harpacticoids, chromodorids and nematodes (Ref. 92840). Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Walking snakehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Are broadly adapted species occurring in rivers, lakes, ponds, mountain streams and even brackish water (Ref. 12693).  Usually hide under the cover of marginal roots and bogwood.  Found in quiet, shaded, clear, flowing water with a silt or gravel substrate (Ref. 6028).  Can tolerate very stagnant, poorly oxygenated and turbid water.  They also tolerate very foul water (Ref. 1479).  Feed largely on insects and crustaceans.  A small percentage of fish is also included in the diet.  Spawn in shallow water with a silt or gravel substrate.  Can tolerate a temperature of 36.5°C.

species.name: Wallaceochromis humilis
species.description: Pair bonding cave spawner (Ref. 52307). Maximum SL was recorded at 9.5 cm (Ref. 7378).

species.name: Wallaceochromis rubrolabiatus
species.description: No information on breeding behavior in the wild; in aquaria it is pair-bonding and cave-breeding (Ref. 52307, 53266).

species.name: Wallaceochromis signatus
species.description: No information on breeding behavior in the wild; in aquaria it is pair-bonding and cave-breeding (Ref. 52307, 53266).

species.name: Wallago
species.description: Found in large rivers, lakes and tanks.  A large, voracious and predatory catfish which thrives in heels with grassy margin (Ref. 6028); mostly hides under holes in river banks and canals (Ref. 44149).  Associated with deep, still or slow-flowing water with a mud or silt substrate (Ref. 6028).  Sluggish and stays on muddy or silty bottom in search of food.  Juveniles feed mainly on insects; adults feed on smaller fish, crustaceans, and mollusks.  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).  Abundant during the warm season; a pre-monsoon summer breeder.  In the Mekong, it is reported to migrate to smaller streams, canals and to the floodplain during the flood season (Ref. 37770).  When the water level in the Mekong drops and the flood recedes, it moves to the Mekong or larger tributaries, where it stays in deep pools until the next inundation period (Ref. 37770).  Destructive to other more valuable food-fishes.  Bites strongly if handled, with its huge mouth, formidable jaws, and band of conical teeth.  Threatened due to over harvesting (Ref. 58490).

species.name: Wallago hexanema
species.description: Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Wallago leerii
species.description: Adults inhabit large streams and rivers (Ref. 12455).  Fry occur at the mouth of small streams connected to larger rivers, where the bottom is muddy and with overhanging vegetation (Ref. 56749).  Feeds on prawns (Ref. 56749).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205). Fishermen along Kapuas in Indonesia observed that it used to form large migratory schools in Kapuas mainstream but such schools had become less noticeable, and this was attributed to intensive gill netting.  Usually consumed fresh or processed as salted fish (Ref. 56749).  Reaches more than 150 cm TL (Ref. 7050).

species.name: Wallago maculatus
species.description: Adults inhabit rivers as well as small forest tributaries. Also Ref. 84801.

species.name: Wallago micropogon
species.description: Adults feed strictly on fishes.  Enters the flooded forest during high water and stays near the edge of the forest during low water (Ref. 9497). Migrates into smaller streams to spawn (Ref. 37770).  Oviparous, distinct pairing possibly like other members of the same family (Ref. 205).

species.name: Walleye surfperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live in surf on sand beaches and over sand near rocks, often around piers.  Often occur in dense schools.  Feed on small crustaceans.  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).  Usually bear 5-12 young.  An important game species.

species.name: Walton's flasherwrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The area of collection (type locality) has a flat, low profile bottom at the base of a gentle (approximately 30°) slope at 34 m depth; substrate consisted of a dense mixture of spindly, branched Seriatopora hystrix coral (Pocilloporidae) and Halimeda alga. Numerous groups of this species were observed, each containing about 1-3 males and up to about 20 females. Courtship activities were common with males continuously 'flashing' a short distance above the bottom (Ref. 75887).

species.name: Walton's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on mud flats.  Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184). Feeds on variety of ocypodid crabs (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Wami tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 118638); oviparous (Ref. 205). A large, fast-growing species heavily exploited in its native range (Ref. 118638). It was globally cultured in the past, making use of its salt tolerance and ability to produce all-male strains through hybridisation with Oreochromis niloticus and O. mossambicus (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Wandering seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults and juveniles found in estuaries and in freshwater (Ref. 58304).

species.name: Wangunu’s pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species appears to be a rare species, with seven specimens collected mostly between 10-16 m. Found living under large pieces of dead foliose coral rubble on a sandy bottom subject to moderate currents and wave action. It is apparently a solitary species, only a single specimen collected from each piece of rubble examined (Ref. 119765).

species.name: Wanieso lizardfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy bottoms in shallow water.  Mainly made into fish cakes and fish balls.

species.name: Ward's damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitarily or in small groups in lagoons and outer reef slopes.  Feed mainly on benthic algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Ward's sleeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas of shallow lagoon reefs.  Inhabits coastal bays and inner reefs, usually on deep silty slopes from about 15 meters down (Ref. 48637). Occurs in pairs (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Ward's tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the continental shelf (Ref. 7300). A benthic carnivore feeding on fish (Apogonops anomalous), mollusks, crustaceans (crabs, amphipods, and stomatopods), and polychaetes (Ref. 8991).

species.name: Warming's lantern fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic species found between 700 and 1,500 m during the day; between 20 and 200 m at night (Ref. 4775) with maximum abundance between 50 and 100 m (Ref. 47377).  Size stratification with depth both day and night (Ref. 4775).  Small juveniles (1.5-1.9 cm) are apparently non-migratory.  Known to feed on zooplankton but appears to be adapted for occasional herbivory (Ref. 28809).

species.name: Warmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found over mud in vegetated lakes, ponds, swamps and quiet water areas of streams.

species.name: Warner sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in lakes, pools and runs of streams and large irrigation canals.

species.name: Warpaint shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits gravel and rubble riffles and adjacent pools of clear, fast creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Common in cool, clear streams with rocky substrates.  Feed on mayfly nymphs and other aquatic immatures, with some terrestrial insects during spring, while summer food consists mostly of insects taken at the surface, with aquatic immatures (Ref. 10294).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably nest spawners like congeners.

species.name: Warrior catfish
species.description: Inhabits coastal and lower mangrove areas, estuaries into main rivers and lagoons (Ref. 40908, 75154).

species.name: Warrior darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Warrior shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: Warteye stargazer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in sand around rocks and patch reefs (Ref. 5521).  Burrows in soft sandy bottom, where it waits for prey, with only the eyes, nose and mouth protruding.

species.name: Warthead blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty barnacles and mollusk tubes on rocky reefs.

species.name: Warthead goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among the branches of live Pocillopora, in lagoons to a depth of at least 7 m (Ref. 1602). Also found among branches of Seriatopora corals in 3-15 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Warthead sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Warty dory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope (Ref. 9563), forming large shoals over rough ground near pinnacles and canyons (Ref. 6390).  Juveniles are pelagic and inhabit oceanic waters in depths of less than 1000 m (Ref. 27230).  They tend to be dispersed over smooth grounds (Ref. 6390).  Feeds on shrimps, cephalopods, and fishes (Ref. 6548).  The eggs float near the sea surface and the larvae also inhabit surface waters (Ref. 6390).  Trawl catch rates for warty oreos, and for oreos in general, show no evidence of vertical migration during day or night (Ref. 27150), even though many of the planktonic species consumed by this species undergo daily migrations within the water column (Ref. 6390).

species.name: Warty frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit sheltered rocky reefs (Ref. 559).  Adults are usually with sponges (Ref. 48635).  Juveniles openly on reefs looking like nudibranchs (Ref. 48635).  Feeds on fishes (Ref. 89972). Oviparous.  Eggs are bound in ribbon-like sheath or mass of gelatinous mucus called 'egg raft' or 'veil' (Ref. 6773). Solitary, frequently among algae, sponges and soft corals (Ref 90102).

species.name: Warty handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154) of the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Warty poacher
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on soft bottoms (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Warty prowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rock reef.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  In shallow coastal waters, occasionally taken by anglers (Ref. 557).  Neither anterolateral glandural groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Waryfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nerito-oceanic, benthopelagic (adults) to mesopelagic (juveniles) over insular slopes (Ref. 6552, 6689).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 6689).

species.name: Wasp goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wasp pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species forms small schools which are sometimes mixed with T. tevegae. The fishes hover in caves, recesses or under the overhangs of coral reefs. When hovering, the ventral side faces the nearest substrate surface (e.g. the wall or roof of a cave) the same as with T. tevegae. However, T. flavatrum tends to be found more towards the back of the caves and recesses (Ref. 58123).

species.name: Wasp roguefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in inshore reefs (Ref. 7300) of the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Wasp-spine velvetfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumed to inhabit interstices on rocky and coral-rubble bottoms, bottoms with coralline algae, or among vegetation (Ref. 12123).

species.name: Wass’ pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 6.95 cm SL.

species.name: Watases lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Pseudoceanic, found over continental shelves and slopes (Ref. 4066).  Mesopelagic species (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Watercress darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in vegetated springs.

species.name: Wattled eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on muddy or sandy bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Feeds on small bivalves and shrimps (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Wavy grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on coastal reefs (Ref. 9563).  A small territorial fish found in protected sandy and muddy areas near reefs and rocky outcrops from the shallows to depths of just over 35 m (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Wavy jaw slopefish
species.description: Depth unknown but specimens were collected as bycatch of hand-lining targeting Priacanthus etelis and Pristipomoides, which are reported to occur at depths between 15 and 400 m. The third author recently obtained a video clip that clearly shows this species in situ was taken off Lembeh Island, near Bitung, North Sulawesi, Indonesia, at 199 m on 12 November 2015, by an ROV as part of an ongoing survey of the Indonesian coelacanth (Ref. 115558).

species.name: Wavy-lined blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit exposed shallow reef flats in the intertidal zone (Ref. 90102).  Also found in surge reef margins (Ref. 1602).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Wavyband sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230)

species.name: Waxy filefish
species.description: Inhabits outer reefs in 15-28 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Wayag shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits sandy slopes in sheltered water at depths ranging between 8-15 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Wayanad leaffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Waziristan snowtrout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Weak lefteye flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on bottom-living animals (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Weakscaled podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A cryptic species found in outer reef slopes (Ref. 116906).

species.name: Web burrfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs with adjacent seagrass and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).  Between 1995 and 2000, at least 10 specimens have been traded as aquarium fish at Ceará, Brazil (Ref. 49392).

species.name: Weber's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur singly or in small to large aggregations in passes and steep outer reef slopes (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Weber's croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters (Ref. 9772).

species.name: Weber's mudskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits brackish mangroves including the margin of estuaries and tidal creeks.  Also penetrates the lower, tidal portions of freshwater streams (Ref. 44894).  Appears to be restricted to tidal fresh waters in areas of mangrove and nipa palms (Ref. 2847).  Amphibious air-breather (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Weberogobius amadi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly extinct.

species.name: Wedge dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wedge-tailed tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat sandy or weedy areas (Ref. 36661).

species.name: Wedged zipper loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wedgehead siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore over soft bottom (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Wedgejaw goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wedgespot damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sheltered inshore coral reefs.  Easily overlooked with similarities to many other species (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Wedgespot shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in flowing pools and runs over sand, gravel and rubble of creeks and small to medium rivers.

species.name: Wedgetail filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Weed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among seagrasses, heavy algal growth, or rubble of shallow sheltered areas (Ref. 1602); sandy substrates (Ref. 76833).  Readily enters brackish and also found in fresh waters (Ref. 27665).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Weed shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs and pools of creeks and small to medium rivers.  Occurs usually in clear water.  Often found near vegetation in the north part of range (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Feeds on filamentous algae and detritus, in addition to the expected small invertebrates (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Weed wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow sheltered rocky areas and reef flats (Ref. 34765), also in seagrass beds and weedy areas, solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Weedsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Weedy cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Enters estuaries and quiet coastal bays, usually on mud or silty substrate with algae-rock outcrops or isolated soft corals (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Weeping dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected on small coral bommie on sandy slope (Ref. 94084).

species.name: Weeping toado
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A shallow water species found in estuaries and coastal waters (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Welander's flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy areas of lagoons and seaward reefs. Usually caught with trawls in deeper water (Ref 90102).

species.name: Welch's grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lentic and lotic freshwater bodies (Ref. 7300).  They inhabit turbid water of gently flowing rivers and waterholes.  Capable of withstanding high temperatures and brackish water conditions (10 ppt. salinity).  Carnivorous, feed on small fishes, crustaceans and worms.  Breed during summer flooding; pelagic eggs are released after an upstream migration and hatch in about 30 hours.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Sexual maturity is reached at a length of about 24-28 centimeters.  One of few good angling species available in the arid interior of the continent (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Weng’s skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental slope off tropical and temperate eastern Australia (Ref. 75647). Adults mainly feed on bony fishes (Ref. 114953). Lengths of adolescent males recorded 108.1-112.2 cm TL, smallest juvenile 25.2 cm TL (Ref. 75647).

species.name: Werner's catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in lakes and rivers. Feeds mainly on insects, consisting of larval and adult aquatic Coleoptera, terrestrial insects, chironomid larvae and larvae of Povilla, culicines and hydroptilids; also feeds on ostracods, gastropods, plants, copepods and Hydracarina; nothing is known about reproduction (Ref. 248).

species.name: Werner's killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, shallow, slow-flowing, heavily shaded streams and rivulets with a silt or clay substrate.  Feeds on insects and fish fry.  9 cm max TL (Ref. 6028).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Werner's smooth-head
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: West African bichir
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mostly found in little rivers, swamps and flooded zones (Ref. 4910, 41580, 46852). Carnivorous (Ref. 41580).

species.name: West African freshwater goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Amphidromous freshwater species (Ref. 92840). Often found in lower courses of rivers, ranging from freshwaters to brackish habitats (Ref. 57403, 79590), including brackish waters of intermittent streams during dry seasons (Ref. 5299), but may ascend far up rivers (Ref. 57403, 79590). Also found in flooded fields and marginal swamps along courses of streams and rivers (Ref. 5299). Not usually exceeding 139.8 mm SL, larger specimens may be misidentifications of A. bustamantei (Ref. 79590).

species.name: West African hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Presumably benthic on hard substratum in relatively shallow water (Ref. 7510).

species.name: West African lungfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Obligate air-breathing (Ref. 126274). Found in marginal swamps and backwaters of rivers and lakes (Ref. 30488). Carnivorous, food includes molluscs (Ref. 30488), but also frogs, fish and seed (Ref. 13851). In Kenya it feeds mostly on plant material, like roots (Ref. 30558). Strongly associated with life of aquatic plants in terms of breeding and feeding ecologies; nests are made in weedy areas (Ref. 30558). Normally lives on flood plains and secretes, when these dry up during the dry season, a thin slime around itself which dries into a fragile cocoon; normally hibernates from the end of one wet season to the start of the next, buut can live in its cocoon for over a year (Ref. 3023, 30558). For hibernating the fish literally chews its way into the substrate ejecting mud out of its gill openings, reaching a depth of 3-25 cm below the surface depending on the length of the fish; the lungfish wriggles around, thereby hollowing out a bulb-shaped chamber and coming to rest with its nose pointing upward; they breathe air at the mouth of the chamber's tube and then sink back into the expanded part of the chamber (Ref. 36739). As the water disappears the respiratory trips cease; air reaches the fish via the tube to the surface (Ref. 36739). Under aquatic conditions this lungfish can survive more than three and half years of starvation, showing the same behavior - no motion and same body posture - as an aestivating specimen (Ref. 51339).

species.name: West African pygmy herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A riverine species, but also in man-made lakes (Ref. 188). Schooling in open waters and at about 2 to 8 m in Lake Kainji, rising to about 30 cm from the surface at night in Lake Volta (Ref. 188, 3034). It feeds on plankton, especially cladocerans and rotifers (Ref. 188, 120915). It breeds at about 1.8-2.0 cm standard length (Ref. 188).

species.name: West African pygmy skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in deeper slope waters.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: West African rockhopper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky shores of coastal waters (Ref. 5298).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: West African seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length type refers to height (= TL - head length).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: West African sharpnose-puffer
species.description: Occurs in reefs (Ref. 43205).

species.name: West African skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: West Atlantic (silver) deepsea herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: West Australian butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky reefs and sandy-weed flats (Ref. 3132).  Occurs in aggregations (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on algae and zooplankton.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Recently discovered in deep water in cold upwelling areas of Bali (Ref. 9710).  Unknown to American and European aquarists although can easily be maintained in a tank according to Australian aquarists.

species.name: West Australian chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral or rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 52881).

species.name: West Australian dhufish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Westralian jewfish live in shallow inshore waters and depths to over 200 m (Ref. 27560).  They are present over hard, flat sea beds (e.g. limestone shelf) and in reefs, wrecks and underwater caverns and gutters.  Adult fish move into shallower waters in the cooler months between April and June (Ref. 27560, 27561).  Juveniles tend to remain in shallower water than adults and are rarely found in waters more than 100 m deep (Ref. 27560).  Adults feed mainly on fish, also rock lobsters, crabs, squid, octopus and cuttlefish.  Marketed as fresh fish (Ref. 10384).

species.name: West Australian seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on edge of rocky areas, muddy bottom and areas of high sediment load; jetty piles and moorings; often associated with sponges or sea squirts or attached to man-made objects; moves to deeper waters in winter.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  This species manifested evidence of genetically monogamous character in seahorses (Ref. 59213).  Site fidelity is observed during breeding season (Ref. 59213).  Length type refers to height (= TL - head length) (Ref. 30915).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: West Gippsland Galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from a moderately shaded, gently flowing, small and shallow (2.0 m average width and 0.5 m average depth) creek, consisting mainly of pools with smaller areas of shallow riffle (0.05 m average depth). The substrate consisted of boulder, cobble and pebble, with small amounts of gravel, sand and clay. Instream cover was provided mainly by rock with smaller amounts of logs, branches and bank/vegetation overhang, and pools averaged 0.9 m (0.6-1.1 m) in depth. In 2002, reported density was 0.27 fish/m2 and in 2012 0.004-0.01 fish/m2. Collected with the native species Shortfinned Eel, Broadfinned Galaxias, Gippsland Spiny Crayfish, a species of burrowing crayfish (Engaeus sp.) and Common Freshwater Shrimp (Ref. 98815).

species.name: West Indian lanternshark
species.description: Espèce de requins. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: West Irian river sprat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The only clupeid in the world known to inhabit mountainous rivers (Ref. 2847).  Occurs in streams with gravel or stony bottoms and feeds primarily on aquatic insect larvae (Ref. 2847).

species.name: West Jumeau bigeye dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: West Pacific (dwarf) deepsea herring
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 122568..

species.name: West Pacific luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic or near crevices and caves (Ref. 58302).

species.name: West-African Parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky reefs at  2-30 m depths, where it grazes on algae growing over rocky or calcareous substrate (Ref. 88982) and seagrasses (Ref. 7360). Males usually solitary, but females are often seen in pairs or small groups, juveniles in loose aggregations of up to 10 individuals (Ref. 88982).

species.name: Westcoast klipfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in tide pools.

species.name: Western angelshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western archerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western Atlantic grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken as bycatch of deepwater trawl fishery for royal red shrimp of western central Atlantic.

species.name: Western atlantic torpedo
species.description: Life history unknown. Males reaches maturity at 75-85 cm TL, females at 125-135 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Western Australian bigeye dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western Australian black-head triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur at shallow depths, often seen associated with coralline rocks, seagrass or algae (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Western Australian demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is generally associated with rocky substrates with ample crevices and coral formations, utilized for shelter. These are captured from about 1-10 m, with considerable tidal fluctuation (10+ m), especially along the Kimberley coast. Usually in large aggregations, which feed well above the bottom on zooplankton (Ref. 117117)..

species.name: Western Australian Legskate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outer continental shelf and upper slope. Presumably feeds on small fishes and invertebrates. Males reaches maturity at ca. 43 cm TL; smallest neonatal juvenile 13 cm TL (Ref. 114953)

species.name: Western Australian salmon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit continental shelf waters including estuaries, bays and inlets (Ref. 6390). They school in shallow, open coastal waters, and can move over reefs in depths just sufficient to cover their bodies (Ref. 6390). Juveniles are found over soft substrates in shallow and sheltered coastal waters (Ref. 6390). They are often found over seagrass (e.g. Posidonia species) beds and in mangrove-lined (Avicennia species) creeks (Ref. 27967). Larger fish move into exposed, coastal waters, such as around rocky headlands, near reefs and the surf zone (Ref. 6390). Feeds on fishes (Ref. 2156). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 57178.

species.name: Western Australian sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons de genre psychrolutes. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Western Australian slope dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western blacknose dace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit cool streams.  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 54729).  Survives well in aquarium conditions and the pink lateral band of mature males make them attractive for native fish aquaria (Ref. 54726).

species.name: Western Blackspot Waspfish
species.description: Often occurs on flat, relatively open bottoms in 12-65 m, usually observed on turbid inshore coral reefs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Western blue devil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs.  Shy and probably nocturnal species (Ref. 33839).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Western blue groper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).  They inhabit rocky areas and feeds on small crabs, fish, mollusks and starfish (Ref. 2156).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Protogynous (Ref. 94078).

species.name: Western bottlenose mormyrid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers quiet stretches of river channels, deep pools and floodplain lagoons with aquatic vegetation; may form small shoals; feeds mainly on insect larvae, shrimps, small snails and small fish (Ref. 52193). Known to move up tributaries when they come down in spate and may breed in newly inundated areas (Ref. 13337). Spawns during the rainy season; females carry up to 7,000 eggs; caught by subsistence fishermen and anglers (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Western buffalo bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Western butterfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits seagrass beds and reef areas.  Also on near shore rocky bottoms of coastal bays (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Western carp gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Normally lives around littoral vegetation and ca be found in dams, lakes and canals as well as streams (Ref. 2906, 44894).  Inhabits slow-flowing rivers or in still water like billabongs (Ref. 44894).  It congregates in large schools below dams and weirs (Ref. 2906).  Feeds on insects, larvae, microcrustaceans and some plant material.  Spawning occurs from late spring to summer when water temperatures rise above 22°C.  The male guards and fans the eggs until hatching about 2 days later.  Young reach sexual maturity by the end of their first year (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western cleaner-clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found among sponges and ascidians (Ref. 9002).  Cleans other fishes, probably feeding on small parasites (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Western creek chubsucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons d'eau douce. Inhabits silt-, sand- and gravel-bottomed pools of clear headwaters, creeks and small rivers,   usually near submergent vegetation.  Occasionally found in lakes (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Western crested loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western crested pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western deepsea cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A mesobenthic-pelagic species living mainly above the bottom (Ref. 31632).

species.name: Western dwarf galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in swift-flowing, tea-colored streams coursing through karri forests.  Also found in swamps, ponds and roadside ditches.  Usually lives in small flowing streams near submerged vegetation.  Water inhabited is darkly tannin-stained and acidic (pH 3.0-6.0) (Ref. 44894).  Feed on insects and their larvae in water; also on micro-crustaceans.  Spawning has been recorded from July to October, peaking between August and September when water temperatures and day length are on the rise.  Multiple-spawning females deposit several clutches of eggs over a protracted period of a few weeks in flooded vegetation.  Sexual maturity is attained in the first year.  Spent adults usually die a few months after spawning (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western frogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore trawling grounds.

species.name: Western galaxias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky pools at the base of rapids and waterfalls.  Occur around submerged vegetation along the edges of pools or slow-flowing water and sometimes in lakes and ponds (Ref. 6896, 33843).  Water is usually clear and fresh or darkly tannin-stained and slightly acidic.  Tolerate brackish conditions found in many salt-affected rivers of the south-west.  A fast swimming species, forming moderately-sized shoals just above the bottom.  With the onset of winter rains, these fish move into small tributaries and feeder streams of rivers and wetlands to spawn among flooded vegetation.  Sexual maturity is reached the following autumn (Ref. 44894).  Feed mainly on insects and small crustaceans.  Considered as the most abundant freshwater fish species in southwestern Western Australia (Ref. 6896, 33843, 44894).

species.name: Western Ghat glassy perchlet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in streams and lakes (Ref. 10429).  Reported to enter marine waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Western Ghat loach
species.description: Found in turbulent and clear water streams (Ref. 41236, 44151).

species.name: Western Greece goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species which inhabits both flowing and stagnant shallows with abundant vegetation and detrital substrate. Spawns in March and April (Ref. 26100).   Feeds on invertebrates, mainly on amphipods and copepods.  Females may spawn more than once during a season. Up to 600 eggs are spawns by several females in a single nest.  Eggs (2.4 x 0.9 mm) are spawned in a cavity (often inside standing, broken reeds); these are cleaned and  guarded by the males.  The eggs hatch probably in one day, larvae living on the bottom; both male and female dying shortly after spawning (Ref.59043).

species.name: Western gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur close to shore in rocky or dead reef areas where visibility is often reduced due to silting and wave action.  Territorial, they maintain and 'weed' filamentous algae patches growing on dead coral (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western gulper shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western hardyhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear, flowing freshwater streams and upper estuaries with reduced salinities.  Often schools near the surface or around the shoreline vegetation and log debris.  Often seen in shoals near the surface of slow-flowing pools (Ref. 44894).  Feeds mainly on insects and small crustaceans.  Spawns during spring and summer.  Becomes sexually mature during the first year (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western highfin spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western jumping blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in intertidal and subtidal areas on exposed rocks covered with algae (Ref. 13227).

species.name: Western kelpfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Small, secretive species living among weeds.

species.name: Western king wrasse
species.description: Inhabits shallow rocky and coral reefs with sand patches.  Juveniles and females act as cleaners (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Western longnose spurdog
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on or near the bottom of the upper continental slope at 298-850 m; viviparous with yolk-sac dependency; no reproductive and diet data are available, however, it is presumed that the species feeds on small fishes, cephalopods, and crustaceans (Ref. 58048). Trawled mainly in 300-400 m (Ref. 58443).  Marketed for its meat, fins, and liver oil which is of high value (Ref. 58048).

species.name: Western luminous roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Western numbfish
species.description: Usually found over sandy and muddy bottoms (Ref. 93928). Maturity size reaches at ca. 24 cm TL; born at ca. 7-8 cm TL. Biology little known (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Western orange perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep shelf waters (Ref. 33839).

species.name: Western Pacific gizzard shad
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In the Trinity Inlet system, North Queensland the temperature range recorded for this fish was 26.0-29.0 °C (Ref. 4959).  A filter-feeder (Ref. 188).  More data needed.

species.name: Western Pacific roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western Pacific tonguefish
species.description: Occurs on a variety of substrata only within active hydrothermal vent sites (Ref. 78522).

species.name: Western pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy bottom and some rock and coral rubble (Ref. 75973); adults inhabit rock reef (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western pygmy perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit almost any permanent fresh water, including flowing or still water of rivers, creeks, wetlands and lakes.  Usually found around aquatic vegetation along the margins of streams or lakes.  Water is fresh to slightly brackish and clear or tannin-stained (Ref. 44894).  Occur at a temperature range of 11.0-26.0 °C (Ref. 1811).  Benthic feeder, consuming a variety of microcrustaceans, insects and their larvae.  Adults move into small side creeks and flooded streamsides to spawn between July and November.  Peak spawning activity is in September and October.  Reproductive biology and habits are typical of the family.  Maturity is attained at the end of the first year, and maximum life expectancy is about 5 years (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western pygmy tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Habitat is highly variable which includes rivers, creeks, swamps, marshy lagoons, lakes and reservoirs (Ref. 44894). Often forms aggregations at or near the surface of rocky pools or congregates along stream margins where there is vegetative cover or submerged logs and branches (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western red scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on reef areas (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Western roughy
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western round skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on outer continental shelf. Life history unknown. Males reaches maturity at ca. 35 cm TL. Caught rarely and discarded as bycatch (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Western sand darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy runs of medium to large rivers (Ref. 5723) and streams (Ref. 10294).  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 79012).

species.name: Western scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore in rocky reefs and occasionally coral reefs (Ref. 75154).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Western seacarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 75154).  Common in weedy reef areas (Ref. 9816, 86913).

species.name: Western shellear
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western shovelnose ray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near the shore and on the continental shelf from coastal fringe. Common on sandy beaches and seagrass beds (Ref. 006871, Ref. 114953). Mainly feeds on decapod crustaceans and small bony fishes.  Females produces litters up to 16 pups. Maturity size for males at ca. 65 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Juveniles are caught with seines.

species.name: Western shovelnose stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sandy substrates or near seagrass.

species.name: Western silverbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Western smooth boxfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: Western sooty grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit still or flowing water of clear or turbid streams.  Particularly common in deep rocky pools (Ref. 44894).  They occur in lentic and lotic freshwater.  Omnivore (Ref. 7300).  They consume invertebrates (especially prawns) and small fishes.  Adults sometimes develop blubber lips, a condition found in several terapontids.  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).  A good angling and eating species growing to 1.5 kilograms (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western spiny seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sheltered bays.  Color varies from either white, orange or yellow with light patches and sometimes network of fine dark lines; also with narrow lines across snout.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), monogamous (Ref. 36642).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western spotted catshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Western spotted smoothhound
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded litter size litter sizes of 5-17 pups with size at birth likely to be around 28.0 cm TL (Ref. 124465).

species.name: Western starhead topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Western striped cardinalfish
species.description: Nocturnal species; occurs inshore (Ref. 7300), and in rocky regions.

species.name: Western striped grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An omnivore found in inshore areas (Ref. 7300).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western talma
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A generally common species found in vertical rock faces.  Feed on worms and crustaceans.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Western tubenose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits a variety of slow-flowing or still waters from estuarine to small, slow flowing premontane streams; usually in dense vegetation or coarse rocks, and often very abundant in backwaters and lakes, breeds in reservoirs and channels.  Preys on benthic invertebrates. Spawns for the first time at 1-2 years, usually for 1-2 seasons only, in April to August.  Females may spawn more than once during the season and males guard the eggs that are deposited in cavities.  Larvae and juveniles are benthic.  It is invasive in Danube and Rhine where reportedly, the spreading was due to canalization of main river and reservoirs or slow-flowing waters created by hydroelectric plants  (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Western wirrah
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Neither opercular spine nor anterolateral glandular grooves with venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Western wobbegong
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Males mature at about 111 cm TL.  Young born at 22-26 cm TL (mean 24.1 cm TL based on 40 specimens). Caught as by-catch of local gillnet, longline, rock lobster and recreational fisheries (Ref. 58024).

species.name: Western yellowfin seabream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters and enters river mouths and estuaries.  Schooling species; often feeds on tidal flats.  A popular angling species, often caught with hook and line and sometimes taken by trawlers (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Western-Australian flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wetzone butter catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among submerged roots and marginal vegetation in slow-flowing, shaded regions of rivers and streams with a substratum of mud or leaf debris (Ref. 116164).

species.name: Whalefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wheelerigobius maltzani
