species.description: Occurs inshore, on rocks.  Enters brackish and nearly fresh waters (Ref. 4343).

species.name: Whip coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives exclusively on Cirripathes anguina found along current-swept drop-offs or backreefs (Ref. 48637). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Occurs in pairs, occasionally with juvenile or a smaller female, Ref. 48637. Also found on seaward and lagoon reefs in 3-45 m (Ref 90102). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Whip eel
species.description: Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 26340).

species.name: Whip sting-ray
species.description: A coastal species, occasionally entering lagoons, shallow bays and estuaries (Ref. 81259). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Whip-fin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in deep coastal slopes and is known from deep water trawls, but also lives in shallow muddy estuaries. Usually in small groups of juveniles, females and a single large males. Mixes with other species of Cirrhilabrus or with Paracheilinus to feed above substrate on zooplankton. A spectacular species during display and can change from normal to nuptial in seconds, and back again (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Whipbeard plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by bottom longline (Ref. 84672).

species.name: Whipfin sea catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whipsnout sorcerer
species.description: Inhabits the lower continental slope (Ref. 4454).

species.name: Whiptail catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Aquarium keeping:  feeds on plants and roots; in groups of 5 or more individuals; minimum aquarium size 80 cm (Ref. 51539).

species.name: Whiptail conger
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whiptail cusk
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).  Common species (Ref. 34024).  Oviparous, with oval pelagic eggs floating in a gelatinous mass (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whiptail gulper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whiptail ribbonfish
species.description: Oceanic.  Adults are epipelagic to upper mesopelagic (Ref. 36610).  Young live near surface.  Adults probably occur in deeper water.  Oviparous, with planktonic eggs and larvae (Ref. 36610).

species.name: Whiskered prowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).  Max length from Fishes of Australia website: http://fishesofaustralia.net.au/home/species/2173.

species.name: Whiskered snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Smallest female with yolked eggs measured 8.5 cm SL; smallest male with enlarged, swollen testes 9.5 cm SL (Ref. 57077).

species.name: Whiskered viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in holes and crevices of coralline and volcanic rock (Ref. 71230). Cryptic and solitary in shallow water (<12 m) (Ref 90102).

species.name: Whiskereye clingfish
species.description: Collected from a nearly vertical slope (Ref. 42102).

species.name: Whitaker's sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A single specimen collected from a lagoon coral head at Rongerik Atoll, at a depth of 6 m (Ref. 1602).

species.name: White anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is observed in brackish lagoons from the start of spring to the end of summer; leaves the lagoons in autumn to the nearby coastal marine waters (see Ref. 126017:598). It is presumed to spawn in lagoons in the summer (based on the observation of concentrations of small-sized anchovies together with large densities of eggs in the Thau lagoon, southern France, in July and on the presence of sexually mature individuals, 8-9 cm SL, in the Mauguio and Prevost lagoons, southern France, observed as early as May.  In the northern Adriatic Sea, it lives at salinities less than 38 psu and depths less than 50 m (Ref. 76782).

species.name: White catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Sluggish, mud-bottomed pools, open channels, and backwaters of small to large rivers; also in lakes and impoundments. Feeds on wide variety of fishes, insects and crustaceans (Ref. 27549).

species.name: White char
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the upper reaches of basins, may be abundantly caught in creeks with flowing waters, sandy to sandy-muddy bottoms, width 3 to 5 m and depth 0.3 to 2 m.  Feeds by driving their snout into the substrate up to the eyes and drawing out dead snails, decaying leaves, worms or other benthic organisms.  They can also catch their prey in open water (Ref. 35381).

species.name: White damsel
species.description: Adults occur in small patch reefs of shallow lagoons, with algae or seagrass habitats.  The stomach of several specimens examined contained mainly algae and detritus mixed with sand grains (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: White hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among rocks and coralline algae (Ref. 7510). Also seen in rock crevices and on scattered rubble to 25 m depth (Ref. 86997).

species.name: White nose loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on pebbly bottom of slow-flowing shallow streams (Ref. 42956).  Feeds on aquatic insects (Ref. 42956).

species.name: White pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White piranha
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White ribbon eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and shallow lagoons, usually buried in the sand or rubble (Ref. 9710, 48635).  Occasionally seen swimming between its burrows in shallow protected areas (Ref. 48635).  A gonochoristic species (Ref. 32169). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: White River spinedace
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits springs and outflows of upper White River, usually in shallow, cool, clear water over sand and gravel (Ref. 86798).

species.name: White River springfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits warm springs and their effluents (Ref. 86798).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: White Sands pupfish
species.description: Occurs in clear, shallow spring-fed marsh pools and saline creek  (Ref. 5327).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: White seaperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults often occur near piers, docks, in bays and sandy areas, but usually in quiet water and offshore areas near rocks (Ref. 2850).  Viviparous, female carries the developing young (Ref. 205).

species.name: White shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky pools near riffles in clear creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 86798).  Oviparous (Ref. 205), probably nest spawners like congeners.

species.name: White sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Holotype which is probably a juvenile or subadult was caught in plastic bag on dark, silty sand (Ref. 75879).

species.name: White spotted triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from rocky shores (Ref. 84020).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: White warehou
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults demersal on the continental shelf and upper slope (Ref. 9563).  Juveniles known from surface waters, commonly with jelly fishes.

species.name: White water goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits relatively fast-flowing streams in hilly or mountainous terrain between about 200 and 1800 m elevation.

species.name: White's seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in coastal estuaries and embayments (Ref. 125503); in shallow, weedy inshore areas and Zostera seagrass beds; also on sponges. Also under jetties on holdfasts of kelp, and on other man-made structures such as shark nets. Diurnal and site faithful (Ref. 30915). Female max length (Ref. 42735). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205). The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128812.

species.name: White-axil damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-backed shrimpgoby
species.description: Lives in silty sandy substrate with small boulders or large rubble pieces in few meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Associated with snapping shrimp in their burrows.

species.name: White-barred boxfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563).

species.name: White-bellied softnose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 8.5 cm long and 4.3-4.8 cm wide (Ref. 41249, 41253).

species.name: White-blotched river stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Buried in sand during day, hunting for benthic invertebrates during night (Ref. 13614).

species.name: White-blotched skate
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth of about 450 m (Ref. 26282).  Maximum depth based on report for Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands (Ref. 80796). Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 10.19 cm long and 6.28 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: White-caudal chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are commonly observed in areas of cool (18°-24°C) upwelling along the northern and western shores of Nusa Penida at about 25-50 m.  They typically form aggregations, which feed high in the water column on zooplankton when currents are strong (Ref. 82433).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: White-dotted rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit exposed rocky shores (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: White-dotted skate
species.description: Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: White-ear scalyfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: White-edge drombus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment needs verification.

species.name: White-eye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Many inhabit brackish waters, found in rivers of low elevation, up to 15 m above seal level.  Feed on detritus, algae and sometimes on terrestrial insects (Ref. 36880).  35 cm max TL (Ref. 2059).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Has been bred in captivity (Ref. 41756).

species.name: White-eye bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast flowing rivers.  Eastern, brackish populations enter the lower reach of rivers for spawning (Ref. 1441).  Inhabit large lowland rivers and estuaries.  Active at night.  Prey on benthic invertebrates.  Semi-anadromous populations forage in large brackish-water habitats in estuaries around Black Sea.  Spawn in large aggregations in fast-flowing water on gravel bottom or submerged vegetation.  Usually rare and threatened due to water pollution (Ref. 59043).

species.name: White-eye goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits offshore waters (Ref. 7251), over mud or sand-mud bottoms (Ref. 13628); flat areas with fine sediment near coral reefs (Ref. 93147).

species.name: White-fin smooth-hound
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-finned flyingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in near-shore surface waters, never spread to open sea (Ref. 9839).

species.name: White-finned gudgeon
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Adults inhabit bottom of moderately flowing lowland rivers, preferring sand bottom. Are nocturnal benthic species feeding on insect larvae and other larger benthic invertebrates. Locally threatened due to pollution and river engineering (Ref. 59043).

species.name: White-freckled surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear outer reef flats and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Solitary or in small wide-ranging groups (Ref. 9710).  Usually in schools of mixed similar species when grazing algae (Ref. 48637).

species.name: White-jawed cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow mangrove creeks and nearby shallow lagoon reefs and seagrass beds; also taken from isolated pools.  Generally found in depths less than 2 m and where water condition is turbid.

species.name: White-line dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow lagoon and channel reefs at depths usually less than 3 m.

species.name: White-lined comb-tooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among corals (Ref. 9710).  Adults occur mainly along outer reef walls with rich coral and other invertebrate growth at moderate depths to about 25 m.  Usually seen in pairs and often perched on large sponges (Ref. 48636).  A deep-dwelling species of the genus.  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: White-lined coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives among branches of certain Pocillopora and Stylophora coral and Pavona cactus (Ref. 34765); a coral-commensal species (Ref. 72446).

species.name: White-lined coralblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary or in small groups on sponges and corals (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: White-margined flathead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-margined goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal shallow environments to depths of 14 m. Found in habitats with mud or sand mixed with shell and/or rock, also in tidepools (Ref. 92840).  Collected with rotenone around gorgonian covered boulders and barnacle rubble, and from scree fields which slope down to silty mud (Ref. 95098).

species.name: White-nosed dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-patch tuskfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reef areas (Ref. 27550) in shallow inshore to deep water (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Usually marketed fresh (Ref. 27550).

species.name: White-ribbed toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-rimmed stingray
species.description: Inhabits sandy bottoms in estuaries and rivers (Ref. 12693).  Feeds on bottom-dwelling crustaceans and shellfish.  Breeds in fresh water (Ref. 32457).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Wounds caused by the dorsal spines are extremely painful and can be fatal.  Sold fresh for human consumption (Ref. 32457).  Total length maybe greater than 200 cm.

species.name: White-shouldered whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in groups in shallow silty coral reef areas (Ref. 90102).  Feeds on small fishes, crustaceans (shrimps, caprellid amphipods) and polychaete worms.

species.name: White-spine butterfyfsh
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Taken in by bottom trawls, thus indicating a sandy bottom habitat. Also, photos taken of this species were from rocky bottom areas in fairly deep water and were observed occurring in pairs (Ref. 123118).

species.name: White-spot damsel
species.description: Adults are found among coral outcrops and seagrass beds of silty areas of lagoon and coastal reefs (Ref. 9710), usually subtidal to a few meters depth (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: White-spotted blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in shallow lagoon reefs, on algal covered rocks and rubble (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: White-spotted chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit steep slopes and rocky bottoms mainly on offshore reefs (Ref. 7247).  Diurnal species (Ref. 52881). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: White-spotted lantern fish
species.description: High-oceanic, found between 325-750 m during daytime (Ref. 4479).  At night, a two layer system occurs, with adults found at 300-600 m and juveniles at 40-200 m (Ref. 4479).

species.name: White-spotted perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-spotted pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species has been observed by divers at 10-27 m on sandy bottom.  Another population is found around 30 m at the northern part of Amami-oshima Island.  Its behavior of building large geometric circles on sandy bottoms, makes this species unique.  Female length (Ref. 97258).  The circular structure plays an important role in influencing female mate choice, it functions to gather fine sand particles for constructing nests in preparaton for spawning (Ref. 97259).

species.name: White-spotted triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Female members of the Tripterygiidae have eggs that are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: White-spotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  Also in deep coastal to outer reef slopes and drop-offs (Ref. 48636).  Solitary or in pairs in the surge zone, rarely to 30 m (Ref. 9710).  They swim in small groups, each with several females and a single dominant male (Ref. 48636).  Feed on small crustaceans, mollusks and polychaetes.  Bury in sand at night (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: White-starred goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: White-streaked grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, rocky estuaries (Ref. 9002).

species.name: White-striped hogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Deep coastal to outer reef habitats.  First found in about 100 m, specimens have since been found much shallower and ranging as far north as Japan.  A second new species in the genus was recently found in the Maldives (Ref. 48636).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: White-tipped sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whiteback signal blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits empty mollusk tubes on sand-rubble bottoms.  Feeds on zooplankton.

species.name: Whitebait smelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal waters (Ref. 2850).  Abundant in bays (Ref. 2850).  Forms schools (Ref. 2850).  Important food for larger fishes (Ref. 2850).  Spawns in subtidal banks (Ref. 2850).

species.name: Whiteband goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare in collections that little is known about the distribution and ecology (Ref. 92840).

species.name: Whitebanded sharpnose wrasse
species.description: Inhabit caves or crevices of lagoon and seaward reefs and drop-offs (Ref. 37816).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Specimens usually taken at depths of at least 30 m.  Secretive (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Whitebar eelpout
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitebar gregory
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A territorial herbivore.  Adults inhabit reef flats, shallow lagoons, and semi-sheltered reef margins; common among patches of rubble or porous reef rock, surrounded by live coral, particularly in areas of mild surge (Ref. 1602).  Also in high energy zones with mixed corals and short algae.  They occur in small loose aggregations (Ref. 48636). Feeds on filamentous algae (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitebarred catfish
species.description: Poisson.

species.name: Whitebarred pink wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).  Cryptic species, prefers darker areas of the reefs (Ref. 33410).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 89972).  Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Whitebarred prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy to rocky bottoms at depths of 46 to 128 meters (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Whitebarred wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are usually found as solitary individuals over sand or sand-and-rubble substrata adjacent to sheltered coral reefs. The large males are usually seen swimming along the reef margin while the juveniles are more secretive and may be found at entrance of small caves or crevices, resembling and often confused with Wetmorella bifasciata. Sometimes this species accompanies goatfishes or even divers who may expose fossorial animals by their flippers. Feeds on benthic invertebrates (Ref. 117607).

species.name: Whitebelly sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitebelly snapper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whiteblotch snake blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef, weedy and sandy areas (Ref. 33839).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Whiteblotched klipfish
species.description: Inhabits sandy areas near rocks.

species.name: Whiteblotched scorpionfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy or muddy bottoms.  Taken occasionally by trawl.

species.name: Whitebonnet anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoons and outer reef slopes. Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). This species may be a hybrid between A. chrysopterus and A. sandaracinos. A. thiellei may be a similar hybrid (Ref. 90102). Associated with the anemones: Heteractis crispa, Heteractis magnifica, and Stichodactyla mertensii (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420).

species.name: Whitebrow skate
species.description: Juveniles feed mainly on amphipods, adults feed on crabs and fish (Ref. 27640).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 7.6 cm long and 5.5 cm wide (Ref. 41249).

species.name: Whitecap goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found only on sandy areas, and symbiotically associates with a snapping shrimp, probably Alpheus djiboutensis where it swims freely at ca. 10-15 cm above the nest hole as it moves its pectoral fins alternately. It was also reported that, in the northern Red Sea, it is associated with an unidentified Alpheus species which is not A. djiboutensis (Ref. 90832).

species.name: Whitecheek blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitechin surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth of capture of the specimens is unknown (Ref. 114728).

species.name: Whitedappled skate
species.description: Occurs in deeper shelf and upper slope waters.  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whiteface moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs among rubble deposits on the lee side of shallow wave-washed reefs.  Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 9710, 58302; 89972).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Whiteface waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits silty coastal reefs (Ref. 9710); also in sheltered sand habitats in coastal bays and deep offshore.  Uncommon and mainly known from prawn trawling grounds.  Nocturnal, coming out on dusk, usually buries itself in the sand during the day (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Whitefin chimarea
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Caught over the upper continental slope (Ref. 76966).

species.name: Whitefin damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore and offshore coral reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitefin plunderfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known only from the holotype.

species.name: Whitefin pupfish
species.description: Occur at relatively high elevations (1800-2300 m).

species.name: Whitefin shiner
species.description: Occurs in sand and gravel runs and riffles, usually in small to medium rivers, less often in creeks (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Whitefin surgeonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found off steep outer-reef escarpments.  May be solitary but most commonly seen in small aggregations feeding on zooplankton well off the bottom.

species.name: Whitefin swellshark
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whiteflag dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitegill dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitehead's sawtooth pellonuline
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is a riverine species (Ref. 188).

species.name: Whitehead's Thryssa
species.description: Pelagic (Ref. 68964). Presumably schooling.  More data needed.  Apparently common but seldom seen in the market at Kuwait.

species.name: Whiteline cardinalfish
species.description: Common in shallow waters along mangrove shores to 6-7 m. Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Whiteline dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from deep crevices on steep outer-reef slopes or walls exposed to current and clear oceanic waters; 4 of the 5 specimens were collected from depths of 50 m or greater. It is probably more widespread in the region in similar habitats (Ref. 123827).

species.name: Whiteline topminnow
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Formerly found in Big Spring, which was impounded, lined with concrete, and stocked with common carp and goldfish (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Whitelined coral goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Live among live coral branches (e.g. Pocillopora and Stylophora) (Ref. 1602). Also found in inshore channels in Acropora thickets (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Whitelined toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitelipped eel catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In tropical areas, inhabits clear and turbid coral reefs; usually found in areas with mixed sand, weed, and coral areas (Ref. 31103).  May be seen resting on sand bottoms under ledges or around coral bommies (Ref. 31103).  Adults solitarily or in small groups.  Presumably nocturnal (Ref. 31103).  Feeds on gastropod mollusks and crustaceans (Ref. 31103).  Spines associated with anterior fins have potent venom (Ref. 9801).

species.name: Whitemargin moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal reef sand slopes.  Secretive in reefs during the day.  Moves out over sand at night to hunt (Ref. 48635).  Benthic (Ref. 58302). Apparently has venomous bite (Ref 90102).

species.name: Whitemargin smoothhound
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Information for Mustelus hacat include mode of reproduction is placental viviparity, having a brood size of 3 to 23 (mean 16); embryo measures 25-34 cm TL (mean 29 cm); young born probably between 30-35 cm TL; females mature between 94-98 cm and males between 90-99 cm TL. Caught by trawlers (Ref. 30948).

species.name: Whitemouth shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy and rocky pools and runs of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Whitemouth skate
species.description: Holotype taken from a depth of 1,000 m (Ref. 26282).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Depth range assumed from two records (1000 and 2000 m) (RF).

species.name: Whitenose pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the continental shelf (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Whitenose pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Coastal species (Ref. 26938), found in seagrass beds.  A cryptic species.  Avoids areas with lowered salinity (Ref. 26938).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitenose snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in mixed rubble and sand and small coral formations. Encoundtered in the open, swimming slowly, apparently in search for prey, probably small fishes or crustaceans (Ref. 89079, 90102).

species.name: Whitenose whipray
species.description: Demersal on soft substrates to a depth of at least 30 m (Ref.58048). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Common catch component of the demersal tangle net and bottom trawl fisheries. Utilized for its meat, skin (high value) and cartilage (Ref.58048).

species.name: Whitepatched splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. An experimental fish.

species.name: Whitepen dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 559, 75154).

species.name: Whitesaddle blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Whitesaddle stargazer
species.description: Found on sandy bottoms near reefs (Ref. 37955).  Feeds on small fishes and invertebrates (Ref. 11482).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Whitesnout anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit the lagoon and rocky reefs (Ref. 7247). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemone Entacmaea quadricolor (Ref. 5911).

species.name: Whitespeckled rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A semi-pelagic species inhabiting deep waters over rocky reefs (Ref. 31047).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Whitespot cusk-eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitespot damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore areas, among rocky outcrops and debris on sand (Ref. 9710).  They occur singly  or in small groups.  Feed primarily on algae.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitespot moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in holes and crevices, sometimes among weed.  Possibly a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32169).

species.name: Whitespot sandsmelt
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A coastal species (Ref. 42740) found in trawling grounds.

species.name: Whitespot soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats, lagoons, and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710).  Commonly found on exposed outer-reef areas; often at low islands and atolls than high islands (Ref. 12419). Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Whitespot triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found at depths of 5 m and shallower, in surge channels and exposed boulders (Ref. 90102). Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Whitespotted anglerfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic (Ref. 75154) and temperate species (Ref. 7300) found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Whitespotted char
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The land-locked form prefers low temperature streams, below 15°C.  Young of the sea-run form enter the sea at 2 years of age and return to the rivers for spawning when they are 4 years or older.  Found in summertime water temperature of 13-15° C (Ref. 12218).  Carnivore, feeding on insects and plankton (Ref. 12218).  Utilized fresh, smoked and frozen; can be broiled, microwaved and baked (Ref. 9988).  Two forms:  the land-locked form which reaches 35 cm, and the ocean form of 70 cm (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Whitespotted dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms in coastal areas.

species.name: Whitespotted frillgoby
species.description: Inhabits clear coastal reef flats, intertidal to about 5 meters depth (Ref. 48637).  Benthic in tidepools and tidal flats; also from seaward reefs (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Whitespotted greenling
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ranges from the intertidal zone to 175 m depth, possibly to 475 m (Ref. 6793).  Found near rocks, pilings and eelgrass beds (Ref. 2850).  Feed on worms, crustaceans, and small fishes (Ref. 6885).  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 37773).

species.name: Whitespotted longfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs.  they hide in holes during the day (Ref. 9710).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitespotted pygmy filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among bottom cover (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Females attach adhesive eggs to seaweed with the mouth and guard them until embryos hatch (Ref. 40060).

species.name: Whitespotted skate
species.description: Occur over soft bottoms of the continental shelf and slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).  Mainly feeds on benthic crustaceans, small fishes and octopi (Ref. 114953). Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules measure 7.0 cm long and 3.8 cm wide (Ref. 6778). This species reaches maturity after 5 years. Maturity size of males at ca. 45 cm TL; young hatch at ca. 11 cm TL (Ref. 114953). Utilized as a food fish (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Whitespotted soapfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitestar cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear coral reefs.

species.name: Whitetail chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in aggregations near ledges and deep patch reefs (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Known only from a few specimens.  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this group is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 13550).

species.name: Whitetail damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit sandy areas of lagoons and inshore reefs around rock or coral outcrops.  Feed primarily on algae (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitetail dogfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 6871).  A rare species known only from a few specimens taken by tuna longliners and trawlers (Ref. 6871).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205), with at least 59 young in a litter (Ref. 26346).

species.name: Whitetail jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits flat, current-swept (3+ knots) sand and rubble plain at approximately 25–30 m depth without coral growth but with an occasional low, stunted gorgonian sea fan present. Opistognathus cyanospilotus, previously known from the Andaman Sea and Bali but not from the Andaman Islands, occurs in the same environment as O. albicaudatus and was collected from four separate burrows (Ref. 88069).

species.name: Whitetail reeffish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on a variety of deep-reef habitats, including on rocky reef slopes, coral outcroppings, around sponges, boulders, and caves. Usually found around artificial substrates such as shipwrecks (e.g., the wreck Queen of Nassau in southeast Florida), tires, and derelict ropes and fishing gear. Together with Chromis insolata, these two are most common pomacentrids on lower-mesophotic and rariphotic reefs in the Caribbean. While in Brazil, C. insolata is replaced by its southern mesophotic counterpart, C. jubauna which often schools with C. vanbebberae on coastal reefs (Ref. 123501).

species.name: Whitetail sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and broken shell bottom; also caught in pelagic environment (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Whitetail shiner
species.description: Inhabits rocky runs, less often in pools and riffles, of clear headwaters, creeks, and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 86798).  Feeds on terrestrial insects and drifting aquatic larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Whitetail whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Whitetip rainbowfish
species.description:
Espèce de poissons. The type locality during January 2013 visit had very clear and slow flowing water with depths
ranging from about 1-3 m while during December 2013 visit it had water levels generally higher with stronger current, and reduced visibility due to the onset of monsoonal rains.  The bottom was composed of relatively smooth limestone pavement with few aquatic plants (<i>Cryptocoryne cilliata), littered with leaf and log debris. Repeatedly took refuge among the dead branches of fallen trees when pursued.  Found syntopic with <i>Melanotaenia senckenbergianus,  <i>Craterocephalus cf. randi,  <i>Ambassis interrupta, <i>Glossamia aprion, <i>Awous acritosus, <i>Glossogobius concavifrons, <i>Redigobius bikolanus<i>Stiphodon atratus, <i>Eleotris fusca, and <i>Oxyeleotris mertoni  (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Whitetip weasel shark
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow coastal waters (Ref. 5578).  Viviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: White’s goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitley's box
species.description: Inhabits clear lagoons and seaward reefs (Ref. 9710) as well as the quiet waters of the shore line.  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on algae and invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Whitley's gurnard perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A temperate species found inshore on reefs (Ref. 7300).

species.name: Whitley's sergeant
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Generally live in relatively shallow water along the outer periphery of individual reef complexes.  Feeding aggregations of a hundred or more individuals are often seen swimming high above the substratum.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Whitley's silverside
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits waters close inshore. Often seen to jump out of the water, especially after sunset when they appear as fluorescent streaks. At night they appear to aggregate with Atherinomorus capricornensis around One Tree Island (eastern Australia). Probably eaten by larger commercial species (Ref. 9760).

species.name: Whitley's splitfin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms a feeding aggregations on zooplankton. Often with Pseudanthias bartlettorum, P.dispar and Lepidozygus tapeinosoma (Ref 90102).

species.name: Whitley's toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whitson's grenadier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Remains of natant crustaceans (especially euphausiids), polychaetes, and fish (gonostomatids) have been found in the stomachs of three specimens examined.

species.name: Whitsunday wire eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Whole fin toothcarp
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wichmann's mouth almighty
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wicker work sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on sand bottoms.

species.name: Wide cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wide stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the outer continental shelf and upper slope.

species.name: Wide-band Anemonefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemone Heteractis crispa (Ref. 5911). Has been reared in captivity (Ref. 35420)

species.name: Wide-barred shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and rubble at depths of 10 to 25 m.  Associated with burrowing alpheid prawns (Ref. 26237).  Found in coastal to outer reef sand slopes, usually in depth over 10 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Wide-bodied pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in bays, estuaries and shallow coastal waters.  Occurs among seagrass and algae (Ref. 31838).  Occasionally found in floating seaweed (Ref. 31838).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  Males may be brooding at 6.5-7 cm TL.

species.name: Wide-lipped Natron tilapia
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A maternal mouthbrooder: males defend spawning territories among rocks in shallow water (Ref. 118638). Potential as an aquarium fish (Ref. 118638).

species.name: Wide-mouthed flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms at depths of about 800 m (Ref. 9824).  Rarely caught with bottom trawls (Ref. 9824).

species.name: Widebanded cleaning goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed cleaning other fishes and commonly occurs with Elacatinus digueti (Ref. 87125). From the subtidal to depths of at least 35 m and commonly found below 15 m (Ref. 87125).

species.name: Widehead catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers (Ref 4967).  Feeds on crustaceans, insects, mollusks and fish (Ref. 28714).

species.name: Widemouth blindcat
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in subterranean waters.  Threatened by groundwater pollution (Ref. 10172).

species.name: Widemouth gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Widenose guitarfish
species.description: Found inshore and offshore (Ref. 9909).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Biology little known (Ref. 9909); but males are known to be mature ca. 48 cm TL (Ref. 114953).  Probably utilized where it occurs, but details lacking (Ref. 9909).

species.name: Wilhelm's hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over rocky bottoms (Ref. 41647).

species.name: Wilhelm's squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from irregular rocky substratum (Ref. 27370).

species.name: William's coralbrotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky and coral reefs, in depths down to about 15 m.  A few specimens are known from mangrove habitats.  A 58 mm SL female specimen contains about 50 eggs, diameter 0.3-0.5 mm and 55 embryos, 6-8 mm TL, with 2 long rows of pigment spots along mid-body and dorsal fin base (Ref. 57883).

species.name: William's mbuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits the rocky biotope of the reefs, where the rocks are permanently covered with a layer of sediment.  Feeds mainly from the phytoplankton in the open water.  Territorial males feed from the biocover on the rocks (Ref. 5595).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).

species.name: William's rockskipper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: William's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found on rocky shores exposed to surge (Ref.54980).

species.name: Williams' viviparous brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Based on collection site, this species is probably adapted to non-reef related rocky inshore environments (Ref. 76869). Cryptic and solitary, inhabitant of reef crevices and caves about 0-4 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Williams’s Goatfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Willowy flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9137, 11230).

species.name: Wilpita rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow, slow-flowing, heavily shaded streams (Ref. 6028).

species.name: Wilson's weedfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky kelp and weed reefs from intertidal to 20 m (Ref. 9002).

species.name: Winch's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Windward triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Winged dragonfish
species.description: Mesopelagic species (Ref. 4468, 75154).

species.name: Winged lanternfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic (Ref. 4066), found between 275-1,000 m during the day; between 40-275 m at night with maximum abundance between 50-100 m (Ref. 4479).  Mesopelagic (Ref. 5951).

species.name: Winged pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Winged spookfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Possibly found in depths shallower than 200 m (Ref. 43939).

species.name: Wingfin snaggletooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Meso- and bathypelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Winterbottom's dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with rotenone and quinaldine (Ref. 83982). Inhabits coral reef crevices in 2-30 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Winterbottom’s flapheaded goby
species.description: Only four specimens where collected, three form the Comoros, a  field station described as 'base of vertical wall with numerous caves' at 9-17 m, and one from South Africa collected at a depth of 26-28 m (Ref. 93174)..

species.name: Wirz's goby
species.description: Occurs in mud and sand bottoms at river mouths (Ref. 5218).

species.name: Wisner's lantern fish
species.description: High-oceanic, meso- (Ref. 4479, 75154) and epipelagic (Ref. 58302).  Found between 225-450 m during the day and between 40-225 m at night (Ref. 4479).  Reach sexual maturity at 5 cm (Ref. 47377).

species.name: Wispy waspfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons osseux. Found inshore on and around corals and hard bottoms (Ref. 39597), silty and muddy habitats (Ref. 48635).  Often taken by nets and handlines (Ref. 39597). Also found in rocky bottoms and coral reef crevices in about 7-70 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Witch guitarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species of continental shelf on rocky and sandy bottoms to depths of 150 m.  It is a night feeder, mainly on small fishes and prawns (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).  Maturity size of males at ca. 47 cm TL, females at ca. 45 cm TL. Species born at ca. 18 cm TL.  It is a likely bycatch of gillnet and prawn trawl fisheries (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Wokam rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams that are typically narrow (about 3-5 m average width) limestone channels flowing through rainforest.  Most common in deeper pools up to 1.5-2.0 m depth below the numerous cascades and small waterfalls (Ref. 110723).

species.name: Wolf blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit mangroves (Ref. 90102).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Wolf cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wolf fangbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults hide in seagrasses, seaweeds, or empty mollusk shells.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Mature females lay eggs on the inner surface of dead bivalve shells which are guarded by the male (Ref. 2334). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Wolfsnout goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits large sponges, usually on the underside of floppy or fan types that grow on shallow reef flats and down on slopes that are subject to moderate currents (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Wonder dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy beaches (Ref. 42598).

species.name: Wongat dragonet
species.description: Inhabits sandy or silty bottoms 15-27 m deep (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Wood River sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rubble and gravel riffles of creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Wood's chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit deep offshore trawling grounds (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Wood's siphonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs over soft bottom in coastal embayments and in the lower reaches of estuaries (Ref. 33616). It is found usually in schools near kelp or seagrass beds of Zostera or Posidonia at depths of 1-10 m (Ref. 90035).

species.name: Woods' barbelgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabitant of sand-rubble bottom near dead and live coral reef (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Woods' clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rocky shores.  Feeds on zooplankton, algae, and benthic invertebrates.

species.name: Woodward's moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) which occurs in inshore waters (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Woodwards pomfret
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Forms schools in shallow coastal waters.

species.name: Woolly sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A resident intertidal species with homing behavior (Ref. 32612).  Often among intertidal algae.  May leave tide pools if aquatic conditions become inhospitable (Ref. 31184).  Breathes air when out of water (Ref. 31184).

species.name: Worm pearlfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species which occurs in inshore waters and inhabits coral reefs (Ref. 75154). Uncommon species (Ref. 34024). Holothurian parasite with male-female pairs in each host (Ref. 34024, 75154). Associated with holothurians including Holothuria leucospilota, H.scabra, H.lubrica, and Thelenota ananas (Ref 90102).

species.name: Wormjawed mormyrid
species.description: Its electric organ discharge (EOD) is steroid-sensitive (Ref. 10763; 10764).

species.name: Wounded darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits fast rocky riffles of small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Adult feeds on midge larvae (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Wouter's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on small invertebrates (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Wrasse ass bass
species.description: Inhabits deep walls and reefs; most common below 33 m.  Reclusive, lurks in cracks, crevices and under large overhangs (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Wrasse bass
species.description: Occurs in deep rocky reefs.

species.name: Wrasse blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in holes in coral and rock, but leaves burrow to swim freely in water column. Mimics the bluehead, Thalassoma bifasciatum, in order to get close to small fish and shrimps on which it preys. Also feeds on copepods (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Wray's gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Wrestling halfbeak
species.description: Found in rivers, rivulets, canals, drains, ponds and lakes (Ref. 4833).  Rarely found in the sea (Ref. 45255).  Inhabits medium to large rivers, flooded fields and mainly stagnant waters including sluggish flowing canals of the lower Mekong (Ref. 12975).  Most common in areas with floating plants or rooted aquatics that reach the surface (Ref. 12693).  Larvae and early juveniles are sometimes found in the upper reaches of mangroves during the wet season (Ref. 43081).  A live-bearer species.  Feed on worms, crustaceans and insects (Ref. 7020).  Rarely taken in commercial catches, although it may be found in subsistence catches.  Not seen in markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Wrinkle-jaw snailfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Species typical of moderately deep waters.  Holotype had ostracods and rocks found in its stomach (Ref.  57784).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Wrinkled slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Wuendsch's killi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Wuhanlinigobius malayensis
species.description: Occurs in the shallow tidal pools of the mangrove region of Malay Peninsula, a muddy intertidal habitat (Ref. 94983).

species.name: Wuhanlinigobius polylepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in mangroves, at sites not far from the sea; collected by beam trawl in shallow water or by hand during low tide on mud-banks, in tiny puddles, on exposed mud surface or partly buried in mud. One specimen in the Gulf of Carpentaria was found alive among the bases of dead mangrove Bruguiera exaristata on quite dry, firm mud (Ref. 80545).

species.name: Wularni whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Xanthichthys lima
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reefs and rocky coasts (Ref. 53568).

species.name: Xenagoniates bondi
species.description: Reported to be aggressive fin nippers and can cut down caudal fins up to its peduncle (F.M. Greco, pers.comm. Apr/2019).

species.name: Xenentodon canciloides
species.description: Occurs at the surface in flowing and non-flowing waters (Ref. 12693).  Found in medium to large-sized rivers and flooded fields (Ref. 12975).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs may be found attached to objects in the water by tendrils on the egg's surface (Ref. 205).

species.name: Xeniamia atrithorax
species.description: This species has been taken in shrimp trawls on muddy bottom. Most specimens were collected from 70-119 m, some from 40-60 m, in the main waterway of the Bay of Nha Trang (latter samples might have been pumped through canyons cutting out the outer shelf as proposed for other fish taxa collected from the unusually shallow depths in this area (Ref. 84063). No specimens or fragments of sea urchins commonly trawled together with Siphamia specimens. Year-to-year fluctuations in density of population were observed with this species present at 18 of 22 stations trawling eastward and southward of Pyramid Island in 2005 and 2007 and two of 17 stations sampled in 2006 and 2009-2012. All samples were made between April and July, and no specimens were collected during a winter monsoon season (October-January). It always appeared in groups of about 10-60 specimens per trawl, with many specimens having ripe ova or brooding eggs. The smallest, 1.45 cm SL was immature. The males with buccal enlargement suggestive of brooding eggs were 2.2-2.4 cm SL and showed loss of teeth on the vomer and palatines. A 2.3 cm SL male had approximately 280 orangish eggs, 0.5 mm in diameter. Females with developed ova were as small as 2.3 cm SL. The largest gravid female was 2.95 cm SL. No possible indications for commensal relationships of this species were present (Ref. 110227).

species.name: Xenichthys agassizii
species.description: Forms large, dense, polarized schools along walls and over rocky slopes, often in somewhat protected areas (Ref. 5227).

species.name: Xenisthmus nigrolateralis
species.description: Collected from sandy bottom (Ref. 127452).

species.name: Xenobarbus loveridgei
species.description: Inhabits Lake Victoria; rare (Ref. 4967). Only known from three specimens (Ref. 89231).

species.name: Xenocephalus elongatus
species.description: Found on the shelf and shelf edge (Ref. 11230)

species.name: Xenocharax crassus
species.description: Found almost exclusively in forested tributaries or in savannah streams under dense gallery forest (Ref. 114931).

species.name: Xenochromis hecqui
species.description: Belongs to the deepwater benthic community (Ref. 53528). Scale-eater (Ref. 7343, 46829), specialized on larger prey such as Bathybates species (Ref. 46829). Copepods have also been found in the stomach (Ref. 53528). Specimens have been caught at a depth of 100 m deep (Ref. 4967, 53528). Little is known of its breeding technique (Ref. 48629).

species.name: Xenolumpenus longipterus
species.description: The specimens have well-developed ovaries containing ca. 1.5 mm diameter eggs, suggesting the spawning of the species occurs in autumn (Ref. 84251).

species.name: Xenotilapia bathyphila
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms.  Forms schools.  Feeds on copepods and small shrimps (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Xenotilapia boulengeri
species.description: Adults are found over sandy bottoms often in pairs.  Form schools.  Feed on copepods and small shrimps (Ref. 6770).  Exhibit biparental mouthbrooding of the young (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Xenotilapia burtoni
species.description: Found on sandy or muddy bottoms and feeds on insect larvae and crustaceans (Ref. 46829). Remnants of ostracods and shells have been found as well (Ref. 93927). Caught at a depth of 40 m (Ref. 93927), but average depth is about 10 m (Ref. 53528). Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Xenotilapia caudafasciata
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms.  Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Xenotilapia leptura
species.description: Occurs in rocky habitats.  Females form small to large schools, sometimes consisting of several hundreds of fish (Ref. 6770).  Feeds on both filamentous and unicellular algae (Ref. 13512).

species.name: Xenotilapia longispinis
species.description: Adults are over sandy bottoms either solitary or in pairs.  Form schools (Ref. 6770).  Exhibit prolonged biparental guarding of the fry after mouthbrooding (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Xenotilapia melanogenys
species.description: Common, sand-dwelling cichlid which forages in large schools over the sandy substrate; maximum depth is 40 metres, but during breeding period they are found in much shallower water (Ref. 46829). Very abundant; copepods, ostracods and shrimps have been found in the stomach (Ref. 53528). Breeds in colonies (lek breeder); polygamous maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52921).

species.name: Xenotilapia nasus
species.description: Occurs on mixed sand and rock bottoms; depth range 30-68 m (Ref. 27630). Stomach contents inventories suggest that it feeds on detritus as well as on plankton (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Xenotilapia nigrolabiata
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms.  Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Xenotilapia ochrogenys
species.description: Adults are found over sandy bottoms.  Form schools (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Xenotilapia ornatipinnis
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms.  Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Xenotilapia papilio
species.description: Found in deeper rocky habitat, in particular where rocks are covered with sand (Ref. 46829). Occurs at depths from 3 to 40 metres (Ref. 93988). Food consists of invertebrates which are extracted by filtering sediment through the gills (Ref. 46829), copepods, ostracods, insect larvae, filamentous algae and sand found in stomach (Ref. 93987, 93988). Territorial; biparental mouthbrooder; subadults live in small groups, larger individuals form pairs (Ref. 46829, 93988).

species.name: Xenotilapia rotundiventralis
species.description: Occurs in shallow, intermediate habitats where the bottom is mainly sand with some rocks (Ref. 46829). Forms slow-moving schools (Ref. 26454) of sometimes more than 1.000 individuals (Ref. 26454, 46829). Feed exclusively on zooplankton (Ref. 26454, 46829) and pick out individual organisms with their rather protractible mouths (Ref. 46829). Parental mouthbrooding is very common by both male and female adults; the young, of about 6 mm SL, are solely mouthbrooded by females; young which had become separated from the parent are found with other cichlid broods e.g. Lepidiolamprologus elongatus and Perissodus microlepis (Ref. 26454).

species.name: Xenotilapia sima
species.description: Adults are found over sandy bottoms.  Form schools (Ref. 6770).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Xenotilapia spilopterus
species.description: Lives in groups, sometimes large schools; biparental mouthbrooder (Ref. 6770, 46829). Lives over the sand of the intermediate habitat; forages by scooping up sandy substrate or sediment and sifting it through gills; feeds mainly on insect larvae; rarely large schools are found in mid-water feeding on zooplankton (Ref. 46829).

species.name: Xenotilapia tenuidentata
species.description: Adults are found in aggregation (Ref. 86760).  Females brood their young in the mouth (Ref. 86760).

species.name: Xenotoca doadrioi
species.description: This species occurs in permanent pond, spring, reservoir, and seasonally affected streams. The type locality is a permanent pond where this species inhabits an area with turbid and shallow water of no more than 1.5 m deep and with bottom comprising of mud and gravel and no water plants present. Other fishes collected in the area are the following: Xenotoca melanosoma, Goodea atripinnis, Poeciliopsis infans, and the introduced Xiphophorus variatus and Oreochromis sp.. In the El Moloya Spring, this species inhabits clear water with gravel to muddy bottom and water plants. The following species are found in this pond: X. melanosoma, Zoogoneticus purepechus, Ameca splendens, G. atripinnis, P. infans, and the introduced Oreochromis sp. In Oconahua Dam, this species live in turbid water with a muddy bottom and with few water plants. Other species occurring in this dam include the following: X. melanosoma, G. atripinnis, P. infans, as well as the introduced Lepomis macrochirus, and Cyprinus carpio. This species is also collected in a seasonally fluctuating stream (San Marcos stream) that is dry for most of the year, but when water is present the surface of the stream is totally cover with Eichhornia crassipes Martius, Thypa sp., and Cyperus sp. and the water at this site is highly polluted by organic matter and is turbid. This species is also found in Sahuaripa stream, an irrigation channel totally modified and fed by a water pump. Other species collected in San Marcos and Sahuaripa streams are X. melanosoma, Allotoca sp., G. atripinnis, P. infans, and Oreochromis sp. (Ref. 117630).

species.name: Xenotoca lyonsi
species.description: The type locality where the this species occurs is characterized by high seasonal changes in water clarity and volume, from a turbid and deep high flow running water in the rainy season to clear and low flow water other times of the year, sometimes reduced to a few shallow pools in the dry season. Its bottom is composed mainly of mud and gravel, and water plants are only evident in the stream bed. Other fishes present in the area include Xenotoca melanosoma (now extirpated), Ilyodon whitei, Poecilia butleri, Allodontichthys tamazulae, Astyanax anaeus, Cyprinus carpio and Oreochromis sp. (Ref. 107630).

species.name: Xenurobrycon macropus
species.description: Aquarium specimens reach 5.0 TL (Ref. 2059).

species.name: Xenurolebias cricarensis
species.description: Occurs in a temporary swamp.  A portion of the swamp is located in the border of a small forest fragment, and a part extending to an area without trees but densely occupied by the cattail <i>Typha domingensis (Ref. 96072).

species.name: Xenurolebias myersi
species.description: Found in seasonal pools as well as river floodplains (Ref. 96072). Bottom spawner, 4 months incubation.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Xenurolebias pataxo
species.description: Occurs in a broad coastal plain area which is situated within a touristic zone.  As a consequence, the natural habitats have experienced a great decline since the 1980s, with remarkable habitat loss in the last two decades due to intensive urbanization (Ref. 96072).

species.name: Xestus sabretooth blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary (Ref. 90102) usually over sandy areas of reef flats and shallow lagoons. Small juveniles were found below the upside-down jelly Cassiopea that moves over sandy substrates providing safe travel (Ref. 48636). Eggs are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Females nest in empty mollusk shells (Ref. 1602). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Xiphophorus mayae
species.description: Collected in an area where the water is gray and substratum consists predominantly of large black boulders, gravel and mud; aquatic vegetation mainly with reeds and Vallisneria (Ref. 42936).

species.name: Xiphophorus signum
species.description: Inhabits fast-flowing waters that are usually densely vegetated and have a temperature of 25°C. Occasionally occurs with the livebearer Scolichthys iota. Males attain a body length up to 7.5 cm plus 3 to 4 cm for the sword.

species.name: Xiurenbagrus dorsalis
species.description: Inhabits a very small underground stream with substrate of small rocks.  The stream flows across the bottom of the well.  A pump is connected to a 4 m depth well with plastic piping.  The type specimen emerged through the water during pumping (Ref. 96642).

species.name: Xyliphius anachoretes
species.description: Found in shallow waters (Ref. 83904).

species.name: Xyliphius sofiae
species.description: Inhabits river. Caught with a large floating net stretched between two canoes and dragged downstream through the water column (Ref. 116022).

species.name: Xyrias guineensis
species.description: Burrows in sand or mud on the continental shelf (Ref. 4455).

species.name: Xyrichtys wellingtoni
species.description: Inhabits sandy areas; specimens collected from a reef-surrounded sand patch (Ref. 31088).

species.name: Xystreurys rasilis
species.description: Feeds on amphipods, small crabs and polychaetes (Ref. 36453).  In spring mature individuals migrate to 37°S and southwards to spawn and in autumn migrate offshore for feeding and growing (Ref. 41500).

species.name: Xénocongre bicolore
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on shelf and upper slope, burrowing on muddy bottoms (Ref. 3250).

species.name: Y-bar moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Minimum depth from Ref. 106682.

species.name: Y-bar shrimp goby
species.description: Found on sand near patch reefs, usually in 5 m but to at least 15 m (Ref. 9710).  Found in burrows with alpheid shrimps (Ref. 2334).  Two individuals sometimes share a burrow, and these may be one of each color (Ref. 9360).  Occurs in clear coastal and inner reef sand slopes, in small colonies in depth of 6-20 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Y-Barred Sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand or sand and rubble substrata in both lagoon and seaward reef areas.  Large and easily approached.  Apparently a protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 48238).

species.name: Y-patterned moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302).  Rare species (Ref. 30404).  Prefers rock and sponge areas (Ref. 30404).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30404.

species.name: Y-prickleback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in sandy to rocky bottoms (Ref. 51666).

species.name: Yaeyama blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur solitary or in small groups on boulder habitats (Ref. 90102) sitting on rock and living coral (Ref. 9710) in shallow coastal reefs.  Common species on coastal and inner reef crests with rich coral growth (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yahyaoui barbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is ubiquist generally inhabiting rivers with sandy and gravel substrates and in downstream muddy substrates; it is also present in reservoirs (Ref. 114135). From April to May the species migrates upstream for spawning (Ref. 114135).

species.name: Yakati rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in streams in mountainous, rainforest terrain at elevations between 200 and 400 m.

species.name: Yakutian char
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lakes.  Feeds on the larvae and pupae of chironomids (Ref. 593).

species.name: Yaldwyn$s triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in rock pools and subtidal areas.  They are found at exposed sites, usually near darker overhangs and walls among encrusting organisms (Ref. 9003).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yamanoue’s seabass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yangambi butterbarbel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefer smaller forest streams with rocky (Ref. 7248, 43912) or sandy bottom (Ref. 43912). Nocturnal (Ref. 43912). Probably carnivorous (Ref. 43912), with a preference for terrestrial and aquatic insects (Ref. 7248, 43912).  Oviparous, eggs are unguarded (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yangtse grenadier anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A purely freshwater species occurring in tributaries and associated lakes.

species.name: Yangtze icefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yang’s longnose catshark
species.description: The pregnant female individual caught contained a single egg capsule (Ref. 116167).

species.name: Yano's snipe eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yano’s cheek-hook goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sandy-mud bottoms at depths of 0-12 m (Ref. 84001).

species.name: Yano’s starry goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered bays on sand, rubble and mud bottoms in 10-25 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yantai stingray
species.description: A demersal species,  inshore on continental shelf over soft bottoms to ca. 60 m.  In the summer, juveniles are found in estuaries and coastal shallows  (Ref. 114953).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449).

species.name: Yao mosquitofish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yapen rainbowfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yaqui catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in quiet water over sandy or rocky bottom in small to medium rivers.

species.name: Yaqui chub
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits quiet pools of headwaters and creeks and usually occurs in vegetation (Ref. 86798).

species.name: Yaqui sucker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small mountain and desert creeks, and deep pools, runs and rapids of medium rivers.

species.name: Yarra pygmy perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and small lakes; prefers flowing water with abundant cover in the form of aquatic vegetation (Ref. 44894). Occurs in creeks and lakes, usually among aquatic weeds. Feeds on insects, insect larvae and planktonic crustaceans (Ref. 5259, 44894). Swims in small shoals, sometimes with N. australis. Breeding season is in spring (September and October). Slight morphological differences exist between populations from the extreme western and eastern parts of the range that could warrant their placement into separate subspecies (Ref. 44894).

species.name: Yarrella blackfordi
species.description: Mesopelagic, adults found in 500-700 m depth (Ref. 4470).  Living on or near the bottom, probably moves in schools (Ref. 37473).

species.name: Yasuhikotakia splendida
species.description: Inhabits swift or moderately swift, clearwater, foothill streams with predominantly rocky or cobblestone bottom (Ref. 31466). Collected together with B. sidthimunki/i> and Botia (Hymenophysa sp. (Ref. 31466).

species.name: Yawning
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Trawled at depths greater than 800-1000 m (Ref. 4241, 83463); seined with unclosing fishing gear at 4500-0 m and  with closing fishing gear at depths of 1300-645 m (Ref. 83463).

species.name: Yazoo darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yazoo shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow acara
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In creeks and small streams (Ref. 40602).

species.name: Yellow angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef slopes, occasionally on lagoon reefs (Ref. 9710).  Herbivorous (Ref. 33482).  Forms harems of 2-4 individuals.  Frequently exported through the aquarium trade (Ref. 48391).

species.name: Yellow banded spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow barred pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Its cryptic habits and small size make it difficult to observe and collect this species (Ref. 112075).

species.name: Yellow bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in pools and backwaters of small to large rivers; also in ponds and lakes (Ref. 5723, 10294).  Young feed on microcrustaceans and midge larvae; adults on fish such as shad and silversides (Ref. 10294).

species.name: Yellow Batasio
species.description: Inhabits the river stretch of Manimala River at Paduthode where it occurs generally on sand or sandy gravel bottom with occasional presence of bed rock or black clays. The width and depth of this area are 45.0-125.0 m and 0.3-6 m, respectively; bank height is 4.0-5.0 m above general water level in summer season; blanketed by moderate to dense riparian vegetation with intermittent occurrence of low riparian vegetation noticed at certain places.  This species is unique for it requires spotless and clear water and is intolerant to the accumulation of organic wastes and other contaminants, thus regular monitoring of the water quality is essential for the protection and preservation of this rare species (Ref. 104688).

species.name: Yellow belly cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Prefers moderate to fast flowing waters of the lower and middle river valleys.  Feeds on macro-invertebrates and small fishes.

species.name: Yellow blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or weedy areas (Ref. 11482).  Feeds on invertebrates (Ref. 11482).

species.name: Yellow cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits sheltered clearwater areas of lagoon and seaward reefs.  Aggregates under ledges, in holes, or even among spines of sea urchins.  Feeds on planktonic crustaceans and small invertebrates by day and night (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Yellow catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur mainly in river channels and lakes.  They feed on the bottom on insects (particularly on trichopterans and chironomids), mollusks, occasionally on fishes (Ref. 6868).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Eggs are guarded by the males (Ref. 45232). Important food fish (Ref. 89718).

species.name: Yellow chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually inhabit steep outer reef slopes and rocky bottoms.  Found singly or in small groups.  Uncommon (Ref. 9710).  Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellow cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lower and middle river valleys.

species.name: Yellow clownfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in lagoon and outer reefs in pairs and small groups (Ref. 48636). Monogamous (Ref. 55367). A protandrous hermaphrodite (Ref. 32166). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Associated with the anemones: Heteractis crispa and Stichodactyla mertensii (Ref. 5911). Have been reared in captivity (Ref. 35413, 35418, 35420).

species.name: Yellow cory
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the sublittoral zone above 120 m in sandy mud bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Yellow devilfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near reefs (Ref. 7300).  In aggregations in caves, often upside down.  Males incubate the egg mass in their mouths (Ref. 9710). Also found in caves, crevices and under ledges (Ref 90102). Brreding in the aquarium is possible (Ref. 130644).

species.name: Yellow Drombus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow face sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons.
