species.name: Yellow fangbelly
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Poisonous canines provide considerable protection from predators.

species.name: Yellow finned medaka
species.description: Adults occur along gently sloping shores with large boulders on sand and pebble bottom (Ref. 26687). Found only below 1.5 m and in small groups of 2-20 individuals (Ref. 26687). Non-annual breeders (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Yellow garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow hawkfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on rocky cliffs in deep water (Ref. 9710).  Also inhabits muddy substrates in protected bays where wave action has no influence (Ref. 48636). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellow Irish lord
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit steep slopes at the edges of banks (Ref. 5521).  Mouthbrooders (Ref. 240).

species.name: Yellow meeki
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits both lakes and lower valley rivers, preferring sandy or soft bottoms with small rocks.

species.name: Yellow moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Stays in holes and crevices.  Feeds mainly on crabs and fish (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Yellow pigmy brotula
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Rare species (Ref. 34024) notable for its strict association with true reef environments and particularly so with outer reefs and reef cores (Ref. 81230).  An indweller of deep interstices of lagoon and seaward reefs to a depth of at least 30 m (Ref. 1602).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 240). Solitary inhabitant of shallow water, cryptic (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellow podge
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow prawn-goby
species.description: Inhabits sandy areas of shallow lagoons and protected coastal bays (Ref. 9710).  Lives in a burrow with alpheid shrimps.  Found in clear coastal sand  slopes and lagoons, usually in depth of 10-25 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Yellow pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Occur in caves of drop-offs at depths of about 25 to at least 50 m (Ref. 48637, 58302). Form loose schools near the roofs or sides of caves and disappears into holes or crevices when approached. Often seen with other species of Trimma and feeds on harpacticoid copepods (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Yellow rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in the basin-wide tributary of the lower Mekong (Ref. 36667).

species.name: Yellow razorfish
species.description: Found over sandy bottoms (Ref. 5288)

species.name: Yellow ruddertail dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Type specimen taken from a reef at 2-8 m depth (Ref. 33021).

species.name: Yellow Sand Cichlid
species.description: Occurs over sandy bottoms.  Forms schools (Ref. 6770).

species.name: Yellow shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow snout seabream
species.description: <i>Dentex<i> species are known to be basically benthic and deep-sea inhabiting, not strong swimmers and considered to be allopatric (Ref. 101630).

species.name: Yellow spotted gurnard
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental slope.  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yellow stingray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found along sandy beaches to the water's edge, and especially in sandy areas in and around coral reefs (Ref. 7251).  Raises front end of disc to attract prey seeking shelter (Ref. 7251).  Feeds on shrimps, probably also on small fishes, clams, and worms (Ref. 12951).  Known to be capable of inflicting dangerous wounds with its venomous spine.  Easily approached (Ref. 9710).  A live-bearing species, produces 3 to 4 young (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Yellow sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Depth range (1-20 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Yellow swordtail
species.description: Common in small streams and brooks with light current and rockpools in areas with extensive limestone outcroppings; relatively uncommon in fast-flowing streams (Ref. 52914).

species.name: Yellow tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found near coastal reefs.  Hovers above its burrow in flat soft silty bottoms (Ref. 9710).  Usually in pairs (Ref. 48635).

species.name: Yellow triangular batfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species (Ref. 75154) found on the continental slope (Ref. 7300, 75154).

species.name: Yellow triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow, sheltered waters, on hard corals; found on the upper part of coral reefs, usually along the reef margin in depths of about 1 m, often on corals covered by low algae. Also found in bays or sheltered lagoons (Ref. 88983).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellow weaver
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-and-black triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults usually inhabit rocky reefs (Ref. 84085). They are found on the sides or under overhangs of large boulders, sheltering in the massive sponge growths or in large, deep crevices.  They feed mainly on amphipods, and also on barnacle cyprids and polychaete larvae.  Males maybe territorial during the breeding season (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellow-axil chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found primarily along deep outer reef walls (Ref. 48636).  They occur singly or in small groups in outer reef slopes.  Feed on plankton (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Yellow-axil damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-banded perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected by bottom trawl (Ref. 123213).

species.name: Yellow-banded pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-belly bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It occupies mostly complex habitats in water shallower than 10 m; mostly found near river outlets and in the southern part of Lake Malawi; in southern Lake Malawi it is generally associated with the rock/sand interface or, associated with submerged aquatic vegetation and among reed beds in shallow water and inlets (Ref. 5595, 128638). Present in calm coves or slow flowing sections of rivers with vegetation; not common in Lake Malawi, but abundant in larger rivers (Ref. 4967). Piscivore, hunting mbuna and sand-dwelling haplochromines; mouthbrooder (Ref. 5595). Oviparous (Ref. 205). Breeds in summer (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Yellow-belly damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in outer reef slopes and passages, usually associated with the coral Pocillopora, generally with three to five individuals per coral head (Ref. 7247). Feeds on benthic algaes (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Yellow-black threefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in shallow tidal pools, and seems to be associated with coralline rock and seagrass (Ref. 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellow-breasted dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rock and coral reefs exposed to wave action in 1-9 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellow-brown chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is usually encountered in clear water over coral reefs at depths between about 12 and at least 45 m.  Habitats include both gradually sloping bottoms and steeper drop-offs, but in the former case it was restricted to depths greater than 20 m in the vicinity of isolated, small patch reefs.  Generally, this species forms aggregations ranging from just a few fish to at least 20-30 individuals, feeding on plankton up to several meters above the bottom. The fish retreat to caves, crevices, and ledges when approached closely by divers (Ref. 75747).  Life history characteristics for the family specify that this species is oviparous, with distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellow-brown sillago
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-brown wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups (Ref. 90102) in clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs, over open sand and rubble as well as dense coral growth.  Common is shallow exposed areas (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds mainly on shelled benthic invertebrates (crabs, shrimps, gastropods, bivalves, brittle stars, sea urchins), also on polychaete worms and fish eggs.  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Yellow-crowned butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Only known from a few specimens collected at depths over 30 m along the current-swept drop-offs of Orote Peninsula, Guam.  Occur singly or in pairs among black corals.  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Form pairs during breeding (Ref. 205).  Do well in captivity.

species.name: Yellow-dabbled flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and mud bottoms (Ref. 9797).  Frequently collected in areas near river mouths (Ref. 9797).  Feeds on bottom-living animals (Ref. 9797).  Mostly used in making fish meal but is also marketed fresh (Ref. 9797).

species.name: Yellow-dotted butterflyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit coastal reefs, primarily on rubble slopes (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous (Ref. 205).  Adults usually swim in pairs in search of small benthic invertebrates (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellow-ear angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas (Ref. 9710).  Often in pairs or small groups (Ref. 9710).  Probably feeds on algae, sponges, and benthic invertebrates (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 9710.

species.name: Yellow-eye mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over sandy and muddy bottoms of coastal waters, bays, estuaries, and may ascend rivers into freshwaters (Ref. 9812, 44894).  Adults inhabit brackish coastal lakes (Ref. 44894).  Found in schools (Ref. 9812).  Shoal-forming (Ref. 44894).  They are omnivores, feeding mostly on benthic detritus, algae and small invertebrates.  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).  Spawn in coastal waters in summer and autumn, probably in estuaries (Ref. 9812, 27012, 28470, 28707, 28708).  Marketed fresh (whole gutted or fillets), smoked, salted or as roe (Ref. 3383).

species.name: Yellow-eyed comb-tooth
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coastal reefs and on deep lagoon bommies.  They occur frequently at depths less than 15 m.  In small groups in shallow depths on large sponges or brain corals (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Yellow-eyed toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal areas.

species.name: Yellow-green goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Secretive species found in shallow seaward reefs (Ref. 34765).  Benthic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Yellow-jaw threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-lined fairygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sheltered reefs with silty sand and rubble bottoms in 25-82 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yellow-lined grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species collected from depths less than 30 meters (Ref. 37522).

species.name: Yellow-lined shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand-rubble slope at the base of a vertical cliff (22-30 m depth) and on small sand patches at the undercut bases of reefs.  Each individual hovers at the entrance of a rubble-lined burrow occupied by an alpheid shrimp, where it hides when disturbed (Ref. 31115).

species.name: Yellow-lined snapper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Swim well above the surface of the reef in aggregations, consisting of several hundred individuals (Ref. 11902, 48635). Feeds on fishes, shrimps, crabs, other crustaceans, cephalopods, and some planktonic items. Caught mainly with handlines and bottom longlines, and marketed fresh (Ref. 9821).

species.name: Yellow-lip threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy or muddy bottoms.  Feeds on small crustaceans.

species.name: Yellow-mouth pikeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in worm tubes on sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 11482).  Males are territorial and vigorously defend their worm tube homes.  When courting, the male will assume the S-shape position and dart quickly back and forth from their place of shelter.  When threatened, it opens its enormous mouth, which significantly increases its apparent size to the invader (Ref. 28023).

species.name: Yellow-red pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-saddled wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Is a selective forager which prefers to feed on small, hard-shelled animals like crabs and gastropods (Ref. 26966).

species.name: Yellow-shoulder dwarfgoby
species.description: Collected on offshore patch reefs exposed to clear water and good current flow, from coral overhangs and crevices on healthy, live coral reefs (Ref. 124592).

species.name: Yellow-snout soldierbream
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-speckled chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in clear lagoon and seaward reefs, usually seen singly or in loose aggregations near caves and ledges.  Abundant over branching corals and leeward coasts (Ref. 9710). Feeds on planktons (Ref. 89972). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellow-spotted anthias
species.description: Inhabits rocky reefs (Ref. 41299). Forms large schools, frequently mixed with other Pseudanthias (Ref 90102). Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Yellow-spotted chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit lagoon and outer coral reefs, boulder bottoms and lava cliffs, in small to large aggregations (Ref. 7247).  Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellow-spotted dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in pairs around rocky outcrops and sponges (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellow-spotted fanray
species.description: Espèce de poissons. From studies on vertebral centra, it has been suggested that females attain a greater asymptotic total length (55.58 cm TL) and grew more slowly than males (45.52 cm TL) (based on specimens from Ariake Bay, western Kyushu Island, Japan). The maximum ages observed were 5 years for males and 12 years for females. Furthermore, it was also reported that females reached sexual maturity at a greater size than males (total length at 50% sexual maturity: males, 39.3 cm; females, 42.1cm). Parturition occurred from August to November followed immediately by mating, ovulation and fertilization. Largest specimen yet recorded (USNM 51295, 68.0 cm TL, Tokyo, sex unknown) with the largest specimens examined and collected from the Hyuga Nada Sea to be 63.9 cm TL for female, and 52.5 cm TL for male; however, the species is likely to grow larger than ca. 70.0 cm TL according to local Miyazaki fishermen (Ref. 86259).

species.name: Yellow-spotted golden bass
species.description: Collected from rocky slopes and ledges.  When threatened, it retreats into small caves and crevices.  Larva from Florida Straits was captured between 25 and 50 m (Ref. 95863).

species.name: Yellow-spotted grayling
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-spotted moray
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-spotted perchlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-spotted shrimpgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from fine mud bottoms and reported to live in association with alpheid shrimps (Ref. 41718).  Hovers up to 5 cm above its burrow (Ref. 41718).  Feeds primarily on plankton in the water column (Ref. 41718).

species.name: Yellow-spotted skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Bottom-dwellers that feed on invertebrates and bony fish (Ref. 9908).  Depth range given by H. Ishihara (pers.comm. 07/07).  Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 5.3-6.7 cm long and 2.7-3.9 cm wide (Ref. 41253, 41298).

species.name: Yellow-spotted snake eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthic (Ref. 58302). Adults of most Callechelys spend most of their lives within the sediment and do not form permanent burrows. This species is exceptional and has on rare occasions been dip-netted beneath lights at the sea surface at night and has been seen encountered with its head protruding from the sand by divers at various Hawaiian locations (Ref. 27478).

species.name: Yellow-spotted tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on silty sand bottoms with coral rocks (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on zooplankton (Ref. 9137). Solitary or in pairs (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellow-striped barracuda
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-striped hogfish
species.description:
An epibenthic species found on sandy, rubble and coral bottoms, with individual males sometimes
accompanied by a small harem (pers. comm. K. Nishiyama). It is most commonly seen at depths of 65-70 m during cold upwelling events (temperatures of 20-24C°) with adults observed to dive into the burrows of other organisms when startled, at Menjangan and Nusa Penida islands off Bali, Indonesia (Ref. 105428).

species.name: Yellow-striped leatherjacket
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rocky reefs (Ref. 9563).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Yellow-striped sandlance
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is reported to be regularly caught by trawlers operating within 80 m depth (mostly within 40 m) along the east coast of India and is locally marketed for domestic consumption (Ref. 124631).

species.name: Yellow-striped sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-striped squirrelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep reefs (Ref. 27370).  Benthopelagic in or near crevices and caves (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Yellow-striped sweetlips
species.description: Espèce de poissons. In coastal reef slopes, inner reefs and deep lagoon (Ref. 48635).  Prefers sheltered reefs and during the day either solitary or in large inactive aggregations (Ref. 34765).

species.name: Yellow-tail parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A rare species found in coastal and outer reefs with dense coral cover (Ref. 9710); often silty habitats (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellow-tailed pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellow-threaded goatfish
species.description: Espèce d'animaux. Found over sand (Ref. 58302).  Generally found at depths deeper than 60 meters (Ref. 54393).

species.name: Yellow-tipped threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on sand or mud bottoms.  Appears in small numbers in local markets.

species.name: Yellowback grunt
species.description: An inshore species generally associated with rocky bottoms.

species.name: Yellowback stingaree
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Little is known of its biology (Ref. 6871).

species.name: Yellowback tubelip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon inhabitant of coral-rich areas of clear outer lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 1602).  May form small groups (Ref. 90102).  Males generally solitary (Ref. 9710).  Juveniles are cleaners while adults feed on coral polyps (Ref. 1602).  Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 128797.

species.name: Yellowband monocle bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in offshore waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates.  Taken by bottom trawls (scampi nets).

species.name: Yellowband wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small groups over lagoon patch reefs (Ref. 1602).  Benthopelagic over coral and rubble (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on zooplankton in the water column (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowbanded perch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  Benthic (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yellowbanded pipefish
species.description: Adults prefer muddy substrate and usually seen by divers in deep waters that are not disturbed by waves, but it enters shallow estuaries.  Adults form pairs and usually swim along the bottom around large remote coral heads on mud slopes.  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).  An active cleaner (Ref. 48635). Solitary or pairs around isolated coral patches on sand/mud slopes (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowbar basslet
species.description: Inhabit deep neritic and epibathyal zones on sedimentary substrates.

species.name: Yellowbar parrot
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in areas of coral rock with coral or rubble, from the lower surge zone to at least 10 m (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).

species.name: Yellowbar sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow protected sandy areas near reefs of lagoons and bays to at least 28 m (Ref. 9710), often amongst boulders (Ref. 48636, 58652).  Minimum depth of 10 m reported from Ref. 37816, 90102.

species.name: Yellowbar tilefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowbarred parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of clear, protected reefs (Ref. 9710). Found in lagoon and seaward reefs (Ref. 90102).   Feeds mainly on algae (Ref. 26993).

species.name: Yellowbelly cardinalfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits protected habitats, where conditions are similar to those of lagoons. Also found on coastal reefs (Ref. 9710). Usually seen solitary, occasionally in pairs. Mimics the sabre-toothed blenny Meiacanthus vittatus. Active during day (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowbelly flounder
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters down to about 50 m (Ref. 9258).  Juveniles gather in sheltered inshore waters, such as estuarine areas, shallow mudflats and sandflats, where they remain for up to two years (Ref. 9072).

species.name: Yellowbelly gudgeon
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rainforest tributaries with gravel or mud bottoms (Ref. 2847).

species.name: Yellowbelly hamlet
species.categoryName: Serranidae (Sea basses: groupers and fairy basslets)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 26340) inhabiting rocky and coral reefs (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on crustaceans (primarily shrimps) (Ref. 26180).

species.name: Yellowbelly pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs near shore (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Yellowbelly threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on sand or mud bottoms.  Abundant in depths between 45 and 90 m, but larger fish generally occur in depths greater than 110 m.  Larger fish feed mainly on crustaceans, fish and cephalopods.  Young fish (< 12 cm) eat copepods, ostracods and amphipods.

species.name: Yellowblotch razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives on open, clean, sandy areas of lagoon and seaward slopes (Ref. 9710, 37816).  Benthic and benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yellowbreasted damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit coral reefs of lagoons and offshore areas.  Also in silty lagoons or sheltered estuaries (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowcheek
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A food fish for humans (Ref. 4537).

species.name: Yellowcheek darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in fast rocky riffles of small to medium rivers.

species.name: Yellowcheek wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over hard substrates (Ref. 9626).  Juveniles up to 8 cm act as specialized cleaners.  Each individual tends a defined cleaning station sought by several species of reef fishes including damselfishes, goatfishes, and surgeonfishes.  At the cleaning station this wrasse swims in a characteristic seesaw motion (Ref. 31373).  Occasionally caught by anglers.  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).  Found at 9 m in Belize (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Yellowchin sculpin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on soft bottom.  Neither anterolateral glandular groove nor venom gland is present (Ref. 57406).

species.name: Yelloweye filefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Uncommon species that occurs in coral and rocky reefs to a depth of about 15 m (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yelloweye nannygai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yelloweye rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in rocky reefs and boulder fields (Ref. 27437), the young found in shallower regions (Ref. 27436).  Feed on fishes and crustaceans (Ref. 28499).  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).  Sold as fillets (Ref. 6885).

species.name: Yellowface pikeblenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups, one to a hole, in limestone or coral rubble in clear water.  Feeds on small crustaceans, worms, and fishes (Ref. 5521).

species.name: Yellowfin angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in area of rubble with little coral growth.  Occurs in small groups on semi-open substrate, Maximum depth reported taken from Ref. 48636.

species.name: Yellowfin barbell
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowfin bass
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowfin blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow coral reefs, probably (Ref. 90102). Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellowfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabitant estuaries, coastal rivers, creeks, lakes and bays, usually in marine or brackish water, but in dry seasons they penetrate the lowermost reaches of fresh water (Ref. 44894). Common in coastal and estuarine rocky habitat. They enter rivers upstream to the limit of brackish waters. They migrate from their feeding to their spawning grounds; they spawn mainly during winter in the vicinity of river entrances; eggs are planktonic and hatch after 2.5 days. A portion of the population changes sex from male to female after spawning. They feed on mollusks, crustaceans, worms, fish and ascidians. It is parasitised by the monogeneans Anoplodiscus australis and A. spari on the fins and body surface (Ref. 124057).

species.name: Yellowfin chromis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral or rocky reefs (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowfin damsel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit inshore coral reefs and steep outer slopes (Ref. 7247).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowfin damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rubble and dead coral outcrops that are often situated in sandy areas (Ref. 7247).  They occur solitarily or in small groups.  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Yellowfin dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs inshore (Ref. 7300).  Found among rubble in crevices of coastal reefs (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowfin dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowfin fairy wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits finely branching corals on protected coral and rubble slopes.  Occurs in aggregations (Ref. 37816).

species.name: Yellowfin flasher wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rubble and weedy bottoms of seaward reefs (Ref. 90102).  Also found in coastal reef slopes and estuaries.  Occurs in small groups with numerous females, juveniles and several males, often covering a large section of reef.  Juveniles are secretive when small and form small groups at later stages (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellowfin fringehead
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocks and bays near jetties.  Usually found in empty shells and holes.

species.name: Yellowfin gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowfin goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy and sandy bottoms along the shore of bays and estuaries, sometimes ascends rivers. Intertidal to at least 6.5 m (Ref. 96339). Oviparous, spawn in winter to early spring (Ref. 205).  Eggs are deposited in Y-shaped nests (Ref. 205).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Yellowfin madtom
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits pools and backwaters around slab rocks, bedrock ledges and tree roots in clear creeks and small rivers (Ref. 5723, 10294).

species.name: Yellowfin notothen
species.description: Espèce de poissons. May be found at depths greater than 250 m in the Patagonian region (Ref. 5179).

species.name: Yellowfin parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and channel reefs, usually deeper 20 m (Ref. 9710).  Minimum depth of 2 m reported from Ref. 2689.

species.name: Yellowfin pigfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in caves and archways on reefs (Ref. 44106).  Likely to occur in depths greater than 250 m (Ref. 44106).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowfin pufferfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in the sublittoral zone and estuaries, on rock bottoms (Ref. 11230).  Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166).

species.name: Yellowfin sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. No data re its habitat or depth of capture (Ref. 116166).

species.name: Yellowfin scorpionfish
species.description: Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 42181, 75154).  Trawled (Ref. 75154). Solitary on open sand/mud bottoms (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowfin sea bream
species.description: Most samples were collected by hand-line (Ref. 75039).

species.name: Yellowfin shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits clear rocky pools of headwaters, creeks and small rivers.

species.name: Yellowfin snapper
species.description: Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 55) in coastal areas and outer slopes.  Forms large and small aggregations (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yellowfin snubnose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow tidal pools of mangroves and muddy intertidal habitat (Ref. 94986). Often occurring with Pseudogobius poicilosoma, and sometimes with P. avicennia and P. verticalis (Ref. 126575).

species.name: Yellowfin sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected with ichthyocide on coral or rocky reefs at depths less than 10 m in areas with ledges, caves, and surge channels (Ref. 95447).

species.name: Yellowfin toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowfin wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length and depth range (10-30 m) given by B. Victor (pers. comm. 10/18).

species.name: Yellowfoot shrimpgoby
species.description: Inhabits sandy shores, sometimes in seagrass, in 8-20 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowhead angelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coral and rubble areas on steep outer reef slopes.  Solitary or in small groups of four to five individuals.

species.name: Yellowhead damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are common on coastal fringing reefs and offshore platform reefs (Ref. 50559).  Found in groups above coral (Ref. 50559).  Feed on zooplankton (Ref. 50559).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowhead hulafish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur inshore near reefs (Ref. 7300).  They feed on crabs, fishes, and larvae (Ref. 9137).  Eggs are guarded by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowhead sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowhead wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Commonly found on shallow and deep reefs and exposed rocky ledges.  Feeds on various invertebrates.  Forms leks during breeding (Ref. 55367).  A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Constantly on the move but easily attracted by divers.  Generally of no interest to fisheries because of its small average size (Ref. 5217).

species.name: Yellowhump eartheater
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowjacket cichlid
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits rivers and lakes, preferring the slower moving waters.  Feeds primarily upon other live fishes.  Enters brackish water.  Used in experimental and behavioral research.

species.name: Yellowline goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Always lives in association with tube sponges or massive sponges.  Difficult to approach (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowline sandperch
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from sand and rubble adjacent to the wreck of a Dutch ship (Ref. 79876).  Inhabits sandy bottoms of coastal reef slopes at 25-70 m, solitray (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yellowlined anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in coastal reefs, along deep slopes, usually in small aggregations.  Also Ref. 48635.

species.name: Yellowlined basslet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits steep outer reef faces (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowlined cardinalfish
species.description: Inhabits inshore reefs, crevices of reef flats and coral slopes (Ref. 9710).  Nocturnal species (Ref. 7300). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowlip dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in reef crevices and under rock outcrops in 14-21 m (Ref 90102).

species.name: Yellowlip grubfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Specimens collected by epibenthic sled and demersal trawl (Ref. 59349).

species.name: Yellowmargin basslet
species.description: A deep-water species that is rarely captured (Ref. 6180).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).

species.name: Yellowmouth jawfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits deep water.

species.name: Yellowmouth rockfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on rough bottoms (Ref. 2850).  Minimum depth reported from Ref. 27437.  Viviparous (Ref. 34817).

species.name: Yellownape tripplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur on rocky substrates in association with coral reefs or coral reef lagoons, from shallow areas to the outer reef slope, also in intertidal rock pools (Ref. 13227, 27223).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellownose goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in groups near coral heads (Ref. 9710).  Picks external parasites found on other fishes (Ref. 13628).  Monogamous (Ref. 52884).

species.name: Yellownose prawn-goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed to hover 1 to 4 cm above the entrance of its burrow, in sand or sand and rubble substrate.  Usually seen in pairs with alpheid shrimps.  Occurs in deep coastal slopes and sand flats, usually in depth over 20 meters (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Yellownose skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Reported size at hatching and incubation period 17.2 cm TL and 252 days, respectively (Ref. 120403). Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205). Inhabits sandy and muddy bottoms at depths (Ref. 104541).

species.name: Yellowpatch razorfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on upper part of sand and mud banks, usually on reef flat areas, just before sloping down in depths from 7 m down to about 15 m. Found in spread out groups, often with X. pentadactylus in the same general area, but this species grows much larger and dominates (Ref. 48636). Dives into sand to sleep safely at night or to hide when alarmed (Ref. 90102). But the biggest males swim over large areas and move away quickly when approached by divers rather than diving into the bottom (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellowprow goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Lives in tubular sponges.  Also found in coral reefs; depths of 18-25 m (Ref. 26938).

species.name: Yellowsnout large-eye bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs over sand, mud, and rubble areas.  Feed mainly on small bottom-living gastropods.  Marketed  fresh or dried-salted.  Also caught with bottom longlines and handlines (Ref. 9775).

species.name: Yellowspot frogmouth
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowspot groppo
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowspotted boarfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on the continental shelf (Ref. 9563, 75154) and continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yellowspotted ponyfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowspotted sandgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Restricted to shallow sand flats, where it is often found with another goby, Pseudogobius olorum.

species.name: Yellowspotted sawtail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found along rocky shores, juveniles in estuaries and bays (Ref. 9710).  Feeds on benthic algae (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowspotted wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits lagoon and seaward reefs, in areas of mixed sand and coral (Ref. 9710).  Post pelagic juveniles carried by currents beyond their normal breeding range.  They are often in pairs or small loose groups, swimming close to the bottom.  When approached, they move up and down in an unusual way that may worry a possible predator.  Adults move about in small groups.  (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellowstem dragonfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Mesopelagic species (Ref. 559).

species.name: Yellowstripe coris
species.description: Inhabits reefs with sand and rubble areas (Ref. 9710).  Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302).  Feeds on sea urchins, heart urchins, bivalves, gastropods, brittle stars, crabs, hermit crabs and polychaetes.  Protogynous (Ref. 55080).  Eaten raw, dried and salted, baked or broiled (Ref. 7364).

species.name: Yellowstripe fusilier
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species forms midwater aggregations that feed on zooplankton, frequently in the company of other caesionids, usually Caesio caerulaurea, C. lunaris, and C. varilineata, from the surface to at least 30 m (Ref. 77031).

species.name: Yellowstripe goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in brackish waters along coastlines, estuaries and tidal reaches of rivers (Ref. 12693).  Feed on small crustaceans, aquatic insects and insect larvae (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Yellowstripe slopefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Solitary or in small groups (Ref. 90102). Lives by rocky reefs at considerable depths (Ref. 9137).

species.name: Yellowstripe threadfin bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154). Solitary or small groups in rubble areas (Ref. 90102)

species.name: Yellowstripe wormfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sand and rubble bottoms (Ref. 9710, 48637). Also found in open sand. Algal flats and seagrass beds in 3-50 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yellowtail anthias
species.description: Espèce de poissons. FishBase common name coined by authors.

species.name: Yellowtail blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Yellowtail croaker
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries (Ref. 9772).  A food fish.

species.name: Yellowtail dascyllus
species.description: Adults inhabit coral and rocky reefs (Ref. 7247). A protogynous hermaphrodite (Ref. 55367).  Feeds on zooplanktons (Ref. 89972). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 54980; 113699).

species.name: Yellowtail demoiselle
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Usually found in outer reef slopes and frequently in the deeper surge channels or adjacent ledges.  Form small groups in sub-tidal habitats (Ref. 48636).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205). Diurnal species (Ref. 113699).

species.name: Yellowtail dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Collected from tidal pools and coral and rock reefs; associated with live and dead branching corals (e.g. Acropora and Pocillopora) (Ref. 12720).

species.name: Yellowtail horse mackerel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur in coastal waters, including estuaries (Ref. 9563), mostly in waters shallower than 150 m and warmer than 13°C (Ref. 9072).  Commonly found on the bottom, in midwater and occasionally at the surface (Ref. 9258), in large schools (Ref. 33616).  Adults are generally found over offshore rocky reefs, while juveniles are generally found in shallow, soft substrate areas (Ref. 6390).  Utilized fresh, smoked, canned and frozen; can be fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Yellowtail mullet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit upper reaches of rivers (Ref. 41236).  Oviparous, eggs are pelagic and non-adhesive (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowtail rasbora
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in streams, canals and ditches in lowland floodplains.  Usually found right at the water surface and is easily recognized by the broad black margin on the bright yellow caudal fin.  Feed on exogenous insects (Ref. 12693).  Spawning sites are found in rivers and ponds (Ref. 33813).  Mature adults probably breed during the rainy season.   Occasionally seen in fish markets (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Yellowtail reeffish
species.description: Adults inhabit steep slopes and outer patch reefs.  They occur in small groups near small outcrops (Ref. 9710).  Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205).  Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205).  Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowtail rriplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowtail tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yellowtail trumpeter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur inshore, in mangrove areas; in lotic and lentic freshwater bodies (Ref. 7300).  Live in coastal marine waters, but also found in estuaries and freshwater sections of rivers (particularly in temperate southern latitudes) (Ref. 44894).  Benthic omnivore, juveniles feed on algae and a range of small crustaceans, while older fish prey mainly on polychaetes (Ref. 34016).  Eggs are guarded and fanned by the male parent (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowtail tubelip
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A solitary species (Ref. 90102) occurring in coral rich areas of shallow lagoons and sheltered seaward reefs.  Adults feed mainly on coral polyps while juveniles remove ectoparasites from small territorial fishes (Ref. 2334, 9710).  Adults swim in small groups.  Usually, only small juveniles clean other fishes (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Yellowtip damselfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit shallow rocky reefs and associated with colonies of Millepora alcicornis (Floeter 1998, pers. comm.). Feed mainly on benthic algae and aggressively territorial (Floeter 1998, pers. comm.). Oviparous, distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 205). Eggs are demersal and adhere to the substrate (Ref. 205). Males guard and aerate the eggs (Ref. 205).

species.name: Yellowtip soldierfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits reef flats and slopes.  May be found at depths greater than 18 m (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Yellowtop Jewelfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yemen sweeper
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yepez’ tube-snouted ghost knifefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yirrkala fusca
species.description: Environment needs verification.

species.name: Yirrkala moorei
species.description: Maximum length (434 mm) given was for an immature male.

species.name: Yirrkala ori
species.description: Inhabits coarse sand substrate (Ref. 86861).

species.name: Yiwarda whiptail
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A benthic species found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yoke darter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in clear, fast, rocky riffles of creeks and small to medium rivers (Ref. 5723).  Spawn in batches (Ref. 36980).  Distinct pairing during breeding (Ref. 36980).

species.name: Yokozuna Slickhead
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yongeichthys criniger
species.description: Inhabits shallow to deep coastal mud or silty sand flats (Ref. 48637).  Toxicity in this species is particularly high in the skin.  Its toxicity varies with the locality and some specimens are nontoxic altogether (Ref. 559).

species.name: Yongeichthys thomasi
species.description: Endemic to brackish waters (Ref. 92840). Usually found in brackish waters of creeks close to river mouths, coastal lagoons (Ref. 4343, 7390, 57403, 79590), mangrove swamps (Ref. 7390, 57403, 79590), ponds and creeks (Ref. 4343). Rare reports of the species ascending rivers to freshwater, which it may tolerate for short periods (Ref. 57403, 79590). Maximum reported standard length 47 mm (=60 mm TL)(Ref. 79590).

species.name: Yoshino's goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits mud-sand bottoms with Caulerpa green alga in 1-12 m (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Yoshino's pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ypsilon bullseye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral reef (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Yu loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yucatan flagfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. 6 cm max TL (Ref. 2060).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Yucatan gambusia
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yucatan goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from rivers, estuaries and inland lagoons (Ref. 30499).

species.name: Yucatan killifish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Not a seasonal killifish (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Yucatan pupfish
species.description: Not a seasonal killifish.  Is easy to maintain in the aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Yucatan skate
species.description: Deep water species (Ref. 6902).  Oviparous (Ref. 50449).  Eggs have horn-like projections on the shell (Ref. 205).  Minimum depth from Ref. 58018.

species.name: Yucatan tetra
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Yunnanilus altus
species.description: Inhabits small stream with moderate flowing water.  Moves slowly in shoals on the bottom.  Feeds on filamentous algae and insects.

species.name: Yunnanilus bailianensis
species.description: A cave-inhabitant (Ref. 89125).

species.name: Yunnanilus brevis
species.description: Found in still and slow running waters (Ref. 4832).  Occurs in a shallow lake, with dense bottom and floating vegetation (Ref. 39226).

species.name: Yunnanilus macrogaster
species.description: Found in a small marsh with abundant vegetation. Sympatric with Y. niger and Y. paludosus. Feeds on worms and insects.

species.name: Yunnanilus niger
species.description: Found in a small marsh with abundant vegetation. Sympatric with Y. macrogaster and Y. paludosus.

species.name: Yunnanilus nigromaculatus
species.description: Adults inhabit shallow waters of lake (less than 1 m deep) among vegetation, but not in inlets or outlets of the lake.  Feed on shrimps (Ref. 12040).

species.name: Yunnanilus niulanensis
species.description: Occurs in Yanglinhe River , China with altitude of 1909 m and with slow flowing and clear water.  The stream of the type locality has sandy or a little muddy substrate (Ref. 89956).

species.name: Yunnanilus pachycephalus
species.description: Inhabits torrential waters under rocks.

species.name: Yunnanilus paludosus
species.description: Found in a small marsh with abundant vegetation.

species.name: Yunnanilus parvus
species.description: Found in the cave outlet.  Feeds on detritus.  A ripe female measuring 3.76 cm SL contains ripe ova, about 1 mm in diameter.

species.name: Yunnanilus pleurotaenia
species.description: Stomach of a ripe female contains a single gammarid crustacean.

species.name: Yunnanilus pulcherrimus
species.description: Inhabits underground river (Ref. 76753).

species.name: Zaca blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Feeds on invertebrates.

species.name: Zacapu allotoca
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in turbid water, over mud bottoms (Ref. 42981).  Hides under vegetation (Ref. 42981).

species.name: Zacapu shiner
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits Lake Zacapu which is fed by at least 12 large springs.  The spring water is clean and supports dense vegetation.  The rest of the lake has turbid water with less vegetation than the spring area (Ref. 84762).

species.name: Zacco taliensis
species.description: Inhabits tranquil and open areas of lake.  Feeds on plankton.  Famous locally for its tender flesh and delicious taste (Ref. 45563).

species.name: Zagros spined loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. At the type locality of this species, the Dehno is a shallow and narrow (up to 5 m wide) stream with diverse structures (pools, riffles, gravel bed, sandy shore, etc.).  At the time of collection, the water was clear with swift current and the specimens were found in shallow water (30-50 cm depth) above gravel (Ref. 99625).

species.name: Zaire lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in clear forest rivers and brooks (Ref. 59344).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Zaireichthys compactus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits muddy brownish and fast flowing water with substrate consisting of muddy sections, areas of sand and stony to rocky regions including the bank zones (Ref. 78218).

species.name: Zaireichthys flavomaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zaireichthys heterurus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear, swift flowing tributaries lying to the east of the Congo River mainstream (Ref. 51287).

species.name: Zaireichthys kafuensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zaireichthys kavangoensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zaireichthys kunenensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zaireichthys lacustris
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is recorded from depths of 10-30 m in the southern part and at a depth of about 20 m at Sanga in the central portion of Lake Malawi (Ref. 86935). It has been taken by trawl over the sandy substrata near Monkey Bay, where it is found in empty gastropod shells, and it is also collected in shells by divers (Ref. 86935). It is inquiline with the cichlid fish Pseudotropheus lanisticola in shells of the large gastropod Lanistes nyassanus; the co-existence of the two species in one shell is fortuitous and the catfish occupies probably the upper part of the shell which the cichlid cannot reach (Ref. 86935). Both sexes attain maturity at a standard length of about 17 mm (Ref. 86935). Mature males take up territories in shells; females may share these for some time before depositing their eggs; it appears that females leave the shells shortly after oviposition whereas the males remain in the shells, presumably to guard the brood; the small size of the buccal cavity and the narrow mouth with a width less than 2.5 egg diameters, suggests that mouth brooding is improbable (Ref. 86935). It feeds on ostracods, cladocerans, copepods, chironomid larvae and small trichopteran larvae; some diatom frustules were also observed but it is possible that these were taken fortuitously with invertebrate food items (Ref. 86935).

species.name: Zaireichthys mandevillei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It is confined to sandy reaches of the mainstream of the Congo River and its largest tributaries (Ref. 51287).

species.name: Zaireichthys maravensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in fast-flowing streams and small rivers with clear water and a sandy bottom (Ref. 86935).

species.name: Zaireichthys wamiensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zaireichthys zonatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Although the habitat was very rocky, specimens were only collected on the edge of a sandy area (Ref. 51287).

species.name: Zalanthias kelloggi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zambesi parrotfish
species.description: Nocturnal shoaling species; favors large river channels with a soft bottom and fringing vegetation (Ref. 7248, 52193). Found mainly in sheltered bays, lagoons and swampy areas; occurs also in typical sandy or rocky rivers (Ref. 13337). Feeds on bottom-living invertebrates (Ref. 52193) and insect larvae at night (Ref. 5595). Known to migrate up tributary rivers of Lake Kariba during rainy season, though it is not yet clear whether this is a breeding migration (Ref. 13337). Breeds during summer rainy season; females carry up to 5,000 eggs (Ref. 7248).

species.name: Zambezi bream
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very adaptive, found across varying habitats; agamous, ovophilic, maternal mouthbrooder (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Zambezi grunter
species.description: Espèce de poissons. It prfers rocky habitats or marginal vegetation in slow-flowing rivers and lagoons, often taking shelter under trees (Ref. 52193). It feeds on small fishes and invertebrates like snails, shrimps and insects (Ref. 52193). Eggs are large and relatively few, suggesting parental care, but no details are know (Ref. 52193). It 'grunts' when removed from the water (Ref. 7248, 52193).

species.name: Zambezi happy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Very adaptive, found in almost every habitat type within its distributional range; feeds mainly on small fish, aquatic insects and crustaceans; females only spawn once a year, around September during the rainy season; spawns of approximately 200 eggs per female are possible; males excavate shallow craters in shallow waters for spawning (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Zamboangan dragonet
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zamurito
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Is reported to commonly attack the fishes caught in fishermen's nets and seines as well as those hooked on trotlines or gaffed (Ref. 6868).

species.name: Zanzibar barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zanzibar guitarfish
species.description: A benthic species on inner continental shelf; rarely caught and its life history is unknown.  Reports to 205 cm TL are likely to be erroneous.  Males mature at ca. 64 cm TL (Ref. 114953).

species.name: Zanzibar sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zapogon isus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zavora pipefish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205).

species.name: Zayan barbel
species.description: Found in riffle areas in headwaters of large rivers (Ref. 107618). Spawning takes place from late April to early May (Ref. 107618).

species.name: Zebra blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults occur along exposed rocky shores from the highest tide pools to the surf zone. Exposed to great fluctuations in temperature, salinity, oxygen content and pH (Ref. 205). Benthic (Ref. 58302). Very agile with remarkable leaping ability, moving rapidly in a series of jumps from pool to pool. Feed on detritus and benthic algae (Ref. 3921). Oviparous. Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114). Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114). With Ophioblennius stage (Ref. 9962).

species.name: Zebra catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebra clingfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in rocky areas (Ref. 37955).  Feeds mainly on barnacles and small crustaceans (Ref. 37955).

species.name: Zebra dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits dead algal-covered reef in 3-15 m (Ref. 90102). Reported to feed primarily on harpacticoid copepods (49.5% - 100% of the gut contents) and they consume an average of 249 copepods per square meter of reef surface (Ref. 116739).

species.name: Zebra fish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow rocky reefs, sandy and weedy flats; also in estuaries.  Feeds on algae.

species.name: Zebra garden eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in shallow water.  Burrows of individuals are in pairs, approximately 8 inches apart; with neighboring pairs at least 3-4 times greater apart from each other.  Usually in moderate sized aggregations that appear during current runs (Ref. 48635). Usually in colonies on sand bottoms near reefs, sheltered bays and coastal sand slopes (Ref 90102).

species.name: Zebra goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas, often in caves and crevices.  Occurs from intertidal to 97 m depth.  Often collected for home aquarium.  Oviparous (Ref. 56079).  Males guard the eggs which are found attached to roof of shelter (Ref. 56079).

species.name: Zebra lampeye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in small forest brooks and rivers, usually moderate to fast-flowing bodies of water under forest cover (Ref. 59344).  Not a seasonal killifish.  Is very difficult to maintain in aquarium (Ref. 27139).

species.name: Zebra loach
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in clear mountain streams (Ref. 41236).

species.name: Zebra mbuna
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in rocky areas which may be sediment-free and shallow or sediment-rich at somewhat deeper levels.  Feeds at right angles with the substrate by combing loose material from the biocover.  Also feeds on plankton in the open water (Ref. 5595).

species.name: Zebra seahorse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found inshore on reef areas (Ref. 7300).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 205).  The male carries the eggs in a brood pouch which is found under the tail (Ref. 205). Also found in sand and mud bottoms, possibly associated with gorgonians (Ref 90102).

species.name: Zebra sole
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits shallow sand and mud bottoms of coastal waters.  Feeds mainly on benthic invertebrates, especially small crustaceans.  Marketed fresh, frozen, and dried-salted.

species.name: Zebra spiny eel
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebra tilapia
species.description: Occurs only in larger rivers with rocky substrates, not found in smaller creeks; not specialized, but prefers a herbivorous diet; pair-bonding, biparental open substratum spawner holding very large territories; might spawn throughout the year (Ref. 52307).

species.name: Zebratail blenny
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Eggs are demersal and adhesive (Ref. 205), and are attached to the substrate via a filamentous, adhesive pad or pedestal (Ref. 94114).  Larvae are planktonic, often found in shallow, coastal waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Zebratail cory
species.description: Often found in the company of C. melanistius brevirostris and C. spilurus on sandy bottoms traversed by a strong current (Ref. 27188). Abundant in the backwaters of sandy beaches downstream from rapids; also occurring in creeks with sandy-rocky bottom and some plant debris (Ref. 35381).

species.name: Zebrette goby
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias altipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias annandalei
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coastal waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Zebrias callizona
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias cochinensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias crossolepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias keralensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in coastal waters (Ref. 45255).

species.name: Zebrias lucapensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias maculosus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias munroi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zebrias zebrinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy-mud bottoms.  Found in sheltered bays and estuaries in shallow sand habitats.  Usually seen only at night (Ref. 48637).

species.name: Zelinda's parrotfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zenarchopterus dux
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zenarchopterus ectuntio
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur at surface levels in estuaries and rivers well upstream from the tidal zone.  Feeds on terrestrial insects.  Marketed fresh (Ref. 12693).

species.name: Zenarchopterus philippinus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits streams and lakes.

species.name: Zenarchopterus quadrimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Environment not certain, another reference is needed.

species.name: Zenarchopterus xiphophorus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zenion hololepis
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found over mud or sand-mud bottom (Ref. 26999). Reported to up to 700m depth (Ref. 89996).

species.name: Zenion longipinnis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zenopsis oblonga
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zenopsis stabilispinosa
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zephyr anchovy
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in estuarine waters and mangrove lagoons and collected abundantly during northeast monsoon seasons (Ref. 123745).

species.name: Zephyrichthys barryi
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zesticelus bathybius
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Minimum depth reported at 700 m (Ref. 41299).

species.name: Zesticelus ochotensis
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zhobi mahseer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Length given by Adnan Khan (pers. comm, 04/07).

species.name: Ziebell’s Handfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Ziegler's triplefin
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults inhabit rock and coral reefs (Ref. 90102).  They are found in very shallow water on coralline ground (Ref 13227).  Eggs are hemispherical and covered with numerous sticky threads that anchor them in the algae on the nesting sites (Ref. 240).  Larvae are planktonic which occur primarily in shallow, nearshore waters (Ref. 94114).

species.name: Zigzag barb
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zigzag pygmygoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in mid to outer barrier reefs, but much more common on outer barrier islands (Ref. 86820). Also found in caves and crevices (Ref. 90102).

species.name: Zingel
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Adults are found in main course of large rivers, in fast-flowing waters.  Active at night, feeding on aquatic invertebrates and small fishes.  Spawning occurs on sand bottom in March-April.  A female spawn with several males in a dense spawning groups.  Eggs are very sticky and attached to gravel (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Zingel balcanicus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits main rivers (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Zipper sand skate
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oviparous.  Distinct pairing with embrace.  Young may tend to follow large objects, such as their mother (Ref. 205).  Eggs are oblong capsules with stiff pointed horns at the corners deposited in sandy or muddy flats (Ref. 205).  Egg capsules are 2.2 cm long and 1.8 cm wide (Ref. 41250).

species.name: Zippered dottyback
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Observed on rubble slopes at depths of 38 to 52 m; solitarily or in pairs around isolated rock-coral outcrops on otherwise low-profile sand/rubble bottoms (Ref. 74964).

species.name: Zirahuen allotica
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits small, deep mountain lake with sandy bottom which is partly covered with mud (Ref. 26130).

species.name: Zoarces andriashevi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Maximum length based on largest known specimen (immature) (Ref. 57828).

species.name: Zoarces elongatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits continental shelves from the littoral zone to about 300 m, where these may enter brackish water during early winter spawning migrations (Ref. 11954).

species.name: Zoarces fedorovi
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found under stones in the channel of a river during low tide (Ref. 74969).  Largest mature individuals caught measure 21.5-31.5 cm TL (Ref. 74969).  Viviparous, with variable number of eggs, 4-131 (Ref. 74969).

species.name: Zoarces gillii
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits sandy mud bottoms of near shore areas and estuaries (Ref. 11230).

species.name: Zoarchias glaber
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Zoarchias hosoyai
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Recorded from rocky shores.

species.name: Zoarchias macrocephalus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zoarchias major
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zoarchias microstomus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabit mainly rocky shores and tidal pools containing small stones and seaweeds.  Feed on polychaetes.

species.name: Zoarchias neglectus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits tide pools.

species.name: Zoarchias uchidai
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zoarchias veneficus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found among seaweed and rock along the coast.

species.name: Zoned dwarfgoby
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits algal covered rocks, rubble, or corals (Ref. 1602).

species.name: Zonetail butterfly ray
species.description: Demersal inshore, in shallow depths to at least 37 m (Ref.58048). Also found offshore (Ref. 9918).  Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Smallest individual was 27 cm WD. Caught often by demersal trawl, trammel and gillnet fisheries, and occasionally using tangle nets. Utilized for its meat, but of limited value due to its typically small size (Ref.58048).

species.name: Zongolica catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zoogoneticus purhepechus
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The type locality is a permanent spring of lentic and clear waters and forms a small pond of approximately 1500 sq.m; the bottom rocky in its periphery and muddy in most of the pond. Aquatic vegetation composed of Iris sp. and Ceratophyllum sp, emergent vegetation Typha sp. and Scirpus sp., and the introduced species Eichhornia sp; the terrestrial vegetation is of the subtropical forest type. Associated fish fauna are the native species, Alloophorus robustus, Chapalichthys encaustus, Goodea atripinnis, Skiffia multipunctata (Goodeidae); Poeciliopsis infans (Poeciliidae); Lampetra geminis (Petromyzontidae); and introduced species Poecilia mexicana, Xiphophorus hellerii (Poeciliidae), Oreochromis spp. (Cichlidae), Cyprinus carpio, and Ctenopharingodon idella (Cyprinidae) (Ref. 83562).

species.name: Zope
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occur in large lowland rivers with backwaters and also in eutrophic lowland lakes.  Feed mainly on zooplankton in open water of backwaters and other still water bodies.  Spawn along shores of rivers or in backwaters on submerged vegetation and also on gravel in moderate current.  Migrate upriver in long distances to suitable spawning sites.  Juveniles stay in backwaters and flooded zones along rivers.  Enter freshened parts of seas to forage.  Life span reaches more than 10 years.  Locally threatened by habitat alterations along river banks (Ref. 59043).

species.name: Zoramia flebila
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zoramia viridiventer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is often seen in aggregations in lagoons or bays, sheltering among branching corals, sponges, etc. Collections come from the depth range of 2-17 m, but it may be seen at least as deep as 50 m (Ref. 58268).

species.name: Zoster wrasse
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found on semi-open sandy substrates along reefs, often in deep channels to lagoons that are prone to strong tidal currents and where seawhips thrive (Ref. 48636).

species.name: Zucchini catfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. One of the largest loricariids.

species.name: Zugmayer's pearleye
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Oceanic, mesopelagic or bathypelagic species (Ref. 6601, 58302).  Most adults have been taken in hauls to depths considerably in excess of 500 m (Ref. 10755).  Adults prey on other midwater fishes (Ref. 6691).

species.name: Zugmayer's slickhead
species.description: Found on the continental slope (Ref. 75154).

species.name: Zulu snakelet
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Known from limestone and coral reefs.

species.name: Zulu toadfish
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This species is not common and apparently choose holes into which it fits snugly. Feeds on whole mlluscs (Amalda optima, Colubraria c.f. castanea, Harpa queketti, Phalium labliatum, and Ranella sp. (Ref. 91120).

species.name: Zungaro dorado
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zungaro jahu
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zungaropsis multimaculatus
species.description: Espèce de poissons.

species.name: Zuojiangia jingxiensis
species.description: Found in a karst cave outlet and connected stream, at 1-2 m depth. Sympatric with Balitora ludongensis, Cophecheilus bamen, Prolixicheilus longisulcus, Rectoris longibarbus and Yunnanilus jinxiensis (Ref. 128942).

species.name: Âne
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A short-lived species reported to live in fast-flowing rivers with a  gravel substrate (Ref. 30578).  Occurs in main course of rivers and large streams and in riffles.  Found on stone bottom (Ref. 59043).  Lurks on the bottom during the day and comes out for crepuscular feeding (Ref. 11941).  Feeds on aquatic invertebrates.  Larvae feed on plankton under surface, then at about 2.5 cm SL, they move to benthic habitats.  Attains first sexual maturity at 2-4 years of age.  Spawns in deeper parts of riffles.  Deposits on gravel strongly adhesive eggs, 2.2 mm in diameter, which hatch in about 14 days at 13° C (Ref. 59043).  Threatened due to habitat destruction and pollution (Ref. 26100).

species.name: Écureuil
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Benthopelagic in or near crevices or caves at 30-188 m (Ref. 58302); collected from 100-190 m (Ref, 117152). Confined to outer reef slopes (Ref. 1602).  Rarely occurring in less than 40 m depth, in current prone areas (Ref. 48635). Solitary or in small groups (Ref 90102). Feeds on crustaceans (Ref. 89972).

species.name: Écureuil des Seychelles
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Found in shallow waters of coral reefs and rocky shores (Ref. 4201).  Often found between branching corals (Ref. 9710).

species.name: Écureuil diadème
species.description: Espèce de poissons. A common species that inhabits shallow coral reefs (Ref. 58534) and lagoon and seaward reefs to depths of 30 m or more. Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Occurs under ledges or in crevices during the day and feeds on isopods; at night it roams over open sand and low-profile reef areas to feed on polychaetes and small crabs. Stomach contents listed gastropods (e.g. Atys sp.), polychaetes, small clams, solenogastrid, isopods, brachyuran crabs, and other crustaceans (Ref. 27370). Tends to occur in aggregations (Ref. 30573). Venomous spine on its preopercle. Size rarely exceeds 13 cm. Minimum depth reported taken from Ref. 30874.

species.name: Écureuil samouraï
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs in outer reef slopes.  A nocturnal species that feeds mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps.  Spine of preopercle venomous. Solitary or in groups (Ref 90102).

species.name: Écureuil tacheté
species.description: Espèce de poissons. This schooling species inhabits seagrass beds and hard-bottomed habitats from the reef flat to depths of 46 m or more on lagoon and seaward reefs. Often found with branching Acropora coral (Ref. 9710). Most common Neophion found in shallow areas (Ref. 9710). Benthopelagic (Ref. 58302). Feeds on small fishes (Ref. 30573), small crabs, and shrimps at night. Venomous spine at the corner of its preopercle. Marketed fresh (Ref. 9948). Solitary (Ref 90102).

species.name: Écureuil à taches noires
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Inhabits coral-rich areas of outer reef slopes and drop-offs to depths greater than 40 m (Ref. 9710).  Hides in caves or beneath ledges by day; forage for food at night, mainly on benthic crabs and shrimps.  Spine of preopercle venomous.

species.name: Élingue
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs on the upper slope (Ref. 6144).  Depth range from 388-754 in the eastern Ionian Sea (Ref. 56504).

species.name: Élingue (Molva molva)
species.description: Espèce de poissons. Occurs mainly on rocky bottoms in fairly deep water (Ref. 9988).  Found more commonly from 100 to 400 m.  Feeds on fish (cod, herring, flatfish), lobsters, cephalopods and starfishes.    Principal spawning areas are Biscay, slopes west of the British Isles and off the Faeroes and southern Iceland (Ref. 35388).  Marketed fresh, dried or salted and frozen; eaten steamed, fried, broiled and baked (Ref. 9988).

species.name: Éléphant de mer
species.description: Espèce de poissons. The second largest shark, reportedly reaching 1,220-1,520 cm TL (Ref. 247). Thought to live up to 50 years (Ref. 9030, 89083). Semi-oceanic or oceanic species, highly migratory (Ref. 43278). Found on continental and insular shelves, offshore and often close to land, just off the surf zone; enters enclosed bays (Ref. 247). Coastal-pelagic at 1 meter to unknown depths, probably epipelagic (Ref. 58302). Occurs singly, in pairs or groups of 3 or more, or in huge schools (group of up to 100 individuals has been reported) (Ref. 6871, 43278). Prefers water temperature between 8-16 °C (Ref. 88171). Makes extensive horizontal and vertical movements along the continental shelf and shelf edge to utilize productive feeding areas (Ref. 50200). During the summer months, it is found near the surface of boreal to warm-temperate areas (Ref. 43278) feeding on zooplankton by filtering (Ref. 88781). Found in deeper waters during winter (Ref. 6871, 50200, 58302). Undertakes long transoceanic migrations (e.g. from the British Isles to Newfoundland, Canada (Ref. 88824)) and moves between the northern and southern hemisphere in tropical mesopelagic water (Ref. 88825). These migrations have been found to cover distances of over 9,000 km. May form segregations by size or sex (Ref. 88171). Ovoviviparous (Ref. 50449). Regarded as ordinarily harmless and inoffensive but potentially dangerous if attacked (particularly when harpooned) (Ref. 247). In Bay of Fundy, Canada parasitic lampreys have been found attached to the back of basking sharks and sucking their blood (Ref. 83375). Utilized fresh, frozen and dried, or salted (Ref. 9987). Also valued for its liver for oil, fins for soup, hide for leather and carcass for fishmeal (Ref. 247). May be a potential source of anti-carcinoma drugs (Ref. 6034, 6035). Used in Chinese medicine (Ref. 12166). Threatened due to bycatch fisheries (Ref. 83294).
